Bretonia quickly contracted Ageira's services for the delicate task of keeping the Gallic gate operational. Using experience gained from dissecting abandoned Gallic infrastructure in Bretonia, Ageira cobbled together various workarounds to keep the Gate in one piece. Despite this, there are frequent outages and the extreme stress placed on the Gate's components is shortening the structure's operational lifespan significantly.

35015.text: The Gallic Union is furious that we’re here with “their” gate. Bretonia and Kusari apparently have some kind of agreement where they’ll back each other up if the Gauls try anything. Maybe they would if it was just Bretonia in the way, but I doubt they fancy taking on two Houses at once, after how that went last time round. Crayter too, I suppose.

35016.text: This is one of Ageira’s more fascinating postings. There is no standardized interface between our proprietary technology and Gallia’s pale imitation. There’s no process manual governing how this works. DSE can’t plug in a White Box and expect the system to function. Instead, we’re in a constant state of on-site assessment, experimentation and fine tuning.

35018.text: London is determined to hold this gate as a bargaining chip. The Gallic Union have never accepted any responsibility for what was done to us, for the crimes against humanity perpetrated by officers who are members of their government. We’ll disassemble this gate and send the parts back to Ile-de-France when they give us those criminals and agree to reparations.

35019.text: The garrison on Scalpay answers to the captain of the J Fendall. There aren’t enough of us here to resist a serious push if it came to that -- but it won’t come to that. The Admiralty euphemistically calls us a “tripwire force”. The Union knows that if they declared on us, the Tadasu Agreement would bring Kusari into the war, and probably Crayter too.

35021.text: There is still a DSE engineering staff assigned to this site, however Ageira are running this show directly. The egg-heads don’t usually like to get their hands dirty, but they couldn’t resist the chance to play with a fully functional Gallic Jump Gate. Our role here is more mundane than normal -- this Gate is continually springing leaks that need patching and welding.

35022.text: Scalpay is probably our most dangerous assignment since the Hokkaido job back at the turn of the century. Drop your guard for a moment and you could be iced by Outcast pirates, GNI spooks, Corsican assassins, or even disgruntled miners. You’d think they at least would appreciate having a stable Jump Gate back to the markets where they sell their goods...

35024.text: Planet Harris is considered a bad assignment to be given, and this is substantially worse than that. We drop off Water, Food Rations and Consumer Goods here at Scalpay before heading on to the BMM and Samura mining site nearby to collect their ore. On just that short stretch, we lost an escort to an Outcast ambush.

35025.text: For years we’ve tried to stabilize this system through consortium funding for bounties on the Outcasts and Gallic pirates that terrorize the area. Bowex, BMM, Crayter and Samura all contributed significantly. Would you believe that Cryer recently joined the arrangement and doubled our combined contributions for killed or captured Outcasts?

35030.text:
The Belfast Belt is all that remains of Belfast Production Facility. Belfast was constructed by BMM in 682 AS, however working conditions aboard were notoriously poor. By 814 AS, matters reached breaking point, when mutinous crew members welcomed in Molly attackers. The Mollys then fortified the captured station with a minefield.

The Mollys continued to hold Belfast up until 825 AS, when they were betrayed by the Gallic Battleship Embrun that had been resupplying there during a temporary ceasefire. Belfast was obliterated by a nuclear device, with the surviving fragments and the defensive minefield eventually falling into a degrading orbit of Middlesbrough. The Belfast Belt now poses a navigational hazard for shipments boosting minerals from terrestrial automated platforms up to Redcarr Refinery.

35032.text:
ARCHON DESIGN SCHEMATICS

This datavault contains detailed schematics for the T-2419-U Archon Medium Mining Ship, allowing for construction at standard shipyard facilities. The file has been cryptographically signed with the name 'Taro Yamada'. Purchase disables the vault's encryption, enabling use.

Properties
Base Price: $500000
Container Hitpoints: 4000
Cargo Space Per Unit: 1

35034.text:
HYDROGEN

Hydrogen is the lightest element and one of the most abundant resources in the galaxy. It is usually found as a colorless, odorless and highly flammable gas. Most of the commercially extracted Hydrogen in Sirius originates from the vast reserves of the Crow Nebula, however gas giant extraction is sometimes used as an expensive alternative. Hydrogen is an essential input for the creation of H-Fuel, and and has many other industrial utilities.

Properties
Base Price: $2
Container Hitpoints: 4000
Cargo Space Per Unit: 1

35039.text:
ARTIFICIAL PERSONALITY FRAGMENT

Gammu AI vessels and their derivatives are almost incomprehensibly strange amalgamations of human originating and alien technology, the product of almost eight centuries of divergence. Destroyed or crippled AI vessels typically self-destruct, however fragments of their internals can sometimes be salvaged for study. Groups such as The Core are keenly interested in reverse engineering the secrets of 'true' AI.

Properties
Base Price: $50
Container Hitpoints: 4000
Cargo Space Per Unit: 1

35076.text:
CLASS: Sarissa
CREW: CLASSIFIED
ARMAMENT: CLASSIFIED

The Battleship Sardinia's keel was first laid down in 825 AS at Corsica Shipyard, commissioned as the crown jewel of the Benitez Cartel's military forces. The Sarissa's lighter frame compared to the heavy Ranseur Dreadnoughts should have allowed the battleship to flexibly and economically support Outcast assassins and raiders in a wider range of combat scenarios. Regrettably, the launch of the Hasta class the following year led many to call the Sardinia's necessity into question, arguing that the modern battlecruisers had already made the battleship redundant in this role.

As a result of these disputes, several cartels withdrew their support from the project - resource shipments and progress accordingly slowed to a crawl. The Maltese Slave Revolt in 831 AS saw the Sardinia's construction halted altogether. The Benitez line was rendered extinct during the Revolt, with many believing the partially completed vessel would be scrapped as a result. Despite this, the conflict instilled the Outcasts with a renewed paranoia for the security of their homeworld. Additionally, many of junior cartels found themselves jockeying to fill the power vacuum left by Malta's badly damaged ancient families.

It was a coalition of these junior cartels that took on the Sardinia, funding its completion as a symbol of their prestige and vitality. The battleship will soon launch from Corsica's drydocks, where it is intended to take on the role of guard ship over Malta. This will allow the Dreadnought Basilica to continue its deadly work elsewhere, while earning the Sardinia's patrons political capital and influence.

35078.text: The Aptera Arena is frequently used by young Cretian teenagers as a means of proving their worth, or by Corsair warriors to settle slights of honor. Periodically, ceremonial fights are held at the arena to showcase Corsair martial prowess, including the notorious Masked Gladiator Contest, where anonymous combatants compete for the Elders' approval. This victorious champion, hailed as a hero of Crete, may choose to unmask and reveal their identity, their triumph broadcast across the Empire.

35085.text:
Site Jarrow is a partially dormant Daam-K’vosh structure, concealed deep within the eye of a vast storm on the gas giant Darlington. Following the collapse of the Craster Initiative in the late 670s, whispers of anomalous minefields and a huge gravity well hidden within the nebula depths trickled back to Bretonian society. This oddity was overlooked for another ten years, until a Cambridge University research team assembled an expedition to investigate the rumors. When the expedition arrived and confirmed the alien origin of the protective minefield, the Bretonia Intelligence Service moved quickly to classify the findings and compel the services of the scientists.

Now fully funded by Bretonia under terms of absolute secrecy, work on mapping the minefields and investigating the newly discovered gas giant Darlington quickly commenced. Site Jarrow was revealed by atmospheric probes soon after. Jarrow was described as a vast, alien station, seemingly suspended in defiance of gravity thanks to 5 enormous generator pylons around the periphery. The central core was believed to be dormant, emitting no detectable energy signatures. The structures’ crystalline skins proved near-impenetrable, frustrating attempts to gain access. For many years, work focused on studying the Site’s exterior, constructing semi-permanent xenoarchaeology camps, and preparing for the deployment of the ambitious Sunderland Research Aerostat. This work was incredibly hazardous, owing to fierce meteorological conditions, including radiation, gale winds and lightning strikes.

While exact figures are also classified, dozens of engineers are believed to have been killed across these projects. Other than periodic breakthroughs, such as the discovery of the Amiatinus Cache, work on Jarrow has been consistently slow and incremental. Towards the end of the Colony Wars, the central structure’s lower pylon reactivated, blasting a beam down into the atmosphere. Later, during 831 AS’ Blackout, Jarrow’s generators “blinked”, causing the entire structure to drop almost a kilometer deeper into Darlington’s atmosphere. During the "Blink" pulse of 836 AS, Site Jarrow's southern island overloaded and shut down. While this partially destabilized the structure's gravity field, it has not slowed Jarrow's escalating energy readings or assuaged the BIS' concerns.

35087.text:
Camp Bede was the first semi-permanent presence established within Darlington’s atmosphere, with construction beginning in 689 AS. Bede was used to pioneer several innovative construction techniques involving adhesives and gravity anchors, as Jarrow’s skin could not at the time be penetrated to drill traditional pilings. Bede’s site was selected due to the level, sheltered surface, and the presence of what was believed to be an airlock that might present a structural weakness that could be exploited.

Little progress was made until 705 AS, when study of the fragment chips produced by tunneling attempts resulted in a breakthrough in the synthesis of similar crystalline compounds. At extreme cost, this allowed for the production of limited quantities of experimental drillbits capable of penetrating Jarrow’s surface. Over the course of several years, an entryway was laboriously bored through the airlock. This revealed a number of antechambers that were isolated from the wider structure. Exploration of these spaces resulted in the discovery of the Amiatinus Cache, which remains a subject of research at an undisclosed location to this day.

Bede’s significance waned after the Sunderland umbilical was established, with work consisting largely of archaeological categorization of the antechambers' architecture. Many BIS researchers now see an assignment at Bede as a punishment detail, given the hazardous, spartan conditions and low likelihood of new breakthroughs occurring there.

35089.text:
Camp Ceolfrith was the third xenoarchaeology camp established within Darlington’s atmosphere, founded in 729 AS to study one of the peripheral active pylons attached to Site Jarrow. For decades, this was limited to surface scans and external analysis of the enigmatic power “leylines” radiating across the structure. Penetrative boring was prohibited during this period, over fears it could damage the mysterious anti-gravity mechanisms within.

Following the “Blink” event of 831 AS, the camp was expanded and boring permitted. The risk of damage was now deemed acceptable to gain insight into how the pylon works. Currently, two bore sites have been established, using an elevator system for access. Sabotage of the gravity pylons is currently being considered as a potential countermeasure against a hostile reactivation scenario for Site Jarrow.

35091.text: Ecgbert is the most recent xenoarchaeology camp to be established in Darlington’s atmosphere, and is actively under construction. Work on Ecgbert began in 835 AS, after new surface scans identified an internal void that could be breached to potentially provide access to more of Jarrow’s core mechanisms. This goal is particularly important to BIS contingency planning, as fears mount over the possibility of Jarrow’s full activation -- whatever form that might take.

35094.text: Redcarr Orbital was constructed by BMM in orbit of Middlesbrough to retrieve minerals collected by automated extraction platforms. Due to the moon's unstable conditions and Bretonia's financial difficulties, the construction of a docking ring was ruled out as infeasible. Instead, the Redcarr Orbital uses its powerful tractor beams and Middlesbrough's low gravity to latch onto containers launched up into the atmosphere, pulling them into orbit. While the Orbital is difficult to maintain, it nonetheless reduces launch costs enough to make mining Middlesbrough practical.

35096.text:
CLASS: Oasis
AMENITIES: Full
CREW: 380

The Apollo is a Cryer Pharmaceuticals research ship that functions as a mobile laboratory and barracks for Cryer personnel. In recent years, the Apollo has primarily been deployed in orbit of Planet Carlisle, supporting the bacterial eradication project and the joint Planetform facilities aboard Gateshead Station. The Apollo regularly shuttles between Newcastle and Planet Denver in Colorado to rotate specialist geneticists between Liberty and the project site.

35098.text: Sensor arrays are powerful scanning satellites that are deployed to detect potential hostile ships. In recent decades, sensor arrays capable of disrupting cloaking devices have been deployed to key areas throughout the Colonies.

35100.text: The Thornton was a Cryer Pharmaceuticals armored courier that disappeared while traveling through Newcastle in 827 AS. The vessel had been stationed at Gateshead Station as a part of Cryer's Carlisle project, and was bound for the Cambridge Research Station. Scans indicate that internal cargo hold quarantine protocols partially triggered, incinerating some portion of the cargo. Based on the Thornton's final transmissions, Bretonian authorities believe the transport was likely intercepted by Gaian terrorists.

35102.text: Sentinel was an Eagle class fighter registered as a civilian freelancer. Its flight manifest and pilot identity have been classified and redacted by Bretonian authorities. Damage patterns indicate it was likely attacked and disabled by Gaian terrorists.

35104.text: The Dupleix was a strike fighter serving in the Gallic Royal Navy during the invasion of Bretonia. It is likely that the ship was destroyed by Outcasts that prowl the Tyne Ice Field. The open canopy indicates the pilot ejected, however the Dupleix’s distress beacon seems to have been intentionally shot out.

35106.text: The Ambitieux was a strike fighter serving in the Gallic Royal Navy during the invasion of Bretonia. It is likely that the ship was lost following a sortie against the MacDuff fleet, then anchored near Planet Carlisle. A ruptured fuel line prevented the Ambitieux’s withdrawal back to Planet Harris in Tau-31.

35108.text: The Surcouf was piloted by notorious Gallic Royal Navy ace Emmanuelle Daigle, who was renowned for capturing downed Bretonian pilots for interrogation. Damage patterns across the Surcouf correspond with both Bretonian and Molly weapons, indicating that there may have been a temporary truce to bring her down.

35110.text: The Duilius was piloted by Arnold De Angelis, youngest son of the De Angelis cartel’s don. Arnold was infamous for toying with IMG vessels before finally dispatching them, and had departed the Destroyer Ceuta to raid South Shields. The Duilius appears to have diverted into the Craster Nebula to mask its approach, before being intercepted and destroyed by unknown vessels.

35111.text: This decrepit fighter has been dumped in the Yorkshire Debris Field. Following the end of the Gallic War, Scarborough Shipyard and many other industrial facilities were tasked with breaking up and recycling surplus assets. Some allege that Border Worlds Exports took payment for these jobs, then simply jettisoned the unwanted hulls into the nearby debris field.

35113.text: The Daydreamer was piloted by Lt Lloyd Parker, launching from the Battleship Harlow. Known for his short attention span and unusually laid back attitude, Lt Parker was investigating reports of Gaian fighters in the Yorkshire Debris Field when he crashed into a discarded engine cowling. Despite ejecting and being recovered by search and rescue soon after, the lieutenant's fighter was lost, blending in with the other wrecked Crusaders littering the area.

35115.text: The Utopian was a Planetform supply freighter headed to Gateshead Station. Its convoy was attacked by Gaian terrorists near the Manchester Jump Gate. The Clydesdale fled into the Craster Nebula, only to be crippled by an explosive gas field. The Utopian's cargo manifest has been redacted.

35117.text: The Méduse was a scout serving with Gallic Naval Intelligence, as a part of the Battleship Embrun's fleet. The fighter was damaged and separated from its squadron during a skirmish with Bretonian defenders. It retreated into the Northumberland Ice Field, expecting deference from the local Gaians. Instead, it appears the vengeful ecoterrorists took the opportunity to eliminate the isolated vessel when the opportunity presented itself.

35119.text: The Dauntless was piloted by Ens Harry Green, launching from the Battleship Harlow. The Ensign's last transmission reported that he was responding to an IMG distress call from the Tyne Ice Field, where an Outcast raid was ongoing. It appears that after arriving and engaging the Outcasts, the IMG security patrol immediately withdrew, leaving the ensign to his fate.

35121.text: The Gatecrasher was piloted by Lt Sophie Harris, launching from the Battleship Harlow. Lieutenant Harris was an ambitious young officer who'd commissioned too late to see service in the Gallic War. Despite this, she quickly amassed an impressive service record, with 12 confirmed kills on domestic terrorists to her name. This bravado lulled her into taking unnecessary risks, vanishing after chasing fleeing Gaian raiders from the Trade Lanes into the Northumberland Ice Field.

35123.text:
Camp Dryhthelm was the second xenoarchaeology camp established within Darlington’s atmosphere, founded in 712 AS to study the upper spire of Site Jarrow. The daring project was based on the hypothesis that the spire tip could contain some form of energy-emitter or aperture. The project was only enabled by a breakthrough in mining technology that allowed structural anchors to be sunk into Jarrow’s previously impenetrable surface.

The incremental insights drawn from this work are jealously guarded by the BIS, however many of the original scientists posted here later formed the core of Bretonia's Advanced Particle Laboratory. This produced several of the precursor theories that later paved the way for a range of Bretonian Tachyon weapons.

Work at the camp has recently taken on a frantic tone, owing to speculation that a potential activation of the Jarrow structure may result in an energy beam being fired from the emitter Dryhthelm is sited atop of. This, combined with a position that is highly exposed to the elements, makes Drythelm Darlington's most dangerous posting.

35124.text:
>>>WARNING: NAVIGATION HAZARD<<<

The Yorkshire Debris Field is the result of decades of shipbuilding and breaking at the nearby Scarborough Shipyard. Authorities recommend travelers avoid the field, as discarded reactor and engine housings have created a significant radiation hazard. Gaian ecoterrorists frequently use the field as cover to launch raids on Scarborough and the nearby Trade Lanes.

35125.text: The BPA runs regular patrols between both Jump Gates and up to Planet Carlisle. Scarborough is a convenient stop-over for refueling and repairs. There's a small BAF garrison onboard that we can call on for quick backup if we run into anything we can't handle ourselves. Usually that'll be Outcasts. It's always nice to see old faces I served alongside during the War, too.

35126.text: The BPA was devastated by the war. Most of our pilots were conscripted or volunteered for armed service, and a great many of them never made it home. I transferred across after the war ended and the big draw-down started. I could see the writing on the wall, I knew my service record wasn't impressive enough to make the cut as one of the BAF's retained officers. Flying for the BPA let me continue to serve, even if the pay and the equipment is pretty terrible these days.

35127.text: Pretty much from its inception, BPA had a reputation as the foremost professional police force in the Colonies. The Gallic War took a hammer to that, sadly. The force came close to collapse from conscription, so Parliament created the Militia as a stop-gap the remaining proper constables could supervise. They're ex-cons, malingerers and mercenaries. Special Constables, Colonial Coppers, whatever you want to call them. They're a stain on our reputation. The Militia should have been dissolved years ago.

35128.text: Carlisle is a hellish mix of heat, humidity, and deadly wildlife. The perfect place to stick the primary training camp of the Bretonian Army, naturally... This is without a doubt the worst posting I have ever had, and I fought on Planet Leeds when the Gauls first touched down. God help any poor Toms that can’t figure out their hazard suits while on maneuvers. If the bacteria doesn’t get them, their sergeant major will.

35129.text: Bretonia acquired a lot of materiel during the Gallic War. Thousands of times more than we need in peacetime. Carlisle was picked as the spot it’d all be dumped; outside the Clean Zone there are vast fields of Military Surplus protected by their own little Clean Bubbles. Parliament reckons having it stored here in the north is a deterrent to Gallia, while the bacteria acts as a free security fence for the stockpiles. Utter madness if you ask me. Carlisle is a hot, damp nightmare. That metal is going to corrode until it’s worthless.

35130.text: Lots of the BAF instructors here have slightly-illicit side-gigs as guides for game hunters. You’re not supposed to leave the Clean Zone, but the biggest, meanest and most valuable carnivores don’t much like straying inside it these days. Of course, outside the Clean Zone, if your hazard suit rips, you’re going to be Man Soup in little more than an hour. Not for me, I’ll tell you. I’ll stick to drinking awful liquor to pass my weekends.

35131.text: Beyond all the normal teething problems you’d expect on a young colony, we suspect Carlisle is also the epicenter of the Slog problem. Running down dealers to try and work up to the source is an endless task. That’s not helped by both the Gaians and Mollys seeming to be up to their elbows in the trade. Interrupt the wrong deal, and you’re getting a pickaxe to the back of the head and a pocketful of pyrite for your troubles.

35132.text: Nothing puts my hackles up like environmentalists on Carlisle. Cambridge students on sabbatical, posing for self-aggrandizing photos. Green Front firebrands sabotaging colony infrastructure and workplaces. Then there’s the bombings. Gaian work, right foul stuff. They’ve attacked the Terraforming Generators too. If they go down, the bacteria could kill us all. Mind you, I heard how the Gaians dealt with Fort Monarch -- maybe they wouldn’t care.

35133.text: There’s a lot of soldiers here in Currock City. From the big training camp out in the wilderness. Newly enlisted squaddies do a rotation out there to get to grips with military life and harsh conditions. Of course, when they get back to civilization, it’s like setting off a firework. Drunk and disorderly, public indecency, fights with the civilians. We give them a cell to cool off and set them loose in the morning. In return, the army’ll back us up if we ever need to cash in a favor.

35134.text: The Governor has a lot riding on her shoulders here. Carlisle is being publicly described as a sister colony to Sprague, but the government knows that Sprague is untenable in the long run. The location, the... challenging societal conditions that developed. Carlisle is a chance to start over and build a foundation for colonization that will last a millennium. It’s vital we don’t repeat the same mistakes that blighted Sprague, even if those mistakes were regrettably necessary due to the war.

35135.text: Colonization is expensive, and credits are something in severely short supply in Bretonia. To fund key infrastructure, the government has issued development charters to foreign corporations, primarily Universal Shipping and Deep Space Engineering. Both are preparing to establish their own frontier settlements. The combination of Liberty credits, Liberty citizens, and Liberty specialists managing Cryer’s bacterial project means Liberty’s interests are a major constituency we need to be mindful of.

35136.text: Any successful colony needs strong political backing to thrive, to access the resources and capabilities it needs. The Governor’s Office maintains a permanent staff on New London for the purpose of building relationships and currying favor with the government and other notable peers. This is an uphill struggle, because we are facing a campaign of political sabotage by Cambridge’s elites. The Lord Regents despise the Carlisle bacterial project, and are intent on seeing us fail.

35137.text: There’s a lot of work to be found here, but most of it is hard going. Lumber -- clearing the forests -- needs a lot of hands. I’d hesitate to call the produce wood, not like the stuff they grow on Cambridge anyway -- but it’s still useful enough for construction or Consumer Goods. Grind the tree flesh down and you can dry the pulp and press it into panels. Surprisingly strong once it binds. Not winning any prizes for beauty however, and it stinks until it's properly treated.

35138.text: Carlisle is the cheapest place in the Colonies to get a good fix of Slog. Yeah, don’t judge. Walk a mile in another bloke’s work boots. After a long day, my joints are on fire, my head is banging, and my stomach is empty. I try to sleep it off and I’m back in the war again. Go to the doctor and they tell me to think happy thoughts and get out their office. Slog makes it all numb, makes it go away. So I’ll take my medicine and make it through another day.

35139.text: Working the forests is dangerous business. The biggest beasties stay out of the Clean Zone, but we keep stun batons on hand for the rest. I hate Sumpers the worst. They’re giant, stinking, carnivorous slugs. Shoot one and the round will punch straight through, annoying it at best. Have to repeatedly shock them until they get the idea and leave. Horrible things burrow below the moss and wait for prey to walk by.

35140.text: The Bretonian economy is growing at a ferocious pace, driven by industrialization here and on Sprague. The loss of Planet Leeds set us back more than a century though. You’ve got room to grow when you’re starting from rock bottom. Where that leaves us compared to the other Houses, in terms of workforce and raw productive capacity, is the problem. BMM spent centuries making the hard decisions that were necessary to keep Bretonia competitive. Now, well... I just don’t know.

35141.text: BMM has a range of operations on Carlisle, ranging from biomass harvesting and mineral extraction to infrastructure development and goods manufacturing. Despite that, Carlisle presents a difficult environment to work in, politically and practically. Our freedom of action has been significantly hamstrung by Cambridge lobbying, which is making it difficult to run our operations effectively. Worker protections and environmental regulations have their place, but this is little more than sabotage by well-connected eco-radicals.

35142.text: Newcastle is significantly easier to operate in than Omega-3. We’re already scaling up Consumer Goods production using a combination of local materials and Kusari Optical Chips -- soon we will be able to meet all of Bretonia’s domestic demand. We are considering deprecating Industrial Material production on Sprague and spooling up factories here instead. Despite the higher regulatory burdens on Carlisle, the security situation alone allows for significant savings.

35143.text: Carlisle is a big opportunity for Gateway. After the disaster that Sprague turned out to be, Bretonia has reigned in the Royal Charters issued to Bowex and BMM. Rather than being an unsupervised playground for Crown Corporations, the government is managing this colony directly. That means we can bid for contracts and win because we’re competitive, without worrying about Bowex locking us out because they have BMM’s ear.

35144.text: Gateway lost a lot of ground when Poole was abandoned -- Caernarfon and Newbury were massive victories, the first time we’d taken government and police contracts from Bowex. Bowex has the audacity to blame us for making Poole cost-prohibitive to operate. Complete nonsense. Our bid was significantly lower than theirs, and they know it. Now we’ve got a taste for public contracts, we’ll just have to prove we can beat them here too.

35145.text: The first ship to set down on Carlisle was the IMG Clydesdale Fortunate in 669 AS. She didn’t live up to her name. Upon disembarking, the crew were exposed to Carlisle’s hostile bacteria, succumbing to infection incredibly quickly. Their wretched final transmission sealed Carlisle’s reputation as a deathworld for over a century. Apparently game hunters will pay a pretty penny to anyone who’ll take them into the wilderness to see the wreck.

35146.text: The Carlisle Eradication Project is mostly staffed by Liberty specialists. Despite being a flagship program of the Cambridge Research Station, you’ll be unofficially blackballed on Cambridge for involvement. Grant applications declined, tenures refused, papers rejected at peer review -- Green Front intellectual terrorism. The only xenogeneticists and microbiologists that will take the role are the ones who don’t see a future in Cambridge academia.

35147.text: Cryer has other Carlisle teams that aren’t working on the Eradication Project. I knew a scientist that was embedded with the BAF out in the wilderness -- wouldn’t say a word about what they were up to though. A few years back, I was drinking with him when we heard one of our transports -- the Thornton -- had gone missing on the way to Leeds. He turned gray and shipped out to Liberty the very next day.

35148.text: Working here comes with a sizable hazard premium. There’s a serious risk of attack by Gaian ecoterrorists, or harassment by their Green Front proxies. Each morning we have to run a full sweep of our shuttles for undercarriage bombs, and all Cryer facilities are patrolled by armed guards. Despite that, environmentalist protesters regularly block the roads leading to our labs. It’s terrifying really. You never know if one of the crowd is going to be a Gaian radical with a gun.

35149.text: This project is a little different to our normal work: we’re adjusting an existing biosphere rather than creating one. Carlisle is no Gaia -- simple, brutish creatures abound -- but I don’t think we’ve fully grasped the secondary effects of what we’re doing. Yes, we’re eradicating harmful bacteria, but there will be knock-on effects neither HQ nor the Bretonian government want to acknowledge. Hopefully I’ll be retired before those pigeons come home to roost.

35150.text: Once Planetform and Cryer synthesized the bacterial treatment aerosol, it was relatively trivial to alter our terraforming generators to distribute it. Bretonia will need to pay for the construction and maintenance of a globe-spanning network, or eventually the bacteria will simply return. Why, that equilibrium could be maintained for centuries. Perhaps there’s a bright and profitable future for Planetform as ecological adjusters?

35151.text: Canterbury has provided the Bretonian government with projections that Carlisle’s bacteria can be fully eradicated within 20 years, if a sufficient terraforming generator network is funded. I don’t see it. Gaians have already intensified their attacks on the project, and the “Clean Zone” site was picked precisely because its climate and terrain were amenable. It’s not realistic to assume we’ll proceed at pace or faster elsewhere.

35152.text: Bowex comes with a long heritage of reliability. We have been integral to Bretonia’s good fortune all the way back to 66 AS. That kind of longevity is vital for the development of a new colony. A logistics contract with Bowex will be as valid in five centuries as it is in five months. A pale imitation like Gateway simply does not have the staying power. They will be gone with the wind in a matter of years, like the countless failed upstarts before them.

35153.text: Military Surplus from the Gallic War is stored in large BAF stockpiles outside of Carlisle’s Clean Zone. Our freighters ship them from there to the space port, and then up to Gateshead Station in orbit where they await export to their final destination. Whenever making these trips from the wilderness, our ships have to be thoroughly decontaminated to ensure there is no possibility of bacterial contamination.

35154.text: Our transports carry a range of goods to the colonies of Carlisle, including Food Rations and Pharmaceuticals. Maybe one day Bretonian scientists will genetically engineer crops that thrive here, but until then Cambridge remains our primary breadbasket. Pharmaceuticals are vital to treat the multitude of tropical illnesses harbored here. Even with the most dangerous bacteria eradicated in the Clean Zone, there are still all manner of things that will make you sick on an alien world.

35155.text: Detroit Light Arms are in high demand across Carlisle. Officially this is because the local wildlife is dangerous, and homesteaders are entitled to arm themselves for protection. Unofficially, I’ve heard there are huge issues with gangs brewing here, thanks to Slog and organized crime. I’m sure our weapons only find their way into the hands of people looking to protect their own property. All I can say is they are in very high demand across Carlisle.

35156.text: During the Gallic War, Liberty housed huge numbers of Bretonian Refugees, mostly on Erie and Houston. Blue collar wages collapsed, and Xeno gang violence followed soon after. Now, Universal has purchased a development charter here on Carlisle, and is running an expatriation program to move those Refugees back to Bretonia. Of course, they will be moving to one of our newly founded company towns, where they will work off the transit costs.

35157.text: Bretonia is funding Carlisle’s growth by selling off development charters. Universal has obtained several such charters as a speculative investment. This isn’t our normal field of work, however we’ve acquired several key tracts of land we believe will be vital for future infrastructure over the coming decades. Staking several settlements which we are populating with expatriated Bretonian Refugees also gives us significant influence on the Colonial Governor, and favorable treatment on import tariffs.

35158.text: Carlisle and Yuma are similar in many ways. Both are tropical exceptions in the Barrier, although each faces different challenges. Both also have Liberty’s covetous eye fixed upon them. Not in terms of conquest, but Liberty’s influence and culture is everywhere you look, with financial strings that inevitably lead back to Manhattan. My trade delegation is here to offer their insight. A strong trade partner is preferable to a leashed hound.

35159.text: We import Copper from Coronado, where recently discovered deposits rival the purity of those in the Walker Nebula. The Crayter Republic refines some of this Copper on Yuma, however we now purchase most of our exports from Deep Space Engineering. They have established their own orbital refinery in the system, and disapprove of our independent production. Previously we had a profitable relationship with the IMG to counterbalance Liberty’s corporations, but this recently collapsed.

35160.text: Bretonia’s current state is a strategic concern for the Crayter Republic. We are aware that Liberty’s primary interest in our Republic is securing a buffer territory in the Barrier Pass. Deterring Gallia before a hypothetical future war occurs requires a credible threat in the Taus. We are pulling our weight in Tau-23, however Bretonia is not. Requests to New London have failed, so now we will try lobbying the Colonial Governor here for their support. If war comes again, Newcastle will also be a front line, after all.

35161.text: It’s said that Carix is made from a local bacteria mixed up with industrial chemicals. Apparently the bacteria’s toxin and its effects were discovered by some Planetform scientists a few years back. There was a pay dispute going on then, so they must have decided they’d get rich their own way. Last I heard, a bunch of Planetform employees got arrested during the police crackdown not so long ago.

35162.text: I lived on Sprague before Carlisle, and Leeds before that. Carlisle takes some getting used to. One-hundred percent humidity most days. Sprague is quite the opposite, so dry it’ll suck the moisture from your mouth. The smell is another issue. The forests stink. It almost reminds me of the smog on Leeds, but rather than acidic fumes that make your sinuses bleed, someone has mixed rotting grass cuttings with milk and left it to curdle in the sun.

35163.text: Despite the problems, people are flocking to the colony here. Majority are Bretonians of some stripe, whether they were Refugees who ended up abroad during The War, or workers who’re trying to escape from Sprague or Croyton. Not to mention the forlorn lot that transferred here from Gran Canaria. Whichever staff officer concocted that campaign should have been court martialled. There’s a large Liberty presence here too, thanks to the Universal Shipping company towns.

35166.text: Bait ships are unfortunate transports that were hijacked while transiting through dangerous Omega border worlds. Those purchased by the cruel Pit Bosses of Bornholm are fitted with explosives that will detonate if the vessel flees the arena. To win their freedom, the captive crews are forced to participate in broadcast blood sports, fighting off deadly assailants. Very few succeed.

35168.text:
BIOMASS

Bioproduce is a catch-all terms for non-edible, organic products that have been harvested in a planetary environment. This covers a range of products including wood and wood-analogues, to fibers, adhesives and pulp. Strains of Bioproduce selected for export generally have a broad range of commercial, industrial and construction uses.

35170.text:
Arcade Ship “Ahoudori Gunji”
An old Ahoudori Explorer that served for many years in Samura and then the Gas Mining Guild’s security fleets, before being purchased at scrap value by the Ginza Development Committee.

The spacious gunboat has been converted into an arcade, featuring a range of popular game cabinets, carnival games, and virtual experiences. The eponymous Ahoudori Gunji experience has a party of visitors take on roles across the vessel’s bridge to fight their way through simulated waves of Colony War-era Rheinland Military vessels. This takes place in an alternate-history KNF counter-attack in Planet New Tokyo’s orbit. Due to popularity, the experience has a reservation waiting list of several months.

35172.text:
Bazaar Ship “Chiyoda Publishing”
This Serenity transport was provided by Bretonia to the stranded Kusari Exile forces during the First Gallic War, where it served as a logistics vessel. After the war ended, it was purchased by Admiral Sakamoto as a personal memento.

The vessel has been heavily refurbished and converted into a publishing house and storefront for Sakamoto Media. It is now prominently moored at Ginza Bazaar, where it produces a range of popular manga franchises, including the ongoing hit series Imperial Ronin. The story follows the heroic Captain Sakamoto as he leads the stranded Exiles to victory against Gallia and Kusari Republican forces in the name of the Emperor. Despite being a commercial success, the series has been criticized for its extreme historical inaccuracies.

35174.text:
CLASS: Amaterasu
AMENITIES: Full
CREW: 670

The Liner Akasaka currently houses the majority of embassies in Kusari space, following the destruction of Roppongi Station. Originally intended as Samura’s corporate flagship, the vessel was instead leased to the Kusari government in late 834 AS. Following the ship’s acquisition, it was moored to the newly constructed Ginza Bazaar, where the starboard wing has been reserved for diplomatic use. As a result, foreign embassy and consular staff were expelled from Planet New Tokyo and required to move into orbit. While this initially caused significant irritation and offense, these feelings have been somewhat mitigated by the liner’s luxurious environment and lavish complimentary facilities.

35176.text:
CLASS: Mitsukoshi
GRAVITY: Complete
DOCKING: Yes
AMENITIES: Yes
CREW: 2150
35176.mapped:
Ginza Bazaar is a popular destination orbiting Planet New Tokyo, featuring amenities ranging from boutique shopping concourses and restaurants to art galleries and arcades. Ginza evolved from an ad hoc orbital market that sprung up following the devastating destruction of Roppongi Station. Seeing the potential to repair New Tokyo’s tarnished reputation and tourism trade, the capital planet’s district governments and proprietors of the original bazaar ships jointly funded the Ginza Development Committee. Across 834 AS, the Committee designed and constructed a permanent station they believed would become an unparalleled cultural and commercial attraction.

Ginza has already begun to draw crowds of visitors, largely due to subsidized shuttle services from Planet New Tokyo. Tokyo’s youth in particular have flocked to Ginza’s bars and arcades, where they can swap gossip, buy designer clothes and discuss politics. Despite booming demand for storefronts and sky-high rental prices, the station’s starboard wing is currently accessible by appointment only, having been rented by Kusari’s government to moor the liner Akasaka. The Akasaka serves as a replacement for Roppongi’s diplomatic quarter, housing the majority of Kusari’s foreign embassies.

35178.text: The Ginza Development Committee is made up of the original proprietors who founded the orbital bazaar, and representatives from Planet New Tokyo’s district governments. Of course, both keiretsu also believe they are secretly running the show. I suspect the chairman is merely humoring them while pursuing whichever course makes the most commercial sense for the facility, and best nurtures the tourist trade.

35179.text: Ginza is almost entirely composed of shops, restaurants and other customer-facing services. As a result, we’re one of the most densely crewed stations in Kusari. Fortunately, so far we’ve had the visitor numbers to turn a healthy profit, but some worry that is mostly driven by the novelty of what we offer. As soon as the district governments tire of subsidizing the shuttles, or young people decide the Bazaar is no longer fashionable, we may struggle.

35180.text: Despite being a tourist attraction, a lot of serious diplomatic work also happens at Ginza -- the Kusari government has rented the station’s other wing for that purpose. Dignitaries frequently meet on this side however, probably hoping to blend into the crowd and avoid the listening ears likely hidden all over the Akasaka. Even when pretending to be tourists, most of them stick out. Yesterday I noticed Liberty’s regional security chief having an affair with Rheinland’s deputy economy attaché.

35182.text: Interspace believes there is a cover-up going on with the Roppongi investigation. It’s no secret that Samura wields the Farmer’s Alliance like a weapon when it serves their interests, even if we can’t prove it. Then they were unexpectedly granted the clean-up contract, despite being completely unqualified for it. I’m here to closely monitor the case, and independently dig up any clues that might have been overlooked... or concealed. If we ever uncover evidence linking Samura to the attack, there will be hell to pay.

35183.text: The loss of Roppongi was the worst terrorist attack in Kusari’s history, killing several ambassadors and hundreds of crew and visitors. Kusari is slow-walking the investigation, despite the outrage abroad. Now there’s been a failed Alliance attack on Deshima Station, too. Interspace had already suspended insurance coverage in Kusari after Roppongi, but clearly further coercion is needed. Liberty is threatening to impose sanctions on Kusari unless they take concrete steps to eradicate the Farmers Alliance altogether.

35184.text: After Interspace withdrew insurance coverage from Kusari, Samura moved to launch its own service. They’re now tripping into the same pitfalls Rheinland did during the Hudson War. For one, we won’t share proprietary Universal Ship Identification data with them, so their assessors are constantly subject to fraudulent claims and tariff evasion. Anonymous insiders have also hinted that they grossly misjudged the capital investment required to underwrite shipping on this scale.

35185.text: Synth Foods and Kishiro have entered into Paste supply agreements with many restaurants here, allowing them to feature exclusive and premium flavors. These are proving to be very successful -- nearly 80%% of young consumers prefer our brands over Kyushu offerings. Moving forward, Synth will likely use Ginza to market test localized Kusari products. The product branding benefits from the fashionable setting and free exposure.

35186.text: While Ginza Bazaar is looking like a profitable market for Synth Foods, there is one significant issue. Neko’s Onigiri. It is by far the most popular restaurant at Ginza. Despite repeated -- and increasingly generous -- offers for a supply contract, Hina Sakuraoka remains disinterested. Whatever we propose, she replies that she simply likes things the way they are.

35188.text: The Hogosha are the guardians of Kusari’s society, against both foreign threats and disturbers of the status quo like the Blood Dragons and Golden C. The Hogosha would like to secure voices on the Ginza Development Committee, to ensure the market holders here remember the importance of traditional Kusari values. When they forget, the Hogosha are of course on hand to remind them.

35189.text: The Hogosha have a profitable relationship with Ikebana Home and several other proprietors here. We supply the most aesthetically pleasing Artifacts to artisans who work them into distinctly Kusari sculptures. Some academics object to this practice, calling it vandalism. I say these paperweights serve a greater purpose as the centerpiece of a wealthy Samura executive’s office, than they would sitting in a dusty university archive.

35190.text: There is an Interspace detective prowling around this station, trying to talk to anyone that might know something about the Roppongi blast. This task is fruitless. Anyone with sense realizes there is nothing further that should be known. If this detective continues to disturb the peace and besmirch the reputation of honorable Kusari investigators, we will be forced to teach him the error of his ways.

35192.text: Kishiro has acquired the supply contracts for dozens of the stores aboard Ginza, including most of the restaurants. Following the Deshima Agreement of 833 AS, Kishiro became Synth Foods’ primary distributor in Kusari. I suspect this was largely motivated by damaging Samura while an opportunity presented itself, given that Shinagawa had otherwise been contemplating divesting our external shipping fleet.

35193.text: Ginza is a striking mix of modern and traditional influences, where local Kusari can rub shoulders with well-traveled foreigners, and locate a range of goods from across Sirius. Kishiro has been keen to steer the Ginza Development Committee towards this kind of approach. It represents a roadmap for progressing responsibly towards an open and forward-looking Kusari. We must embrace the future rather than clinging to a stagnant past.

35194.text: In years past, I would visit Roppongi while off-duty. When I saw women wearing thick, garish lipstick, I wondered if they were secretly Chrysanthemums trying to hide the stains that drugs apparently leave on their lips. Allegedly Interspace would let them dock to go shopping. Mind you, I still see such lipstick here on Ginza too. Perhaps this is simply a Libertonian fashion they are copying?

35196.text: Samura operates the passenger shuttles that move commuters and guests between Planet New Tokyo and Ginza. The contract is a relatively small one, but heavily subsidized by the district governments and Ginza Development Committee. It makes sense that the Committee should favor Samura; we are after all, also committed to the tourism trade’s recovery by dismantling Roppongi’s unsightly wreckage. Soon that unpleasantness will be nothing but a memory.

35197.text: Samura was an early backer of the Ginza Development Committee. As a result, we have an understanding with the appropriate decision makers, and influence over rental decisions and policy changes. Samura sees directing Ginza’s operations as a means of directing Kusari’s youth in a more reasonable direction by controlling their interests. We’ve made some initial concessions on outside influences to appear “hip” with the younger demographic, but soon enough we will subtly set a more traditional agenda.

35198.text: While visiting the station, more than once I have had some impudent Interspace gaijin sneer at me and mutter absurd accusations. I welcome him to do so again; I have friends in high places who can make his life very difficult indeed. Those Liberty foreigners should learn their place. They are in Kusari -- we do not bow to their demands.

35200.text: Many of the visitors to Ginza are local youths or foreign tourists. It is a relatively quiet and pleasant posting, mostly providing directions to lost visitors. There are some Hogosha bosozoku aboard however -- pickpockets and bag snatchers mostly. HQ is keen to make sure that nothing scares the tourists away, so there’ll be no leniency for Hogosha targeting foreigners here.

35201.text: Ginza’s starboard wing is a high security zone. It’s been reserved for use by the Kusari government as a diplomatic quarter. There are many embassies that were relocated aboard the Liner Akasaka, and support offices for the foreign diplomats’ staff in the storefronts nearby. We maintain a heavily armed KSP precinct house there to make sure no dignitaries are disturbed by uninvited intruders.

35202.text: We’ve recently had a rash of vandalism cases along the main concourse. Windows broken and graffiti, usually targeting stores selling foreign goods, or restaurants serving Synth products. It’s almost certainly Hogosha work, but we can’t nail them for it because the security cameras suspiciously fail during the incidents. When I figure out which tech they’ve paid off, I’m going to break his ankles.

35204.text: I work at the Liberty embassy as a Kusari liaison. It is difficult work, as the relationship is currently... strained. There are multiple troubling issues that have been worsening for many years now. Regrettably, Liberty has become accustomed to dictating terms to the other Houses, and is struggling to adjust to a status quo where this no longer applies. We do not want conflict, but we will do whatever is required to assert our independence.

35205.text: I hear the Ministry of Trade and Economy will soon announce the commercial deployment of a ship-mounted Jump Drive! This is thrilling but terrifying news. The Boorman Treaty created neutral buffer zones in the Independent Worlds. The ability to hypothetically bypass these zones will inevitably result in militarization as the Houses adapt to the possibility of attacks directly into their core territory. I hope my superiors have considered all the ramifications.

35206.text: Liberty has imposed security checkpoints in Galileo and announced sanctions to cut off Kusari’s supply of Superconductors. This mirrors their aggressive posturing in the direct lead-up to the Hudson War with Rheinland. Our analysts hope this is only a negotiating tactic to coerce concessions in Kusari’s domestic, economic and technological policies, rather than something more sinister. Despite this, the KNF is preparing for the worst.

35208.text: The Biwa Maru was a GMG fuel transport that regularly operated in Sigma-13 and Honshu. In 834 AS, the vessel was hijacked by Corsair raiders. The vessel was moored to Petra Base when it was attacked by Bundschuh and GMG forces, and destroyed in the resulting explosion.

35210.text: The Nakaumi Maru was a GMG fuel transport that regularly operated across the Sigmas. In 835 AS, the vessel was hijacked by Corsair raiders. The vessel was moored to Petra Base when it was attacked by Bundschuh and GMG forces, and destroyed in the resulting explosion.

35212.text: The Notoro Maru was a Kishiro transport that regularly shuttled H-Fuel to Mainz Storage Facility in Frankfurt. In 834 AS, the vessel was hijacked by Corsair raiders. The vessel was moored to Petra Base when it was attacked by Bundschuh and GMG forces, and destroyed in the resulting explosion.

35214.text: The Cabrera was attached to the Battlecruiser Penitence during the Corsair invasion of Dresden, where it focused on destroying Red Hessian miners and infrastructure. In early 835 AS, the gunboat was ambushed while raiding the Innenstadfeld and suffered heavy damage. The ship was withdrawn to Petra Base for field repairs, and remained behind when most of the station's garrison was dispatched to cover the Penitence's own retreat. When Petra came under assault by the Bundschuh and GMG soon after, the Cabrera fought to the death in an attempt to buy time for the base's crew to evacuate.

35216.text: The Gozo was a Corsair supply ship, responsible for stocking Petra Base with the supplies needed by the forces attacking the Red Hessians in Dresden. It was moored to Petra when the station came under attack by the Bundschuh and GMG. Despite initially escaping the onslaught, it was disabled before managing to flee to Sigma-13.

35217.text:
"Bulwark" Bristol-Kress Heavy Explorer

The Bulwark was designed in a cooperative venture between Bristol and Kress, built to match the demands of the wild frontier represented by the Independent Worlds. It boasts a blend of sturdy reinforcement and an expanded berth. This allows the ship to ferry large quantities of cargo and crew in relative safety.

Due to Bristol's lack of facilities to produce the vessel directly, Kress Industrial has rented excess capacity aboard Alster Shipyard to carry out small-scale production runs. Kress produces the vessels under license for Bristol, who then ships completed products to Bristol Bay in Bering to manage purchase and deployment arrangements. Imperial Shipping is content to profit from Alster's slack capacity, however they are likely to terminate the deal should demand for their own ship building further increase.

35220.text:
CLASS: Refuge
GRAVITY: Partial
DOCKING: RESTRICTED
AMENITIES: CLASSIFIED
CREW: CLASSIFIED

Titusville Station was a recently constructed H-Fuel refinery in orbit of Planet Tremont. At the point Kusari declared war and launched its surprise first strike, Titusville was undergoing the final commissioning of its gas resynthesis plants, ahead of primary production beginning. Observers had previously noted that there was no feasible business case for gas giant H-Fuel resynthesis in Pennsylvania, with most concluding the plant would run at a steep loss through government subsidies. In light of this, it was widely assumed the station was intended as a domestic fuel reserve, as a hedge against supply restrictions caused by a potential conflict with Kusari.

This made the facility a popular target for Erie Militants, with the Battleship Alma regularly having to scramble squadrons or intervene directly, depending on the scale of the inbound threat. This was the case twice in 836 AS, when the Alma successfully repelled a heavy Militant assault involving several cruisers and over a dozen fighters. Several weeks later, the Alma was deployed again after a distress call from Titusville was abruptly cut off by heavy signal jamming. Upon arrival, it found Titusville ablaze and breaking apart, having been attacked by Jump Drive-equipped Kusari special forces.

Desperate rescue operations are currently ongoing to rescue construction crews trapped within the burning station.

35222.text:
CLASS: Bulwark
AMENITIES: Limited
CREW: 95
35222.mapped:
The Keystone was the first Bulwark heavy frigate produced by Kress Industrial in 834 AS, under license from Bristol Construction and Manufacturing. Designed as a robust armored transport that could brave the wilds of the frontier and exploit its resources, the Keystone was initially deployed to Pennsylvania. Orbiting the moon Hallam, it collected the minerals boosted into orbit from Bristol's small work camps, before transferring them for shipment to Erie or Bristol Bay. Dissatisfied with the operation's meager profits, the Keystone instead elected to adopt a high-risk, high-reward strategy.

The frigate was dispatched to Colorado's Alamosa Asteroid Field, allowing Bristol miners to sneak through a nearby Jump Hole to Galileo. Bristol has so far kept its operations discrete, pilfering small quantities Galileo's Platinum and avoiding the attention of larger corporations. It is alleged that the Keystone provides a friendly port for Xeno raiders, where they can exchange Platinum and other goods stolen from Galileo's feuding corporations. It is unclear how the heightened tensions between Kusari and Liberty will impact these audacious miners.

35227.text:
The Keystone was the first Bulwark heavy frigate produced by Kress Industrial in 834 AS, under license from Bristol Construction and Manufacturing. Designed as a robust armored transport that could brave the wilds of the frontier and exploit its resources, the Keystone was initially deployed to Pennsylvania.
