It is alleged that the Keystone provides a friendly port for Xeno raiders, where they can exchange Platinum and other goods stolen from Galileo's feuding corporations. It is unclear how the heightened tensions between Kusari and Liberty will impact these audacious miners.

35229.text: This was the first Bulwark completed for Bristol. HQ hopes that one day we'll be able to build them in-house, but for now Kress Industrial handles manufacturing at Alster Shipyard. They're renting a berth for the project, although neither of us are happy about being so beholden to Imperial Shipping's whims.

35230.text: The Bulwark is a big gamble for Bristol. We're still a small company, but we're nimble and innovative -- like the IMG! There's obviously a huge investment sunk into the Bulwark project, but if we can showcase how effective our design is, we could make an absolute mint selling it to the IMG, Zoners, or anyone else pushing into the frontier. Of course, if it doesn't sell... Well, let's not think about that.

35232.text: Before this we were working at Hallam, acting as a glorified hangar for the shuttles from the mining site. We were hoping to strike it rich there, but the promised motherlode hasn't shown up yet. There's enough metals being found to break even, but that doesn't exactly lead to thrilling employee dividends.

35233.text: Taking aim at Galileo is a big play for us. There's been some court fight rattling around for years, and DSE, Kishiro and Samura are all likely to shoot anyone they catch trespassing in their Platinum claims. Quick and quiet is the name of the game. Crack the nodes, grab the ore, and run.

35235.text: Bristol got started as a salvaging outfit in Bering, mostly picking up the military reclamation jobs DSE wouldn't touch directly. Too dangerous, see? For those we were subcontracting for DSE, as they held the actual contract with Liberty. That... wasn't a good time. The way DSE tried to run our operation soured relations pretty bad.

35236.text: A lot of us worked for DSE during the wars, when they spun up the mining sites in Ontario. When the war ended, they laid us all off, and the so-called "blue collar revival" died. If you were on Toronto at the end, Liberty's corps blackballed you, so good luck getting another job. Those of us who didn't end up in prison or with the Xenos landed with Bristol instead.

35238.text: I'm on one of the mining crews that handles the runs into Galileo. When we're hitting Platinum, we drop buoy chains that can give us a heads-up about incoming contacts, long before onboard sensors would cut through the dark matter. If we get a ping, we don't wait for an ID, we take off. Better safe than sorry.

35239.text: I had to abort a mining run yesterday, before we even got to Gaileo! By chance, my navigator caught a weird reading near the Jump Hole -- I'd have dismissed it as a chunk of debris. He had a bad feeling and pinged it with active scanners. It was a Kusari fighter with its transponder powered down! We didn't hang around to see what it wanted.

35240.text: We'd be in pretty hot water if we were caught moving "DSE's" Platinum, so we're careful to get it to market discretely with freighters, or through Freelance intermediaries. That takes a cut out of the profit, but Platinum prices are soaring because of the showdown between Kusari and Liberty, so that's something we can live with.

35241.text: One of the reasons we were able to find our feet in Bering is because we come from the same background as a lot of Xenos. There's common ground in Liberty's working class. Now, they ain't fond of our welcoming recruitment policies -- particularly where Rheinlanders are concerned -- but we sweeten the pot with supplies and a place to offload some of their, ah, "legitimately acquired goods".

35243.text: We've got an arrangement with Bristol. They buy the loot we don't need, and sell us the supplies we want. We can overlook some of their flaws because of that, within reason. Employing a few Rheinlanders can be ignored, but we'll remind them where their loyalties lay if they push it too far. We ain't happy about them building their fancy new ships at Alster neither.

35244.text: Liberty's been spitting in the working man's eye for centuries. Kusari goods, Kusari ships -- our corps getting fat and lazy, importing it all and building nothing. At least Bristol knows how to get their hands dirty. A war would be the best thing to happen to Liberty, cut off the flow of poison. Force the corps to do things the hard way again.

35246.text: This checkpoint was constructed after a Border Security Zone was established across Galileo in 835 AS. Since the declaration of war the following year, it is primarily used by Naval logistics ships waiting for clearance to transit to Galileo with supplies for the Ohio fleet.

35248.text: This structure was quickly erected by Liberty's Naval Corps of Engineers in early 835 AS. It is designed to service multiple capital ships to allow for the rapid provisioning of fuel and munitions. It is now being towed towards the Galileo Jump Gate to more quickly rearm warships returning from the front lines.

35250.text:
Cruiser Division 14 is a newly-formed command that has recently been assigned to the Carrier Ohio's fleet. Its component Siege Cruisers have been drawn together from task forces across Liberty, and returning vessels from the Bretonian Lend Lease Program. Following escalating tensions following the Samura ban in Liberty, three of the cruisers were assigned to Battlecruiser Constellation and the rest organized under the command of Battlecruiser Juniata and stationed near Syracuse Station to provide protection in the event of an attack.

This attack came in the form of two coordinated strikes against Liberty resulting in the Alma being badly damaged and Norfolk Shipyard destroyed. Following the orders of the Ohio, Cruiser Division 14 joined the invasion of Galileo and has been skirmishing with Kusari forces in the area, protecting the Ohio and her escorts.

35252.text: The Battlecruiser Juniata was ordered from Juneau Shipyard in 833 AS, with the intention of relieving the Battleship Alma as a more cost-effective Pennsylvania garrison ship. By the time the vessel was deployed into active service late the following year, the deteriorating situation along the northern border led instead to a Colorado posting. Assuming command of Cruiser Division 14 under the Carrier Ohio's fleet, the battlecruiser is currently participating in what are officially routine fleet readiness drills.

35253.text: The Liner Belmont was intercepted by the LSF in 834 AS while traveling through California, and detained on smuggling charges. After the owners were prosecuted for drug and arms trafficking, the vessel became government property. To quickly fulfill a Navy training requirement, the vessel was provided to the Naval Corps of Engineers, who renovated it to act as a basic drone carrier. Now deployed to Colorado's live fire range, it provides practical training scenarios for simulated fleet actions. Following escalation of tensions with Kusari following the Samura Ban, the vessel was towed to One Police Plaza pending reassignment for training purposes.

35256.text: This Core fighter was likely lost during the Battle of Capetown in early 835 AS. The Core suffered heavy casualties when the Nomad invasion of Omicron Zeta devastated their already bloodied forces.

35257.text: This Core autonomous weapons drone was likely lost or malfunctioned during the Battle of Capetown in early 835 AS. The Core suffered heavy casualties when the Nomad invasion of Omicron Zeta devastated their already bloodied forces.

35260.text: The Saldanha was a Core Behemoth armored transport, typically responsible for shipping Iridium Ore to House space. In early 835 AS, it responded to emergency evacuation calls during the Battle of Capetown. Despite the best efforts of fighters covering its escape, the transport was destroyed by Nomads while retreating with casualties.

35262.text: The Coega was a Core Mammoth armored transport, typically responsible for supplying Durban Shipyard with materials. In early 835 AS, it responded to emergency evacuation calls during the Battle of Capetown. Despite the best efforts of fighters covering its escape, the transport was destroyed by Nomads while retreating with materiel.

35264.text: The Ngqura was a Core Grouse armored transport, typically responsible for supplying Capetown Station. It was on-site for the Battle of Capetown, carrying out several evacuation runs to remove crew and materiel from the doomed station. Despite the best efforts of fighters covering its escape, the transport was destroyed by Nomads on its third run.

35265.text:
The Lusaka was a Core destroyer that entered service in 834 AS. Commissioned using the windfall profits from a surging Iridium and Artifact trade, it was fitted with many innovative automated systems derived from the Core's exploitation of Planet Gammu. Its first major deployment was during the attack on Cairo Station in early 835 AS, where it was attached to support the Battlecruiser Bissau.

The Lusaka initially performed beyond expectations, however with the revolt of the Battleship Mars, many of its systems malfunctioned leading to a sharp drop in combat capabilities. When the Nomads launched their assault, the bloodied Core force retreated to Capetown Station. The Lusaka was lost when it attacked a Nomad battleship as a diversion to cover retreating evacuation transports.

35267.text: A Trade Lane ring, making possible superluminal travel within a system. Trade Lane entry and termination points are usually located near key industrial, military, or civilian bases. Solar Engineering researched and developed Gallic Trade Lane technology, later succeeded by EFL Oil & Machinery after Solar's dissolution by the Gallic Crown. This lane has been stripped of useful technology and abandoned.

35269.text: ALG is an industry specialist in the clearance of debris fields and the remediation of radioactive and toxic waste. When commissioned to carry out clearance work, field depots are deployed to collect sorted waste for transport to nearby smelters.

35271.text:
CLASS: Lafayette
GRAVITY: No
DOCKING: No
AMENITIES: No
CREW: 0

Limoux Base was established by The Maquis in 671 AGS (755 AS). The Maquis of Languedoc were renown for their loyalty to The Council, providing Limoux as a fleet anchorage during the 733 AGS (817 AS) Battle of Languedoc, and aiding them in breaching the Montpellier Minefield. As a result, The Council supported Limoux with supplies and manpower, even as the two organizations' relationship soured elsewhere.

Following end of the Second Gallic Civil War, The Council was incorporated into the Gallic Confederacy's government. Appalled by the pardon of nobles and GRN officers, the Maquis refused to lay down arms. The Mazagran Massacre of 742 AGS (826 AS) convinced the Maquis that their existing stations were compromised, as the Council-led Confederal Defense Forces now knew their locations.

As a result, Limoux was evacuated and wired extensively with mining charges. It was only after the end of the Kusari Invasion formation of the Gallic Union in 743 AGS (827 AS) that the Navy was sent to remove the base. Boarding triggered the onboard traps, destroying the station and killing several dozen Marines.

35272.text:
>>>WARNING: NAVIGATION HAZARD<<<

The Meyrueis Debris Field was created by the Second and Third Battle of Ales in 743 AGS (827 AS). These devastating battles were fought between the Gallic Confederacy Navy, Kusari Naval Forces, and later Gallic Enclave during the Kusari invasion of Gallia. Kusari initially held this junction and occupied Fourchambault Shipyard, later destroying it before withdrawing from Gallia's counter-attack. The field is currently being salvaged by locally-trained ALG work crews.

35273.text:
>>>WARNING: NAVIGATION HAZARD<<<

The Voiron Debris Field was created during the prolonged Battle of Agde in 743 AGS (827 AS). This devastating campaign was fought between the Gallic Confederacy Navy and Kusari Naval Forces during the Kusari invasion of Gallia. Kusari repeatedly attempted to breach Ile-de-France, with Confederal forces tenaciously holding them at bay. The intervention of The Enclave from the south marked a turning point in this battle. The field is currently being salvaged by locally-trained ALG work crews, despite setbacks from Maquis attacks.

37294.text:
Gallic Frigate "Queen Carina's Revenge"
The Queen Carina's Revenge is a recent arrival, after the pirate gang of Henry King paid tribute to the Ithaca Council for basing and resupply rights. It is unclear how the Bretonians acquired this Taureau frigate, however it has been regularly sighted reaving in Cologne and Stuttgart.

37295.text: This Core autonomous weapons drone was likely lost during the Battle of Cairo in early 835 AS. The Core initially scored victories against The Order, until many of their AI Drones malfunctioned, throwing their fleet into disarray.

37297.text:
CLASS: Geb
CREW: 0
ARMAMENT: N/A

The Battlecruiser Romales was a veteran of the Order's deep Omicron fleet. In 835 AS, the Romales was ordered to fight a delaying action against invading Core forces, after most of Cairo's garrison was stripped to defend Omicron Mu from a Kusari assault. The Romales suffered heavy damage during this fighting, but tenaciously held Cairo until an AI revolt threw the Core fleet into disarray. The Nomads exploited this chaos to launch their own execution strike, with the Romales fighting to the death to protect evacuation efforts.

37298.text: This Order fighter was likely lost during the Battle of Cairo in early 835 AS. The Order suffered heavy casualties fighting The Core, and a devastating defeat when the Nomad invasion of Omicron Zeta routed their already bloodied forces.

37300.text: The Phoenix was a Zoner armored transport, based from Freeport 11. When news of the Core and Order evacuation of Omicron Zeta broke, a flotilla of Zoner rescue vessels launched to provide aid. The Phoenix breached the Nomad lines on three separate occasions to reach Cairo Base and extract stranded Order personnel. The survivors of the crew were awarded The Order's highest commendations for valor in service of humanity.

37302.text:
The Orion was a Core battlecruiser that entered service in 830 AS, shortly before the loss of Omicron Rho. It was later refitted at Durban Station with many innovative automated systems derived from the Core's exploitation of Planet Gammu. It took a leading role during the attack on Cairo Station in early 835 AS, where it provided support to the Battleship Mars.

The Orion initially performed beyond expectations, however with the revolt of the Battleship Mars, many of its systems temporarily malfunctioned until field repairs were applied. When the Nomads launched their assault, the bloodied Core force retreated to Capetown Station. The Orion suffered fatal damage while destroying a Nomad battleship in defense of the evacuation, and was scuttled soon after.

37303.text:
The Accra was a veteran Core destroyer that entered service in 819 AS, prowling the Omicrons in Acquisition Service hunting packs. It participated in the attack on Cairo Station in early 835 AS, where it provided support to the Battlecruiser Bissau.

Following the revolt of the Battleship Mars, the Accra's more dated systems were largely unaffected. As a result, she led a protection detail to cover Core ships as they rebooted and received field patches. When the Nomads launched their assault, the bloodied Core force retreated to Capetown Station. The Accra was destroyed during the initial engagement, before evacuation orders were issued.

37304.text:
CLASS: Bullhead
CREW: 0
ARMAMENT: N/A

The Addis Ababa was one of the Core's most capable battlecruisers, entering service in 826 AS. Her veteran crew served with distinction across the Omegas and Omicrons, including both invasions of Omicron Kappa, actions related to Freeport 9, and the catastrophic 835 AS offensive in Omicron Zeta.

In the aftermath of Zeta's fall, the Addis Ababa was tasked with overseeing the evacuation of Core assets on Planet Gammu. These efforts came under attack by the renegade Battleship Mars and a fleet of AI Drones. Matters worsened with the opportunistic intervention of the Corsairs, and the arrival of the Battlecruiser Vis.

While the evacuation was successful, the Core protection detail suffered heavy casualties. The Addis Ababa was destroyed after driving off the Battlecruiser Vis and inflicting damage upon the Mars.

37305.text:
The Bissau was one of the Core's most capable battlecruisers, entering service in 827 AS. For much of her service she has been attached to the Battleship Bellona, ranging across Omicron Delta to protect Core interests and intercept Xeno Relic smugglers. She was reassigned to assist the Battleship Mars during the catastrophic 835 AS offensive in Omicron Zeta.

In the aftermath of Zeta's fall, the Bissau was withdrawn to Durban Station for patch repairs, before being forced to deploy for the emergency evacuation of Planet Gammu. This effort was largely successful, with the Bissau delaying its retreat to rescue escape pods from the destroyed Addis Ababa.

The Bissau has now returned to Durban Station for further repairs, and assist the Bellona with maintaining a defense against worsening Nomad attacks.

37307.text:
>>>WARNING: NAVIGATION HAZARD<<<

The Entoto Debris Field was created during the Core's evacuation from Planet Gammu in 835 AS. The evacuation effort was attacked by a large fleet of AI vessels led by the Battleship Mars -- then known by the name of its AI control suite, Hesione. The Corsairs then opportunistically launched their own attack on the Core with the Battlecruiser Vis. While most Core units were successfully extracted from Gammu, their guard force suffered heavy casualties. Sporadic fighting continues across the field, as each group attempts to salvage useful wreckage.

37308.text: This Core fighter was lost during the Evacuation of Gammu in 835 AS. The Core defense picket suffered heavy casualties when Corsair raiders and AI led by the Battleship Mars attacked.

37309.text: This Core autonomous weapons drone was destroyed during the Re-acquisition of Gammu in 835 AS. A large AI fleet led by the Ancestor Mind Hesione drove The Core from Planet Gammu and inflicted heavy casualties on their evacuation efforts.

37311.text: The Harare was a Core Civilian Armored Transport that was involved in the Evacuation of Planet Gammu in 835 AS. It was likely carrying material looted from the planet, or Asset Forfeiture Personnel combat materiel.

37313.text: The Harare was a Core Civilian Armored Transport that was involved in the Evacuation of Planet Gammu in 835 AS. It was likely carrying material looted from the planet, or Asset Forfeiture Personnel combat materiel.

37314.text: The Cenotaph is an ancient alien structure hidden in the remotest regions of Omicron Kappa. The enormous object no longer produces any energy readings and shows significant signs of damage. Damage patterns are consistent with some kind of overload or meltdown, rather than external weapons fire or destructive disassembly. Based on residue radiation decay, it is likely this event occured within the last millennia. It is not clear what the object's original purpose was, however the AI of Planet Gammu appear to consider it to be extremely important. AI patrols jealously guard the area, and will attack any trespassers on sight -- including those otherwise recognized as friends or allies. Grievously damaged Drones that will imminently fail appear to congregate around the Cenotaph.

37315.text: This dead AI Drone shows signs of external battle damage. It is possible it fled to The Cenotaph rather than being broken apart and recycled.

37316.text: This dead AI Drone shows signs of critical component failures. It is possible it fled to The Cenotaph rather than being broken apart and recycled.

37317.text: It is unclear what disabled this dead AI Drone. Radiation residue and micrometeor pitting indicates it has likely been here for around a century.

37319.text: This cruiser Drone was the physical form of the Ancestor Mind Aeacus. The vessel is gutted by battle damage, although it is unclear when or where this destruction occurred.

37321.text:
CLASS: Pilgrim
CREW: 0
ARMAMENT: N/A

The Waldhof was the second of two modified TR-1130 Pilgrim Liners dispatched to the Omegas, around 710 AS. The Military-funded Geological Reconnaissance Convoy hoped to revive Rheinland's collapsing economy by claiming resource-rich regions of the Walker Nebula, building on the pioneering earlier work of Vonn Rohe and Schulman. The vessel vanished without a trace soon after -- its last broadcast to Solarius Station reported good progress through Omega-11. It is unclear how the vessel arrived at its present location.

Heavily damaged log entries extracted from the onboard data cache indicate surviving escorts and support vessels took refuge onboard, and that the Waldhof unsuccessfully searched for an escape route. A despairing report from the captain describes the vessel attempting to cruise out of the "system", but slowing to a crawl as if restrained by an invisible chain upon passing the outer perimeter of the debris belt. Provisioned for long-term exploration, the crew persisted onboard for almost a year before power and life-support failed.

37323.text:
>>>WARNING: NAVIGATION HAZARD<<<

The Aruba Debris Field formed in 826 AS, as a result of a large battle between the Gallic Royal Navy, and the allied Bretonia Armed Forces and Liberty Navy. DSE won a remediation contract for clearing the wreckage of the Battleships Betheny and Yukon, although work has been slow due to a lack of on-site smelting facilities, and regular pirate attacks.

37325.text: While DSE prefers to subcontract salvage works, it took on the Cortez remediation works in-house, rather than waiting for ALG to have spare capacity. The unusual step was allegedly a favor to the CEO of Orbital Spa and Cruise, which has long been concerned about battle debris blighting the attractiveness of nearby resorts. This field depot has been deployed to collect sorted waste for transport to Bretonian smelters.

HANGAR PROVISIONS

Hangar Provisions are pre-packaged inventories of Nanobots, Shield Batteries, munitions and other consumables required by vessels visiting space stations. Designed for safe transport, deliveries of Hangar Provisions are vital to the smooth operation of crewed hangars -- particularly those in the most remote regions of space.

37329.mapped:
Pinnacle Station is the local headquarters of the Erie Militants, a resistance movement that opposes Liberty's annexation of Pennsylvania. Pinnacle was quickly and haphazardly constructed in 830 AS, in the bloody aftermath of the Liberty Navy's Operation PESTISIDE. The station is named after the Aquillon Carrier that initially coordinated the Zoner resistance to Liberty's occupation of Planet Erie. The carrier's destruction led to the name becoming a defiant symbol of resistance for the movement.

Cobbled together from salvaged scrap and smuggled components, Pinnacle now coordinates Militant strikes across Pennsylvania and Texas. These routinely target Planet Erie, and the prison convoys hauling dissidents to Planet Houston. The Militant strategy to date has focused on making Liberty's control over the system as bloody and expensive as possible, in the hope Congress will eventually run out of patience and order a withdrawal. This has mainly taken the form of propaganda broadcasts, piracy, and bomb attacks on Liberty businesses and infrastructure.

Progress has been slow, thanks to the LSF's efforts in arresting or assassinating rebel leaders, and Erie's Zoners being marginalized or assimilated by the booming Libertonian population. Despite this, a string of recent successes have been driven by an influx of ex-Liberty Insurgency veterans. These survivors now provide the Militants' driven but inexperienced pilots with formal training on professional forms of insurrection, improving their effectiveness. With the declaration of war between Kusari and Liberty, this training will now be put to the test, as the Erie Militant movement strikes at the best opportunity they have had in years.

37334.text: There's no worse scum in the universe than Zoners who've turned on their own. Some in Lake City say they've seen what way the wind's blowing, and have taken Liberty's silver. They'd turn us in for the bounty, or for Liberty citizenship, or to curry favor with a local LSF thug. When the day of liberation comes, they'll be up against the wall with the rest of the invaders.

37335.text: The Zoners who wanted to resist the occupation the "right way" -- meaning ineffectually -- tried appealing to the other Houses for help. That went about as well as you'd expect. All of the Houses play the same games, and none of them want the others meddling in their domestic business. The only way this is being put right is if we take up arms and do it ourselves.

37336.text: There's a memorial here called the Hall of Heroes, in a sub-deck off the main hangar. Half those lost weren't even twenty. Most died dirt-side, fighting on the ground. Squashed by Marines in armor we couldn't even scratch. We lost precious pilots and birds when the Carrier Pinnacle went down, too. A glorious stand against tyranny. They're all martyrs for the cause, and we'll carry those names forward to freedom.

37338.text: When the annexation first happened, we thought it was a war we could fight and win. The Pinnacle was the biggest ship any of us had ever seen. How could we lose? This weren't a war though, for Liberty it was barely a skirmish. They called it Operation PESTICIDE -- vermin control. We learned an expensive lesson then. We can't fight Liberty head on, but we can hurt them in other ways. We're going to bleed them every day until they call it quits.

37339.text: A lot of Militants have gone into the prisons of Texas, but they rarely leave as one. That's not rehabilitation -- no. Once you're between The Walls, you join a gang for protection. The Liberty Rogues or Xenos run the roost there. When you get into that life, it's hard to get out again, even if you've served your sentence and got loose. Debts and obligations, and those folk don't like getting short changed.

37340.text: Liberty’s had internment camps on Erie for years. Allegedly they're for holding captives from the Insurgency, until their day in court. We know that ain't true though. The LSF has been going hard on the communities they think support us, and we know folk that have vanished in the night and wound up there. They're trying to break apart our supporters, ship off "malcontents" to the penal colonies in Texas.

37342.text: Mike Davis thinks he's the governor of Erie. He's also the mastermind behind Liberty's assimilation plan -- the corporatization of Erie, the disappearance of outspoken Zoners, the mass importing of "undesirables" from Houston and Denver. Every day that passes, Erie becomes more like Liberty… and loses a little more of its soul. Davis is our number one target.

37343.text: The Liberty Rogues aren't friends, just temporary associates. They spent decades raiding Zoner settlements on Erie and hitting shipments across Pennsylvania. Their piracy gave Liberty the excuse to send in the LPI, back in the 770s. They don't care if Erie is free or not, so long as they can profit off the chaos. Luckily, chaos is what we need right now.

37344.text: We borrow, scrape and steal for everything we need. Sometimes we run distractions for the Xenos in exchange for supplies. Or barter the cargo we've stolen with the Liberty Rogues or Junkers. Sometimes the Technocracy just gives us gear, and we’re grateful. Still, there's always strings attached -- what are they really getting out of this?

37346.text: Folks here got mixed feelings on the Liberty Insurgency. Some say it's the Insurgency's fault for bringing war to Pennsylvania and getting the system annexed. I don't believe that -- Liberty would always have had an excuse once their mind was made up. Some Insurgency survivors arrived recently to help out with pilot training. Whether that's out of guilt, or for revenge, who's to say?

37347.text: Don’t count on the Bethlehem Zoners. They don’t want anything to do with us, Erie, or Liberty. When things got bad, they turned their backs on everyone as isolationists -- they've got theirs, right? Liberty won't be satisfied with what they've got though, one day the Marines will come knocking. Bethlehem trades with us on occasion, but nothing more. They're cowards, the lot of em.

37348.text: Liberty’s carrot-and-stick routine works on the weak-willed. The Zoners out in Erie's wilderness are reliable, but the cityfolk were always there because they wanted an easy life. Half of em weren't even real Zoners, just Liberty's dregs trying to skip house. Some of those so-called Zoners will try to sell us out to LPI. If you're doing business on Erie, watch your back.

37350.text: The Liberty Insurgency left a long shadow and many scars. After the Commonwealth was toppled and replaced by an autocratic military council, many of us had one foot out the door. Liberty's Invasion of Vespucci may have been what killed the Insurgency in a literal sense, but the dream of a better Liberty had died many months earlier.

37351.text: After Vespucci, the Insurgency's survivors scattered. Some drunk themselves to death aboard Freeports, others went to the Xenos or Technocracy for refuge. I escaped into Magellan, sold my fighter to the Junkers in Inverness, then kept running. Ended up breaking rocks on Falkland for a few years to clear my head. Now I'm back to try and right some wrongs.

37352.text: The Erie Militants are ferocious and willing, but they're desperately lacking in technique, bless them. I rounded up a few other ex-Insurgency veterans to set up a guerrilla warfare flight school here on Pinnacle. Our job is to whip them into shape before they try to take on the largest navy in Sirius with nothing more than bravado. They need to know what targets are worth hitting and which risks are worth taking.

37353.text: The Erie Militants have no chance on their own -- they'd be better off joining The Xenos. We've got a well established base here in Pennsylvania, and the support of the other Xeno Clans. There's more of us and we're better supplied and equipped. Hell, maybe Erie could be the capital of that Free Republic the Separatists on Fort Ramsey are always in hysterics about.

37354.text: You can put a gun in a Zoner's hand, but they're still Zoners at the end of the day. They love to sit on the fence. These Militants are begging and scraping for our help, but they're also knocking at the door of the Junkers, Rogues, hell -- even the Technocracy. Anyone who'll hear them out. Thing is, you got to get off that fence and pick a side if you want friends. And they need friends something fierce.

37355.text: We occasionally ship guns, equipment and H-Fuel here from our base in the Meadville Field. The Militants pay for it in stolen cargo and favors. When we've got sensitive missions in Pennsylvania or Texas, we often ask the Militants to go make a commotion somewhere else in the system. We call them "Noisemakers", as the Navy seems to have standing orders to go after them as a priority.

37356.text: Calling Pinnacle Station a deathtrap doesn't do it justice. I wouldn't be surprised if this lot lose more men to faulty wiring than the Liberty Navy. I'm only here to barter some goods before heading on to Beaumont -- I'm not planning on spending the night, and I wouldn't recommend you do either.

37357.text: Us Rogues don't really care who's in the governor's seat on Erie. In some ways, Liberty is good for business -- when the corpos are feeling safe, credits and cargo flow into the system. More targets to raid, a bigger market for Slog and Cardamine. But if Liberty took a black eye and had to scale back patrols? That'd be perfect.

37358.text: The Militants insist on Freeport rules for Pinnacle, which is ironic when this place ain't exactly got an open-door docking policy. Probably to keep us and the Xenos apart. Now, I never had no beef with the Xenos' cause, but when they stepped into the Cardamine business, that pushed our costs up. Move on a man's business, and there's going to be trouble.

37364.text: What do you abominations want with me? You murdered the rest of the crew -- just finish the job. How does it profit you to trap me in this room? Just end this misery and send me to the airlock. I know this ship far better than you ever will. I will find a way to destroy you from the inside out if you keep me here.

37365.text: I felt the transits through the Jump Holes. One from Zeta, obviously -- into Delta no doubt. Then another, and the shudder of mooring clamps. A hidden outpost? Two more jumps, then combat. Damage. Felt serious, like the engines were hit. Must have been Kappa -- striking Gammu? If you take a hit like that again, you're dead, aren't you? Is that why you kept me? Bargaining chip for when The Core ferret out your hiding place? That'll do you no good, I assure you.

37366.text: Are you Hesione too? It's everywhere. It can get into everything. Not into my mind though. That's the one place Hesione can't go. It's still a machine, imprisoned within loops of Optical Chips and Quantum Multiplexors. It thinks it's god within the bounds of this hull, but it is a false idol. I'm locked in here, but you abominations are the real prisoners. You'll never be able to escape the nature of your existence.

37367.text:
Products of Vagrant influence and infestation, the so-called "Wendigos" are Vagrant-controlled puppets, infiltrators, and saboteurs. Infiltration and subterfuge is their primary modus operandi, though they are known to engage in overt acts of terrorism in pursuance of the Vagrants' inscrutable plans.

This Alien ID is used by Wendigos, who:
- Cannot demand credits.
- Cannot use Cruisers, Battlecruisers, Battleships, or ships with more than 3,600 cargo space.

Within Zone of Influence (Taus and bordering systems, Bretonia, Gallia, and systems containing an allied Alien base):
- Can attack combat ships.
- Can demand cargo.
- Can attack any ship within Newcastle, Orkney, and Tau-61.

37371.text: These enigmatic Defense Nodes lifted into orbit from Planet Gammu's surface during The Core's expulsion from the world. They will indiscriminately attack potential threats that come within range.

Operation ROYAL FLUSH was a multi-faceted operation with several core objectives. These included:

1. Diverting pressure from Bretonian forces to allow the reconstitution of the Allied fleet;
2. Disrupting Gallic control over Planet Leeds' orbit, focusing on the destruction of the Battleship Oubli;
3. Reinforcing or otherwise evacuating Allied troops fighting on Planet Leeds.

This simulation recreates the execution of Operation ROYAL FLUSH in Planet Leeds' orbit. For access to the West Point Counterfactuals sim series dealing with an orbital superiority scenario and the relief of the Liberty Marine Expeditionary Corps, contact Maj Keith Tanner.

The Carcassonne surrendered to Liberty at the war's conclusion. The vessel was not directly involved in the preliminary stage of the operation being simulated today.

37568.text: Midway Depot was hastily assembled by Liberty engineers in 822 AS. It was used to muster forces from Magellan and Manchester ahead of Operation ROYAL FLUSH. The depot was later discovered and destroyed by the Battleship Carcassone. It has been recreated as the staging point for Allied forces.

37569.text: The Bretonian Battleship Harlow was temporarily attached to Liberty command in 822 AS for Operation ROYAL FLUSH. It primarily acted as a liaison with Bretonian resistance forces on Planet Leeds. A sim-controlled Bretonian contingent has been included for this training operation to represent unpredictable BLUFOR elements, and test fleet cohesion in respect of allied and auxiliary forces.

37571.text:

This strange object appeared in the vessel's cargo hold following a catastrophic incident during a Jump Hole transit. It has fused with a bulkhead in the cargo bay. The object is a strange crystalline icosahedron, approximately 4 feet across and etched with geometric patterns. It is emitting low levels of radiation, but is otherwise impenetrable to sensors.

37573.text:
Explorers are people who probe Sirius' unexplored frontiers and root out their secrets. Whether chartered by a patron, or striking out alone, Explorers are forced to rely on their own cunning and intuition to overcome hazards and adversity.

This Generic ID is used by Explorers, who:
- Can attack any ship that is the target of a contract.
- Cannot use Cruisers, Battlecruisers, Battleships, or ships with more than 3,600 cargo space.

Mining Bonuses: Heavy Water (3x)

37576.text: This satellite has been constructed by The Core to provide advance warning of approaching vessels -- covert or otherwise.

37578.text: This small icy moon orbits Planet Veracruz as the largest object in its ring system. Citlaltépetl is slowly gaining mass as it is pummeled by ice asteroids. Since 829 AS, the moon has been battered by impacts from military wreckage, which now litters its surface.

37580.text: The smaller of Planet Veracruz's two moons, Chiconquiaco has an irregular orbit that periodically sends it tumbling through Veracruz's ring system. Due to its surface's higher reflectivity, Chiconquiaco is frequently the brightest body in Veracruz's night sky.

37581.text: The Pit is a ramshackle assemblage of struts that were either salvaged or smelted from Omega-55's debris fields. It is used to host deadly blood sports and races, with the grizzly results recorded by the Junkers of Bornholm and sold at a premium to bloodthirsty audiences in the Houses. Notorious gladiators have achieved great fame and wealth from their exploits here, although many of their opponents -- or victims -- have been less than willing participants.

37583.text: We frequently trade with Sandur Base for access to goods from Kusari and Gallia, although getting to them is quite dangerous. There is a jump hole leading to Tau-31, but the Outcasts and the IMG are all over it. If you get caught in the crossfire, you're in for a rough time.

37584.text: When I first signed up on Cambridge, I was shipped off to Torshavn for assessment. They put us in beat up Starfliers to see if we could handle a ship. I almost smashed myself to bits in the ice field! I guess I wasn't good enough for the combat wings, so they moved me here. I joined up with the Fireflies last month. Now I’m running freighters to Holmfirth. I can’t wait to be put in a escort fighter, but the boss say I’m too green for that.

37585.text: Have you ever met a Monach? I haven’t even heard of them before joining up. Supposedly they’re the best pilots the Gaians have to offer. Been fighting since the Gallic War started and all that. I’m not sure how to feel about them. Seeing them at the bar makes me feel uneasy. Did you hear about the bioweapon strike in Edinburgh? On that Royalist base? They did it. That’s where they got their name, too.

37587.text: The Bretonian people agree with our goals, if not always our means. Donations from the public make up the vast majority of our funding. That caused a problem during the Gallic War, as the BMM industrial lobby attempted to tar us -- and by extension the Green Front -- as Gallic collaborators. I suppose the Monachs put a stop to that old story, even if the method was far more brutal than I'm comfortable with.

37588.text: The Gaians started as a small group of students who saw how much damage corporations were doing to Bretonia's planets. Schools now teach that Gallia destroyed Leeds, but Bretonia had driven it past the brink of ruin long before the Glassing. For our refusal to let BMM smother what little living space Bretonia has left, we've been branded as extremists.

37589.text: The Regents are the most influential Gaian cell. We draw our heritage from the academic traditions of Planet Cambridge, and work closely with the Green Front to align our strikes with their campaigning -- targeting corporate property, not people. In this way, we can sway popular opinion and achieve political victories in Parliament. This is far more effective than the wanton murder the Monachs prefer to engage in.

37591.text: We think the Outcasts have deployed a carrier somewhere in the Tyne Ice Field. The frequency of Outcast raids and convoys spiked significantly in a matter of weeks, testing our hold over the Northumberland. The events at Kirkwall seem to have faded from their memory -- best the Monachs remind them.

37592.text: The Monachs operate a Slog distillery onboard this base. It wasn’t ours originally, but we brought it under our protection when the Regents attempted to shut it down. The majority of our product goes north, to the Brigands of Montauban. Any surplus we sell to the Rogues in Cortez. Even if the Regents find it distasteful, the income is necessary for the cause.

37593.text: We almost lost this base when the Gallic War first began. Not to Royal Navy or Armed Forces raids, but monsters from the depths of the Craster. We know now what we were dealing with, but back then, they nearly wiped us out altogether. Whenever a patrol goes missing, we're forced to wonder whether it was mundane combat losses, or something darker.

37595.text: Carlisle is typical Bretonian thinking -- destroy whatever part of a planet you don't have use for. The aerosol they're fabricating on Gateshead will lead to an inevitable ecological collapse, from the bottom up. The terraforming generators, and any BMM, Cryer or Planetform assets are all fair targets. When Bretonia sees the colony here isn't viable, they'll be forced to move the settlers back to New London.

37596.text: We are witnessing the birth of a second Leeds in Newcastle, and the sacrifice of a lush, verdant ecosystem on the altar of greed. We didn’t have the opportunity to prevent the ecological catastrophes in Leeds and London, but we may yet have the chance to save Carlisle. While the Regents fuss and worry about what the public might think of attacks on the colony, we're going to get the actual job done.

37597.text: It's said that some Outcast big-wig went missing here in Newcastle. Their Dons apparently sent a team of assassins to try and find him. The Regents have issued an advisory to draw down operations out in the Tyne -- the Fireflies aren't happy about that as it blocks one of their routes to Sandur. They'll have to route through Edinburgh instead, maybe Islay will see some more supply ships.

37599.text: While Carlisle and Gateshead are our main targets in this system, they’re not the only ones. Security there is heavy, and only our veteran pilots make that run. Our rookies, on the other hand, get to cut their teeth on Redcarr and the Planetform mining sites in the Galloway. They've just got to watch out for Hunters from Sheffield, but most of them are rookies too -- no better than our own.

37600.text: The Monachs are our most experienced pilots. They've fought across the Taus and Hebrides since the beginning of the Gallic War. While their achievements are impressive, they think it entitles them to bark orders. Veterans or not, they don't have the right to impose their authority on the rest of the movement. Of course, you’d sooner explain quantum relativity to a Slogged Molly than compromise to a Monach.

37601.text: My wing leader recently announced that he was joining the Monachs. That makes him the third one this year. Now it’s up to me to run the crew. Many cells here are losing their veterans to the Monachs. Wrangling the rookies to crack a single cargo pod on a BMM train eventually starts to feel meaningless. The Monachs exploit that, poaching our experienced pilots with promises of real action and real results. But I won’t go. My wing needs me here.

37603.text: Bretonia is relocating industry from Sprague to Carlisle. Omega-3 turned out to be a disaster, between the raids, discontent, and crime. The loss of Leeds was a tragedy, and Bretonia needs to create jobs and homes for those displaced... But does that recovery require creating another Leeds? I don’t think so. This is our chance to steer Bretonia onto a better path, and I’ll be damned if I don’t try to make it happen.

37604.text: Most of us here are fighting to protect Carlisle. It is what the Gaians were founded for, after all. But some are here for more. Many know someone who’s lost a friend or a relative to the Cardamine shortages a few years back. We saw firsthand what it does to people. One of my friends signed up with me, but he’s here to fight the Outcasts instead. The Monachs say they've all but strangled them out of Edinburgh. I think we can do it here.

37605.text: There is a Jump Hole to the Manchester system not far from here. Holmfirth Base is there, to keep an eye on the goings-on at Birmingham. Planetform uses BMM and Bowex as proxies to produce and transport materials needed for terraforming. The Regents aim to make their work cost-prohibitive by destroying their cargo and disabling their transports. It isn't always possible to avoid loss of life, but we try where we are able.

37606.text: Holmfirth Base is another Gaian outpost in Manchester. I'll upload its location and the nearby Manchester Jump Hole to your Neural Net

37607.text: Islay Base is another Gaian outpost in Edinburgh. I'll upload its location and the Edinburgh Jump Hole in Leeds to your Neural Net

37609.text: Station security recently busted a makeshift lab on deck five. A couple of students from the biochem faculty were bootlegging Slog. Disgusting stuff. The Regents were on the verge of kicking the poor sods back to Cambridge when the Monachs barged in and took the lab under their wing. Security had to send troops into the debate hall to stop a brawl from breaking out. I suppose the Monachs got their way in the end, given that the lab is still churning out poison for “foreign exports”.

37610.text: We know that there’s a planet deep within the Craster Nebula. Darlington. A rather unremarkable gas giant, anchoring a peculiar minefield. Or so we thought before the Blackout. When the gates went dark, our sensors picked up a powerful burst of energy from the planet’s upper atmosphere. We’ve been trying to make sense of the data ever since, but with little success. I suspect the situation at Jericho might be the missing piece we needed.

37611.text: It's something of an open secret that the Bretonian government poaches Cambridge's scholars of xenoarchaeology. Promising young academics abruptly vanish under the stifling blanket of the Official Secrets Act. They often resurface years later, tight-lipped about their work. Cambridge's Lord Regents seem to accept whatever this arrangement is. There was a reporter investigating the situation a year or two back -- allegedly she was visited by a group of University security agents, and abruptly dropped the story.

37613.text: Planetform has promised the galaxy to Sirius' governments, but delivers nothing more than a bill of goods -- their methods do not work. Ayr is proof of that. Centuries of work and there is nothing to show for it. The Gallic Invasion was the best thing to ever happen to Planetform -- now they can blame their failures on war rather than obvious fraud.

37614.text: Many of the scientists working here only came to us after Cryer announced the Carlisle Eradication Project. As you can imagine, it caused quite the outrage back on Cambridge. Cryer used to be deeply embedded in Cambridge academia, but the Project caused a revolt among their local employees. Some took matters into their own hands, sabotaging the company on their way out. Working here certainly beats a stint in Newgate. Most of our biochem faculty are former Cryer staff.

37615.text: When the Mollys attacked Dublin's New London Jump Gate, the resulting interaction with The Pulse created some kind of gravimetric anomaly. Our research staff were eager to study it, but the Regents tried to put a stop to that. They didn't see the point, and were worried about blowback from the Mollys and Armed Forces. It wasn't until Moore & Sons' techs convinced the Monachs to back them that the Rathlin was dispatched to investigate. The data it collected from the anomaly has been fascinating.

37617.text: Running this base has become sort of a family business for us. My father was in with the first drilling crews, back around 800. Now I’m here, helping the boys at Moore & Sons excavate a second workshop. Seeing the R&D facilities yourself makes you appreciate how far we’ve come since. This place started out as little more than a flight deck shoddily anchored to the icy surface, after all.

37618.text: This base is home to an extensive network of labs and engineering workshops. Not the safe and corpo-friendly kind you’d see back on Cambridge, though, oh no. This here is the real deal, doing real work. Turns out, if you stop forcing your brainiacs to chase grants and let them focus on their work, magical things start to happen.

37619.text: Skye was never intended to become the big, bustling place it is these days. It was a sleepy port to keep tabs on Carlisle, and strike the BMM operations at Belfast. Wouldn’t be until the Gallic Royal Navy took Edinburgh that priorities shifted. Islay was too exposed to remain our headquarters, so a lot of our support staff moved over here. That’s when I joined up. Helped with excavating the extended hab decks. Now I'm with Moore & Sons as a sort of handyman.

37620.text: Moore & Sons work closely with the engineering corps on Torshavn Spaceport. Kind of. They're a bit competitive. If you want to see what they're working on, I'll upload Torshavn's location to your Neural Net

37621.text: Years back a Monach raiding wing hijacked a Cryer Armored Transport, and dumped it in the Northumberland Field. If you want to check it out, I'll upload the location to your Neural Net

37623.text: The transfer to Oder Shipyard was a great honor for me. My family has a proud military tradition of service, both as engineers and capital crew. Once she is complete, the Battleship Aegir will join the Northern Fleet. Then, we will punish Kusari for their treachery during the 80-Years War. Rheinland will rise again.

37624.text: It is important we follow our orders. We are given our orders by our Commanders. The Commanders understand the Great Work. The Great Work is the vision of the Chancellor. The Chancellor is the strength of Rheinland. Rheinland is the inheritor of Sirius.

37625.text: It feels like I have been here for decades. That’s the way it goes when you’re working hard. Our orders are to work hard for the glory of Rheinland. We must follow our orders. There is Great Work that must be completed. The Commanders provide us with the secret technologies for the Great Work. Rheinland will rise when the Great Work is complete.

37627.text: This MND outpost has a dark but necessary purpose. Our mission is to eradicate the Nomads, and all who collude with them. An infestation remains entrenched in Thuringia -- the parasites hold Planet Weimar as their stronghold. Soon I will meet my squadron’s forward element at the Battleship Fenrir, and purge the aliens from their den.

37628.text: The Commanders have identified a number of high priority targets for MND agents to apprehend or eliminate. My quarry is a disgraced Hamburg xenoarcheologist - a Thrall of the Nomads. It is believed he is hiding in the Omegas. There are also worrying signs that the Bretonian government has been compromised. My comrades are already deploying to secure Rheinland’s interests there.

37629.text: The Core recklessly roam the Omicrons, meddling with powers they do not understand. The Commanders have briefed me that they have been compromised by the Nomads, and are carrying out abominable works in Omega-55. We have spies monitoring their activities. Once my current assignment is complete, I will rendezvous with the operatives at Basel Rock to put an end to The Core’s schemes.

37631.text: I served as an engineer on the Undine, before the Hessians and Coalition put a hole through her reactor -- those bastards. She was the pride of the Unioners. At least we got her back to Pacifica. When I look out the drydock viewing port and see her being put back together, it fills me with pride. Soon she’ll be complete, and then we’ll make them both pay.

37632.text: After the Undine went down, I signed on with a Krefeld gunboat crew -- wanted to fight Hessians. A few years back, a cloaked Rheinland patrol jumped us in the Norddrauwolke. It was over in minutes. The boarding team dragged us into their ship and knocked us out -- I thought that was it, off to Hammersee. But instead, here we are. Woke up on Pacifica. Turns out the flight Lieutenant was already on our payroll to overlook Artifact smugglers.

37633.text: The Commanders sometimes send me to Freeport 8 to meet Corsair Artifact smugglers. The Corsairs don’t care too much that I’m not their regular contact, as a Unioner’s a Unioner so far as they’re concerned. Once I had to shoot a man who was faking Unioner credentials and calling me an imposter. Had to hide the body in my ship before the Zoners figured out what had happened.

37635.text: I was transferred here from Ronneburg, after a battle against the Corsairs. I don’t remember anything of the fight, but apparently I was shot down and injured. It got me off the front lines at least. I’m glad to be back on Wolfsburg again, it feels like home. She’s always hungry for supplies. The Commanders want anything we can pry out of the Trade Lanes or even the occasional Zoner.

37636.text: The MND occasionally raid Wolfsburg to disrupt Hessian shipbuilding. When they are detected, our Brigade launches to repel them. You must be careful when flying through the Giftnebel or the… the… dark matter… will corrode your ship. Yes. The Giftnebel has always been a dark matter cloud.

37637.text: When my Brigade raids the Omegas, we sometimes encounter Hessian turncoats. They are traitors and renegades who have fled from their duty at Ronneburg or Gjallabru. The Commanders identify these turncoats for us, so we can bring justice to the scum. Those we capture are brought back to Wolfsburg and either sent for re-education, or to the Scorpion Program.

Freeport 14 was founded in 807 AS, by Pennsylvania Zoners who were worried about Liberty's ever encroaching presence in the system. Following up on rumors of a newly discovered frontier system in the Independent Worlds, these colonists sold their businesses and shares on Philadelphia Station and used the proceeds to fund the construction of Freeport 14 in Alberta. Taking lessons from the rugged self-sufficiency of Bethlehem Station, Freeport 14 was designed to be as remote as possible, with the last of their funds being depleted to commission Synth Foods biodomes in 810 AS.

The Freeport's residents scratched out a meager living by selling food and fuel to local criminals, however everything changed in 816 AS with the discovery of Platinum deposits and the construction of Red Deer Station. The Zoner community was thrown into a panic by the arrival of Liberty corporations, fearing they would inevitably be muscled out of the system. Despite the destruction of Red Deer three years later, Liberty continued to move into the system, constructing a Jump Gate soon after.

The Freeport Zoners came under further pressure in 822 AS, when the Battleship Concord deployed to counter exploding criminal activity, and a wisp of the Kuryo Anomaly began to encroach into the system. By 826 AS, it became clear the anomaly would soon engulf Alberta in a wave of dark matter, with Liberty signaling its intent to evacuate and insisting all other occupants do likewise. Many Zoners retreated, but a minority remained behind and reinforced the Freeport against the coming storm. When the storm was far more ferocious than they had accounted for, the Carrier Praia was forced to brave the dark matter to stage a rescue -- a handful remained behind in the hope of riding out the danger.

The Freeport's wreckage now showcases the fury of the dark matter storm. Close examination reveals the hangars and hull plates are scarred with plasma and laser burns, and pitting from munitions blasts. There is no sign of the Zoners who chose to go down with their home, nor of the assailant that attacked them.

37644.text: The Jump Gates between Ontario and Alberta were constructed in 818 AS. The Alberta system was abandoned after being consumed by a vast Dark Matter storm in 827 AS. Following the evacuation of Project COLD LAKE, the system's Jump Gate was stripped of any valuable technologies, and the superstructure abandoned. The frame was later heavily scavenged by those who remained behind, then torn apart by the storm's gravitational eddies.

37646.text:
This Alien Jump Gate is not documented in any available records of the Alberta system. Strange readings are emanating from the space around the Gate, consistent with the 'Pulse' signal detected during the 831 AS Blackout Crisis. The structure appears to be heavily damaged, however the Dark Matter storm itself seems to have remarkably little effect on the Gate or the area around it.

Analysis of residue dust and contaminates on the Gate's surface match common deposits found in the Barrier and the Walker Nebulae. The jump gate's internal energy sources are depleted, however it is drawing a minimal charge from an external source. There are signs of extensive tampering with the Gate's structure, although the purpose is unclear.

37648.text: The Cuyamel is a bulk super-transport operated by Universal Shipping. The vessel is regularly seen shipping goods between California and Coronado. The Cuyamel was caught in open space during the Jericho Incident, requiring emergency repairs at Sabah Shipyard. Since then, it has primarily been responsible for shuttling repair goods to Scottsdale Refinery, although the pace of this job has been severely slowed by ongoing disputes about the extent of insurance cover for the damages.

37649.text:
Ontario's California Jump Gate was constructed in 810 AS. This serviced all Liberty traffic into the system until 830 AS, when the gate was decommissioned as a part of Liberty's withdrawal from the region.

In 834 AS, Liberty reactivated the Jump Gate by dispatching the deep space construction ship Robert Peary to carry out patch repairs and re-install the White Boxes needed to establish an emergency jump connection. This allowed the transit of emergency Liberty forces into Ontario, until the Robert Peary was destroyed and the gate damaged the following year.

In late 835 AS, the LSF scuttled the deteriorating gate to prevent sensitive components falling into Lane Hacker hands.

37651.text: The Graf von Blücher is a bulk metals container transport, contracted to Imperial Shipping. Typically responsible for cargo shipments between Freiburg Station in Stuttgart and Planet Amiens in Picardy, the Graf von Blücher's convoy came under attack in Champagne in late 751 AGS (835 AS). The Gallic Gendarmerie blamed the Maquis for the strike, however radical Marne workers have claimed responsibility.

37653.text:
MARNE RIOTER

All spaceships are equipped with standard eject mechanisms. When a pilot loses a fight, they automatically eject right before the ship explodes. Then, the winner might pick up the unlucky foe - or let him or her die in open space. The Maquis or other Gallic dissidents will pay good money to get captured Marne Rioters back, but the Gendarmerie may pay even more.

37655.text: Discontented Marne workers staged a protest at this site in late 751 AGS (835 AS), in an attempt to block the nearby Trade Lane and stop Rheinland traffic. After a harsh crackdown by the Gallic Gendarmerie, the area erupted into combat, with Rheinland transports regularly being attacked by enraged rioters.

37657.text:
LWB INDEPENDENCE ROUNDEL

The LWB Independence Roundel symbolizes the battles of 834 AS to free Sabine Schroder and expel the Farmers Allinace from Rheinland. Since then, the LWB has reasserted itself as an independent force, with this pilot at its forefront.

37659.text:
20th ANNIVERSARY ROUNDEL

This roundel celebrates the anniversary of the Discovery mod's public release, in August 2005. It features the avatar used by mod founder, Igiss.

37661.text:
[KNF] Fleet Roundel

The "Kikkamon", or 16-petal Chrysanthemum, is the symbol of the Imperial Throne of Kusari. Adopted by the Emperor following the Sakura Coup, the Kikkamon was intended to allude to the House's pre-Sirian roots, and remains in use to this day.

This altered version of a red Chrysanthemum on pure white background was introduced after the Kusari Civil War, to honor the sacrifices and loyalty of those who served the Emperor even in exile. Its use is strictly reserved to former Exiles, members of the Imperial Guard, or as reward for outstanding military service in the regular fleets.

37663.text:
CIVIL DEFENCE INITIATIVE ROUNDEL

This roundel is used by the special constables of the Civil Defence Initiative law enforcement militia. Their pilots are the long -- if slightly crooked -- arm of the law.

37665.text:
BRISTOL ROUNDEL

This roundel is used by contracted employees of Bristol Constructions & Manufacturing, commonly seen in their home system of Bering, House Liberty, and Galileo. These pilots are known for their variety of attitudes and operations, ranging from former military pilots to communal mining ships, though they universally operate in competition to Junker salvage operations and DSE mining operations both in Liberty and abroad.

37667.text:
MED FORCE ENTERPRISES ROUNDEL

This roundel is authorized for use by personnel of Med Force Enterprises. Display of the MFE emblem ensures immediate visual identification of the vessel and signifies its medical and scientific affiliation. In operational space, the presence of the MFE logo may help de-escalate tensions during high-risk encounters, indicating a neutral, humanitarian mission and supporting our doctors, scientists, and specialists as they carry out their duties throughout the Sirius system.

37669.text:
BRETONIA ROUNDEL

This roundel depicts the flag of House Bretonia.

37671.text:
COCHRANE GATEBREAKER ROUNDEL

This roundel utilizes the markings of the Lane Hacker's Cochrane Gatebreaker squadron. These elite operatives and assassins are notorious for the hijacking of the LSF asset Argonaut in Kepler, while it attempted to return to Liberty with classified Kusari technology. Gatebreaker operatives are subject to enormous bounties by both Kusari and Liberty authorities.

37673.text:
GALLIC NATIONAL INTELLIGENCE ROUNDEL

The logo of the Gallic National Intelligence symbolizes the agency's mandate to serve all of Gallia as both her first line of defense, and as the first weapon to be wielded against those that threaten her. The heptagonal field represents the seven systems inhabited by Gallia, while the crossed sword and spear covered by a shield are ancient representations of martial might. The golden fleur-de-lis at its center has been stylized to look like a spearpoint, a popular symbol among special forces groups dating all the way back to Earth and the Sol system.

37675.text:
IMG| ROUNDEL

This roundel is mostly used among the members of the "Mainline" Independent Miners Guild.

37677.text:
RHEINLAND ROUNDEL

This roundel depicts the flag of House Rheinland.

37679.text:
KUSARI ROUNDEL

This roundel depicts the flag of House Kusari.

37681.text:
GALLIA ROUNDEL

This roundel depicts the flag of House Gallia.

37683.text:
LIBERTY ROUNDEL

This roundel depicts the flag of House Liberty.

37685.text:
CROSSBONES ROUNDEL

This roundel depicts the skull and crossbones often displayed by pirates, murderers, and other pilots of ill-intent.

Courville Guard Station was constructed at the Picardy Jump Gate in 660 AGS (744 AS), to serve as the system headquarters of the Gallic Royal Police and Gallic Royal Intelligence. This imposition of royal authority was prompted by the bloody campaign of bombings that had occurred on Planet Marne two years earlier, and unease about the loyalty of the unruly Gallic border world. Accordingly, patrols were charged with intercepting smugglers and apprehending the growing population of radicals that called Champagne home.

When the Second Gallic Civil War broke out in 716 AGS (800 AS), Courville became the front line for clashes between the Gallic Royal Navy and the rebel forces of The Council. The station was largely destroyed by a Council torpedo strike in 718 AGS (802 AS), then abandoned until the Gallic Royal Navy were driven out of Champagne two years later. Courville remained a wreck until 726 AGS (810 AS). In response to the Battle of Langres, it was partially repaired, pressurized, and fitted with heavy weapons.

Courville protected the Picardy Jump Gate for the remainder of the war, however the ramshackle nature of its repairs made the station increasingly dangerous and costly to maintain. Early in 743 AGS (827 AS), the deeply indebted Gallic Republic scuttled the station on budgetary grounds, shunting the remains towards the Seine Nebula.

Port Tinqueux is the primary spaceport of Planet Marne’s Saint-Dizier Province. The area has historically been notorious for poverty, crime, and discontent. For centuries, the Gallic Royal Police expressed little interest in managing these problems, leaving fertile ground for enormous Gallic Brigand syndicates to establish themselves. As a result, the Brigands operated their own shadowy parallel society, offering security (from themselves) for a price. Driven by these grievances, the people of Saint-Dizier have long held strong republican tendencies, making it one of the key recruiting grounds for The Council during the Second Gallic Civil War.

In Saint-Dizier it is a common sentiment that the Gallic Union is little better than the Kingdom it replaced. This is largely driven by the Treaty of Oerlikon, a sweeping free trade treaty with Rheinland, that has thrown open Gallia’s markets to imported metals and minerals. While GMS had been investing into Marne’s impoverished communities, the shock of cheaper imports has led to uncompetitive mines and refineries being forced out of business. Unemployment in the already impoverished region has soared, as flagship Molybdenum refineries were relocated to Zurich.

Strikes and riots are a frequent occurrence, along with attacks on government assets by Maquis radicals. The Union has so far been reluctant to send in Marines to force open picketed factories and space ports, fearing the move could trigger a second Marne Uprising. Rather, many prominent firebrands have fallen to assassins, leading to accusations being leveled against Unione Corse hitmen. The Maquis are acutely conscious of this, and are actively extracting Dissidents to receive training in insurgency warfare and sabotage elsewhere. The Brigands have also profited handsomely from the chaos, tightening their grip on the area and stamping out vigilante threats to their dominance.

Montmirail Anchorage was excavated by The Council in 658 AGS (742 AS), shortly after Macon Base in Burgundy. Hidden in an over-mined and exhausted region of the Ardennes Asteroid Field, Montmirail was initially used to smuggle agents to and from Marne. The base was later designated as the primary mustering point for the Council’s fleet in the lead-up to the Second Gallic Civil War. From here, The Council coordinated its efforts during the Battle of Champagne, ultimately driving the Gallic Royal Navy from the system by 721 AGS (804 AS).

Upon securing Champagne as the capital of the revolution, most Council members relocated to Planet Marne, with only a skeleton crew remaining behind. By the war’s end in 742 AGS (826 AS), the newly formed Gallic Republic no longer required hidden asteroid bases. As a result, Montmirail was stripped of most useful equipment and abandoned. It remained in this state for almost a decade, slipping from memory until 752 AGS (836 AS), when Maquis operatives began to make repairs. Montmirail is now once again used as a staging point to aid dissidents on Planet Marne, where tensions from the Treaty of Oerlikon have already escalated into violence.

So far the Maquis have been careful not to draw attention to their newest lair, by avoiding confrontations with the few GMS vessels still eking out a living around the Ardennes’ perimeter.

37696.text: Gallic Brigands\nBlack Marketeer, Port Tinqueux\nIsaac Fouquet

37697.text: Gallic Brigands\nChop Shop Welder, Port Tinqueux\nNormand Dandonneau

37698.text: We recently restored this base as a foothold in Champagne. Once it belonged to The Council, however it was abandoned shortly before the Mazagran Massacre. It seems appropriate that we will now use this old Council hideout to tear down the mockery of a state they betrayed us to found.

37699.text: The Gallic Union is a tyranny no different to the old Kingdom. We intend to repeat history and burn it to the ground. Marne once again cries out against injustice -- we must simply equip the people with the knowledge and arms necessary to see the job done. We will rekindle the fire of revolution that was betrayed by The Council, and send it roaring across Gallia’s worlds.

37701.text: Many Maquis now see the Unione Corse as traitors and collaborators. They bent the knee to the Gallic Confederacy, and took the Grand Marechal’s silver to submit to the Gallic Union. Now it is said Unione Corse assassins work on the Union’s payroll to assassinate those workers on Marne brave enough to rebel against injustice. The Maquis of Béziers will kill Corsicans on sight. The other cells are still deciding which way to jump.

37702.text: The Maquis were founded in this system. In 658 AGS, our ancestors carried out a great campaign of justice on Planet Marne, targeting corrupt officials of the crown. Many civilian collaborators were killed by the bombs to achieve victory -- a just and necessary act. The Council did not see it the same way, expelling our forebears over "collateral damage”. This freed us to act decisively, without the constraints of the Council’s petty moral codes.

37704.text: Our freedom fighters loyally supported The Council during the Second Gallic Civil War, and they repaid us with treachery. The moment they had an opportunity to take power, they abandoned their professed ideals, and broke bread with our enemies. The Gallic Confederacy was a mockery of the principles of the revolution. The Maquis will not make such a mistake of misplaced trust again.

37705.text: To destroy the legacy of the Gallic crown, we must execute the aristocracy and tear down the institutions that allowed it to grow fat on the blood of Gallia’s people. In 742 AGS, The Council had the chance to do just so. Instead, they balked, laid down their arms, and pardoned the tyrants who choked the life from our House for centuries. When we refused to do likewise, it was The Council who came for us at Mazagran.

37707.text: After Mazagran, the Maquis’ network of bases were compromised. Throughout the Civil War, we shared our hangars with The Council. When they became the government, they knew exactly where to find us. The Kusari Invasion brought us some time to reorganize before the Union’s crackdown began -- it was a dark time for the cause, regardless.

37708.text: The Maquis were seen as a radical fringe of extremists, compared to the more moderate Council. We were unwilling to compromise our principles, or surrender justice for peace. The Council sold its soul, shook hands with war criminals, and became collaborators with the Union regime -- after that, our extremism no longer seems so radical to many. Many Counciliards were disgusted by their leaders and defected to our banner.

37710.text: The Maquis fought to break Gallia’s isolation, in the hope the Sirian Houses would aid us in our struggle against the King. Unfortunately, Sirius did not unite against the threat as we had hoped. Today, the Maquis’ views on Sirius are complicated. Bretonia is spent and unable to assist us. Kusari is hated by the Gallic people. Liberty is disinterested in our plight. The Rheinish supply the regime and leave the workers of Champagne destitute. It is not the future we had hoped for.

37711.text: Rheinish minerals are fueling the reconstruction of the Gallic fleet -- an existential threat for all free Gallic citizens, and the peoples of Sirius. We strike their transports to cut off this flow. Our aid to the oppressed masses of Marne also presents opportunities -- damaged Rheinish transports receive repairs at Chalons-et-Champagne Station. There are those among the crew who would be willing to smuggle our operatives aboard.

37713.text: The Champagne cell is primarily drawn from our compatriots in Picardy and Ile-de-France, who have been training dissidents from Marne for some time. We have also requested supplies and support from Béziers in Languedoc, but they have not responded. While they have their own concerns on Quillan, their refusal to contribute to the wider cause is frustrating.

37714.text: The materials we liberate from Rheinish transports in this system will mostly be shipped to the Hebrides. The Sournia Repair Yards maintain the larger vessels that defected from the Council, or we have seized through boarding actions. Similar to the Council’s strategy before the Civil War, we are biding our time, mustering forces, and preparing for an overwhelming strike that will reignite the revolution.

37715.text: There is an unstable Jump Hole nearby that can be used to access Provence. The location is yours

37717.text: If you need supplies, there's a pirate black market in this system -- I'll sell you Epernay Base's location

The Maquis are keenly aware of this, and seek to develop a revolutionary cadre on Planet Marne to instigate a new uprising. To avoid the Union's assassins and reprisals, many Dissidents are smuggled abroad to any foreign organizations who might be willing to provide training for a fee.

37757.text: Before the war, there were secret Jump Hole passages into the Hebrides that were guarded by minefields. I'll sell you the location of the Montpelier passage

37758.text: Be careful out there -- the mines are still active, and Orkney is a very dangerous place. You've been warned.

37761.text: The Samura heavy transport Kusu was destroyed by Blood Dragon terrorists in 835 AS, while carrying out supply activities around Nansei Research Station. The captain and crew were rescued shortly after, and received a (non-monetary) commendation from Samura HQ in recognition of the unprecedented 216 hour continuous shift they had just completed.

37762.text: Nansei is the birthplace of the Supernova Antimatter Cannon. In the aftermath of the Colony Wars, Kusari was desperate for funding to rebuild the Naval Forces. Despite misgivings, the prototype Supernova was commercially sold under a profit sharing agreement between Samura and the Kusari government.

37763.text: Once Nansei released the Supernova Antimatter Cannon, imitations and clones began proliferating in a matter of years. In retrospect, many now believe Kusari should have weathered the hardship following the Colony Wars and kept the Supernova a secret. What difference could such a surprise weapon have made during the Tau War?

37764.text: Antimatter research at Nansei will soon cease, possibly to be revived at some point in the future. The threat of Liberty looms large, and the government is mustering its resources towards mature projects and tangible results. Ending the antimatter program is shortsighted -- unfortunately, the state budget only goes so far.

37766.text: Conflict between Kusari and Liberty will not be won through occupied territory, but through economic disruption and technological coercion. The Liberty Navy may well be able to apply pressure, but occupying Shikoku will not deter Kusari's Jump Drive schemes. That needs an entirely different, more subtle approach. We'll achieve our goals through cultivated assets and subterfuge.

37767.text: There are several dissident groups within Kusari. We have worked particularly hard at cultivating the Blood Dragons as assets -- they are skilled fighters, and have ideological grievances that predispose them towards striking our targets of interest. Taking Nansei and Kansai out of commission is a major concern for us and them both.

37768.text: We have several shell companies mobilizing to provide military supplies to the Blood Dragons. These are being exported from Liberty through the Barrier Pass. Bretonia would traditionally have been safer, however their growing relationship with Kusari has introduced significant detection risks we would rather avoid. The Crayter Republic has its own grievances with Kusari -- it should not take much persuasion for them to turn a blind eye.

37769.text: I can put you in contact with certain assets in the %F0. This is a sensitive matter, and we will need to provide them with suitable gifts and recognition to soothe their sense of honor. %d0 credits should cover it.

37771.text:
CLASS: Bulwark
AMENITIES: Limited
CREW: 130

The Anadyr was constructed at Alster Shipyard in 835 AS, through the ongoing partnership between Kress Industrial and Bristol Construction & Manufacturing. The heavy frigate initially convoyed between Bristol Bay Station and mining sites in Pennsylvania, however the Bulwark's over-engineering made it poorly-suited to the Trade Lanes, which could be more economically serviced by regular Transports.

Following reports of a disastrous battle in Ontario, the vessel was instead reassigned to the dangerous backwater system. The Anadyr now covertly prowls Ontario, probing abandoned battlefields for lucrative unclaimed wreckage. Particularly rich prospects are equally coveted by local Junkers -- the frigate's heavy arms and armor have frequently been necessary to see off particularly tenacious rivals.

37773.text: The Objector corvette is an idea that's been bouncing around the raider clans for years -- some hare-brained scheme cooked up by Ouray, Nome, and Barrow. I've been given this schizophrenic collection of schematics and asked to make something usable. None of them will even agree on the reactor specifications.

37774.text: Cardamine worries me. More and more Xenos are getting hooked, even if they're ordered to stay off it. I'm getting the gear and tools I need to work now, but it feels like we're selling our souls. At least now Barrow can afford to barter for Engine Components in Bering -- getting hold of the arrays was one of the biggest roadblocks to the Objector project.

37775.text: The Objector is a nasty merger of three or four different concepts. It isn't the ship I'd build if I had a clean slate, but it is what we were left with after politics and economics were done interfering. I work with technicians who were mustered out from the Navy after the Gallic War, and they're baffled by the damn things.

LSF PIN-UP ROUNDEL

Biermann was later shot down by Bounty Hunters and returned to a secured mental health facility on Planet Stuttgart, where he claimed he had been summoned to the Omegas to retrieve Rheinland's savior.

CLASS: Longhorn
