The Lassen was a Deep Space Engineering stores and munitions ship, once contracted to service with the Liberty Navy. Assigned as a fleet tender to Norfolk Shipyard, it assisted with refilling the magazines of moored warships. When Kusari launched its surprise first strike assault in mid 836 AS, the Lassen was struck by torpedoes. The resulting detonation destroyed a squadron of nearby cruisers.

37788.text: Intelligence staff can prepare a falsified transponder for your field operations. This will resist basic scrutiny, but will not hold up to close inspection or docking control verification. %d0 credits will cover the expenses of our assets in the %F0 to make this happen.

37790.text: The Akatsuki is unique in that it boasts both a Cloaking Device and a Generation 4 Jump Drive. The Cloak has previously been used to great effect for infiltration and ambush, however the Drive is a more complicated affair. The power requirements are huge, and require external tankers for fueling. Our officers are still debating how this should be factored into our doctrine.

37791.text: The operatives here have been launching into the Independent Worlds and beyond to monitor Liberty's naval buildup and watch for signs of invasion. Signals intelligence indicates that Liberty or another third party are planning to move against us imminently. In preparation, we have drawn up lists of priority targets across Liberty that could be struck with Jump Drive assistance.

37792.text: Our orders are to be ready for immediate combat operations using our Jump Drive. The Drive's capabilities remain classified, so we do not know its strike range. It is suggested that all of Liberty is within reach. I feel we are stood on the edge of an abyss, awaiting the order to jump.

37793.text: In addition to our standard combat wing, the Akatsuki maintains civilian ships for covert reconnaissance and strike missions. Liberty has a number of internal disputes and societal defects, however an overt KOI presence would be ill suited to exploit them. The Militant insurgency in Pennsylvania is of particular interest to us and the Chochinbi Division.

37794.text: The Akatsuki's Jump Drive can generate a Drive Breach, which functions like a Jump Hole. The scientists assure me it is nothing at all like a Jump Hole, but a spade is a spade. Regardless, we can project small groups of ships through each Breach -- the Akatsuki is not required to follow them through, although in this eventuality the taskforce will be stranded at their destination.

37795.text: I have the barest understanding of the Jump Drive's functionality, but a technician explained that it darts through Hyperspace using the path of least resistance, tunneling where necessary. In this way, it burrows through the fabric of reality at the point of entrance and exit -- otherwise tracking the course and flow of existing Jump Holes and Gates.

37796.text: The arrival point of a Drive Breach is unpredictable. Early experiments demonstrated we could improve our precision thirty-fold with a paired array of Jump Drives. The so-called Drive Bridge is the pairing of generators across star systems, to perforate the fabric of realspace in a desirable location. The fundamental problem is fueling the insatiable thirst of the Drive situated in a military bridgehead.

37797.text: Drive Strike doctrine is still in its infancy. It should be possible to launch a capital ship battlegroup into enemy territory and inflict a decisive blow. Much of our mass allowance will be occupied by the fuel tankers needed to generate the Breach home -- this has been the Bretonian experience in Dublin. For deep strikes against military targets, admiralty planners have factored an extreme casualty ratio into their calculations for return fuel requirements.

37798.text: This ship was the second battlecruiser launched by Kusari, and probably the most studied. From teething problems with the design, to Ichigaya Drydock's experimental enhancements, the Akatsuki has been stripped and rebuilt a dozen times. There is not a bolt or conduit aboard that has not been scrutinized many times over. So much has been modified, tweaked and altered over the years, that she is entirely unique. There is no ship in the fleet quite like this one.

37800.text:
OSI ROUNDEL

The OSI roundel is the primary visual identifier of Omicron Supply Industries, a Zoner-based trade corporation. It is designed for fast recognition across cargo, documents, equipment, and digital systems, marking verified origin, authorization, and handling. Its represents central OSI monogram and uses a clear industrial style for legibility at any scale. It signifies protected logistics and certified transaction channels. Wherever displayed, the roundel communicates commercial neutrality, traceable supply origin, and reliable trade oversight within the Zoner operating environment.

37801.text: Before the Second Civil War, The Council was an underground political movement, rather than a rebellion. A subversive ideology in barracks rooms and coffee houses, insidiously spreading from one generation of officers to the next. The crown had no idea how far it had gone. Not until the Marne Pacification Fleet mutinied and it was far too late.

37802.text: By the end of the Conquest of Sirius, King Charles was a paranoid wreck, lashing out at enemies real and imaginary. His neurosis tore Solar Engineering apart, decapitated the Huissiers, and alienated the nobility. We might have won the war, were it not for the meritless execution of Duke Créquy and all the woes that ensued.

37803.text: I served in the Gallic Royal Navy during the Conquest of Sirius, aboard the Battleship Dax. Thankfully I was rotated back to the Kingdom before the Siege of New London. It is difficult to say what I would have done, had I been in Leeds at the end. We all like to believe we would have been among those who disobeyed the order. It is a comforting thought.

37804.text: There are some aboard this ship who served in the Enclave. Many crew have complicated feelings about the Enclave. For almost a year they raided the Republic and Minarchy, killing many fellow servicemen. Most are also unrepentant war criminals, and believe what happened in Leeds was justified. Despite that, they are still the main reason Kusari did not reach Ile-de-France during their invasion.

37805.text: The Union projects strength, but those of us who fought in the Civil War can see where the fractures hide. Many capital ships are still crewed by local levies, and loyalties to home systems are often stronger than their duty to the Union. The Grand Marshall wants this changed, but fears pressing the issue in case his officers refuse. Who knows what would happen then?

37806.text: When the De Grasse was damaged during the Kusari Invasion, she was sent to Maintenon Shipyard in Orleanais. The repairs took so long that the crew was dismissed. That’s why the Union had a free hand to assign a new mixed crew from across Gallia -- to ensure there were no overriding loyalties to old Confederal states or causes. We're the model for the modern Navy.

37807.text: Many now believe the Kingdom was correct in its assessment of the Sirians. Kusari was a supposedly neutral state, one we had traded with for many years. Then without warning or provocation, they invaded our territory and murdered our countrymen. Rather than seek revenge for the desolation of Lorraine, we agree to a treaty surrendering the Taus to them. Is that justice?

37808.text: Bretonia continues to yap like a small dog, barking about reparations, war criminals, and enough else to send a man to sleep. Bretonia will yap so long as it can hide behind the skirts of Liberty and Kusari. However, we suspect neither will be inclined to fight Bretonia’s wars soon enough. Perhaps the small dog should be disciplined so it learns its place?

37809.text: The Seigneur commanding this system -- Ansel Bousquet -- has committed our Marines to assist with maintaining order on Quillan. But orbital insertion drops are not necessary to deal with strikes and picket lines. We all suspect it is inevitable that we will soon deploy to Tau-23, but these drills make me wonder what else may be afoot.

37810.text: The officers of this ship have been drawn from across Gallia, and do not cooperate well. They have backgrounds in the Duchy, Enclave and Republic, or are green from the academy. I have seen strategy briefings devolve into screaming, and the captain will not speak to his first officer. No doubt the reports sent to New Paris talk of a wonderful esprit de corps.

37811.text: I served on the Battleship Epinal during the Kusari Invasion, under the flag of the Grand Duchy. I still have comrades stationed in Burgundy, aboard the Montmorency. Sometimes I hear mutterings of stray princes or princesses that survived the Kingdon's collapse -- a dangerous symbol for disgruntled nobles on Nevers.

37812.text: Duke Créquy was one of the finest military minds in Gallic history. He masterminded the initial invasion of the Taus, and the 8 Day War that annhilated the Kusari Naval Forces in one fell swoop. He rose too high in the hearts of the Parisian people, and made many enemies in the royal court. King Charles executed him on trumped-up charges of treason, leaving his war machine in the hands of fools.

37825.text:
46TH FLEET ROUNDEL

The 46th Fleet is the youngest of the Liberty Navy's primary formations. Initially a mere strike force formed to serve as a proving ground for cadets fresh out of West Point, a recent naval restructuring has seen the 46th ascend to the status of a full, numbered fleet. Despite incurring much critique during its early days due to its use of controversial tactics, the 46th Fleet has since earned its rightful place among its more veteran counterparts. The 46th Fleet's units can frequently be seen patrolling Liberty's shipping lanes, safeguarding her borders, and fending off attacks, both foreign and domestic.

37827.text:
1ST FLEET ROUNDEL

Since its foundation, the Liberty Navy First Fleet has used a white Liberty Star as its standard, carrying it into every notable battle Liberty has fought since the end of the Colony Wars. The First Fleet has been placed against the gravest threats to ever stand against Liberty, and has proven itself to be capable of meeting the challenge every time.

37829.text:
GEN'AN ROUNDEL

The stylised chrysanthemum of the Gen'an Cell. It represents the ideals of a GC elite, signifying purity of purpose, unity among sisters, the elegance of the goddess, and the burning fury of the Kusari sun in the face of oppression.

XENO ALLIANCE ROUNDEL

The Alliance Militia forms the fighting backbone of the Xeno Alliance, a diverse coalition of squadrons and units dedicated to securing independence from House Liberty.

37833.text:
CLASS: Barge
GRAVITY: Partial
DOCKING: Restricted
AMENITIES: Complete
CREW: 4,300

The Construction Ship Fenland was launched from Southampton Shipyard in 768 AS, as one of BMM's largest and most ambitious projects to date. Designed to carry pre-fabricated station modules in its cavernous hold, the Fenland could facilitate the mass deployment of infrastructure, or provide on-site fabrication for bespoke construction materials and fittings. Equipped with onboard factories and crew facilities, the Fenland is capable of crawling through the extended space between star systems, arriving up to a year later to deploy its stations. This ideally suits BMM's preferred corporate approach of charting projects years in advance, rather than reacting flexibly to emerging circumstances.

The Fenland narrowly avoided being caught in the Belfast Uprising in 814 AS, having departed towards Scarborough Shipyard several weeks before. Until the beginning of the Gallic War, the Barge primarily shuttled between Newcastle and New London, transferring industrial goods and shipyard modules. This changed in 821 AS, with the Gallic invasion of Newcastle -- after reinforcing Gateshead Station and deploying Supply Depot Carham, the Fenland was withdrawn from the increasingly dangerous front line. It was instead dispatched to Poole, arriving in 822 AS to begin work as a sheltered fabrication hub for war supplies.

Following the loss of Southampton Shipyard in 825 AS, the Fenland was tasked with constructing its replacement. Arriving in Cambridge in 826 AS, it occupied the Trade Lane junction of the recently-sabotaged Cardiff Mining Station to deploy Portsmouth Shipyard. Following the war, the elderly Barge was returned to Newcastle for refitting, then assisted with the development of Redcarr Production Facility and later LD-14 in Leeds. Following this, the vessel sat idle for several years due to funding constraints. Matters only changed in early 836 AS, when a landmark funding deal was secured with Samura Heavy Industries, covering much of the cost of rebuilding Stokes Smelter.

37835.text:
CLASS: Benford
GRAVITY: No
DOCKING: No
AMENITIES: N/A
CREW: 0

Leduc Station was torn apart by the ferocious Dark Matter storm that swept through Alberta. Scans indicate the wreckage and nearby debris is coated in an unusual biological film. The station was constructed in 818 AS, and initially operated as a classified Ageira Technologies quarantine lab. This work was allegedly linked to Ageira's intense interest in Planet Edmonton, with several high security labs being established aboard. The station was notorious for its spartan conditions, severe isolation, and lack of recreational amenities, making it an extremely unpopular posting for senior researchers.

Despite this, postings were incredibly well paid, and the station saw significant further investment from 821 AS onward. This resulted in Leduc leading on a number of highly classified research projects, including the manufacture of the first commercially viable Bioneural Processors. As Liberty's strategic planners became increasingly concerned about the direction of the Gallic War, Leduc's role shifted. Appointed as the headquarters of Project COLD LAKE in 823 AS, Leduc pioneered the construction of the first Supergate terminal in over three hundred years. Shrouded in secrecy, the station was placed under guard by both the Liberty Navy and LSF, and supplied by heavily armed convoys.

The project was completed in early 826 AS, connecting to a receiver terminal in Poole and enabling Liberty to break the Siege of New London. Leduc managed the Supergate connection for less than a year before the Poole terminal was catastrophically sabotaged, ending the project. By the end of the year, the encroaching Dark Matter storm posed an extreme risk to any further attempts to reactivate the Supergate program. A general evacuation order was issued, with Leduc coordinating efforts to strip the Supergate of sensitive components for transport to testing sites elsewhere in Liberty. Leduc continued to operate its Bioneural Processor plants up until the point of final shutdown.

37837.text:
ANOMALOUS ORGANISMS
>>> HAZARDOUS CARGO <<<
Colonies of these bacterial lifeforms were found -- against all odds -- teeming on the wreckage of Leduc Station in Alberta. The Dark Matter that has consumed the system is inimical to life in any known configuration, rendering these organisms perplexing anomalies. Samples begin to deteriorate when removed from the Dark Matter environment, while emitting radiation that is damaging to shipboard systems. The best guess of researchers is that the organisms were intentionally engineered, but the why and how so far eludes explanation.

37839.text:
Pentester Cabin Recorder:

Okay. I don't think I'm making it back to Airdrie. Okay. Got greedy.

Seems unlikely anyone is going to find me. Or the Pentester... afterwards... if we're being honest.

[Inaudible] get started just in case. The flight recorder is sturdy and rad hardened. If you're hearing this, hi. What were the odds, huh?

First, if you picked up any new friends over at Le[inaudiable] them, immediately. Airlock your bay, flush everything. If you're lucky enough to have a decontamination cycler, good for you. Use it.

I tried breaking into Leduc to see if I could rip anything from any redundant datavaults that might've been left behind. If you've not been there yet, do not land.

Some crazy bastard let their pet project out of the hotlabs. There's mold all over the place. Some of it hitched a ride out.

[Laughter]

Ate through my ship's hold and got into the systems. What kind of unholy mold thrives in a Dark Matter storm?

40008.text:
This Hammerhead has been cut almost in half by a vicious hull breach carved up its left side, with distinctive, angry scorch marks indicative of a Natterturm-series laser burn shearing across the ship from that angle. Telemetry data from the wreck indicates that the vessel eventually burst into flame following a rupture of the main fuel line, and today it is little more than a burnt-out husk.

The ship's logs indicate that this ship belonged to a Libertonian pilot -- Frankie 'Lucky' Day, a rising star among Bounty Hunters in the near Omicrons. A known veteran of this area of space, his aim with a full spread of Buckshots was said to be shaky at best, but his skill at maneuvering his ship bought time for the one lucky shot that always seemed to connect.

40010.text:
A Hammerhead wreck languishing in space, this ship's aft section has been torn wide open. Tungsten shards litter the affected area, deeply embedded in the hull. The nature of the damage appears to indicate a premature mine detonation, with the shape of the affected area and severity of the damage suggesting that the ordnance exploded almost immediately after being launched.

The pilot's log makes mention of the ship's owner: a Bretonian by the name of Sara Khansari, a Bounty Hunter of some renown with tens of kills to her name, and an apparent predilection for a bold, daring flight style. The last entry details her intention to pursue reports of Hessian targets in the Omega-41 system, alongside a fellow veteran Hunter.

40012.text:
This Dagger's cockpit has been practically ripped off the ship's main structure, blown apart by a ferocious concussive impact. The ship's hull is peppered with tungsten spikes, indicative of a direct hit by some manner of mine, and data recovered from the wreck suggests that the vessel lost all control shortly thereafter. The pilot was likely killed instantly.

The devastation wrought upon the ship has rendered most of the black box recorder unsalvageable, but Dagger-class light fighters are issued predominantly to newer, more inexperienced pilots among the Red Hessian movement. Very little personal data can be recovered from the ship's log, save for an untitled entry detailing the unnamed pilot's admiration for their flight lead, and a short mention of a planned patrol run together through Omega-41, heading as far afield as the jump hole to Omicron Theta.

40014.text:
The apparent lead craft of a pair of Hessian scouts, at first glance this Sabre appears almost entirely undamaged. Closer inspection reveals that the ship's life support system was disabled by a blast of Buckshot-pattern particle fire, whether by sheer luck or preternatural aim on the part of an adversary. Thereafter, the Sabre appears to have intentionally powered down next to its counterpart, rather than attempting to limp home. The pilot is likely to have suffocated within minutes.

Upon inspection, the logbook names the ship's owner as one Alisa Reis, an ace pilot of the Red Hessians famous for her skill in combat and ability as a flight lead. The last entry is very short, evidently written in great haste, and details only her regret at losing a comrade particularly close to her heart.

X-509 is a recently-created minefield deployed by the Gammu AI in response to Core aggression in the Omicron Kappa system. After the assault on planet Gammu, the closest point of retreat for the AI was Secundus Outpost, a former Crayter installation located in Omicron Pi, that was repurposed by the AI as a logistics-hub. The minefield was presumably deployed, to complicate navigating Omicron Kappa for everyone that isn't the AI, thus assisting in their retreat, and hindering future movements by the Core in the system.

40020.text:
***GRAVITATIONAL ANOMALY DETECTED***
The magnetic and gravimetric readings of this object are difficult to classify, but they most closely resemble those of a jump hole. Like Jump Gates, jump holes are naturally occurring regions of space that represent a breach in the natural boundaries of spacetime. Unlike Jump Gates, which are artificially stabilised via a finely-tuned combination of delicate programming and careful construction, jump holes occur naturally and are comparatively unpredictable and unstable. According to Ageira Technologies, transit through jump holes is a risky proposition, and can prove dangerous even for jump holes in a highly stable state of being.

Scanner telemetry coming from this jump hole suggests it is in an ongoing state of gravitational collapse, and its use is highly inadvisable. Standard travel guidelines from reputable travel advisories across the sector emphatically recommend maintaining a five-kilometre minimum exclusion zone from stellar bodies of this nature.

40025.text:
>>>WARNING: NAVIGATIONAL HAZARD<<<
A transparent green nebula located deep within the Omicron Pi system. Initially, it was thought to be a detached section of the larger Edge cloud, mainly due to its color. However, further examination refuted this theory as no ionized oxygen or hydrogen gases were detected. The full structure of this nebula remains unknown, and the possibility of it having an artificial origin has not been ruled out. The presence of high radiation, in conjunction with unidentified structures visible from the outside, point to only one conclusion: avoid Dolos at all costs.

40027.text:
The fifth craft of the Voyager exploration team, an expedition spearheaded by a Zoner organisation with interests in surveying the deepest reaches of the Omicrons. The ship itself is pristine, showing no signs of damage or malfunction; however, an automated biohazard warning has been left on a repeating broadcast. Telemetry data indicates the crew succumbed to some unknown disease, although neither the ship's computer nor the crew's logs shed any light on what the illness might have been.

The ship's captain, Matthijs Bergwijn, was known to have a lifelong background in xenobiology. His intent in coming to Omicron Pi was to search for new alien life forms to study and research, leaving the rest of the expeditionary force to focus on cartography. In succumbing to an alien disease and dying as a direct result of his life's work, his fate can only be described as ironic.

A brief message can be found at the very end of the ship's log, likely appended some time after the crew met their demise. It reads simply: "Find the Lost One".

40029.text:
The second craft of the Voyager exploration team, an expedition spearheaded by a Zoner organisation with interests in surveying the deepest reaches of the Omicrons. The Dromedary shows no signs of damage or malfunction, but a brief scan of the ship's cargo bay show no signs of any food or nutritional substances aboard. The crew appear to have starved to death in low orbit of this alien world. Having been low on supplies before approaching the planet, the starvation is likely a result of either mismanagement of food supplies or a drastically increased consumption of such due to the hostile environment of the cloud.

The ship's captain, Khaled al-Bastaki, was an old, decorated explorer of the Omicrons, and was responsible for charting several locations of great value across this most remote and violent region of the Sirius sector. It is only fitting he departed this world doing what he did best.

A brief message can be found at the very end of the ship's log, likely appended some time after the crew met their demise. It reads: "-42842".

40031.text:
The third craft of the Voyager exploration team, an expedition spearheaded by a Zoner organisation with interests in surveying the deepest reaches of the Omicrons. This Dromedary drifts listlessly in the local anomaly's gravity well, and a more detailed examination of the ship reveals that the fuel tanks ran dry some time ago. The fate of the crew is difficult to ascertain; the ship's log ends abruptly, alluding to nothing out of the ordinary.

The woman leading the expedition, Cyma Yazdani, was an ambitious young explorer hailing from the other side of the sector. In a complex turn of events in her life, she ended up leaving her birthplace to join the ranks of the Zoners, and subsequently distinguished herself in her exploratory career. Soon, she became the captain of her own ship, and was ultimately placed in charge of the third Voyager's mission.

A brief message can be found at the very end of the ship's log, likely appended some time after the crew met their demise. It reads: "23211".

40033.text:
The fourth craft of the Voyager exploration team, an expedition spearheaded by a Zoner organisation with interests in surveying the deepest reaches of the Omicrons. The Dromedary's cargo bay is completely empty, indicating that the crew ran dry of provisions, fuel, water, and oxygen all within a similar timeframe. The vessel's escape pod bays are all empty; the crew may have fled with some of the provisions before the situation deteriorated beyond expectations, but the their true fate is difficult to ascertain.

The captain was one Emilia Strauss, a seasoned and skillful explorer of the remote regions bordering her House of origin. She participated in charting parts of the Omegas, Sigmas, and Omicrons, publishing several scientific papers in the field of cartography. Only recently gaining captaincy, she and her crew surpassed all expectations on their maiden voyage and ended up inside what looks like the cooling core of a larger stellar object, its purpose unknown. The crew appears to have met with a tragic end; having expended all their resources to locate another jump hole they hoped might lead them back to Omicron Delta, they soon realised that it had been a pointless endeavour. The nearby jump hole was one of those affected by the Pi Catastrophe, and suffered from a gravitational collapse that rendered it useless to the stricken Dromedary and her crew.

A brief message can be found at the very end of the ship's log, likely appended some time after the crew met their demise. It reads: "171792".

40035.text:
The wreckage of the Lost Voyager, also known as Voyager 1, the lead ship of the Voyager expedition. The crew appears to have exhausted any and all life support supplies. After running out of fuel, the vessel appears to have been left to drift in the vast and endless void of deep space. Either against all odds or through incredible piloting skill and foresight, the ship eventually became caught in the gravity well of a rogue exoplanet, and is now trapped in a slowly decaying orbit.

The ship's black box contains a short audio log detailing some of what befell the ill-fated expedition. Playback commencing...

"This is captain Richard Keane, leader of the Voyager expedition. The date is May the sixth, 831 A.S., and we are in distress. Please, if anyone is able to read this message, we desperately need assistance! After entering the system less than a week ago, as scheduled for our mission, we have experienced an unprecedented catastrophe we are struggling to describe, let alone understand.

The jump hole leading back to Omicron Delta has collapsed, leaving us cut off from the rest of the sector. We will attempt to explore the rest of the system in hopes of finding another way home before it is too late. Perhaps there's another jump hole out there, somewhere.

The phenomenon itself-- it's like the entire system is... flashing before our eyes, like a kaleidoscope flickering through pattern after pattern. I don't even know how to describe it-- hopefully, the video we have will do it more justice than my words can. It's fascinating -- breathtaking, even -- but terrifying at the same time; we can see a sort of... wave of colour rippling across the endless void. Even the nebula here looks like it was pl--"

The rest of the file has suffered from data corruption, and playback stops at this point. No evidence of the referenced video file can be found.

A brief message can be found at the very end of the ship's log, likely appended some time after the crew met their demise. It reads: "WE SHALL RISE AGAIN".

40037.text:
One of the Voyager exploration team's escort craft, this Eagle appears undamaged at first glance; however, more detailed scans of the fighter show massive internal damage to the ship's electronics and control systems. It is likely it was hit by some kind of electromagnetic pulse and lost all manoeuvrability soon after. The pilot appears to have suffocated after the on-board oxygen regenerator failed. The internal damage is severe enough to render the vessel essentially scrap metal; no amount of repairs could restore such a total overload of its core systems.

The last entry in the ship's log makes reference to an unstable jumphole to the Omicron Delta system.

40039.text: One of the Voyager exploration team's escort craft, this Eagle appears to have suffered a high-speed, head-on collision with an asteroid or other spaceborne debris. The remaining wreck is beyond repair, rendered totally inoperable by subsequent micrometeorite impacts and deep space radiation from the system's star. Whether due to pilot error or outside influences beyond its owner's control, this fighter will never fly again.

40041.text: The remains of the Eagle Delta-4, shot down by the Chaser. The pilot was killed instantly by laser damage that pierced the right side of her cockpit. A quick and painless death.

40043.text:
The wreckage of the Core fighter Chaser, which belonged to the pilot Steve Collins. A bold and daring pilot, he was part of the Core vanguard that pursued the Gammu Artificial Intelligence forces deep into Omicron Pi. He became trapped in the A.I. Minefield when he failed to obey orders from his superiors and overextended himself.

In the midst of the chaotic battle, he engaged in a duel with Delta-4, a Technocracy Eagle. Collins lured the Eagle into a trap by stopping his ship, then executing a sharp right turn while simultaneously deploying a mine. Caught in the trap, Delta-4's shields were disabled by the mine as Collins outmaneuvered the Eagle and targeted its exposed side with his laser cannons. The right wing was completely destroyed and the cockpit was breached, killing the pilot instantly.

However, Collins' victory was short-lived. Immediately after the engagement, he was surrounded and forced to surrender. The ship itself is almost entirely intact, suggesting that Collins may have surrendered preemptively. The fate of the pilot is unknown, but it is believed that he was killed in captivity.

40045.text:
***GRAVITATIONAL ANOMALY DETECTED*** WARNING: This jump hole cannot be activated by vessels carrying more than 650 units of cargo.
The magnetic and gravimetric readings of this object are difficult to classify, but they most closely resemble those of a jump hole. Like Jump Gates, jump holes are naturally occurring regions of space that represent a breach in the natural boundaries of spacetime. Unlike Jump Gates, which are artificially stabilised via a finely-tuned combination of delicate programming and careful construction, jump holes occur naturally and are comparatively unpredictable and unstable. According to Ageira Technologies, transit through jump holes is a risky proposition, and can prove dangerous even for jump holes in a highly stable state of being.

Scanner telemetry coming from this jump hole suggests it is in an ongoing state of gravitational expansion, and its use is highly inadvisable. Standard travel guidelines from reputable travel advisories across the sector emphatically recommend maintaining a five-kilometre minimum exclusion zone from stellar bodies of this nature. The high-energy readings emanating from this jump hole indicate that it is still in its infancy, and its spacetime breach between the Omicron Delta and Omicron Pi systems continues to expand. However, further examination indicates that process has been disrupted by an overabundance of mass passing through the jump hole in a short period of time, rendering it unsuitable for larger vessels and a high-risk proposition for smaller craft.

40047.text: The wreck of the Intrepide, a Brigands Cuirassier belonging to Liliane LeClerc. With a bold and adventurous personality, she was one of the first to interact with the unstable jump hole in the wreckage's vicinity. Enduring a series of interferences during the journey, the ship's engines malfunctioned, leaving it stranded in hostile territory. The fate of the pilot is unknown.

40049.text: A large, lifeless comet floating on the outskirts of the Omicron Pi system. Analysis of the comet indicates it is an M-type asteroid, rich in iron and nickel. Such a composition suggests the comet formed from the metallic cores of different progenitor bodies that were violently merged in a collision. Its discovery is very recent, and it could carry significant importance in understanding the Omicron Pi catastrophe.

40050.text:
***GRAVITATIONAL ANOMALY DETECTED***
The magnetic and gravimetric readings of this object are difficult to classify, but they most closely resemble those of a jump hole. Like Jump Gates, jump holes are naturally occurring regions of space that represent a breach in the natural boundaries of spacetime. Unlike Jump Gates, which are artificially stabilised via a finely-tuned combination of delicate programming and careful construction, jump holes occur naturally and are comparatively unpredictable and unstable. According to Ageira Technologies, transit through jump holes is a risky proposition, and can prove dangerous even for jump holes in a highly stable state of being.

Scanner telemetry coming from this jump hole suggests it is in an ongoing state of gravitational collapse, and its use is highly inadvisable. Standard travel guidelines from reputable travel advisories across the sector emphatically recommend maintaining a five-kilometre minimum exclusion zone from stellar bodies of this nature. The residual signals emanating from this jump hole indicate a past connection to the Omicron Delta system. The cause of its collapse is difficult to determine, but it continues to emit high-frequency readings uncharacteristic of jump holes that have undergone a natural collapse as part of their life cycle.

40051.text:
***GRAVITATIONAL ANOMALY DETECTED*** WARNING: This jump hole cannot be activated by vessels carrying more than 650 units of cargo.
The magnetic and gravimetric readings of this object are difficult to classify, but they most closely resemble those of a jump hole. Like Jump Gates, jump holes are naturally occurring regions of space that represent a breach in the natural boundaries of spacetime. Unlike Jump Gates, which are artificially stabilised via a finely-tuned combination of delicate programming and careful construction, jump holes occur naturally and are comparatively unpredictable and unstable. According to Ageira Technologies, transit through jump holes is a risky proposition, and can prove dangerous even for jump holes in a highly stable state of being.

Scanner telemetry coming from this jump hole suggests it is in an early stage of gravitational collapse, and its use is highly inadvisable for any ship. The jump tunnel appears stable enough to permit passage for smaller craft or craft with enough hull reinforcements, but such usage is still discouraged by travel advisory bodies across the sector.

40053.text: The wreckage of the Outcast Dagger, La Entrega, which belonged to a rookie Outcast pilot Maria Montez. She seems to have stumbled across a nearby undiscovered jump hole. Hoping to be the first to explore the other side and prove herself, she preemptively jumped in. Her wish came true, but not without the complete failure of the life support systems due to turbulence during the jump. The pilot likely suffocated to death, and the wreckage now lingers in the vicinity of the jump hole.

40055.text: This is the wreck of the Zoner exploration vessel Dauntless, tasked with exploring the Omicron Pi system. The ship appears to have nearly foundered in close proximity to Knossos, intent on observing the planet and seeking an entry point into its atmosphere south of the equator. However, it became ensnared between several of the gas giant's violent storms, and only just managed to escape their grasp. It remains in orbit around the planet to this day. It is assumed that a system malfunction was responsible for the ship becoming stranded.

40069.text:
This beacon container marks the site at which the ship of Hayakawa Uemura, a Golden Chrysanthemum veteran and ace, was seemingly lost. It was placed at the location by her wife, the Bounty Hunter Yugure Uemura. The pair had built up a serious reputation over the years, in no small part due to their seemingly incompatible affiliations. Yugure avoided any contracts aimed at the Chrysanthemums or their allies, targeting enemies they had in common instead, while Hayakawa resisted all pressure to reveal her partner's movements to the underworld.

Together, they had logged thousands of flight hours in a career spanning decades, always by each others' side, and more commonly focused on exploration and travel than martial pursuits. Much of the current-day mapping data registered at stations in the Crow region was provided by the couple.

When the pair was exploring the newly-discovered Copernicus system, they lost radio contact and, hit by an intense radiation spike which caused sensor misreads, Yugure assumed Hayakawa had perished when her Eagle lost life support. She placed this beacon as a memorial to her lost love, and with the light extinguished from her life, endeavored upon a final journey to end her own existence. A set of coordinates can be read: -80 000, ?, -80 000.

40071.text:
Cloudpiercer is a derelict Eagle belonging to the Bounty Hunter Yugure Uemura, who abandoned it deliberately with the intent to end her life. Believing to have lost her wife and exploration partner of three decades, Hayakawa, Yugure had set a course for the last waypoint they had plotted together, to leave her ship and all its gathered treasures at the spot for the next pioneering spirit to discover, should they find her trail.

In actuality, the radiation spike she believed had killed her partner had merely incapacitated the ship. Hayakawa had survived with quick thinking and action in the hold, after raising the flameout bulkhead, and had managed to repair her craft within a few hours on-site.

Having instinctively pursued the same shared last waypoint, Hayakawa found Yugure's pod drifting, her partner resigned to her fate. With seemingly everything lost, she had surrendered herself to the eternal silence of the cosmos, before the love of her life's voice pinged the pod's comms. Rather than return to her own ship, Yugure decided to leave the Eagle and all its priceless relics, a monument to what she had intended to do, and the fact that she wanted nothing but her rescuer herself. Happily reunited, the couple retired from their more spectacular exploits to live out their later years together in private.

40073.text:
An almost perfectly intact Kestrel belonging to the Xenos, the Raleigh was among the earliest explorers of the system. The ship experienced an electrical failure and was abandoned by its crew, who survived for several weeks in their escape pod before being found. The tale of captain Walter Sollbright and his crew's heroic journey quickly entered Xeno folklore, and what may have been an EMP effect from a nearby volatile jump hole has since taken on ever grander proportions of epic space-time explosions every time the story is retold.

The ship itself has since become a popular landmark for other pioneers, its hull speckled with graffiti of names and dates. Paying respects at the wreck site is considered to bring good fortune, and so the area has become littered with offerings left by other explorers hoping for greater success than the Raleigh's crew.

40075.text:
The remains of Livingstone, a derelict Dromedary formerly operated by the Lane Hackers, its exterior unblemished but without life on board. The vessel's crew and her captain, Kalani Haoa, were responsible for the very first flood of data on the Copernicus system, her advanced comm arrays having provided a constant feed of information back to Leiden.

Her last outgoing comms also provided insight into the tragic life of the doomed crew, who, as their harrowing messages tell, were upset by engine trouble while dealing with an outbreak of sickness the small team was unequipped to handle. Rather than turning around, Haoa made the difficult decision to keep the vessel flying forwards on what they then knew would be a one-way trip, providing a wealth of insight on the mysterious star system.

Two bodies rest in their cots, likely victims of the disease, while Haoa and their first mate lie together on the bridge, victims of what appear to be self-inflicted gunshot wounds. Their mission having gone as far as it would take them, the Livingstone's crew had reached their grave site, the ship's name ready for the annals of exploration history.

40078.text:
>>>WARNING: NAVIGATIONAL HAZARD<<<
A medium-sized arm of the Crow Nebula, famed throughout Sirius for its beautiful vistas. The nebula is rich in ionized Hydrogen, Helium and Oxygen. Explosive gas pockets and likely other undetected hazards can be found within the cloud. All pilots are advised to take caution.

40080.text:
>>>WARNING: NAVIGATIONAL HAZARD<<<
A beautiful medium-sized ice field located within the Copernicus system. It was charted and named in 833 A.S. by the Xeno exploration vessel Raleigh, immediately after the system's discovery. The field's origin is unknown, but it likely drifted through deep space until it was caught by the gravitational wells of the system's brown dwarf and the nearby jump hole. The field holds no valuable resources and is almost entirely composed of ice asteroids and ionized hydrogen, responsible for its color.

40082.text:
>>>WARNING: NAVIGATIONAL HAZARD<<<
A small dust field located within the Copernicus system. It was charted and named in 833 A.S. by the Lane Hacker exploration vessel Livingstone, soon after the system's discovery. The field was likely formed from surrounding dust particles drawn together by a nearby jump hole's gravitational well over a long period of time. It holds no valuable resources.

40084.text:

MASS: N/A
TERRAIN: N/A
TEMPERATURE: N/A
ESCAPE VELOCITY: N/A

A colourful rogue planet charted and named in 833 A.S. by the Lane Hacker exploration vessel Livingstone shortly after the system's discovery. It appears that the planet was captured by the gravitational well of the nearby star after drifting through deep space. Galle has one natural satellite, Hevelius. The gas giant has not yet been observed from up close and further analysis is needed to more closely study its origin and composition.

A rocky moon charted and named in 833 A.S. by the Lane Hacker exploration vessel Livingstone shortly after the system's discovery. It orbits Planet Halle, a nearby gas giant. Hevelius has not yet been observed from up close and further analysis is needed to study its origin and composition.

A frozen world charted and named in 833 A.S. by the Xeno exploration vessel Raleigh shortly after the system's discovery. Titius shares an orbit with its binary twin, Bode. It remains a mystery how the two planets ended up in this state, and conducting a close-up analysis is necessary to uncover the twins' shared history and composition.

It remains a mystery how the two planets ended up in this state, and conducting a close-up analysis is necessary to uncover the twins' shared history and composition.

40092.text:
The remains of the Tsuiseki, a Gas Miners Guild vessel registered to Misaki Oshiro. Known for his bold and daring personality, the pilot was among the first to discover the connection between Copernicus and the Sigmas, venturing into unexplored territory in search of glory.

While exploring the uncharted region of the Crow Nebula, known for its treacherous gas pockets, the Otte successfully navigated the hazardous terrain. However, a mistake on the pilot's part exposed the ship to a series of gas pocket explosions. In an attempt to take a shortcut through the gas-filled nebula, the pilot underestimated the width of the gap, triggering one gas pocket after another as the ship took unrecoverable damage. The pilot likely died on the spot.

40094.text:
The wreck of the Gambler, a Bounty Hunter Hammerhead. The ship looks to have sustained critical damage from the surrounding violent gas pockets, likely due to a loss of maneuverability.

The pilot, Uwe Friedrich, was a renowned Bounty Hunter of the Sigmas and east Omicrons, having killed many notorious criminals. He was likely ambushed by local pirates, seeking revenge for one of their downed friends. The Gambler's left wing was crippled, inflicting critical damage on the ship's maneuverability systems. Resourceful and experienced, Friedrich made a run for the nearby gas pockets. While he managed to shake off the pursuers, the ship was too damaged to survive the violent explosions. The ship was lost along with all the valuables collected across this Hunter's envious career.

40096.text:
>>>WARNING: SEVERE DANGER<<<
A field of highly radioactive dust surrounding the Brown Dwarf in the Copernicus system. The field likely formed from surrounding dust particles attracted by the star's gravity over time. Avoid the belt at all costs.

40101.text:
Gambit's Fortune, an unaffiliated smuggling vessel belonging to an illustrious pilot named Maria Castillo, met its somber fate when it inadvertently triggered a high-yield mine during its final leg. The detonation was caused by her own blundered move of ramming a Defender belonging to the Liberty Navy that had caught up finally. This desperate attempt ricocheted both ships off-course, resulting in heavy structural damage to the fighter and an abrupt catastrophic retirement of the freighter's pilot.

Castillo's decision to navigate the perilous mine-ridden system was driven by the irresistible allure of wealth concealed within her enigmatic cargo. This pilot's departure from life is a little-known rumor among the smugglers as no source has published the loss of this particular runner. The R1 "Draugr" Edge Worlds Freighter remains a dormant reminder of the dangers that await any careless soul in Alaska.

40103.text:
The torn wreck of a BDR-337 "Defender" nicknamed "Sentinel" was once piloted by a senior Liberty Navy pilot Dante Chapman who chased the dubious Gambit's Fortune.

As the pursuit of Gambit's Fortune unfolded in the hazardous mine corridor, Chapman's focus was primarily on closing the gap and ensuring the capture of the elusive vessel. Despite being a capable pilot, Dante was caught off-guard by Maria Castillo's desperate bid to evade her capture. The sudden maneuver of the audacious captain sheared parts of the Guardian off, shutting most functions of the fighter craft offline.

Sentinel's cockpit was vacant with a blown-out missing canopy, indicating that the pilot had ejected during or after the ram. The fate of Dante remains unknown, presumed retrieval and hospitalization.

40110.text: Wichter is ALG's headquarters. It wasn't planned that way, but management had to move here when we blew up Dortmund at the start of the civil war. So if things seem a little chaotic around here, that's why - the station had to be urgently expanded to hold more administrative offices, and also some of Dortmund's smelting equipment, the stuff we managed to save before we scuttled the place. It's been a few years now, but we're still catching up on re-organizing.

40111.text: This is primarily a ship-building station. We build mostly fighters and cargo ships for our own use and to sell commercially. Because we're so far from Rheinland's eyes, we can sell to some of the organizations that aren't welcome in the house, especially the Bundschuh. One design that we practically never sell outside the company though is the HWDU-430, the "Golem". It's a heavy transport specially designed for hazardous materials, and its design specifications are top secret. Don't bother asking for one if you aren't an employee.

40112.text: You might be wondering why there's so many combat ships and personnel stationed here. Well, when we lost Dortmund and Wuppertal in the civil war, this was our last holdout around Rheinland. So if Wichter had fallen, it would have been the end for ALG. Things are quieter now, the war's over, and we got Wuppertal back. But we're definitely not letting our guard down - you never know when the Unioners or the Corsairs decide to attack, and Rheinland sure isn't going to be sending ships this far out to assist us. We have to rely on ourselves out here.

40113.text: Not impressed by the food and drinks selection here, huh? That's the price you pay for building a secluded station away from the trade networks of the house. Our supply situation is a lot trickier out here, since not that many suppliers are willing to leave the lanes for a low-profit food or consumer goods run. We get most of our stuff from the Freeport, the Zoners are used to supplying off-the-grid places like this.

40114.text: I make regular runs here from our stations in the Crow, we sell H-fuel and buy ship hull panels. It's usually a quiet trip, although sometimes Kruger will harass us if they think they can get away with it. But if the Guild and ALG blow up a Kruger ship deep in the clouds, who's going to report it?

40115.text: ALG is the only company in Rheinland the Gas Miners Guild has good relations with. The 80-years-war might have been a long time ago, but if there was any hope of normalizing relations with Rheinland, the Sigma war put an end to that. They will never accept that the Crow's resources belong to us. But we do not care for their ambitions, we have already proven that to them twice.

40116.text: This is an important station for us, since they have the facilities and personnel to service our larger ships. We can work on our snubcraft well enough at our bases, but if our transports or gunships need repairs, we bring them to Wichter. The police isn't paid well enough to patrol this far out, so ALG doesn't have to worry about getting in trouble for letting us dock.

40117.text: ALG isn't like the other big Rheinland corps. They believe in democracy in Rheinland, and were willing to go to war for it. Our ships fought the monarchists side-by-side in the civil war, and our pilots celebrated victories and lamented our losses together. The new government might be more democratic than what the monarchists wanted, but we are in no way willing to accept their rule, and it doesn't seem like ALG will be regaining their good standing either. Maybe we will end up fighting together again.

40119.text: The wreckage of the Wolf, a Hessian Odin. At first glance, the ship appears to have suffered no direct damage. Upon further inspection, however, the ship's engine is completely disabled, likely due to an electrical failure due to the radiation emitting from the system's Neutron Star. It is possible the engine was already damaged as a result of a skirmish with the Corsairs. The pilot's fate is unknown.

40121.text:
The BES Barrhead was the lead vessel of an infamous Borderworlds Exports expedition, launched to chart the depths of the Barrier in 487 AS. The expedition was organised, funded and led by a famous bretonian explorer, Lord Finnley Palmer. While nominally tasked with charting the ice nebula, its primary objective was a strong gravitational anomaly detected in the stellar vicinity of the Magellan system. After departing Gough Station and diving into the icy depths, the expedition was never heard from again, and the anomaly would vanish soon afterwards.

The Barrhead, under the command of Lord Palmer himself, served as the lead ship and nerve center of the expedition. Equipped with powerful scanners and a reinforced hull, Palmer’s ship was outfitted specifically for close up study of dangerous phenomena and hazardous locations. It appears that the preparations were for naught, as the Barrhead now floats dead at the heart of an uncharted nebula, everything except the ship’s blackbox fried by an electromagnetic blast. The bodies of the crew, including Lord Palmer himself, are still onboard.

According to the ship’s blackbox, the expedition would arrive at the anomaly after a few weeks of navigating the murky depths of the Barrier. Their objective turned out to be a stable jump hole, and the expedition would proceed through to explore the uncharted system on the other side. Upon arrival, the expedition found itself on the edge of a small nebula emitting anomalous readings. The BES Lugton, equipped with the most powerful sensor suite among the expedition, would perform a sweep of the system, detecting numerous anomalies throughout, though these appear absent from the Barrhead’s logs.

Lord Palmer would dispatch each of the other ships to survey a different anomaly while the Barrhead moved deeper into the cloud, seeking out the source of the readings. The final entry in the log describes the approach to an electromagnetic anomaly. Any further data has been corrupted beyond use.

A part of an unknown broadcast can be picked up on the ship's readings. Commencing the log...

...20000...(unintelligible signals)...Robert Carver, captain of BES Wrexham. We are members of the grand mapping project organized by the great explorer Lord Finnley Palmer, traveling together with BES Scott. The future of our mission now lies in uncertain hands, and I fear there is a strong possibility we may not return. In such a case, may this log enlighten future pioneers as to the circumstances of our demise. We began our journey into the Barrier in March 487, and within weeks, had located a wormhole anomaly. It took us to this unknown system, but destabilized shortly after, leaving us here to continue the effort with but the faintest hope for return. The system has a beauty to its oddness, and...

40123.text:
The hulk of the Caracal, a modified B1 interceptor that took part in the infamous Palmer Expedition. The ship was assigned to the BES Uplawmoor, an expeditionary Clydesdale modified to carry a B1 inside its cargo bay. The ship itself is also heavily modified, ditching most of its armaments in favour of vastly expanded fuel tanks and sensor suite. The vessel’s assigned pilot was Jake O’Regan, a BMM surveyor with experience among the icy depths of the Barrier.

The onboard logs indicate that the Caracal was dispatched in search for the BES Barrhead, the lead vessel of the expedition, after all communications with the ship suddenly ceased. It appears the Caracal never reached its target, the ship’s internal components having suffered a powerful EMP blast. The vessel, besides the age, appears relatively intact, the pilot’s remains still present inside the cockpit.

40125.text:
The BES Neilston was the second ship of the infamous Palmer Expedition of 487 AS. Organised by Lord Finnley Palmer, a famous explorer and a Bowex executive, the expedition set out to study a gravitational anomaly in the stellar vicinity of the Magellan system, never to be heard from again.

The Neilston, alongside its sister ships BES Shillford and BES Uplawmoor, was an experimental design, with most of its cargo hold converted into a docking bay for a single modified B1 interceptor. These specially modified fighters sacrificed weaponry and armour for an increased range and expanded sensors, allowing the expedition to cover more ground.

The ship’s commander was Doctor Lewis Moore, an old friend of Palmer and the expedition’s chief engineer, responsible for the modifications to both the Clydesdales and their B1 scouts. While not much of an explorer himself, Moore’s intimate knowledge of the expeditionary ships made him an invaluable asset in the unknown. Sadly, in the end, it does not appear that his knowledge was of much use.

According to Neilston’s onboard logs, Moore, in command of the expedition after the Barrhead was lost, decided to carry on with Palmer’s original plan. According to the sensor scans performed by the BES Lugton, the uncharted system was host to a potentially habitable planet. Before the Barrhead’s disappearance, the Neilston was assigned the task of surveying said planet. The ship’s journey across the system was uneventful, however, upon arrival, the ship’s sensors picked up a garbled signal coming from the planet’s surface. While mostly unintelligible, there was a possibility it was a distress call from another expedition vessel. As such, the Neilston’s scout ship was dispatched for an atmospheric fly-by. The signal turned out to be nothing more than an echo, and the scout returned to the Neilston empty handed.

The next entry in the log was made soon after, as the crew observed strange, fungal growth appearing on the B1’s hull. The next, and final, two log entries are filled with meaningless ramblings. The exact fate of the crew is unknown, though scans indicate a mass of unidentified organic matter permeating both ships.

A part of an unknown broadcast can be picked up on the ship's readings. Commencing the log...

...0...(unintelligible signals)...acquired a feel for the system, which features unusual sights that helped stave off the boredom of long travel. 40127.text: Wreck of BES Neilston's escort attached to the ship.

40129.text:
The BES Shillford was the third ship of the infamous Palmer Expedition of 487 AS. Organised by Lord Finnley Palmer, a famous explorer and a Bowex executive, the expedition set out to study a gravitational anomaly in the stellar vicinity of the Magellan system, never to be heard from again.

The Shillford, alongside its sister ships BES Neilston and BES Uplawmoor, was an experimental design, with most of its cargo hold converted into a docking bay for a single modified B1 interceptor. These specially modified fighters sacrificed weaponry and armour for an increased range and expanded sensors, allowing the expedition to cover more ground.

The ship’s captain was Doctor Agnes Parry, at the time a well known astrophysicist from Cambridge. She was one of Bretonia’s leading experts in the field of Jump Hole research, and was recruited by Lord Palmer for her expertise. As Palmer’s ship was preparing to descend into a mysterious nebula, Parry and her crew were assigned to study a gravitational anomaly detected by BES Lugton’s sensor sweep.

The Shillford, or what’s left of it, appears to have been violently ripped apart by a strong gravitational force, the ship’s remains still orbiting the collapsed jumphole nearby. However, scans indicate that its assigned B1, the Bobcat, is not among the debris.

According to the ship’s logs, the Shillford reached its assigned anomaly without significant trouble, although one entry notes a sharp drop of crew morale upon the news of the Barrhead’s demise. Logs indicate that the anomaly turned out to be an unstable Jump Hole in the process of collapse, and the Shillford would spend the next few hours studying it up close. The final entry indicates the crew observed unusual shifts in the Jump Hole’s phase alignment. Given the state of the ship, and the fully collapsed Jump Hole it orbits, it is likely the ship was destroyed when the anomaly it was studying suffered a sudden and violent collapse.

A part of an unknown broadcast can be picked up on the ship's readings. Commencing the log...

...20000...(unintelligible signals)...Blasted cloud! We have taken heavy damage to the engines, and Scott was hit even worse. Thankfully, we were able to evacuate their crew in time. It is difficult to say what is causing these dangerous energy fluctuations, as our scanners are no longer producing reliable readouts. We have dropped some emergency beacons for the unlikely chance that some other might find themselves here. This may be crucial, as for all our hardships, we have found something which could be of immense importance: A spherical object the size of a man's head, emitting dangerous energy signatures. It appears artificially made, and we have managed to suspend it in a containment field in the hold - not before junior officer Kimbley received a bad radiation burn to her hand from it....

40131.text:
Scans indicate that this vessel is most likely the Bobcat, a modified B1 interceptor that took part in the infamous Palmer Expedition. The ship was assigned to the BES Shillford, an expeditionary Clydesdale modified to carry a B1 inside its cargo bay. The ship itself is also heavily modified, ditching most of its armaments in favour of vastly expanded fuel tanks and sensor suite. The vessel’s assigned pilot was Vanessa Gallagher, a veteran Police Authority pilot.

According to the ship’s logs, the Bobcat was docked with the BES Shillford during the crew’s study of a gravitational anomaly. The ship’s pilot was passing time performing checks on the Bobcat when an unknown force tore the Shillford into pieces. The small and sturdy interceptor was ripped out of its berth and flung across the system, Gallagher herself knocked out in the process. When she came to her senses, she would find herself alone in the depths of the uncharted system. The accident damaged one of her ship’s oxygen tanks, the other slowly running dry at this point. Gallagher recalled the BES Neilston’s assignment of studying a possibly habitable world and, with no other options, made a gamble, heading for the nearest planet in the hopes of receiving help from the Neilston and its crew. Sadly, the gamble did not pay off, and the Bobcat’s life support failed shortly after its arrival at the desolate world it now orbits.

40133.text:
>>>WARNING: EXTREME DANGER<<<
A specific composite of nebulae filled with elongated asteroids. Charting reports from an unnamed Rogue warns any pilot from entering the cloud as it's been described as "blackout area." Light from the Brown Dwarf enters the cloud and dissipates as it bounces around the asteroids, leaving behind a dark and dangerous navigational nightmare. Among the light rays that disappear, a couple of electronic signals are recorded, though positional details within the cloud are scrambled. Two words are appended to the end of the charting report: Slow down.

40138.text:
CONSUMER GOODS

Once the basic necessities of survival have been met, most human beings look for ways to improve their life or to entertain themselves along the way. Consumer Goods satisfy these needs and include a broad range of relatively inexpensive bulk items such as clothing, toiletries, housewares, and Consumer Optronics. While most Consumer Goods are mass produced in automated factories, the ongoing rise in the prison population within the colonies has yielded a cheap labor force that many governments have turned to for handmade goods. On close inspection, scanner spectrometry readings indicate the presence of contraband Alien Artifacts concealed within this cargo.
