40142.text:
The BES Uplawmoor was the fourth ship of the infamous Palmer Expedition of 487 AS. Organised by Lord Finnley Palmer, a famous explorer and a Bowex executive, the expedition set out to study a gravitational anomaly in the stellar vicinity of the Magellan system, never to be heard from again.

The Uplawmoor, alongside its sister ships BES Neilston and BES Shillford, was an experimental design, with most of its cargo hold converted into a docking bay for a single modified B1 interceptor. These specially modified fighters sacrificed weaponry and armour for an increased range and expanded sensors, allowing the expedition to cover more ground.

The ship’s captain was Doctor Jamie Dunn, a geologist from New London and BMM’s representative on the expedition. He and his crew were tasked with gathering and cataloguing mineral samples, to be studied and evaluated for exploitation by BMM. The Uplawmoor itself was also equipped for the task, as was its assigned B1, the Caracal, both vessels outfitted with mining and survey equipment.

The vessel appears mangled from an impact, most likely having struck an unexpected asteroid on its way through the field. The collision crushed the cockpit and crew quarters nearly instantly, leaving no chance for the crew to survive. The ship’s assigned B1 scout, the Caracal, is absent from the cracked cargo bay.

According to the onboard logs, before Lord Palmer’s flagship, the BES Barrhead, descended into the depths of an unknown nebula, the BES Lugton performed a sensor sweep of the system. Among various other anomalies, a dense asteroid field with hints of mineral resources was detected by the sweep, with the Uplawmoor tasked with exploring the field once the Barrhead returned. However, as the Barrhead fell silent, the Uplawmoor’s scout pilot volunteered to search for the missing vessel. Hours passed, and as it became clear the scout was not making it back either, the expedition’s new leader, Doctor Moore, ordered the remaining vessels to carry on with their assigned tasks.

The Uplawmoor would then make its way to the asteroid field, slipping between the dense rocks in search of any potential resource deposits. The logs indicate that the search was rather unsuccessful, only trace amounts of valuable minerals permeating the field. The entries cut off abruptly, the last one referencing irregularities in the port engine’s fusion chamber.

A part of an unknown broadcast can be picked up on the ship's readings. Commencing the log...

...face the southeast and fly directly...(unintelligible signals)...if I fall to madness, let it be known for posterity that Kimbley was the cause of it. She speaks incessantly of the artifact, and our need to understand it. Engine repairs are progressing slowly. With the Scott's crew on board, we are desperately overcrowded, and disputes are becoming more frequent...

40144.text:
The BES Lugton was the fifth ship of the infamous Palmer Expedition of 487 AS. Organised by Lord Finnley Palmer, a famous explorer and a Bowex executive, the expedition set out to study a gravitational anomaly in the stellar vicinity of the Magellan system, never to be heard from again.

The Lugton was the expedition’s designated watchtower, with powerful long range sensors and communications equipment, allowing the vessel to perform broad system sweeps and serve as a relay for other members of the expedition.

The ship’s captain was Millie Campbell, a self made expert in stellar astronomy and an associate of Palmer’s. Campbell worked as an advisor for Ageira Technologies, helping them adapt Jump Gate and Trade Lane communication protocols for the conditions within the Barrier.

The ship’s outer hull appears to be charred and burned, both inside and out. Given its general proximity to the unstable star nearby, it is likely the vessel was struck by a solar flare while attempting to reach a small planet.

According to the vessel’s blackbox, the Lugton performed a sensor sweep of the system shortly after the expedition’s arrival, using its powerful suite to locate potential points of interest. In addition to hints of rich ore veins and a habitable planet, the Lugton also detected a small, charred world in close proximity to one of the system’s suns. The world gave off strange, anomalous readings, almost consistent with artificial signals. Before Lord Palmer and his crew moved to explore the strange nebula they arrived in, the Lugton would be assigned to study the strange world.

With the Barrhead and the Caracal lost, the expedition’s second in command would dispatch the remaining ships to their assigned objectives. The Lugton would head for the anomalous planet, at first maintaining contact with other expeditionary vessels. As the ship neared the star and its objective, one by one, the ships would fall silent. First Uplawmoor, then Shillford, then finally Neilston. The Lugton’s crew chalked it up to solar interference, their suspicions confirmed during a lull in the star’s activity, when the Neilston reestablished communications.

A part of an unknown broadcast can be picked up on the ship's readings. Commencing the log...

...between the eyes...(unintelligible signals)...the crew have suggested that we must use the clearly immense power of the strange artifact to overcome our inevitable fuel shortage. Food is running low as well, and engineer Grosham of the Scott has passed, a victim of an injury sustained in the ship's initial calamity...

40146.text:
The wreck of the BES Scott, the sixth vessel of the Palmer expedition and the expedition’s designated supply vessel. A standard, relatively unmodified Clydesdale, it was carrying much of the food, oxygen and water that the ships’ collective crews needed to survive. The vessel was captained by Sir Geoffrey Holmes, an experienced explorer known for his work in charting the Taus, brought on as a liaison for the expedition.

The vessel’s role in supply was short-lived, however. Once the anomaly they had entered through collapsed behind them, it rapidly became clear that the expedition would need to find their own way out. It was rapidly deduced that their best chance of finding an exit would be to split up to cover more of the system, and thus each ship would need their portion of the supplies held aboard the Scott. Cargo was stored wherever it would fit, in corridors, in vacant bunks, until practically every spare inch of every vessel was brimming with as many supplies as they could carry for their respective voyages.

The Scott shortly thereafter set to work much like its sister vessels. It was to coordinate alongside the expedition’s medical ship, the Wrexham, surveying a large dark matter storm. Just a few hours after being engulfed by the cloud however, a powerful shockwave of unknown origin struck the Scott, rending a tear in the ship’s outer hull and leaving fractures in the inner hull of the cargo hold and engineering sections, injuring several crew members in the process.

With engines failing and many of the ship’s systems shut down and refusing to reboot, an evacuation was ordered to bring the entire ship’s crew aboard the Wrexham, which was damaged but not crippled by the same blast, before the ship either suffered further damage from the storm or broke apart of its own volition. The last recording of the black box notes the evactuation of all crew and shut down of all essential systems.

The ship today stands much as it was left, with a cracked outer hull, though atmosphere in the cargo hold has long since completely vented. Its remaining cargo sits perfectly preserved in vacuum, while its corridors remain pressurised due to emergency doors sealing them off.

A part of an unknown broadcast can be picked up on the ship's readings. Commencing the log...

...follow the beacons and keep going forward...(unintelligible signals)...dreadful reality is sinking in, as with our supply situation being what it is, we have eaten engineer Grosham. The artifact in the hold draws our attention evermore. It beckons, and the crews have taken to offering prayer towards it...

40148.text:
Through markings on the hull, it can be made out that this vessel is the BES Wrexham, the assigned medical ship of the Palmer expedition. The vessel’s engines and fuel tanks appear to have been cracked by an external force of some kind, however its hull remains otherwise structurally sound even today. The vessel’s logs, and thus any detail of its activities, have been deliberately wiped from the ship’s black box, manually replaced by runes and symbols of unknown origin. Scans of the vessel reveal the bodies of most of its crew and personnel in the ship’s medical bay, situated in what would be the cargo hold of other Clydesdales. Many of the fallen seem to have been involved in a physical struggle, suffering unspeakable wounds from both bare hands and weapons improvised from whatever they could grab a hold of. A portion of the reading can be picked up, broadcast from the ship on repeat. Commencing the log...

(Unknown System - Day 13 log)

If I fall to madness, let it be known for posterity that Kimbley was the cause of it. She speaks incessantly of the artifact, and our need to understand it. Engine repairs are progressing slowly. With the Scott's crew on board, we are desperately overcrowded, and disputes are becoming more frequent.

(Unknown System - Day 15 log)

Some of the crew have suggested that we must use the clearly immense power of the strange artifact to overcome our inevitable fuel shortage. Food is running low as well, and engineer Grosham of the Scott has passed, a victim of an injury sustained in the ship's initial calamity.

(Unknown System - Day 18 log)

Dreadful reality is sinking in, as with our supply situation being what it is, we have eaten engineer Grosham. The artifact in the hold draws our attention evermore. It beckons, and the crews have taken to offering prayer towards it.

(Unknown System - Day 21 log)

Like a watchful eye, the dark crystal observes our progress. We are grateful for its guidance, as we can detect the edge of the storm. Kimbley is speaking a tongue we do not yet comprehend - she is closest to the artifact. We have eaten the Scott's captain, Holly Forsythe. May her nourishment sustain us throughout this ordeal.

(Unknown System - Day unknown)

Candles are lit at the altar of the Eye. What oxygen we have, is best used to satisfy it. Unsure how many remain. I do not enter their rooms. We are blessed eternally by its gaze.

40150.text:
The wreck of the Jaguar, a modified B1 interceptor that took part in the infamous Palmer Expedition. The ship was assigned to the BES Wrexham, an expeditionary Clydesdale modified to carry a B1 inside its cargo bay. The ship itself is also heavily modified, ditching most of its armaments in favour of vastly expanded fuel tanks and sensor suite. The vessel’s assigned pilot was John Walker, an experienced Police Authority pilot. The ship sustained critical damage to its electronics systems and has been left stranded on the verge of this dark matter cloud. A reading can be picked up by a nearby source, commencing the log...

(Unknown System - Day 1 log)

This is Robert Carver, captain of BES Wrexham. We are members of the grand mapping project organized by the great explorer Lord Finnley Palmer, traveling together with BES Scott. The future of our mission now lies in uncertain hands, and I fear there is a strong possibility we may not return. In such a case, may this log enlighten future pioneers as to the circumstances of our demise. We began our journey into the Barrier in March 487, and within weeks, had located a wormhole anomaly. It took us to this unknown system, but destabilized shortly after, leaving us here to continue the effort with but the faintest hope for return. The system has a beauty to its oddness, and we shall fulfill our mission dutifully.

(Unknown System - Day 9 log)

We have acquired a feel for the system, which features unusual sights that helped stave off the boredom of long travel. We have made mark of a great blue gas giant, which features a moon covered in liquid water. A bright patch in an otherwise dark system, and fate. Continuing, we have picked up a peculiar gravitational source which emanates from a cloud of dark matter. Risky though it may be, we have little to lose.

(Unknown System - Day 11 log)

Blasted cloud! We have taken heavy damage to the engines, and Scott was hit even worse. Thankfully, we were able to evacuate their crew in time. It is difficult to say what is causing these dangerous energy fluctuations, as our scanners are no longer producing reliable readouts. We have dropped some emergency beacons for the unlikely chance that some other might find themselves here. This may be crucial, as for all our hardships, we have found something which could be of immense importance: A spherical object the size of a man's head, emitting dangerous energy signatures. It appears artificially made, and we have managed to suspend it in a containment field in the hold - not before junior officer Kimbley received a bad radiation burn to her hand from it.

40152.text:
DIAMETER: 30,212 km
MASS: 4.64 x 10e24 kg
TERRAIN: N/A
TEMPERATURE: N/A
ESCAPE VELOCITY: N/A

A beautiful gas giant and the largest planetary body in the system, this planet’s extreme wind speeds, measured in the tens of thousands of kilometers-per-hour, make it impossible for any scans to penetrate particularly far into its atmosphere. What is clear, however, is that the entirety of the planet’s atmosphere is ionically charged and capable of conducting vast amounts of energy, causing the entire planet to seemingly glow. Any attempt to draw close or enter the atmosphere would result in the immediate destruction of any modern Sirian vessel. Bretonian vessel BES Barrhead, responsible for discovering the planet, did not rule out a potential artificial source of the energy causing the glow.

40154.text:
DIAMETER: 12,841 km
MASS: 9.12 x 10e23 kg
TERRAIN: Ocean
TEMPERATURE: N/A
ESCAPE VELOCITY: N/A

Situated far from what the Bretonian vessel BES Barrhead termed the system’s two solar ‘eyes’, Planet Faraday is an ocean world by technicality with seas of cold liquid methane. Due to Hawking’s immense gravity, however, the deepest point so far measured is only two kilometers in depth, with an existent but thin methane-based atmosphere extending only a few kilometers more above the ocean’s surface. The world’s orbit of Planet Hawking is notably long, with an estimated orbital cycle of nine years, and while the system’s yellow dwarf does not provide a great deal of warmth to the world, its light ensures that the world’s period of ambient darkness lasts for only an hour before the twin sunrise illuminates the surface once more. Further information on the composition of the planet’s crust, core, or how it came to orbit Hawking, is not known.

40156.text:
DIAMETER: 9,515 km
MASS: 8.77 x 10e23 kg
TERRAIN: Barren
TEMPERATURE: -83 degrees C to -123 degrees C
ESCAPE VELOCITY: 15.47 km/s

A small, but very dense metallic world with a surface consisting primarily of iron and nickel, Planet Shackleton is entirely barren, lacking even in volcanic activity. Despite this however, the world’s surface is highly rich in elemental minerals, perfectly preserved by a relatively thick inert argon atmosphere. Nothing is known about what lies below the planet’s surface due to the strong magnetic field and hard outer crust of the world. In its orbit, however, an unknown structure looms. Preliminary scans seem to indicate that it maintains a form of an artificial jump hole, however the technology it uses to do so is entirely unknown to human science.

40158.text:
DIAMETER: 14,236 km
MASS: 7.66 x 10e24 kg
TERRAIN: Volcanic
TEMPERATURE: 64 degrees C to 112 degrees C
ESCAPE VELOCITY: 15.92 km/s

Planet Maxwell is a very young, tectonically active volcanic world and, due to this nature, it has the most detailed information available of any world in the system. The planet has an iron-nickel core and, by all means, may one day in the far future be suitable for habitation. At present, however, the surface is constantly being scarred and reformed by myriad eruptions of supervolcanoes and vast earthquakes alike. A thick, noxious smog of greenhouse gases permeate much of the lower atmosphere, illuminated and shone through solely by the glow of vast oceans of magma. Such an active planet is, of course, a veritable gold mine of resources, however even were it to be located in a part of inhabited space, the planet’s exceptionally harsh conditions would render mining operations all but impossible.

40160.text:
DIAMETER: 11,131 km
MASS: 1.20 x 10e24 kg
TERRAIN: Ice
TEMPERATURE: -9 degrees C to -84 degrees C
ESCAPE VELOCITY: 11.99 km/s

An arctic world situated deep within an ice field, Planet Fiennes was only briefly closely observed by the Bretonian expedition vessel BES Shillford. The planet has a surprisingly breathable atmosphere, although the surface would be deadly to humans through both extreme cold and high concentrations of radioactive material that also permeate throughout the wider nebula. It is unknown for certain if there is any relation to the formation of the planet and the formation of the surrounding ice field and oxygen nebula, however the planet is noted for having especially light gravity for its size at 0.4g due to its unusually fast spin rate. The cause for this rapid spin is unknown, however the planet is remarkably free of impact craters likely because of relatively few asteroids being drawn far enough into the gravity well to collide with the surface.

40162.text:
DIAMETER: 7,373 km
MASS: 9.01 x 10e21 kg
TERRAIN: Volcanic
TEMPERATURE: 64 degrees C to 459 degrees C
ESCAPE VELOCITY: N/A

A hot, molten world located in the eastern part of the system. The proximity to the system's two largest stars, coupled with its small size, indicates the planet is doomed to a violent fate as it spirals into evaporation. The Bretonian vessel BES Lugton, responsible for charting and observing the planet from up close, noted the planet as a "beautiful, yet unfortunate circumstance".

40164.text:
DIAMETER: 15,369 km
MASS: N/A
TERRAIN: Terrestrial
TEMPERATURE: N/A
ESCAPE VELOCITY: N/A

Buried deep within a calm dark matter nebula on the very edge of the system, Planet Newton is a terrestrial world orbited by the collapsed jumphole through which the fateful Bretonian expedition of years past entered. Completely engulfed by the nebula, the planet is impossible to gather detailed scans of from orbit besides basic gathering of samples from its outer atmosphere, which seems to be largely composed of nitrogen, carbon dioxide, and trace amounts of elemental oxygen. Further surveys and measurements were never undertaken by the expedition, due to the requirement for planetary landing to ignore the interference of the surrounding nebula.

40166.text:
DARK MATTER CORE

A core filled with concentrated dark matter, containing a vast amount of energy. The core exhibits high density values and appears to be unstable yet active. The method by which dark matter became ensnared inside the core, as well as how to harness its energy potential, remains beyond current human comprehension of physics. Nevertheless, such a discovery could prove revolutionary.

40168.text:
Weapon Codename: BEOWULF
A product of a small arms manufacturer in fifth century Bretonia, the Beowulf was born of a contest to develop new weaponry for the nation's Armed Forces. It is by all counts an unorthodox design, favouring raw firepower, recharge rate and short term reliability over long term endurance. The design’s tradeoffs were deemed as acceptable, however, with it being assumed that military logistics would be able to support the maintenance and replacement rate of the Beowulf in exchange for the greater offensive capability the weapon provided.

The weapon, once released to the civilian market, found a similar popularity in some circles of corporate security where similar supply and maintenance requirements could be absorbed. The design proved extremely unpopular with mercenaries and freelancers, however, many of whom preferred the greater durability of lower power weapons systems, even with the Beowulf’s advantages. Despite its success, the Armed Forces would, several decades later, list out a specification for a more durable and longer lasting replacement to cut down on logistics expenditure. As a result, the Beowulf was phased out in favour of newer replacements, with the last known example being lost by the turn of the century in 500 A.S.

This weapon, an original production from the fifth century, appears to be repairable enough with modern technology to make it operational once more. Proprietary tachyon lenses, however, are heavily worn and irreplaceable; the weapon’s accuracy is likely to have faded as a result.

40170.text: A depot which was likely voluntarily abandoned due to the hostile nature of the system. The base is dockable, though it has nothing of value otherwise.

40178.text:
TYPE: N/A
LUMINOSITY: N/A
COLOR: N/A
TEMPERATURE: N/A
MASS: 3.13 x 10e24 kg
DIAMETER: 18 km

Pulsar P-58 is a remnant of a cataclysmic stellar collapse that resulted in the system's destruction in 818 AS. This event was precipitated by the activation of an Alien Jump Gate that appears to have been triggered by local Wild forces. As a cosmic entity, P-58 is an exceptionally young neutron star. It possesses a remarkably strong magnetic field and a rapid rate of rotation, making it a valuable energy resource in an otherwise desolate and radiation-devastated system.

40180.text: Recklinghausen Base was carved into an asteroid fragment at some point following the calamity of 818 AS, during The Wild's long isolation in Omega-58. Scans indicate the base is likely acting as a modulator or convertor for power extracted from the nearby pulsar beam, then feeding this energy into the Alien Jump Gate it orbits. Recklinghausen is a critical element in the energy network the Wild rely on to survive. Accordingly, it is fiercely protected by aggressive and well-armed alien patrols.

40182.text: An inactive alien Jump Gate.

40186.text: A dormant Alien Jump Gate, being fed the power of the nearby pulsar. It is believed that these Alien Gates were originally powered by the Daam-K'Vosh energy field that blankets all of Sirius. During their extended imprisonment in Omega-58, local Wild forces appear to have intentionally sabotaged these gates to sever their connection to this field. Instead, they have been modified to create a localized system power buffer, allowing energy fed into one gate to be extracted from another.

40188.text: The Nairobi was completed in 815 AS, and was among the first Thresher class destroyers deployed by The Core. The Nairobi’s hunting pack operated throughout the deep Omegas and Omicrons, primarily carrying out smash-and-grab raids to steal valuable technology or Artifacts from the Order and Corsairs. The Core appears to have become aware of the Wild presence in Omega-58 in 818 AS, and tasked the Nairobi’s squadron with capturing hybrid technology. Their final, garbled transmission described a large formation of Rheinland battleships near an activating Alien Jump Gate. The Nairobi's hull appears to have been torn open by heavy weapons fire. There is no sign of its sister ships Kisumu or Nakuru.

40190.text: The remains of the MND agent codenamed Detzner. Detzner had been patrolling the Suhl Anomaly in early 834 AS, near Meningen Research Station. When a Jump Hole unexpectedly formed nearby and the station came under attack by the Battleship Fenrir, Detzner appears to have jumped in a desperate attempt to avoid capture. The agent was quickly intercepted by Wild forces in Omega-58, fighting to the death rather than risking capture. The Wild left the wreckage in place, apparently concluding there was nothing worth salvaging.

40192.text: The remains of the Eindringling, piloted by former Colonel Alexander von Waldstein. Von Waldstein - known as the Butcher of Shinagawa - disappeared in 800 AS, along with the rest of the Rheinland Northern Fleet. There were several sightings of the Eindringling during the Purge of Thuringia, and sporadic reports of shipping raids involving von Waldstein in the years after. The Eindringling was ultimately destroyed by the MND agent Detzner. The Wild left the wreckage in place, apparently concluding there was nothing worth salvaging.

40194.text: Despite extensive damage, this wreckage can still be identified as the missing Daumann freighter Loreley. The Loreley was presumed lost to Red Hessians in 822 AS, after vanishing somewhere between Solarius Station and Konstanz Border Station. At some point following its disappearance, the ship’s cargo hold was retrofitted with sensor and sampling equipment, while the engines were overhauled for extreme long range flights. The now ruined equipment does not match the specifications of any known model. The surviving black box data fragments indicate the ship was studying the nearby pulsar before being caught in an unexpected solar storm. The charred and unrecognizable remains of the crew can be found aboard.

40196.text: Despite extensive damage, this wreckage can still be identified as the missing Kruger mining freighter Glocke. The Glocke was last sighted in 819 AS, fleeing a raiding party of alleged Daumann mercenaries in Omega-7’s Ebersfelde Cloud. At some point following its disappearance, the ship’s cargo hold was retrofitted with sensor and sampling equipment, while the engines were overhauled for extreme long range flights. The now ruined equipment does not match the specifications of any known model. While no data can be retrieved from the ship’s black box, the hull damage pattern is consistent with Dark Matter ablation. The crew is missing.

40198.text: The Van Wolfswinkel is a new variant of the popular Humpback freighter, equipped with extensive aftermarket upgrades to all onboard systems. The vessel possessed expanded fuel cells, military-grade weapons, and much more powerful scanners than those typically found aboard civilian ships. The Van Wolfswinkel’s public flight manifest is classified, suggesting it may have been a government deep space reconnaissance vessel. It is likely the ship arrived in the system very recently and - as demonstrated by the extensive weapons damage - perished during an attack by unknown assailants. The black box and crew are both missing.

40200.text:
CLASS: Resheph
CREW: CLASSIFIED
ARMAMENT: CLASSIFIED

Upon its discovery, The Order flagged Omega-58 as a priority target, owing to its graveyard of Alien Jump Gates and intense Wild activity. Their concerns proved well founded in 818 AS, when the Wild triggered a system-wide cataclysm while attempting to reactivate one of these gates. This created a rift that dragged the gate and much of Omega-58 into the Drake System, destroying the star in the process. While the stellar collapse seemingly ended the Nomads’ aspirations in the region, the realignment of local Jump Holes in 834 AS revealed that 4 Alien Jump Gates remained, seemingly undisturbed and undamaged.

After its arrival, the Khonsu’s cutting-edge sensors recorded strange readings emanating from the space around the Alien Jump Gates, consistent with the ‘Pulse’ signal detected during the 831 AS Blackout Crisis. The cruiser remained hidden, silently observing its enemies.

Among other duties, Khonsu's sensors were tasked to conduct a long-exposure scan of Kaarst Drydock. This in-depth scan revealed a new project of the Wild's, and returned critical spectrographic data on the hybrid battleship Verthandi which the Nomad-aligned forces were nearly ready to field. With the end of her deployment at hand, the Khonsu waited for her sister ship, the Jeddah, to arrive so that she might return to Omicron Mu with the reams of data-files onboard. However, when the Jeddah finally arrived, the toll of extended deployment and consistent exposure to the Pulsar's radioactivity meant that a malfunction occurred upon the initiation of Khonsu's impulse drive: A power spike that revealed the presence of the Order Recon Cruiser to nearby Wild patrols. She was caught at last, and in a running battle with Wild forces nipping at her heels, was forced away from her sister ship and only a dive into the pulsar's jet itself finally allowed Khonsu to shake her pursuers and make it to the Omega 41 jumphole.

Order forces and their allies clashed with the Wild chasing after the ship. With Khonsu's engines critically damaged, it came down to a duel between the Order's Jeddah and the Wild's Einbeck to see who could tow the ship to damnation or salvation. In the end, the Wild prevailed, and Khonsu was dragged back into Omega-58. Khonsu's commanding officer, Captain Julie Bouchard, ensured the Order's protocols were fulfilled to the fullest able. Given the cruiser's reactors were offline, the crew resorted to placing charges, and all life and equipment onboard were snuffed out as a result.

Now Khonsu rests, a brutal totem, at Kaarst Drydock. It is unknown what plans the Wild have with her wrecked hull.

40202.text: A remote lava field in the southeast part of the system, believed to have drifted into the system from the nearby Walker Nebula. Little is known about the field's contents, as the conflict in Dresden over recent years has prevented surveys.

40204.text:

A remote lava field in the northwest part of Omicron Theta. Sensors detect a gravitational source inside the field, though nothing has been confirmed so far. Avoid at all costs.

40209.text:
>>>WARNING: RESTRICTED AREA<<<
All information concerning Sector-9 is classified by the MND and the area protected by a minefield. Any unauthorised ships approaching Sector-9 will be nullified without exception or exemption.

40211.text:
Atka Research Station was constructed by Cryer Pharmaceuticals to study the Alien Organisms found on Planet Kurile and across the mysterious Edge Nebula. Cryer was intensely interested in the commercial applications of these Organisms, with a primary focus on biomedical uses. The product of decades of research was Cryer’s landmark product: Stabiline. This synthetic replacement for the narcotic Cardamine suppresses withdrawals in addicts, providing a legal alternative that removes dependency on criminal cartels.

Stabiline was produced exclusively aboard Atka, with Cryer arguing this allowed for the rapid development of proprietary manufacturing processes without the burdens of House bureaucracy. In reality, it allowed Cryer to hide its manufacturing process and material inputs, while avoiding regulatory scrutiny. This lack of oversight led to many dark rumors about the facility, including allegations of human experimentation on captured pirates. Bounty Hunters frequently stopped at the base, and there were whispered allegations of Corsairs mercenaries being hired for security. Despite a substantial private security fleet and the protection of the nearby Gas Miner’s Guild, Atka remained a high profile target for the Outcasts.

Staff were frequently the subject of assassination attempts, while supply ships were mercilessly attacked by the Outcasts and their allies throughout the Sigmas and Kusari core space. In late 833 AS, Atka was taken by surprise as the Outcast Battlecruisers Augusta and Tercio launched a lightning raid on the facility. Facing insurmountable odds, Cryer shuttles evacuated their most valuable Scientists and research data and fled towards Honshu. Hired security brought time for the escape, but ultimately were no match for the Outcast force. Atka was viciously torn to pieces and left as a twisted ruin.

40217.text:
***GRAVITATIONAL ANOMALY DETECTED***
Magnetic and gravimetric analysis is reading a gravitational anomaly not yet seen. Due to its unpredictability it is highly dangerous to approach the rift. All ships are advised to maintain a minimum perimeter of five kilometers.

40220.text:
Wreckage of the Tiger's Solidarity, flagship of the gang of outlaws known as Tiger's Renegades. The Series C Gunship has served as the vanguard of the gang's main raiding force, spearheaded by their ruthless leader Mustafa Salihamidžić. The ship's left engine is badly damaged, suggesting it was left for dead in the heart of the gang's fortified hideout. It appears that Tiger and his crew found themselves in a skirmish nearby, seeking refuge within the hideout to regroup and plan their escape. Tiger abandoned the gunship, opting for a more agile vessel to flee the area. In their haste, they also left behind the experimental equipment piece that drew the attention of their pursuers, still mounted on the ship.

Not much is known about Mustafa Salihamidžić, though he is rumored to have been a charismatic and cold-blooded leader. Skilled enough to maintain control over his tight-knit gang and adept at garnering support from larger factions, he was the driving force behind the Renegades. The details of his path to becoming an anarcho-syndicalist remain shrouded in mystery, but it is suspected to be linked to a turbulent upbringing. As Mustafa has never been pursued or fully located, it is believed he remains at large, possibly assuming a new identity by now.

40222.text:
A smuggling freighter belonging to the gang of outlaws known as Tiger's Renegades. The freighter was caught by pilots of the Bauer-Sicherheitsagentur coming from the Cologne system.

Unprepared for combat, the freighter had no chance against the Bauer pilots. The metal grave sits silently in the Nordnebel, haunting the smugglers who continue to run routes within the cloud.

Tiger's Renegades were a small scale gang of outlaws spearheaded by their leader, Mustafa "Tiger" Salihamidžić. The group primarily operated in southern Rheinland and the Omegas, utilizing underhanded tactics such as ambush, diversion, and sabotage to engage in piracy and pillaging of commerce in the region. Their motives are not entirely clear, though they are widely regarded as an extremist anarcho-syndicalist group.

They cooperated with the farmers' movement originating in Stuttgart and a small wing of the Bundschuh aligning with their views, enjoying their logistics support in exchange for aid in space and spreading anarchy. However, the gang and the larger Rheinland factions were only loosely affiliated, as the farmers and the Bundschuh found the Tigers' modus operandi drawing too much attention too often, which likely led to the gang's demise. Tiger's Renegades are considered to have disbanded sometime in the late 8th century, just before the Nomad War, after the gang mysteriously ceased all activities. Mustafa "Tiger" Salihamidžić has never been captured or found since.

40224.text:
The remains of a Tiger's Renegades escort and a Bauer-Sicherheitsagentur agent. During a routine patrol of the perimeter of Steinfurt, two Bauer agents caught a lone fighter and chased it to the Norddrauwolke.

Unprepared for the chaos within the cloud, the pirate was able to drop a mine directly on one of the Bauer agents, killing him instantly and disabling the ship. The remaining Bauer ship bested the Renegade after a long, difficult duel. The surviving Bauer vessel fled the cloud as quickly as possible and headed back to Battleship Altenburg for emergency repairs.

A brief battle ensued, and the Renegade who originally got caught was destroyed, but not before the Bauer Agents lost one of their own. Both sides fearing heavier casualties, the battle ended with one casualty each. Only the husks of the two destroyed ships remain.

The deal went south, heavily implying the Hessians double crossed the desperate and wanted group. The pilot was executed on sight, outnumbered without a chance.

40230.text:
An escort fighter belonging to a gang of outlaws known as Tiger's Renegades. Following the retrieval of a a valuable item in the Omegas, the pilot was tasked with brokering a sale deal with the Unioners. The meeting was crashed by Bauer-Sicherheitsagentur pilots, a group of private mercenaries hired to hunt down and eradicate the Renegades following the retrieval of the weapon. The Unioners partaking in the deal appeared to have fled the scene, leaving Bengal outmanned and outgunned. The Tiger escort did their best to evade the Bauer pilots, but to no avail. Eventually, a missle from one of the Bauer security pilots landed a critical hit on the engine, disabling the ship and killing the pilot. The ship remains within the Kielfeld, reminding pirates of the risks they take daily.

Unprepared for the chaos within the cloud, the pirate was able to drop a mine directly on one of the Bauer agents, killing him instantly and disabling the ship. The remaining Bauer ship bested the Renegade after a long, difficult duel. The surviving Bauer vessel fled the cloud as quickly as possible and headed back to Battleship Altenburg for emergency repairs.

Bauer-Sicherheitsagentur, or simply Bauer, is a small private mercenary company known for undertaking various security, detective, and bounty hunting contracts across Rheinland. The group remains active, but due to its limited scale and expertise in more specialized tasks, they only accept contracts that regular bounty hunters would consider too difficult or advanced to pursue. Founded sometime in the late eighth century, its muscle is primarily composed of ex-military and bounty hunter pilots seeking more unconventional work for higher pay.

One notable contract of Bauer in recent history involved tracking down and eliminating the outlaw gang known as the Tiger's Renegades after the anarchist group acquired an experimental equipment piece. Though the identity of their employer has never been disclosed, it is likely one of the original inventors of the prototype, seeking to reclaim their weapon. Bauer successfully pursued most of the gang and dispersed the remaining members, but they have not managed to locate the prototype weapon or capture the notorious leader of the Renegades, Mustafa Salihamidžić.

40236.text:
Listen up, you dimwits. I thought I made myself clear regarding instructions on how to navigate the vault, but considering we've lost more people than we should've due to taking a wrong turn, I'll repeat it one more time. You've all been given a full set of directions with a path on how to reach the vault center. The starting point is where there's a chance to turn towards one of the lights. Don't end up like old man Charles, who took a right before even reaching the lights.

Before taking the next light it's crucial to align your ship with the plane and look directly south. If you don't follow this pattern, the chances of becoming disoriented and taking a wrong turn increase tenfold. Take it slow and steady. The radiation on the path isn't to be dismissed, but your ship will hold. The highly toxic waste we've distributed around the path will make you wish you put a bullet through your head.

Take your time; this isn't a race. If you think you're being watched or tracked, and you compromise the vault, I'll kill you myself. Mustafa out.

40238.text: Wreckage of an old Retrofit labeled Tiger's Concord, likely used as a stash by a gang of outlaws known as Tiger's Renegades. The obsolete transport has been disabled for a long time with valuable loot being hidden away in its still-compact pieces. In light of the crew's demise, the transport has been swiped clean by the crew members picking up as many valuables as they can in a rush.

40240.text:
An ALG Stork-class train that was lost in an engagement with Corsairs. The lone ship had radioed for help the moment the bandits appeared, and fortunately for its crew, a security squad happened to be on patrol relatively nearby. The Corsairs, unable to haul much of the transport's varius industrial cargo themselves in their small strike craft, were attempting to arrange its diversion to a location where they could take over the load. While talks were ongoing, the security squadron arrived, and communication turned into fighting in the confusion.

With an easy victory and rescue of their ship seeming unlikely as the fight wore on, and the transport itself taking fire, the crew decided to abandon ship, and six of the seven returned to safety in their pods with the retreating ALG force. The Corsairs had taken casualties as well and didn't risk pursuit, and the Aspern remained derelict in the field.

40242.text:
A wrecked Sunrider, flown on its last journey by ALG security pilot Marta Holek. Along with her wingmates, she had been sent to respond to a distress call by the transport Aspern. Their quick response interrupted negotiations with the Corsairs that were holding it, and the talks quickly broke down into a disorderly skirmish.

Holek was an experienced war veteran and her squadron held up well enough to evacuate the transport's crew, but not its load. As they were preparing to retreat, Marta released one last mine under fire, when her already damaged ship took a direct neutron hit to the cockpit, suffering instant decompression.

40244.text: Conejo, "Rabbit", is a disabled Centurion-class fighter. Its name comes from the quick reversal maneuvers its pilot, Rafael Soria, was best known for. Soria's band had come across the ALG transport Aspern and were attempting to arrange delivery of its cargo for their own bounty, but ALG security vessels showed up sooner than expected, and fighting broke out. The Rabbit danced across the battlefield taking unexpected shots against his less experienced opponents, but just after landing a perfect hit on their squad leader, Rafael's slide took him right into a mine he had no chance of seeing.

40246.text:
A wreckage of a Mule which telemetry data could verify with an probability of 68.5% to be a lost rumored pilot of the Jacks. A pack with a lousy reputation, who were often cornered and coerced to pay chunks of their profits to the local leading figures of Alcatraz, the place where they originally staged all their gigs from approximately two centuries ago - The last known time the Jacks have been seen since their final heist. The Great Heist of the Montserrat.

The Montserrat was back then considered a state of the art Luxury Liner of Orbital Spa and Cruise which was last seen in California on their way to the Prism Fair, a highly prestigeous exposition of Libertys scientific and cultural history, carrying high valuable items and VIPs for the elites, by the elites.

Left with frustration their leader grew ambitious and spiteful, tired from the meager leftovers they picked from the ground, he saw a chance making one big coup to grasp for power and let the other Rogues tremble in fear with one bold move, thus they stole the entire liner escort with a rumored large flight wing of Mules, heavily up armored and modified to their needs, one Mule was rumored to go into direct course and ramming into the side of Montserrat leaving a huge hull breech, where they entered the ship and seized control, murdering all, but a few lucky VIPs kept as hostages for extortion money. Instead of heading back to Alcatraz, the motley group of pirates decided to claim all the booty for themselfes and vanished with little to no trace.

Further analysis of the ship's status indicates scarred markings, from what was possibly usage of explosives, to detonate something.

The vessel was hastily refitted with equipment for deep core mining and a broken mining arm sticks out of one of the crafts points, where usually a wing would be mounted.

The ship fell victim to the volatile experiments, the Jacks attempted in order to hide away something from their greatest coup.

Scans indicate the vessel got only recently captured in the local stars gravitational well and must have been adrift for a long while. The nearby comet indicate similar markings of debris and ruptures from the assumed after-effects of the detonation.

A short message could be traced attached to the craft reading; "Snitches get stitched to a rock, blasted to bits! Atleast you make use for an great doorstopper now to our resort!"

The finding of this information matches with the rumors, that the Jacks were assumed to have taken off somewhere into the independent worlds, never to be seen again.

40248.text:
Here lies the remains of Ryan Townsen, who was an escort pilot of the infamous Allan B. Wescott, a so self absorbed Rogue, that in his pride he simply named his group the Charming Wescotts. A legend which stories were told all aboard the spelunks of Alcatraz back then, they were last seen two centuries ago, trying to hunt after a group they ridiculed as the Jackasses to collect their tax. The pilot was tracing down their clue they followed after subverting a rogue of another pack, promising him a fancy lie to believe in, of going to higher places.

The vessel appeared to be struck by a load of missiles that were launched by the fading Fat Beetle, rendering it incapicated. Leaving Ryan with a similar fate, slowly starving and fading away into the succumbing darkness.

40250.text:
Left untouched over the long time it has been around the Fremantle Wreckside, this Storage Container contains high valuable items, addressed as property of the OS&C Montserrat, a prestigeous luxury liner rumored to be stolen in a great heist by the Liberty Rogues two centuries ago. The nearby asteroid base indicates no signs of life, with only some debris left afloat into nothingness.

It is rumored that finders await a great reward by Orbital Spa and Cruise for any rock solid lead. Take note that this might be already outdated... as any searches on the Montserrat eventually were given up.

40252.text:
A heavily modified Mule, that were piloted by the Jacks, a rogue pack linked to the theft of the Montserrat. The ship drifts around Fremantle Base, an abandoned hollowed out asteroid base, which could have been one of the secret hideouts the Jacks stored their booty in.

Burnt markings, indicate the vessel was disabled by hostile fighters. A fight must have occured, leaving only a small graveyard of what could be the story of one of the greatest thefts in libertonian history.

40258.text:
Scarred to a crisp by heavy ordnances lies this old reminder of a ship. Signs of a fight occured around this Ramshackle hap-hazardly carved out asteroid, rumored to be an old pirate hidey-hole.

The pilot rumored to be one of the Charming Wescotts, their vessels must have found one of the secret loot stashes, built by the Jacks, which probably led to heavy fighting.

40262.text:
Here rests the remains of Jacob H. Lesley, more infamously known as Jack the Lesser, with his burnt out ride, that made squash out of one of his greatest rivals in his final hour, ramming his freighter into the cockpit of Wescotts Wolfhound.

Leader of the Jacks, an peculiar pack even among the Liberty Rogues, often looked down upon and exploited by other rogue packs, taking chunks of their booty leaving them with a meager profit. Jacob grew tired of this and went for a bold move in hope to gain power.

The Jacks were however quite crafty and their dirty work for other Rogues paid in great fortune of knowledge. They forged a plan and tracked down the estimated route of the Luxury Liner Montserrat, which was routed towards New York, upon passing by the Mojave the Jacks emerged from the dark side of the planet going in completely in radio silence.

Managing to steal the entire liner escort, Jack The Lesser was not sated yet, knowing best that the moment they set foot back on Alcatraz they would have been greeted by gunfire on the docks by their rivals, thus he ordered his men to take off and search a place to store their bounty with. Coming up with a plan of carving out an entire asteroid, they found in the Independent Worlds to hide away the Montserrat.

They were searching for a possible hideout for months, often pillaging to merely survive and worked with what they had with them from the theft. With their numbers diminishing it even got worse, as they took note of a S.O.S signal finding out that the Charming Wescotts were trailing them. In a final attempt of a monthly long expenditure of deep core mining they attached the ship of a traitor altogether with explosives to blow a wide opening into the hollowed out giant asteroid, to anchor the Liner inside of it... the detonation caused chunks of debris and splinters of comets to break off, one being the entrance the Fancy was attached to it, left to its fate in flames.

While they managed to set the asteroid fast adrift into the void, Wescott and his henchmen just arrived to the scene, but it was already too late. One can only figure how this final stand-off took place and how long the fighting went on leaving no witnesses, to ever unravel the secret of the Montserrat Heist, only a haunted sinister place filled with floating husks and graves was left behind, resembling what greed and pride does to a man.

Over the time the asteroid was passing through several pockets of Dark Matter Storms getting engulfed by their grasp, some chunks of them trapped by a nearby gravitational well.

40264.text:
Here lies of what could be the brutal reminder of the last battle over Montserrat between the two infamous rogue packs, the leader of the Charming Wescotts, left completely defiled in his final moment as the Mule of the Great Jackass was used in a daring attempt as a battering ram, just leaving a squash out of this self absorbed rogue who loved to pick onto their smaller ones... may this be a reminder to be wary of who you pick onto, as they eventually get back in your weakest moment.

A pilot who liked to dictate and juggle around with his own bretheren, oh the irony of how both packs shared the same fate, but resembled almost polar opposites to each other.

40266.text:
Telemetry Data verifies high probability of the lost luxury liner Hull designated as the OS&C Montserrat. A highly prestigeous back then state to the art liner, now merely moored to this eerie pirate hideout, roaming dormant almost fully unscathed...

On closer inspections various luxurious items and artifacts could be oberved roaming the dark void in this secluded field resembling an epheral beauty, just being an ugly reminder of the lives wasted in both pack leaders ambitions...

Old rumors indicate a high ransom to be earned reporting the exact location to Orbital Spa and Cruise of the Montserrat liner. This could be however already outdated, since the last contract for search and rescue operations were handed out a mere two centuries ago and OS&C eventually gave up on the vessel.

Various valuable items may include experimental technological contraptions and devices, lost cumulative knowledges of old research papers and high cultural value items and artifacts related to the history of Liberty, among many more considered luxurious items, one may find some interesting valuables when looking out with a keen eye.
