40275.text: Wreck of a rookie pilot likely losing its bearing due to the blinding lights in the ship's vicinity, causing the pilot to eject out of panic. The pilot has been labeled a "Swatter Mine enjoyer" despite it not having much application in combat.

40282.text:
CLASS: Archer
CREW: CLASSIFIED
ARMAMENT: CLASSIFIED
Tallapoosa is a more recent addition to Liberty's fleet, constructed in the aftermath of the Insurgency collapse. Serving under the Tuscaloosa battlegroup, her first task was helping Liberty establish a foothold in the Inverness system. However, upon the movement of the Tuscaloosa to Ontario, Tallapoosa was recalled to core Liberty space. Officially, she performed anti piracy duties for the LSF in Colorado and Galileo. Unofficially, Tallapoosa kept an eye on Kusari movements in Galileo throughout early 836.

When the Liberty-Kusari war began, the Navy took over operations in Galileo and Tallapoosa was once again recalled to New York. She is currently assisting Battlecruiser Chickamauga in guarding Zone-21 in the aftermath of the attack on Norfolk.

40284.text: A recently constructed cruiser from Sabah shipyard, the Pattaya's first ongoing action was supporting the Liberty battlegroup Tuscaloosa in establishing a foothold in the Inverness system. Following the withdrawal of the Tuscaloosa battlegroup in 835 AS, the Crayter Republic have been left to hold the line against "Vagrant" threats alone.

40286.text:
First of the two escort ships belonging to the BES Wrexham, part of the Bretonian expedition funded by Lord Palmer. The two B1 interceptors entered the unknown rift in close proximity to Wrexham's last location, likely indicating they were unable to return the same way or notify their parent vessel. Consequently, the two interceptors were left to their own fate in the dark and hazardous field.

Gepard 1, spearheading the path through the dense nebula, seems to have met his demise due to heavy storm damage slowly engulfing the ship. Just before the pilot collapsed, the two interceptors managed to reach something resembling a safe zone before Gepard 1 ultimately succumbed to injuries.

A transmission has been left broadcasting by the sister vessel, Gepard 2: 'May you forever rest in peace, dear brother. I don't think I have much time left, but if any human ever ventures into this hellhole and discovers my colleague, know that I have located a gravitational source resembling a planet towards the northeast part of the system. My sensors are picking up some kind of reading directly behind the object, which will be my last effort. I will fly as closely as possible to the planet to navigate between its atmosphere and the deadly radiation in its surrounding area."

40288.text:
Second of the two escort ships belonging to the BES Wrexham, part of the Bretonian expedition funded by Lord Palmer. The two B1 interceptors entered the unknown rift in close proximity to Wrexham's last location, likely indicating they were unable to return the same way or notify their parent vessel. Consequently, the two interceptors were left to their own fate in the dark and hazardous field.

Gepard 2 appears to be stranded near an unknown gravitational rift, with the pilot likely succumbing to injuries inflicted by the dark matter storm. Despite following the instructions left on Gepard 1, the efforts were sadly in vain. Strangely, however, the gravitational rift keeps the radiation at bay, meaning the ship will linger here indefinitely.

40290.text: A highly hazardous scrap field full of toxic elements and substances hidden inside the thick orange clouds of the Ostnebel. Rumors suggest it was an illegal old Imperial Stuttgart dump site, although no official records exist. Recent spikes in high radioactivity appear unrelated to the field's original purpose, leading to speculation about its weaponization for an unknown cause. Even the Junkers are hesitant to commence cleanup efforts.

40295.text:
>>>WARNING: PHOTOSENSITIVITY AREA<<<
A deadly nebula full of strong, turbulent lightning storms Photosensitive pilots are highly advised to take care when flying through it.

40297.text:
***PHOTOSENSITIVE AREA AHEAD***
Magnetic and gravimetric analysis is reading a gravitational anomaly not yet seen with high storm activity on the other side of the anomaly. Due to its unpredictability it is highly dangerous to approach the rift. All ships are advised to maintain a minimum perimeter of five kilometers. PILOTS WITH PHOTOSENSITIVITY SHOULD THINK TWICE BEFORE ENTERING.

40298.text: We're making groundbreaking progress here. We have managed to turn the excavated Weimar artifact into a weapon, mount it on our mightiest ship, and use it to destroy the infected shipyard plaguing the system. Now it's time for us scientists to do the hard work necessary for the next advancement in warfare by replicating Kolleda's assault, so that Rheinland can rise again. After a turbulent few centuries, we deserve it.

40299.text: This place has an odd, eerie feeling to it. All this talk of alien ruins is slowly getting into my head, to the point that I feel like I will go mad if I stay here much longer. The pay for us security pilots isn't too great either. I should request another transfer so I can go back to patrolling New Berlin against pirates or something.

40300.text: I hope you have the UX-009 clearance to be here. Vessels without this clearance are not allowed entry into the Unstrutt-Minesektor, including all ships not belonging to Rheinland law enforcement entities. Otherwise, I'm obligated to apprehend you for questioning, and I'm sure you wouldn't want me to interrogate you in such a dark and isolated place...

40302.text:
A wreckage of a Mule which telemetry data could verify with an probability of 68.5% to be a lost rumored pilot of the Jacks. A pack with a lousy reputation, who were often cornered and coerced to pay chunks of their profits to the local leading figures of Alcatraz, the place where they originally staged all their gigs from approximately two centuries ago - The last known time the Jacks have been seen since their final heist. The Great Heist of the Montserrat.

The Montserrat was back then considered a state of the art Luxury Liner of Orbital Spa and Cruise which was last seen in California on their way to the Prism Fair, a highly prestigeous exposition of Libertys scientific and cultural history, carrying high valuable items and VIPs for the elites, by the elites.

Left with frustration their leader grew ambitious and spiteful, tired from the meager leftovers they picked from the ground, he saw a chance making one big coup to grasp for power and let the other Rogues tremble in fear with one bold move, thus they stole the entire liner escort with a rumored large flight wing of Mules, heavily up armored and modified to their needs, one Mule was rumored to go into direct course and ramming into the side of Montserrat leaving a huge hull breech, where they entered the ship and seized control, murdering all, but a few lucky VIPs kept as hostages for extortion money. Instead of heading back to Alcatraz, the motley group of pirates decided to claim all the booty for themselfes and vanished with little to no trace.

Further analysis of the ship's status indicates scarred markings, from what was possibly usage of explosives, to detonate something.

The vessel was hastily refitted with equipment for deep core mining and a broken mining arm sticks out of one of the crafts points, where usually a wing would be mounted.

The ship fell victim to the volatile experiments, the Jacks attempted in order to hide away something from their greatest coup.

Scans indicate the vessel got only recently captured in the local stars gravitational well and must have been adrift for a long while. The nearby comet indicate similar markings of debris and ruptures from the assumed after-effects of the detonation.

A short message could be traced attached to the craft reading; "Snitches get stitched to a rock, blasted to bits! Atleast you make use for an great doorstopper now to our resort!"

The finding of this information matches with the rumors, that the Jacks were assumed to have taken off somewhere into the independent worlds, never to be seen again.

40304.text:
This wreckage of a Rogue Vessel, that has met a terrible fate, indicating no vital signs. Over the time the vessels hull simply molten away to an almost unrecognizable state, leaving only a faint jamming signal of its blackbox.

In a final attempt the pilot left an S.O.S signal. "We have been compromised, Fancy is a damn snitch, ratted us all out... Wescotts Men are already onto us, stay on guar--- static. Rendezvous at the--- static, coordinates -72275, -7000, 444..."

The vessel attempted to run away from something, but was left with its engines critically damaged, to slowly melt away in the looming dark matter storm.

40306.text:
Here lies the remains of Ryan Townsen, who was an escort pilot of the infamous Allan B. Wescott, a so self absorbed Rogue, that in his pride he simply named his group the Charming Wescotts.

A legend which stories were told all aboard the spelunks of Alcatraz back then, they were last seen two centuries ago, trying to hunt after a group they ridiculed as the Jackasses to collect their tax. The pilot was tracing down their clue they followed after subverting a rogue of another pack, promising him a fancy lie to believe in, of going to higher places.

The vessel appeared to be struck by a load of missiles that were launched by the fading Fat Beetle, rendering it incapicated. Leaving Ryan with a similar fate, slowly starving and fading away into the succumbing darkness.

40308.text:
Left untouched over the long time it has been around the Fremantle Wreckside, this Storage Container contains high valuable items, addressed as property of the OS&C Montserrat, a prestigeous luxury liner rumored to be stolen in a great heist by the Liberty Rogues two centuries ago. The nearby asteroid base indicates no signs of life, with only some debris left afloat into nothingness.

It is rumored that finders await a great reward by Orbital Spa and Cruise for any rock solid lead. Take note that this might be already outdated... as any searches on the Montserrat eventually were given up.

40312.text:
A heavily modified Mule, that were piloted by the Jacks, a rogue pack linked to the theft of the Montserrat. The ship drifts around Fremantle Base, an abandoned hollowed out asteroid base, which could have been one of the secret hideouts the Jacks stored their booty in.

Burnt markings, indicate the vessel was disabled by hostile fighters. A fight must have occured, leaving only a small graveyard of what could be the story of one of the greatest thefts in libertonian history.

40316.text:
Scarred to a crisp by heavy ordnances lies this old reminder of a ship. Signs of a fight occured around this Ramshackle hap-hazardly carved out asteroid, rumored to be an old pirate hidey-hole.

The pilot rumored to be one of the Charming Wescotts, their vessels must have found one of the secret loot stashes, built by the Jacks, which probably led to heavy fighting.

40318.text:
Here rests the remains of Jacob H. Lesley, more infamously known as Jack the Lesser, with his burnt out ride, that made squash out of one of his greatest rivals in his final hour, ramming his freighter into the cockpit of Wescotts Wolfhound.

Leader of the Jacks, an peculiar pack even among the Liberty Rogues, often looked down upon and exploited by other rogue packs, taking chunks of their booty leaving them with a meager profit. Jacob grew tired of this and went for a bold move in hope to gain power.

The Jacks were however quite crafty and their dirty work for other Rogues paid in great fortune of knowledge. They forged a plan and tracked down the estimated route of the Luxury Liner Montserrat, which was routed towards New York, upon passing by the Mojave the Jacks emerged from the dark side of the planet going in completely in radio silence.

Managing to steal the entire liner escort, Jack The Lesser was not sated yet, knowing best that the moment they set foot back on Alcatraz they would have been greeted by gunfire on the docks by their rivals, thus he ordered his men to take off and search a place to store their bounty with. Coming up with a plan of carving out an entire asteroid, they found in the Independent Worlds to hide away the Montserrat.

They were searching for a possible hideout for months, often pillaging to merely survive and worked with what they had with them from the theft. With their numbers diminishing it even got worse, as they took note of a S.O.S signal finding out that the Charming Wescotts were trailing them. In a final attempt of a monthly long expenditure of deep core mining they attached the ship of a traitor altogether with explosives to blow a wide opening into the hollowed out giant asteroid, to anchor the Liner inside of it... the detonation caused chunks of debris and splinters of comets to break off, one being the entrance the Fancy was attached to it, left to its fate in flames.

While they managed to set the asteroid fast adrift into the void, Wescott and his henchmen just arrived to the scene, but it was already too late. One can only figure how this final stand-off took place and how long the fighting went on leaving no witnesses, to ever unravel the secret of the Montserrat Heist, only a haunted sinister place filled with floating husks and graves was left behind, resembling what greed and pride does to a man.

Over the time the asteroid was passing through several pockets of Dark Matter Storms getting engulfed by their grasp, some chunks of them trapped by a nearby gravitational well.

40320.text:
Here lies of what could be the brutal reminder of the last battle over Montserrat between the two infamous rogue packs, the leader of the Charming Wescotts, left completely defiled in his final moment as the Mule of the Great Jackass was used in a daring attempt as a battering ram, just leaving a squash out of this self absorbed rogue who loved to pick onto their smaller ones... may this be a reminder to be wary of who you pick onto, as they eventually get back in your weakest moment.

A pilot who liked to dictate and juggle around with his own bretheren, oh the irony of how both packs shared the same fate, but resembled almost polar opposites to each other.

40322.text:
Telemetry Data verifies high probability of the lost luxury liner Hull designated as the OS&C Montserrat. A highly prestigeous back then state to the art liner, now merely moored to this eerie pirate hideout, roaming dormant almost fully unscathed...

On closer inspections various luxurious items and artifacts could be oberved roaming the dark void in this secluded field resembling an epheral beauty, just being an ugly reminder of the lives wasted in both pack leaders ambitions...

Old rumors indicate a high ransom to be earned reporting the exact location to Orbital Spa and Cruise of the Montserrat liner. This could be however already outdated, since the last contract for search and rescue operations were handed out a mere two centuries ago and OS&C eventually gave up on the vessel.

Various valuable items may include experimental technological contraptions and devices, lost cumulative knowledges of old research papers and high cultural value items and artifacts related to the history of Liberty, among many more considered luxurious items, one may find some interesting valuables when looking out with a keen eye.

40323.text:
A heavily modified Mule, that were piloted by the Jacks, a rogue pack linked to the theft of the Montserrat. The ship drifts around Fremantle Base, an abandoned hollowed out asteroid base, which could have been one of the secret hideouts the Jacks stored their booty in.

Burnt markings, indicate the vessel was disabled by hostile fighters. A fight must have occured, leaving only a small graveyard of what could be the story of one of the greatest thefts in libertonian history.

This mule appears to have a message appended to it. Commencing the transmission...

Listen up you jarheads. I know we're in a bit of a pickle, but we still have the Montserrat. We got no choice but to take it away far from everyone. I found just the perfect spot, do NOT share this with anyone. Uploading the coordinates now... 151288, -26026, 7896.

40325.text: The wreck of an Insurgency Fighter craft, destroyed in violent combat against the Liberty Navy. Only the battered hull of the craft remains.

40327.text: This hub connects the probes in orbit of Veracruz and gathers data for collection. DSE frequently visits the site for maintenance, to replace probes and to collect data to return to the Liberty Navy.

40329.text: As of the original vessels that were part of the Separatist rebellion in New York, this vessel has survived many battles with the Navy and other foes. As one of the most loyal crews of its origin battlegroup, it hit them hard when the ships engine got hit in the initial skirmishes. Spot repair was attempted but inevitebly futile. It was hit by one of the first salvos that would mark Marshall Station's demise.

40331.text: The remains of the transport craft Philadelphia. Originally a separatist craft, it was repurposed to support Veracruz military industry. For its last operation it attempted to desperately bring remaining ground based personnel out of the system. Its escorts perished with it when Navy reinforcements finally broke the Insurgency defenses.

40333.text: This gunboat was once a crucial part of the Separatist defense forces in Bering. Having defended Marshall station there on numerous occasions, it too defended Marshall until the end. The ship was destroyed before Marshall was, but shrapnel from the installation ripped it in half.

40335.text: The crushed remains of Kelly O'Brien's Defender craft. Having survived Alaska, Bering and the exodus to Vespucci, she met her demise defending Marshall. When the core of the installation ruptured, the already damaged craft lost steering and was pushed into one of small moons. Once a liberty hero, she was always right in the middle of any erupting conflict that involved the Separatists. The LSF investigation into her can finally be closed.

40337.text: The siege cruiser Baltimore was the last remaining ship of its class during the assault by the Navy. In a desperate attempt it came from the far side of the planet to ambush the approaching Ohio. By the time it finished the maneuver, there was not even small craft screen left and Navy bomber craft quickly picked it off. The Baltimore was one of the original ships of the Separatist rebellion and had been wanted by the Navy for many years.

40339.text: A rocky asteroid field in the south of Dublin. While trace deposits of Gold were initially surveyed in the Inishmore, they were never considered feasible for extraction, with industrial efforts focusing elsewhere in the system. Coalition, Corsair and Molly patrols are frequently sighted around the area.

40343.text: A small field of lava asteroids in the south of Dresden. Since the destruction of Leipzig Station, the field has mainly been used as a waypoint for smugglers. Hessians have been reported in the area.

40345.text: A small field of ice asteroids located in the northern part of Coronado. The ice field is reported to have unlawful activity, likely due to a gravitational source in the middle of the field.

40347.text: Construction site of the Cortez jumpgate, recently built by Deep Space Engineering, in partnership with Crayter Republic, Ageira Technologies, Liberty Navy, and the Kingdom of Bretonia.

40349.text: A minor supply point built by the Independent Miners Guild to secure easier access to the Niobium fields.

40351.text: A recently discovered large comet in the heart of Coronado. Its sharp orbit is estimated to narrowly miss planet Baja, after which the comet is expected to vanish into the Sierra Vista Nebula. Authorities on Scottsdale have a team of scientists monitoring the comet's activity.

40353.text: Remains of Ponferrada, an Outcast smuggler who was pursued and chased out of the Barrier Nebula by Crayter forces. The smuggler tried to make a run for the Caminha comet nearby, hoping to lose the attackers behind it, but its engines incinerated under enemy fire, and the ship spiraled into the comet's orbit. Having effectively killed off the ship's crew for good, the Crayter forces retreated before potential Outcast reinforcements could show up.

40355.text:
Wreck of the Hopper, a vessel belonging to Dean Hopper, an esteemed explorer. After getting rich from his exploration endeavors in the Taus, he retired early on Curacao.

However, he realized that spending the rest of his days indulging on an island was too tame an end for his energetic temperament. He decided to venture towards the edges of Coronado to rekindle his spark one last time. He likely met his demise by hitting an asteroid and becoming stranded.

It is debated whether Hopper suffocated or starved to death.

40357.text: A highly contested Beryllium field in the southeast part of Tau-23.

40359.text: A highly contested Niobium field in the west part of Tau-23.

40361.text: A Bowex supply depot in Tau-31 system part of the supply network towards the deeper Taus.

40363.text: Remains of a Rheinland Gunboat after a large battle between the Rheinland and Hessian forces.

40365.text:
>>>WARNING: SEVERE DANGER<<<
Remains of an accident known as the 'K7 Disaster', a failed experiment involving the new jump drive technology conducted by the Kusari Naval Forces and the Kusari Office of Intelligence. The cause of the disaster remains unknown. Kusari officials deny that any accident occurred, instead labeling the nebula as a waste deposit site.

40367.text:
>>>WARNING: SEVERE DANGER<<<
A collapsed jump drive breach, likely the cause of the accident known as the "R7 disaster". Energetic injection from Ichigaya Drydock and the use of Jump Drives as breach modulators has attempted to stabilize the anomaly. Exercise extreme caution.

40369.text:
The Coronado Trade Lane project was a partnership between the Crayter Republic and the Republic of Liberty, with Liberty footing much of the bill in exchange for trade concessions and future toll rights.

The project has been placed on hold after much of the critical infrastructure burned out during the Jericho Incident of 835 AS.

Interspace Commerce is currently refusing to pay Deep Space Engineering's claims for the damages, arguing the situation was not covered by their underwriting contract as an "act of god".

40371.text:
>>>WARNING: NAVIGATIONAL HAZARD<<<
A small cloud of dark matter. Scanner efficiency is greatly reduced within the cloud. Rogues and other criminals have been known to reside in the cloud and will often use it to escape pursuit by the military or Bounty Hunters after stealing cargo passing between Liberty and Kusari.

40373.text:
Remains of the Shutendoji, a Kishiro Stork-class train wrecked in the northeastern part of Galileo. The ship is stranded in a strong radiation pocket and is slowly decaying.

The Shutendoji appears to be rendered immobile, likely indicating that it was ambushed by local pirates who damaged the engines. In an attempt to flee, the Shutendoji ended up in one of the dangerous radiation pockets, which ultimately finished off the engines.

The crew on board is believed to have suffocated to death.

40375.text:
>>>WARNING: NAVIGATIONAL HAZARD<<<
A pocket of strong radiation inside the Raiden cloud, containing higher concentration of Platinum minerals than average. All ships are advised to stay away from the pockets despite their rich yield.

40386.text: Warship of the Core fleet, accompanying the Mars on its offensive campaign in Omicron Zeta.

40387.text: Warship of the Core fleet, part of the battlegroup left in Planet Gammu's perimeter to hold the line and defend the area from the upcoming Corsair strike.

40390.text: One of the recently-manufactured cruisers belonging to the Corsair armada accompanying Battlecruiser Vis in its campaign to strike Planet Gammu.

40392.text:
Built in 299 AS, the New York-Magellan Jump Gate was one of the earliest jumpgates built in Sirius. The motivation behind its construction was to create a highway between Liberty and Bretonia. It was deemed a great success by Ageira at the time, being able to hold a jumpgate reaching that far that stable.

The success was not to last, however. When an accident known as the "Badlands Disaster" struck in the jumpgate's proximity, the gate was swiftly abandoned for safety reasons. Several centuries later Liberty Navy managed to salvage the New York gate, however the Magellan gate did not share the same fate. The jumpgate has been left to evaporate and is slowly decaying.

40394.text:
>>>WARNING: NAVIGATIONAL HAZARD<<<
A field of intense radioactive particles, emitted by the Omicron Kappa star.

40396.text:
>>>WARNING: NAVIGATIONAL HAZARD<<<
A massive asteroid field engulfing Omicron Kappa. The central star emits moderate radiation that can be detected throughout the entire field. Travellers are advised to pass through Omicron Kappa as fast as possible.

40398.text: A veteran Corsair pilot, Piniones was notorious for preying on BMM near the Dublin jump hole. She finally met her demise after the BMM called in the big guns.

40401.text:
>>>WARNING: RESTRICTED AREA<<<
A recently deployed minefield around Havana Prison, serving as a highly restricted and secluded area. Intruders will be indiscriminately shot on sight.

40404.text:
>>>WARNING: NAVIGATIONAL HAZARD<<<
During the early days of colonization, the Outcasts actively explored and charted Omicron Alpha to familiarize themselves with their claimed territory. While venturing into the northeastern part of the system, they discovered an eerie purple nebula. Few dared to enter, and even fewer returned, bringing back chilling tales of unknown entities within the cloud. In response, the Outcasts immediately restricted access to the nebula until more information could be gathered.

Word spread, however, of mysterious entities resembling gods, technologically far more advanced than early humans. As superstition took hold, more people began believing these stories, eventually forming various sects. They declared the nebula Zonas Sagradas - a sacred zone - and forbade anyone but the most devoted followers from entering. Rumors say there is a particular area of the nebula serving as an Outcast burial ground.

40406.text: The Quartermaster of the Aptera Arena is a prestigious, ceremonial office, otherwise known as the Munerator of Crete. The position is typically held by a venerable warrior who has survived countless battles into their old age. The quartermaster presides over bouts and ceremonies conducted at the arena, as well as verifying the vessels of gladiators are fit to participate in combat. The quartermaster's vessel has the exclusive right to recover those pilots forced to eject during bouts, and may decide to abandon those to death who are believed to have fought without dignity or honor.

40408.text: When battles rage in the gladiator arena, many eagerly gather to spectate. Special vessels are commissioned by the Council to transport various Cretans, tourists, and others - particularly those without their own ships - to the event. For some, this is a once-in-a-lifetime experience, offering a chance to witness the spectacle of space combat after spending their entire lives on Crete. This high demand ensures these transport vessels are always in great need.

40410.text:
Manufactured on Invergordon Shipyard in 825 AS, the logistics vessel Santo Domingo is one of the many transports participating in regular Cardamine distribution throughout Sirius. The vessel has been purchased by the Outcasts in 826 AS on Cali, Tau-23.

Santo Domingo is currently moored with the Valletta Terminal, awaiting minor electronics systems repairs before departing with another Cardamine shipment.

40411.text: Please excuse me; I am still mourning my son. An ordinary Bounty Hunter from Liberty humbled him. He put too much faith in our innate abilities and the tales that we are naturally the best pilots in Sirius. Well, we are, but it's much more complicated than it appears at first glance. We seem to always know where we are and where our target or destination are, regardless of visibility or interference, but we have to know how to use this sense. My son, as you can see, couldn't harness this and allowed himself to be challenged to a deadly duel in open, unobstructed space.

40412.text: How long can our kind actually live? No one knows, not even our foremost geneticists. The fact is, our lives extend with each generation, and we already live much longer than we did a century or two ago. Nevertheless, it's quite peculiar how many of us choose premature death over dying of old age. They want everyone to remember them when they were in their prime, not helpless and on their deathbed. Premature death takes many forms -- from fighting against overwhelming odds to Morte Dormiente -- the Sleeping Death from planet Carinea.

40413.text: We are incredibly vain beings when you think about it. We're obsessed with our own perfection, from superficial aesthetic perfection to more abstract matters like spiritual perfection. Not only do we not show weaknesses, but we often don't even admit them to ourselves. That's why the Slave Rebellion happened as it did, and we almost lost everything.

40414.text: Death and the afterlife have always been integral parts of our culture and identity. Death for us, at least according to our traditions, isn't a definitive end but a form of spiritual transformation, even though currently irreversible. That's why funeral rituals are very important to us, and our burial sites are extremely sacred. Insulting our dear departed is often as serious as insulting a living family member, if not worse. They may be dead, but they are not gone.

40415.text: Have you ever seen the shrines in Santa Verna? They are masterpieces of art, a sensory experience you'll remember for the rest of your life. Master sculptor Estebano Solano, who was responsible for the decorations in the early seventh century, imprinted the philosophical wisdom of life, death, and transformation into the local stone as if guided by divine inspiration. It is truly an honor for our elites and celebrities to rest there in eternal sleep.

40416.text: That our nation is plagued by infertility? It's a two headed issue; the problem of our population growth is much more complicated. As our lives lengthen, our biological instincts change, and there's very little that can be done about that. Our families are large, larger than is common in the Colonies, but siblings can be separated by decades or entire generations. That's the price of our longevity, and the reason why, even though our population is steadily growing, we are not able to compete in numbers with the Corsairs.

40417.text: Reproductive medicine will never solve our population problems. It's a cultural matter and the pace at which we plan and live our long lives. However, I don't see this as a fundamental problem unless some of our Dons come up with some foolish idea like conquering other systems by force and numbers. Compared to our enemies, we have a unique and long-term perspective, and that should be our main advantage around which all our future plans should revolve. Memories and focus of our enemies tend to be short, after all.

40418.text: Enslave Sirius? Some of us would like to do it, but Malta can’t produce enough harvest for such aspirations. No, no, our long-term goals are influence operations aimed at the wealthy elites in the Colonies through our Cardamine. The highest echelons in Liberty are not so far from being willing to listen to our whispers -- that is, unless something goes wrong again in our distribution network, or we fail to cut Stabiline production enough.

40419.text: Malta has never been more united than it is now, especially after the Slave Rebellion reminded us of the intentions all outsiders in Sirius have towards our people. However, this does not mean our society is free of political tension. The fall of the Benitez family has created a power vacuum, which various smaller families and cartels, now free from their influence, are attempting to fill.

40420.text: Few things unsettle our people as much as the thought of being sent to the destroyer Havana for re-education as punishment. The new owners of this vessel, the De Angelis Cartel, are experts at manipulating our minds to achieve their goals. Nobody aboard Havana is subjected to physical torture, yet everyone who returns is a completely changed person. Fortunately, this punishment is exceedingly rare, reserved only for the most troublesome criminals and traitors.

40421.text: If I were to tell you what matters most to our people, the answer might surprise you -- it’s not money, power, or starships. Our families are the very purpose of our existence and the reason we do what we do. We strive to provide for our loved ones, protect them, and pass on the torch to the next generation. Entire family branches live close together, often forming villages or smaller towns. Every Outcast has a large family -- life without one is practically unimaginable, incomprehensible to us.

40422.text: Although rare, it is not impossible for a Maltese man or woman to take a outsider as a life partner. These are usually short-lived romances, more of a distraction than anything else. Even if we don't have the familial customs of the Corsairs, such affairs do not always leave foreigners unscathed -- our men are known as free-spirited heartbreakers, while our women... well, I would compare them to the wild Maltese roses: stunning, eternally youthful, but with deadly, poisonous thorns.

40423.text: The dreadnought Basilica does not belong to any specific family or cartel; it answers directly to the Council of Dons, who are also responsible for appointing her captain. Their sacred duty is to safeguard Malta from any invaders who might threaten it. Although she is unlikely to leave Omicron Alpha anytime soon, serving aboard the Basilica is an exceptionally demanding role, reserved for only the most experienced among us. The position requires an unusually high degree of discipline and responsibility, even by our standards.

40434.text:
The Advisor Nergal has been present at almost every important event in Nomad history, acting as the wise old guiding hand for the Advisors, making sure that they never stray too far from the old ways, and never forget what and who they once were.

Nergal now stands guard over the home of the Nomads as an impassable defender, to ensure that no tragedy like the end of the Nomad War ever befalls their people again.

40435.text:
People say the stars hold the stories of those who came before us. I like to think that’s true. There’s someone who guided me, someone who shaped the path I walk today. Their wisdom, their laughter - it’s etched into every choice I make, every leap into the void.

Even now, as I chart my course, I feel them here. Not as a shadow, but as a light, reminding me that no matter how far I go or what I face, I carry a part of them with me. And maybe, just maybe, one day the stars will carry my story too, for someone else to follow.

40436.text:
I haven't been flying with the Navy for long, and I'm not the most gifted of pilots, so I was surprised when I was transferred to West Point to help teach the next generation of midshipmen. I'm pretty nervous about it, actually, and I asked the Commandant why I was chosen for this position, and their response wasn't what I had expected. They looked at me for a moment, seeming to really think about how to answer, before they finally let out a gentle sigh and responded.

"Rebecca, you're here because you can teach what's important," they said, "Regardless of everything else we teach here, there is only one truly important thing that we teach, and it is the singular universal truth of war. During a war, young men and women die, and there's nothing we can do to stop that."

They turned their head away from me, looking at a collection of photographs on their wall, seeming to take in every face collected there for a very long time. "Though their deaths are tragic and regrettable, it's important to understand that those who die did so to protect others, and that to truly honor their ultimate sacrifice we must remember why."

I looked at him, my throat clenched so tightly that it was hard for me to breathe, before I finally managed to ask him. "How can we teach that, sir, it seems impossible."

His gaze returned to me, his own voice gravelly when he spoke. "If you figure it out, let me know, and you can have my job. Until then, you teach them what you can, and ensure that they do the most important thing of all."

"What’s that, sir?"

"That we never forget."

40437.text:
People say the stars hold the stories of those who came before us. I like to think that’s true. There’s someone who guided me, someone who shaped the path I walk today. Their wisdom, their laughter - it’s etched into every choice I make, every leap into the void.

Even now, as I chart my course, I feel them here. Not as a shadow, but as a light, reminding me that no matter how far I go or what I face, I carry a part of them with me. And maybe, just maybe, one day the stars will carry my story too, for someone else to follow.

40438.text:
I haven't been flying with the Navy for long, and I'm not the most gifted of pilots, so I was surprised when I was transferred to West Point to help teach the next generation of midshipmen. I'm pretty nervous about it, actually, and I asked the Commandant why I was chosen for this position, and their response wasn't what I had expected. They looked at me for a moment, seeming to really think about how to answer, before they finally let out a gentle sigh and responded.

"Rebecca, you're here because you can teach what's important," they said, "Regardless of everything else we teach here, there is only one truly important thing that we teach, and it is the singular universal truth of war. During a war, young men and women die, and there's nothing we can do to stop that."
