40446.text: A beautiful formation of ice rocks in the northern part of Newcastle. The Independent Miners Guild mines the southeast of the field, primarily for Water, Oxygen and Hydrocarbons. A recent increase in Outcast activity has led some to believe the pirate group may have a mobile base deeper into the field, though no official sources have been able to verify this.

40448.text:
CLASS: Hasta
CREW: CLASSIFIED
ARMAMENT: CLASSIFIED
The battlecruiser Bastia is among the first second-generation Hasta-class ships, launched in 825 AS. The primary enhancements over her predecessor focus on improved modularity, ensuring extended service life for these costly and resource-intensive vessels. From her inception, she has been operated by the Alborghetti Cartel -- who are known for their sizeable trade and intelligence gathering operations based in Coronado and neighboring independent worlds.

Bastia began its operations securing trade routes through the Coronado system from 826 to 830 AS, primarily conducting ambushes against any potentially hostile patrols. Following her success, the ship transitioned to disrupting Crayter Republic and IMG logistics in Tau 23 during the infamous Slave Revolt.

Not long after being refitted at Corsica in 833 AS, Bastia is currently tasked with accompanying the destroyer Ceuta in Newcastle, lending her heavier firepower to the smaller flight-deck destroyer when necessary.

40450.text:
After discovering the Nomad Minefield in the Newcastle system, the Bretonia Intelligence Service faced the daunting task of recruiting agents brave enough to explore the unknown. Puck and Duck, inseparable twin brothers, were among the first pilots to accept the mission with pride. Unfortunately, Puck’s pride was short-lived, as he collided with one of the mines on the edge of the field. He survived the initial crash and abandoned the ship before it fully broke apart.

Puck succumbed to his injuries days later. His Crusader was left behind, serving as a lasting memorial to his sacrifice.

40452.text:
After discovering the Nomad Minefield in the Newcastle system, the Bretonia Intelligence Service faced the daunting task of recruiting agents brave enough to explore the unknown. Puck and Duck, inseparable twin brothers, were among the first pilots to accept the mission with pride. During an unfortunate accident, Duck, still in shock, rescued his injured brother and flew him to the Verwood for emergency medical care. Tragically, Puck succumbed to his injuries days later.

Sometime after the accident, Duck vowed to continue their mission in his brother's honor and resumed exploring the mysterious Nomad Minefield. He ventured further than anyone before him, but just as he prepared to return and share his success, he suffered a heart attack and died instantly. His ship remains idle to this day in the endless minefield within the Craster Nebula.

40454.text: Remains of the Mindflayer, an infected Bretonian Wild vessel tasked with patrolling the Nomad minefield in Newcastle. It is believed the ship suffered an electromagnetic pulse from the nearby mines, rendering it immobile. The wreck was left to linger in Newcastle until the minefield consumes it.

40456.text: The wreckage of an allegedly defected Bretonian pilot who engaged in a battle against his own kin at the western edge of the Craster Nebula. After winning the skirmish, Soulpiercer managed to escape the area before additional hostiles arrived. However, it did not get far, as heavily damaged engines forced the pilot to stop the ship near a nearby minefield and await allied reinforcements.

40458.text: Presented are the remains of the Rabbit, a Bretonia Armed Forces ship once piloted by Grimsby McInally. The pilot, overly eager to pursue a hostile patrol, was lured deep into the western nebula of Newcastle, where he met his fate in a Molly ambush.

40460.text:
CLASS: Crecy
CREW: CLASSIFIED
ARMAMENT: CLASSIFIED
The HMS Rockhope launched in 819 AS from Southampton Shipyard during the Tau War. Deployed directly to the frontlines, first against Kusari and later against Gallia, the Rockhope saw more action than most ships in the Bretonian Royal Fleet and lived to tell the tale.

The survival, unfortunately, came at a cost. Over its decade-and-a-half service span, numerous repairs and upgrades resulted in a significant loss of power, particularly in the ship's maneuverability area. Combined with the introduction of the Agincourt model, the Rockhope had no future on the frontlines. Instead, it was repurposed as a stationary guard and control vessel, securing the entrance to the restricted Craster Nebula in the Newcastle system until its eventual replacement by one of the new Agincourts.

40462.text: Supply Depot Carham was a Bretonian Armed Forces installation built during the Gallic War as a refueling and emergency repair facility for Bretonian snubcraft, with the purpose of preventing the Gallic Royal Navy's invasion of Newcastle via the Tau-31 jump hole. Despite Bretonia's best efforts, the station was overrun and subsequently destroyed by Gallic forces.

40464.text:
DIAMETER: 6,521 km
MASS: 2.33 x 10e24 kg
TERRAIN: Ice
TEMPERATURE: -175°C to -98°C
ESCAPE VELOCITY: 6.42 km/sec

A remote, lifeless, icy planet devoid of an atmosphere. Surveys have revealed no significant gas deposits or mineral resources worth exploiting. Due to its secluded location, Bretonia previously conducted weapons experiments on the planet's surface; however, the site was abandoned when the Gallic War began.

40466.text:
Remains of the Maverick, a Bretonia Intelligence Service ship orbiting planet Warrington. Scans indicate the ship has been hit by an unknown weapon, likely during weapons testing conducted by Bretonia in the planet's vicinity.

The pilot of the vessel, their fate, and the reason why the wreck was not removed, are unknown. It is believed the accident happened around the beginning of the Gallic war, forcing Bretonia to abandon the Warrington testing area in a haste, and Maverick with it.

40468.text: A remnant of both the Tau War against Kusari and the Gallic War against the Gallic Royal Forces, Huddersfield serves as a stark display of war's lasting consequences. The area is littered with scrap, wreckage, and debris, a grim reminder of the conflicts that will take decades to fully clear. Local pirates, emboldened by the post-war devastation of Leeds, exploit the field as a haven, evading nearby lawful patrols. Trade lane attacks in the region are frequent, further complicating efforts to protect LD-14’s already isolated position.

40470.text: Similar to the Islay Ice Cloud, Coll is a beautiful cloud of ice crystals surrounding a field of ice asteroids considered one of the wonders of Sirius. It is also home to a large contingent of Outcasts, Gaian eco-terrorists, and other pirates, who frequently attack unprotected transports.

40472.text:
DIAMETER: 6,190 km
MASS: 3.12 x 10e24 kg
TERRAIN: Ice
TEMPERATURE: -186°C to -96°C
ESCAPE VELOCITY: 10.83 km/sec

An icy, remote planet in the south of Sigma-19. Lack of valuable resources, coupled with Senkaku's remote location, have left no factions interested in pursuing a mining operation on the planet's surface. The planet's gravity attracted a nearby wormhole to Sigma-13.

40474.text: A small field of rock asteroids. Rheinland authorities believe that Rogues, Xenos, and other criminals are using the asteroids as cover for their various illegal activities. Despite recent requests from Liberty, Rheinland has shown little interest in sending patrols into the field to root the pirates out.

40476.text: A small outcropping of the Barrier Nebula, rich with ice asteroids.

40478.text: A mid sized outcropping of the Barrier Nebula.

40481.text: A mysterious oddity in the heart of the Manaus nebula of Cayman discovered by a Zoner explorer Hugo Mendez. Due to the remote location of the system, there has been no notable research on the anomaly to determine its origin, danger level, or purpose. All ships are advised to keep a minimum perimeter of 700 meters from the object.

40483.text:
Originally part of the Slaugh Brigade, a recently assembled Molly formation created following the liberation of Dublin, the Donegal has been sent to Omega-49 to guard Garvagh base from a potential Corsair assault, in case the Mollys decide to get the base up and running again.

The destroyer is supporting the Ben Warner, which is serving as a staging and re-fuelling ground for Molly and Coalition snubcraft in the system, primarily fending off any Corsair reinforcements from the Omegas into Dublin, and supporting the carrier Ben Warner.

40485.text:
>>>WARNING: UNKNOWN TERRITORY<<<
A sizeable outcropping of the Walker Nebula in the southeastern region of Omega-55. It is believed the Nebula was first charted by Rheinland in 798 AS, however all records of this expedition were seemingly expunged during the Colony Wars. The Reykjavik Nebula remains shrouded in mystery and speculation.

40487.text: An outcropping of the Walker Nebula that remained after the formation of Omega-47. The nebula was first discovered by the famous Corsair explorer Carlos Fuentes after arriving from Omega-5. The swirling molten depths are frequently prowled by Corsairs, Wild and enigmatic, alien machines. No commercial surveys for resources have been conducted.

40490.text:
DIAMETER: 7,867 km
MASS: 2.31 x 10e24 kg
TERRAIN: Rocky
TEMPERATURE: -115°C to -55°C
ESCAPE VELOCITY: 8.35 km/sec

A rocky, atmosphereless planet, located on the outskirts of Omega-49, travelling along a long elliptical orbit around the system's central star. As a result, Inishsirrer spends extended periods of time isolated from any other stellar objects, apart from its own satellite.

40492.text:
DIAMETER: 4,867 km
MASS: 1.50 x 10e24 kg
TERRAIN: Rocky
TEMPERATURE: -125°C to -65°C
ESCAPE VELOCITY: 8.35 km/sec

A small rocky moon orbiting Inishsirrer on the outskirts of Omega-49. Both the moon and its parent planet follow a long elliptical orbit around the system's central star, causing the two celestial bodies to drift far from any other stellar objects for extended periods of time.

40494.text:
The CPW Astana was one of the Coalition battlecruisers involved in the battle against the HMS Stirling in 827 AS. During the Gallic War, Bretonia sought to open a new frontier in Omega-49 after establishing a connection to Poole. Aware of Bretonia's plans, the Coalition launched an ambush on the Stirling with superior force, ultimately losing the Astana in the process.

The Astana suffered a devastating blow to its engines from the Stirling, triggering an explosion that spread through the rear of the ship. However, the extent of the damage exceeded expectations, raising questions about possible negligence during the Astana's maintenance and inspection, or even the possibility of sabotage. While most of the crew managed to evacuate in time, the battlecruiser was damaged beyond repair.

40496.text: Remains of the Battle of Stirling in 827 AS, between Bretonia and the combined Coalition and Molly forces. The Stirling and the Astana, along with various debris from the battle, linger inside the field.

40498.text: Let me share something that might shift your perspective on the world. Every day, for thousands of years, there’s killing, pillaging, stealing - every kind of darkness you can imagine. It’s the same in Omicron Mu as it is in New York. I’ve seen it in all my lifetime here. And yet, I like to believe there’s hope - a future where humanity sets aside its ego-driven differences and comes together for the greater good. Maybe I’m just a naive fool or a hopeless optimist, but I’ll carry this belief with me to the grave. Be the change you want to see. Live the life you want to live, my friend.

40500.text:
>>>WARNING: NAVIGATIONAL HAZARD<<<
A fragmented, dense cluster of planetary debris on the outskirts of Omega-55. Disappearances and ferocious pirate attacks thwarted all initial surveying attempts, with most travelers now limiting their incursions to only those strictly necessary to reach Omega-41.

40502.text:
>>>WARNING: NAVIGATIONAL HAZARD<<<
The Utrecht Cloud is a beautiful, lush nebula on the outskirts of Omega-55, orbiting its two central stars. There are persistent rumors of hidden secrets and failed experiments lurking within the cloud dating back to the initial Rheinland colonization of the system. Even Bornholm's most foolhardy prospectors avoid the Utrecht.

40506.text:
>>>CAUTION<<<
One of Omega-55’s many suppressed secrets, Sektor-15 was a small experimental zone within the Reykjavik Nebula. The debris within the field is of Rheinland origin, and dates to around 800 AS. Whatever occurred here went catastrophically wrong, leaving the area a desolate wasteland.

40508.text:
>>>WARNING: UNKNOWN TERRITORY<<<
Charted in 798 AS by Rheinland explorers eager to unlock Omega-55’s mysteries, the Groningen Cloud is a small outcropping of the Walker Nebula located on the system’s outskirts. Initially overlooked during the system’s early years, Rheinland’s later attempts at a thorough exploration were thwarted by fierce resistance from the Red Hessians. With no official reports ever published, the Groningen Cloud remains one of the many mysteries of the deep Omegas.

40517.text: Rheinland was up to something out here, just before the Colony Wars started. Over the years we've lifted all kinds of weird military salvage from Rugen and Skagen's orbit, but nothing you'll find any official records about. Apparently there's even more stuff deep in the Reykjavik Nebula, but you'd be risking your skin to go looking.

40518.text: "Mad" Lehmann first drove the Bornholm out here, back when there was still a Jump Hole to Omega-11. His treasure hunters set up shop before the Corsairs or Hessians appeared -- that came later, after their war spread to Omega-47. These days, rather than shipping merch back to Rheinland, we'll sell salvage to anyone local who'll buy it. Even The Core, if the price is right. Not to mention the blood sports.

40519.text: Lehmann started out as an independent explorer, looking for lost treasures. Spending enough time in the Omegas changes a man, though. He's spilled a lot of blood to keep Bornholm going. By the time The Pit got started around 823 AS, his own brother would hardly have recognized him. He's now wanted in four of the Houses for kidnapping, piracy and murder. He's built himself a private fiefdom on the edge of a blade and has no intention of ever returning to the Houses.

40520.text: We Junkers have to stick together in an area as remote as this. Between your run-of-the-mill Corsairs and Hessians, there are far more dangerous entities out there. One of our transport convoys full of food rations got blown up by them. No negotiations, just bam. Imagine living on two cans of synth paste per day for a month. Ugh, never again.

40522.text: Artifacts? Here? No, no, amigo. There are no customers worth selling to in Omega-55. Then why are the Corsairs here? Strategic importance. This system is a direct supply route to Casablanca Base, and a part of a pincer strategy to keep the pressure on the Coalition in Omega-47. We also hear The Core have found Artifacts of their own here, and that does not sit well with us.

40524.text: Freelancer? More of a mercenary. I'm here to hunt Bounty Hunters. The Corsairs pay generously to kill the hunters specifically. Sure collecting an odd Hessian or two might help, but it's the Hunters that the Imperio wants, and that's what I came to do to secure an early retirement. I guess if there's one thing that unites the Corsairs and the Hessians, it's their hatred towards the Bounty Hunters Guild.

40525.text: I used to be a Bounty Hunter before going independent. Mercenary life was always for me, but I never cared much about the Guild. So many jobs you're not allowed to take, credits you have to leave on the table. When I heard how much the Corsairs were offering for each Bounty Hunter killed in the Omegas, I flogged my Hammerhead and purchased a new identity on Ithaca.

40526.text: Who granted you access to be here? Was it Hans? He usually checks all the newcomers to see if they're eligible to stay. You don't know Hans? Uhm... you should leave.

40527.text: The Red Hessians found this base, we didn't originally build it. The databanks were mostly scrubbed clean, but we're fairly sure this was an MND outpost that was abandoned. I think they were probably trying to trace Coalition raids back to their source, or maybe investigating this system's Rheinland wreckage.

40528.text: I'm not allowed to talk about what I'm working on, but hopefully it'll give us an edge over the Corsairs. What I really think we should be doing is studying the nearby anomaly. What is it? A collapsed wormhole? Imagine if we understood how to collapse wormholes manually. We'd seal the Corsairs away and crush the survivors in a few months.

40529.text: I have to admit something - I am feeling quite lonely here. We don't get many visitors due to the secrecy of the station, and Omega-55 is as far from home as it gets. The Hessians pay me handsomely as a researcher, and I'm no longer welcome in Rheinland academia, so here I'll stay. The Omega war has no end in sight, so I doubt things will change for the better anytime soon.

40530.text: If you asked me what my ideal destination would be, I can't say I'd ever choose Omega-55. The place is beautiful, don't get me wrong, but the beauty eventually becomes stale, and the remoteness can get to you. At least the pay is good, even for a bartender, and being on a mobile ship means we'll likely sooner or later be out of here.

40531.text: I am the main representative of the Core on this vessel. When my employer and the Bounty Hunters Guild signed the Skagen Treaty about mutual defense between the two entities, I was sent here to make sure the hunters stick to their end of the deal. So far so good - they are skillful, direct, and don't talk much. They better keep it that way, we're paying them a lot of money to help us secure Skagen.

40532.text: I'm one of the odd independent contractors who like to combine business with pleasure. My Dromedary cannot hold too much cargo, but it's perfect for supplying vessels such as the Helsingborg, and as a bonus I get to explore the beautiful spaces of the deep Omegas. My usual deliveries involve the standard stuff - food rations, water, consumer goods - which don't pay too much, yet they pay well enough due to the dangers of undertaking such a task.

40533.text: In 833 AS I almost died to mysterious Rheinland ships in the northern part of the system. Rheinland, can you believe it? Shooting an innocent independent freighter, hauling water? The only reason why I'm still here today, is that a local Bounty Hunter patrol scared them away. The hunters were outnumbering them 3:1. I guess there is power in raw numbers after all. Later on the hunters told me that they aren't ordinary Rheinlanders, but I'm sure they were kidding. What the hell is that supposed to mean?

40534.text: Welcome to the Helsingborg. Looking for work? Report to quartermaster Berg, he'll be assigning you a room to stay, contracts to do, and all the legal nonsense regarding workers rights and all. If you manage to survive while scoring a few bounties, you'll walk out a rich person. If not, you'll be dead before the New Year.

40535.text: Dagger is our only outpost in the Omegas. Managing imports and exports here is challenging, given the heavy Corsair and Red Hessian presence in surrounding systems. For basic supplies we can barter with the Zoners of Freeport 5 using intermediaries, however those goods need to be carefully checked for sabotage. More than once we've had to filter out toxins or other poisons from drinking Water after a Corsair figured out where some stored barrels were going and spiked them.

40536.text: Hey sugar, would you be so kind and fetch me a bottle of rum from the bartender? I just got back from a patrol around Skagen's perimeter. We were attacked by AI Drones from the west -- probably out of Omega-55. The AI were always pretty passive and used to run unless we cornered them. Since a swarm recaptured Gammu, they've gone berserk. Several raids a week, at least -- I've lost three wingmen. Luckily Dagger's quick-responders got to us in time and drove the AI off. I just... don't think I can take much more of this. I need a good drink to forget about it, and some good company.

40537.text: I work dig site security down on Skagen. My team is there to protect the scientists from Corsairs, Hessians... others. Not wildlife. So far as we know, Skagen is dead, completely sterile. Doesn't seem to have always been that way though. Once you scratch the surface, it's a planet-wide mass grave. I've never heard of anything like it.

40538.text: I'm currently recovering from a back injury I sustained during a skirmish with a Hessian squadron northwest of here. They ambushed us from the nebula, taking down two of my companions almost instantly. Chaos erupted, and we were scattered across the battlefield. No amount of theory can truly prepare you for the reality of combat when adrenaline takes over.

40540.text: I used to work for Kruger in Sigma-15. It's a hell of a change of pace, but Tangier isn't so bad. The volcanoes are absolutely beautiful - it's like the planet itself is happily offering its riches up to us with every eruption. The Hessians are a rough crowd, but with them and the Coalition keeping us safe, I can't think of anywhere I'd rather be working. It's good to be free.

40542.text: The Coalition commissars are strict with their own men, and keep a close eye on the few foreigners that pass through. They mostly leave us alone though, probably because we couldn't pose much of a threat to them even if we wanted to.

40544.text: Me and my crew came here from Pecos when things started getting really tense with Crayter. Out of the freezer and into the deep-fryer, huh? We need almost as much protective gear to work here as we did on that iceball, but at least there's no risk of snow-blindness.

40545.text: I came here as part of Alistair's crew from Pecos. I don't give a damn what he says, I miss the snow and ice. Thank god this coat is fire-retardant.

40546.text: It's been several years since we lost Viernheim up in orbit. I still remember the day with shame. But the Coalition have made good use of this place, and they even share its bounty with us. Together we'll push back the Corsair barbarians and show everyone once and for all who really owns the Walker.

40547.text: I'm about to go fly wingman for a Coalition patrol headed into the eastern Walker nebula. Joint patrols are uncommon, but we're after a particular Corsair that's been giving our suppliers a lot of trouble recently. Everyone with a stake in Tangier has a claim on his head, so we'll take him out together.

40548.text: The volcanic eruptions here are a sight to behold. This outpost is far enough away to be safe, but you can see the eruptions to the south. Sometimes they go on for days. That's where the richest mineral deposits are, too; I don't envy the Coalition colonists that trek out there for the mining operations.

40549.text: I'm waiting for the dockworkers to load my Dromedary with aluminum. Once they're done, it's all the way back home to Dresden, where it'll be refined into valuable alloys.

40550.text: The Hessians are an extremely militarized organization, especially on the Omega front. The Hammen Hole is no joke. But these Coalition guys take it to another level entirely. I wouldn't mess with them if I were you.

40551.text: A month ago we had a Freelancer visitor running away from the Corsairs. Apparently he assassinated the Corsair in his sleep. He fled to Tangier, thinking we'd save him. He's part of the volcanoes now.

40552.text: You didn't hear this from me; I think what we're doing here is a giant waste of resources. Sure, colonizing a planet sounds great and all, but it's not like we don't already have one in Omega-52. The costs of upkeep are taking a serious toll on us. If it were up to me I'd establish a small outpost in the orbit, and focus our funds elsewhere, such as Omega-5. I heard it's pretty rough for the Hessians there currently.

40554.text: I fled from New Berlin to join the Hessian cause, because I bought into their propaganda. Now that I've been with them for a few years, I'm not sure I want to stay here. It's two sides of the same coin, both justifying endless violence until one side gives in, which won't happen anytime soon. I think I'll join the Zoners on Gran Canaria and find a job there, at least I'll be less involved with all the endless space warfare.

40555.text: Fucking Joachim over there thinks he's so slick for finding a way to leave this life behind him. I'd take him out myself, but it would cause a diplomatic incident between us and the Independent Miners. It's cowards like him that caused us to lose Viernheim in the first place.

40556.text: Yeah, I used to be a Hessian. Why'd I give it up, you ask? Honestly, I'm not cut out for the fighting. It never sat right with me that we were killing and robbing the people we were supposedly fighting for. Normally, being a Hessian is for life and you don't get to just leave, but with how close they are with the Guild, there wasn't much my former superiors could do.

40557.text: Before the civil war in Rheinland, I ran a small business on Stuttgart with my wife. When the Imperialist riots broke out, we knew we had to escape. We sold it all at a deflated price and hitched a ride with a Guild transport. The military government here had a shocking shortage of administrative staff, so now we help coordinate supply deliveries with IMG bases elsewhere in the Omegas. I'm not actually sure we're any better off than we would have been if we'd stayed.

40558.text: The lads back at Madeira haven't found much silver or copper in this region of the Walker. Some of them have turned to buying slog -- or "carix", I guess -- from the Mollys who produce the stuff. Only a few Guildsmembers partake; most of what they buy gets smuggled into Rheinland. I don't feel so good about sellin' the shite to people down on their luck, I've heard nasty rumors about what it does. But the money's really good, and the Mollys are our friends. God knows they need the support right now.

40559.text:
We’ve had a lot of refugees pouring in lately. Between the Gallic war, our beef with Bretonia, the Rheinland civil war, and now this mess with the backstabbing Crayter "Republic," there’s no shortage of hands around here. That’s good news, though - it means we can shove more of ‘em out there to hunt for silver and whatever else might be worth something. Sometimes, you gotta toss enough bodies at a problem to get it solved. Think they all make it back? Nah, we’d risk starving the station if they did.

The Corsairs don’t know exactly where this base is, but they don’t care - they’ll slaughter any miner they catch out in the field. Honestly, I’ve started seeing it as a win-win situation. Cold? Yeah, maybe. But we’ve got way too many mouths to feed for what the station can handle right now. Guess that changes if we strike it big with a juicy deposit somewhere. Until then, it is what it is.

40560.text: You ever stop and think about how little most people know about space? Like, you’re a pilot, right? Can you guess what percentage of the Sirius population actually has a spacecraft license? It’s about 1%. Yeah, that’s right - apart from the passengers, for every pilot out there, there’s ninety nine people just chilling on planets, never actively setting foot off-world. And yet, it’s the pilots - the tiny handful of you - who end up deciding the fate of everyone else. Look at Leeds. Billions of people, a whole damn planet, wiped out because of a minority making decisions. It’s insane to think we’ve come to this point. But honestly, it’s also kinda wild to realize just how much power you’ve got. If you really want to make a difference in the world, being a pilot is hands-down the fastest, most direct way to do it.

40561.text: After the Bretonians abandoned Gran Canaria, the Corsair dogs were quick to re-populate their colonies here. I suppose they had all the infrastructure set up, and the connections with the local Zoners. Despite the recent Freeport nine tensions between the Zoners and the Corsairs, Gran Canaria Corsairs were always much closer to the Zoners than your average Corsair. It makes our task of driving them out of Omega-49 that much harder, but we're not planning on giving up.

40562.text: People from elsewhere do not know how to manage this place. The Bretonians have tried and failed, their ridiculous expedition smashed and run out, and the Coalition still try and cannot make progress. We have good arrangements with the people here, arrangements that give stability and should not be messed with. A while back, a warlord from Crete arrived, Don Paco. Fat windbag used to easy life on his estate. His people tried to break apart the trade networks so that the goods at our spaceport would be scanned by him, and delivered to him if he desired them. He was killed by a bomb on his speeder. I don't know who is responsible, but nobody misses him.

40563.text: The Corsairs and the Zoners from Gran Canaria got a long history of working together - way stronger than any crap stirring up in the western Omicrons. They get why we’re here, which is why they handed over their maps in exchange for protection in the first place. And we respect them for coming to us - it’s a win-win setup. Take El Hierro, for example. That colony is strictly for Corsairs and the most trusted Zoners. You can’t just waltz in there. Either cough up a serious fee or try sneaking in - though if you’re dumb enough to go for the latter, don’t think I won’t gut you myself.

40564.text: I hate to hear the news from the east. Nine ransacked? Open conflict between Zoners and Corsairs? It's not like that over here. We pay our tributes and the Empire protects us. We can trade food, some basic goods we make, and sometimes Molly gold. They don't run files on every person and try to control every part of our society, just simple exchanges, goods for safety. That works for us, and it works for them. Definitely much better than what you'd be agreeing to in the houses. I don't know how it could have gone so wrong over there.

40565.text: There's a new wormhole that opened up in the western nebula. The Mollys are guarding it heavily, denying the Corsairs from discovering it. You didn't hear it from me, but I got a rumor that it's somewhere in the north part of the cloud.

40566.text:
When Bretonia decided to invade, most of the Corsairs bailed ahead of time. Me? I stayed back, pretending to be a peaceful Zoner, spying for the Imperio. In my colony, we hashed out a solid plan - how to get people out, how to handle things during the occupation, and how to move back in once those Bretonian idiots were booted out.

We saw their weak attempt of a conquest coming from a mile away and figured it was smarter to get folks out rather than waste lives fighting. And guess what? We were right. The occupation didn’t last long, no damage to the colony, no lives lost. Worked out pretty damn well if you ask me.

40567.text: I get a lot of people here daily during my shift, and it's a real colorful place out here. If you're from somewhere else, you probably won't believe this, but I've seen a Corsair and a redhead girl with every indication of Molly affiliation 'bout her, talking and laughing and then getting a room together. That's not as crazy as it sounds down here on the Gran Canaria, but if you see something like that, do yourself a favor and keep it to yourself. That's not information that'll be healthy for anyone involved, if you know what I mean.

40568.text: The Athos has been through more fights than most warships ever will. But let’s be real - she’s seen better days. It’s not just the battle scars; it’s the new tech rolling out. Those Tribinus and Consul battlecruisers? They’re the real deal. If you ask me, it’s time to scrap the Athos, break her down, and use the parts to construct a few Consuls. With those monsters in the fleet, we’d own the Omegas in no time. Mark my words.

40569.text: If I had to sum up the Corsairs in one word, it’d be pragmatic. Everything we do has a clear, no-nonsense purpose. Yeah, some might call it ruthless, but look at the deals we make with our trade partners - there’s plenty of ways for both sides to benefit without spilling blood.

40570.text: The Athos is here to reinforce our position in Omega-49. I don't think she can survive a direct 1v1 against another warship of its size though, so we need to keep her hidden here, and deter any warship from charging it in open space should she be detected.

40571.text: Welcome aboard the Ben Warner. Since your docking rights have been cleared, I’ll assume you’re trustworthy enough for level 1 access around the ship. You’ll always find company in the bar—myself included. The leisure and living quarters are located toward the south of the ship, but don’t stray too far in that direction, or you might find yourself in trouble for trespassing.

40572.text: The Ben Warner is a fine warship, one of the mightiest in our fleet. What’s missing? Hunting down the Athos and starting a blockade around the Omega-5 jumphole to suffocate the Corsairs on Gran Canaria. Unfortunately, the Zoners of Omega-49 seem oddly fond of the Corsairs, so if a full-scale blockade ever happens, we’d have to inspect them as well.

40573.text: Earlier this year, I went out on a patrol to harass Corsair supply lines in the Omegas. Four of us intercepted a Correo with two Titans as wingmen - a fight that seemed favorable for us. We engaged the Correo first, assuming it would be an easy target. Unfortunately, the Correo crew pulled off a stunning maneuver, landing a direct hit with double Swatter mines that took out two of my wingmen in an instant. Stunned by their move and the shock of narrowly escaping death, my remaining wingman and I made a run for it. We lost the Titans in a nearby nebula. Luckily, they didn’t pursue us too far - I’d guess that Correo was hauling some seriously valuable cargo.

40574.text:
The Hessians and the Coalition have been working together ever since we got our higher-ups to sit down at the table and lay out just how big of a threat the Corsairs really are. Sure, the Bounty Hunters, Core, and the Houses are annoying, but the real war is here in the Omegas. This is our home, after all.

If we can sever the Corsair presence in the deep Omegas from the rest of their so-called "Empire," I believe we can start turning the tide. We've been on the back foot for long enough. How do we achieve this? Hit them where it hurts - their wallets. Focus on targeting freighters and transport convoys, especially those carrying Artifacts. You’d be amazed at how quickly they’d crumble without their Artifact trade propping up their war effort.

40575.text: I've been a bartender here for a decade now. You'd think life on a remote station in a system on the edge of the sector would be as dull as it gets, but you'd be dead wrong. The introduction of the Peregrine patent production revitalized this place. We've got more personnel on board and a steady flow of customers coming to check out the ships, many of them ending up buying or leasing one. Then there was the invasion of Gran Canaria by Bretonia not long ago. That kept everyone on edge, with every day feeling unpredictable. It's that fear of the unknown - the tension of not knowing what tomorrow will bring - that gives you sleepless nights, but it also makes life here anything but boring.

40576.text: Our Imperio is vast, and we are many. You’d be surprised at how different the Corsairs on Crete and Gran Canaria are. Despite being unified under one banner, most of them never visit the other planet and stick to their routines on the surface. For example, the Gran Canaria Corsairs hold the Zoners in much higher regard than your average Corsair on Crete. The whole Freeport 9 fiasco didn’t sit well with people here, yet it feels like barely anyone noticed. The deep western Omegas and southern Omicrons are far enough apart for these kinds of events to not ripple through. But if a full-blown war escalated and reinforcements from Crete were sent here, it would be a different story altogether. I hope it never comes to that.

40577.text: I’m from Planet Los Angeles in Liberty. Pretty far away, huh? I used to be a security pilot for Interspace Commerce until I met a Core liaison on Newark. He laid out the Core’s vision, told us about the frontiers of the Omegas and Omicrons, and offered great pay for anyone bold enough to take the leap. I didn’t think twice. I figured, if there’s any way to make a real impact in this world, it’s to aim high.

40580.text: This prospecting expedition went a lot further than intended, and we do not have much in the way of usable results. The deposits we have found are already swarming with Independent Miners Guild rats. So now we take respite here on this strange distant planet, and go home. I do not have a problem with that, I am paid by the lightminute, and we have traveled far indeed.

40581.text: Do the Corsairs over there make nervous? Of course. But I have told them of our engagements with the Hessian scum, get some drinks for all, you know. Maybe exaggerate some tales a little bit, and we get along. I look forward to getting home, but I do not mind it here. Yes, the selection of food and drink might be small and very expensive, but it is refreshing to stay at such a frontier location.

40582.text: Hey, follow my gaze. Her over there, with the shoulder length dark hair. Do you see? Don't look so obviously! I think I fancy her, and I will try my luck before we depart. We are in the deep bowels of the Omegas now, I can get it on with a Corsair lady if I dare. If you do not mind, send a message to my family if I do not make it. Tell them I died doing what I loved.

40585.text:
The wreck of the Luchnik, a Coalition Insurgent belonging to Mihail Dzyuba, lies adrift in space. The Luchnik, along with its wingman Volshebnik, was involved in a multi-sided brawl between the Corsairs, Bounty Hunters, and the Coalition. Unfortunately for the Coalition duo, they drew the short end of the stick, being targeted first by the other two sides. Their ships were not destroyed, however, as the Corsairs and the Hunters turned on each other, leaving the wreckage to drift.

The Luchnik was inflicted an EMP pulse shock that disabled its electronic systems. The pilot, ejecting in panic, is believed to have been captured by the victor of the Corsair-Bounty Hunter clash.

40587.text: Wreck of the Volshebnik, a Coalition Insurgent belonging to Mihail Dzyuba. The Volshebnik, along with its wingman Luchnik, was involved in a multi-sided brawl between the Corsairs and the Bounty Hunters. Unfortunately for the Coalition duo, they drew the short end of the stick, being targeted first by the other two sides. Their ships were not destroyed, however, as the Corsairs and the Hunters turned on each other, leaving the wreckage to drift. The Volshebnik suffered a missile blast to the engines, rendering it immobile. The pilot, ejecting in haste, is believed to have been captured by the victor of the Corsair-Bounty Hunter clash.

40589.text:
The remains of the Drunken Squirrel, a Molly Harrier once piloted by Sinead O'Shea, lingering in the ice field. The ship was on a routine patrol through a dense asteroid field when an unexpected asteroid crossed its path. Sinead made a desperate last-second maneuver, clipping the asteroid with the Harrier's left wing. The vessel was immediately rendered inoperable, and Sinead's escape pod was retrieved by one of her colleagues.

The story of the Drunken Squirrel quickly became infamous among the local Molly garrison, with many poking fun at Sinead's misfortune. Rumor has it that Sinead has vowed never to fly in asteroid fields again.

40591.text:
The wreckage of the Hammerhead belonging to bounty hunter John "Mauler" Gallagher, drifting in orbit around a nearby planetoid. Gallagher, in pursuit of the notorious Corsair Santiago Rivera, received a tip from the Junkers regarding Rivera's location. The two clashed in a fierce duel above Aarhus.

In a critical moment, Gallagher executed a sharp right turn in an attempt to flank Rivera, but Rivera anticipated the maneuver, responding with an even sharper turn that placed him perfectly on Gallagher's tail. A full barrage from Rivera's Escopeta Cannons resulted in the swift destruction of Gallagher's ship, bringing his hunt - and his life - to an abrupt end.

40593.text:
The remains of the Sapphire Sparrow, a young Zoner explorer eager to chart the uncharted dangers of the Omegas. Despite her skill in navigating the region’s many natural hazards, her end came at the hands of an artificial foe.

During the Freeport 9 tensions between the Corsairs and the Zoners, she was intercepted and shot down by an overzealous Corsair patrol. Her Dromedary now drifts endlessly amidst the haunting beauty of the Omega-55 system, a somber reminder of the fragility of peace in such volatile space.

40595.text:
The wreckage of a Valkyrie, once part of Rheinland Patrol 33 during the early stages of Rheinland's expeditions in Omega-55.

Despite the squadron's involvement in the mysterious operations within the Utrecht Cloud, Rheinland has never publicly acknowledged what was discovered there, leaving the fate of Patrol 33 forever shrouded in mystery.

40597.text:
The wreckage of the Illusionist, once piloted by Rheinland Military officer Ana Richter. Richter's Banshee shows significant damage around its wings and the front of the vessel. Despite this, the compact hull remains largely intact, suggesting much of its equipment may still be attached.

The most plausible theory to date states that the Banshee got hit by a sudden, noticeable kinetic force, strong enough to rip off the ship's limbs without shredding through the hull.

Whereabouts of the Illusionist's accident are unknown, though it is likely related to the Sektor-15 disaster. No public records of the accident have ever been disclosed, leaving this wreck a mystery eternally sealed in space.

40599.text:
The remains of the Deceiver, a Banshee-class fighter of the Rheinland Military, resting deep within the remote southeastern nebula of Omega-55. Once piloted by David Reus, the vessel has been adrift for over a decade. Extensive damage across its hull renders it unfit for anything beyond serving as a point of navigation.

A pathway leading deeper into the nebula appears visible near the wreckage. No official records document what lies within the tunnel, or beyond it.

40601.text: A heavily armed defense platform controlled by an onboard threat/response artificial intelligence. The platform's automated detection system seems to have malfunctioned, treating any moving vessel approaching it as a hostile target.

40602.text: I hate to hear the news from the east. Nine ransacked? Open conflict between Zoners and Corsairs? It's not like that over here. We pay our tributes and the Empire protects us. We can trade food, some basic goods we make, and sometimes Molly gold. They don't run files on every person and try to control every part of our society, just simple exchanges, goods for safety. That works for us, and it works for them. Definitely much better than what you'd be agreeing to in the houses. I don't know how it could have gone so wrong over there.

40604.text: The remains of the Data Miner, a broker who once worked for Interspace Commerce before becoming an independent contractor. The Eagle appears to be heavily damaged and showing no signs of life. The ship's black box contains no recorded data, leaving its location and purpose shrouded in mystery. Rumors suggest that the pilot was a master at mining and deciphering data.

40608.text:
Launched in 826 AS from Singapore Shipyard, the Independent Miners Guild's battlecruiser Remembrance serves as the primary protector of the Guild's sole installation in the deep Omegas - Madeira.

The region's remoteness, combined with a high Corsair presence and numerous natural hazards, makes establishing and maintaining a mining base a logistically and financially daunting challenge. While the potential rewards outweigh the risks, the Guild’s significant investment has yet to yield returns. The Rememberance is for that reason here to ensure the venture's ultimate success.

40610.text: An asteroid field in the southeast of Tau-29, mostly composed of ice crystals.

40613.text:
Petra was once an important Corsair raiding and logistics base, designed to launch attacks into Rheinland's northern regions. This staging point was vital to supporting the Battlecruiser Penitence's assault into Dresden. Following the destruction of Madrid Base and the expulsion of the Junkers from Sigmas-13, Petra also became an important way station for Artifact smugglers heading for Rheinland. The steady flow of Corsair supply ships were frequently raided by the Bundschuh, who sought to expel the Corsairs from Frankfurt and Dresden.

Accordingly, Petra's garrison was strengthened with additional squadrons several times to deter these attacks. This garrison was ordered en-masse into Frankfurt in 835 AS to rescue the retreating Battlecruiser Penitence, which had suffered heavy damage in Dresden to break out of a Red Hessian encirclement. Seeing a rare opportunity, Bundschuh scouts notified the GMG of the Corsair installation's weakness and moved in to attack. After a short but fierce battle, a torpedo struck one of Petra's H-Fuel storage tanks, detonating them. Explosions gutted the station, before the reactor also detonated.

40621.text:
DIAMETER: 200 km
MASS: 0.69 x 10e20 kg
TERRAIN: N/A
TEMPERATURE: N/A
ESCAPE VELOCITY: N/A

Smaller than some asteroids, the Granada Planetoid exists at a gravitational sink where planetary fragments have collected over the millennia and begun to compact under their own weight into the seed of what might eventually become a planet. Granada presents a unique opportunity for the local researchers to study planetary formation and extend their terraforming technology.

40623.text:
DIAMETER: 300 km
MASS: 0.32 x 15e21 kg
TERRAIN: N/A
TEMPERATURE: N/A
ESCAPE VELOCITY: N/A

Smaller than some asteroids, the Cordoba Planetoid exists at a gravitational sink where planetary fragments have collected over the millennia and begun to compact under their own weight into the seed of what might eventually become a planet. Cordoba presents a unique opportunity for the local researchers to study planetary formation and extend their terraforming technology.

40625.text:
The Almeria Planetary Fragments are an accumulation of rocks formed during the early stages of the universe, as well as the remains of a shattered celestial body, drifting across the Omega-43 system. Astronomers theorize that most of the fragments were once part of a protoplanet destabilized by gravitational interactions with a larger planetary body or perhaps destroyed by an ancient cataclysm, such as a collision with a massive rogue asteroid or a powerful explosion. The result is a sprawling asteroid field, with chunks of varying sizes stretching across a vast expanse, forming a perilous yet mesmerizing region for explorers and miners alike.

Rich in diverse materials, the Almeria Planetary Fragments are primarily composed of silicates, iron, and carbonaceous minerals, with deposits of rare beryllium and molybdenum scattered throughout. Due to its remote nature, however, any form of exploitation is decades, if not centuries, away.

40627.text:
Built in 828 AS, shortly after the system's discovery, Sevilla was the first attempt by the Corsairs to establish a foothold in Omega-43. This small depot served primarily as a supply point for operations toward Leon Base in Omega-41.

In 833 AS, the depot suffered a catastrophic event when a large stray asteroid from the Almeria Planetary Fragments collided with the station, opening its airlocks instantly. Most of the crew perished immediately, with only a few fortunate individuals managing to evacuate in their ships. The station's remains now serve as a solemn reminder that, despite humanity's relentless pursuit of power and resources, nature continues to operate on its own terms. Despite the catastrophe wiping out human life, the hull is still holding together barely.

40629.text: An area in the heart of Omega-43, looking seemingly devoid of asteroids from the surrounding Almeria planetary fragments. Occasional asteroids burst in, one of which has destroyed Sevilla Station, a Corsair installation in the system.

40631.text:
This large asteroid field, located at the edge of Omega-2, is made up of dense fragments from what was once a planet. The remnants, though small in size, are densely packed together, creating a chaotic maze of jagged rock and debris. The sheer concentration of material makes navigation difficult, as massive clusters of fragments drift perilously close to one another.

The asteroids are primarily composed of nickel, iron, and other metals, with some having traces of rare minerals. Their immense density and heavy composition, coupled with the Omega-2's isolated position, make them a challenge to mine in, but the potential reward is great for those willing to venture into this remote and barren stretch of space.

40633.text:
A medium-large asteroid field on the outskirts of Omega-2, Narvik is a phenomenon due to the size and rarity of its rocks. Unlike more densely packed fields, the asteroids here are sparse and massive, scattered across space.

Rich in diverse materials, the Narvik Planetary Fragments are primarily composed of silicates, iron, and carbonaceous minerals, with deposits of rare beryllium and molybdenum scattered throughout. Due to its remote nature, however, any form of exploitation is decades, if not centuries, away.

40635.text:
>>>WARNING: NAVIGATIONAL HAZARD<<<
A stunning red sight stretching across Omega-2's outskirts, this nebula is home to an unusual cluster of lava-filled asteroids. The intense heat from these asteroids creates an unpredictable environment, with sudden bursts of volcanic activity disrupting the otherwise serene beauty of the nebula. The region is as dangerous as it is breathtaking, making it a challenging yet mesmerizing destination for those brave enough to explore.

40637.text: The accretion disk of Fischer-1171 is composed of gas and matter spiraling at incredible speeds as it is drawn toward the black hole’s event horizon. The disk emits a bright yellow glow, caused by the intense friction and heat generated as particles collide and compress, reaching temperatures high enough to radiate visible light. Intermittent red flares and jets of superheated matter erupt from the disk, propelled along the black hole's magnetic field lines. These flares, combined with the chaotic swirling of the disk, create a striking and violent visual spectacle, marking Fischer-1171 as a captivating and dangerous celestial body in the depths of the Omega-1 system.

40639.text:
TYPE: Stellar
LUMINOSITY: 10e35 to 10e38 W
DISK COLOR: Yellow/Red
DISK TEMPERATURE: 2 x 10e7K
MASS: 1.989 x 10e31 kg
SCHWARZSCHILD RADIUS: 29.5 km

Fischer-1171 is a Stellar-type black hole located on the distant edge of the Omega-1171 system, named Fischer. Discovered by Rheinland astronomer Manuel Ludwig Fischer in 56 AS, it is one of the earliest celestial phenomena documented in Sirius' recorded history. The black hole is estimated to have a mass roughly ten times that of Sol's sun, its immense gravity bending light and distorting the surrounding space. Its appearance is both captivating and ominous, featuring a striking yellow accretion disk swirling chaotically at incredible speeds, interspersed with brilliant red flares and jets of superheated matter escaping along its magnetic field lines. This unique visual phenomenon makes Fischer-1171 a standout celestial body observable from the southern Omega systems.

The black hole is believed to have formed from the collapse of a massive star millions of years ago, leaving behind a gravitational singularity encircled by remnants of the star's matter. Fischer identified its presence not through direct observation, as the Walker Nebula interfered with clear visibility, but by meticulously analyzing unusual gravitational distortions in the surrounding star field. When the Omega-11 system was discovered in 110 AS, Fischer-1171 became a focal point for further study, its beautiful and distant appearance reinforcing the astronomer's legacy and cementing its place in Sirius' astronomical lore.

40644.text:
The remains of the San Agustín, a Corsair Praefect-class cruiser, serving as a grim reminder of the relentless bloodshed in Omega-47 between the Corsairs, Hessians, the Coalition, and Bounty Hunters, with casualties mounting daily. Launched in 833 AS from Tripoli Shipyard, the San Agustín was swiftly dispatched to Casablanca to bolster the Corsair presence in the system. However, she became one of the shortest-lived warships the Imperio had ever produced, meeting her fate in her very first battle against a combined Hessian and Coalition assault.

The exact circumstances of the Praefect's downfall remain unknown, but her shattered hull drifts as a silent testament to the ongoing conflict. Until one faction claims dominance over Omega-47, the wreck will continue to float, a haunting monument to the brutal war for control of the system.

40645.text: Hey, you haven't seen my twin around here, have you? If so, don't trust a word that idiot says. The guy is a complete thief! Just last week we pulled in a set of samples that we leveraged off of a local Hessian with a bit of a bribe. Some handheld weapons fresh out of the Coalition, and he takes credit for it all?! I did all the heavy lifting! No way I'm going to let him get away with this. I'll go straight to the deck officer!

40646.text: Given our lack of intel on nearby hostiles, this place is as good as any for the Orion to lay low. The nebula is great cover for the comings and goings of our scouts, and our constant contact with Primus Outpost keeps us in touch with our people while they explore the region. As long as we keep our emissions low and everyone sticks to protocol, nobody's liable to find us any time soon.

40647.text: Careful. I don't know how long you've been here, but there's a guy around here who looks just like me. He's a jerk, and likes to lie about the work he does. Don't take him seriously, though. My brother can barely fly a ship and typically sticks to the labs. I'm the one out there getting in the line of fire of these locals. I'm not going to let him take credit for my recovery ops. Absolutely not. I'm going to see the officer in charge after this shift.

40648.text: Skagen is in our sights now. We've been trying to get a probe or two out, but The Core's patrols shoot them down. What's worse is they've got some pretty nasty Bounty Hunters with them this time, too. We've got to pick our targets and act on opportunity. I don't think we'll be able to take them toe to toe, so our standing orders are to lay low and poke around. With the Citadel being so far away, some data is just too sensitive to transmit on the relays. Data runners are invaluable out here.

40649.text: Keeping people fed a variety out here has been a real challenge for the cooks. There's limited rations, and our supply lines can only do so much. I get enough complaints that there's not enough options, but the people are lucky they even have more than two right now. The only drinks we've got on board that aren't water are what I can source from the Junkers. That's only if I'm quick to get a requisition form in before the next orders go out.

40652.text:
CLASS: Toitsu
CREW: 0
ARMAMENT: N/A

The Battleship Hakodate was one of the early Toitsu class battleships. Initially laid down at Kure Shipyard during the Kusari Civil War, she launched in late 825 AS, shortly after the outbreak of the Saigon War. While the Hakodate was being fitted out for service in the Sigmas, the Battleship Sado was crippled by a Blood Dragon attack in Tohoku. The Hakodate was quickly rushed to replace it, with final adjustments being made at Ichigaya Drydock. By 827 AS, she had been transferred to the Kusari Office of Intelligence, and utilized as a technology demonstrator platform. During the Invasion of Gallia, Chochinbi attaches were posted aboard for field trials of cloaking devices, experimental sensors, and prototype weapons.

The Hakodate accompanied the northern fleets, seeing battle in Lorraine and Burgundy. She earned several elite combat honors during these campaigns, primarily for high-risk raiding actions that maximized the impact of its technological capabilities. Following the war's conclusion, the Hakodate returned to Tohoku as a garrison ship, where it adopted an increasingly aggressive approach to suppressing Blood Dragon and Order raids. By 829 AS, the Chochinbi obtained permission for a daring mission, uniquely suited to the Hakodate's specialisms: assaulting Omicron Mu -- the home of The Order. Tasked with curtailing the secretive terrorist group, the Hakodate used its cloaking device and hybrid weapons to great effect, winning early victories with the surprise destruction of Alexandria Research Station.

A major Order attack on Ichigaya Drydock in 834 AS outraged Kusari's Shogun, with the Hakodate and Chochinbi warning further strikes were imminent. As a result, a full punitive expedition to destroy Fort Carthage was approved the following year. KOI and KNF elements reinforced the Hakodate and launched a major offensive through the Wall of Seth, soon encountering unexpectedly fierce resistance. While Chochinbi bombers succeeded in reaching Carthage and inflicting minor damage, the Hakodate itself was quickly snared by Order cloak disruptors. Despite tearing its way through several battlecruisers and heavily damaging an enemy Osiris, the Hakodate was eventually immobilized by a Blood Dragon bombers, and ripped apart under the weight of enemy fire.

40653.text:
That thumping? Yeah, that's the rave hall. You kinda stop hearing the noise after a while. Go check it if you're down to party, and if you're offered a little somethin', say thank you because drugs are expensive. This is a dark and depressing place otherwise, so we gotta do something to keep us entertained. Sometimes GC girls come down here to party, and they're lovely to have around.

Definitely don't go in there if you're sensitive to bright flashing lights though. Or a square.

40656.text:
DIAMETER: 300 km
MASS: 0.32 x 15e21 kg
TERRAIN: N/A
TEMPERATURE: N/A
ESCAPE VELOCITY: N/A

A dwarf rogue planet on the outskirts of Omega-43, Malaga is slowly drifting out of the system towards the northwestern Omegas. Its original location, source of the planet's creation, as well as the event that made it lose its gravitational parent, are unknown. The surface is made of frozen nitrogen, methane, and carbon monoxide ices, with a smaller amount of water ice.

40701.text:
Genoa was an important Outcast foothold located in Tau-37, serving as a border station that monitored traffic between Tau-37 and Omicron Alpha. It was built shortly after the discovery of a mysterious jump hole in Tau-37, which turned out to lead to Lorraine. When the Council discovered the Gallia side of the hole in 817 AS, Genoa's fighters and bombers were responsible for intercepting and eliminating intruders from Sirius who were approaching Omicron Alpha.

In 831 AS, there was a large-scale slave revolt on the planet Malta, which resulted in a significant portion of the Outcast forces from Sirius being called back to quell the rebellion. With a weakened crew Genoa Station was unable to withstand the combined forces of the Crayter Republic and Indepdent Miners Guild and was destroyed less than a month after the Malta slave revolt began. The destruction of the station weakened the Outcast's position in Tau-37 enough for the CR and IMG to send blockade runners to Omicron Alpha with supplies for the rebellious slaves.

40702.text:
You hear about that Crayter patrol that vanished last week? Some say it was just another routine ambush, but I was on standby when the Quezon intercepted their distress call. They were panicking, calling out positions that didn’t make sense—like their own ships were firing on them. Now, I know our nebula tricks the sensors, but even we don’t have the kind of jamming tech to make pilots shoot at ghosts. Whatever happened to them, no wreckage was ever found. Just empty space where they were supposed to be. Makes you wonder what else is hiding out here in this storm.

Still, it’s not all bad. This place is perfect for training new pilots. The nebula helps us stay hidden, and we get to launch from Quezon on quick strikes against Crayter supply lines. Most of the time, they never see us coming until it’s too late. I’d be lying if I said I didn’t enjoy the look on their faces when they realize it's already over. The way I see it, every patrol we take down is one less obstacle between us and turning Gallia into our next Cardamine empire.

40703.text:
People like to talk about the big hauls - the freighters we manage to snatch or the pilots we space for trying to resist - but no one talks about the logistics. You ever try keeping Cardamine fresh in a place like this? The humidity in the storage bays messes with the packaging, and if the filters fail, we’ll be breathing in more of it than we should. Not that I’d complain - plenty of us on the Quezon would rather breathe Cardamine than this recycled, stale air. But if the product gets contaminated or degrades before we offload it in Gallia, that's lost profit, and trust me, nobody wants to answer to the bosses for that.

Last time I was in the cargo hold, I caught some rookie trying to siphon off a few doses for himself. Idiot must’ve thought no one would notice. He’s lucky I did instead of one of the officers - if they caught him, he’d be floating outside in the storm by now. You don’t steal from the trade that keeps us alive. I sent him to scrub down the fuel lines for a week instead. If he still has a death wish after that, well... maybe I’ll be the one tossing him out next time.

40704.text:
You think maintaining a destroyer's weapons is all just loading torpedoes and cleaning barrels? Ha! If only. The Quezon was built fast, and I mean fast.

But hey, at least I get to see some real action. Every time we set up an ambush, I’m in the thick of it, making sure our guns don’t fry themselves when the captain calls for full firepower. Last week, we took out a Crayter gunboat in under a minute - one clean volley, and boom, it was space dust. That’s when you know you did your job right. Of course, when things don’t go right, well... let’s just say I keep my escape pod prepped, just in case.

40705.text:
You wouldn’t think a destroyer like this needs a bar, but trust me, after a long shift dodging Crayter patrols, even the hardest Outcast needs a drink. I run this little corner of the ship, keeping everyone’s glasses full and ears open. If there’s a story floating around, it passes through here first. Like that one about the supply freighter that went missing last month? Supposed to rendezvous with us near the nebula’s edge, but it never showed. No wreckage, no distress call - just gone. Some say Crayter got them, but I’ve heard whispers that something else is lurking in this storm, something that swallows ships whole.

Of course, most of the crew laughs it off. We’re Outcasts - we live in the dark, we own the dark. But I’ve been on enough ships to know when people start getting twitchy, there’s usually a reason. Some of the veterans drink a little heavier when we’re stationed here. They keep their backs to the walls, eyes always watching the viewport like they're expecting to see something looking back. Me? I don’t ask too many questions. I just pour the drinks and make sure everyone’s got something strong enough to keep their nerves steady. But between you and me? If the Quezon ever gets reassigned, I won’t be the last one off this ship.

40807.text: Of course there's always resistance in Sigma-17. The Guild isn’t thrilled about some of our methods, and neither are certain parties in Kusari and Rheinland. But they fund the project because they need it to succeed just as much as we do. If the Sigmas become a warzone, trade with the Omicrons collapses, and we all lose. I just wish people understood that sometimes, a little harshness now prevents a catastrophe later.

40808.text: Fiji is only a temporary measure—just a holding point until Bora Bora is fully operational. The Core needs this route secured, and we need a place to manage prisoners, personnel, and logistics in the meantime. Some think it's unusual for a prison liner to play such a crucial role, but out here, we use what we have. Fiji provides security, supplies, and a strategic foothold all in one.

40809.text:
Name’s Callie. I run supply runs between here and the Core’s stations. Not glamorous, but it pays the bills, and in the Sigmas, that’s what matters. Fiji is an easy stopover - fuel up, grab a meal, and maybe pick up a side job while waiting for clearance. It’s not exactly a luxury resort, but compared to drifting in space? I’ll take it.

Most of the chatter around here is about Bora Bora. Every time I’m docked, someone’s complaining about delays, missing shipments, or unexpected “labor” on the site. Not my problem, though. I take the crates, fly the route, and get paid. What’s inside them? Not my concern. But if I had to guess, not all of them are full of construction materials.

40810.text:
You’d think the Core runs everything here, but we hunters are the ones doing the dirty work. Pirates, terrorists, even ex-Guild traitors who think they can escape their debts - we track them all down. Sigma-17’s a mess of a system, and with Atka’s destruction, the scum have gotten bolder. That’s why we’re here: to keep things in check until the Core’s new station is fully operational.

Fiji’s a strange place to be stationed, though. It’s half a prison, half a logistics hub, and somehow also a war room. I hear whispers that some prisoners are being put to work on Bora Bora, but that’s none of my business. My job is simple - hunt, capture, and bring them in. And if they resist? Well, let’s just say I don’t always bring them in breathing.

40815.text:

An accumulation of various radioactive particles orbiting the Fischer Singularity at high speeds. All ships not properly equipped to handle high radioactivity are advised to turn away at once. Based on the analysis of the gravitational waves surrounding the black hole, all ships are advised to maintain a minimum 100k perimeter from the stellar object.
