65802.text:
The fifth sleeper ship, the Hispania, launched at the same time as its sister ships and broke through the Coalition blockade in the Sol system. Unfortunately, sabotage by Coalition agents that had secreted themselves onboard crippled the engines just as the vessel arrived in the Sirius sector. The passengers awakened from their cryogenic sleep to discover the ship was drifting towards an unknown star system. When the Hispania drifted within range of a red dwarf system, conflict aboard the ship escalated, and about half of the surviving colonists decided to take escape pods, chancing their survival on the promise of a habitable world. The remaining half coaxed the damaged vessel onwards to its eventual destination in the Omicron Alpha system, arriving some time in the year 41 AS Upon their arrival, the crew discovered a planet capable of supporting human life in orbit of the primary star. The Hispania's passengers named the planet Malta -- a harsh place of acidic oceans, gray skies, and vast plains covered in a species of tall, thin, orange grass. Taking whatever equipment they could salvage from the crippled Hispania, they left the hulk in orbit of Malta and began to make a home for themselves on Malta.

Eventually the Outcasts -- as they came to think of themselves -- began a limited exploration of their home system. As pilots wandered farther and farther afield in search of resources, many became seriously ill. Upon returning to Malta, the crews recovered quickly. After making a number of genetic scans of critically ill pilots, the doctors made a startling and disturbing discovery. Their genetic code had been altered considerably. The Outcast human DNA was found to contain strands identical to that of the orange grasses that covered the planet -- from which the drug Cardamine was derived. Trace amounts were present in everything on the planet, in their food, their water, even the very air. Once pilots made lengthier journeys away from Malta, their bodies went into shock, followed by death.

The Outcasts were now truly separated from the rest of humanity -- changed so that they could never expand beyond the planet on which they had landed. They needed Cardamine now, like air, food, or water. But with the origin of the sickness solved, they could at least compensate by carrying supplies of Cardamine with them and resume their exploration of their surrounding systems. Over time, their knowledge of Cardamine improved, and the Outcasts learned that distributing it in a highly concentrated dose causes extreme euphoria. When they finally encountered the rest of the Houses in the seventh century, a new strategy emerged. The Outcasts would deliver the poison that would rot the other Houses from the inside out and grow rich from the profits of their trade.

The planet's crust is largely devoid of usable metallic elements, with a few notable exceptions, namely at the heart of her largest continent, and highly unusual deposits of metallic Copper on the ocean floor. Most of its landmass is covered in prairies with natural, low-grade Cardamine grass; large plantations with heavily bred and modified strains have been built on the most fertile sites. Malta's architecture is a largely low-hung and flat, one-story affair in the rural areas; cities are an expression of extremes, built almost entirely in the rare hilly regions of the planet. There is little at ground-level, except starports; most structures are built both deep into the ground and into massive towers that reach towards the sky, constructed yet again as to mimic the textures of the ground. Malta's oceans are strongly acidic and home to algae that tolerate its high acidity. They appear to hold a slightly green tint from the surface.

These days the Outcasts conduct a lucrative drug-smuggling operation using the network of Jump Holes to escape detection and transport their product into the heart of the House systems through various proxies. They remain relatively few in number; a crash in the birth rate seems to have been another side effect of their genetic modification, although the modifications have lengthened the Outcast's lifespan and physical resilience considerably. There have been no known cases of cancer on Malta since the Outcasts made planetfall.

A new development has been Cryer's continued efforts to create a synthetic version of Cardamine that would be approved as a legal medication within Liberty. This poses a direct threat to the Outcasts' source of income. The Atka Research Station, with nearby access to Edge Nebula clouds, is the most immediate threat to the Outcasts. The location of the base within Corsair territory has brought the Outcasts into conflict with their ancient brethren. The Atka Research Station has come under repeated attacks by Outcast raiding parties in recent years, and the Outcasts always destroy any Cryer transports encountered throughout Sirius without mercy.

When the Dons instituted new disciplinary and security measures for Malta's plantations following Albegna's mining colony slave revolt in 831 AS, fear spread among Malta-bound slaves of mass executions and worsened living conditions. On plantations whose owners took a more lax approach to the new protocols, many slaves began to steal and cache weapons and materiel from their Outcast masters, culminating in a slave revolt that captured a starport and seized control of Malta's defenses.

Though many slaves died or were recaptured by Outcasts during the struggle, many others escaped off-world, either in stolen ships moored at the starport, or in ships flown by IMG, Crayter Republic, or abolitionist group pilots. Ultimately, the revolt was quelled, leaving the Outcasts without enough cardamine to meet market demand, and raising the problem of seeking a newer, more obedient source of labor.

Heaven's Gate was once one of the wonders of Kusari - a massive space fortress built to shelter the Emperor, laden with enough defenses to render any assault pointless. Aside from being a massive bastion, the Arch also holds some of Kusari's finest artistic designs, including the "Waterfall of Light".

After the coup of 330 AS, Heaven's Gate fell out of favor. Samura felt the Emperor would be a stronger figurehead if he was visible, so the throne remained on New Tokyo. Unwilling to let this marvel of Kusari culture decay, the Arch was kept operational, serving as an archive for Kusari's most guarded secrets and precious treasures.

The base was subverted during the Colony Wars, when Governor Tekagi, having met with Rheinland officials, was dominated by the Nomads. Tekagi was able to indoctrinate the fortress' guards, until its full staff and garrison fleet were under Nomad control as Thralls. The Blood Dragons learned of this subversion through their contacts with the Order, and were able to penetrate the base once during the Nomad Wars, stealing an important Artifact at the cost of a small fleet of their ships.

The Nomad presence was never fully eradicated; Shogun Edo appointed surviving infectees to command the newly created Kusari Office of Intelligence in the aftermath of the war. The organization has grown substantially since then, siting its headquarters aboard Heaven's Gate. To this day, the Infiltrators sequestered inside Aonyobo Annex continue to lead and misdirect the organization purportedly formed to exterminate them.

Autonomous software aboard each individual Construction Machine then executes the plan in the most efficient way possible based on local conditions.

66030.text: During the Eighty Years War between Rheinland and the Gas Miners Guild (GMG), the decisive battle was fought in Sigma-13 when the bulk of the Rheinland battle group was ambushed by GMG forces and destroyed. With thousands of lives lost and the Rheinland Imperial Navy disgraced, the government was forced to negotiate with the GMG and their ill-advised war. The wreckage of that battle provides a constant, painful reminder of Rheinland's defeat at the hands of the GMG, though ALG Waste Disposal has recently been awarded the contract to clear the area and properly dispose of any remains. Not surprisingly, Junkers have also moved into the area and are less concerned with the burial of the dead than busily salvaging any and all of the ships, parts, and weapons they can find.

DIAMETER: 4,821 km
MASS: 3.17 x 10e24 kg
TERRAIN: Desert
TEMPERATURE: -46°C to 34°C
ESCAPE VELOCITY: 5.56 km/sec

A desert world scoured clean by ceaseless sandstorms that wash across its surface. During initial surveys, individual sandstorms that lasted for several years and reached top speeds of 805 km/h were observed. Most surface probes were destroyed in a matter of hours, but revealed the existance of unnatural rock formations buried beneath the sands. In 763 AS Rheinland, jealous of the massive technological advantage Liberty had over them through the Valhalla archives, dispatched a deep space survey team to the planet to uncover what secrets might lie beneath the raging sands. They found something unexpected: An underground city, perfectly preserved, with a trove of alien technologies - some of which were alive. Curiosity turned to carelessness, and some chambers that should have stayed sealed, were opened. The Nomads, as they later came to known, awoke from their stasis and were quick to overwhelm and subvert the science teams. After learning from their memories what had happened in the past centuries, they return to Rheinland with them with a wealth of artifacts, data, and other Nomads, masquerading as a highly successful expedition. This set events in motion that would later trigger the Nomad War.

Pygar has since then been visited a number of times by other, more cautious science teams. The Nomad infections that triggered the Nomad war were traced back to Pygar, but subsequent searches showed the alien city devoid of any activity. The Nomads had left, and taken whatever technology was left on Pygar, with them. Surface conditions remain extremely hazardous, and it can be months before a window opens in the atmosphere for ships to safely land or lift off. Still, the chance of unlocking alien secrets is a major draw to xenoarcheologists, and the planet can have as many as 2.000 people investigating it's ruins at any given time.

67000.text: [834 AS] Cadet fraternity disciplined over hazing

67001.text: WEST POINT -- 834 -- West Point command staff have issued a reprimand against a popular cadet fraternity after being implicated in the hazing of new applicants. The practice has been prohibited since the death of Christine Belton 33 years ago, however it is widely understood that hazing at the academy has continued by imposing bizarre, dangerous or humiliating tasks on potential aspirants. The most recent incident was detected when the Mississippi Training Facility’s transponder was overwritten to broadcast as the Battleship Missouri. Investigation revealed cadets training aboard to be the culprits, who had pulled the prank in an attempt to impress fraternity leaders.

131129.text: We are in the heart of Liberty, right in the center of all Sirius, far from our homeland. This is the place we have to pump the majority of our drug shipments into. Since the Libertonians have the most money and the most people, they have the most junkies. If we could find a faster route into Liberty we could increase the amount of Cardamine that gets here.

131140.text: Rogues come in here and pick up Side Arm shipments for their Badlands base. It's a long haul around the system to safety for them.

131164.text: The Rogues can get to New York through the Jump Hole hidden in the same debris field this base is in. Also, there is a Jump Hole to California in the West Dallas Debris Field, though you have to be careful. Parts of that area are radioactive. There's another Jump Hole to the Hudson system in the South Dallas Debris Field.

131231.text: Scrap Metal ain't the only kind of debris you'll find in the Jersey. Ever heard somebody refer to another person as "good debris"? That means the guy they're talking about went on a little space walk without a suit on. That's what happens to rats and traitors. You want to hear the juicy part? LPI will put you into the debris too, if you make 'em angry enough.

131246.text: Republican Shipping has always specialized in shipping concerns between Liberty and Rheinland, via Hamburg and Texas. Unfortunately, rising crime and piracy within Texas and the Independent Worlds has in the past made it difficult to maintain our excellent standards. The war between our two Houses certainly didn't improve that situation. When diplomacy fails, it's never the diplomats and politicians who suffer.

131247.text: We ship the finest in Silver from Omega 7 into Manhattan. We also ship Diamonds into Liberty from New Berlin. Both Commodities are used in the manufacture of Luxury Goods, a Manhattan specialty.

131248.text: Republican Shipping sends the Luxury Consumer Goods produced here to New Berlin via distribution from Newark. Sometimes it gets to me that I'm putting my life on the line to haul some rich executive a Diamond tie pin or real leather shoes.

131253.text: Synth Foods offers tasty Pastes throughout all of Liberty and beyond. Our Paste containers are always filled and always on the go with your favorite Synth Foods flavors. Sure we lose daring pilots and gunners and engineers all the time, but when you have a job to do, it's just part of the work day.

131291.text: The Bounty Hunters will hunt down and kill just about anybody for the right price. A lot of talk around here makes them sound more like hit men than Bounty Hunters. Sure, they nab a lot of criminals and make Liberty space safer, but they smoke plenty of innocents, too. Just because you are wanted by a corporation doesn't necessarily mean you did anything illegal; you might have made the wrong enemies is all.

131295.text: Our transports take containers of Boron from here to Planet Kyushu. Even though this is Liberty, my superiors in Rheinland are making sure we do our shipping on time and on schedule.

131296.text: This mining operation requires our services in many ways. It just goes to show that Liberty would not be all that she is without the support of the other Houses. Consumer Goods are brought to this base from Ft. Bush.

131297.text: The war between Rheinland and Liberty made suspected spies out of the pilots caught behind the lines. Getting a permit to continue doing business was almost impossible, and even if you did, you get stopped by every last law enforcement officer and navy pilot demanding to inspect your vessel and authorization.

131301.text: We at ALG are committed to making Sirius space a safe place to fly. Our company processes and disposes of waste in every House in Sirius. Damned the Xenos who attack our ships simply because we are a Rheinland firm. Their harassment is not treated sternly enough by the Liberty Police or the navy.

131302.text: I've been trying to renegotiate our Toxic Waste disposal contract with the Missouri's commander, but so far I can't even get a meeting with him. I'm beginning to suspect that I'm just getting the good old Liberty runaround.

131303.text: The Toxic Waste produced in the engines of this ship used to be sent to the plant in Dortmund and disposed of properly. The amount of Xenos we had to fight off just to haul Toxic Waste is stupefying. Those bloodthirsty animals attack anything without a Liberty flag stamped on the outside of its hull. All that risk was for nothing, apparently. I hope the Xenos are happy that the navy is just jettisoning waste into the debris fields now.

131343.text: The navy gives Universal special protection. After all, Universal Shipping handles Ageira's "black boxes," covert military and government shipments, munitions -- you name it. If it's dangerous or expensive, Universal has its fingers in it.

131348.text: ALG ships Toxic Waste produced here to our facilities in Rheinland. Every shipyard produces Toxic Waste, which ALG gladly collects for recycling into MOX.

131349.text: ALG ships High-Temperature Alloys and MOX to this facility from Rheinland. On the last run we lost two in our convoy to Xenos and Rogues as we passed through Texas.

131350.text: We supply Nuclear Devices from Helgoland to replenish the power cores used here at the shipyard.

131374.text: The Trade Lanes between Rheinland and Liberty are dangerous ones. In Hudson the Xenos attack our transports, and in Bering we are attacked by Unionist scum.

131375.text: Republican Shipping is the premier Rheinland shipping firm. If it weren't for the massive debts that Rheinland accumulated during the 80-Years War, Republican would still be the only shippers in Rheinland space.

131376.text: War is a travesty, both for those killed, and those stuck behind enemy lines being scowled at by cocky teenagers with too much money and free time on their hands. I want to just punch them in the nose or tell them to go back to playing their dumb space combat hologames. War is not a game!

131432.text: The weapon platforms that surround this base make it almost impossible for an attacker to survive a direct assault on our station. As of yet, none who've tried have lasted five minutes.

131442.text: It is a bad influence to have this Bounty Hunter scum amongst all of our cadets. The young lads are still easily influenced, and Bounty Hunters have no code, no honor, and no loyalty. It's not good for the newest of ours to be exposed to this.

131471.text: There used to be a ton of work for a Bounty Hunter here, but not so much anymore. Without the Jump Gate to Rheinland, there's no commercial traffic here. Without traffic, there's no pirates harassing them. Which means no bounties. Crazy as it may sound, we're still mostly employed by Republican, to track down pirates for them. The Unioners have a strong presence in this system, and they never really used the Jump Gates anyway. They use the Jump Hole into Hamburg to cause problems around Alster, and smuggle Artifacts and Hessian Tears to Liberty.

131473.text: It's a good thing the Zoners let us land on their bases. The criminals don't like it, but fair is fair. If the Zoners didn't allow us to land Liberty would declare this base a pirate hive, and the Liberty Navy would shut this Freeport down in a second. The Zoners know that.

131474.text: We are one of the few corporations that still visits this Freeport. Bering isn't interesting to the other corporations. Despite extensive surveys, the debris field that covers most of the system has proven to have no worthwhile resources. When the Jump Gates were built, Bering was chosen as a crossover because there was already a Republican waystation here at the time, which made building up the gates a lot easier.

131475.text: We used to get the Fertilizers needed for the biodomes on this base from Holstein, out in Frankfurt. But now that path is gone, so we had to make other arrangements. Our new patented FloraGro fertilizer was being developed on California. We didn't know if this product would perform well out in space, so we used Freeport 2 as a test case. We gave them a discount on the product in return for their assistance in the trial. And I must say, the results are encouraging so far.

131476.text: Our ships still get hit by pirates every now and then while making their way to the Freeport. Even criminals need food I guess. I hear the company is reconsidering whether or not we should handle long distance transport ourselves, or let companies like Universal or Republican handle that for us. They've got more experience in Borderworld crossings. But this hop from Liberty to Freeport 2 will likely stay our own. The volume is too low to outsource it.

131479.text: The current workers in the Alster Shipyards and Altona hate us for the attacks we make against those facilities. They don't understand the way they are being exploited by Republican Shipping. Not yet anyway. If only we could open their eyes, we'd have more strong hands to join us in our cause.

131481.text: So, the Rheinlanders decide to wall themselves up and blow those Jump Gates to hell? Nice, wish they'd done so sooner, now we don't need to deal with their rabble anymore. Of course, there's still those Unioners, but hey, the fewer of those Rheinies, the better.

131482.text: The Rogues and Unioners run a smuggling line from Liberty to Rheinland through here. We hit the Unioners whenever we can, but they are tough bastards. From what we can tell, they're handling all kinds of goods - Hessian Tears, Artifacts, Munitions and other stuff we can use ourselves.

131483.text: We make supply runs to Texas to import essential Commodities like Oxygen, Water, and Consumer Goods. We produce a bit of Oxygen ourselves in the domes, but it's not enough. Unlike the Freeports out in the Barrier, there's no water in this system so we have to import what we need.

131486.text: Our main activity on Freeport 2 is Food production. With Holstein no longer accessible, Synth has started to switch their Fertilizer deliveries to be that new FloraGro stuff of theirs. They bring it in from California. It's good stuff, if a bit more expensive, but it allows us to produce so much more Food that it's worth the extra cost.

131487.text: The Xenos visit our base to buy all of their supplies and to purchase Consumer Goods. They often get cranky when they spot Unioners here. They don't like foreigners, you see? Think they're not good for Liberty. Me, I don't care about either of them. We Zoners left the Houses to be done with those kinds of politics.

131488.text: Attacks on the Trade Lanes have almost ground to a halt. There's simply no traffic anymore, other then whatever comes to our Freeport. The Liberty Rogues and Xenos might occasionally try to hijack a Synth Foods food shipment, but it's rare.

131489.text: We run Consumer Goods in from Texas. We used to get them from Hamburg, which caused a bit of discussion among the station council. That discussion was ended when Rheinland blew the gates into Hamburg. Now we can't get there, so Liberty is really our only option left.

131490.text: This station originally belonged to Republican Shipping, who used it as a supply and repair depot before the Trade Lanes were built in 550. At the time it was called Schiltberger Base, but it was abandoned after the Trade Lanes made it obsolete. In 650 our ancestors drifted in from Texas and Hamburg and refurbished the abandoned station, naming it Freeport 2, the second in the Sirius Sector. The practise of restoring these abandoned "midway stations" continued, although a few of them have been lost over the years.

131491.text: Zoners firmly believe in the concept of Freeports - places where anyone, regardless of their criminal or political affiliation, is welcome. Unfortunately, the authorities in the House systems do not subscribe to this philosophy, so there are very few within House boundaries. Those that are within House space are usually there because the Houses expanded their borders around them. Liberty often tries to pressure us into disallowing Rogues and Unioners to dock here, but we'll have none of that. Ironic, no? That our port enjoys more freedom then a House named for that concept. Ruddy corporate hypocrites...

131492.text: Synth Foods has been good for us. They helped install and maintain the biodomes, provided the special seeds, and sold us the processing and flavorant units that turn inedible crops into digestible food. Until they came along, the Zoners and other free thinkers struggled with the starvation caused by the lack of arable planets in the Independent and Border Worlds.

131493.text: This system only exists as a way point on the Jump Gate routes because the distance between Hamburg and Texas was longer than the six-light-year limit of early Jump Gates. Before the Trade Lanes were built, the asteroids caused constant problems with shipping. Now that the Jump Gates to Rheinland are gone, I expect traffic to almost cease here. Good. It'll make this system a nice backwater area. Just the way we like it.

131494.text: We sheltered the Unioners when they first fled Hamburg in the years following the Popular Revolution, but they soon became too numerous for this station to support. Many of the inhabitants of this station come from Hamburg, and were sympathetic to the Unioner cause. When Republican hired Bounty Hunters and the Rheinland Military started to harass us, the Unioners left and established their own base at our request. They still come for supplies, though.

131507.text: There's plenty of work for us Bounty Hunters in this part of the Barrier. Between the Rogues in the Weddell field and the Lane Hackers and Outcasts in the Barrier Cloud, it's a non-stop hunting party. Gotta watch out for those Outcasts, though - I've lost more than a few buddies to those lowlifes. Tough bastards those.

131509.text: I don't get why everyone hates us so much. We're providing a service to society, cleaning up all the criminal dregs, and making the Trade Lanes and Jump Gates safer for commerce. It's not an easy life, living out in these hellhole Freeports at the edge of nowhere. I'd much rather base out of Curacao, thank you very much.

131510.text: We run patrols throughout the system. Most of the bounties are put up by Interspace and Ageira, who seem to really hate the Lane Hackers' guts. You get a lot less for a Rogue, but they're easier to find and take out. Outcasts tend to be problematic. Unless you're good, they're not worth the credits on their head. They make you work for it. Me, I like that. My buddies, most of em don't.

131512.text: It's pretty frustrating not being able to just take out my Detroit Executioner and waste the Lane Hackers that come into this bar. It'd certainly be easier than chasing them down in space. Guess that's the downside of Freeports, but you can still pick up on a good lead or two. The IMG folks running the place are okay, but not real friendly. Got that Bretonian superiority attitude going or something.

131513.text: I just made a run from Liberty with Food, H-fuel, and Engine Components. A quick trip but a dangerous one. My escorts had to earn their pay against a small Rogue ambush, but we made it out. I bought the lads a round or two, they deserve it.

131514.text: Industrial Materials are in demand here. We ship it in from Trenton to help our IMG friends out. I'll probably head back with some Passengers bound for Planet Erie, then take some Mining Machinery back here.

131515.text: Be careful in those Barrier Clouds. It's hard to see until it's too late. Lots of Lane Hackers and Outcasts but little in the way of security forces. My best friend's convoy got nailed last week at the Manchester Gate by some Lane Hackers. He was hauling Gold from Bretonia to New York, not low-value stuff like Oxygen and Water.

131516.text: We buy supplies here for our base in the Barrier Cloud to the west. It's pretty mundane stuff - H-Fuel, Food, Oxygen, and Water. We prefer if freelancers like you haul them, as it attracts less attention with Bounty Hunters. Watch out for the Rogues though, they will try to rob freelancers like yourself blind.

131517.text: Between you and me, that chunk of ice in the Barrier Cloud gets a little close at times, especially with those weirdo Outcasts stopping by on their drug runs all the time. It's a beautiful view of the Barrier from the Freeport, so we visit here as often as we can sneak by the Bounty Hunters. Or blast through them if need be. It helps to know when they go out there alone.

131519.text: We produce Water and Oxygen here from our mining operations north of the base, in the Weddell Ice Field. The Liberty government used the area for Jump Gate technology tests in the past, but those operations have been moved. The Lane Hackers have secreted away whatever Liberty left behind, so it's just us and the ice up there.

131520.text: Universal Shipping brings us our Mining Machinery out of Liberty. We also need a steady supply of Engine Components for ships that need repairs. These Independent Worlds can be a bit rough, especially towards Bretonia. Their Armed Forces are a bit tied up with Gallia at the moment, so they don't have many patrols out. The nebula is also much more dense at their end, which makes for a better ambushing spot, something the Hackers make liberal use of.

131521.text: The Lane Hackers sometimes land here to get supplies. The Bounty Hunters are always hovering around the station, watching their prey mosey right by them. That's the way it is with Freeports. Both the Bounty Hunters and Hackers know better than to start trouble near a freeport. That just gets them thrown out.

131522.text: Our Freeport doesn't produce a whole lot. The Water and Oxygen we mine supplies a few bases in Manchester and California. There isn't a whole lot else here other then ice. We've tried to extract a bit of Deuterium from the ice, but it's too expensive for the gains. Just producing Water and Oxygen in bulk makes up the most of our lives. Gateway will transport it to where it is needed. We're also occasionally contracted by DSE to remove dangerous asteroids that stray near the Trade Lanes, and we repair the occasional ship that gets damaged, either from the asteroids or a pirate ambush.

131523.text: I'm not supposed to say anything, but there's a Lane Hacker base in the Barrier Cloud in the west. You'll also find Jump Holes to Manchester and Cortez. Watch yourself out there. Outcast drug runners will waste you in a second if you don't know what you're doing. They don't like us miners much.

131524.text: The asteroid fields of Magellan were notorious for their unpredictability. The Bretonian government established this base in 220 and called it the Gough Station. Repair and tug ships were stationed here to assist disabled ships and to remove errant asteroids as they crossed the cleared trade routes. After the Trade Lanes were established the station fell out of use. Eventually it was reoccupied by a few unemployed miners - and it's been going ever since.

131525.text: The bulk of the Water mined here goes to the terraforming operation on California Minor or Los Angeles. It's cheaper to import it from Magellan than to desalinize their nasty seawater. Gateway handles the shipment - it's a short run for them, and relatively safe.

131526.text: The Lane Hackers and Outcasts prefer the safety of the Barrier Clouds for their attacks. The bloody Rogues don't care - they'll attack shipping in the Weddell Field, until the Liberty Navy shows up from the California Gate. Then they all scatter like rats. Kind of funny to see as long as you're not the one getting shot at.

131527.text: With the completion of Trade Lanes across the Barrier by Deep Space in 535, the old Bretonia station was no longer needed. The station was officially decommissioned by the Bretonian government and left to drift. Early IMG folks came in around 580 from New London and reopened the place. Been going ever since. It's our only outpost in the Independent Worlds - a little too close to Liberty for our taste, but so far Liberty doesn't seem to have much of an interest in Magellan. Nothing of value here and all that.

131528.text: Those Lane Hackers are a funny bunch. They fancy themselves as the Sirius Sector's Robin Hoods. They avoid direct confrontation when possible, unless it is the henchmen of Interspace, DSE or Ageira. They like to frequent our base a lot, as that cloudy ice asteroid base of theirs can become a wee bit claustrophobic at times. A lot of them are addicted to Cardamine. They also trade drugs for Trade Lane info with the Outcasts.

131529.text: We haul a lot of Water from here to the California Minor terraforming operation, which is in its final stages. Centuries of ice mining by Los Angeles has depleted almost all of California's pure ice. These Independent Miners aren't the worst bunch to deal with, and they can handle the volume we need. They just refuse to ship it themselves. I guess they don't like going into Liberty much. I don't blame them.

131530.text: The Rogues are our main problem between here and California Minor. They like to hit you in the asteroid fields or in the Sierra Cloud. You can't really see much ahead of you, so the first sign of trouble you get is when you're getting shot at. All escorts and turret gunners are on high alert as soon as we enter into one.

131531.text: At least we don't have the Gaian problem in Magellan. That begins in Manchester and is widespread throughout Bretonian space, and I've heared rumors of Gaian propaganda being spotted down on California Minor as well! Not sure how they became so misguided. We're performing a valuable service for humankind by bringing dead worlds to life.

131577.text: The Rogues are very good customers for the Software we distribute through the Zoners. Cardi and the latest hologames make for serious relaxation after a day of raiding.

131579.text: We'd like to use the hotel on Curacao. Orbital Spa and Cruise wouldn't care if we did, but IC won't insure any Trade Lane shipping in this system. Besides, there are too many Bounty Hunters lurking around the hotel. They give me the creeps.

131580.text: The Rogues are a simple lot. We don't really have much in common with them, except maybe the love for Cardamine. Most Rogues are products of the Liberty penal system. We're too smart to get caught by the LPI or navy. We'd rather die than set foot in Texas.

131592.text: There's an old Trade Lane route through this system that was damaged during a storm around 20 years ago. People say there are some old shipwrecks along it.

131602.text: Our numbers are growing, and in time we will be strong enough to stop all foreign shippers from crossing this system. The Kusari corporations must understand that it is not worth the money they earn to ship their goods into Liberty.

131614.text: This base serves as the primary trans-shipment point for Artifacts inbound from Sigma-17. The Hogosha run them through Kusari space, terminating their long run here. The Rogues then haul the Artifacts into Rochester via their base in the southern end of the system. Don't know why people love those Artifacts so much.

131630.text: With their old union destroyed after the Popular Revolt, the Unioners reformed to become what they are today: political criminals dedicated to making Republican Shipping pay for the wrongs it committed against its workers.

131632.text: The Bounty Hunters are the biggest nuisance to the Rogue way of life. Many of our boys have been sent out to Texas or the next life by those bastards. If you want to do us Rogues a favor, burn as many of them from the sky. Do that, and you'll be okay in our books.

131634.text: Bounty Hunters and the Liberty Navy patrol the gap between the Weddell Ice Field and the Barrier. If you wanna do a little piracy, it's better to hit the Trade Lanes as they pass into the Barrier. Among the asteroids, they can't scan for you so if a patrol happens to come across you, they won't be getting help soon. Stay in protected space as much as you can if you don't want to get swarmed by the Navy or Hunters.

131635.text: Most of the corporate types in Liberty hate the Rogues, but the truth is, the suits are the ones who made us. You think I'd be doing this if I could have made it in their world? The only choice I had was to become a Rogue or burn my life away in the Boron mines of Pittsburg. If you aren't born into a company, you aren't going anywhere but the slag pile.

131636.text: The Junkers don't take a lot of new blood these days; they have their own inner circle. The LPI are corporate lap dogs, the Lane Hackers are rich corporate types turned bad, and the Outcasts - hell, they aren't even human anymore. And don't even get me started on the Xenos or the Insurgency; fanatical patriots, the whole lot of them. It was Rogues or nothing for me.

131655.text: Padua receives the supplies we get from the Lane Hackers at this base. Padua requires the importation of all of its vital supplies, including Food, Consumer Goods, Oxygen, and Water.

131656.text: The Artifacts that the Lane Hackers receive from the Hogosha at this base are taken by us to Rochester.

131657.text: The Golden Chrysanthemums that hang out at this base are into their Luxury Goods, probably the daughters of rich Samura and Kishiro executives in Kusari. I like 'em. They're all into Cardamine and stealing -- my two favorite past times.

131710.text: We get attacked frequently by Xenos on our runs through Colorado, Texas, and the Independent Worlds of Hudson and Bering. They are one of the few criminal factions that attack out Toxic Waste shipments. We are friendly to Liberty, so I don't understand their hostility.

131711.text: ALG used to handle all of the MOX delivery and Toxic Waste disposal for Liberty Navy battleships.

131729.text: They say there are still some small amounts of Silver and Copper in the Silverton and Copperton Fields. Takes a lot of shots to get much, though. We don't have time for that with Bounty Hunters around.

131738.text: The very best students from the Liberty University of New York are handpicked by Ageira recruiters. Our corporation has always selected from the top one percent of each graduating class. The members of the Lane Hackers who left Ageira were no different.

131740.text: ALG delivers large quantities of HazMat Canisters to this facility. This is one of our largest customers for this product. Unlike the Liberty Navy, Ageira is very responsible with its waste disposal since that unfortunate incident in Texas so long ago.

131741.text: We haul tremendous amounts of Toxic Waste away from this plant. The Xenos are always waiting in the asteroid field it seems.

131742.text: ALG would like to handle Toxic Waste Disposal for the Liberty Navy. Since the war between our two nations began, that seems less and less likely in the future.

131752.text: I just finished a very difficult run from Omega 7 with a load of Daumann-mined Cobalt and Copper. First we have to deal with the Corsairs in Omega 3. Then the Mollys take over in Cambridge. Then we get hit again just down the Lane in Manchester by the Gaians. You'd think they wouldn't care about a bunch of ore, but they all just hate us.

131753.text: We're heading out tomorrow for Bretonia with a load of Superconductors from Denver. I need a drink before pondering that journey. Wish I could find a decent beer around here; that Liberty ale is awful.

131754.text: It's too bad Rheinland can't manufacture these goods herself, because we certainly have the raw materials. Rheinland innovation and entrepreneurship has lagged since the 80-Years War.

131786.text: Is personal armor putting a damper on your fun? Try Detroit's newest hypersonic Polymer jacketed round. That's right, our latest Barrier Breaker Armor Piercing Shells travel so fast you'll hear them break the sound barrier! They can penetrate ceramic armor plating, hull plating, engine blocks, reactor chambers -- you name it.

131825.text: I'm taking a quick break before heading out on the last leg to Pittsburgh with a load of Mining Machinery from Hamilton in Ontario. We pick up Boron for the outbound trip to Bretonia.

131826.text: I left Berlin weeks ago. We were attacked no less than five times. I'm getting too old for this. We usually ship in Cobalt and Copper from Omega-7 bound for Ageira's big plant in Colorado. We also handle Mining Machinery from Hamilton on occasion, bound for Pittsburgh.

131827.text: The Xenos aren't too bad in the southern area of New York. Just Rogues and occasional Outcasts. We Rheinlanders don't have to deal with them too often. Now Corsairs and Red Hessians, that's a different story. I told my dispatcher, "No more of those Omega-7 runs -- I want to live to retirement."

131838.text: ALG disposes of the waste that this shipyard produces. We ship Toxic Waste to Dortmund in New Berlin.

131839.text: Some of the off duty Crews at this shipyard are eager for transport to Manhattan. Our freighters then bring Basic Alloy back .

131840.text: MOX and Ship Hull Panels are brought to this base from their suppliers in Bretonia or Kusari for Deep Space Engineering's use in the construction of ships. Before the Rheinland war we used to handle those supplies.

131869.text: Rheinland Engine Components are the best around. During hte war between Liberty and Rheinland, DSE ship builders have to use Kishiro's or Samura's instead.

131870.text: The Xenos are a thorn in our side at Republican Shipping, and yet the Liberty government does next to nothing to curb their piracy. It is obvious they are being bribed by Liberty corporations who do not want outside competition.

131871.text: We have been the premier Rheinland Shipping firm since before the 80-Years War. Back then we were known as Imperial Shipping, a name we have taken once more to honor the glorious reinstatement of the Emperor. Now we represent our mighty Empire in shipping concerns throughout Sirius.

131908.text: I heard some Bounty Hunters talking about trailing an Outcast in the Tahoe the other day. He lost 'em before they could get close enough. Probably hauling Cardamine. All those scum use it.

131945.text: You'd think Liberty would take advantage of all this potentially valuable Toxic Waste, but they were throwing it out in the debris fields of Texas before we started our program.

131946.text: Running MOX in from Dortmund is pretty risky for us in Liberty. The criminals would love to get their hands on it, especially the Xenos. At least there aren't any of those annoying people in California.

131947.text: California doesn't offer us much in the way of useful Scrap Metal or Toxic Waste. Nothing like the other Liberty systems. Liberty has been very profitable for ALG, which is helpful for our company. During the war between Liberty and Rheinland, the only Rheinland company allowed to cross the border was ALG.

131948.text: I'm pretty new to the Bounty Hunters Guild. They call me a "reformed" Rogue. Spent ten years in Sugarland rolling Sheet Metal. Now I'm out here hunting my old comrades down. At least it's legit work. I can live on a real planet instead of inside a stinky rock somewhere out in an asteroid field.

131949.text: I just got back from Cortez. Did an assault patrol into the Corcovado Field. It's crawling with Rogues. We got a bunch, but there were plenty more. They should send the military in there to clean it out. Its like a rat's nest.

131950.text: This is a good spot for hunting Hackers and Outcasts, probably the best in Liberty space. They all collect in the Tahoe Cloud to the west of the Lane. Happy hunting!

131951.text: The navy guys don't give us access to a lot of this ship. Guess they're suspicious of a lot of the Guild members; a lot of them have done time in Texas. I don't blame 'em, some of the Hunters can be pretty rough looking.

131952.text: Bounty Hunters have a difficult job and we certainly aren't a very popular group, but the best of us are the finest pilots in all of Sirius. Many will look down upon us, because most of our ranks were once criminals, but that is their mistake. It is just as honorable to fall and rise again, than never to fall at all.

131953.text: I'm a second-generation Bounty Hunter. My dad was famous; he made it all the way out to the Edge Worlds before gettin' toasted by those Outcast bastards. Me, I'm going to hunt them down till the day I die. I'm gonna stuff that Cardamine down their throats until they gag.

131954.text: I just got out of West Point last week. This is my first assignment. I'm patrolling the Lane between here and the Cortez Gate. So far it hasn't been as interesting as I thought it would be.

131955.text: We could clean up all the Independent Worlds like Cortez and Magellan in a flash if the other Houses would just let us base our battleships there. Guess they're afraid we'd annex them eventually. Not much there to exploit as far as I can tell.

131956.text: Our toughest patrol in the system is the Tahoe Cloud circuit. We usually see somebody in there. Tough to track them down, though -- short visibility and lots of asteroids.

131957.text: The Outcast smuggling route goes right along the Trade Lane in the Tahoe Cloud for some reason. We've caught a few that way. Guess they can't resist the temptation to snag some cargo.

131958.text: We handle the west side of the Trade Lane to the Magellan Gate, LPI, the east. In my opinion, we should handle everything in there. They wouldn't know what to do with a Lane Hacker or an Outcast if they caught one.

131959.text: I just got reassigned from the Mississippi based in Texas. We were in Hudson chasing down Xenos and Rogues. The Rheinland Military doesn't help at all in that area. Guess they're broke.

131960.text: I'm doing patrols into Cortez. We usually just hang around at the Gate, but sometimes we venture down to Curacao. After that the convoys are on their own. I call it the "Cortez gap."

131961.text: We could clean up this second if the Guild would just tell us where the Jump Holes are. We know one is in the Tahoe Cloud, but have been unable to locate it. New York doesn't let us vary our patrol routes as much as we would like.

131962.text: I don't know what they're doing on that research base Willard. I hear it's something with those Nomad remains they ship in from the Omicrons. I never have figured out how exactly they obtain the samples, or who provides them.

131963.text: I hope one day to get assigned a shipment of H-Fuel from Okinawa. The fighters based off the battleships all need H-Fuel for patrols. I'd like to see Kusari for myself one day.

131964.text: I'm hoping my transport doesn't get requisitioned for a Prisoner convoy to Texas. Your transport smells for weeks after one of those trips.

131965.text: I'm based in Detroit. Just making my monthly rounds to all the police and military bases to deliver Side Arms to the new recruits. At least there aren't any of those pesky Xenos in California.

131986.text: I love it out here. I grew up on Houston, but I always dreamed about going to the Barrier. It's so beautiful in the skies of Liberty. Who would've known it was chock-full of nasties? I use this as my base for popping into Magellan. I'd rather have the LPI as roommates than the criminals on those Freeports.

131988.text: The Guild does a regular "fishing" trip into the Cloud every day. We usually snag something. A Rogue or two -- once in a while you get an Outcast. Like catching one of those giant black two-finned sharks they have on Curacao. You have to let it run the line till it tires out.

131989.text: They say if you want to get in with the Outcasts, get friendly with the Rogues. Then graduate to the Lane Hackers. Run some drugs. Then you're on your way. Hard to turn back at that point, since you'll be a Cardamine addict for life.

131991.text: The Corsairs are a tough lot. Best chance to get in with them is with the Junkers. Whatever you do, stay away from the Hessian and Outcast alliances. As I said, hard to do.

131992.text: Talk about bad luck... I got posted here six months ago. LPI shouldn't even be here. This is practically Border World territory. We got a huge cloud full of nasties separating us from civilization. Can't just go for a pleasure run to Los Angeles.

131993.text: They send all the problem people here, literally to kill you. Our western patrol goes right into the thick of the cloud west of the Lane. I've seen more than one of my buddies disappear in a puff of smoke. One moment they're joking with you about their next vacation, next thing, poof!

131994.text: They set up this border station to keep a watch on the Magellan Gate, since it's so isolated from everything else in the system. Then some genius planetside decided that we needed to do patrols into the Tahoe Cloud.

131995.text: The eastern patrol goes through some old abandoned paths from the ice mining days. Then it loops back towards the Trade Lane. I just grit my teeth the whole way and hope that no baddies show up on radar.

131996.text: I'm just countin' the days. I got thirty-two left before I go back to a life. The attrition rate here is real bad. So far, twenty guys this month got vaporized by Outcasts, Hackers, or Rogues. That's some bad odds. I need to look for a new line of work if I make it through this.

131997.text: I may as well join the Bounty Hunters if I'm going to get posts like this. When they told me back on Sugarland that there was a combat opening in California, I jumped at the chance. Now I know why. I was replacing some other fool who lasted all of three days.

131998.text: Just dropping off some basic supplies from Los Angeles. We usually stop at Willard first. Today we're bringing in Food, Oxygen, Water, and H-Fuel. I'm getting out of here as fast as I can.

131999.text: They ordered some Side Arms, so we're obliging. I wish they could just come to Los Angeles to pick them up; it would make life a lot easier. I guess the replacement rate for new recruits is pretty high, so they need a lot of new issues on Side Arms.

132000.text: I guess the Universal contract with LPI and the navy is real lucrative. Half the time we're flying half-empty. I don't care. Just give me my paycheck. At least the pirates don't hassle us too much.

132040.text: ALG ships Toxic Waste from the prison station reactors to our processing facility in Rheinland. There we process it into useable MOX.

132041.text: Liberty's need is our gain. The war with Kusari prevented BMM from expanding their waste disposal business, and we took advantage of that to increase our services to Liberty.

132042.text: The Xenos in this system make themselves a constant problem to us. The fools do not understand that without our services Liberty could not safely dispose of radioactive materials and other Toxic Waste. More aggravating is that Liberty authorities do not seem to take the Xeno threat seriously.

132067.text: Republican ships goods from this base to the heart of Bretonia: New London. Nanocapacitors are sent to Southampton Shipyard for use in the contruction of new ships.

132068.text: We bring H-Fuel to Pennsylvania from this planet. Bethlehem, Erie, and Harrisburg are all solid customers.

132069.text: Republican ships Nanocapacitors to Denver, and we then pick up with Superconductors bound for the Southampton Shipyard in New London.

132070.text: Many of the Commodities traded here are shipped to Bretonia. From Houston we ship Nanocapacitors to New London, Cambridge, and Leeds.

132071.text: Many of the stations in the Newcastle system are consumers for Nanocapacitors. Gateshead, Lancaster, and Scarborough are all on my route.

132101.text: The Xenos must be destroyed at all costs -- they make it difficult for non-Liberty corporations to do their jobs here. Perhaps if Liberty does not care about this problem, we will begin letting them take care of their own waste problems.

132102.text: Somehow we lost the Toxic Waste contract for this battleship. So far as I can tell, they just dump it into the Texas star now. What a waste.

132103.text: ALG has had to take some of the profits gained from doing business in this sector to pay Bounty Hunters for protection. There are all manner of criminals in this system, and this last leg of our journey is usually the most dangerous. So a little protection from the Bounty Hunters is always welcome.

132122.text: You can find good Scrap Metal in this system. As the radiation slowly dies down, more and more of it will be accessible to us.

132124.text: Though the Rogues try to be friends with the Xenos, the simple truth is that they are friends with no one and nothing but money and Cardamine. So if the Xenos start becoming too troublesome, we pay a few Rogues to go bag a couple.

132131.text: We are a Rheinland company committed to disposing of all of Sirius' waste. Just think of the future when there will be no more toxic radiation areas in space, no more debris fields for criminals to hide in. All of Sirius will be clean, thanks to ALG.

132132.text: Our transports will pick up Toxic Waste from Norfolk and Baltimore in New York and bring them here to await pick up by ALG, which will transport it to Rheinland for processing.

132133.text: We bring HazMat Canisters to store the Toxic Waste produced by the reactors aboard this manufacturing platform, then take the Toxic Waste produced here back to our facilities in Rheinland to be reprocessed into new MOX fuel pellets -- a highly efficient process that is more cost-effective than that used at LD-14 in Leeds.

132149.text: The smelters that work our metal works are oftentimes well-trained before they come here. A lot of these prisoners were legitimate factory workers who got tired of working for a pittance; now they work for free.

132152.text: From Denver we bring Pharmaceuticals to administer to the inmates. Of course, we make more money hauling Commodities from Bretonia and Kusari, but the supplemental income from these smaller runs is worth our valuable time.

132153.text: I shouldn't tell you this, but there is a thriving market in Synthetic Marijuana on board this station.

132154.text: There is no system in Rheinland with this much widespread crime and violence. And we certainly don't have any dark matter pockets like the ones found here. Also look at all the debris. This system is the armpit of Sirius.

132186.text: Southampton is a strategic base for the Armed Forces. It is a major production and maintenance center for our capital ships, and a large industrial center for all of Bretonia, especially now that Stokes and Leeds are behind enemy lines. While the police run patrols along the lanes, the Armed Forces have some heavier assets here to deter enemies from raiding Southampton directly.

132187.text: Cardamine use is also on the rise in New London. We once thought it was exclusively a problem in Liberty. Outcasts have been sighted in the debris fields and along the Trade Lanes near the Leeds Jump Gate, presumably engaged in smuggling and piracy activities. We've also noticed them entangled with the Gallics forces in Leeds and the Tau systems.

132188.text: The Armed Forces have several patrols near key bases and planets throughout Bretonia. This is mainly to deter pirates from disrupting the local economy. But the Armed Forces don't have the assets to deal with both local pirates and the Gallic menace at once. So the Trade Lanes have become the police's responsibility. I don't know if they'll be up to the challeng though. The Corsairs have given them a lot of grief.

132189.text: Frankly, the Bretonian Armed Forces fell behind Kusari and Liberty in terms of military prowess. Look where it got us - invaded, twice, and now even Rheinland is making a military statement with that battleship of theirs in Omega-7.

132190.text: Most of the times we get entangled with criminal raiders, they're coming out of the debis field. Standing orders are to not pursue them too far within. The field is a mess of volatile debris and radioactive hazards, with too many places for criminals to hide. Southampton would be a lot safer if we cleaned that mess up, but the priority right now is beating back Gallia.

132191.text: We've noticed a marked increase in New London Artifact availability and a corresponding drop in price since the Corsairs arrived. The Junkers are suspected in importing the banned trinkets, but they're difficult to catch red-handed. Still, once the war is over and this scrap field is cleared, I think the need for Junkers in Bretonia will be long past.

132192.text: Welcome to the Bridge. That's what we call this part of Southampton, which houses the bulk of the factories and processing plants. And just when you thought we couldn't get much bigger, we get half of Stokes welded onto us to boot... Suppose we've got the Gauls to "thank" for that one.

132193.text: The loss of Leeds Planet has been disastrous for the BMM. A few space stations is one thing, but Leeds housed over half of the entire Bretonian industrial infrastructure. Sure, we'll manage, we always do. But this is going to take some mighty rebuilding.

132194.text: Just when you thought we could catch a break... Stokes is gone, and this time, we won't be back in Leeds any time soon. Good thing the higher ups figured this would happen and moved much of the important gear onto the Bridge, here. Still, just haphazardly moving huge station components tends to cause problems. Not to mention raw material shortages. There's very little left in New London, mineral wise. We'll have to find new sources, fast, or we'll be done for.

132195.text: Those Gaians are a bunch of upper-class Cambridge snobs that don't have their heads screwed on straight. I would welcome a new planet to live on. We'll need a new place to settle down if we lose Leeds. I bet the Gaians will make trouble over Nottingham next.

132196.text: The Mollys are always sittin' out in the Southampton or Cumbria Fields waiting for some poor BMM bloke to come along, just minding his own business. A nasty lot, they are. Good thing that most anyone you ask feels the same way about 'em. 'Xept maybe those IMG traitors out on Hood.

132197.text: Those Junkers are bad for this area. Ever since they showed up we've been getting Outcasts. Now the Corsairs are starting to arrive. They should go in and clean them out. Seems like they can never catch them red-handed, but there's plenty o' reason to space the lot of em.

132198.text: I've been looking for a new place to move my family too. They used to live on Leeds, but I managed to get them off to my friends place on New London before the Gallic armada arrived. Now I've done a deal with a trade captain to move them to Rheinland. I hope they'll be safe there.

132199.text: New London used to be the mining center of Bretonia. Cornwall, Devon, Somerset, and Cumbria were all famous in their day. Those fields employed hundreds of thousands of the Bretonian working class. Now they import everything from the Border Worlds. Everyone's had to migrate out there in search of the work.

132200.text: I'm a third-generation Yardie here on Southampton. We've built all of Bretonia's great ships ever since anyone can remember. My ancestors have worked here for hundreds of years.

132201.text: The Junkers are a slimy set. They like to come and steal from our storage depots when no one is looking. We had to arm them, we did. Was a real shock to the lads that tried to pry them open shortly after we installed a few blasters on them. And to think that the Junkers used to be proper Yardies - what a shame.

132202.text: Let me tell you, this is right in the thick of it as far as bad guys in Bretonia. You've got Gaians and Corsairs in the Devon Field, Mollys coming in from the Cumbria, and everyone imaginable in the Southampton Debris Field.

132204.text: I'm a former Molly that saw the light in Newgate. I won't go after my old comrades, I prefer to hunt the foreign invaders of our space like the Corsairs and Outcasts. I also don't mind to nab the odd Gaian - those guys have thrown their lot in with both the Corsairs and the Gallics. Feels right to make them suffer for that.

132206.text: You don't get much of a bounty for Gaians. The Corsairs and the Outcasts are a different matter. Bag one of them and you'll be taking it easy for a while. Problem is, they ain't the easiest marks to take down.

132207.text: I used to work these fields - know 'em like the back of my hand. That's what gives me the edge against the baddies. Gotta watch out for those gas pockets. They're in most of the fields in this system. They got them marked, but not everyone pays attention.

132208.text: On our trips from Pittsburg we bring in the Boron they use for the Hull Panels. We also pick up Superconductors and Optical Chips in Los Angeles every other trip. Those are used for engine combustion chambers and avionics.

132209.text: Running the MOX in from Birmingham can be a real nail biter. Rumor has it that the Mollys are trying to steal some to make a bomb. After the mess a large dirty bomb made on Cambridge, we're none to keen on letting those brutes make off with any.

132210.text: With Glasgow gone, Bowex has had to move it's base of operations. Most of the auxiliary staff and executives are running the company from New London, but the most important base we have right now is Scarborough. Aside from civilian shipbuilding and maintenance facilities which keeps Southampton free for our military, it has become the home for BMM's Super Alloying plants. Those were moved when Kusari threatened to breach Leeds, quite a few months ago.

132211.text: We just started shipping High-Temperature Alloys from ALG's Wuppertal plant to Southampton. BMM normally doesn't give us the time of day, but they'd like to get a cheaper supplier and be less dependent on those arrogant Republican shippers. Besides, with the war going the way it does, they can't affort to be picky. In some matters, we're all Bretonians first, and competitors second.

132212.text: We don't get hassled by pirates nearly as much as our competitors do. Our allies, the IMG, get along pretty well with the Mollys and the Hessians. That's a big advantage for us in the Omega Border World Trade Lane routes to Rheinland. Of course, we still have to deal with the Corsairs.

132213.text: I'm headed back out to Kensington as soon as I can. I don't like having to deal with BMM, as they get fed by the same spoon that feeds Bowex. But there's really no way around Southampton when you're a serious shipper in Bretonia. It is the main industrial facility in the capitol.

132214.text: They are unloading my ship right now. We ship Optronics and Engine Components from Honshu on a regular basis, but the route is a lot longer now that we need to go over Liberty. You should visit my homeland sometime. It's very beautiful. The lovely blue clouds of the Crow Nebula surround my system.

132215.text: Kishiro is a progressive company. We are much more innovative than Samura, which uses its influence to resist change rather than embrace it. Our willingness to adapt to changing situations has bore fruit: We now are the sole shipping partner for the Gas Miners Guild, a very lucrative contract.

132216.text: The Outcasts are very troublesome. Ever since we opened our Hydrocarbon and Polymer plant in Tau-29, they have become very aggressive. Their ilk seems to be everywhere - Liberty, Bretonia, the Sigmas and our homeland are all blighted by their presence.

132217.text: Republican has been providing High-Temperature Alloys to the Sirius Sector for centuries. We still dominate this specialty, aided by our easy access to the raw materials of the Walker Nebula in Dresden and Omega-7. Daumann manufactures these alloys, but ALG has been trying to gain ground in this market as well.

132218.text: I noticed that the Kusari transports are unloading Engine Components also. Do you wonder where they get all the raw materials to produce those components from? That's right, Rheinland, since Kusari has no mineral resources whatsoever in those clouds of theirs. I'll have to let our execs know, we may need to take some measures against this.

132219.text: The route for Republican through the Omega Border Worlds is very difficult - but with the Tau route gone, Kusari shippers are at a disadvantage now. Rheinland is finally back in the position it deserves to be - delivering the most durable alloys and engine components at the best rates.

132220.text: This is just a quick stop for our ship. We're dropping off a load of H-Fuel from Osaka in the Honshu system. We'll be heading back up to Scarborough to pick up our return cargo, which is Super Alloys for Yokohama.

132221.text: Bretonia's not too dangerous. At least compared to Kusari space and the Independent Worlds we now must cross. The Blood Dragons are the most serious menace with Kusari. The Outcasts, Lane Hackers and Xenos replace them as the threat once you leave Shikoku.

132222.text: The most valuable Commodity Bretonia has to offer us is Gold. We use it in our ship construction site at Yokohama for coating windows. There are very few sources for Gold in Sirius, the metal is quite rare.

132223.text: We're just making a pit stop to unload some Superconductors. Then it's back to Waterloo for a little break before heading home to Trenton. It's kind of polluted here in Bretonia - and I thought New York was bad.

132224.text: Universal doesn't bother hauling stuff past the capitol systems like New London. We let the local shippers take over. They can have the Border Worlds, as far as we're concerned. Insurance premiums go up quite a bit. The only time we go into the Border Worlds is when we need to deliver Gate or Lane Parts to a DSE construction site.

132225.text: This Southampton yard is impressive - lots of stalls, and it's quite a hub of activity right now. They call this section "The Bridge," which sounds kind of optimistic to me. It just looks a little... haphazard. But that might just be me being used to clean, well-planned DSE constructs.

132342.text: The day after BMM signed the aluminium supply contract with Daumann, the miners called off the strike, but it was too late. The BMM number crunchers had already concluded that even with the added cost of shipment from Rheinland, Daumann could supply aluminium cheaper than BMM could mine and refine bauxite here on Planet Leeds. You should have seen those miners' faces when they found out that they were all out of a job. It could be worse, at least they weren't transferred to LD-14.

132343.text: For months and months every time you tuned into a holofeed you saw some politician calling on the patriotic citizens of Bretonia to make sacrifices for the common good, and to unite for the defeat of the Kusari invaders. I guess the bauxite miners here on Leeds figured that there was no more need for sacrifice or patriotism once Kusari withdrew. The same day BMM returned to Stokes the miners went on strike.

132344.text: Planet Leeds was BMM's main source for bauxite, which is refined to remove the pure aluminium. The strike went on so long that our stockpiles were exhausted. Then, Daumann shows up with guarantees of regular shipments. With the government demanding that Stokes get back to full manufacturing capacity for ship hull panels immediately, BMM had no choice but to sign a supply contract with Daumann.

132345.text: Bowex ships basic supplies throughout this system, keeping several Leeds bases equipped. I fly Oxygen, Water, and Food to York, Glasgow, and Durham. It might be a short jaunt, but I lose escorts every week.

132346.text: I have a couple of friends in Parliament, and I've heard them mention that there is some back room talk about the government cutting off funding for the Planet Harris terraforming project. With first Kusari and now Gallia threatening Tau-31, it doesn't look like such a good investment anymore. You know what, maybe Gallia should try it's hand at terraforming. It can't do any worse than Planetform has.

132347.text: If the government cuts off funding for Planetform's Harris project, I don't know how that company will survive. With Perth Station in Gallic hands, their Bretonian operations would be all but finished. I need to call my broker and dump my Planetform shares before they're worthless.

132348.text: Planetform is touting a breakthrough new product that they're manufacturing in Liberty, but Planetform press releases aren't worth the bytes they're transmitted with, if you ask me. If that company's promises could be believed, Harris would have been feeding Sirius all by itself a decade ago. Instead, it's still importing food rations.

132349.text: Do you see that smog out there? You know why we have that smog? This used to be an industrial powerhouse. Now it's just a way station for people fleeing from whichever armada happens to be attacking Leeds at the moment. First Kusari, now Gallia, what's next? Little green men? Oh, right, I forgot. We already have Gaians.

132350.text: Just between you and me, the reason BMM was so anxious to get back onto Stokes had nothing to do with the "precision machinery" they were always lamenting having lost to Kusari. What they were really unhappy about was having to do business on Planet Leeds, where the unions and government bureaucracy could just drop in unannounced and inspect their operations. Up there on the space station, all those visits have to be scheduled days in advance, and the head honchos can make sure the wrong things aren't exposed to view. Corporate responsibility is just a slogan. Just take a look at the sky outside if you doubt me.

132351.text: Any chance you can cram any of these Refugees into your ship when you leave? I hear that Liberty is resettling them on Planet Pittsburgh. These Refugees are either half-starved, or they seem to have swiped everything in sight before they escaped. Between the depressed wages due to the excess labor, and the sky high prices being charged to gouge the Refugees with fat wallets, the Leeds economy is going down the toilet. Matter of fact, maybe I should catch a lift on your ship myself.

132352.text: You ever want to head into Kusari space? It's quite a different bag of socks, I'll be the first to say. But if you want to get out there and see Sirius, like every young buck, then off ya go to Narita. We need their Optronics here at this base.

132353.text: Look, every bobby knows that Gaians smell like week old socks, never trust a Mollys' golden grin because his mate is sneaking up behind you with a laserdrill, and you can't turn your back on your meal while there's a Corsair in the room. But what's with those Lane Hackers? We busted up some piracy they were doing on the lane to Planet Leeds a few days ago, and I got called names with so many syllables I thought those Hackers must have been having seizures. Maybe it was cardamine withdrawal or something.

132354.text: If you fly your ship through either one of the smog clouds in this system, get it washed before you touch it. The industrial waste you're flying through is highly acidic and though it might not do a great deal to your ship, it'll burn through your skin in seconds.

132355.text: The Bretonian Police patrol this sector for unlawful activity. The military takes care of the northern part of Leeds mostly around the Trade Lanes leading to Tau-31 and LD-14. It's more of a military matter protecting the processed MOX nuclear fuel produced at the plant there.

132356.text: I always believed in what the Gaians were fighting for; I just didn't like the way they went about doing things. I didn't take them as seriously as the others -- just rich kids ya know. Well, that all changed a few months ago when they zapped my mate on a routine patrol. We weren't even in attack formation -- just flying by -- and they opened up on us. Roger's ship imploded before I could blink.

132357.text: The Bretonian Police aren't like them Liberty coppers you'll find glossing it up in New York. No sir, we don't take bribes and we don't take it easy. If you break the law in Bretonia, you're going to pay. That I promise you.

132358.text: I patrol down the south side near the New London Jump Gate. I know that them damn criminals are making a way into our capital system somehow; I just wish I knew where. I make certain that they don't slip past me into the Jump Gate.

132359.text: My folks and their ancestors all come from Leeds. We've been workin' the foundries in my family as long as I can remember -- except me. My father was always moaning about getting the rake from BMM, so I figured I'd get out from under that thumb. I apprenticed myself to a freelancer and learned to fly. After a bit I took the opportunity to join the authorities.

132360.text: I enjoy doing my job and putting away the malcontents, but I wouldn't do it in Dublin. No lad, them Mollys will blow a hole in you the size o' the West Smog. I'll take 'em in smaller doses right here.

132361.text: The Outcasts make their appearance in this system quite often. This is part of their route into center Sirius and Bretonia with that blasted Cardamine they peddle. They are tough ones I don't like to tangle with -- makes me doubt my pension.

132362.text: In Tau-31 there is a base named Holman. Gateway used to ship them supplies once a week before the war with Kusari. We thought that after Kusari withdrew from Leeds these supply runs would resume, but now that there is a Gallic battleship in Tau-31, nobody knows what is going to happen.

132363.text: Kensington buys some of the Mining Machinery produced in Leeds. It is a nice, easy run once you make it past the smog clouds and are about to hit the Jump Gates. Of course, making it past the smog clouds is the trick, isn't it? All manner of scoundrel lay in wait for you in there.

132364.text: Ever heard the saying "Keep your head down"? Of course you have, but it doesn't seem like it would matter in a spaceship, does it? I mean either you decompress or you don't, right? No head ducking is gonna save you if the hull caves in. Well, that's what I used to think until the last run I made. Old Charles, my tail gunner, got his head taken off by a chunk of metal that blew free of a relay panel on my ship. Charlie always was a bit too tall.

132365.text: You know how far I have to fly to deliver this H-Fuel to this base? It is a long way across Sirius at the Ogashawa Refinery in Sigma-19. Here's the worst part -- I have to get through Outcasts to get into Kusari space, and then I deal with the pirates there, including the Hogosha and the Golden Chrysanthemums. Finally I get through all that and have to fly through the Border Worlds on the other side of Kusari space. Guess who attacks me there? That's right, more Outcasts.

132366.text: We ship Optronics to this base from Honshu. It is better than having to ship H-Fuel here, which is a longer flight. Don't misunderstand. It is a long and dangerous flight from Honshu. Any travel across the Border Worlds is risky.

132367.text: When you cross Kusari space you have to be careful of the Hogosha. You are Gaijin and therefore unprotected, and I have to be careful because I work for Kishiro. Yet Samura does not have to be wary of the Hogosha. What does that tell you?

132368.text: Care to make a jaunt into Tau-31? Planetform needs Commodities at its base, and though we do our best to ship them everything, they always want more. Ah, I can hear the damn supply master whining in my ear even now, and he's a Jump Gate away. You'll find him at Harris. He always needs more Construction and Mining Machinery.

132369.text: I'm just glad I was on the first transport off Harris after Kusari pulled back. Now that Gallia has a battleship in Tau-31, there's no telling what is going to happen. Some Planetform officials are even talking about evacuating the planet. That would be suicidal for our Bretonian operations.

132370.text: Planetform is working on making another planet for Bretonia to grow crops in. Cambridge is helping to alleviate the Food shortage in this sector of space, but it is only a temporary fix. If we don't create more arable land, then Bretonia will have major Food shortages within two hundred years. That is a fact, at least according to our data.

132371.text: The Mollys here in this system are quite disturbing -- so vicious they remind me of the Blood Dragons in Kusari space. I have to fly food and basic commodities to our stranded forces in Newcastle. Have you ever touched your ship after flying through a smog cloud? Well, don't do it. I hate this place, and I hate Bretonia.

132372.text: The Gallic invasion has left many of our soldiers cut off from home. And now those accursed traitors backed by Kishiro have rebelled against the Emperor? Disgraceful. Once this Gallic threat has been dealt with, they will all be put to the sword, every last one of them.

132373.text: I keep hearing about the Gaians and I know they operate in this system, but I have not seen any yet. Perhaps the Gallic forces have destroyed them all. There's a rumor going around that a system occupied by them was the first Bretonian system to be hit by the invading Gallic navy.

132374.text: Welcome to... what was this place called again? Stokes? Ach, I'm sure we will think of a proper name for an industrial facility like this once the dust has settled. If this is your first visit, don't go wandering without an escort. Some sections of the station are not yet safe.

132375.text: The Bretonians used this facility to produce different kinds of alloys and Ship Hull Panels, but when our Navy took posession, all that was left were a few partially scuttled smelters. I think the Bretonians willingly ceded this base. Aside from the station core and a few storage silos - empty ones - there was nothing here.

132376.text: We have repaired one of the smelters and can now process some raw materials, but getting those is another story. The nearby asteroid field isn't safe yet - there are Bretonian saboteurs lurking in there, just waiting for us to bring in our mining fleet. The resources mined in Tau-23 are likely the ones that will be brought here.

132377.text: Bretonians know how to build something to last, I'll give them that. Not many space stations could take the abuse of being conquered trice and survive. Sure, there are parts missing, but the integrity of the station core is sound. We'll need to make some modifications to the station power grid so it will run on our fuel, but after that, this could become an important forward production center. The station core could even support a drydock.

132378.text: I'm not a soldier. GMS refused to send employees into the system until the fighting was over. Sure, there are some skirmishes here and there still, but that is minor, not unlike the Brigand raids back home. We can survive those.

132379.text: This station has potential, but not in the short term. Aside from the difficulties of making Bretonian technology compatible with ours, it will take a lot of supplies to bring this station back online fully. Unless the war is put on hold, that isn't likely to happen soon. Our own transport fleet can't handle that volume, and IDF is tasked with supplying the frontline, they don't have the capacity either.

132380.text: I'm a mining prospector brought in from Isle de France. I was supposed to be surveying the asteroid field east of this base for exploitable resources, but that operation has been put on hold indefinitely. Bretonians and pirates both seem to inhabit that field, which makes going in there unescorted suicide. Until we get a better understanding of what hostiles are in there, prospecting and mining are out of the question.

132381.text: According to our various reports, this station used to produce Basic Alloys and some extra strong Super Alloys. I think we can get Basic Alloy production going again once we have a stable supply of Aluminium. That alloy isn't hard to make, but it forms the core of almost all constructions these days, so producing it here would save us hauling tons of it from home.

132382.text: The state of this system is truly appalling. True, Gallia has its own debris fields - but we would not be so reckless that we would vent Toxic Waste directly into nebulas for decades! At least package it and shoot it into the nearest star to burn up. All these idiot Bretonians have done is give their future generation a mess to clean up.

132383.text: I came across an old pad that had fallen in a floor grate. Some personal messages from one of the people that used to manage this station, apparantly.
