Nothing important, but it does give you a feel for the kind of person he was. Most of the things I've read would be grounds for immediate dismissal in the GMS.

132384.text: This pad I found just keeps getting better and better. I think I might see about passing it on to the Navy, to see if they can use it down on Leeds - I wonder how much support the Bretonian government would have when it comes out that their aristocracy feels that, and I quote, "the common rabble down on Leeds exists to work, and if need be, perish for their betters".

132385.text: We had to push some of the debris that was once part of this station out into the asteroid field. Some of those pieces are large, and if they impact the intact portion of the station they could do considerable damage. There's also the chance that Bretonia had them rigged. We're not bothering to salvage something like that, it is easier to rebuild those modules from scratch using proper Gallic technology.

132386.text: There are a lot of wrecks floating around this station. Kusari, Bretonian... and to a lesser extent, ours. Some of them predate our navy's invasion. Kusari and Bretonia weakened themselves considerably prior to our arrival, which made our advance a lot easier.

132387.text: The Tau worlds are incredably rich in resources - much more so then any Gallic deposits. I don't get why our Navy didn't chose to seize and fortify them. Between that planet in Tau-31 and the riches in Tau-23 and Tau-29, we could have fueled Gallic industry for another three centuries at least. Instead the Navy goes here, further away from home, ever closer to the heart of those we made enemies. They'd better hope Kusari doesn't hit the flank, or else we might be the ones finding ourselves behind enemy lines.

132388.text: This station was described as one of the big prizes of Leeds, one of the reasons why this system had to be captured quickly. Not quickly enough, it seems, Bretonia has evacuated anything of real value. We won't have the production capabilities on the front we had hoped for. Not the most ideal outcome, but we planned for this.

132389.text: Judging from the age of some of the wreckage and intelligence reports, Kusari captured this station in their own attack on the system. A pity, that weakened the Bretonian resolve to defend here most likely. They were willing to abandon it without a significant battle and concentrated their forces around the planet. It was harder to dislodge them, but we had the forces to overpower them.

132390.text: The docking bays are still sound, but civilian bays aren't very useful to a military force. They are mostly designed with more "cost-effective" berths and bays designed for rapid cargo transfers, not combat repair docks that service multiple fighters. As such, turning stations over to corporate control as part of their contracts to support the military is sensible.

132391.text: The sooner the civilians can get this place operational again, the better. We can't keep relying on importing from Gallia forever. As we push deeper into enemy territory that supply line keeps getting longer. There comes a point when that becomes unmanagable. I hate to say it, but if we can't capture Leeds somewhat intact, the push towards Liberty is going to stall out. What we've encountered so far isn't encouraging.

132392.text: Stripped to the bulkhead. Bretonian architecture maybe? I jest of course, but all three stations in this system show signs of extensive sabotage and salvage. I bet if they'd fit through the Jump Gates, Bretonia would have tried slapping thrusters at them and pushing them trough. Oui, another jest, Jump travel would tear any station apart. Too much mass.

132393.text: I am not impressed with Bretonian space-based construction. Of the four stations we've encountered so far, two have parts that have gone missing, one is permanently on fire, and the other will make you glow like a Metz Wisp.

132394.text: So, Bretonia resorts to demolishing their own gates now? All the better, they will need to be rebuilt anyway. A Vache barely fits through one of those tiny Sirian gates. Sirian. Small. It should not come as a surprise I suppose.

132395.text: Well, the Navy told us to expect an industrial station to be captured in the initial push to Leeds, and they did not disappoint on that promise. Too bad it is a totally stripped down station. All we have is one smelter of questionable integrity still operational. No production capabilities to speak of. We've got some work to do here.

132396.text: GMS and EFL will probably both be operating parts of this facility once it is repaired. GMS specializes in alloying and refining, EFL in heavy industrial production. Both are integral components to a large facility like this. Our first job will be to get the Hull Panel production restored, as producing those locally will reduce the strain on our supply line significantly. It will mean reconstructing the modules that handled material alloying, and the Hull Panel production plant itself. The remains of the old one are floating roughly a kilometer away.

132397.text: It is going to be a gargantuan job to get this station up and running again. Truth be told, the company isn't too thrilled about investing in this place. The Bretonians couldn't defend it, twice. Should we ever get attacked in earnest here, who is to say it wouldn't fall trice? I doubt we can entice the Navy to have the Carcassonne relocated here.

132398.text: Some in the Guild are hoping that Bretonia lays bounties on Gallic forces if they enter Leeds. It would certainly go a long way to improving our financial situation, but on the other hand, the Guild has been successful largely by making sure not to irritate any of the House governments by taking sides in their wars. We aren't mercenaries, and if we start acting like mercenaries, then we're going to have to be prepared to be executed like mercenaries if we back the losing side.

132399.text: Bounty hunting is a very different occupation than soldiering. Bounty hunters can follow orders, but at the end of the day, we are in it for the credits, not the glory. A tactical retreat is always in our best interests. That's not the case with the military. If we somehow get pulled into fighting the BAF's war with Gallia, I don't want to get killed because some Admiral needs more time for his own withdrawal. I signed up for a payday, not a posthumous medal for valor.

132415.text: It's a quick jaunt up from Leeds. We have to bring all the essentials up here, like life support gases, Food -- the usual. Nobody bothers us most of the time.

132416.text: Bowex handles shipping to the Border Worlds to keep this base running. I don't make the shipments; I leave that to the pilots who enjoy danger. We deliver Pharmaceuticals and Consumer Goods to Freeport 6 and return with Fertilizers and Alien Organisms.

132417.text: Ever think about traveling to foreign lands? Do you enjoy white-knuckle danger? Well this station could always use more H-Fuel. We get it from Osaka in Honshu. While you are buried in the middle of Kusari space you might as well stop and pick up some Optronics and Engine Components from Narita in New Tokyo. We buy them at a good price here.

132418.text: Cambridge may be the breadbasket of Bretonia, but they need their Fertilizers to grow all that food, which is where Bowex comes in. We make the return trip with Consumer Goods bound for Freeport 6 and points beyond.

132419.text: Once we get past the smog clouds to the south it is a pretty easy flight into New London. Bowex delivers Optronics and Engine Components to Southampton. Then we head to New London to drop off H-Fuel, often loading Pharmaceuticals for the return.

132420.text: Glasgow has served as our company headquarters and shipping portal to the Border Worlds for centuries. It is now used mainly as a fuel distribution point for northern Bretonia, although in the past it contained most of the corporate offices. New London is now the center of operations.

132421.text: I was raised in this system and was smart enough to get out of the smelters. It is a dead end to try and be a part of BMM. They will use you up and throw you away, just like they did with this system. Look around you. Does this place look like the work of conscientious people? Some say it was Bretonia's only choice. I think there is always another way.

132422.text: We have been serving Sirius since 66 AS. That makes us one of the oldest surviving companies in Bretonia. We didn't get this far by being easy on our competitors and enemies. That irritating upstart, Gateway, will fail soon enough. Our influential friends in London will make sure of that.

132423.text: We are experts at shipping between Kusari and Bretonia. It has been this way for several centuries, and though it was Bretonia's industry that kept the system alive, Bowex was the life blood of Bretonia's industrial prowess. Remember that the next time you encounter some Gateway trash trying to haul scrap across Bowex space.

132424.text: This base trades in Alien Organisms and H-Fuel, two Commodities we need in our operations in Perth. We prefer to ship these vital project Commodities ourselves, but qualified freelancers are welcome to do the job. It is a good way to make money, if traveling into Gaian territory doesn't bother you.

132425.text: The Gaians in this system are losing more of their numbers everyday to our Bounty Hunters. Planetform will not be beaten by pseudo-intellectual rabble. Although they are still very strong in Edinburgh, we will overcome them in time.

132426.text: If it weren't for the Green Front, the Gaian political action group, funds wouldn't be available to conduct their operations. Why this political cabal is not persecuted by the Bretonian government is beyond my understanding. The terrorists in this group are not protesters; they are murderers and deserve to be dealt with accordingly.

132427.text: I run the marine contingent on this base. It's one of the worst duties you can pull. If you get sent here, someone up top really hates you. They can't send the dregs here you know, so we have an important job to do.

132428.text: Everyone stationed at this base has it bad for the Mollys. The ones that get captured don't survive long enough to be shipped out of here. The last one we captured was found the next morning in his cell with two pieces of MOX where his eyes used to be.

132429.text: We come across the Outcasts at this base occasionally. I think they are just passing through, but we are bound by duty to engage them. They are one tough fight. Their ships are better than ours -- makes me a bit angry to think about that -- but I do what I have to.

132430.text: Bounty Hunters refuse to come to this base. I can't say that I blame them, but I'm glad they don't. We have enough criminals in these parts as it is. Most Bounty Hunters have done a turn or two at one of our prisons. How do you think they know all the underworld secrets that they do?

132431.text: Once a pilot has completed a tour of duty at this base he gets his choice of assignments. Most go right to New London. I've got three months left of duty left here. I transferred in with six others, all pretty green. I'm the only one left. Mollys and Outcasts killed the rest of my mates. I try not to make friends here anymore; I just do my job.

132432.text: I like to fly out into the fields alone. I fight best solo. I don't have to worry about some stupid kid just out of the academy getting more of our equipment destroyed. It's dangerous, though -- no one to watch your back if you get jumped by a pair of Outcasts or Mollys.

132433.text: BMM ships the majority of its basic supplies from Leeds to this base. Let me tell you, it is a relief to see those weapon platforms encircling this base when I'm bringing in a load of supplies.

132434.text: I'm waiting here to meet the BMM replacement pilot who will be taking the place of John Gibbs, the chap who used to make the run from Southampton with Toxic Waste. He got jumped by a couple of Mollys. They say the first shot that went through his shields hit a Toxic Waste container. No more John Gibbs, unless you count the tiny little chunks floating in space.

132435.text: Stokes Smelter, just down the Trade Lane, provides most of our raw materials here, beyond the Uranium itself. They do the run every week, slipping in a Toxic Waste shipment on occasion to keep the Mollys guessing.

132436.text: You know what the workers at this base call it? Heh, they call it "short time." It's a fitting name. The employees who work here make three times their normal salary, but their exposure to radiation ages them untold years. So, if you walk too long a stretch here you won't be alive very long.

132437.text: The Mollys have been trying to get at this base for as long as I can remember. That's why we have the military here. The Mollys are either trying to steal Toxic Waste or MOX to make weapons of mass destruction, or they are trying to blow this place up.

132438.text: BMM will chew you up and spit you out. The company has no regard for worker safety since it cuts down on the profits. Most of the employees who work this station aren't ever the same again afterwards -- all kinds of health problems, but that doesn't stop BMM from pumping out the MOX.

132439.text: The weapon platforms they installed in this area have gone a long way to curbing attacks on the base, even though our miners still get perforated in the fields by the occasional Molly attack. Hey, that's why they take the danger pay. You just hope you're not the one who takes a ship-to-ship missile in the chest -- ain't much left of you when that happens.

132440.text: My father worked on this base trying to get enough money together to get our family out of this system. We received a letter of grievance signed with a rubber stamp when an explosion occurred in the refinery unit where he worked. There were no survivors. The bodies were so irradiated that they had to be sealed in special containers for the funerals.

132441.text: One of my mates has been losing his hair, and not bit by bit either, if you catch my drift. He's been on this base longer than anyone else, but I think it's time he took his pay and pulled stakes. The greed is going to kill him if he lets it. I guess that goes for anybody, really. You have to know when its time to leave.

132442.text: Bowex ships H-Fuel to this base from Glasgow. It's the only shipment we make that doesn't involve MOX or Toxic Waste, so it is considerably less dangerous. Toxic Waste is flammable or even explosive, and the MOX makes you a prime target for the Mollys.

132443.text: It makes me worried just to step foot on this base. Do you know how many times this base has gone critical and flooded the corridors with radiation? More than once, you can be sure of that. I make a decent living working for Bowex running MOX from this base to the Armed Forces battleships. I pick up their spent fuel pellets for reprocessing on the return trip.

132444.text: When the bauxite miners on Leeds went on strike right after Kusari pulled out of the system, it looked like we were going to be left with nothing to transport to Stokes just as soon as the station was open for business again. Fortunately, Daumann was waiting in the wings, and we're booked solid bringing in aluminium from Munich so BMM can manufacture ship hull panels.

132445.text: The military and the police might have their orders concerning which targets are the highest priority, but I don't see it that way. Planetform will pay me a lot more for a dead Gaian than a Molly, so I kill Gaians -- they are easy pickings. If I wanted a challenge I'd square off with some Mollys. BMM will pay you well to take them down.

132446.text: I'm not bound by jurisdiction, so if a company puts a contract out on you, I'm going to hunt you down. And when I find you I'm gonna kill you, because that's how I put food on the table for my son.

132448.text: If you choose the life of a Bounty Hunter, you should know that you'll never win any popularity contests. The crooks hate you cuz you make a living of putting them in the past tense. The police and military envy you because you can take on the jobs they can't always do. The corporations dislike you because you don't follow the rules, and other Bounty Hunters might not like you because you are their competition.

132451.text: Drink up me laddie! Tomorrow we may be dead, but today we can be merry! We don't offer tabs, mind you. Trick I learned from a mate on the Derby before the blasted fools went and crashed themselves into the enemy. There's a discount for serving troops, and a free drink if you've done a tour on the front. A free round if you've killed a few of them invading buggers!

132452.text: We're under siege, in the literal sense - them Gauls have got a bloody battleship sat in orbit, with its blasted fleet scouring our orbital paths to make sure nothing gets in. Of course, they're not perfect and we've got some mighty crazy bastards on our side. You'd have to be to run that gauntlet. It's martial law up there. If you're caught breaching the siege lines, they'll shoot you down so fast you won't know what hit you.

132453.text: Come from off-world, ey? How'd you like the ride in? You never know what you've got until it's gone. How you'll wish you had a nice Ageira docking ring when your teeth are being shaken from your skull and you can see the flames licking at your heat absorbers. Don't carry any valuables in your cargo hold is what I say. The ride out is a little more gentle, don't you worry - presuming you're not shot down.

132454.text: The Royal Engineers have been kept busy by this war. Rigging factories, setting traps, blowing bridges. It might seem a bit underhand, but this is a war of survival. What we do here decides what they can do to the rest of Bretonia later on. The Army is going to send a message to the King, and he ain't gonna like it one bit.

132455.text: Sappers don't just take care of the death and destruction - we build, too. Shelter for the blokes, field repairs for the armor. It takes a certain knack to survive rough on Leeds, and we've had a hell of a lot more practice than the Frogs. I'll bet they'll lose a lot more men to the planet than to us - Leeds is a fearsome mother, and she just hates them that'd kill her children.

132456.text: Want to know the only thing worse than being invaded? Tratiors! If you ain't heard of Lord Evan Wilson yet, you will do soon enough. He was one of the aristocracy, chief advisor to the governor. He waited for the guv to evacuate, them promptly surrendered the sodding planet to the Frogs! If I get the chance, I'm gonna stick a satchel up his arse and pull the trigger. Boom.

132457.text: There's more of us than them at the moment, but that'll be changing, I'll wager. We ain't got no more lads coming in to back us up, while they're bringing people in from all across Gallia. Still, they've got no idea what they're stepping into. Literally! Step in the wrong puddle around here, and it'll eat your Goddamn boots off.

132458.text: Three years. Three bloody years, the government spent upgrading our armories and squirrelling away Military Vehicles from Rheinland and Liberty. We fired up an armored division on day one to throw the Frogs back from the landing zones, only to have them glassed from orbit by that bastard battleship. We learned a lot from that. Lots of tanks in one place draw attention. Now there are flashpoints of violence all over the planet. What we can't hold, we blow. King Charles is going to have so much ash to play with if he thinks he's taking this planet.

132459.text: Ammo and equipment isn't so much of a problem on an industrial planet. We can use the factories we still hold to manufacture more. The problem is with the more basic supplies. Consumer Goods used to be ordered in from London, and we were entirely reliant on Cambridge Food Rations. With the siege in place, we've got finite stockpiles that we're having to ration carefully. Once they're gone, things get... interesting. Hopefully the engineers will have some biopods up by then so we can grow stuff here. Much like on spacestations, if you recycle everything, the only thing you need is energy, and that's something we can manage on Leeds.

132460.text: It was not twenty years ago that it was Rheinland that invaded our home. Then it was Kusari, not ten years after that. And now these Gallic interlopers are asking for the same education in foreign policy they won't soon forget. Well now, we Bretonians should not disappoint them, then.

132461.text: True, I may be a bit of a fossil, but I'm not going to sit by idle while these invaders trod all over the works that were built by Bretonian hand. 'Tis not theirs to take. I may not be a good a pilot as I once was, but I can still work the shop. You'd be surprised how similar piecing together a cruise engine is from rigging up a large demolition charge.

132462.text: It was beautiful to see the Gallic supply dump in sector 12 blow sky-high. 'Though had I known they also stowed explosives there, a smaller charge would have been enough. Still, I bet they saw that explosion all the way from that battleship of theirs in orbit. It won't be the last one they see.

132463.text: I like visiting this place. Normally I look out my office window in Leeds and can't see anything green through all of the sulfurous clouds. My company's executive office wants to exploit Gaia much as they did with Leeds, with little or no government foresight. I'm not sure that's such a good idea at this point, given our track record.

132464.text: I'm going on an unofficial hunting expedition tomorrow. I met a Bounty Hunter who says he can find me a blue ground sloth. That would be an interesting addition to the collection of heads in my study.

132465.text: I've seen company documents that described negligible amounts of Cobalt on Gaia. It was a ploy for the government to let us in and begin full-scale strip mining of Aluminum and Titanium, the Basic Alloy metals that we have almost exhausted in Stokes. So, the Gaians and Cambridge researchers were not unfounded in their accusations.

132467.text: Those Gaians don't really seem to be a bad lot -- maybe a little up in the clouds, if you know what I mean. They haven't had to deal with makin' a living, like us working-class folks. Orbital has brought us here to bring in a few scalps, and that's what I'll do.

132483.text: Gaia is the reason I am here. We have the cruise ship Hawaii in Sigma-19, which offers everything that the Shetland can in terms of luxuries and pleasures, but this planet is unique. I come here every year and explore a different area.

132484.text: Gaia has many attractions. There is a beautiful stretch of beaches, a large preserve dedicated to wild animals, and a mountain range this is twice as high as anything I've ever seen in Kusari.

132485.text: It is a long journey here from Kusari. I'm stationed in Kyushu on the battleship Nagumo. I normally do Tau-29 patrols but never go further than that. Tau-31 is pretty, but Leeds is horribly polluted. We have nothing like that in Kusari.

132492.text: London doesn't give us much for a Gaian bounty. Outcasts, on the other hand -- they'll keep you in business. This is their main access route to the inner systems of Bretonia.

132494.text: Those Gaians are a stubborn lot. I had me one on his knees -- a flaming wreck, weapons gone. He tried to ram me, so I had to finish him off. I guess he knew what was waiting for him in Newgate. All those working-class blokes in there fancy a little upper-crust Cambridge companionship on occasion.

132495.text: We do a daily run down to the Skye Field. The Gaians like to hang out there, waiting for Planetform to stick their heads out. If we haven't been chasing the Gaians hard enough. Planetform sometimes gives us better bounties as a temporary incentive.

132496.text: The reason that Edinburgh is so important? There's no Jump Hole from Tau-31 to Leeds. Outcasts and Gaians have to come through here to get to the Border Worlds. There's lots of cover in the clouds here. The only point of vulnerability is the crossing north of the cruise ship. You just sit there, and eventually an Outcast is bound to turn up.

132497.text: The Guild has members in almost every system of Sirius. Once you get off the Trade Lanes, we're it as far as law and order goes, though some types might take offense to that. They would say that we're the problem. Don't matter to me.

132498.text: I've just dropped off our monthly supply shipment for this base. We bring it in from Leeds, Side Arms and all. I'm not in a hurry to get back to Leeds, because I've got a respiratory problem that always acts up when I land there.

132499.text: This is a beautiful place. I'll have to come back sometime to visit the Shetland. I'm glad that Bowex doesn't have to supply the other bases, though. Security gets to be a much bigger issue once you leave the safety of Aberdeen and the Gate area.

132500.text: Had a rough run through the West Leeds Smog Cloud on my last return trip. Some Outcasts mistook me for something juicy, like a VIP ship. They never should have let that cloud get so out of hand. That's our efficient government for you -- always on top of it.

132501.text: Aberdeen serves as the guardian for the rest of Bretonian space in this sector. Before the establishment of this post, the Outcasts and the Gaian eco-terrorists had free reign in this system.

132502.text: I think it's a bloody waste of taxpayer money having us up here. This really shouldn't be under the Authority's jurisdiction. My guess is that some private contributions were made by Planetform to certain Bretonian government officials.

132503.text: The Cambridge researchers on Gaia have made quite a stink about us all being here in Edinburgh. They think it'll lead to the deterioration of the environment and mass extinctions. I don't think I'd go that far.

132504.text: The positioning of Aberdeen is quite strategic. We can protect the Gate and sit astride the Gaian attack parties bound for the Sky Ice Field. The Islay Cloud is also in close proximity, enabling easy monitoring of Gaian movements along the Shetland access route.

132505.text: We aren't really here to control the Gaians. That's just the public version that the government spewed out. Our primary mission, as far as London is concerned, is Outcast monitoring and suppression.

132506.text: We get conflicting reports from London on how to handle the Gaians. One week it's "Vaporize them all on sight"; next week it's "Leave them be if they aren't causing problems."

132507.text: We send out two daily patrols: one to Perth, and one to Shetland. These keep the Gaians in check most of the time. If the Outcasts show up, we can only hope that the Bounty Hunters are close by.

132508.text: Since we established Aberdeen, those rich folks on the Shetland have had to clean up their act. No more Cardamine coming through this Gate. I hear it's not quite the party it once was.

132509.text: We're pretty certain the Gaian base is in the Islay Cloud. It's hard to find it in there though; those ice asteroids look all the same after a while. If you're unlucky, you could stumble into an Outcast doing some smuggling. My former wing man did that last year -- may he rest in peace.

132518.text: We have to ship in a lot of supplies for a Phase I operation. Phase I means there is no breathable atmosphere planetside yet. All procedures like ice asteroid bombardment are done from orbit. Gotta wear a suit to go down on the surface and do Organism placements.

132519.text: I just came back from Stokes with a load of PFCs. They'll dump it into the upper atmosphere of Ayr starting next week. That's the preferred Stage I Terraforming Gas. It's nine thousand times more potent than CO2 as far as GWP potential -- gets a planet warmed up real quick.

132520.text: Our Construction and Mining Machinery comes from Leeds. It's a pretty rough run through the smog clouds. If the Gaians don't get you there, they'll try again right up the road off the Skye Field.

132521.text: We ship the Alien Organisms from Glasgow at the northern edge of Leeds. Surface crews are sent down to survey for the correct geological and physical surface conditions. Then they scatter the Organisms with modified planet dusters and let them go to work eating the rock.

132522.text: Company headquarters in Canterbury supplies us with Food and crew replacements. Every few weeks they send up one of their office staff to take a look. We put on a good show and then go back to work.

132523.text: We've dramatically improved the process since we started on Harris 400 years ago. We expect Ayr to take only a hundred years, from start to finish. That's if the Gaians will let us -- pain in the arse, they are.

132575.text: We're unloading supplies from Cambridge, and then we'll reload with Beryllium and head for the ALG Dortmund smelter. It should be a smooth trip once we get past the Keswick Cloud and Omega-3 - Keswick in particular has gotten a lot more dangerous lately. Mollys have rolled into the area and are fighting a full scale war with the Corsairs, by the look of it. Sometimes we're lucky and they're too busy fighting to notice us slipping by.

132576.text: The IMG has been good for us. We were really struggling, shipping Water and Oxygen to corporate bases and Freeports, until they selected us as their shipper of choice. We ship Beryllium from this base to Rheinland and Liberty, and a little bit of Gold from the Hood.

132577.text: Gateway hopes to surpass Bowex someday, but that'll be a tall order with all of the aristocratic friends they have in London. IMG has the same problem with BMM. Still, it helps being the outsider sometimes. Take Kusari for one - they were a lot less eager to let Bowex back in then us.

132578.text: This is the first IMG base established. BMM surveyors somehow missed it during the great mapping period in 450 AS. A couple of Cambridge geology professors on research sabbatical stumbled across it in 554. Lacking the practical experience to develop it, they persuaded some BMM mining engineers to start a new company. The BMM figured it would be easiest to let the upstart company build the mining infrastructure, then drive it bankrupt and buy up our assets, but unfortunately for them, the Cambridge professors anticipated that strategy. Profits from the operation were "miraculously" three times as high as projected, so everything got paid in full. Cardiff remains in operation to this day.

132579.text: The IMG is a consortium of former BMM workers, independent miners of various creeds, and more recently, the unemployed Insurgencys of Rheinland workers resulting from the collapse of the Rheinland economy in 702. Workers of Rheinland and Bretonian origin make up the bulk of the company. We're still receiving new folk daily, from both the dislodged Leeds population and from Rheinland, where trouble in Dresden is causing some miners to go unemployed.

132580.text: The IMG has encountered unexpected resistance in the Edge Worlds. The very territorial Corsairs and Outcasts view any incursions into the outer Omega or Tau worlds as direct assaults on them. Still, we have no choice but to press on, as the resources inside the house core worlds are rapidly declining. Not to mention the house governments tend to favor the government owned companies heavily.

132581.text: Cardiff produces the bulk of the Beryllium in the Sirius Sector, especially considering BMM's operations in Tau-23 got destroyed. Gateway ships it either to Rheinland or Liberty, while the IMG handles the short runs to Kensington. For the return journey, our transports purchase either Mining Machinery or Basic Alloy from Waterloo. It's a fairly safe trip for us. The Mollys rarely give us trouble, and the Corsairs aren't as big a problem in the Bretonian core worlds as they are in the Border Worlds.

132582.text: Until quite recently, the IMG lacked the shipping capabilities to compete with BMM, Bowex and Republican. Now that Gateway and ALG have joined forces with us, we are a much stronger entity. Those corporate fossils are going to regret to have shut us out over the years.

132583.text: ALG has recently joined our cause, which makes our loose alliance very powerful. It has the most advanced refining capabilities in all of Bretonia and Rheinland. We now have all the pieces to establish a more progressive corporation than our competitors. It has some folk in Rheinland and Bretonia worried. Folk who are on the payroll of Bowex, BMM, Daumann and Republican, mainly...

132584.text: The IMG has been forced to conduct patrols since the arrival of Corsairs in our space. They have destroyed mining ships and stolen the Beryllium that was being mined. The Corsairs are the only real enemies we have here - the Outcasts don't come this far south into Bretonia, and the Mollys focus elsewhere.

132585.text: The IMG feels that the Mollys were wronged by BMM. We should know, since most of us were exploited for years. Our Rheinland brethren can tell much the same story. Part of the Guild's charter is to share the wealth with as many of our rank and file as possible.

132586.text: The Hood, Freistadt, and Freeport 4 are open to all - all who don't shoot us miners that is. This is part of our Freeport philosophy that we adopted from the Zoners. It is very effective in the Border and Independent Worlds and allows us to coexist with most criminal factions, unlike BMM, Daumann, and Kruger.

132587.text: I'm just over here picking up some Oxygen and Ice for the Shetland. It's easier than going into Leeds for the same of slightly more dubious quality. The only drawback is the potential of a Gaian attack.

132588.text: Can't say I really like these Planetform folks and what their operation could mean for our tourist business if they continue. The Gaians would certainly hassle us more if they left, so the operation diverts a lot of Gaian energy.

132589.text: I'm due to be transferred to the Hawaii in Sigma-19 next month. They rotate all Orbital Spa personnel every two years. That way we get to see all the different areas of the Sirius Sector -- a nice fringe benefit of working for Orbital.

132590.text: Just between you and me, the real reason we've started Ayr is that the government contracts pay the bulk of the milestone payments for an entire process during Phase I. Harris is so far behind schedule that it's on company costs now. A lot of our money is being siphoned off to Tau-31. Once it's complete, we'll probably bail out on Edinburgh and the Gaians.

132591.text: Planetform doesn't actually mind the Gaians as much as you would think. Truth is, they're a good excuse when it comes to cost overruns and other delays. Blame it on the Gaians, that's what we do.

132592.text: The ice mining we do is part of Phase I terraforming. We look for a large ice asteroid field nearby with appreciable amounts of frozen methane, C02, water, and ammonia. We set off explosives in strategic positions on asteroids, which set them into a collision course with the planet. There's an art to it -- maximum asteroid size for minimum energy expenditure.

132607.text: Corsairs enter this system from several Jump Holes. They are attracted by all the Gold that gets mined here, and they know it is the most lawless of all the Bretonian systems - the police don't have a large presence here, it is just the military and us.

132608.text: The Mollys are tough, but BMM pays big money for every one I kill. The Mollys have pretty much fought the Bretonian military to a standstill in this system, using guerrilla style hit-and-run tactics, so BMM hires us to kill 'em off one by one. The Hood is in a good spot to launch from.

132610.text: The Corsairs will fight anyone; they have no fear. I guess they don't have much reason to be too afraid of anyone. If you don't respect them, you are either stupid or dead. They attack all of the Gold transport routes out of the system, whether they are Molly, BMM, Bowex or Gateway. Indiscriminate, those Corsairs are.

132611.text: Bowex has hired me to kill Corsairs in this system. Those trouble makers attack Bowex, IMG, and BMM in the open, and the Mollys near the Jump Hole. Best time to catch one is when they're already fighting with the civvies. We get a mark who's either already damaged or has some ammo gone, get to play hero, and get paid all in one go.

132612.text: The mine field surrounding the Arranmore Asteroid Field has dissuaded the military from sending any of its larger ships into the field. I guess they learned their lesson when they lost the Hood. The smaller patrols are pretty hesitant to enter as well, but that doesn't stop me from going in. I kill Mollys for a living, so that's where I go. Besides, most of their ships can't maneuver worth a damn, so while in a minefield, I actually have the advantage over them.

132613.text: I don't even like stepping foot onto this base because the stench is overpowering on the cargo deck. No telling what goods pass through there, but that's a freeport for you. Next time I'm going to bring a breather mask. I run the Gold from this base to Liberty. Once I leave this system I have to cross the Independent Worlds, which is always a fight. The criminals always seem to know when I'm passing through, too.

132614.text: BMM is Graves' parent corporation, and they are putting on the pressure to keep the Gold shipments flowing from Graves. The Mollys are making it tough for BMM to pull a large profit here. The word is that The Crown is tired of stationing one of its expensive capital ships in Dublin on a semi-permanent basis. But without Essex providing security for Graves and the gate, the Mollys and Corsairs would overrun the system.

132615.text: The last thing I want to do when I'm in this system is come up against a group of Corsairs. They raid this system for any Gold they can swipe. I always start sweating as I'm approaching the Jump Gate out of here. If the Corsairs are gonna hit us, they will hit us there. We got jumped three runs ago. I made it out of the system with one escort, but I was too badly damaged to take the Gold to Liberty. I had to stop in New London for repairs.

132616.text: The one Commodity that we use too much to trade is Pharmaceuticals. Mining is dangerous work, and this base doesn't provide the finest of living conditions, if you catch my drift. You can always head to Kensington with a shipment of Gold and come back with Pharmaceuticals.

132617.text: All the supplies that keep this base running are shipped from Kensington. It's a pretty easy run for me, but no one really messes with us around here. If you want to earn some funds, you can always bring us basic supplies: Food, Oxygen, Water, and H-Fuel. We also need Mining Machinery and Consumer Goods brought in for work and play.

132618.text: The race track near this base has some of the best gambling you are going to find in Sirius. If you like playing the odds, you can bet on the pilots to see who will win. The odds are usually fifty-fifty, 'cuz usually one of 'em is gonna hit a chunk of rock while flying a rocket engine with a few thousand pounds of fuel aboard.

132619.text: The IMG miners make a living in this system selling supplies to the Mollys and mining the Gold in the Independent Gold Field to the northeast of here. The other two Gold fields belong to the Mollys and BMM, respectively. If you try to pull Gold from those fields, you are asking to get clipped.

132620.text: We are lucky enough to provide the Mollys with their supplies in this system, so they don't really mess with us IMG. But a word of warning to you: Mollys have no problem with killing. All of them are killers and will not hesitate to bury you if you make yourself a nuisance to them.

132621.text: This ship has so many decks and rooms that people can get lost. The worst kinds of people are often attracted to the anonymity a Freeport offers; some decide to make it their home. Stay on the safe side and don't wander too far from this area or the Engineering Deck. If you do have to walk through the dark corridors, keep your gun ready and be prepared to use it.

132622.text: There's Cardamine here at the base, if that's your pleasure, but if you want the best moonshine in all of Sirius, you should swing by the Engineering Deck. Make sure you get your liquor and get out of there, though. You never know when one of those stills are gonna explode.

132623.text: I still hope for the day that I hit that big pocket of Gold and strike it rich. I came here ten years ago from Newgate Prison, but this is pretty much the end of the line for work in Bretonia. I didn't want to go back to the Newgate "Hotel", so I decided to mine for Gold.

132624.text: The Hood was a Bretonian battleship that chased a squad of Molly guerillas into this field. The Mollys had laid a trap, and just as the ship entered the field, it got hit by a highly explosive mine. Mollys stole aboard, fought their way to the engine room, and set off a chain reaction in the engines, crippling the ship. Bretonia abandoned it, but most of the hull was still intact. Some IMG engineers decided to claim right of salvage, and managed to repressurise the ship and convert it into a floating base. Bretonia doesn't like it, but it was all done legitimately.

132625.text: We hold our own Gold field with mines and malice. Ya don't cross a Molly in Dublin or you'll be wearing a pick axe for a hat and some fools gold in your pocket. Or sockets.

132627.text: The Bounty Hunters at this base keep an eye poked in our direction, but they won't do anything while we are here. They wouldn't be able to come here anymore if they crossed IMG by attacking the Mollys openly at this base. Still, every now and then a Hunter ends up with a piece of fool's gold between the eyes on the lower decks. Just as surely as some of our own "vanish" from this base. Freeports may be free, but they ain't the safest places.

132628.text: Sir Edmund Graves used to run this station. He was known as a tyrant who didn't mind risking his miners' lives to boost Gold shipments to New London. Until the Founders Day Revolt, that was fine with BMM. That was the day that the Mollys were officially formed. It was also the day that old man Graves got his head taken off, courtesy of the Mollys.

132629.text: Sir Edmund's daughter runs this station now, and she does so pretty well. Most everybody thinks she's as mean as her old man, but she's smarter than he was. She realizes it is his fault that the Mollys exist, so she gives the miners just enough to keep them from quitting or joining the Mollys.

132630.text: The Bretonian military supports this station to the best of its ability, but the Mollys are fighting very effectively. The military escorts for Gold shipments leaving this station are not enough. The Mollys will attack several locations simultaneously in small groups.

132631.text: I fly one of the Gold transports from this base into New London. It is dangerous as hell to do what I do, even with the military escorts. Mollys are always attacking our shipments, and if it isn't the Mollys, it's the Corsairs.

132632.text: This base gets all of its basic supplies and Mining Machinery from Thames in New London. It's not as dangerous of a run as the Gold run into New London, but it is still pretty bad. The Mollys will attack us to disrupt operations at our base. If you want to make the run, you might attract less attention. Then again, maybe not.

132633.text: With the military's help BMM controls the most lucrative Gold field in the system. It still isn't safe. The Mollys have no fear and fight as viciously as anyone possibly can, maybe with the exception of the Corsairs. Fortunately, those two groups fight eachother too.

132634.text: After the Founders Day Revolt the Bretonian government sent several capital ships to quell the uprising. The miners had captured two mining ships: the Endeavor and Glorious, and the Armed Forces immediately opened fire on them. The Endeavor got hit in the reactor core and went up with all hands; the Glorious fled to an asteroid field to escape. The Armed Forces pursued Glorious into the field and right through a trap that the insurgents had set. One destroyer, the Longfield, was blown in half; three other destroyers suffered terrible damage and heavy casualties.

132635.text: The first battleship that entered the system was the Hood. The miners had revolted in reaction to their atrocious working conditions, but the arrival of the battleship was the last straw. They declared their independence from the Bretonian government and became separatists. The Hood was lost when it fell into a Molly trap, and the Essex has since then been guarding the Jump Gate. The Armed Forces aren't risking more warships into the asteroid fields.

132636.text: The Molly guerilla warfare tactics are too tenacious for the military. Though they haven't had any significant victories, the Mollys are still here and make themselves quite the thorn in BMM's side. They are financed by the Gold they mine from their own asteroid field, which is surrounded by a very dangerous minefield.

132646.text: The Corsairs are one of the fiercest criminal groups in Sirius, rivaled only by the Red Hessians in Rheinland and the Outcasts of the Northern Border Worlds. The Corsairs are usually found in the Southern Border Worlds and Rheinland, but since Bretonia pulled out of Dublin, they've been fighting the Mollys tooth and nail for the system's Gold.

132647.text: A Molly's natural environment is an asteroid field, and they've turned the damn things into weapons in Dublin. The Achill Field has been heavily mined and is lousy with Corsair and Molly ambushes. I figured the Bretonian advance was going to be a bloodbath, right up until the Sommerset pulled a magic Kusari rabbit out its hat.

132650.text: The Bounty Hunters you see at this base are here because Bowex wants them here. The bottom line is that they help reduce the attacks on our shipping convoys, which means we lose less money to pirates. They are a scruffy lot and the truth is I don't like them very much, but I am glad they are here.

132651.text: Gold from this base gets shipped to the rest of the colonies. Liberty, Rheinland and Kusari do not have major gold reserves, and the metal is essential in coating transparant surfaces on spaceships, such as cockpits and viewports. It is also a very strong electrical conductor, and is used in some high power superconductors. Bowex ships BMM gold to Rheinland, Kusari and Liberty. We don't ship to Gallia though, even a corporation has some standards.

132652.text: We've got a right neat little supply chain goin' on here. We try to pick off the Light Arms shipments that are headin' to the Norfolk before the BAF can scramble. The ones we do get, we trade back to Arranmore for Gold. From there, we can fence it to the Hessians or try our luck with freelancers.

132661.text: I love this place -- nice scenery, gambling to your heart's content, Food like I've never tasted before. They let you eat all you want -- go figure. This is nothing like my days growing up in Leeds. Joining the Guild was definitely a good thing for me.

132662.text: I just made a run into the Arran Ice Cloud. That's Outcast country out there. They make their Cardamine runs into Bretonia through a Jump Hole somewhere in there. They don't mess around, so you'd better be prepared.

132663.text: I came out here to hunt for Outcasts and Gaians, but there's more reliable business taking out tourists on trips to the clouds, or down to Gaia. I specialize in a little area of jungle in Pangaea known for its ferocious monster reptiles.

132664.text: We run a regular assault patrol into the Islay Cloud. The Gaians usually oblige us with at least one skirmish. What we're really hoping to find is an Outcast smuggler. That pays for more than a few nights in the Shetland Casino.

132665.text: Orbital does a patrol run across the edge of the Islay Cloud to keep the Gaians in check. We know their base is in there somewhere, but that is a police and Bounty Hunter affair, not our problem.

132666.text: The Outcasts have been attacking some of our runs. For this reason we invited the Bounty Hunters to use our ship as a forward base. They are not exactly the kind of guests we like to have on the Shetland, but sometimes one has few choices.

132667.text: The Shetland offers discriminating travelers everything they could desire: luxurious buffets with delicacies such as lettuce, apples, and roast hindcow; lavish boutiques stocked with all of the latest Manhattan fashions; and wild, exotic animals.

132668.text: Frankly, most people come for the gambling and feasting. The younger set opts for the planetside excursions. Most of the retirees just sit here and gorge themselves. Many are New Londoners, but we get a few of the Leedites, as we call them. They want one big trip before they die of whatever affliction Leeds gave them after living 40 years in that nightmare.

132680.text: There are several Commodities consumed at this base that we do not produce ourselves: Mining Machinery, Industrial Materials, and Consumer Goods for the workers. We ship here from New London, Thames, and Lancaster.

132681.text: We used to ship mainly Hydrocarbons, but the focus lays on MOX production now. It gets shipped to various Battleships from both the Liberty Navy and the Armed Forces mainly. We compete with Rheinland on MOX production.

132682.text: The Outcasts must be rich from the Cardamine trade. I don't understand why they would risk their lives attacking convoys of basic supplies and other low-priced Commodities. They either hate everyone, or they just enjoy fighting.

132683.text: If you are a BMM grunt, then this is the place to be. Don't get me wrong. The workers here spend long hours on unsavory tasks, but at least here there isn't a short life expectancy. Unless you work in the MOX processor of course, since the bosses decided against springing for a decent rad shield. Ah well, at least it keeps the "surprise inspections" to a minimum.

132684.text: The Bounty Hunters here are filthy chaps who curse and drink too much, but it makes us pilots feel a bit safer to know that they are nearby. More than once my ship's hull has been close to imploding from pirate attacks, when one of these boys swooped in to help. They ain't kind or cheap, but they sure know how to crack open a Molly raider.

132685.text: The nearby ice asteroid field is the source for most of this plant's raw materials. It's a real hodgepodge of resources in there. Sometimes huge chunks of ice from the fields drift into the Trade Lanes. If a ship moving at Lane speed plows through a sizeable enough piece of ice... well, you can imagine what happens: Hull panel pancake. The Police Authority patrol the lanes to try and prevent it from happening, but we still lose ships that way.

132686.text: It makes me nervous working and living in the same system as the most infamous prison in Bretonia. I know that it's supposed to be impossible to escape from Newgate, but the idea of all those murderers right here in this system just gives me the chills. On the other hand, it does mean there's a good number of Police patrols in the system.

132687.text: I'm glad I'm not stationed in Leeds anymore. My family has suffered enough from the five years I worked there. It is the filthiest system in all of Bretonia, in all of Sirius. It is also incredibly dangerous. I hear Gallia is landing troops there now. If our chaps won't kill them, the planet will.

132688.text: Mollys attack this base quite frequently. They hate all BMM employees and try to destroy every base or ship that has the name BMM painted into it. A shame Sir Edmund had to treat his workers so deplorably that they would revolt and become the Mollys. Not that the company has learned anything from it...

132689.text: Gaians used to be the easiest kill in the book, and they still are pretty much, but they're getting better at fighting and coordinating attacks. Some of them are rather good pilots now. I still kill them.

132690.text: We do well cooperating with the IMG. They provide us with contracts that we could not get from BMM. They are an old company just like Bowex, so they usually hand the choice jobs to Bowex instead of us.

132691.text: I believe that the Mollys take it easier on us than they do the other companies. This is because of our alliance with IMG and because we are not part of the group of old corporations that they have so much hatred for. They still attack our shipments, but not like they do the other companies.

132692.text: The last thing I want to do when I'm in this system is come up against a Corsair. I always start sweating as I'm approaching the Jump Gate out of here. We got jumped three runs ago. I made it out of the system with one escort, but I was too badly damaged to take the Gold to Liberty. I had to stop in New London for repairs.

132812.text: Kishiro has entered into very important negotiations with the GMG. If we are successful, there is a possibility that the two entities could merge, thereby making Kishiro the most powerful corporation in all of Sirius.

132815.text: We rely upon the Outcasts of Tau-23 to supply us with our Cardamine. We sell it to New Tokyo through Rappongi to fund our operations and to pay for the drugs that we use ourselves. Cardamine use is part of our culture. It is a symbol of our free spirit and the dream of a better life.

132816.text: Tau-23 is our space. Unfortunately BMM and the IMG have begun encroaching upon us. Niobium and Beryllium have been discovered here, and the miners have followed looking for it. That is why this base is mobilized for sorties. We're fighting to keep their operations from spreading beyond this system towards Malta.

132821.text: We used to get our sidearms shipped from New London here, but right now that route's cut off. Sure, a trickle still comes in through Newcastle... but most the smaller weapons we get from Liberty these days, by going through Baffin and Coronado.

132822.text: If you don't mind risking NCR status in Liberty, you may be interested in shipping our drugs. You can take the Cardamine from here and sell it at any Rogue or Junker base. The closer you get to capitol systems, the more dangerous it gets. But it's also more rewarding.

132823.text: One of our allies is the Rogues. They aren't our partners as much as our pawns. We have them under control because they are addicted to Cardamine. Soon more groups will fall to the allure of the drug, and they will also be ours to control. I see this upon the horizon for the Golden Chrysanthemums.

132825.text: I yearn for my return to Malta. I miss the orange fields of grass and sprawling plantations. The Cardamine is so woven into my blood that even my skin feels dry and cracked without the winds of my home planet upon it.

132827.text: I have killed more than a thousand men and stolen a kingdom of riches. Even now there are two veteran Bounty Hunters that stalk me: one for revenge, the other for reward. They will have to follow me across the stars, for I am bound to another place. Neither one will live beyond Tau-37; Benitez will see to that.

132828.text: With mineral resources almost depleted within Bretonian space, we had no choice but to look elsewhere. When we found this system it was the answer that BMM had been looking for. Of course it has been quite a struggle against the Outcasts, and the IMG sucking up the Niobium does not help either.

132829.text: When DSE was building the Jump Gate into this system, there were never any Outcast attacks. Those crafty bastards were biding their time until the Gate was completed, and then they attacked in force. They were just waiting until we had committed ourselves to this area so they could pirate our shipping.

132830.text: BMM pilots in this part of Sirius die all the time. It's not like in civilized space where you can drop your cargo and run. Out here the Outcasts will chase you down and kill you after you've dropped cargo. It's like a sport for them.

132831.text: There is a permanent DSE staff here that repairs Jump Gate and Trade Lane Rings. The Outcasts just love shooting the Rings to bits, even though they never manage to destroy them. Those DSE chaps sure do earn a lot of money. Of course I earn danger pay for being stationed in the Border Worlds, but I'm just a miner, so I'm only going to earn so much.

132832.text: The Beryllium that we mine here gets shipped right to Stokes in the heart of Leeds. We do not want to be dependent on the IMG any longer. Unfortunately, if we do not find a new source of Niobium, we will soon need to buy that from them, too.

132833.text: The Niobium in this system should be mined by BMM, too, but those dirty independent miners set up their operation before we had a chance to file a claim. Here we are trying to save Bretonian industry, and those damned independents are sucking up the Niobium for their own benefit. What's worse is that we take the brunt of the Outcast attacks in this system.

132834.text: There are no authorities whatsoever in this system; we are too far from Bretonian space to get protection from the military or the police. The Bounty Hunters who do come into the system loiter near the Tau-29 Jump Hole, but that strategy does us no good against the Outcasts attacking this base and the Trade Lanes!

132835.text: My shift starts soon, and I'll have to get onboard that death trap we call a mining ship. DSE is still working on the Trade Lane that runs to the Beryllium fields, so in the mean time we are most vulnerable to the Outcasts aboard the miner. It's pretty safe once you get to the mining area; the trip is the dangerous part.

132836.text: There are Jump Holes throughout this system that are used by criminals and independents. We believe that the Tau-29 Hole lies just to the east of the Beryllium fields. Look to the northeast for the Kyushu Hole.

132837.text: The run between here and Holman isn't too bad considering what part of space you are in right now. DSE brings a lot of supplies to this base from Holman, including Trade Lane Parts and Construction Machinery.

132838.text: BMM is paying the bill for us to complete the Trade Lane to their mining area. The operation must be costing them a fortune considering the number of Outcast attacks on our construction sites. I'm glad I don't have to go out there and work on the Rings. I'm a desk jockey -- the guy who makes sure we ship all the right supplies to this base, plus I get danger pay. It's a good job.

132839.text: The Trade Lane Parts that come to this base are shipped to us from two different bases, depending on who has what we need at the time. Sometimes we need to special order a component all the way from Waterloo in New London.

132840.text: The IMG guys at this base are nuts! You ever talk to one of these psychos? It's like they enjoy being out here in the middle of nowhere. I hate it out here, and I can't wait until I cycle back into regular space. There I can get back to worrying about Mollys instead of Outcasts and crackpot miners.

132841.text: Because this base has a lousy filtration system, it stinks here, and the water is brown. Even though the miners talk your ear off, it's a lot safer than our base near the Beryllium fields. I don't know why the Outcasts don't attack these jerks like they attack the BMM base, but while I'm here I'll enjoy the relative safety.

132842.text: The jerks here don't know it, but BMM has its sights on the Niobium fields in this part of the system. IMG doesn't deserve to mine here; it was BMM's lobbying that got the Jump Gate built here in the first place. This base is pretty safe right now, but as soon as I leave here and it's just IMG guys, you better watch out. Sometimes BMM pays pilots to pose as Outcasts and attack this place.

132852.text: Most Bounty Hunters have left the system by now. The Gaians have received serious blows from the invading Gallics and seem to be keeping their heads down. While that's all fine and dandy, we ourselves have been cut off from Bretonia. A good thing that we're already self-sufficient as far as food, water and oxygen are concerned, because I don't think we'll be able to count on the Crown to bring us any.

132853.text: There are signs that the terraforming process may be completely infeasible. Though we have been dumping Oxygen into this planet's atmosphere for centuries, our studies show that outgassing is beginning to occur. This means that no matter how much Oxygen we pump in, eventually Harris will revert back to its original condition.

132854.text: The money given to us by the Bretonian government to terraform Harris has already been used up. We would not have the funds to complete this project if we did not divert capitol from other operations to this one. Luckily, we have been able to sell the government on terraforming more than one planet.

132855.text: I never thought I'd live to see the day when Kusari was ejected from Tau-31. I thought I'd surely be killed by their long range bombardment first! It's hard to believe that what finally saved us from a successful Kusari invasion was an invasion by another enemy. What was that expression about frying pans and fires again?

132856.text: I don't believe this peace treaty nonsense. I just know there is some treacherous scheme in the works. First we're at war with Kusari, then they make peace while Gallia attacks us for some long lost vengeance nobody has ever even heard of, and suddenly the battleship that was trying to blast us into fragments one day is "our loyal ally and guest" in Newcastle!

132857.text: The original CEOs and board members who founded Planetform are all dead and gone, but before they died they became very wealthy. Their families are all part of the New London elite. I only hope that I can make my fortune and get out of the company before the government discovers what is truly going on.

132858.text: Personally, I think the Kusari and the Gaians are hand in glove with each other. There have been just too many "coincidental" simultaneous attacks in Tau-31 during the war to believe they aren't cooperating. If the Gaians have gotten their hands on our technological secrets, I wouldn't put it past them to sell the information to Samura. If it's true, I'd be all for nuclear carpet bombing that planet the Gaians love so much. Then Planetform can terraform it back to habitability again. Of course, there is the small problem of the Gallic battleships in Edinburgh.

132859.text: War is good for business? Who are you kidding! Maybe for Bowex or Gateway. They have enough of the right people in their back pockets that they can gouge the government for shipping toilet paper. Terraforming is a long term project. Do you have any idea how much grease has to go on the wheels of government for something like that?

132860.text: The most efficient way to get Water onto a planet's surface is to push ice asteroids into the atmosphere. Unfortunately, that is not possible here like it is in Edinburgh. Granted, there is an abundance of Ice and Oxygen in this system, which is very helpful, but the asteroids have contaminants that would hamper the terraforming project. Water extracted from the Tau-31 asteroids has to be purified before it can be used.

132877.text: Unbelievable! Two years of sweat, blood, and more funerals than I can count, all to push those Kusari battleships out of Bretonia, and now we have to sit here day and night grinning at each other like fools! Every time I go out on a combat mission against those Gallians, I expect to come back to find a hole in space where the MacDuff used to be. One of these days those Kusari are going to blow us out of the sky without warning, and the blasted politicians will just use that peace treaty to mop their phony tears at the memorial services.

132878.text: After so many months of trying to blast those Kusari out of the sky, on our first patrol after the Yamaguchi parked over there my wingman went nuts and lined up on it for a bombing run! Good thing we managed to talk him down before he fired. This peace treaty is nuts, but I sure don't want to be the one to blow it up either. Too bad about my wingman, though. The old boy was shipped planetside for "rest", but I doubt he'll ever see the inside of a cockpit again. Even in peace these Kusari are managing to kill our minds if not our bodies.

132879.text: I thank my lucky stars for the minefields around Planet Harris. The Gallic Navy dispatched an attack force to assault our position as soon as they arrived in Tau-31, but apparently they didn't reconnoiter the minefields before planning their attack, and that gave us enough time to withdraw. For some strange reason they didn't assault the planet. I guess they know that it is of little value until the terraforming is complete.

132913.text: I'm not really comfortable having to come back to Kusari. I'm not the only one who thinks it is too soon since the war ended to contemplate restoring trade relations with our enemies. But really, what choice do we have?

132914.text: Bowex has provided the most reliable transport of Kusari and Bretonia goods across the Border Worlds since 258. Before the Trade Lanes were built through the Tau systems, it was a long and dangerous journey across the ice fields of the Barrier, sometimes taking upwards of six months. With Gallia now dominating the region that is all but impassable.

132915.text: We've just come over from Yokohama to pick up a return cargo for Glasgow. It looks like it'll be Engine Components or Optronics. It's an odd place, Kusari. The two giants control everything -- no mid-sized companies like the other Houses. I'd give Kishiro the technical edge of the two, but Samura has far better cash flow. Kishiro gained the edge in politics here, but had to spend a lot of money in the process.

132916.text: I used to do the Kensington-Narita run before the war. Now to get home I either travel through Liberty, or take my chances crossing Bretonia's newest front line in the Taus. Good thing I like Liberty Ale!

132917.text: This bloody hole is awful. I can't wait to get back to a civilized place like Kensington. All the beer tastes the same -- no character to it. Nothing like a good Bretonia pint with a nice head to it. I'm leaving in the morning to run a load of H-Fuel back home. At least the Outcasts don't get into that too much.

132918.text: We handle the IMG Silver shipments from Freistadt in Omega-7. The Rheinlanders seem to be quite agitated in that area of the Sirius Sector, probably because of the squabbles between the IMG and the Rheinland mining companies. At least that's what I've heard.

132937.text: How the world turns. Not long ago the ships coming from this base were killing my countrymen. Now I am here buying Engine Components to take back to Southampton. I can't travel across the Taus with Gallia in they way though. I have to make the long, dangerous journey through Liberty. We do what we must to survive.

132938.text: We've got a contract to bring Super Alloy into Kusari from Scarborough. Bringing Super Alloy across the Border Worlds is a nail biter, to say the least. Once you get past the Gallic blockade, you find that pirates of all types fancy getting their hands on high value cargo.

132939.text: Bowex used to have an exclusive contract with Samura to handle Kusari government MOX and Toxic Waste delivery and disposal. We had to be pretty competitive on our rates, since ALG already has a foothold in Honshu. Nowdays we can only hope to regain market share, Bretonia needs all the support it can get right now, even from our former enemies. Samura is particularly keen to do business with us, I think it's because they still support their old monarch, who fights with us now.

132955.text: I'm on a crew replacement and supply run to the Tau-53 Gate. We've been burning through a lot of spare parts and construction machinery up there. Talk about bait-and-switch advertising! For years the gate was planned to go to Chugoku, then at the last minute Samura unveils new plans to connect to a system we never even heard of before? We could have saved countless credits, and lives, if they were upfront about this. Nothing like telling some criminals you're coming to get them by building a trillion credit Jump Gate to the middle of nowhere.

132956.text: I'm hoping to transfer to duty in the Sigma-19 area soon. It's supposed to be much easier now we have new access to Okinawa in the system. At least you aren't in the middle of some nebula with desperate Kusari terrorists fighting to the death -- although being in a nebula with a bunch of suicidal Outcasts probably ain't much better. Guess that's why they call it hazard pay.

132957.text: You see Golden C. out there in Hokkaido also. I guess that's where they've got their base. They are just a crazy bunch, in my opinion. Bartender, give me a shot of whiskey for the road.

132958.text: Roppongi is nice to visit. The foreigners are polite to us, much better than Kusari would ever be. They have lots of luxury boutiques for all those IC employees here, so we take advantage of the opportunity to shop in relative peace. I hate Ainu. If only I could live in New Tokyo again ...

132959.text: We will continue our fight until a woman leads this country. I do not believe in much of the strange things they preach on Ainu, but one thing is certain. The women of Kusari must be freed of the oppressive yoke of our paternal society. Only then will Kusari move forward again.

132960.text: I think it's time for my afternoon Cardamine break. We sell our cargo here, since they won't let us land on Tokyo. All the hip Tokyo types come here to get their supply. That's how we recruit new girls to join the cause.

132961.text: Non-Kusari companies based in Roppongi had a rough time dealing with Kusari for centuries. Roppongi was established in 321 AS, when the Hideyoshi dynasty was more open too foreigners - perhaps too open, and we've had to suffer the consequences for the past five centuries. With the current regime backed by Kishiro, things might turn out better, but make no misstake. Kusari does not like outsiders.

132962.text: The Tau-53 Jump Gate project has not been insured or sanctioned by IC. We view the Hokkaido affair as a deliberate deception plotted by the Kusari government against its own people. They need an enemy such as the Blood Dragons to justify their enormous public expenditures incurred when opening up the Hokkaido system for Samura's personal gain. There is no better evidence for this than the fact the 'Chugoku Gate' never ended up connecting to Chugoku at all! All this money and fighting, and hey presto - the gate now links to Samura's brand new holdings in the Tau-53 and Tottori systems.

132963.text: Kusari would have minimal criminal problems if the government agreed to some of the reforms proposed by Blood Dragon and Golden C. sympathizers some time ago. The new government insists on those groups laying down arms first, more likely they just don't want any radical voices in the government.

132964.text: We allow the Golden Chrysanthemums to land here, since they do not attack shipping indiscriminately. Their dispute is with the Kusari government and industry, and its stifling, paternalistic traditions. We at IC would view any reforms of Kusari society as beneficial to IC's interests.

132965.text: The most troubling development in this sector is the growing strength of Gallia in the Tau sector. The military seems distracted by the Blood Dragons, and Kusari has a peace treaty with Gallia - but for how long?

132966.text: We are currently investigating rumored Farmers Alliance links with Samura. The attacks on Synth Foods transports within Kusari are blatant acts by Samura to discourage foreign competitors who threaten their business. We will press criminal charges against Samura and refuse their use of Trade Lanes within Libertonian space if they are found guilty.

132967.text: We've never been allowed to establish permanent offices anywhere except on Deshima and Roppongi. Kusari is very distrustful of outside influences. Roppongi was closed for a short duration following the Trade Lane Dispute of 521, when all Liberty representatives were evicted from Kusari space. However, eventually deals were worked out - Kusari needed Liberty's cooperation to maintain the gates and lanes. We're despised by most of Kusari, but they know they need us to keep their empire running.

132968.text: We use this station to monitor the Trade Lane network within Kusari, Tau-29, and Sigma-13. The Tau Lanes are most affected by the Outcasts, who seem to have been disturbed by the opening of the Tau-29 Jump Gate in Tau-23. Sigma-13 is threatened by Corsairs and Outcasts, though the two groups do not seem to be acting in concert.

132969.text: Unlike our other House bases, Bounty Hunters Guild members are not allowed to base themselves on our station, at the request of the Kusari government. So we must make frequent visits to Deshima to communicate with the Guild management -- a process that I find distasteful.

132970.text: We supply Roppongi with its needs. Being the place this is, that means bringing in Luxury Foods for those IC snobs, who are too lazy to go down to the planet. We also use this as our transfer point for Luxury Goods arriving from Manhattan.

132971.text: We're supplying the Jump Gate Parts used in that crazy money pit they now call the Tau-53 Gate in Hokkaido. We've already shipped enough for those Deep Space builders to construct at least two. Now we know they really were building two gates!

132972.text: They don't let us ship our cargo directly to Yokohama -- go figure -- so we stop by here for a little R & R and then do the hop up the yard. Usually we pick up some Niobium at Narita for the return trip to Liberty.

133069.text: I am paid to kill Mollys near this base, but that may change. A group of BMM executives got mashed by a giant ice cube last week. They were here doing a routine inspection, and on their way back, their ship collided with an ice asteroid. The word is that the Gaians towed it into the Trade Lanes. Cunning bastards.

133070.text: Did you hear about the transport that got blown open just outside this base a short while ago? I found them fighting off a couple of Outcasts that they must have dragged in from the Trade Lanes. I got there too late. Just as I was about to engage the Outcasts, the transport's engines went critical. Too bad, I knew the pilot; he was a good guy.

133071.text: Peace is maintained in this system by the police and the Bounty Hunters. The Bretonian Armed Forces used to keep a battleship, the Essex, in here, but it is up to us to regulate order here now that it has been moved to Dublin to pacify the Mollys. Heh, pacify. Who are they kidding...

133072.text: The Mollys hit the Trade Lane between here and the New London Jump Gate quite frequently. I specialize in killing Mollys. My brother was onboard the Newgate as an inmate when Mollys attacked it trying to free one of their own. He got killed in the raid, with only six months left to serve. Made me join the Guild to get even.

133074.text: Hydrocarbons are essential in many industries. Polymers, lubricants, even some Super Alloys requires a good deal of them. Any industrialised world will have a demand for them, so it is easy enough to find clients to deliver them to. BMM operates 2 Hydrocarbon production facilities, this one and Douglas Station in Omega-3.

133075.text: Polymers are a valued Commodity in Liberty. We used to produce them here, but Douglas Station in Omega 3 received equipment upgrades that we didn't get, so now they are BMM's main supplier. The Liberty Navy is responsible for patrolling the Independent Worlds, but I can tell you her fleet ain't big enough to get the job done.

133076.text: Birmingham has been retooled to take over MOX production from the fallen LD-14 facility. I'm staying well clear of the part of the station that is doing it. Bowex refused to call port in LD-14 because of the poor radiation shielding the station employed. Birmingham wasn't even designed to handle nuclear material! Still, we've got contracts, so Bowex will supply both Liberty and the Armed Forces with MOX.

133077.text: Terraforming gases used to be produced here by BMM directly, but that has changed. BMM had to shift the focus of their production, and as a result, we take raw Hydrocarbons to our new facility in Poole instead. There, they get synthesized into Carbon Fluorides, which make excellent Terraforming Gases.

133078.text: Planetform has just increased bounties for Gaians in this system. Their attacks are becoming more accurate and frequent, which is hurting our operations in Liberty, in both Hudson and California. I believe if they could just understand exactly what it is we are doing and why, they would cease their attacks against us. I don't understand what their problem is with bringing life to dead worlds!

133079.text: Once you leave Bretonian space into the Independent Worlds, you are usually rid of the Gaians. Of course, that's when the Outcasts and Liberty Rogues become a problem instead. We rarely get hit by the Lane Hackers, I guess they don't think our cargo is worth the time.

133107.text: This station is supplied entirely by Bowex. We deliver Side Arms directly from Detroit Munitions. That requires you to cross the Independent Worlds, so it is a dangerous run.

133108.text: Birmingham provides this base with Oxygen and Water. It's nice running supplies to a police station. You get to know the men and women who are out there protecting you.

133109.text: The demand here for H-Fuel is pretty high since patrols are constantly launching from this base. Military patrols heading out into Magellan also refuel here.

133110.text: This base was built here to protect damaged ships arriving from the Border Worlds and to patrol the Trade Lanes between the Gate and Sheffield. More recently, Armed Forces have started to use it to patrol from here to Freeport 4. We see ships in all kinds of conditions. Once a ship that was on fire arrived with no engines. The pilot brought it in using inertia from the Jump Gate. Bloody good feat of flying that was. We had to use a few service pods to bring it to the station.

133111.text: I'm glad that we don't have to patrol into the Independent Worlds. I hear Magellan is a dangerous place. Luckily, that's assigned to the Armed Forces and Liberty Navy. From the condition of some of the ships that arrive, I'd say they are understaffed.

133112.text: The Outcasts hang around in Sheffield North a lot. I hate pulling that beat. A lot of our ships are lost in that field. My wingman of six years died a few months ago when his ship smacked an ice asteroid while chasing an Outcast.

133113.text: The police in Bretonia are nothing like Liberty's corrupt LPI. For some reason an idiot Liberty Rogue flew into this system once. After he was apprehended he tried to offer me a bribe and was astonished when I turned it down and brought him in.

133114.text: Mollys - I hate those vile miscreants with passion. Their lack of regard for human life makes them terrible hypocrites, especially since they were formed to fight the barbarity of BMM. I wish old man Graves had worked all his miners to death before they could revolt.
