GRAVITY: Complete
DOCKING: Yes
AMENITIES: Yes
CREW: 325
589872.mapped:
Soon after tourists began to arrive in Edinburgh in 690 AS, Cambridge scientists voiced their concern over the enormous ecological damage that even the most regulated visits could inflict on the planet. Almost from birth Cambridgers had drilled into them the stories of how New London and Leeds were blighted, so they tended to be very environmentally sensitive. A few of the younger and more militant scientists studying Planet Gaia actually went so far as to begin a campaign to sabotage tourist transports in an effort to discourage visits, but with little effect.

Once Cobalt was discovered on Gaia in 740, BMM began to lobby for the need to establish a mining base there. What had been a quiet, bloodless campaign of active resistance blossomed into full-fledged conflict. Graffiti with slogans such as "GAIA WILL NOT BLEED" were spotted soon after. The eco-terrorist movement had begun.

Eventually any plans to mine the surface of Gaia were dropped -- mostly out of fear that it might cut into the burgeoning tourist industry -- but the Gaians had already broadened their horizons by an influx of radical elements from Cambridge who sought a ban on terraforming technologies. Planetform, Inc. was the natural target. What emerged was a militant terrorist group philosophically opposed to the exploitation of planets, and terraforming in particular. The group enjoyed considerable popular support on Cambridge, funded by the efforts of the legitimate arm of the Gaians called the Green Front.

While the Gaians and the eco-terrorist movement as a whole have made little progress outside of Bretonian space, Green Front propaganda is a common sight in Bretonia. Green Front commentators are often present on the news, and unlike the Mollys, a certain amount of tolerance for them exists in the government from those disinclined to antagonize their Cambridge connections. Over the years, the movement has broadened considerably until the majority of its sympathizers are environmentally conscious individuals from throughout Bretonia.

The sole Gaian base in Edinburgh lies deep within the Islay Ice Cloud at the northeastern edge of the system. With the invasion of the Gallic Navy and the subsequent withdrawal of Planetform and the Bretonian Armed Forces from the system, activity at the Gaian base had decreased significantly.

To say that the hasty settlement and fortification of Gaia itself by the badly battered Enclave has incited panic and fury in the Gaian movement is a significant understatement. The population onboard Islay has skyrocketed and currently outpaces efforts to further hollow out its parent asteroid for more living room. Indeed, activity at other suspected Gaian strongholds has dwindled as many members of their movement have "come home" to defend their unifying ward. Bretonia's opinion of Enclave soldiers and noncombatants could scarcely be lower and as such, the movement needs not concern itself with the methods used against their foe.

Islay has also become host to a number of groups and organizations volunteering their capabilities against the Enclave as the "front line" against its last redoubt - Most numerously among them the Maquis. Aside from increasing the security measures of the base's munitions, some among the Gaians have reservations against their increasing presence in the region, particularly concerning their penchant for collateral damage should their particular brand of terrorism become more commonplace on Gaia itself.

589874.mapped:
Perth Station was originally owned and operated by Planetform Inc. as a base for the arduous process of terraforming Planet Ayr. This operation was under constant attack by Gaian eco-terrorists, despite continually increased security budgets by the Bretonian government. From 816 AS, Perth was appointed as a Bretonia Armed Forces supply depot, primarily used to circumvent the Kusari blockade of Planet Harris in Tau-31. In 819 AS, the First Battle of Edinburgh resulted in the facility being occupied instead by the Gallic Royal Navy, and renamed to Orthez Station. Orthez was used as a fuelling depot and munitions store for Gallic capital ships, before being largely abandoned upon the construction of Issoudun Drydock in 825 AS.

The Gallic Enclave were expelled from Edinburgh in late 827 AS through the Second Battle of Edinburgh. The base was re-occupied by Bretonia, with the Perth Outpost now serving as a northern listening post for the Bretonia Intelligence Service. The permanent garrison fastidiously monitors for signs of Gallic intrusion, fearing that Edinburgh may one day be an exposed and vulnerable flank the Gallic Union could exploit. BIS operatives also run periodic missions to Planet Gaia's surface, rooting out Royalist and poacher camps in the wilderness. Planet Ayr's terraforming project has been formally terminated by the Bretonian government, due to the many and immense strains on Bretonia's post-war economy.

589876.mapped:
The Shetland was for decades an iconic fixture of the Edinburgh system, offering lavish Orbital Spa & Cruise retreats to wealthy patrons. Despite frequent attacks by The Gaians, it was not until 819 AS that the Shetland was forced to flee during the Gallic Royal Navy's (GRN) Invasion of Edinburgh. The liner incurred damage during its dramatic retreat into deep space, however no passengers were seriously hurt -- the incident was later adapted into the holoviral wartime thriller "Last Resort", starring Donovan Jenners as Helmsman Jonty Stevens. The drifting Shetland was later rescued from the far outskirts of Dublin by the Bretonia Armed Forces (BAF).

Following state-funded emergency repairs at Scarborough Shipyard, OS&C lent the ship to the BAF for service as a hospital ship. In this capacity, it served in Leeds and later Newcastle, mainly triaging injured pilots. The Shetland also participated in the Liberation of Leeds in 826 AS, providing emergency medical aid to survivors extracted from Planet Leeds in the immediate aftermath of The Glassing. With the war's conclusion, OS&C resumed ownership of the vessel, and commissioned extensive refits at Baltimore Shipyard. By 828 AS, the Shetland returned to Bretonia, and offering resort services in Poole until the system's abandonment in 831 AS.

The Shetland then took up position in orbit of Planet Curacao in Cortez, in hopes of re-vitalizing local OS&C resorts that had languished since the Gallic War. Apparently dissatisfied with the aging liner's performance, the Shetland was withdrawn from service in early 836 AS and returned to Scarborough Shipyard in Newcastle for further refitting. Sold to the Bretonian government for a symbolic single credit, the Shetland has now been adopted as a memorial ship at the Leeds Monument, ahead of the 10 year anniversary of The Glassing. This allows visitors to interactively learn about the Gallic War and its victims, without disturbing the serene sanctity of the Monument itself.

589878.mapped:
Believed to be founded by a group of New Berlin University students in 679 AS, the movement had much support among the liberal elite of New Berlin, tired of the corrupt practices of the government that had led them to financial ruin near the end of the 80-Years War. During the Dresden rebellion of 700 AS, the Bundschuh found their first official cause -- shipping supplies "liberated" from Frankfurt to the Kruger and Daumann rebels. Three months after that, sympathetic maintenance workers started sabotaging Daumann manufacturing operations in New Berlin. The industrial heart of Rheinland stopped beating, and the Popular Revolution had begun.

Five years later the Emperor was overthrown, and a new coalition government was established in its place. While the Bundschuh initially pushed for a full investigation into the activities of companies such as Kruger Mining and Daumann Heavy Construction, more pragmatic elements within the government decided that for the newly formed Rheinland Republic to succeed, it needed the support of the aristocrats who controlled those and other major companies. Both Kruger and Daumann were eventually required to pay substantial reparations intended to "improve the Rheinland Republic for the good of all people," and all Rheinland companies were forced to comply with a newly ratified Workers' Rights Convention.

By 715 AS business in Dresden had more or less resumed as usual. The Bundschuh were driven underground, an impractical brand of idealism ill-suited to building a consensus among the many different government factions and the aristocrats who controlled the purse strings. The Bundschuh took the ideological high route, attracting the purists dedicated to overthrowing the corrupt Rheinland regime represented by the government, Daumann, and Republican. The Red Hessians adapted the more pragmatic approach of stealing and plundering in the guise of fighting the powers that be. As a result, the Red Hessian ranks swelled, and the Bundschuh dwindled.

The Bundschuh historically looked to the Unioners, LWB, Red Hessians, and disgruntled workers for possible recruits. In recent years, relations with the Unioners collapsed as the two groups took opposite sides in the Rheinland Civil War. Similarly, the merger between LWB survivors and the Farmer's Alliance soured relations with the Bundschuh over links to the Corsairs. Despite an amnesty offered after the Civil War, attacks on Bundschuh members and failures to implement promised state reforms quickly resulted in the organisation taking up arms once more. The Bundschuh prefer to focus on Daumann, Republican, and military bases, although they do occasionally raid ships for supplies, preferentially targetting Kusari transports.

Bruchsal itself is an old Popular Revolution-era supply depot formed from a hollowed asteroid; it has slowly expanded over the decades to house many hundreds of people and a wider range of facilities. The proximity to the Westerwald, Sigmas, and various Rheinland population centers means that Bruchsal stands as the political, military and administrative heart of the Bundschuh Underground. The local patrols based from the station are known to be particularly ferocious and capable, a fact that has been of endless frustration to Corsair forces transiting towards the Dresden system.

Fulda Border Station serves as the central command hub for the Rheinland Federal Police operating in the Frankfurt system. Its primary mission is to combat and intercept all forms of illicit activities in the area, such as drug trafficking, smuggling, and pirate operations. The station was originally established in the aftermath of the 80-Years War, with the specific goal of monitoring and regulating traffic emerging from Sigma-13. Fulda also aimed to discourage Gas Miners Guild (GMG) raids into Frankfurt, which had largely subsided until the attacks which triggered the Saigon War.

In recent years, the establishment of a prison colony on Hammersee has given Fulda a new and perilous mission. The RFP are often called upon to defend prison convoys in the dangerous Sigma-15 border world, in addition to carrying out anti-piracy patrols up to Freeport 8. These patrols have drawn the ire of the GMG, despite Rheinland's objections that the Treaty of Honshu only extends so far as the system's Nordsee Cloud.

ESCAPE VELOCITY: 12.11 km/sec
589882.mapped:
Initially charted in 82 AS, Holstein was ignored for centuries until the government decided that it would be politically advantageous to develop the planet as a hedge against encroachment by the Gas Miners Guild (GMG). However, Rheinland’s crushing defeat in the 80-Years War and resulting economic collapse doomed the project before its completion; Holstein was depopulated by conscription, and only marginally habitable. The planet would have remained an abandoned footnote in Rheinland’s history, were it not for a routine survey conducted by Daumann engineers in 789 AS. The discovery of large amounts of valuable mineral salts in the oceans resulted in the construction of planetside Boron extraction facilities.

In 813 AS, Daumann announced further investment in chemical Fertilizer plants utilizing extracted salts. Many of Stuttgart’s unemployed independent farmers would go on to find work in these plants as an alternative to working for Synth directly. These operations were profitable enough for Daumann to resume limited terraforming in 816 AS. Imported Terraforming Gases began to incrementally improve the planet’s temperature, with initial estimates placing project completion a century away. This seemingly optimistic picture would attract other investors, with The Core opening a regional office in 823 AS for coordinating Edge World expeditions with Rheinland partners.

Activities on Holstein ground to a halt during the Rheinland Civil War. While falling under tenuous Imperial control, it was caught between Federalist strongholds in Munich and Thuringia. The Federalists expressed little interest in conquering the planet, however the space around it was the site of numerous bloody battles. After the war ground to a stalemate, Holstein hosted the peace negotiations that ended the conflict. Through the Holstein Accords, the Rheinland Federal Empire was created, led by Emperor von Albrecht and the Consensus Government composed of senior officials from both sides. Daumann has moved quickly to resume operations on Holstein to recoup the war’s enormous losses.

Mainz Storage Facility was originally built as a military supply depot during the 80-Years War. The peace treaty between Rheinland and the GMG imposed harsh restrictions on trade, and blocked the Rheinland Military and Kruger Minerals from entering the Crow Nebula. During the post-war economic collapse, Mainz was auctioned away to Imperial Shipping, and for nearly a century was the sole permitted location for Kusari corporations to import and export goods in Rheinland.

Mainz would take on a darker role in 800 AS, when the Military requisitioned the station as a staging point for the invasion of Kusari. Journalists investigating the buildup of forces in Frankfurt were imprisoned on Mainz, with many vanishing forever. In retaliation for the Colony Wars, Kusari imposed an embargo on exports to Rheinland until the Second Treaty of Honshu normalized relations in 804 AS. This would see Mainz’s role significantly diminished, as Rheinland was forced to abolish its protectionist trade policies and grant Kusari corporations full access to its internal markets.

While Mainz remained an important destination for H-Fuel imports, Imperial Shipping still recorded consistently falling profits. This situation was further worsened by the Rheinland Civil War, which heavily disrupted trade in Frankfurt. In the uneasy peace that followed, Imperial Shipping has grown increasingly concerned over profitability, imposing several rounds of harsh pay cuts and layoffs on Mainz's crew to make savings.

589886.mapped:
For over a century, Mannheim Station was the northernmost outpost of the once vast Kruger Minerals commercial empire. Ever since the devastating loss of the 80-Years War, Kruger has eked out a minimal yield of H-Fuel by mining the upper atmosphere of Planet Heidelberg. This process has never been economical, as the impure gasses require expensive resynthesis. Despite this, Mannheim has always been heavily subsidized by Rheinland as the sole remaining domestic source of H-Fuel.

In the aftermath of the Rheinland Civil War, Kruger found itself flush with questionably awarded government contracts as a reward for its early and enthusiastic support of the Imperial movement. Having won the Emperor’s favor, Kruger were allocated a generous grant to renovate Mannheim’s facilities with little scrutiny or oversight. Kruger has since struck a deal with IDF Shipping, beginning to incorporate Gallic Cracking Catalysts and processes into their own extraction methods.

Kruger claims to have made a major breakthrough in the resynthesis process, with H-Fuel exports from Mannheim increasing eightfold since 830 AS. The sudden and uncharacteristic jump has raised the suspicions of some regulators on New Berlin. Kruger has so far used its newfound political influence in the capital to resist demands for an audit of the station’s records and production chain.

Infamous as the largest Rogue installation, Padua Station is a place of debauchery and sin, where some of Liberty's most notorious and violent criminals reside. In contrast to Junker bases -- which put great effort into keeping the peace -- Padua is frequently wracked by violent clashes between rival Rogue gangs. As a result, Padua's prosperity waxes and wanes with the influence and brutality of whichever warlord is currently attempting to wrest control.

The Reppu cloud scatters readings from most scanners. The Rogues use this effect to strike from the nebula unexpectedly, hitting local trade and Platinum mining operations with near-impunity, and even pillaging north into Kusari itself. The Kusari and Liberty navies are reluctant to give chase into the Reppu because of its hull-eroding dark matter; this would allow the Rogues to act with impunity, were it not for the Bounty Hunters that often chase down returning raiders.

Padua has an informal understanding with the Lane Hackers of Leiden, swapping loot for technical expertise, contraband and lane data. While this relationship was severely strained by the Cardamine shortages of 831 AS, mutual greed has begun to slowly sweep past bloodshed under the rug.

Leiden Base was built in 782 AS by a group of former Ageira Technologies employees after the Galileo bypass scandal resulted in several executives and an elite development team being forced out of Ageira. They quickly got in contact with the Lane Hackers at Mactan, securing the northern Independent Worlds as their primary areas of operation, preying on the heavy shipping between Liberty and Kusari.

Originally the Lane Hackers on Leiden focused on simple piracy, using their knowledge of the Trade Lane systems to obtain information on the most tempting of targets, carrying off what they could loot and destroying the rest. In recent time, the Lane Hackers have also begun to take an interest in smuggling Alien Artifacts. 589892.mapped:
Constructed by Imperial Shipping in 412 AS, the Alster Shipyard specializes in the construction of utility ships and transports. However, the shipyard is better known for its pivotal role in the emergence of the Unioner movement. Following the economic collapse of Rheinland in the aftermath of the 80-Years War, Imperial Shipping, subsequently renamed Republican, found itself compelled to downsize its operations in Hamburg to remain profitable.

In an effort to reduce costs, Republican terminated the employment of hundreds of shipwrights and thousands of surface laborers, ostensibly claiming a lack of work. In reality, the company was purging members of the "Alster Union," a labor rights organization that had long dominated labor negotiations. The Unioners responded to their expulsion with violence, commencing an armed campaign against Republican. Even with the rebranding to the Imperial Shipping name, the Unioners remain skeptical about any reconciliation with their former employers, and attacks persist without abating.

In the years preceding the Colony Wars, the shipyard was controversially pressed into service for the construction of military vessels, and in the aftermath, would assist with breaking up large capital ships in fulfilment of treaty obligations. To this day, the yard occasionally secures maintenance and refurbishment contracts from the Rheinland Military. Nonetheless, the majority of its projects are civilian in nature, with the maintenance of Imperial Shipping and Kruger fleets forming a significant portion of its workload.

589894.mapped:
Originally built in 326 AS, Altona Station was the primary clearing house for goods going to or from Liberty. After the 80-Years War, Rheinland was forced to abandon its protectionist trade policies in exchange for Liberty loans, allowing foreign shippers to bypass Altona altogether. This situation would worsen over time, with Altona scheduled for permanent closure in 801 AS. Fortunately for Republican Shipping, the station would be rented by the Rheinland Military as a stockpile and staging post during the Colony Wars.

Following the war, the newly elected government would prematurely end the lease, with Republican suing them successfully for breach of contract. Using the funds from this legal battle, Republican would lay off the remaining crew in 809 AS, and repurpose Altona for high tech orbital manufacturing. Using intellectual property developed by Hamburg University but owned by Republican, Altona would become a testbed Nanotube production facility, acting as an extension of the corporation's attempt to pivot Planet Hamburg's economy.

589896.mapped:
Named after the sole surviving battleship of the 80-Years War, the Westfalen was completed in 813 AS alongside its sister ships Karlsruhe and Koblenz. It was the first next-generation battleship constructed in Rheinland after the devastation of the Colony Wars. Carrying on in the tradition of its namesake, the vessel was deployed to Hamburg to carry out trade security duties stretching into the Independent Worlds. This afforded the Westfalen’s fighter squadrons a great deal of experience in Hudson and Bering, primarily fighting pirates such as the Liberty Rogues, Xenos and Unioners.

When the Hudson War erupted in 817 AS, the Westfalen initially acquitted itself well, becoming known as “the Beast of Bering” by Liberty crews. Following Rheinland’s retreat from the Independent Worlds in 819 AS, it continued to garrison Hamburg, primarily securing shipping routes against LSF privateers. The Westfalen again saw intense fighting during the Saigon War, incurring heavy damage during a daring push into Honshu aimed at severing Kusari's Sigma-19 supply lines. This damage required lengthy repairs, with much of the crew transferring to the Carrier Soltau in the interim.

During the Civil War, the vessel initially assisted the Soltau in securing Hamburg for the Imperial cause. From there it was deployed to Stuttgart alongside the Altenburg to pacify the planet and deter further Federalist attacks. Due to the Battleship Karlsruhe’s destruction during the conflict, the Westfalen has since been permanently stationed in Stuttgart’s orbit. Its officers maintain a far frostier relationship with planetary authorities than their predecessors, to Synth Food’s dismay. The Westfalen provides protection against Farmers’ Alliance raids, while also acting as an unspoken warning to Synth that the new government is paying very close attention.

589898.mapped:
While slightly more pleasant than New Berlin, Hamburg is still a planet of forbidding gray skies, frosty summers and bitterly cold winters. First discovered by Joachim Schiller in 87 AS, settlers arrived two years later to colonize the planet. Several corporations including Kruger Minerals and Imperial Shipping quickly set up bases, with Imperial going on to dominate nearly all aspects of the planet’s economy. Hamburg suffered severely in the aftermath of the 80-Years War, with over 30% of the system's population unemployed by 685 AS. This situation worsened further following the end of the Colony Wars in 800 AS, with then-Republican Shipping carrying out vast layoffs and relocating its corporate HQ to Munich.

Republican later launched several projects to return the planet to profitability. Most significantly, the corporation invested in the near-bankrupt Hamburg University in exchange for exclusive rights to exploit any resulting intellectual property. This bore fruit in 809 AS, after a new process for commercially producing Nanotubes was developed. Republican quickly retooled Altona Station as an orbital production hub, with this forming the seed of a new high tech manufacturing industry. The growth of elite manufacturing would see wealth disparity on Hamburg balloon, with low-skilled workers excluded from this new prosperity. A combination of poverty, unemployment and crime created a radical breeding ground for Bundschuh and Unioner gangs.

This resentment exploded during the 827 AS Civil War. Nostalgic for the boom days of the Alster Union, pro-Imperial militias seized control of Federal and System government buildings. Hamburg remained firmly under the control of Imperial forces until the Holstein Accords ended the conflict in 829 AS. In the aftermath, little has changed on Hamburg, as the newly rebranded Imperial Shipping pays mere lip-service to the promises made during the Civil War. The planet’s industries remain fragile while Imperial attempts to entice the many specialists and Scientists who fled abroad to return -- a prospect made more complicated by the recent "Hamburg Blast".

Vierlande Prison was built in Hamburg in 715 AS. For one hundred years, its extreme isolation and lack of appreciable sunlight made it one of the most dreaded destinations for Rheinland's terrorists and activists alike. Sentences to Vierlande were almost always for life, and those few who walked were forever changed.

On March 23rd, 826 AS, the walls of Vierlande Prison, once thought impenetrable, were finally breached. A revolutionary force spearheaded by the Coalition's carrier Alvin Katz led the assault using intelligence gathered by the Unioners. Upon the successful breach of Vierlande's defenses, however, the Coalition and Hessians brought their guns to bear on the Unioner battleship Undine, one only Bismarck-class warships in the Unioner's position. Through sabotage and force of arms, the Bayern was sunk, Wedel Mining Facility destroyed, and the Unioners of Hamburg left broken.

The Unioners launched a search and rescue operation from Pacifica, and among the plethora of bodies and debris found no trace of the military nor their socialist rivals. Vierlande was abandoned and broken. Not only could the station serve as recompense for some of their losses, but its position near the Cologne jump corridor made it the perfect bulwark against their former allies in the Omegas and southern Rheinland.

The Unioners now work tirelessly to repair Vierlande, though it is expected to take some time before the station is once more operational. For now, Vierlande remains vulnerable, and it appears to be only by the good graces of Rheinland's military that they are allowed to continue their work in restoring the derelict facility.

589904.mapped:
Most scholars date the start of the group as the publication of Golden Chrysanthemum in Bloom in 642 AS. The author, Yuyu Matsuda, was a young but critically acclaimed poet. Charismatic and well-spoken, Matsuda had a considerable following among young Kusari women who found their lives lacking in direction but were reluctant to become married and fulfil their traditional role in Kusari society.

Yuyu decried what she saw as the corruption of the Kusari male-dominated culture and preached a revolution led by the long-suffering women of Kusari. These ideas were eventually encapsulated in Golden Chrysanthemum in Bloom, in which Matsuda described a fictitious nation called Yomi. A place of fat, lazy male bureaucrats who handed out concessions at the whim of entrenched mega-corporations, Yomi was eventually engulfed in revolution and united under the rule of a benevolent Empress personally selected by the goddess Amaterasu to watch over her people.

Matsuda looked to the foreigners as a model, where women could be president and run corporations. The Chrysanthemum went on to become a best-seller. Unfortunately, in 648 AS, Matsuda crossed the dangerous line between ideas and actions when she was implicated in the botched assassination attempt of the planetary governor of Kyushu. Rather than face the ignominy of imprisonment, Matsuda chose ritual suicide instead. With the death of Matsuda, the radicalization of most of her followers began and an increase in attacks on government personnel and installations followed soon after.

Ainu Depot was the first space station built by the Golden Chrysanthemums, though the exact date of its construction is unknown it is speculated to date back to late 660 AS. Ever since its construction, Ainu has served as a valuable launchpad for raids upon traffic passing through Kyushu and Hokkaido much to the discontent of the Kusari State Police.

589906.mapped:
Constructed in 798 AS, the Matsumoto saw brief service in the Colony Wars, but was crippled during the devastating Battle of Honshu. Later repaired during the post-war fleet reconstruction, it was stationed in Hokkaido to protect Samura gas mining operations and the Jump Gate construction site to Chugoku. The Matsumoto did not directly participate in the Tau War, Kusari Civil War or Saigon War, remaining in Hokkaido to safeguard Kusari's domestic fuel reserves against Golden Chrysanthemum and Blood Dragon attacks. When the Chugoku Gate project was canceled and redirected to Tau-53, the Matsumoto also gained experience suppressing Gallic criminal elements.

During the Invasion of Gallia in 827 AS, the Matsumoto supported the assault on Tau-53, before pushing into Lorraine and then Burgundy. After being repulsed near the Ile-de-France Jump Gate, Matsumoto retreated and led the Sacking of Lorraine -- including the destruction of Planet Metz’ orbital mirrors. In 832 AS, the Matsumoto was scrambled from a New Tokyo refit to Kyushu, where the KOI believed the Chrysanthemum flagship Matsuda would soon be transiting through open space. The battleship's squadrons successfully intercepted the Matsuda, destroying it after a pitched engagement. The Matsumoto itself incurred moderate damage through several Chrysanthemum suicide attacks.

Rather than being withdrawn for servicing, the Matsumoto and its fleet were called to provide emergency aid to Planet Kyushu due to ongoing, devastating typhoon storms. This period was also marked by escalating Blood Dragon attacks across the system, which forced the Matsumoto to dilute its squadrons and incur heavy casualties to relieve overwhelmed State Police patrols. This tour came to an end in 835 AS, when the battleship was withdrawn to Ichigaya Drydock in Tohoku for experimental refitting. As tensions with Liberty heightened following the leak of Jump Drive schematics in 836 AS, the Matsumoto was returned to service and stationed near Yokohama Shipyard.

589908.mapped:
Constructed by Samura after the completion of the Jump Gate linking Hokkaido and New Tokyo, Sapporo Station was intended to act as a local base from which Samura could survey the surrounding systems for mineral resources. For a time, the station was repurposed to house the DSE construction crews working on the Chugoku Jump Gate, but since it's completion, the station has slowly returned to its original purpose, which is the exploitation of resources in the Hokkaido system. Ever since Kishiro and the GMG signed an agreement in 801 AS to open up Sigma 19 for exclusive exploitation, Samura found itself all but locked out of the H-Fuel markets, despite the majority of their fuel having previously been stored at Osaka Storage Facility.

Realising that GMG's reliance on Osaka would rapidly wane, Samura restarted its own gas mining operations shortly thereafter, something they had been forbidden to do under the terms of their terminated prior agreement with the Guild. The Gas mining operations continue to meet strong resistance from the unlawful elements of Hokkaido, particularly the Golden Chrysanthemums who have a base hidden somewhere in the Shiden Cloud. Despite this, with a recent influx of funds from the late Osaka's insurance policy, Samura have been stepping up their operation to extract the valuable H-Fuel gases that are abundant in the southern part of the system. Undergoing almost continual upgrades, Samura hopes Sapporo Station will one day anchor a vast network of Gas Miners as Kusari seeks to exert dominance as a major player in the H-Fuel Industry.

589912.mapped:
Steeped in history, Aomori Station is the primary base of operations of the Gas Miners Guild within Kusari space. Built in 284 AS, it began life as an equipment and ship repair depot for the fledgling GMG miners, who were working the dangerous gas clouds of the Crow Nebula. It has been expanded and extensively renovated over the centuries to become a massive space habitat and administrative heart of the Gas Miners Guild.

Originally, Aomori was the main point of contact between Samura and the GMG. For almost five centuries, Samura would buy H-Fuel from the Gas Miners, which was then stored at Osaka before being shipped to the rest of Sirius. After their "special relationship" broke down and the GMG joined forces with Kishiro, virtually all of Samura's administrative staff left the station. Kishiro maintains a much smaller presence on Aomori since they have large offices on nearby Planet Honshu. The GMG considers Aomori Station and the surrounding area, including the jump gate, to be their sovereign territory.

Settled in 56 AS, planet Honshu was the first colony in Kusari, after the initial colonisation of planet New Tokyo. It bears a number of similarities to the capital planet, mainly in that it is an ocean world with few sizeable land masses. With so little land available for farming, the settlers turned to fishing as their primary industry. Unfortunately, very few Terran fish species took to the oceans of Honshu, although tuna and salmon were among those that were able to survive. The colonists struggled to feed themselves for several centuries, until overfishing caused a catastrophic decline in the fish stocks in 250 AS, which caused most of the inhabitants to abandon the planet and seek their fortunes elsewhere. The population dropped from roughly a 1.5 million inhabitants to 250.000 over decade that followed. Most emigrated to Planet Kyushu and it's vast rice farms, but others cast their eyes on the nearby Crow Nebula and the bountiful fuel gases therein. These pioneers eventually became known as the Gas Miners Guild.

With the colonists abandoning their ancestral home in favour of the Crow Nebula, Honshu lay fallow for over 250 years. Those that remained scratched out a meager living, trading what little resources the planet had to offer with New Tokyo, and supplying the Gas Miners Guild with water and oxygen - both of which Honshu possessed plenty of. Eventually, in 510 AS, Kishiro Technologies decided that Honshu would be the perfect location to construct its main optronics production facility, especially after planetary surveys revealed the oceans to contain significant quantities of various chemicals and raw materials that were useful in the manufacture of optronics themselves. Since the optronics factories could be built at seabed or on platforms, this has left a significant amount of the available land masses for the construction of towns and cities, and the population of Honshu has climbed steadily ever since. Recent Honshu architecture closely resembles that of New Tokyo - compact, towering cities that economise on land use.

Built by Kishiro Technologies in 748 AS, Kansei Research Station was formed as a joint project between Kishiro and the Kusari Naval Forces, much to the ire of Samura. The facility is tasked with developing new shielding and scanning technology that are specifically designed to operate within the treacherous gas nebulas common throughout Kusari, although there are many whispered claims of alien artifacts research and jump gate technology filtering out of the station from time to time.

Kansei is a highly prestigious posting for Kishiro scientists fresh out of New Tokyo University, though the security measures can be rather daunting, and the Kusari Naval Forces have constant patrols coupled with heavy weapons platforms and a defensive minefield. The Blood Dragons pose the biggest threat to the facility, frequently launching raids and disrupting operations.

Construction finished on Yukawa Shipyard in 118 AS, and it is the primary shipbuilding facility for Kishiro Technologies. Historically, the shipyard has focused on the mass-production of civilian transports. Yukawa and it's chief competitor Yokohama outcompeted the Liberty shipyards in Colorado, and to this day remain the choice yards for many smaller shipping companies who favor pricing over patriotism. Yukawa has been expanded, modified and partially rebuilt over the centuries. Virtually no part of the original construction remains. Aside from Optronics and Polymer-based materials, Yukawa is forced to import most of it's materials from other houses.

Yukawa Shipyard also constructs many midsized ships for the Gas Miners Guild, such as the Kamome-class Gas Miner. The GMG contracts account for over half the work being done at the yard, most of which was previously handled at Yokohama.

Little is known about this shady asteroid base, tucked away in the southeast of Hudson. It was originally constructed in 736 AS by the Liberty Rogues who wanted to gain a foothold in the southern Independent Worlds. The base is well hidden inside the Wrangell Asteroid Field, however it was nearly detected multiple times during the Hudson War due to nearby fighting. Despite this, the Rogues have so far kept a low profile, and Rheinland seems disinterested in sending patrols to root the Rogues out.

Dawson is primarily used by smugglers, serving as an important point of contact between the Rogues and Unioners. Unioner smugglers bring in Artifacts, Hessian Tears and more recently Nox to sell, which the Rogues then distribute onward through Liberty. The Xenos, envious of the profits this brings, often attack these smugglers. In recent years, Dawson’s Rogues have taken a more aggressive approach to countering Xeno activities, motivated in part by handsome Junker bribes.

589922.mapped:
The Xenos descend from heavy manufacturing and mining workers from Colorado and Texas. Excavated in 764 AS, Barrow Base was originally a Deep Space Engineering (DSE) extraction platform from the "days when Liberty did its own mining". DSE chose to shutter expensive local operations and import cheaper minerals from Rheinland and Bretonia instead. Over time, most blue-collar miners became unemployed and were pushed to the economic fringe of Liberty society.

By 816 AS, Barrow’s population had exploded due to mass recruitment aboard the LPI’s prisons, and sudden layoffs at Houston’s Fertilizer chemical plants. Despite expansions to the base's cramped tunnels and caves, overcrowding quickly hit critical levels. The southern Xeno clans were forced to expel surplus pilots, sending them away to larger bases such as Fort Ramsey. Despite this, Barrow remains a claustrophobic bastion of the Xeno cause against Rheinland, primarily targeting Republican and ALG transports.

Barrow’s patrols are also a persistent thorn in the side of the Junkers, Liberty Rogues and Unioners, as Xenos frequently disrupt their smuggling operations across Texas and the Independent Worlds, stealing valuable contraband. Since 827 AS, the Rogues have become more aggressive in proactively targeting the Xenos in return, with some speculating that furious Junkers have handsomely paid them off as mercenaries.

589924.mapped:
Ames Research Station was originally constructed in 773 AS by Deep Space Engineering, to investigate the strange dark matter clouds that were in the eastern areas of the system, and also to study the dark matter storm that was scheduled to pass through the system in 780 AS. As it happened, the storm entered Kepler 4 years later than it was expected to, destroying the old trade lane that passed through the eastern area of the system and rendering it extremely dangerous to travel through. Deep Space Engineering incurred heavy financial losses during the construction of the new lane to the Shikoku Jump Gate, and as a result their operations on Ames were scaled back almost completely to the point of abandoning the station.

Having been taken over by the Zoners through a legal purchase of administration rights in 790 AS, the station was run as a Freeport for decades, serving all manner of pilots. This peaceful, albeit uneasy existence was thrown into disarray by a sharp intensification of the dark matter storm's potency. And while Ames had prepared for such an eventuality, life here still hangs on by a thread.

The unique conditions of Ames have attracted quite a lot of attention by the scientific community from all over Sirius.

Entering service in 827 AS, the Hamamatsu is the latest battleship to join the arsenal of the Kusari Naval Forces. Boasting the most recent technological advancements of Kure Shipyard and superior expeditionary capabilities, the Hamamatsu fleet was appointed as the vanguard for the Invasion of Gallia later that year. Firmly crushing all Confederal opposition in Tau-53, it then breached Lorraine, allowing supporting fleets to pour into Gallia and exploit the breakthrough.

Following its highly successful war service, the battleship was assigned to Honshu as a garrison ship. For this deployment it was responsible for deterring Blood Dragon attacks on Kansai Research Institute, and protecting shipping across the system. This period saw the restless Sigma border grow increasingly dangerous, with the Hamamatsu's officers frequently criticizing the GMG for failing to curb piracy and smuggling in their territory. In early 835 AS, the vessel was relieved by the Battleship Sado and instead dispatched to New Tokyo.

Now orbiting the capital planet, the Hamamatsu's potent blend of military might and cutting-edge technology sends a bold and unmistakable message to the foreign diplomats housed on the nearby Liner Akasaka. Despite this, its prestigious image was tarnished in early 836 AS, when the Hamamatsu notably failed to intervene during the attempted coup of Lord Protector Akihiro Mitsuo. Several of the Hamamatsu's flag officers were arrested on suspicion of collusion with the rebels. In mid 836 AS, these officers were returned to service, and tasked with executing Operation Ichi-Go: a first strike against the Republic of Liberty.

The Hamamatsu's mission was to destroy Norfolk Shipyard, in the hopes of shaking Liberty's resolve and undermining their naval capabilities. Tokyo analysts forecast that this would be a borderline suicide mission, and the fleet suffered grievous casualties to penetrate Norfolk's defenses. The Hamamatsu finally succumbed to fire from the Battleship Missouri and Liberty reinforcements. Admiral Hayakawa ultimately chose to ram his dying vessel through Norfolk's hangar doors, before detonating his compromised reactor. Scattered Kusari survivors from the attack broke free and fled for the Badlands.

589930.mapped:
Kyushu is known as the "company" planet within Kusari, as many of its inhabitants depend on Samura for their livelihoods. Over the years Samura organized Kyushu farmers into cooperatives to stimulate rice production and sold the rice at premium prices in Tokyo supermarkets.

The introduction of Trade Lanes led to competition with foreign agricultural imports, and the Farmers Alliance, supported by Samura, lobbies for government subsidies and restrictions on foreign foods in Kusari.

Under these circumstances Synth Foods proved to be an overnight success. Particularly in the urban areas of Honshu and New Tokyo. The Farmers were quick to be pulled under Samura's umbrella of influence and weaponised as a means to oppose not merely the Liberty food giant, but tackle all foreign trade.

Today, Kagoshima while ostensibly still labelled a depot, is more akin to a militarized launchpad for Farmers Alliance raiders to strike at Synth's operations in the system. This has become a prevalent focus of the movement in the wake of the Kyushu cyclonic storm that provided foreign competition with the potential for good press. Though unsuccessful in preventing Synth Food's involvement wholesale, the Farmers have made the new market a costly affair.

589932.mapped:
First surveyed in 65 AS by Isao Yoshida, Kyushu possesses arable land and an ideal climate for rice farming. While the independent farmers of Kyushu provided much of the basic Food stuffs for New Tokyo for over three centuries, Shogunate development directives in the late 790s saw Samura assume control under a government contract. Samura immediately reorganized the planet’s independent plantations into collectives that were forced to grow strains of genetically engineered Samura rice. The Kyushu farmers increasingly struggled to recoup the costs of these changes due to competition from Synth Foods, whose products are more popular among Kusari’s youth.

Living standards on Kyushu have declined with its profits, leading to the rise of the Farmers Alliance terrorist group who viciously target Synth Foods. This situation worsened with the overthrow of the Shogunate in 817 AS, as the new Republic further liberalized trade restrictions, and withdrew Samura’s governance contract. With the return of the “Imperial Exiles” to Kusari in 823 AS, Kyushu -- with Samura backing -- revolted against the Republic. For the duration of the civil war, Kyushu was the acting capital of the Emperor. After two years of conflict, the Shogunate was restored, with Kyushu remaining under government administration.

Kyushu’s farmers faced further shocks in early 833 AS, as unprecedented storms wracked the planet. These colossal typhoons dominated Kyushu’s monsoon season, devastating coastal settlements and destroying many of the rice plantations. The severe disruption to Kyushu’s Food production infrastructure caused prices to spike across Kusari, with Synth Foods rapidly exploiting the situation. While an enormous humanitarian response allowed many farmers to recover from the damage, many others were left destitute and resentful of a lack of government support.

589934.mapped:
In 400 AS the Kusari Government began offering development incentives to attract investment to Kyushu, with Samura quickly taking up the offer and constructing Nansei Research Complex. After cycling through several programs, Nansei was eventually chosen to pioneer Kusari’s antimatter research, with a focus on propulsion and armaments. The Samura-Naval Forces partnership has made slow progress over the centuries, with the most notable public development being the Supernova Antimatter Cannon. Released for sale shortly after the Colony Wars, Supernova type weapons have since proliferated across Sirius, through both licensing deals and imitations.

The volatility of antimatter means a failure in the facility’s containment fields will result in a catastrophic annihilation event. Nansei has suffered several major disasters across its service, with the most severe being the 799 AS detonation of an antimatter micrograin sample that killed over 100 staff. In the aftermath of that incident, Samura was severely criticized when government investigations found the cause was negligence and cost-cutting. Since then, a significant Naval Forces garrison has been stationed aboard -- primarily to deter Blood Dragon attacks -- but also to ensure Samura observes necessary rigorous safety standards.

The combination of sensitive research and significant Naval presence also made Nansei a target during the Kusari Civil War, with Imperial forces laying siege rather than risking an explosion from a direct attack. In 825 AS, Republican forces abandoned Nansei and broke through Imperial lines to retreat to New Tokyo. Following the Civil War, Nansei has seen its subsidies consistently cut in favor of Kansai Research Institute in Honshu. This continued until 835 AS, when Kusari and Samura jointly funded a large-scale expansion of a pilot Superconductor fabrication project in response to Liberty's economic sanctions. Small quantities of Superconductors are now produced locally, despite soaring Blood Dragon strikes.

589936.mapped: Tsushima Depot was launched as the start of a vertically integrated chain completely owned and operated by Samura, and has grown in scale over the years. Hydrocarbons imported from the Shikoku system are processed into Polymers here and then shipped to Samura's shipyards and manufacturing plants in New Tokyo. The base once processed Hydrocarbons directly from the massive rings orbiting Aso, but these have since been mined out. Sections of the depot have also been subject to repurposing, instead storing relief supplies bound for Kyushu. It also serves as an impromptu headquarters for Samura to aggregate its brightest minds, albeit sometimes through coercive means, in an effort to project itself as being fully invested in Kyushu's quick recovery. The atmosphere aboard the depot is therefore tense, as company management intends to run a watertight ship in order to deprive Synth Foods of any controversy from which they could profit.

In the aftermath of the Gallic invasion and destruction of Leeds, Bretonians were left in shock. This left an opening for a motley band of looters, smugglers, pirates, and desperate survivors to cobble together Halifax Freeport out of whatever remotely serviceable wreckage they could grab. The clumsy integration of disparate modules with no regard for origin or safety standards combine with the hazards of the smog cloud that conceals Halifax to make one of the most unpleasant and dangerous stations in Sirius.

Despite the hazards, or perhaps because of them, Halifax accepts all visitors. Much of the station's income is dedicated to patching up the constant mechanical and power failures that plague the base, the base however has proved resilient despite these challenges.

Perpetually swathed in its trademark smog storms, planet Leeds is a vast metropolis of manufacturing facilities, smelters, processing plants and environmentally sealed apartment blocks. Centuries of industrial abuse aided and abetted by morally corrupt corporations, lack of official oversight and severe overpopulation have lead to the planet being the symbol of everything the Green Front, and their unlawful counterparts the Gaians, fight against.

The Leeds system was quickly recognised as the most resource rich system under Bretonian control during the House's formative years. Many new companies, including Bretonia Mining and Manufacturing, were given near carte blanche to develop the system as they saw fit, and many colonists were given extremely generous incentives in order to move to Leeds and serve as the workforce. The planetary population has since climbed steadily, and the last census of the Leeds system in 810 AS listed the planet as having over 15.6 billion inhabitants, making it one of the most heavily populated planets in the Sirius sector. This number has since been decimated by repeated wars and the gallic invasion. An exact census has not been taken in over five years, but it is expected the planet houses roughly 7.7 billion people as of 818 AS.

Planet Leeds has suffered considerably from the continuous threat of hostile invasion. When it became clear that the Gallic Royal Navy would breach Leeds and lay siege to the planet, the ground contingent on Planet Leeds began fortifying themselves against an orbital assault. Using the deep mines and large subterranean industrial complexes which are practically impervious to orbital bombardment as shelters, the Armed Forces on Leeds and the Gallic Marines invading were both prepared for a long and bloody conflict in extremely hazardous conditions.

After years of brutal warfare the Gallic Marines were able to attain control over the majority of Leeds' surface, including most major cities and industrial centers. Despite that, the fierce fighting continues, with many Bretonian units still entrenched in numerous underground complexes and rural areas far from main megacities of Leeds.

One of the frontrunners of the Toitsu class, the Hyono deployed from Kure Shipyard in 825 AS, shortly before the Saigon War with Rheinland. Following the destruction of Ibusuki Survey Platform in Sigma-21, the Hyono fleet was dispatched to aid the Gas Miners Guild against the Rheinland Military. While the ship's expanded hangar bays initially allowed generous strike wings to contest Planet Saigon, the tide dramatically turned with the arrival of Rheinland reinforcements. By exploiting Sigma-21's open space, the Bayern and Westfalen fleets forced their enemies to fight on unfavorable terms, inflicting heavy casualties. The Hyono was damaged during the 826 AS rout back to Honshu, where it regrouped to rally a defense.

Using the cover of Honshu's Hiryo Cloud, the Hyono and other KNF elements succeeded in holding the Rheinland fleets at bay, while severing their Sigma-21 supply lines. Following the war's end, the battleship was sent for extensive repairs and refits at Kure Shipyard. Its next assignment in 827 AS shocked Sirius, when a significant Kusari military buildup along the Tau borders was justified as a dispute with the Crayter Republic. While the KNF did then expel the Republic from Tau-31, this was a pretext for maneuvering their fleets closer to the Gallic border to launch a surprise invasion. As a result, Gallic Confederal forces were taken by surprise when the Hyono, Nagasaki, and Yamaguchi fleets swung north into Tau-23.

The Kusari fleet rapidly scattered the local Tau garrison and destroyed Cheronsee Outpost, to avoid a time-consuming boarding attempt. Breaching the Languedoc Jump Gate, the Hyono was met by the Battleship Cassard, which was heavily damaged and driven off. The Hyono then advanced with the Nagasaki alongside the Trade Lanes, and was responsible for disabling Nimes Station while the Nagasaki destroyed Quillan's spaceports. It later participated in the Battles of Ales, scuttling Fourchambalt Shipyard late in the year when the joint Confederal-Enclave counter-offensive was launched. The Hyono was eventually lost while retreating back towards the Taus, falling to the Warwolf cannon of the Enclave's Battleship Rocroi.

589947.mapped:
Lane Hackers are mostly composed of former Los Angeles Ageira Technologies employees who created the extremely complex scanning and database system known as USI (Universal Ship Identification). Departing the company rather acrimoniously in 750 AS, they have become a growing problem in the Independent Worlds.
The Lane Hackers in Magellan and Galileo share one common origin -- Ageira. The scandal that erupted within the company after the great Galileo bypass project, which resulted in the unnecessary construction of a hugely expensive set of Jump Gates and Trade Lanes, forced several executives and an elite development team out. This would become the second part of the core of the Lane Hackers, along with the original California scanner group that fled to Magellan.

The investigation continues to this day, but has so far been unsuccessful in locating the Lane Hacker bases. No Hacker leader has ever been captured, although various Rogues in the Independent Worlds have been caught possessing remarkably accurate information regarding upcoming high-value shipments.

Security measures have been added to the software, but the Hackers remain one step ahead, leading Ageira security experts to believe that there are many sympathetic programrs still within the company, possibly being secretly paid off with the proceeds from the thefts. The Lane Hackers prefer to sell their information to others rather than do the dirty work themselves, although they sometimes swoop in and tractor in cargo if it's particularly juicy. Fancying themselves as modern-day Robinhoods, they avoid direct confrontation when possible, unless they are dealing with Interspace Commerce or Ageira.

They like to frequent Freeport 4 and the Ames Research Station, as their asteroid bases within the clouds can become claustrophobic. Their cardamine addiction forces them to trade Lane shipment info for drugs with the Outcasts and the Liberty Rogues at Mactan, although usually it ends up being the Liberty Rogues who act upon any information, and take the fall when anything goes wrong.

Prior to its 825 AS destruction during the Gallic War, Birmingham was a sizable ice processing facility run by BMM. With the war's end, Birmingham was the first destroyed station to be reconstructed, through a private funding initiative bankrolled by Planetform Inc. With the Edinburgh system then under Gallic Enclave occupation and the terraforming project on Ayr likely to be lost indefinitely, Planetform began to intensely lobby the Bretonian Government to fund alternatives -- using its investment in Manchester as leverage.

Bretonia controversially agreed to fund a comprehensive Planetform feasibility study of Planet Wight in 829 AS. In addition to managing Planetform's activities on Wight, Birmingham also continues to serve it's pre-war purpose -- processing, storing, and transporting Methane, CO2, and Hydrocarbons mined by BMM from the nearby ice asteroids. Planetform currently takes a cut of all profits from BMM's resource sales at Birmingham, and expects that most of the station's output will be earmarked for the terraforming effort once the project's Phase One is greenlit.

The project took the next step forward in early 836 AS, when Planetform formally submitted its findings to the Bretonian government. Despite Planetform's optimistic sales pitch, the project is wildly unpopular with the Bretonian public, who have endured a decade of financial hardship following the Gallic War. As political blowback grows, Gaian ecoterrorists have likewise escalated their own attacks on the station, promising a rocky road if terraforming is formally approved.

589957.mapped:
Originally constructed in 521 AS, to oversee the transition of trade lanes and jump gates to Rheinland ownership after Interspace Commerce (IC) was all but forced to sign agreements to nationalize them, Bonn Station has since become the headquarters of IC within Rheinland, and is the station where all cargo being shipped out of Rheinland is insured for the journey.

Thoroughly angry with having to wipe countless billions of credits of debt away almost overnight, after Kusari and Rheinland both nationalized their trade lanes and jump gates, IC had never been satisfied with the two hundred years of tolls it got in exchange, and it is for this chief reason that a good deal of animosity towards Rheinland and Kusari exists even today. As a result, IC often allowed ships from the Bundschuh, Red Hessians and even the Unioners to dock and purchase supplies, and was even going so far as to donate money to their causes or share information of cargo shipments with them.

This angered the Rheinland government considerably, and when hard proof was finally obtained in late 818, Rheinland wasted no time in evicting IC from its borders. Bonn Station was seized and put under Police administration for several years, but the upkeep costs proved too much for an already heavily burdened governmental budget, even with the aid of Bonn's many onboard transactions.

After the Liberty War's end, the government decided to sell Bonn Station to IC again as a hasty means to recoup some of its wartime losses; but with far heavier and more stringent on-station surveillance with permanent garrisons of police and security. Additionally, Brandenburg was towed and expanded upon whilst the Battleship Strausberg was called to the Southern flank of New Berlin.

IC has once again returned to insuring outbound shipments and managing the billions of credits transacted upon Bonn every day, but rumors still circulate that occasionally they manage to smuggle Rheinland criminals aboard through bribery and other subterfuge. At present these rumors are denied by both IC and the Federal Republic.

589959.mapped:
Brandenburg Station is the command center for the Rheinland Federal Police in New Berlin. The RFP is tasked with handling the interdiction of all illegal activity in the area, including smuggling and piracy. In the aftermath of the 80-Years War, the RFP was forced to carry out many of the Military’s typical duties, including the suppression of terrorism in Dresden and the border worlds. The station was frequently called upon to reinforce overwhelmed RFP system garrisons, and was expanded over the century with larger hangars to accommodate a strategic reserve of quickly deployable squadrons. In 826 AS Wildau Station was completed nearby, with the intention of creating a cutting edge replacement for the increasingly outdated Brandenburg.

Extreme political dysfunction repeatedly derailed the decommissioning, resulting in the somewhat farcical situation of the RFP continuing to maintain two neighboring headquarters, with each operating at half hangar capacity as squadrons were split between the two. In the aftermath of the Civil War, Rheinland’s government finally decided that it would divest Wildau instead, due to its extreme operating costs. As a result, the centuries-old Brandenburg remains functional, if dated. Many RFP commanders bitterly lament the resources squandered on Wildau, noting that the funds could have been used to address the forces’ chronic pilot recruitment and retention issues, potentially preventing the loss of Vierlande Prison.

589961.mapped:
Essen Station is the headquarters of one of Rheinland's oldest corporations, Kruger Minerals. Kruger was a primary supporter of the 80-Years War, with the disastrous conflict exhausting the company’s capital and leaving them as pariahs in the wake of the Popular Revolution. Facing spiraling debts, Kruger initially attempted to rebuild by allying itself with ALG Waste Disposal. This relationship came to an acrimonious end in 806 AS when Kruger narrowly avoided liquidation through an ALG hostile takeover.

The company successfully restructured itself by radically downsizing, abandoning unprofitable manufacturing operations that competed with Daumann, and focusing primarily on resource extraction. Kruger later earned significant dividends through its enthusiastic support of the Imperials during the Civil War, winning influence with the Emperor and governing elite. Now flush with questionably awarded government contracts, the station bustles with activity, as Kruger begins to invest in expansion for the first time in decades.

Essen serves as a processing and distribution hub for the company's raw materials, and as a manufacturing plant for Mining Machinery. In recent years, Essen has also opened new factories producing rudimentary Robotics, fuelled by generous grants provided by the Rheinland government. Despite lawsuits from Kishiro claiming patent theft, Kruger has capitalized on its Robotics to automate several operations, attempting to cut costs by laying off significant numbers of employees.

589963.mapped:
On New Berlin, each day and night lasts for nearly a standard year; the nightside is plunged into frigid, bitter winter, while the dayside experiences a milder summer slightly warmer than freezing. Settled in 3 AS, Rheinland's capital is very close to the abundant mineral resources of the Walker Nebula, rapidly fuelling its development as the House's industrial heart. After the economic collapse brought about by the loss of the 80-Years War with the Gas Miners Guild, New Berlin became a society of extreme contrasts, marked by political radicalism, corruption, black markets, and decadent underground clubs and cabarets.

Recent decades subjected Rheinland to a string of military defeats and scandals, deepening the state's heavy debts. What resulted was a demoralized Military and a population deeply resentful of the corruption and mismanagement that characterized the Federal Republic. Berlin politics became increasingly polarized and violent, with opposing Imperial and Progressive blocs emerging in opposition to mainstream Federal politics. Imperial parties campaigned on the restoration of the protectionist and insular Old Empire, peddling nostalgia for a glorious past that never existed. Reformist parties made unrealistic pledges to fulfil the spirit of the Popular Revolution, offering hollow promises that Rheinland could neither afford or execute.

In 826 AS, a coalition of Progressive reformists won a narrow plurality of seats in the Reichstag. The following months saw Imperial-agitated riots across New Berlin, and brutal RFP reprisals. Matters came to a head the following year with the attempted assassination of Fredrick von Albrecht, the sole remaining heir of the last Emperor of Rheinland. A Military-backed Imperial coup then plunged Rheinland into civil war, with bloody fighting persisting across Planet New Berlin for the duration of the conflict. After fighting one another to an exhausted stalemate, the Holstein Accords ended the conflict in 829 AS with a mutually dissatisfactory compromise, creating the Federal Empire of Rheinland.

Observing the requirements of the Accords, Federalist and Imperial representatives created the Rheinland Consensus Government, formed of senior officials from both factions. The elected Reichstag and office of Chancellor were also restored, with Emperor Fredrick II formally coronated as the Federal Empire's head of state shortly after. The Consensus Government remains rife with political infighting and dysfunction, but is still seen as preferential to resumed bloodshed. Life in Rheinland has gradually returned to normal, although New Berlin's cities still bear many of the scars of the recent conflict.

One of the first large-scale projects undertaken by Daumann Heavy Construction, the Oder Shipyards are responsible for the bulk of current Rheinland Military ship production and maintenance. In the past, Oder’s massive berths built the Imperial Rheinland Navy, with these huge military contracts fuelling much of Daumann’s growth. After the destruction of the Navy during the 80-Years War and the economic crash that followed, Military contracts largely ceased. Daumann was instead forced to expand into the less lucrative fields of commercial and civilian ship construction, where profit margins were heavily stressed by competition from both the Alster Shipyards and Kusari imports.

The explosion of Military ship building contracts across the late 790s saw Oder expand significantly, fuelling Chancellor Niemann's war machine. The immense profits from these contracts subsidized Oder’s operations following the abrupt end of the Colony Wars and the sharp economic crash that followed, despite later scandals and government attempts to claw back the funds. Nevertheless, the shipyard continues to produce and maintain ships for the Rheinland Military using many components produced locally in The Ring's vast factories.

The immense profits from these contracts subsidized Oder’s operations following the abrupt end of the Colony Wars and the sharp economic crash that followed, despite later scandals and government attempts to claw back the funds. Nevertheless, the shipyard continues to produce and maintain ships for the Rheinland Military using many components produced locally in The Ring's vast factories.

589967.text:

GRAVITY: Partial
DOCKING: Yes
AMENITIES: Limited
CREW: 450
589967.mapped:
Where there's junk, there are the Junkers. They've been around since the earliest days of the Trade Lanes. Descended from the working classes, they developed within the House systems as a sort of necessary evil, handling the dirty work that no one else would. They do well salvaging valuable materials from the ever-increasing debris fields throughout Sirius, with the notable exception of Kusari. To this day they remain held at bay by the Hogosha.

Anyone who deals with Junkers knows they live by a strict code; if you're not a Junker, you're not part of the family. A Junker will double-cross you without a second thought, and they're fiercely protective of each other. Most House corporations consider the Junkers to be simple criminals, but Junkers will occasionally do favors for the police, turning in the odd, mid-level criminal or letting them know about the occasional drug shipment. So despite some harassment, the police stop short of shutting them down. The infrequent police cleanup operations are little more than exercises in public relations, though there's no love lost between the two groups.

The Junkers make their official money from salvaging debris within the fields, but also have a good deal going with various criminals, who like their "no questions asked" policy. Tolerated by the governments, Junkers sometimes deal in contraband, but they are extremely hard to catch red-handed. They are frequently patronized by the criminal element for the refuge they offer within the often hostile territory of House capitol systems.

The Rheinland authorities dislike the Junkers, but have so far made no attempt to remove them, as they provide a valuable service in clearing up dangerous wreckage and debris that not even ALG is willing to deal with. In the aftermath of the Civil War, the Junkers have lined their pockets by discretely salvaging lost military wrecks. This is highly illegal but lucrative work that the Junkers have decades of experience in, following the Sigma-13 cleanup project.

589969.mapped:
Stretching around Planet New Berlin's equator, The Ring is the largest human-built structure in Sirius. It is a source of great pride for Rheinland's citizens and its preeminent company and architect, Daumann Heavy Construction. Daumann's rapid expansion in the first centuries after settlement saw the construction of numerous specialized manufacturing, storage, and administrative stations in the capital's orbit, which were connected piece by piece into an ever-growing band. This vast network of facilities are linked by the guide rails of the famous "Ringbahn" shuttle service.

The Ring hosts sections for every purpose imaginable: smelters, foundries, and factories form industrial segments; vast compartmentalized tubes and warehouses provide storage. In recent years, Augsburg-pattern habitats have been added, with these cramped units offering views of New Berlin's frozen landscapes. The Ring's literal encirclement of Planet New Berlin reflects Daumann's dominant position in the House, and announces to the megastructure's visitors that the corporation should be the first choice for anything that can be bought, sold or manufactured in Rheinland.

589971.mapped:
The Somerset is the product of the Warwick Dreadnought program, which aimed to create a class capable of tackling Gallic Valors head-on. Ultimately, the Somerset was not completed until 827 AS, too late for the war it was designed for. The Somerset was eventually deployed to New London orbit to provide symbolic reassurance to the traumatized population, allowing more battle-tested garrison vessels to be released for the Invasion of Edinburgh.

Despite glossy Bretonian propaganda, the reality is that the prototype dreadnought was plagued by technical errors, cost overruns and performance concerns. These technical issues persisted through a major overhaul in 830 AS, leading Armed Forces engineers derisively referring to the ship as “Some Resets” due to frequent electrical failures. The Admiralty remains adamant that the dreadnought is performing adequately regardless.

In 834 AS, the vessel was recalled to Portsmouth Shipyard alongside the Battleship Essex, receiving classified refits overseen by specialist Kusari contractors. The Somerset's overhaul took considerably longer to complete than the Essex's, with military sources adamant that all teething issues have now been worked out. Despite insider concerns, the Somerset was deployed to Dublin via Kusari Jump Drive, and now anchors half of a "Jump Bridge" that is supplying the Bretonian invasion. So far, the ship has performed beyond expectations, with the Jump Drive seeming to benefit from the battleship's significantly heavier reactor.

589973.mapped:
Canterbury Station houses the headquarters for Planetform Inc., a pioneer in transforming uninhabitable or marginally habitable planets into terrestrial worlds. With the sparseness of suitable planets outside of the core systems claimed by Liberty, Planetform Inc. has conducted a considerable amount of business in Bretonia and abroad.

During the conflict with Gallia, Planetform suffered several severe losses of business in Edinburgh and Tau-31, due to the occupation of Planet Harris and the cessation of work on Planet Ayr. Canterbury itself played host to Allied forces during the Battle of New London, weathering many attacks by the Gallic Royal Navy. Owing mostly to the bravery of the Battleships MacDuff and Ottawa, damage to the base was limited.

Following the cessation of hostilities, Planetform began to assess the extent of damage to existing projects, and explore new business opportunities to replace those contracts that were deemed non-viable. Work has already been resumed on Planet Harris, although Planet Ayr's project remains mired in contractual disputes with the Bretonian government. New projects have also been authorized by the Bretonian government on Planet Wight in Manchester, although this decision is deeply controversial.

Gallia - the cause of many of Planetform's woes over the last decade - may also engage the corporation's services in the years to come. Such agreements have been heavily endorsed by the Bretonian government, who see Planetform's work as a means to build centuries-spanning economic links between the two Houses.

589975.mapped:
Constructed in 672 AS, Kensington Shipping Platform was the fruit of Gateway's relative success in the past two centuries. Rising from relative obscurity, Gateway Shipping has shown itself to be a strong competitor to Border Worlds Exports.

Though they may not hold major contracts with Bretonian giants such as BMM and Border Worlds Exports, Gateway Shipping has had great breakthroughs with upstart corporations such as the Independent Miners Guild, Planetform, ALG Waste Disposal, and several other small firms that produce domestic products within Bretonia who were scorned from their respective businesses by BMM and Bowex. By filling niche markets, Gateway has found its place in the Bretonian market, a place large enough to actively compete with Bowex, though the former giant still holds the majority of market share.

With the advance of the Royal Navy into the heart of Bretonia, New London, Kensington sustained damage during raids. However, following the end of hostilities, Gateway has found new opportunities within Bretonia owing to the construction of the nearby Belvedere Refinery, made possible in part in thanks to Gateway lobbying of the Bretonian governement that ALG was the best fit for the job, ignoring recent issues with the Rheinland corporation. With the facility operational, Gateway business in New London is experiencing a much needed boom after some very difficult years. Despite this improvement of the business environment, refugee issues Bretonia is facing in the wake of Leeds and the danger of the route to Kusari remains a concern for the shipping corporation.

ESCAPE VELOCITY: 10.27 km/sec
589977.mapped:
Shrouded in an almost perpetual fog, not helped by the constant drizzling rain, the heart of Bretonia is planet New London, with its capital city and seat of government bearing the same name. Colonized in 19 AS, the vast majority of the Bretonian aristocracy lives here, although even the poorest citizen lives in relative comfort and security. A large majority of New London's population works to support Bretonia's obscenely large bureaucratic system, an almost impenetrable network of obscure titles, government offices and paperwork.

Most of the New Londoners are a dour and cynical sort, no doubt enhanced by the miserable weather, what with the fog and the acid rain, not to mention the atmospheric pollutants from the unregulated heavy industry used extensively in the formative years of the colony. Nevertheless, New London is a considered to be a desirable place to live, and attracts countless tourists and immigrants. The planetary population suffered during the bombardment during the war with Gallia, but is thought to be heavily inflated by Leeds refugees, which is an ongoing issue for Bretonia.

All of the major Bretonian corporations have offices on New London, including Bowex and Gateway. The Bretonia Police Authority's central headquarters is here, but the Armed Forces only have recruitment outlets on the planet, with the majority of the Armed Forces administrative capabilties kept in space.

589979.mapped:
After the Gallic War's conclusion, the Bretonian government was forced to evaluate its long term options for the construction of a military shipyard. Despite the symbolic and cultural value of Southampton Shipyard, it was ultimately determined that the cost of recovery and the wider strategic position made a New London site infeasible. Following the Glassing of Leeds, Bretonia's reduced ability to adequately secure the Tau frontier would place a repaired Southampton at unacceptable risk in the event of a future war. Similarly, it was deemed unacceptable for Aland to continue operating as Bretonia's main military shipyard on anything but a short-term emergency basis due to its exposed location and inadequate facilities. After a protracted deliberation period a decision was made to develop a new installation in Cambridge, orbiting Planet Sarum. The Construction Ship Fenland was deployed to handle this task, hauling large sections of the new shipyard consisting of individually constructed modules. Each module is hauled to the construction site to be welded together.

After a lengthy construction period which saw non-Bretonian participation, even from BMM mining rival Daumann, the ship yard was completed in late 827, and was officially named Portsmouth Shipyard in a ceremony observed by the monarch. The shipyard completion has made Aland no longer required for ship building efforts, with most of the production being moved over to the far more capable Portsmouth.

589981.mapped:
An old space station from Bretonia's age of expansion, Thames was designed to function as a hub for in and outbound cargo for Planet New London, and a storehouse for BMM Gold exports from Dublin. In 826 AS, Thames found itself in the middle of the Battle for Planet New London, the largest fleet battle in human history. It is believed that Thames survived the battle with minimal damage because Gallic forces had intended to use the station as a staging depot for a terrestrial invasion once orbital space had been secured.

With the loss of Graves Station in 831 AS, Thames saw a sharp drop in traffic, although some Gold continued to be stocked as a result of confiscations by the Essex blockade. When the Battleships Essex and Somerset were sent for overhauls in Cambridge, the BAF temporarily requisitioned the Outpost as a patrol base. Following the 835 AS Invasion of Dublin, BMM has resumed Thames' administration, and has begun constructing smelting facilities in anticipation of a surging stock of Gold.
