589983.mapped:
Trafalgar Station was founded shortly after Bretonia's industrial boom when mass amounts of salvage and ship debris were beginning to coalesce into the Southampton Debris Field. During the Gallic War, many pirate factions utilized Trafalgar as a launching point for raids on Gallic supply transports in Leeds. This made the base a high priority target for the Gallic Royal Navy when they stormed New London using the nearby jump hole. While largely destroyed during Gallia's assault, repairs and repressurization were quickly carried out to bring the station back into service as a fuel depot and staging ground.

Following the devastating conclusion of the Battle of New London, the Bretonia Armed Forces occupied the station to monitor smuggling routes through the debris field. In a seemingly bizarre show of generosity, Bretonia later ceded control of the station back to the Junkers in early 827 AS. As a consequence, there is uneasy speculation in the Bretonian underworld about the nature of any deal the Junkers may have cut with the Crown, and what that means for their own interests. Despite this, scrap salvaging has resumed, as has Trafalgar's role as Bretonia's black market of choice.

With the opening of Belvedere Refinery, Trafalgar has added a veneer of legitimacy to its operations, mimicking the mutually beneficial relationship the Junkers and ALG shared during the Sigma 13 cleanup. Since the Bretonian withdrawal from Dublin in 831 AS, the space around Trafalgar has also been the site of several bloody clashes between Corsair and Molly patrols. While the Junkers have attempted to keep the peace around their base, neither faction appears willing to accept a truce, however temporary.

589987.mapped:
Hogosha translates literally as "guardian" or "protector," reflecting the organization's rather romantic view held not only by its own members, but by a large portion of the Kusari population -- though by no means the majority. Far from protectors, the Hogosha are actually descendents of the organized crime syndicates that grow within the shadow of any sizable human society -- though the Hogosha have an oddly symbiotic relationship with both the government and Samura.

Their political connections would make any serious attempt to dismantle them an embarrassment to Kusari as any number of secrets and deals that had been kept out of the public eye came to light. However, neither do the Hogosha have a free license to operate. Arrests of low-level Hogosha operators who flaunt their activities are frequent and help keep up appearances - very important in Kusari. "Hard" crime, such as drug smuggling, is not tolerated, both by the Hogosha and the Kusari government.

Individual opinions vary, but most police consider the Hogosha a necessary evil required for the smooth functioning of Kusari society. The government simply treats the Hogosha like any other large keiretsu. The Kusari population as a whole has a similar attitude: It is pointless to like or dislike the Hogosha; they are simply a fact of life.

The Hogosha handle Artifact and gun smuggling and the fencing of stolen goods. They also do occasional dirty work for Samura. They view the Blood Dragons as a major threat to their existence and have engaged in turf wars with them, mostly in the asteroid fields of Tokyo. The Golden Chrysanthemums are a new problem, as they have few qualms about dealing in the drug trade or its consequences. Since they have no corruptible leaders or long associations with Samura or the Kusari government and police, The GC, like the Blood Dragons, are dangerous to the Hogosha way of life. They view the Junkers as their only real competitors within the Sirius Sector, and their only obstacle to expansion into the other Houses. They have approached the Corsairs to assist them in their expansion plans, which has resulted in a loose alliance between the two groups.

The Hogosha made a recent arrangement to purchase Artifacts directly from the Corsairs on the cruise ship Hawaii, a move that infuriated the GMG, who formerly served as the middleman between the two crime syndicates. It also raised the ire of the LSF, who applied pressure on Orbital Spa to deny landing privileges to the two factions.

After the construction of the Jump Gates that linked Kusari to the other Houses, it was decided that a new station would be necessary to offload and store the new goods flowing into the New Tokyo system, and also serve as an administrative centre for foreign corporations. Initially, this was all done onboard Roppongi and Deshima, but as time went by it became clear that this wasn't enough. With this in mind, Narita Outpost was completed in late 714 AS

While not as large as Roppongi Station was in terms of population, the bulk of Narita consists of warehouses and deep freeze storage bunkers. It is designed to be a large depot where cargo bound for or coming from other houses is transferred, and then distributed by smaller Kusari shippers to the local economies. Settled in 5 AS, New Tokyo is the capitol of the Kusari Empire and, with nearly 11 billion people spread across various island groups, its most populous planet. Despite (or perhaps because of) this crowding, New Tokyo is a vibrant world with centuries of history and some of the most advanced technology in the colonies. Due to the lack of available land on which to farm and build, the Kusari have economised land use, and much of their technological advances have been geared towards constructing huge glittering skyscrapers and even entire "tower cities", packing as much as possible into as small a space as possible. To foreigners, Kusari architecture often feels cramped.

It is a vibrant world with centuries of history and some of the most advanced technology in Sirius, but it is not without conflict. Kusari culture is in a transitional state, with a relatively small feudal-style aristocracy leading an increasing number of citizens who are developing a stronger sense of individuality. Bureaucrats and corporations wrestle with the popular media and the younger generations over how best to handle the rapidly increasing changes in Kusari society.

589993.text:
In the early years of the Kusari Shogunate, foreign immigration was strictly controlled and permanent foreign settlement on New Tokyo were strictly forbidden. While the Shogunate was unwilling to bend these rules, it still accommodated foreign business interests by constructing Roppongi Station in 318 AS. Roppongi quickly became home to large numbers of elite repatriates from New York and New London who had long term business interests in Kusari. Roppongi later became the focal point of the 521 AS Kusari-Rheinland Nationalization Crisis, when both Houses seized their Trade Lanes and Jump Gates, expelling Interspace Commerce in the process.

Interspace was permitted to return in the aftermath of the 80-Years War between Rheinland and the GMG, owing to financial transactions between Kusari and Liberty and quickly established several major offices on Roppongi. By the time of the short-lived Kusari Republic, many of the restrictions on foreign companies had been lifted in the interests of progress. Roppongi became a busy trade center and luxury concourse, bustling with corporations, local celebrities and thronging crowds of New Tokyo socialites. Most of the major houses maintained their Kusari embassies or consular services aboard.

In 832 AS, a nuclear dirty bomb was detonated in the station’s lower hangars. Although emergency bulkheads were able to prevent complete disintegration, the interior was heavily irradiated and swept by fires that smoldered for months after. The attack provoked immediate outrage from the other Houses due to the heavy loss of life, and the destruction of embassy facilities. Kusari now faces intense pressure to crack down on the Farmer’s Alliance, who claimed responsibility for the attack. As of 834 AS, Samura Heavy Industries is leading efforts to decontaminate and dismantle the station.

Constructed in 50 AS by Samura Industries, Yokohama Shipyard was the first orbital construction facility in Kusari, and also the first shipyard built by any House in Sirius. Originally it manufactured gas miners and gas transports for the H-Fuel industry, but it was eventually forced to concede the gas miners and transport contracts to its archrival, Kishiro Technologies. The shipyard has since then retooled to produce as smaller military ships for the Kusari Naval Forces, as well as large station components - a task few other yards in Kusari, including Yukawa, are big enough for.

Yokohama still does a considerable amount of business manufacturing space habitats and despite stiff competition from Kishiro, in 815 AS it was granted the license to continue its centuries old tradition of constructing Kusari Naval Forces ships for another 15 years at least.

590000.mapped:
Baltimore Shipyard was constructed by Deep Space Engineering (DSE) in 54 AS -- the second shipyard in Sirius. DSE produced many of the ships, station components and later, Docking Rings, that fueled Liberty's early expansion. Notable products included the progenitors of the "Heron" line of commercial cargo Trains. For centuries Baltimore was a key player in civilian shipbuilding, however this period came to a gradual close by 600 AS. Cheap and efficient transports from Kusari drove Liberty's domestic shipbuilding out of the market. DSE was forced into the industry's margins, primarily constructing prison ships and custom-built luxury liners.

Baltimore made a significant return to the freight construction market in 812 AS, with the production of the first Bison heavy transports for the Liberty Navy. This design became popular with local corporations soon after, when the Tau War between Bretonia and Kusari prompted a domestic backlash against Kusari produced products. This prompted a refresh of the ancient Mastodon design, and a return to market soon after -- with sales booming thanks to a patriotic fervor triggered by the Gallic War. While orders for these more complicated and expensive designs began to dwindle in the peacetime following 826 AS, a combination of cost-cutting and moderate government and corporate interest justified continued production.

In 836 AS, Liberty nationalized Baltimore due to the devastating Kusari first strike against Norfolk Shipyard. The Navy engineers who survived the destruction of Norfolk were dismayed to discover Baltimore's inadequate plant machinery, which is decades old and long overdue replacement. Navy repair crews and Deep Space Engineering technicians are now battling to save critically damaged capital ships, despite of the inadequacy of the available facilities. The Liberty Government has begun to issue War Bonds to raise funds for immediate upgrades.

590002.mapped:
The flagship of the Liberty Navy since 799 AS, the Missouri has for decades served as a mascot for the Republic's military prowess. Originally a testbed for pioneering new engineering processes, the Missouri became a standard of excellence against which all later Liberty capital ships were compared. Equipped with some of the most capable technologies in the Navy's arsenal, the Missouri's genetics can be found in all future warship classes.

Despite the battleship's revered symbolic status within the Navy, its service record is notably sparse. The Missouri has traditionally maintained its posting in New York as the capital's guardian, far from hostile front lines. While its fleet elements contributed commendably to several battles during the Gallic War and Insurgency Campaign, the ship itself was until recently primarily credited with counter piracy patrols around New York.

The Missouri's reputation was severely dented in mid 836 AS, when Kusari launched a surprise assault on Norfolk Shipyard. The Missouri and its fleet were already on-site as the Kusari force deployed. Despite this, Admiral Matthew Oldendorf ordered his ships to pull back and regroup into a standard battle-line formation before confronting the enemy. Furious senators have blamed the delays from this maneuver for the catastrophic damage inflicted upon the shipyard.

Some theorists speculate that the Badlands Disaster anomaly was involved, but no official sources have spoken about the destruction as anything other than an accident.

GRAVITY: Complete
DOCKING: Yes
AMENITIES: Limited
CREW: 760
590006.mapped:
The Rogues are a product of over two centuries of systematic lower-class cleansing that occurred on the Liberty planets of Manhattan, Denver, and Los Angeles. Relocated to the Texas prison system, many of them end up planetside on Houston upon release. Some stayed straight and joined the population scratching out a living. The rest returned to their life of crime, often ending up vaporized by a pursuing Liberty police patrol or back in prison for longer stretches, manning the prison factories that are the economic lifeblood of the Texas system.

Some say the massive LPI roundups of even minor offenders in Liberty have more to do with staffing these plants cheaply than reducing crime. Fresh out of the incubator of the Texas prison system, they have limited choices. Either they work in the factories of Houston for a pittance, join the Bounty Hunters and hunt down their former brethren, go radical and hook up with the Xenos, or rejoin their former partners in crime. The latter path is the obvious one for most. Simply put, these are not-too-quick opportunists, people willing to do whatever it takes to make a buck and get by until tomorrow. Usually they end up taking the fall for anything illegal that occurs in Liberty, whether they were involved or not.

The Rogues were initially a disorganized lot, but over the last century have slowly evolved into quite a highly organised collection of criminals. They are responsible for most of the Trade Lane attacks in Liberty space and the adjacent Independent Worlds, usually operating in groups of three or more ships, utilising a variety of tactics that generally revolve around blasting their unsuspecting targets with overcharged laser weapons. They occasionally provide shelter for the Outcasts in exchange for Cardamine, but they are not averse to dealing in the artifacts trade either. The main Rogue ethos seems to be to make money however possible, regardless of how low or uncivilized their actions may be.

Buffalo Base is the original Liberty Rogue hideout, deep in the badlands of the New York system. Constructed in 672 AS by malcontents from Houston and Manhattan, it has served as the main operations centre for the Rogues across the entire of Liberty. With the authorities loathe to patrol or pursue suspects within the confines of the extremely dangerous Badlands, Buffalo Base is the safest criminal hideout in New York.

Detroit is the headquarters for Detroit Munitions, one of the oldest privately owned companies in Liberty. Detroit has been manufacturing small- and medium-sized arms since its founding by patriarch Ed Garner in 614 AS His name still graces the company's most popular line of blasters, despite the occasional attempt by an Ageira executive to have his own name imprinted onto a weapons line.

Although Detroit Munitions as a company has been extremely successful, it eventually decided to partner with Ageira Technologies, in an effort to gain access to even more advanced weapons research, particularly in light of the contracts that Ageira holds with the Liberty Navy and the Liberty Security Forces. Ageira now owns the station itself and pays for its upkeep, although Detroit Munitions has several new outlets on Denver and a weapons testing range on Pittsburgh's moon of Maine.

Fort Bush was one of the earliest outposts established during the settlement of Liberty, constructed in 70 AS to manage the settlement of Texas, Colorado, and Planet Pittsburgh. As Liberty expanded, Fort Bush became a popular jumping-off point for any number of wild business ventures as explorers set out to make their fortunes among the stars.

For centuries, Fort Bush provided a haven for traders from all over Sirius who had business to conduct in Liberty. A branch of Liberty Police, Inc. (LPI) headquartered aboard the station maintained the peace necessary for a free economy by suppressing pirate activity in the debris fields and maintaining the automated weapons platforms that defend the nearby Trade Lane junction.

Following the surprise Kusari assault on Norfolk Shipyard, Fort Bush's defenses were requisitioned by the Liberty Navy, and significant hangar space garrisoned by area protection squadrons. As a result of the Baltimore Defense Grid, merchant shipping bound for Fort Bush has precipitously declined with most commercial functions instead being absorbed by Trenton Outpost and Newark Station.

590013.mapped:
Founded in the year 1 AS, Manhattan was the first human colony established in the Sirius Sector. Over the last eight centuries it has grown into a teeming world of billions who live and work in a number of large metropolises that dot the planet's surface, making Manhattan the most densely populated planet in Sirius. Its main metropolis, suburbs not counting, numbers over 220 million people - with the hull of the Liberty sleeper ship as a towering beacon at it's center. It still remains a bustling tourist destination, with many gorgeous sandy beaches and crowded shopping promenades.

Nearly the entire population is dedicated to the manifest destiny of the Liberty free market, and today Manhattan is the hub of a vast commercial network that stretches into almost every corner of Sirius. While "going to Manhattan" has become a commonly accepted phrase for leaving home to seek your fortune, the cost of living on Manhattan itself is extravagantly high. If a trend is new and exciting -- and expensive -- then it almost certainly originated here.

Despite the turmoil surrounding the brief, but bloody, Nomad war that ended in 801 AS, Manhattan has continued to grow, and shipments arrive from all over Sirius on a daily basis. While there are reminders of the Nomad War still left over, most people prefer to focus on the future and, for Liberty at least, it appears to be a bright one.

Interspace Corporate was founded in 204 AS by Ageira and Deep Space Engineering, since they could pool the necessary capital in insurance and finance. Built in the same year, Newark Station is the local headquarters for the now renamed "Interspace Commerce" (IC), one of the largest financial concerns in the Sirius Sector. While Interspace was initially responsible for financing the construction of the vast Jump Gate and Trade Lane network that connects the various colonies, it was forced to divest itself of these holdings as a result of the Rheinland-Kusari Trade Embargo in 521 AS

The corporation changed its name to Interspace Commerce and has since transitioned to insuring cargo shipments within and between the various colonies. The remainder of the Newark Station population is a constantly shifting crowd of traders, technocrats, executives, and Bounty Hunters, all cutting deals and arranging for the transport or protection of their goods.

Norfolk Shipyard was built in 230 AS as Liberty's primary military shipyard, and the headquarters of the Liberty Navy. Its dockyards were the birthplace of almost all of Liberty's capital ships, and responsible for pioneering many of technological advances that came to define the Liberty Navy. Norfolk Shipyard possessed some of the most advanced shipbuilding and manufacturing facilities in Sirius, producing the unique, triple hulled armor plating design that protects all of Liberty's largest capital ships. The Navy jealously guarded the Norfolk's commercial and military secrets, to the extent that even civilian defense contractors were granted limited access to the facility with great reluctance.

In recent years, Norfolk has been at its busiest since the Gallic War, with its berths fully occupied with the construction of new ships and the refitting of older vessels. This tracks Liberty's escalating feuds with Kusari, which threatened to spill over into active conflict at any moment. The leak of the Niyodo Files in early 836 AS prompted significant debate among Liberty's admiralty on how forces should be deployed to counter the threat of Jump Drive assaults. Common consensus agreed that Kusari would likely strike lightly defended infrastructure, to maximize damage and minimize casualties. Light rapid response forces were distributed widely across Liberty to respond to these raids. This projection proved to be woefully inaccurate, when Kusari launched a decisive first strike later that year.

The Battleship Hamamatsu and a supporting fleet were jumped directly inside Norfolk's defense grid, utilizing a "Jump Matrix" that had been smuggled into the system aboard a neutral-flagged transport shortly before. The Kusari fleet flung itself into the teeth of Norfolk's garrison, bombing the shipyard scaffolds and blasting open bulkheads to devastate the shipyard's hangars. Kusari endured horrific casualties to execute this ambush, with the Battleship Hamamatsu eventually succumbing to damage and ramming the shipyard. Both the battleship and shipyard suffered critical reactor meltdowns as a result, with the shell of station's core now blazing in nuclear fire. A massive rescue operation is ongoing, in an attempt to extract any surviving senior officers or engineers trapped within.

Early estimates fear that the destruction of Norfolk Shipyard represents the worst single day losses in the history of the Liberty Navy, with more than a dozen Admirals believed to have been killed.

Pittsburgh is covered by a single vast desert, broken only by large rocky outcroppings that were big enough to escape being swallowed up by the sand. Without any ice asteroids in close proximity, the planet was not considered a good candidate for terraforming and remained sparsely populated until a full-scale mineral survey in 650 AS pinpointed enormous deposits of Boron in the form of borax salts deep within the Corridera Plateau. A large scale mining operation was established on the planet in 660 AS by Deep Space Engineering to exploit these deposits, and it is now one of the only raw material extraction facility left within Liberty space.

Since the success of DSE's boron mining concerns, there has been an increasing need for miners and other workers. DSE has also started to establish other manufacturing plants at the planet, as environmental regulations on Pittsburgh are virtually nonexistant. Many refugees that come seeking asylum in Liberty often get redirected to Pittsburgh to find work in the boron mines, and to live in the cities that are slowly sprawling outwards around the industrial facilities. Liberty authorities estimate that Pittsburgh's population will grow to meet the demand for labor.

GRAVITY: Partial
DOCKING: Yes
AMENITIES: Limited
CREW: 430
590021.mapped:
Where there's junk, there are the Junkers. They've been around since the earliest days of the Trade Lanes. Descended from the working classes, they developed within the House systems as a sort of necessary evil, handling the dirty work that no one else would. They do well salvaging valuable materials from the ever-increasing debris fields throughout Sirius, with the notable exception of Kusari. To this day they remain held at bay by the Hogosha.

Anyone who deals with Junkers knows they live by a strict code; if you're not a Junker, you're not part of the family. A Junker will double-cross you without a second thought, and they're fiercely protective of each other. Most House corporations consider the Junkers to be simple criminals, but Junkers will occasionally do favors for the police, turning in the odd, mid-level criminal or letting them know about the occasional drug shipment. So despite some harassment, the police stop short of shutting them down. The infrequent police cleanup operations are little more than exercises in public relations, though there's no love lost between the two groups.

The Junkers make their official money from salvaging debris within the fields, but also have a good deal going with various criminals, who like their "no questions asked" policy. Tolerated by the governments, Junkers sometimes deal in contraband, but they are extremely hard to catch red-handed. They are frequently patronized by the criminal element for the refuge they offer within the often hostile territory of House capitol systems.

The Junkers of Rochester have a particularly hard time with a wide variety of issues, both from the law, and from unlawful elements fighting over the lucrative business the base is key to. Recently, a large scale attack by the Xenos caused the base significant damage, though it is difficult to tell the difference considering the original state of the base.

590023.mapped:
Trenton Outpost is the headquarters of Universal Shipping, one of the "Big Three" family of Liberty companies that also includes Ageira Technologies and Interspace Commerce. Universal Shipping made its fortune by gambling on shipping silver from Colorado to California for use in terraforming Los Angeles, long before Jump Gates and Trade Lanes reduced the risk of transporting goods over such long distances. Universal then cemented its reputation as the premiere Liberty shipping company in 181 AS by signing a contract to handle all shipping between Ageira Technologies facilities and Deep Space Engineering construction sites, a contract they old to this date.

It is often rumoured that Universal Shipping has made several clandestine deals with the Xenos, Universal Shipping convoys are often ignored by them. This is strenuously denied by the Universal's Executive Board, but nevertheless the rumours continue to persist.

590025.mapped:
West Point Military Academy has been training the best and brightest officers in the Liberty military for over 600 years. Completed in 189 AS and formally opened a year later, the current commandant of West Point is Admiral Matthew Evans, son of the former commandant, Walter Evans. West Point has had many famous personalities who have both trained at the Academy and served on its teaching staff, including decorated veterans such as Captain Jason Findley, Captain Marcus Walker and Commander (now Rear Admiral) Jun'ko Zane.

Utilized as the primary military training center for the Liberty Armed Forces, almost any pilot and commander within the Liberty Navy, LSF, and even some within the Liberty Police have gone through the station's training regimens. After the Gallic war, an expansion project was initiated which actually saw the Academy close for the entire month of January in 827 A.S., the first time in over six centuries, with supporting training taking place on Richmond Military Academy in Virginia. These renovations were completed a few months later, with new intructional wings being completed on the underbelly of the Academy. In addition to these new wings, mooring berths for retired warships were also added, allowing for warship crew in-training to serve aboard a physical model as opposed to a digital model via virtual reality.

Following the vessel's decommissioning after 82 years of valiant service, the first ship to occupy these new berths was the aging Battleship Mississippi, a welcome sight to station staff and travelers alike. For some who go through warship training at West Point, training aboard the Mississippi has even become a point of pride, defining a new era of post-Gallic war officers and enlisted.

590027.text:
CLASS: Tempest
CREW: CLASSIFIED
ARMAMENT: CLASSIFIED

This formidable ship patrols Omega-52, guarding the heart of the Coalition from invaders.

Bold letters on the ship's stern plating proclaim "Katz lives!", a statement of the vessel's symbolic value to the Coalition. The Alvin Katz is more than a warship. It is a testament to the courage of the Coalition's people, and proudly carries the name of a hero.
590027.mapped:
The Alvin Katz, named after a historical leader of the Coalition, was, in 823 AS, the first Tempest-class carrier launched commissioned from Aralsk. Acting as an advanced forward operating base, this ship has traveled all across the Omegas, projecting the Coalition's military power.

In its first major operation, the Alvin Katz struck into Rheinland. Its task force helped liberate political prisoners from Vierlande Prison in Hamburg, escaping before Rheinland forces could properly retaliate. Following this mission, it was ordered to return to Omega-47.

After the Red Hessians redeployed Battleship Kassel to the same system, there were concerns that their bases were exposed to Corsair attack. These fears ultimately proved accurate when, in 827 AS, the raiders of the Battleship Fes attacked Planet Tangier. The CPW Alvin Katz was faced with its gravest challenge yet as it defended the planet together with a small Hessian garrison.

The battle was fierce, and the Alvin Katz task force took heavy casualties from the Corsair assault. The Hessian installation orbiting the planet was destroyed in a last-ditch push by the Fes, but it was costly for the Corsairs: they took many losses themselves and could not capture Tangier before being forced to retreat by the Alvin Katz.

While the outcome is regarded in hindsight as a victory, the toll on the flagship and its fleet was severe. They spent some time in Tangier orbit for long, arduous repairs and refits, often flying patrols with unarmed hulks as decoys. Fortunately for the Coalition, the Alvin Katz's career was quiet until after its repairs. On the way back through Omega-47, the carrier had a close encounter with Battleship Athos, but it only amounted to skirmishes between the fleets' escorts.

In 831 AS, Alvin Katz was returned to service. It received new shipboard electronics, optimized subsystems, and newly built strike craft wings, ready to be flown by new recruits. At the head of a proper fleet once more, this formidable ship now patrols Omega-52 to guard the heart of the Coalition from invaders.

590033.mapped:
Freeport 1 was opened in 738 AS, by a group of vagrants, wanderers and social outcasts that had left territories of the Houses in order to live beyond the rules and regulations enforced in the core systems. It was the first ever Freeport to be constructed, as the name clearly states, and it quickly gained popularity with the criminals, outlaws and others of a dubious disposition as a place to easily obtain supplies and repair their ships. Most of the criminals who visit Freeport 1 tend to be members of the Mollys or the Corsairs, although the occasional Red Hessian and Gaian are seen onboard.

Originally a small abandoned DSE depot left over from the construction of the Omega 3 trade lane, Freeport 1 has grown, with new cargo modules and habitation decks being constructed until the station was barely recognisable from the small platform it started out as. Small ships are known to be constructed here, sold to both freelancers, criminals and other zoners, and although Bretonia has made irritated noises towards the Freeport, they have as yet left it alone, preferring to put up with the annoyance of criminals docking there to the unknown consequences that might otherwise occur by antagonising the largely peaceful Zoner society.

590037.text:
DIAMETER: 7,053 km.
MASS: 10.98 x 10e23 kg.
TERRAIN: Desert.
TEMPERATURE: -71°C to 70°C
ESCAPE VELOCITY: 13.57 km/sec
590037.mapped:
Planet Sprague (referred to in Bretonia as Planet Nottingham) is an arid world that was marked for Bretonian exploitation as early as 663 AS. BMM orbital surveys initially indicated the presence valuable minerals, however early prospectors were stunned to discover that the detected "deposits" were actually ancient ruins. Cambridge xenoarchaeologists identified these as Dom'Kavash structures, constructed millennia before humanity's arrival in Sirius. Several key sites were destroyed during the Nomad war, along with the planet's docking ring.

In response to the impending loss of Leeds, Bretonia authorised the settlement of Nottingham in 818 AS. This was intended preserve as much of Leeds' war-critical heavy industry as possible, and rehouse refugees fleeing the warzone. Following the Glassing of Leeds, the colony must now permanently house a substantial population that is primarily concerned with mining, manufacturing and construction. Nottingham's hastily developed infrastructure has resulted in poor living standards, with many settlements comparable to previous slum zones on Planet Leeds.

While there is no shortage of employment to be found, BMM has been accused of corner cutting and unsafe practices in its management of the colony. Groups such as the Mollys have been quick to prey on these tensions, and frequently recruit from dissatisfied workers. The BPA have struggled to control criminal and radical activity on the colony, and have resorted to the enlistment of local militias to try and keep the peace.

The planet also hosts a considerable population of migrant labor, who are rotated continually from other planets within Bretonia. This population is heavily engaged in vital construction and mining projects on the surface to make the inhospitable planet worth living on long term. Transports carrying these laborors however come under attack frequently by Mollys preaching freedom, or slavers looking for produce.

590041.mapped:
Leon Base was established by the Corsairs around 550 AS, almost a century after the Corsair return to the stars. Corsair raiders were frequently lost in the intense radiation emitted by the neutron star of Omega-41 while moving to, or returning from, raids into Bretonia or Rheinland. Hollowing out one of the largest planetary fragments in the system was a logical choice, but the work was dangerous and countless lives were lost due to radiation poisoning.

Radiation poisoning remains a major concern to the occupants of Leon to date. The asteroid absorbs most radiation, but occasional bursts from the dead star can overwhelm the safety it provides. Radiation treatment drugs are always in high demand at the base.

Cadiz is a Corsair base floating next to the infamous Hammen Hole in Omega-5. Formerly designed as a large population centre to house nearly 1,200 people, it has since mostly turned into a war armory, with crowds of rough and rowdy pirates inhabiting its quarters.

The Corsairs had originally founded the base in 720 AS after surveying the Omega-5 system and discovering several jump holes leading to a number of important systems within, quickly realising the potential of the system as a key point for launching raids into the lower Omega systems and Bretonia. Unwilling to share the "Omega Crossroads", the Corsairs have been trying to remove the Hessian presence from Omega-5 for over 70 years, but so far without much success.

GRAVITY: Complete
DOCKING: Yes
AMENITIES: Limited
CREW: 470
590045.mapped:
Ronneburg is the name of a Red Hessian base located near the infamous Hammen Hole in Omega-5. Functioning almost solely as a resupply and repair station, it is known among the ranks of the Hessians as "the last gate to hell".

Originally founded in 724 AS (before the beginning of the actual Hessian - Corsair conflict) Ronneburg was a base composed of a few asteroids joined together to create a strong outer crust, while still allowing for an installation to be built within. Originally, the point of this was to protect the base against collisions with other, nearby rocks. Ronneburg was to become a major staging point for Hessian raids into Omega-3 and Omega-7. The Omega-5 system, although without any clear purpose or resources, contained abnormal amounts of jump hole anomalies leading to all across southern Sirius. Such a crossroads system was immediately recognised as being extremely valuable for the purposes of launching supply raids further and further away from the Dresden system.

When the Corsairs began their all out assault on Hessian bases in 740 AS, Ronneburg was quickly established as the very frontline, and the focal point of the Hessian defence until a few years later, when the Corsair offensive had lost the initiative, and the Hessians successfully managed to push the attackers back towards their own base in the system. For the next seventy years a nigh constant string of conflicts would rage on between the two bases, obliterating men, ships and asteroids alike, slowly clearing a large empty area in-between the bases which eventually became known as the Hammen Hole. Strong defensive lines created by both sides on either side of the Hole quickly brought the war to a stalemate, as neither side was strong enough to breach each other's defences. Battles would still rage on in the middle, with both sides sending small raiding parties to distant jump holes. A careful, if not terrible, balance would be achieved at the cost of hundreds of lives lost in this drawn out war. Despite all this, Ronneburg still serves as the most important defensive point and supply base for the Hessians in the distant Omega systems, particularly for raiding parties heading to the Casablanca base in Omega-47.

CREW: 1,970
590047.mapped:
Briesen Mining Facility was established by Daumann Heavy Construction in 798 AS for the extraction of Copper and Cobalt deposits. This was heavily subsidized by the Rheinland government, with the extracted resources being used to bolster the massive expansion of the Military in the buildup to the Colony Wars. Further expansion was significantly hindered in the aftermath of the war as economic depression made new investments risky. Even worse, leaked documents revealed the extent of Daumann's wartime profiteering, and “corrupt” payments gifted to the corporation by Niemann’s administration.

Forced by public outrage, Chancellor Steller began the difficult process of clawing back the previously awarded grants. After years of lengthy court challenges, the government eventually agreed to levy a special tax on extracted minerals as a way of gradually recovering these funds. By this point, Daumann had realized the richness of deposits to be found in Omega-7, and knew neither the IMG nor Kruger had the scale or capital to fully exploit them. Their plan to seize sole control of these minerals involved frequent use of mercenaries to harass rival groups, as well as intense political lobbying on New Berlin.

This bore fruit in 821 AS, when the Battleship Schwerin was controversially deployed to the system. The battleship's patrols allowed Daumann to significantly reduce its security and escort service, effectively offloading security costs onto the government. It instead reinvested these funds into expanding its mining fleet. As Briesen expanded, so did its profits -- attracting the attention of both the Corsairs and Red Hessians. These frequent raids against mining operations have drawn a number of Bounty Hunters to the station, while beleaguered RFP patrols also frequently resupply here.

Elbich Mining Facility was established by Kruger Minerals in 797 AS for the extraction of Silver and Cobalt deposits. Kruger were initially unwilling to expand into the dangerous Border World, however they eventually caved to lobbying by ALG, hoping to curry favor for a corporate merger that would stave off imminent bankruptcy. While much of Elbich’s output was initially earmarked for ALG’s smelters at Dortmund Station, stocks were quickly requisitioned by the government to bolster the massive expansion of the Military in the buildup to the Colony Wars.

The business arrangement with ALG had collapsed acrimoniously by 806 AS, following a failed hostile takeover. Kruger was left facing near-bankruptcy once more, avoiding dissolution only through the timely intervention of private New Berlin investors. During this period, Kruger’s Omega-7 operations languished, as the corporation did not have the available capital to expand Elbich or its mining fleet. Only through dramatically cutting manufacturing operations elsewhere did Kruger bring its losses under control. By the time the board was able to fully focus on Omega-7 once more, their rival Daumann had become incredibly well entrenched.

In 830 AS, Kruger released a new line of industrial Robotics on Essen Station. Before long, it sought to demonstrate the effectiveness of this crude, semi-autonomous machinery by overhauling Elbich as a test-case. Hundreds of mining crews were laid off once installation was completed in 834 AS. Despite expectations of increased profits and grand savings from the reduced payroll, Elbich’s actual output has been reduced to a trickle, largely due to sabotage by infuriated crew members. Kruger has vowed to root out and prosecute these “IMG sympathizers”, but faces an increasingly difficult situation in the interim.

Freistadt Base is run by the Independent Miners Guild (IMG) to provide support for the mining of Copper, Cobalt, and Silver from nearby asteroid fields. Originally a Deep Space Engineering (DSE) waystation left over from the construction of the Omega-7 Trade Lane, it was reoccupied by unemployed miners in the wake of the economic collapse of Rheinland after the 80-Year War. These miners joined with the IMG not long after the discovery of abundant mineral deposits in the surrounding asteroid fields.

The IMG have attempted to navigate the escalating tensions in the system after both Daumann and Kruger established their own local operations in the late 790s. Both groups are believed to have bankrolled mercenaries to harass one another and the Guild’s operations, although the Rheinland corporations typically jointly blame the IMG for these attacks. As a result, the Rheinland Military’s Battleship Schwerin was posted near Freistadt for many years -- despite Bretonia and the IMG’s protests -- before eventually being replaced by the permanent Elbe Border Fortress.

In 834 AS, Omega-7 became more turbulent than ever for the Guild, following the arrival of BMM wildcat miners from neighboring Omega-3. The Bretonians have attempted to steal Silver deposits, sparking conflict with the system’s locals. Kruger has also laid off hundreds of its Elbich mining crews after implementing crude Robotics to automate many functions. As a result, Freistadt has been inundated with furious, unemployed miners who are eager to get even with their former employers.

590053.text:

TERRAIN: Terrestrial
TEMPERATURE: -23°C to 31°C
ESCAPE VELOCITY: 12.69 km/sec
590053.mapped:
The fifth sleeper ship, the Hispania, launched at the same time as its sister ships and broke through the Coalition blockade in the Sol system. Unfortunately, sabotage by Coalition agents that had secreted themselves onboard crippled the engines just as the vessel arrived in the Sirius sector. The passengers awakened from their cryogenic sleep to discover the ship was drifting towards an unknown star system. When the Hispania drifted within range of a red dwarf system, conflict aboard the ship escalated, and about half of the surviving colonists decided to take escape pods, chancing their survival on the promise of a habitable world. The remaining half coaxed the damaged vessel onwards to its eventual destination in the Omicron Alpha system, arriving some time in the year 41 AS Upon their arrival, the crew discovered a planet capable of supporting human life in orbit of the primary star. The Hispania's passengers named the planet Malta -- a harsh place of acidic oceans, gray skies, and vast plains covered in a species of tall, thin, orange grass. Taking whatever equipment they could salvage from the crippled Hispania, they left the hulk in orbit of Malta and began to make a home for themselves on Malta.

Eventually the Outcasts -- as they came to think of themselves -- began a limited exploration of their home system. As pilots wandered farther and farther afield in search of resources, many became seriously ill. Upon returning to Malta, the crews recovered quickly. After making a number of genetic scans of critically ill pilots, the doctors made a startling and disturbing discovery. Their genetic code had been altered considerably. The Outcast human DNA was found to contain strands identical to that of the orange grasses that covered the planet -- from which the drug Cardamine was derived. Trace amounts were present in everything on the planet, in their food, their water, even the very air. Once pilots made lengthier journeys away from Malta, their bodies went into shock, followed by death.

The Outcasts were now truly separated from the rest of humanity -- changed so that they could never expand beyond the planet on which they had landed. They needed Cardamine now, like air, food, or water. But with the origin of the sickness solved, they could at least compensate by carrying supplies of Cardamine with them and resume their exploration of their surrounding systems. Over time, their knowledge of Cardamine improved, and the Outcasts learned that distributing it in a highly concentrated dose causes extreme euphoria. When they finally encountered the rest of the Houses in the seventh century, a new strategy emerged. The Outcasts would deliver the poison that would rot the other Houses from the inside out and grow rich from the profits of their trade.

The planet's crust is largely devoid of usable metallic elements, with a few notable exceptions, namely at the heart of her largest continent, and highly unusual deposits of metallic Copper on the ocean floor. Most of its landmass is covered in prairies with natural, low-grade Cardamine grass; large plantations with heavily bred and modified strains have been built on the most fertile sites. Malta's architecture is a largely low-hung and flat, one-story affair in the rural areas; cities are an expression of extremes, built almost entirely in the rare hilly regions of the planet. There is little at ground-level, except starports; most structures are built both deep into the ground and into massive towers that reach towards the sky, constructed yet again as to mimic the textures of the ground. Malta's oceans are strongly acidic and home to algae that tolerate its high acidity. They appear to hold a slightly green tint from the surface.

These days the Outcasts conduct a lucrative drug-smuggling operation using the network of Jump Holes to escape detection and transport their product into the heart of the House systems through various proxies. They remain relatively few in number; a crash in the birth rate seems to have been another side effect of their genetic modification, although the modifications have lengthened the Outcast's lifespan and physical resilience considerably. There have been no known cases of cancer on Malta since the Outcasts made planetfall.

A new development has been Cryer's continued efforts to create a synthetic version of Cardamine that would be approved as a legal medication within Liberty. This poses a direct threat to the Outcasts' source of income. The Atka Research Station, with nearby access to Edge Nebula clouds, is the most immediate threat to the Outcasts. The location of the base within Corsair territory has brought the Outcasts into conflict with their ancient brethren. The Atka Research Station has come under repeated attacks by Outcast raiding parties in recent years, and the Outcasts always destroy any Cryer transports encountered throughout Sirius without mercy.

When the Dons instituted new disciplinary and security measures for Malta's plantations following Albegna's mining colony slave revolt in 831 AS, fear spread among Malta-bound slaves of mass executions and worsened living conditions. On plantations whose owners took a more lax approach to the new protocols, many slaves began to steal and cache weapons and materiel from their Outcast masters, culminating in a slave revolt that captured a starport and seized control of Malta's defenses.

Though many slaves died or were recaptured by Outcasts during the struggle, many others escaped off-world, either in stolen ships moored at the starport, or in ships flown by IMG, Crayter Republic, or abolitionist group pilots. Ultimately, the revolt was quelled, leaving the Outcasts without enough cardamine to meet market demand, and raising the problem of seeking a newer, more obedient source of labor.

The asteroid and most of the surrounding fragments orbit Planet Elysium slowly, suggesting that Elysium itself is the gravitational heart of this region of space. The ancestors of the Corsairs were survivors of the crippled Sleeper Ship Hispania, who used the vessel's escape pods to land on Crete in 35 AS. Those settlers found themselves on a harsh, rocky world that was ill suited to human colonisation or the crops brought from Sol. The Corsairs scratched out a bleak existence for four centuries, suffering many famines that threatened to eradicate their shrinking population. Through these hardships, the Corsairs would develop a strong, insular self-identity that separated them from the other Houses. In 450 AS, that insular world changed.

An exploratory expedition headed by Franz Schulman - financed by Daumann and the Rheinland government - stumbled into the system while mapping the far reaches of the Walker Nebula. Crete's desperate inhabitants, sensing a historic opportunity, attacked the landing party en masse. They killed all save Schulman, whom they took hostage to gain control of the orbiting mother ship Schiller. Once they had secured the ship and all of its technologies, they were outraged. The Schiller's databases indicated that the Houses had made no attempt to locate the Hispania or its survivors. Suspicion that the other Houses were behind the sabotage of the Hispania turned into hatred, and with a renewed determination, the sons and daughters of Crete took to the stars again.

No one is entirely sure who first nicknamed them the "Corsairs," recalling the ancient pirate clans of the Mediterranean, but the name came into popular use among the Houses sometime around 500 AS. The Corsairs began attacking unprotected outposts and ships, plundering whatever supplies and equipment they could lay their hands on, before escaping through one of their secret Jump Holes. The systematic expansion of the Houses into the Omega Border Worlds further fueled the Corsairs, dramatically increasing the quantity and variety of accessible goods. This in turn allowed them to build stronger ships and weapons and grow their population.

The final chapter began in the sixth century AS, when an enterprising, well-armed Liberty freelancer named Jim Bown made his way to Omicron Gamma. He brought Consumer Goods and Food to trade, but the Corsairs could offer little but Artifacts. A year later, he returned. Those trinkets were all the rage with the elite of Manhattan. He saw a great business opportunity if they could set up a viable trade route to Liberty. The Corsairs were on their way. They grew rapidly in size and sophistication as they built up the Artifact trade. The primary smuggling route now goes north to Sigma-19, where Artifacts are traded with the Hogosha onboard the Hawaii. They have also opened up a route into Rheinland via Freeport 8 in Sigma 15. In the west the Corsairs invaded Bretonia in order to reach the Junker's Trafalgar Base in New London.

In recent years, tensions between the Corsairs and local Zoners have steadily grown. This is caused partially by Bounty Hunters using nearby Freeports to attack the Corsairs' home system, but also concerns that Zoner colonies on Pygar would compete for Freeport 9's Food exports to Crete. Crete currently has a population the planet can barely support, with regional famines a commonplace occurrence if crops fail. The Corsairs attempted to resolve Crete's Food insecurity in 831 AS by seizing control of Freeport 9 and its biodomes, although this has also severed their access to Zoner markets for other essential goods such as Fertilisers and Pharmaceuticals.

590058.mapped:
In the earliest days of the Corsair raids on the houses, many bases and ships did not have any kind of defenses or escort at all. While the most common Corsair tactic was to pillage whatever they could carry back home and leave the rest as wreckage, some of their more bold raids boarded and took over entire ships. The Corsairs didn't have much use for unarmed transports once their cargo had been transferred, so they were set adrift in Omicron Gamma. The Corsairs realised that these ships themselves could be a valuable source of materials if they could be stripped down, and set out to build a space-based facility for this purpose. At the time, the Corsairs did not posess the technology or resources to build an entire base from scratch, so they improvised, hollowing out a largest asteroid in the Tenerife asteroid field.

Tripoli Shipyard, as it came to be known, spent the next two centuries doing what it was built to do, that is to strip down captured ships, send whatever material is worth saving to Crete, to be used in the construction of more fighters, and eject the worthless chunks into the Tenerife field. This debris, mostly large sheets of twisted hull plating, settled around the station.

Tripoli's role changed slowly in the last century, as the Corsairs started to experiment with larger ships that could not be built on Crete. The yard was expanded, a large construction moor added, and the base's role changed from salvage yard to ship production.

Today, Tripoli is the most vital base for the Corsairs, handling the construction and maintenance of all ships their engineers have the blueprints for.

590060.mapped:
Freeport 9 was one of the first human settlements in the Edge Nebula. Built by Zoners who felt they could not be far enough from the influence of the major Houses, it was the most remote civilian outpost in the colonies until the construction of Freeport 11. Despite its location in a system filled with strange nebulae and forbidding black crystals, the Freeport became a relatively busy destination, hosting a diverse range of pirates, explorers and corporate researchers. Despite this, 9’s open-door neutrality was a constant source of friction with the Corsairs and Outcasts, largely due to Bounty Hunters and The Core frequently visiting.

These tensions were managed by the Zoners providing useful cargo services, and the Corsairs and Outcasts keeping one another in check. This dramatically changed in 831 AS with Theta’s Outcasts vanishing overnight to respond to the Maltese Slave Revolt. The Corsairs reacted almost immediately by launching a surprise attack, boarding the Freeport using warriors aboard a transport that claimed to be purchasing Food Rations. The Corsairs have since maintained control over the station through military force and Zoner hostages. When the Outcasts returned to Omicron Theta in 833 AS, the resulting battles were the bloodiest seen in decades. Following a humiliating defeat that saw the Battlecruiser Kefalonia destroyed, the Corsairs raised additional reinforcements and dug in.

When the next wave of attacks came late in the year, the Outcasts unexpectedly withdrew, abandoning the Zoner Militias as a mere diversion to occupy the Corsairs’ attention. The conflict spluttered to an end with all involved parties badly bloodied. Seemingly drawn like sharks to the conflict, Theta has since been subject to unprecedented Nomad raids. With neither the Corsairs or Zoners having the appetite for further fighting, a peace treaty was begrudgingly negotiated that established a joint administration of Freeport 9. While the station is far from free, the Zoners have regained a large degree of autonomy over their own affairs.

590062.mapped:
The Myoko is the oldest active-service battleship in the Kusari Naval Forces and Sirius more broadly. Despite having been thoroughly obsolete for over a century, the Myoko continued to receive minor modernization packages to enable it to continue to function as a mobile hangar for Naval squadrons. Despite this, it is widely understood that the Myoko is not fit to face other warships on equal terms. Consequently, the battleship did not see direct action during the Colony Wars, instead donating its squadrons to bolster the New Tokyo defense.

In the aftermath of the Colony Wars, the Myoko primarily acted as a patrol base for the suppression of piracy and terrorism throughout Shikoku. It also held a large Marine contingent that could be used to support Fuchu Prison in the event of serious disorder. This posting continued until 834 AS, when the Myoko was withdrawn to Junyo to join the terrestrial training facility being constructed at Fort Ainoura. There, the battleship assisted with pre-war training for Kusari’s Marines on shipboard protocol, vacuum operations and opposed boarding.

Following the outbreak of war in 836 AS, the Myoko was withdrawn from Shikoku as modernized ships from across Kusari were surged into the system. The venerable battleship instead relieved the Battleship Matsumoto, and has taken up a guard position near Yokohama Shipyard as a patrol base. From here, its fighter squadrons maintain careful watch over both of New Tokyo's strategically vital shipyards.

590064.mapped:
Since the completion of the great Kusari-Liberty Jump Gate project in 310 AS, Shikoku has been the primary gateway for almost all traffic originating from Liberty and the Independent Worlds. Entry requirements for the New Tokyo system were initially very strict, and as a result, Shikoku became home to a large population of itinerant foreigners. Deshima Station was constructed by the Kusari Shogunate in 362 AS to house this steadily growing population, with further rounds of expansions taking place in 680 AS following the terraforming of Junyo, to accommodate internal Kusari workers. While the Shogunate initially kept a firm grasp over the station's administration, recent decades saw a loosening of restrictions.

This included a breakthrough agreement with the Bounty Hunters Guild in 785 AS, which permitted the foreign mercenaries to work throughout Shikoku, and the agricultural deregulation of 790 AS, which allowed Synth Foods to open their first offices on Deshima. By 796 AS, the Bounty Hunters Guild were subcontracted to take over Deshima's administration and security as a cost-saving measure. Guild administrators then oversaw the construction of Synth Foods biodomes, the modernization of habitat spaces, and a partnership with Kishiro to exploit cheap Libertonian labor to manufacture Consumer Goods onboard. Deshima's role in housing foreign influences and producing Synth Paste also made it a high priority target for the Farmer's Alliance.

While the terrorist movement has made dozens of attacks over the years, the most serious attempt occurred in 835 AS. In an effort to repeat their successful strike on Roppongi Station, a nuclear device was smuggled aboard. Local security measures put in place to foil this type of attack succeeded in thwarting the attempt, however the incident caused a significant further rupture between Liberty and Kusari's governments. The following year, a state of war erupted between the two Houses. Kusari immediately dissolved the Guild's management contract under wartime powers, and has since commandeered the station's facilities to house Naval personnel. Kusari has announced that the Liberty citizens stranded aboard will be extradited to Bretonia as a neutral destination.

590066.mapped:
Originally located in the New Tokyo system, Fuchu Prison was moved to the Shikoku system in 600 AS to handle the burgeoning foreign criminal element that was plaguing the area. While nearly 70% of the prisoners are from outside of Kusari space, the remaining 30% are almost exclusively members of a radical, political terrorist groups such as the Blood Dragons and Golden Chrysanthemums. "Rehabilitation through work" is a core principal of the Fuchu Prison mandate, and inmates are routinely deployed to mine Hydrocarbon and work the Junyo fishing platforms.

In 833 AS, the Kusari government denied permits for either Kishiro Technologies or Samura Heavy Industries to construct a Platinum refinery in Shikoku. Mining operations in Galileo has been blocked by separate court orders in both New Tokyo and New York, as the two Kusari corporations and Deep Space Engineering battled over extraction rights. Coincidentally, Fuchu Prison’s rehabilitation program expanded the following year to include an on-site metals refining annex. Liberty has since accused Kusari of undermining the rule of law and flouting legal convention.

590068.mapped:
Planet Junyo was surveyed in 57 AS by the famous Kusari explorer, Isao Yoshida, who named the planet after his ship, the Junyo Maru. It is covered almost entirely by a single deep ocean that remains liquid across the entire surface of the planet. Junyo was ignored by the Kusari government for centuries due to a lack of landmasses that could relieve New Tokyo's overcrowding. A small number of private citizens did colonize the Ishizuki Plateau - Junyo's sole landmass - and for centuries the planetary population lingered in the mere hundreds.

With the impending collapse of Kusari's fisheries in 630 AS, Samura Industries purchased the planet from the government. Using Planet Kurile's recently discovered Alien Organisms, Samura launched a campaign to terraform Junyo's oceans. By 680 AS the ecosystem had been altered to such an extent that wide-scale production of Food was able to begin planet-wide. Samura continued to experiment with the microorganisms, tuning their use to maximise their effect on the Junyo fisheries and becoming increasingly dependent on them to increase yields.

In 824 AS the GMG seized Planet Kurile. Junyo’s fisheries saw an immediate drop in output, with many collapsing entirely over the following years as Alien Organism stocks depleted. Mass unemployment and failing industries have now left Junyo a shadow of its past. While Fire Pearl harvesting continues at a much reduced scale, Food exports have ceased over fears of total fish stock extinction. Synth Foods has exploited the situation to integrate itself ever further into Kusari food markets. In recent years, Samura has begun to open Basic Alloy foundries to exploit the wage depression caused by Junyo's rampant unemployment.

590072.mapped: Rich in vital gas resources, the Sigma-13 system has been contested by a number of groups since its discovery in 60 AS. Conflict reached a fever pitch when the system became one of the more fiercely contested prizes during the 80-Years War between the Gas Miners Guild (GMG) and Rheinland. Using speed and a thorough knowledge of the territory, the GMG managed to push back the Rheinland forces, finally obliterating the bulk of the Rheinland Navy at the Battle of the Yanagi Nebula. Since that time the system has been almost exclusively under GMG control, and the Gas Miner Naha has provided support for the GMG's extensive mining operations.

590074.mapped:
At the Battle of the Yanagi Nebula, the forces of the Gas Miners Guild managed to obliterate almost the entire Rheinland Navy in a surprise maneuver. The remnant of that great battle became a vast field of Scrap Metal and radioactive cores that has rendered the area a major navigational hazard. Under an agreement brokered by Interspace Commerce, ALG Waste Disposal was allowed to build Helgoland Station and begin clean-up of the affected area, shipping Scrap Metal and other waste back to Rheinland for re-smelting.

The Yanagi cleanup was finally completed in late 818. As part of the original contract, the Gas Miners Guild purchased the Helgoland facility from ALG and has begun converting the facility in a small shipyard, with the intent to sell shipbuilding capacity to Kusari and maintain their transports and gas miners at Helgoland.

The Liner Samsara bears many of the unique construction characteristics of the Pilgrim class smuggler Karnap. For decades, the Karnap was sighted plying trade across the backwaters of Rheinland, the Sigmas and Kusari. In 834 AS, the Karnap failed to arrive for a contracted delivery to Noshima Freeport. Many assume the vanished ship was caught up in the GMG's recent Sigma-13 security operation against the Junkers.
590078.mapped:
In reality, the Karnap was intercepted and boarded by the Kusari Office of Intelligence, who had been carrying out their own investigation into local smuggling rings and the trade of dangerous Xeno Relics. The Karnap was requisitioned by the Nomad-controlled special operations division based on Tohoku’s Arch, then expunged from all official records.

Now renamed the Samsara, the liner acts as a staging point for Wild raids across the Sigmas. These attacks often target Artifact smugglers, in a seeming mockery of the KOI’s official mission. Wild patrols have also prioritized waylaying excursion shuttles from the Luxury Liner Hawaii, in an effort to compromise wealthy and influential House civilians.

Initially discovered by the Gas Miners Guild (GMG) in 620 AS, the planet Kurile exists at the heart of an anomaly, a gravitational tidal pool that creates a clear zone in the middle of the otherwise treacherous nebula. The planet itself is entirely covered in water with a saline content so high that it is toxic to almost all known aquatic life elsewhere in Sirius. Despite this, Kurile possesses a single native life form, a microorganism that manages to thrive in its otherwise poisonous oceans. Samura eventually managed to construct a collection platform on Kurile to harvest the microorganisms for use at the fisheries on Planet Junyo. The planet harbors some 2500 workers, all of whom live on the floating platform.

Taking advantage of Samura's divided attention, the Gas Miner's Guild launched a successful attack upon planet Kurile in 824 AS removing Samura Heavy Industries presence in its entirety. However, the GMG now face the daunting task of securing the planet against raids by Outcast and Corsair forces while simultaneously attempting to halt the rampant smuggling made profitable by the lack of a functional docking facilities. Repairs are currently underway yet recent aggression from Rheinland may place considerable strain on all of the Gas Miner's plans.

590084.mapped: The spectacular vistas of the Sigma-19 system -- said by many to be among the most beautiful in all of Sirius -- did not go unnoticed by the tourist industry for long, and in 791 AS Orbital Spa and Cruise Lines stationed its state-of-the-art luxury liner Hawaii in the system. An incredibly popular destination, the Hawaii has operated at near capacity almost from the beginning. The location of the ship outside the policed boundaries of the colonies is also rumored to be part of the attraction, and much of the popularity of the Hawaii lies in the implied promise of forbidden fruit available to those who can afford a ticket.

590086.mapped:
Planet Baden Baden is an idyllic world of large, sterile oceans, black sand archipelagos, and the odd hot spring bubbling from rocky volcanic outcroppings. Orbital Spa and Cruise (OS&C) has operated multiple resorts across the planet since 685 AS, as well as leasing land to wealthy Rheinlanders looking to establish their own private villas and complexes. Baden Baden has historically suffered from Rheinland’s broader economic woes, and struggled to turn a profit. Controversial attempts to boost profitability by shipping in econoclass Liberty vacationers temporarily boosted the resort’s income, however this revenue dried up with the outbreak of the Hudson War in 817 AS.

OS&C’s operation continued to limp on, but suffered additional setbacks during the Rheinland Civil War, during which all trade ceased. Many of the resorts were leased to Rheinland aid organizations as neutral emergency hospitals for the wounded of both Imperial and Federalist forces. Baden Baden received an unexpected boost in 834 AS with the Treaty of Oerlikon, as Gallic vacationers flocked to the planet to experience Rheinland culture. Similarly, wealthy tourists from Kusari, Bretonia and Liberty have begun to favor Baden Baden for its relative safety compared to the increasingly troubled operations on Curacao and the Liner Hawaii.

ARMAMENT: CLASSIFIED
590088.mapped:
The Greifswald was a Red Hessian Hel cruiser, sold to the LWB as it reached the end of its service life. After the Hessians completed hand-over training, the LWB returned the vessel to Stuttgart. It initially served as a heavy raider, attacking Synth Foods convoys with overwhelming firepower before vanishing back into the asteroid fields. This lasted until 824 AS, when the loss of Saalburg Depot and a humiliating defeat during an attack on Neckar Supply Station’s opening ceremony threw the LWB’s weak leadership into disarray. As Darmstadt fell to the chaos of infighting factions, the Greifswald watched on helplessly as their cause ripped itself apart. Other Rheinland groups quickly began to dismember the LWB’s carcass to bolster their own movements, with the Bundschuh, Hessians and Unioners all seizing different assets.

The Greifswald was soon joined by a handful of like-minded refugees from Darmstadt, who vowed to continue their own fight without ideological compromise. To achieve this, they reached out to the Bretonian Gaians, who were likewise appalled by Stuttgart’s fate. The Gaians eventually offered to provide some funding and basic supplies to allow the LWB remnants to continue striking Synth shipping, with the cruiser later assisting with some joint operations in the Omegas in return. The Greifswald attempted to avoid being dragged into the Rheinland Civil War, instead continuing to focus on Synth shipping. This led to the vessel being flagged as pirates by the Imperial forces occupying Stuttgart.

When the Farmer’s Alliance expanded to Rheinland in 828 AS, they organized and funded ex-Imperial militants who were outraged at the failure to evict Synth. The Greifswald quickly moved to rejoin these resurgent LWB activists, providing local expertise and training. Despite this, it quickly became apparent that all was not well, and the Alliance had dramatically different priorities to the LWB and Rheinland farmers. This came to a boil in 834 AS, when the Greifswald and Schwarzwald coordinated to expel the FA and reassert their independence. The cruiser now stalks New Berlin, hunting Synth and Gallic shipments.

590090.mapped:
Freiburg Station was originally constructed in 312 AS as a clearinghouse for produce harvested on Stuttgart, and a drop-off point for goods imported from Bretonia. Following the 80-Years War, Rheinland was forced to abandon many of its protectionist policies that blocked foreign shippers from entering their core space. As a result, Freiburg’s importance waned as Bretonian corporations began to bypass it. This would change with Daumann and later Kruger’s expansion into Omega-7 in the late 790s, with Freiburg providing a convenient staging point for mining and construction supplies.

Since the expulsion of the Red Hessians from Cologne and the reopening of the Alsace Passage for trade, Freiburg also served as an exchange for goods bound to or from Gallia. Due to incompatible fuel standards, many Gallic transports preferred the shorter trip to drop off their cargo on Freiburg. The completion of the Treaty of Oerlikon and the conversion of Wildau Station into a Promethene depot has already impacted this practice, with an increasing proportion of Gallic shipping proceeding onward to New Berlin. A substantial RFP presence is stationed aboard, primarily to manage conflict between Bretonian and Gallic traffic.

In 835 AS, Freiburg was damaged during a terrorist attack targeting a moored Gallic convoy. A trio of Bretonian flagged Gull transports approached the station, with two ramming the Gallic vessels and exploding. The third Gull was targeted by Freiburg's defense grid and exploded prematurely, damaging nearby storage tanks.

Stuttgart is a green, almost inconceivably fertile world. It owes this fertility to the rich soils and high concentration of carbon dioxide and oxygen in its atmosphere. While the atmosphere makes industrial development infeasible -- one stray spark could set off a massive conflagration -- farming has been hugely successful as many Earth and Sirian plants immediately took to the environment. Stuttgart has been Rheinland’s primary source of Food for centuries, creating aristocratic farming dynasties that became incredibly wealthy on state subsidies. These subsidies abruptly ended in 685 AS with the end of the 80-Years War. In the aftermath, Liberty forced Rheinland to make a number of painful concessions to clear its wartime debts, the most significant being Synth Food access to Stuttgart. Over the following century, Synth acquired most of the planet’s struggling farms, rapidly dominating Rheinland agriculture.

Across the 770s, Synth consolidated its hold on the planet by assuming control of the Stuttgart Growing Association (WVS), clearing the way for the controversial “CO2 enhancement project”. ALG Terraforming Gases were used to adapt the atmosphere to better suit Synth crops. This would spur the creation of the LWB farmers rights group who began a campaign of terrorism against Synth interests. Despite this opposition, Synth’s land ownership of Stuttgart would reach a peak of 89% by 826 AS. Undeterred by attacks, Synth continually scaled up its Synth Paste production, saturating the Rheinland market and exporting surplus to Kusari and Liberty. These operations would be thrown into chaos in 827 AS by the Rheinland Civil War. Pro-Imperial militias launched attacks on the polar spaceports and rapidly took control of Federal government facilities. Following bloody battles across these regions, Federalist forces ultimately retreated, fearing the fighting could spill over into fertile regions and cause mass firestorms and famine.

While remaining independent farmers had hoped the new Imperial government would evict Synth entirely, the actual response was more muted. Due to a military threats from Liberty and a desperate need for funding, Synth operations were permitted to continue, subject to harsher taxation and regulation. This uneasy status quo persisted after the war, with the Federal Empire maintaining many previous Imperial policies. In 834 AS, Synth profits were further damaged by the Treaty of Oerlikon, which abolished tariffs on the import of Gallic Food products. Synth has been forced to drastically cut its prices in Rheinland to fend off this new market competition. This has resulted in many of Stuttgart’s remaining independent farmers going under, fueling outrage and demonstrations against Synth, the Rheinland government and Gallic corporations.

The Independent Miners Guild established Java Station in order to lay claim to the rich mineral resources present here. Originally, the Guild met stiff resistance from Bretonia Mining and Manufacturing, but the arrival of the Gallic Navy in the Tau borderworlds effectively ended Bretonia's attempts to pressure IMG out of the system.

Java Station was expanded with a refinery module purchased from Kishiro. Able to refine both Niobium and Beryllium, Java has become a large supplier of these metals, both to Kusari and Gallia. An EFL-supplied Gallic mooring and refueling facility has been added to the station to accomodate Gallic ships coming to make a purchase.

590100.mapped:
Locked in a geosynchronous orbit within the planetary shadow of Schutz, Solarius Station is the sole safe haven in the dangerous environment of Omega-11. At the heart of the system is a late-stage red giant that releases random radiation storms, fatal to any organic life unfortunate enough to be caught without protection. Despite the hazards, however, the Omega-11 system is also one of the most abundant sources of Diamonds in Sirius, the valuable gemstones locked in the circle of volcanic asteroids that ring the dying sun. Daumann Heavy Construction obtained the contract to develop Omega-11 and by 410 AS had managed to finish the construction of Solarius Station -- at the cost of 87 men and women who died "for the greater glory of Rheinland and its people."

In 822 AS, Daumann was forced to abandon Solarius Station after the system’s red giant entered a period of extreme activity, producing devastating solar flares that destroyed ships and infrastructure. While some speculated that this may have been a prelude to the dying star’s collapse, the activity subsided to relatively “safe” levels over the next three years. Daumann returned to find Solarius ruined and was forced to invest heavily to rebuild the station, completing the project by the end of 825 AS. In the aftermath of the Rheinland Civil War, Daumann lobbying on New Berlin resulted in the reactivation of the Solarius Trade Lane project, with Deep Space Engineering crews now temporarily staging from the base.

590108.text:
DIAMETER: 23,118 km.
MASS: 8.76 x 10e24 kg.
TERRAIN: Transitional (Desert)
TEMPERATURE: -35°C to 48°C
ESCAPE VELOCITY: 16.78 km/sec
590108.mapped:
Previously a barren world, Harris was the first large-scale terraforming effort by Planetform, Inc. Initiated in 450 AS, the project was made easier by the abundance of pure Water and Oxygen ice in the system, while Terraforming Gases were easily transported by Bowex from the Stokes Mining Station in nearby Leeds. While the Harris Terraforming project is almost complete, wars with Kusari and Gallia from 813 to 826 AS made any kind of mass colonization impossible. During these conflicts, significant defenses were erected around Harris, including concealed minefields and autonomous weapon platforms.

During their initial 818 AS invasion, Gallic forces bypassed Harris to concentrate their strength on the Bretonian core systems. The garrison was placed under siege, and slowly starved. Once the frontlines in Bretonia stabilized, the Royal Navy dispatched the Dax fleet to breach Harris' defenses and secure its orbit, mercilessly crushing what little resistance was left. The planet fell into Gallia's hands in mid 823 AS, with the Crown transferring it to EFL to resume the terraforming project. The Gaians resumed attacks on the site in response, collapsing the neutrality with Gallia that had held to that point.

In 826 AS, the Crayter Republic launched Operation Ice Lance, an assault across Tau-31. This exploited depleted Gallic garrisons after many were stripped to reinforce the Siege of New London. EFL quickly abandoned Harris, which the Republic occupied for the remainder of the war. Upon resuming control of the colony in 827 AS, the Bretonian government urged Planetform to finish the terraforming project, as the refugee crisis from the loss of Leeds was placing exceptional strain on existing infrastructure. To fund the ongoing costs of colonization, Bretonia opened up the vast virgin resources of Harris for purchase by foreign corporations.

Interest was first expressed by Synth Foods, who believed the harsh frontier could be tamed by their robust synthetic crops -- creating a potential opening into the Bretonian market, and a new avenue of attack on Kusari’s. Samura followed soon after, purchasing vast tracts for factories it anticipated would soon be filled by destitute Bretonian colonists who would work for a fraction of a Kusari wage. The animosity between the two corporations has led to smoldering bush conflicts, with Bretonian authorities periodically intervening when the violence gets out of hand. As of 834 AS, Liberty mediated Cryer Pharmaceuticals’ lease of Harris' north pole, where the Clisham Research Complex is now situated.
