The gas giant Seto consists primarily of hydrogen. Its striking orange color and location astride the primary Liberty-Kusari trade route make it a memorable landmark. Its only moon, Junyo, is the sole habitable planet within the Shikoku system.

590363.text: Probable remains of the Trujillo, a Corsair ship smuggling Artifacts into New London.

590364.text: The Molly fighter Vanguard, identified and pursued by Bretonia Armed Forces fighters several weeks ago. Could be carrying Gold.

590365.text: The wreck of the Outcast fighter Puno, missing since 751. Most likely contains a cargo of Cardamine.

590366.text: The wreck of the Henry Jones armored transport, a Bowex ship that was hijacked by Corsairs. It was transporting a shipment of Gold to Rheinland.

590367.text: The Corsair ship Caraz, intercepted and pursued by an Armed Forces patrol deep into the asteroid field. It had Artifacts in the cargo hold.

590368.text: The remains of the San Vicente, an Outcast Cardamine smuggler, which was intercepted and destroyed by an Armed Forces patrol several weeks ago.

590369.text: The remains of the lost Outcast ship Lorenzo, caught by the military and pursued into this radioactive area. Its Cardamine cargo has not been recovered.

590370.text: An escort of the Storm, a Bretonian gunboat that hit a mine and exploded while chasing rebels in the Founders Day Revolt of 752.

590371.text: A dead Corsair warrior's ship. There are many of these scattered throughout the Omega-5 battlefield, especially in the vicinity of the Hammen Hole.

590372.text: One of many Red Hessian fighter wrecks in this battlefield. Most of them are picked clean, but some yield weapons.

590373.text: The wreck of the Monschau, a Kruger Silver freighter that was attacked by Hessians.

590374.text: Remnants of an early Corsair raiding party, in the Omega-7 system, that blundered into this gas pocket.

590375.text: The remains of a Bounty Hunter. The Hunter may have been stalking Red Hessians, but more likely just looking for Diamonds.

590376.text: The remains of a Corsair fighter. They often come in from Omega-41 for a little raiding and Diamond mining.

590377.text: The wreckage of a Daumann company ship. Most likely an employee trying to find some Diamonds to sell on their own.

590378.text: The remnants of a Red Hessian fighter. The pirates in the area often come here looking for Diamonds.

590379.text: Wreckage of one of the escorts of the Kassel, a Rheinland Heavy Cruiser that was destroyed during the 80-Years War.

590380.text: Destroyed Rheinland Imperial Fleet fighter from the 80-Years War. This one was lost in the Battle of the Yanagi Cloud.

590381.text: The wreck of the Mongoose, a ship flown by the Bounty Hunter named Jim Adams. He disappeared shortly after the Freeport disaster.

590382.text: The wreck of the Robert Fitzgerald, a Cryer freighter that was attacked by Outcasts some weeks ago. It was hauling Alien Organisms to Atka for research purposes.

590383.text: The remains of the Menorca. The Corsair ship was lost in a recent skirmish with Outcasts. It is believed to be carrying Artifacts.

590384.text: The wreck of the Hien, the ship of a famous GMG ace. Most likely the work of Outcasts.

590385.text: The wreck of the Perez, the ship of an Outcast Cardamine smuggler. The GMG claims responsibility.

590386.text: The wreck of the Wolverine, flown by Bounty Hunter Ryan McKeen, left as a warning to others who venture too close to Outcast bases.

590387.text: The wreck of the hijacked freight train Edward Marshall. It was later disabled by a BMM patrol. Its cargo was Beryllium.

590388.text: The wreck of the DSE freighter Whetstone, which carried Construction Machinery. Most likely the work of Outcasts.

590389.text: Wreckage of the Valiant, a Gaian fighter flown by Lucy Collins.

590390.text:
The Griffin was a Bounty Hunter Vessel that was lost after the pilot, Jessica Stephenson, chased some Outcasts into the Bermejo Cloud. According to the Bounty Hunter's Guild, Jessica was known to have close ties with APM, the developers of the Bounty Hunter's shiplines.

Given her history, it is unknown why the ship would have been so far out in the Edgeworlds, especially as the ship had not accepted any bounty request at the time.

590391.text: The Barossa was an Independent Miners Guild freighter attempting to transport Niobium out of Tau-37. The ship was attacked by Outcasts. While an IMG patrol managed to chase off the Outcasts, with its crew dead and engines damaged, the freighter drifted off into the cloud and was lost.

590392.text:
The wreck of the Pathfinder is all that remains of the famous Bounty Hunter T. "Bob" Biggs's last voyage.

Sharing an eerily similar story as other pilots in search of fortune through pillaging and assassinating Outcast ships, Biggs followed this course of action after finishing his sentence aboard the LPI Prison Ship Sugarland. He rose through the ranks of the Guild at a rapid pace, and acquired significant wealth from hunting down Liberty Rogues and Xenos. However, still desiring for more, he set off to Tau-37, from which he launched frequent raids into Outcast space, going as far as the other regions of the Omicron Alpha system and even entering into the nearby ones.

One day, the patrols finally caught up with his ship on the outskirts of Omicron Alpha, close to the Beta Jump Hole. He was promptly shot down, with the Pathfinder towed to Omicron Beta, acting as a reminder to Bounty Hunters and other intruders alike of the dangers posed by entering such areas.

590393.text:
Launched in 786 AS, the Hosho Maru was a top-of-the-line GMG vessel equipped for surveying gas fields for resources. With the Sigma-13 gas mining slowing down, it embarked upon a journey of discovering new fields for the GMG to exploit.

This took it to the outskirts of the Sigmas, whereupon it entered a new Jump Hole previously uncharted. The thirst for curiosity was the crew's downfall, however, as they did not spend much time in the Omicron Beta before being located and captured by the Outcasts.

No signs of the crew have ever been returned, but the wreck of the Hosho Maru remains as intact as it has been at launch, still containing many of the materials used for its mission.

590394.text: One of the GMG escorts of the Hosho Maru. The expedition was in search of new H-Fuel deposits when they were set upon by unknown assailants.

590395.text: The remains of the IMG freighter Independence. The ship is part of the failed IMG effort to establish Diamond mining operations in Omega-41.

590396.text: The wreck of the Red Hessian fighter Volsung. The ship belonged to an elite pilot.

590397.text: The remains of the Rebel. This ship was flown by a Corsair turncoat named Jesse Casas, who joined the Bounty Hunters.

590398.text: The wreck of the Fearless, a Bretonian research vessel lost in 550. It may contain Artifacts.

590399.text: The wreckage of the Viking, flown by Bounty Hunter Kelly Nielson.

590400.text: An Outcast tomb. This ship contains the deceased pilot and his most prized possessions.

590401.text: The wreck of the Bounty Hunter fighter Vengeance. This ship was flown by "Lucky" Logan Conner, who stretched his luck a little too far.

590402.text: This ship is part of the Graveyard of the Innocents, where young Corsairs must prove their worthiness or perish in the process. Many of these ships contain Artifacts.

590403.text: Remnants of a Xeno fighter. It was probably destroyed by the Unioners, who have no use for Xeno weapons.

590404.text: The Universal Shipping transport Bradley. It was reported missing yesterday. The cargo manifest lists Trade Lane Parts.

590405.text: The wreck of the Edward Kane, a Bowex armored transport carrying Gold. Hijacked by the Rogues.

590406.text: The Universal large transport McKinley, hauling Superconductors. This is one of three known ships that were destroyed in 784 by a dark matter storm.

590407.text: The wreck of the Kamakura Maru, a Samura transport carrying Niobium that was lost in the Dark Matter Storm of 784.

590408.text: Wreckage of the Samura armored transport Nikko Maru. It was carrying Luxury Goods from New York to New Tokyo when it was caught in the Dark Matter Storm of 784.

590409.text: The Universal Shipping transport Chesapeake was hijacked several months ago. It may still have Pharmaceuticals aboard.

590410.text: Remains of the Freespirit, the ship of a Rogue Artifact smuggler. It was lost after a Bounty Hunter ambush.

590411.text: The remains of the Shibuya Maru. The Golden C. ship was making a Cardamine run to Galileo when it was intercepted by a Bounty Hunter.

590412.text: The wreck of the Kobe Maru. The Hogosha used this ship as an Artifact smuggler. It disappeared some time ago.

590413.text: The Blood Dragon fighter Shoki. This is the patrol leader's ship that has been missing since a battle with Kusari Naval Forces.

590414.text: The remnants of the Ohtori, an escort to the Golden C. ship Yukari Maru. The ship was intercepted by a Kusari Naval Forces patrol while crossing the Kyushu system.

590415.text: The wreck of the Thomas Morrel. The Universal ship was transporting Trade Lane Parts to the Chugoku Gate construction site when it was attacked by Blood Dragons.

590416.text: A destroyed Kusari Naval Forces fighter. One of many unretrieved military ships in the Kayo Cloud.

590417.text: The wreckage of the Aggressor, the ship of infamous Bounty Hunter, Harry Riggs.

590418.text: Probable remains of missing Liberty Navy Patrol 27.

590419.text: Wreckage of the Rogue Fighter Flint, which has been missing for several weeks. There may be Cardamine cargo aboard.

590420.text: The wreck of the Outcast ship Balboa. It was identified and pursued by LPI forces several weeks ago. There may be Cardamine in the hold.

590421.text: The remains of the Dallas Research Station Superconductor Laboratory, which was destroyed in 500 AS after a failed Jump Gate experiment.

590422.text: The remains of a Red Hessian fighter, probably trapped by the radiation in the area.

590423.text: A destroyed Unioner ship. Most likely cause is radiation. There may be Diamonds aboard.

590424.text: Scanning reveals older Rheinland Freighter model. The most likely candidate is the Danzig, a Kruger minerals ship lost in 450. It may be carrying Diamonds.

590425.text: A mooring fixture is a temporary resting area for idle ships within active shipping zones, allowing transports and other large vessels to be unloaded and passengers transferred.

590426.text:
CTE-3000 "Falcon" Civilian Heavy Fighter

As the name attests, this ship is formidable and is well-deserving of the reputation that it enjoys. With a balanced combination of refined offensive and defensive technologies, the Falcon delivers an astonishing amount of potential firepower to potential adversaries quickly and efficiently.

590427.text:
Heavy Lifter

The workers of the corporate matrix. These ships are generally employed in the moving of cargo of all types between transports, trains, and bases.

590428.text:
Kusari Battleship

Engineered by the Kusari Armed Forces and their military industrial complex, this class utilizes many advances that are considered classified.

590429.text:
J20P - 21F "Drone" Kusari Freighter

Often referred to as "bees of the golden hive," this freighter class is widely recognized as playing a key role in Kusari's trade and commercial viability. The vast cargo space and significant offensive and defensive capabilities of the Drone ensure that the individual merchants are empowered to deliver.

590430.text:
Nomad Battleship

No further information available. Power signature is alien, compositional elements are alien, weapon system is alien. Avoid contact.

590431.text: A lightweight, easily repairable alloy ring specifically designed to support lights and timing devices used in various racecourse.

590433.text: We ship Luxury Consumer Goods and Superconductors to Buffalo. The Rogues can't get enough of these pricy goods, and they can't seem to keep Superconductors in their ships functioning, so they constantly have to replace them. Must be all the banging into things they do in the Badlands.

590434.text: The Unioner base is out there in the southwestern part of the system. You'll know if you've stumbled onto that hornet's nest, believe me. The Xenos and Rogues tend to be more in the northwest part of the system. The Rogues deal with the Unioners at Pacifica, part of their smuggling business I guess. The Xenos mostly head to the Freeport. When Xenos and Unioners meet, it usually gets violent.

590435.text: We run supply shipments of Food, Oxygen, Consumer Goods, and Water to our base out in the southern asteroid fields of this system. Just watch out for Bounty Hunters and Xenos. Both of them are our enemies. The Liberty Rogues, not so much. You still need to watch them, some of their lot can get a bit triggerhappy, but we try to stay friendly with them, since they have connections in Liberty that we can use.

590436.text: We left Hamburg for this system after we reformed into the Unioners, but too many of us flooded onto this Freeport. It was an obvious target for the Rheinland Military, so the Zoners eventually asked us to leave. We put our skills to use and carved a hidden base out of an asteroid in the Tanner Asteroid Field. The field is too dense for bigger capital ships to navigate, so we're fairly safe out there.

590437.text: This is one of the only bases around that lets us land. Those Zoners are good people, although they do seem to like thosed damned Rheinlanders a bit too much. We run supply shipments for basic needs like Food, Oxygen, Consumer Goods, and Water from here to our bases in Hudson and Minnesota.

590438.text: The Unioners have a base out in the asteroid fields in the southwestern part of the system. They visit us frequently to purchase supplies - a freeport is the easiest place for them to get your basics from. The Liberty Rogues sometimes visit us for the same reason.

590439.text: There are a few Jump Holes into this system. Most of them lie in Unioner territory, so be careful. The one to Hamburg is in the southwestern quadrant; the one to Hudson is straight across on the western edge of the system. North of here there is one to Minnesota, but that one tends to be in Xeno space.

590440.text: There's a couple of Jump Holes in this system - the one to Cortez in the northern part of the system is easy to find. If you wait patiently enough, you can pop a Rogue or two as they come through. They won't even know what hit them. If you see an Outcast, you better have some support, though. They usually don't come alone either, and the Outcasts pack a punch.

590441.text: If you want to find Rogues, just pop through the Cortez Hole. You'll find them in abundance over there. I think their base is pretty close to the Hole. Just watch yourself out there, the Outcasts also use that hole. If you get swarmed, things can turn ugly real quick. Don't play with your prey.

590442.text: There's a Jump Hole into Cortez from here. That's how the Rogues get into this system. There's no way directly into California except through the Gate. It's been a while since I've seen the beautiful skies of Los Angeles.

590443.text: We mainly use Montezuma as a forward tactical base to stage attacks on Trade Lanes in Cortez via the Jump Hole into California. We prefer the safety of the Barrier Clouds, whereas the Rogues will attack almost anywhere.

590444.text: The Lane Hackers got themselves a deal with those miners on Freeport 4. They pick up a lot of basic stuff. Food, Water, Oxygen, that kind of things. We need some of that for Montezuma in Cortez, so we pick that up here, if we can't grab what we need from passing transports.

590445.text: We pick up Cardamine from this base and take it out to Montezuma and further into Liberty. The Outcasts sometimes carry it in themselves, but other times they don't want to and we have to handle the last leg. That's fine though, bringing in a load of Cardi always gets you free drinks at the bar in Buffalo.

590446.text: I got the Jump Hole routes down in this part of Sirius. The Outcasts run their drugs from Manchester through a Hole to Magellan, then across to Cortez. From there, into the Tahoe Cloud, then across this system to the Texas Hole. Pretty good, eh? I dare you to follow it.

590447.text: I'm doing long-range recon patrols into the Whitney Field. We do a lazy loop around it, keeping our distance from the Rogue base. Our usual path runs right along the Outcast smuggling route, so you have to be real careful.

590448.text: This is the crossroads of the criminal universe: Jump Holes to Hudson, New York, and California. Without this lovely lawless area of west Texas connecting them so conveniently, we'd have a much harder time operating in Liberty space.

590449.text: Word is, the Corsairs found some old Jump Hole in the Somerset Field from Cambridge. That's when all the problems started over there. I'm heading over to check it out pretty soon.

590450.text: New London is a just a sideshow for the Outcasts, 'cause there's no Jump Hole into Manchester from here. The main Cardamine route is through the Leeds smog clouds, and from there over to Magellan.

590451.text: I'm a Leedite, born and raised here in Leeds, son of a Uranium miner. Did a turn in prison too, but that's all behind me now. I know where the Jump Holes are in this system. I learned about them in Newgate. You can get to Manchester under wraps in the East Leeds, New London through the West Leeds.

590452.text: If I'm hired to pop Gaians, I'll head for the Edinburgh Jump Hole. If the contract reads for Mollys, I'm gonna head for the New London or Manchester Holes -- most likely the New London Hole. That's really where the majority of 'em come from.

590453.text: The Edinburgh Jump Hole is a dangerous place to hang out. It's in the LD-14 field, and all manner of thieves and killers pass through that area. Not only that, it is just slightly west of a pocket of radiation in the field, so an inexperienced pilot might get cooked.

590454.text: If you want to rack up the bounties, just hang out by the Leeds Jump Hole in the Islay Cloud. You'll have company, since it's the main supply and smuggling route into the rest of Bretonia for the Outcasts and Gaians.

590455.text: The Jump Hole in the Islay Cloud is a pretty rough place to hang out. If you're quick, you can catch a few Outcasts unaware, before they have a chance to respond. On the other hand, the Gaians will really swarm you since it's so close to their base.

590456.text: There is a Jump Hole to New London in this system. That's how all the Molly Gold gets out of Dublin. It is located in the Independent Gold Field northeast of here. That's where I lie in wait to ambush Molly Gold runners.

590457.text: It's my turn to pick up supplies from this base and deliver them to Arranmore. This week I'm picking up the basics plus Consumer Goods and Mining Machinery. And dropping off a few crates of the finest Whiskey our base can manage, for a few bucks on the side.

590458.text: The Jump Hole to New London is in the south side of the Independent Gold Field. That is also one of the main entry point for the Corsairs who come raiding for Gold. The Corsairs will attack corporate and Molly separatist shipments alike; they don't care who they piss off.

590459.text: The basic supplies that come to this base from New London are under constant attack from Mollys and other undesirables. I know this because I run the shipment every once in a while. This station also needs Side Arms and Pharmaceuticals shipped from New London.

590460.text: We use the Kyushu Jump Hole to the northeast of this base to get into the system. These Outcasts are weird guys, but they sell us what we want. Cardamine is essential to the Golden Chrysanthemum way of life.

590461.text: The Cardamine we get from this base goes straight to Ainu. Sometimes we come here with H-Fuel from our base so that we can make a little money to buy extra Cardamine for personal use. We don't get bothered by anyone in this system. Even the Bounty Hunters leave us alone.

590462.text: We receive the Cardamine from where it is processed on Malta, and then we distribute it into Sirius. Our path towards the Liberty and Bretonian systems used to pass through Edinburgh, but right now shipments are diverted away from the front. Bretonian traffic goes over Newcastle via Destroyer Ceuta, shipments to Liberty go through Baffin and Coronado. It's not getting any easier to keep those markets supplied.

590463.text: The Jump Hole to Tau-37 remains hidden to most amongst the asteroids that populate this system. Unfortunately the IMG found their way there. Beyond it you will find Omicron Alpha, which is the location of our home planet, Malta.

590464.text: We trust you, so I will tell you how to make yourself very rich. The Cardamine brought to this base comes from Malta. It is there that we also receive all necessary supplies to run this base.

590465.text: I was patrolling the Sheffield North a few weeks ago when I stumbled across three Lane Hackers. They were caught by surprise, too busy waiting on a Gold shipment that was coming by. I bagged one of them before they knew what hit 'em. The other two punched it for the Jump Hole to Magellan and escaped. That's how they work, those Hackers. They know when the good shipments are coming. So you know when to expect them to lay in wait.

590466.text: Sigma-17 is the next stop between here and the Junker bases where we offload the Artifacts marked for Rheinland. You'll find the Jump Hole in the Orinoco Cloud. The other distribution point for our Artifacts is aboard the Hawaii. The Hogosha on that ship will fence our goods into Kusari.

590467.text: The Hole that leads to our home system is in the Napo Cloud. Unwanted intruders who get taken alive have it worst of all, we keelhaul them. Try to imagine being in a vac-suit lashed to the outside of a ship that's headed into a Jump Hole.

590468.text: The Side Arm you see me carrying came from Yanagi. It's a Rheinlander piece, because I'm an eastern Corsair. The western Corsairs get Detroit weaponry from Bretonia. The Yanagi Junkers supply this base with Engine Components, too. We use those at Tripoli.

590469.text: There are five Jump Holes in this system. The Corsairs come in from Omega-41, which is in the Madsack Fragment. The Holes to the other two Border Worlds connected to this system are in the Jeschke Fragment. That field is loaded with Hessians; don't go there unless that's what you're looking for.

590470.text: The war between the Hessians and the Corsairs is still raging in Omega-5, but here the Hessians are in control. The Corsairs still come to Omega-11 by way of the Omega-41 Jump Hole, but they are looking for Diamonds usually. They do make hit and runs on the Hessians, too.

590471.text: The Jump Hole to Dresden is in the Kraft Fragment. It is just south of the Jump Gate to Stuttgart. The Red Hessians make use of that Hole quite often, so be careful.

590472.text: If you want to get into Stuttgart, and you don't need any authorities scanning your ship, I recommend using the Jump Hole in the Franke Fragment. This system is littered with Hessians, so you'll find them in that field.

590473.text: Everything needed to keep a base running is sent from Freital to Ronneburg. We are their suppliers, as Vogtland supplies us. If you enjoy being friends with the Hessians, you can always help us out by running these shipments.

590474.text: This system offers plenty of mobility; she's got five Jump Holes that will take you to Omega-41, Omega-5, Omega-7, Stuttgart, or Dresden. The one to Dresden leads to Vogtland; that's where our diamonds go. Then they get hauled to Kreuzberg where the Junkers fence them.

590475.text: The Hessians use this base as a stopover between Vogtland and Ronneburg. We ship all the basic supplies to this base. Some of them we sell to the LWB, the rest we deliver to the Ronneburg.

590476.text: Aside from basic supplies, we bring Side Arms and Engine Components here. The LWB are only too happy to purchase those goods. Whatever we don't sell continues on to Ronneburg.

590477.text: The Red Hessians use this base as a rest stop in their travels through Rheinland. In return we may purchase many Commodities from their base, Vogtland. The Engine Components we get from them help keep our ships operational.

590478.text: A benefit of the Ostnebel Cloud that hides Darmstaad is the Jump Hole that leads to Dresden. It makes travel throughout Rheinland easier. The other Jump Hole in Stuttgart is across the system in the Westnebel; it will lead you to Omega 11.

590479.text: In the Lavafeld you will find a Jump Hole to Omega-11; that is where the Red Hessians enter and exit this system for the western Border Worlds. If you are looking for them, and you want to pop them with Diamonds in their holds, then that is where you go.

590480.text: The LWB are not a huge presence in this system. They are more concerned with keeping supplies running between the Hessian base here and their base in Stuttgart. This system is also their transit point to New Berlin. If you are looking for them, do your hunting in the Giftnebel.

590481.text: This is the backbone of Daumann's mining concerns, so of course you will find a Red Hessian base here in Dresden. Look in the Giftnebel, you will encounter it, along with Jump Holes that lead to New Berlin and Stuttgart. If you go there, I hope that you are a good pilot and not afraid to go up against multiple targets.

590482.text: The Schwefelnebel hides the Jump Hole leading into Frankfurt. Red Hessians make supply runs into that system, so it is a good place to hunt for them. Plus, the proximity to this base from there means that if you get shot up and need repairs, you don't have to fly far with a leaky ship.

590483.text: If you want some real trouble, you might try heading to Omega 11 -- there are Diamonds and Hessians all over that system. It's one of the most dangerous places in Sirius. If the pirates don't kill you, the solar flares usually will. The Jump Hole is in the Lavafeld.

590484.text: You can kill LWB and Red Hessians in the Giftnebel. There are Jump Holes in there as well as a Hessian base. It is extremely dangerous, though; you must excerise caution if you go. I tell newbie Bounty Hunters I don't like, that it is the place they need to be.

590511.text:
Discovered by the renowned Corsair explorer Claudia Fuentes in 455 AS, the Thales Anomaly has become a central focus for the Corsair scientific community, drawing scientists and researchers from across the Imperio. The anomaly emits unusual pulses in a strangely consistent and predictable pattern, allowing a small fraction of its energy to be harvested for research purposes.

Because the origin of the anomaly's source matter remains unknown, the harvested energy has yet to find practical applications. Nevertheless, the crew aboard the nearby research station continue to study and experiment with it, driven by the hope of unlocking the next great scientific breakthrough.

590513.text:
CLASS: Brenner
GRAVITY: Complete
DOCKING: Yes
AMENITIES: Yes
CREW: 100
590513.mapped:
Evia Research Complex was constructed in 654 AS, more than two centuries after the discovery of the Thales Anomaly. The delay in interest stemmed from a widespread belief that the anomaly was nothing more than a dangerous and useless phenomenon.

This perception changed in the early 650s, when Corsair physicist Ivan de Guzman presented a theory to the Council of Elders about the potential to harness the anomaly's energy. The Council approved his proposal, allocating resources to expand the Imperio's scientific branch. The station was tasked not only with studying the anomaly but also with advancing xenoarchaeological research, particularly in the fields of artifact and alien organism analysis.

This mission gained even greater significance with the discovery of Xeno Relics - volatile, live Artifacts - that have sparked curiosity among even the most traditional scientists and researchers throughout the empire.

The station is currently experiencing its golden age, as the rising importance of xenoarchaeology and the tantalizing possibility of unlocking and utilizing the mysteries of the Thales Anomaly have attracted many new researchers and scientists eager to delve into the unknown.

590516.text:
Antares bears no cargo manifests in its computer system, but its recording devices indicate it was last moored on Malta's surface. The telltale blisters of particle blasts spot its hull, and its engines and life support systems are completely destroyed.

The bodies aboard, though bloated and desiccated by vacuum exposure, distinctly seem to lack Outcast uniforms.

590519.text: The communication logs in the black box recorder show navigation requests from IMG ships.

590521.text: Freeport 10's launch records list Siren's last launch as a search and rescue mission. The hull is riddled with debris, and an umbilical connection hangs damaged and lifeless from the craft's cargo hold airlock.

590523.text: Most of the ship's cruise disruptor supply has been expended. System logs indicate outbound transmissions requesting backup. The hull bears the scorch marks of transport-class turrets, and the shield generator has been rendered inoperable.

590525.text:
Little remains of this vessel but its computer systems' logs.

590527.text:
Torpedo strikes to the Curie's engines and first coupling have left the craft dead in space. The cargo pods were laden with an assortment of necessities—medical supplies, rations, and potable water.

Registered to Cryer Pharmaceuticals, Curie was bound for Freeport 10, having departed its port of call with two fighter escorts, Barberry and Narcissus.

590529.text: A Cryer Pharmaceuticals escort fighter, piloted by Jake Thompson. Nearly every external component of Barberry is damaged or missing.

590530.text: With structural failure, a shattered hull, and other signs of damage, this ship bears the scars of battle, never to be healed.

590533.text:
***EXTREME GRAVITATIONAL ANOMALY DETECTED***
Magnetic and gravimetric readings are inconsistent with known phenomenon. This anomaly bears some similarities to jump holes, semi-permeable areas in real-space that have a tendency to breach the natural boundaries of linear time and space. Due to some cataclysmic event, or extreme gravimetric stresses, the permeable barrier between real-space and hyperspace has ruptured. Pilots are advised to maintain distance at all times.

590535.text: This navigational buoy's power cells have run flat; it has been left to drift.

590537.text: This Prosecutor has been set down in the dust of an asteroid's crater. While the vessel's name is emblazoned on its flanks, the onboard nav computer and transponder has been thoroughly purged. There is no sign of battle damage or mechanical malfunction, however scans indicate the pilot remains in the cockpit.

590539.text:
CLASS: Caliburn
CREW: CLASSIFIED
ARMAMENT: CLASSIFIED

The Artemis was the first of the fearsome Caliburn destroyers, produced in 826 AS at Torshavn Space Port. For years, it struck high value targets from the ice clouds of Cambridge, Edinburgh and Tau-31, slinking away before Armed Forces or Royalist reinforcements could arrive. In early 835 AS, Islay Base was alerted that Atacama in Vespucci was coming under regular attack by unknown hostile vessels, with renegade Gaians among their number.

Recognizing prior agreements with Atacama's salvagers, sect leaders dispatched the Artemis to bolster the Atacama garrison and investigate the source of the attacks. Shortly after arriving, the destroyer repelled a number of rapidly intensifying attacks, and prevented the abduction of several salvage crews near Planet Veracruz. A month after its initial deployment, the Gaians detected a battleship class vessel entering the Sonora Ice Field.

Scrambling with a hastily assembled attack wing, the Artemis was among the first to intercept; the initially hostile standoff would have resulted in bloodshed, had The Order bridge crew aboard the Atum not powered down their weapons and signaled a request for parlay. With approval from Atacama, the Artemis assisted with towing the damaged Atum to an anchorage near the Warspite's wreckage. It now warily monitors the Osiris while its officers negotiate with local Gaian leaders.

590541.text: This network of satellites was deployed by Deep Space Engineering around Planet Veracruz in 830 AS. Designed to monitor for intruders or technological signs on the planet's surface, the network functions as a dead man's hand, beaming FTL updates back to Liberty. A significant network outage will provoke an investigation by the Liberty Navy, leading most local forces to ignore the satellites as an annoying cost of business. Onboard transponders declare that interference with the network is a criminal offense that may be punished with lethal force.

590543.text: This Order fighter was heavily damaged in 835 AS, during a battle between the Battleship Atum and alien Vagrant forces. Stranded when the Atum retreated, the pilot concealed themselves among Marshall Station's wreckage, and was later rescued by Gaian salvagers.

590545.text: The Santa Clara was the personal fighter of notorious Coalition commissar Sophia Wirtz. Her ship was destroyed in 830 AS, with the hull being scored by impacts consistent with both Coalition tachyon and Core particle weapons.

590547.text: The Core destroyer Hoedspruit was constructed at Alabama Shipyard in 829 AS. Dispatched to Dagger Outpost to serve in the local defense force, it later participated in the assault on Kamchatka Station alongside its sister ship Letaba. While patrolling in early 835 AS, it encountered a large swarm of AI Drones. The Hoedspruit was quickly overwhelmed and torn apart; no survivors or bodies were found at the wreck.

590549.text: From the construction style and materials, Outpost Deisenhausen appears to be of Rheinland origin, likely dating to approximately 800 AS. There are no identifying markings or functional active systems that indicate who precisely built the outpost or why. The station's reactor has exploded, although there is no way to verify whether this was caused by an accident, attack, or intentional sabotage. There are no public records indicating any past Rheinland presence in this region.

590551.text: This Xeno fighter was lost during the assault on the Battlecruiser Lehigh in 835 AS. Many Xenos were killed after massed wave tactics were adopted to mitigate Liberty's technological superiority.

590552.text: The Independence was a Liberty Separatist gunboat that the Xenos acquired after the fall of Vespucci. After serving for several years as a heavy raider in Magellan, the Independence participated in the Expulsion Campaign of 835 AS. The gunboat was destroyed while ramming the Battlecruiser Lehigh.

590554.text:
CLASS: Hercules (Unique)
CREW: 0
ARMAMENT: N/A

The Argonaut is a remote-piloted Heavy Lifter that was originally owned by the Liberty Security Force. The ship was opportunistically hijacked by Lane Hackers in 835 AS, after the LSF operation involving it was disrupted by the Kusari Office of Intelligence in Kepler. The theft of the Argonaut provided the Hackers with access to its cargo and fragments of onboard databanks that survived purge protocols during the hijacking.

Careful decryption and reconstruction of this information has provided details about the Argonaut's original mission. The Hackers have surmised that this was the salvaging of a classified Kusari project located in an unknown region code-named "Earhart". Earhart's location, Liberty's means of access, and how the expedition arrived in Kepler are all subject to intense speculation.

590556.text:
This component was salvaged from the Kusari Battlecruiser Niyodo, coming into the Lane Hacker's possession in 835 AS. The LSF Heavy Lifter Argonaut was attacked by Kusari fighters while towing the component through Kepler. Leiden's squadrons investigated after Ames Research Station was damaged in the crossfire and issued a distress call. The Lifter was remotely hijacked in the chaos. Cochrane Depot's drydock has been reinforced to facilitate the object's study.

The drive core is largely intact, but intensely radioactive owing to multiple cracks in the superstructure drive shielding. Initial study indicates the contents of the Niyodo Component are potentially revolutionary -- Cochrane's Executives speculate that it may contain a portable Jump Hole generator, and this is why Liberty risked a direct confrontation with Kusari to acquire it.

Lane Hacker researchers are working feverishly to understand the technology, seeing a unique opportunity for both self-enrichment and decimating Ageira's technological monopolies. Despite this, some argue that stealing the Component has drawn more attention than the Hackers can comfortably handle. Despite Liberty's activities in Ontario being fatally wounded, Lane Hackers are now facing unprecedented LSF pressure across all other operations.

590558.text:
CLASS: Thanatos
CREW: CLASSIFIED
ARMAMENT: CLASSIFIED

The Oizys is a Crayter Republic guard ship that has spent its service life patrolling Coronado. Typically holding in orbit of the moon Jericho, the Oizys was responsible for deterring local pirate activity and enforcing the Jericho exclusion zone. The cruiser has long been an irritant to the Independent Miner's Guild, who suspected it of primarily monitoring their activities.

In 835 AS, the vessel bore the full force of the energy pulse emitted from Jericho as an alien facility reactivated. Most electronic components immediately burned out, with a number of sub-systems exploding. The heavily damaged cruiser was towed to Sabah Shipyard where it received emergency repairs. It is currently undergoing final testing ahead of field redeployment.

590560.text:
CLASS: Thanatos
CREW: CLASSIFIED
ARMAMENT: CLASSIFIED

The Ponos is a Crayter Republic guard ship that has spent its service life patrolling Coronado. Typically holding in orbit of Planet Yuma, the Ponos was responsible for monitoring inbound traffic and deterring pirate attacks on convoys. In recent years, it has also participated in policing actions to curtail Outcast smuggling.

Following the Jericho Pulse in 835 AS, the vessel was urgently dispatched to help rescue the Cruiser Oizys and coordinate local emergency responses. The Assembly on Yuma have deemed Jericho a potential existential threat to the Republic, and have imposed themselves as the leaders of the ongoing investigation.

590563.text: This structure appears to be the remains of an ancient alien Jump Gate. It is covered in scorch marks and pitting from heavy weapons fire. Sensors indicate that the structure is no longer active, but still crackles with latent energy.

590566.text: This Valkyrie's serial codes match with declassified Rheinland records indicating it was assigned to the Battleship Verthandi. The battleship and its squadrons were listed as lost in 800 AS. It is unclear how the Aggressor came to be located in The Barrier.

590568.text: This vessel bears the livery of the infamous Tourmenteur squadron, a Gallic Royal Intelligence unit based off the Battleship Embrun. The Tormenteurs were renown for their brutal tactics and frequent war crimes. There are no known records of the squadron operating in Coronado during the Gallic War.

590570.text: This Nyx fighter belonged to Major Rya Drosos, Crayter flight leader of the Carrier Malachite's Apollo squadron. Drosos appears to have ejected, with the wreckage of her vessel abandoned on the battlefield. Critical damage was inflicted by weapons of an unknown type.

590573.text:
>>>WARNING: NAVIGATION HAZARD<<<

The Isere Debris Field was created during the Battles of Montpellier in 733 AGS and 734 AGS (817 - 818 AS), during the Second Gallic Civil War. This conflict between the Council and Gallic Royal Navy resulted in the breaching of the Montpellier Minefield, and the Council’s Languedoc fleet escaping into Sirius. The battlefield’s wreckage is often scavenged by Gallic Brigands.

590575.text:
>>>WARNING: MINES DETECTED<<<
The Montpellier Minefield was first laid in 652 AGS (736 AS) to guard the entrance to Gallia. Until breached by The Council in 733 AGS (817 AS), the minefield was protected by Montpellier Fortress, and accessible only to the Gallic Crown's autonomous spies -- The Huissiers. In the years since the First Gallic War, the minefield has fallen into disrepair and begun to disperse explosives across the Aveyron Nebula.

590576.text:
>>>WARNING: NAVIGATION HAZARD<<<

The Archachon Debris Field was created during Kusari’s initial Invasion of Languedoc in 743 AGS (827 AS). The opening to the Third Battle of Languedoc saw the Gallic Confederal Navy take devastating casualties and lose control of Planet Quillan. Kusari later saw its fortunes reversed on this battlefield, losing a number of prestigious ships during their retreat back to the Taus. The field is currently being salvaged by locally-trained ALG work crews.

590582.text: The Royal Engineers are a specialist unit of the Bretonia Armed Forces responsible for battlefield repairs, the laying and clearance of minefields, and the preparation of fixed defenses. Adapted Royal Engineer repair ships are being used to program and deploy mines around the Sommerset bridgehead in Dublin.

590584.text:
CLASS: Fortitude
CREW: CLASSIFIED
ARMAMENT: CLASSIFIED

The Battlecruiser Bracknell was launched in 825 AS, shortly before the fall of Southampton Shipyard. It participated in the Battle of Trafalgar, the Siege of New London, the Liberation of Leeds, and later the Invasion of Edinburgh. Post-war, it was appointed to command the First Royal Cruiser Flotilla, which it led into Dublin in 835 AS. During the initial phases of the campaign, the First were dispatched to secure the perimeter of the Achill Asteroid Field, in the hope of completely severing Molly supply lines into New London. The Mollys were quick to counter-attack with an improvised fleet, including Coalition, Militant and pirate auxiliaries.

The Bracknell initially prioritised enemy cruisers, ignoring the fleet of Asteroid Miners slowly advancing toward them; the captain had written them off as pressganged indications of the Mollys' desperation. This threat assessment quickly changed after the comm net filled with reports that the Hegemon flagged as Fortune had detonated, destroying the Battlecruiser Adlington. The flotilla began focusing their fire on the Miners, however it was too little, too late. While outside the optimal blast range, the Hegemon Hope prematurely detonated before it could be destroyed, obliterating the Bracknell's engines as it turned to flee. After several days of bloody fighting, Royal Engineer Lifters successfully towed the stricken vessel back to the Somerset.

Urgent field assessments are ongoing to establish whether the Bracknell can be made safe to jump out of the system for evacuation to Portsmouth Shipyard. Contingency plans have been made to jettison the reactor core into the Somerset minefield, in the event of a critical integrity deterioration.

590586.text: The Shannon was a Crecy class cruiser assigned to the Fifth Royal Cruiser Flotilla. The cruiser served throughout the Gallic War, and participated in the ill-fated Bretonian intervention into Vespucci during Liberty's campaign against the Insurgency. The Shannon was destroyed in Dublin with the detonation of the fire ship Fortune.

590587.text: The Orlando was a Crecy class cruiser assigned to the Fifth Royal Cruiser Flotilla. The cruiser served throughout the Gallic War, and participated in the Invasion of Edinburgh to eradicate The Enclave. The Orlando was destroyed in Dublin during battle with the Molly Powrie Brigade.

590589.text: The Blake was a Crecy class cruiser assigned to the Fifth Royal Cruiser Flotilla. The cruiser served throughout the Gallic War, being mothballed in the aftermath until reactivated for the Invasion of Dublin. The Blake was destroyed in Dublin during battle with the Molly Powrie Brigade.

590591.text: The Narcissus was a Agincourt class cruiser assigned to the First Royal Cruiser Flotilla. The cruiser served throughout the Gallic War, receiving an Agincourt upgrade package at Portsmouth Shipyard prior to the Invasion of Dublin. The Narcissus was destroyed in Dublin during battle with the Molly Sluagh Brigade.

590593.text: The Endymion was a Agincourt class cruiser assigned to the First Royal Cruiser Flotilla. The cruiser was constructed at Portsmouth Shipyard and launched shortly prior to the Invasion of Dublin. The Endymion was destroyed in Dublin with the detonation of the fire ship Hope.

590594.text: When Graves Station was destroyed and the Battleship Essex retreated, many BMM crews were left behind in their mining ships. Most of these crews later surrendered their equipment, willingly or otherwise. When Bretonia invaded Dublin in 835 AS, many of these captured Asteroid Miners were driven directly at Bretonian formations, usually as diversions to conceal the approach of explosive fire ships.

590596.text: The Damuji was a Coalition Typhoon class cruiser, assigned to the Molly's Powrie Brigade. The cruiser served across the Omegas, seeing combat against the Corsairs, The Core, and the Bretonian Armed Forces during their occupation of Planet Gran Canaria. The Damuji was destroyed in Dublin during battle with the Bretonian Fifth Royal Cruiser Flotilla.

590598.text: The Jatibonico was a Coalition Typhoon class cruiser, assigned to the Molly's Powrie Brigade. The cruiser served across the Omegas and Rheinland, notably participating in the breaching of Vierlande Prison and reprisal attacks on the Unioners. The Jatibonico was destroyed in Dublin by the Battlecruiser Adlington, shortly before its own destruction.

590600.text: The Gobnait was a Molly Hel class cruiser, assigned to the Powrie Brigade. The cruiser was purchased from the Red Hessians shortly before the Bretonian invasion of Dublin. The Gobnait was destroyed in Dublin during battle with the Bretonian Fifth Royal Cruiser Flotilla.

590601.text:
This formerly BMM-owned Hegemon Asteroid Miner was recorded as lost during the fall of Graves Station and resulting secession of Dublin. The Mollys have since repurposed many of these ships for their own ends. The mining ships Hope and Fortune were withdrawn to Arranmore Base in 834 AS amid fears of an imminent Bretonian invasion of Dublin. The pair were then worked on as an "insurance policy" by Mull Base's Hellburner Squadron, and converted into enormous armored bombs.

When Bretonia eventually attacked in 835 AS, the Hope was dispatched towards the Bretonian offensive aiming for the Achill Asteroid Field. Concealed among a screen of fellow Asteroid Miners, the Hope was heavily damaged on approach to the Battlecruiser Bracknell. Unwilling to allow the Bretonian capital ship to escape, Captain Saoirse Keane elected to forego evacuation and detonate immediately. The Bracknell's engines were crippled by this sacrifice. The immobilized ship was towed away after several days of fierce fighting.

590602.text: This Bretonia Armed Forces Fighter was lost in battle during the 835 AS Bretonian Invasion of Dublin.

590603.text: This Molly Fighter was lost in battle during the 835 AS Bretonian Invasion of Dublin.

590606.text:
>>>WARNING: NAVIGATION HAZARD<<<

The Flodden Debris Field was formed through the Second Battle of Edinburgh between the Bretonia Armed Forces and Gallic Enclave. It is composed the wreckage of combatants and discarded modules from Issoudun Drydock. In the aftermath of the conflict, Bretonia stripped weapon systems and sensitive components from many of the wrecks, abandoning the rest. The remains are frequently picked over by Gaians and Gallic Royalists, often resulting in fierce clashes.

590608.text: This Gallic Jump Gate was constructed by EFL Oil & Machinery in 824 AS, when the previous Ageira Jump Gate to Leeds was disassembled and shipped away for study. After the Glassing of Leeds and the collapse of the Gallic Royal Navy in 826 AS, the Jump Gate was disabled and then stripped of its components to prevent an immediate Bretonian invasion. When Bretonia launched its assault from the Tain Asteroid Field in late 827 AS, the Gallic Enclave detonated the Jump Gate's frame to prevent its capture.

590609.text: This Gallic Jump Gate was constructed by EFL Oil & Machinery in 744 AGS (828 AS), following the Kusari Invasion of Gallia. The Treaty of Rishiri setting out the terms of peace conceded Gallia's access to Tau-23. The Gallic Union then authorized the construction of a Gate connection to Orkney as an alternate route to the resources of the Hebrides. The Gate was abruptly disabled and sealed by the Gallic Navy in 745 AGS (829 AS), following a "security incident" in Orkney.

590611.text:
CLASS: Charlemagne
CREW: N/A
ARMAMENT: N/A

The Charlemagne battleships were designed around 676 AGS (760 AS), specifically for defensive and support purposes. Battleships of this class were configured to hold and maintain large numbers of fighters and cover them with powerful point defense turrets. By the time of the Gallic invasion of Bretonia, the dated Charlemagnes were used as the rearguard for advancing forces and for protecting vulnerable supply lines.

Originally a warship of the Gallic Royal Navy, the Battleship Oblique was tasked with garrisoning occupied Tau-44 against Crayter and Council attacks. The Oblique and its fleet shockingly deserted to The Council in 732 AGS (822 AS), after receiving brutal orders to execute the remaining Crayter civilians and prisoners of war being held on Borneo. The fleet played a key role in liberating the system, before moving on to participate in the Council's campaigns across Burgundy. In 741 AGS (825 AS), the Oblique was dispatched south to establish a new front and capture Provence -- opening another direction of attack on Ile-de-France.

The battleship and its forces hid in the Mer Mediterrainee, skirmishing with the system garrison commanded by the Battleship Arles. Late in the year, the Oblique was reinforced by Council survivors from Roussillon. During the so-called "Clash of the Titans", both the Arles and the Oblique were destroyed outright. The Council's depleted forces retreated to Champagne, and the crippled Royal garrison fell back to Ile-de-France -- creating the power vacuum later exploited by The Minarchy. The wreckage of the Oblique, however, remained -- its unspent ordinance and molten hull plating raining down upon Planet Marseille. EFL is now working to salvage the Oblique's wreckage, however progress has been glacially slow.

590613.text: A veteran cruiser of the Gallic War, the Leros accompanied the Battlecruiser Momus from Tau-44, for its deployment to Inverness. Following the withdrawal of the LSF's Tuscaloosa battlegroup in 835 AS, the Crayter Republic have been left to hold the line against "Vagrant" threats alone.

590615.text: This temporary depot was established to facilitate the return of vessels provided to Bretonia under the Gallic War Lend-Lease program. Liberty abruptly triggered premature return clauses in 835 AS, forcing Bretonia to immediately return ships that had been assigned to internal garrison duties.

590617.text: This depot has been hastily constructed by BMM to stage mines, munitions and other explosives for deployment in Dublin. Despite Bowex's best efforts, Royal Engineers have quickly depleted this stockpile.

590619.text: The O'Doherty was a Molly Hel class cruiser, assigned to the Sluagh Brigade. The cruiser was purchased from the Red Hessians in 827 AS, after being retired from their fleet. The O'Doherty was destroyed in Dublin during battle with the Bretonian First Royal Cruiser Flotilla.

590621.text: The Ballingarry was a Molly Scylla class cruiser, assigned to the Sluagh Brigade. The cruiser was purchased from the Liberty Rogues in 832 AS, and smuggled into Dublin to resist the pending Bretonian invasion. The Ballingarry was destroyed in Dublin during battle with the Bretonian First Royal Cruiser Flotilla.

590622.text: You are now departing the Independent Worlds and entering the Kingdom of Bretonia.

590623.text: You are now departing the Independent Worlds and entering the Republic of Liberty.

590625.text: The Shikoku Internment Zone is a holding pen operated by the Kusari State Police. Liberty vessels waiting in Shikoku were seized and held here following the outbreak of war.

590626.text:
>>>PUBLIC WARNING<<<
Non-native traffic departing the Empire of Kusari and entering the Independent Worlds is to report to the Shikoku Foreign Traffic Control Zone for mandatory cargo inspection.

590628.text: The Hitokappu Logistics area is currently being constructed by the Kusari Naval Forces. No public information currently exists about the project, however Naval spokesmen have announced ongoing initiatives in the Keiun Cloud intended to curtail Golden Chrysanthemum and Liberty criminal activities.

590630.text: This satellite has been constructed by the Kusari Naval Forces to provide advance warning of approaching forces -- covert or otherwise.

590632.text: This depot is being rapidly constructed by Kusari Naval Forces engineers within the sensor obscuring depths of the Keiun Cloud. Storage tanks and rapid refueling moors appear to be designed to quickly service capital grade vessels.

590633.text: This Order fighter was destroyed holding the Orillion Minefield against Nomad assaults, following the loss of Cairo Base.

590635.text: This Order gunboat was destroyed holding the Orillion Minefield against Nomad assaults, following the loss of Cairo Base.

590636.text: This Order fighter was destroyed repelling Kusari's assault into Omicron Mu in 835 AS.

590638.text: This Kusari fighter was destroyed during Kusari's punitive expedition into Omicron Mu in 835 AS.

590639.text: This Order gunboat was destroyed repelling Kusari's assault into Omicron Mu in 835 AS.

590641.text:
CLASS: Bismarck
CREW: 0
ARMAMENT: N/A

The Battleship Undine was deployed in 798 AS during Rheinland's explosive military buildup prior to the Colony Wars. Assigned to the Western Fleet, the ship was dispatched to the Hamburg border, before pushing into the Bering Independent Worlds on the outbreak of war in 800 AS. The Undine suffered heavy damage to its engines when a temporary refueling depot it was moored to was destroyed by renegade Liberty cruisers. In the chaos of Rheinland's government collapsing soon after, survivors describe the Undine's officers going "berserk" and massacring fellow crewmen, before being overwhelmed. The remaining crew abandoned the immobilized ship using onboard shuttles and fled back to Rheinland.

Drifting inside the Tanner Asteroid Belt, the Undine's location was quickly lost -- it would be many years before Rheinland's authorities were stable enough to dispatch search parties in vain. Instead, the asteroid-battered hulk was rediscovered by Unioner scavengers, who were prowling Colony War battlefields for military grade salvage. After slowly towing the battleship back to Pacifica Base, work began on tearing out internal components and valuable subsystems for use in the development of the early Hel class cruisers. When the Red Hessians launched their first battleship in 819 AS, the Unioners rushed to compete, fearing the Hessian's rising influence and prestige within Rheinland's underworld.

The stripped hull of the Undine was selected for repair, with the Unioners bartering components from the Junkers of Yanagi and the Corsairs, and scavenging from Thuringia, Bering, and Hudson. The Undine's first major deployment came in 826 AS against the vulnerable Vierlande Prison. The Unioners led a flotilla of Coalition and Red Hessian forces in capturing the station and freeing its inmates. Little did the Unioners know that their "allies" were aware of the Unioners' cooperation with the Corsairs, using the joint assault to spring an ambush that tore the Undine apart. After the shellshocked Unioners re-occupied the Prison, they assessed that the Undine was completely unsalvagable, and could not make a jump back to Bering. As a result, it was once again stripped of components for recycling into other projects.

590643.text:
CLASS: Oasis
GRAVITY: Complete
DOCKING: Yes
AMENITIES: Restricted
CREW: 40
590643.mapped:
Located in one of the most remote regions of Sirius, the Intrepid Maiden is a Zoner Passenger Liner repurposed as a refueling and resupply outpost for explorers venturing into the uncharted depths of the deep Omegas. Constructed in 825 AS at Baltimore Shipyard, the vessel was originally sold and deployed to Bretonia's frontlines during the Gallic War, where it provided crucial logistical support.

As the war neared its end, the Maiden was ambushed by a Gallic Royal Navy squadron while delivering supplies for the Battle of Southampton Shipyard. Though her escorts bought enough time for her escape, the liner sustained significant damage to her cargo and engine compartments. With the war’s conclusion, the diminished demand for logistics vessels, combined with the costly repairs needed to restore her, led to the ship being auctioned off to the Zoners at Freeport 1.

Repaired and refitted for deep space exploration, and given the nickname "Intrepid", the Maiden was sent to orbit a gas giant in the newly explored Cayman system. As the vast and untamed deep Omegas remain largely unexplored, the vessel now serves as a pioneering foothold for those daring enough to venture into the unknown.

Formerly an open-to-all gateway, this Jump Gate is all that remains of the busy commercial highway connecting Gallia and the Taus.

In use until the end of the Confederacy, the Gallic Union decided to restrict this pathway owing in part due to the events that led to the invasion by Kusari. Any unauthorized ship found in the Gate's vicinity will be dealt with accordingly.

590763.text:
CLASS: Zachary
GRAVITY: Complete
DOCKING: Yes
AMENITIES: Full
CREW: 550
590763.mapped:
Sierra Starport was constructed shortly after Canberra Star City was fully settled. While Canberra handled the fledgling Natio Octavarium's population with little difficulty, it didn't offer much to kickstart their economy. Sierra began as a refinery, hosting freighters loaded with shielded mining vehicles and skimming equipment, to harvest the copper on Oraibi and the gases of Salina respectively. As more and more smugglers stopped at Sierra for supplies, the station continued to expand.

Unfortunately, that expansion combined with the gravity of Salina's moons and Salina itself to make approach to the station increasingly complicated. As a result, Natio Octavarium towed the station to its new location before further expansion.

Natio ownership of the station would be short-lived however, as a decrease in membership meant the base administration would be transferred to a group of Freelancers willing to pay to keep the station operational and for Natio to recoup some of their investment. With Barrier Gate Station serving as an informal rest stop for the Outcasts on their long distance Cardamine runs, the relatively new Starport has wedged itself in a niche as the port of call for all those people tired of a certain shade of orange, and the associated crowd that brings. This has brought conflict which would otherwise be confined to the inner systems of Liberty or other border worlds to Coronado. And the market is literally booming for it.
