590765.text:
The supergate began as a joint project between Deep Space Engineering and Ageira Technologies as Project COLD LAKE -- an attempt at directly connecting Poole and Alberta as a means to bypass the Gallic blockade of Magellan and Cortez. Although initially successful in delivering reinforcements to the Bretonian front, the 826 AS sabotage of the supergate resulted in two Navy battlegroups going missing in transit -- a catastrophe that prompted the gate's immediate shutdown and a formal inquiry from both governmental and corporate angles. The incident prompted a swift response from Ageira, and a team of experts were tasked with painstakingly tracking down the hyperspace signature used to connect the two systems; a gruelling process that eventually resulted in a singular promising result.

Once the most probable destination of the supergate's jump failure had been pinpointed, Deep Space Engineering and Universal Shipping -- in partnership with Cryer Pharmaceuticals, Ageira Technologies, and Synth Foods Inc. -- were quick to assemble a task force called Expedition Oregon. The concept was simple but bold; a seven-month journey via conventional cruise engines to deliver pre-constructed jump stabilizers that could establish a connection point on the other side, linking the Alaska supergate to the pinpointed destination system. The expedition launched in January of 827, and after months of travel the convoy arrived in Omicron Nu. It took weeks to successfully stabilize the connection between Nu itself and the Alaska system after their arrival; a process that unexpectedly applied itself to the other jump anomalies in the system, linking Omicron Nu to several neighbouring systems as well as Alaska itself. Regardless, their work laid the foundation for finishing the Omicron Nu supergate in its entirety.

With the COLD LAKE supergate malfunction still fresh in their memories, a separate team of Ageira scientists began cross-referencing their data with archives dating back to the Texas Incident of 500 AS, drawing what parallels they could between the two disasters to ensure a third could never happen. The Alberta supergate was disassembled as quickly as possible and prepared for relocation and reconstruction in Alaska proper -- with a team of Ageira Technologies, Deep Space Engineering, and Universal Shipping working round-the-clock to reassemble the gate under the Liberty government's watchful eye. It took them less than a year to complete the gate and prepare it for initialization -- and when the Oregon expeditioners successfully engaged their jump stabilizers and signalled back to the Alaska team, the connection was rapidly finalised, allowing the Liberty government to begin projecting influence into Omicron Nu with impunity.

590767.text:
>>>WARNING: NAVIGATION HAZARD<<<

The Calanques Debris Field was created by the "Clash of the Titans" that claimed the Battleship Arles, Battleship Oblique, and most of their attendant fleets in 742 AGS (826 AS). EFL Oil and Machinery were appointed by the Parisian Assembly in 743 AGS (827 AS) to clear the wreckage. The Minarchy took issue with the disturbance of war graves, despite warnings on the dangers posed to the planet below. Brigand vessels occasionally harass the cleanup vessels, amid rumors the Union Corse have placed a bounty on vessels taking part in the operation.

590769.text: Wreckage of a Military Fighter that was part of the attack force during the Conflict of Cologne. The hull has markings that are typically found on fighters that were involved in a heavy dog fight.

590770.text: A Hessian Fighter whose last orders were to defend the evacuees from Tholey station before its destruction. Much of the damage to the hull shows different layers of fighter fire, which leads to the conclusion that the hull was never entirely repaired before being used for its next assignment.

590772.text:
Tholey Station was established as a joint operation between Daumann, the Bounty Hunters Guild and the Rheinland authorities. The Guild had been commissioned by Rheinland to help bring order to the rampant, lawless frontier of Cologne whilst Federal forces were occupied in Dresden and elsewhere. Faced by Unioners to the north and Hessians to the south, Tholey's bounty hunters became some of the highest paid in Federal Rheinland space.

As the old Republic government started to fall, so too did Federal investment in Cologne slacken. This development led to the Guild being trusted with the administration of the station. Corporations moved in to profit off the opportunity; a biodome was constructed by Synth Foods and Daumann utilized the production facilities to compete with ALG – The station was now valuable corporate real estate.

With the fall of the Republic government and the start of the Rheinland civil war Tholey Station quickly found itself isolated and under assault by the Red Hessians. Choosing not to fight a war they were no longer being paid for, the Guild mounted a token defense before retreating, allowing the onboard civilians to evacuate. The Hessians captured Tholey and once the reunited house of Rheinland came to reclaim Cologne, the Hessians left a skeleton crew onboard to aid the defense efforts. Ultimately, Tholey station was destroyed by Battleship Altenburg during the siege of Saarbrucken, where its wreck remains as a grim reminder of the Hessian occupation of the nearby planet.

590774.text:
Aland Shipyard was a former IMG installation tooled to produce and maintain a wide variety of mining ships in the region. At the height of the Gallic war, its potential to serve as the provider of emergency repairs for the drydock deprived Bretonian Kingdom came under scrutiny. And after a series of botched negotiations, tensions escalated and the shipyard was forcibly occupied for the remainder of the war. Placed under BMM's charge as the seemingly pertinent industrial authority, the station remained in Bretonian hands post-war, intended to be auctioned off to a favorably inclined third party.

These plans would neither be finalized nor come to fruition as the shipyard would be struck by the worst incident of sabotage to date. Station overrides were engaged to run the reactor at emergency output, while also sealing the towers responsible for venting the pungent byproduct. The resulting systems failure made it impossible to rectify before the effects became station-wide, at which point an explosive device was triggered. As a result of its direct impact being coupled with the pervasive amount of toxic smog, the explosion ripped much of the shipyard inside out during operational hours, producing a substantial death toll of hundreds.

The damage is so thorough and extensive that there is little utility to any considerations of repair or reactivation. Though BMM has not yet made any move to comment on the incident, the Mollys have passionately taken credit for the destruction of this formerly independent asset.

590776.text:
This Gammu Drone appears to be fully shut down. A thin layer of crystaline material covers the hull. Due to the system-wide radiation, standard scanners are unable to analyze the exact structural composition. Livadia's published drone research registry lists this drone as "Peeper" - with a note regarding this drone's particularly nosy yet pacifistic nature.

"Peeper, Gammu AI Drone, registered entity #378 - nickname given by Alexander Winslow. We marked Peeper with a photon-based tattoo after getting its permission. We are not sure why Peeper agreed to the procedure without any question. We assume Peeper finds merit in the idea of being easily distinguishable from other, otherwise pristine AI drones. Peeper seems to avoid conflict at all cost and generally flees from any non-livadian vessel. In fact, Peeper allows any liviadian asset to get close, yet not closer than 27.315 feet. No, Shane, I do not know what that is in meters."

The livadian drone research registry does not mention Shane at any other point.

590778.text:
This Gammu Cruiser appears to be fully shut down. A thin layer of crystaline material covers the hull. Due to the system-wide radiation, standard scanners are unable to analyze the exact structural composition. Livadia's published drone research registry lists this cruiser as "Frosty" - with a note regarding this unit's extraordinary behavior.

"Frosty, Gammu AI Harvester, registered entity #215 - nickname given by Alexander Winslow. While attempts to communicate Gammu AI units, especially cruiser-sized ones, has always been rather difficult, it was not with this one. I was talking with Tim about something trivial while observing this cruiser from close proximity. It seemed to be in a passive state."

"At the end of the conversation, Tim said 'Stay frosty!' while the comms must have been active. As immediate response, the cruiser reacted by repeating the recorded voice line over and over again - 'Frosty'. We are yet to figure out why it did it, but the reaction resulted in this nickname for 215."

590780.text:
This Gammu Drone appears to be fully shut down. A thin layer of crystaline material covers the hull. Due to the system-wide radiation, standard scanners are unable to analyze the exact structural composition. Livadia's published drone research registry lists this drone as "Skoot" - with a note.

"Skoot, Gammu AI Drone, registered entity #304 - nickname given by Alexander Winslow. Named this one after Vanessa's gaian ground sloth - because it might just be the laziest drone I have been watching. Skoot is easily identified because of its incredibly weak energy signature, possibly as a result of a damaged component. This drone seems to avoid the proximity of other drones. I wonder if it is afraid of getting replaced. Need to look into that, after the date with Vanessa."

590782.text:
The remains of the Core fighter "Timothy Avarice", named by his pilot of the same name. Avarice was known among the crew of Battleship Mars as youngster who desperately tried to convince people to name things after him. Due to the constant refusals of this request, Avarice simply christened his ship with his name.

During the fight over Gammu, Avarice was listed as MIA - resulting in his wing getting renamed to "Battleship Mars - 4th Avarice Avengers".

590784.text:
These are the unmistakable remains of a Gammu drone dispatched from the frigid surface of Gammu. The scarred hull, once composed of various complex alloys stretched and re-arranged into unrecognizable and mystifying patterns, appears to have been sundered apart by relentless plasma cannons, leaving nothing but a dead vessel behind, its technological innards still floating in the hollow vacuum of space.

The complete absence of any recognizable navigational hardware or data memory banks suggest that this particular vessel was shot down, and later divested and desecrated from the more valuable parts by an unknown party.

590786.text:
Scanner and data profiling confirms that this inert vessel is another drone sent the elusive Gammu, hailing from their eponymous planet. The sheer distance travelled by this particular drone combined with a basic carbonic analysis suggests that this particular drone was deployed for space reconnaissance decades ago, as the puzzling on-board reactor appears to have already seen a lot of mileage.

Any navigational data extracted from this wrecked machine only confirms the baffling protocols and algorithms followed by the Gammu, as the vessel seems to have travelled the entire solar system in an elliptical pattern repeatedly several thousands of times, before finally breaking apart and finding refuge in a large, hollow asteroid in a remote periphery within the system.

The latest encrypted and undecipherable transmissions sent by this machine back to the subnet relays of Gammu were met with no response.

590788.text:
The fast and unremitting precision of the Cruisers lurking in the vicinity of Gammu during the final offensive orchestrated by the Mars were the very reason behind the top Core battle analysts and strategists believing that deploying a mass-scale offensive towards their frigid home in such a small window of time would likely result in a dismal and pyrrhic victory. But against every possible odd, the Core forces buckled the defensive perimeter composed of Gammu Cruiser assault packs and the Carrier Orion deployed by the Technocracy through sheer aggression with only minimal losses, resulting in the Gammu’s subsequent and questionably quick retreat as the Core quickly established dominance over the entire perimeter of the planet.

A quick data analysis within the almost oceanic pool of data stored inside the data banks profiles displays multiple baffling directives followed by the large automation flawlessly. Such directives consisted in investigating and archiving nearby asteroid and debris activity, registering the radioactive emissions unleashed by the raging radioactive sun of Omicron Kappa, as well as relaying the trajectory of tantalized and foolhardy pilots who were bold enough to enter the vicinity of Gammu’s orbit.

There are several thousands of other such entries within the navigational archives, repeating themselves in precise and unerring patterns for entire decades, until one particular directive tasked the machine with repelling the incoming Core assault team advancing towards Gammu's orbit. In adherence with the glaring reported damage visible to the naked eye sustained by ballistic and concentrated high energy fire, this vessel retreated in the far distance away from the losing battle, prioritizing its own escape according to the ubiquitous directives dispensed from Gammu prior to their catastrophic fall by the hands of their aggressors.

Now, the thing from the stars rests in an empty asteroid. Inert, battered and broken, the impossible wiring tangled into impossible shapes still floating aimlessly in the emptiness of space.

The machine’s final set destination is towards home.

590790.text:
A heavily damaged lone Core Requiem rests inside this hollow asteroid. According to the on-board data, it belonged to fighter pilot Oliver "Badmouth" Emerson. The inside of the cockpit appears to be still pressurised, while the late pilot has been presumably retrieved by his cohorts. The composition of the cabin appears to be mostly composed of carbon dioxide, making the fate of the pilot inside uncertain.

The Requiem presents severe lesions and dire wounds inflicted by several laser cuts, some of which severely impacted and knocked out the main reactor, leaving the reckless pilot stranded, alone and unable to contact anyone.

According to the mission logs, Badmouth was part of the strike wing of fighters who laid waste to the ground defenses through the employment of explosive ordinance. The pilot, in his hubris, disregarded a direct order to not give chase to any fleeing Gammu drones. The pilot continued to open fire at the remaining automations, before being ultimately cornered by them as they fought back, leaving his disabled ship out to drift into a nearby asteroid.

The disabled ship's final log recordings are appended within the blackbox.

"To anyone who can read this: this is Badmouth. I thought I could show those Gammu tangos who's boss. They were just a bunch of glorified toasters who never stood a chance against us... until I tried to chase them down by myself. I tried telling my CO that I have been scrapping these things for a while now, but as it turns out, a cornered animal really knows how to put up a fight... They've messed me up good. Life support's offline, comms are offline, my engine's gone bust. I can still see Gammu from all the way out here... the lights and the explosions and the works, and I'm stranded here to sit and watch, and breathe my own air until I'll die. I'm leaving this homing beacon online until somebody finds me."

590802.text:
Gran Canarian Shipwrights Headquarters
Gran Canarian Shipwrights (GCSW) is a Zoner shipbuilding company headquartered on Lanzarote Station in Omega-49, renowned for their patented ZC-410 "Peregrine"-class civilian frigate. With the increasing demand for both the ZC-410 "Peregrine"-class frigates and ZC-240 "Condor"-class gunboats, GCSW acquired the disassembled prefab modules of Grand Vista Orbital to expand Lanzarote Station. This strategic move reduced their reliance on external shipyards and enhanced their production capabilities.

Shuttles regularly transport materials from the planet to the station, while locally contracted freighters handle the export of much-needed spare parts to stations across Sirius that support GCSW’s products.

590804.text:
GCWS Supply Ship "Vikrant"
Registered as one of Gran Canarian Shipwrights' many transports, the Vikrant was famous among Zoners for breaching blockades during the hostilities with the Corsairs across the early 830s.

It is unknown how the transport ended up in this location, however, it is irrecoverably damaged and irradiated. Scanners indicate plasmatic residue matching that of the Corsair "Ignis" cannon.

590806.text:
Pirate Frigate "Rotkehlchen mit Haube"
A popular pirate from Rheinland and a frequent guest of Ithaca Base.

Inspired by the Sol-era story of Robin Hood, the charismatic Captain Sebastian Scharlach takes from the rich and gives a substantial amount of his exploits to the poor. Due to his reputation, Scharlach's influence on the Ithaca Captain's Council is not to be underestimated.

590808.text:
Pirate Combat Transport "Railgum"
The Railgum, commanded by Emma Gum, a frequent guest of Ithaca Base.

This ship became a legend for dropping a cargo container filled with a reactive sticky extinguishing foam into the engine exhaust of the Battleship Norfolk, immobilising it in the orbit of the Ross Planetoid until repair ships from Portsmouth Shipyard could carry out field maintenance.

590810.text:
Pirate Frigate "Dundercat"
The Dundercat, a frequent guest of Ithaca Base.

Captain Kathryn Wolpertinger has offered her support to Ithaca Base since 834 AS. She gained influence with the Council after destroying the Rheinland Military Gunboat "Spandau-2". It came close to discovering the base's location while investigating pirate raids from the Furstenfelde.

590812.text:
Pirate Gunboat "Pie Rat"
While the name of this ship is a pun, the history of this gunboat is no joke at all. Known for having ended the career of countless Bounty Hunters, the Pie Rat's captain joined the Ithaca Council in 834 AS. The gunboat's presence makes even the greediest members of the Bounty Hunters Guild think twice about approaching Ithaca.

Lloyd Rath is known for his cooperations with Kathryn Wolpertinger of the Dundercat. Rumors about a personal relationship between the pirates are yet to be confirmed.

590814.text:
Pirate Cruiser "Grand Serpent"
A Judicator-class cruiser under the command of Colonel Bryce "Ripper" Thorn.

With the defeat of the Liberty Insurgency, the fate of many ships remained unclear. The exact history of the Grand Serpent is even murkier, but it is certain that "Ripper" Thorn has never been part of the Insurgency or any related groups. In fact, he is primarily known for hijacking transports and ransoming them back to their previous owners. It is possible the Grand Serpent was his largest and most audacious catch. The arrival of the cruiser at Ithaca also marked the day Thorn joined the Ithaca Council in an uncontested vote.

590816.text:
Pirate Cruiser "Walker Wraith"
The Walker Wraith is a Hel-class cruiser commanded by the Lichtenberg Twins, Rosmarie Lichtenberg and Horst-Volker Lichtenberg.

Hired as mercenaries by the Ithaca Council to provide security around the station, the Walker Wraith has a trigger-happy reputation when responding to the slightest of threats or provocations. The message is clear: Stick to the Council's Code while visiting, or else...

590818.text:
Pirate Frigate "And one for the road!"
This iconically named frigate has a reputation for raiding transports carrying alcoholic drinks.

Captain Liam Hardrada enjoys an excellent reputation in the Sirian underworld as a provider of large quantities and varieties of beverages. Seeing Hardrada's frigate after a Trade Lane disruption is often a relief for many of his victims, as they know he rarely cares for any other goods or passengers. It is alleged Orbital Spa and Cruise pay a monthly tribute in exotic alcohols to avoid Hardrada's attention.

590820.text:
Pirate Freighter "Cannibal"
Piloted by Bretonian criminal Two-Bite James, this Draugr freighter has been trimmed of much of its excess exterior plating, lending it a skeletal appearance but significantly reducing its mass. His modifications grant the Cannibal the agility necessary for its role as a blockade runner on behalf of the Ithaca Council. As an art thief of some renown, James' skill at evading police pursuit has earned him the trust of Ithaca's pirates in keeping the station flush with new weapons and illicit supplies. In return, they keep the man flush with credits and stiff drinks, and offer him a safe haven if he takes one too many risks in his daring career.

590822.text:
Pirate Transport "Siren"
The Siren, an infrequent guest at Ithaca, is presumed to to be piloted by missing Hamburg opera singer and actress Hilda Richterfeld, along with another unknown accomplice. Local rumors across Omega-7 warn nearby travelers not to "listen to the siren's song call"; the few naive pilots who instead foolishly chase the mysterious woman's false cries for help vanish into the Walker Nebula. Those ships that do reappear weeks later will be little more than gutted, empty wrecks.

The Siren's enigmatic crew neither confirms nor denies whether they are involved in any of these incidents.

590824.text:
Pirate Gunship "Halligan"
A raider reportedly sighted prowling the ice clouds of Cambridge and Omega-3, this Galatine-class gunship earned a reputation for challenging Bretonian destroyer patrols along the trade lanes towards Sprague. Using the hull's razor-thin profile to its advantage, the Halligan's preferred strategy is to lure their pursuers deep within the cloud, then pour focused fire on the foe's engines until they are left disabled and stranded. These pirates almost never finish their foes off, however, and seem content to harass civilians with oddball requests and petty theft, extorting only modest sums from transports compared to the other pirates at Ithaca. Some at the station believe that the captain is acting out a personal grudge against the Bretonian authorities, and another popular rumor proposes that he and his men could be former BPA personnel.

590826.text:
Restaurant Ship "Neko's Onigiri"
A Bumblebee-class hauler, refitted into a mobile restaurant ship. Customers may either take a quick space walk over to Neko's or get their fresh food vacuum-sealed per food container drop. The space restaurant can serve up to 40 guests at once.

Hina Sakuraoka, known as Mrs. Neko, opened her space restaurant in 834 A.S. in New Tokyo's orbit. With Roppongi Station's ongoing deconstruction, "Neko's Onigiri" not only profits from the lack of competition in orbit but also from the local salvage crews and patrols being all too happy about freshly prepared food as alternative to Synth Paste. Every day of the week comes with a different daily special, with Saturday's "Sweet Kitty Cat Onigiri" being so high in demand that late arrivals run risk of not getting any at all.

590828.text:
"Samura Atoshori Team"
One of several treatment teams assigned to the Samura clean-up of Roppongi Station. Samura won the contract for the difficult decontamination and deconstruction project in 833 AS, after negotiations with ALG were abruptly terminated by the Kusari government. The appointment of Samura has been questioned by many, as the industrial corporation has no appreciable background or experience in this line of work. Already there have been a number of deaths among inexperienced remediation crews, likely caused by inadequate equipment and training.

590830.text:
Barrier Gate Ramen is one of the two successful restaurants on Barrier Gate. Situated at the very top section of Station B, Barrier Gate Ramen's view over The Gap is probably one of the major selling points for customers to dine here instead of at Barrier Bites, which is in the very center of Station C.

The other selling point is that unlike at Barrier Bites, guests simply accept being in the same room with their enemies - this has been a tradition every single visitor so far has been respecting. There has literally never been an instance of violence at Barrier Gate Ramen. This fact has lead people to believe in the "Ramengate" conspiracy theory.

In January 834 A. S., Administrator Tinsley spoke about this in an interview with the CNS: "They are just damn good noodles, and people love them. Nothing more, nothing less."

590832.text:
Gunship "Winter King"
A rare sight in this region of Sirius, the Winter King is a Bishamon-class GMG Gunship owned by Administrator George Tinsley himself. While the details of how Tinsley got his hand on this ship are not publicly known, it is usually used by Tinsley when he needs to leave the station.

Due to the rarity of Bishamon-class gunships getting handed out to outsiders, many people have paid with their lives as consequences for the attempt to lay a finger on this vessel. The armaments of this ship are known to be able to cut even through the shields of frigates and cruisers.

590833.text: A scientific satellite with space research equipment onboard. This satellite is also used as mid-range radar

590837.text:
Deep Space Explorer "Kho"
An abandoned Voyager-class freighter. Scans indicate a highly irradiated interior and no traces of human life signs.

The only escape pod is missing. The cargo bay appears to be sealed off. Further scanning reveals plant-based biomatter spread out in the entire cargo hold.

590839.text:
Samura Train "Dragonfyre"
A wrecked Ryuujin-class train. Scans are unable to locate traces of life signs.

Despite the heavily damaged condition of this vessel, some compartments seem to still be pressurized. The black box was accessed recently and is still emitting a low-frequency data signal.

SUIT-ID: Kaworu - [Heavy breathing can be heard.] Tried my best, but the engine exploded last second. Life support is offline, the oxygen is now part of the Crow. Pretty sure I lost them but me crashing into the rock probably drew attention. Stuff's just not working out for me today. At least I'm still breathing. For now. Gonna be a long suit jump. I'm not going to give up just yet, though. Pilfered all remaining supplies, maybe I can get some makeshift repairs for the escape pod going. Need to find the way back to the Hokkaido jump hole, then all the way to... whatever is out there.

[PROXIMITY ALERT]

SUIT-ID: Kaworu - [A chuckle can be heard.] ... Yeah, they got me. But not the cache. They'll need to fly up the serpentine trail to find it. All the way up to the shattered egg. Hidden in plain sight, really. Who knows. Maybe I can come back and get it. Or I should just cut my losses here.

590841.text:
Kusari Naval Forces Heavy Fighter "Seraphic Feather"
This is the wreck of a Chimaera-class Kusari Heavy Fighter. While the chassis itself appears to be mostly intact, scans indicate that the entire interior suffered from multiple explosions and loss of atmosphere. The hull appears to be slightly irradiated.

Minor traces of human residue detected.

590843.text:
Kusari Naval Forces Gunship "Naeba Guard"
Naeba Guard is the nickname of the New Tokyo orbit patrol gunship frequently seen near the restaurant ship Neko's Onigiri.

Ever since the Roppongi Station incident rendering the orbital station uninhabitable and an eye sore, opportunists have shown interest in the establishment of an orbital bazaar. With the restaurant ship Neko's Onigiri acting as the spaceborne version of a yatai, chain reaction was set in motion, leading to many small companies applying for a permanent spot right between the trade lane entries leading to the headquarters of Kishiro and Samura.

590845.text:
Bazaar Ship "Ikebana Home"
An old GMG mining vessel, repurposed to serve as mobile art vendor as part of the New Tokyo Bazaar.

Mr. Zen offers a wide variety of typical kusari art items, from Ikebana artworks to holographic statues. Prices range from questionably cheap to remarkably expensive, the latter usually applying to non-digital items.

590847.text:
Restaurant Ship "Bodos Wurstbude"
This Grouse-class transport was repurposed to serve as mobile art restaurant ship, providing freshly prepared fast food for anyone with a few spare credits.

Bodo Uwe Bartels, nicknamed "Bub", runs this little snack bar with his wife Magda and his son Ottmar. The Wurstbude's "Currywurst mit geriffelten Fritten" meal received a surprisingly high rating in Interspace Cousine's Space Food Poll, indicating especially high popularity among visitors from Gallia.

590849.text:
***GRAVITATIONAL ANOMALY DETECTED***
The magnetic and gravimetric readings of this object are difficult to classify, but they most closely resemble those of a jump hole. Like Jump Gates, jump holes are naturally occurring regions of space that represent a breach in the natural boundaries of spacetime. Unlike Jump Gates, which are artificially stabilised via a finely-tuned combination of delicate programming and careful construction, jump holes occur naturally and are comparatively unpredictable and unstable.

Scanner telemetry coming from this jump hole suggests it is in the early stage of forming.

590851.text:
Search and Rescue Frigate "Sunnyvale"
A Peregrine-class frigate, commissioned by Ames Research Station as part of the Ames Search and Rescue team.

With the lasting Dark Matter Storm, Ames Research Station invested into multiple sturdy yet nimble ships to test prototype technologies to counter the otherwise fatal system-wide environmental hazard. The group lead by the Sunnyvale gained popularity all over the neural net for successfully rescuing countless stranded ships and escape pods.

590853.text:
Search and Rescue Gunship "Moffett"
A Mantis-class gunship, commissioned by Ames Research Station as part of the Ames Search and Rescue team.

With the lasting Dark Matter Storm, Ames Research Station invested into multiple sturdy yet nimble ships to test prototype technologies to counter the otherwise fatal system-wide environmental hazard. The group lead by the Sunnyvale gained popularity all over the neural net for successfully rescuing countless stranded ships and escape pods.

Captain Weylyn Jeffersson holds the record for the fastest run from the Colorado Jump Hole to Ames with a gunship in 3:09:03 (February 11th, 834 A.S.).

590855.text:
Search and Rescue Gunship "Deacon"
A Mantis-class gunship, commissioned by Ames Research Station as part of the Ames Search and Rescue team.

With the lasting Dark Matter Storm, Ames Research Station invested into multiple sturdy yet nimble ships to test prototype technologies to counter the otherwise fatal system-wide environmental hazard. The group lead by the Sunnyvale gained popularity all over the neural net for successfully rescuing countless stranded ships and escape pods.

Captain Jody Bo became a local legend for being the first pilot to find and mark the secure route from Ames Research Station to the Colorado Jump Hole.

590857.text:
Ames Research Project "DMSG"
This satellite marks a rock sample of the DMSG research operation.

Project DMSG - Dark Matter Storm Geology - researches the effects of prolonged exposure of Kepler's native asteroids to the regional Dark Matter Storm.

590859.text:
Deconstruction Frigate "Riff-Raff Ruffler"
A Salvager-class frigate, under command of Captain Carla "Meats" Poler and her motley crew.

The Riff-Raff Ruffler is a common sight at Ames Research Station since the station fell into forced isolation due to the Dark Matter Storm. Ever since then, the salvage frigate leads recover and recycling operations and sells the spoils to both Ames and the few visiting traders.

The frigate itself appears to be in a surprisingly mint condition.

590861.text:
Recycling Ship "Savage Gardener"
A Wrecker-class gunboat, property of Angus Laramis.

With the Kepler Dark Matter Storm resulting in a constant supply of freshly disabled ships of various origins, it was only a matter of time until Junkers would seize the opportunity and salvage anything of value from the carcasses.

Angus Laramis joined the salvage operations near Ames in August, 834 AS.

590863.text:
Salvage Triage Marker: Area 1
Area 1 - Survey
The following objects have been marked for survey:

"Big Duck" - Mammoth-class Transport - Status: in progress - Note: Pre-DMS wreck
"CV Tough Times" - Serenity-class Transport - Status: waiting - Note: DMS victim (July, 834 AS)
"ZSV Pneumonoultramicroscopicsilicovolcanoconiosis" - Corvo-class Research Vessel - Status: waiting - Note: DMS victim (April, 834 AS)
"CV Pipsqueak" - Peregrine-class Frigate - Status: waiting - Note: DMS victim (April, 834 AS)
"USV Planck" - Bison-class Combat Transport - Status: waiting - Note: Pre-DMS wreck
"Wire Tapper" - Bayonet-class Fighter - Status: waiting - Note: DMS victim

590865.text:
Salvage Triage Marker: Area 2
Area 2 - Recovery
The following objects have been marked for recovery to sellable condition:

"CV Leap of Faith" - Dunlin-class Frigate - Status: 91 percent - Note: DMS victim
"Daruma" - Drone-class Freighter - Status: 76 percent - Note: DMS victim (January, 832 AS)
"Tobusaku" - Bumblebee-class Transport - Status: 36% - Note: Pre-DMS wreck (829 AS)
"Speed Rummer" - Kestrel-class Freighter - Status: 57% - Note: DMS victim (August, 834 AS)
"Grandmother" - Voyager-class Freighter - Status: 88% - Note: DMS victim (January, 834 AS)
"Sludge Hammer" - Grendel-class Freigther - Status: 59% - Note: DMS victim (July, 834 AS)

590867.text:
Salvage Triage Marker: Area 3
Area 3 - Deconstruction
The following objects have been marked for deconstruction:

"KTV Suwa-maru" - Akegata-class Container Transport - Status: in progress - Note: pre-DMS wreck
"STS Ieyoshi-maru" - Ryuujin-class Train - Status: waiting - Note: pre-DMS wreck (825 AS)
"Unidentified Kusari Destroyer" - Takeda-class Destroyer - Status: waiting - Note: Pre-DMS wreck (probably pre-800 AS)
"Unidentified Liberty Cruiser" - Archer-class Cruiser - Status: waiting - Note: Pre-DMS wreck (possibly Insurgency, 830 AS)
"SFS Long Drive" - Stork-class Train - Status: waiting - Note: DMS victim (833 AS or so)
"Point Offense" - Bullmastiff-class Transport - Status: waiting - Note: DMS victim (March, 834 AS)
"Ohio 109th Spearheads: Beta 2" - Defender-class Fighter - Status: waiting - Note: DMS victim (March, 834 AS)
"Sir Rancid Drake" - Pitbull-class Train - Status: waiting - Note: DMS victim (833 AS)
"Nagoya-5" - Ashikaga-class Gunboat - Status: waiting - Note: Pre-DMS wreck (820-ish AS)

590869.text:
Freeport 6 Auction Office "Day 6"
With Freeport 6 generally enjoying high popularity both among visitors as well as the regional factions, including the House of Kusari, it was only a matter of time until a clever entrepreneur would use the opportunity at hand and establish and provide a moderated location for used ships to change their owners legally. As a result, Mirjam "Gold Hand" Krasinski convinced enough investors to fund the construction of the Freeport 6 Auction Office, an extension of Freeport 6 that is all about trading and auctioning vessels from all over Sirius.

The construction of the extension ended in 834 AS and was celebrated widely among ship vendors, who finally have a legal and unified marketplace. Even with rather strict limitations on what types of ships may be auctioned and traded, many regional parties are strongly interested in the ever changing offers and auctions.

The public attention and frequent inspections of faction representatives who wish to ensure that their technologies don't end up in the wrong hands leave little wiggle room for more exotic trade opportunities. Nevertheless, with Freeport 6 and the Taus being rather crowded and full of hidden locations, it might just be impossible to fully prevent black market ship auctions.

590871.text:
Snack Bar "The Distress Bacon"
Due to the popularity of "Distress Bacon" on Planet Manhattan, Interspace permitted the gastronomy chain to open up a promoted branch for spacers on Newark Station.

Among the "Distress Bacon", the establishment also offers other award-winning snacks like the "HazMato Salad", "High-Temperature Ale", "Solar Pan", "Pittsburgers", "Circuit Fries" as well as "Molybdoni and Cheese" and "Tox-Mox". Spacers can request their foods to be dispensed, vacuum-sealed, into space for a delicious treat to-go.

590873.text:
Studio Ship "Tabula Smaragdina"
Auctioned off in december 834 A.S. to Bloodbag Films, a popular and successful holotainment company from Liberty, the Bustard-class carrier has been modified to serve as zero gravity studio ship.

Due to the sirius-wide popularity of authentic holotainment products, Bloodbag Films invested into this vessel to provide such authenticity - nothing is more real than the actual real thing. Especially space-themed holotainment media is recorded here, in direct cooperation with Freeport 6 and multiple smaller media studios and artists. The freeport itself profits highly from the sudden arrival of VIPs from all Houses.

590874.text:
Antonio
You know what you did.

Now clean up this mess.

590875.text: SES Elected Representative of Individual Merit

590876.text:
Super Destroyer
SES Elected Representative of Individual Merit
Look familiar? Scenes like this are happening all over the galaxy, right now! You could be next. That is unless you make the most important decision of your life. Prove to yourself that you have the strength and the courage to be free. Join the Zoners. Become a part of an elite peacekeeping force! See exotic new lifeforms. And spread Managed Confusion throughout the Galaxy.
Become a HERO.
Become a LEGEND.

Become a ZONER!

590878.text:
Mobile Assembly Ship
The Radiant Lynx
ALG Waste Disposal suffered a massive hit to their reputation within Rheinland during the past decade, resulting in Rheinland companies seeking alternatives for large-scale organized recycling operations. The Junkers of Kreuzberg Depot were all too happy to offer their expertise and services, leading to a surprisingly clean and professional upgrade of the station and a notable extension of assets.

This included the purchase of the Radiant Lynx, which primarily acts as a barge for storing valuable objects with a comparatively high resale value. Once filled, the licensed Bustard-class Carrier leaves the debris field, heading for the various ship-producing workshops in Rheinland to provide the spare parts that the Kreuzberg Junkers gathered from any wreck they pulled into the Ruhrfeld.

590880.text:
Compact Debris
The Wall of Trash
Mareike "Moehrchen" Buttenberg, a local artist from Kreuzberg Depot, created this controversial piece of art by chaining several leftover pieces of debris to several lattices. All materials used are of exceptionally low quality, irradiated, chemically corrupted, or otherwise undesirable enough not to bother with any attempts at recycling.

While the Rheinland Art Society "Neue Welle" praises the Wall of Trash as something that adds character to the system's otherwise boring space landscape, the Junkers of Kreuzberg simply appreciate the considerably large obstacle for blatantly blocking the view of several long-range telescopes of The Ring that otherwise try to keep an eye on the depot's activities.

590882.text:
Independent Freelancer Vessel
Curie
This transport was cheaply requisitioned by a small circle of physicists and archaeologists aboard Heisenberg. While the Gull-class itself is not suitable for exploratory scientific efforts, this ship carries a detachable research module in place of its cargo pods. This allows it to function as an exolab for potentially hazardous experimentation, taking on more risk than would be tolerated aboard the station.

The Curie's current project is in developing iterations on the gravity snare technology utilized in the Heisenberg racetrack, investigating the potential for miniaturization and possible applications in law enforcement. It has previously been involved in exotic materials research, sourcing samples from the criminal element that now frequent the station, but the project was abandoned following multiple researcher disappearances.

590884.text:
Bounty Hunter
Winslow
The Montante-class gunboat "Winslow", piloted by Bounty Hunter Jonathan Woodcock. Nobeoka Bounty Score in 835 A.S.: 145 Points

Woodcock is a member of Nobeoka's "Gods of Love and Death" hunter group. He is known for an extremely aggressive piloting style, which lead to a list of friendly fire incidents. Some of them ended lethal.

590886.text:
Bounty Hunter
Magau's Trophy
The Aspis-class Outcast Heavy Transport "Magau's Trophy", commandeered by Bounty Hunter Alexa Magau. Nobeoka Bounty Score in 835 A.S.: 182 Points

Magau is a member of Nobeoka's "Twilight Assassins" hunter group. The Twilight Assassins are quite famous in the Sigmas and Omicrons for their repeated raids into the Omicron Beta system, where they ambush otherwise heavily armed cardamine convoys. Sacrificing her own Orca, Alexa Magau launched herself with a modified escape pod into the cargo bay of an Aspis and took out every single Outcast on the vessel before taking control of it, entirely on her own. Overriding the computers, she permanently changed the system to block out incoming kill switch signals, allowing her to claim the ship and display it proudly at Nobeoka as a trophy.

590888.text:
Bounty Hunter
Albedo
The Corvo-class Hybrid Gunboat "Albedo", captained by Bounty Hunter Elite Christoph "Warlock" Trestle. Nobeoka Bounty Score in 835 A.S.: 201 Points

Trestle is a member of Nobeoka's "Overload" hunter group. He is primarily known for pushing his ship to the absolute limits, eliminating the target in a swift and surgical strike with kamikaze-overloaded turret settings. In case the calculated risk is not in his favor, the Albedo is capable of escaping at speeds higher than usual. While this usually impresses both friends and foes, the most impressive fact about the Albedo is that Trestle somehow manages to pay the repair bills for frequently deformed turrets and heat sinks.

590890.text:
Bounty Hunter
Guppy
The popular Grouse-class Transport "Guppy", controlled by Bounty Hunter Mariko Wada. Nobeoka Bounty Score in 835 A.S.: 103 Points

Wada is a member of Nobeoka's "Gods of Love and Death" hunter group. The Guppy is frequently used as bait in hunts, only to surprise rookies with the heavy punch a hunter-modified Grouse can pack. Her success in the bounty hunting business is commonly attributed to the Guppy's armor reinforcements, which can handle both enemy and friendly fire.

590892.text:
Bounty Hunter
Destiny
The always reliable Condor-class Gunboat "Destiny", operated by Bounty Hunter Elite Jennifer "Hailstorm" Hail. Nobeoka Bounty Score in 835 A.S.: 372 Points

Hail is the leader of Nobeoka's "Gods of Love and Death" hunter group. Bounty Hunters of her group only survive if strictly following her command. Insubordination justifies death, as it means a threat to those that follow orders. Her Nobeoka Bounty Score suffers from deductions frequently because of that, however still stands among the highest. A controversial sign of success.

590894.text:
Bounty Hunter
Brawler
The low-comfort Mantis-class Gunboat "Brawler", piloted by Bounty Hunter Rookie Asuna Nashima. Nobeoka Bounty Score in 835 A.S.: 57 Points

Nashima is a member of Nobeoka's "Twilight Assassins" hunter group. Despite her rookie status, Nashima quickly managed to establish a reputation as rogue Rogue, due to her previous ties with the Liberty Rogues, as well as Lane Hacker hacker - due to her brilliant counterhacks on Lane Hacker ships. Finally, the Brawler is feared as Bounty Hunter-Hunter-Hunter, collecting chevrons of ships by people who found an early end during a career as Bounty Hunter hunter.

590896.text:
Bounty Hunter
The Crusher
The Lifter-class Utility Ship "The Crusher", owned by Bounty Hunter Veteran Bryce "Constable" Howards. Nobeoka Bounty Score in 835 A.S.: 122 Points

Howards is a lone operating assassin. And given his methods, nobody else is required. The Crusher is usually ignored due to the ship class usually just being background noise compared to any other ship, allowing Howards to sneak up on unsuspecting vessels to trap them with crushing force in the lifter clamps, which are modified to blast the ship's own shield bubble into the hull of the target. By the time the victim realizes what is happening, it is already too late. Several criminals lost their moored ships this way.

590898.text:
Bounty Hunter
Saya Maru
The Kusari Container Transport "Saya", or Saya Maru, run by Bounty Hunter Logistics Master Quentin "Trebuchet" Loggins. Nobeoka Bounty Score in 835 A.S.: 78 Points

Loggins is a member of Nobeoka's "Warbond" logistical division. While they are occasionally get their hands dirty themselves, they mostly relocate captured vessels and confiscated goods. To that matter, the Saya Maru received an over-budget equipment loadout. Many unprepared pirates found out too late they were trying to bite off more than they can chew.

590900.text:
Militant Cruiser
Ophan
Commissioned by an influential Zoner named Jordan Dryfuss, the Ophan was constructed at the Livadia Shipyards with the initial premise of safeguarding Zoner assets in the Omega-49 system. However, the passionate speech of a certain Z. A. Graham for the cause of the Zoners of Erie resulted in an alteration of course after departing from Omicron Kappa, heading for Liberty instead of the Omegas, to meet with a small group of smaller assets.

The loss of Carrier Pinnacle in combat with Battleship Alma during the early stages of the contest for Planet Erie resulted in a revision of possible strategies to support the resistance. Instead of attempting to assemble another Aquilon-class carrier, the resisting Zoners managed to prove that quick, decisive strikes on less important targets cause more disarray to Liberty than assaulting key structures. With this in mind, the Ophan focuses on swift hit-and-run attacks, relying more on its improved engines than on raw cruiser firepower.

Some say the Ophan's primary target is to lure out an LSF Task Force operating in the Pennsylvania system's outskirts.

590902.text:
LSF Hunter Killer Cruiser
Visalia
Facing a relentless, pesky resistance on and around Planet Erie, the LSF deployed the Visalia to the Pennsylvania system in order to react to potential threats similar to an Aquilon-class carrier named Pinnacle, which arrived in Liberty space to challenge Liberty's operations.

Remaining mostly hidden yet ever vigilant, the Visalia and its escorts are just waiting for strike orders on larger targets.

590904.text:
Deep Space Exploration Carrier
Odyssey
Fed up with the constant threat of the Houses to what used to be unclaimed space, Zoners and other individuals founded the Odyssey Exploration Group in 830 A. S. with one goal in mind: Leaving Sirius. Their combined efforts culminated into the Odyssey, a strongly modified Aquilon-class carrier.

Enjoying safety through the strict procedures and comparatively strong defenses around Livadia, the Odyssey is preparing to leave Sirius in the coming months, along with several smaller vessels. The intended direction is kept secret to prevent ambushes as well as followers.

590906.text:
Militant AWACS Transport
Grasshopper
The Grasshopper is a transport last registered as Ageira personnel transport. It disappeared in 827 A. S. during trade lane maintenance operations in the Galileo system. Left behind was an disabled Screamer mine with several profane insults targetting the megacorporation written on the shell, leading the investigating officials to assume an involvement of the Lane Hackers.

Scans indicate a powerful sensor scrambling effect originating from this ship, resulting in triangulation errors.

590908.text:
Alien Construct
Pylon
Assembled from nomad materials and parts of the excavated ruins of Tritonis, this overtly alien construct emits highly irregular readings. While regular ship scanners are unable to make sense of them, more sophisticated arrays can find similarities to periodic patterns found in hyperspace.

Space-time fabric surrounding the structure appears to be unstable.

590909.text:
Border Control
Navigation Buoy
You are about to enter a different region.

Proceed with caution.

590911.text:
Independent Freelancer Vessel
Equinox
The IFV Equinox is a frequent sight in the Pennsylvania system, often escorting various transports to and from the New York system. Captain Julie Carpenter cashed in several bounties since the ship's arrival in the system in 836 A.S., primarily targeting Xenos and Liberty Rogues.

The Equinox sports unusually dangerous weapons for a Montante-class gunboat.

590913.text:
Sector Classification Xi
Xi 101
The Jump Drive technology rush quickly resulted in experiments replacing technical prowess and scientific guidance with a pressure for results, a lack of security measures, and pure luck. Specifically the latter was necessary for ships to actually arrive in one piece in a system that both adheres to known realspace physics and provides comparatively safe locations for arrival.

These systems, exclusively accessible via jump drive leap of faiths, are catalogued as Xi-class systems by scientists all over Sirius and Gallia. Very little is known about these systems.

590916.text: Gathering saturated energy from the surrounding nebula, these Power Spheres hold immense levels of radiation that provides backup power for Dur-Shurrikun.

590919.text: No further information available. Power signature is alien, compositional elements are alien, weapon system is alien.

590922.text:
CLASS: Pilgrim
GRAVITY: Unknown
DOCKING: Yes
AMENITIES: Limited
CREW: 20
590922.mapped:
Santa Lucia is a Pilgrim Liner on the outskirts of Omega-43, serving as the most isolated Corsair snubcraft outpost in the region. Established as a staging ground for expeditions into the deep Omegas, the Liner plays a role in the Imperio's ongoing push for exploration and expansion.

Manufactured on Invergordon Shipyard in 826 AS, Santa Lucia was one of many transports partaking in the Artifact trade. The ship was exchanged over to the Corsairs at Trafalgar a month after its maiden flight, as part of strengthening the Corsair-Junker ties in Bretonia.

The decision to use a Pilgrim Liner as a staging ground was a pragmatic one - three years after the Corsairs purchased the vessel, on one of the routine Artifact runs, the liner, along with its escorts, was ambushed by combined Hessian and Molly forces at the Cambridge - Omega-5 border. Barely making it to Cadiz, the ship's core reactor and the engines were severely damaged.

Re-fitting the liner to be tailored to exploration and more of a stationary role posed logistical challenges, but the Corsairs capitalized on a wormhole to Omega-41 before it de-stabilized. With much of the base hull of the ship intact, the Imperio deemed the endeavor a worthy investment despite the risks. A few years later, Santa Lucia now serves as the primary refueling and resupply point for local explorers, relying on logistical support from Leon Base in Omega-41.

590925.text:
DIAMETER: 2,890 km
MASS: 1.72 x 10e22 kg kg
TERRAIN: Barren
TEMPERATURE: 700°C to 1,400°C
ESCAPE VELOCITY: 3.4 km/sec

A small but violent moon, constantly reshaped by volcanic activity. Its orbit around the frozen world of Tija generates intense tidal forces, keeping its interior molten and its surface unstable. Lava flows stretch for kilometers, and eruptions are frequent enough to make landings a high-risk operation. Anything left on the surface for too long will either melt or be buried under fresh layers of rock.

590927.text:
DIAMETER: 6,471 km
MASS: 3.12 x 10e24 kg
TERRAIN: Arctic
TEMPERATURE: -220°C to -180°C
ESCAPE VELOCITY: 8.4 km/sec

An inhospitable, frozen world with a thin atmosphere orbiting Omega-2's central star. The surface is mostly solid ice, broken up by jagged ridges and deep crevasses. There are traces of past geological activity, but these days, it’s little more than a lifeless, frozen desert. The temperature is low enough to make most materials brittle. No native life, no real atmosphere, just an endless stretch of ice under an empty sky.

590929.text:
Wreckage of the Liner Edenvale, the lead ship of the eponymous Edenvale Expedition. Launched in late 832 AS from Dagger Outpost, Omega-55, the expedition aimed to reach a yet-uncharted black hole on the southern fringes of the Omega region. Previously considered unremarkable, the black hole became a source of anomalous readings during the Blackout.

Detected by both the Core at Dagger and, surprisingly, the sensor network of the Cambridge Line, the readings became of interest to both the Core and the Bretonian government, resulting in the commissioning of a joint expedition. Cambridge Research Institute would provide funding and research equipment, while the Core provided manpower and security.

Thus assembled, the expedition left Dagger for a newly discovered jumphole found to connect to the black hole’s stellar vicinity. After the convoy’s rear-guard escorts jumped through, the expedition was never heard from again.

The Edenvale was a state of the art research vessel, outfitted with all the sensor and sampling equipment necessary to study the black hole. Its defenses were also specially reinforced, with thicker armor and gunboat-grade weaponry serving as strong deterrence for any would-be attackers. The hull of the liner is pockmarked with impacts from both laser and neutron weaponry, though neither seems to have inflicted any serious damage. Analysis of the wreckage indicated that it lost structural integrity to a precise strike from an unknown weapon, shattering the ship into three pieces.

The liner’s databanks appear to have been purged while the blackboxes are missing. There is little useful data to be retrieved from the wreckage, with only a fraction of a message playing: "...help us all. Whatever it is that got us, do NOT approach the vessel. Save yourselves you d... tell anyone back home to organize expeditions towards the F... retrieve the...

590931.text:
The remains of Ensis, the lead escort of the ill-fated Edenvale Expedition. Captained by commander Jesse Reilly, the Ensis and its crew were veterans of the Omega theatre. First deployed in 829 AS, the Ensis was put under the command of freshly promoted Reilly right out of the drydock.

The vessel would spend the entirety of its service life assigned to Dagger Outpost, supporting patrol and raider wings against Corsairs and Coalition forces alike. Both the captain and the crew would earn themselves a reputation for a spotless, if unremarkable, service record.

The Ensis appears to have succumbed to numerous impacts from weaponry inflicted by unknown entities, the vessel clearly proving too large to effectively navigate a field this hostile. The radiation-induced loss of data prevents a full blackbox recovery, although an analysis of the remaining information indicates the Ensis attempted to use the field to shake off a group of pursuers. Evidently, the gambit has failed.

590933.text:
The wreckage of the Lapin, flown by Remi Corriveau. A renowned ace in the Council Navy, Corriveau served as an officer of the OCI during the Confederacy and the subsequent invasion by Kusari. He would flee Gallia after the royalist takeover of the Office in the wake of the conflict, his skill as a pilot landing him a lucrative post with the Core’s paramilitary.

His proficiency and adaptability would quickly earn him the position of a squadron leader. It was shortly after this promotion that Corriveau and his squadron were assigned to the Edenvale as escorts for its upcoming mission. Further reinforced by the WV Ensis, the squadron and its charge departed for the deep Omegas, never to be seen again.

The ship’s hull is riddled with damage typically inflicted by neutron weaponry, the killing shot having struck the main powerplant. The ship's blackbox is severely damaged. The remaining snippets of data indicate the expedition went through multiple engagements against unspecified attackers. The final entry suggests Corriveau was ambushed by an unidentified freighter.

590935.text:
The remains of the Killjoy, a Core fighter flown by lieutenant Harvey Chapman. Once a Bounty Hunter of some renown, Chapman was known for his particular hatred towards the Liberty Insurgency and his many successful sorties deep into Vespucci itself. After the Insurgency fell, Chapman would travel Sirius, eventually ending up employed by the Core.

With plenty of experience in the depths of the Walker Nebula and behind-enemy-lines operations, Chapman was a natural pick for the Edenvale Expedition’s security detail. Unfortunately, the Edenvale’s departure would be the last time Killjoy was seen or heard from.

The ship appears to have taken significant damage from both neutron and plasma weapons. The cockpit is little more than slag, likely hit with a spread of plasma projectiles at close range. Although the ship’s blackbox is damaged, a few partial data entries remain. The final entry suggests the Killjoy split off from its pack to take down an isolated enemy bomber.

590937.text:
The remains of the Merry, a Core fighter flown by lieutenant Jared Graham. A former LPI officer, Graham became infamous for daring interceptions and captures, often well outside usual LPI jurisdiction. Although showered in promotion and bonuses back home, Graham ended up looking for more, both challenge and money. This pursuit would lead Graham to join the Core paramilitary, soon climbing their ranks as a scout.

The ship appears to have suffered catastrophic damage in a collision with one of the surrounding asteroids. Based on local conditions, it is likely the heat and radiation blinded the pilot as they made their run across the field.

Surrounding the wreckage is a number of blackboxes and data drives, likely ejected from the ship during the collision. They have long since been rendered defunct by the environmental conditions.

590939.text:
The wreckage of the Cerbero, a specially modified Correo-class freighter flown by Cleonico Cavaleri. A veteran of the Bretonian front, Cavaleri had a legendary reputation amongst the garrison of Leon, using his freighter to turn the tables on many Bretonian and Hessian pilots alike. His exploits would earn him extensive fame, so much so he would receive a special assignment from the Elders themselves.

Thus, in late 830 AS, Cavaleri was made the leader of a newly formed squadron. Comprised of other irregulars like himself, the squadron had a simple purpose - to give the Core a taste of their own medicine. As the corporate mercenaries entrenched themselves in the Omicron and Omega systems, the Elders had sensed an opportunity. With every raid and incursion, the Core amassed more and more wealth and exotic technologies, the valuable loot then shipped off to their customers among the Houses. Mirroring the Core’s own brazen tactics, Cavaleri and his squadron were tasked with hounding the mercenaries much like they did the Empire, utilizing quick smash-and-grab raids to take back what rightfully belonged to Crete.

The squadron’s career was as successful as it was short lived, however, as Cavaleri and his men went missing while shadowing a Core research ship in late 831 AS. Analysis of the wreckage indicates the Cerbero went through multiple engagements, suffering heavy damage from fighter-grade lasers and gunboat-grade particle weapons. The vessel’s fuel tanks are ruptured, the loss of fuel leaving the ship stranded over the uncharted world. The pilot’s body, equipment and any potential cargo are likely still onboard.

590941.text:
The remains of the Gaviota, a Titan-class fighter flown by veteran raider Natalia Sa. Known for her daring raids deep behind Hessian lines, even as far as Stuttgart itself, Sa earned herself significant wealth and many commendations. Her fame and indisputable skill would earn her a place in the newly formed Cerbero squadron as its second in command.

Like the rest of the Cerbero squadron, Sa was last seen trailing a Core convoy through the southern Omega systems.

The remains of the vessel show signs of widespread, if superficial, damage, likely inflicted by fighter-grade weapons over the course of multiple engagements. As the ship’s structure remains sound, it is likely the killing blow was dealt against the cockpit with a precise burst of laser weapons fire.

590943.text:
The wreckage of Pejesapo, a Centurion-class fighter flown by Diego Moliner. Unlike his wingmen, Moliner was a largely unremarkable irregular, working perimeter security for Leon Base for most of his career. He was, however, a close friend of Cleonic Cavaleri, the founder of the infamous Cerbero squadron. It was through this connection that he found himself recruited for the team, proving himself as a reliable fighter who prioritized the safety of his fellow pilots.

Like the rest of the Cerbero squadron, Moliner was last seen trailing a Core convoy through the southern Omega systems.

Analysis of the wreckage indicates the ship was crippled by a salvo of particle blasts, then finished off in the ensuing battle. The onboard logs are damaged, the remaining data indicating the Pejesapo used its armor to absorb the opening volley of an ambush, though the resulting damage proved too much for the ship to handle.

590945.text:
The wreckage of Comodin, flown by Silvio Queiroz. A raider from Cadiz, Queiroz made a name for himself through daring raids against Bretonian shipping in Cambridge and New London. Known for a particularly reckless flight style that threw his enemies off-balance, Queiroz was eventually chosen to join an elite raiding team, colloquially known as the Cerbero squadron.

Like the rest of his squadron, Queiroz was last seen trailing a Core convoy through the southern Omega systems.

The ship appears to have been ripped to pieces by heavy particle weapons, likely gunboat-grade. The data onboard the ship is only partially preserved. The log entries suggest Queiroz, together with his wingman, Gaviota, ambushed a Core gunboat traversing the system. The bold fighting style employed by Comodin backfired, a reckless strafing run bringing him right in front of the enemy vessel.

590947.text:
The lead ship of the Maulwurf wing, flown by Sebastian Enzenauer. Originally working for Daumann as a Diamond prospector in Omega-11, Enzenauer became disillusioned by the corporation’s treatment of himself and his fellow workers. Like many before, it would lead him to abandon his employer in favor of the Independent Miners Guild, where his skills as a surveyor would find him plenty of work on Omega-7’s Silver fields. As Enzenauer climbed the Guild’s ranks, he would end up attracting a small group of like-minded pilots, eventually forming the Maulwurfs.

The Maulwurf wing began its life as an IMG prospecting team, credited with finding many previously-unknown Silver deposits in the depths of Omega-7. However, during one of their prospecting runs in the mid 831 AS, the team ran into an ambush set by Daumann-affiliated mercenaries. Kitted out for sampling rather than combat, the Maulwurfs suffered many casualties during their escape attempt - only three of the seven members managed to make it back to Freistadt. Enraged by their losses, the Maulwurfs soon left the Guild and joined up with the Hessians, seeking to avenge their fallen comrades.

Their final assignment was much like their previous work, the wing tasked with prospecting the systems of Omega-47 and Omega-55 for potential resource deposits. In their last communication, the wing relayed they were following a Corsair raiding party into an uncharted system. None of the Maulwurfs would return from the chase.

Most of the ship’s damage appears to be of environmental origin, its hull panels warped by high temperatures and intense radiation, but also pockmarked with laser and neutron weapon impacts. Analysis suggests the vessel suffered a gradual build up of damage over multiple engagements, the ship subsequently succumbing to the field it presumably used to conceal its retreat. The ship’s damaged equipment and the pilot’s body are still present.

590949.text:
The remains of Maulwurf 2, flown by Hugo Bergler. Once a veteran scout for the Rheinland Military, Bergler left military service for the Guild shortly after the Rheinland Civil War. He spent most of his career working security around Freistadt, escorting miners and prospectors across Omega-7 and Omega-3, using his inside knowledge of Military training and tactics to counter Daumann and Kruger raids against IMG operations in the region.

His performance would eventually draw the attention of Sebastian Enzenauer, the flight leader of the infamous Maulwurf wing. Bergler would enlist with the wing just weeks before their ill-fated encounter with Daumann mercenaries. Blaming himself for the losses that day, it would be Bergler who pushed the other survivors to join the Hessians to get their revenge.

The Manaslu appears to have been disabled by accurate particle weapons fire, most closely matching damage typically inflicted by APM-made weaponry. The onboard blackbox is largely intact, and analysis of the data entries indicate the Maulwurfs were trailing what they perceived to be a Corsair smuggling convoy. Bergler’s wingmen appear to have perished in the resulting skirmish, the Manaslu intercepted and crippled soon after by an unidentified Silvertip-class fighter.

590951.text:
The remains of Maulwurf 3, flown by Jordan Allen. Born onboard Holman Outpost, Allen was one of the only two Maulwurfs who began their career flying for the Guild. After spending his early years working maintenance on the ice miners from Holman, Allen would be forced to flee for the Omegas during the Gallic War. He would find work as a mechanic on Aland Shipyard, and would continue to work there until the station’s seizure by Bretonia.

Like many other members of the Guild, Allen was enraged by the transgression, enlisting with Freistadt’s security wings shortly after. However, he would not be able to finish his flight training before the conflict over Aland fizzled out. Instead, Allen’s freshly acquired training and years of technical expertise made him a prime recruit for the Maulwurf wing.

The ship appears to have been destroyed in just a few, pinpoint accurate salvos of plasma and neutron weapons fire. The damage is consistent with armaments used by Corsairs. The ship’s blackbox did not survive the encounter.

590953.text:
The Astral Nomad was a standard Dromedary-class freighter under the command of Captain Elira Voss, a veteran Zoner navigator known for her meticulous logs and fascination with pre-human stellar ruins. The vessel carried minimal cargo and had been stripped of civilian fittings to accommodate extended-range sensor equipment. Its assignment was reconnaissance: charting the immediate periphery of the Fischer singularity and surveying gravitational anomalies for safe approach vectors.

According to fragments recovered from her logs, Voss’s crew encountered what appeared to be an alien structure orbiting uncomfortably close to the singularity’s event horizon. The ship’s sensor arrays registered readings inconsistent with known physics-repeating geometric patterns and oscillating energy fields.

Her last recorded transmission ended abruptly during an evasive maneuver. Automated distress pings later placed the Astral Nomad drifting with catastrophic hull breaches, its engines torn free as though pulled towards a nearby planet where the crew made a desperate last attempt. The transmission also mentioned an unknown artifact located in the vessel's cargo hold...

590955.text:
Commanded by Captain Ilar Renn, the Solstice Runner was a heavily modified Dromedary optimized for long-haul endurance, equipped with reinforced shielding and redundant reactor systems. Renn had a reputation among Zoner crews for stubbornness and a habit of ignoring retreat protocols. His ship’s task was to push beyond the sensor perimeter into regions where light itself bent unnaturally, gathering data other crews hesitated to pursue.

Telemetry fragments suggest Renn’s ship reached the same alien structure minutes after the Astral Nomad, part of the same Zoner expedition 13. His notes, later recovered from databanks, speak of “a brilliance folded into itself” and a surge of coherent signals transmitted in tight-band bursts. The Solstice Runner’s instruments were still processing when unidentified contacts emerged - large, red-tinged anomalies moving with purposeful trajectories.

The Solstice Runner attempted a high-thrust escape into a denser debris corridor. Wreckage indicates the vessel suffered catastrophic shield collapse before breaching its fuel core. The remains drift in a wide arc around a cracked planet in its vicinity, fragments charred but strangely uniform, as though sectioned deliberately.

590957.text:
DIAMETER: 27,551 km
MASS: 1.55 x 10e26 kg
TERRAIN: N/A
TEMPERATURE: N/A
ESCAPE VELOCITY: 60.2 km/sec

A yellow gas giant with an unpredictable atmosphere, orbiting Omega-2's central star. Its upper layers are in constant motion, with storms that stretch for thousands of kilometers and winds that can easily rip apart unshielded ships. The deeper one goes, the pressure and heat skyrocket, making it impossible to explore beyond a certain depth. Strong electromagnetic fields interfere with most standard sensors, and its gravity well can easily claim careless pilots underestimating the planet's dangers.

590959.text:
DIAMETER: 3,924 km
MASS: 2.19 x 10e23 kg
TERRAIN: Barren
TEMPERATURE: -80°C to 15°C
ESCAPE VELOCITY: 2.3 km/sec

A barren, reddish moon orbiting Omega-2's distant blue star. Its thin atmosphere doesn’t provide much protection from radiation, and its surface is covered in craters and wind-carved rock formations. Occasional dust storms sweep across the landscape, making navigation difficult. While there are no signs of life, traces of ice have been found beneath the surface, making it a potential stop for deep-space operations.
