591564.mapped:
Outpost Hesperia was formerly a Legion installation poised to enable strikes within the system of California against criminals and the forces of Liberty alike. It also served to bridge a gap between the Legion and its ally in the Xenos. Unfortunately, due to Commonwealth leadership's rhetoric and increasing doubts within the Xenos about the value of their alliance, relations soured sharply in the weeks prior to Liberty's strike on Seperatist forces in Bering.

The Xenos elected to keep most of their forces away from the massacre in Bering, conserving their manpower for two more important strategic and symbolic operations. The Liberty Rose and it's sizable attachment of snubcraft were sent after Rochester and the Xenos of Ramsey made it clear what they thought of the Commonwealth.

The outpost was bombarded while most Legion forces were occupied with Bering. Knowing reinforcements would be slow to arrive, outpost administrators surrendered and opened up the bay doors to the assault wing, who took control of the station swiftly and executed any who continued to profess support for the Commonwealth. Those that surrendered were spared. Though the operation to take the station was a success, the Xenos knew there would be retaliation.

Now rechristened Fontana, a new Xeno-approved crew bearing loyalties to the idea of a Free Republic were given administrative control and the doors were opened to all manner of scum and entrepreneurs. The station now gives a percentage of all the profit it makes to the Xenos, and the Xenos are quick to retaliate against anyone that interferes with this vital revenue source.

The Lane Hackers' are notorious as information brokers, selling stolen manifests for lucrative convoys to the Liberty underworld. It is rare that they get their own hands dirty, usually claiming loot through business arrangements with their clients. The Destroyer Insidious is an extension of that philosophy -- the Storta was gifted to the Lane Hackers in 825 AS by the Outcasts’ Fanucci Cartel. Timely Lane Hacker intelligence had resulted in the Don’s eldest son being rescued from an LSF prisoner convoy.

While no longer the most modern of ships, the Lane Hackers have extensively customized it as a mobile long-range sensor platform. In this role it has roamed Liberty sniffing out classified secrets that might be of interest to wealthy benefactors. As a result, the Insidious is among the LSF's most wanted targets, with an eye-watering reward for its destruction. Following sensor firmware updates at Cochrane Depot in 833 AS, the Insidious deployed to Coronado. It now monitors Crayter Republic patrols, selling optimal route data to Outcast smugglers for a handsome fee.

CLASS: Eagle
CREW: Unknown
ARMAMENT: Unknown

The elderly Battleship Alabama was assigned to watch over Ontario's newly completed California jump gate in 809 AS. Later that year, a DSE survey operation orbiting Blezard Valley came under attack by the Xenos. The Alabama and its contingent responded, setting a direct course through the Georgian Ice Field. Having successfully lured the Alabama into the ice field, a Xeno ambush was launched. The Alabama was crippled by mines concealed among the asteroids, and finished off by waves of Xeno attack craft. Liberty rescue patrols launched from the Battleship Ottawa later scoured the field, finding nothing but scattered wreckage.

The Ontario Xenos towed the hulk back to the newly constructed Fort Ramsey with the intention of stripping it. News of the battle quickly spread to other Xeno clans however, prompting a gathering of leaders from across Liberty to discuss the stricken battleship's fate. Opinions ranged from scrapping the hull for parts, to its sale to the Hellfire Legion for renovation. While the conclave ultimately decided that an attempt should be made to repair the Alabama, technical and logistics problems dogged the project, slowing progress to a crawl. It would take almost 20 years of incremental tinkering by Fort Ramsey's technicians to get the ship into a serviceable state.

Emboldened by the conquest of Hesperia Outpost in mid-827 AS, the newly renamed Liberty Rose undertook its maiden flight against Rochester Station - a target long coveted by the movement. The battleship crippled the base, but could not finish it off before being driven away by a coalition of Junker, Rogue and Lane Hacker defenders. The resulting disruption to the Cardamine trade created a gap the Xenos exploited to negotiate with frustrated Outcast cartels, securing their own entry into the market. The Liberty Rose again returned to Fort Ramsey for repairs, where it remained until the Ontario Liberation Offensive of 835 AS.

The Rose served as the spine of the assault force that attacked the LSF Battlecruiser Lehigh. Despite being outclassed by the Lehigh in every category except mass, the Rose successfully destroyed the defensive emplacements surrounding the California Jump Gate, allowing waves of fighters to pour into the area and overrun the Liberty defenders. The Lehigh and its bombers inflicted severe damage during the battle, with the Rose's primary bridge being destroyed, and engines crippled. The Lehigh was forced to retreat before the Rose could be dispatched, allowing the Xenos to tow it back to Fort Ramsey. The Rose is now sheltering nearby after receiving basic patch repairs, having been displaced from its mooring by the construction of Objector corvettes.

591572.text:
DIAMETER: 6,485 km
MASS: 4.73 x 10e24 kg
TERRAIN: Barren
TEMPERATURE: -38°C to 69°C
ESCAPE VELOCITY: 9.04 km/sec

Devoid of water, atmosphere or life, Sudbury is a planet whose core cooled eons ago. Nothing of interest was discovered during initial system surveys, with most attention instead focused on its moon. Due to its mass, Sudbury attracts most asteroids that are flung out from the Georgian Ice Field, shielding Blezard Valley from impacts. In 834 AS, a hyperspace pulse was detected in Ontario, originating from Planet Sudbury. This wave bore a striking similarity to the readings detected during the Blackout several years prior, destroying sensitive equipment and sensors throughout the system. An energy field activated on Sudbury’s darkside, partially submerged into the planet’s surface.

Speculation that an ancient facility had awoken were borne out when artificial structures pushed through the surface's regolith. It soon became apparent that these were some form of emitter array, as a sustained beam was projected out into deep space, towards The Barrier. Lane Hacker sensors begun broadcasting Sudbury data onto the neural net soon after. This led to significant public debate around Artifact sites, and the dangers they pose. Researchers analyzing the Lane Hacker data believe there were intricate energy fluctuations being transmitted along the now terminated beam, potentially indicating pulsed data or instructions. Debate on this hypothesis has since taken on a frenzied edge, amid speculation about what will now occur at the target destination -- the moon Jericho in Coronado.

While various factions struggled to control Sudbury's orbit for access to the Sudbury facility, the LSF eventually ousted their rivals by deploying the Battlecruiser Tuscaloosa nearby. Liberty expeditions sank antimatter blasting charges into boreholes around "Site Alpha", in an attempt to undermine the protective shield. After almost a year of unsuccessful attempts to breach the shield, the Tuscaloosa was forced to withdraw through deep space as supplies ran low. Despite ominous warnings prohibiting landing, a rag-tag expedition of Xeno, IMG and Order agents landed to explore the site in mid 836 AS. This triggered a buried explosive countermeasure left behind by the LSF, resulting in secondary detonations within Site Alpha, and substantial damage to Planet Sudbury.

591574.text:
DIAMETER: N/A
MASS: N/A
TERRAIN: Desert
TEMPERATURE: N/A
ESCAPE VELOCITY: N/A

A small, airless moon orbiting Planet Sudbury. Surveys detected various precious metals on its surface, however early Deep Space Engineering (DSE) automated mining platforms were quickly destroyed. Following this, the DSE construction vessel Edwin DeHaven was dispatched to carry out repairs. Before long a distress call was broadcast, with the vessel assumed lost. The Battleship Alabama subsequently disappeared while responding to this alert. Owing to the moon's remote location and challenging security situation, further operations were deemed untenable.

591579.mapped:
Battleship Thebes is the Order's flagship. Its main function is to serve as a mobile command post and to deal with threats that the smaller Osiris-class warships are inadequate against. Fortuitously for the Omicron organization, its production was safely cloistered away until the vessel's unveiling. As the Core pushed for the final confrontation over Toledo, the Thebes achieved full combat readiness and was prepared prematurely for deployment before construction could have been finished and tests run. Arriving late to the Battle of Omicron Minor, encountering Nomads assaulting both fleets alike; The Order made the decision to evacuate all personnel from Toledo and a full retreat to Omicron Epsilon.

The Thebes escaped from Omicron Minor through a destabilizing wormhole leading to Omicron Mu, a tentatively mapped star system with a habitable planet. However, the gravitational forces of the unstable wormhole damaged the Thebes' systems and it was forced to offload any surviving refugees from the planet Toledo to the planet Akabat. The Thebes had to spend several long months in a specially constructed dry dock before it could be fully repaired again and become the iconic protector of the Omicron Mu system, and more importantly, of planet Akabat and its inhabitants.

CREW: 500
591582.mapped:
A garrison of the Order built after the colonization of Akabat, Taba was strategically positioned between the major egress points of Omicron Mu. It is considered a forward operating base in the region, and serves as a major link in the supply chain to the Omicron Minor front line. Its larger-than-typical hospital receives injured pilots and crew from skirmishes amid the Toledo Graveyard, and its hangars are fitted for rapid repair of small craft, though larger vessels are sent on to Carthage.

Busy and crowded, Taba Starbase is one of the closest manned bases to the Nomad Worlds, and is known to the Order's deep space explorers as "Hell's Gateway".

TERRAIN: Terrestial
TEMPERATURE: -48°C to 23°C
ESCAPE VELOCITY: 9.04 km/s
591585.mapped:
Akabat is the largest moon of Planet Nebet. It has an erratic climate that strongly relies on its and Nebet's orbital cycle. Planet Nebet frequently eclipses the sun, which causes the occasional "long night". Akabat's atmosphere is dry and cold.

The Order found Akabat to be a suitable settlement, inhabiting near its lush rivers that flow downwards from snowy mountains. Many regions of the planet have not been explored yet as The Order was more concerned with establishing its defenses, especially after the devastation of Toledo.

TERRAIN: N/A
TEMPERATURE: N/A

Nebet is a medium-large gas giant with three natural satellites, among which is the system's only habitable astronomical body, Akabat. Its striking orange color and extensive ring system make it a memorable sight for the few pilots that venture this far into the Omicrons. The latter provides an important resource as well, offering relatively accessible water ice in abundance.

591590.text:
TERRAIN: Barren
TEMPERATURE: -44°C to 106°C

Jerba is a young rocky world featuring significant tectonic activity. Its thin, loose crust floats on a largely molten mantle, resulting in near-constant volcanic activity. Plumes of sulfur compounds create yellow clouds dozens of kilometers high, and buckling landmasses frequently reveal immense lava flows, bleeding a dramatic vista for the eyes of passing ships to marvel at. The hostility of the environment categorically precludes any potential prospecting operations.

591592.text:
Named after the founder of the Order and hero of the Nomad War, Casper Orillion, the jagged shards of this asteroid field are host to a myriad of space-borne microorganisms, providing a wealth of research material for the xenobiologists of the Order and others that find their way to the remote system. Relation to the organisms found in other parts of the Edge nebula is still unconfirmed, and beyond their scientific value no commercial applications have been tested.

With the connection to the Minor system being located within it, the Order maintains regular patrols in the field to warn of potential incursions.

591594.text:
Known as the "Wall of Seth" by the locals, this outcropping of the Edge nebula experiences frequent and perilous electrical storms. These stunning spectacles are both dangerous and awe-inspiring, capable of disrupting long-range scanners and disabling unprepared ships entirely.

Following the cataclysmic destruction of planet Toledo in 818 A.S., the remaining forces of the Order's Omicron division scoured the Edge in search of a new home. After an extensive search, they eventually discovered a system with favorable conditions for their reconstruction efforts, now known as Omicron Mu. The adverse properties of the Wall proved advantageous, providing a shield for their reconstruction efforts against both human and non-human adversaries. However, it is strongly advised not to traverse the nebula without obtaining up-to-date navigational instructions.

591596.text: The main entrance to the Omicron Mu system, the Omicron Mu Minefield guards the jumphole to Omicron Zeta. A twisting path throughout the minefield confuses the many unfortunate victims who are lost within the maze.

591598.text:
DIAMETER: 12,097 km.
MASS: 5.61 x 10^24 kg
TERRAIN: Water
TEMPERATURE: 68°C to 185°C
ESCAPE VELOCITY: 8.04 km/s

Planet Nile, located deep within the Wall of Seth nebula, is a vast aquatic world characterized by its inhospitable nature. Largely unexplored, Nile harbors a unique environment that poses significant challenges to human life. The combination of high pressure and chemical compounds found in both the water and atmosphere makes it unsuitable for sustaining human life. However, Order scientists have not ruled out other organisms thriving in the planet's oceanic depths.

591600.text:
DIAMETER: 3,195 km
MASS: 6.41×10^23 kg
TERRAIN: Barren
TEMPERATURE: -268°C to 185°C
ESCAPE VELOCITY: 1.1 km/sec

A small and airless moon that serves as a navigational landmark within Nebet's ring system. It posseses no resources worth of note and thus it is never expected to be developed or colonized.

591602.text:
DIAMETER: 7,580 km
MASS: 7.41×10^23 kg
TERRAIN: Desert
TEMPERATURE: -55°C to 18°C
ESCAPE VELOCITY: 2.5 km/sec

Distantly orbiting the Gas Giant Nebet, Tingar could be considered a planet in itself were it to have its own orbit around the Mu star. Containing deposits of various metals underground, it has sparked interest of The Order in establishing automatic mining rigs for extraction. Rumored to posess thicker atmosphere in the past, however it appears to have been shed early in Omicron Mu's stellar history, leaving behind only a thin atmosphere of carbon and non-reactive gases.

591606.text:
DIAMETER: 29,723
MASS: 8.90 x10e25 kg
TERRAIN: N/A
TEMPERATURE: N/A
ESCAPE VELOCITY: 19.27 km/sec

Planet Braillia is a beautiful gas giant orbiting closely around Cayman's central star. Formed billions of years ago from the remnants of a massive protostellar disk, Braillia coalesced as gravity drew in abundant hydrogen and helium, which dominate its composition. Trace amounts of methane, ammonia, and exotic organic compounds lend the planet its deep crimson tones.

Swirling storms and dynamic cloud bands decorate its upper atmosphere, hinting at powerful winds and turbulent weather patterns below. Despite its beauty, Braillia's intense gravity and hostile environment make it an awe-inspiring but unreachable marvel in the starry expanse.

591608.text:
DIAMETER: 3,216 km
MASS: 3.89 x 10e23 kg
TERRAIN: Rock
TEMPERATURE: 125°C to 443°C
ESCAPE VELOCITY: 13.42 km/sec

Bactun, the volcanic moon of Braillia, is a rocky satellite marked by a landscape of towering peaks, vast lava plains, and active calderas. Formed from the debris captured by Braillia’s immense gravity, Bactun's proximity to the gas giant subjects it to strong tidal forces, which drive its intense volcanic activity. The surface is riddled with glowing rivers of molten rock and plumes of sulfuric gases venting into the thin, tenuous atmosphere. This dynamic geology makes Bactun a captivating sight, with its fiery surface contrasting starkly against the crimson backdrop of Braillia. It stands as a testament to the power of gravitational interplay in shaping celestial bodies.

591610.text:
DIAMETER: 30,216 km
MASS: 9.89 x 10e26 kg
TERRAIN: N/A
TEMPERATURE: N/A
ESCAPE VELOCITY: 15.42 km/sec

Planet Fuere is a massive gas giant orbiting the outer reaches of Cayman's central star. Its turbulent atmosphere experiences frequent contractions of hot gases, resulting in colossal electrostatic discharges in the planet's lower layers. Chemical reactions occurring near the core produce unique compounds, some of which gradually drift upward to the upper atmosphere, adding to the planet's complex and dynamic weather systems.

591612.text: A serene and visually striking cloud, this nebula stretches across the outer reaches of the Cayman system. Unlike its more turbulent twin, this nebula lacks valuable resources but offers a far safer and less hostile environment for those navigating through the cloud.

591614.text:
>>>WARNING: NAVIGATIONAL HAZARD<<<
The Fuego Nebula is a magnificent red cloud stretching across the distant reaches of the Cayman system. Composed primarily of elemental hydrogen with trace amounts of heavier gases, the nebula is gradually collapsing under its own gravitational pull. As its density increases, the nebula has started to heat up, hinting at the early stages of stellar formation. In several million years, it may give rise to a new star, adding a brilliant chapter to the story of Sirius.

591616.text:
CLASS: Schuppen
GRAVITY: Partial
DOCKING: Yes
AMENITIES: Limited
CREW: 290
591616.mapped:
For centuries, the Stuttgart Growers Association (WVS) successfully lobbied for rich agricultural subsidies from the Rheinland government. During the 80-Years War, the Rheinland government secretly borrowed huge sums from Liberty and by the war’s end in 685 AS, was on the brink of bankruptcy. The subsidies were cut almost overnight. In exchange for debt relief, Rheinland sold Synth Foods complete access to Stuttgart. Immediately the corporate giant moved in, buying out huge numbers of nearly bankrupt Stuttgart farmers. Much of Stuttgart was rapidly converted into vast expanses of Synth Foods’ bio-engineered mono-crops. Over the following century, Synth expanded their grip on Stuttgart by unethically coercing independent farmers into selling their land, or forcing them into punishing and restrictive supply contracts. The once proud Stuttgart farmers were reduced to indentured servants.

The WVS tried to fight back legally in the courts but soon discovered that their influence had been sold to a higher bidder. In 772 AS, the VWS was struck a fatal blow when Synth accused them of facilitating arson attacks against their properties. The WVS board was removed by the Rheinland government, and replaced with Synth corporate stooges. In an act of desperation, radical elements of the WVS left and founded the Landwirtrechtbewegung (LWB) farmers rights movement. They built a small depot called Darmstadt within the Ostnebel and began attacking Synth transports, expanding across Rheinland over the following decades. Despite this, the LWB had little appreciable impact on Synth’s operations. By 825 AS, Synth controlled almost 90% of Stuttgart’s agriculture, up from 60% five decades earlier. The LWB’s decline began with the opening of Supply Station Neckar.

Intending a once in a generation show of force, the movement planned to destroy the station during its opening ceremony. Anticipating an attack, Synth had hired a large force of Bounty Hunters to stage an ambush, shattering the attack and killing or capturing many commanders. Interrogations led to a crackdown across Stuttgart -- sympathizers who funded the LWB were rounded up by the Battleship Karlsruhe’s Marines. On Darmstadt, internal conflict exploded as factions clashed over who should now assume leadership. Between infighting, broken morale and crippled finances, the movement collapsed by the year’s end -- by the end, Darmstadt was left a burnt out wreck. The survivors scattered, with some returning to Planet Stuttgart, others resorting to independent piracy, or joining the Bundschuh and Unioners.

Many later flocked to the Imperial cause during the Civil War, serving in the rebel militias of Stuttgart. Despite hopes the new Empire would expel Synth entirely, little practically changed. By the time of the Holstein Accords, Synth remained entrenched, and the previously useful Stuttgart rebels were discarded as inconvenient. Furious at this betrayal, a new generation of radicals trained during the Civil War began to reach out for support to reform the LWB. They found willing patrons in Kusari’s Farmer’s Alliance, who quickly offered funding and resources to establish an Alliance presence in Rheinland. This partnership was initially celebrated, however LWB fighters quickly became resentful of the exploitative relationship imposed by their Kusari commanders. By late 834 AS the relationship had collapsed, and FA officers expelled from LWB stations. The movement now faces a difficult but truly independent future.

CREW: Unknown
ARMAMENT: Unknown
591619.mapped:
The Praia started life as an experiment by the Zoners of Bethlehem, where it served as a mobile mining platform in the Hydrogen fields of Pennsylvania. Fielding a fleet of mining ships, it served as a drop off and collection point for the extracted gas. After Bering quietly fell to pirates and other opportunists, the Zoners were driven off Freeport 2 and Bethlehem experienced an influx of refugees seeking to rebuild their lives on the nearest Zoner station to their former home.

After having lived for so long without the oversight of house law, the newly arrived inhabitants of Bethlehem soon began to chafe under the restrictions of Liberty law. When a mining ship collided with the Praia, forcing it to return to Bethlehem for repairs, a sect of radical Freeport 2 Zoners entered negotiations with the owners to purchase the carrier.

The negotiations finally resulted in the full purchase of the Praia for the Zoners who wished to reclaim Freeport 2. Mining ships and transports were replaced with fighters and other ships designed for combat. Setting off for the edges of the Tanner field in Bering, the Praia, once a platform of business, now carried the Militant Zoners who sought to reclaim their former home.

News of Gran Canaria's fall to the Bretonians eventually reached those in Bering and a decision by those in command of Praia was made that the carrier should abandon the stalemate of Bering and head for the distant Omega-49 system so that it could assist the Zoners fighting to liberate their home planet from Bretonian rule. The carrier survived the dangerous journey through Rheinland and the Omegas, spending several years hidden in the Barrier Nebula to assist the Gran Canarian Resistance against the Bretonian authorities.

Following the withdrawal of Bretonia from Omega-49, the Praia's Militants continued their mantra of helping Zoners resist tyranny across Sirius. To this end, the Praia made for Alberta, to help the stranded Zoners of Freeport 14 relocate to Inverness. Following this, it briefly saw service alongside the Carrier Pinnacle during the annexation of Pennsylvania, however severe damaged inflicted by the Liberty Navy forced the Militants to withdraw back to Inverness to regroup.

The Liner Verwood conducted itself through much of the Gallic War as an unofficial asset of the Bretonian Crown in the Taus. Far from Bretonia's supply lines, the liner was operated by Privateers who were primarily engaged in piracy against Gallic civilians, supply line sabotage, and cargo interdiction against hostile and neutral interests in the region. These activities led to a significant redeployment of Gallic forces to convoy protection, easing pressure on the front lines. Some Bretonian military officials have argued that this vindicated their highly controversial strategic doctrine of commerce raiding.

While nominally operating under Bretonian Letters of Marque, the Privateers tended to act without oversight and on the basis of their own personal views of Bretonian interests. This resulted in a tumultuous relationship with Bretonian officials, with arrest warrants eventually issued against a number of Privateers who more flagrantly crossed the line for personal gain. This frequently involved attacking Kusari or Rheinland shipping they suspected of trading with Gallia. After the war, the legal status of the Privateers and their Letters of Marque were called into question. It was quickly realized that failing to find the 'irregulars' gainful employment elsewhere would lead to an influx of veteran pirates at a time when the House desperately needed stability to recover.

Officials ultimately insinuated to privateer commanders that there would be fertile grounds for their work in the Omegas, managing Rheinland corporations that were steadily encroaching on Bretonian interests. Following the revocation of all Letters of Marque by the Bretonian Crown in 827 AS, the Privateers dissolved, with many fleeing into the open arms of pirate gangs operating in the Omegas. The commanding staff of the Verwood chose loyalty to their homeland, patriotism that cost them dearly. The returners were imprisoned and the Verwood transferred to the BIS, where it now serves as a surveillance and security checkpoint for the Bretonian Archaeological Executive.

591623.text:
The Liner Verwood conducted itself through much of the Gallic War as an unofficial asset of the Bretonian Crown in the Taus. Far from Bretonia's supply lines, the liner was operated by Privateers who were primarily engaged in piracy against Gallic civilians, supply line sabotage, and cargo interdiction against hostile and neutral interests in the region. These activities led to a significant redeployment of Gallic forces to convoy protection, easing pressure on the front lines. Some Bretonian military officials have argued that this vindicated their highly controversial strategic doctrine of commerce raiding.

While nominally operating under Bretonian Letters of Marque, the Privateers tended to act without oversight and on the basis of their own personal views of Bretonian interests. This resulted in a tumultuous relationship with Bretonian officials, with arrest warrants eventually issued against a number of Privateers who more flagrantly crossed the line for personal gain. This frequently involved attacking Kusari or Rheinland shipping they suspected of trading with Gallia. After the war, the legal status of the Privateers and their Letters of Marque were called into question. It was quickly realized that failing to find the 'irregulars' gainful employment elsewhere would lead to an influx of veteran pirates at a time when the House desperately needed stability to recover.

591633.text:
The Acasta was a Crecy-class destroyer in long service of the Norfolk Fleet and saw some minor action in the Nomad War. However, its glory, but also its undoing, would come in 826, at the battle of Aland. Finding themselves significantly outnumbered, outmatched and outwitted, the IMG garrison realized that something had gone wrong with the explosives set to scuttle Aland should it fall into enemy hands and decided to fire at their own station.

The pillar of their hopes to scuttle Aland from the outside was the GPV Andaman, a Sagarmatha-class battle-cruiser. The ship's armor was very durable and it seemed like it would succeed despite being under focused enemy fire, until the Acasta unexpectedly assumed position between Aland and the Andaman, which it managed to keep thanks to the ship's superior agility and speed. Nevertheless, it was obvious to everyone that the Acasta, a much smaller vessel, was not built to take continuous direct fire from a battlecruiser, and it suffered a catastrophic decompression only seconds before the Andaman, too, stopped firing.

All crew was lost. Under normal circumstances such a ship would be preserved as a monument, but due to Bretonia's desperate situation in the war with Gallia the Acasta is scheduled to be recycled for materials.

591635.text:
The Andaman was a Sagarmatha-class battlecruiser constructed by Singapore Shipyard in 824 AS, two months after the Gallic Royal Navy had abandoned Tau-44. When it was laid down, the intention was that it would remain close to Singapore and protects it in case of a possible Gallic or Outcast attack, but after the recapture of Tau-44 by the IMG's allies from the Crayter Republic and the Council, the Andaman was repurposed into an exploration vessel.

In 826 AS, after the scuttling of Southampton Shipyard, the Kingdom of Bretonia demanded to nationalize Aland Shipyard from the IMG. Aland was the most important IMG station in the region and, since the Guild perceived Bretonia as weak enough, the demand was rejected. All available assets were called to defend the shipyard. The Andaman, which was on an exploration mission in the Omegas at the time, answered the call. The Guild's assumptions proved to be wrong when the mustered garrison of Aland, without the expected support from the RHB Kassel, found itself significantly outmatched and outmaneuvered by the Norfolk Fleet.

As there was no real possibility of victory and the explosives set all over Aland to prevent it from falling into enemy hands were taking too long to detonate, the captain of the Andaman redirected fire from the enemy ships to the Guild's own station. The battlecruiser would have probably succeeded in its intentions was there not the HMS Acasta, which sacrificed itself by blocking the fire with its own hull. The Andaman did not go down violently when it was disabled by focused enemy fire, but simply stopped functioning. Most of the crew survived and was taken prisoner. As the internal systems were devastated beyond recognition, the outer shell is now scheduled for recycling.

591645.mapped:
Having seen early success in its audacious expansion into the Omicrons, the Core set its sights on the deep Omegas in 823 AS. Following rumors of treasure-hordes of Artifacts and other alien secrets, executives quickly authorized the deployment of a permanent station in orbit of Planet Skagen. Commissioning Kruger for the construction of prefabricated modules, the components were shipped into the system under the watchful guns of the Battleship Mars. While this process was immensely expensive and the convoys frequently attacked, the Core remained confident they would quickly recoup their costs, launching mining expeditions across Skagen.

These expeditions soon began to earn dividends after Daam-K'vosh ruins were discovered that contained rich caches of Artifacts. While many of these objects are exported to the Houses for sale, the most interesting finds are held aboard for study. Work to convert this study into monetizable products resulted in the development of APM Hardware, which is primarily produced aboard. Dagger's success prompted the MND strike an understanding with the Core, with Rheinland agreeing to partially underwrite the operation in 829 AS. In exchange, they negotiated preferential access Dagger's results, and staging rights for MND operatives working in the region. This prompted a sharp escalation in attacks by the Coalition, until the destruction of Kamchatka Base later the following year.

With the loss of the Battleship Mars and the fall of Omicron Zeta in 835 AS, much of Dagger's garrison was redeployed to Omicron Delta to reinforce Durban Station against a feared Nomad onslaught. To patch the holes left in local security, the Skagen Agreement was signed with the Bounty Hunter's Guild, who were paid richly to take on much of the system's patrols. Since then, Dagger Outpost has come under intense attack by both Artificial Intelligence and Wild vessels who see an opportunity to wrest control of Skagen and its prizes.

Durban Station is the headquarters of the Core orbiting the gas giant Tuvalu. Outfitted with specially modified military-grade scanners and radars, Durban acts as high precision listening post and early detection system aimed at detecting alien activity in the surrounding space.

Whilst being a residential mega-complex, it also contains a multitude of different research laboratories - ranging from xeno-agricultural to weapon testing - ran by AP Manufacturing personnel. The vast majority of research conducted on Durban involves alien artifacts and technology and aims to secure the Core a technological advantage against their foes.

Freital Base is a key logistics and secondary combat hub of the Red Hessians. Patrols from Freital launch raids on Rheinland corporate mining operations across the Omegas, with a particular focus on Daumann Diamond extraction. Stolen Diamonds are then used to supplement the depleted stocks of Dresden and sold on the black market to fund the movement. Freital is also vital to blocking Corsair advances into Stuttgart and protecting the supply lines from Dresden to Omega-5. Hessian pilots serving on the brutal Ronneburg front line are often rotated back to Freital to rest, while still being close enough to respond to Corsair breakthroughs as a strategic reserve.

In 822 AS, the Hessians were forced to abandon Freital after the system’s red giant entered a period of extreme activity, producing devastating solar flares that destroyed ships and destabilized local Jump Holes. While some speculated that this may have been a prelude to the dying star’s collapse, the activity subsided to relatively “safe” levels over the next three years. During that period, the Hessian supply lines to Omega-5 were stretched to breaking point, as longer and more dangerous routes from Dresden were required. Ronneburg nearly fell at several points before Freital was restored in late 825 AS.

Since 833 AS, the base has been forced to cut the number of reinforcements supplied to Omega-5 due to the Corsair attack on Dresden. In recent months, Vogtland has turned the tide in that battle, freeing Freital’s squadrons to support the Battleship Zuschen’s daring counter-attack on the Corsair flank in Omega-41.

591663.text: Odenwald is a large asteroid field on the edge of the Omega-54 system. This field is one of the primary sources of metals for the Red Hessians, with several commandeered Daumann asteroid miners toiling away inside of it to provide a constant influx of resources used to build new ships. Several mined out areas in the Odenwald have been reappropriated for hazardous training fields for fighter pilots.

591665.mapped:
Wolfsburg Shipyard is the facility responsible for Red Hessian vessel design and construction. With the escalation of the Hessian-Corsair conflict in the middle of the 8th century, demand for heavier and larger vessels began to rise. The improvised dry dock at Vogtland was hard pressed by the ever increasing need for more starships -- a dedicated shipyard facility was required to continue the Hessians' expansion into the Omega systems.

Wolfsburg's first components were completed in 775 AS. Since then shipyard has been responsible for constructing all of the Hessian capital ships fighting in the Omega border worlds. Its engineering crews are constantly working on new or improved designs to further the fighting ability of Hessians across all their battle lines. The pinnacle of this work came with the completion of the Battleship Kassel in 820 AS, the Hessians' first "Jormungand" class battleship.

Due to the losses suffered during the Rheinland Military's attack of 832 AS, Wolfsburg's crew is now working overtime to replenish the defensive garrison with whatever shipbuilding materials they can get their hands on. The devastation wrought on Hessian mining and refining infrastructure in Dresden means the shipyard is now more reliant than ever on imported goods from Bundschuh and Junker smugglers.

591667.mapped:
In 796 AS, Omega-55 received its first visitors since the disappearance of the Daam-K’vosh -- the Nomad-controlled explorers of Chancellor Niemann's Rheinland. This discovery was no accident, as the Nomads possessed ancient star charts of their once-masters' domain. One such chart marked Omega-55 as an important site. Secretly establishing an outpost in orbit of Planet Skagen, Rheinland diverted countless millions of embezzled credits into the Nomads' expeditions. By late 799 AS, two Daam-K'vosh Power Cells were discovered deep under Skagen's surface. The terrifyingly powerful Artifacts had been sealed in stasis chambers, and were capable of generating vast outputs of power by directly converting mass to energy.

One of these Cells was successfully extracted and then evacuated to the murky tunnels of Planet Weimar. The second immediately destabilized when moved, catastrophically exploding in low orbit. The orbiting station was destroyed, with the debris falling into a ring around the newly scarred planet. Soon after, the Nomad War came to its inglorious end when the Hypergate network was reactivated, draining Sirius' latent Daam-K'vosh power field and shattering the Nomad Mindshare. It is unclear what happened in the chaos that followed this traumatic severing -- even to the Wild themselves. By the time the Nomad-infested remnants of the Rheinland Nothern Fleet began raiding Omega-55 in 811 AS, the system was a desolate ruin.

As the Wild's first staging post outside Omega-58, Basel Rock was excavated the following year. Initially the Wild abducted stray explorers venturing out from Bornholm, sending them down to Skagen's surface to pick through the wreckage of the blast crater. In 818 AS, any hope of capturing the system was ended by the Omega-58 Cataclysm that sealed away or destroyed much of the Wild's local strength. After that, Basel hosted Wild raiders who abducted unsuspecting traffic to recruit as unwilling infiltrators and thralls. This changed with the unsealing of Omega-58 in 834 AS, as a flood of freed Wild poured into the region. Deadly Wild assaults are now felt across the system, with a focus on dislodging The Core at Dagger Outpost.

591670.text:
The Heppenheim was constructed at Wolfsburg Shipyard in 830 AS, and tasked with patrolling the eastern half of the system to repel Military and Corsair incursions. Two years later, the Hessians were thrown into disarray when the news was leaked that the Rheinland Military would soon launch a full-scale invasion of Dresden. The Heppenheim was immediately pulled back to Vogtland as defensive brigades were organized, using forces stripped from Freital and other system garrisons. The Vidar was one of several attached as escort cruisers to the Battleship Kassel.

When the Strausberg finally launched its attack, the Kassel fleet was forced to prioritize responding to a daring attack on the Giftnebel by the 4th Strike Flotilla. By the time this threat had been repelled, the Military was already battering down the gates at Leipzig. When the Kassel later succeeded in executing an improvised ambush on the Strausberg’s column, the Heppenheim engaged its counterpart cruisers, buying time for the Kassel to work. While executing a tight evasive turn, the cruiser’s aft engine array was struck by a torpedo, locking it into a death spiral. As a result, it slammed into an asteroid at high speed, killing all aboard.

591672.text: Leader of the Schalke squadron, Captain Graf, is a former Kruger escort pilot who took part in the attack on Bautzen. He led his squadron in a hopeless battle against the Military assault on the Leipzig station. Their main accomplishment before being overwhelmed by the enemy was keeping enemy bombers from disabling the bases' turrets with precision strikes.

591674.text: Member of the Schalke squadron, composed entirely of fresh recruits. The pilots desperately fought to defend Leipzig, but their sacrifice allowed the Kassel to ambush the Strausberg and its escorts.

591676.text: Schalke squadron was stationed aboard Leipzig on an off chance Military would actually perform an attack in Dresden System. Neither they nor Leipzig itself was, however, ready for a full-blown battleship led assault a mere week after the news broke.

Kaarst Drydock is an eldritch blend of human and Nomad technologies, and the heart of the Wild presence in Omega-58. Little is known about the facility for sure, however MND scouting reports indicate the drydock was constructed around 804 AS. Until the collapse of the system’s Jump Holes in 818 AS, Wild patrols roamed surrounding systems, hijacking ships and abducting pilots. Dark rumors whisper that these unfortunate captives were dragged back to Kaarst and subjected to horrific experiments on the hybridization of human and Nomad technologies. This resulted in the emergence of the deadly Scorpion drone, and many other abominations. When the system became accessible again in 834 AS, The Order were alarmed to discover that Kaarst had been entirely unaffected by the stellar cataclysm 16 years earlier.
591683.mapped:
The Drydock was excavated into an enormous asteroid as the Nomads reeled from the collapse of their Mindshare, and defeats in Thuringia at the hands of The Order and MND. Facing imminent starvation due to the depleted Daam-K’vosh power grid, Kaarst hosted the Wild’s desperate research into the surviving Alien Power Cell that had been retrieved from Omega-55. Upon unlocking the Cell’s secret of mass to energy conversion, they interfaced with Omega-58’s dormant Jump Gates to trickle enough power back into the grid to sustain themselves. The Wild were forced to repeatedly strip away the Cell’s safety controls and boost the rate of mass conversion to counteract other isolated Nomad Mindshare fragments siphoning the energy away.

The Wild later planned to use the Cell to reactivate an Alien Jump Gate, creating a bridge to the Nomad home systems. This ended in disaster when the fatally overstressed cell triggered a run-away conversion effect in 818 AS. A singularity began tearing the system apart, while the star collapsed into the P58 Pulsar. The surviving Wild were forced into hibernation on Kaarst until solar conditions settled, at which point they cannibalized surviving ships and stations to create the pulsar harvesting arrays that powered the facility through the long isolation. With this isolation now lifted, slumbering Infiltrators have awoken and Kaarst’s foul machinery has ground back to life. A dark tide of Wild ships now pour into the unsuspecting Omegas and Rheinland.

The Battleship Fenrir was constructed in 797 AS and formed the cornerstone of Rheinland’s Northern Fleet. Infamously, the ship would lead Rheinland’s invasion of Kusari alongside the Battleship Jormungand during the Colony Wars, culminating in the destruction of the KNF in New Tokyo. The Northern Fleet would abruptly withdraw following the disappearance of Chancellor Niemann, and vanish into the Sigmas. The entire fleet is officially recorded as having deserted after refusing to acknowledge the orders of the emergency Rheinland Provisional Government.
591686.mapped:
When The Order activated the Hypergate in Omicron-Major, it drained the Daam-K’vosh energy field that sustained the Nomads. The Nomad Mindshare immediately collapsed, plunging the surviving entities into disarray. The Thralls of the Northern Fleet withdrew to Thuringia to regroup, but in 802 AS, found themselves under attack by The Order and newly formed MND. The Fenrir was used to evacuate a recently retrieved Daam K’Vosh Power Cell from Planet Weimar to Bottrop Depot in Omega-58. Its infected crew were then placed in hibernation to ration energy for fighter combat forces in Thuringia.

In 818 AS, the Fenrir would receive deadly hybrid weaponry at Kaarst Drydock ahead of the planned activation of the Alien Jump Gate. When the Jump Gate prematurely activated, it created a runaway singularity that collapsed the system’s star. While the Fenrir was preserved due to its proximity to the Kaarst Object, the majority of the Northern Fleet was obliterated as it mustered for an anticipated invasion of Rheinland. When Omega-58’s Jump Holes realigned in 834 AS, the Fenrir deployed back to Thuringia. It quickly overwhelmed Meningen Research Station and has since taken up position in the depths of the treacherous Suhl Anomaly.

591691.text:
>>>CAUTION<<<
An accumulation of molten rock, liquidized by Omega-55's twin stars and especially violent asteroid collisions. The Kattegat field itself is a veritable treasure trove of all manner of minerals, metals and radioactive isotopes; historically, attempts to exploit these resources have been deterred by fierce Coalition attacks, the remote location, and the dangerous conditions. From a distance, the scattered light from the roiling volatility is starkly beautiful.

591693.text:
Battleship Canaan was commissioned by the Order in the year 819 AS in the aftermath of the destruction of Toledo. Unfinished at the time, parts of critically damaged warships that had been crippled in battle were incorporated into its chassis to rush its construction. .

Five years later, with the need for the Order to move on, Canaan was sent on a reconnaissance mission into Omicron Zeta. Shortly after its arrival, the Canaan picked up a distress signal from Battleship Mars as it was engaged by several large Nomad lifeforms. Although the Mars was holding its own, it was slowly being overpowered by Nomad reinforcements. After analysing the situation, the Canaan brokered a temporary ceasefire with The Core, and assisted the Mars in successfully pushing back the Nomads – both taking heavy damage in the process.

After the Nomads had been beaten, there was a momentary pause as the battlefield stood silent. With the fighting over, the Battleship Canaan began to charge its engines and chart a return course to Cario Station. But suddenly and without warning, the Battleship Mars opened fire on the Canaan. In a last-ditch effort, the Canaan tried to return fire, but was unable to take down the Mars with it as it was destroyed.

591703.text: A BMM base. Bretonia Mining and Manufacturing (BMM) is one of the largest commercial concerns in Bretonia, a network of semi-autonomous operations that range throughout Bretonian space.

591706.text: A Zoner base. The Zoners are a diverse group of individuals who, for various reasons, have decided to live in the wild and unregulated systems outside of House control. Over time, the various Zoner communities have evolved to adapt to the unique geopolitical situations present around the various Freeports. While many Zoners simply enjoy the freedom away from stifling House laws, others have invested in private deep space exploration ventures, either for the adventure or to further an interest in deregulated scientific discovery.

CLASS: Mponeng
GRAVITY: Complete
DOCKING: Yes
AMENITIES: Yes
CREW: 360
591708.mapped:
Madeira Base is the second serious attempt of the Independent Miners Guild to establish a foothold in the deeper Omegas, after historic failures in Omega-41. Established in 826 AS, Madeira's existence still remains tenuous due to the remote and hazardous nature of Omega-47, and the deadly supply route through Omega-5. Despite this, the Guild has successfully scratched out a living mining the El Aaiun Field's untapped resources, primarily by bartering goods for protection with the Red Hessians and Coalition. This has -- for now -- kept the Corsairs at bay.

The Guild envisions Madeira as the first step of a pivot away from the political volatility of the Houses, toward servicing the lawless customers of the untamed frontier. So far this has largely been limited to smuggling smelted metals to the Zoner shipwrights of Omega-49. Owing to the perpetual warfare of Omega-5 and the intensifying conflict in Omega-47 itself, this is considered to be the single most dangerous contract available to Guild crews. This strategy has also proved controversial within the Guild, as it distances traditional allies such as ALG and Gateway who are unwilling to provide support in such deadly regions.

Despite the risks, Guildmasters have continued to authorize expansions of Madeira, notably including a small drydock to repair arriving transports and their defense garrison. Madeira is also the launching point for IMG surveyors in the region -- these are primarily concerned with trying to locate Silver deposits that are alleged to exist in the El Aaiun field. As of 835 AS, a feverish excitement has seized the station amid rumors of a pioneer team's discovery of a nearby Jump Hole to a new, unexplored sector of the Omegas.

591713.text: A small wisp of the Walker Nebula in the southeast of the Omega-11 system. Particularly brave IMG pilots occasionally prospect this cloud for Diamonds, as the intense Hessian presence has driven away the Daumann patrols that would normally evict them.

591716.text:
Jakarta is an expansion to Singapore Shipyard, built in 816 AS as a habitat for Guild families. It grew to be a popular trading station in the Taus, as well as where the Board of Guildmasters convenes. Due to its secluded location in the nebula and the neutrality of the IMG, it remains untouched by Gallic occupation.

The Pennitry is currently tasked with safeguarding Singapore Shipyard and the Jakarta Colony, always being on standby for intruders. Originally built as an expedition vessel, the Pennitry prepared travel to an uncharted system by conventional engines. With its particular equipment, the sensors detect every movement in the thick Sumatra, and so ongoing and outgoing traffic is vigilantly monitored.

591718.text: Originally built for deep space exploration, the Pennitry traveled around unexplored systems in search of new stakes for the IMG to claim. The operation "Orange Hammer" in Tau-44 by the Outcasts forced the Guild to return the Pennitry as guard ship to its place of origin; Singapore Shipyard. While not as heavily armed as other Cruisers, its complex sensor arrays grant Singapore and Jakarta Annex a significant advance warning in case of hostile forces approaching from inside the Sumatra Cloud.

591720.text: The wreck of the Jamaica, Junker ship carrying a cargo of synthetic marijuana. Apparently, rogues in Humboldt prefer cardamine.

591722.text:
The Rogues of Fortaleza was fairly confident in the fact that Delaware's attack group would fail to find them. This overconfidence naturally served as an insidious means for that very thing to occur.

A supply convoy bound for the base was interdicted by a rather proactive element of Delaware's retinue, one ship was ensnared and prevented from escaping, while the other only narrowly managed. Evidently, the base's location has been compromised as a result, with the crew of the captured vessel either being tortured for information or its location simply downloaded from the onboard computer, while the Rogues themselves were given a long walk out of a short airlock.

Neither conclusion is particularly relevant, as the sight of an incoming siege cruiser prompted the local Rogues to bolt for greener pastures or whatever spatial equivalent they could find.

591726.mapped:
Bounty Hunters are nothing if not an innovative and adaptable people. While Kusari's glut of clashing rogue ideologies and proximity to the contested Sigma systems would make it highly appealing to the Trans-Sirian Guild; the Kusari leadership - Imperial or Republican - has flatly refused the involvement of these mercenaries.

When the GMG converged most of their Sigma-59 operations into Niigata, they left behind remnants and derelicts. Sensing an opportunity and acting rapidly, the BHG was granted clearance to operate in the immediate, neighboring territory, and a void was filled in the Hunters' ports of call since the destruction of Freeport 7.

This place also serves as a vibrant cantina for grizzled hunters, adventurous GMG employees, and hard-drinking Freelancers. While the Core attempted to negotiate with the station administrators to expand upon the size and capabilities of the chassis, a stationwide referendum returned overwhelmingly negative to the notion. These representatives have stubbornly remained, along with a garrison and an entire deck legally owned by the paramilitary.

591729.mapped:
Niigata is a gargantuan space colony established in the otherwise-remote Sigma-59 system. With the influx of inmates and colonists actually outpacing the number of jobs on the surface of Miura, the GMG unveiled an equally ambitious project. Pushing the limits of structural integrity and with enthusiastic investment from Interspace Commerce, GMG unveiled the first "Star City" constructed within Sirius by appending the original GMG-owned stations of Sigma-59 onto Niigata's chassis, forming one titanic construct.

Niigata's internal bustle belies the frontier nature of Sigma-59. While transports and Guild patrols are common around the immediate fortresslike periphery of the City and the nearby jump hole, the station has a population easily capable of self-sufficiency. Advanced hydroponic technology and frequent imports from Synth Foods ensure that the vast majority of the over six-thousand people aboard Niigata are fed and thus able to contribute to the full-blown metropolitan economy aboard, whose goal by a year's time is to become a net exporter.

While the corporate sectors of Sirius have either applauded or looked enviously on at the GMG's overall success with this audacious project, the lower reaches of the maintenance decks are rumored to already be an impoverished nightmare. Station security is rumored not to enter certain decks without heavy arms and numbers, causing some aboard to worry for the station's integrity. GMG continues to assure the sector that its investment is safe, claiming that the sheer number of failsafes and redundant life support systems mean that a serious threat from within is unlikely.

A vast nebula of carbonaceous and rock asteroids combined with a hodgepodge of Hydrogen-based Crow gases and dust from the central planetary fragments. Likely of a nominally brown color, the light from the intense Blue Giant at the system's center turns the foreboding cloud purple.

The GMG ascertained that space aboard Niigata could be granted for Hydrocarbon mining or otherwise, pending more thorough exploration. Said exploration has been hampered by a minimum of scanner penetration through the chaotic mixture of dust. Oddly, rumors claim that Samura ships have been sighted within.

591739.mapped:
Daishouri, or "Triumphant Victory," is one of three Rheinland warships commandeered from the Rheinland Military by GMG Paramilitary during the apex of the 80 year war between the two. Thanks to the early brilliance of famed GMG engineer, Dr. Ito Namura, all three battleships were dissected, studied and made operational with GMG developed technology. Daishouri sustained the least amount of damage when commandeered and was thus the easiest to modify and the first battleship deployed to begin its role of guarding Sigma 59.

The other GMG warships were the Ayakashi Maru or "Ghost Ship That Appears After a Shipwreck" and Namura (named after the same famous engineer that lost his life reviving the ship, Dr. Namura). After a later loss of the Namura, the GMG decommissioned the remaining warships and hid them deep in Sigma 59. In recent years, with the system fully developed, GMG once again had the two battleships augmented with modern technology and they were redeployed. Daishouri resumes its guardianship of Sigma-59 from its southern flank, while the Ayakashi Maru slipped off into deep space.

A field of planetary debris dragged into close orbit of the intense blue giant at the system's heart. Scientific surveys based from Niigata determined that the rocks were once a moon of the gas giant Nagaoka that was wrenched from its orbit by the star's gravity well, and destroyed by the incredible heat.

Intense solar radiation at a distance so near the star poses a tremendous risk to the ships of any curious sightseers, and the GMG has cautioned any tourists from Niigata from drawing too close.

591749.mapped:
The Havana is one of the first Storta-class destroyers to leave the dry docks at Corsica Shipyard, and for that reason, it has one of the richest and most decorated careers. The Havana has ended the existence of numerous Gallic, Crayterian, and Corsair ships, both as an escort vessel for the Basilica and in the role of a successful, solitary raider.

Everything, however, must come to an end. The fact that it is a first-generation Storta-class ship eventually led to its obsolescence, and so after the successful siege of Atka Station, it was decided to transfer and reassign it to a secondary role. The Havana passed into the ownership of the new yet dynamic and influential De Angelis Cartel, which currently uses the ship to extract information from important prisoners and to re-educate several, especially unruly Outcasts.

Although the conditions aboard this relatively small mobile prison seem to be more than above average compared to the Colonies, Outcast prisoners mostly carry away mental scars due to prolonged denial of Cardamine. As for the fate of captured high profile Bounty Hunters, Independent Miners, or Crayter pilots -- it's hard to imagine, because although none of them have ever left Havana alive, they all eventually talked truth.

591769.text:
CLASS: Komainu (experimental)
CREW: CLASSIFIED
ARMAMENT: CLASSIFIED
591769.mapped:
The Akatsuki was launched in 821 AS as one of the first Komainu battlecruisers, and assigned to the Nagumo fleet. Stationed in Kyushu and responsible for joint patrols with Tau-29's Gallic garrison, the Akatsuki witnessed the system's invasion by Kusari Exile forces in 822 AS. The battlecruiser quickly joined the rebel fleet and aided the Battleship Nagasaki in destroying the Gallic occupation force. Through the Kusari Civil War, the vessel fought in several battles across Kyushu in the name of Tetsuya Kogen, the son of the recently deceased Emperor-in-Exile. The Akatsuki participated in the siege and capture of Nansei Research Complex, shortly before the war's end in a negotiated peace.

Following the war, the Akatsuki's command was transferred to the Kusari Office of Intelligence, then deployed to Orkney, Tau-23 and Tau-31. Here it monitored the collapse of the Gallic Kingdom and the emergence of the Gallic Confederation. The intelligence gathered by the Akatsuki's pilots informed Kusari's strategic planning for the Invasion of Gallia in 827 AS. The battlecruiser was dispatched to raid Languedoc early in the war, striking Gallic logistics and rear echelon units while the main fleet battered through Gallic defenses and breached the Tau-23 Jump Gate. Through the conflict, the taskforce was renown for its daring strikes against critical infrastructure and high value targets.

Following the war, the Akatsuki and its flight wings were formally recognised as special forces, and the vessel recalled to Ichigaya for refitting with advanced cloaking devices. Since then, the vessel has been involved in multiple covert operations across Kusari and the Sigmas. This includes ambushes on priority Blood Dragon targets using bait transports, and the assassination of a travelling Outcast Don. In 835 AS, the Akatsuki was recalled to Tohoku for further modifications, and was temporarily tasked with stabilizing experiments involving the R7 Drive Breach.

In 836 AS, the Akatsuki was assigned to lead a taskforce during Operation Ichi-Go, Kusari's first strike blitz against the Republic of Liberty. The KOI detatchment utilized the battlecruiser's Jump Drive to infiltrate Pennsylvania, coordinating a strike on Titusville Refinery with the assault on Norfolk Shipyard in New York. Despite its flight wing taking heavy casualties, the Akatsuki succeeded in destroying Titusville and crippling the Battleship Alma. It now lurks in Pennsylvania, where it can sow chaos and distract Kusari by bolstering Erie Militants and other domestic insurrectionists.

ARMAMENT: CLASSIFIED
591772.mapped:
Dating all the way back to the original Sakura Coup, and one of the few Togos reactivated by the Blood Dragons, Kokura spent much of its life hidden in the Crow Nebula, receiving only minimal maintenance over the centuries. Kokura completed its reactivation in 831 A.S. and spent much of the next year and a half guarding Mito Shipyard while the scant few of the ship's sisters that could still be saved completed their own refurbishment and modernisation.

In late 832, however, the great battleship received a new deployment; the Dragons had received word of Battleship Matsuda's destruction, leaving the Kyushu system entirely without any base for either Dragon or Chrysanthemum operations. Enraged though the Dragons were at such a careless loss of such a valuable asset in the Matsuda, they could not allow Kyushu to become ever more heavily blockaded. Over the next few months, Kokura was prepared with all the resources it would need for a permanent deployment to the Seiran dust cloud.

Once it arrived in the system, its contingent of veteran pilots set about patrolling Kyushu and ambushing trade convoys where they could. Much to the Dragons' surprise, Battleship Matsumoto had not been relieved by another warship, and instead stood in-system, still with much of the damage it sustained from its duel with the Matsuda. As a result, flights based from Kokura work to soften the Matsumoto's contingent of fightercraft in an attempt to create an opening to strike the warship and finish what the Matsuda started.

The Blood Dragons have notably abstained from raiding relief vessels bound for the storm-ravaged Planet Kyushu, only targeting vessels whose cargos consist primarily of supplies to rebuild the planet's farming infrastructure and leaving food and medical vessels usually untouched.

A Rheinland Fleet headed towards Kusari was equipped by one Nomad Power Cell that was handed over to them by the Nomads somewhere in Sigma space in 800 AS Miraculously, the Cell survived when scattered forces of a group that would later be known as The Wilde passed through Rheinland and headed towards the distant Omega worlds.

When The Wilde settled in the Omegas, they initiated construction of a Nomad Jump Gate to provide a direct access to their brethren. The Power Cell was necessary to collect silicate matter from nearby planetoids and asteroid fields to complete construction of the massive Gate. However, uncontrolled use of the Cell led to hazardous consequences for the entire Omega-58 system where Gate construction took place.

The Nomad Cell reached full capacity by absorbing massive amounts of matter in the Omega-58 system. The Wilde then tried to activate their completed Nomad Gate, using the Cell as it's power source. While they succeeded, they were unable to control the singularity building inside the gate. Within a matter of minutes, it grew exponentially, eventually encompassing the entire Omega-58 solar system. As the gate triggered, it linked to a second gate in a system halfway across the galaxy, forming a brief but stable system-wide portal. All stellar bodies, except for the Omega-58 sun were instantly drawn into the gate and emerged in the Drake system. The gate itself, as well as the Nomad bases and ships in the vicinity were pulled out of Omega-58 as well.

Without the Gate, the portal immediately destabilized, locking on to the nearest gravity well - the Omega-58 star. The resulting compression caused the star to consume all fusion materials in seconds. As the portal collapsed completely, what remained of the star went supernova, blasting it's outer layers away to form a large, heavily irradiated debris field, shrouded in a dark matter nebula dragged into the system by the unstable portal.

When the portal opened in Drake, the nearby parts of the Barrier Nebula were completely blown away. The only object heavy enough to resist the immense gravitational push was a young star, at the edge of the system.

Depleted once more, the Nomad Power Cell has once again begun a charging cycle, consuming matter in Drake to fuel itself.

591777.text:
CLASS: Sekigahara
CREW: CLASSIFIED
ARMAMENT: CLASSIFIED

According to sensor readings, this Kusari Sekigahara-class warship is equipped with passive cloaking systems, making it difficult to locate on remote sensors and interfering with more detailed scans of the ship and crew. The ship also appears to have its IFF transponder disabled, and all incoming and outgoing communications are highly encrypted. With its turrets ready to strike down any unexpected guest, the ship lies in the depths of the nebula, awaiting its prey.

Consequently, the only reliable identifier of the ship is its name, which the ship still proudly wears on both sides of its bow and stern, IKN Hakodate, alongside its unique hull identification number. It is alleged, by explorers and reporters, to belong to the Kusari Office of Intelligence, and to be protecting Kusari's interests beyond the House's borders, but Kusari government officials have stated that no Sekigahara-class ship was ever assigned to KOI, and have denied all claims of the ship's activities.
591777.mapped:
The IKN Hakodate is a Sekigahara-class battleship that was secretly assigned to the Kusari Intelligence Office during the late years of the Gallic invasion. At the time, the Hakodate served as an equipment testbed for new computer systems and sensors, conducting technology evaluation and personnel training.

The vessel's first combat deployment came during its rearmament and tasking as an escort to the battleship Sado, where the ship assisted with monitoring Order and Blood Dragon activities in Tohoku. During this brief deployment, a flurry of incidents and military engagements occurred in its area of operation, providing opportunities for the Wild to infiltrate the ship's ranks and compromise key personnel.

When war broke out between Kusari and Gallia, the Hakodate was reassigned to the front lines, where the ship earned several combat honors as an aggressive scout against the new and relatively disorganized Gallic Confederacy.

When Kusari withdrew from Gallia, the Hakodate returned to Tohoku, quietly streaming its intelligence transmissions to Wild recipients while its Kusari officers were none the wiser.

More recently, the Hakodate has been deployed deeper into the Omicrons—a mission for which the ship is better suited than nearly any other in the entire House of Kusari. With only infrequent need to report back to Kusari, it now "guards" the home of the Order with purpose: to annihilate the Nomads' nemesis and its puppets.

AMENITIES: Unknown
CREW: Unknown

While no surviving public records identify this depot, it is likely to have been constructed at some point in the 670s. At the height of the 80-Years War between Rheinland and the Gas Miners Guild, H-Fuel supplies across the Colonies were both erratic and expensive. Numerous projects were launched by the other Houses to develop their own domestic alternatives. Bretonia sponsored the Craster Initiative, following supposed discoveries of trace amounts of fuel-rich gasses. Despite more than a decade of fruitless searching, the promised gas deposits were never found. The BMM subsidiary responsible was driven into bankruptcy, leaving abandoned infrastructure scattered across the nebula edge.
591780.mapped:
In 818 AS, the Wild of Omega-58 overloaded an Alien Jump Gate, with catastrophic consequences. The system was ripped apart and dragged through a rift into the distant Drake system. The survivors of this disaster began to explore the surrounding area, discovering Jump Holes into Bretonia and Liberty. When these infiltrators found Stockton Depot, it was adopted as a staging post for raids across Newcastle. While the nearby Alien City was too well protected by entrenched BIS forces, cloaked Wild raiders frequently attacked freighters transporting Scientists and Artifacts to and from the site, and raided corporate transports for materials to repair the damaged Gate with.

In 827 AS, Stockton was transformed from a minor staging ground into the last holdout of the Drake remnants. Having become aware of the Wild’s plans to reactivate the repaired Alien Jump Gate, The Order and Crayter Republic launched an invasion of the system. In desperation, the Wild overloaded the Alien Gate once more, triggering a second cataclysm. Bottrop Station was immediately destroyed, while the Battleship Embrun and many Wild patrols were dragged away to Alberta. Cut off after Drake's Jump Holes collapsed, the remaining Wild of Stockton have been forced to return to more covert methods, in particular targeting the system’s Gaians, Mollys and corporate vessels for subversion.

591795.text: A large belt of asteroids attracted to the Nomad Gate from the outer reaches of the Drake system. The gravitational impact of the Gate is estimated to reach 0,5 light years from its location in every direction.

591797.text: Asteroid belt comprised of rocky asteroids and planetary fragments dragged into the Nomad Gate anomaly. Asteroids of this belt are more dense than Outer Belt asteroids, but are also smaller.

591801.text:
CLASS: Nadezhda
GRAVITY: Full
DOCKING: Yes
AMENITIES: Full
CREW: 2200

Once a mere asteroid orbiting Volgograd, the Coalition found a use for the irregularly shaped miniature moon; by hollowing it out and constructing a starbase complex within and around it, the Zvyozdny Gorodok, or "Star City", was born.

The Zvyozdny Gorodok is a multi-purpose military installation charted as one of the largest asteroid bases in Sirius. It is a Coalition military base, fighter production plant, and spaceport all in one. Hundreds of atmospheric-capable shuttles carry cargo and passengers between the base and the planet below, with each transport carefully scanned to ensure the safety of the capital.
591801.mapped:
The Coalition's embedded saboteurs traveled to the Sirius sector aboard the sleeper ship Hispania, stowing away as the Alliance remnants fled. After the Hispania drifted helplessly into the Omicrons, the Coalitioneers scattered across Sirius in small craft, eventually establishing a colony in Omega-52.

Centuries later, the descendants of those settlers and their sympathizers from all over Sirius gathered into one resurgent Coalition, with more swelling their ranks every day. Though they bear little more than a passing resemblance to the original Coalition of Sol and its ideals, they promise an end to the tyranny of the imperialist Houses, a promise which resonates with many disgruntled Sirians. Thus the echo of the Sol War continues to haunt the survivors' descendants, the sides drawn mere shadows of their former selves.

The station houses barracks and training facilities, with a permanent garrison of experienced pilots guarding the facility and the planet below. The close proximity to strike craft manufacturing facilities conveniently allows pilots to become more familiar with the inner workings of their machines before their first deployments.

591805.text:
CLASS: Volya
GRAVITY: Complete
DOCKING: Yes
AMENITIES: Limited
CREW: 3000

Aralsk Research Station, in low Aralkum orbit, is the Coalition's primary research, development and shipbuilding facility. The station is heavily guarded by Coalition Military patrols, and no vessel is permitted to dock without authorization.
591805.mapped:
The station was built to house the Aralsk Research Division—a group of brilliant minds hard at work advancing Coalition science and reverse-engineering captured technology. Most Coalition ships and weapons were prototyped here, modified from samples purchased from allies or taken from enemies.

The station has limited shipbuilding facilities for developing and testing the Research Division's designs. The tachyon cannons used by Coalition fighters were designed here, as was the Storm-class gunboat and the fearsome Typhoon-class destroyer.

To take advantage of Aralkum's helium-rich atmosphere, the facilities also include a fuel refinery, making it the Coalition's main source of H-Fuel. Its output can supply in-system patrols by local fleets, but struggles to keep up with demand of Coalition strike groups launched further afield.

The station's trajectory is constantly degraded by impacts and friction from debris in the Aralkum Belt; a portion of its harvested fuel is dedicated to course corrections.

In 830 AS, the Premier ordered the expansion of Aralsk, adding further shipbuilding facilities, slipways, and industrial smelters to process resources mined from the Aralkum Belt and imported from the Coalition's trading partners. With these upgrades, Aralsk is now the Coalition's premier shipyard, producing and servicing both capital ships and strike craft. However, the station's fuel consumption increased accordingly to almost three quarters of its output, making it one of the most expensive bases to maintain in the entire Sirius Sector.

CLASS: Progress
GRAVITY: Complete
DOCKING: Yes
AMENITIES: Full
CREW: 900

Zhejiang Orbital is administered by the Coalition, and it is their oldest installation in Omega-52, built while the rest of the system was still being charted.
591808.mapped:
Intending to colonize Planet Jiangxi, they realized they needed an outpost in orbit to coordinate their efforts, house their personnel, and service their fleet of starships. Many of the system's initial settlers lived here before relocating to Jiangxi's surface or Volgograd.

Since those days, the station has been given over to civilian administration. It now serves as a trading post, receiving merchant ships from the Coalition's authorized trading partners. Zhejiang also houses immigration and diplomatic offices, welcoming guests from the rest of Sirius and processing those who wish to join the Coalition.

A small contingent of Coalition military fighter squadrons is based here, patrolling space around Planet Jiangxi and maintaining security. This is often the first assignment of freshly graduated Coalition pilots.

591811.text:
DIAMETER: 13,396 km.
MASS: 6.03 x 10e24 kg.
TERRAIN: Terrestrial
TEMPERATURE: -78°C to 87°C
ESCAPE VELOCITY: 11.83 km/sec
POPULATION: CLASSIFIED

Nominally habitable, Jiangxi is a world of extremes, harboring lush jungles, vast deserts, deep oceans, and frozen wastelands in the polar regions. The Coalition constructed outposts on Jiangxi not long after exploring Omega-52, expecting to turn it into their primary colony and capital.
591811.mapped:
Small farming, mining and industrial towns were established on the surface, but attempts at further development have suffered setback after setback. Failing equipment in the harsh weather, crops dying in the unpredictable climate, deadly attacks from enemies, and diseases from the displaced native wildlife proved to be constant challenges for the settlers. As the centuries passed, the less hospitable but more pliable Volgograd actually outpaced Jiangxi in growth. Nevertheless, Jiangxi remained a valuable asset due to the presence of arable land, supplying the Coalition with food and organic materials even as it continued to resist colonization efforts.

In 817 AS, Jiangxi was bombarded by a rogue fleet that managed to breach the system's defenses in a surprise attack. Much of the planet's industry and nearly every civilian settlement were destroyed in what was meant to be a killing blow to the Coalition. The attack also caused fires on a planetary scale, leading to widespread ecological disaster. The resulting ash clouds have since receded, but for a while, the planet was plunged into a global cooling period.

Relief forces lifted the siege three days after it started, and the Coalition endured despite the devastation. The arduous process of rebuilding began, with the least hard-hit areas being given priority. Several small settlements escaped destruction. Santiago de la Omega avoided notice by virtue of being located underwater, while New Hong Kong managed to shoot down the missiles bound for it. These lucky few are now the schelling points for civilization on the surface.

However, most of Jiangxi's population centers and military installations weren't as fortunate. Their ruins are now located in irradiated wastelands, with both the Coalition government and independent teams brought in from off-world launching salvaging expeditions as part of the recovery effort. They explore the underground complexes buried under broken slabs of concrete and gnarled metal fingers of ruined buildings.

Despite propaganda about rapid reconstruction, the wastelands and radiation have only added to the colonists' problems, and Jiangxi remains as dangerous as ever. Access to the surface is heavily regulated by the Coalition, ostensibly to protect the populace from radiation. Even so, factories on the planet continue to operate, and the Coalition government is even deliberating relocating the capital there to more directly oversee the colony's development.
