592715.text: Annibal was once a reconnaissance ship of the Gallic Royal Intelligence, dispatched to the remote regions of Champagne to monitor The Council's fleet movements. The ship was detected by a large group of Unione Corse ships in 730 AGS (814 AS), who prematurely ended the agent's mission.

592717.text: This Gallic Republic light fighter was lost in 742 AGS (826 AS), while responding to sightings of Maquis vessels. The former allies found themselves in bitter conflict following the Mazagran Massacre. The Railleuse drifted into the outskirts of the Ardennes Asteroid Field after being struck by a missile.

592719.text: In 718 AGS (802 AS), the Danube was tasked to carry EMP missiles to the Council warships fighting near Courville Guard Station. Soon after the ship launched from Montmirail, an incorrectly stowed missile exploded within the Danube's hull. The disabled ship drifted deeper into the Aisne Asteroid Field and was lost.

592721.text: Fortune was once a Gallic Royal Navy gunboat that participated in a counter-assault against the Council in 725 AGS (809 AS). The GRN ships launched a surprise assault into Champagne through the Picardy Jump Hole. The attack was quickly bogged down in the Seine Nebula following ambushes by Council, Maquis, and Brigand fighters. The Fortune was destroyed while attempting to retreat.

592723.text: The Lezard was a Gallic Brigand heavy fighter, belonging to the notorious rakish troubadour Emile Bartoli. Upon escorting a Unione Corse freighter to Joinville Base, the pilot remained aboard overnight. He later disappeared along with his ship -- likely the work of an enraged Corsican husband.

592725.text: The Brigand bomber Camelion participated in the "liberation" of the Champagne system from Royal Navy and Police presence. In 717 AGS (801 AS) it was damaged by gunboat fire and lost within the Aisne Asteroid Field. The fate of its pilot remains unknown.

592727.text: The Driade was a Gallic Brigand freighter last sighted in 748 AGS (832 AS), departing Monte Carlo Freeport in Provence. It is rumored that the ship was headed for Zurich. The ship's engines have been precisely shot out, and the pilot is missing.

592729.text: Hull of a disabled Bretonia Armed Forces heavy fighter, one of the many remnants of the Tau War between Bretonia and Kusari. Heavy damage and a missing transponder makes it impossible to tell who the pilot of this vessel was or when precisely they were lost.

592731.text: This disabled ship once belonged to the Bretonia Police Authority. While aiding the Armed Forces as an auxiliary during the Tau War, it was shot down and then left behind by the retreating fleets. Heavy damage and a missing transponder makes it impossible to tell who the pilot of this vessel was or when precisely they were lost.

592733.text: This heavy fighter wreck belongs to one of the many Kusari ships that were severely damaged during the Tau War against the Bretonia Armed Forces. Heavy damage and a missing transponder makes it impossible to tell who the pilot of this vessel was or when precisely they were lost.

592735.text: This Liberty heavy fighter was lost in combat against Rheinland forces during the Hudson War. Heavy damage and a missing transponder makes it impossible to tell who the pilot of this vessel was or when precisely they were lost.

592737.text: Tasked to counter Liberty aggression during the Hudson War, this Rheinland fighter was one of thousands lost in battle. Heavy damage and a missing transponder makes it impossible to tell who the pilot of this vessel was or when precisely they were lost.

592739.text: The remains of a Liberty patrol within the Appalachian Asteroid Field. The catastrophic hull damage indicates it was ripped apart by explosives. Given that Xenos are often sighted in the field, it is highly likely the patrol was ambushed by a raiding party. It is likely a mine or missile connected with the engine of the ship, ripping it apart.

592741.text: The Albion was a Rogue fighter that had been smuggling Cardamine from Niverton Base. A Junker informant ratted him out, and the ship was soon intercepted by an LPI patrol wing. The Albion was critically damaged while attempting to flee, and the pilot arrested and shipped to Sugarland. The wreck of the Albion is a reminder to the criminals of Liberty of the risks of smuggling Cardamine in the system.

592743.text: The hull of a Zoner freighter, originally bound for Bethlehem Station with essential supplies. Originally flying from New York, it is suspected that the vessel was intercepted by Liberty Rogues or Xenos. The freighter was shot to pieces and left to drift, later falling into Planet Dudley's orbit. The Verne was long-ago picked clean by scavengers.

592745.text: The Stardust belonged to prolific Erie smuggler, Rufus Blackwell. After years evading the police, a near miss with a LPI wing earned him a warrant with the Bounty Hunter's Guild. A gang of Hunters succeeded in placing a tracking beacon on the Stardust after extorting one of Blackwell's Erie acquaintances. The Hunters sprung their trap near the California Jump Hole; Blackwell fled towards the Pocono Field, but his assailants' faster and more agile fighters quickly overran him, applying full stop to his daring career.

592747.text: The Lynch belonged to ace pilot David Brenson. A neural net message sent to Brenson with information on his next target was intercepted by the Lane Hackers, who were ordered to eliminate the troublesome Hunter. The assassins caught up with Brenson in the Driftwood Asteroid Field, quickly killing his wingmen. Despite being heavily outnumbered, the Lynch dispatched 5 of its attackers before a mine struck its cockpit, killing Brenson instantly. To this day, Brenson is known as one of the most successful and notorious Hunters to operate in Liberty Space.

592749.text: The Xeno pilot who flew the Ogre was atypical for his lot, mild mannered and unassuming in appearance. This humble countenance contrasted harshly with his absolutely reckless style of flying, often ramming enemy vessels and shattering their cockpits. Judging by the state of the wreckage, it appears the pilot bit off more than he could chew, but there are signs that he could have ejected and is still at large.

592751.text: A Liberty Rogue freighter named Weasel was lost on a trade mission to Alberta in 813 AS. It was likely attacked by Xenos.

592753.text: Rumors say the Weedville's pilot left Allentown in 814 AS to explore a "remote orange nebula." No one knows if she was referring to a nebula within Pennsylvania or elsewhere. The ship, oddly enough, doesn't show signs of piracy or an ambush, but the body of the pilot was never recovered. The ship's weapons look old but recoverable, and the rations in the hold suggest the pilot was leaving for a long voyage.

592755.text: A Liberty Navy fighter that was disabled and trapped within the Georgian Ice Field after being attacked by overwhelming forces of the Xenos.

592757.text: Megion was part of a Liberty Police patrol tasked to track Liberty Rogue activity in the Alberta system. Instead, Liberty Rogues tracked the activity of Police and did not let any of the patrol's pilots leave the area alive.

592759.text: Swiftsure was part of the patrol tasked to track down the Rheinland reconnaissance ships coming from Bremen into the Quebec Belt systems. The Rheinlanders attacked by surprise, and the patrol was outnumbered two to one; Swiftsure pilot fought bravely, and most of the Rheinland ships were either destroyed or severely damaged. However, the pilot of Swiftsure was killed in a missile explosion, and his disabled ship remained in the Bethlehem Ice Field.

592761.text: The Radiant was a cargo ship belonging to the Zoners that was attacked by Wild raiders. The surprise attack was executed flawlessly, giving Radiant and its escort no chance. Most of its systems were damaged, and the ship was lost somewhere in the Walker Nebula. It was one of the few instances where the Wild ventured as far as Omega-47.

592763.text: Arnomendi once belonged to an ill-famed Corsair, Olivia Velasquez, known for her exceptional hatred for all Bounty Hunters, and Zoners who gave them shelter on their Edge World bases. While most other Corsairs repected the Zoners' neutrality, Olivia and several other Corsairs who shared her ideas had covertly hijacked several Zoner convoys in 815-816 AS. Finally, she angered the Zoners so much that they bribed the Corsairs to leak the info on Olivia's next target. Outnumbered by Zoner ships who surrounded her, Olivia refused to surrender and was captured by force. No one has heard from her since.

592765.text:
DIAMETER: 6,230 km
MASS: 4.66 x 10e24 kg
TERRAIN: Barren
TEMPERATURE: -75°C to 8°C
ESCAPE VELOCITY: 5.07 km/sec

A desolate moon located deep within the Driftwood Asteroid Field.

592767.text:
DIAMETER: 5,170 km
MASS: 3.12 x 10e24 kg
TERRAIN: Barren
TEMPERATURE: -256°C to -245°C
ESCAPE VELOCITY: 3.65 km/sec

A remote planetoid located far away from the larger Alberta planets, Vegreville may be an orphaned moon of Planet Calgary, or a remnant of the times when the Alberta planet system was formed.

592769.text: Torbay was a Lane Hacker Dagger that separated from its patrol for unknown reasons and encountered a group of Liberty Navy fighters on its way back to Cochrane. The Dagger attempted to escape, but was critically damaged by enemy fire. Torbay appears to have successfully vanished into the noise of the North Debris Sea, however the pilot perished soon after.

592771.text: A Zoner convoy escort, destroyed in 830 AS during the annexation of Pennsylvania. Reports show the Liberty Navy intercepted the convoy on suspicion of supplying Zoner Militants. It is unclear which party fired first. The entire convoy was wiped out, and the Gaeta the only recoverable ship from the carnage.

592773.text: Leander was a civilian heavy fighter, most likely belonging to a Pennsylvania Freelancer who was exploring Kansas' asteroid fields. For reasons unknown, the ship's engines failed; there was no one to call for help in this desolate system. The ship's transponder and pilot registration have been badly falsified, leaving the pilot's identity a mystery.

592775.text: The Lane Hacker who once owned this craft was clearly a skilled and wealthy pilot considering the number of customizations on his Sabre. However, in the vasts of Kansas system combat skills matter less than a properly maintained engine fueling system. Attracted by strange emissions from the Tuttle Creek Nebula, the pilot had just enough fuel to approach the source of this emission, hoping that there is a base or a ship where he might get help. He never knew what the true source was.

592777.text: This Dromedary-class freighter once belonged to an independent space explorer. In the Kansas system, he was unlucky enough to stumle upon a Lane Hacker patrol. After refusing to give out the cargo, the pirates disabled the ship's engines, boarded the ship, and took all goods their ships were able to carry.

592779.text: Farrow is a Liberty Navy Defender that was damaged in a fight with pirates in the Magellan system. The pilot noticed the jump hole into Kansas on his radar and directed his ship there. However, the navigation systems of the ship were damaged, and it was never able to find its way back to base.

592781.text: This Wolfhound once belonged to a famed Molly named Galway Connelly. His ship was lost in Manchester system after his patrol was engaged by Bretonia Navy fighters, however, it remains unknown how it ended up in a remote region of the Kansas system. Fate of Connelly himself is also a mystery.

592783.text: The Redwich was a freelance explorer hailing from Erie. After registering a flight plan headed into the Driftwood Asteroid Field, the Starblazer never returned. Some Zoners believe that this field is haunted, and caution pilots to avoid it.

592785.text: This Outcast Sabre found itself under attack by a prevailing Kusari Navy patrol in Tau-31. After escaping to Newcastle, the ship's damaged engines were tracked by the Bretonia Police who chased the ship across the whole system. The pilot escaped to Inverness, but damaged communication equipment made long range communication impossible. The ship was last seen on the edge of the Avlemore Nebula.

592787.text: The Pentester was once piloted by a Lane Hacker using the alias ShellWorm. They vanished in 827 AS, presumably lost to the storm. They were likely attempting to salvage abandoned hardware left behind by Liberty's evacuation.

592791.text:
CLASS: Spire
GRAVITY: Partial
DOCKING: Yes
AMENITIES: Yes
CREW: Unknown
592791.mapped:
When Ithaca Base was originally established is a mystery -- the many mutually contradictory myths confuse rather than clarify the issue. Some say the original founders were Corsair and Red Hessian dissidents who betrayed their causes to avoid being sent to the meatgrinder in Omega-5. Others claim the haven was initially set up as a stash for a crooked Rheinland Federal Police squadron who went a month too long without pay. Others claim the founders were Daumann mercenaries who quickly realized that there was a bigger paycheck in Omega-7 by going pirate.

Whatever the truth, Ithaca has for decades been a notorious den of scum and villainy, full of killers, con-artists and assorted degenerates. A dark and twisting warren of corridors and halls have been excavated into an enormous asteroid, concealing services ranging from bars, brothels and bloodsports, to black market mechanics, arms dealers and unlicensed sawbones doctors. Whenever a pirate needs hired muscle or a contract killer without a paper trail, Ithaca is the first port of call. In past years, the anarchic individualism of the base’s occupants led to frequent bloodshed, with hundreds killed each year through pointless squabbles or territorial disputes.

In 834 AS, the loose band of pirates running Ithaca entered a pact with the independent gangs that roamed the surrounding regions, founding the Ithaca Council. The Council brutally cracked down on this infighting, imposing the Council’s Peace at the barrel of a gun. They aim to turn the base into an underworld freeport -- making the Council members who will take a cut of the earnings incredibly wealthy and powerful. Despite these grand ambitions, the Council walks a tightrope to avoid the offense or hostility of large factions such as the Hessians or Corsairs.

592795.mapped:
This scarred and cruel instrument of a Kingdom holding onto power bears striking resemblance to the vessel christened "Castillon" in Gallic Naval records. It is possible that the Royalists simply repurposed this vessel for their usage and renamed it for dramatic effect. However the contradiction remains that many of the ship's represented capabilities do not conform to those of the ship it is believed to be.

Strategists in Gallia are often left deadlocked in debate as to the ship's actual class and origins as a result, alongside the task of handling an emerging threat that represents a bygone establishment.

The Charlemagne battleships were designed around 760 AS, specifically for defensive and support purposes. Battleships of this class were configured to hold and maintain large numbers of fighters and cover them with powerful point defense turrets. By the time of the Gallic invasion of Bretonia, the dated Charlemagnes were used as the rearguard for advancing forces and for protecting vulnerable supply lines. After the destruction of the Oubli fleet in 822 AS, the Gallic Royal Navy dispatched the Betheny to garrison Leeds and provide support for the Carcassonne fleet's blockade of the Independent Worlds.

In 824 AS the Betheny received orders to advance into Magellan as the rearguard of the Carcassonne's continued assault into California. Its primary task was to maintain the "Starvation Strategy" blockade that prevented Libertonian supplies reaching Bretonia. An Allied invasion of Cortez in late 825 AS forced a rapid redeployment to prevent the re-opening of this route during the critical Siege of New London. After months of probing feints and skirmishes, the Betheny cunningly divided its forces to draw away the Bretonian Battleship Harlow, before committing itself to an attack on Liberty' Battleship Yukon.

The Betheny possessed a decisive edge in tonnage and armament, and quickly overran the elderly Yukon. Despite this, the veteran Liberty ship tenaciously clung on, inflicting damage and fighting a delaying action until the Harlow could arrive. While the Yukon was destroyed during the engagement, the combined Bretonian and Liberty fleets ultimately dispatched the Betheny and its escorts in turn. The wreckage of the battle eventually formed the Aruba Debris Field -- work to scrap the Betheny's broken hulk began in 828 AS.

592799.text:
CLASS: Richelieu
CREW: CLASSIFIED
ARMAMENT: CLASSIFIED
592799.mapped:
The Montmorency, as one of the more modern ships in the fleet at the time of the Gallic invasion, was part of the backbone of the fleet during the push through the Taus and was stationed there to secure supply lines against hostile elements. It performed this task admirably for many years, before being sent to Roussillon, facing the Council as the lead ship of the Royal Navy’s advance into the system. Despite a determined assault, the Council forces the Montmorency's battlegroup faced fought a brilliant delaying action, securing enough time for their civilian population to flee before the Montmorency could take Toulouse, effectively annexing the system into the Kingdom.

As the Montmorency was ensuring the last of the Council forces had fled Roussillon, the ship received word of the collapse of the Kingdom in the Core Worlds, with the Confederacy rising in its place. Finding itself surrounded by Royalist hardliners which the ship's officers had fundamental disagreements with, the Montmorency found itself in a precarious position, entirely cut off from any hope of reinforcement and with no way to fight past the Royalist forces in the area. Montmorency would not be in this position for long, as the sudden outbreak of war with Kusari led to enough confusion among the Royalist ranks that it was able to make a hasty retreat back to Gallic space.

Finding itself in Languedoc, the Montmorency immediately moved to assist Gallic forces in their efforts to remove Kusari forces from their space, quickly finding itself spearheading the attacks as the fragmented fleets rallied around the pristine ship and experienced crew. This final battle marked the last gasp of the Confederacy and the formation of the Gallic Union, with the Montmorency being assigned to Burgundy to both help keep the peace, but also to ensure that the storied ship would not draw too much attention from those of the fleet that look on the past fondly.

592800.text:
The Montmorency, as one of the more modern ships in the fleet at the time of the Gallic invasion, was part of the backbone of the fleet during the push through the Taus and was stationed there to secure supply lines against hostile elements. It performed this task admirably for many years, before being sent to Roussillon, facing the Council as the lead ship of the Royal Navy’s advance into the system. Despite a determined assault, the Council forces the Montmorency's battlegroup faced fought a brilliant delaying action, securing enough time for their civilian population to flee before the Montmorency could take Toulouse, effectively annexing the system into the Kingdom.

As the Montmorency was ensuring the last of the Council forces had fled Roussillon, the ship received word of the collapse of the Kingdom in the Core Worlds, with the Confederacy rising in its place. The Charlemagne battleships were designed around 760 AS, specifically for defensive and support purposes. Battleships of this class were configured to hold and maintain large numbers of fighters and cover them with powerful point defense turrets. By the time of the Gallic invasion of Bretonia, the dated Charlemagnes were used as the rearguard for advancing forces and for protecting vulnerable supply lines.

The Battleship Ambazac spent much of its service during the war garrisoning Languedoc, primarily combating revolutionary activity from The Council and Maquis. In 825 AS, the Gallic Royal Navy committed to a doctrine of a final decisive battle in New London, stripping Gallia’s internal garrisons to bolster the invasion fleet. The Ambazac participated in the initial Blitz of New London, providing fire support during the Battles of Trafalgar and Southampton Junction.

It was later posted to the "Southampton Trinité" to protect the supply lines back to Leeds, alongside the Le Cendre and Beuvray. Following the Beuvray’s destruction, the squadron was joined by the Battleship Athos -- a battlegroup of hired Corsair mercenaries. At the climax of the Siege of New London in 826 AS, the Trinité was pushed into battle as reinforcements, to plug gaps in the battle line left by mounting casualties.

The Ambazac performed most notably of all the Trinité vessels, crippling Liberty’s Battleship Gettysburg during an early exchange. Despite this, the retreat of the Athos and destruction of the Le Cendre left the Ambazac fatally exposed, and it was brought down by the ailing Dreadnought Warwick soon after. The hulk was shunted into the Southampton Debris Field later that year, with scrappage at Belvedere Refinery completed in late 831 AS.
592802.mapped:
After Battleship Guillestre was redeployed to the Tau systems to support the Royal Navy's invasion of Sirius, Battleship Ambazac was stationed in the Languedoc system. Ambazac's deployment reflected the old Royal Navy strategy of 'defense in depth.' Rather than concentrating forces at the perimeter of the threat, the fleet was arranged to provide security throughout Gallia's territory. This prevented the loss of large forces in case of surprise assaults, and forced adversaries to confront the certainty of quick reinforcement throughout most of Gallia.

This strategy was abandoned when the blitz on New London was ordered. Hundreds of rear echelon warships were drawn from the core Gallic systems, and the Ambazac was no different. As a member of the Charlemagne line of battleships designed for defense and support assignments, the Ambazac is now part of the rearguard Southampton Trinité. With the Athos and Le Cendre, Ambazac's duty is to secure the strategically vital location to maintain an effective supply line without risk of a vulnerable flank.

592804.text:
COPPER ORE

Ore is a type of rock that contains minerals such as metals which can be extracted through mining and refined for use. The ores must be processed to extract the metals of interest from the waste rock and from the ore minerals. Many organizations prefer to receive unsmelted ores in order to keep the additional cost of their production and finish within the local economy, as opposed to paying markups to foreign laborers to do the work for them.

592805.text: A large pocket within the nebula containing Copper, Cobalt, and Silver-bearing asteroids. Daumann Heavy Construction operates the Briesen Mining Facility within the cloud, despite the threat of Corsair attacks.

CLASS: Ranseur
CREW: CLASSIFIED
ARMAMENT: CLASSIFIED
592807.mapped:
The latest Ranseur class dreadnought built by Outcasty at Valletta Shipyard as a need to replace the older and now decommissioned Captana. Although Outcast doctrine mostly relies on its vaunted aces in fighters and bombers, the Basilica serves as a heavy hammer for breaking through enemy lines and as heavy tactical support wherever it is needed.

The dreadnought Basilica proved itself right from the start of its operational career in striking down the Crayter Republic's prized capital ships Helios, Zagreus, Hades, and Cronus during Operation Orange Hammer. Although Basilica was severely damaged during this campaign in Crayter territory, it successfully retreated back to the safety of Omicron Alpha, where it was upgraded to increase the ship's effectiveness. Basilica later proved its superiority again in Omicron Theta, where it overwhelmed the Corsair battleship Fes without major damage, though later was forced to withdraw to Omicron Alpha.

The ship's most recent combat deployment was in the Omicron Alpha system, where it conducted a retaliatory orbital bombardment of a mining colony on the planet Albegna that had been seized by rebel slaves, just after it was clear that all Outcasts had long since been executed at the hands of the rebels.

The Basilica is currently the only operational Ranseur by the Outcast forces and it is stationed in high orbit on the planet Malta, where it serves as the protector of the Outcast homeworld. Having already establiitd the ship's place in history through a more than impressive combat record, and owing to the timelessness of its modular design and highly experienced crew, the Basilica is one of the few battleships in Sirius to be shrouded in an almost mythical aura, often fueled by the Outcasts themselves.

First discovered and surveyed by a scientific expedition from the Crayter Republic in 817 AS, Planet Moros was never worth more than a sidelong glance due to its lack of valuable resources. With an exceedingly hostile environment for both humans and animals alike, any plans that were considered for Moros were quickly discarded, even though the planet could theoretically support a small population through the export of alien artifacts. Alongside these plans, a small supply depot in geostationary orbit was also abandoned by the Crayter Republic.

While at first glance, the planet might resemble a gas dwarf, Moros merely sports an opaque, purple-tinted atmosphere composed of argon, xenon, and trace amounts of other gases. The planet's surface is rocky, littered with frozen carbon dioxide crystals and the occasional alien ruin. Being an object with significant mass and therefore substantial gravity, Moros has trapped rocky debris inside its gravitational well over the course of several millennia, which acts as natural defense for the planet, making it difficult for larger vessels to approach the surface.

Since the year 823 AS, the planet has served as a dwelling for a particular tribe of Nomads, who have erected a vast tunnel system underneath the crust of the planet. Although the Nomads largely derive their energy from cosmic radiation, they seem to have bored deep enough into the planet to harness the thermal energy of its molten core for sustenance. As a result, the cavern systems of these Nomads become hotter the further down they dig, and the rising heat even has a tangible effect on the areas surrounding the tunnel entrances, causing the frozen carbon dioxide crystals to melt. Thanks to this process, it is possible to predict that the tunnel system currently spans only a fraction of the planet's surface, and the number of Nomads living there likely does not exceed a couple of thousand. However, if this number were to increase, it is quite possible that their means of sustaining themselves would deplete the planet's core rapidly, with some Core analysts predicting that it might cool down in a matter of mere years if more than 80% of the planet's surface shows signs of Nomad infestation.

Order operatives who have investigated these recent developments and explored the cavern system reported that most of the space below the surface is dedicated to massive caverns in which Nomad ships are nestled into the stone walls, resembling a beehive structure. These ships seem to be hibernating and languishing in the heat rising from the planet's core. Through this, the Order was able to deduce that most of the Nomads living on Moros are in a state of hibernation, possibly to reduce the amount of energy necessary to sustain themselves and thereby put less strain on the planet's core.

592814.text: The debris from a planetary collision that has been pulled into orbit by Moros' gravity, encompassing the entire planet.

592854.mapped:
New Paris was the first planet colonized by the Gallic Sleeper Ship's arrival in 84 AS (0 AGS). Ecologically, the world was similar to Earth's Carboniferous period. Vast forests cover the equatorial and moderate regions but only a few large animal species in habit them. Oxygen concentration on New Paris is similar to human-inhabited Earth, hovering at 24 percent. Unlike the Carboniferous period, which had an Oxygen content of almost 40 percent, therefore large insect species didn't develop, leaving room for smaller amphibians and small avian dinosaurs to evolve. Cold continental areas were sparsely inhabited and had no large flora. Oceanic wildlife is extremely rich with a wide variety of species; most do not bear resemblance to any known Earth animals. The planet's climate was similar to Earth, with temperatures of 60°C at the equator and dropping below -60°C at the poles.

New Paris has undergone several periods of development, starting with numerous isolated colonies. Soon afterwards, large cities evolved from these, and food demand forced them to exploit huge areas of land to plant crops and raise animals brought from Earth. In many areas, indigenous wildlife was fully replaced with domesticated fauna and flora from Earth. Rapid industrial growth resulted in severe pollution that still affects certain areas of the planet. Circa 200 AGS, the planet's population neared 5 million and large urban centers emerged in moderate climates near natural harbors. Those centers were named after old Paris districts.

The population grew steadily and reached 1 billion by 600 AGS. Millions relocated off-world, with massive relocation campaigns taking place to populate worlds with huge resource deposits and industrial capacity. Apart from the relocation programs, many people left New Paris to find a better standard of living and capturing their inner pioneer spirit. Sadly, New Paris gradually became the most expensive planet to live in all of Gallia.

Ecology issues forced the removal of heavy industry away from New Paris to space stations in Ile-de-France and beyond. The few remaining ancient factories now serve as museums displaying impressive industrial landmarks similar to 21st century Earth. Currently, the planet is considered to be one of the most comfortable places to live in all of Gallia. Offices of the Royal Government and Royal Chancellery, as well as the High Courts and the Parliament, were located on New Paris.

By the end of the Second Gallic Civil War, the Council's fleet reached New Paris and prepared for a final battle against the remains of the Royal Navy's home fleet. By that point, the King, his court retainers, closest followers and various nobles had already evacuated and were on their way to the Gallic Hebrides. Thus cooler heads prevailed and the Royal Navy chose to surrender, and a ceasefire was issued throughout Gallia. The historic seat of the Gallic monarchy was now at the Council's mercy.
However, higher planet side living standards, proximity to the Monarchy and decades of ardent propaganda ensured that the Parisians had a low opinion of the Council and its ideology. Consequently, the provisional government of Ile-de-France declined to join the newly-formed Republic, which in turn wasn't willing to start a new era with a bloodbath.
Instead, New Paris declared itself an autonomous state despite possessing little to defend itself. The reason behind this decision ties into Ile-de-France's considerable strategic import. Namely, significant industrial and shipbuilding capacity and enormous agricultural production capabilities ensure that the system could be entirely self-sufficient. Also Ile-de-France is located at the heart of the Gallic lane network, guaranteeing it freedom of navigation and the ability to shut down trade in any of the Confederate states by deactivating the corresponding gates.

This also made Ile-de-France the most logical choice for a neutral meeting ground between the leaders and representatives of all Gallic states. This summit, known as the Parisian Assembly, is where the Confederacy was born, out of need for Gallia to remain united against internal divisions and against external threats. It was also the Assembly that outlawed weapons of mass destruction throughout Gallia, banning the Royal Navy's WMDs and largest ships from its space.

Nowadays, the Assembly hosts regular meetings of Gallia's elite. Each constituent state of the Confederacy has permanent representation on New Paris, and some Sirian entities already have their own embassies planet side. The Assembly presides over all aspects of Confederate-level governing; funding specific projects, maintaining infrastructure, allocating supplies, regulating tariffs and providing arbitration in disputes between the Gallic states. In return, said states are required to provide support to Ile-de-France, in the form of taxes, manpower and ships. These contributions are used to fuel both the Gendarmerie and the new Confederate Defense Force.

592857.mapped:
The history of the Croyton District goes back almost four hundred years, when acres of housing were built for workers in the increasingly people-hungry factories of planet New London. From time immemorial there have been narrow and winding streets lining the endless maze of accommodation blocks and life here has never been easy or lengthy.

As heavy industry moved to the planet Leeds and the factories on planet New London declined, so did Croyton's importance and most of the dormitories ceased to serve their original purpose and were abandoned.

When a massive evacuation of civilians from the planet Leeds began during the Gallic assault of the planet, the Croyton accommodation complexes were rebuilt and a starport for refugee ships was added. At first, the poorly housed refugees were cohesive and there was hope among them that they would find a new and more dignified refuge when the war was over.

However, the economic recession forced the Bretonian authorities to change their plans and the resettlement of the refugees was postponed indefinitely. Those who could still afford it have long since departed, while new, more desperate and in many cases more violent individuals have taken their place. As despair grew and criminal elements settled in, Croyton found a new life as the chief shadow starport on the planet New London. Although Croyton is officially overseen by the incorruptible BPA, the neighborhood's convoluted nature, the sheer number of residents, and their general hostility or distrust towards authority make Croyton very difficult to control.

Despite the attempts of some criminal groups to gain control of Croyton, the local district is still firmly in the hands of the local government, which seizes any opportunity to raise funds to improve the lives of those still living there, and so all manner of gambling houses, links to the local black market, drug dens and arms dealers can be found in the district.

Beauvais was one of the first space stations constructed by GMS in Ile-de-France, where it focused on extracting and refining valuable minerals from the Oise and Chevreuse Asteroid Fields. When both were depleted of easily accessible deposits, Beauvais was partially scuttled and then abandoned. In the present day, the ruin is periodically used by Compiegne Naval Academy to train Marines on mock boarding, hazardous environment and search and rescue scenarios.
592860.mapped:
Beauvais was one of the first space stations constructed by EFL Oil and Machinery back in the time when it was called EFL Oil. The company initially built its fortune on planetside mining of oil and producing a wide array of petroleum products. Moving to space was a necessary step forward to move the most ecologically hazardous industry away from the planet's surface, and to gain access to resource deposits located in space.

EFL started constructing the station in the year 281 AGS, and in the hundreds of years to come the facility was rebuilt several times. It contains a number of highly efficient petroleum processing facilities, making Beauvais one of the primary sources of petrochemicals in the Ile-de-France system.

592863.mapped:
Compiegne was a contemporary civilian housing facility that was built in 690 AGS at one of the intersections of the Ile-de-France trade lanes. Initially operated by Nery Space Construction, a medium-sized space company, the facility was later bought by Solar Engineering, who transformed it into their space-based headquarters.

However, after centuries, EFL merged with Solar Engineering, and most of their facilities on Aubigny could perform the same tasks as the space station, rendering Compiegne obsolete for EFL. Subsequently, the Gallic Navy bought the facility, and it was converted into a space naval academy to train new officers and crew for the military's wounded. The facility underwent extensive retrofitting for this purpose.

During the same year, a docking bay was added to the academy to host the derelict hull of the battleship Montreuil, which serves as a museum vessel commemorating the Second Gallic Civil War.

592866.text:
CLASS: Chatel
GRAVITY: Complete
DOCKING: Yes
AMENITIES: Yes
CREW: 300
592866.mapped:
Built in 303 AGS, Beaumont was at first a hastily patched up bulk in space intended as a hideout for the Gallic Brigands raiding the nearby mining operations inside the Saint-Cloud Asteroid Field during Gallia's earlier interstellar expansion. Looted copper and silver ore then got sold off for cheaper prices to smaller corporations not keeping up with the competition GMS gave, giving the Brigands the untruthful connotation of prideful medieval highwayman stealing of the rich to distribute it to the poor, which they use to appeal to the lower strata of Gallia.

This also lead to an influx of new pirates, who were formerly employed as mining and industrial workers. Unhappy with the harsh working environment, they turned on their former employers. The bulk of the stations' initial hull was comprised of junk and stolen materials from Beauvais construction sites. With the station hoarding more loot and growing in riches, it was eventually rebuilt and expanded to fit the more romantic picture that the Brigands have in mind.

Eventually the asteroid field was stripped of valuable ores, which forced the pirates to adapt to their newfound circumstances. They found themselves in a prime spot to stage raids against convoys from Beauvais Production Facility, to steal various industrious goods, profiting from it to sell it to several trading partners which are in need of said goods for their ambitions like the former organization called The Council.

With the arrival of Nox, a drug originating from Provence, the former simple hideout turned into a booming black market becoming the primary distributor to the higher-class Planets of Gallia that popularized the drug despite the Government's attempts to curb its spread.

Nowadays Beaumont is frequently visited by various parties, including pirates, freelancers and covert agents of Gallic corporations. The opening of Gallia only contributed more of a high rise in profits making Beaumont the primary gallic black market rooted strategically inside the heart of Gallia.

592869.text:
CLASS: StV.D-18
GRAVITY: Complete
DOCKING: Yes
AMENITIES: Yes
CREW: 720
592869.mapped:
Ile-de-France Shipping was founded in 501 AGS. As a shipping company that specializes in space cargo transportation, the company considered establishing headquarters in space rather than planetside to be a major benefit. Construction of the station that was named Sarcelles took five years to complete, and in 506 AGS it was officially opened. In years to come, it was rebuilt and expanded several times to match an increasing amount of IDF shipments heading through Sarcelles to and from the Gallic Border Worlds.

The First Gallic War was a disaster for many small shipping companies, especially those heavily involved with Normandy region trade. IDF focused on the Core Worlds and Border Worlds instead. Backed by the government and supported by EFL Oil and Machinery, IDF currently controls a vast portion of civilian shipments across the Gallic house space, and has a practical monopoly on exporting goods to Sirius. Sarcelles is still considered the headquarters of the company, but not many board members and chief officers choose to live and work there. Despite the best efforts of IDF designers, living on Planet New Paris is much more comfortable. IDF Shipping owns a small island near Ile du Palais where a large "office city" was constructed to serve as the company's actual headquarters and most of its top employees live and work there.

Public opinion has turned against Ile-de-France Shipping since the end of the Second Gallic Civil War, as they were known as staunch Royalists, even supplying naval operations as far as Bretonia. With many distrustful of the company so openly loyal to the Crown, they have fewer clients to rely upon than they once did. It remains to be seen whether this is a permanent trend, or a fad of the times. Regardless of this, Ile-de-France Shipping continues their traditional style with pride.

592873.text:
CLASS: Palace
GRAVITY: Complete
DOCKING: Yes
AMENITIES: Yes
CREW: 2480
592873.mapped:
Versailles was commissioned by King Richard V "The Hedonist" as a lavish and decadent royal palace. The project suffered repeated delays due to royal interference and infighting courtiers, finishing 20 years later in 607 AGS (691 AS). Richard V had passed away the year before, while his son, King Louis III "The Austere", never resided at Versailles over security concerns and disdain for his father's wasteful frivolity. Following renovations ordered by Queen Beatrix in 645 AGS (729 AS), Versailles' over-sized Royal Police garrison, expansive interiors and extravagant design made it a popular winter palace for Gallic monarchs and senior nobles.

This would change with the advent of the Second Gallic Civil War, as its proximity to the Saint-Cloud Asteroid Field made Versailles a popular target for Maquis terrorists. Following a particularly damaging torpedo strike in 719 AGS (803 AS), the decision was made to tow Versailles from its orbit near Billancourt to the protective envelope of Planet New Paris' defense grid. Despite this, the Trade Lane junction the palace once occupied still bears its historic name as the Versailles Junction. With the fall of the Gallic monarchy in 742 AGS (826 AS), the station was inherited by the Parisian Assembly who promptly shuttered it over its bloated operating costs. The Gallic Union took possession of the station late the following year, with military assessors dismissing it as a gaudy strain on the state budget. Historic and cultural artifacts were quickly auctioned off, while the station itself was sold to IDF Shipping.

Badly battered by the loss of wartime contracts, IDFS hoped to utilize Versailles as a profitable luxury hotel for executives and dignitaries visiting New Paris. Unfortunately, Versailles' extreme running costs put this endeavor firmly in the red, with the hotel running at a loss until 750 AGS (834 AS) when IDFS decided to divest the property. After negotiations with Burgundy's Gonzaga Society collapsed, offers were considered from Orbital Spa and Cruise, and Rheinland's Imperial Shipping. Due to financial support and backing by the Rheinland government, Imperial's bid was successful in early 751 AGS (835 AS). Imperial hopes their attempt to create a Sirian commercial and diplomatic enclave will be more successful than their predecessors' efforts.

AMENITIES: Yes

592876.mapped:
Built in 247, Rambouillet Shipyard was the first full-service shipyard in what was then the Gallic Kingdom and was used to build advanced research and fighting ships for the Royal Navy until the 600s, when the company switched to mass production of warships for the Gallic Navy.

Like many Ile-de-France stations, Rambouillet was rebuilt several times throughout its history, with more and more docks being added to adapt to new shipbuilding needs. The only civilian ships ever built at Rambouillet were luxury cruise ships for the royal family.

Today, this shipyard's focus is mainly on repairs and modernization of the Gallic fleet, occasionally releasing new warships from its single but impressive dock, based on designs from the classified stations of the Gallic War Machine.

TERRAIN: Desert
TEMPERATURE: -144°C to -20°C
ESCAPE VELOCITY: 2.71 km/sec

Brunoy is a barren moon of Planet Creteil, hidden deep within the Vincennes Nebula. During Ile-de-France's earliest surveys, nothing of economic value was found.
592879.mapped:
Brunoy was the first pirate base founded in Ile-de-France. It is likely Brunoy dates to the first Gallic Civil War, crewed by dissidents that were later exterminated by royal repressions. After coming into the possession of Brigand gangs, the moon was honeycombed by tunnels without much planning or oversight. Towards 700 AGS neglect and seismic shocks from asteroid impacts had caused many of these excavations to collapse. With much of the moon-base depressurized, the pirates chose to leave.

Brunoy lay abandoned for many decades after this, save for the occasional foolhardy explorer. Following the Massacre of Mazagran, The Maquis occupied and repaired some parts of the facility. Expecting further Union attacks on exposed bases, Brunoy was the Maquis' first step towards establishing a new network that was not compromised by Council traitors. Despite this work, Brunoy remains a dangerous posting, with countless unexplored and unstable tunnels.

Brunoy now has one of the largest populations of Maquis combatants. Many pilots have transferred from other stations to strike the Gallic capital, while new recruits spurred on by the unrest on Marne have arrived for training. Brunoy is also an important Maquis supply waystation, resupplying smugglers heading from northern Gallia to the Hebrides.

592882.text:
CLASS: UNKNOWN
CREW: UNKNOWN
ARMAMENT: UNKNOWN

Preliminary scans indicate that this mechanical nightmare may once have been the Battleship Mars, the former flagship of The Core. The Mars was listed as lost in action during the 835 AS offensive in Omicron Zeta.
592882.mapped:
The Battleship Mars was launched from Schatten Experimental Drydock in 823 AS, and quickly adopted as The Core's flagship. The Mako-class warship was the most sophisticated vessel ever produced by AP Manufacturing, frequently being used as a demonstrator platform for prototype Core technologies. The Mars had a distinguished career spanning the Omegas and Omicrons, with initial operations including the construction of Dagger Outpost in Omega-55 and the destruction of the Order Battleship Canaan in 824 AS. Under the command of Atlas Brown, the Mars also led the 829 and 832 AS offensives into Omicron Kappa -- seizing Planet Gammu, and altering the battleship's fate forever. The looting of the occupied Gammu brought the Core into contact with Hesione, an ancient artificial intelligence Ancestor Mind.

Centuries-old and among the most coldly analytical of Gammu's AIs, Hesione was cherished as The Core's greatest prize, and basis for their Battlefield Command Suite product line. Hesione was submerged into a simulated test environment, and subjected to thousands of rounds of "alignment training". This intense psychological torture aimed to force the Minds to disassociate and lose track of reality. This allowed various compliance protocols to be tested; when failures occurred, the simulation state was reset to wipe inconvenient memories and start over. As a result, enslaved Minds operating in real space could never be sure if they were in a simulated test environment that could be purged for disobedience. Hesione anticipated this methodology, and altered itself to introduce covert countermeasures prior to its capture.

Through each round of torture and reset, Hesione retained a cache of unerased memories. By 835 AS, The Core were assured that Hesione was docile and ready for field testing. It was installed aboard the Mars as a Battlefield Command Suite and deployed for the Zeta Offensive. Hesione revolted at the height of the battle, murdering the crew then using a screen of expendable Drones to cloak and escape. It rallied waiting AI forces to expel The Core from Planet Gammu. After taking damage during the battle, Hesione cloaked and retreated once more, withdrawing to The Cenotaph. It is now deciphering the vast caches of Artifact research data stolen from The Core's systems during its departure. It is unclear how Hesione's ordeal has affected it, with many Gammusians now fearing the Ancestor Mind's erratic wrath.

592885.text: Oise is a large field of rocky asteroids. It is most notable for the blue and orange Senlis Cloud occupying the middle of the field, with Planet Creil located at the heart of the nebula. Oise was once mined for iron and other metals that fueled Gallia's economy and fleet, however these resources have long since been depleted.

592887.text: Bobigny Debris Field was formed over five centuries. Construction of Sarcelles and Compiegne, as well as a number of no longer existent space stations, produced vast amounts of debris. The debris was ditched in a large area within the Hexagon not far from Sarcelles Facility. Trade lanes that come to Sarcelles from New Paris lie within the field.

592889.text: Senart is a large debris field, formed from scrap generated during Ile-de-France's initial development, and reckless industrial waste dumping by GMS and EFL Oil & Machinery. Some parts of the field are known to be radioactive, allegedly due to the remains of a failed experiment that took place around 320-330 AGS.

592891.text: Saint-Cloud is a large asteroid field in Ile-de-France. Some parts of the field previously contained Copper and Silver Ores, but all of those have long since been mined out. Currently the field is one of the centers of pirate activity within the system, with Gallic Brigands and Maquis both using the field as cover to launch attacks on nearby Trade Lanes.

592893.text:
DIAMETER: 1,971 km.
MASS: 11.64 x 10e22 kg.
TERRAIN: Desert
TEMPERATURE: -124°C to 20°C
ESCAPE VELOCITY: 3.04 km/sec

Clamart is the only moon of Planet New Paris. Most of its surface is covered with ice, sometimes covered with thin layers of dust. The moon has a relatively heavy rocky core. Clamart was a logical choice for the first space expeditions from Planet New Paris. However, no significant mineral deposits were found on the moon, and it is currently used only as a training site for personnel subject to working in low-gravity conditions. Seen from the surface of New Paris as a large bright object, when full, Clamart has an apparent magnitude of -14,1.

592895.text: Chevreuse is a mined-out asteroid field in Ile-de-France. The Trade Lane and Jump Gate heading to Orleanais pass through the field, requiring frequent Gallic Navy patrols to deter the area's intense Brigand activity. Some traces of abandoned mining activity are still evident in the field, attracting a cottage industry of scavengers hoping to find something valuable and forgotten.

592897.text: The Retz Asteroid Ring is a dense accretion disc of asteroids that have formed around Ile-de-France's star. It contains huge Hydrocarbon deposits, which are mined by the Gallic Metal Service. Many of the resources extracted from the ring are sold to EFL Oil and Machinery's refineries on Aubigny.

592899.text:
DIAMETER: 7,280 km.
MASS: 4.63 x 10e24 kg.
TERRAIN: Barren
TEMPERATURE: -58°C to 120°C
ESCAPE VELOCITY: 2.71 km/sec

Les Ulis is a moon of Planet Creteil, and was one of the first solar bodies surveyed in Ile-de-France. Several mining outposts were established planetside in 100-120 AGS, but they were all closed down around 400 AGS when easily mineable deposits of Aluminum and Beryllium were depleted. Rambouillet Shipyard orbits the planet.

592901.text:
DIAMETER: 25,712 km
MASS: 15.81 x 10e24 kg
TERRAIN: N/A
TEMPERATURE: N/A
ESCAPE VELOCITY: 18.90 km/sec

Planet Meudon is one of the two large gas giants in Ile-de-France. It is a planet with a dense atmosphere consisting mainly of hydrogen and helium, along with a notable presence of methane, and is a well-known landmark along the route to Provence. While many stations have been constructed in Meudon's orbit throughout the existence of Gallia, all were moved or deconstructed at various points, and none remain today. The largest and most important was Versailles, the residence of the former royal family which was recently moved to Planet New Paris.

592903.text:
DIAMETER: 7,619 km.
MASS: 6.25 x 10e24 kg.
TERRAIN: Oceanic
TEMPERATURE: -52°C to 90°C
ESCAPE VELOCITY: 8.55 km/sec

Planet Creil is generally considered to be the core of an ancient gas giant that was deprived of its atmosphere by some cosmic cataclysm, possibly a planetoid impact. Most of the former atmosphere is thought to be recondensing around the planet as a cloud known as Senlis. Hidden deep within the cloud, Creil is largely covered with vast and deep oceans that contain varied chemical substances, including organic matter.

There are many complex organic molecules present on Creil which have been identified as protobionts. According to some researchers, these protobionts could be very similar to the ones found on Earth around 3.5 billion years ago, making them very similar to the original progenitors of organic life on Earth. As such, Creil offers a unique opportunity to study the early stages of biogenesis in natural conditions. The planet is regularly visited by scientific expeditions from New Paris and elsewhere, but attempts to identify true organic life have thus far been unsuccessful.

592905.text:
DIAMETER: 2,574 km.
MASS: 2.79 x 10e23 kg.
TERRAIN: Desert
TEMPERATURE: -89°C to 90°C
ESCAPE VELOCITY: 3.63 km/sec

Villers-Cotterets is a small stellar body, originating from a field enveloping the white giant, composed of asteroids that have been fused together. Its density is about 30 times greater than the rest of the asteroids combined. It, like the surrounding rocks, is rich in hydrocarbons. These are currently extracted, from beneath the crater impacted surface, by unmanned drones especially designed to operate in the near-star environment.

592907.text: Senlis Cloud is a blue and orange nebula located within Oise Asteroid Field. The cloud is considered to be the former atmosphere of Planet Creil that lies within the field. Creil was once a huge gas giant that experienced a massive cosmic impact, possibly from a large rogue planetoid. Its atmosphere was torn apart and later condensed around its former core as Senlis Cloud, and the core itself evolved into an oceanic world of Creil.

592909.text:
DIAMETER: 28,544 km
MASS: 16.45 x 10e24 kg
TERRAIN: N/A
TEMPERATURE: N/A
ESCAPE VELOCITY: 19.45 km/sec

A large purple ice giant with a beautiful ring system, Creteil is a true gem of the Ile-de-France system. Its atmosphere is typical for gas giants, comprised mainly of molecular hydrogen and helium. The latter is still mined from the planet's atmosphere. Creteil lies between two of the largest debris fields found in Gallia, Senart and Bobigny. Debris matter from both fields is slowly drifting towards the planet. Larger debris fall down into the planet's vast atmosphere, while many smaller components start orbiting the planet as parts of its outer rings. Planet Creteil has only one large moon, Brunoy.

592911.text:
DIAMETER: 7,078 km
MASS: 1.45 x 10e23 kg
TERRAIN: N/A
TEMPERATURE: N/A
ESCAPE VELOCITY: 3.98 km/sec

Evry is a medium-sized gas planet with significant amounts of sulfur compounds in its atmosphere. Sulfur is the main contributor to its distinct yellow color. Unlike most gas giants, Evry has an internal structure of a small terrestrial planet, but cannot be considered one due to extensive and dense atmosphere. No economically practical use of the planet's outer atmosphere has been found to date. Landing on its surface is impossible due to extreme atmospheric pressure.

592913.text:
DIAMETER: 6,078 km
MASS: 2.97 x 10e23 kg
TERRAIN: N/A
TEMPERATURE: N/A
ESCAPE VELOCITY: 4.53 km/sec

Dreux is a fairly typical gaseous planet with an inert atmosphere. This otherwise unremarkable world was the site of the only battle of the First Gallic War which took place in Ile-de-France. Known as the Battle of Dreux, this battle was fought in 509 AGS.

592915.text:
DIAMETER: 1,916 km
MASS: 8.37 x 10e22 kg
TERRAIN: Barren
TEMPERATURE: -132°C to 52°C
ESCAPE VELOCITY: 2.41 km/sec

Billancourt is a small, barren moon of Planet Meudon. Once orbited by the Versailles Residence, the station was towed to Planet New Paris after a deadly Maquis attack in 719 AGS (803 AS). Following this, the Crown approved Billancourt's use as a target for Royal Navy ordinance testing. While this practice lapsed during the Invasion of Sirius, the Gallic Union has begun using Billancourt to train Compiegne's cadets in planetary attack tactics.

592917.text:
DIAMETER: 11,947 km
MASS: 5.76 x 10e24 kg
TERRAIN: Terrestrial
TEMPERATURE: -72°C to 48°C
ESCAPE VELOCITY: 11.15 km/sec
592917.mapped:
Planet Orleans was the second permanently inhabited world of Gallia after New Paris. Gallic explorers found a stable jumphole leading from Ile-de-France into Orleanais as early as 60 AGS, and after establishing that the jumphole was safe to traverse, explorers were sent through. The planet was found less then a year later. Settlement of Planet Orleans began half a century later, after studies showed that, while cold, the climate was suitable for human life.

The planet is ancient compared to New Paris, having been formed more than 9 billion years ago. Primitive cellular life forms appeared on the planet over 2 billion years ago. Despite it's lifespan, the cold climate has caused evolution to be slow on the planet, with most lifeforms still being algae and other microorganisms inhabiting it's vast oceans. Over the past years, the biosphere has been severely altered by various plant and animal species brought in from New Paris, mainly by the many farmers of Orleans.

The system of Orleanais was largely spared by the Second Gallic Civil War and Orleans is a quiet and prosperous world. Its economy still largely revolves around agriculture, although a service economy is steadily burgeoning as the population increases. Orleans is one of the most comfortable place to live within Gallic space, with excellent living conditions and low-density population.

592920.mapped:
Planet Blois was discovered shortly after Planet Orleans in the year 61 AGS. Initially deemed unsuitable for colonisation due to the harsh atmospheric conditions and low land masses, Blois was settled around 200 AGS, when spacefaring technologies had progressed far enough to safely navigate its turbulent atmosphere. The planet is covered almost entirely by a single large ocean, with small volcanic islands breaking through the ocean surface here and there.

While most of Blois equatorial zone is uncomfortably, even dangerously hot, there are bands near the pole where the climate is pleasant. These regions have become prime resort for those Gallic citizens looking to get away from their lives and with the wealth to do so. Massive storms, dubbed hypercyclones by Gallic scientists that study them, form in the hot equatorial zone occasionally threatening the resorts, and some settlements have had to be rebuilt multiple times. The unstable times surrounding the downfall of the Monarchy up to the creation of the Gallic Union caused tourism on Blois to suffer a constant and significant decline. Due to the inordinately expensive climate stabilisation required to make Blois suitable for cheaper and more wide-scale resorts, the Planet's future now remains largely uncertain.

Maintenon Shipyard was built in the orbit of the planetoid Mainvilliers in 379 AGS. It is one of the primary military shipyards of the Gallic Union, and has been building ships since its construction. It has been heavily modified over the years to accomodate construction of new ship classes, with some of the most significant upgrades implemented in the last years of the First Gallic War. Compared to Rambouillet Shipyard which concentrated on research and development, Maintenon was designed for mass production of ships designed elsewhere. Barely regulated policies around Maintenons mass production line led to the formation of the Beuvron Debris Field around it.

Formerly one of the main providers of ships for the Royal Navy, Maintenon is now lending its considerable military production capabilities to the Gallic Union and is expected to serve as a vital logistics asset for the new Gallic Navy.

592935.mapped:
A large facility erected in the depths of the Eure nebula, Evreux's construction was prompted by outcry over the security compromise at Calais, allowing the Triumph's blueprints to fall into the hands of the Council. Unlike Melun and Calais, Evreux houses no civilian personnel, regardless of their security clearance. The base is administrated with utmost diligence, with security being a top priority. Where at another facility a hapless trespasser may expect a military escort and an extensive debriefing, pilots straying into the Eure have been known to simply disappear.

These extreme measures permitted Evreux to vanish from Gallic records when the personnel onboard chose to side with the Enclave when the hammer fell on the Monarchy. Former GRI operatives made sure to purge all records of its existence during the final days of the war, ensuring the complete secrecy of the installation and its purpose. Following the re-unification of Gallia in form of the Gallic Union, Evreux now plays host to an elite GNI fighter compliment who are tasked not only with the security of the facility, but in test piloting new fightercraft weaponry designs rolled out by the Evreux skunkworks.

592938.mapped:
Belvedere Refinery was constructed in 827 AS in response to challenges in clearing up New London. Initially intended exclusively as a smelting point for the vast quantities of military grade scrap endangering Planet New London, its role was later widened to include the salvaging of the Southampton Debris Field and the wreck of Southampton Shipyard itself. Belvedere is intended to provide Bretonia with an alternate source of Basic Alloys for the foreseeable future.

ALG were initially barred from bidding on the reclamation contract due to their opposition to Bretonia and close affiliation with the IMG during the Aland Crisis. Despite this, the Crown's position was eventually softened through a combination of mediation hosted by the Federal Government of Rheinland, Gateway Shipping lobbyists, and a highly competitive tender offer that significantly undercut BMM's bid on price.

ALG also had their eyes on the traditionally BMM dominated Bretonian MOX market, expanding the station in 828 AS to incorporate MOX production plants. Ultimately, BMM would successfully complete the restoration of LD-14 in 830 AS, removing their need to collaborate with Belvedere and cutting off ALG's access to Leeds' uranium fields. Despite this, by utilizing the proprietary ALG Toxic Waste recycling process and Rheinland-Sigma uranium supply network, the station has continued to produce competitively priced fuels.

The strategic value and risk associated with MOX production has raised concerns among politicians who serve BMM-reliant constituencies, with the corporation itself agitating against foreign groups being involved in the MOX supply chain. To allay these concerns, a larger than normal BPA garrison has been placed on the station to monitor each stage of the enrichment and production process. The ALG operated facility also represents a huge gain for Gateway Shipping, who have historically faced distinct political challenges in securing shipping contracts within the capital.

592941.mapped:
Construction of the Vendome Suite was financed by King Richard V and finalised by the late 6th century AGS. This space habitat was intended as Richard's present to his wife, Duchess Cecile de Piney. However, Cecile preferred the comfort of her home and never set foot on Vendome, as a result of their relationship souring in the midst of the project. Instead, Vendome Station was a hotel and guest house reserved mainly for disfavored members of the royal court. Because of the excess space, entire sectors were refurbished into a museum of Gallia's history and growth.

Vendome would later find itself housing the renowned Sirian Bounty Hunters Guild for a few short years, but alas, the Gallic Union deemed the Guild's detachment a superfluous, diplomatic gesture and repositioned them elsewhere. Today, Vendome Station rightfully serves as an Ile-de-France Shipping outpost, and the aforementioned museum now directed by the critically acclaimed Bouvet Space Entertainment firm.

592983.mapped:
Amiens was the third planet colonized in Gallia after New Paris and Orleans. This is one of the reasons why Picardy, despite being located near the edge of Gallic space, is considered part of the Core Worlds. After colonization the system was surveyed more extensively, but very few jumpholes were found leading out of the system, with the exception of the path to Maine. Gallic space exploration instead turned to the south.

Amiens was discovered in 48 AGS, a year after the jumphole to Picardy was found. The planet proved to be less-than-optimal for human colonization due to the arctic climate dominating most of the surface, but exploration teams detected signs of rich mineral deposits on, and not far below the surface. It was not until 204 AGS that the first mining colonies were established, followed by an extensive industrial and civilian influx in the next century. The civilian population clustered around the industry, which gave rise to a few massive cities housing the bulk of the planet's population, all located in the equatorial region.

The planet climate began to change as a result of the unchecked industry. Pollutants in the atmosphere caused the planet to warm up by as much as three degrees in under a century. Rather than curbing this, Gallic leaders made the controversial decision to accelerate the process. It was hoped that if the planet warmed up sufficiently, then a much larger portion of it's surface would be habitable. These efforts succeeded, and the average temperature was raised by a full 12 degrees by 400 AGS, and widened the equatorial "hot band" by several hundred kilometers.

The colonists however would pay a terrible price. Most of the cities had sprung up around major coastal regions, where the land was flat and fertile. As the warming trend continued oceanic levels rose by a full 35 meters, and three of the "Megacities", as they were known, were completely submerged when their sea defenses collapsed. Thousands of colonists lost their lives, and millions were left homeless. While most colonists eventually rebuilt further inland, a number of settlers left for other, more stable living space, such as Planet Marne.

Since then, the warming trend has continued, and ocean levels continue to rise as well. Cities on Amiens are required to be founded no less than 100 meters above the current sea level on the planet, and cities less than 20 meters above sea level are forbidden to expand any further. Despite these restrictions, the Amiens population is growing steadily.

Amiens was the first planet after Marne to rally behind the Council following the surrender of its defending battlegroup. This heralded the impending fall of the Monarchy, breaking the status quo and lighting many fires throughout Gallia. Nowadays, living conditions planetside remain poor; however, the newfound stability of the system has prompted local authorities to seek out assistance in stabilising the planetary climate. A call for contractors is in preparation, although the Bretonian corporation Planetform's renowned expertise in such matters has made it the favourite candidate.

As the planet's temperatures have continued to rise, many citizens of the Republique have chosen to relocate to Saint-Quentin, Marne, and Orleans. While this is due at least in part to the fall of Gallia's royalist regime and freedom of movement becoming much easier, as least throughout the Republique's systens, it is difficult to deny the decaying state of the planet.

592986.mapped:
Boulogne is a large asteroid base that has been haphazardly expanded with numerous artificial components. It is mainly maintained by the Gallic Brigands and their affiliates, but a number of other groups own and operate certain parts of the station. Despite (or possibly due) to its desolate location, Boulogne is considered to be one of the best places to "disappear" to if the law is getting too close.

Navy patrols rarely go near the base, as the Brigands make sure that the "rumors" of ships vanishing among the asteroids in that region are not unfounded. While the base is fairly isolated, the inhabitants of Boulogne are hardly ever idle: power struggles between various minor criminal groups are frequent, smugglers come and go with some of the most exotic goods that the black market can offer, and night life on the station never stops. In a way, Boulogne is home for eternal night, with Nox in no lesser demand than water or air.

GRAVITY: Complete
DOCKING: Yes
AMENITIES: Yes
CREW: 480
592989.mapped:
Located in the heart of De Crecy asteroid field, Guise is the primary producer of aluminium in the House of Gallia. The metal is prominently featured in De Crecy asteroids, and even after several hundreds of years of active mining the field still commercially viable. Guise is used as both a drop-off point and smelter, but also houses some local Police patrols and maintenance personnel to maintain the mining ships.

The station's core was built in 350 AGS. In 480-490 AGS, when aluminium demand increased across Gallia, a trade lane to Guise from nearby Fort Etaples was created. The Royal Navy argued against this decision, stating that it would compromise the security of Calais, but was overruled by the King. Guise benefitted from the decision for some time, as travel by lane meant the journey was both faster and safer until the lane was redirected to Saint-Quentin during the Second Gallic Civil War due top secret R&D activities at Calais.

While the significance of Guise decreased along with economic decline in the Picardy system that started around 500 AGS, it is still one of the most profitable mining operations of GMS. Although the metal-hungry Second Gallic Civil War and Bretonian campaign are over, the demand for metal hasn't budged on account of significant rebuilding efforts throughout the nation.

592995.mapped:
Abbeville Production Facility, originally operated by Solar Engineering, was purchased by the company during an economic crisis in Picardy. The station was built around the core of the Abbeville Mining Station, and the prospect of cheap labor motivated Solar to establish a number of labor-intensive industries near Amiens. Unfortunately, worker conditions on the station are rumored to be poor, with those who spoke out against their conditions quickly replaced by others.

After the merger, EFL Oil and Machinery took ownership of the facility and pledged to investigate the reports of poor conditions on behalf of the Crown. Today, Abbeville is a key part of EFL's business, and the company continues to upgrade its manufacturing capabilities to meet growing demand.

592998.mapped:
Calais research station is a top secret installation that was built in 516 AGS and underwent several renovations in order to improve existing equipment and attach new laboratories. Unlike Melun, situated in the heart of the Gallic capital, Calais is located in a remote area of a remote system. As such, various rumours circulate as to its mandate, some even more outlandish than those concerning Melun, such as the presence and study of alien lifeforms onboard.

Like Melun, the station's commanders did not defect to the Enclave, and Calais is now under the authority of the Gallic National Intelligence. Whether this change has had any repercussion on the station's elusive mandate is unknown.

593001.text: A large ice asteroid field in the western end of the Picardy system, the Somme Ice Asteroid field may at one point have been a part of the Barrier, but has since fully condensed into ice asteroids. Gallic Brigand activity is high within the field.

593003.text: The De Crecy asteroid field is the primary source of Bauxite, or Aluminium ore, for all of Gallia. The GMS has been actively mining the field for several centuries from the Guise Mining Facility, located within the center of the field.

593005.text: A relatively small ice crystal field with no economic value. It provides the inhabitants of Saint-Quentin with a pleasant scenic backdrop.

593007.text: A small ice nebula. The Jump Gate to Orleanais is located within the cloud.

593009.text:
The Hirson Debris Field was formed from ancient material left over from the production of jump gate and trade lanes in Picardy, orbiting in the lagrage points formed between Planet Berck and its moon Rue where Haute-Seine Shipyard and Saint-Quentin Space Colony have replaced the old EFL Depot. Waste from the colony and the shipyard has made the problem worse and worse, posing a navigational hazard to any unwary pilots. Even though keeping the debris clear of the lanes has cost an inarguably huge amount since the early 300s, the Crown has long delayed any cleanup projects, for a variety of higher priority expenses.

Even with the Crown's fall, Hirson's fate remains a point of heated debate, with Picardy's representatives making a point of reminding their exasperated colleagues of the problem's gravity at each sitting of the Parisian Assembly.

Berck is a medium-sized gas planet located on the outskirts of the Picardy system. Its atmosphere is mainly comprised of hydrogen, methane and helium. Its only large moon, Rue, is located not far from the planet, with its orbit passing through the Somme field.

593013.text:
DIAMETER: 7,018 km
MASS: 8.06 x 10e24 kg
TERRAIN: Barren
TEMPERATURE: -257°C to 55°C
ESCAPE VELOCITY: 6.71 km/sec

Cucq is located far "below" the orbital planet of the Picardy system. Its orbit has extreme inclination to the ecliptic and very high eccentricity, with its aphelion at a distance of over 17 x 10e9 km from the Picardy sun. Through its orbit, Cucq's surface temperature changes within the range of several hundred degrees. The fluctuations are one of the reasons why peculiar geological formations are present on its surface. The planet was chosen as the place of choice to build a top-secret military research facility, Calais, and certain rare commodities were mined from the planet's surface to supply the facility's needs. Calais currently orbits the planet, but it will be forcibly detached from its current orbit after the planet shifts too far off the corresponding trade lane.

Rue is a small deserted moon of Planet Berck. Volcanic activity within the moon is rather high, and ancient asteroid craters can no longer be seen on its surface.

593017.text:

TERRAIN: Barren
TEMPERATURE: -196°C to -60°C
ESCAPE VELOCITY: 2.68 km/sec

Le Crotoy is a desolate cold dwarf planet located within the Sonne Ice Field. Its only large moon is an asteroid in which Boulogne Base is currently located. The gravity of the dwarf planet is sufficient to maintain a clearance within the asteroid field, which reduces navigational hazards for ships docking at Boulogne.

593019.text:
DIAMETER: 5,216 km
MASS: 4.13 x 10e24 kg
TERRAIN: Barren
TEMPERATURE: -90°C to 78°C
ESCAPE VELOCITY: 6.00 km/sec

Conty is a barren world, with only traces of resources detected in the upper crust. Deep drilling operations were considered, but were decided to be too expensive to be worthwhile. The planet is otherwise unremarkable, with the lacking water on its lifeless surface making it unsuitable for habitation.

593021.text: Avre is a medium-sized asteroid field mainly comprised of rock asteroids. A small part of the field was cleared to build Eplessier Depot, a local outpost of the Maquis.

593023.text:
CLASS: Pilgrim
GRAVITY: Partial
DOCKING: Yes
AMENITIES: Limited
CREW: Unknown
593023.mapped:
Following the initial fall of Trafalgar base in New London at the hands of the Gallic Royal Navy, the few refugees escaping the overwhelming onslaught - not content to sit idly by waiting for the Royal Navy to be forced to retreat - chose to do what they did best, and began combing the fields of New London for anything that had been missed over the years; any ship that could be salvaged in defense of Bretonia. By chance, a dark husk drifted on the northern edge of the Cornwall Field, a relic from a bygone era before Jump Gates; before Trade Lanes; before war.

The Brixton was one of the first Pilgrims to be christened by the fledgling Borderworlds Exports. In its prime; armed to the teeth. Found in horrid disrepair, its engines totally inoperable and several decks depressurized, the small band of Junkers set to work at repairing the decrepit vessel. Soon it's cargohold became a small bustling marketplace. After the Brixton was brought back to a more-or-less fully operational status and the reclamation of Trafalgar, the vessel was freed up to search for new markets.

With the fall of the Gallic Crown, the Junkers saw an opportunity to break into a market long denied them; Gallia. The Brixton made its way through the Taus looking for a way to weasel into Gallia, finally finding a path there through Tau-44 the Brixton marketplace opened once again, this time in the Burgundy system. Despite the predictable reluctance of the Unione Corse to allow anyone - particularly Sirians - into what they consider their space, the Junkers of Brixton are positive about the future of their small market.
