593026.text:
The Normandie battleship design was first deployed around 656 AGS (740 AS) for offensive assault purposes. These ships were produced in large numbers by royal Gallic shipyards until the early 730s (810s), when the battles of the Second Gallic Civil War revealed several critical flaws in the ships’ construction. Existing vessels were retrofitted to correct various defects, but no new Normandies were built - instead the modernized Richelieu class was developed. Normandie battleships formed the bulk of Gallia’s original Sirius invasion forces.

The Venissieux spent the majority of its service at Kusari's doorstep, ensuring that none would challenge Royal Gallia's dominance over the Taus as the Second Gallic Civil War drew onwards.

This was, however, the ship's very downfall, as it was hit by a streak of bad luck following the dissolution of the Kingdom and the arrival of the Confederacy as the successor state.

For its service in the border regions, the Venissieux was rewarded with the flagship title for one of the Confederacy's states, acting as the mainstay of the eastern fleet. While it marked a new age for the crew, it quickly became evident that the vessel would not fare well in this endeavor once it suffered equipment issues en route to the border.

Initially dismissed, the warship continued making its way to Kusari's frontier, however the unexpected invasion culminated in a full rout of the Venissieux and its subsequent near-guaranteed destruction. It was saved through the efforts of Gallic repair teams, and, despite the vessel making little progress in the field of battle, it eventually recaptured the regions conquered by Kusari.

Once the war had ended, and with control established over the reunified forces, the Gallic Union chose to scrap the Venissieux in 745 AGS.

593028.text:
CLASS: Arago
GRAVITY: None
DOCKING: No
AMENITIES: None
CREW: 0

Le Boulou was a joint operation between the IMG and Council meant to defend the system against incursions from the Edinburgh Jump Hole, where the IMG constructed the habitat complex and the Council provided military grade armor and weaponry. Even though the station was fully operational by the time of the invasion in 741 AGS, Le Boulou was never expected to have to hold off large such a force. The Montmorency Battlegroup was able to deploy bomber wings to neutralize its defenses, and move into the resulting blind spots where the station lacked sufficient firing solutions to deter the Royalist warships. Le Boulou to was reduced to ruin without being able to so much as fire a shot, and all lives aboard were lost in the bombardment.

593030.text:
CLASS: Henshaw
GRAVITY: None
DOCKING: No
AMENITIES: No
CREW: 0

What was once a mining project in the far reach of the Taus for BMM soon became the symbol of the Gallic invasion of Sirius. In Gallic hands, Indochine was used not only as a forward supply depot for the invading Gallic forces in Tau-31 and Bretonia, but later on as mining outpost for the GMS to mine the rich Berylium fields present in Tau-23.

As the front lines moved even further into Bretonia and its supply lines became overly stretched, the Gallic Crown commissioned EFL to build a trade lane between the Languedoc Jump Gate and the Indochine Outpost to aid the increasingly taxed supply line and to secure their dominion over the Tau systems. To that end, the construction of a more suitable station began elsewhere in the system that soon became to be known as Cheronsee Outpost.

However, while the Indochine Outpost security focused mainly in protecting the lanes construction, gate and mining operations against Outcast and pirate actions, they disregarded their own domestic enemies, namely the Maquis. In a daring and uncompromising operation, with the help of a turncoat operating inside and the increased traffic that was fueling the latest stage of the Royal Navy invasion, several Maquis operatives visited the station with false identification and security clerances granting them access to restricted sections of the outpost, planting several explosive charges over the course of days and avoiding the weekly security sweep.

With the flick of a button, Indochine Outpost was gutted from the inside out, with the reactor core reaching a critical status and finally ending its existence, alongside over two hundred souls. Propaganda videos of the attack soon flooded the Gallic media courtesy of the very people that turned the Indochine Outpost into a wreck, reminding the Crown of the Maquis manifesto and mission.

593032.text:
CLASS: Winchester
GRAVITY: None
DOCKING: No
AMENITIES: None
CREW: 0

Throughout the war against Kusari and later Gallia, Southampton Shipyard was always a vital manufacturing and production center of the Bretonian Armed Forces. The colossal structure was the birthplace of most of the Bretonian fleet. Its yards were organized around an enormous structure known as "The Bridge" -- an object of pride for Bretonia and a symbol of the brilliance, dedication and ingenuity of its people. That military significance made it the primary focus of Gallia's first forays into the New London system, and the reason for the subsequent redeployment of the York and its battlegroup to the station's vicinity.

Using lessons learned from Glasgow, LD-14 and Stokes, the Armed Forces took steps ensure that the station, only a stone's throw away from the capital, would not fall into the enemy's hands. As the blitz arrived, the Battleship York issued the demolition order. Several key structures - including The Bridge - were destroyed through controlled nuclear meltdowns of the station's reactors, stymieing Gallic hopes of occupying the facility as a forward repair yard. In the war's aftermath, the shipyard's twisted ruins were unceremoniously dumped in the Debris Field it once created.

593034.text:
CLASS: Dunkirk
CREW: N/A
ARMAMENT: N/A

The Battleship York was launched in 790 AS, and tasked with securing Leeds from pirate attacks. Over time, these duties extended to the patrolling of Tau-31 and 23 to protect Bretonian interests there. When the Tau War with Kusari broke out in 813 AS, the York led the initial Bretonian offensives in Tau-29 and 31, before being pushed back to Leeds in 816 AS. It saw extensive combat through the Battles of Glasgow and Stokes, and continued to be an indispensable linchpin of the Bretonian defense following Gallia's invasion in 818 AS. In 820 AS, the York delayed the Gallic spearhead as Allied forces retreated from the system, allowing the Armed Forces to disable the Jump Gates to New London and Newcastle. This stalled Gallia's progress until their scouts could locate jump holes into Bretonian systems.

The York then coordinated the defense of Southampton Shipyard, repelling regular raids from the Southampton Debris Field and launching fighter squadrons into Leeds in return. The York Participated in the Liberty-led 822 AS Operation SAVIOR, which attempted a counter-assault into Leeds. This succeeded in destroying the Oubli fleet, but failed in its primary objective of relieving Bretonian Army forces on Planet Leeds. When the Gallic Royal Navy initiated the overwhelming New London Blitz in 825 AS, the York's fleet carried out deadly delaying actions during the Battle of Trafalgar, before falling back to Southampton. In a battle stretching over 17 hours, it became clear Southampton would not hold, and a fallback order was triggered.

While shielding these efforts, the York was cut off from retreat by the Battleship Le Cendre. As the York buckled under fire, Admiral George Hall ordered crew to launch escape pods and locked his dying vessel into a collision course. The York slammed into the Le Cendre's engines before disintegrating, with Admiral Hall posthumously awarded the Golden Sable Of Freedom, the highest Bretonian commendation an officer of the Armed Forces can receive. In the aftermath of the war, the remaining sections of the York were towed to the Romsey Graveyard, where they await scrappage at Belvedere Refinery.

593035.text:
Newly constructed in 824 AS, Bochum was hastily thrown together by Kruger in an effort to help legitimize Rheinland operations and authority in Sigma-15. While the rapid funding and construction of the facility threw expected efficiency and budgets off by some margin, Bochum was fully operational by 825, handling both mineral processing from nearby Hammersee and fuel processing from gas miners in the Nordsee.

A location of strategic importance to the Rheinland war effort, Bochum was the target of Kusari's first real victory in the Second Sigma Conflict. Despite continued losses against Rheinland in fleet to fleet combat, Kusari's forces proved to be more mobile owing to their offensive posture. Using this to their advantage to cause a breakdown in Rheinland OPSEC, Kusari Intelligence forces launched lightning strikes consisting of gunships and fighter wings against Mecklenburg, the Bayern, and the Frankfurt jumphole for several days until communication had deteriorated, and Military forces were too focused on putting out fires to see the big picture. Amidst the chaos, an unmanned, captured Oder gunship packed with thermonuclear warheads slipped through the typically stringent security of Bochum's airspace, and came alongside one of the refinery's mooring fixtures, placing the entirety of the station within the no-survive radius before the warheads were remotely detonated. All hands were lost in the ensuing blast, placing the final death toll at roughly ten thousand souls.

The destruction of Bochum has led to a growing anti Kusari sentiment among the officers and pilots of the Rheinland military, citing the offensive as stare decisis for an underhanded and dishonorable doctrine followed by a nation they once deemed worthy of respect.

593037.text:
Renovations of Carrier Helios were completed on Sabah Shipyard in early 822 AS, and after initial trial exercises, the vessel was immediately deployed to Baffin. Although Gallic Royal Navy incursions into the system are few and far between, this ship has been tasked with helping defend the region in concert with the local Zoner leaders.

Sensing an opportunity in 824 AS, the Helios was repositioned into Tau-29, taking up the offense and striking out at the Gallic Royal Navy in the area. Combat operations were well underway as the Carrier lended its considerable forces towards offensive action, abandoning the defensive stance that held it in Baffin for so long.

As it initiated its new set of orders that involved to move to Tau-31, the Helios and its support task force was met by the Basilica, and a furious battle ensued. In what many call a close victory, the Outcasts managed to cleave the Helios in half, breaking not only the ship but also the morale of the Crayterian supporting forces.

Now, a smoldering wreck in Tau-29, the Crayterians have yet to decide to recuperate the wreck and tow it to their shipyard or to leave it there, a reminder of the price that Crayter Republic has paid to defend themselves from Outcast advances.

593039.text:
CLASS: Ribeauville
GRAVITY: None
DOCKING: No
AMENITIES: None
CREW: 0
INMATES: 0

La Fere was built in 364 AGS, only ten years after the nearby Saint-Quentin colony was constructed. Ironically, the convicts who were employed to assist the prison's construction were housed in Saint-Quentin until La Fere was completed. While prisoners did not form the majority of the construction workforce, several acts of sabotage were attempted with only one such plot being enacted. An explosive device detonated behind a bulkhead which caused an entire module to be jettisoned from the station, eventually burning up within the atmosphere of planet Laon. The only casualty; the convict who was foolish enough to detonate the bomb while aboard the doomed module. Though the act was only moderately successful, it did serve to highlight the dangers of a criminal workforce and the use prisoners was immediately ceased.

La Fere eventually became known as possibly the worst space prison currently maintained in Gallia. The facility was not particularly large yet held more than 40,000 prisoners at its peak, many being convicted for collaborating with the Council and Maquis. In 724 AGS after a barrage of reports and constant complaints, the Crown was forced to investigate conditions within La Fere culminating in the demotion of the warden and plans to enlarge the facility. Yet the outbreak of war in 733 AGS diverted much of the allocated resources, leaving the prison in it's heavily overcrowded state.

In 740 AGS Council forces launched a daring raid against the facility, successfully freeing the numerous supporters and criminals incarcerated within. The battle and subsequent riot by the newly liberated prisoners has left La Fere as a lifeless charred monument, dedicated to Royalist cruelty. While the Council's ranks and morale may have been bolstered by the storming of La Fere, the group's actions have also granted the freedom of thousands of hardened criminals who are new free to descend upon the unsuspecting citizens of Gallia once more.

593041.text:
The Battleship Gwent was one of four next generation Dunkirks rolled out of Southampton Shipyard in late 822 AS. Initially earmarked as a new flagship for the destroyed Derby Great Fleet, the Gwent was deployed to Manchester to oversee the shoring up of defenses against GRN attacks. This service was cut short four months later when the vessel was irreparably crippled by a Gallic attack group led by the RNS Embrun. With fatal damage dealt to the propulsion systems and core, the Gwent was towed back to New London for assessment.

BMM engineering evaluations bluntly indicated that the only people mad enough to use a ruined hulk in the Gwent's state would be the squatters inhabiting the Hood. The fiscal expenditure involved in restoring the vessel was declared inexcusable, while the political cost of scuttling would be disastrous. In a compromise, the vessel was superficially patched and re-pressurized, with a Crecy nuclear MOX reactor installed as a cost saving measure. Immobile and under-powered, it was redeployed to Planet Nottingham, Omega 3 early in 823 AS.

In 826 AS Bretonia launched an operation to nationalize Aland Shipyard, as Southampton had been destroyed. The Gwent's squadron of fighters and bombers was tasked with policing the Omega 3 System until the Norfolk's arrival. BAF Admiralty did not expect the Red Hessians to join the IMG's resistance, and the attack by the Red Hessian battleship Kassel came as a surprise. Not able to move, the Gwent was an easy target for the Kassel's bomber squadron and the battleship's forward cannon. The hull burst under critical pressure, but the ship's squadrons endured and kept the Kassel and the flotilla pinned, although at a great cost, until the Nottingham garrison was launched and reinforcements from the Norfolk arrived.

593043.text:
DIAMETER: 9,057 km
MASS: 4.81 x 10e19 kg
TERRAIN: Arctic
TEMPERATURE: -105°C to 11°C
ESCAPE VELOCITY: 10.73 km/sec
593043.mapped:
Aubigny is the cold, primary moon of Planet Meudon. Discovered early in the exploration of the Ile-de-France system, it was deemed unsuitable for colonization despite its breathable atmosphere because of its extremely low temperatures. Centuries later, when the planet's climate was studied in more detail, it became clear that human settlement could be possible in the equatorial regions, leading to EFL Oil and Machinery being commissioned to colonize the satellite. Between 575 and 650, efforts were made by the corporation to raise the temperature, taking advantage of existing Gallic terraforming technologies, and settlements quickly sprang up.

During the Second Gallic Civil War, significant deposits of fossil fuels were discovered beneath the glaciers of the moon, and the population grew in pace with the need for mining workers. Aubigny is also a well-known choice for server farms, with many dotting the icy deserts thanks to the inexpensive land combined with low ambient temperatures making such enterprises highly economical compared to the other habitable worlds in Gallia.

Despite previous population booms, harsh environmental conditions and the isolation of the central colony and mining settlements have prevented the moon from becoming more populated in contemporary times, and the newest generations born here report that they have great difficulty fitting into the more cosmopolitan society on New Paris and elsewhere.

Aubigny is also a well-known choice for server farms, with many dotting the icy deserts thanks to the inexpensive land combined with low ambient temperatures making such enterprises highly economical compared to the other habitable worlds in Gallia.

Despite previous population booms, harsh environmental conditions and the isolation of the central colony and mining settlements have prevented the moon from becoming more populated in contemporary times, and the newest generations born here report that they have great difficulty fitting into the more cosmopolitan society on New Paris and elsewhere.

593049.mapped:
Haute-Seine Shipyard was built in 578 AGS by EFL Oil and Machinery, on the site of a small depot that had shipped ice from the Doullens Ice Field. It was one of the first stations built in order to restore the economy of the Picardy system, and the government granted EFL huge subsidies and tax breaks in order to make the facility profitable. Moreover, because the GRN financed the trade lanes in Picardy for national defense reasons, the costs of shipping throughout the system to the shipyard were negligible to EFL.

EFL enjoyed these benefits for over a hundred years, until it was long evident that Picardy's space stations were in no real danger. Growing public outrage over this fact forced EFL into several troublesome corruption hearings in the Estates-General and funding was cancelled circa 680 AGS, though by that time Haute-Seine was already one of the largest facilities for producing civilian ships in Gallia. Today, Haute-Seine still serves as one of main civilian shipyards in Gallia, focusing mainly on the construction of mining vessels and midsized transports.

593052.mapped:
Atacama was the first outpost established in Vespucci, excavated in 811 AS by the Lane Hackers. Abandoned by 818 AS in favor of bases operated jointly with the now defunct Hellfire Legion, Atacama was soon forgotten by all save the tiny crew that once served there. With the formation of the Liberty Commonwealth in 822 AS, a number of minor industrial corporations and OS&C were invited into the system. This decision prompted a schism within the Hellfire Legion, who accused civilian leaders of importing Liberty's oppressive corporate structures and selling out the system's security for a pocketful of silver. A number of disgruntled veterans deserted the Legion over this perceived betrayal of its founding ideals.

These defectors restored Atacama and reached out to the Gaians for support with expelling the newly arrived corporations. The proportion of ex-Legionnaires dwindled through attrition with time, while Gaian recruits continued to arrive from Manchester. By 826 AS, the Gaians had become the majority onboard, and their objective shifted from attacking corporate interests to targeting the colonies of Veracruz to deter further industrialization. When the Insurgency succumbed to the Liberty Navy onslaught in 829 AS, Veracruz's colonies were destroyed and Atacama's importance waned. The base's garrison shrank significantly as Gaian agents deployed elsewhere.

For several years, Atacama maintained little more than a skeleton crew. Gaian ecologists monitor the recovering environment of Veracruz through Lane Hacker-compromised DSE satellites, while scrappers pick through Vespucci's battlefields to find components that can be dispatched back to Torshavn Space Port. As of late 834 AS, Atacama has been subject to probing attacks by unknown vessels. The regular disappearance of patrols prompted a call for aid, with the Destroyer Artemis being dispatched to investigate. In early 835 AS, the Gaians were startled by the intrusion of the Order Battleship Atum into the Sonora Ice Field. Following a tense set of negotiations, the Gaians assisted the Order with emergency repairs, and provided an escort into the Barrier of Field of Magellan. A number of Order specialists are now providing ongoing assistance aboard Atacama as compensation.

593055.mapped:
The Normandie class of battleships were first deployed in 656 AGS (740 AS), and designed for offensive assault purposes. These ships were produced in large numbers, with the De Grasse entering service at Fourchambalt Shipyard in 710 AGS (794 AS). The Council had extensively infiltrated the battleship’s newly appointed crew and command staff, while sympathetic senior officers within the GRN assigned the De Grasse and other Council-influenced vessels to the assembling Marne Pacification Fleet. As the fleet entered into a bombardment orbit around Marne in 716 AGS (800 AS), The Council openly declared their armed rebellion, with much of the fleet revolting to liberate Champagne.

The De Grasse was vital to The Council throughout the Second Gallic Civil War, leading the Council fleet during the Battles of Champagne, and later Languedoc, where it breached the Montpellier Minefield and ended Gallia’s seclusion from Sirius. During the resulting Gallic Invasion, the De Grasse primarily operated in Orkney, hitting Gallic supply lines and military targets of opportunity. During the GRN assault on Roussillon in 742 AGS (826 AS), the De Grasse broke the royal blockade, leading a refugee fleet back into Languedoc, and then Provence. It then joined Council forces preparing to invade Ile-de-France following the collapse of the monarchy. In the aftermath, the De Grasse was flagged to the Council-affiliated Gallic Republic, a signatory of the fractured Gallic Confederacy.

When Kusari invaded Gallia in 743 AGS (827 AS), the De Grasse was dispatched by the Republic to assist the Minarchy in Languedoc. It initially fought in the Second Battle of Ales, which ended with the loss of Fourchambalt Shipyard. It was later heavily damaged during the Battle of Agde near the Ile-de-France Jump Gate, ironically surviving only due to the intervention of the Gallic Enclave. Owing to extensive battle damage, the De Grasse was withdrawn back to Orleanais for extensive repairs and modernization. These were not completed until 751 AGS (835 AS), when the Gallic Union assigned the venerable ship a new crew drawn from across Gallia, deploying them to Languedoc for unspecified "border defense duties".

TERRAIN: Terrestrial/Volcanic

ESCAPE VELOCITY: 7.73 km/sec
593057.mapped:
Planet Tangier is a cold, rocky world that follows a distant orbit through the remote reaches of Omega-47. Volcanoes and earthquakes wrack the surface, unleashing rivers of magma and plumes of ash and noxious gasses that cast a permanent volcanic winter. Upon its discovery in 647 AS, Tangier was described by Corsair explorer Carlos Fuentes as, "a hell by which Crete can be called paradise." As a result, the planet was largely ignored until 810 AS, when engineers from the newly built Casablanca Base first established camps to survey for minerals. They discovered rich seams of metals, churned near to the surface by countless millennia of violent volcanism.

Before a mining colony could be established, the Red Hessians launched the Casablanca Offensive of 811 AS. The Hessians were quick to capitalize on the Corsairs' groundwork, developing the abandoned camps into a series of prisoner-operated mining colonies. By 813 AS, the penal workforce was bolstered with internal dissidents from the newly-allied Coalition, while Viernheim Station refinery was built three years later as a joint endeavour. The Coalition's deployment of an Electromagnetic Tether in 824 AS reduced the launch costs for atmospheric shuttles, further increasing the export of metals. Across this period, the Hessians came under increasing pressure in Omega-5, straining their commitment to Omega-47's defense.

This came to a head in 827 AS, when the Hessians withdrew the Battleship Kassel to exploit the raging civil war in Rheinland. The Corsairs quickly took advantage of this lapse with the Battleship Fes, destroying Viernheim and bombarding Tangier's mines. The assault was only driven off through the intervention of the Coalition Carrier Alvin Katz, which was critically damaged in the battle. With the Hessians unwilling to commit the resources needed to rebuild and defend Tangier, it was mutually agreed that its administration would fall instead to The Coalition. They have since repaired and expanded many of the penal colonies, however persistent Corsair raids from Omega-5, Omega-55 and the recaptured Casablanca Base impose a harsh cost.

593061.mapped:
The latest addition to the Orbital Spa and Cruise fleet, the Barbados sits in orbit around the planet of Iridescencia, a beautiful yet incredibly hostile world whose frequent electrical storms and volcanic eruptions wrack the sky, putting on a spectacular lightshow which changes in hue when viewed from different angles. OS&C has been quick to capitalise upon the spectacle by setting the Barbados' orbital path to slowly wind its way around the planet, giving visitors a once in a lifetime show on every pass.

The placement of the new liner has also caused controversy within Liberty as the Vespucci system is located in the heart of the Insurgency space, a nation openly at war with the Republic. To compound the matter, rumours have begun to circulate that Synthetic Marijuana, a banned substance in Liberty, is used and freely available aboard the Barbados, though the supply of which is unknown.

In light of Liberty's Navy offensive against the Insurgency in the years 829-830 AS, the liner temporarily relocated back to Cortez for extended maintenance, returning into the system in 832 AS, long after Insurgency was no more.

593064.mapped:
Asahikawa Outpost formerly known as La Charite Spaceport, was Ile-De-France's first endeavor outside of the Kingdoms borders. La Charite was built with hopes of creating a trade hub where Gallic and Sirian business interests could mix and mingle. Under the nose of the Kingdom, the Spaceport gave opportunity to traders who were not authorised to enter Gallia to still conduct business.

IDF has not fared well following the dissolution of the Gallic Crown, its primary stockholder, and it was under scrutiny by the law enforcement agencies of the Gallic Confederation for suspected collaboration with the Royal Enclave. Because of this, there had been talks among upper management of relocating the company headquarters from Sarcelles Shipping Platform to La Charite as part of many proposals to reinvigorate the company and ensure its survival.

Ile-De-France's plan met a sudden end with the Kusari invasion of Gallic core space in 827 A.S, causing the station to fall under Kusari administration. Following the end of the conflict, La Charite was turned over to the Kusari State Police and was re-branded Asahikawa Outpost. Now the KSP slowly converts the installation into a proper Police hub. In order to better finance this project, most of Asahikawa's storage facilities - much to the displeasure of Samura - are rented out to Kishiro, effectively providing Samura's largest rival a small foothold in long-years uncontested space.

Pittsburgh is covered by a single vast desert, broken only by large rocky outcroppings that were big enough to escape being swallowed up by the sand. Without any ice asteroids in close proximity, the planet was not considered a good candidate for terraforming and remained sparsely populated until a full-scale mineral survey in 650 AS pinpointed enormous deposits of Boron in the form of borax salts deep within the Corridera Plateau. A large scale mining operation was established on the planet in 660 AS by Deep Space Engineering to exploit these deposits, and it is now one of the only raw material extraction facility left within Liberty space.

Since the success of DSE's boron mining concerns, there has been an increasing need for miners and other workers. Many refugees that come seeking asylum in Liberty often get redirected to Pittsburgh to find work in the boron mines, and to live in the cities that are slowly sprawling outwards around the mining facilities, and Liberty authorities estimate that Pittsburgh's population will reach grow further.

Charost Depot was covertly excavated by The Maquis in 819 AS, the result of a collaboration with The Council. Carved into one of Tau-31's ice rocks, Charost was the Maquis' most remote staging point. Throughout the Gallic Invasion, it was used for guerrilla strikes on Gallic Royal Navy and corporate supply lines that stretched through the Tau systems to Bretonia.

In the aftermath of the war and the expulsion of the Gallic presence from Tau-31, the Maquis opted to abandon the depot, which had become an expensive, purposeless burden. On the rare occasion Maquis fighters roam into Tau-31, they are now more likely to be seen partnered with local Gaians.

593072.mapped:
The Luxury Liner Argenton is a "Lucullus" class vessel recently bought and refitted by the Unione Corse in order to compete with IDF Shipping's luxury business operations. It is one of the more legal business ventures owned by the Unione Corse, and the vessel contains all of the modern amenities one would expect to find on the highest class of luxury liner operated within Gallia. In addition, with its ever expanding reach into the markets of Kusari, Rheinland, and by some rumors even Liberty, the Unione Corse provide goods not commonly found in Gallia to those with discerning tastes - for the right price, of course.

Operating on the outskirts of the Tau-44 system following the discovery of a recently formed jump hole from Languedoc, the Argenton caters to a more diverse consumer base with a spectacular view of the system's unique scenery. Orbiting Malacca along the L1 Lagrange Point with Palawan, the Argenton provides an environment more relaxed and less under watch by the Union than any IDF luxury liner could provide within Gallic space. Apparently, Nox and other illicit goods are sold at late night rave parties that occur in certain secluded clubs aboard the vessel, but no substantial proof has ever been brought to light that this is the case.

593075.text:
A Gallic minefield deployed around the Lausanne Complex, referring to the codename of the Complex as Research Station 19. The minefield is hidden deep within the Vaud cloud, making any early detection of the minefield by passing ships impossible.

Authorized ships are guided through the minefield by automatic and continuously coded radio beacons, which provide much needed vectors for safe navigation.

Rumors circulate among informed sources close to the higher echelons in the GNI, that Lausanne's complement and automatic weapon systems are authorized to fire on any unauthorized ships regardless of their origin or identification.

593077.text:
CLASS: Gilbert Romme
GRAVITY: CLASSIFIED
DOCKING: RESTRICTED
AMENITIES: CLASSIFIED
CREW: CLASSIFIED
593077.mapped:
The Lausanne Complex, code named Research Station 19, is a top-secret Gallic intelligence base situated within the Vaud Cloud in the Zurich system.

Work on the station began in 732 AGS under the auspices of the GRI, and the primary purpose was to build a research station out of sight of other Gallic authorities, which would in turn allow them to conduct classified and dangerous research without directly endangering Gallia itself. Construction was completed by 736 AGS and all traces leading to its existence have been carefully erased from most databases in Gallia.

The security and secrecy of this research base are of the highest level, and to prevent information leaks, transfers to this base are usually one-way, often preceded by fabricated reports of the deaths of future station's inhabitants to prevent unnecessary searches for seemingly missing researchers and intelligence agents.

The exact extent of the research conducted at the Lausanne Complex is unknown, but a large number of prisoners have been brought to the station in the past and were clearly not expected to be released again. It is therefore safe to assume that new technologies requiring human subjects - advanced and questionable cybernetics and biological weapons - are being researched here.

According to unverified information from less than trustworthy sources, Lausanne Complex currently operates under strict lockdown protocols and the transfer of personnel between the Complex and its parent organization is severely restricted for security reasons. Reasons for the Complex's lockdown are unknown, but it is likely that there has been some containment breach at the station or that the research itself or its operations have moved into a more hazardous phase.

593080.mapped:
Scottsdale Refinery was originally the Deep Space Engineering (DSE) construction site for the Cortez - Coronado Jump Gates, part of a broader effort to invigorate the Crayter Republic’s economy and open it to Libertonian trade. The base served as the logistics hub for construction supplies and personnel assignments until the completion of the Gates, when plans were set in motion to decommission the station. Before this could happen, Liberty’s Hawthorne administration applied significant political pressure to encourage the administrators to develop Copper mining operations in Coronado's Sierra Vista nebula.

With the station re-tooling to attempt what many believed was an excessively risky and unprofitable venture, subsidies from Libertonian and even Crayterian investors ensured a rapid initial growth. Despite this, the remote nature of the largest deposits, the lack of a convenient shipping pipeline, and harassment by local unlawful elements left DSE sour on the operation's future. In response, Liberty threatened to cut DSE's state contracts if they downscaled the operation before the next Federal election. As a result, Scottsdale continued to produce nominal amounts of Copper for export back to Texas and Colorado.

By late 834 AS, Scottsdale was "complete", however frequent attacks on mining ships continued to depress productivity. The situation dramatically worsened the following year, when an energy pulse from the moon Jericho struck the station, knocking out most onboard systems. While basic functionality was quickly restored, DSE faces the difficult prospect of rebuilding its refinery hardware, and recouping the costs from Interspace -- who claim this kind of situation is not covered by a standard insurance policy.

593083.mapped:
The Oerlikon Observatory was constructed in 697 AGS, the first permanent base in Zurich. The facility was initially operated by Solar Engineering to study the unusual effect the local star had on the stability of jump connections. The connection between Champagne and Zurich was abnormally long and stable, leading many to believe that study of the specific qualities of the yellow giant could lead to innovations in Gallic Jump Gate technology. These plans were scuppered by the Marne Uprising a few short years later, cutting Zurich off from core House space for the duration of the Second Gallic Civil War.

In 737 AGS, Solar Engineering was forcibly dissolved by the Gallic Crown and its assets redistributed. Oerlikon came under the nominal ownership of EFL Oil & Machinery, however the Council’s occupation of Champagne prevented them from taking possession of the derelict station until the war’s end in 741 AGS. When they eventually arrived, they found much of the cutting edge equipment pillaged. After extensive lobbying, EFL was able to convince the newly formed Gallic Confederacy to fund the refurbishment of Oerlikon’s arrays. Despite this, the loss of Solar specialists meant their own scientists’ work quickly hit a frustrating dead end, yielding few interesting results.

Soon after, surveying revealed the possibility of a stable jump connection to Cologne, near Rheinland. Following initial discussions between the Confederacy and the Rheinland Republic, EFL majority-funded the necessary construction in exchange for tolls rights. Mere days after the Alsace Passage opened, the Rheinland Civil War erupted. Trade abruptly ceased, and Cologne fell soon after to the Red Hessians. EFL was saddled with crippling debts as their investment collapsed, with no prospect of recouping them while Cologne remained in pirate hands.

Desperate to offload these liabilities, EFL passed Oerlikon to the Gallic Union and waived its toll rights in exchange for debt forgiveness. Soon after, the Rheinland Civil War ended in reunification and the Hessians were expelled from Cologne. In the aftermath, Oerlikon provided the venue for initial talks on a broad free trade and security treaty between the two Houses. Despite calls to restore Oerlikon as a scientific outpost, the Navy instead divested the station to the Gallic Metal Service in 749 AGS, which has renovated it into a Molybdenum refinery. This has outraged the academic community, with some calling it the “worst case of scientific desecration in recent Gallic history”.

593086.mapped:
The main criminal and black market hub in Zurich and the first Sirian base in the system. The base was established almost immediately after the discovery of a stable wormhole between the Cologne and Zurich systems and was initially built as quickly as possible using prefabricated parts manufactured in Rheinland and assembled on site in the Valais Cloud.

The original purpose of the base was to serve as a smuggling den and liaison with the Gallic criminal underworld, however in this regard the base did not fare well at all - Gallic criminals and smugglers showed little interest in the installation and so the base gradually became more of a launching pad for armed Unioner raids and operations in general.

In early 828 A.S. Davos faced its greatest challenge when the Valais Cloud proved to inflicting a long term corrosive effect on the station's exposed structures, especially when it reacted with the station's leaking fuel. The base's administrators considered abandoning it at first, but ultimately decided to excavate a new base in a large asteroid in the cloud to provide the necessary protection for all sensitive equipment due to its operational importance in the area.

Work on the new base began around mid-year, and for this purpose the Unioners flew to the site with two tugs to tow the existing station closer to the asteroid to make it easier and safer to work on the new base.By the beginning of 829 A.S., all work on the new base was completed and the old Davos base was dismantled and abandoned.

Although living conditions on Davos can still be considered less favorable than is customary on similar bases, the crew and equipment are now considerably less exposed to the corrosive effects of the Valais Cloud.

As the base gradually became more important to the Unione Corse and the Corsairs after the Red Hessian's defeat in Cologne System, the Unioners were forced to intensify the supply of distilled water and alkaline salts to the base to neutralize the corrosive effects on the docked ships and to decontaminate the smaller ships arriving at the station.

Lapalisse depot is a relatively new construction by the Maquis in the Tau-53 system, built to serve as a refuel point for Maquis raids into Kusari when trade between the two houses started to rise. Work on Lapalisse was delayed, as shipments into Tau-53 from the Maquis' power base in Gallia came to a grinding halt during the tenure of the Battleship Venisseux in the system.

Following the turmoil caused by the Kusari invasion of 827, the Maquis have finally finished the construction of Lapalisse. Redoubled in their efforts to make use of the now fully operational base, the Maquis frequently engage into strikes against nearby miners and sometimes even the Misaki junction itself.

The Charlemagne battleships were designed around 676 AGS (760 AS), specifically for defensive and support purposes. Battleships of this class were configured to hold and maintain large numbers of fighters and cover them with powerful point defense turrets. By the time of the Gallic invasion of Bretonia, the dated Charlemagnes were used as the rearguard for advancing forces and for protecting vulnerable supply lines. The Battleship Le Cendre spent much of its service during the war garrisoning Ile-de-France and Lorraine, primarily combating revolutionary activity from The Council and Maquis.

In 825 AS, the Gallic Royal Navy committed to a doctrine of a final decisive battle in New London, stripping Gallia’s internal garrisons to bolster the invasion fleet. The Le Cendre participated in the initial Blitz of New London, incurring damage to its engines when the crippled Battleship York rammed it. Due to this, it was posted to the "Southampton Trinité" to protect the supply lines back to Leeds, alongside the Ambazac and Beuvray. Following the Beuvray’s destruction, the squadron was joined by the Battleship Athos -- hired Corsair mercenaries. At the climax of the Siege of New London, the Trinité was pushed into battle as reinforcements, to plug gaps in the battle line left by mounting casualties.

Despite initially performing well, the Le Cendre’s flank collapsed when the Athos was routed by the Battleship Essex, with the Corsairs fleeing into the Cumbria Asteroid Field. Unable to maneuver effectively with its damaged engines, Le Cendre was destroyed by the Bretonian 1st Cruiser Flotilla after an extended battle. The hulk was shunted into the Southampton Debris Field the following year, and as of 833 AS, had begun to be disassembled at Belvedere Refinery.
593092.mapped:
The Charlemagne class warship was designed in the 680s specifically for defensive and support purposes. Battleships of this class are capable of holding and maintaining large numbers of fighters and are equipped with powerful point defense turrets, yet lack powerful anti-capital ship armament. During military campaigns, Charlemagne battleships are used as the rearguard for advancing forces and for guarding supply lines. They are also used for system defense purposes. While stationed within a system, a Charlemagne also serves as a base of operations for the local Navy patrols.

Battleship Le Cendre's last assignment was patrol duty in the vicinity of the stable jump hole between Provence and Ile-de-France. Construction of the jump gate was scheduled to happen eleven years earlier, but the war and criminal activity postponed construction efforts, forcing the Royal Navy to deploy the battleship to that location.

Le Cendre is part of the "Southampton Trinité", comprised of the Battleships Le Cendre, Ambazac and prior to its destruction, Beuvray. Military analysts fiercely debated the intelligence of withdrawing so many forces from the Gallic Core Worlds, but their warnings fell on deaf ears as the Crown pushed for a decisive end to the war.

593098.text:
A gas cloud in the Zurich system that was once a single gas ring along with other clouds. A more detailed analysis of the cloud suggests that it is of stellar origin and corresponds in composition to the upper layers of the Zurich star. Current scientific knowledge cannot satisfactorily explain this phenomenon, as the Zurich star is not currently at the end of its life, but only in the first third of its estimated lifetime.

An increased electrostatic charge has been detected inside the Vaud cloud compared to other gas clouds and navigating through it is potentially dangerous without specialized sensors. For safety reasons, entry into the Vaud cloud is officially prohibited and all ships are required to avoid it.

While there have certainly been a few brave and enterprising people who have chosen to enter the Vaud Cloud for various reasons, most have never returned or the electronics on their ships have been badly damaged.

Acidic chemical compounds have been detected in the Valais cloud, probably formed by the reaction of a stellar gas cloud with rock fragments inside. Although these corrosive properties are not aggressive enough to threaten ships passing through the cloud, prolonged exposure can cause serious damage to ships' propulsion systems.

Civilian ships are advised to avoid the Valais cloud due to increased criminal activity in the area. Although the Gallic authorities are monitoring this area closely, patrols do not generally venture deep into the cloud because of the greatly increased danger and threat of losing their bearings.

The remote Glarus cloud is often used by local criminals as a place to safely and discreetly transfer cargo between ships, away from the prying eyes of both the law and other criminals.

593104.text:
A huge asteroid field orbiting the star of Zurich. A preliminary astrogeological survey has revealed that the field is much younger than the star itself. The structure of the debris suggests melting and recrystallization, so it is most likely a field formed from one or more planets or protoplanets that were destroyed when the yellow giant threw some of its surface into interplanetary space for unknown reasons.

In addition to providing a glimpse into the past of the Zurich system, the Bern field is also significant for its richness in metals, especially Molybdenum. Therefore, shortly after the settlement of the Zurich system, GMS began mining operations here and many prospectors predict that the importance of the Bern Field will only grow in the future.

593106.text:

A more detailed analysis of the cloud suggests that it is of stellar origin and corresponds in composition to the upper layers of the Zurich star. Current scientific knowledge cannot satisfactorily explain this phenomenon, as the Zurich star is not currently at the end of its life, but only in the first third of its estimated lifetime.

From the Verrier cloud, strange gravimetric data was recorded that did not match the related gas plumes in Zurich. However, due to the cuts in scientific capacity and budgets at the Oerlikon Observatory, no research has yet been initiated and grants and research goals are still under discussion.

Leading Gallic academic figures in astronomy and astrophysics assume that whatever happened to the local star in the Zurich system, it is the Verrier cloud that may provide answers to these questions. Pilots on both sides of the law try to avoid this cloud as much as possible and it is generally recommended to move only along its edge precisely because of its unpredictable properties.

Planet Avers is the only gas giant in the Zurich system. Although the chemical composition of it is unremarkable, and like most gas giants it consists mainly of hydrogen and helium, it is the remarkably strong magnetosphere and powerful plasma storms in the upper atmosphere that make the gas giant a subject of interest for the academics of either nation present in the system.

Although these storms and the strong electromagnetic interference that make any attempts to examine the planet closely extremely difficult, preliminary scientific theories suggest that Avers once formed as a regular gas giant, which then suffered the same catastrophic event as the rest of the star system.

Scientists on Oerlikon have observed anomalous electromagnetic coupling between the giant and the Verrier gas cloud, causing the plasma storms in the upper atmosphere of Avers to transfer their charge to the cloud, thus ionising it.

The belt orbiting the planet is of little economic importance, but astrogeological studies show that it is the youngest cosmic body in the Zurich system, having formed from a third moon that once orbitted its parent.

Ramsen is a medium-sized moon orbiting the planet Avers and is primarily of silicate and iron origin with rich proportions of rare and heavy metals. In the distant past, the moon's surface was baked and transformed into a glass-like wasteland like that of the much smaller Cresta.

Unlike Cresta, Ramsen has retained a geologically active core, and so its glassy surface is disturbed and cracked by many active volcanoes, which also give Ramsen its thick abrasive atmosphere. The moon's surface is whipped by electrically charged sandstorms of sharp volcanic glass that make any attempts to settle or mine the moon impossible.

593114.text:
DIAMETER: N/A
MASS: N/A
TERRAIN: Ice
TEMPERATURE: N/A
ESCAPE VELOCITY: N/A

Cresta is a smaller cousin of the larger Ramsen orbiting the planet Avers and is composed primarily of simple silicates with a thin methane atmosphere. The moon's surface has been melted and baked into a glassy desert in the past, which is undisturbed in comparison to the surface of Ramsen except for a few craters on the surface.

Astrogeological exploration of Cresta has not shown the presence of significant deposits of rarer and more valuable elements and minerals and so no economic exploitation of the moon is foreseen in the near future.

593116.mapped:
Planet Marseille is an oceanic paradise, with verdant archipelagos scattered across its lush seas -- it is also the only Gallic planet to be settled without royal approval. The first illegal colonists arrived in 599 AGS (683 AS), almost 20 years before a colonization charter was issued by New Paris. Early settlements clung to islands or ramshackle seasteads, trading novel sea life to Brigand black markets in exchange for supplies. These communities were fiercely independent, adopting codes of omertà -- vows of silence and non-cooperation -- in the face of royal authority being imposed in 619 AGS (703 AS). Drawn by the stunning vistas and pleasant climate, many Gallic nobles began to invest in Marseille, constructing luxurious resorts and docks that they crewed with their own serfs.

Many resorts quickly failed due to seasonal tidal flooding, or enormous sea creature attacks. Initially the natives were marginalized and excluded from Marseille's new boom businesses. This rapidly changed when the Unione Corse arrived, pursuing the scent of wealth and Gallia's aristocracy. The Corsicans noted that Marseille's independent communities were not beset by the same issues facing offworld investors, thanks to hard-won local experience. Agreements were struck soon after, with the Corse funding a number of resorts that were operated in partnership with local families. As these businesses thrived, rival entrepreneurs began to suffer accidents, or humiliating scandals. By 650 AGS (734 AS), the symbiotic Corse-Marseillian cartel owned or operated most of the planet's tourist trade.

Since then, Marseille has offered a lavish, if raw, experience to discerning travelers for whom budget is no concern. The explosive success of locally-produced Nox across the 680s (760s) saw further wealth pour into Marsielle, paving the way for local shipyards capable of producing the planet's infamous armed oceanic liners -- and allegedly, the Unione Corse's deadly star fighters. Marseille's fortunes waned during the Second Gallic Civil War, as tourism crashed amid fears of Maquis attacks. In late 741 AGS (825 AS), the Gallic crown abandoned the system following the destruction of the Battleship Arles and death of the Duke of Provence. After local communities were devastated by falling battle debris, the planet's cartels combined into The Minarchy, declaring Provence's independence from the Kingdom.

When the Gallic Kingdom collapsed the following year, The Minarchy seized assets across nearby Languedoc -- this fait accompli allowed the mafia-state to strongarm its way into the Gallic Confederacy with Marseille as its capital. This arrangement was short-lived, as the Confederacy was dissolved and replaced by the militaristic Gallic Union in 743 AGS (827 AS), as a result of the Kusari Invasion. The Union would not tolerate Provence's complete independence, but was equally anxious to avoid beginning its reign with further civil conflict. The Minarchy's leaders received substantial bribes to concede, and infrastructure investments connecting both Languedoc and Orkney. Tourism in Provence has begun to recover under the Union's autocratic stability, while Marseille's cartels continue to govern from the shadows.

593119.mapped:
Built at Rambouillet Shipyards for the Gallic Royal Intelligence, the Sisteron has since been the foremost vessel in Gallia's arsenal tasked with surveillance missions against the state's rivals.

Its first deployments came in early 826 AS, when it set up near Kusari's border, monitoring for any fleet movements. Enjoying a quiet post, it remained in Orkney until the end of the Kingdom, a moment in which it found itself with little contact to other Gallic forces. Choosing to side with remnants of the Royalist units that were left behind in Bretonia, the Sisteron became their main warship of the Royalist remnants during the invasion of Gallia by Kusari forces in the Languedoc system.

Shortly after redeployment back into the Taus, Sisteron found itself in the middle of an apparent Nomad invasion into the Orkney system. Being unable to face the aliens head on, it resorted to hit and run tactics, poised to give both Issoudun and Vierzon time to evacuate. After both stations were destroyed, The nomad activity in the area sharply went down. Despite that, a decision was made to lock down the system's gate into Languedoc system, and the battlecruiser remained stationed in the area to keep tabs on the alien menace.

Choosing to side with remnants of the Royalist units that were left behind in Bretonia, the Sisteron became their main warship of the Royalist remnants during the invasion of Gallia by Kusari forces in the Languedoc system.

Shortly after redeployment back into the Taus, Sisteron found itself in the middle of an apparent Nomad invasion into the Orkney system. Being unable to face the aliens head on, it resorted to hit and run tactics, poised to give both Issoudun and Vierzon time to evacuate. After both stations were destroyed, The nomad activity in the area sharply went down. Despite that, a decision was made to lock down the system's gate into Languedoc system, and the battlecruiser remained stationed in the area to keep tabs on the alien menace.

593122.text:
CLASS: C-20 (Capucine)
GRAVITY: No
DOCKING: No
AMENITIES: No
CREW: 0

Constructed in the Vaccares Asteroid Belt centuries ago, Toulon Mining Station was a Gallic Metal Service facility that was built to process the rare ores harvested from the local large asteroids.

As the field was depleted of accessible deposits, GMS determined the operation was no longer commercially viable. Despite this, the base limped along for several years on Corsican subsidies and the tiny quantities of ore still to be found.

It was the Treaty of Oerlikon that finally dealt the station its death-blow, as Rheinlandic minerals flooded the Gallic market. Facing falling prices, Toulon's operating costs could no longer be justified, forcing GMS to shutter the facility and lay off the crew.

593123.text:
Constructed in the Vaccares Asteroid Belt, Toulon Mining Station is a Gallic Metal Service facility that was originally built to process the rare ores harvested from the local large asteroids.

After the quantities of refined ore dropped to a level that was no longer commercially viable, GMS was unable to figure out how to re-purpose the base. While the base currently limps along on the tiny quantities of ore still found, falling profits and recent case studies have revealed better long-term benefits in stripping the base and moving the processing equipment closer to other mining operations.

This has left the future of Toulon and its staff, many of whom grew up on the station, in a somewhat nebulous position.

593125.text:
CLASS: Zidane
GRAVITY: Complete
DOCKING: Yes
AMENITIES: Yes
CREW: 670
593125.mapped:
Cannes Resort Station was established in 668 AGS (752 AS) in orbit of Planet Marseille. Initially operated by Bouvet Space Entertainment -- a subsidiary of Ile-de-France Shipping -- Cannes was conceptualized as a way of marketing the raw and unruly attractions of Provence to the domesticated aristocrats of the Gallic core worlds. Cannes provided the manufactured facsimile of an exotic, savage frontier, but with the creature comforts of law and luxury such clients had come to expect. As a result, Cannes has always boasted an outsized security force, and regularly played host to Crown and senior military officials.

During the tumultuous days of the Gallic Crown's fall, Cannes was temporarily closed. Operations only resumed after the Unione Corse seized control of the system at the head of the Minarchy, restoring a semblance of order to the region. Despite this, trade was severely depressed due to ongoing economic turmoil, and the flight of many of Bouvet's core New Paris clientele to either the Gallic Hebrides or Grand Duchy. Simultaneously, their parent company, IDF Shipping, was reeling from the blow of its many military contracts being abruptly dissolved. The bulk of Cannes' crew were laid off as a cost saving measure, with the station itself coming perilously close to being sold altogether.

While business has slowly recovered under the repressive stability of the Gallic Union, Cannes has struggled to draw in Gallia's newly evolving middle class, which see its parlours and concourses as an antiquated throwback to the old regime. IDF is loathe to invest the funds needed to properly renovate the Resort's offer, however they were impressed with the business model put forward by Orbital Spa and Cruise during their bid to purchase Versailles Station in 750 AGS (834 AS). While Orbital were unsuccessful in that bid, IDFS has instead agreed to lease Cannes' management contract to them, hoping the novel Sirian approach will revitalize Bouvet's flagging brand.

Frejus Base was built around 600 AGS (684 AS), shortly after the first illegal settlements on Planet Marseille. Initially established to smuggle goods to Provence's unsanctioned colonists, the Brigand hideout is notable for being the first location to experiment with synthesizing Nox's narcotic properties. Despite lofty ambitions, these attempts proved less successful than the Unione Corse's own experiments, with the Brigands eventually settling into the role of distributor for Corse product.

Brigand activity in Provence frequently targeted tourist traffic for ransoms, and the GMS mining operations of the Vaccares Belt. Despite this, most piracy was tempered by threats or bribes by Corsican enforcers, ensuring there was little need for a heavy Royal garrison that could upset the Corse's plans in Provence. In 740 AGS (824 AS), disaster struck when a Brigand raiding party intercepted and boarded a pleasure yacht that was bound for Monte Carlo Freeport.

The Brigands did not realize they had disturbed Corsican patriarch Carisio Lucchesi while entertaining an influential patron -- Felicien Leroux, nephew of Duke Auguste-Henri Hennequin. Both were killed during the chaos of the hijacking. The Corsican response was immediate and furious, with their agents boarding Frejus and massacring all aboard. When officers of the Arles fleet arrived to investigate an anonymous tip, they found a deserted slaughterhouse. The Gallic Royal Navy bombarded the station to prevent its re-occupation, then departed.

593130.text:
CLASS: Kelly Grace
GRAVITY: Complete
DOCKING: Yes
AMENITIES: Yes
CREW: 570
593130.mapped:
Orbiting Planet Istres, Monte Carlo was originally built by the Huissiers in 690 AGS (774 AS). The Huissiers were formed from minor noble houses during the First Gallic Civil War, receiving hereditary charters as royal spies with broad privileges and autonomy. They were the only citizens sanctioned by the Crown to leave Gallia, and carried out infiltration missions throughout the colonies of Sirius. Over the centuries, many Huissier Lodges abused their Charters of Enforcement to engage in blackmarket activities and enrich themselves through criminal means. Monte Carlo was one such example, established after the puritanical Duke François-Henri d'Avignon's 687 AGS (771 AS) decree, banning gambling and the sale of Nox in Provence.

The Huissiers' businesses had long since been forced off Planet Marseille itself, after the Unione Corse consolidated control over its resorts. In the aftermath of d'Avignon's decree, the Huissiers exploited the broad powers of their Charters of Enforcement to open a range of casinos, betting houses, and other "unsavory" pleasures the Duke disapproved of. While Duke d'Avignon was eaten by a Marseillian sea monster in 697 AGS (780 AS) -- purportedly with Corsican assistance -- Monte Carlo was already well established as a freeport and resort. Nox was freely traded between Brigand and Corse representatives, while lower class gentry flocked to the station's cheaper thrills -- Provence on a budget. The station's success was further bolstered with the opening of its infamous race track in 699 AGS (783 AS), drawing adrenalin junkies and bravos.

Monte Carlo fell into sharp decline during the Second Gallic Civil War, as Provence's tourist industry crashed. After the Invasion of Sirius, King Charles XI became increasingly paranoid and suspicious of the Huissiers, goaded on by their rivals in Gallic Royal Intelligence. Believing the Huissier's wealth and independence promised imminent treachery, he voided their Charters of Enforcement in 738 AGS (822 AS), withdrawing all royal patronage and protection. After massacres and seizures elsewhere in Gallia, the Huissiers of Monte Carlo fled, abandoning the station. The Corse quickly appointed several Marseillian families to continue running the station as a neutral Freeport. As Provence has slowly recovered under the autocratic stability of the Gallic Union, the Families have begun to restore the station's former glory.

GRAVITY: Complete
DOCKING: Yes
AMENITIES: Yes
CREW: 900
593133.mapped:
Monaco is the remote headquarters of the Unione Corse, orbiting Planet Nice deep within Mer Méditerranée. Established in 680 AGS (764 AS) with Huissier support, Monaco was originally created as a top-secret zero-G lab for the synthesis of the narcotic Nox. Nox's properties were accidentally discovered after Marseillian colonists consumed the carcasses of giant starfish that periodically washed up on shore. Improper cooking preserved the toxins of gut bacteria, tainting the meat and causing mild hallucinogenic episodes. The Unione Corse became aware of this folk knowledge around 650 AGS (730 AS), after cooperating with native cartels to seize control of Marseille's resorts. The Corse quickly began work on harvesting bacterial samples, and refining them to produce more potent narcotic effects.

Nox was a runaway success among Gallia's aristocracy, with demand far outstripping Marseille's artisanal production over the following decades. Monaco was constructed to house teams of blackmarket biologists and chemists, in the hope of industrializing the harvest of Nox-yielding bacteria. Early experiments failed, as the bacteria were symbiotically dependent on Marseille's echinoderms. It is alleged the Corse eventually solved this issue by transplanting several captive specimens into huge seawater tanks. Whatever the truth, Monaco-produced Nox has a distinct chemical composition, more intense psychedelic effects, and a premium pricetag. Flush with income, Monaco has consistently expanded over the years -- housing many of the Corse's most influential patriarchs and matriarchs in luxurious accommodation.

Between 741 - 743 AGS (825 - 827 AS), Monaco was privately considered the true capital of The Minarchy. The station benefited from the seizure and looting of Languedoc, as acquired taxes paid for renovations to install decadent promenades and concourses overlooking Planet Nice. Following the Gallic Confederacy's dissolution, Corsican leaders received substantial bribes from the Gallic Union to back the Minarchy's disbandment, and the imposition of Union law. Badly bloodied by the Kusari Invasion, Minarchy leaders were forced to accept, after negotiating a degree of autonomy for Provence as a Gallic Border World. The Gallic Union has so far avoided searching for Monaco out of respect for this deal, and to avoid upsetting the Parisian and Nevers elites who appreciate its produce.

593136.text: A dense field of asteroids, believed to originate from a small moon or planet that broke apart during Provence's formation. Once rich in rare minerals, the field has been depleted of the most economic ore deposits. GMS recently abandoned operations in the field due to mounting costs.

593138.text: A rather compact field of dust and small asteroids, the Camargue Dust Field is held in tight orbit of Planet Marseille and regularly trawled by the Gallic Metal Service's Toulon installation. Many of the small rocks and compacted dust within the field contain extremely rare metals and minerals, making the efforts of the GMS - and the illicit miners that they have tried repeatedly to stop - more than worth the trouble it takes to collect such miniscule returns.

593140.text: A field of rock asteroids, likely formed of fragments from a planetoid's collision with another stellar body. It contains trace amounts of useful resources, with GMS surveys of the belt revealing gneiss and schist formations laced with minuscule veins of rhodium. The nearby Monte Carlo Station has established a race track within, where many a Gallic youth or Corsican bravo has discovered their boasts exceeded their talent.

593142.text:
Mer Méditerranée is a massive blue nebula comprised primarily of methane and water ice. The tiny part of the cloud that touches Provence often changes shape as it is affected by the gravitational forces in the system.

The extremely slow but constant changes in this portion of the nebula have become a major tourism market in Gallia known as "Cloud watching".

MASS: 3.01 x 10e24 kg
TERRAIN: Barren
TEMPERATURE: -165°C to 94°C
ESCAPE VELOCITY: 6.71 km/sec

The barren moon of Cavallion distantly orbits Planet Marseilles. Though tectonically active, its weak gravity results in most of the volcanic gasses being lost to space. As such, its thin atmosphere offers little in the way of protection from solar hazards, and its surface is pockmarked with craters formed by asteroid impacts and manmade debris. Chateau d'If Prison Station once orbited nearby.

593146.text: Istres is a small gas dwarf with an atmosphere mostly containing hydrogen and methane. Monte Carlo Freeport orbits the planet closely. Istres forms a spectacular background visible to Monte Carlo's visitors, with its rapidly changing cloud cover and storms mesmerizing even the most jaded of tourists as they gamble away their worries.

593148.text: Planet Nice is a gas giant that lurks deep within the light-deprived environment of the Mer Méditerranée. The common gasses of the atmosphere means that there is no value in attempting expensive harvesting operations. It is orbited by the three moons of La Gaude, La Trinite, and La Turbie. The nearby Unione Corse headquarters ensures that very few outsiders are permitted to see this beautiful arrangement.

593150.text: La Gaude is the nearest moon of Planet Nice. As with the other two moons, it is fully covered with water ice and other frozen compounds. Unlike the other moons, La Gaude posesses no detectable atmosphere at any time.

593152.text:
La Trinite is the largest moon of Planet Nice. The surface is almost entirely covered in thick ice, though liquid water and volcanoes can be found deep beneath the surface.

This moon has a thin atmosphere mostly consisting of nitrogen with traces of other noble gases being detected. The core of La Trinite is still molten, so the surface temperature averages -100°C, warmer than either of its sister moons.

593154.text: La Turbie is the smallest moon orbiting Planet Nice. The surface is almost identical to that of La Trinite, being composed of ice and solid nitrogen. Traces of solid methane have been detected beneath the surface. For the brief portion of time that La Turbie is brought out of the Méditerranée, the nitrogen on its surface will melt and form liquid nitrogen lakes and a barely detectable atmosphere.

593157.text: Melun Minefield is an artificial spherical formation deployed circa 744 AGS around Melun Research Institution as part of its defense grid.

AMENITIES: Limited

>>>HIGH SECURITY<<<
593164.mapped:
Melun Research Facility is a top secret installation formerly operated by the Gallic Royal Intelligence (GRI) service. Initially constructed in the first century of Gallia's settlement, Melun enforced the Crown's exclusive access to Mennecy with an iron fist. The initial cadre of Scientists working aboard Melun would later go on to form Solar Engineering, bound by a personal contract with Gallia's monarch to develop technology on their behalf.

Unlike other stations under GRI management, Melun's allegiance remained with New Paris rather than The Enclave during the rise of the Gallic Confederacy. It is now administrated by Gallic National Intelligence, the successor of the GRI. Its mandate remains as highly classified as ever, but whispers surrounding its role in experimental infrastructure research are fueled by regular EFL delegations from Abbevile Production Facility.

593167.mapped:
Fleury-Mérogis was for centuries the largest prison facility in all of Gallia, housing tens of thousands of high security prisoners in its heyday. The facility was feared by the Gallic population, as few of the enemies of the Crown who were incarcerated there ever left. Rumors abound, describing a living hell due to inhumane conditions and complete anarchy in some cell blocks.

In the turmoil following the creation of the Gallic Confederacy, Parisian authorities requested a complete shutdown of the facility, arguing it was a dark reminder of the deposed Monarchy. The Confederacy eventually agreed to this, shuttering the prison and voting to finance the construction of a new penitentiary in Languedoc. Despite this, the practicalities of how the facility should be constructed was immediately mired in bickering faction-controlled committees.

With the emergence of the Gallic Union, the Grand Marechal personally intervened to cancel the Languedoc project, instead forcing the reopening of Fleury-Mérogis. Inspired by Rheinlandic examples, the Prison has been renovated to include a production line for military grade Enfer Blasters, where their distribution can be tightly controlled by the state. Fleury-Mérogis has already begun to fill with a new generation of political prisoners who are to be put to work for the good of the Gallic Navy.

Mennecy is a small, airless moon of Planet Creteil. Officially, it is an ordinary solar body comprised of methane ice and silicates of no economic note. Despite this, access to the moon was jealously guarded by the Gallic crown for centuries, protected with minefields, weapon platforms and armed patrols. The Gallic Union has continued with this approach. Many say that Melun Research Facility was built in orbit for a specific purpose, and that there must be something incredibly valuable hidden under Mennecy's surface to justify the level of cost and paranoia.

593171.mapped: The Pontus Cloud is situated in orbit of one of the two stars of the Tau-61 system and primarily composed of icy fragments of water, hydrogen and methane. Gravimetric disturbances indicate the presence of a sizable celestial body within its depths.

593174.mapped:
The flagship of the Gallic Union, this venerable battleship has also served a pivotal role in establishing Gallia as a superpower worthy of challenging the other Houses.

Representative of Royal Gallia's technological advancement, the Dax served as a backwater defense vessel for much of the Second Gallic Civil War, guarding Planet Harris. However, during the Blitz on New London, the battleship was sent as the vanguard of the Royal forces, and despite only relative successes, it broke through the Allied Blockade and staged some of the first planetary bombardments.

Once the tide of the war had turned against Gallia, the Dax escaped to the Taus, where it was stationed for much of 742 AGS. Enjoying a relative victory in making the exiled Gallic Royal a regional power, with the arrival of stronger Bretonian forces, the warship departed for Gallia once more.

With minimal damage after the withdrawal, and, after the Gallic Reunification, the Dax took up position in Ile-de-France as Gallia's foremost defender.

>>>CAUTION: EXTREME HAZARD<<<

This object does not conform to any known scanner profile. The Pylon is generating vast quantities of energy and appears to be linked to the surrounding structures. The artifact is evidently ancient and of alien origin, and is likely responsible for maintaining the Earhart pocket within hyperspace.

Researchers working for The Order have correlated pulses of energy within the Pylon with shifting phase alignments of Jump Holes across the sector. Whether the structure is reacting to or controlling these fluctuations remains subject to intense debate.

Power readings emitted from the Pylon have incrementally escalated over the period of human observation. Significant bursts were detected in 834 AS, and again in 836 AS following "The Blink". In the aftermath of this event, the Pylon's rotations accelerated, entering what the LSF are terming an "activation state".

It is speculated that the Pylon may have existed for millennia in a dormant state, and has been slowly reawakened by external stimuli across Sirius.

593181.text:
>>>CAUTION: EXTREME HAZARD<<<

This object does not conform to any known scanner profile. It appears to be focusing vast quantities of energy into the object at its core, enclosing it in an impenetrable field. While the artifact is evidently ancient and of alien origin, little has been conclusively discerned about its purpose or contents.

MND scouts have taken to calling the structure "Gefängnis", believing it to be a quarantine or prison to secure an object or entity. The LSF conversely suspects the structure is an power tap, either extracting or injecting vast quantities of energy into the fabric of Hyperspace, potentially acting as a load-balancing mechanism for the long-coveted Daam-K’vosh Energy Field.

The Order believe the structure may be concentrating energy into a central compression chamber to produce as-yet unidentified materials, similar to the gravimetric lenses found in Fischer. The KOI's suspicions are that the structure is somehow tied to dimensional manipulation and the disappearance of the Daam-K’vosh, and have taken to referring to it as the "Ascension Engine".

So far, none of the observers have been able to agree on how the structure is powered, or even whether it is drawing reserves from the orbiting structures, or offloading charge into them as a failsafe.

A beacon demarcating a favorable entry point into the planet's atmosphere for small vessels.
593188.mapped: Initially discovered by the Gas Miners Guild (GMG) in 620 AS, the planet Kurile exists at the heart of an anomaly, a gravitational tidal pool that creates a clear zone in the middle of the otherwise treacherous nebula. The planet itself is entirely covered in water with a saline content so high that it is toxic to almost all known aquatic life elsewhere in Sirius. Despite this, Kurile possesses a single native life form, a microorganism that manages to thrive in its otherwise poisonous oceans. Samura eventually managed to construct a collection platform on Kurile to harvest the microorganisms for use at the fisheries on Planet Junyo. The planet harbors some 2500 workers, all of whom live on the floating platform.

593189.text: Initially discovered by the Gas Miners Guild (GMG) in 620 AS, the planet Kurile exists at the heart of an anomaly, a gravitational tidal pool that creates a clear zone in the middle of the otherwise treacherous nebula. The planet itself is entirely covered in water with a saline content so high that it is toxic to almost all known aquatic life elsewhere in Sirius. Despite this, Kurile possesses a single native life form, a microorganism that manages to thrive in its otherwise poisonous oceans. Samura eventually managed to construct a collection platform on Kurile to harvest the microorganisms for use at the fisheries on Planet Junyo. The planet harbors some 2500 workers, all of whom live on the floating platform.

593191.text:
CLASS: Triomphant (Refit)
CREW: CLASSIFIED
ARMAMENT: CLASSIFIED
593191.mapped:
Constructed for rearguard duties, the Saumur never saw action beyond basic patrols of controlled space. This, along with its outdated design, turned it into the ideal vessel for housing a military academy, from where recruits could be sent to the regions most lacking in manpower.

With little in the way of defending itself, the Saumur surrendered to the Council once the Picardy system reached an open revolt. For this very reason, the Confederacy that followed chose to keep the outdated warship in the same system, although without any substantial changes to the ship's armaments, rendering the Saumur as a lost cause should large battles involve it.

It continues to serve as Picardy's stalwart defender against Brigand and Maquis activity to this day.
