The Charlemagne battleships were designed around 676 AGS (760 AS), specifically for defensive and support purposes. Battleships of this class were configured to hold and maintain large numbers of fighters and cover them with powerful point defense turrets. By the time of the Gallic invasion of Bretonia, the dated Charlemagnes were used as the rearguard for advancing forces and for protecting vulnerable supply lines.

The Battleship Arles was long considered the best position an officer of the Royal Navy could ask for -- assuming they wanted to be as far from combat as possible. First participating in operations against The Council in Burgundy, the Arles was tasked in 726 AGS (810 AS) with the defense of Marseille and Cannes. The infrequency of pirate raids against the resorts -- likely due to the Unione Corse's affiliation with both operations -- left the Arles' sailors with little to do for the better part of twenty years. Shore leave was freely authorized, and many of the garrison's senior roles were gifted to the sons and daughters of favored nobles. The remainder were filled by officers that had not served adequately on the front, but the Royal Navy were unable to dispose of for political reasons.

In 741 AGS (825 AS), The Council surged into Provence from Languedoc, spearheaded by the Battleship Oblique. Commanded by the Duke of Provence himself (Auguste-Henri Hennequin d'Avignon), the pride of Provence's garrison met the forces of the Council in Planet Marseille's orbit. During the so-called "Clash of the Titans", both the Arles and the Oblique were destroyed outright. The Council's depleted forces retreated to Champagne, and the crippled Royal garrison fell back to Ile-de-France -- creating the power vacuum later exploited by The Minarchy. The wreckage of the Arles, however, remained -- its unspent ordinance and molten hull plating raining down upon the former resort planet. EFL is now working to salvage the Arles' wreckage, however progress has been glacially slow.

593197.text:
CLASS: Monte Cristo
GRAVITY: None
DOCKING: No
AMENITIES: None
CREW: 0
INMATES: 0

Chateau d'lf was constructed shortly before the eruption of the Second Gallic Civil War, completed in 711 AGS (795 AS). A joint project between the Police and Royal Navy, the facility was designed as a remote supermax prison in the Gallic border worlds, where Champagne dissidents could be isolated. The prison quickly became a quarantine for captive Council and Maquis agents, in the hopes of avoiding the radicalization of other provincial convict populations. Inmates were left shivering in cramped, dimly-lit steel cubes, and fed with rations that were often maggot-ridden and stale. By contrast, guards were hosted comfortably, with fittings and meals imported directly from the resorts of Marseilles.

Following the Gallic Invasion of Sirius in 734 AGS (818 AS), Chateau d'lf was used to hold Sirian prisoners -- again, to minimize the exposure of Gallic convicts to outside influences. Notable examples included the Gaians of Kirkwall Base in Orkney, who were held hostage to ensure the Gaians' compliance with Gallic occupation. In 741 AGS (825 AS), much of Chateau d'lf's fighter garrison was dispatched to assist the Arles fleet with repelling a Council invasion led by the Battleship Oblique. While the prison's defenses were vulnerable, The Maquis launched their own assault, breaching the facility with freighters full of fire-teams. After almost a day of heavy fighting, the Maquis subdued the station, executing any captive guards.

Hundreds of prisoners died during the action, through combat, smoke inhalation, and vacuum exposure. Despite this, the Maquis still successfully evacuated thousands of prisoners before detonating bombs throughout the station. Following the collapse of the Gallic crown the following year, several fruitless proposals on salvaging or restoration were made by The Minarchy and the Union Corse. These came to nothing, and the gutted hulk was left to drift -- with most hoping it will eventually break up on its own and crash into Cavallion.

593199.text:
Previously a rearguard for the Gallic advance into Sirius, the Battleship Betheny followed the much more advanced Carcassonne as it departed the main bulk of forces at Leeds for a new target - California. Guarding the former flagship's flank as it secured a foothold into Liberty's doorstep, the Betheny then saw itself deployed to the Cortez system, stretching the front-line even farther as the Royal Navy made a bid to constrict the crucial supply line from Liberty to the besieged Bretonian state.

Betheny's presence in the system ground trade to a crawl, even with the deployment of the Yukon as a counterweight. While the Alberta-Poole hypergate lane kept Bretonia afloat, its eventual discovery and sabotage by Royal Intelligence put the focus of war planners on both sides back on the crucial artery of Cortez, and the Betheny battlegroup in particular. Quickly outnumbered and outgunned, the Betheny nevertheless held the line in a desperate last stand, crippling the Yukon as it went up in flames. Now little more than a burning husk, the Betheny stands as both a rare trophy for the beleaguered Allies, and a blow to the Royal Navy's once unshakeable belief in their war strategy.

593201.text:
CLASS: Eagle
CREW: 0
ARMAMENT: N/A

Commissioned in 745 AS, the Yukon was one of Liberty's oldest serving vessels at the start of the Gallic War, with some senior officers joking that it was more "modernization package" than hull. The battleship's wartime presence as California's garrison ship is seen in hindsight as a symptom of deep-seated complacency among Liberty's military planners, who could not conceive of an enemy capable of defeating the might of the Liberty Navy. When the Gallic Carcassonne fleet breached California and destroyed San Diego Border Station in 824 AS, Congress was thrown into panic. The outmatched Yukon was quickly pulled back to Planet Los Angeles and reinforced by the Battleship Alma from Hudson.

While the Alma tackled the Carcassone, the Yukon was ordered to link up with Bretonia's Battleship Harlow for a joint offensive into Cortez. This bid to re-open a desperately needed supply artery to New London was quickly complicated by the counter-attack of Gallia's Betheny fleet. After months of feints, raids, and counter-raids, the Betheny divided its forces to lure the Harlow away, in what West Point begrudgingly studies as a masterpiece of deception warfare. The Yukon fleet found itself isolated and under attack by the heavier and more modern Valor. The Yukon suffered extensive damage in the resulting battle, with the crew tenaciously fighting a delaying action to buy time for Allied reinforcements to arrive.

The Yukon fell shortly after the Harlow entered the fight, however the damage the battleship and its escorts inflicted on its bitter enemy turned the tide of the ensuing battle. The Yukon's last stand resulted in the award of multiple Lone Star medals for heroism, and is a popular subject of novels, games, and holoreels in post-war Liberty. The wreckage of the battle eventually formed the Aruba Debris Field -- work to scrap the Yukon's broken hulk began in 828 AS.

593203.text:
CLASS: Arago
GRAVITY: None
DOCKING: No
AMENITIES: None
CREW: 0

Perpignan Spaceport was built in 818 AS as a framework for a future trading outpost in the Roussillon system. Since not much trade actually took place along the surrounding war-torn region, it served as a supply station and a defensive hub to keep the system secured from possible intruders. The spaceport was located on the edge of the Ariege Nebula, halfway between planets Toulouse and Foix.

After the fall of Le Boulou Outpost Council forces gathered at the station to form several defensive lines between the Montmorency Battlegroup and Toulouse to cover the planet's evacuation, with the venerable Battleship Pamiers assigned to be the flagship of this defensive contingent.

The spaceport held into 826 AS but defences failed when Montmorency battered its way almost into point defence weapons range. At such a short-range Perpignan stood no chance, the station was reduced to a glowing wreck in a matter of minutes. Battleship Pamiers withdrew to Toulouse, poised to buy as much time as possible for the evacuation. The fighting soon resumed, ending with the Council's defeat. Perpignan's Wreck is now a desolate reminder of the battles fought.

593206.text:
CLASS: Normandie
CREW: N/A
ARMAMENT: N/A

The Normandie battleship design was first deployed around 656 AGS (740 AS) for offensive assault purposes. These ships were produced in large numbers by royal Gallic shipyards until the early 730s (810s), when the battles of the Second Gallic Civil War revealed several critical flaws in the ships’ construction. Existing vessels were retrofitted to correct various defects, but no new Normandies were built - instead the modernized Richelieu class was developed. Normandie battleships formed the bulk of Gallia’s original Sirius invasion forces.

The Beuvray was initially stationed in Burgundy and saw heavy fighting during the Second Gallic Civil War against The Council -- it later served as the system garrison. Upon being relieved by the Rocroi in 825 AS, the Beuvray was assigned to the Bretonian front for the planned decisive battle in New London. During the London Blitz, the vessel acted as the command ship for the Southampton Trinité. It was widely seen as the most capable and modern ship of the formation, however its experienced crew frequently complained bitterly that their breakthrough capabilities were wasted in the rearguard.

When the Battleship Embrun withdrew from Manchester, Liberty began to surge supplies towards the Bretonian capital through the weakened blockade. The Beuvray and Guillestre fleets ordered to seize the Kensington junction to sever this logistics artery. The extended campaign inflicted heavy casualties during clashes with the Allied MacDuff and Gettysburg fleets. The offensive came to a head when Gallic Royal Intelligence reported that the Gettysburg had suffered damage and retreated to Cambridge. Exploiting the initiative, the Gallic fleets immediately launched a renewed attack, quickly breaking through to Kensington and inflicting heavy damage.

The tide turned when the Gettysburg emerged from the Devon Asteroid Field, successfully executing a deadly trap. Caught between two battleships, the Beuvray was run down by packs of Liberty Siege Cruisers while attempting to withdraw. Their powerful siege cannons detonated the Beuvray’s magazines, blasting the ship apart. A massive reactor meltdown followed, scattering contaminated material across the Hounslow Debris Field. The fragments of the ship that were safe to access were shunted into the Southampton Debris Field later that year, where it awaits eventual disassembly at Belvedere Refinery.

593208.text: A fighter of the Bretonia Armed Forces. It was destroyed fighting Gallic forces in orbit of New London.

593210.text: The wreck of a fighter from the Liberty Navy's expeditionary force in Bretonia. It was destroyed fighting Gallic Royal Navy forces.

593212.text: One of hundreds of Royal Navy fighters destroyed during Gallia's final push on Planet New London.

593214.text: A casualty from the fighter wings of the Athos battlegroup, a Corsair fleet that joined forces with the Gallic Royalists.

593216.text:
CLASS: Charlemagne
CREW: N/A
ARMAMENT: N/A

The Charlemagne battleships were designed around 760 AS, specifically for defensive and support purposes. Battleships of this class were configured to hold and maintain large numbers of fighters and cover them with powerful point defense turrets. By the time of the Gallic invasion of Bretonia, the dated Charlemagnes were used as the rearguard for advancing forces and for protecting vulnerable supply lines.

The Battleship Castres was among the most modern of the Charlemagnes, and served in the invasion vanguard as a forward carrier. Seeing action in Edinburgh and later Leeds, the Castres battlegroup was in 825 AS assigned to provide frontline support for the Dax and Nogent-le-Rotrou fleets for the anticipated decisive battle in New London. During the New London Blitz, Castres strike squadrons significantly damaged the Bretonian Battleship York, allowing it to be dispatched by the Le Cendre.

Operating in the second line behind the Dax and Nogent-le-Rotrou, the Castres' forces were responsible for ensuring the siege fleets' flanks were not attacked by Liberty forces advancing from Kensington and Cambridge. In the final climactic battle in New London orbit, the Castres was drawn into a prolonged engagement with the Battleship Suffolk, which had refused to withdraw to buy time for the scattered Allied fleet to regroup. Facing all three of the Gallic fleet anchors, the Suffolk was destroyed, but not before inflicting serious damage on the Castres and disrupting the Dax's orbital bombardment.

The Allied counter-attack led by the Dreadnought Warwick arrived soon after, while countless civilian craft launched from Planet New London in a desperate attempt to prevent further bombardment. The Castres was pinned in place by these desperate wave attacks, allowing the Warwick and Liberty’s Ottawa to close distance and tear it to pieces. The hulk was shunted into the Southampton Debris Field the following year, where it still awaits eventual disassembly at Belvedere Refinery.

593218.text:
CLASS: Dunkirk
CREW: N/A
ARMAMENT: N/A

Deployed from Southampton Shipyard in 797 AS, the Battleship Suffolk was Her Majesty's chief display of military might, and the flagship of the Bretonian Armed Forces. Initially stationed between Planet New London and the Cumbria Asteroid Field, the Suffolk was responsible for protecting civilian and commercial traffic across the system, as well as deterring potential Molly attacks on the capital. During the Gallic War, the Suffolk commanded the New London garrison, one of the largest Bretonian fleets of the conflict.

In this capacity it saw action at the Battle of Durham during the retreat from Leeds, and over the following years, provided a reserve of reinforcements to repel attacks in Manchester and Newcastle. Most notably, it formed the centerpiece of the Allied defense during Invasion of New London in 825 AS. During the following year’s final battle for Planet New London's orbit, the Allied forces were thrown into disarray and forced to retreat, exposing the capital to deadly bombardment. The Suffolk fleet disobeyed orders to withdraw, instead skirmishing alone against the combined Gallic siege force as a desperate diversion.

The Suffolk's last stand lasted almost 6 hours, as it tenaciously harassed the Gallic formation. As the engagement continued, the Suffolk fleet was gradually whittled away while the battleship itself suffered increasingly heavy damage. When the Dax finally opened fire on Buckingham Palace, Admiral Foyer ordered all ships forward in a suicidal attempt to disrupt the attack. The Dax was forced to temporarily cease fire to meet the charge, while the Castres was heavily damaged in the action. The Suffolk was lost with all hands to the withering counter-fire from the Dax and Nogent-le-Rotrau.

This brought time for scattered Bretonian and Liberty forces to regroup, counterattack and turn the tide of the battle. Admiral Foyer and the Suffolk's crew were posthumously awarded the Victoria Cross, with dramatizations of the battle becoming a popular subject of patriotic post-war holovirals such as The Forlorn Hope. The wreckage of the Suffolk's fleet was later towed to the Southampton Debris Field by ALG and BMM crews to make the space around Planet New London safe for navigation. As of 834 AS, Belvedere Refinery has finally begun work on breaking the Suffolk up. Elements of the bridge are expected to be incorporated into the Leeds Monument.

593220.text: The wreck of a Gallic destroyer, one of numerous ships whose crews mutinied and attempted to desert the Royal Navy in defiance of the order to bombard Planet Leeds.

593222.text: Stokes Mining Station was the largest and longest-running orbital facility in Bretonia, having served the resource and manufacturing needs of the burgeoning house for several centuries. All sorts of industrial materials and components were handled at the BMM facility, which also served as a shipping and distribution hub for the industrial machine of Leeds. While its brief occupation by Kusari Naval Forces during the Tau War left the smelter in disarray, it was not until the Gallic Metal Service took control of the station and surrounding field during the Gallic Invasion that the smelter's fate was sealed. When the order was given to burn Leeds, Stokes was not spared from the fleeing Royal Navy, and now only the scuttled remains of BMM's crown jewel remain as a bitter reminder of what once was.

593224.text:
Glasgow Outpost was once the headquarters of Border World Exports, Bretonia's premier shipping conglomerate. Constructed a few decades after the Stokes smelter, Glasgow served as the port of entry for traders arriving for Kusari, and the last safe port for Bretonian vessels venturing into the Border Worlds. Its proximity to the Taus and importance to Bretonia would seal Glasgow's fate, with Bowex all but abandoning the station in the opening shots of the Tau War, fearful of Kusari invasion. The Bretonian Armed Forces overhauled the station into a first line of defense for Leeds, though ultimately Kusari forces were able to take partial control of the station. Fighting continued in and around the station until the close of the Tau War, when it returned to Bretonian hands.

The Gallic invasion of Bretonia saw conflict visit Glasgow once again, as its perilous position at the Tau-31 Jump Gate led to it being one of the first Bretonian outposts to come under siege. Gallic forces quickly overwhelmed the defending fleet and stormed the outpost, eventually bringing in IDF Shipping to run the post as a wartime supply depot. Several improvements were made to the structure by Gallic engineers both in terms of fortification and logistical efficiency, though such alterations were all for naught when the Royal Navy was routed from Leeds. As the beleaguered Gallic forces retreated, orders were given to scuttle anything that could not be kept from Bretonian hands, and so Glasgow was decommissioned without fanfare, left as one of many monuments of war-torn Bretonia.

After the war, Bowex saw little desire to rebuild in such a precarious location, and instead commissioned the construction of a new trading center in Leeds orbit, which would double as a reconstruction center in the aftermath of the war. Stripped of any critical components, the largely-untouched wreckage of Glasgow has been left to rot, with only Junkers occasionally visiting the station's wreck for salvage.

593226.text:
Commissioned in 804 AS, this Overlord class Battleship would have replaced the aging Battleship Yukon. Before the Ottawa was christened in 806 AS, a public nostalgia campaign persuaded the Navy to have the Yukon refitted, and its serviceable life extended until 825 AS. Left without a battlegroup to spearhead, the Ottawa was used to placate concerns from Ageira executives about supposed Lane Hacker incursions from the Tahoe Ice Cloud. During this time, the Ottawa saw little action on its lonely surveys of California space, but when the Ontario system was opened in 809 AS, the Ottawa was made the flagship of its own battlegroup.

The Ottawa's service life was increasingly varied. Seeing little action in the Liberty-Rheinland War, the Ottawa combatted domestic insurgencies with a taciturn delicacy rarely seen outside outside of the LSF within the Libertonian uniformed services. Surreptitious field retrofits to the Ottawa's sensor grids, along with the addition of highly classified spyglass rectenna cut directly off an older, failed Liberty Navy Research and Development program, made the Ottawa and her airwing uniquely suited to hunting Cardamine smugglers and trade lane inhibitors between California all the way up to Alberta. The Ottawa forged a formidable record for herself over her twenty years of service, rarely deployed to the front due to her value as a homeland security asset, and the 'goodwill' of Los Angeles' senate, who politically benefited from the efficacy of her battlegroup.

When the Gallic war finally came to California, the Ottawa was valuable in halting the invasion, her advanced sensor suits allowing for fighter co-ordination through the mirrored ice of the Tahoe nebula. The Ottawa, along with her accompanying vessels, battled the superior tonnage Carcassonne to a tactical standstill, preventing a ground war from breaking out in Liberty and potentially reducing the theoretical losses of the Gallic War.

In the final months of the conflict, the Ottawa was rushed into Bretonian space for the final, desperate effort to lift the New London bombardment. With insufficient intelligence data as to the formation of the Gallic defences, it was hoped that the Ottawa's extensive signal intelligence capabilities would provide the united task force of battered, demoralised, and structurally crippled Allied forces with early warning to the extremist nucleus of King Charles' armada. Between the steel tombs of the greatest military engagement in history, the Ottawa survived, her battlegroup smashed around her.

The Ottawa's final operation occurred only a matter of days after the New London engagement. Leading a disorganised, war weary column of battered Bretonian and Libertonian survivors of the new London siege in various states of repair to break the bombardment of Leeds in Operation Dunkirk. Any major capital asset not required for maintaining civil order that still had propulsion control followed her lead into the previously locked gate, the codes having been provided by Gallic defectors who were unable to stomach the immolation of Leeds.

Moving ahead of the allied fleet, sensor suites path-finding for rest of the invasion force, the Ottawa hoped to jam the improvised Gallic early warning systems beyond the gate. Probes deployed into Leeds had sent back telemetry on what appeared to be storage containers and little else surrounding the gate, presumably in preparation for abandonment of the New London gate site. The false negative provided by the probes heuristic algorithms proved fatal, as the 'storage containers' were in fact a new Gallic super-weapon – the 'Montagne'-class beam platform.

The Ottawa's luck had failed her, as the scarred battleship had expected to encounter only conventional weaponry within the Gallic defence grid. Instead, the Montagne platforms locked on to the advancing Ottawa and stripped her of resistance within a seconds, hot plasma searing away shield emitters, turret blisters and communication rectennas into molten, blinding slag. Before her destruction, the Ottawa was able to transit one last message to the Norfolk and her battlegroup which were directly behind her, and due to the Ottawa's sacrifice, loss of life in Operation Dunkirk was somewhat lessened.

Blind, crippled, and lame, the battleship's wreck drifts in a wide heliocentric orbit around the Leeds star. No escape pods could have viably been deployed from the deformed hull, and any crew members who may have survived the initial blast have long since suffocated; trapped within the wreck. All members of the Ottawa's bridge crew were posthumously decorated by President Powell, and were listed in the postwar memorial celebrations by order of the Bretonian Queen.

593228.text:
DIAMETER: 14,723 km.
MASS: 5.11 x 10e25 kg.
TERRAIN: Barren
TEMPERATURE: -90°C to 13°C
ESCAPE VELOCITY: 9.21 km/sec

The ruins of Planet Leeds, once an ecumenopolis of industrial plants, smelters, and residential blocks tightly sealed against the acrid smog belched by Bretonian industry. From early settlement the Crown rushed to exploit the planet's natural resources, working its settlers to the bone attempting to keep up with the other houses. The wanton exploitation of Leeds eventually served as both target and rallying cry for the Green Front and Molly movements.

When invading Gallic forces reached Leeds, millions of residents rushed to flee the planet before the invaders made landfall. Those who were left were forced to dig in against the encroaching invaders, carving out foxholes and firing lines within the busy factory complexes. While the Gauls inevitably took control of large portions of the planet, fierce pockets of resistance meant that her subjugation was never absolute, and when the Gallic gambit in New London failed, desperate measures followed.

The Glassing of Leeds saw the massed remains of Leeds' Royal Navy garrison bombard the planet indiscriminately. Ostensibly targeting industrial and logistics centers, white-hot lances carved through city centers as resistance fighters fought to stop local garrisons from setting off area-denial cobalt bombs. Between orbital bombardment and Gallic ground forces adopting scorched-earth tactics, untold masses of Bretonian civilians lay dead. The bombing coalesced Leeds' thick smog clouds into poisonous, radioactive storms, bringing acidic monsoons to the war-torn streets.

While the thick, ever-present fallout has brought a seemingly permanent winter to Leeds' surface, Planetform studies show that in the long-term, greenhouse effects are projected to raise global temperatures by at least 25°C, rendering the surface wholly uninhabitable.

593230.text: No information about this debris field is present in the Neural Net.

593232.text:
CLASS: Logger
GRAVITY: None

AMENITIES: None
CREW: 0

Camrose Supply Depot was constructed in 818 AS to support DSE survey teams that were charting the Peace River Asteroid Field. This included servicing mining ships headed to the recently discovered Platinum deposits. Following the destruction of Red Deer Station, Camrose was also adopted as a base for Liberty Navy patrols launching from Fort Severn in Ontario -- until the arrival of the Battleship Concord made this role redundant. Camrose was also a vital installation for Ageira Technologies, who regularly launched expeditions towards Planet Edmonton and the Cold Lake Nebula.

When Liberty announced its intention to abandon Alberta in 826 AS, Camrose remained as one of the last occupied stations, coordinating evacuation and salvaging operations. When the Jump Gate to Ontario was finally commissioned late that year, Camrose was similarly deactivated and abandoned. The station was heavily stripped after this, although it is unclear whether the Zoners of Freeport 14 or unknown third parties were responsible. In the years since, the station's hull has been torn apart and irreparably degraded by the harsh conditions of the dark matter storm.

593234.text:
CLASS: Poigne
GRAVITY: No
DOCKING: No
AMENITIES: No
CREW: 0

Mazagran Station was built by the Huissiers in 638 AGS (722 AS), allegedly as a staging post for explorers charting the Gallic Border Worlds. Despite these claims, the citizens of Planet Marne referred to Mazagran as the “Black Citadel”, believing it to have been deployed in response to riots that had rocked the system a year earlier. Rumors quickly spread that the Huissiers were abducting and torturing dissident ringleaders aboard Mazagran. When the Council-orchestrated mutiny of the Marne Pacification Fleet triggered the Second Gallic Civil War in 716 AGS (800 AS), the Maquis executed their own plot at Mazagran.

A Maquis agent infiltrated the station as a prisoner in order to detonate a sub-dermal bomb as she was transferred into the hangar. In the resulting chaos, Maquis attack squadrons and boarding teams swarmed from the Seine Nebula, quickly overwhelming local resistance and massacring any Huissiers found aboard. The Maquis then openly adopted Mazagran as their Champagne headquarters -- this irritated The Council, who worried their reputation would be damaged by harboring terrorists in the capital system of the revolution.

The uncomfortable partnership continued until the end of the war in 742 AGS (826 AS), when The Council formed the Gallic Republic, and joined their former enemies in creating the Gallic Confederacy. Appalled by the pardon of nobles and Gallic Royal Navy officers, the Maquis refused to lay down arms and continued to strike Confederal targets. Soon after, the Battleship De Grasse was deployed to Mazagran to demand the Maquis’ surrender. Negotiations failed with the murder of a Confederal negotiator, leading to several furious boarding attempts -- each being repulsed with heavy casualties.

The fleet was pushed to resolve the issue immediately, to avoid an embarrassing early challenge to the Confederacy's political authority. Unwilling to suffer further casualties, the De Grasse bombarded Mazagran to scrap, in what was quickly labeled the “Mazagran Massacre”. Controversy about the incident roiled the Confederacy, winning considerable public support for the Maquis movement. Many believe ex-GRN officers intentionally sabotaged the Mazagran negotiations to justify exterminating their most hated wartime enemy.

593236.text:
Once renowned for its valiant fights against the Kusari Naval Forces and the Gallic Royal Navy in the Taus, Battleship Stirling survived many battles. However, its age soon began to show and the old Nessie class battleship was soon withdrawn from the front lines as the war went on, for fear of losing valuable resources in a war theatre where the Stirling would be hopelessly outclassed.

Having been tasked with minor defense missions for the last couple of months while undergoing an extensive refit, Battleship Stirling was deployed to Omega-49 alongside its small group of escorts, more a flotilla than a full fleet, to secure Bretonian interests in-system and to act as a stop-gap measure against the Corsair presence and that of other hostile factions present in Omega-49. Stirling would end up securing the system for Bretonia with the capture of the planet.

In December of 826 AS, following the end of the Gallic war and the loss of Planet Leeds, the Bretonian government began work on a connection between Poole and Omega-49. This prompted a breakdown of relations between the Coalition and the Bretonian Crown, who had enjoyed a non-aggression pact for the final year of the war.

On the fourth day of 827, a Coalition warship was detected by patrols in Omega-49 near the unfinished Poole Gate, prompting the Stirling and its rag-tag collection of escorts to raise the alarm and sortie against the invading force. After the Stirling had arrived at the construction site, the Coalition vessel revealed that it was not alone: a well planned attack from the Barrier Nebula ambushed the Bretonian flotilla. The joint Coalition and Molly force attacked the Stirling, and although the veteran BAF personnel initially provided stiff resistance, the Stirling's age began to show. Surprised, outnumbered and obsolete, this relic of Bretonia's golden age gave way to the enemy's pressure, and its proud bicentennial history came to an end. The remnants of the flotilla regrouped at the planet, awaiting reinforcements from Poole, while the Coalition forces, not unscathed in the battle, returned to Omega-5 to regroup and consider their options.

Today the wreck stands as a reminder to Bretonia that the dangers of the Omegas are not to be underestimated.

593238.text:
CLASS: Chapel
GRAVITY: None
DOCKING: No
AMENITIES: None
CREW: 0

Olpe Border Station was a command centre for Rheinland's Federal Police services in the developing Cologne system. Its main task was to safeguard convoys on their way to and from the Wuppertal Refinery from Cologne's numerous pirates.

The station was to become a casualty of the fall of the Rheinland Republic in 827 AS. Far from the streets of Hamburg and Berlin where the government and military were re-assembling themselves, Olpe found itself handling the Hessian invasion of Cologne without support by the Imperial or Federal administrations.

Without support, the police aboard Olpe Border Station evacuated the neighbouring Wuppertal refinery, escorting civilians unlucky enough to be caught in the crossfire back to Stuttgart. Olpe was destroyed several hours afterwards by the guns of the Red Hessian Battleship Zuschen. The wreck drifts as a reminder of Rheinland's historic borders.

593240.text: Heldrungen Prison was constructed in orbit of Planet Artern in 822 AS. Established as a joint project between the MND and Rheinland Military, the prison was designed to replace temporary ‘black sites’ on Planet Weimar. Intended to house captured Wild and other high value targets for interrogation, the facility was associated with dark rumors of torture and human experimentation. In the opening hours of the Civil War, Rheinland Military crewmen seized control of the station. When an immediate Imperial victory failed to materialize, the Military officers scuttled the station and attempted to link up with sympathetic Unioner forces elsewhere in the system. This plan was unsuccessful with the escaping ships quickly being intercepted and destroyed by responding MND squadrons. The prison’s wreckage now occupies a degrading orbit around Planet Artem. Budgetary constraints have so far blocked any proposals for a replacement facility.

593242.text:
CLASS: Westfalen
CREW: 0
ARMAMENT: N/A

The Battleship Koblenz was commissioned in 813 AS alongside its sister ships Westfalen and Karlsruhe. Intended to revitalize the chronically under-equipped Rheinland Military, the Koblenz was initially deployed to Frankfurt to respond to aggressive pirate attacks along Rheinland’s northern borders. The novice battlegroup met its first serious test with the Corsair invasion of Frankfurt in 815 AS, as hundreds of strike craft poured into the system from the Sigmas. While the Koblenz successfully repelled the incursions with RFP and Bundschuh assistance, it came at a bloody cost in lost pilots.

The Koblenz saw brief service during the opening months of the Hudson War, taking heavy damage during an engagement in Hudson with the Liberty battleship Whitefield. Following emergency repairs at Alster Shipyard, the Koblenz was returned to Frankfurt amid fears that newly identified construction flaws had undermined its combat performance. It continued in these duties until 827 AS, repelling multiple GMG raids from Sigma-13 during the Saigon War. The Koblenz’s senior officers were fervent members of the Imperial coup, having long resented the chronic mismanagement of the Rheinland Military. On the outbreak of the Rheinland Civil War, they were tasked with capturing Schatten Research Facility before a cohesive resistance could form.

Many junior crew members were outraged by this treason, and a mutiny broke out onboard. While the pro-Imperial faction ultimately prevailed, the Koblenz was left severely under-manned. Still believing a fait accompli could be achieved, the Imperial commanders pressed the attack on Schatten. The Koblenz rapidly overran the confused defenders, however its forces were trapped inside the Sector-7 minefield when the Federalist Battleship Bayern deployed from Thuringia and attacked. The Koblenz was destroyed in the resulting battle, providing a rallying victory that unified scattered Federalist forces. As of 831 AS, the wreckage was towed to Schatten’s drydocks for destructive testing and eventual disposal.

593244.text:
CLASS: Aegir
GRAVITY: None
DOCKING: No
AMENITIES: None
CREW: 0

Viernheim was built by the Red Hessians in early 815 AS, and was designated to assist in the construction of the planet's docking ring, as well as serve as a logistics base for Hessian operations within the system. The base has come under attack from Corsairs in its 12 year history, but its biggest test yet came during the attack by the Corsair Battleship Fes in 827 AS.

The garrison was deployed to fight in unison with the Coalition Carrier Alvin Katz, which had arrived from Rheinland to cover the system from Corsair aggression following the Kassel being taken out of action. The fighting proved to be intense, with much of the garrison falling in the attempt to defend the base and planet. Thanks to the efforts of the Alvin Katz, it seemed as if the day would be won, if barely. However, during the battle, the Corsairs had boarded the station with marines intended for ground warfare, and knowing the battle was lost, instructed the boarding parties to sabotage the base before withdrawing. The resulting catastrophic explosion destroyed the base, the explosives used to destroy the base were so excessive, several unfortunate boarding ships found themselves caught in the blast. The Fes fleet fled the scene with considerable damage, testament to the fierceness of the defense.

A hollow structure made of an unknown material. Nomad Hives similar to this can be found in dangerously remote or far-flung locations around the sector, each sharing the same disk-like shape and containing a variety of smaller chambers. A mysterious font of energy appears to be at its core.

Cited by the human intelligence communities as the responsible entity for launching the strikes which destroyed Freeport 7, this hive was placed under considerable threat by LSF forces that had been sent to investigate the attack. During their investigations, an LSF ship stumbled up the hive's location, forcing the Nomads to destroy the entire squadron in order to protect their whereabouts. What conclusions drawn from the investigation and the onimous disappearance of the agents were promptly overshadowed by the outbreak of the Nomad War. Though no further attempts have been made to uncover the cause of Freeport's destruction, which is still considered a mystery by many to this day.

Formerly part of the Council's fleets that broke into Ile-de-France, the battlecruiser has seen little action beyond its first engagement in Gallia's capital.

It spent the years of the Confederacy's in Picardy, where it assisted the Saumur with various tasks and training of the officers aboard. Its time in the system was also spent testing several new weapons engineered at the Navy facility in the same region.

With the end of the Confederacy and the rise of a united Rheinland, the Aubagne has taken up position in the Zurich system, watching the Rheinland Military's every step as the Union rebuilds.

The Battlecruiser Valmy entered service in 741 AGS (825 AS) as a part of the Castillon fleet. It initially participated in the capture of Roussillon, where its officers became notorious as "King Charles' Headsmen" for the mass execution of captured Council dissidents. The battlecruiser went on to repeat this approach during the Siege of New London, frequently shooting Bretonian escape pods and surrendered vessels. Following the offensive's failure, the battlecruiser retreated to Leeds, where it carried out the elimination of Bretonian Resistance vessels attempting to evacuate survivors from the Glassing. When the Gallic Royal Navy collapsed and the monarchy was toppled in 742 AGS (826 AS), the hardline monarchist crew of the Valmy turned to the Gallic Enclave in Edinburgh.

The Valmy formed part of the raiding force that attacked Gallic Republic and Minarchy positions across Champagne, Languedoc, and Provence. They hoped that by destabilizing these "traitor states", King Charles would emerge from hiding to crush the Parisian Assembly and resume the throne. A schism formed within the Enclave in 743 AGS (827 AS) in response to the Kusari Invasion of Gallia. Enclave leadership secretly negotiated a reunification pathway with Gallic authorities -- in exchange for the heads of those responsible for high profile crimes against Council pilots and civilians. The Valmy was among the radical sect that immediately fled to form the even more extremist Royalists, both out of hatred for collaborating with "traitors", and fear of execution following reunification.

Following the emergence of the Gallic Union, the Valmy primarily raided across Orkney and Languedoc for supplies. In 745 AGS (829 AS), they were caught by the Vagrants' mass migration into Orkney, while hiding in the Eynhallow Asteroid Field. The battlecruiser and its crew were quickly subdued, and interrogated for information about Gallia and the Hebrides. After being indoctrinated as Thralls, the crew were cut loose and allowed to continue operating as Royalist terrorists. The vessel now lurks once more in Champagne, where it serves as the eyes and executioner's axe of an absent king and an alien threat.

Notably, the composition of the cloud features exotic particles that would be more at home in the Edge Nebula of eastern Sirius than the Barrier Rim, as well as significant trace materials typically found in planetary environs. Sensors indicate the presence of strange bodies within.

593260.mapped:
White Ridge District, is a remote industrial district on Planet Manhattan. The local starport was built 500 years ago and was primarily used to supply and factories and workshops throughout the District.

As interstellar freight traffic intensified and larger starports became more important, the local starport gradually lost its commercial importance, which also led to the closure of several local industries and the transfer of assets to Planet Houston.

The District found new life after 801 A.S. when this particular backwater starport became the center of attention for all manner of small businessmen and traders, and a free trade zone was created around it for anyone with enough credits to pay the local LPI authorities to look the other way.

Nowadays, there are a mix of small and big-time criminals, freelancers, junkers, and the occasional Outcast or Order operative. A favorite hangout for weary pilots and deal makers is the Blue Knight bar, famous in the gray zone for its anonymous, above-standard services and lounges.

While Hessians once launched raids on nearby Mannheim Station from the field, these have sharply dropped in recent years. Corsair pirates are often sighted in combat with Red Hessians in the area.

593272.text:

A small field of rocky asteroids, split off from the nearby Weisserfeld. For many years the field was used by the LWB to launch attacks on Fertilizer shipments, however this presence has more recently been entirely displaced by Corsairs and Unioners. Initial surveys indicated mineral rich rocks that react with the radiation from the nearby sun, creating a powerful electromagnetic disturbance in the field. Preliminary mining operations were abandoned with the economic crash following the 80-Years War, with the navigational hazards and criminal activity deterring further corporate exploitation.

593274.text:
>>>WARNING: NAVIGATIONAL HAZARD<<<
A small cloud of dark matter and ship debris. During the climax of the war with Rheinland, a Liberty Carrier christened the "Haverhill" was ambushed near the Coos Asteroid Field by a hunter-killer squadron of Rheinland Cruisers and Spectres. Unable to make it fully behind Libertonian lines, the Haverhill made a last-ditch effort to activate its experimental onboard jump drive while taking heavy fire.

A mortar struck the aft, and sheared the jump drive in two. The ship imploded, then sent out a massive dark matter explosion which enveloped most of the nearby ships. Many were destroyed, instantly killing hundreds of soldiers on both sides of the conflict.

As one of the few human-caused dark matter catastrophes in Sirius' history, Liberty has shown an interest in researching the leftover dark matter as it took up orbit around the New Hampshire star. The line of experimental jump drives that caused this anomaly has since been recalled. Scanners do not function within the confines of the cloud, making any exploration difficult.

Battleship Bellona is the current flagship of the Core.
593282.mapped:
The battleship Bellona was launched at Norfolk in 816 AS with the intent serving as the Core’s first battleship and flagship. During its career, has always been considered the less significant counterpart to its more renowned, modern and adventurous sister ship launched nine years later, the battleship Mars. Much of this perception, however, is unfounded. While the Bellona may not have seen as many high-profile battles or explored as many star systems as the Mars, its contribution to securing Core’s foothold in the Omicron Delta system and safeguarding the orbit of Nauru is indisputable.

The loss of its sister ship in Omicron Zeta dealt a heavy moral blow to Bellona’s crew, as a friendly rivalry between engineers and technicians aboard both ships had kept the two crews closely connected. Ironically, it was this same spirit of technical competition that allowed Bellona’s crew to implement new security protocols in record time -- measures that successfully prevented the AI entity known as Isonoe from infiltrating the ship’s systems and replicating the same catastrophic scenario.

Today, the battleship Bellona remains stationed in Omicron Delta, vigilantly protecting the moon Nauru and Core operations, which are increasingly threatened by unfolding events in both Omicron Zeta and Omicron Kappa.

Torshavn Space Port was first established in 821 AS, initially as a factory for Gaian fighters. The station was covertly funded by Green Front sympathizers who had laundered donations received from the Cambridge population. Torshavn is housed inside a large, partially hollowed ice asteroid, which masks the sensor readings of the production facilities the Gaians so desperately needed. Shipping in the supplies for this unusually bold venture was made possible by the extreme draw-down of Armed Forces patrols in Cambridge during the Gallic War.

Over the following years, Torshavn's facilities expanded in scale and sophistication, culminating in the installation of a small drydock inside the asteroid's sheltered cave. In addition to the deadly Anaconda fighter, Torshavn now produces fearsome Galatine gunships and the prized but rare Caliburn destroyer. Torshavn has become a fortified Gaian strongpoint in the Grasmere Ice Field and an important Gaian supply hub. The conflict between producing new ships and maintaining the Gaians' existing smuggling transports means Torshavn is usually busy around the clock.

Torshavn is also frequently visited by Corsair patrols. The Gaians have a complicated relationship with the Corsairs, owing to their activities during the Gallic War, and Cambridge raids that disproportionately affect sympathetic civilians. It is rumored that the Gaians often bribe the Corsairs with useful supplies to encourage them to raid elsewhere. While the truth of this is dubious, the Gaians do frequently receive shipments of Corsair Artifacts in payment for services, many of which are sold on to Cambridge academics for further study.

593289.mapped:
The Gaians of Handayan worked diligently to establish a fully operational base after the struggles with the Outpost's initial dilemmas were surmounted. However good news for the cells operating out of the base was a commodity suffering acute deficit. Gaia had been lost to the Enclave and Planetform had been successful in its project on California Minor. Morale buckled and resolve was ultimately tested.

The more radical of the cells departed not long after Gaia's occupation, feeling they would be better suited reclaiming something so symbolic of their struggle. Those that remained were fairly content with the occasional act of piracy on targets of opportunity, primarily whenever Planetform vessels frequented the system while transporting equipment away from California Minor after a successful operation.

Conflicts of the territorial variety with the Xenos were not uncommon, but they had never posed such a threat as they did now. With the station teetering on abandonment and operating at far less than optimal efficiency, the remaining inhabitants were driven away by the constant pressure they had done well to manage a year prior. The Base would subsequently fall into Xeno hands, adding to the long intended ability for the Xenos to operate in all three of Liberty's border systems with the neighboring Houses.

Having secured a new installation with which to bolster the existing network and now dedicated toward violent assault of Bretonian commerce, the Xenos were also aware of the logistical benefits their new den represented. It was now significantly easier to trade and conspire with elements in the independent worlds, properly linked to those cut from the same cloth the freshly renamed Leyte Base serves three distinct purposes, symbolic of the success of the Xenos with operating in all three corners of Liberty henceforth.

593292.mapped:
Sandur Base was established by the Gaians in 819 AS, with support and funding from the Hogosha. Initially conceived as a staging post for joint raids on the supply lines of Bretonian hold-outs on Planet Harris, these plans were scuppered by the Gallic Invasion in 818 AS. With the Kusari Naval Forces largely destroyed, the Tau War -- and Hogosha privateering in Bretonia -- abruptly ended. Despite this, the Hogosha upheld their pledges of support, seeing Sandur as a strategically useful stopping-off point for shipping supplies to the stranded Exile fleet in Leeds, or purchasing stolen Bretonian goods.

Since then, the steadily growing volume of trade has drawn a range of visitors, including Maquis and Brigands from as far afield as Roussillon. As a result, Sandur has become a prime destination to swap illicitly sourced Bretonian, Gallic or Kusari goods. This has become particularly profitable for the Gaians in recent years, due to the so-called “Green Gold Road”. This scheme sees Gaian smugglers purchase Wildcat Gold from Trafalgar Base for sale to the Hogosha.

Sandur has also seen a spike in funding from concerned Cambridge activists, who urge the Gaians to “take action” against the growing Synth Foods presence on Planet Harris. The idea of Synth gaining a foothold on Bretonia’s border is disquieting to Cambridge’s farmers and academics alike. As a result, Sandur has been expanded with passive sensor arrays to better coordinate raids on the near-complete terraforming operation with a new and ferocious intensity.

CREW: CLASSIFIED
ARMAMENT: CLASSIFIED
593296.mapped:
Deployed in 826 AS, the Red Hessian Battleship Zuschen incorporates the latest advancements developed by Wolfsburg Shipyard. Its first assignment was the assault on Vierlande Prison alongside the Coalition and Unioners, indiscriminately freeing the thousands of inmates within. The Zuschen and Carrier Alvin Katz then turned on the Unioners, accusing them of collaborating with the Corsairs. The ensuing massacre saw the Unioners’ Vierlande force destroyed, and Hamburg's Wedel Station wrecked with no survivors.

The Zuschen later led the Hessian invasion of Cologne alongside the Battleship Kassel, exploiting the chaos of the Rheinland Civil War. It first destroyed Olpe Border Station before advancing to support the Kassel's attack on Saarbrucken and Tholey Station. The Hessians would hold the system until 828 AS, when the newly formed Federal Empire’s first act was to dispatch a Military expedition to expel the Hessians and reopen the Alsace Passage trade route. The Zuschen fled to avoid a direct fight against the Battleship Altenburg.

Following the Kassel's loss in 831 AS, the Zuschen was left as the sole operational Hessian battleship. The Corsairs launched their own invasion of southern Rheinland soon after, intent on breaking the Hessian backlines in Dresden. In 833 AS, the Zuschen launched the Hessian counter-attack in Omega-41. Its mission is to cut Corsair supply lines to Omega-5, in the hope of drawing away reinforcements from Dresden. Its mission has been complicated by frequent clashes with Wild vessels that have flooded into the system.

The Corsairs launched their own invasion of southern Rheinland soon after, intent on breaking the Hessian backlines in Dresden. In 833 AS, the Zuschen launched the Hessian counter-attack in Omega-41. Its mission is to cut Corsair supply lines to Omega-5, in the hope of drawing away reinforcements from Dresden. Its mission has been complicated by frequent clashes with Wild vessels that have flooded into the system.

593299.text:
CLASS: Alsace
CREW: CLASSIFIED
ARMAMENT: CLASSIFIED
593299.mapped:
Nicknamed "Lucky Heavy" on account of its escape from the Languedoc system, as part of the original fleet of Council warships, to the Roussillon system, the former main hideout of the Council during the Second Gallic Civil War.

There, it squared off against the Montmorency and other Gallic Royal Navy vessels, making a fighting withdrawal to Toulouse and later to safer regions of the Taus. During this invasion by Royalist forces, it sustained moderate damage only, and eventually led the way into Gallia proper.

Having flown under the pavillion of the Confederacy for several months, after the outbreak of war with Gallia it was routed in the Languedoc system, and, on the way to Orleanais, was boarded and captured during a Maquis ambush.

Nowadays, the Pamiers is a hopelessly outdated vessel, utilized at large as staging ground for Maquis patrols into Roussillon and deeper Taus alike.

593302.text:
CLASS: Gouges
GRAVITY: Complete
DOCKING: Yes
AMENITIES: Yes
CREW: 260
593302.mapped:
Most of the Gallic Brigands who came from Languedoc with the Council fleet stayed on Toulouse, but some chose to secure their own outpost at the very beginning. Within the gloaming depths of the Ariege Nebula, they found a suitably large asteroid in orbit of Planet Prades. Docking ports and hallways were built inside the asteroid by Brigand workers and IMG engineers that were hired to help with base construction.

Nicknamed Le Donjon Cramoisi - The Crimson Keep - the romantic, swashbuckling hedonism that holds such a grip over Brigand bases in the core worlds like Salbris and Pelussin is notably absent from Montauban. The Brigands of Roussillon lack the luxury of earthly pleasures, and the station is more often than not home to various criminals hiding from the preying eyes of the Gallic authorities.

593305.text:
CLASS: Robespierre
GRAVITY: Complete
DOCKING: Yes
AMENITIES: Yes
CREW: 190
593305.mapped:
Constructed at the fringes of the Burgundy system, Vercors serves as both a listening post and a resupply station for Maquis patrols in the north of Gallia. As the most recently built station operated by the Maquis, the vast majority of those posted to this station are fresh recruits, all eager to prove themselves against the Union. Because of this the personnel of Vercors are, although new under the banner of the rebels, less hardline than those elsewhere.

Though they still oppose the forces of the Union militarily, the Maquis - at least those on Vercors - desire to replace current Union leadership with figures more sympathetic to their own goals. This represents an important distinction from other factions within the movement, as Vercors is the nearest base to Nevers, one of the most important planets for Royalist-aligned Gallic citizens. Because of this relatively more open minded view, Vercors sees more success than other Maquis bases in recruiting new members from the local populace, which seems to be more interested in replacing the Union than necessarily placing the Royalists back in charge.

The base has scored a multitude of successes already, and the Maquis hope to expand on its capability by allowing gunboats to resupply for missions in the region – a far-cry from the days of the Council.

593308.text:
The Ariege Nebula is a cluster of dense particulates, primarily hydrogen and is thought to be a nodule of the Hebrides Nebula so prominent in the skies of Bretonia.

The presence of the Ariege in Roussillon, and Roussillon's distance from the Barrier Nebulae have led cartographers and astronomers to argue that Roussillon should not be categorized as part of Tau. The new cluster would be called Lambda.

593310.text: The Tarn Ice Field is a cloud of asteroids captured from the Barrier Nebula as the Rousillion system passed through the nebula's reaches long ago. The field is composed of particularly dirty bodies of frozen water, which the cost of refining has made any mining of the field to be prohibitively expensive when compared to other sources. Until recently it was notable due to council traffic plying the route from Rousillion to Tau, but the recent instability that collapsed the Tau-29 hole has left the expanse of the Tarn with little to offer.

593312.text:
DIAMETER: 10,620 km
MASS: 5.68 x 10e24 kg
TERRAIN: Terrestrial
TEMPERATURE: 60°C to 140°C
ESCAPE VELOCITY: 11.21 km/sec

Toulouse is a boiling world cloaked in a dense atmosphere of nitrogen, sulfur dioxide, and hydrogen sulfide. These caustic conditions render the majority of the planet entirely inhospitable to humans, and capable of rapidly corroding even hardened equipment. Toulouse was first discovered by by an IMG expedition in 814 AS, and labeled as T115-C1. They noted several mountainous mega-formations that protruded above the opaque layer of acidic clouds into a cooler, potentially habitable band. Plans to further survey these sites were derailed by the escalating Tau War between Bretonia and Kusari, which resulted in funding being withdrawn for further IMG expeditions in the region.

In 817 AS, The Council -- a powerful dissident group fighting a civil war in Gallia -- breached the hidden minefield in Orkney, revealing Gallia’s existence to Sirius. The IMG were the first to encounter Council pioneers, who were desperate to find a new home for the refugees fleeing the looming Gallic Royal Navy counterattack into Languedoc. Sympathizing with their plight, the IMG offered the location of Tau-115, which The Council renamed Roussillon as their new hidden base of operations. With IMG assistance, colonies were sited on the three mountain peaks of de Peguilhan, de Bornelh, and de Born.

Over subsequent years, the Council developed the mountains of Toulouse into the mines, factories, and habitats that sustained their raids on Gallic supply lines. The colonists required respirators to breathe, and were frequently forced into lockdowns when hurricane storms below drove acidic fogs into higher altitudes. In late 825 AS, the Gallic Crown became aware of Roussillon’s location following a disastrous Council raid on Issoudon Shipyard in Edinburgh. Early the next year, the Royal Navy’s Montmorency fleet launched a decisive invasion of the system, quickly destroying Perpignan Spaceport and routing the Council defenders.

While many settlers were successfully evacuated to Provence, those stranded when the Montmorency achieved orbital supremacy opted for a strategy of scorched earth to deny the planet to Gallia. Nuclear devices were detonated on and within the three mountain peaks, destroying the colonies, prompting massive landslides, and heavily irradiating the mountaintops. Token efforts to explore and remediate the sites were undertaken by EFL Oil & Machinery soon after, however all work ceased with the Gallic Crown’s fall. Despite sporadic scavenging expeditions by the Maquis and Royalists, the prospect of future colonization is remote at best.

593314.text: When the Council, Brigand and Maquis forces first arrived in Roussillon, this asteroid field was the first obstacle they encountered. Frozen pockets of oxygen were quickly marked a navigational hazard. However, as the construction of several space stations and settlement of Toulouse began, that same field became a valuable local source of oxygen, which was scarce in the system due to the toxicity of Toulouse's atmosphere.

593316.text:
DIAMETER: 5,651 km
MASS: 4.48 x 10e24 kg
TERRAIN: Barren
TEMPERATURE: -16°C to 142°C
ESCAPE VELOCITY: 6.02 km/sec

Planet Foix is a deserted world with a thin methane-rich atmosphere. Severe temperature fluctuations make human colonization impossible, however, the planet has certain rich mineral deposits that could be mined in the future if appropriate technologies are available.

593318.text:
DIAMETER: 3,104 km
MASS: 1.12 x 10e24 kg
TERRAIN: Ice
TEMPERATURE: -220°C to -70°C
ESCAPE VELOCITY: 1.97 km/sec

Tarascon is a small moon on the far orbit of Planet Argeles. The Tet Asteroid Field is concentrated around the moon, and the field might have formed after a cosmic impact that happened in the past, possibly a collision between two Argeles moons of which only one survived.

593320.text:
DIAMETER: 17,917 km
MASS: 12.64 x 10e24 kg
TERRAIN: N/A
TEMPERATURE: N/A
ESCAPE VELOCITY: 14.11 km/sec

A large planet that is usually classified as a gas giant, Argeles has only one large moon: Tarascon. Located in a remote area of Roussillon, it is rarely visited by piloted spacecrafts.

593322.text:
DIAMETER: 8,215 km
MASS: 7.02 x 10e24 kg
TERRAIN: Barren
TEMPERATURE: -72°C to 40°C
ESCAPE VELOCITY: 7.90 km/sec

Elne is a large barren world with a thin atmosphere. Its gravity has presumably played an important role in forming the surrounding Tarn Asteroid Field.

593324.text:
DIAMETER: 2,890 km
MASS: 1.94 x 10e24 kg
TERRAIN: Barren
TEMPERATURE: -90°C to 160°C
ESCAPE VELOCITY: 2.15 km/sec

Le Soler is a relatively large barren moon of Planet Toulouse. It only has traces of atmosphere, and its surface is covered with numerous asteroid craters.

593326.text:
DIAMETER: 2,687 km
MASS: 2.55 x 10e24 kg
TERRAIN: Barren
TEMPERATURE: -135°C to 42°C
ESCAPE VELOCITY: 3.00 km/sec

Planet Prades is a small rocky world that forms a spectacular background for Montauban Base. The world itself has no significant traits or resource deposits, and is by no means habitable by humans.

593327.text:
CLASS: Meskhenet-Andjety
GRAVITY: Complete
DOCKING:Yes
AMENITIES: Yes
CREW: 320
593327.mapped: Cairo is one of the most recently constructed outposts put into service by the Order. It serves as a waystation for patrols heading into the upper Omicrons, and a rest stop for vessels returning from there. The station itself dedicates a significant amount of resources to monitoring Omicron Zeta traffic and tracking the unusually high Nomad presence in the system. Patrol paths are frequently updated with new flight patterns to cover and defend the station, as the Order is functionally unable to secure the whole system from potential and real hostile forces alike.

CLASS: Unknown
GRAVITY: None
DOCKING: None
AMENITIES: None
CREW: None
593330.mapped:
The remnants of Tarancon space station marked the Junkers' boldest venture yet - establishing their base in the perilous and untamed Edgeworlds. Originally established as a foothold for salvage operations shortly after the Battle of Toledo, the station later became a major sanctuary for a variety of smugglers navigating the Omicrons.

The station fulfilled its role until 831 AS when, shortly after the withdrawal of the battleship Thebes from the Omicron Minor system, Tarancon base was discovered suddenly abandoned. All escape pods remained on board, and the hangars were devoid of any ships. No evidence of a significant attack on the station was found on the hull, aside from a few cut airlocks.

Left without a crew to maintain its operations or steer clear of potential collisions with debris and asteroids orbiting the lifeless planet Toledo, Tarancon disintegrated shortly thereafter under the impact of the aforementioned celestial bodies. None of the crew members who were on Tarancon at the time of its abandonment have ever been found again.

593333.text:
Apeiron is potentially the most important moon of Planet Erebus. Although freezing and inhospitable, unlike Hypnos, the moon has a breathable atmosphere for humans and a geologically active core. This sporadic volcanic activity sets it apart from Hypnos and provides enough greenhouse gasses to keep Apeiron from freezing over completely. The celestial body possesses a strong magnetic field that protects its surface from the violent stellar winds of the Tau-61 binary system by the intervention of its stormy older sibling, Planet Erebus.

Although currently a difficult moon to inhabit, Apeiron has the potential to be an oasis with determined and patient terraforming efforts.
593333.mapped:
Apeiron initially seemed like the perfect haven for the willing and unwilling servants of the Vagrants. Groundbreaking of the first tunnels began in 828 AS, and by the beginning of 829 AS, Apeiron already had its first functional subterranean bunker for its inhabitants. The most basic needs were immediately met with the help of smaller fusion reactors powered by the ubiquitous ice on Apeiron, providing enough energy for heating as well as water purification and air filtration. Not long after, the first simple hydroponic farms were also built with the aim of sustainably fulfilling food needs.

The colonists soon discovered extensive underground cave systems on Apeiron. These caverns are defined by ethereally beautiful crystalline formations that immediately became the epicenter of settler indoctrination and religious ceremonies.

The honeymoon period of the colony’s initial years ended with the increasingly low harvest yields and dying off of much of the settlement’s crops. Compounding issues was an ever-increasing infant mortality rate brought on by an increase in premature births and stillbirths. The cause of these problems and any potential relation between them is still a matter of speculation, but it is a clear threat to the survival of all colonization efforts on Apeiron.

593336.text: Yap Edge Nebula is the center for most Order activities in the Omicron Zeta system. The nebula contains a jump hole leading into Omicron Mu. The Order keeps the nebula under close control, and its patrols frequent the area.

593338.text: Yap Asteroid Field is located within the nebula designated with the same name. The Order cleared several passages within the field for its capital ships to move around safely.

593340.text: Chuuk field of rock asteroids is a remnant of a cosmic cataclysm that occured many millenia ago. A particularly large planetesimal hit Planet Magur that was split into several parts after the impact. The largest formed Magur dwarf planet that is currently seen in the central part of the field. Other remnants of Magur were crushed into smaller fragments and now comprise a large formation of asteroids that are held together by Magur's gravitation.

593342.text: Pohnpei Nebula is the largest cloud of Omicron Zeta, orbiting on the outskirts of the system. First noted by Zoner explorers from Freeport 11 in 815 AS, the nebula is infamous for exceptionally high Nomad activity. This presence has only grown worse since the desolation of Cairo and Capetown bases, leading many to believe the nebula contains the entrance to the Nomads' secretive home worlds.

593344.text: A smaller outcropping of the Pohnpei Nebula, Tofol is a more dense, asteroid-filled cloud on the outskirts of Omicron Zeta. Its remoteness and lack of any immediate points of interest, mean that barely any human dares venture into it, and even fewer return.

593346.text: A remote field of ice asteroids. No further information available.

593350.text:
DIAMETER: 13,428 km
MASS: 3.18 x 10e24 kg
TERRAIN: Barren
TEMPERATURE: -149°C to 10°C
ESCAPE VELOCITY: 6.56 km/sec

Murilo is a large icy planet located in a desolate region of Omicron Zeta. The Order had once considered the possibility of mining Water from ice located on Murilo's surface, however the Nomad Invasion of Omicron Zeta in 835 AS ended these aspirations.

593352.text:
DIAMETER: 3,720 km
MASS: 2.27 x 10e24 kg
TERRAIN: N/A
TEMPERATURE: N/A
ESCAPE VELOCITY: 3.81 km/sec

Magur is a gas planet, or, a dwarf planet with thick atmosphere that is a remnant of a once much larger planet. In the relatively young planetary system of Omicron Zeta, the planet fell victim to a large-scale planetesimal impact some 200-300 millions years ago. The impact destroyed a large part of the planet, leaving only the core intact. Over time, gases and dust from the surrounding field of planetary remains formed a thick atmosphere around Magur's silicate core.

593354.text:
CLASS: Menorca
GRAVITY: Complete
DOCKING: Yes
AMENITIES: Yes
CREW: 250
593354.mapped:
The Corsairs first detected the AI of Planet Gammu almost a century ago as they emerged from their mysterious underground cities. The machines would only respond aggressively when provoked, leading most Corsairs to avoid them when possible, unwilling to trigger a conflict with unknowable consequences. Despite this, concern would grow on Crete in 810 AS following a sudden surge in AI activity across Kappa. Ciutadella was rapidly constructed as a monitoring station in response. Following the completion of Yaren Base in Omicron Delta, Ciutadella's squadrons would frequently scramble to chase off AI drones who were shadowing Corsair Iridium transports and pulsing garbled transmission bursts.

When these transmissions were later studied by Order analysts based on Crete, they were discovered to be using extensively modified Western Alliance encoding. Using preserved records from the Hispania, the first meaningful communications were established with Kappa's AI drones. Ciutadella's role changed significantly following the Corsair expulsion from Omicron Delta in 822 AS. No longer needed as a supply relay, the station instead became responsible for blocking potential Nomad or Core advances on Gamma. When these invasions failed to materialise over the following years and with eventual collapse of Delta jump hole, Ciutadella's garrison was steadily eroded away. As Corsair operations intensified elsewhere, many believed the station had outlived its purpose and could be decommissioned.

Spared only by lingering paranoia about the Gammu AI's intentions, Ciutadella continued with a skeleton crew up until the Core invasion of 830 AS, which was repulsed by the nearby Corsair home fleet. When the Core tried again in 832 AS, the Corsairs were preoccupied in Omicron Theta. Without the reinforcements to meaningfully intervene, Ciutadella observed while Planet Gammu was occupied and looted. This changed in 835 AS, when the Core came under attack by a massive AI fleet, and abruptly abandoned the planet. Ciutadella immediately launched its own attack, to bloody the Core as severely as possible. The Battlecruiser Vis was severely damaged during the operation, however the Core defenders suffered heavy casualties in the process.
