593457.text:
South Shields Refinery is a large mining and processing complex orbiting the gas giant Hartlepool. The Independent Miners Guild first arrived in Newcastle in 668 AS, to significant controversy. Border World Exports had announced promising astronomical studies of the star the year before, and later dispatched a slow-burn deep space expedition to carry out a detailed survey. The young Guild instead wagered a significant portion of its early resources on charting Leeds in detail, looking for a Jump Hole they believed could provide a substantial shortcut.

This extreme gamble paid off, allowing the first Guild explorers to arrive six months before Bowex entered the system’s borders. By 670 AS, the IMG began construction of South Shields -- their second station. This provided the Guild with a local headquarters and mineral claims at a time when other Bretonian corporations were only just beginning to carry out detailed evaluations. South Shields’ completion prior to the deployment of a Jump Gate to Leeds also allowed the IMG to exploit a Bretonian legal loophole, circumventing various regulatory issues and colonial taxes.

For over a century, South Shields made relatively easy money by harvesting Water and Oxygen from the nearby Tyne Ice Field, and filtering trace Hydrocarbon impurities. Potable supplies were then sold to local stations and the then-enormous population of Planet Leeds. With Rheinland's economic collapse after the Colony Wars, the Guild received a wave of recruits from Kruger Minerals, including several specialists from Mannheim. This provided the Guild with the expertise to begin skimming Hartlepool's atmosphere for the Hydrogen and Deuterium needed to produce H-Fuel. While this resynthesis process has never been consistently profitable, it has allowed the Guild to maintain a strategic fuel reserve for its own Tau operations.

593458.text:
CLASS: Hawking
GRAVITY: Complete
DOCKING: Yes
AMENITIES: Yes
CREW: CLASSIFIED
593458.mapped:
The Sunderland Research Aerostat was constructed at Scarborough Shipyard in 736 AS, and towed to the gas giant Darlington later the following year. The Aerostat is the Bretonia Intelligence Service’s most ambitious and expensive project, acting as the headquarters for the research and exploration of the Dom’Kavash structure known as Site Jarrow. Sunderland relies on a combination of locally harvested buoyancy gasses, onboard thrusters, and secured anchor struts to maintain its altitude in spite of the planet’s tumultuous atmosphere and intense gravity well.

The decision to deploy Sunderland followed a breakthrough in the study of the Amiatinus Cache, a recovered Artifact that had progressed the then-rudimentary understanding of Dom’Kavash glyphs. This hinted at an acoustic, almost musical, component to their language. Experiments in this area revealed the presence of a concealed airlock on Site Jarrow, allowing for the creation of the Sunderland Umbilical to gain access to further sections of the interior. While scientists now have access to several isolated compartments within Jarrow, understanding of its purpose and technologies remains stubbornly limited.

Despite this, even small insights have occasionally advanced Bretonian science by decades. Notable examples include the 798 AS discovery of an Artifact fragment depicting part of a novel chemical process for the production of Super Alloys. By 806 AS, Sunderland provided an experimental procedure to Scarborough Shipyard for implementation; this revolutionized the previously inefficient and expensive method used aboard Stokes Smelter, allowing the faltering industry to catch and then surpass Liberty's progress in the field.

Bretonia’s recent wars and dire situation have placed Sunderland under incredible pressure to produce useful military technologies. This created a culture of high-stakes risk-taking, causing the injury or death of numerous explorers and scientists. In 831 AS, Sunderland also received significant damage during “The Blink”, in which Jarrow’s anti-gravity pylons momentarily failed, causing it to drop over a kilometer. As of 834 AS, there are signs that Jarrow may be preparing to fully awaken. Most other avenues of research have been halted, in favor of investigating the implications of an activation scenario -- and developing contingencies for Jarrow’s destruction should this pose a threat to Bretonia.

593459.text:
Scarborough Shipyard is the local headquarters of Border World Exports, and an important shipbuilding and manufacturing center. It was originally constructed in 679 AS as the sister station of Belfast Production Facility, forming a link in a planned vertically-integrated supply chain. While the joint Bowex-BMM project initially saw success, Scarborough was severely impacted by Belfast's loss in 814 AS. Following the Gallic conquest of Leeds in 819 AS, Scarborough's operating coasts soared due to the need to rely on resources imported from Liberty and Rheinland. During this period, the operation was largely sustained by expansive wartime subsidies.

During the Gallic War, Scarborough was frequently pressed into service as a repair yard for damaged Armed Forces assets. This became particularly important following the Siege of New London and the destruction of Southampton Shipyard. While neither Scarborough nor the seized Aland Shipyard were equipped with the sophisticated military tooling necessary for capital production or full servicing, improvised repairs enabled Bretonia to continue fighting until the siege was broken. This made the shipyard a priority target for Gallic raids in Newcastle for the duration of the war. Additionally, Gaian raiders frequently attack the station, pointing to the Yorkshire Debris Field as evidence of Bowex's wasteful practices. As a result, a large Bounty Hunter community has congregated aboard, attracted by generous payouts for killed terrorists.

Following the Gallic War, Scarborough was left with significant slack capacity, leading to layoffs and one berth being rented to mothball the Battleship Harlow. From 827 AS, Scarborough's subsidies were drastically cut, however access to locally produced minerals from Redcarr Production Facility brought costs under control once more. While Bretonia still imports much of its transport fleet from Kusari, the heavily armored Shetland and Shire remain popular due to their proven wartime performance, ensuring a steady order flow. Scarborough is also renown as the primary producer of the "Gloriette" export class of Royal Liner, although only a handful of these extravagant vessels have been commissioned in recent years.

593460.text:
Redcarr Refinery was built by BMM in 827 AS. Like Belfast Station before it, Redcarr's primary purpose is the refinement of minerals mined on Middlesbrough, an uninhabitable but mineral-rich moon. These minerals were more important than ever to rebuild Bretonia's devastated infrastructure in the aftermath of the Gallic Invasion.

Redcarr was thus hastily built and its workers driven hard to continuously increase output. Remembering well the mutiny that led to the loss of Belfast in 750 AS, Redcarr is well staffed by political "morale officers" who ensure potential disloyalty is promptly reported and dealt with. BMM also closely coordinates their patrols with the BPA and Bounty Hunters Guild to deter Gaian, Outcast, and Molly attacks.

593461.text:
Destroyer Ceuta is one of the newer destroyers in the Outcast armada, built in the aftermath of the Outcast Slave Revolt in 832 AS. Its owners, the renowned Wenceslaus Cartel, aim to re-establish the Bretonian smuggling routes and consolidate power within the Outcasts' southwestern sphere of influence.

Following initial tests, the destroyer's first major campaign involves serving as a mobile base in the Newcastle system, providing resupply, minor goods exchange, and a staging ground for raids on nearby points of interest.

593462.text:
Concealed deep within the Northumberland Ice Field, Skye Base was constructed by the Gaians in 798 AS. Skye initially provided a convenient staging point to target industrial sites across Newcastle, and the Terraforming Gasses plant at Birmingham Station. Newcastle in particular was a growing area of concern for the Gaians over fears that BMM and Bowex were repeating the same ecologically devastating carte blanche playbook as Leeds. Despite this, Skye spent its first two decades as a minor outpost, secondary to Gaian activities prioritizing Edinburgh, New London and Tau-31. This changed with the Gallic Royal Navy's advance into Edinburgh, and the subsequent lock-down of Islay Base.

Skye's secluded location quickly made it the preferred destination for Gaian evacuees and non-combatants who had been displaced by the Gallic invasion. The following years saw a frenzied campaign of tunneling and construction to expand the habitats needed to accommodate this exploding population. Skye quickly became the Gaians' largest and most populous station, housing both civilians and radical, subversive academics who had fled Bretonian society to avoid arrest. Many now refer to Skye as the "Underground University", with its labyrinthine warren of tunnels hosting labs, engineering workshops and seminar halls. Most of the designs later produced aboard Torshavn Drydock originated from projects on Skye.

Skye spearheads the Gaian effort to disrupt the Carlisle bacterial eradication project. While some Gaian cells are divided on the ethics of terraforming sterile worlds, there is unanimous agreement that the joint Cryer-Planetform extermination of an existing, thriving biosphere is a crime against nature. In a twist of irony, disillusioned settlers from the Carlisle colony were also responsible for smuggling samples of the bacterial strain required for the production of Slog to Gaian contacts. There is now a booming -- and internally controversial -- black market industry for Slog synthesis aboard Skye. It remains to be seen whether local leaders will endorse this source of revenue, or stamp it out.

593463.text: Stationed in orbit of planet Carlisle, Gateshead is a staging ground for the ships guarding the colony, currently administered by the Bretonia Police Authority. From here, police ships patrol the surrounding field boundaries, protecting nearby Trade Lanes from Outcast, Gaian, and Molly raiders. The BPA also dispatches patrols to nearby mining operations in the west and north, and the jumpgate to Leeds. Additionally, the station houses numerous fabrication units to produce goods associated with the colonization of Carlisle.

593464.text:
DIAMETER: 12,642 km
MASS: 6,11 x 10e24 kg
TERRAIN: Terrestrial
TEMPERATURE: -8°C to 53°C
ESCAPE VELOCITY: 11.15 km/sec
593464.mapped:
From orbit, Planet Carlisle initially appears lush and hospitable. The ideal atmosphere, rolling jungles and deep oceans presented a pristine jewel in the barren wastes of The Barrier. When the earliest IMG explorers first landed in 669 AS, they discovered that Carlisle’s sweltering rainforests concealed a deadly secret. The biosphere was saturated with hostile strains of bacteria, many immediately deadly to humans. Highly contagious infections spread through the body like wildfire, dissolving internal organs. This devastating threat effectively stalled any consideration of colonization until a resolution could be found.

The “Carlisle Problem” became a long running project of Cambridge Research Station’s hot labs, studying how bacterial eradication could be achieved reliably and at scale. On-site trials began in 812 AS after Cryer Pharmaceuticals synthesized a protein capable of neutralizing the bacteria under lab conditions. This did not translate into real world results, as an effective delivery mechanism remained elusive. Despite setbacks caused by the Gallic War, a breakthrough came in 825 AS, when a joint Cryer-Planetform partnership successfully deployed an aerosolized treatment through adapted terraforming generators.

By 827 AS, this network of generators had created a 500km radius, self-certified “clean zone”. Cambridge University academics have warned of protein contamination across the wider Carlisle biosphere, and challenged the rigor of Cryer’s safety testing. Despite this, the Bretonian government quickly moved to certify Carlisle as fit for colonization, due to the urgent need to create jobs and housing for the enormous Refugee population scattered across Liberty, Rheinland and New London. To fund the colony, Bretonia has been forced to sell colonial development and extraction charters to Liberty corporations such as Universal Shipping and DSE.

Boom towns have now begun to sprout across Carlisle’s Clean Zone, focusing on mining, logging and manufacturing. Many among the Bretonian government see Carlisle as the only sustainable, long term solution to the loss of Leeds, owing to Sprague’s precarious location and disastrous development. Smog-belching factories have begun to churn out locally produced Consumer Goods and Industrial Materials. Organized crime quickly took root on Carlisle however, with the planet becoming an epicenter for Slog production and distribution. Gaian terrorist cells frequently strike at targets across the planet, usually hitting terraforming generators or deforestation camps.

593465.text: A large, blue gas giant in the Newcastle system, Hartlepool has significant oxygen and hydrogen reserves in the atmosphere, along with small quantities of tritium and helium. The IMG have several gas miners in the atmosphere to harvest the various gases, and they are processed onboard the orbiting IMG refinery of South Shields.

593466.text: A small, pock marked moon of the planet Carlisle. Ashington has several BMM mining camps near its south pole, prospecting promising mineral lodes.

593467.text:
A volcanic moon of Planet Carlisle, Middlesbrough's surface is a wracked by earthquakes and volcanic eruptions. The moon first came to BMM's attention in 671 AS, after it was found these chaotic conditions regularly churned rich mineral deposits to the surface. After an ownership dispute with the IMG was resolved in 678 AS, BMM begun deploying automated miners to crawl the perimeter of vast magma oceans. Cargo was then boosted into orbit to the nearby Belfast Production Facility. The platforms were lost along with Belfast itself in 814 AS, after a crew mutiny seized control of the station and handed it to the Mollys.

Following Belfast's destruction during the Gallic War, Bretonia moved quickly to re-secure its hold over the moon. By 827 AS, Redcarr had been constructed in orbit, and a number of mining crawlers were repaired. This work was significantly complicated by unexploded mines in orbit, the remnants of the Molly minefield used for Belfast's defense. Middlesbrough has received significant state investment in the years following the war, with Bretonia hoping the moon's resources can sustain its faltering economy.

593468.text:
>>>WARNING: NAVIGATIONAL HAZARD<<<
A smaller region of dark matter and radiation left behind in the wake of the Texas Incident. Pilots should not be fooled by the Pequena Negra's relatively compact size; its composition is precisely the same as that of its larger sibling and is equally lethal to unshielded organics. Despite the Pequena Negra's dangers, it experiences at least sporadic traffic due to its proximity to the criminals of the North Dallas Debris Field. The occasional Liberty Rogue can be seen escaping pursuit into the cloud, as there is believed to be a jump hole located somewhere inside the cloud; Texan authorities are under strict orders not to pursue into either Negra. The question is merely how many fugitives ever come out again.

593469.text:
>>>WARNING: NAVIGATIONAL HAZARD<<<
A large region of dark matter and radiation left behind after the Texas Incident of 500 AS decimated the system. Unlike the northern Pequena Negra, the Grande Negra is centred around the fatal Jump Gate's destructive epicentre; as a result, the Grande Negra is far larger than its sibling, although the two clouds' compositions are identical. Much of the Dallas Research Complex was forever swallowed by the Jump Gate's detonation; therefore, whatever resources and technology the Liberty government of over three centuries ago stored there might still remain, shielded from dark matter by storage containers. Archaeologists speculate that were the Grande Negra to be lifted, a perfect tableau of life prior to the Incident would be found; Police patrols going about their business, supply transports, and personnel carriers, frozen doing what they had been when the Incident happened. Other than treasure-hunters and suicidal explorers, however, no ships are ever seen entering this zone; even the truly desperate aren't mad enough.

593470.text:
The oldest vessel still active in Liberty's Navy, the Mississippi has served as an icon of Houston's oppression and a symbol of fear for those willing to break the law.

Though originally set to be decommissioned in 805 AS, criticism of the move and public support of the warship's presence in Texas has led to it being kept in the Navy until 827 AS.

Following ample expansion plans at West Point Military Academy, and with the Mississippi now out of service, the Liberty Navy turned the veteran vessel into a training facility for new generations of officers.

593471.text: A medium-sized field of debris that is home to a large settlement of Junkers that have, according to sporadic reports from Liberty Police patrols that wandered into the area, constructed a permanent base amongst the scrap. Though criminals such as Rogues and Outcasts are frequently seen near Junker bases (indeed, Texas is the furthest south Outcasts are seen in Sirius), the North Dallas Debris Field remained relatively harmless up until several years ago, when Texan authorities first began to suspect the field as sheltering slavers. Despite an increase in patrols in the region, however, nothing definite has yet been proven.

593472.text:
>>>WARNING: NAVIGATIONAL HAZARD<<<
This debris field is all that remains of the Jump Gate machinery whose malfunction in 500 AS led to the Texas Incident. Liberty technicians were testing the prototype of a new form of Jump Gate that was intended to revolutionize travel across Sirius; their prototype version was to connect California to Texas. Due to a bizarre and critical technical error, the Jump Gate, instead of initializing upon start up, fatally ruptured; the initial explosion, setting free copious amounts of dark matter and radiation, inundated half a star system before petering off. Texas' beauty was forever ruined in the disaster, with half the system made fatal to all organic life; its economy was shattered, and the system experienced a massive exodus that would cripple its productivity for the indefinite future. Curious pilots may see the cataclysmic Jump Gate's core here, although they are cautioned, for the area is heavily radioactive; for the most part, however, it's merely a refuge of last resort for criminals seeking to avoid capture by Liberty authorities.

593473.text: The South Dallas Debris Field consists of the remnants of the Dallas Research Complex; those that hadn't been swallowed by the Grande Negra after the Texas Incident. The zone appears to house a large contingent of Xeno terrorists, and it is rumoured that they are engaged in constructing a more permanent home.

593474.text: Surveyed in 1 AS along with the rest of the New York system, Maine has never had any resources worth the effort to extract them, or enough atmosphere to allow any effective colonisation effort. Deep Space Engineering, who own the rights to Maine, sometimes lease it out to the Liberty Navy and Detroit Munitions, in order for them to conduct weapons testing on the planet.

593475.text:
With an ever-increasing presence of Police and Navy patrols, raiding New York's Trade Lanes became ever more difficult and dangerous. Eventually, the Rogue ringleaders had enough of their raiding parties dying or getting captured due to their ships malfunctioning mid-fight or guns falling off.

The Rogue leaders decided to move the destroyer, lovingly dubbed "Drunken Codger", to the heart of Liberty. The main goal was to use the destroyer as a rearming, staging and repairing outpost, conveniently hidden near the major trade arteries in the system. The destroyer often became a loot drop-off point for raiders, protecting their stolen goods until they could ship them en masse to Rochester or Buffalo and beyond for profit. Despite its intimidating appearance, the ship often has something breaking down and its true capabilities are never certain.

When the Rogues presence was firmly established in New York thanks to Buffalo Base, the Drunken Codger was stirred from its inebriated rest and redeployed into the Texas system in early 824 AS where the Rogues intended to use the ship to further expand their influence, and hopefully, their profits. At the beginning of 825 AS, the Drunker Codger was moved into the Bering system in an attempt to assert their control over the more disorganised pirate bands hanging around the Freeport 2.

The Drunker Codger was quietly relocated to Texas yet again as the Liberty Navy had begun its campaign against the Separatists in the Bering system, where it assumed its previous role as a mobile base for the Rogues.

There it remained mostly undisturbed for nearly two years. In 829 AS it was used to take any remaining valuables from the remains of the Galveston outpost. The ship's senior command never told anyone else how they learned of Galveston's location, causing the crew to buzz with speculations about defectors or captives taken shortly before the raid.

593476.text: The Westerwald Cloud is a large, copper-hued nebula that covers the western side of Frankfurt. Bundschuh and Unioners frequently launch raids from the cloud. Armed MND convoys are regularly observed entering and leaving the area. Local authorities caution against traversing this region, citing treacherous navigation conditions. Civilian vessels venturing into the cloud are intercepted by MND patrols and compelled to change course.

593477.text: A large rocky asteroid field. The Alsterfeld is littered with the wreckage of mining operations that were abandoned as cost-prohibitive in the aftermath of the 80-Years War. The field is frequently used by the Unioners to launch raids on Alster Shipyard and Planet Hamburg.

593478.text:
Orbiting Nauru in the Omicron Delta system, Yaren Base was one of the Corsairs' most distant outposts. Built in 812 AS to better facilitate the construction of planet-side mining camps and research installations, Yaren Base has since been expanded to include ship repair and refuelling capabilities, as well as a few long term habitat modules. After the alliance between the Order and the Corsairs broke down around 818 AS as well as priority changes, Yaren has since been of much lesser significance for the Corsairs.

The Core, an elite military force, took the insignificant focus of the Corsairs on Yaren as a chance and annexed the station in an attempt to secure themselves more parts at the crossroads to the upper Omicron systems. Most of the Iridium mined in the captured facilities on Nauru gets transported up to Yaren and then either onto Freeport 11 or into Omicron Rho to sell it in borderworlds, edge worlds and sometimes even in the houses, or to use it in their own shipyards. Given this newfound outpost, the Core seeks to expand their grasp onto the planets resources and colonize the desert world.

593479.text:
DIAMETER: 4,482 km
MASS: 9.01 x 10e22 kg
TERRAIN: Rock
TEMPERATURE: -210°C to 180°C
ESCAPE VELOCITY: 2.21 km/sec

Khemmiset is a rocky, airless moon orbiting planet Tangier. While no comprehensive surveys have been carried out, preliminary exploration revealed deposits of Iron and silicates. There is little interest in developing the necessary infrastructure needed to mine the moon, largely due to a combination of cost, security issues, and Tangier overshadowing Khemmiset's potential.

593480.text:
DIAMETER: 50,980 km
MASS: 1.56 x 10e26 kg
TERRAIN: Rock
TEMPERATURE: -210°C to 180°C
ESCAPE VELOCITY: 28.9 km/sec

Planet Rabat is a relatively small gas giant that orbits the remote outskirts of Omega-47. While no commercial surveys have been conducted, cursory scans detect Hydrogen, argon, Neon and xenon in the upper atmosphere. The Corsairs initially attempted to harvest the outgassed Hydrogen and Oxygen caught in Rabat's rings, however this enterprise was abandoned with the Casablanca Offensive of 811 AS. In recent years, both Corsair and Red Hessian vessels have been sighted attempting to skim the rings for resources.

593481.text:
Discovered in 769 AS by an expedition mapping the uncharted systems beyond Freeport 5, Planet Gran Canaria was thought to be a new hope for a peaceful life on a hospitable world far from House territory. Hailed as a paradise world among the barren and lifeless rocks so common in the Edge Worlds, the local Zoners quickly took advantage of their discovery, sending a large survey and colonization team to the Omega-49 system, hoping to establish an independent colony there before other groups arrived in-system. Not long after, migrants fed up with living under House laws and taxes began arriving on Gran Canaria, establishing many loosely connected settlements around a particularly lush river delta.

In 772 AS, a jump hole to Dublin was discovered in an outcropping of the Barrier Nebula in the system, revealing that Omega-49 was much closer to Bretonian Space than had been thought. The Zoners, considering the overcrowding on planets New London and Leeds, realized that if the Bretonians discovered the system, the planet would be overrun by Bretonian settlers and possibly brought under Bretonian, or even worse, BMM control. Fearing that either Bretonia or the Mollys of Dublin would try to claim the system, the Zoners of Gran Canaria launched a series of disinformation campaigns seeking to hide any evidence of the world. For a time, the planet was hidden, but as the Dublin Conflict expanded, the Gran Canarians became concerned that Bretonia would eventually stumble upon the system during its endless skirmishes with the Mollys.

In 803 AS, the Gran Canarians made a strategic decision to disclose the routes into Omega-49 to the Corsair Empire, in exchange for protection from other aggressive parties and rights to establish their own settlements on the planet. Under this agreement the Zoners persuaded the Corsairs to treat the Freeports in their territory more favorably, while the Corsairs would develop a colony on the vibrant world and gain an alternate route to strike Bretonia and the Mollys from an unexpected quarter. This route was later used by the Corsair Empire to destroy the Molly colony on Planet Cork in the bitter conflict between Corsairs and Mollys in Poole.

Soon after Corsairs raiders began streaming through Bretonia from Omega-49, the system was discovered by both the Mollys and Bretonia. The Mollys, furious that the Zoners had sided with the Corsairs, found themselves unable to remove the established Corsair presence from the system, and the Bretonian Government was uninterested in the expense of a costly guerilla war against the entrenched Corsair forces on the planet while it had to respond to Kusari fortifying Tau-29 in 810 AS. Making friends of the Corsair Empire had bought the Gran Canarians time, but by 817 AS, Border World Exports had begun administering a refugee settlement on the planet, on the opposite hemisphere from the original settlements.

While the Zoners were successful in making the first claim to the planet, it proved to be only a temporary paradise, as the Omega-49 beta star has a highly elliptical orbit, and while it is near aphelion, the planet experience cyclic ice ages. Temperatures are expected to drop sharply over the coming years, and mass climate destabilization is expected while the seas fall and the glaciers advance.

The population of the planet jumped following the deployment of a force of Bretonian troops to hold the planet, and an exodus of Corsairs and Zoners unwilling to live under Bretonian occupation. In the months following the invasion, plans for large scale, organised and drastic settlement had been set in motion.

After the Gallic war ended, following the breakthrough in making Planet Carlisle habitable, the use of planet Gran Canaria became increasingly seen as an unnecessary burden on Bretonia, and the government enacted a policy of withdrawal from the volatile system in favor of the Newcastle system which is much safer and secured.

593482.text:
Lanzarote Station was originally constructed in 773 AS as a base of operations for the Zoner expedition that charted the Omega-49 system. Upon the discovery of the Dublin wormhole in 772 AS, the station was rapidly assembled by the Zoners, who saw significant potential in Gran Canaria. The orbit of Fuerteventura was chosen, as Zoner surveyors identified mineral deposits on the planet. Lanzarote was initially designed as a storage and transfer point for resources extracted from its icy surface. However, after Gran Canaria was deemed more suitable for preliminary colonization, these mining efforts were largely abandoned due to the logistical challenges of extracting and lifting materials from the arctic planet.

The abandonment of planetary mining, coupled with the collapse of the old wormhole connecting to Dublin - removing Lanzarote from its strategic position between Bretonian space and Gran Canaria - left the station in need of a new purpose.

That new purpose emerged in 828 AS when the company "Gran Canarian Shipwrights" patented the ZC-410 "Peregrine" Civilian Frigate. Instead of manufacturing the frigate on Gran Canaria, the Zoners repurposed Lanzarote Station into a minor shipbuilding facility. It primarily supports the production of the Peregrine, along with smaller Zoner vessels like the Osprey. The station also functions as a minor trading and refueling outpost for ships unwilling to land on Gran Canaria as they transit through the deeper Omegas.

593483.text:
A frozen, lifeless world, Fuerteventura was surveyed by the Zoners upon their arrival in the system. Lanzarote Station was constructed in its orbit to facilitate the efficient transfer of resources and materials from the planet, aiding in the construction and colonization of Planet Gran Canaria. The most notable resource discovered was gold. While extracting it in significant quantities proved unfeasible, the amount that was mined played a role in accelerating Gran Canaria's early development.

Unfortunately, the scarcity of easily accessible natural resources on the planet forced the Zoners to import raw materials from other systems. Over time, they shifted their reliance to resources available on Planet Gran Canaria itself. The high costs of maintaining a gold mining operation led to its eventual abandonment. Today, Fuerteventura serves as a silent companion to Lanzarote Station, which has found a new purpose: the production of the ZC-410 "Peregrine," the latest Zoner-originating frigate on the market.

593484.text: Scanners read this elongated lump of metal as being not just another piece of scrap but an older model of the C-class utility transport; caked with grime and decay, it's hardly identifiable after centuries in the Grande Negra. The only database match is the Ft. Worth, a supply vessel that had been dispatched to Dallas with a load of Gate/Lane Parts sometime immediately prior to the Texas Incident of 500 AS

593485.text: This tattered Piranha wreck is only recognizable by its shape; most all else has been eaten away over the years, although certain protrusions might be intact weaponry. Judging by its position in the Pequena Negra, it might be the Avenger, last registered to Bounty Hunter Annie "Shorty" Davis; she was presumed dead in 801 AS after being dragged through the dark matter cloud by an Outcast bandit.

593486.text: Though etched by dark matter and fried by years of irradiation, this wreck is still clearly identifiable as a pirate Bloodhound; likely the Rogue fighter Prudhoe, reported missing in 800 AS after it vanished into the Pequena Negra while hauling contraband Diamonds.

593487.text: A relatively small gas planet with no useful resources. The LPI Sugarland prison station and recycling operation orbits nearby, dumping much of its toxic waste into the planet's gravitational well. Every criminal on Sugarland sees blue when waking up; for those labelled NCR, blue and grey will be all there is to see ever again.

593488.text:
Casablanca Base orbits the gas giant Rabat in Omega-47, serving as a supply depot, staging point and emergency repair dock for local Corsair forces. Constructed by the Corsairs in 810 AS, Casablanca was intended to be an experimental gas miner in what was then an uncontested system. Despite this, it did not take long for Red Hessian scouts to identify the Corsairs' activities, and perceive them as a threat on their flanks in Omega-5. They quickly launched the Casablanca Offensive of 811 AS, driving the Corsairs out of the system and capturing the base. This opened Omega-47 as a major theatre of the war, with the Hessians using Casablanca as a fortified position to repel attacks from Omega-55.

The Treaty of Casablanca was signed aboard in 813 AS, securing the alliance between the Red Hessians and the previously aloof Coalition. This intended to check Corsair influence across the Omegas, bolstering the Hessian position in Omega-5, which had been nearing collapse. This partnership was put to the test in early 819 AS, when the Corsairs launched the Second Casablanca Offensive. The two-pronged attack from Omega-5 and 55 succeeded in capturing Casablanca but stalled soon after, failing in its remaining objectives of eliminating Tangier, and pushing on into Omega-52.

Since then, Casablanca has been renovated several times, to repair battle damage and expand its facilities. This most prominently includes the addition of an armored drydock, capable of providing emergency repairs to lighter classes of capital ship. In cases of the utmost desperation, damaged Corsair cruisers may attempt to break through the Coalition's lines to Casablanca from Omega-5. In recent years, the Corsairs have also resumed scavenging resources from Rabat's rings, with the harvested gasses shipped back to Omicron Gamma for industrial uses. The local garrison is frequently required to scramble fighters to assist the convoys of armored transports that supply the base through Omega-55.

593490.text:
The craft before you is affixed in a way that feels unnatural. Like a corpse mangled in death, frozen in a position that leaves a permanent record on the mind. The longer you look at it, the more you feel something is looking back at you. Inspecting the damage reveals that the ship has been torn into three neat pieces, surprisingly almost of equal size and from this close the recorded distress signal can be received and played back, otherwise no doubt rendered lost to all the interference of the anomalies. The message itself seems to just be white noise, but something seems to echo in the background, like the gentle hum of a person in song. Listening closely, it sounds like words are whispered.

"Here to stay. Here to stay. Here to stay."

593492.text:
>>>WARNING: EXTREME GRAVITATIONAL ANOMALY<<<

The almost wistful and decrepit core of the gate left behind by the cataclysmic failure of the Dallas project. Had fortune been kinder, this would have served as a gateway between worlds. Instead it serves as a monument to the fact that Ageira is far from infallible.

593494.text: The Hubble was for its time a famed research liner, crewed by some of Liberty's most eminent explorers and scientists. Their reputation for being on the forefront of discoveries was ultimately the sole cause of their untimely demise, but their legacy still lives on in the form of a chilling picture of the gate overloading.

593496.text:
This Patriot-class interceptor belonged to officer Amy Douglas, assigned to the Dallas Project security unit. It was a prestigious appointment within the LPI and widely coveted by officers of all stripes. When the gate began to malfunction, she tried to escape, hoping her ship could outrun the ensuing blast wave.

It is clear from the well preserved body behind the canopy that she did not make it.

593498.text: This ship is part of a convoy on the way to the Dallas project site, frozen in time with its crew likely having been killed instantly.

593501.text: Cricket was a smalltime mercenary who primarily offered his services to Liberty's finest and her corporations. Stuck here now and left with a contract forever unfulfilled.

593503.text: A Liberty Navy patrol group, consisting of three fighters on a routine patrol path around the Dallas project site, they had just been launched when the wave of dark matter washed over their outpost in lethal amounts.

593505.text: Despite the almost rabid enthusiasm of the project leaders, many of their chief engineers and technicians felt that the gate's output threshold simply went beyond the norms of what the infrastructure housing it could handle. This ship was accordingly contracted by them in secret, to deliver a batch of prototype wormhole stabilizers, hoping this would offset the risks posed by the clearly volatile activation process. Instead, the timeline was accelerated and the gate was turned on before the ship reached its destination.

593507.text: A pair of LPI interceptors instructed to make sure the Ferryman, which had been classified as a high priority asset to Ageira, reached its destination without having to endure the hassle of petty pirates.

593509.text: A Pelican that was tasked with having to rotate personnel away from the project site, it had only just departed with people who had completed their tenure of involvement here.

593511.text: Paul was a middle aged "veteran" of the LPI that had earned his involvement in overseeing much of the security arrangements at the periphery of the site. He had been largely strict and professional about his duties, but his subordinates had developed a great sense of affection for him over the time they had worked together. His Patriot was pulling in to dock, and his colleagues were waiting on the other side of the threshold to surprise him with a birthday cake.

593513.text: A Synth Foods transport having its hold full of synth paste unloaded.

593515.text: The clamps had just locked in place when the Captain complained that the sun was obscuring his view from the helm, soon made aware of the fact that they were not actually facing it.

593517.text: The headquarters of the historic effort to create a galaxy spanning jump corridor, it was at that point in history the home of some of Liberty's brightest minds and most skilled engineers.

593519.text:
The wreck of the Hassani belonged to Red Hessian ace Jakob Bautzen, whose ship was disabled during a failed raid to capture Casablanca from the Corsairs. Bautzen attempted to flee the area while being pursued by Corsair patrols. He managed to shake them in the dense El Aaiun field, but the damage to his fuel compartment was too severe.

Stranded without fuel in the middle of nowhere, the pilot was destined for a slow death. However, the equipment appears to remain intact.

593521.text: Harry Emerson, test pilot for Division 42, was one of the recent casualties of the Tau War. He was killed while on a weapon testing mission, and though he was not killed by the Kusari Naval Forces, the Cardamine smugglers who stumbled upon him made short work of his ship during a brief skirmish, near the Tau-31 Jump Hole.

593523.text: The wreck of the Adventure Galley, belonging to an infamous Liberty Rogue ace called Jacob Crowley. After fleeing from the Liberty Navy into the Raiden dark matter cloud, his ship was crippled by the excessive radiation and he was forced to use his escape pod. Incredibly, a fellow Rogue patrol picked him up and he survived, but they were unable to locate his ship and it has lain in the dark matter cloud since, hidden from sensors.

593526.text: The wreck of the venerable Gettysburg stands as a reminder to the people of Bretonia of the sacrifice of the Liberty Navy in defense of its capital against the Gallic onslaught that threatened to conquer both houses.

593528.text: Cheronsee was destroyed in the Kusari Blitz of Tau-23 by the Battleship Nagasaki. Defenders of the base had little warning of the attack, and the main command module of the base was pounded until it cracked, with the rest of the base mostly intact.

593530.text: This wreck is all that is left of the Lane Hacker base that once occupied this space.

593533.text:
CLASS: Under construction
GRAVITY: No
DOCKING: No
AMENITIES: N/A
CREW: 0

In the aftermath of the Gallic War, the Bretonian government was left to pick up the pieces. The grim calculus of the situation rested on the fact that Leeds was perhaps the single most important economic engine in Sirius, and the Gallic invasion and the Glassing had left it in irreparable ruins. Reconstruction efforts quickly began regardless, in an attempt to restore some semblance of what was. BMM had jumped at the opportunity to restore LD-14, which was completed in 832 AS thanks to generous state grants. Despite this, the Stokes junction silently languished for years.

In late 833 the first haltering signs of a reconstruction project emerged -- little more than a series of depots and refueling stations for BMM asteroid miners heading into the Stokes Asteroid Field. Rumors swirled that the Crown had revoked the Stokes development charter in hopes of selling it to a foreign party, given the dire financial hardship suffered by many of BMM's autonomous concerns. A bidding process involving Daumann, Deep Space Engineering, and Samura was eventually resolved in mid 835 AS, with Samura ultimately prevailing. The project began in earnest early the next year, after joint ownership contracts and financial investments were secured.

It is expected that BMM will eventually manage the day to day operations of the refinery, with Samura obtaining a share of all profits and resources produced.

593537.text: Bristol Depot is an independent base in Bering.

593539.text: The wreck of the Muscat, former sister ship of the Pamiers. The ship was lost during the retreat to Languedoc in the Kusari invasion of 827.

593542.text:
Once representative of the new Charlemagne-class Battleships built by the Confederacy, the Les Voges and its sister ship, the Hossegor, saw little action before the outbreak of war with Kusari. Having spent such little time training, the obvious result was a lack of experience both for the crew and officers. In spite of substantial efforts to adapt to the changing situation on the battlefield, the Les Voges posed no challenge to the Matsumoto and Hamamatsu battlegroups.

Its wreck is in a highly radioactive state that prevents relocation, and the local Junkers have begun preying upon its components, drawing the ire of the Gallic Union's forces.

593544.text:
Much like its fleet’s flagship - the Epinal - the Sault spent a large portion of its service in regions held by the Gallic Royal Navy that were contested by the Council. During the closing days of the Second Gallic Civil War, the crew of the Saulx was unlike any other in its fleet -- a mixture of loyalists to the King, sympathizers of the Council, and a small number of personnel forcibly drafted into the Navy. The result was an incident that almost resulted in the ship being fired upon by its counterparts, largely due to an initial refusal to stand down upon receiving the order from Nevers.

The Confederacy did not overlook the incident, deciding that the best course of action would be to continue deploying the Saulx in the fringe regions of the state, ensuring that the crew was kept busy by the many enemies Gallia still had. In the initial days of the invasion by Kusari, the Saulx was the first to receive the baptism of fire from the Hamamatsu, resulting in a large portion of the hull being blown off and having to be sent to Avallon Fortress for emergency repairs.

Despite their differences the crew stood united in their fight against the Kusari Naval Forces, making their final stand in the northern regions of Burgundy and becoming one of the very last casualties of the war.

593546.text:
Like the ship's sister ship the Shimada, the Tawara was a state of the art Showa-class Battleship, expanding on the capabilities of the older Tokugawa-class. Designed by the Kusari Naval Forces to face off against the Valor-class, which had torn its way through their fleet in the Taus at the start of the Gallic Invasion, the Showa-class were heavily armed and armored in an attempt to match the Gallic Royal Navy ship for ship. The Tawara took this theory to the next level, with several additional mounting points being added for heavy weaponry, sacrificing defensive capability, but allowing the ship to act as a mobile artillery platform for the fleet.

During the invasion of Burgundy, it played one such crucial role when it was ordered to launch a devastating barrage upon Avallon Fortress, and later Nevers itself, footage of which was broadcast across Sirius. As the KNF was driven ever-closer to defeat, the Tawara continued to act in a support role until the onset of the retreat from Gallia, quickly becoming the center of the force which the rest of the fleet was arrayed around.

Led by a mishmash crew of Civil War and Tau War veterans, the Tawara refused to retreat with the rest of the fleet, knowing that if a delaying action was not fought, then the entire fleet would likely be picked apart piece by piece. Though successful in their chosen mission, the Tawara was always doomed to fall, with most of the crew dying at their stations as the ship’s systems failed one by one. It was the last Kusari warship disabled by the Confederacy, the smoldering wreck a valuable prize for hardliners in the soon to form Gallic Union, glad of the retribution carried out against the ship that had so publicly attacked them.

593548.text:
The Shimada - a state of the art Showa-class Battleship - was designed with the ability to go toe-to-toe with any Valor-class and prevail with ease. The crew was drilled to the highest of the Kusari Naval Forces standards, with frequent exercises taking place to simulate any possible scenario that the ship’s command crew could think of. This rigorous training proved extremely valuable when Kusari declared war on Gallia, as the invasion gave free reign to the veteran Kusari forces to devastate both the military and populace of the Confederacy.

With a swift move, the Shimada, alongside the rest of the forces gathered, crippled the Gallic defenses in Lorraine, then proceeded to advance into Burgundy, putting even New Paris at risk of capture. However, the sacrifice of the Epinal and the arrival of fresh ships to the battle forced the Kusari Naval Forces to retreat to a more favorable position in the northern reaches of the system.

The ship met its demise when the Gallic Navy launched an offensive to pin down the remainder of the Hamamatsu fleet, being the first of several losses that the KNF would suffer at the hands of the vengeful Gallic Navy, suffering heavily under the long range firepower that Gallic Battleships are so well known for.

593550.text:
The Ueda was a Toitsu-class Battleship launched shortly before the onset of the invasion of Gallia. With the ship's construction having been held up by the outbreak of the Civil War, it actually launched after the first of the new Showa-class Battleships, and as such crew priorities were given to the more advanced ships. This meant that the crew of the Ueda was assembled at the last minute, and the hope was that any necessary training could happen during deployment.

This strategy failed however, as the rapid advance of the Hamamatsu and its fleet into Gallia stretched Kusari’s limited manpower reserves to their limit. Being forced to deploy the Ueda regardless of the inexperience of the crew, it arrived to reinforce the fleet just in time to join the initial push into Burgundy. During this initial engagement, the Ueda was targeted by a flotilla of Gallant-class Cruisers, suffering heavy damage to the ship's engines in the fighting. Without the ability to withdraw the ship for repairs, it was decided that the Ueda would instead assume a position at the very front of the fleet, helping to reduce the need for the ship to maneuver.

This led to the ship also taking increased fire, and a well-timed shot from the Hossegor knocked out all power to the ship, leaving it completely defenseless. Managing to weather the fire directed at the ship until the crew managed to restore power, the inexperienced officers of the Ueda thought that it would be able to engage the Epinal as it advanced towards the fleet. Shortly after they began their assault, another blow disabled all weapons aboard, and with no other option the Ueda rammed the Epinal at full speed.

The resulting explosion caused a shockwave that killed all hands aboard both ships, and the Ueda now lies in space next to the ship's nemesis, the Epinal.

593552.text:
Dortmund Station was the primary processing facility and headquarters of ALG Waste Disposal. Prior to the Rheinland Civil War, ALG had expanded Dortmund into the re-smelting of Scrap Metal and Toxic Waste to produce Alloys and MOX, and were also experimenting with the production of High-Temperature Alloys.

Following the Imperial coup of 827 AS, ALG's relationship with what they perceived as an illegitimate government soured. As a result, the Imperial Military attempted to capture Dortmund to secure the production of strategically vital MOX.

This attempt failed however, and the base was scuttled to deny the Imperials their desired fuel source. The wreck was quickly shunted into the Ruhrfeld in the hope of preventing contaminants from leaking out into the lane junction and endangering traffic. So far ALG has shown little interest in taking on the clean-up operation for the station, however the Junkers have done a lively job of picking over its carcass for valuable salvage.

593554.text: The Tsuyama was an escort of the Hyono, before it was destroyed fighting Gallic forces in Languedoc.

593556.text: The Roussanne was an escort of the De Grasse, before it was destroyed in the second battle of Languedoc.

593557.text:
CLASS: Tyrell
GRAVITY: Complete
DOCKING: Yes
AMENITIES: Limited
CREW: 340
593557.mapped: San Diego Border Station monitors the Magellan Jump Gate to stem the rise of criminal activity throughout the area, particularly that of Lane Hackers, Rogues, and Outcasts. The facility is entirely owned and operated by Liberty Police, Inc. (LPI) and its support staff. The station was destroyed during the Gallic war, but was later rebuilt to return to its original role.

593558.text: San Diego Border Station monitors the Magellan Jump Gate to stem the rise of criminal activity throughout the area, particularly that of Lane Hackers, Rogues, and Outcasts. The facility is entirely owned and operated by Liberty Police, Inc. (LPI) and its support staff. The station was destroyed during the Gallic war, but was later rebuilt to return to its original role.

593561.text:
The wreck of the Battlecuiser Blackrock. Following the conclusion of the Gallic War, the Blackrock was redeployed to secure Bretonian interests in the Dublin system.

With the Ark Royale being repositioned closer to Dublin, the Blackrock took the opportunity to bait the Carllion out of the asteroid field for an open engagement, to end the threat it has posed on Bretonian shipping and mining in the system. Both the Carrillion and Blackrock fleets fought to a near standstill before the Mollys of Dublin deployed their own ambush over the remnance of both forces.

593562.text: First sighted by Bretonia Mining and Manufacturing employees in the Dublin system, the Battlecruiser Carillon has repeatedly disrupted mining operations of the BMM in the system. Employing hit and run tactics, the miners have little to no alternative to fleeing whenever the warship strikes. However, the Carillon does not appear to be part of the major force amassing for an assault on New London, and so it is believed that the Carillon is affiliated with the Gallic Royal Intelligence in order to disrupt Bretonian commerce in Dublin. The luck of the ship would run out however, and it was destroyed fighting the Blackrock by opportunistic Molly forces.

593564.text: This Destroyer was destroyed fighting the many enemies of the Molly cause.

593566.text:
The remains of the APM transport vessel christened as Brilliance, which was commanded by the relatively successful captain Charlotte Sterris with Bretonian origins.

Charlotte Sterris was an outstanding transport captain and was known for several successful blockade runs during the Gallic War. She joined APM once the war ended, selling her skills to the highest bidder around Bretonia.

The Brilliance became her personal ship and thanks to her blockade running experience, it became a thorn in the Order's and Corsairs' side as they have not been able to intercept her successfully, only losing several fighters when trying to do so.

But it was not the Order or Corsairs who finally managed to catch her vessel off guard as the wreck bears critical damage caused by alien weaponry. Cut marks around the airlocks suggest that the vessel has been boarded afterwards and there is no whereabouts of what happened with the crew. There is a slight possibility that there still might be valuable cargo onboard.

593568.text:
The Epinal was an aging Richelieu-class Battleship that saw much of its service being deployed in the Champagne and Lorraine systems to counter Council activity. In the late stages of the Second Gallic Civil War, it was the first ship to stand down after receiving permission from the newly-proclaimed Grand Duchy of Burgundy. Subsequently, it remained a vanguard of the new Gallic Confederacy in Lorraine, whilst also guarding the important border fortress that overlooked the boundary with the Taus.

When Kusari launched their invasion of Gallia, the Epinal was the first line of defence against the advancing Kusari forces. Forced to cede more and more territory to the invaders, the Epinal was withdrawn to Burgundy, having bought enough time for the Confederacy to move ships to reinforce it once it arrived.

Slowly withdrawing towards the Picardy Jump Gate, the Epinal was the core of the fleet that stood between the Naval Forces and the Gallic Core Worlds. Shortly before reinforcements were due to arrive from deeper in Gallia, the KNF launched a desperate attack to take the Jump Gate, which would have allowed them to hold there and consolidate their position. Determined to hold out, the Epinal led its fleet in a brilliant defense, managing to force the KNF forces to withdraw in the face of their unrelenting firepower.

This would also lead to the ship's undoing. One of the attacking KNF ships, the Ueda, had been disabled partway through the battle. Managing to restore power to their ship, the Ueda’s crew launched into a headlong attack directly into the teeth of the Epinal, knowing that any attempt to retreat would simply lead to their own demise. Seeing this attack coming but with little time for the ship's more conventional weapons to be brought to bear, the Epinal began charging the massive Warwolf cannon, hoping to destroy the charging Ueda in a single well placed shot.

The Ueda struck the Epinal just as the massive cannon finished charging, but before it could fire its devastating payload, feeding back into the main reactor and causing a critical failure. The resulting explosion, believed to be the largest man-made explosion in recorded history, consumed both ships, as well as many smaller ships in the immediate vicinity. The explosion - visible as far away as Nevers - caused the entire battle to come to a stand still for a brief moment, which was only broken when the nearby gate activated and the Gallic reinforcements started to pour through.

593570.text: Shunan was an escort of the Yamaguchi.

593575.text:
The Bradford, a Victoria class Dunkirk ship, was an escort of the Grimsby until its demise in 827. Originally hailing from the Derby fleet, the aging Dunkirk was selected as the vanguard for the Invasion of Edinburgh due to the age of the ship.

Facing almost certain doom upon entry, the Bradford was reduced to a skeleton crew prior to the operation. Nicknamed the "greybeard" due to corrosion of the "beard" section of the Dunkirk chassis, not much of the front section of the ship would survive the onslaught from Gallic Royal Navy defensive placements. The sacrifice however would not be in vain, as the remaining ships of the Grimsby fleet entered after it, pathing the way for the eventual pacification of Edinburgh.

593577.text: The Hornsea was an escort of the Grimsby until its untimely demise in Edinburgh in 827. Together with the Grimsby and Rutland it succeeded in breaching the first layer of defenses following the sacrifice of the aged Bradford. Together with the Grimsby it was succesful in holding the La Riche and Dax fleets around the Leeds hole, while the Macduff and Ark Royal arrived to force the Gallic Royal Navy to pull back to the safety of their final lines at Gaia. The Hornsea, like other Grimsby vessels, took the brunt of the fighting, and would not survive the battle.

593579.text: Rutland was an escort of the Grimsby. One of the first Invincible class Dreadnoughts constructed by Bretonia, it was given the daunting task of securing Edinburgh from former Gallic Royal Navy forces that had made the system their stronghold. While the Rutland fell in the ensuing battle, the Armed Forces consider the performance of the new design to be beyond expectations, the ship going toe to toe with even the heaviest of Gallic capital ships and holding its own.

593581.text: The Chartes was an escort of the La Riche. The Chartes found itself in direct competition with a much larger Bretonian capital ship than those seen in New London, and became embroilled in an uncharacteristically close range battle with the Rutland, a Dreadnought. Outclassed by the state of the arc Bretonian warship, Chartes pulled a tactic from the York and attempted to ram the Rutland, achieving a more solid impact than the York was able to, but ultimately rendering itself inoperable.

593583.text: The Breteuil was an escort of the La Riche. Like La Riche itself, the Breteuil would not survive to see Gallia again, falling in defense of Edinburgh, the last bastion of Gallia in Bretonia.

593585.text:
Valletta Mooring Terminal serves as the central trading hub of Omicron Alpha. It is primarily used for loading and unloading cargo, refitting ships, and providing emergency servicing for Outcast military vessels too large to land on Malta.

With the Cardamine trade stabilizing after the Maltese slave revolt, the terminal has returned to being busy and active, bringing wealth to the Maltese people.

593587.text: Epirus Mooring Terminal is the main trade center in Omicron Gamma. Its primary purpose is loading and unloading Artifacts or goods being brought to Crete, as well as emergency repairs for military vessels.

593590.text:
The Battleship Wessex was originally stationed outside the research facility Sunderland when it was first being built, but after many years it was decided that the battleship was unnecessary as the alien ruins were completely lifeless. Shortly after the Nomad War, however, it was decided to station the newly commissioned Grimsby nearby to reassure the public.

Many of the scientists initially objected to having a heavily armed battleship keeping watch over Sunderland, but in recent times strange raids by unidentified hostile ships has persuaded a lot of the protestors to accept the military guard force as a neccesity.

At the end of the Gallic invasion, the Grimsby and her escorts were been diverted to Leeds in order to secure Bretonia's route to Tau space. Like most of the Bretonia Armed Forces, Grimsby's fleet is operating well below full strength, but the crew are confident they can handle whatever might oppose them.

The Grimsby was to take part in the invasion of Edinburgh in late 827, facing the majority of the fighting around the Leeds entry point, and suffering disproportionate casualties as a result. The Grimby was lost with all hands in the fighting.

593591.text:
From orbit, Planet Carlisle initially appears lush and hospitable. The ideal atmosphere, rolling jungles and deep oceans presented a pristine jewel in the barren wastes of The Barrier. When the earliest IMG explorers first landed in 669 AS, they discovered that Carlisle’s sweltering rainforests concealed a deadly secret. The biosphere was saturated with hostile strains of bacteria, many immediately deadly to humans. Highly contagious infections spread through the body like wildfire, dissolving internal organs. This devastating threat effectively stalled any consideration of colonization until a resolution could be found.

The “Carlisle Problem” became a long running project of Cambridge Research Station’s hot labs, studying how bacterial eradication could be achieved reliably and at scale. On-site trials began in 812 AS after Cryer Pharmaceuticals synthesized a protein capable of neutralizing the bacteria under lab conditions. This did not translate into real world results, as an effective delivery mechanism remained elusive. Despite setbacks caused by the Gallic War, a breakthrough came in 825 AS, when a joint Cryer-Planetform partnership successfully deployed an aerosolized treatment through adapted terraforming generators.

By 827 AS, this network of generators had created a 500km radius, self-certified “clean zone”. Cambridge University academics have warned of protein contamination across the wider Carlisle biosphere, and challenged the rigor of Cryer’s safety testing. Despite this, the Bretonian government quickly moved to certify Carlisle as fit for colonization, due to the urgent need to create jobs and housing for the enormous Refugee population scattered across Liberty, Rheinland and New London. To fund the colony, Bretonia has been forced to sell colonial development and extraction charters to Liberty corporations such as Universal Shipping and DSE.

Boom towns have now begun to sprout across Carlisle’s Clean Zone, focusing on mining, logging and manufacturing. Many among the Bretonian government see Carlisle as the only sustainable, long term solution to the loss of Leeds, owing to Sprague’s precarious location and disastrous development. Smog-belching factories have begun to churn out locally produced Consumer Goods and Industrial Materials. Organized crime quickly took root on Carlisle however, with the planet becoming an epicenter for Slog production and distribution. Gaian terrorist cells frequently strike at targets across the planet, usually hitting terraforming generators or deforestation camps.

593593.text:
CLASS: Orion
CREW: CLASSIFIED
ARMAMENT: CLASSIFIED
593593.mapped:
The Carrier Orion is a warship derived from the rugged Bustard-class platform. Commissioned by the Technocracy in 824 AS to serve as a command-and-control ship and electronic warfare platform, the Orion was placed into military service following a prototyping phase involving Technocrat and Zoner research teams.

Acting as the Technocracy's primary staging point for operations beyond Valravn's reach, the Orion was initially deployed in the borderworlds connecting Rheinland to Gallia, where it monitored the activities of both lawful forces and the Hessians during clashes over Tholey Station. Throughout this deployment, Orion kept a safe distance from any patrols, and after Rheinland's reunification there was little reason to remain in Cologne. Thus, the carrier was redeployed to Omicron Kappa.

Apart from brief hostilities when the Core's Battleship Mars attempted to enter the system in 829 AS, the Orion spent most of its time conducting scientific experiments in Gammu's orbit. Its research efforts were abruptly halted when the Mars returned to Kappa; this time, it came with a larger supporting fleet in order to launch the conquest of Planet Gammu. Still essentially a civilian capital ship despite her modifications, the Orion had to withdraw from Gammu's orbit around the time the artificial intelligences decided to abandon the planet.

The Orion, accompanied by AI vessels, sustained noncritical damage during an engagement with a Corsair heavy patrol in the Malvada Cloud. Despite these setbacks, the damaged Orion managed to reach Primus Outpost safely, where it undertook gradual repairs in preparation for its planned departure to Inverness for refit and resupply.

As the emergency repairs have been completed, the Orion returned to Inverness where it will stay until it is fully functional again.
