593607.text:
CLASS: Bakumatsu
CREW: N/A
ARMAMENT: N/A

The Battleship Yamaguchi was among the first generation of the Bakumatsu class, deployed in 813 AS to bolster Kusari's ambitions in the Taus. The Yamaguchi -- as all Bakumatsu battleships -- was criticized for the lack of innovation in its design, which Samura had produced as a minor modernization on the much older Meiji class. The Battleships Yamaguchi and Nagasaki were the speartip of the KNF's expeditionary force during the 813 AS Tau War with Bretonia. This culminated with the Invasion of Leeds in 816 AS, and the capture of Stokes Mining Station the following year. During a tour of the front lines by Emperor Jien Kogen in 818 AS, disaster struck when Gallia launched the Invasion of Sirius.

The Gallic Royal Navy poured into the Taus, slamming into the flanks of Kusari's supply lines. Caught between the Gallic fleet and Bretonian defenses, the 8 Day War saw much of Kusari's Tau fleet destroyed, and the expeditionary force stranded abroad. When a coup toppled the government in the Emperor's absence, the Yamaguchi and Nagasaki refused to recognize the new Republic's legitimacy. The so-called Exiles pledged their service to the Emperor, and swore to retake their home. The Yamaguchi was then contacted by Council Gallic dissidents, who provided a route to their new refuge in Roussillon. They hoped the Exiles would restore a Kusari that was hostile to the Gallic crown, opening another front in the war.

For several years, the Yamaguchi resupplied from Council bases, while striking Gallic and Kusari collaborator targets across the Taus. In 824 AS, both Exile battleships reunited to initiate the Kusari Civil War with the Kyushu Uprising. Following reunification and restoration of the Imperial line the following year, the Yamaguchi received extensive repairs and modernization. This delayed its deployment to the Saigon War against Rheinland, which saw Kusari repulsed from Sigma-21. The Yamaguchi instead reinforced the Hyono in Honshu, cutting Rheinland supply lines and helping to force the eventual peace. The Battleship then patrolled the Sigma border, before being recalled to Kyushu in 827 AS, amid disputes with the Crayter Republic.

The KNF expelled the Republic from Tau-31, however this was a pretext to maneuver their fleets closer to the Gallic border for a surprise invasion. Gallic Confederal forces were shocked when the Hyono, Nagasaki, and Yamaguchi fleets swung north into Tau-23, rapidly breaching Languedoc. The Yamaguchi then led a flanking assault, decisively defeating Confederal forces at the Battle of Sete. The Battle of Agde marked the turning point of Kusari's campaign -- after dispatching the Le Fierte and pressing towards the Ile-de-France Jump Gate, the Yamaguchi was crippled by the Battleship Embrun. Decloaking and launching salvos of torpedoes and trebuchets at short range, the Yamaguchi's reactor detonated before the crew could react.

593609.text:
CLASS: Charlamagne (Redemption)
CREW: N/A
ARMAMENT: N/A

The Charlemagne battleships were designed around 676 AGS (760 AS), specifically for defensive and support purposes. Battleships of this class were configured to hold and maintain large numbers of fighters and cover them with powerful point defense turrets. The La Fierte was deployed from Rambouillet Shipyard in 697 AGS (781 AS), serving unremarkably until it was assigned to the Marne Pacification Fleet in 712 AGS (796 AS). One of several Council infiltrated warships, the La Fierte defected upon entering Marne orbit, initiating the Battle of Champagne and contributing to the Council's liberation of the system. Due to their dramatic sorties against royal assaults, the Le Fierte's strike wings quickly became the pride of Marne.

The Invasion of Sirius lessened the GRN's focus on Champagne, allowing the La Fierte to strike into Picardy in the hope of inciting unrest on Planet Amiens. When news of war crimes and military collapse trickled back to the core systems in 742 AGS (826 AS), the Le Fierte launched an attack on Amiens. The Battleship Samur immediately surrendered, while Le Fierte's fighters supported revolts across the planet in toppling the leaderless Royal Army regiments. Having secured Picardy for the Gallic Republic, the battleship pushed into to Ile-de-France to support the planned Council assault on New Paris. In the uncomfortable peace following the emergence of the Gallic Confederacy, the La Fierte returned to Picardy to suppress Enclave holdouts.

Following much needed repairs and maintenance, the battleship was assigned to Zurich to oversee the completion of the trade corridor connecting to Rheinland. Within days of the Alsace Passage's opening in 743 AGS (827 AS), Rheinland devolved into civil war. The Confederacy reeled with shock as the Red Hessians conquered Cologne and the Federalist battleship Karlsruhe fled into Gallic territory. Fearing an incident that would drag them into the conflict, the La Fierte was ordered to intern the battleship. While negotiating the Karlsruhe's surrender, Captain Michaud instead agreed to provide supplies for an assault on Cologne, intending to dislodge the Red Hessians and re-open trade.

When the Karlsruhe eventually departed, it slipped through Cologne and instead invaded Stuttgart. Outraged, the Confederal Navy would have court martialled Captain Michaud for insubordination, were it not for the Kusari Invasion of Gallia. The La Fierte was rushed to Languedoc to support the collapsing Minarchy positions, arriving to reinforce the Confederal lines during the Battle of Agde. The La Fierte's strike wings performed according to the mythos they had developed during the Second Gallic Civil War, punching the holes in the Battleship Yamaguchi's escorts that the Embrun later exploited. The La Fierte's valiant but fatal last stand brought time for the joint Confederal-Enclave counter assault that ended Kusari's advance towards Ile-de-France.

593611.text:
CLASS: Richelieu
CREW: N/A
ARMAMENT: N/A

The Richelieu battleships were designed around 731 AGS (815 AS) to correct design flaws identified in the Normandie class during the Second Gallic Civil War. Richelieu battleships provided a blend of withering firepower and heavy armor, built around the fearsome Warwolf spinal cannons. By the time of the Gallic invasion of Sirius, the modernized Richelieus were used as the armored fist of the Gallic Royal Navy, inflicting a deadly toll during their engagements with Bretonia, Kusari and Liberty. As one of the first Richelieus, the Rocroi saw extensive service during the Second Gallic Civil War. Led by Rear Admiral Bastien de Fontenoy, the unwaveringly loyal fleet was charged with the defense of the King and Planet New Paris.

When the GRN collapsed in 742 AGS (826 AS), the Rocroi executed plans to evacuate the King. To their shock, the King had already vanished, consumed by paranoia that the Navy was planning to betray him. Instead, the Rocroi prepared Ile-de-France's garrison for a forlorn and bloody resistance against The Council's looming assault. When de Fontenoy and his crew received a ceasefire order from the Grand Duchy of Burgundy, it was seen as a gross betrayal of their oath. In the chaos of the Gallic Confederacy's formation, the Rocroi and its fleet slipped away to Burgundy, hoping to find noble supporters to aid in toppling Grand Duke Valentin Trintignant, and restore the absent King Charles at the head of the Gallic Enclave.

Her campaign against Confederal and Maquis forces in Burgundy was cut short by the Kusari Invasion the following year. As the situation became increasingly dire for Gallia, the Confederation was forced into negotiations with the Enclave on reintegration. As a result, the Enclave ordered the Rocroi south, to support a renewed counteroffensive in Languedoc. Significanty, the Rocroi succeeded in destroying the retreating Battleship Hyono with its Warwolf cannon, before being dispatched in turn by the Nagasaki's fleet. The battleship's survivors have since been awarded prestigious postings throughout the Gallic Union fleet, with now-Admiral de Fontenoy appointed to lead Compiegne Naval Academy.

593613.text:
CLASS: Normandie
CREW: N/A
ARMAMENT: N/A

The Normandie battleship design was first deployed around 656 AGS (740 AS) for offensive assault purposes. These ships were produced in large numbers by royal Gallic shipyards until the early 730s (810s), when the battles of the Second Gallic Civil War revealed several critical flaws in the ships’ construction. Existing vessels were retrofitted to correct various defects, but no new Normandies were built - instead the modernized Richelieu class was developed. Normandie battleships formed the bulk of Gallia’s original Sirius invasion forces.

The Embrun was deployed in 710 AGS (794 AS) and saw initial service against The Council, before joining the invasion of Bretonia in 735 AGS (819 AS). Using irregular tactics, it struck military and civilian targets across Newcastle and Manchester, quickly accruing a merciless reputation amid accusations of war crimes. It is believed that the Embrun topped the Bretonian Armed Force's most wanted list for several years, gaining an enormous bounty in the process. Commanded by Gallic Royal Intelligence special forces, the Embrun's squadrons were responsible for devious hit and run strategies that pinned Newcastle's fleets, preventing them from supporting the Allied efforts during the devastating Siege of New London.

Following the war's disastrous end in 742 AGS (826 AS), the Embrun was stranded behind Bretonian lines and unable to retreat to the Gallic Enclave in the Hebrides. Efforts to resupply by extorting Newcastle's Gaians were initially successful, however their compliance was a ruse to buy time for vengeful Gaian reinforcements to converge from across Bretonia. The improvised force struck the Embrun at an agreed supply rendezvous in the Craster Nebula early the next year. Guided by a local freelancer, the damaged battleship fled through a previously uncharted Jump Hole as a desperate means of escape. Little is known about the Embrun's activities until it reappeared later that year to aid Confederal forces during Kusari's Invasion of Gallia.

The battleship famously turned the tide of the Battle of Agde when it used a cloaking device to ambush the Battleship Yamaguchi, destroying its reactor. The Embrun was subject to withering counter-fire from the surrounding Kusari fleet, and broke in half after its hangar fuel tanks exploded. Regardless, the Yamaguchi's loss threw Kusari's forces into disarray, dooming the Languedoc advance. The Embrun's surviving crew members were hailed as heroes and have since been posted to senior positions throughout the Gallic Union fleet. The battleship's remains are now being salvaged at Briancon Station, under strict GNI supervision.

593615.text:
A Royal Enclave base, Rodez was a small, modular station that took after appraisal and scavenging of formerly Council-owned Perpignan. It was little more than a cluster of hangar modules.

Patrols from Rodez made frequent sorties in an attempt to crack down upon Brigand and Maquis presence striking from the system's fields and nebulae, but little progress can be made against such guerilla warfare given the means currently availible to the Enclave in Roussillon.

The Base would not survive the upheaval within the Enclave, and the Maquis, together with the Gaians from nearby Edinburgh destroyed the base and the Enclave within the system retreated to Orkney.

593617.text: The wreck of the prototype Carrier Warwick, rescued from Southampton Shipyard in the closing stages of the war by the Battleship York, it would be destroyed in the defense of Planet New London, and subsequently towed to the Belvedere Debris Field for eventual scrapping.

593619.text:
CLASS: La Mole
GRAVITY: None
DOCKING: No
AMENITIES: No
CREW: 0

Constructed in 663 AGS (747 AS), Fourchambault quickly grew to become a symbol of the Gallic Royal Navy's might in Languedoc. As the launching point for the inevitable invasion of Sirius, the shipyard produced armaments, ship parts, and even warships using Quillan's resources. In 733 AGS (817 AS), Fourchambault briefly fell to The Council, as sympathizers and infiltrated agents among the GRN garrison mutinied. The Council's occupation did not last long however, as their fleet and local supporters were pushed south into the Hebrides by the Crown's counterattack the following year. The GRN quickly boarded the station, and after repairing hasty sabotage efforts, returned the shipyard to service.

For the rest of the war, the grandiose installation repaired warships and logistics vessels damaged during the Invasion of Sirius. This made the facility a primary target for local Maquis terrorists, who successfully struck the station several times. As a result, the Gallic Monarchy was forced to maintain a significant garrison at all times, drawing troops away from the frontlines. In the chaos of the war's end and the collapse of the GRN, the shipyard was quickly seized by Provence's Minarchy, and used as a bargaining chip to secure their place in the newly created Confederacy.

When the Kusari Naval Forces invaded the system in 742 AGS (827 AS), the Gallic Confederacy committed significant reserves to holding Fourchambault. After several grinding, attritional battles, Kusari occupied the Ales junction, seizing the station. It was not until The Enclave's counter-attack and the creation of the Gallic Union later that year, that the Kusari presence was dislodged. Fourchambault was scuttled before Kusari withdrew, denying its use to Gallia. Following the war's end, the wreckage was shunted into the nearby Leucate Debris Field, where ALG has since begun salvage operations.

593621.text:
CLASS: Martel
GRAVITY: None
DOCKING: No
AMENITIES: No
CREW: 0

Montpellier Fortress was a defensive installation built by the Gallic Royal Navy in 651 AGS (735 AS). Constructed to deploy and then secure the minefield that blocked access to the Orkney system, it boasted a fearsome garrison and extensive defenses. For almost a century, Montpellier remained a state secret, visited only by Huissier spies launching long range missions into Sirius. In 733 AGS (817 AS), Montpellier and its guard fleet were cut off by The Council’s occupation of Languedoc. The Council’s plan to starve the fleet into submission was narrowly defeated by an audacious resupply operation launched through the Taus by Huissier smugglers from Lorraine.

The Council were instead forced onto the offensive, directly attacking Montpellier with the bulk of their local fleet. The GRN initially performed well, however the defense crumbled when the GRN Battleship Tarn was rammed by the Cruiser Solférino, and destroyed by an onboard fusion bomb. Council marines soon captured Montpellier, and began desperately funneling ships and materiel through the Jump Hole into Orkney. Early in 734 AGS (818 AS), the GRN launched its counterattack into Languedoc. The Council rapidly retreated from most of their gains, choosing to stand their ground at Planet Quillan and Montpellier, to buy time for the Council fleet and its sympathizers to evacuate from the King's wrath.

The Council marine rearguard left at Montpellier eventually fought to the death, preventing the GRN from capturing the station intact. After numerous failed boarding attempts, royal commanders were forced to reduce the fortress to molten scrap through repeated Warwolf bombardments. GRN fleets then began to pour into Orkney, executing the occupation of the Taus and the invasion of Sirius. Following the capture of Reunion Station, it was decided that rebuilding Montpellier was unnecessary. After the construction of the Tau-23 Jump Gate several years later, the Jump Hole crossing to Orkney was largely abandoned, with Montpellier accordingly falling into obscurity.

593623.text:
A rear-echelon warship for the entirety of the Second Gallic Civil War, some of the Gallic Navy's more hardened leaders lament that the La Riche survived instead of a seasoned warship such as the Embrun or Beuvray in her place. With the Royalist remnants beset on all sides by hostile powers, the La Riche has been deployed to Roussillon to safeguard against the Crayter Republic, the smallest and weakest of the Enclave's belligerant neighbors.

While the La Riche has so far managed to prevent Roussillon's significant Maquis presence from becoming overwhelming, it is unknown how well they would fare if met by a Crayterian strike force.

The La Riche was recalled to Edinburgh to take part in the defense of the system from the Bretonian invasion of late 827, where it mets its end in the fighting while other Enclave forces were able to withdraw.

593625.text:
>>>WARNING: NAVIGATION HAZARD<<<

This debris field was formed in 827 AS, after the Gallic Enclave stripped and then destroyed the sealed Gallic Jump Gate to Leeds. The shattered remains of the Jump Gate can be found in the center of the field.

593628.text:
CLASS: Liberte
GRAVITY: None
DOCKING: No
AMENITIES: No
CREW: 0

Originally constructed by The Council in 817 AS, Cordes began its service as Reunion Station. Following a decisive but short-lived victory in Languedoc, The Council breached the Montpellier Minefield and cleared a path into Orkney. The base was hastily assembled with aid from the first Sirians The Council encountered - the IMG. As The Council broadcast their existence to Sirius alongside dire warnings of the Gallic Crown's intentions, the station became the symbol of Sirius' very literal reunion with a seemingly lost Alliance nation, after seven centuries of seclusion.

The Council's warning to Bretonia and Liberty forced King Charles of Gallia to launch the invasion of Sirius immediately. By 818 AS, Languedoc had fallen entirely under Crown control, with Reunion captured soon after. Renamed to Cordes Outpost, the Gallic Royal Navy put the station to use as a logistics platform, supporting the fleet that was pouring through the Westray into Tau-23. This role continued until a permanent Jump Gate was constructed between Languedoc and Tau-23 in 821 AS. Then deemed redundant for supply purposes, the station fell into obscurity as little more than a Gallic Royal Intelligence listening post.

Despite -- or perhaps because -- of this, Cordes was one of the first installations to pledge loyalty to the Royal Enclave in 826 AS. After receiving reinforcements from the Battleship Montmorency, Cordes was fortified as a bulwark against Confederal Gallia and a launching point for raids into Gallic core space. This came to an end in late 827 AS with the incorporation of the Enclave into the Gallic Union. As a sign of good faith during negotiations with the then-Confederacy, Enclave leaders agreed to scuttle Cordes as a symbolic laying down of arms

593630.text:
CLASS: Westfalen
CREW: N/A
ARMAMENT: N/A

The Battleship Karlsruhe was completed in 813 AS alongside its sister ships Westfalen and Koblenz. Intended to revitalize the chronically under-equipped Rheinland Military, the Karlsruhe was deployed to Stuttgart in response to escalating LWB and Red Hessian attacks on Planet Stuttgart’s orbit. The Karlsruhe’s Marines were frequently deployed to execute arrest warrants against suspected LWB activists on the planet, leading to complaints from both the sidelined RFP and concerned progressive politicians. The captain of the Karlsruhe traditionally held a well-compensated seat on the Stuttgart Grower’s Association (WVS), while many officers moonlighted as Synth Foods security consultants.

The battleship saw no significant action until the Rheinland Civil War, avoiding deployment during the Hudson and Saigon Wars thanks to Stuttgart lobbying. Caught entirely unaware by the Imperial coup, the vessel was forced to fight off mutinous elements of its own battlegroup, before fleeing to Cologne to escape the approaching Battleship Altenburg. The Karlsruhe eventually withdrew to Zurich, after being forced from Cologne by the Red Hessian conquest. The Gallic Confederation demanded the Westfalen's internment for the duration of the conflict in an attempt to avoid being drawn into their neighbor’s dispute. Following months of difficult negotiations, the Westfalen’s captain eventually secured resupply and permission to depart, on the terms that the battlegroup only be used to attack the Red Hessians and reopen the Alsace Passage for neutral trade.

Despite this, the Karlsruhe immediately set a course for Stuttgart, avoiding Red Hessian positions. Having received orders to launch a diversionary attack in support of the Federalist summer offensive of 827 AS, the Karlsruhe’s reappearance immediately drew Imperial reinforcements from New Berlin and the Omegas. In the Battle of the Nordnebel, the Battleships Altenburg and Westfalen finally pinned the Karlsruhe, which ultimately sacrificed itself to enable the survivors of its battlegroup to escape. In the years since the Civil War, ALG has worked to decontaminate the outskirts of the Nordnebel, and recover the most sensitive pieces of military wreckage.

593632.text:
>>>CAUTION<<<
This field was formed by the Rheinland Civil War’s Battle of the Nordnebel. It contains the wrecks of the Battleship Karlsruhe, and support ships from the Altenburg and Westfalen fleets. Due to the highly toxic material leaking from the reactors of the ships, salvage operations are extremely hazardous. ALG has been offered a contract to isolate the highly radioactive reactor cores so they can be safely disposed of.

Junkers have been sighted in the field, despite subcontracting being prohibited by ALG’s terms of appointment. Many consider the cleanup effort to be an impossibility while the reactors are still ‘hot’, and see this project as little more than political theater. Despite this, New Berlin remains concerned about the possibility of radioactive materials or Military secrets falling into the hands of the Farmer’s Alliance, Red Hessians or Bundschuh.

593634.text:
Williamstown Depot was hastily constructed in 828 AS as a logistics hub and refueling platform for Liberty's invasion of Kansas. During the campaign against the Liberty Insurgency, Williamstown expanded significantly to keep pace with fleet demands for Munitions, H-Fuel and MOX. Shortly before the Insurgency stronghold of Vespucci was breached, much of the Depot's garrison were drawn away by a large diversionary attack on Philadelphia Station.

The remaining Liberty Navy fighters were quickly overwhelmed by an Insurgency force of bombers and gunboats which succeeded in detonating Williamstown's fuel tanks, as well as a number of moored fuel tankers. The station was never salvaged, instead being left to fall into Tremont's atmosphere where it will soon burn up. The LSF has long suspected that the attack was facilitated by intelligence provided by local Pennsylvania informants.

593636.text:
The Dreadnought Barcelona was the pinnacle of Corsair imperial ambition, intended to serve as an armored fist smashing through enemies in the Omegas and Sigmas. For this purpose, it was outfitted with the most modern and advanced weaponry available in 820 AS. For Crete, Barcelona was such a critical project that part of its systems required technical expertise from the Order.

However, these ambitions were never fully realized, mainly due to the Order's reluctance to assist the Corsairs in operationalizing such a dangerous vessel. This led to never-ending technical issues and complicated maintenance. Instead of becoming the steel fist leading Corsair armies, Barcelona was merely a mobile base in the Sigmas.

The final nail in the coffin for this battleship was an attempt to deploy it in Sigma-17 in 830 AS against the Outcasts, a task it ultimately failed to accomplish due to its unreliable systems. Shortly after that, due to the Prox's ability to perform Barcelona's job more efficiently, it was decided to decommission and scrap the ship. While the story of this majestic vessel is a sad one, the experiences gained from its operation and systems led to the development of much more efficient and deadly ships - the Tribunus-class battlecruisers.

593638.text: Remains of disabled pit-fighters. The ships appear to have been stripped of reusable internal components.

593640.text: The Nueburg is a disabled Rheinland gunship, apparently dating to a rumored raid on Dublin during the Colony Wars. The ship appears to have been destroyed when its engines were targeted. Broken and gaunt, it remains adrift near the Glorious as if an ill omen.

593642.text:
>>>WARNING: RESTRICTED AREA<<<
Access to the Craster Nebula has been restricted by Bretonian authorities due to the extreme navigational and radiation hazards within. The area has been the origin of numerous horror stories among pilots, as well as urban legends about bad luck or curses. This stems in part from rumors about the doomed Craster Initiative of the 670s, a BMM-funded project for domestic H-Fuel production. Despite (potentially fraudulent) early signs, no viable gas deposits were ever located, while dozens of workers lost their lives to accidents. When the project failed, several BMM subsidiaries declared bankruptcy and dissolved, leaving abandoned infrastructure littered across the area.

593644.text: A field of debris forming after Aland Shipyard was rendered inoperable.

593646.text:
This liner was disabled after a long chase in Pennsylvania after being stopped by a local patrol. After further inspection the liner was found to be laden with illegal Rheinland black market firearms, including many biological weapons thought to be intended for use in terrorist activities.

The owners of the ship escaped in light ships mid pursuit and are currently on the run. In an unprecedented move, the Battleship Delaware relocated to the scene to secure the area, known to be frequented by various undesirables.

593647.text:
CLASS: New Brooklyn
GRAVITY: Complete
DOCKING: Yes
AMENITIES: Yes
CREW: 350
593647.mapped:
Singlehandedly responsible for the rejuvenation of Planet Los Angeles' economy, Synth Foods sought to put all the profit gleaned from their operations from the ground to good use further beyond. To this end Riverside was constructed early in 815 A.S and equipped to accommodate a business venture complimentary to the mainstay of the food giant.

With a multitude of factions reaching for the stars and require a reliable stream of food to do so, Synth Foods saw that maintaining an orbital construction plant for biodomes would propel their business model into the infrastructure market as well. Groups like the Zoners or other ambitious parties carving out homes in the frontiers of space could be enticed to buy into Synth's compelling portfolio of not just food products, but the means by which to maintain life in such harsh places.

As a result, Riverside is a never ending forge for such complex structures and is a popular commercial and industrial destination in the system of California.

593650.text: The Sierra Vista Nebula is a remarkable sight for travellers passing through Coronado, and those that venture inside are met with a vast field of very large asteroids that render any travel through the field to be quite difficult for anything but small ships.

593652.text:
Constructed at the southern end of the Orkney system, Fort Albi was a small waystation for Gallic shipments and patrols being sent to the Bretonian front through the Hebrides and Taus. Additional modules were installed throughout the Gallic War to fortify the station against threats pouring from the Tau region.

With the end of the Gallic War, Fort Albi became a reinforced border station, providing much needed vigil from the lawless Taus. Although, recently the Gallic Union had repurposed the station to instead serve as a Bounty Hunters Guild headquarters in Gallia, deeming their potential to be more fruitful at her borders, rather than the heartlands.

The base would be abandoned following the appearance of Nomads within Orkney in addition to the cessation of trade flowing through the system.

593655.text:
CLASS: Eden
GRAVITY: None
DOCKING: No
AMENITIES: N/A
CREW: 0

The remnants of the Liverpool Border Station, which served as a coordination center and crew base for the Bretonia Police Authority in the Manchester system. During its operation, service at this station was considered a matter of great pride, with many families providing multiple generations of constables. In 829 AS, Liverpool was adopted as a staging post for the Armed Forces task force dispatched to aid the Liberty Navy with their campaign against the Insurgency.

The station's proud tradition was abruptly ended later that same year when the reactor was sabotaged, resulting in the loss of nearly two-thirds of the crew. Although the Mollys initially claimed responsibility for the attack, BPA investigators later dismissed this as incompatible with recovered evidence. Reconstructed security footage indicated that hacked service droids may have played a role in the attack, pointing the finger at either the Technocracy or Lane Hackers.

593657.text: Part of a trade convoy travelling from Vierzon, this unfortunate transport ship fell victom to a savage assault by Nomad ships. The Battlecruiser Sisteron arrived too late to prevent casualities, however further losses were prevented.

593660.text: This base is being towed to a new location.

593662.text:
Asahikawa Outpost formerly known as La Charite Spaceport, was Ile-De-France's first endeavor outside of the Kingdoms borders. La Charite was built with hopes of creating a trade hub where Gallic and Sirian business interests could mix and mingle. Under the nose of the Kingdom, the Spaceport gave opportunity to traders who were not authorised to enter Gallia to still conduct business.

IDF has not fared well following the dissolution of the Gallic Crown, its primary stockholder, and it was under scrutiny by the law enforcement agencies of the Gallic Confederation for suspected collaboration with the Royal Enclave. Because of this, there had been talks among upper management of relocating the company headquarters from Sarcelles Shipping Platform to La Charite as part of many proposals to reinvigorate the company and ensure its survival.

Ile-De-France's plan met a sudden end with the Kusari invasion of Gallic core space in 827 A.S, causing the station to fall under Kusari administration. Following the end of the conflict, La Charite was turned over to the Kusari State Police and was re-branded Asahikawa Outpost. The KSP slowly converted the installation into a proper Police hub. In order to better finance this project, most of Asahikawa's storage facilities - much to the displeasure of Samura - were rented out to Kishiro, effectively providing Samura's largest rival a small foothold in long-years uncontested space.

593664.text:
Samura has taken considerable blows in the last two decades. The loss of its exclusive Gas Miners Guild (GMG) H-Fuel contract meant a large portion of its shipping fleet would soon sit idle and the Tau invasion of Royal Gallia made an expansion into the Tau sector impossible for the time being. Samura however, still had several highly successful industries from which to draw on. Its recent Quantum Multiplexor products have begun to be adopted in Sirian shipbuilding. While expensive, Quantum Computing is much more powerful then traditional Optronic processing – a market almost exclusively dominated by Samura's main rival Kishiro.

With the demand for Quantum Multiplexors rising steadily, Samura erected Misaki Station as a large manufacturing plant exclusively for the purpose of speeding up their production. The absence of any larger gravitational bodies in Tau-53 provided the ideal environment – enabling the manufacturing plant to operate at almost absolute zero gravity which significantly increasing the manufacturing capabilities when compared to planet-side plants.

Misaki remained in relative seclusion until late 819 A.S. when Gallia revealed the existence of a Jump Gate connection to the Lorraine system. As Kusari and Gallia opened their borders for each other, Misaki became an important way-station for trade between the two houses. Following the rise of tensions between the two houses in 827 A.S. and the resulting cold relations, Misaki lost its position as way-station again but its Quantum Multiplexors production is still growing.

593666.text: This science ship is currently searching the local area for scientific value.

593669.text:
The battlecruiser Augusta is currently the Outcasts' newest warship, signifying a new shift in the strategic thinking of the Outcasts and their approach to military operations. It was launched at the Corsica Shipyard as the much larger, more obsolete, and cumbersome dreadnought Captana was decommissioned at the beginning of 831 AS. Like its sister ship, the Tercio, Augusta primarily serves as a mobile base for Outcast raiders in the area. It is mainly intended as heavy support for smaller, more agile, and in many ways, more effective Outcast fighter aces and gunships.

The full commissioning of Augusta was interrupted by the Slave Revolt on the planet Malta in 831 AS, so the finalization of construction and the first operational tests were not completed until 832 AS. Augusta’s initial role was to oversee combat operations against the Corsairs in Omicron Theta and their newly acquired Freeport Nine.

The situation between the Corsairs and Outcasts in the region escalated towards the end of 833 AS when both these age-old rivals decided to resolve the status quo in the system once and for all. The battlecruiser, Augusta, once again took the lead in combat operations. With the help of Zoner volunteers, the Outcasts managed to break through the defensive lines around the occupied freeport. However, before they could capture and liberate Freeport 9 from the Corsairs, a new opportunity arose in the Sigma 17 system, and the slightly damaged Augusta was hastily tasked with a new mission - the destruction of Atka Research Station. Despite sustaining damage and losses to its escort ships, it successfully joined forces with its sister ship, Tercio, and together, they destroyed much-loathed research station producing Stabiline.

The Augusta hastily retreated from the Sigmas before losing the element of surprise and headed for Corsica. After repairs were completed, the Augusta's current purpose is serving as a guard of the infamous Havana prison in the aftermath of the Outcast slave revolt.

593671.text:
Outcast Destroyers are built with attack in mind, with speed and agility being prioritised to make best use of the Outcasts' piloting skills. The Bella was commissioned in 822 AS as part of a destroyer hunting pack assigned to the Dreadnought Basilica. In this capacity, it would carry out several tours of the Taus, participating with distinction in the 827 AS offensive against the Crayter Republic. The Bella would later accompany the Basilica to its new posting in Omicron Theta, where it was primarily responsible for hunting down Corsair Artifact smugglers.

Bella's pack would be prematurely withdrawn to Omicron Alpha with the Basilica because of the Maltese Slave Revolt. Following the Revolt's defeat, the Bella was reassigned to the Battlecruiser Augusta to provide local experience for its posting to Omicron Theta. The strike force was instructed to undermine the Corsairs in the system, and to destroy Freeport 9's biodomes if possible. Early in their deployment, the group caught the venerable Battleship Fes on patrol near the Orinoco Cloud.

While the relatively new and advanced Outcast ships significantly outclassed the Fes, the Bella would take critical damage during a recklessly close run on the Corsair battleship's engines. The Fes would be dispatched by the Augusta, while the Bella's surviving crew scuttled the destroyer to prevent Corsair reinforcements from capturing it. The two wrecks now drift through the Theta warzone side by side.

593674.text:
The Battleship Fes was a heavily modified Osiris-class vessel that was commissioned at Tripoli Shipyard in 809 AS. As the prototype Corsair battleship, the Fes spent its initial years patrolling Omicron Gamma, before being deployed to the Hessian fronts of Omega 5 and 48. It would spend the next decade and a half embroiled in these stalemates, gradually becoming more outdated and outclassed as time went on. When the Corsairs sent a fleet to assist in the Gallic invasion of New London in 826 AS, the Elders felt the venerable Fes would be a liability on the front line. Instead it was redeployed to Cambridge and tasked with targeting Bretonian shipping.

With the Corsairs' New London fleet routed soon after, the Fes withdrew for refitting, emerging once more in Omega-47 several months later. The Fes launched a probing attack on Planet Tangier, finding unexpected success when it was revealed that much of the garrison had been sent to reinforce Hessian activities in Cologne and Dresden. Viernheim Base was quickly destroyed, with the operation on Planet Tangier being saved only by the intervention of the Coalition carrier Alvin Katz. The two warships inflicted heavy damage on one another, with the Fes ultimately retreating back to Omega 5.

Upon reaching Tripoli Shipyard, a full damage assessment indicated that the Fes would be prohibitively expensive to fully repair, especially when more advanced generations of warships had left it largely obsolete. The Fes languished for several years before receiving basic patch repairs and being deployed to Omicron Theta as a guard ship. In 832 AS, the Fes would be caught by an Outcast strike group led by the Battlecruiser Augusta while maneuvering near the Orinoco Cloud. The battleship stood little chance against these modern vessels, but succeeded in raising the alarm and dispatching the Destroyer Bella and several Outcast strike wings during its last stand.

593675.text:
CLASS: Tirpitz
CREW: CLASSIFIED
ARMAMENT: CLASSIFIED
593675.mapped:
The Battlecruiser Trier was built shortly after the Hudson War’s armistice with Liberty, implementing the lessons Rheinland learned from that bitter conflict. The cutting-edge warship vanished during its maiden voyage in Hamburg, after reporting that it was investigating an urgent distress signal. An extensive search was conducted, yet no trace of the vessel or its crew could be found. In reality, the Trier had been lured into the Kielfeld by The Wild, and was quickly overrun by external attackers and infiltrators within the crew. The Trier was a significant prize for the Nomads, who -- cultivating lurid tales of ghost ships -- used it to brutally target civilians across Rheinland. More significantly, the Trier was ideally positioned to infect poorly-protected Independent World pirates, and intercept Artifacts bound to Liberty.

In 833 AS, the Trier abandoned its Kielfeld lair and redeployed through Thuringia's Suhl into Omicron Theta, where The Wild began an overt campaign of terror. This conspicuously and intentionally drew attention, prompting a buildup of Order forces from deeper in the Omicrons. As human conflicts in Theta over Freeport 9 subsided and successes against increasing Wild raids grew, Trier was withdrawn to Omega-58. There, it received much needed maintenance at Kaarst Drydock. This included a devastating complement of enhanced hybrid weapons, an improved cloaking device, and a restocked fighter squadron. Prepared for action once more, the Trier was dispatched through the Omegas towards Bretonia where it has been tasked with maximizing conflict, and reinforcing local Infiltrators against Wendigo intrusion.

593678.text:
Fort Leniex was originally constructed in utmost secrecy as a fallback point and bastion for the Hellfire Legion. Used as both a HQ and the main shipyard for the Legion's military forces, Leniex has been consistently expanded over the course of many years. Leniex housed a large proportion of the Legion's senior officers prior to the devastation of the scouring of Bering.

The Fort possesses several warship berths capable of constructing the infamous Arbiter class battleship, as well as the facilities to service and maintain said ships. Due to Leniex's role as a central command structure, it was equipped with extensive communications arrays, and was heavily guarded through both internal security features and a significant garrison fleet.

When the Insurgency was formed, Leniex sided with what remained of the Legion's Military High Command instead of the Commonwealth civilian government. The local garrison moved quickly to secure the surrounding system, a task that was largely accomplished before Commonwealth reinforcements from Monterrey arrived. After a brief battle, the system was subdued and Leniex formally appointed as the HQ for the new Insurgency.

Fort Leniex continued functioning as a military HQ for the Insurgency until the middle of 829 AS, when the Liberty Navy forces had managed to break through the Insurgent heavy defenses and managed to reach planet Veracruz.
As the situation was hopeless and supplies were running low, the Insurgency High Command had issued the order to evacuate and scuttle Fort Leniex so it would not fall into enemy hands. Unbeknownst to them, not all of the demolition charges had been successfully detonated and a large portion of the station remained intact, but with a majority of its once extensive ship producing facilities irreparably damaged, Leniex is now the relic of a bygone era.

593680.text:
Marshall Station was the headquarters of the Liberty Separatists, a military rebellion formed from rogue Liberty Navy and LSF elements. Marshall Station was assembled in secrecy in the Bering jump gate debris field, and was used to service Separatist capital ships for operations against Liberty. Marshall Station's location was identified by LSF operatives in early 827 AS, with the Battleship Concord deploying to the Texas system with its support fleet shortly after.

In mid-827 AS Liberty initiated an operation to clear the Bering system, intending to root out the pirates of Freeport 2 and the insurrectionists aboard Marshall Station. Separatist scouts quickly identified the fleets on a heading towards Bering system, and initiated an emergency evacuation. Commonwealth leaders ordered the immediate withdrawal of Hellfire Legion assets from the Marshall garrison, a move that would have ultimately resulted in the Separatists' destruction.

Refusing these orders in an act of mutiny, a joint Separatist and Hellfire Legion attack group deployed to intercept the Concord fleet and buy time for Marshall's evacuation. While this desperate rearguard action was successful, it came at a terrible cost, with much of the garrison fleet's senior leadership being annihilated. Liberty eventually broke through the Marshall picket line, with siege cruisers venting the once-proud Separatist bastion with sustained fire. The grievous losses suffered by the Hellfire Legion and Separatists would ultimately prompted the formation of the Liberty Insurgency, and its forcible disbandment of the Commonwealth civilian government.

Today however, the ambitious effort undertaken by the combined movement to recreate the original station has been laid to rest permanently by an uncharacteristically aggressive Liberty Navy assault.

593682.text:
Galveston Outpost was originally constructed in 826 A.S. as a listening post and supply depot for Separatist forces. Concealed in the West Dallas Debris Field and made largely out of locally salvaged materials, Galveston was well hidden from any attackers. Raids on LPI operations were frequently conducted from the station, often in support of Xeno operations.

In 827, the Separatists were forced out of the Bering system by the siege of Marshall Station. The Liberty Navy doggedly pursued retreating Separatists, with the intent of permanently crippling the movement. A timely counterattack by joint Separatist and Hellfire Legion forces enabled a successful evacuation, but at a terrible cost to both organizations.

After reorganizing into the Insurgency, Galveston Outpost was repurposed as the Insurgency's operational hub for Texas and the surrounding systems. Strikes against LPI operations have resumed, with the Insurgency desperately seeking to win minor victories in order to rehabilitate their severely tarnished image. It was hoped that this would spur on the enlistments that are sorely needed to replenish their diminished ranks.

When the Liberty Insurgency was defeated in Kansas and Vespucci in 829 AS, the remaining garrison decided to abandon and scuttle the station as it was only a matter of time before the Liberty Navy found out about Galveston from prisoner interrogations and from recovered records. Approximately two weeks after the station was quietly scuttled, the Liberty Rogues arrived with the destroyer Drunken Codger and stripped the station of all valuable equipment.

It is not known exactly how the Liberty Rogues learned of Galveston's location, but it is likely that a small group of original crew members gave up the station's location in exchange for their survival or future.

593684.text:
Soon after the Hellfire Legion's formation it became clear that new pilots would need to be recruited from the Liberty population if the movement was to continue to conduct combat operations. A location was required to train these applicants and filter out the inevitable security risks posed by infiltrators.

The remote Kansas system was chosen as a destination for such an installation, resulting in the excavation of a large asteroid in the strategic field. Fort Riley's dense rocky shell serves as excellent protection for those living at the base. Fort Riley's primary facilities cater to the manufacturing and maintenance of fighters and other small craft, usually working independently of the production lines on Fort Leniex.

Long tasked with defending the Commonwealth's civilian assets in Kansas, Fort Riley, then named Monterrey, had a much stronger attachment to the Commonwealth than the forces in Vespucci. When the Insurgency arrived in Vespucci, Fort Riley quickly dispatched its squadrons to assist the Ravager in the defense of the Commonwealth. Ultimately they were too late to make a difference; Ravager had already fallen by the time Fort Riley's reinforcements arrived.

The Insurgency turned its guns on the remaining defenders of the Commonwealth, and fought them back to Fort Riley itself. Boarding action ensued, resulting in the Insurgency securing Monterrey and ending the uprising. Training operations aboard Fort Riley have since resumed at a frantic pace, with the Insurgency expediting field deployments to refill its depleted ranks.

In response to a sizable incursion of ships belonging to the Bretonian Armed Forces, Riley was ordered to have its garrison consolidate with Vespucci's defenders and fight them back. It followed through with these orders without delay, and as a result swayed the fight in the Insurgency's favor. However, this left Mulvane sorely exposed to the inbound assault force Liberty had deployed from Pennsylvania, and the outpost's destruction came about in short order.

593686.text:
The Insurgency had sufficient reason to believe that a concerted effort was going to be made by a combined Liberty-Bretonia strike group into Vespucci, in order to entirely destroy the holdout.

However, the unified defensive front drawn from all Insurgency stations would only be met by a light Bretonian attack group, composed of mostly destroyers. With Liberty's own elements nowhere to be seen, thus routing this element proved to be suspiciously easy.

As a result of this desperate measure, Mulvane and Riley were lacking the garrisons needed to defend themselves from the Delaware's attack group and ultimately both succumbed to an extremely aggressive albeit somewhat costly siege by the Liberty Navy.

593688.text:
The Battlecruiser Triton became the last surviving heavy warship in the Insurgency's brutalized armada, and it would be forced to face off against the Delaware's own formation that had superior numbers but lacked the cohesion and determination that its opposition did.

This ultimately spelled the Delaware's doom and cut short any notion of this campaign being an ideal victory for Liberty. In effect, the Insurgency's surviving forces did exactly what they had hoped for in this situation, showcasing the image of an immortal Liberty as a lie.

Despite this achievement, the Triton suffered catastrophic damage, and its Commanding Officer died from blood loss after shrapnel had wounded him during the engagement with the Delaware. The ship was little more than a drifting hulk by the time the Ohio managed to finish what the Delaware should have waited for.

593690.text:
Planet Veracruz was the sole inhabited world of the Vespucci system, and previous seat of power for the Commonwealth of Liberty - an independent civilian government formed by the Hellfire Legion in 822 AS. Veracruz was a harsh frontier world, complicating early colonisation attempts. Its various administrations had attempted to develop local industrial capacity, however a lack of civilian specialists and interference by the Gaian movement impeded these efforts. A large portion of Veracruz's population was composed of destitute Bretonian refugees, who were relied upon as a cheap labor force. This caused the schism with the previously allied Xeno movement, who accused the Commonwealth - and later Insurgency - of betraying its Libertonian roots.

Following the disastrous Scouring of Bering in 827 AS, the newly formed Liberty Insurgency launched a coup and reasserted military rule. The junta's heavy handed governance and imposition of martial law would cause increasing civil unrest, resulting in riots that were brutally suppressed. This period of repression and a string of defeats against the Liberty Navy prompted many to flee the planet, with thousands heading to Planet Erie in Pennsylvania. In early 829 AS, the Liberty Navy broke through the Insurgency's Kansas defences and launched its final assault on Vespucci itself. After the gruelling battle to dispatch Marshall Station, Liberty's forces discovered Veracruz largely depopulated, save for Insurgency marines who had vowed to die in their fortifications before surrendering.

The Carrier Ohio and its battlegroup elected not to land troops to contest the surface, instead carrying out weeks of devastating saturation bombardment. This attack was carried out methodically to erase any large settlements or infrastructure that might assist future parties with colonising the world. Several monitoring probes were placed in orbit to ensure Veracruz remained undisturbed in the future, with DSE being awarded a maintenance contract for the network. Veracruz's colonies are now little more than shattered rubble, and a monument to the Insurgency's grand but ultimately futile ambitions.

593692.text:
CLASS: Pharos
GRAVITY: No
DOCKING: No
AMENITIES: No
CREW: 0

The remains of Alexandria Research Station, once the most secretive black site of The Order. Established in 810 AS shortly after Order scouts discovered Omicron Mu, Alexandria was mined into a large asteroid within the remote depths of the Wall of Seth. It conducted The Order's most dangerous and unethical experiments under strict quarantine, pursuing an extremist "greater good" ideology that was justified as necessary to prevent humanity's extinction. The black site officially never existed, however many Order pilots whisper of harrowing experiments on live Nomads and infested or enthralled humans. Agents with more lurid imaginations claim Alexandria led Order research into human psionics, allegedly pairing volunteers with active Artifacts, genetic alterations, and mind-altering drugs.

Alexandria's work came to an abrupt end in 829 AS, when the Kusari Battleship Hakodate launched an unexpected attack from Tohoku, supported by Chochinbi special forces. Appearing at close range thanks to sophisticated cloaking devices, the Kusari attackers quickly overwhelmed the base's small garrison. Before Order reinforcements could arrive, the asteroid was shattered through torpedo strikes and the battleship's bombardment. Fearing a large-scale breach of Alexandria's internal quarantines, the station commander initiated a purge protocol, sending the reactor into an explosive meltdown and killing any survivors. Despite speculation that some research materials may have survived the catastrophe, The Order has not attempted to salvage the radioactive sarcophagus.

593694.text:
CLASS: Apagado
GRAVITY: None
DOCKING: No
AMENITIES: No
CREW: 0, Formerly 360

Santa Verna was carved into a large asteroid within the mysterious cloud known as the Zonas Sagradas, originally intended to serve as a listening station for the early, vulnerable society on the planet Malta. As rumors spread about unknown entities and anomalies within this cloud, Santa Verna gradually became a pilgrimage site for spiritual individuals and sects from Malta.

Although this development stirred disapproval among the more secular-minded strata on Malta, there was never an official ban on the practices at Santa Verna. Over the centuries, these practices slowly expanded as the station transformed into an ornately decorated shrine, visited even by some non-Outcast pilgrims seeking spiritual enlightenment.

The end of the shrine came in 831 AS during the Slave Rebellion, which affected the local population as well. Although the uprising was seemingly quickly suppressed, a small group of slaves managed to sabotage the communication systems and life support, leading to the demise of the crew before anyone could come to their aid.

Santa Verna was never restored -- instead, Malta decided to transform this unique and hauntingly adorned shrine into a sacred necropolis. Here, wealthy and influential Outcasts may lay themselves to eternal rest, preserving their physical bodies from the ravages of time for all eternity.

593695.text:
DIAMETER: 10,289 km
MASS: 8.12 x 10e24 kg
TERRAIN: Desert
TEMPERATURE: -25°C to 83°C
ESCAPE VELOCITY: 7.80 km/sec

Albegna is a desert world with a thin atmosphere comprised of mainly carbon dioxide (96%) and trace amounts of argon and nitrogen. While initial surveys detected little to no precious metals on the surface, more thorough scans revealed the presence of large deposits of Titanium and veins of more precious metals within the planet's crust. As a result, the Outcasts elected to establish an underground colony.

Despite the colony's purpose as a mining outpost and military facility, further study is being carried out to address the possibility of terraforming the planet using massive bodies of water provided by comets or ice asteroids found in abundance in the Tau-37 system.

593696.text:
CLASS: Fortitude
CREW: CLASSIFIED
ARMAMENT: CLASSIFIED
593696.mapped:
The Livingston was constructed in the aftermath of the Gallic War as an experimental pivot towards smaller, cheaper garrison ships that could be run by lighter crews. The Livingston's first deployment came in 829 AS, when it was attached to Perth Station in Edinburgh to provide area security.

This tour lasted for a year, before new orders dispatched the battlecruiser to Planet Harris' orbit to relieve the expensive Battleship MacDuff. In this new role, the Livingston was tasked with deterring Gaian attacks on the terraforming project and securing the Tau-23 Jump Gates alongside the Crayter Republic. Since the establishment of Clisham Research Complex in 834 AS, Harris orbit has also come under frequent attack by Outcast raiders.

Increasing tensions with Gallia have also led the Livingston to raise alarms with New London over the escalating risk of direct confrontation. Despite this, requests for reinforcement have gone unanswered, particularly with the fleet largely occupied with preparations for an assault into Dublin. The Livingston's officers have since stopped work on mine clearance, believing the defensive position may soon be necessary once more.
