593699.text:
Constructed in 825 AS, Fort Wakkanai was a large Naval facility situated strategically at the edge of the Unyo cloud to serve multiple roles, most importantly as a training facility for new pilots. Trainees based out of Wakkanai fly CAP and drill for advanced maneuvers in Unyo for a minimum of 200 hours before being transferred to postings around Kusari. Naval Statistics showed that trainees from Wakkanai have a 40% lower mortality rate, a rate expected to drop even further in the future.

For pilots permanently posted at Wakkanai, the base serves as a beachhead for operations in northern Kusari. Fighter wings spearheaded by gunships bound for the Chugoku and Tohoku systems were not uncommon.

Fort Wakkanai following the closure of the Tau-53 gate and that proceeded freezing of trade with Gallia in 828 AS, steadily became a needless facility in an inhospitable system. Matters would come to a head following the mothballing of Battleship Sado in 831 AS as the burden of Tohoku patrols fell on Wakkanai. The demise of the station would come as increasingly aggressive Kusari criminals attacked KNF facilities in response to the encroachment on their revenue sources originating from Tau.

593701.text:
The Battleship Himeji was originally stationed outside Heaven's Gate in the Tohoku system, serving alongside a guard fleet led by the Battleships Ishioka, Musashi and Sennan. At the peak of the Colony Wars in 800 AS, the Blood Dragons and The Order conducted an attack on the Arch, striking the Himeij’s bridge and engines. The surviving crew was forced to abandon ship, with the burning wreck assumed destroyed by both the Blood Dragons and Kusari.

Golden Chrysanthemum scouts encountered the wreck in a nearby asteroid field in 810 AS. The GC ultimately decided it was worth the expense of salvaging the ship, and with the assistance of their Blood Dragon allies, patched the engines to the point that it could safely leave the system. The vessel was then re-named 'Matsuda', in honour of Yuyu Matsuda, the inspiration for the Golden Chrysanthemum movement. Further restorations would occur in the Okinawa system with the assistance of Outcast engineers.

Entering full service in 825 AS, Matsuda was deployed into Kyushu’s Seiran Dust Cloud as a forward raiding base. Later in 831 AS, the GC found themselves pressured by the Outcasts to secure Cardamine smuggling routes through the Taus while they were preoccupied with the Maltese Slave Revolt. The Matsuda took up position in Ohka Dust Cloud to better project patrols into Tau-23, bringing it into conflict with the IMG and Crayter Republic. Two years later, the Matsuda was intercepted by the Battleship Matsumoto while attempting to return to Hokkaido, and destroyed after a pitched battle.

593703.text:
Built in 288 AS, Bautzen Station supported Kruger Minerals’ mining operations in Dresden. Smaller than the rival Daumann facility at Leipzig, Kruger focused solely on the extraction of Diamonds from the Schwefelnebel. It is from here that the famous Blue Diamonds -- also known as "Hessian Tears'' -- originated. The vast majority of the Diamonds mined in Dresden were used for industrial drills, as their quality was usually not high enough for luxury markets. Many believed Kruger would abandon the station by 820 AS, owing to failing infrastructure and dwindling Diamond yields. The station received a slight reprieve in 815 AS, when surveyors identified new deposits of Diamonds deeper than ever in the dangerous Schwefelwolke.

Despite this, the Hessian surge of 818 AS saw Leipzig fall and Pirna Border Station destroyed, with Bautzen only surviving after the Battleship Altenburg routed a large Hessian attack on the base. Kruger was reluctant to abandon Bautzen so soon after discovering a profitable new claim, however the Rheinland government forced the corporation to subsidize the cost of maintaining Dresden’s Military garrison. By 824 AS, Bautzen needed urgent renovations to continue operating. Loathe to invest the needed funds and facing ever increasing security costs, Kruger finally agreed to pull out of the system.

When several demolition charges failed to detonate, Bundschuh engineers were able to board and make them safe, occupying the station. The Bundschuh put the base to work as a smuggling depot, selling Hessian-refined resources to contacts in the Sigmas to raise funds for both movements. In the aftermath of the Rheinland Civil War, the technically-legalized Bundschuh occupied a tenuous position at Bautzen, which breached Rheinland laws quarantining Dresden. When the Rheinland Military invaded the system in 832 AS, they had little patience for Bundschuh legality -- the Battleship Strausberg razed the station without warning, later claiming to have acted in self-defense after coming under attack.

593705.text: A vast stream of debris stretching from Leipzig to Pirna Border Station, the Strausberg-Kassel Debris Field is named for its principle architects. The southern push by the Rheinland Military led to near total collapse of any economic infrastructure left in Dresden, denying the Hessians easy access to Dresden's remaining resources.

593707.text:
Once the heart of Daumann ore processing in Dresden, Leipzig was abandoned in 818 AS as viable mining deposits dwindled. While Daumann had evacuated as much of the station's processing machinery to The Ring as was possible, the Red Hessians were still able to put Leipzig's integrated foundries to use for well over a decade.

What remains of the station now is a twisted, perforated, and half-melted mass of scrap metal. Despite forewarning of Rheinland's impending attack, the Hessians were caught off guard by the diversionary attack into the Giftnebel by the 4th Strike Flotilla. The main Strausberg fleet was barely slowed by Bautzen Station, and closed in on Leipzig rapidly. The station garrison engaged the incoming fleet at the edge of the Innenstadtfeld and awaited reinforcements.

The Battleship Kassel and its support group were delayed, having first dispatched the attackers pushing into Vogtland's minefield. It was too late to save Leipzig or its defenders, however the Hessians successfully sprung an ambush on the Military fleet in retribution.

593709.text:
Battleship Kassel was launched in 820 AS, and initially saw action in Omega-3, 5 and 11. This included tours fighting the Corsairs, and engagements with the Bretonia Armed Forces during the Aland Crisis, notoriously destroying the Gwent in Sprague orbit. The battleship is most famous for its role in the Conquest of Cologne, during which the Red Hessians entirely drove out Rheinland and Bounty Hunter forces. As of 832 AS, the Kassel was still undergoing repairs at Wolfsburg Shipyard for damage inflicted by the Battleship Altenburg during Rheinland’s operation to recapture Cologne. Despite this, it was prematurely pressed back into service with a motley garrison fleet when it became clear Rheinland planned to strike directly at Dresden too.

When the Battleship Strausberg first launched its attack, the Hessians intended to wear it down through attritional raids as it advanced through the system, with the Kassel finally delivering the killing blow. What the Hessians did not expect was a large diversionary attack into the prepared defenses of the Giftnebel, pinning the Kassel until the 4th Strike Flotilla was repelled. By this point, the Strausberg was bearing down on Leipzig Station, with the Hessian defense forces significantly out of position. While Leipzig was lost, the defenders had succeeded in destroying a number of its cruiser picket ships, denting Rheinland’s sensor perimeter. The Kassel exploited the confusion of battle and the Innenstadtfeld’s treacherous conditions to hit the Strausberg’s column in its exposed flank.

The Hessian counter-attack initially inflicted heavy damage on the Strausberg, blasting away its reactor shielding and setting several decks ablaze. Despite this, the larger Rheinland fleet was steadily overwhelming their smaller Hessian opponents, and the Kassel’s rushed repairs were beginning to buckle under the strain. After a cascading electrical failure blew out one of the battleship’s engines, it lost the ability to maneuver effectively and was slowly torn to pieces by Military capital ships. The few surviving crewmembers ejected and were rescued by the escort cruiser Dieburg. Despite initial attempts at covering up the Kessel’s loss, the news of the infamous ship’s destruction has since spread, dealing a significant blow to Hessian morale.

593711.text:
CLASS: Westfalen
CREW: N/A
ARMAMENT: N/A

The Battleship Strausberg was completed in 815 AS and deployed to bolster security in New Berlin. During its initial years of service, the Strausberg acquired a reputation for ruthlessness, with a disproportionately high kill to capture ratio against Bundschuh and Red Hessian targets. During the Fall of Dresden in 818 AS, the Strausberg was ordered to prevent “contagion” disorder in Berlin by conducting aggressive anti-Hessian operations in the Saarfield. It departed New Berlin in 825 AS with the outbreak of the Saigon War, where it assisted with the invasion of Sigma-21 and occupation of Planet Saigon. Similar to the Battleship Kolleda, Strausberg initially refused to honor the Sigma Treaty ending the war, only withdrawing to Rheinland when threatened with desertion charges.

In the days before the Civil War, the Strausberg returned to Oder Shipyard for ‘unscheduled’ maintenance. From there it unsuccessfully attempted to arrest the Federal government, who were instead evacuated by the loyalist Carrier Saar. The Strausberg fired several times on Planet New Berlin during the war, and frequently fought the Saar’s strike wings as they sortied from Frankfurt. Following the Holstein Accords in 828 AS, the Strausberg participated successfully in the Recapture of Cologne, alongside the Battleship Altenburg. Believing the Hessians to be significantly weaker than previously thought, the Strausberg later led Rheinland’s Dresden Campaign in 832 AS.

The expedition was ambushed by the Hessian Battleship Kassel in the Innenstadtfeld. Despite suffering heavy damage to its reactor plating, the Strausberg’s heavier armament and fleet allowed it to overpower its opponent. The fleet was forced to abandon the attack on Leipzig, initiating a slow retreat towards New Berlin. Near the Bautzen Wreck, the Strausberg again came under heavy assault by Hessian bomber squadrons. These wings successfully landed several torpedoes on the damaged reactor, leading to a critical meltdown. Orders were given to strip and scuttle the ship to prevent it falling into enemy hands. Some in the Military have bitterly complained that the Hessian defense was significantly aided by the operation’s start date being announced by the Emperor at a social event, while gloating about the Hessians’ impending destruction.

593713.text:
CLASS: Petersburg
Gravity: No
Docking: No
Amenities: No
Crew: 0

Kamchatka Base was constructed by the Coalition in 820 AS, hidden deep within the Kattegat Lava Field. The Coalition and their Red Hessian allies had been deeply shocked by the Second Casablanca Offensive, as the Corsair assault from Omega-55 had exposed a severe vulnerability in their flanks. The installation was strategically situated to monitor traffic headed to or from Omega-47, with orders to sever Corsair supply lines while protecting the Coalition's own convoys to Omega-11. Kamchatka was a bloody and swelteringly hot posting that was deeply unpopular with serving crews; despite this, Coalition commanders believed the costs were justified by the security buffer created for Omega-52.

Kamchatka's garrison were routinely ordered to attack difficult targets across Omega-55, despite being haphazardly equipped with the leftovers of priority squadrons in Omega-5, 47 and 52. As a result, pilot casualties were high and morale low, with many coming to see their commanders on Volgograd as ignorant of their circumstances, or maliciously incompetent. The garrison's failure to make significant headway against either the Corsairs or Core eventually led to suspicions that Kamchatka may be "politically unreliable", or even harboring "counter-revolutionary saboteurs". As a result, the station commandant was dismissed in 826 AS, and a cadre of political officers dispatched to enforce party loyalty and revolutionary fervor with an iron fist.

Matters came to a head in 830 AS, when the Core battleship Bellona was sighted moored at Dagger Outpost. Kamchatka's squadrons were commanded to destroy the target; when Lieutenant Zacarías Riojas objected to the practicality of the order, he was promptly executed for insubordination. This triggered a mutiny as a decade of resentment boiled up. In the chaos, several pilots fled in an attempt to escape The Coalition and surrender to the Bellona. Now aware of the disarray at Kamchatka, The Core quickly launched their own assault, offering an amnesty to any dissidents taking up arms against their former officers. The battle was brief, with the station destroyed and loyalist Coalition forces scattered towards Omega-47.

593715.text:
CLASS: Abbey
GRAVITY: N/A
DOCKING: No
AMENITIES: None
CREW: 0
INMATES: 0

Vierlande Prison was built in 715 AS and breached in 826 AS. For over one hundred years, its extreme conditions made it one of the most dreaded destinations for Rheinland's terrorists and political prisoners. Sentences to Vierlande were almost always for life, with those few discharged forever changed. With the Rheinland Military distracted by the Saigon War, a force consisting of the Coalition, Red Hessians and Unioners took advantage of a lapse in security to capture the station, indiscriminately releasing the thousands of inmates within.

During the victory celebrations, the Coalition and Red Hessians turned on their former allies, accusing the Unioners of collaboration with the Corsairs. The Coalition Carrier Alvin Katz and Hessian Battleship Zuschen took the Unioner flagship Undine by surprise, destroying it and scattering her escorts. As the Coalition and Hessians withdrew, surviving Unioners reoccupied the Prison. Despite some probing attacks by outgunned RFP patrols, they successfully converted the base into a smuggling way-station, and front line against further Hessian attacks.

During the Civil War, Imperial forces would turn a blind eye to the Unioner occupation of the prison, seeing them as a useful irregular force. Despite this, tolerance of Unioner piracy would quickly wane, with the post-war armistice offered to the Unioners almost immediately collapsing in 829 AS. In one of the first military operations of the new Consensus Government, the Battleship Kolleda was dispatched to 'deconstruct' the station, with the Unioners hastily retreating rather than fighting the Military head-on.

593717.text: Kruger Minerals built Pomerania Annex in 830 AS, working in close partnership with the Rheinland Federal Police of Mecklenburg Prison. Kruger claims the annex is used to sort and store the goods refined in the penal colonies of Hammersee, ready for export back to Frankfurt. While the annex is fully segregated from the prison itself, Kruger regularly makes use of inmate work gangs for routine operations -- amid rumors of kickbacks and bribes paid to prison overseers.

593719.text: The Causeway was made to navigate through the dense asteroid field that separated Gallia from the larger region of Tau. After years of effort, the Council successfully breached the field and was able to send warning of an impending invasion to Sirius. Today, the Causeway is littered with the remnants of past battles and Gallic structures. Despite this, Gallia still relies on the Causeway as a means of accessing the valuable resources found in Tau as its own resources become scarce.

593732.text:
While Planet Eday was found by the IMG to be an unremarkable cold lifeless planet, its gravity well attracts micrometeors that orbit around the Orkney main star. The micrometeor dust field is almost impossible to notice with the naked eye, but a more extensive study proved said micrometeors to be rich in precious metals, materials rarely encountered in large quantities in Gallia.

Finding this trove was one thing, mining it was another. It took the Gallic Metal Service some time to come up with a reliable way to capture and process the rapid meteors, and used the natural gravity well of Lannion to harness them. Once successful field tests had been carried out, Vierzon was completed to maintain the small mining fleet of specialized craft that work the field and process the various metals.

In the disarray of the war's conclusion, GMS abandoned Vierzon. Despite this, the Enclave quickly secured the station and resumed mining. Following the incorporation of the Enclave into the new Gallic Union, Vierzon was returned to GMS control. The return to GMS ownership would not last long however, as Orkney suffered as a result of Vagrant migration from the Omicrons, ultimately resulting in the destruction of the facility along with others in the System.

593734.text: Like a great ocean of waste, the Ontario Debris Sea drowns the system under a tide of detritus. The North patch is largely made up of dumped waste from Fort Severn, Toronto Station, and Liberty's secretive Alberta projects. Much of the waste is heavily contaminated, and is now a frequently used as cover by Lane Hackers.

593736.text: Skiros was built in 816-817 AS using mostly materials either stolen or looted from various convoys and sites, Freeport 7 among them. Heavily defended due to its location in the heart of the Corsair Empire, Skiros fulfulls several functions, some of which being maintenance of space ships and food production. Due to its biodome, Skiros has picked up the interest of several influential figures within Corsair society who either want the produced food for their own ships or to study the architecture of it to maybe allow other Corsair installations to produce their own food -- and maybe one day solve one of the biggest problems associated with spaceborne travel. The station however was abandoned following the spread of influence over the Zoners of Theta.

593739.text: The destruction of the New London Gate, in addition to contributing to the collapse of several connections to Dublin, also resulted in a considerable field of debris and toxic waste.

593741.text: Sometimes limbo is a tolerable place to be stuck.

593743.text: The inside of a ship-mounted modular docking bay. All ammunition and repair services are available from the equipment dealer.

593745.text:
Following the conclusion of the Gallic War, a group of citizens, corporations, and public entities under the name of the Leeds Restoration League gathered to construct a war memorial to honor all who died in service to Bretonia during the war, soldiers and civilians alike. Constructed with shards of Leeds soil glass and salvaged station parts from the system's destroyed stations, the monument has engraved on its exterior a poem, written by Bretonian poet laureate Guinevere Mitchell. Inside the memorial is a radio transmitter, powered by the radioactivity of harvested toxic waste from the system's smog clouds, which repeatedly broadcasts an audio recording of Mitchell reciting the poem. The signal is strong enough to be detected by ships passing close to the planet's orbit.

A Hymn to Leeds

In the ashes below lies a city in pieces,
cut by a furious blade.
Roiling earth and a sky of shadows
and plains of lifeless glass
form humanity's foulest grave.

But around us, see our finest work,
thought it has yet to be done.
Hail Bretonia! May her banner fly,
but never flee,
'round every ship and sun.

We find ourselves in Leeds,
but where her heart is laid to rest,
our hearts,
broken,
may heal.

593747.text:
With the Corsair advance towards Dublin becoming an increasingly alarming issue amongst the Mollys, the need for a forward base to help curb Corsair ambitions became paramount. Every step the Corsairs took in Omega-49 pressured the Mollys into taking action, resulting in their decision to construct Garvagh Base as an answer to the issue.

Following the abandonment of Poole and the Corsair push in Dublin however, Garvagh no longer became tenable and the base was subsequently abandoned as the expenses maintaining it were better spent on the Dublin front.

593749.text: The wreck of a Liberty Navy Fighter craft, destroyed in the service of Liberty, the hull of the ship surviving the loss of pilot.

593752.text:
Once a proud flagship of the Pennsylvania Zoner Militants, the Pinnacle was a Aquillon-class carrier, originally built to protect new Zoner settlements and stations across the Omegas and Omicrons. When tensions between Liberty and the Pennsylvania Zoners reached a boiling point, the crew collectively voted to redeploy to Liberty and render aid against perceived House imperialism.

The Pinnacle was outfitted with the most powerful weapons available to the Zoners, with its arrival serving as a rallying cry for Erie's Militants. As Liberty deployed Marines to occupy Erie, the carrier did it's best to protect the Zoners fleeing the planet. Despite a valiant battle, the Pinnacle proved no match for Liberty's professionally trained and battle tested forces. During its final clash with the Battleship Alma, the carrier took a direct hit to the reactor, resulting in a catastrophic explosion that ripped through the stern of the ship.

The battle's few survivors were recovered by Navy pilots and taken to Sugarland for sentencing.The scattered fragments of the Pinnacle now serve as a stark reminder to the Pennsylvania Zoners of Liberty's capacity for violence, and the consequences of disobedience. Remaining Zoner Militants visit the wreck as an initiation before formally taking up arms, memorializing those who were lost.

593754.text: A convoy of relief ships assigned to deliver relief supplies and evacuate stranded victims of the disaster.

593756.text: A depot dedicated to housing relief supplies to be transported to disaster areas planet-side.

593757.text:
The Galloway Nebula is a large outcropping of the Barrier, covering much of the western side of the Newcastle system. Initial Bowex surveys indicated only Terraforming Gases and trace amounts of Hydrocarbons, leading BMM to pull funding for exploration in favor of focusing on the known resources of Middlesbrough. Molly raiders and Outcast smugglers alike soon began to use the field as a staging ground for ventures deeper into the system.

Galloway saw a surge of activity in 832 AS following the abandonment of Poole. Planetform quickly acquired the mining rights for any Terraforming Gasses from BMM, eager to replace the loss of the Merthyr Tydfil Mining Station. The mining site regularly comes under attack by Molly patrols.

593759.text: The remains of jump control for Ageira's first supergate project, and home of the first casualties of the Texas Incident. What wasn't instantly incinerated by the massive energy spike immediately leading up to the incident appears to have been deposited here, alongside a steady stream of dark matter from the supergate's intended destination.

593761.text: The wreck of a Universal transport captained by Briggs Stuart. The convoy was last sighted heading toward Dallas Research Station in 500 AS, moments before the Texas Incident. The ship appears to have been kept relatively intact, though acute radiation from the surrounding dark matter cloud has caused its pressurized cargo pods to rupture.

593763.text: The wreck of an independent transport captained by Jeremy Rose. The transport was last sighted leaving Houston orbit in 500 AS, moments before the Texas Incident. The ship appears to have been kept relatively intact, though acute radiation from the surrounding dark matter cloud has caused its pressurized cargo pods to rupture.

593765.text: The wreck of a Universal escort belonging to Jenna Patterson. The convoy was last sighted heading toward Dallas Research Station in 500 AS, moments before the Texas Incident. The ship appears to have been kept relatively intact.

593767.text: The wreck of a Universal escort belonging to Logan Carlsen. The convoy was last sighted heading toward Dallas Research Station in 500 AS, moments before the Texas Incident. The ship appears to have been kept relatively intact.

593769.text: The wreck of a Liberty Space Exploration Council transport captained by Alicia Murphy. The Ordway was last sighted departing Manhattan orbit for the Crow Nebula in 60 AS. Scans reveal extremely primitive survey equipment remaining on-board, alongside depleted fuel tanks and life support systems.

593771.text: The wreck of a Liberty Communications Corps transport captained by Jackson Monroe. The Bell was last sighted departing Manhattan orbit for Kusari space in 92 AS. A handful of ancient FTL relay-buoys remain in its cargo hold, long since degraded beyond usefulness.

593773.text: The wreck of an Outcast scout belonging to Arcibaldo Veno. The fighter was last sighted in 831 AS departing from Ruiz Base to raid the Sigmas. The ship appears to have depleted its fuel and life support.

593775.text: The wreck of an Outcast scout belonging to Stella Cardillo. The fighter was last sighted in 831 AS departing from Ruiz Base to raid the Sigmas. The ship appears to have depleted its fuel and life support.

593777.text: The wreck of a Molly smuggler ship belonging to Conor Sharpe. The freighter was last sighted in 831 AS while preparing to evacuate the Poole system. The ship appears to have been shattered by heavy weapons fire.

593779.text: The wreck of a Corsair raider belonging to Santiago Moreno. The fighter was last sighted in 831 AS while departing from Casablanca Base to raid the Poole system. The ship appears to have depleted its fuel and life support.

593781.text: The wreck of a Core supply ship belonging to Samantha Janssen. The freighter was last sighted in 831 AS while departing from Freeport 8 on a routine run towards Omicron Rho. The ship appears to have depleted its fuel and life support.

593783.text: The wreck of a Brigand scout belonging to Dominique LeGrand. The fighter was last sighted in 831 AS departing from Burgundy to loot abandoned infrastructure in Lorraine. The ship appears to have depleted its fuel and life support.

593785.text: The wreck of a Corse interceptor belonging to Arnaude Chesnay. The fighter was last sighted in 831 AS while hunting for Cardamine smugglers in Tau-53. The ship appears to have been ruptured by particle weapons fire.

593787.text: The wreck of an Outcast raider belonging to Basilio Padovano. The fighter was last sighted in 831 AS while departing the Tau 37 towards Tau 53. The ship has been scored by plasma fire, but appears to have depleted its fuel and life support.

593789.text: The wreck of a Red Hessian smuggler ship belonging to Dieter Vogt. The freighter was last sighted in 831 AS while headed to Munich on a salvaging operation. The ship appears to have depleted its fuel and life support.

593791.text: The wreck of a Daumann-sponsored explorer belonging to Christian Eisenhauer. The freighter was last sighted in 831 AS departing towards Omicron Rho to carry out a survey expedition. The ship appears to have attempted to interface with an alien weapons platform before being shattered by heavy weapons fire.

593793.text: The wreck of a Zoner trader belonging to Eduarda Fajardo. The freighter was last sighted in 831 AS departing Freeport 11 on a bearing towards Omicron Kappa. The ship appears to have depleted its fuel and life support.

593795.text: The wreck of a Synth Foods transport captained by Lukas Baecker. The convoy was last sighted jumping out of Stuttgart in 831 AS, moments before the Blackout. The ship appears to have depleted its fuel, life support and part of its cargo. Official records had claimed the convoy was destroyed by Farmers Alliance terrorists.

593797.text: The wreck of a Synth Foods escort belonging to Monika Fleischer. The convoy was last sighted jumping out of Stuttgart in 831 AS, moments before the Blackout. The ship appears to have been stripped and abandoned. Official records had claimed the convoy was destroyed by Farmers Alliance terrorists.

593799.text: The wreck of a Synth Foods escort belonging to Wolfgang Werfel. The convoy was last sighted jumping out of Stuttgart in 831 AS, moments before the Blackout. The ship appears to have been stripped and abandoned. Official records had claimed the convoy was destroyed by Farmers Alliance terrorists.

593801.text: The wreck of a Kusari Naval Forces battlecruiser captained by Isamu Kojima. The Niyodo was last sighted in 832 AS at Kansai Research Institute, departing on special assignment. The Niyodo appears to have been fitted with heavily modified, experimental propulsion and drive systems. The battlecruiser looks to have taken extensive damage from heavy weapons fire, breaking apart under the barrage. Many of the crew launched life pods, but ultimately depleted their fuel and life support. The ship's drive core has been crudely extracted and is now missing.

593803.text: The wreck of a Kusari Naval Forces auxiliary transport captained by Hokama Takao. The Yamafaku Maru was last sighted in 832 AS at Kansai Research Institute, departing on special assignment. The Yamafaku Maru appears to have been configured as a fuel carrier, with its cargo detonating after taking heavy weapons fire.

593805.text: The wreck of a veteran Liberty Navy dreadnought captained by Hannah Enriquez. The Whitefield was last sighted in 826 AS, transiting into the Alberta Supergate during the Gallic War. With the gate’s sabotage, the Whitefield, Fairmont and supporting battlegroups were lost, presumed destroyed. The Whitefield appears to have been stripped, scuttled, and abandoned.

593807.text: The wreck of a modern Liberty Navy dreadnought captained by Adrian Keller. The Fairmont was last sighted in 826 AS, transiting into the Alberta Supergate during the Gallic War. With the gate’s sabotage, the Whitefield, Fairmont and supporting battlegroups were lost, presumed destroyed. Stranded Liberty Navy personnel appear to have congregated aboard the Fairmont before its life support was eventually depleted.

593809.text: The wreck of a Liberty Navy cruiser captained by Betty Geist. The Boise was last sighted in 826 AS, transiting into the Alberta Supergate during the Gallic War. With the gate’s sabotage, the Whitefield, Fairmont and supporting battlegroups were lost, presumed destroyed. The Boise appears to have been stripped, scuttled, and abandoned.

593811.text: The wreck of a Liberty Navy cruiser captained by Andrew Ayotte. The Montpelier was last sighted in 826 AS, transiting into the Alberta Supergate during the Gallic War. With the gate’s sabotage, the Whitefield, Fairmont and supporting battlegroups were lost, presumed destroyed. The Montpelier appears to have been stripped, scuttled, and abandoned.

593813.text: The wreck of a Liberty Navy gunboat captained by Steve Plumb. The Huntington was last sighted in 826 AS, transiting into the Alberta Supergate during the Gallic War. With the gate’s sabotage, the Whitefield, Fairmont and supporting battlegroups were lost, presumed destroyed. The Huntington appears to have been stripped and abandoned.

593815.text: The wreck of a Liberty Navy gunboat captained by Michael Frost. The Aurora was last sighted in 826 AS, transiting into the Alberta Supergate during the Gallic War. With the gate’s sabotage, the Whitefield, Fairmont and supporting battlegroups were lost, presumed destroyed. The Aurora appears to have gone AWOL from its battlegroup, venturing deeper into the unknown before depleting its fuel and life support.

593817.text: The wreck of a Royal Navy battleship captained by Silvain Bettencourt. The Alsace was last sighted in 826 AS, leading a flotilla of mutinous Royalist warships away from the glassing of Leeds. The Alsace appears to have suffered a catastrophic containment breach from heavy weapons fire, leaving only the burnt husk of its fore section as remains.

593819.text: The wreck of a Royal Navy battlecruiser captained by Marine D'Aboville. The Béarn was last sighted in 826 AS, as part of a flotilla of mutinous Royalist warships fleeing from the glassing of Leeds. The Béarn appears to have ruptured in two from sustained heavy weapons fire.

593821.text: The wreck of a Royal Navy destroyer captained by Perrine Nicollier. The Duguay-Trouin was last sighted in 826 AS, as part of a flotilla of mutinous Royalist warships fleeing from the glassing of Leeds. The Duguay-Trouin appears to have broken apart under heavy weapons fire.

593824.text: Debris left over after the hastily abandoned Rho Gate Project.

593826.text: Tasked with delivering gate construction materials for EFLs gate and lane project in Sigma 15, the Gaston had been conducting task of collecting equipment stored at the Rho gate site for relocation to the Sigma-13 project following issues with the original Frankfurt to Sigma 13 connection. Unfortunately for Gaston, Corsair raiders caught the transport loading supplies at the Rho site, and destroyed its engines before a nearby Bounty Hunter patrol intervened. EFL determined that further relocation was too risky and the fully loaded transport and a considerable field of debris was left behind.

593827.text:
Before the great exodus from Sol, there had been a great war which had plagued the system for over one hundred years. There were two primary combatants in the war: the Eastern Coalition and the Western Alliance. The Coalition would eventually gain the upper hand, and in desperation the Alliance launched sleeper ships with the aim of fleeing to the Sirius sector.
Upon arrival to the Sirius Sector, each sleeper ship went their separate ways. The Liberty arrived in the center of the Sirius Sector, the first of the colony ships to arrive and claiming the central systems of the sector. The Hispania was sabotaged on its way to Sirius and was thought to be lost. The Bretonia was hit when the ship broke the Coalition blockade and arrived 20 years later in a resource-rich region of the sector. The Kusari came out of jump amid systems rich in water and H-fuel, though the local planets had little in the way of landmasses to establish settlements upon. The Rheinland arrived in a system whose best candidate for a colony was almost perpetually locked in a frigid winter. The colonists settled down on different planets in different systems, and without the influence of the war, began the process of rebuilding their societies. Eventually, contact was re-established between the disparate colonies. Although the history of Sirius has been plagued by hostilities and hardships, nothing on the scale of the great war has yet become reality.

593829.text: This depot has been hastily constructed by BMM to stage supplies ahead of upcoming military activity in Dublin. Bowex supply ships are frequently forced into holding patterns nearby due to long waiting times for cargo offloading and stowage.

593830.text: Nothing is known about this object.

593834.text: Atmospheric flight above the terminal velocity area.

593836.text:

A beacon demarcating a favorable entry point into the planet's atmosphere for small vessels.

593839.text: The so-called Remains, is a debris field mainly compiled from the wrecks of Gallic and Bretonian ships destroyed in the battle between the battlecruisers Carillon and Blackrock. Mixed in are a handful of Molly ships who fell in the fighting. Currently, the area is under the Mollys control and salvaging operations are being performed at a slow rate, saving what can be saved and melting down what could be used later.

593840.text:
The Triomphant-class Montreuil was an old battleship in service of the Royal Navy, responsible for defending Ile-de-France from Council strikes from the less secure Burgundy system during the latter half of the Second Gallic Civil War. Its extremely deprecated spaceframe was woefully outclassed even by the weakest of the Council's warships, and the ship was almost immediately crippled by the Council's fleet during the opening minutes of the Battle of New Paris.

Although the Montreuil's hull remained relatively intact, the ship's reactor was heavily damaged and put into emergency shutdown to prevent a catastrophic failure. With its weak hull and outdated systems, the damaged Montreuil was deemed too old to repair, and the vessel was converted into a museum ship in commemoration of the Second Gallic Civil War. The historic ship is a popular tourist destination, and even Sirian visitors are a common sight throughout its corridors.

593842.text: This is one of two halves of the carrier Hades, destroyed during the so-called Orange Hammer operation which saw the Hades fall in Tau-44.

593844.text: The Peterborough Asteroid field is a sister to the northern Cardiff Asteroid Field. BMM prospectors found substantial traces of Beryllium, which led to the commisioning of an additional mining facility nearby. Frequent Molly activity disturbs both BMM operations and outgoing Bowex shipments.

593846.text: The wreck of the Zekkz, once flown by a legendary fighter pilot. It now stands as an immortal guard over Planet Hallam.

593849.text:
Deployed in mid-834, the Harz was commissioned as a new support vessel for the headquarters of the Unioner movement, the Harz acts as the first stop for prospective crew members before moving on to other capital ships such as the Sachsenwald.

The Harz has also been conducting raids on the few convoys that traverse through Bering and making the trade route even more unappealing as law enforcement presence is nearly non-existent.

593851.text:
CLASS: Komainu
CREW: N/A
ARMAMENT: N/A

The Battlecruiser Haruna was once the flagship of Lord Protector Akihiro Mitsuo, a senior officer of Kusari’s admiralty and government. Mitsuo was a military hardliner, who frequently agitated for enhanced Naval autonomy and power. This led to frequent conflict with Kusari’s civilian government, and Lord Protector Tazuka, his primary rival within the Kusari Office of Intelligence. As inter-service rivalries became increasingly bitter, the KOI succeeded in purging a number of Mitsuo's Naval allies, allegedly for incompetence during Kusari’s punitive Omicron Campaign.

This and the government’s response to the assassination of Admiral Goro Okamoto were the final straw. A conspiracy of senior Naval officers led by the Lord Protector determined that the current government must be reformed if Kusari was to survive an inevitable war with Liberty. Acting on this impulse, forces loyal to Lord Mitsuo, and fugitive rioters from a violent anti-Liberty demonstration in Galileo, acted together in an attempted coup. Following a lockdown order issued by Lord Mitsuo, traffic across New Tokyo was abruptly paralyzed.

Marines were landed on Planet New Tokyo amid the confusion, attacking the Imperial Diet. Despite hopes the local garrisons would join the coup, reinforcements from the Battleship Matsumoto arrived soon after, declaring the Haruna and its flotilla rebels. After a decisive firefight in orbit, the Haruna’s reactors overloaded, killing all aboard. In the wake of the Lord Protector’s actions, New Tokyo has been plunged into paranoia. Officials now fearfully see Mitsuo’s collaborators behind every shadow, and worry that others in the military may revolt if not appeased.

593853.text:
An unlucky Bloodhound

The Coyote was a Liberty Rogue fighter flown by the wingman of a notorious bandit ace who quickly garnered too much attention from the local authorities. His squad of Rogues had planned an ambitious hijacking of a Kishiro transport in the Texas system, however the information that was provided to the gang turned out to be bait from an LPI plant. When his squadron got into position to disable the lane, a group of LPI fighters and gunboats ambushed the Rogues. The Coyote’s engines were disabled in the battle, and its pilot arrested.

The Coyote has since been picked clean of any valuable equipment by the local Junkers.

593855.text:
An unlucky Wolfhound

The Apache was the personal ship of a notorious Liberty Rogue ace. Considered charismatic and cunning, he was quick to surround himself with loyal thugs that helped him pull off his increasingly bold and daring heists. However, his greed got the better of him in the end. After planning the hijacking of a Kishiro transport his gang was ambushed by the LPI. What he expected would be an easy robbery turned into a bloody firefight.

The Apache’s powerplant was nearly destroyed by LPI weapons fire early in the ambush, rendering his weapons useless. While some of his men initially stayed to try to cover his escape, the crew ran after their boss and his wingman had their ships completely disabled by LPI fire. The pilot was arrested after he surrendered.

The Apache has since been picked clean by the local Junkers.

593857.text: When Graves Station was destroyed and the Battleship Essex retreated, many BMM crews were left behind in their mining ships. Most of these crews later surrendered their equipment, willingly or otherwise. Barring some instances of sabotage or retrofits for other purposes, the Mollys returned most of these ships to their work, bolstering their Gold production capacity. This ship was destroyed during the Bretonian counter-attack into the Founders Field.

593859.text: Following Bretonia's invasion of Dublin in 835 AS, the Armed Forces initially adopted a conservative strategy of capturing open space, to sever enemy supply lines and cut off reinforcements. This forced the Mollys and their allies to commit to costly battles where their guerrilla experience was of little use. Amid growing pressure from New London, the BAF have now pressed into the asteroid fields en-masse, in the hope of finally securing the precious Gold reserves.

593861.text:
TAU EDGE WORLDS

Tau-53 was first charted in 804 AS by Samura scouts, who informally recorded the area as Rishiri. Not a star system in a tradition sense, the sector is a confluence point of the Barrier, Crow and Edge nebulae, lending the sector its unusual coloration and composition. Once a teeming trade corridor between Kusari and Gallia, the system was left devastated and abandoned in the aftermath of Kusari's Invasion of Gallia in 827 AS.

593870.text:
A Jump Gate is a conveyance technology that facilitates near-instantaneous mass transit between two distinct points in space. The technology was first pioneered by Ageira Technologies in 130 AS -- Liberty jealously guards the secrets of their design and construction to this day. Deep Space Engineering (DSE) is the sole authorized contractor for Ageira Jump Gate construction and maintenance.

The Jump Gate connecting Tau-53 to Hokkaido was completed in 812 AS, after re-purposing infrastructure intended for the doomed Chugoku Gate project. Samura lobbyists persuaded Kusari and Liberty to approve the redirect, arguing that Rishiri would provide safer access to interstellar resources, and act as a gateway for future exploitation of the remote northern Taus.

593872.text: These repair docks are utilized to provide emergency repairs to damaged vessels to either return them to the frontlines in Dublin or to be diverted to Portsmouth Shipyard for extensive repairs.

593874.text:
CLASS: Resheph
CREW: CLASSIFIED
ARMAMENT: CLASSIFIED

The Order Recon Cruiser Khepri has been deployed Newcastle as of 836 AS to monitor the situation within the Craster Nebula. While interference from the Craster limits the Khepri's sensor range, the Order Recon Cruiser's sophisticated sensor suite gives it a distinct advantage compared to more basic sensors within the nebula. This combined with running on minimal engine power and lurking close to dangerous explosive pockets gives Khepri the edge in remaining hidden within the cloud.

593876.text: Task Force 17 was assembled from some of the anchored vessels at the Ohio's staging grounds. Led by Battlecruiser Constellation, TF 17 leads a tactical strike fleet of itself and three Liberty Siege Cruisers. As tensions boiled over and Kusari launched their dual strike against Liberty, Task Force 17 charged forward towards the Galileo gate upon the orders of the Ohio. Upon arrival in Galileo, they learned that they had taken a Kusari squadron by surprise and all ships opened fire with all guns. Although two warships escaped, TF 17 took no prisoners in their first engagement of the war.

593878.text: Destroyer Division 13 is formed from two new Ikazuchi-class destroyers under the command of a veteran warship, IKN Hatsuzuki. A veteran of the Tau Conflict, Gallic Invasion, Exile Period, and Kusari Civil War, this veteran warship has been relocated from Kyushu from it's monitoring post to lead these new warships in their pending assignments. Following the Naval Forces reform in May 836, Destroyer Division 13 was placed under the 5th Battleship Division, positioned around Fuchu Prison as a vanguard against both an unthinkable flanking attack and an even less thinkable attack on Fuchu itself.

593879.text:
CLASS: Geb
CREW: CLASSIFIED
ARMAMENT: CLASSIFIED

Launched in 816 AS, the Ennead is one of the precious few carriers to escape the Fall of Toledo. Receiving repairs at Carthage Capital Yards and deploying back into the war, the Ennead saw combat in Delta during Operation Spear and the Takeover of Dabadoru, the destruction of Cairo Station and Zeta's fall to to Nomads, until finally assisting Order forces in defending Fort Carthage from the Battleship Hakodate. Receiving heavy damage holding the line, the Ennead was relaunched from Carthage Capital Yards and deployed to Sigma 19 in 836 AS. The carrier has rendezvoused with the Blood Dragon cruiser Zuijin to act as a mobile base and monitor increased Nomad activity in the Sigmas.

593881.text:
CLASS: Kagutsuchi
CREW: CLASSIFIED
ARMAMENT: CLASSIFIED

The Blood Dragon Cruiser Zuijin deployed to Sigma 19 in 836 in support of the Order's Ennead to act as escort and guide for Order forces in the area. It was agreed that Order forces would supply the Zuijin's logistical requirements to enable the deployment, but in reality most supplies for the cruiser and Ennead both come from Kusari markets, with the Order fitting the bill.

593883.text: Destroyer Division 22 was formed around IKN Harugumo, one of the newer Ikazuchi-class destroyers put into service, currently assigned to security around the primary staging ground within the Keiun Cloud, ensuring that neither Liberty spies nor Golden Chrysanthemum harassment wings cause disruption to ongoing preparations and operations. Once the limping remnants of Torpedo Squadron 3 returned, Destroyer Division 22 was deployed to Galileo to delay the invading Liberty force by fighting with disruption instead of victory in mind. Under the lead of the Harugumo, they have organized their strikes to appear to be a larger force than they are.

593885.text:
Cruiser Division 5 is a mobile strike force attached to the Matsumoto Fleet. It is tasked with using the Matsumoto's Jump Drive to repeatedly strike across Liberty's systems, primarily to destroy vulnerable infrastructure or isolated military targets.

Commanded by the Battlecruiser Kii, the flotilla's cruisers are the division's primary offensive tool, while the Kii lurks nearby with its attendant fuel tankers. This protects its Jump Drive -- a critical military secret, and the Division's only route home.

593982.text: Several Nomads have been seen collecting materials from asteroids within the Donryu and 'sticking' them to their veils. The material has been brought to this location and deposited to form this slowly growing object. Scans indicate the structure is inert for now.

593984.text:
CLASS: Geb
CREW: CLASSIFIED
ARMAMENT: CLASSIFIED

OCV Asyut is the Order's newest Geb, currently under construction at Carthage Capital Yards. Leaning on hard learned lessons from the fall of Omicron Zeta, Asyut's new block IIa design eschews heavy armor in favor of increased snub capacity and a more capable logistical profile. As a result, the carrier is able to field an additional fighter squadron over her earlier sisters. Order planners insist the extra fighter coverage will do more to protect her than any armor plating ever could.

593986.text:
CLASS: Resheph Block 2
CREW: CLASSIFIED
ARMAMENT: CLASSIFIED

The Order Recon Cruiser Neith-II arrived in the Omicron Theta System in 836 to relieve the OCV Mafdet. The original sudden spike of Nomad activity observed in 834 has now grown into a consistent and pervasive presence. Neith-II continues her predecessor's protection of Corfu Station while monitoring the western reaches of the system, where the cruiser's cutting edge sensors are cataloging patterns in large scale cloak use.

593988.text:
CLASS: Resheph Block 2
CREW: CLASSIFIED
ARMAMENT: CLASSIFIED

The Order Recon Cruiser Jeddah was intended to rotate with the OCV Khonsu in the Omega 58 system. However, when Jeddah arrived in Omega 58 in 836, the cruiser was ambushed by Wilde patrols with no hint of the Khonsu in sight. Retreating the Omega 41, the Jeddah lead a week-long search for her missing sister. Jeddah spearheaded the effort to rescue the heavily damaged Khonsu once it was finally located, clashing with the Wilde cruiser Einbeck in the process. Now licking her wounds, the OCV Jeddah has docked at Freeport 5 to effect repairs after reaching an agreement with the Zoners and Red Hessians to provide limited protection.

593990.text:
CLASS: Osiris Block 3f
CREW: CLASSIFIED
ARMAMENT: CLASSIFIED

The Battleship Horus is the Order's next generation Osiris, lead ship of the third generation of the venerable design. It was initially launched in a prototype state for an emergency deployment against a previously unseen nomad warform.

After the initial deployment, Horus returned to drydock to resolve major issues with its weapons systems and finish fitting-out. However, what was supposed to be a swift and decisive fitting-out has now dragged on as Horus has languished in Carthage's drydocks for years. The ship has been plagued by a cornucopia of setbacks and difficulties: The hull was damaged in the Chochinbi's attack on Fort Carthage, went through extensive rewiring after weapons tests revealed critical flaws in the electrical feed systems, and was set back by progressive changes to the core design intended to better resist nomad weapons yet resulting in expensive rearmoring.

In 836, the last of the damage from the Fort Carthage attack has been repaired and the expensive modifications to the design are complete. Some designers are pushing to redesignate the Horus as a fourth generation Osiris now, but most are simply praying the ship launches no matter the designation it bares.

593992.text:
The Rathlin is believed to be a Gaian science ship -- the Corvo has been sighted at various anomalies within and around Bretonia in recent years. This included an incursion into Dublin, where it was seemingly drawn to the bizarre phenomena developing around the destroyed New London Jump Gate. While it is unclear what the Gaians' interest there was, several Cambridge physics papers were published on the anomaly soon after, analyzing suspiciously clear sensor readings.

The Bretonian invasion of Dublin prompted the Rathlin's retreat -- having captured unexpected sensor readings of the Battleship Somerset's Jump Drive in action. Since then, cursory glimpses of the ship have been reported in Tau-31, with the vessel eventually adopting a semi-permanent mooring at Barrier Gate in Coronado. The Rathlin routinely vanished for weeks at a time before returning to resupply, with some suspecting they may be capturing longitudinal data on the system storm, and the developing situation around the moon Jericho.

In mid-836 AS, the Rathlin departed Coronado with a small group of IMG and Order vessels, having agreed to provide sensor support for a planned expedition to Planet Sudbury in Ontario. As a result, it captured readings of the detonation of Sudbury's artifact site, suffering significant electrical damage in the process. Initial work to decipher the surviving fragments of data has revealed an extraordinarily powerful but brief hyperspace pulse.

593994.text:
Battleship Fukuyama is one of the newest battleships to be constructed for the Imperial Kusari Navy. Having learned hard lessons during recent conflicts, most notably with Gallia, Kure's engineers came up with a new design. Largely similar to other battleships on the outside, the Fukuyama features a redesigned interior with a focus on crew survivability and critical systems redundancies to ensure longevity during battle-line action.

Despite war being on the horizon and Imperial High Command pressuring Kure to complete construction ahead of schedule, Kure's engineers have maintained their steady pace to ensure their work isn't wasted through rushed efforts causing unseen flaws.

593996.text:
CLASS: Enterprise
AMENITIES: N/A
CREW: 0

The Kumeyaay was an expedition ship owned by the Independent Miners Guild. Once a Universal Shipping passenger liner, the IMG purchased the ship at the end of its service life and retrofitted it as a support ship for surveying expeditions. In mid-836 AS, the Kumeyaay was volunteered to assist The Order with an expedition to Planet Sudbury in Ontario.

After a ground team began preliminary excavation works, an enormous subterranean explosive charge was triggered. Secondary explosions within the "Site Alpha" complex then triggered an EMP blast which disabled the liner. Before the ship's systems could be restarted, it was struck by molten debris thrown up from Sudbury's surface, breaking apart on impact.

593998.text: This array of storage depots was constructed to allow quicker turnarounds for corporate transports collecting Pennyslvania's exports. The terminal comes under frequent attack by Erie Militants, who see its destruction as a means of inflicting financial hardship on Liberty's occupation of the system.

594000.text:
CLASS: Hegemon
AMENITIES: N/A
CREW: 0

This Hegemon originally belonged to Deep Space Engineering, and was used to prospect the Ralston Ice Field. The ship vanished in mid 836 AS, after a brief distress call indicated it was under attack by Erie Militants. The miner reappeared at the head of an attack flotilla soon after, with the Militants intending to use it as an improvised ram to destroy the New York Cargo Terminal. Rapid response units from the Liberty Navy quickly shot out its engines, significantly reducing the damage from the eventual collision.

594002.text:
CLASS: Defiant
CREW: 26
ARMAMENT: CLASSIFIED

The LNS Panay is one of the Liberty Navy's oldest serving gunboats. First launched in 746 AS at Norfolk Shipyard, it served primarily as an escort gunboat within Liberty house space with the ship's most frequent duties being the escort of supply convoys to and from Pennsylvania. The gunboat persisted in this role through the Colony Wars, and at the end was retired with the majority of the ship's sisters and sold to DSE for demilitarization and scrapping.

LNS Panay was one of the last of its lot in the queue for scrapping, and when the Gallic War broke out Panay was still waiting its turn. The Navy purchased the gunboat's partly stripped hull back from DSE as part of wartime emergency measures and hastily outfitted Panay with what was needed to get it back in space again. Unable to match the speed and armor of its more modern sisters, Panay continued its familiar escort duties throughout the Gallic War. The Panay's only combat action took place in 826 AS in Magellan as it was escorting a convoy into Bretonia following the destruction of the Gallic Royal Navy's Betheny. When its convoy came under attack by a wing of Gallic bombers, Panay returned fire with diligence and escorted its charges through to Manchester despite losses.

Panay was found to be surplus to requirements after the Gallic War. However, rather than scrap the old ship after its recent reactivation, the Liberty Navy assigned Panay to the Planet Harris contingent in Tau-31. Acting as the Liberty Navy's commitment to Bretonian's northern defense, Panay has reliably conducted duties in Tau-31, continuing Panay's venerable back-line escort duties and scaring away the occasional Outcast raider.

594004.text: A simple platform for spectating vessels to watch over the race track. Automated gravimetric repulsors keep debris and rocks away.

594006.text:
CLASS: Monument
CREW: CLASSIFIED
ARMAMENT: CLASSIFIED
The Rio Grande is one of the longest serving Liberty battleships, entering active service in 777 AS. The venerable battleship became famous for its campaigns against piracy across Hudson in 792 and 808 AS. For decades, it was deployed to Colorado, where it was responsible for securing the vitally important Ageira Technologies manufacturing center at Pueblo Station. Additional duties included ensuring the security of Colorado more broadly, and maintaining patrols across the nearby Independent Worlds of Galileo and Kepler.

While the vessel was not deployed in a front line capacity during the Hudson and Gallic Wars, it did take on a greater share of domestic security duties. This entailed expanded patrols across New York and even Pennsylvania. In the aftermath of the wars, Liberty’s Congress made the decision to divest the aging Rio Grande to the LPI, as a testbed for outsourcing the Navy's traditional domestic assignments to the private sector. Unfortunately, the LPI’s operation of the Rio Grande was widely seen as a disaster, with security standards dramatically slipping across Colorado after the Navy’s handover.

Following a major scandal, Liberty’s government terminated the experimental contract in 828 AS, less than a year later. With its Navy commission restored, the Rio Grande was mothballed at Norfolk Shipyard until funding could be secured for a significant modernization program. After languishing for 7 years, a rushed upgrade package was applied in early 835 AS, with the ship then being restored to active duty. It has now been stationed outside Pueblo Station where it was ordered to high alert to repel Kusari attackers or saboteurs.

Once the modernization of the Battleship Minneapolis was complete, the Rio Grande was relieved from it's station at Pueblo and ordered back to Norfolk Shipyard for more comprehensive refits. When Kusari launched its Jump Drive powered first strike on Norfolk, the Rio Grande had been stripped of its weapons for servicing, and was manned by a skeleton crew of junior ratings. Watch officer Lieutenant Hayley Winton drove the unarmed ship into battle to ram and destroy an approaching Kusari Destroyer that was preparing to drop gravimetric mines on the shipyard.

594008.text:
CLASS: Oasis
GRAVITY: No
DOCKING: No
AMENITIES: N/A
CREW: 0

This Bowex passenger liner recently entered Liberty from the Magellan border. Allegedly headed to Baltimore Shipyard for refits, the vessel halted near Norfolk Shipyard after suffering an engine problem. It then began to emit an unusual energy signature. Before Navy patrols could intervene, a Drive Breach opened nearby -- the Kusari Battleship Hamamatsu emerged, leading its fleet to attack Norfolk Shipyard.

It was quickly realized that the Courageous was enabling the Kusari attack -- upon arriving with LSF reinforcements, the Battlecruiser Lehigh dispatched the liner with a main battery shot through its center mass. This triggered a cataclysmic explosion, tearing the liner in half. Urgent LSF inquiries indicate that the liner's transponder was spoofed, and its flight plan forged. Work has now begun to salvage whatever may have survived of the liner's equipment.

594009.text:
CLASS: Overlord
CREW: CLASSIFIED
ARMAMENT: CLASSIFIED

Commissioned in 814 AS, the Alma was one of the first Overlords to take part in operations against Rheinland during the Hudson War. It initially served as the vanguard of the new formed Independent Worlds fleet. After Rheinland destroyed the Jump Gates leading to their space in 819 AS, the Alma was stationed in orbit of Planet Atka, where it protected Liberty's nascent terraforming project from MND sabotage and pirate attacks. At the end of the Hudson War in 823 AS, the Alma was withdrawn to Norfolk Shipyard for substantial refitting and maintenance.

With the fall of Magellan to the Gallic Royal Navy in 824 AS, the battleship was pushed forward into California as a part of the home fleet, supporting the battleships Concord and Rio Grand. This led to a final confrontation with the Carcassone fleet near Los Angeles in 826 AS, in which Gallic battleship surrendered upon learning of the collapse of the Gallic Kingdom. After several years garrisoning California, the Alma was tasked with the pacification and then annexation of Pennsylvania in 830 AS. Leading Operation Pesticide, the Alma notably destroyed the Zoner Carrier Pinnacle before deploying its Marine contingent to occupy Planet Erie's Lake City.

Since then, the Alma has earned an extremely capable reputation for its systematic suppression of Erie Militant attacks. This made the Alma a high profile target for Kusari when planning their first-strike operation in mid 836 AS. The Alma deployed to respond to an attack on Titusville Refinery, expecting to find Militant raiders due to signal jamming. Instead, it was ambushed and severely damaged by Kusari special forces. Fighting a retreat back to Erie's defense grid, the ship is now undergoing emergency damage control to extinguish fires and stabilize the reactor. As news spreads that the Alma has been incapacitated, Militant, Liberty Rogue, and Xeno attacks across the system have sharply escalated.

594011.text: The recent nationalization of Baltimore Shipyard immediately displaced all of the facility's commissions and ship renovations on an emergency basis. Deep Space Engineering has triggered contractual force majeure to the fury of its clients, as shipyard capacity across Liberty is expected to be occupied for the foreseeable future.

594013.text: Following Kusari's devastating surprise first strike on New York and Pennsylvania, Liberty enforced sweeping seizures of Kusari property. The Kusari transports caught in traffic checkpoints across Colorado at the war's start were confiscated and are now being held in orbit of Planet Denver.

594015.text:
>>>WARNING: RESTRICTED AREA<<<

Due to the state of war between the Republic of Liberty and Empire of Kusari, the Galileo Jump Gate is off-limits to unauthorized traffic.

594017.text:
Border Control
Navigation Buoy
Galileo is a warzone between the Republic of Liberty and Empire of Kusari. Entry is restricted to authorized ships only. Unidentified or unauthorized ships may fired upon without warning.

594018.text:
>>>WARNING: RESTRICTED AREA<<<

Due to the state of war between the Republic of Liberty and Empire of Kusari, the Shikoku Jump Gate is off-limits to unauthorized traffic.

594020.text: Following the outbreak of war between the Republic of Liberty and the Empire of Kusari, Galileo has been the site of brutal clashes between their respective navies. Unauthorized vessels are advised to stay clear for their own safety.

594022.text:
CLASS: Interdictor
CREW: CLASSIFIED
ARMAMENT: CLASSIFIED
594022.mapped:
The Battlecruiser Lehigh was deployed in 822 AS, shortly after the end of the Hudson War. Designed as an LSF deep space raider, its original mission brief was to cross the vast spaces between Bering and Hamburg to disrupt commerce, applying pressure for Rheinland to accept peace terms. Instead, its first assignments included tours of Pennsylvania and later Kansas to suppress pirate and Hellfire Legion activity. It later participated in the Scouring of Bering, working with the Battleship Concord to rout the newly formed Liberty Insurgency. During the Vespucci Campaign, the Lehigh gained a bloody reputation for its actions in Magellan, where it blocked the retreat of defeated Insurgency survivors -- allegedly under standing orders to take no prisoners.

It was then deployed to Colorado to guard the locked Kepler Jump Gate, although some allege the LSF were actually scouting paths through the system’s dark matter storm to find Jump Holes into Kusari. This tour came to an end in 834 AS, when LSF spy satellites detected a large hyperspace pulse in Ontario. Due to its deep space capabilities, the Lehigh was dispatched to urgently investigate. The battlecruiser secured a defensive zone near Ontario’s abandoned Jump Gate, protecting the construction ship Robert Peary as it carried out emergency reactivation repairs. The Lehigh’s patrols confirmed Planet Sudbury was source of the initial hyperspace reading, and later obtained scans of further pulses when an enormous beam was fired from the planet into deep space.

The Lehigh's deployment came to an ignoble end in 835 AS, when it was attacked by a massed swarm of Xeno fighters, led by the Liberty Rose -- later identified through hull scans as the lost Battleship Alabama. While the LSF task force inflicted brutal losses on the Xenos, the battlecruiser was eventually overwhelmed by weight of numbers and badly damaged. Forced to retreat, the Lehigh underwent emergency repairs at Norfolk Shipyard and final fittings for a modular Cloaking Device at Chadwick Station. The battlecruiser was preparing for launch at the time of Kusari's surprise attack, allowing it to lead the Zone-21 garrison in a counter-attack on the Kusari fleet. The LSF strike force received commendations for the rapid destruction of the Liner Courageous that appeared to be anchoring the attacker's exit point.

Lehigh is now temporarily overseeing the preparation of Baltimore's defenses. It is expected to soon deploy to battle on special assignment.
