Despite the large number of habitable planets across the sector, very few are capable of supporting large mammalian creatures. Some worlds such as Cambridge and Stuttgart have been seeded with larger agriculturally valuable animals like cows and sheep, fewer still have native fauna viable for leather production.

The Commonwealth's capital of Guadalajara in the Vespucci system is one of those rare exceptions, with sizable populations of large herd animals suitable for leather production. The Commonwealth has quickly become the foremost producer of leather within the sector, providing a safe and simple source of jobs and a steady source of income for the newly formed government, much to the Republic's dismay.

Despite this, there is still a large market for leather apparel and accessories with upper crust Sirians. Leather's applications are many and varied, and not all of them are considered kosher.

The first documented use of the so called "Jumphole Generator" was performed by the Outcasts in Sigma 19 - forcing a connection between it and the Colorado System in Liberty. It is still unknown whether or not there are any immediate dangers in activating the device and the only thing that scientists know for certain at this point is that the device should be used at one's own risk.
Considered as "Highly Advanced Technology" on par with jumpdrives and cloak-fields, the blueprints for these generators are available on the Neural Net. The issue in building one, however, stems from the wide variety of parts and components - including those of Alien origin. The latter alone makes these items contraband in House space by default.

Despite the brute force they are designed to exert, weapons of all kinds are packed with sensitive equipment—most often computers and motors—which are vulnerable to micrometeorite strikes or weaponsfire if not protected. Housings made of metal plate or energy-absorbing meshes are necessary to keep weapons functioning under duress, and furthermore serve as space for manufacturers to apply company branding or style. All weapons but the earliest of laboratory prototypes use such housing, but the state of the art is reputed to come from Rheinland, where durability is a priority among nearly all shipbuilders, lawful or otherwise.

Particle Ram

Certain types of energy weapons require some extra help to drive their projectile out of the chamber and through the barrel—particularly plasma- and particle-based weapons. Where the guns and cannons of ancient humanity required a ram to load, modern rams are used during the firing process, applying an electrical charge or magnetic force to expel the contents of the focusing chamber. 852016.text:
VP-E5 Intermix Chamber Mk I

Rheinland's VP-series is the primary engine type used by ships in the house. VP engines are designed with modularity above all else: Initial designs were fuel-hungry, high power units, reflective of the expectation of constant fuel supply from the Crow. When difficulties with the Gas Miners' Guild put that supply in question, fuel efficiency became a greater priority, with short-burn, short-range engines taking priority. Rheinland's explorers in the southern Omegas however still required long-range engines, and the models split apart. Today, VP engines can be configured for any compromise between efficiency and power that is desired, to fit any role, their only outwards commonality being the distinctive green exhaust signature, courtesy of the typical copper sulfate vent burn. The tradeoff of this flexibility is high maintenance costs, as the complex engines can only be effectively serviced by engineers familiar with the type. This engine is intended for use primarily on light fighters.

852207.text:
Adv. Countermeasure Flare

Developed by BMM and quickly spread across markets far and wide, the Adv. Countermeasure Flare is characterized by its adjustable high-yield thermal charge, which effectively targets and confuses targeting sensors of most fire-and-forget missiles currently present on the market. However, its high effectiveness comes at a price, as the larger size of the flare results in a smaller launcher ammo capacity and longer reload time.

*Fired by Adv. Countermeasure Dropper

852208.text:
Countermeasure Flare

Building upon the technology of the first CM series, the CM-3 strikes a balance between diverting enemy ordnance and size reduction, thanks to its enhanced EMR generator. While it may not excel in diverting enemy projectiles, the CM-3 compensates by offering increased ammo counts. This versatile countermeasure provides a reliable option for countering a variety of threats without compromising on ammunition capacity or decoy effectiveness.

*Fired by Imp. Countermeasure Dropper

852220.text:
CNO-S Bomber Engine

Originally designed by Solar Engineering for use on GMS utility vessels, the CNO-S became the most popular engine used throughout the Gallic civilian market within a decade, and soon leaked into the black market of Gallia. Favored by long-distance haulers, vessels manufactured by GMS and the Gallic Brigands are known to have undergone extensive modifications to make full use of the engine's efficiency. Similar in design to other CNO-based engines, they are manufactured in Gallia and use Promethene as a catalyst to fuse petroleum. Due to the fuel being only available in significant quantities within Gallia, the engines have no export market to speak of. This engine is intended for use on bombers.

Stats

Cruise Speed: 510 m/s
Cruise Charge Time: 5s

852222.text:
CNO-R Bomber Engine

Being the most commonly used engine by the Gallic Navy, the CNO-R propulsion system was designed during the days of the Kingdom, and continues to prove itself to be more efficient and durable than civilian counterparts, as well as being more stable than the experimental CNO-X. Similar in design to other CNO-based engines, they are manufactured in Gallia and use Promethene as a catalyst to fuse petroleum. Due to the fuel being only available in significant quantities within Gallia, the engines have no export market to speak of. This engine is intended for use on bombers.

Stats

Cruise Charge Time: 5s

852224.text:
CNO-C Bomber Engine

An archaic variant of the CNO-R engine, the CNO-C series is in many ways identical to its parent, but doesn't deliver the same performance curve, having been modified originally to serve the moderate republican Council's need for getting in and out of skirmishes fast in the face of royalist enforcers. The CNO-C propulsion system has been designed with ease of maintenance in mind and is claimed to be repairable as long as supplies of spare parts last. However, following the Council's choice to disarm and join the Confederacy, and following their assimilation into the Union, the CNO-C series is now mostly utilized by the radical republican Maquis. Similar in design to other CNO-based engines, they are manufactured in Gallia and use Promethene as a catalyst to fuse petroleum. Due to the fuel being only available in significant quantities within Gallia, the engines have no export market to speak of. This engine is intended for use on bombers.

Stats

852242.text:
"Cascade" Prototype Drive Series I

Like a pebble through the surface of a calm reflecting pool, a ship equipped with this device can "fall" from one point in Einsteinian space to another, leaving a small though distinct wake rippling behind it. No other known jump drive design produces quite the same signature.

So far the "Cascade" Series I Drive Prototype remains unsuited to mass production, owing to the specialized exotic matter batteries required to meet its energy demands, but the compactness of the design makes it suitable for vessels as small as gunboats.

Properties
Compatible Ship Types: Gunboat
Maximum Jump Range: 3
Charge Time: 10 Seconds
Jumphole Lifetime: 20 Seconds
Jumphole Traffic Limit: 1 Ship

Fuel Consumption Rates
1-System Jump: 375 Batteries
2-System Jump: 600 Batteries
3-System Jump: 975 Batteries

852457.text:
Adapted AI Shield

Adapted AI shields are the latest shield technology developed by Core after a thorough analysis of the acquired Gammu AI ships after the conquest of their homeworld. Compared to standard human technology, Adapted AI Shields provide a new perspective into the issue of spaceship protection. As on Gammu ships, these shields provide equal protection against all types of weapons, simplifying overall logistics and preparation for combat operations. An interesting feature of all adapted AI systems is the fact that they need to be reset to factory settings periodically to maintain full functionality. The cores of these pieces of technology are also known for creating seemingly random electric signals and noises.

852459.text:
Adapted AI Thruster

This advanced thruster was developed by the Core shortly after their conquest of the planet Gammu, based on knowledge gained from a thorough examination and disassembly of the recovered Gammu ships. Compared to normal human thrusters, the Adapted AI Thruster is more compact and streamlined, and requires less intensive cooling -- its major drawback then is the need for fairly extensive modification of the ship's powerplant to accommodate and ensure optimal functionality of this still experimental technology. An interesting feature of all adapted AI systems is the fact that they need to be reset to factory settings periodically to maintain full functionality. The cores of these pieces of technology are also known for creating seemingly random electric signals and noises.

852476.text:
Shield Codename: ROSEGUARD

Cropping up somewhere in the Sigmas in a small batch, these shields are truly a wonder of science. Making use of positron-tachyon emitters akin to those employed by the similarly-named ROSETHORN guns, the ROSEGUARD complements its offensive counterpart perfectly. Like all modern shielding tech, ROSEGUARD's utilize advanced adaptive harmonic frequencies, but the few technicians brilliant or mad enough to tinker with and reverse-engineer them claim that these harmonics are special -- allegedly, the shield sings. More down-to-earth minds insist this is nonsense. After all, shield frequencies can't even be heard by the human ear.
