1114285.text:
Once renowned for its valiant fights against the Kusari Naval Forces and the Gallic Royal Navy in the Taus, Battleship Stirling survived many battles. However, its age soon began to show and the old Nessie class battleship was soon withdrawn from the front lines as the war went on, for fear of losing valuable resources in a war theatre where the Stirling would be hopelessly outclassed.

Having been tasked with minor defense missions for the last couple of months while undergoing a severe systemic refit, Battleship Stirling recently appeared in Omega-49 alongside with its escorts, to secure Bretonian interests in-system and to act as a stop-gap measure against the Corsair presence and that of other hostile factions present in Omega-49.

1114291.text: Welcome to Glendale. It's not much, true... but it was the first Bretonian base we seized on the route to Edinburgh. Bretonia never expected the invasion to come from this direction. They thought themselves safe and focused their defense in Leeds. Their misstake, and it cost them.

1114294.text: If all our efforts in this war go as smoothly as the invasion of this system, we'll be home before the end of the year, with his Grace in charge of ALL of Sirius. These so called "Gaians" were pathetic. All they managed to do was slow the Bethany down a bit.

1114295.text: I'm in charge of an infantry regiment. We're scheduled to depart later this month as part of the Leeds ground invasion. I hear the Marines are meeting stiff resistance now that they are on Bretonian soil. It won't be getting any easier from this point out.

1114296.text: We've run multiple patrols through this system. Apart from this station and the jump holes to Orkney and Edinburgh there isn't much here. The planets are just balls of ice, unfeasable for colonisation. This system's true value lies in the fact that it is a key supply route between home and the Bretonian front, and that is why it's vital for us to keep it secure.

1114297.text: I tried to offer the quartermaster some of my pay to find room for a crate of wine on the next food transport... for me and my comrades of course. I even invited the bastard to drink it with us. All I got was a week's latrine duty. Figures, the one "officer" that doesn't take a bribe is sent to this hellhole. Merde!

1114298.text: This base now supplies most of the fighting in Edinburgh. The supply line is secure as long as we can hold on to this station. We have begun upgrading its armor and armaments so that it can better defend itself. Not that we have many attacks out here - Bethany sees to that.

1114299.text: The Bretonians that held this base barely put up any fight at all. We were able to capture the station without needing to do significant damage to it. Now, we use it to supply the frontline. EFL brings fuel, and the IDF brings all kinds of other commodities we need.

1114300.text: I don't like this. We took this station far too easy. Where were all these so-called terrorists? Hiding somewhere else no doubt. Problem is we don't know where, and that is dangerous. I also heard the last shipment of food rations never made it to Glendale as well... I don't like this one bit, no sir.

1114301.text: It used to be quite rough to come this far into the border regions, when the Council first blew through the minefields. But with the Navy showing their muscle, we can move in relative peace. Nowadays there is always at least a cruiser patrol in range, so we don't have to worry about getting hit by the Brigands as much.

1114302.text: Our fleet consumes vast quantities of fuel, and it's up to us to keep those engines running. We supply the spare parts to repair the engines and powerplants, as well as the fuel to run them. Not a glamorous job but face it - without us this invasion would grind to a halt in a matter of days.

1114303.text: Sirian engine designs and fuel differ radically from our own. We captured some engine components when our Navy seized this base, but they're useless. I suspect we'll be asked to haul them back to Gallia for analysis, or scrap. The remaining fuel stores are used to run that Sirian reactor until the fuel supply for it runs dry. By then our own power core will be up and running.

1114304.text: The invasion of Planet Leeds is going to be a logistical nightmare. The Bretonians have been preparing and stockpiling for almost five years on that planet. True, His Excellency has been preparing for much longer then that, but all our supplies are back on the Gallic Core Worlds, and take ages to get here. There simply aren't enough transports for the .

1114305.text: The invasion of Planet Leeds will require quite a bit of extra fuel. Not the Promethene that our starships run on, but regular Gasoline for the Military Vehicles that our forces use to move about. Promethene is much to energy-dense for that purpose, it would be a major risk for any friendly troops if a Promethene-fueled reactor exploded on a battlefield.

1114310.text: Welcome to the Bethany. We might not be in the thick of things, but we do our part for our glorious conquest. Someone has to keep an eye on the rear, no? Heh, I used to say the same thing about the miss back home.

1114311.text: Most of the supplies bound for Edinburgh still come by this system. Once the Leeds system is secure and it's infrastructure repaired, I suspect holding this place will become pointless. There is nothing of value here.

1114312.text: If holding this system becomes pointless I'm sure we'll be retasked to another recently captured system. Leeds perhaps? Taking the planet will not be a quick process, there are simply too many Bretonians and too much surface to cover.

1114313.text: Being here feels almost like training again. I'm constantly receiving green cadets fresh from Anjou, with orders to rotate them on patrols for a few weeks, then transfer them to the front. There are worse assignments, yes, but this wasn't why I signed up with the Navy.

1114314.text: We keep an eye on those Gaians. The profile on them is interesting. Ecoterrorists opposed to ecoforming... I wonder how they will react when they learn EFL is heavily involved in that business. No matter, if they break their truce with us, we will simply remove them.

1114315.text: Being on an auxiliary supply line isn't all bad. At the very least it means we have no shortages. Ships that are damaged must transfer their cargo here to Glendale, then head back home for repairs. But since there aren't many ships available to take cargo from Glendale to the front, those supplies generally become our stock.

1114316.text: I'm off duty, so don't even think about ordering me around. Flying around this desolate excuse for a starsystem looking for trouble that isn't there is bad enough. I don't need your nagging added to my misery.

1114317.text: Twelve more days. Then I can leave this pit and join the fighting where it matters. I finished top of my class in Anjou, and they send me on another training exercise while my comerades in arms are already fighting.

1114318.text: If Command is trying to infuriate privates being sent to the front by sticking them in training before doing what matters, then I can tell them: It is working.

1114319.text: As we push out further into Bretonia, bases like these become obsolete. It is a convenient place to dock and base patrols out of, but that can be done out of the Bethany as well. I wouldn't be surprised if His Grace will simply order this base stripped down and scuttled.

1114320.text: I'm not sure where my next patrol will take me. Sometimes they send us north along the supply route, towards Albi. Other times we get sent south, towards Edinburgh, but that's only a short run. The most dangerous route is the nebula perimiter. Sometimes we lose patrols there, but so far we've not been able to figure out to whom. We know there are Gaians in there, but they claim to not be responsible, and also lose people. I'm not sure if I believe them.

1114329.text: We built this base to keep a back road between Dublin and Newcastle open. That went to hell fast when those damned Kusari showed their faces here. Figures, we give them the boot and the frogs show up.

1114330.text: Rumor has it the drinks here are better than any other Molly base. I think it's cause we have to handle the stress of those giant battleships sitting out there. Guess they're allright so long as they keep their guns pointed at eachother though.

1114331.text: Moving stuff through Edinburgh ain't exactly cake these days. Same goes for the Newcastle route. Hope the boys back on Arranmore are holding out. Not a lot we can do for em at the moment. First save your own hide, then worry about others, I say.

1114332.text: Dunblane isn't that big of a problem for us. It's got nice scanners and all, but it ain't got the biggest arsenal. And them Armed Forces ain't too worried about a few Molly smugglers when the frogs launch a wave at em. So we watch the frogs and move out when they do.

1114333.text: This ain't our fight. That queeney never did anything for us, so us Mollys won't bleed for Bretonia. Not while that bloody insult of a BMM station is still in one piece. 'Though if them frogs make a move on Dublin, we'll bury em just like the rest.

1114334.text: Ol' Angus there got bet that he wouldn't make it through one of the clashes near the sun. Well, bless me heart, he did. Bagged himself a Crusader too, and made a nice vid of it. Guess that was worth pickin' up his tab for the rest of the month.

1114335.text: Most of the boys here don't feel like joining the fighting. I do. Bloody Armed Forces took my brother and father from me, and they'll get theirs tenfold before I'm through. Maybe it'll be the end of the MacNeirs. Hopefully it'll be the end of Bretonia.

1114336.text: That old rat Forbes bet me I couldn't dip into a scrim and live. Little does he know I do so almost every day. I think the frogs have recognized my ship by now. They ain't shooting at me anymore in any case. Want a drink? Forbes' buying.

1114337.text: I don't know if those frogs will be any better than the Brets. They got more ships. Bigger ones too. But size ain't all. Us Mollys have managed to thrive for over 50 years now, even scored a few big victories. The fight ain't over though. Not until them Brets give in it ain't.

1114339.text: Welcome to Dunblane, sir. Roughest border outpost in the entire Police Authority, that I can guarantee you. Between Mollys and Gaians wanting to smuggle their cargoes of contraband across to and fro Newcastle, we had our hands full since the station became operational. Now we've got Gaul spies attempting to get into Newcastle too. And they don't have any visas, no sirreh.

1114340.text: We tend to be the main brig in the system for any Bretonian captives. Mollys and Gaians. The lot that get transferred to Newgate or New London for incarceration. They used to go to Leeds, but that's no longer an option, obviously.

1114341.text: We help the Armed Forces mainly by guarding their supply line. While our military boys focus on killing the invaders, we make sure their goods get through unhindered.

1114342.text: The Police Authority generally doesn't get involved in the fighting with the Gauls. We're law enforcement, not soldiers. That's not to say we haven't gotten into those fights - the enemy isn't too particular about whose Crusader it is they are shooting.

1114343.text: Enforcing the law in Dundee feels somewhat pointless now. There is no law in this system beside the one that tells you to stay alive out here. War is like that, and those that have come here have come for conquest, not pillaging. We should not be here.

1114344.text: Over a third of our staff is either killed, missing or wounded in action. What do they expect? We're not soldiers. We handle criminals, not fullsized military invasions. If New London would get it's head out of it's rear for even a few minutes they'd see we can't do any good here. At most we're getting in the way of our soldiers.

1114345.text: Whew. When I asked the Sarge for the toughest post he could find, he wasn't joking when he said it'd be all I ever wished for. Mollys, Gaians, Gauls... An officers work is never done in this system. The Lieut doesn't like it when we go chasing after Gauls, something about making us a target, but we should all do our part for Queen and House.

1114346.text: I hear there's a Molly that's giving our lads quite a bit of grief, by siding with the Gauls diving in once the real fighting has already started. One of these days I'll give that fool what he has coming. There won't be a stay in Newgate for him, no sirreh. Just a slow, agonizing fall into the Dundee star's corona.

1114347.text: Ach, who am I kidding. All we ever get to do is watch the Bowex freighters when they move between Newcastle and the Stirling. A scrim with a few pirate smugglers is the worst fighting we'll see here. Toughest post my hind quarter, just the same bollocks in a different system.

1114348.text: I'm just here so long as it takes to make repairs. I was on a supply run to the Stirling when a pack of Mollys jumped me. Bloody bastards thought to take a load of ammo. I got them good though. Rigged a small part of the cargo with a mine and let them tractor it in. Boom! Bit of a bigger boom then I thought though, so I'm stuck here until my engines are fixed.

1114349.text: It is risky making these runs. Materials headed to the front line are almost always the kind of thing criminals need as well, so the Gaians and Mollys will both try to hit us to try and steal what we carry. The Police Authority station here tries to curb that behaviour, but even they can't be everywhere at once.

1114350.text: Prisoners of war and Criminals caught by our lads are the only "cargo" that leaves this system. The list of needed goods is much longer - MOX and Deuterium for the Stirlings reactors, Pharmaceuticals to patch up the wounded, Light Arms and Side Arms for the marines, and of course Food, Water and Oxygen to keep everyone alive and well.

1114352.text: Bonjour, and welcome to Embrun. Spearhead of his Royal Excellency's forces, and, incidentally, the furthest fleet out in Bretonian space. Well, so long as you do not count Leeds, but I hear those Bretonians have destroyed the Jump Gates leading out of the system. A pity, for they only delay the inevitable.

1114353.text: With Leeds now a dead end, Embrun is likely to receive reinforcements. We can then overwhelm the Bretonians here and force them out. After that, we can take Newcastle at leisure. When our fleet has room to maneuver, our numbers will allow us to easily overwhelm the Bretonian forces, just as we did here.

1114354.text: Yes, we haven't yet made much progress in this system. But that is of no consequence. Our orders are to keep the Bretonians on their toes, and to prevent them from organising themselves here. In that we succeed with the fleet we have. If we see an opportunity to break through we'll take it, but for now biding our time seems appropriate.

1114355.text: I just rotated in from Orleans. I've not even seen any Bretonians yet. Has the Royal Navy pushed up the lines again? All I saw on the way here was a group of miners which we were ordered to leave alone, and a group of Outcasts which we were ordered to evade. I suppose the supply freighters were more important then a few dead criminals. No matter, there'll be plenty to shoot here. Right?

1114356.text: I'm scheduled to go on a patrol in three hours, so only mineral water for me right now. I want to be at my very best out there, as this will be my first live engagement in the Sirian Campaign. Oh, I'm not worried, my training has given me all I need to know about space combat. Besides, the Bretonian craft are inferior to ours. Right?

1114357.text: I hear rumors of a strange pirate ship, a "Molly" I believe they call themselves. It sometimes pops out of the asteroid fields, darts into a fight and blows up a few Bretonians before retreating. We're told not to open fire on these "Mollys" unless they open fire first, and focus on the Bretonians instead. But, aren't the Mollys Bretonian too?

1114358.text: All our forces need supplies, and the Embrun is no exception. We bring in supplies through Aquitaine, but the route is very long. It's one of the lines we still run through Orkney and Edinburgh. Those systems are safer then Leeds right now.

1114359.text: We bring in everything our forces need - replacement Engine Components, Promethene, Biomonitors and Deuterium. Even Marines sometimes come along on the freight runs. The only thing leaving this slaughterfield are Prisoners of war. We have to take them back all the way to Quillan. That is where the Navy is setting up the main POW camps.

1114360.text: Things will be a lot easier once we capture Planet Leeds. Sure, the surface will be rubble and the atmosphere will still be less hospitable or safe then the main engine exhaust ports of a Valor moving at full speed, but at least we'll have a proper place to coordinate supplies from. These extreme distance freighter runs are costly and inefficient. I hope the Royal Navy knows we can't keep doing this indefinitely.

1114363.text: The Liberty Navy has an odd system for supplying their battleships. Individual commands are responsible for their own supply shipments. I guess it makes sense for commanders to have control over what they requisition, since some paper pusher in another system is unlikely to know what's going on, but that does make it more difficult for us to negotiate contracts.

1114364.text: Despite the war, the naval officers and men here don't get too excited over my Rheinland accent. That's a joke. I've spent enough time here in Liberty that I don't have an accent. Actually, back on Dortmund they make fun of my Libertonian pronunciation.

1114365.text: Have you heard why are there so many tree lined streets and leafy lanes in Liberty? Rheinlanders like to march in the shade.

1114366.text: I don't recommend talking to the Republican Shipping rep that you might run into around here. Most of the station's crew treat him like a spy. I think I caught sight of a LSF tail following him around earlier.

1114367.text: The war with Rheinland has certainly strained our corporate relations with Liberty, but credits spread around in the right places usually smoothes things over.

1114368.text: I'm thinking about hauling some H-Fuel down to Planet Los Angeles so I can check out the Optical Chip factories on the planet. Staying ahead of the competition means knowing what they're doing.

1114369.text: Security around here seems pretty lax compared to a Kishiro base. I guess Ageira is not nearly so paranoid. You'd think they would be, since so many of their former employees are now Lane Hackers.

1114370.text: I've just delivered Engine Components, and I'm picking up some Mining Machinery to take to Toronto Station before I head back to Kusari with Platinum.

1114371.text: I sometimes have trouble with Xenos between Toronto and the Colorado jump hole, but if you spread enough credits around, you can usually persuade a few Navy pilots to modify their patrol just enough to scare off any prowlers.

1114372.text: Despite the war with Rheinland, we managed to keep our contracts with Liberty. Political neutrality does have its advantages sometimes. Eat your heart out BMM, this Toxic Waste is all mine!

1114373.text: Our HazMat Canisters are a big hit up here. The station commander feels a lot more secure with storing Toxic Waste on board his station when he knows that our money is backing up our leak free guarantee.

1114374.text: Don't believe a word that other Hunter tells you. He just loves to scare the locals with his tall tales about his measly little stay on Huntsville. He talks like he was some dashing criminal mastermind before he saw the light, but I heard that all he did was skip out on his bar tab at Newark.

1114375.text: The LPI clearly has more than it can handle. They barely even make a show of it anymore. It does make sense, though. As a business, LPI saves a lot in pensions and health benefits by outsourcing a lot of their policing duties with straight bounties. Either way the crooks get caught, but it's cheaper in the long run if I do it rather than some LPI officer.

1114376.text: You have no idea the stings I had to pull to get this gig. I was originally assigned to the Whitehead. I can't think of a more boring place to tend bar than in a battlezone. I'm not kidding. All you have time to do out there is serve drinks to cocky pilots. No time for the holofeeds at all!

1114377.text: I got so lucky, I can scarcely believe it. Not only is this a quiet post, but all the corporate reps who swing through here pad my paycheck. Naval pilots are lousy tippers, but the reps are always willing to tip well, especially if you can toss them some inside information that will help them beat out their competition.

1114378.text: The Navy must be preparing for a ground offensive. The Whitefield in the New Hampshire system is stockpiling Military Vehicles like they're going out of style.

1114379.text: It looks like Bretonia is going to be a solid customer for a long time. First, they were buying Military Vehicles because of the Kusari invasion. Now it's Gallia they're worried about. All three of their core planets are building inventory.

1114380.text: I sure wish I had been born Bretonian! I'd love to get a piece of the action in Tau-31. The stories I've heard about Planet Harris are incredible. Those are some ace pilots who are operating out of there. I'm hoping to catch a life on a transport with Military Vehicles bound for Harris next time I get a three day pass.

1114381.text: Ageira may have taken over the production of Military Vehicles, but we still run the day to day operations of this station. I can't wait for one of those pencil necked geeks to step out of line.

1114382.text: There's a strange rumor going around that we're selling Military Vehicles to the Zoners. I know, I know, it's crazy. What would the Zoners want with such equipment? That's what I heard, though. If that's right, Gran Canaria may be a war zone within a year, since that's where I heard they're going.

1114383.text: There's something mighty strange going on up in Alberta. All those Scientists flocking up there...that many eggheads in one place can't be safe.

1114384.text: The Zoners at Freeport 14 in the Yukon system place regular orders for Mining Machinery. I'm not entirely sure what it is they are mining, but I know they harvest water from the ice fields.

1114385.text: I've heard that you can haul Mining Machinery to Freeport 4, and easily find enough Passengers to bring back to Manhattan, Pittsburgh, or Erie.

1114386.text: Hey, I know a guy on that depot they set up in Kyushu's orbit. Whatever you need, be it controlled medical substances, or even just a discounted food shipment now that Samura's price has shot through the roof, give me a call.

1114388.text: These old liners are good for us. If we need to ship artifacts discreetly or need something with a good cargo hold on a raid, they can fill the gap nicely. Only problem is having to be near those dirty maltese.

1114389.text: The Junkers call this place a shipyard. They give us a good price and their ships mostly hold together, so we let them enjoy their fantasy.

1114390.text: What's worse than a dirty Molly? A dirty Maltese. Even worse is when they're together. If I hadn't given up my guns already, their guts would be painting the wall behind you.

1114391.text: Gallia, strange place. We don't have to deal much the people from there but they are giving the 'Queens men' a kicking, so they are helping us anyway. As Bretonia is hammered from one side, we will hammer it from the other, crushing the welps between us.

1114392.text: Watch what you say around here. Although the Mollys, Outcasts and Corsairs look like they get along nice enough here, folks tend to go missing all the same. They found a Molly in one of the access tunnels yesterday, now they just need to find the rest of him.

1114393.text: If you consider yourself a good talker, you can learn a lot from the folks here. You got both sides of the war sitting down here, all loosening their tongues. A few more drinks and they'll sing whatever song you ask.

1114394.text: Bretonia, Gallia, all the same. They both want to kill that which made us. If the Royalists hadn't stormed through our home, we'd be making them pay for what they did to their homes.

1114395.text: Have you ever seen Gaia? She's beautiful. You might want to go soon if you want to see her unspoiled, the Gallics want to start stripping her soon.

1114396.text: This is where we tear apart the old and make the new. In less sentimental terms, we take old freighters, strip them down and refit them for moden service. Most folks call them slave liners but they get used for a lot of other things too.

1114397.text: Slaves. We don't have too many here on the station, too risky. Slaves tend to cause problems mostly. Safer and more efficient to just use our own family members. Can't trust a slave, you can trust your brother. Especially when it comes to fitting slavery based modules. Doubt a slave would be too happy about helping to enslave more folks.

1114398.text: When your ship gets a bit battered, bring it here. We can either fix it up cheaply or give you a fair price for it and use it for parts. Old ships are great, our business with the liners is booming, we even had to construct some permanent drydocks. Looking like a proper shipyard now!

1114399.text: Don't try to pull anything when on the station. Although the station may not look like much, it's wired up with monitoring tech. If you do something stupid, we'll know.

1114400.text: See that one over there? I've got my eye on them. They look a little shifty to me, even for here. If you see any trouble, either help me or don't get involved.

1114401.text: Junkers, Mollys, Outcasts, Corsairs, Gaians, we're all the same. Just some of us hate the others. Can't see why, we all look like scum to me.

1114402.text: Corsairs are being pushed out of Dublin and don't let anyone tell you otherwise. We even managed to get one of our beautiful destroyers into Omega-49. If we keep on like this, we'll push them the whole way to Gamma, and then we'll keep on pushing!

1114403.text: Gallia, bloody pain in the arse. I'll admit that we took a bit of damage in Leeds but we paid them back in kind and gave them some extra. We'll hold the line and keep them out of Dublin while we push the Corsairs back, just you watch.

1114404.text: This is a good place to make contact with slave dealers, new or old. We need a lot of slaves and have the credits to pay for them. If you ever feel the need to make some credits and to help Malta, ship some workers up to us and we'll pay you nicely.

1114405.text: The Mollys are causing us pains. They don't much like Cardamine, nor our pilots pirating on what they call their turf. I think the only thing keeping our friendship together are our supplies and their guns against the Corsairs. Can't say I'd miss them if we parted ways, idiots are probably more worthwhile as slaves on our farms.

1114412.text: [818 AS] Slavery Scandal Rocks Corsair Society

1114413.text: CRETE -- 818 AS -- The Corsair Empire was rocked last year by allegations that human organs from Etna Base that were being supplied to injured Corsair soldiers and ailing citizens of Crete were not being taken from captured Outcasts or fallen Corsair heroes as their final sacrifice for the Empire after all, but were in fact being harvested in a monstrous and wholesale fashion from helpless, enslaved citizens of the other Sirian Houses. The sensational military trial of the so called Etna Six, four doctors and two logistics officers of Etna Base, having concluded with their convictions on all counts, leaves the population across the Corsair Empire to come to terms with the full scope of the traitorous deviousness that existed among them in such a beguiling form.\nCitizens of Crete who received organs have rushed to their doctors for medical checks, but the medical profession insists that even if organs from slaves were given to citizens, full and complete screenings were conducted before each transplant operation was carried out. So far, while some citizens have insisted that their elective organ transplants be removed, no cases of disease or illness related to transplants from slaves have been reported.

1114415.text: CRETE -- 818 AS -- Following the revelations of slavery at Etna Base, laws expressly forbidding slavery have been passed governing the entirety of Corsair territory. The penalties for involvement in slavery range from ten year prison sentences, to execution. Laws regulating the transport of human organs within the Corsair Empire have also been passed, to insure that all such shipments are composed entirely of either organs produced in scientific laboratories, or harvested from voluntary donations.\nEven after the executions of the Etna Six for their egregious violations of military regulations, rampant rumors persist of slaves being used on remote Corsair bases for vile purposes. The Elders have appointed a special Inspector General, Javier Morales, to investigate all rumors of slavery within the Corsair Empire, and to prosecute all perpetrators to the fullest extent of the laws.\nWhile most citizens blame the Outcasts for somehow instigating the activites on Etna Base, many rumors of involvement by the Hessians, Liberty Rogues, Mollys, Junkers, Lane Hackers, and even Zoners also persist. The long term consequences for Corsair relations with these factions are yet to be determined.

1114417.text: MALTA -- 818 AS -- Reports of Corsair atrocities in Omicron Eta are now confirmed. The Corsairs were systematically transporting slaves and prisoners to their lair in Eta and butchering them to harvest their organs. These organs were then provided to the rich and elites of Corsair society as replacements for the damage they did to their own bodies during their privileged and debauched lives. Fallen Outcast heroes from the Eta battlefield were dishonorably stolen by the Corsairs to cover up the source of the illicit organs being moved to Crete.\nOnce the truth surfaced, the Corsairs further attempted to cover up their crimes by staging sham trials to place the blame on "rogue officers" who were in fact criminals already condemned to death. The Corsairs will stop at nothing to spread their lies throughout Sirius. Their renewed propaganda against "Maltese slavery" is merely a diversion from the truth of their own abominations.\nThe Outcasts will continue to offer the poor and oppressed of the Houses an opportunity to come to Malta and live and work honorably for their livelihood, while enjoying the benefits of the Orange Dream for themselves. In stark contrast, the Corsairs defile the honorable dead, murder the innocent out of greed, and slander the noble Outcast nation out of envy. All Outcasts must redouble their efforts to end the rule of the Corsairs over the systems that suffer under their cruel tyrannies.

The impound station of the Bretonia Police Authority is where all ships found to be inoperable, either because of mechanical inability or incapable pilots, are towed to rest. This rest is not permanent, as fines may always be paid and paperwork may always be filed.

Most ships however are either auctioned off whole, or stripped down for parts. Ships that are too damaged to be of any value are often used for target practise by Police and Armed Forces trainees, in orbit of planet Lyndhurst.

1114425.mapped:
Caernarfon Station represents two major changes in Bretonian attitude. As Newbury became the first police operation to be supplied by Gateway Shipping, Caernarfon broke the tradition of Border World Exports supplying government operations. Additionally, the station is designed to be able to shelter the entire Bretonian cabinet and the Royal Family, acting as a fallback point if the capitol of New London were to ever fall. As such, Caernarfon remains true to its historical precedent of being both a busy port and a defensible stronghold.

With the Omega-49 no longer being within the sphere of control for Bretonia, the exact position of Caernarfon came under question. In order to reduce the burden shouldered by patrols in the system the station was towed to its new anchored location near Newbury and Merthyr Tydfil stations.

A landmark in the Poole system, the Sleeper Ship Bretonia was said to be less than one astronomical unit from Broadstone when it detected the New London system. Whether or not this myth is true or not is of little consequence, as Broadstone has been hailed as a national landmark.

1114430.text:

TERRAIN: Ice
TEMPERATURE: -51°C to -2°C
ESCAPE VELOCITY: 3.60 km/sec

Studland is a small planet in the Poole system owing its sparse atmosphere to the frequent volcanic activity on its surface. Deemed unsuitable for settlement, Studland was largely ignored until early 816 AS when Stokes Mining Station was captured by the Kusari, removing BMM's primary source of Beryllium. Laying claim to barely significant deposits of Beryllium, Studland was targeted by BMM for Beryllium extraction, however, the advent of Kusari's repulsion from Leeds and the formation of the Torfaen Asteroid Field has changed the pace of the Studland operation to a sluggish crawl.

1114431.text:
DIAMETER: 8,201 km.
MASS: 3.38 x 10e24 kg.
TERRAIN: Desert
TEMPERATURE: -88°C to 100°C
ESCAPE VELOCITY: 9.02 km/sec

Planet Lyndhurst claims no significant mineral resources, atmosphere, or life. These traits, along with the secrecy of its location, make Lyndhurst the perfect place for government weapons testing. As the Poole system is further colonized, the testing remains undeterred, even with the construction of the nearby Merthyr Tydfil Mining Facility.

1114433.text: A large asteroid field rich in frozen noble gases, the Torfaen Asteroid Field is a newer resident of the Poole system. Having settled in the system after being pulled away from the far reaches Omega-49 system, the growing Torfaen Asteroid Field has been targeted by BMM as a source of terraforming gases to last for centuries as the field grows. The asteroid field is split in the middle, with the two halves seperated by Planet Cork.

1114437.text: Bretonia Police Authority\nNewbury Commodity Trader\nDerek Wonsley

1114438.text: Bretonia Police Authority\nNewbury Equipment Dealer\nAlston Trowne

1114439.text: Bretonia Police Authority\nDeputy Chief Brian Wairfax

1114445.text: Bretonia Armed Forces\nCaernarfon Commodity Trader\nPeter Chet

1114446.text: Bretonia Armed Forces\nCaernarfon Equipment Dealer\nCollin Roddy

1114447.text: Bretonia Armed Forces\nCaernarfon Ship Dealer\nCarter Thorburn

1114449.text: Bretonia Armed Forces\nFlight Officer Steven Cloud

1114452.text: Welcome to Caernarfon. Fort Caernarfon or Market Caernarfon, whichever suits your fancy. Gateway has been assigned to handle the civilian maintenance, logistics and daily operations of this base, and we take our job very seriously. Not to mention it put a major bee in Bowex' bonnet to see us handle this post.

1114453.text: Fort Caernarfon? Ah, yes, this place was originally intended as an emergency shelter for the Bretonian Royal House and government in times of war. To date however, it's not been used as such. New London is secure enough that there is no need. Still, we conduct a weekly drill to ensure it remains available for use at a moments notice.

1114454.text: Market Caernarfon? Yes, more or less. The very nature of this station as a defensive strongpoint for Bretonia, lends it to trading high value cargo, right here. The only drawback is that it's not on any real traderoutes - but that can be an advantage as well.

1114455.text: Can you believe it? The designs for the Shire and Shetland, licensed to us! No doubt that's a prelude to Scarborough getting into the more lucrative military ship designs, but still, that's a major boon for us! And the IMG who are handling the actual construction over at Aland. Bretonian regulations require the actual sale to be done at one of our stations, since we're the licencees, so the newbuilds get flown here as bare hulls, then receive their transponder and registration on this station.

1114456.text: I'm usually doing the Omega run, sometimes going up as far as Honshu. It all depends where the highest needs are. Delivering Optronics to Aland, H-Fuel, Copper or Cobalt to Kensington for use in Bretonia's industry, and taking mainly Gold to Rheinland and Kusari for use in shipbuilding. These aren't the easiest runs to do. Corsairs and Hessians tend to want those materials for themselves.

1114457.text: Our partnership with the IMG isn't as profitable as it once was. But that's not their fault - almost half their bases are now within Gallic held territory, not exactly the most accessible place for us. Still, our focus historically has been largely on the Omega passage, which is still wide open for us.

1114458.text: I handle cargo runs inside Bretonia mainly. Freighter runs between Kensington, Cambridge planet, London planet and occasionally the Hood, and of course this base. Sure, you don't rack up as much hazard pay, but you aren't as likely to get your ship shot out from under you either. No sirree, I'd rather stay under the umbrella of the Bretonia Police - or the IMG escorts when entering Dublin. They're usually good enough to chat the Mollys down with a bribe before any shooting starts, if we happen upon them at all. The Bretonian Police, not so much, but the Mollys usually prefer to shoot them rather then me.

1114459.text: My sister got it in her head to enlist in the Armed Forces. I hope she'll be allright. Grapevine says the war isn't going too well for Bretonia. The fall of Leeds didn't help with that. Sure, they're still fighting on the planet, but without support from space even a planet, especially one as toxic as Leeds, is isolated. Only a matter of time before supplies starve any resistance.

1114460.text: The loss of Leeds hasn't impacted Gateway as much as it has Bowex. They, and their BMM counterparts had invested heavily in that system, and I reckon that'll end up a total loss. Part of me feels this is justice on the part of those greedy bastards, but to see Bretonia as a whole suffer... just doesn't make it feel right. I'm sure the boffins will seize upon the moment and try to overtake Bowex now that they're vulnerable though.

1114461.text: I'll be headed towards Liberty once I'm done here, but I'll pick up a cargo of Beryllium first. From Cardiff of course. The BMM has an odd standard when it comes to the purity of refined metals they sell to us, a problem Bowex never seems to have. Our IMG partners I trust.

1114462.text: Liberty and Rheinland are our only main routes now. From those houses we can even reach Kusari again, although some anti-Bretonian sentiments linger among the population there. Can't say I'm surprised, you won't find me docking on New Tokyo, no sir. But a cargo trip to Narita, like the ones we used to do over the Tau borderworlds, why not? Gold is as high in demand in Kusari as it was in the old days.

1114463.text: Bowex is finished and they know it. They've been able to bribe their way into government contracts for decades, and have been living on their reputation mainly. Now that costs need to be cut, and budgets receive greater scrutiny, it is all coming out. This operation we have here is only the beginning. We'll not become Bowex, but we're not going to stay in their shadow forever either.

1114464.text: Not up to trouble I hope, good sir? We do have standards to maintain here on Caernarfon. Not that there is too much trouble here. The station is more than capable of handling the odd Corsair or Molly visit, and the Police Authority maintains order within.

1114465.text: This station is built as a bastion. I'm not sure what the wisdom was in having these Gateway chappies run the place, but I suspect it has something to do with both cutting costs and earning revenue. Gateway hires the station and maintains it - aside from a few high-security government areas under our juristiction, and pays the Crown a goodly amount in lease. In turn, they have one of the most secure facilities in the kingdom, something that appeals to folk in need of a good strongbox. Those are generally folk with deep pockets, too.

1114466.text: I dare say, I hope the day will never come that this station must fulfill the task it was designed for. Should New London be threatened... No, the Armed Forces would need to have fallen, to the last man, before that point would be conceded. Those Gallic curs may be tenacious, but they cannot match the tenacity of a Bretonian defending his home. Coming here was their folly, they just haven't realised it yet.

1114467.text: Good day to you, and welcome to Newbury. Are you one of the constables dropping off an impounded ship, or perhaps one of the chaps looking to try their luck at the auctions? We do get a rather colorful bunch of ships pass through. Word has it that lot 82 is a real bargain - an Arrow-class interceptor in pristine condition. If that is your fancy. Seems it belonged to some Gaian activist who had used the ship as a courier for things that were too sensitive to send by Net. The logs we found aboard should keep the BIS chaps busy for a while.

1114468.text: Not every ship sent to Newbury gets auctioned off. Occasionally an offender might pay their fines and recover their property. Combat worthy ships, rare as they may be, might get sent to the CDI initiative down near Nottingham. And then there's the ships that are barely, or not at all, spaceworthy. Those end up on Lyndhurst in pieces, after target practise.

1114469.text: The oddest ship we've had here? Uncertain, we've had quite a few. I think it might have been a pair of Rheinland Gunboats that were abandoned not long after a brief conflict in the Omegas. Rheinland claimed to not have commissioned their hulls, so they were impounded as pirate vessels until their ownership could be determined, but noone ever stepped forward. I think it were the Daumann chappies that eventually bought them. For quite a hefty sum too.

1114470.text: I'm in charge of this place, as it is. Watching over a ship graveyard is more of a job for an accountant then a police chief, but in times as these, Newbury has become an unusual asset for Bretonia. With civilians stepping up to the plate to fill the gaps left by our overstrained Armed Forces, the need for civilian combat ships is evident. And we do get a few of those here, 'though they're usually brought in as pirate ships. But, after providing them with a civilian registration and spaceworthiness checks, nearly any ship can be brought back into service.

1114471.text: This is the first government operation to have the majority of it's logistics handled by Gateway. Truth be told, I suspect some of the higherups on New London assigned them this yard, to fail. The multitude of ships of different classes and designs that end up here provide a logistical nightmare with little margin, but so far Gateway's performance has been tolerable. I suspect they too know that this is a trial run.

1114472.text: Aside from running Newbury, the local security of the Poole system also falls under the responsibility of the Police Authority. Until recently this was quite the backwater system, but that asteroid belt arriving has changed that a bit. First Planetform finds some useful chemicals in the mix. Then the Gaians show in their wake. Then the Corsairs, and now the Mollys as well. It isn't as bad as in Omega-3, but still, civilian traffic isn't advisable inside the fields. Stick to the buoy paths.

1114473.text: Requisition forms, transfer forms, impound forms. You know, the Police Authority could do with half the men if they'd just let the service droids handle all the formalities. As monotonous as those are, you'd think a non-sentient droid is perfect for the job. One also wonders if New London is inhabited by sentient droids of the organic nature. If you catch my meaning.

1114474.text: One of the perks of being stationed here is the allowance to run "space worthiness tests" on nearly any vehicle that gets transferred to Newgate. It may seem irresponsible, but if it'll keep you from going barmy in this place, all the better. I've seen freight trains perform moves that definately do not conform to standard cargo handling...

1114475.text: You still have to be careful with these ships, especially if they've belonged to Mollys or Gaians. It's not unlike them to abandon a vehicle fitted with some sort of selfdestruct. We missed one such device on a craft deemed a wreck. When a training crew blew it out of Lyndhursts orbit, they got a bit of a bigger bang then they expected. No harm done, but it does serve as a reminder who we're dealing with.

1114476.text: I just dropped off an impounded transport. The gall of some folk - fleeing into the Waterloo moorings while being pursued by Bretonia's Finest? Per our order the moorings and airlocks were locked, while an Armed Forces gunboat patrol ensured the captain wouldn't try any more foolishness. The transport itself is a Gull in fair state, I suspect it should do well on the auctions.

1114477.text: Ferry service is dull, but it does get you around, and gives you piloting experience in a wide range of craft. I've even been at the helm of a Rheinland Gunboat. Now that was an oddity. The Armed Forces disabled the craft in Omega-3, but when they were boarded, they found the vessels deserted and not under Rheinland Military registration. I guess they didn't know what to make of it either, so they dumped the case into our lap as suspected piracy.

1114478.text: Gallic vehicles are strange. We don't get too many of them here - most of them are shot on sight by the Armed Forces. But those that do get captured intact usually don't run very long. They use a different fuel source - some kind of Deuterium-rich hydrocarbon strains instead of H-Fuel. We can't refuel them, so their uses are limited.

1114479.text: I've just delivered a load of H-Fuel. It's one of the commodities that this facility needs a lot of, most of the ships that end up here require some flight testing to ensure they are safe. It isn't exactly cheap in these parts, most of the fuel has to come via Rheinland. Luckily, Gateway has quite a bit of experience on the Omega run, and our partner ALG has good standing with the Gas Miners Guild. It isn't hard for us to secure H-Fuel supplies.

1114480.text: This is a major step forward for Gateway. Up until now, Bowex has always been the primary supplier for all government agencies, and they've abused this position by charging the government much higher rates then is appropriate for their services. With the Constabulary budget being cut in favor of military expenses, Gateway could finally offer them a contract that they literally could no longer refuse. Many officials are uneasy about us being here. It wouldn't surprise me if the lot of them are on Bowex payroll as "advisors".

1114481.text: Some of the ships are just too far gone to even be towed to Lyndhurst for target practise. Those end up being scrapped, and the scrap gets sent to various places for reprocessing. We often take it to Aland Shipyard in Omega-3. Not the most profitable run, but it's a nice extra while on the way to pick up H-Fuel.

1114482.text: I'm just here to see what those cops got in terms of pirate craft. If there's any new tweaks or designs that the Bounty Hunters need to know about, or could exploit, that's worth a few credits. Besides, half the tubs that get dragged to this place do so after a meeting with one of us Hunters, heh. Any ships that had some odd tricks on them get marked too, so we can check what makes them tick.

1114483.text: The Police Authority does confiscate most weapons when a vehicle is seized, but we have some leeway in that department. They'll release the ships as-is for a surcharge to us and a few trusted organizations. The Constables figure, helping us Hunters is helping themselves. True to an extent I suppose, so long as the credits keep flowing our way.

1114484.text: Sometimes I just like to go out and watch those rookie cops blow up stuff in orbit of Lyndhurst. I don't get to chase many thugs myself being assigned here and all, but it's still satisfying to see rustbuckets we disabled finally burst apart. I wager Lyndhurst has a metal-rich crust by now.

1114485.text: It took only the mere sight of our capital ships to send the Bretonians fleeing from this system. The way I see it, this could mean one of two things. Either they don't have enough ships to defend this system, or there's nothing of value here to defend.

1114486.text: Oui, that planet in the distance looks rather lush and surprisingly untouched. Gaia, they call it? It will make a fine location for a Royal vacation resort. Scans did not detect much in the way of a defense on the planet, so it'll be easy enough to take control once planetary landers arrive here. But we'll handle that once New London is in our grasp.

1114487.text: That ball of dust called Ayr over there? From our interrogations of captured Bretonians we've learned they were trying to make the world more habitable by crashing ice asteroids into it. Trying to turn a dustball into a mudball... That makes no sense at all.

1114488.text: This system is fully under our control now, but there's not much here. Still, with Aquitaine secure, we can press into Leeds from two directions. The pincer movement, age old, but still works wonders. It won't be long until we secure it, and after that it's on to New London!

1114489.text: There are three kinds of pirate groups I have to contend with while on escort. First, there's the usual Gallic riffraff. Council, Brigands, Maquis - all of those have no qualms about hitting a military convoy if they think they have the upper hand. Beyond Gallia, there's the Outcasts. Those favor hit and run attacks, and usually try to disable one ship to give us the choice of splitting the convoy, abandoning the disabled ship to them, or leave one behind. Last are the Mollys and Corsairs, which seem your average Bretonian pirates. They're not the toughest of the bunch, usually, but they try to swarm you and take the entire convoy down.

1114490.text: The Aquitaine passage is still being used, but isn't all that important anymore. When our forces seized the Leeds Jump Gate, and our rear guard completed the preconstructed gates in Languedoc and Tau-23, it opened up a Jump Gate path directly to Leeds. That route is much easier to defend, so the majority of the cargo now goes by gate.

1114491.text: I'm just here on escort duty. We brought a shipment of fuel to this battleship, and I'm about to head back towards Gallia. I'm escorting some IDF freighters between Albi and our frontline ships. Not too glamorous, but you'll see plenty of action. Those freighters are attractive targets for pirates, even this close to the frontline.

1114492.text: I'm part of a local patrol squad, and am honestly, bored out of my mind. The Gaians appear to honor their agreement with us, and there's really no other threats here. Occasionally we'll pick up a Bretonian scout at long range, but they usually avoid a confrontation. When they do confront us the fights usually last only a few minutes - until a Gunboat group from Castres responds.

1114493.text: On the outer edges of the system you'll sometimes find Outcasts or Mollys. We've seen them use freighters - most likely there's a smuggling route going through the far ends of the system. Out of boredom patrols sometimes head that way - it's against standing orders, but there's literally nothing else to do around here for a combat pilot.

1114494.text: I almost wish those Gaians would make a move. The profile on them suggests they are antagonistic towards anyone with designs on that lush planet in this system. If that's the case then I wonder why we're not preemptively removing them - it's only a matter of time before we'll settle that world. Better that one then Planet Leeds.

1114497.text: We keep an eye on ships trying to head to the two jumpholes within range of us. One leads to Lewis, which is our main supply line, the other leads to Dundee, which isn't fully under our control yet. So far it's been a dull assignment. The enemy has been pushed back so far that this area is almost secure.

1114498.text: The Dundee system still has a strong defense. Securing it is vital however, both to be able to strike at Newcastle and to secure our flank here. We're meeting stiff resistance however, from Bretonians and other groups that have joined forces with them.

1114499.text: We are the tip of the spear now, oh yes, we are. Tip of the spear. Villeneuve is knocking on the Leeds door, and soon we'll kick it wide open. Then, it's off to New London with us, and we will be home before the end of the year!

1114500.text: The Armed forces still raid our positions here, trying to slow us down, most likely. The bulk of their forces is reported to be massing in Leeds and Dundee. It does not matter. We're bringing in reinforcements by the hour. What chance do these Bretonians really think they have?

1114501.text: The Mollys have proven a greater nuisance then we had initially anticipated. Yesterday they made off with three freighter loads of hull panels, which were needed to repair one of our cruisers. Earlier today we received a report that a gunboat of theirs engaged one of our scout wings - with some of those same panels grafted on it.

1114502.text: We've got a small purification plant down in the engineering deck to purify gold mined in the system. Sure, it doesn't carry anywhere near the capacity of the Graves Station smelters, but that's all right. We're not looking to be top dog in this system. Just ensuring our people make enough to keep themselves afloat is enough.

1114503.text: The Mollys don't target us like they do BMM, but all the same, you've got to be careful around them. If you try to smart mouth them, they'll not think twice before spacing you. Us independent miners aren't out for a fight with them, so don't expect a whole lot of help if you run into trouble with them.

1114504.text: Corsair attacks have become more numerous of late. They are also coming from different directions - makes me wonder if those barbarians have found a new way into the system.

1114505.text: Some of the Bounty Hunters on this base give me the willies. I'm positive at least two of them were Mollys once. I don't like those kind of folk around. What if they are just pretending to be on our side? Are we going to have another Graves massacre on our hands?

1114506.text: Things were looking pretty bleak during the Gallic war. Between Corsairs, Mollys, IMG poachers and other assorted riffraff, the Gallic Navy would have been the final straw. Now that the war is over and Leeds decimated there is significant pressure on us from the top to keep performing.

Protected by the Newgate Minefield, Fort Winchester, as one of the high security areas of the Bretonian Armed Forces, first and foremost serves as a training facility to prepare recruits of the Armed Forces for the arduous task of fighting Gallia and the various criminal elements of Bretonia. Fort Winchester, together with the Battleship Harlow that protects the entrance of the mine field, is equipped with the best technology to both efficiently train soldiers and save valuable resources that are desperately needed to fuel the war effort.

Every four months, new conscripts are brought in from the various military facilities on New London and Cambridge. However, with the Bretonian birth rate at an all time low, the casualties of war are increasingly hard to counteract with a steady influx of new soldiers, and as such, with each shipment of new conscripts, less arrive to undergo the government mandated training on Fort Winchester.

1114515.text: Bretonia Armed Forces\nWinchester Commodity Trader\nEly Leonard

1114516.text: Bretonia Armed Forces\nWinchester Equipment Dealer\nCameron Marcusson

1114517.text: Bretonia Armed Forces\nWinchester Ship Dealer\nValentine Rowles

1114521.text: Good day there, welcome to Winchester Station. Are you a recruit awaiting assignment, or one of the chaps coming bringing or taking supplies? Folks coming here are usually one or the other. Logistics and training, that's about what we do here.

1114522.text: This station has been running at peak capacity ever since the war in the Taus broke out. First is was Kusari that gave us grief. Now it's the Gallics... Gauls... Whatever you call them. They certainly keep our boys busy from the sound of it.

1114523.text: I do hope our boys will get the job done. These cowardly Gauls attacked us when we were still recovering from the damage Kusari inflicted. That madman king of theirs has lashed out at everyone he's come in contact with. I'm glad Liberty has acknowledged they'll likely be next if Bretonia would fall. With their help we should be able to outlast those overextended fools.

1114524.text: There's a few minor powers aside from Liberty that help us out against the Gallic forces sometimes. First there's the Council and the Maquis. They were rebel groups inside Gallia that fought the mad king and lost. They've fled to a world in the lower Taus from what I've heared. There's the Crayter Republic, which got soundly beaten by the Gallic Navy but also managed to get most their civilians out. There's the Imperial Kusari who were left behind when Gallia attacked their home. Even their combined strength doesn't account for much, but hey, I won't stop them from shooting Bretonia's enemies.

1114525.text: The Kusari forces which were stuck in Leeds after Gallia's invasion are going home I hear. Too bad, those chaps knew how to fly a ship. I wonder how they got past the enemy lines, those Kusari capital ships they had aren't exactly tiny.

1114526.text: Morale was pretty low for a while after the withdrawal from Leeds. People thought we'd given up on that system. The truth is very different. Gallia will have to engage in a messy ground war to gain control of the planet. We've had over five years to prepare for a planetary invasion, and the ground troops are more than ready. The Gauls on the other hand have no idea what they're blundering into. Leeds was lethal enough in peacetime, can you imagine it in a fullscale war? I hope they've perfected the massproduction of bodybags on their end.

1114527.text: I'm in charge of certifying the heavy weapons revisions for our fleet. There's no shortage of work for me, as the R&D boys are working overtime. Gaul armor was until recently unknown to, but the Council folk have been kind enough to reveal their composition. Our weapons are being adjusted for maximum efficiency against that type of armor. Once these refits are installed on our destroyers and battleships, those Gauls won't know what hit them.

1114528.text: I'm due for a test of a new gunboat-class weapon. Pretty standard fare those, not even classified, so I can talk a bit more freely about it. Basically these gunboat turrets fire small charges of superheated matter, typically iron, out of a superconducting rail. The charges are small so their mass is low, allowing the rails to accellerate them to immense speeds. Upon impact the shell vaporises in a small explosion. Not as useful against strong armor, but very effective against strikecraft. This new gun has a new style of superconductors and a different means of cooling them. I'm not holding my breath, the last 3 experimentals like this exploded when stresstested when their cooling failed.

1114529.text: We've done some experimenting with an oversized massive weapon like the Gauls use on their main battleships, but the truth of it is that these weapons are impractical. Yes, their damage is several orders of magnitude higher then a standard capital cannon, but what good does that do if you can't aim it at your target? The Dunkirk class is about a quarter the size as those Kusari giants that they proved effective against. I reckon the cost in resources for a Dunkirk is also about a third of that of the Gaul main battleship.

1114530.text: Good day to you. Care for a drink? The bar should be fully stocked again, courtesy of yours truly. Sure, they always say to bring essential supplies only, but what's a soldier with low morale? An accident waiting to happen, I tell you. That's why there's always room for a few crates of military comfort in the BES-Hartford, yes sir.

1114531.text: I have a brother down on Leeds. I don't expect to hear from him any time soon. Contact with the planet has been spotty since the withdrawal of our space forces, but the ground troops are far from defeated. I hear the Gallic invasion force is having some problems with the weather. Guess they didn't get the memo: Fighting on Leeds is chemical warfare by default.

1114532.text: I must say, those Ageira chaps were mighty smart to salvage the Leeds gates in New London and Newcastle, tying those two together. Makes you wonder if they can do that on the fly in other systems. That gives one potential, doesn't it? None of the boffins here seem to know much about it though.

1114533.text: Welcome to Birmingham, heart of Manchester. Not that that says a whole lot, for besides us, there's only the Newgate prison and that Sheffield clearing house here. Bretonia settled this system to take advantage of the abundant resources in the asteroid fields surrounding this base. When the Trade Lanes were built, it also became an important system in the trade route between Liberty and Bretonia.

1114534.text: Birmingham used to be Bretonia's sole supplier of Hydrocarbons until Douglas was built, but those aren't the only resources found in this system. The rocky cores of many ice asteroids contain various metals. BMM found a patch of them containing high quantities of Uranium, but that was kept confidential until recently. It helps to have a hidden reserve. Birmingham now produces MOX more than it does Hydrocarbons.

1114535.text: I hear whispers that Gallia has it's sights set on this system. That'll get Liberty riled up, for certain. Their rather large Navy relies a lot on Bretonian-produced MOX to keep itself running, and Birmingham is the chief producer of such. Unless they want their own fleet to go dry, they'll have to intervene. There's been rumors about that happening for months now.

ESCAPE VELOCITY: 14.45 km/sec

Planet Cork, a world barely considered habitable for human life, was ignored by Planetform for terraforming in favor of Planet Harris, which showed more promise as a colonial investment. However, this did not stop the Mollys from attempting their own colonial effort that saw the rising of several underground facilities to house a sizable number of Molly colonists as a place of refuge from Bretonia's law enforcement agencies.

The sanctuary came to an unfortunate end with the discovery of this planet by the Corsairs; soon the colonies were targeted from orbit by a strike force of theirs. Once where there were subterranean complexes, now sit a number of craters, with the hunreds sheltered there forever lost. Cork instantly became a rallying cry for the Molly movement against the Corsairs.

Recently, with the influx of traffic from Bretonia, the Mollys decided that in the long run, it would be too expensive for the risk to resettle Cork. While Bretonia came seeking to develop new infrastructure in the system, they pose a considerable threat to any colonial effort, even without direct knowledge of Cork's history. The Mollys now hope to drive Bretonia out of the system so they may one day attempt to re-establish a new colony, broadening the scope of their cause beyond Dublin.

1114567.mapped:
Following the destruction of their colony on Planet Cork, many surviving colonists fled to the orbiting Colerain base, one of the larger orbital facilities. Colerain was not outfitted to maintain so many refugee's, so the station had to be hastily expanded. Even so, Colerain was not designed to handle a large population indefinitely.

A larger civilian station had to be created to accommodate many of the families of the Molly fighters. The station was named Kilrea, after Shamus Kilrea, the man who helped to evacuate thousands of refugees from Cork's surface just before the orbital bombardment commenced. Kilrea Station orbits the now desolate planet Cork. To date, it houses a large portion of the Mollys and their families and offers a safe smuggler haven far from the prying eyes of law enforcement.

1114573.text: A lot of the boys are getting nervous. I try to tell 'um to keep their hopes high and give them some inspiration, but drinks are expensive these days!

1114574.text: Teaming with our enemy? Ya right, you won't catch me saving their arse in space. I'd gladly let 'um roast.

1114575.text: Quit standing around and go blow something up.

1114576.text: Friend hit an asteroid yesterday. He was probably drunk. As a matter of fact so was I at the time.

1114577.text: SAVE YOURSELF MAN SAVE YOURSELF AND GET THE FRAK OUT OF HERE THE SAIRS ARE COMIN'!

1114578.text: They're coming! I can hear the engines of their ships already! God help us all..

1114579.text: You've been talking to Crazy Steve haven't you? Eh, don't mind him he's a little on the drunk side.

1114580.text: Someone needs to tell Steve to be quiet, he'll scare away all the recruits! Lord knows we need them..

1114581.text: Sure am glad you're on our side, we need all the help we can get if we're going up against two entire nations.

1114582.text: Never thought we would be siding with the Coalition. Though anything works if it saves us from getting our arses handed to us on a silver platter.

1114583.text: Oi! I'm not stealing the drinks for myself! Have you gone mad?!

1114584.text: If you've been talking to Crazy Steve, ignore anything he's said. I think I served him one to many drinks.

1114585.text: We'll never let any enemy near this place. Heck, if need be, even the women and children are prepared to fight against our enemies to defend our home.

1114586.text: These are stressfull times. I've had to be more lenient with the drinks lately, out of respect for those who risk their lives for us.

1114591.text: We have strengthened a lot since the beginnings of our movement and our influence among the Kusari women keeps growing. Our numbers have increased dramatically and our technology is catching up with the help of our allies. The Golden Chrysanthemums have climbed to a whole new different level. We're at the peak of our power right now, but even such advances are not enough to take on the Kusari Naval Forces in head on combat.

1114592.text:

MASS: 6.35 x 10e24 kg
TERRAIN: Terrestrial
TEMPERATURE: -14°C to 54°C
ESCAPE VELOCITY: 6.29 km/sec
1114592.mapped:
When Samura first surveyed Planet Tomioka they found it to be similar to Planet Kyushu, an even mix of land and water, with a large variety of primitive sea life. Many of the land masses on the planet are rich in plant life with some smaller lizard-like creatures appearing the main animal species on the planet. The usually calm weather and large, open "shrub forests" have become an attractive retreat for the wealthy well-connected Kusari citizen who just wants to get away from the crowded cities of New Tokyo.

Samura has begun developing the planet, creating large farmlands on one continent, while leaving an entire second continent completely allocated as a resort. Small villas are erected, with dozens of square kilometers of open country in between them - making a Tomioka visit "an undisturbed time".

Samura is also experimenting with the native fish-like life in the oceans, but has thus far not found anything worthwhile. Some of the species seem edible, but their appearance and taste make them unappealing. Samura established two small mining outposts on the planet on sites where prospectors found deposits of valuable minerals - naturally, these are nowhere near the resorts. Between the fledgeling farming communities, miners and the people employed at the resorts.

In 823 AS the Blood Dragons commenced an offensive on the planet, taking advantage of the lack of substantial local support from Republican forces. Fighting was intense on the southern hemisphere, where the Blood Dragons attempted to make advances against the Samura security forces in the hopes of one day capturing the planet for their own ends.

While the Matsumoto group provided much needed support not only in space but also planet-side, the redeployment of the Matsumoto back to Hokkaido has left only the Samura security forces and a small detachment of Naval Forces to hold the Dragons' advance at bay.

1114596.text:
The Midori Cloud is the youngest nebula in human knowledge. The Midori Nebula is really nothing more than a small pocket of Ionized Hydrogen pulled into the Tottori system. Having orbited the system's three suns, the cloud gradually settled around a previously-unknown jumphole to the Tau borderworlds. Once caught in the jumpholes gravity, the cloud regained an elliptical shape as it spun around it.

With the increasing presence of Kusari Naval Forces' patrols in the system and less need for the Farmers Alliance to act as a sort of civilian militia, Shibukawa Depot was towed into the cloud for cover and secrecy from a now less "understanding" State Police. Prior to the depot's destruction the Farmers Alliance kept vigil over the jumphole and the Outcasts that attempt to enter the system through it.

1114601.text: This place is a paradise! They've got everything here from local delicacies to wonderful beaches, great service, and even some 'mood enhancers' if you can find one of the Hogosha around here.

1114603.text: These Kusari in their rich suits take everything on this damn planet. Go to a restaurant, all the seats are 'reserved.' The servants act more like masters, always acting haughty with their chin in the air, as if you're beneath them. Even the criminals treat you like you're nothing, charging exhorbant prices for a high. I know a guy who works for Cryer who can get me Synthetic Marijuana for half as much as they sell it for here. I'm going back up to Mackinac, I can't stand the arrogance of this place anymore.

1114605.text: Did you know that Samura wasn't the first group to find Tottori? I heard that the Farmer's Alliance led them to this place. Samura even built a huge compound on one of the islands for some Alliance leader. Wouldn't surprise me if those radicals had a space station or a depot in this system too.

1114607.text: This place has great fish! Do you like fish? I like fish! I couldn't imagine living if I didn't have any fish. Yes sir, a little fish, a little rice and ol' Puffy's as happy as a kid on his first birthday. Oh look the waiter! Fish! Waiter, fish!

1114609.text: You looking for something special, something to make your vacation better? I've got anything you want, for a price.

Deliberately placed deep inside the Tojimbo ice field, Anijima base was the most concealed Hogosha facility in existence. As such, it was often used by Hogosha leaders of various locations to meet and discuss plans for the future of both themselves and Kusari as a whole. Aside from the covert nature of the base, it had numerous patrols and strong defenses to keep its occupants safe in case of an attack.

As part of an agreement between the Hogosha and the Kusari Intelligence, Anijima station was traded to the Kusari Intelligence in return for Suzuka station. The well-hidden location of Anijima has immense value to the Kusari Intelligence who wish to keep a watchful eye on Tottori and its neighboring systems, while its array of defenses ensure the safety of the station and its operators.

1114652.text:
With construction of the Jump Gate having been underway for some time, the project is still expected to take a while longer to complete, especially given the strict directives to Deep Space Engineering, who are being paid a very handsome amount of money for their silence and speed in the construction project.

Considerable amounts of supplies are constantly being shipped in to both the construction site and the nascent beginnings of a Trade Lane route to the planet Miura, all paid for by the GMG and Kishiro. Despite the extremely high levels of security, there have been a number of attacks on the installation by the Hogosha, who prefer to use lightning hit and run strikes against the Jump Gate site in order to disrupt progress. Because of this, many of the DSE workers are demanding higher wages due to the dangers involved, and efforts are being increased to tighten security around the base.

1114665.text: Fujisawa is one of the newest generations of H-Fuel processing platforms, and our output is higher than any other platform in Sirius. This is partially due to hydrogen in the Mintaka Field being so abundant, but mainly because our automated processes are so advanced, thanks to Kishiro's research into more sophisticated computer systems.

1114666.text: This station hasn't been in operation as long as all our others, so everything is still fairly new here. I shouldn't say this, but I hated working on the gas miner Naha. Because the Sigma-13 hydrogen fields are slowly depleting, it isn't given priority for maintenance repairs and supplies anymore. I was walking through one of the older sections once and the artificial gravity cut out briefly. I spent a couple of days in the medical bay for concussion.

1114667.text: The GMG trusts the Kusari government a good deal more these days. Kishiro Technologies are more forward-thinking and reliable business partners, and also the more honourable of the two keiretsu. We are glad they are in control now.

1114668.text: We don't like the Hogosha, and they are not welcome at our bases. They are rumoured to have a base in the south of this system, but our patrols have as yet been unable to find it. We know that Samura hires the Hogosha to attack its rivals, and both the GMG and Kishiro have had trouble with them in the past, but we can never finger Samura with anything.

1114669.text: I was born on Aomori Station and worked there for years, until this place opened, whereupon I requested a transfer and got posted here a few weeks after construction was finished. In the time that I have been onboard Fujisawa, I've come to love this station and it is more my home than any planet ever will be.

1114670.text: I ran afoul of a Corsair patrol while hauling Deuterium through Sigma-19. I barely made it out alive, thanks to my escorts. I lost two gunners when a missile penetrated my shields, and my escorts are never seeing home again. Protection in the Border Worlds is nearly non-existent, and the Corsairs have been upping their attacks as of late.

1114671.text: Transporting H-Fuel to Rheinland always makes me grin. Striking isn't it, how their glorious, rebuilt armada's just so much scrap metal without the Guild? Their battleships have massive reactors that spew forth green flame, how silent and cold they'd be if we ever chose to cut off their shipments.

1114672.text: The Mintaka field's not as harmless as it seems. It's studded with pockets of explosive gas, and I've seen more than a few Hogosha in there. It seems they're trying to sabotage our mining efforts. There are whispers that the New Tokyo crime syndicate has been hired by Samura to confound our expansion in the region. Between you and me, I believe my fellow miners, Samura's infamous for its cutthroat business practices.

1114673.text: We have a remarkable cultural diversity here on board the Fujisawa. We've got miners from practically everywhere, even Rheinlanders, ex-Kruger workers, mainly, ancient prejudices have no place in modern business. Now the war is over we can even include Bretonians in our roster.

1114676.text: MIURA -- 819 AS -- Despite many sabotage attempts and material shortages, the Sigma-19 Jump Gate in Okinawa has been completed only slightly behind schedule, which finally allows Gas Miners Guild ships to travel freely between the developing Okinawa system and the mining operations on Ogashawa. The construction was completed roughly 9 months behind schedule, which DSE attributes to the many attacks on supply ships heading for the construction site, as well as the site itself. GMG officials have accused the Hogosha of being behind the sabotage, but Kusari authorities have not found any evidence to back this claim thus far.

1114678.text: MIURA -- 818 AS -- A number of disturbing reports have surfaced recently regarding the treatment of prisoners in the uranium mines on the planet Miura. Allegations of physical and sexual abuse are regularly filed with the prison authorities, although it appears that little is being done to resolve the issues. One prison guard, who would speak only on condition of anonymity, stated: "The conditions down here are appalling. The guards are not paid enough for the work they are doing, and the prisoners have it much worse. Most of them are Bretonians, although there are a lot of political prisoners from New Tokyo as well."\n\nIn the meantime the uranium shipments continue to arrive at Isehara Orbital Refinery on time, and despite the relatively high turnover of prisoners, more continue to be shipped in from various prison stations to serve as the GMG's cheap workforce.

1114679.text: [817 AS] Kishiro Calls For Calm In The Sirius Market

1114680.text:
MIURA -- 817 AS -- The terraforming of Planet Miura is on schedule as planned, according to several top Kishiro executives who spoke earlier today, in an attempt to calm the nerves of panicky investors after the terrorist bombing of the Sigma 19 Jump Gate project. Stocks in Kishiro plummeted following the terrorist attack, but rose again and stabilised after the announcement by Kishiro Technologies' financial executive, Mr. Yutaka Kinjo.

"This terrible attack on the Sigma 19 Jump Gate has in no way set back the scheduled date for completion of the Planet Miura terraforming project. Shipments of terraforming materials continue to arrive safely and security has been further tightened to ensure the continued safety of everyone working on the project."

Officials from the GMG, who own Planet Miura, could not be reached for comment although it is believed that their security has increased considerably around Isehara since the incident at the Jump Gate.

Constructed in 825 AS, Fort Wakkanai is a large Naval facility situated strategically at the edge of the Unyo cloud to serve multiple roles, most importantly as a training facility for new pilots. Trainees based out of Wakkanai fly CAP and drill for advanced maneuvers in Unyo for a minimum of 200 hours before being transferred to postings around Kusari. Naval Statistics showed that trainees from Wakkanai have a 40% lower mortality rate, a rate expected to drop even further in the future.

For pilots permanently posted at Wakkanai, the base serves as a beachhead for operations in northern Kusari. Fighter wings spearheaded by gunships bound for the Chugoku and Tohoku systems are not uncommon.

Lastly, Wakkanai serves an ancillary role as an early warning listening and defense post on the Gallic border. Although currently host to only gunship and fighter patrols, Wakkanai boasts dry-dock facilities capable of servicing larger capital vessels, and could be reinforced at any moment to lock down the Hokkaido system should Gallia attempt a counter-invasion.
