1114701.text: The Iwo Jima cloud is an outcropping of the Crow nebula attracted by the Hiroshima's twin suns gravitational field. Venturing inside is to avoid, because of extreme high radiation sweeping its depths, apparently produced by the remaining parts of a destroyed station. Rumors are spread about a failed antimatter experiment by the Naval Forces.

1114704.text:
The Battleship Nagumo was the only Meiji-class battleship to remain in service for over a century. Constructed in 723 AS, it was designed as part of Kusari's emphasis on centralization and self-preservation known as Sakoku, functioning as a strategically placed deterrent against any hostile intrusion coming from the neighbouring Tau systems. While it could be classified as a historical monument due to its age and uniqueness, the Kusari government have chosen not to promote the battleship in this way, as to them it is seen as a failure.

The Nagumo was the last Meiji-class battleship scheduled to be decommissioned and be replaced by the new Bakumatsu-class battleships that were being produced by Samura. As its militarily vital position in Kusari was one of great importance, the Nagumo could not be moved until another ship was deployed to take its place. The rising tensions in the Tau borderworlds prevented such a replacement from being constructed. Instead, the Battleship Nagasaki briefly replaced Nagumo, allowing Samura to refit the ship and shore up the structural weaknesses that led to the discontinuation of the Meiji class. Nagumo then resumed her assigned station, freeing up the Nagasaki for action in the Tau borderworlds.

Later on the Nagumo was a major actor in the battle for the Tau-29 gate. Although ultimately forced to retreat, the actions of this battlegroup managed to slow down the momentum of the IKN forces, and allowed the Republic to hold most of the Kyushu system for the remainder of the year. The Nagumo held the lines of defence over Planet Kyushu's orbital area, and actively organized the military actions against Imperial forces in the system. Without the arrival of a sufficient aid however, due to fighting elsewhere on the fringes of Kusari, it was only a matter of time before the venerable Nagumo was defeated again.

With the push into Kyushu by the Imperial fleets, the Nagumo wound up face to face with the far more modern Nagasaki. Despite the technological disadvantage, the captain of the Nagumo chose to order the Exiles to surrender rather than opening fire, forgoing an opportunity to land the first crucial shot. The engagement ended inconclusively after the Republican battlecruiser Akatsuki refused to fire on their own brethren, defecting to the Imperial forces shortly after the battle.

1114716.text: You find me here at the Ships Inn most days now. At my age, dodging law dogs and pirates just doesn't have the same appeal as it used to have. Now I have people to bring everything I could want. Plus Sophie knows to keep the bar stocked with Maltese Brandy and Gallic cigars, what more could some over the hill smuggler ask for in life?

1114717.text: I started the IND so I would have a way to clean all the money I was making hauling Cardamine from Malta to New York. Made a fortune, but I couldn't do anything with it, unless I wanted to explain to the authorities where the billions of credits where coming from.

1114718.text: I approached Interspace Commerce to create an independent subsidiary of the IC. It just so happened at the time IC was looking to hide some of its less than legitimate dealings and contacts, so the deal was perfect for everyone. We pay IC a dividend while providing them with plausible deniability, and IC gives us access to their networks, giving us a market for our products all around Sirius. Enmeshed with the hundreds of billions of credits that IC handles on a daily basis, our income comes out squeaky clean.

1114719.text: What? Who? Well what the hell do you want?

1114720.text: Hello there, I am Ted, I like to drink.

1114721.text: I am so tired of Sophie yelling at me, you would think after all these years she would be used to it, but every time it is the same thing.

1114722.text: Heh, trade? I made my fortune selling "My other ship's been repo'd to pay off my tab at The Ship's Inn" bumper stickers. Yeah, laugh, think it's a joke?

1114723.text: The hell does "Interspace Neural Net Division" even mean? Hell if I know. Sounds like some jerk made it up while buzzed on a business flight to fit "IND".

1114724.text: Here is to hoping that the new Kusari government does more to stop the attacks on foreign shipping than the last one did. I have basically stopped trading in Kusari altogether. The profit is not worth having those angry Farmers coming after you.

1114725.text: Being a pilot for IND has let me travel from one corner of Sirius to the others. We work very hard to make sure our ships have access to the markets all thoughout Sirius.

1114726.text: Got to go, here comes Ted.

1114736.text: The calamity at Red Deer Station is an unfortunate circumstance, and rest assured that the criminals responsible will be pried out of their hiding places and brought to justice. The Liberty Rogues have gone too far this time.

1114737.text: Red Deer suffered a catastrophic decompression from hostile laser fire, it's all in the official report. It's odd though, because I've never heard of a laser that could cut through our station's ablative armor plating like that. After all, why build an outpost if a fighter can carve it up like a chicken dinner? They must have just gotten lucky and happened to hit a defect in the station's construction.

1114738.text: Don't tell anyone you heard this from me, but I managed to read the preliminary report about the Red Deer disaster. There was laser damage found on the station's hull, but it was on the opposite side from where the hull rupture occurred. And the hull rupture was several meters across and centered on one of the station's main support beams. Decompression couldn't blow out that much of the hull, and certainly not right across a structural beam. But all of that was left out of the public report. There's something not right about that whole incident, and somebody doesn't want the public asking too many inconvenient questions.

1114739.text: This right here? Us getting here? That will go down in history I tell you. The big three of Liberty worked together to make this happen, so we could find the lost fleets and bring them home. Ageira did most of the work of course, working on Jump Gates is what we do. But building another super gate all the way out here without any other assistance? A crowning achievement.

1114740.text: Seven months. It took seven months of full burn on the interstellar drives for us to get here. I was never told that the engines would sound like my teeth grinding incessantly to the backdrop of blood rushing through my temples. We've been out of interstellar space for two months now, but I can still feel the coarse hum grinding into my skull. I can't work like this. I need to get out of here.

1114741.text: The other day I was right in the middle of demonstrating the most advanced neuromechanical interlink in Sirius, and then I heard one of the visiting scientists mutter something about "the main show". The nerve of that guy! Some of these geniuses are so smart in their narrow field that they have no sense of the big picture.

1114742.text: This ship is truly incredible, utilising a miniaturized version of the drive that brought our predecessors to Sirius; combined with the advances in modern technology, we've been able to travel in seven months what would have previously taken years. Ageira likes to think they did all of the work! But let me tell you, it was the ingenuity of a Liberty united in purpose that made the magic happen.

1114743.text: I can't believe we're finally here! To think, a whole new system had been this close to Liberty all this time. If only the big three had been allowed into the Alaska system sooner, can you imagine how different the development of Liberty would have been? Initial scans are very promising about the Omicron Nu system, though we are picking up some strange readings from Planet Marshall and the center of the system. When sufficient reinforcements arrive through the gate we intend to investigate and see what's going on.

1114744.text: Now that I think about it, when I was lost the other night I saw an emblem on a door that doesn't make any sense. It looked like a radiological warning, but that can't be right. We don't do anything on this station that involves radioactivity.

1114745.text: Leduc is an absolute bonanza for DSE. With the completion of the Jump Gates in Okinawa and Hokkaido, I was expecting layoffs this year, but instead we're busier than ever keeping this base supplied and stockpiling for future expansions in the system.

1114746.text: I've had to mediate the sixth disciplinary write-up this week. I don't know if it's because of the cramped quarters, or the months of having to hear that incessant engine hum - it's making my engineers quite irritable. Medical is telling me that more than half my team are pushing the regulatory limit on prescription sleep aids just to get by. I don't blame them, The senior project managers are contantly hounding us for results, and it feels like the LSF spooks are always hovering around our consoles.

1114747.text: IWe helped build the supergate you know, marvel of a construction that is. Able to travel far greater distances than conventional Jump Gates. Of course, if you were to believe Ageira they built it all themselves. It's true that they alone posess the knowhow of how these things work, but we play an essential part in building the actual physical thing.

1114748.text: Hey there, you can't believe how glad I am to see a new face around here. It took the Oregon seven months to get here, traveling to another system on nothing but your engines nonstop, it's an experience we all thought we had left behind us hundreds of years ago with the advent of Jump Gates. Kind of makes me feel bad for Ageira and DSE, I bet they had to make trips like this quite frequently in the early days. That said, if anyone starts singing about bottles of Liberty Ale on the wall again I swear to god I'm going to *grumbles unintelligently*

1114749.text: I was a little worried about pirate activity in this system after Red Deer Station was destroyed, but so far I haven't seen any signs of Rogues. They must be laying low in fear of Navy retaliation.

1114750.text: I dont know what it is but let me tell you I can't shake the feeling that someone or something is watching us, lurking in one of the many clouds in this system. A colleague of mine, Patrick Nova said he saw some ships off the starboard bow when we got here, he disappeared just several days later! We are on a spaceship, all escapepods are accounted for. It makes no sense that he's just gone like that. There are weird things happening here I tell you.

1114751.text: Enjoy your stay on Leduc Station, although I don't know where you'll go to enjoy anything. This cantina and the station mess hall are the only areas of the station open to public gatherings.

1114752.text: As much money as Ageira makes, you'd think they'd install full recreation facilities on a remote station like this. Most people get so sick of the mess hall and the cantina they just go to work and then to their bunks. It's almost like Ageira wants people functioning like robots around here with no social time. I just can't figure it out. What are they afraid people are going to do, spill trade secrets or something?

1114765.text: I've been working on some of the early warning systems we installed here a few years back. These Rogues really need to learn how to handle this stuff. Trust me, it's like working with trained monkeys.

1114769.text: Stuck on this rock for months at a time? Ain't the fun it looks, let me tell you. As one of our newer bases it lacks the usual facilities you'd expect from an asteroid base. Like hot water on demand, and plumbing that works. I tell you it stinks down near the living quarters.

1114770.text: It was busy around here for a while, some bigshot Rogue bosses and even some Junker chick were visiting for a few weeks, but now it's gone quiet again. We're back to being that ball of rock stuck out in the arse end of nowhere. Even the Hackers visit us less.

1114771.text: There's a Hacker knocking about somewhere, been looking at some of our sensor technology. I don't see why we need a Hacker to service it, we're plenty capable of doing it ourselves. I hate that sense of smug superiority they have, makes me want to smack them in the mouth. I know what would happen if I did that though. Boss would sling me out of the airlock.

1114772.text: I just dropped by with this month's supplies, few thousand tons of food rations, some med supplies, water, that kind of thing. This place needs the stuff and will pay a decent amount for them, make yourself a tidy sum, although what you'd take away I have no idea. I ain't a trader, I'm a Rogue that does the shopping run, know what I mean?

1114773.text: My ship is in pieces, man. It ain't good. I was flying in Ontario, shooting the breeze, couple of cops jumped me out near the Colorado Jump Hole. I swear dude, I was nowhere near Toronto. The chief, he don't believe me none, says he's gonna have me flyin' a Bloodhound for a month. That's not right, man. Not right at all.

1114801.text: Since the station's construction, the government has begun to slowly transfer some delicate projects based on "Valhalla 1" to this base for safety reasons and also to keep a certain level of secrecy around it. Of course, we know what we are doing here. However, if someone dares to reveal anything about it, they will disappear pretty fast. Kind of scary, in a way.

1114802.text: The LSF has been extremely interested in the research done by the Order on antimatter technology. Luckily, we have been able to reproduce some prototypes based on some technology we have sometimes managed to capture from them.

1114803.text: The LSF has been extremely interested in the research done by the Order on antimatter technology. Luckily, we have been able to reproduce some prototypes based on some technology we have sometimes managed to capture from them.

1114804.text: As you may not be aware, the Nomads appear to call themselves the Slomon-K'Hara. After extensive researches on them we discovered that they had a high-degree of genetic adaptability. Those creatures, while being dangerous, are the living wonders of their creators, the Daam-K'Vosh.

1114805.text: The reality about the Nomad war is that we are the aggressors. Sirius was intended to be their playground, and yet, we stole it from them. The Nomads tried to reclaim what was supposed belong to them, and we would have done the same in their place. Can we really blame them for it?

1114806.text: *sigh*...They...just don't stop...*shakes head* Arghh You cannot kill them...they...they just keep coming and coming. This isn't looking good.*shudders* and they...know you! Yeah you! They know ...everything! They never forget...*sigh* Get away from them as soon as you can.

1114807.text: I heard that our instructor once had hair... But I think this is a lie. Speaking of him, you should have seen the joke we did to him. He was so angry at everyone, it was funny... Except the part where he put us in our suits in space for 3 hours as revenge...

1114808.text: Training here is very intensive: they push us to our limits, ask us to do near suicidal things. Last week, one of the recruit got wounded during a training test. He was so close to dying it wasn't even funny. How is that supposed to help us, if we get killed? They seem to have a blatant disregard for even the most basic of safety protocols here.

1114809.text: You should see the last test they made us do. They put you near a nomad, and ask you to resist as long as possible to its thoughts. You must not bend to its wishes. Most of us simply lose consciousness after a while. However, not long ago, one of the recruits had his mind so completely dominated by the Nomad that he was going to free it. Those scientists and instructors are really playing with fire. I personally think we should just kill every last one of the damn aliens.

1114810.text: Alert station is also used as traffic control base. Patrols and operations are monitored from here most of the time. Additional fighter wings are always on standby in case of an attack from enemies, although normally it's only really the Order or the Nomads that present a threat out here. Some people say that's enemies enough, but I reckon we're fairly safe here.

1114829.text: Rumor has it that these track rings were placed here by pirates needing a back way into Attica. Others say they are there to lead pirates deep into the minefield to be lost forever...follow at your own risk.

1114830.text: This must be the most secure system in Sirius. Anything not sending out a police Transponder signal and ID -including Navy and LSF- are shot down immediately. This is a fortress.

1114831.text: Once while on the graveyard shift, I saw an empty cell reserved for the rogue crime boss... I guess reservations can be made here...it actually was a pretty nice cell compared to most of the others.

1114832.text: They gotta cell in this joint with the name 'Mon'Star' on the door. The one next to it has 'Darkstar' written. This must be one tough prison, but lemme tell you... there's a pool goin' on how long it takes us to nab them bastards.

1114833.text: No ships are allowed to stay on Attica, ships dock... unload or load personnel and leave immediately, while under heavy guard.

1114834.text: Apparently, in the case of multiple prisoners escaping, sections of the station can have its atmosphere vented into space to stop them right there from moving any further.

1114835.text: I hear we got some Aunt Billies on this prison station -- Nomads! Scary critters, but we keep 'em locked up in an EMP field that deflects their telepathy and stops their power. Still scares me.

1114836.text: One time while on patrol, we intercepted a civilian freighter entering the Attica passage.... poor bastard didn't know what hit him, four patrols descended upon his ship and blasted him to pieces within seconds...

1114837.text: Last guard around here that messed up ended up stationed in the Alberta precinct. I swear, we stepped softly for a week...

1114851.text: A bounty hunter who survived hundreds of fights with Edge World pirates once found a desolate system... and ran out of fuel trying to find way back home.

1114857.text: We hit a Liberty Rogue convoy the other day near the Huron. We disabled one of the freighters, but an LPI wing ran into us before we could strip anything useful from the wreck. It's probably still drifting out there in the ice field.

1114858.text: Someone's gonna have to make a run for some more Black Market Munitions soon. We're almost dry in countermeasures, and I can't remember the last time I saw any mines on the deck.

1114859.text: I am partial to a bottle of Vodka now and then, don't tell anyone I said that though.

1114860.text: Some Navy jock bumbled his way into the upper Georgian Field a while ago. Some hotshot ace wanna-be with the word 'Unity' scrawled across the nose of his ship. Probably thought a solo patrol'd look good to the bigwigs. We sure showed him, though. His ship's probably still drifting out there.

1114861.text: With that battleship near Toronto, it's hard to do anything near the only lane in this system. But they don't have enough patrols for the entire system, and it's a long way across open space to Fort Severn.

1114862.text: There's three ways out of this system for us, but only one we actually use. The California Jump Hole is too close to that Lane Hacker base in the St. Lawrence Field, and Fort Severn's practically sitting atop the Alberta one. We have to dodge the Ottawa's patrols every time we head for Colorado, but once we're through, it's just a short flight to good old Ouray.

1114863.text: We just can't get a break from those bloody Junkers. Everywhere we go, they're almost one step ahead of us. New York, Texas, Pennsylvania, and they've even got their little depot here up behind Orillia. I can't take it. Someone should just kill them all and be done with it.

1114864.text: I don't trust those Insurgency boys. They're too uptight, too military. They've even got their own fancy little fighters, and meanwhile ours are just barely held together. All those resources have to come from somewhere. It's a conspiracy, I say. Someone's supporting them, I just don't know who or why.

1114865.text: I hate this place. I hate every inch of this stinking, ice-covered, rusted junkpile. It's not enough that we can barely hit a convoy without a Navy patrol showing up or a bunch of Junkers running across us, or that we have to dodge half the Ottawa's fighters if we want to head for Ouray. No, we have to live in freezing cold too! The only warm place on this entire station is near the reactor, and unless they like rad-poisoning, no one's stupid enough to sleep down there. I can't take it much longer.

1114867.text: If it comes to a foreign invader reaching Liberty's doorstep, have no doubts about where the Xenos will stand. We'll help the Navy beat back those foreign pipsqueeks, then we'll go back to dealing with the Navy like we always have: a middle finger in their face and a dagger in their back.

1114868.text: Ever since the Zoners got run out of Bering, we've had to scrape together whatever weapons we can. Doesn't matter who, we'll rob Ageira if we have to. We need guns.

1114869.text: We can barely keep up with the orders from BMM for Platinum. In addition to delivering straight to their processing sites, they also keep a stockpile on Thames Outpost in case of supply disruptions.

1114870.text: Platinum is heavily used in producing Military Vehicles. Fortunately, the war with Rheinland didn't disrupt our own supply lines, but I don't know where Nuremburg got enough Platinum to keep up production during the war.

1114871.text: Freiburg Station in Stuttgart stores a lot of Platinum. Before the war with Rheinland we shipped large quantities down there on a regular basis.

1114872.text: Before the war with Bretonia, Kusari was largely dependent on BMM for Ship Hull Panels. But once the war began, Samura had a patriotic duty to meet that need. We are now proudly a strong rival in that market. We are experimenting with incorporating Platinum into our product. Once we are successful, BMM's antique design won't be able to compete, and the ships built with their obsolete alloys won't last either.

1114873.text: Osaka Storage Facility is critical to Samura's operations. From there we can schedule just in time supply deliveries that minimize production waste and maximize efficiency. We can also stockpile materials like Platinum there in case our foreign suppliers fail to deliver on their contracts in a timely fashion.

1114874.text: Kishiro has developed a next generation Optronics technology on Planet Honshu using Platinum as a critical ingredient. That breakthrough will keep us light years ahead of our competition for at least a decade.

1114875.text: Unfortunately, we don't possess a storage facility like Osaka, ourselves. Instead, we tap into the government's stockpile on Narita when we need extra Platinum on short notice.

1114876.text: We are experimenting with Platinum in developing a next generation of Super Alloys. You can never rest easy in this business. You have to beat the competition to the next technological breakthrough.

1114877.text: Lancaster Trade Center is Bowex's all purpose storage and distribution facility. We distribute Platinum throughout Bretonia, as needed, from that location.

1114878.text: The operation here on Toronto is certainly impressive. Unfortunately, the workers are too well paid to be much interested in Synth Paste. No worries, though, we're hard at work on that little problem.

1114879.text: I noticed that the food storage compartments on board are not very secure. It would be a great shame if some foreign agent of Rheinland or Gallia infiltrated this station and poisoned the food supply. Why, then it would be up to Synth Foods to save the day, wouldn't it?

1114880.text: The war between Liberty and Rheinland disrupted a lot of Platinum supply routes that we used to run. The Ring, Ingolstadt, Leipzig, Bonn, Planet New Berlin...oh well, it's just boring old Kensington nowadays.

1114881.text: Now that the war with Kusari is over, perhaps Gateway will be allowed to ship up there now. I've heard that Shinjuku Station is quite a sight. I overheard a Samura pilot saying they experiment with Platinum there, too.

1114882.text: Roppongi Station gets regular Platinum deliveries. Samura and Kishiro go through this stuff like there's an endless supply of it, and we're happy to sell it to them at a premium when they run short.

1114883.text: The war with Rheinland really put a damper on our shipments of Platinum to Bonn. Well, some of them, anyway. The ones the Navy had an eye on. You know what I mean.

1114884.text: If you have to be stationed on a corporate space station, I recommend one that has a large mix of personnel. There's nothing like a bar fight between miners and middle management to lighten up a shift.

1114885.text: Apparently a lot of corporate interests are convinced that Huron is the next big thing. I can't quite figure it out, myself. Sure, Platinum is valuable enough, but it's not a high tech product. The corps must have something up there sleeves, though, if all their reps that keep traipsing through this bar is any indication.

1114886.text: The criminals in this system keep us busy. Fortunately, there is only one Trade Lane, so patrols are fairly simple. Don't leave the main routes or you're asking for serious trouble.

1114887.text: What happened to Red Deer Station is unbelievable. The Liberty Rogues have never done something so brazen before. Personally, I think the Navy ought to handle Alberta. Military justice often has a lot less red tape to deal with when it comes to rules of engagement.

1114888.text: Wait, don't tell me, let me guess. Interspace Commerce is an insurance company, not a shipper, right? You're either drunk or just naturally an ignoramus, aren't you?

1114889.text: Go blather at someone else. If I want to hear tired old pick up lines, I'll finish my drink within range of a bounty hunter.

1114890.text: Sure Interspace primarily used to be an insurance company, but every business has to change with the times. Of course, insuring cargo shipments is still our core business, but you do know what we do with all of those insurance premiums, don't you? We invest them by making loans to all sorts of commercial interests, including shippers.

1114891.text: Here's how it works. Some shipping company wants to expand their operation and they need transports. We loan them the credits to buy new ships, and they have to offer teh new ships as collateral for the loan. If they go bankrupt, or miss too many loan payments, then we foreclose on the assets and take ownership. A lot of the time we try to sell off the assets, but sometimes we just keep them for internal use. That's how Interspace got into the shipping business.

1114892.text: Platinum is big business in Liberty these days, so it's big business for Interspace, too. We have to maintain a large staff here to audit the shipments that we are insuring.

1114893.text: Sometimes a corporation fails to pay all its insurance premiums, and we have to seize assets to make up the difference. Often, they sign over the cargo itself to us. All our stations have substantial storage areas to house such materials. Effectively, we get the goods for free, and can sell it for any price we choose with a huge profit margin.

1114894.text: The Interspace babes who hang out in this bar are smoking hot, man. One of them is a real fire breather, though. She sends tingles up my spine every time she sneers at me.

1114895.text: The LPI is too scared to patrol the various stellar fields in this system. They think they're full of criminals. Of course they're full of criminals! They breed in their like bunnies. Speaking of...where did that Interspace babe go?

1114896.text: Don't mind my comrade, there's only two things on his mind. Hunting criminals and hunting women. When we actually go up against a criminal woman, well, she'd better hope she doesn't survive the initial arrest. Personally, I think I'd plow myself into an asteroid before allowing myself to be interrogated by that guy.

1114897.text: We all figured there would be big bounties coming down after Red Deer Station met its end. The LPI has been strangely silent about the whole affair, though. Something's not right there.

Universal Shipping constructed St. Albans as an auxiliary shipyard in 821 AS with the help of generous investment from the Liberty government and the unspoken promise of future shipping contracts related to construction within the Virginia system. Since then, it has grown surprisingly quickly to become an important endpoint for all sorts of shipments, as well as a place for contractors and corporate representatives who have business with the Navy to meet and negotiate in quiet with ease.

1114910.mapped:
Located deep in the Concord belt, Beckley is a lightly populated base by Xeno standards. Though seemingly in contradiction with the Xeno modus operandi, the base was founded by a group of radicals who were spared a lengthy sentence on the Wall by a Xeno raiding party which attacked and boarded the liner transporting them. Deciding to champion the same cause as their rescuers, the rebels saw an opportunity to wedge themselves in the path of Junker smugglers, beginning to make frequent usage of the Virginia system's more discreet jump hole passages.

The inhabitants of Beckley now launch frequent raids on smugglers passing through the system, often destroying the ships they find and extracting what remains to further strengthen their position. Their effectiveness as a thorn in the side of the Junkers has lead to increased Rogue patrols in the Concord belt, to take care of the budding nuisance.

Beckley's raiders continue a proud tradition of pulling recruits off of prison liners bound for the Wall and occasionally attract those tired of the straight and narrow on Houston. These pilots also frequently target Navy and Police ships, relying on ambushes and other underhanded tactics to remain competitive with their numerous foes. This has in turn made them the focus of urban legends and other exaggerated tales, used to keep cadets sharp and aware of their mortality.

1114932.mapped:
The Liberty Insurgency has begun construction of a new bastion of the same class as the former Marshall Station, going so far as to use the same name. It was intended as both a memorial to those lost in the destruction of the original in Bering, and a show of open defiance. It was also considered strategically sound, as Marshall's design had been very effective, necessitating overwhelming force to finally bring it down.

In the first half of 829 AS, Liberty Navy forces broke through the Kansas defensive lines and laid siege to Planet Veracruz. Destined to never be finished and restored to its original state, the station was quickly fitted with additional improvised weaponry and manned by volunteers for its glorious last stand against an overwhelming Navy assault.

The station endured repeated bombardments by the Ohio and her escort vessels throughout a seventeen hour long battle before its hull finally gave in and explosive decompression killed everyone onboard. In a final act of defiance, the crew onboard Marshall launched last ditch missile salvos from the station's improvised silos, managing to critically damage Ohio's lead escort vessel, the battlecruiser Guam.

1114935.text: The Concord Belt is a large but sparsely packed field of asteroids, much like those found in Hudson and Bering. It contains no resources of value but plays host to a contingent of Xenos. While traversing such fields is usually deemed a flight risk, this has not stopped local forces from subjecting fresh recruits to pursuit drills among the rocks. These exercises however became increasingly unpopular, as members of such flight wings have on occasion gone missing, while those who return claim to have been chased out of the field by patchwork monstrosities that refused all hails. With mounting superstition, patrols typically draw the line at the field's edge, any tales regarding 'ghost' ships are dismissed as fabrications.

1114937.mapped:
To Liberty, Nu represents a treasure trove of potential discoveries, the kind which she believes might provide her with the means to circumvent the barriers imposed by the currently defined borders of the Great Houses on every side.

The Order's view of the situation is decidedly the opposite. To it, the system is a coffin nailed shut for good reason and Liberty's expansion represents a Pandora's box situation. Intent on preventing disaster should Liberty find anything that ought to stay unfound, the Mehit has been assigned to the mysterious system to keep a watchful vigil. Relying on networks of informants and operatives rather than brute force, it pits Liberty's greed against its own bureaucracy and ensures this expansion is stalled sufficiently enough to contain potential risks.

1114940.mapped:
One of the Navy's most closely guarded secrets, Radford Research Station is a clandestine research facility, built exclusively for Liberty Navy usage in the seclusion of the radar-dampening Newport Anomaly. The station houses numerous research projects for the Navy and the Government, although what these projects entail is little more than a mystery at this point.

Much like Radford's (former) sister installations, Benford and Ithaca, the station's primary research directive is probably that of alternative energy sources and jump technology. Radford houses a large "Baxter Anomaly" in an enclosure on the ventral end of the station, and a large portion of the station's science teams are likely devoted to the research and investigation of this anomaly. The station is also seemingly charged with the reverse engineering and research of enemy vessels, given the battle-damaged hulls of Rheinland Military vessels resting in the station's drydocks.

Regardless, the one certainty surrounding Radford Research Station is that its secrets are well-guarded, insofar that the entirety of the Newport Anomaly is an off-limits zone, and any unauthorized vessel flying near the Anomaly may be fired upon without warning.

1114943.text:
The Newport Anomaly is a large dark matter cloud found in the Virginia system. Newport's exact origin and composition are unknown, the cloud itself rendering any attempts at gathering scan data close to impossible.
Initial theories suggested that it was an outcropping of the Grande Negra in the Texas system, although the limited analysis conducted about the cloud's composition in recent years has proven that theory false.
Its origin remains a mystery, however that did not stop the Liberty Navy from constructing Radford Research Station inside Newport, its scanner-suppressing nature along with the scattered pockets of radiation making for the ideal environment to hide a secret installation within.

1114946.text: A large and dense field of ice in the Virginia system, not unlike those found within the Barrier. Scientists believe the Charleston Ice Field holds the key to determining the origin of the Lamberton field, but the LSF have restricted entry to the field for reasons they choose not to elaborate on.

A large gas giant with an atmosphere comprised mostly of Helium and Hydrogen and faint traces of other noble gasses, along with a recently discovered one dubbed 'Phlebotinum' by Liberty Navy scientists. It is believed that the latter is responsible for the planet's distinctive blue-green tint, however exact information is classified. Hampton is a barren moon with a very thin atmosphere that provides little protection from the sun. The moon is devoid of any signs of life or exploitable natural resources, and it is because of this fact that Hampton has become such an asset for the Liberty Navy.

The Navy has constructed a large training facility and firing range on the surface, for the purposes of advanced infantry training in exotic environments. Many of the Navy's marine cadets spend their first few months in orbital facilities and planetside recruitment depots, before being shipped to planetoids like Hampton to participate in hazardous environment training amongst harsh sandstorms and an extreme low pressure environment.

The moon is also used by the Navy itself, typically for weapons tests of newly constructed vessels coming out of the Washington drydocks. While orbital bombardment is largely an obsolete tactic (due to the widespread use of point-defense systems), it still remains an important training mechanism and a useful strategy, should the planet's orbital defenses be disabled, or be nonexistent in the first place. Several large craters from these weapons tests can be seen on the far side of the planet, opposite the training center.

1114954.text:

TERRAIN: Barren
TEMPERATURE: -69°C to 72°C
ESCAPE VELOCITY: 13.66 km/sec

A volcanic world by nature where day and night each last almost as long as a whole year on Planet Manhattan, Reston is an unhospitable planet of no strategic value. With surface temperatures ranging from -118 to 243 Celsius and no resources or wildlife present, it has been deemed unsuitable for terraforming and merely serves as a landmark in the Virginia system. It has been nicknamed "Planet Hell" by pilots of the Liberty Navy, thanks to the firestorms ravaging its surface on the side exposed to the nearby star. There are also rumors of top-secret subterranean installations going around, however those can be dismissed as lies and slander, attributed to Reston's extremely hostile nature.

1114956.text:
DIAMETER: 12,753 km.
MASS: 5.98 x 10e24 kg.
TERRAIN: Terrestrial
TEMPERATURE: -46°C to 23°C
ESCAPE VELOCITY: 8.27 km/sec

Columbia is rather frigid for a terrestrial world, but it is capable of supporting human life. It has a relatively thin atmosphere and low gravity, which has given rise to numerous large flying species, many of which are predatory carnivores. Its flora has evolved to immense sizes, with shrubs standing as tall as 20 meters, and forests easily towering upwards of 500 meters, yet still have flexible trunks. These are major hazards to landing craft and surface teams.

Nevertheless, Liberty colonized Columbia. Its inhospitable nature gives it an excellent natural barrier against infiltration, so it was given to the Liberty Navy, in order to establish a secure facility on the surface. Liberty built a single, massive pyramid-shaped complex on the surface. Nicknamed the "Cheyenne Mountain Complex" (partly to throw off foreign infiltrators so they would investigate the planet's mountain ranges) it houses the bulk of the Liberty Navy strategic command staff, and can serve as a point-of-retreat for the Liberty government in case Manhattan were ever to be threatened.

The Cheyenne facility is protected by a powerful shield grid drawing power from immense subterranean geothermal power stations, constructed to ensure self-sufficiency in energy and also to protect the generators from the wildlife. Beyond that the planet has little of value. What resources it does posess are inaccessible due to the extremely hazardous ecology, and restricted nature of the Virginia system as a whole.

1115015.text: Olpe Border Station is a command centre for Rheinland's Federal Police services within the developing Cologne system. Its main task is to safeguard cargo convoys on their way to and from the Wuppertal Refinery from the numerous pirate raiders that are known to operate in the system.

1115022.text: It is great that the Red Hessians keep giving us military support and all, but sometimes I get the feeling they're trying to get us to do more than we originally set out to do. We really just want a free Planet Stuttgart, not necessarily everything else the Hessians stand for.

1115023.text: This ship is a fine piece of machinery, even in its older age. Why, I bet if the LWB could build some of these ourselves, we could really teach Synth Foods a lesson!

1115024.text: This system is really a crossroads of sorts. From here, it's easy to visit Hamburg or Stuttgart - one on each end of Rheinland. Not to mention the possibilities through Duesseldorf. Yeah, quite a nice place for a jumphole traveler to visit.

1115025.text: We're far enough away from the eyes of the police to be able to supply ourselves nicely here. We have some Freelancers bringing supplies from various "anonymous donors" from the core systems, as well as what the Unioners and Red Hessians can acquire through strong arm tactics.

1115026.text: Those Red Hessians really like those Hessian Tears. Why, they seem to be bringing them through all the time!

1115027.text: The Hessian Tears mined by the Red Hessians pass through this way often on their way to Liberty. Sometimes we bring a few shipments here ourselves from Vogtland to trade with the Unioners. The Hessians don't mind so much, as they're our closest allies. Plus we make sure not to do it too often.

1115028.text: Since we arrived in Cologne, our opportunities to supply our allies in Rheinland have grown greatly. In addition to our Humpbacks, we've even managed to acquire a few Behemoths to move goods around. It's much more effective that way but also rather risky.

1115029.text: A lot of the surplus food we produce at Merzig is brought here to be traded with the Unioners. We don't have the capacity to produce too much, but they pay us nicely. In particular, they always have a lot of engine components and ship hull panels, which they get from their raids on Alster Shipyard. We're in desperate need of those.

1115030.text: I'd stay away from that Udo character out in Saar if I were you. He seems nice enough, but he has a strange feeling around him. I'm not sure what it is, but he seems to especially scare the female LWB members.

1115031.text: The LWB can barely maintain this ship on their own. Without us helping them fix it all the time, they'd probably have burnt the reactor long ago.

Jena Station was constructed in 804 AS as an MND quarantine lab for sensitive materials discovered on Planet Weimar, and as an interrogation site for Military personnel suspected of being “Niemann sympathizers”. The facility would be heavily damaged in 817 AS, when an LSF strike force breached Weimar’s defense perimeter and boarded the station. After abducting a number of senior Scientists and their research materials, the boarders detonated explosive devices and withdrew towards Hamburg. Rheinland’s retaliatory strike on Liberty forces near Atka later triggered the Hudson War.

Liberty claims to have only become aware of the Jena Incident during ceasefire negotiations 6 years later, and continues to disavow knowledge of the ships involved to this day. Following the incident, Jena saw significant security enhancements, including an extension of the Unstrut Minefield and a significantly expanded local garrison. Jena is now manned by several elite squadrons of MND, who are determined to prevent the humiliation of 817 from repeating.

The planet Stuttgart has been the breadbasket of Rheinland since its settlement in 94 AS. Over time, its farmers formed a powerful union, named the Weltbau Verein von Stuttgart (WVS). The organization managed to successfully lobby the Rheinland government to subsidize Stuttgart agriculture for hundreds of years, generating a huge amount of wealth amongst the farming dynasties and increasing the planet's food output considerably, especially in the growing of Blue Jillies. But with the end of the Eighty Years War in 669 AS and the government completely bankrupted, the subsidies were no longer tenable and were cut almost overnight.

In a secret deal during the war, the Rheinland government desperately borrowed huge sums from Liberty. Facing default on their loans at the end of the war, they were forced to offer something to House Liberty. Synth Foods wanted complete access to planet Stuttgart, which the Rheinland government granted in exchange for renegotiated debt repayment terms. The Liberty food giant moved in immediately, buying out huge numbers of nearly bankrupt Stuttgart farmers and proceeded to crush entire farming dynasties over the following decades. Some collapsed in suspicious circumstances, such as the Erlichmann family whose farms and plantations suffered a number of sabotages shortly before their buyout by Synth Foods. Much of Stuttgart was subsequently converted into vast expanses of the bioengineered mono-crops of Synth Foods.

The government backed the foreign company wholeheartedly and looked the other way as Synth Foods used unscrupulous business practices to further consolidate its control over Stuttgart. The remaining independent farmers were ultimately forced to lower the prices of their produce in order to compete with Synth Foods, which greatly reduced their income.

The once proud Stuttgart farmers were reduced to indentured servants. Inexorably, Synth Foods assimilated the bulk of the planet's arable land, dutifully paying its Rheinland federal taxes and feeding the bribe machine in New Berlin. The WVS tried to fight back legally in the courts but soon discovered that their influence had been sold to a higher bidder. This sparked a number of sabotage incidents at Synth Food owned factories and it lead to Synth Foods forcing the Rheinland government to replace virtually all of the original WVS board members with their lackeys in 775 AS, destroying the farming union's voice in New Berlin. It was this final act that lead radicals from the WVS, including the former head of the Erlichmann family, to found the Landwirtrechtbewegung ("Farmers Rights Movement"), simply referred to as the LWB, later the same year.

The LWB built a small depot called Darmstadt within the Ostnebel to serve as a base for operations targeted at Synth Foods convoys within Rheinland space. The Red Hessians also used it as way station along one of their routes to Omega-11. Yet as of 825 AS the LWB has begun to self-destruct as more and more infighting takes place between the previously united cells.

Darmstadt Depot itself became a battleground with multiple splinter factions of the dying LWB vying for control of the station. As the situation aboard Darmstadt became more desperate, a handful of hardline members took it upon themselves to put an end to the madness, and in a fit of self-righteous fury the group rigged the stations reactors to blow. Destroying Darmstadt and burning the shattered remnants of the LWB upon the very pyre that first ignited the Landwirtrechtbewegung.

1115051.text: This is a collection of heavily modified biodomes that allows the LWB to continue their farming lifestyle, at least to a small degree. Owing to having been built from salvaged biodome parts, however, their production is less than a tenth that of conventional biodomes.

1115052.text: This station here is pretty nice and laid back. I just came from Northeim Base and the Red Hessians have great security, let me tell you. It's good to feel safe but it's also nice to not get overly questioned.

1115053.text: I heard someone say there's a suspicious Freelancer around. I think he's on Eindhoven right now. Rumor has it that he may be working for the infected. If you run into him, I'd appreciate if you didn't mention me. I'm scared of those infected.

1115054.text: It's always interesting to see how people run around their little stations, isn't it? Some people think so highly of themselves. Like they're above everything else in the sector. It never fails to make me wonder.

1115055.text: I'm on the payroll of an outside organization. We do have some agreements with the LWB here, even if they're a bit suspicious. Everyone appreciates it when we help to secure their stations though.

1115056.text: The infected coming from out in the deep Omegas are a threat to us all! If you find one, don't think twice about shooting it. It would do the same to you.

1115057.text: The infected appear to do the majority of their fighting lately against the Corsairs, Red Hessians, and militaries, but they also seem to be sneaking operatives into the smaller groups in Rheinland. The LWB and Bundschuh are at great risk due to their lax security.

1115058.text: I work for Orbi--myself. Yes, that's it, I'm a freelancer. I'm just here to discuss various... things with the LWB concerning Planet Stuttgart. Don't worry - nothing involving arson or anything.

1115059.text: Have you ever visited Baden Baden? It's a great place. It's as beautiful as Stuttgart used to be. I think it serves as a great reminder of the LWB's fight. By chance, I happen to have some brochures here somewhere. I'll send one along to you.

1115060.text: I've heard that Orbital Spa and Cruise has been working with the WVS on Planet Stuttgart to send LWB supporters on conveniently timed vacations that just happen to avoid police raids. Though that's probably untrue and it's just a coincidence.

1115061.text: It's quite the flight from Bruchsal to get down here, but the LWB has begun to house many additional Refugees from Planet Stuttgart who've run afoul of the police or those Synth Foods people. It gives us a chance to recruit even more for our movement.

1115062.text: The LWB are good friends. They're rather undertrained, yes, but they have the concerns of the people in mind just as the Bundschuh does.

1115063.text: The LWB and Unioners conduct a good amount of business up in Cologne. Sometimes we'll come down here for some supplies - they seem to have a good amount of food and fuel - and in exchange they'll come to us to purchase some ship parts.

1115064.text: We'd really prefer if the LWB took a stronger stand against Republican. Of all the Corporations in Rheinland, Republican seems to have angered them the least. We want to get them to assist more, that accursed corporation needs to pay for its crimes against the people!

1115065.text: We Junkers don't usually head down this way much. Usually the Landbewhatnot - let's stick with LWB - come up to Kreuzberg for supplies. I've found they have some rather nice food around these parts. It's expensive - much more than paste - but we run across a lot of people who'll pay even more for it. Everyone wins.

1115066.text: I'm getting ready to make a run out to Yanagi. It's a bit of a trip from here - and not without its dangers - but H-fuel comes cheap up there and the LWB are always willing to trade for it. Sometimes shipments of Fertilizers from Kusari will also be found. We'll bring them around, too.

1115067.text: I'm not your typical Hessian. I had been captured by slavers and was being sent to mine diamonds for Daumann in Omega-11 when a Red Hessian attack saved me. I was so grateful that I joined their cause. Right now I'm on assignment helping people from the same situation in the LWB adapt.

1115068.text: There are some Hessians who don't fully trust me because of my background. I'm trying to work extra hard to prove myself to them. The LWB, not being as skilled as the Hessians, are much easier to impress.

1115069.text: We've gotten several strange readings from an area on the far side of the system. We've taken to calling it "the Ackermann Anomaly" after the pilot who initially, err, discovered it. A strange story, that incident. Needless to say, our Red Hessian allies have been doing all manner of research on it.

1115070.text: There's a rather unusual asteroid field opposite our position relative to the suns. It's just recently been discovered in fact, initial reports suggest its source is different than that of the Felsenmeer.

1115071.text: Without the help of the Red Hessians, the LWB would most likely have failed early in its life. This station represents those links, as it ensures we are able to continue moving back and forth from their stations with supplies.

1115072.text: If you continue toward the Felsenmeer, you will find a fairly stable jumphole that leads to a major area of Red Hessian activity. I recommend at least a visit - unless you've crossed them, that is. If so, I suggest you go no further than this base.

1115073.text: This is currently the largest LWB installation in the whole sector. Which isn't saying that much if you consider the size of some of the Red Hessians' stations. It makes me proud nonetheless.

1115074.text: After years of living in the Ostnebel, the clouds of the Walker nebula feel somehow safe to me. I wonder what will happen when I am able to return to Planet Stuttgart after all of this?

1115075.text: Merzig is possibly the most unstable of all the stations in this system. Solar flares blast the station often, though most are not too damaging. On occasion, a powerful one will knock out power or damage ships. I hope that life support is never damaged.

1115076.text: While dangerous, this is a very nice station to visit. Many civilian farmers come from Voelklingen to help grow food, as they had for generations before this. It's no Planet Stuttgart, but at least it allows them to remember their past. We still hope to return triumphant one day soon.

1115077.text: It makes me sad whenever I hear of a fellow farmer being imprisoned at Vierlande. It's a horrible, horrible place. I heard a story from a woman on Voelklingen that one of our members once escaped from the place. That is heartening.

1115078.text: I miss being able to caress the plantations of my family farm under the warm red Stuttgart sun.

1115079.text: The Red Hessians have always been generous in their support of the LWB. Why, they've even donated a couple older cruisers for us to help our cause! Unfortunately, they are too important to risk losing, so we do not use them very often.

1115080.text: The Bundschuh is a group that the LWB really looks up to. They tend to be very well educated and serve as wonderful role models for patriotism and dedication for our newer members.

1115081.text: Rumor has it that we're making friendly with OSC. While it's true we haven't attacked them recently for many reasons, I'm not sure that really means anything. Or does it?

The newest project of the Core, Bora Bora, is an under-construction depot considered one of the most ambitious endeavors in the remote border worlds. The Core, struck by a crisis following the collapse of Omicron Rho's connections, needed a quick solution to establish new trade routes toward the Houses. The only viable path for this was through Omicron Delta, Kappa, Theta, Sigma-17, Sigma-19, and from there into Kusari or Rheinland.

The project is financed by Kusari, Liberty, Rheinland, Bretonia, the Gas Miners Guild, and the Core itself. Recognizing the critical importance of maintaining the Core's influence in the Omicrons, all involved parties swiftly allocated resources to Sigma-17 as soon as the first convoys were organized.

The timing of this project comes as no surprise. Following Atka's destruction by the Outcasts, the Houses feared that Sigma-17 could become a major choke point, potentially cutting the Core off from the rest of Sirius. To prevent this, the Core, in cooperation with Interspace Commerce, convened an emergency meeting on Newark Station with representatives from all sponsoring factions. They successfully persuaded all sides, emphasizing the Core’s vital contributions to technological advancements—thus, the Bora Bora project was set into motion.

1115110.text: Times are tough, but they have never been anything but.

1115111.text: They say over 80% of our high command was wiped out during the Bering evacuation. To hell with them I say, we have squandered years sat on our thumbs doing nothing. Shame about the boys who served under them though.

1115112.text: The Commonwealth was a bad idea. What is the point in trying to make a nation when Liberty Core systems have more people, more ships and more money? We have to get a real foothold on a real planet with real people on it, not this empty ball of mud in Vespucci.

1115113.text: I see a lot more Seps come in every day. I should not call them that really, word from above is that anyone referring to people as former Sep or former Legion will have their rations stripped. They want to start anew or something.

1115114.text: A typical Insurgency formation is an absolute hot-mess. Former Navy ships in varying states of modification, borderworlds tech, those ugly things we make ourselves all combine into a single blob and hurl themselves at the enemy. It works though, probably owing to the skill of the pilots more than anything.

1115115.text: We get a lot of recruits through agents in Pennsylvania. Anyone related to the Insurgency will have trouble operating openly on the Core planets, so the Zoner settlements on Erie are where interested parties go to get picked up.

1115116.text: The Commonwealth was a mistake. The idea of setting up a democratic government as an example of how we could do better was sound in principle. But once politicians started constraining our military options, our ability to reform Liberty as a whole was threatened.

1115117.text: We've been stuck on asteroid bases for decades. The biodome gardens on America changed that a bit, at least we have a place at our headquarters to chill out. Before that, flying to purchase supplies from nearby independent bases was all the shoreleave we could get. Visiting Curacao or Los Angeles was an eternal temptation, but we're good at going undercover.

1115118.text: With the war over, we are running out of time to make an impact. The longer we wait, the more time the Navy has to recover. It aint nice, but I honestly wish another war would break out.

1115119.text: There's a Jump Hole in the southern part of Vespucci. We use it less frequently than the Jump Hole to Magellan, but it provides alternative access to other Independent systems in proximity to Liberty.

1115141.text: The remains of a Hydrogen-Helium gas dwarf, the former planet Tiksi now finds itself on an outbound trajectory, spewing out gases and collapsing inward as it fails to recover from its collision with the much larger gas giant Taymyr.

1115143.text: A thin, wide cloud of ice and dust, formed in the hectic and cataclysmic birth of the Bering system. The edge of this collection of icy planetesimals represents the furthest reaches of Bering's sphere of influence.

1115145.text: Once-superheated gases ejected from the collision between Tiksi and Taymyr, the now-cooled Tiksi Cloud has condensed into a dark, heavy field of purplish volatile gases that obscure the slow decay of its parent gas dwarf.

1115147.text: The edge of Bering's Tanner Belt, stretching from the edge of the system into Laptev. The result of some massive primordial collision between worlds, the leftover rocks stretch on throughout the system, and serve no purpose beyond creating a navigational hazard.

1115149.text:
The first expeditionary vessel of its kind built by the fledgling Rheinland state just before the turn of the second century, the Dallmann was meant to serve as a test-bed of the recently-acquired Liberty engine, acquired in 96 AS. Upon arrival and final deceleration into the sector, however, the experimental engine broke down under extreme duress and was subsequently rendered inoperable by asteroid strikes before the crew could successfully repair it. Left adrift without control, additional strikes then disabled the power and communications systems, leaving the ship powerless and unable to be rescued.

The supplies aboard the ship left the crew alive for some time, and one of their final acts as noted in the black box records was the christening of the sector 'Laptev', due to its overlap of the Bering system; a name that the Rheinland government, and Sirius at large, accepted alongside their posthumous award ceremony held not long after the discovery of the wreckage.

1115153.mapped:
Soon after the Hellfire Legion's formation it became clear that new pilots would need to be recruited from the Liberty population if the movement was to continue to conduct combat operations. A location was required to train these applicants and filter out the inevitable security risks posed by infiltrators.

The remote Kansas system was chosen as a destination for such an installation, resulting in the excavation of a large asteroid in the strategic field. Fort Riley's dense rocky shell serves as excellent protection for those living at the base. Fort Riley's primary facilities cater to the manufacturing and maintenance of fighters and other small craft, usually working independently of the production lines on Fort Leniex.

Long tasked with defending the Commonwealth's civilian assets in Kansas, Fort Riley, then named Monterrey, had a much stronger attachment to the Commonwealth than the forces in Vespucci. When the Insurgency arrived in Vespucci, Fort Riley quickly dispatched its squadrons to assist the Ravager in the defense of the Commonwealth. Ultimately they were too late to make a difference; Ravager had already fallen by the time Fort Riley's reinforcements arrived.

The Insurgency turned its guns on the remaining defenders of the Commonwealth, and fought them back to Fort Riley itself. Boarding action ensued, resulting in the Insurgency securing Monterrey and ending the uprising. Training operations aboard Fort Riley have since resumed at a frantic pace, with the Insurgency expediting field deployments to refill its depleted ranks.

In response to a sizable incursion of ships belonging to the Bretonian Armed Forces, Riley was ordered to have its garrison consolidate with Vespucci's defenders and fight them back. It followed through with these orders without delay, and as a result swayed the fight in the Insurgency's favor. It was however unable to prevent Mulvane's destruction, as fighting and logistical issues delayed any plans for relieving the besieged outpost.

With Mulvane destroyed, and its garrison battered, Riley faces a precarious situation - the Battleship Delaware

The Dreadnought Ravager began its service as the Outcast battleship MNS Ampoliros. In the earliest days of the Hellfire Legion's uprising, military commanders identified a pressing need to replace or supplement their limited supply of capital class hardware if they were to continue resisting Liberty effectively. This requirement would eventually result in the development of the Arbiter class battleship. Prior to this, the Legion's admirals sought assistance from foreign powers to bolster their own capabilities.

The only such endeavour to bear fruit was a negotiation with the Outcasts brokered by the Lane Hackers. Seeing the value in a local insurgency disrupting Liberty's authorities, the Toruella Cartel agreed to the sale of a prototype Ranseur hull. Upon receipt of the Ampoliros, the Legion's engineers were aghast to discover that they had been sold an ancient and obselete hulk that had been stripped of its most sensitive and useful components. Despite the Legion's complaints, the Outcasts advised they had upheld exactly the bargain they had agreed to - a prototype first generation battleship.

The newly christened Ravager was plagued by mechanical issues that prevented its front line deployment, resulting in a permanent assignment to Vespucci as a traffic checkpoint. Most of its officers dealt closely with Commonwealth officials during this period, creating strong loyalties to the separatist state. With the formation of the Insurgency in 827 AS, the Ravager quickly declared in favour of the civilian government. It was destroyed soon after the arrival of the joint Insurgent Fleet following the shattering of Willard Research Station. The wreck remains unsalvaged as a reminder of the Commonwealth's dissolution.

The Insurgency had sufficient reason to believe that a concerted effort was going to be made by a combined Liberty/Bretonia strike group into Vespucci, in order to entirely destroy the holdout.

However, the unified defensive front drawn from all Insurgency stations would only be met by a light Bretonian attack group, composed of mostly destroyers. With Liberty's own elements nowhere to be seen, thus routing this element proved to be suspiciously easy.

As a result of this desperate measure, Mulvane and Riley were lacking the garrisons needed to defend themselves from the Delaware's attack group and ultimately both succumbed to an extremely aggressive albeit somewhat costly siege by the Liberty Navy.

Vespucci now truly stands as the last bastion of the Insurgency, with nothing left in Kansas to hold back the Liberty Navy's advance.

Yuma is a lush world that, at first, seems ideal for human population; with its vast seas, temperate islands, and a wide equatorial band of humid tropical terrain, it seems to practically beg for human inhabitants. Since its discovery in 640 AS by Zoner explorers, there have been nearly a dozen attempts at colonization, all of which (save the most recent) failed. The overly-aggressive native flora is capable of re-growing in cleared land at astonishing speeds and chokes out synthetic crops with ease; as such, early attempts at colonization failed because they lacked strong supply lines from off-world.

In 817 AS, Deep Space Engineering surveyors based their ship, the Armstrong, in orbit of the planet. When DSE revealed their discovery of the planet to the Libertonian public, intense bidding for rights on Yuma ensued, and the resultant capital gave DSE the funds necessary to initiate construction of a docking ring.

However, the Armstrong came under increasingly frequent and organized attacks from pirates in the system. Dozens of survey probes sent throughout the system were destroyed, and it soon became clear to the Armstrong's crew that they were not welcome in the system. Pirates, utilizing more advanced weaponry than previous raids, managed to destroy the Armstrong in a single concentrated assault, with all DSE crew onboard lost, and the docking ring not quite complete.

The Crayter Republic entered the system shortly after the Armstrong met its demise. Seeing an opportunity to ensure a strong claim to at least half of Coronado, the refugee Crayterians constructed Sabah Shipyard in orbit of the planet. In conjunction with Liberty and with clandestine financial backing from the Independent Miners Guild, the Crayterians have nearly finished the docking ring's construction, and, thanks to a discriminating campaign of eliminating the native flora in conjunction with Cryer Pharmaceuticals, have established several successful colonies on the planet's surface.

The largest settlement on Yuma is the capital city of New Thessalonica, which is home to over three million souls. New Thessalonica, as well as a handful of smaller settlements, represent a new class of "floating cities" built atop Yuma's various oceans. These cities have been kept well-fed in the process of establishing sustainable agriculture thanks to the Republic's extensive agreements with Synth Foods.

In total, Yuma's total population sits comfortably at just barely under five million, with the majority being citizens of the Crayter Republic. Crayterians from their home sector form a plurality of their citizenry, with a large portion of others having their roots in the IMG, and many freed former slaves who have been naturalized. Additionally, the non-citizen part of this planet's population is made up primarily of refugees from Bretonia with some Libertonian entrepeneurs looking to sell supplies to the nation which has finally secured itself a real home.

1115213.mapped:
The Product is a product of Rogue overambition and avarice. Formerly known as the LNS Magnificent, this ship was crippled during an ill-fated sortie into Cassini. Deemed unsalvagable by her crew, the ship was scuttled by the Liberty Navy. The Rogues dragged the wreckage back to Terra Haute and began to try to restore the ship. In the end, this proved all but impossible, as the Rogues did not have access to either a suitable shipyard, the required parts, nor the design schematics for the ship itself.

Unwilling to let their prize go to waste, the Rogues did what they do best: They improvised. In the end, they managed to seal most hull breeches and install a generator capable of powering almost the entire ship, but the massive engines proved impossible to repair. In essence, the ship has been turned into one giant (and highly effective) weapons platform, which still tends to take more damage from the occasional asteroid impact, then from would-be threats.

1115218.text: A medium sized ice asteroid field orbiting Planet Sausalito. Skheliton Khey is named after an ancient island called Skeleton Key. Ships would be lost as their keels were dashed against sharp rocks around the island, and in the same way, Skheliton Khey can quickly rip ships to pieces. Many of it's asteroids contain a volatile mix of chemicals, which in frozen state are stable, but when ignited by a ship's shield or engine, can send out a crippling shockwave.

1115220.text: The Casey asteroid field is a coagulation of asteroids of various sizes and shapes, all caught in orbit of the sun in the Cassini system. The scattering effects of the nebula reduce sensor range dramatically. Pilots have been known to test their courage by flying through the field at full speed.

1115222.text: The Marshall field is a medium sized ice asteroid field which orbits the sun in the Cassini system. Smaller than the Casey field, it may have broken away from it under the gravitational influence of Planet Sausalito.

1115224.text: A highly localised anomaly. It is emitting intense radiation.

1115233.text: See that guy over there? Man, am I glad he's on our side. Ekky's the Push Damn Button, you know that? Heh, not much to look at, is he, but don't let that fool you.

1115234.text: I first met Ekky about twenty-five years ago back on Alcatraz. He's a nice guy, 'cept when you get in front of his whiskey. Poor fools didn't know what hit them.

1115235.text: Whiskey's nice, don't get me wrong, but some people can take it to an extreme obsession. Case in point: Ekky Z'Bang. Last time someone got in his way, he carved a path through what, three bombers, two fighters, and a cruiser?

1115236.text: Name's Ekky Z'Bang, kid. Pass me that whiskey there, would ya? Did I ever tell ya about the time I was out there with no backup and had to take out a battlecruiser...

1115237.text: Danny White may come across dense or something, but he's smart by half again, if you know what I mean. I think it's the coughing that confuses people. Nobody really knows why he does, 'cept Danny hisself. If you want my opinion, I think it has to do with the duels he's apparently fought.

1115238.text: Heh, Danny never fought any duels that I know of. Might be lung cancer, but I don't think he's ever smoked in his life. If you want anything more concrete, ask him yourself instead of bugging me. Now gimme that whiskey!

1115239.text: Who? The guy that coughs alla time? That's Danny White, Underboss. Don't mess with him, the last few people to try and take his position got messed up bad.

1115240.text: Tox'c waste when *cough* I'as a kid, bucko, *cough* tox'c waste. Nothin' more'n *cough* that. Now go 'way.

1115256.text: Those who don't break server rules never get to this place.

1115257.text: Don't bother trying to stay on that planet at night. Those vines never stop growing and they will climb anything, including your sleeping bag or tent. A couple days ago we had to call someone from the ship to come and cut us out of our temp shelter because the vines had bound the door closed!

1115258.text: Cabin fever is always a problem on these long survey voyages. This ship is pretty big but if you stay on here long enough you feel like you are in a coffin.

1115259.text: The boys thought we lucked out a week ago when we found a jump hole not far from Planet Baja. Turns out that it is unstable, not that it is the one we were looking for anyway. Not once have we seen an IMG ship go near it. To be honest I don't even think they know about it.

1115261.text: If you take a truck east from here and keep on going, you'll eventually hit the largest wasteland on Pecos. You don't want to be stuck out there, trust me on that.

1115262.text: [818 AS] Coronado Pronounced as new Crayter Republic Capital

1115263.text: PECOS -- 818 AS -- The Crayter Republic has suffered greatly in the past year. Although we fought bravely, valiantly and without ceasing, we have lost much. Our families have been torn apart as sons and daughters march to war in the defense of our homes, homes that we now have lost. The Gallic Navy's invasion of Tau-44 will forever be remembered. Yet it is in these troubled times, when we have had to flee to Coronado, that hope springs anew. We can stand united against this tyrannical force, righteous in our fury and steadfast in our resolve. Together, as one nation, we can rebuild and even surpass what we once lost. We are the Crayter Republic and we will not go down without a fight or go quietly into the night!

1115276.mapped:
As the Farmers Alliance raised its profile in Kusari, its leaders and bases were soon the target of frequent Blood Dragon and Golden Chrysanthemum attacks. It became apparent that the organizations had learned of Samura's involvement with the Farmers Alliance, and the general location of their base in Kyushu had never been a true secret. The leader of the Farmers Alliance were in dire need of a more secluded base from where they could coordinate their actions in peace.

Samura's construction project on and in orbit of Planet Miyazaki provided an ideal cover for Samura to help the Farmers Alliance establish a facility in Tottori. It diverted several transports into the nearby asteroid field, then blamed their disappearance on Blood Dragon piracy - and recouped their ""loss"" from their Interspace insurance policy.

Cape Soya was completed in 814 AS. but construction of additional modules continued well into 818 AS. It is the largest station the Alliance possesses, sheltering their leadership and a number of people that either the Alliance or Samura needs to see "disappear" for a while - it is rumored there are both Hogosha and Gaians among these guests. Cape Soya also contains a small drydock for the construction and repair of mid-sized ships, such as the infamous Raba Armored Transport.

Discovered in 810 AS, Planet Miyazaki is the centerpiece (along with Planet Tomioka) of Samura's plans to re-monopolize the Kusari food markets. The planet possesses favourable growing conditions and has shown to support a diverse array of crops, however those wishing to stay upon Miyazaki must endure a lengthy and thoroughly uncomfortable acclimatization period. The newly arrived tend to experience mild to moderate lightheadedness, muscle stiffness, and difficulty with equilibrium throughout the process with symptoms lessening over three weeks. These effects have been attributed to the planet's extremely strong magnetosphere, generated by the unusually large iron concentration within its core.

1115281.text: A dense nebula in Tottori. Scanner efficiency is greatly reduced inside it.

1115283.text: A relatively small field of mostly ice asteroids which most likely broke away from the larger Tojimbo field.

1115287.text: This platform orbits Miyazaki, unload goods off the heavy lifters from the planet, and pack them for transport to the rest of Kusari.

1115288.text: Samura Heavy Industries helped us colonize Planet Miyazaki as well as build this shipping platform. We have reports Synth Foods has built secret biodomes in Tau-65, so our representatives went to Samura and lobbied for more funds. This systems development was paid for with those funds.

1115289.text: I pilot a transport for Samura. My ship comes here three times a week, picking up food and bringing in supplies for the Farmers on Cape Soya.

1115290.text: This base was built as a last line of defense for The Alliance. The constant GC and Blood Dragon attacks on Kagoshima forced our leadership to build this complex. It's loaded with all sorts of top of the line Samura equipment.

1115291.text: The real reason Samura has spent all this money on the Alliance is Planet Miyazaki, we see it as our checkmate in the battle for the Kusari food market.

1115292.text: We know Samura gives us money for their own reasons, but we have our own agenda, which all these wonderful toys from Samura make much easier.

1115293.text: I'll upload the location of Cape Soya into your Neural Net
