1115310.text: Welcome to Manoel. An orange cloud among the blue ones, heh. True, it is a minor base, but it suits its purpose, which is to secure our trade routes into Kusari through Sigma space. The Golden Chrysantemums have been given the coordinates of this station, and they can now buy Cardamine here. Given the mess in Tau space, this route is a bit safer for them. The GMG doesn't like it, but they won't attack the GC.

1115311.text: Eventually, we will try to get a better foothold in Rheinland. The Hessians are the logical choice to partner with, given their conflict with the Corsairs, but they haven't been very receptive to the idea of doing business with us. Their loss, I suppose. The Junkers run a small bit of Cardamine into Rheinland from here, but that is only a trickle. There is a much greater potential customer base.

1115313.text: I just came from Malta with a fresh cargo of Cardamine. We keep this base well-stocked, since we expect a good number of Kusari and eventually, Rheinland customers will be taking their supplies from this base. In addition, our own pilots who need to resupply will do so here. This is our southernmost base in Sigma space.

1115314.text: Without visible landmarks, navigation in this dense region of the Crow can be difficult. The two protostars that form the center of this region help a bit, but even they are too faint to get an accurate bearing. Ships that travel by Jump Hole through this space need special navigational aids, or risk venturing far off course.

1115315.text: We don't usually deliver Cardamine ourselves through Kusari. It is more convenient to let the Golden Chrysantemums do so. They don't have issues with the GMG and Blood Dragons, whereas those groups violently oppose us. Why risk our own pilots when we can have others do the work for us?

1115316.text: I'm not sure if it was that smart to establish a base out here in the Sigmas. Sure, it's easy enough to hide, but it's also easy to get ambushed. This ground favors those who have greater numbers, and sadly, that's not us. We have to keep a lot of our fighters in the vicinity of this base to ensure it's safety.

1115317.text: Individually, our pilots are more than a match for anything they will encounter down here. Cardamine has sharpened our wit and improved our reflexes, well beyond anything the Corsairs or GMG are capable of. But it doesn't make our people invulnerable, especially in those damned explosive gas pockets. Those will tear just about any fighter up.

1115318.text: It is tempting to go and hit the Trade Lanes on occasion. Samura, Republican, Kishiro... even Gallic transports come by there now. Yet we should try and keep a low profile, at least around here, at least until some better defenses have been established. This base isn't even entirely finished yet.

1115319.text: Bah, why did I get sent to this forsaken place. I prefer orange clouds, not blue ones. Guess wooing Don Bernadino's son was a bad career choice on my part. I mean, what's the big deal? I thought the Don would appreciate an expansion of the family - that doesn't happen all that often in Maltan society.

1115320.text: I hate it here, but at least there's plenty of folk to direct my anger onto. Last time I went out, I grazed a couple of the Gas Mining platforms. Strafed a transport that was loading fuel. Lit it up like a small, very short star. Boom! Those Gas Miner transports have pitiful armor.

1115321.text: Yes, we know the Corsairs have established themselves somewhere in the south. We're not concerned with that. They do what they always do - shoot everyone and everything in their sights. Their presence is convenient actually - it makes them the biggest threat in the system. Which means we'll be largely left alone here.

1115322.text: I am here to pick up a load of Cardamine, then I will head for our base in Shikoku. It is a long journey, but away from the Trade Lanes, we have few enemies. Only the Hogosha pursue us there, and sometimes the Farmers Alliance will attack us too, but they are more after their own interests. We can sell part of our Cardamine supply to the Junkers and Liberty Rogues, and make some credits for our cause that way.

1115323.text: Some people are scared by the alterations Cardamine makes to the body. But are our bodies not as books, for us to rewrite as we would seek to? Through the orange mist, our lives will be long, and our families smaller. I made my choice in this, and I am proud to offer others the same choice.

1115324.text: Sadly, we cannot offer our Outcast allies as warm a welcome in Kusari as they offer us, here. The Blood Dragons, Hogosha and the military forces all hunt them relentlessly. It falls to us to deliver their Cardamine to those who would wish it. In turn, we try to offer the Outcasts what products Kusari has to offer. We take that which we are denied to earn, by force, if need be.

1115325.text: Scuttlebutt has it that both the sons of the Hispania have set up shop in yon cloud. Ohh boy, there's going to be some fireworks here, yes sir. Between the GMG, the Outcasts, the Corsairs and all their respective allies, we got ourselves a real powderkeg. Suppose that's going to drive up the demand for spare Hull Panels and Engine Components.

1115326.text: Those halfwit Gas Miners figured that muscling us out of the Yanagi Depot would be the end of us here. Tch. All they did was multiply their foes. Hope they'll be happy with the result, heh. Sure, the Cardamine route through this system is a bit longer now, down over Frankfurt, and Berlin afterward, but that's not much of a problem. This entire damned system is one big hiding hole.

1115327.text: There ain't a big demand for Cardamine in Rheinland, but what demand there is, we cater to. Always a few wealthy snobs on either Berlin or Baden-Baden who want a taste of the orange. Heck, we even make an occasional run to Stuttgart. Word has it a few of the Synth Foods higherups are hooked.

1115329.text: According to researchers, the asteroids of the Makassar field are most likely remnants of a rocky moon destroyed by an asteroid impact millions of years ago.

1115331.text: You won't find very much to drink here my friend. Our shipments of wine have still to arrive. All we have is this muck the Colonials left behind.

1115334.text: I have heard that the campaign is going well. No doubt our navy is crushing those Bretonian dogs. Do away with the lot I say, fewer Bretonians around means more room for us.

1115335.text: This station is a wreck. The Colonials hadn't even finished restoring it when we liberated the system. Bastards set charges on the station and blew half of it to pieces. They didn't realise that we already had civilians onboard when their bombs went off. I lost a good friend in it all. Those bastards just ran and hide. They'll pay.

1115336.text: We know the Independent Miners used to work closely with those Colonials. It would not surprise me if some of them still do. We'll be keeping a close eye on them, if they step out of line it will give the Crown yet one more reason to evict those rock rats as well.

1115337.text: Most of our supplies are still enroute. The campaign has slowed down our transports and the continuing attacks by the Outcasts and Colonials aren't helping either. If we don't strengthen our convoys, we might soon find ourselves losing critical supplies.

1115338.text: I was out near Java, blasting some Outcast folk when along comes a shiney Gallic convoy. I took no interest in it of course, not my thing. The Colonials that appeared certainly did though. Tore through the transports like a pack of wolves, was beautiful. Right up until a stray couple of mines blew me outta the water. Navy folk came along soon enough, picked up the survivors. Luckily, my co-pilot convinced em to pick us up and they brought us here. Now I just need a new ship. Don't suppose you got a spare one?

1115339.text: Idiot. That's what he is. We had done our job and were about to clear outta there. Nope, he insists we sit and watch some stupid convoy getting shot up. Then he wonders how we might suddenly find ourselves floating with no engines and failing life support. Even when the Navy came along he thought all was well. Idiot doesn't know I had to flash one of the pilots over the comms just to get us a lift here!

1115340.text: I got shipped out here a week ago. I haven't received my assigment yet, so I'm stuck waiting. At least I've got a friend onboard here who I can pass the time with.

1115341.text: Yes, we're quite a distance from the front. The Oblique sits at the Kusari flank, and this system is relatively quiet now that the Crayter Republic is surpressed. Since we're so remote, the Crown doesn't seem to be too concerned with fully exploring this system.

1115342.text: Aside from the occasional Outcast raids, we've also encountered what appear to be Kusari criminals. Most likely there are more jumpholes somewhere in the east of the system. No matter, a few pirates are no match for the Gallic Navy

1115343.text: All kinds of alcohol here. Even some of that Gallic wine. Unlike the other stations, we don't need to rely on Gallic supply convoys. Our usual flow of goods has continued without trouble, even the Outcasts aren't causing us much bother.

1115344.text: Gallia may control the tau's but that won't stop Gateway getting where we need to be. I'm here to assess the situation in the tau's and keep my superiors up to date.

1115345.text: Heading down to the planet? Be careful, I hear they've had a bit of trouble with the shuttles. Seems the lack of spare parts is leaving a few of them dangerous. Shuttle parts aren't exactly the highest priority in the supply convoys so they don't tend to take too many of them. When a convoy carrying them gets hit, you might not get any parts for another week or more.

1115346.text: Interesting planet down there. Pretty easy to colonize and the native life should be good make good foodstuff. Only problem is the amount of water. While we could pretty easily build over the water, it costs a hell of a lot more.

1115347.text: If you are looking to head down to the planet surface, you'll need a permit. You can get one from the Navy's office down the corridor from here. Don't expect to be heading down instantly though, there's a waiting time. Shuttles had to be taken off active duty so we're a bit tight on transportation.

1115348.text: This station is pretty well built. It looks like it housed a good chunk of the Colonial's spaceborne population so it needed to be well kept. From what we can tell, they were preparing for a limited move down to Borneo itself. I can imagine the logistical nightmare that would've been. I'm having enough trouble keeping track of all the supplies that come into the station, some figures just aren't adding up.

1115349.text: This used to be a large civilian station, and as such, has large habitation areas and big cargo bays. Minato could have served as a forward command center for the attack on Kusari, but those orders never came. It's a lot bigger than we need it to be, so we only inhabit a part of it. IDF Shipping makes use of the cargo bays, and the GMS boys have gotten a derelict smelter operational already.

1115350.text: We found out that some of the technologies employed here are quite useful and adopted them. There was a functional smelter still attached to the station, which I imagine was too big for those Colonials to move. We've put it to good use, smelting Beryllium mined in Tau-23 down before shipping it back to the Core Worlds.

1115351.text: Because the installation is so far off, we don't get as much action as Sulawesi. We've got problems of our own nevertheless - the nebula is taking someone away every so often. We never know what happens with those we lose contact with and we don't have enough ships to investigate a nebula of that size.

1115352.text: I run the route from here back to the Core Worlds. From Minato to Sulawesi, then past Java to the Guillestre, and then into Languedoc. The stretch between Sulawesi and Java is very dangerous, and often the Navy can't spare more than a small escort.

1115353.text: I've been going over what was left of the stations computer archives. Only a few scraps of data were left, but some of the folk here were pretty supersticious from the sound of it. There's references to a "dark ghost" of some sort, and things called Zephyrs and Hydras. Silly Sirians, no?

1115354.text: The Colonials made an effort to leave as little behind as possible. It surprises me that they did not scuttle this entire station. It makes me suspect that they plan to come back some day. I think our commanders have the same thought, which is why Oblique is here and not in Tau-31.

1115355.text: As far as resources go this system is pretty barren. Certainly, there's plenty of water in those ice asteroids, but it requires purification. The other planets in the system are either dangerous or devoid of resources. Borneo might be interesting, if we can get a survey party down some day. When will they fix those blasted shuttles?

1115356.text: The Independent Miners are a strange bunch. Our company offered to take them into the fold, but they refused! Do they truly believe that they have a better future going at it alone, rather then have our glorious company behind them? Inconceivable!

1115357.text: Ah, a new guest! Well sit down, what are you waiting for... Now what's your poison, hm? Ambrosia perhaps? A Sidewinder Fang? Yamaguchi Nova? Kraken Surprise? Black Hole Hook? We've got it all! The bigger the punch, the better the pleasure, so make your pick!

1115358.text: See those uniformed types sitting around here? Those are Colonial Fleet. All business, most of the time. Agressive too. Be careful what you say to those types, they're trained to be paranoid. Don't want you getting thrown out of the airlock for something you formulated badly. Why the worried face, I'm just pulling your leg. Seriously, man, lighten up!

1115359.text: The carrier has such a poetic name, doesn't it? "The Underworld". There's nothing poetic about it's main use though. Rocks rocks and more rocks, kind of numbs the brain you know? Rear end of the world if you ask me. But it is what we call home. And we won't let it go without a fight!

1115360.text: Oh? I remember them arriving here first. Those strange ships... completely unlike any we've seen, though they did resemble the pictures of the old sleeper ships. Well... Can't say that was unwelcome - they paid in gold for the whole system's development. I just get some of that funny-tasting tobacco-like stuff here.

1115361.text: That nebula? Wouldn't go there if I were you. There's something real spooky inside... Whatever it is - it already took a few of my colleagues. And I'm not intending to join them.

1115362.text: That's right, but I was born on New Berlin. Well... there aren't many left alive who can say they saw the exodus first-hand. Anyways, it was about some sort of cosmic prank on us, back in the Crayter sector. Kinda like in some lame holovid, but it ended up with countless people vaporized. Luckily some of us escaped in the sleeper ships we got to Crayter with in the first place. It was a thorny path for all of us, I can tell you that.

1115363.text: The first people we contacted were the Zoners in Omega-3. They helped us out, and pointed to some more... Civilized space. First order of business was to find some solid ground to live on. Some left the fleet and settled among the sirians, some stayed and made a deal with Planetform. They were supposed to get us some place to live on, but in the end it turned out to be a lie... So we eventually got to where we are now. Those who left the fleet returned after being alienated by House societies. Many of them are surely still be out there..

1115364.text: I hear most of our people have made it safely to one of the Independent Worlds south of the Taus. No, I've not seen them since the exodus, but it's good to know they're allright. I had a lot of friends on Minato.

1115370.text: Welcome to the Oblique monsieur. I'm afraid our stocks are somewhat depleted. The last supply run did not arrive on schedule, and we're not expecting the next one until tomorrow.

1115385.text: The Hades is the last Colonial asset that remains in the Tau worlds. After the loss of Tau-44 it was clear that directly engaging the Gallic forces would be suicidal - we simply don't have the numbers to defeat them conventionally. Our tactic is geared around fast precision strikes against their supply ships. Hopefully the Bretonian forces will be able to take them headon if we weaken them enough here.

1115386.text: The IMG miners have no love for these Gallics, but they're, pardon the pun, caught between a rock and a hard place. If they'd opposed them, they'd have fared no better than us. Still, they do what they can. For instance, they supply us with Food, Water and Oxygen on the carrier, and some basic materials needed to maintain damaged fighters.

1115388.text:
CLASS: Zephyr
CREW: CLASSIFIED
ARMAMENT: CLASSIFIED
1115388.mapped: The Zephyr class carrier Hades has seen action in nearly every major engagement the Crayter Republic has been involved in within the Barrier Theater since the start of the Gallic war. Instrumental in the reclaimation of Tau-44, raids against the Outcasts in the northern Omicrons, and the spearhead of Operation Ice Lance within Tau-31, the Hades stood watch over the Holman Junction following the Crayter Republic's victory in the system. Following the invasion of Gallia by Kusari, the Hades withdrew to the Tau-44 system, where it is currently regrouping and awaiting its next set of orders.

1115389.text: The Zephyr class carrier Hades has seen action in nearly every major engagement the Crayter Republic has been involved in within the Barrier Theater since the start of the Gallic war. Instrumental in the reclaimation of Tau-44, raids against the Outcasts in the northern Omicrons, and the spearhead of Operation Ice Lance within Tau-31, the Hades stood watch over the Holman Junction following the Crayter Republic's victory in the system. Following the invasion of Gallia by Kusari, the Hades withdrew to the Tau-44 system, where it is currently regrouping and awaiting its next set of orders.

1115391.text: The Hera was sent to the Tau-23 system as an addition to the Colonial Zephyr Hades. Hera's mission in Tau-23 is to guard the Jump Hole leading to Colonial System.

1115393.text: Apollo is also one of the guardians to the Tau-44 system. The Hydra vessel was assigned to protect the Jump Hole against any intruders to the system and to serve as a warning beacon to the Colonial Forces in Tau-44.

1115395.text: Like the IMG miners, we know these systems well. Unlike the miners, we're not bound by some kind of forced neutrality, so we're hitting those Gallic invaders where it hurts the most. Especially supply ships going to that battleship of theirs in Tau-44 are priority targets.

1115396.text: We had such high hopes to be able to establish ourselves on Borneo. Granted, it's not an ideal planet, but it is a hell of a lot better than living out in space. Our nation hasn't had the best of luck in Sirius. I wonder why.

1115401.text: Eventually, we'll make these Gallic interlopers pay for what they've done. Their king demanded subjugation, which we equate to slavery. We are a democracy, and we won't bow down to anyone. We choose our own destiny.

1115403.text: The Crayter Republic needed power for their factories and their ships. The best source of power inside the system are the two suns. The Republic applied a method that they used in the Crayter sector.Huge power plants were build in space at a safe distance from the suns so that the installation won't get damaged by the solar winds.The construction of the energy collector site lasted several years,being finished in the 817 AS The station now provide powercells that power the entire nation.

1115405.text: This is quite the pleasant gig, I can tell you that. I don't work that much, that's the top perk, hehe. The pay isn't anything spectacular, but at least I earn more than the bartender.

1115406.text: Let me give you a piece of advice, stranger. Whatever you do, don't venture too far south from here. Why, you ask? I'll tell you why, because you might get blown to smithereens! Seriously, there's an Outcast base somewhere down there, and they can be pretty nasty customers, I can tell you that. Unless you got a good escort, steer clear of them.

1115407.text: Oh my god, I am so tired... I've just spent nine hours straight on my mining shift in a field a bit off from the station, only to have a band of pirates take all of my cargo. I'm going to have to be smarter and hire an escort next time. At least I got out with my life.

1115409.text: We've been fighting the Outcasts ever since we came into this region. We'd have been happy to coexist, but they forced the issue. Ever since we've been growing closer to the Independent Miners, who have also ran afoul of those savages.

1115410.text: I do not like having to hide in this nebula, but must admit it's the wisest course of action. The Hades is a fine carrier, but no match for one of those massive Gallic battleships. Acting in the open would also endanger the miner bases elsewhere in the Taus, and since they're supplying this carrier, that would be shooting ourselves in the foot.

1115411.text: The loss of Tau-44 has been a blow for us in more than one way. Just when our people got back on their feet, the rug gets swept out from under us. We lost our established industries, at least those that couldn't be evacuated. But we won't give up, ever. It'll take wiping us out to the last man, woman and child for that to happen.

1115412.text: Passing my training at the Academy without any major hitch is one of the hardest, craziest things I've pulled off in all my life. Blood, sweat and tears all the way, and it hasn't changed much now in the service either. But don't get me wrong, I wouldn't give what I have for anything in the world. Pride, respect, always having someone covering your back, and most of all, family. That's what the Fleet's become to me.

1115413.text: You've got a firm stance about you, you know that? We could use someone like you in one of our Nyxes, eh? We can never have too many capable men and women on our side. Tell you what, here's a recruitment brochure, study it a bit, and send an application to the Flight Academy. You seem like proper military material, though passing muster ain't no picnic, I can tell you that. But I'm sure someone like you can pull it off, and tell you what, I'll even support your enrollment.

1115414.text: Eh, I'm pretty tired, I can tell you that. Could you believe that I've served in the military for twenty years... Well better believe it. Getting out of my second ten year contract in five more months. Sweet retirement, you bet. 'Though if our war with the Gauls isn't done by then, I might stay on a while longer. The Fleet needs veterans.

1115416.text: Hey there, here is an advice for you.You see, we produce a lot of Niobium here, practically throwing it away by the shovel, it's pretty cheap.Buy low, sell high. Just haul it somewhere down below, Rheinland for example, is one of the best places in Sirius for exporting it.Just be careful not to get robbed by many of the pirate groups that infest the roads. Better safe than sorry, so hire an escort squadron.

1115417.text: I'm a hauler. Kind of proud to say this, just saved enough money to purchase a fifty percent share in the ownership of the Atlas I'm the captain of. That means more money, and more freedom for me. CMI still has my contract, but this way I'm at least partly working for myself. And it's a comfortable gig, I can tell you that. A bit risky though, so keep it frosty out there if you're in the business.

1115418.text: If you're mining out there, always keep an eye on the asteroids, and another one on your radar. Can't tell you how many times you could end up badly if you get caught off guard by pirates. I even heard that an occasional BMM ship flies by, hoping to catch one of us off guard and rid the IMG of another mining ship. Bullies...

1115420.text: The Outcasts are always around these parts. The 44th tries to fight them back, but they can't be everywhere, so be careful.

1115424.text: This is a nice place, I can tell you that. A bit away from civilization, good to lay low. That's why you should keep an eye out for dangerous types around here. Despite the military presence around here, there's always some shady dealings in dark corners. But maybe that's why you came here.Just don't spread the word around too eagerly.

1115425.text: I'm one of the Zoner minority around here, by the way. Name's Hilliard, Hilliard Annidon. Anyways, what I was going to say is, these Colonials are good people. Open to all sorts of guests, as long as you're not looking for trouble. I mostly earn good credits selling them food and water from Freeport 10. It's a low risk, medium pay situation. Perfect for a lazy sod like me.

1115468.mapped:
Galveston Outpost was originally constructed in 826 A.S. as a listening post and supply depot for Separatist forces. Concealed in the West Dallas Debris Field and made largely out of locally salvaged materials, Galveston remains well hidden from any attackers. Raids on LPI operations were frequently conducted from the station, often in support of Xeno operations.

In 827, the Separatists were forced out of the Bering system by the siege of Marshall Station. The Liberty Navy doggedly pursued retreating Separatists, with the intent of permanently crippling the movement. A timely counterattack by joint Separatist and Hellfire Legion forces enabled a successful evacuation, but at a terrible cost to both organisations.

After reorganising into the Insurgency, Galveston Outpost was repurposed as the Insurgency's operational hub for Texas and the surrounding systems. Strikes against LPI operations have resumed, with the Insurgency desperately seeking to win minor victories in order to rehabilitate their severely tarnished image. It was hoped that this would spur on the enlistments that are sorely needed to replenish their diminished ranks.

When the Liberty Insurgency was defeated in Kansas and Vespucci in 829 AS, the remaining garrison decided to abandon and scuttle the station as it was only a matter of time before the Liberty Navy found out about Galveston. Approximately two weeks after the station was quietly scuttled, the Liberty Rogues arrived with the destroyer Drunken Codger and stripped the station of all valuable equipment.

It is not known exactly how the Liberty Rogues learned of Galveston's location, but it is likely that a small group of original crew members gave up the station's location in exchange for a new life.

1115471.text: Commonly known as "The Devil's Golf Course" by the Xenos, this asteroid field contains no known usable resources. However, the high density of the rocks makes it perfect for defending the field against larger, less maneuverable vessels. This, along with the presence of very large asteroids in the field, are among the reasons that the Xenos chose it for the site of Refugio Base.

1115473.text: Commonly known as 'Lake Manly' by the Xenos, this field is the Xenos' primary source of Water. Some of the water is mined directly by small freighters, but the great majority is collected at Gonzales Station and transferred to Refugio for further processing into the drinking water, oxygen, and fuel that the Xenos need to survive.

1115475.text: The wreck of a Junker CSV that wandered into the system. The pilot appears to have been Dana McLaughlin. No need to guess how it got destroyed...

1115477.text:
This is the wreck of a Liberty Navy fighter that was escorting the LNS Alabama. The pilot looks to have been Cmdr. Sarah Fitzgerald. It no longer appears to be in working order.

The Xeno Guard might have been involved.

1115484.text: ALAMO -- Encouraged by the recent success that the Mollys in Bretonia have had in getting the Government there to come to the table and talk terms. The Xenos have stepped up their attacks on targets throughout Liberty in the hope of provoking a similar response from the Liberty Government. "We know they are hurting" a spokesman for the Xenos said recently, "For every 3 ships that make it into Liberty, they are losing at least one". The Xenos attacks have recently become Liberty-wide, indicating a degree of organization higher than what was originally believed, Liberty forces, while coping for now are finding themselves increasingly stretched thin by the constant harassment.

1115485.text: [816 AS] A Problem of Cash Flow

1115486.text: ALAMO -- Money has always been a problem for the Xenos. A grass roots organization made up of mostly disgruntled lower class workers and their families, the Xenos have never had much of a cash reserve to call upon. Raiding supplements their income, through the sale of stolen parts and commodities, as well as plundering the last remains of silver from the silver fields of Colorado. It is rumoured that they may also have a number of secret beneficiaries within the upper classes of Liberty itself who donate funds and support to the group. Though this has never been proven and no one has ever been formally charged in this area.

1115488.text: ALAMO -- Xenos have no shortage of manpower. As the number of dissatisfied workers in Liberty grows owing to the Governments economic policies there, so to do ranks of the Xenos. Their brand of simple politics and nationalism is an attractive drawcard for many among the millions of bitter and angry out of work people of Liberty. The prison stations of Texas also provide a reservoir of hardened recruits, where the Xenos are aided by insiders in the LPI itself, who are always eager to make a quick buck under the table.

1115490.text: ALAMO -- Or do they? Recent reports have indicated a level of tolerance shown to some non-Liberty factions from the Xenos themselves. Particularly the Zoners and the IMG. Speculation about possible attempts at real diplomacy from the Xenos might be premature however, as indicated in comments made during a recent Xeno pirate radio broadcast in New York. "We don't need anyone else in Liberty" the speaker said, "We look after our own. We won't go trashing through someone else's backyard, but we don't welcome others coming and trashing through ours".

1115492.text: ALAMO -- The desperate Liberty citizens that join the Xenos bring with them a multitude of skills and abilities. Ranging from technicians to Doctors, Priests to labourers there is no shortage of ability within the ranks. "It's not technical skill we lack" said a Xeno spokesman, "That we have plenty of, if your ship is damaged, we have ample people who can fix it, it's the parts to fix it with that we sometimes lack".\n\nThe fickle nature of supply and the deep pool of talent has made the Xenos skilled improvisers and well versed in "making do". Skills which will be needed if they ever hope to achieve their political aims in the face of the stiff and determined resistance from the Liberty military.

1115493.text: This base used to belong to DSE, until we took it and drove them from the system. Someday, Death Valley's going to guarantee us our future after we've won the war against the corrupt Liberty government and their Corporate masters.

1115494.text: This base used to belong to DSE, until we took it and drove them from the system. Someday, Death Valley's going to guarantee us our future after we've won the war against the corrupt Liberty government and their Corporate masters.

1115495.text: I sure do miss Denver. I left for Ouray on my 20th and havn't been back since. My family live well here on Refugio, but you know, it isn't the same as Denver.

1115496.text: Well, if you've been with us for a while you'll notice we've just got some ships here on Alamo and over on Refugio. We sealed a deal with the Zoners and a few independent ship dealers. Saves a lot of our precious credits in the long run.

1115497.text: Since we "evicted" DSE from the Alamo, this has been the main supply and equipment base for the Xeno Guard. I think you'll notice that our best equipment is available here.

1115498.text: Too bad we can't get some more Synth Mary Jane in here. That's the only thing I like about Barrow. Unfortunately, making cargo runs from Barrow to here is dangerous, and many of our shipments don't make it.

1115499.text: I wouldn't fly into New York if I were you, it's suicide. I hear that the Navy sends out a half-dozen capital ships at the sight of a single Xeno there. Heh, it's nice to be feared.

1115500.text: Not too long ago, myself and a Guard Wing repelled a Junker raiding party that came through the Kepler Hole. Those idiots thought they could raid us with four ships. I think we taught them a lesson.

1115501.text: When we get caught, the LPI just keep throwing us in Huntsville. I figure they would've learned that all that accomplishes is us recruiting new Xenos. Still, nobody expects the donut munchers to be smart.

1115502.text: Did you see the Alabama on the way in? We're rather proud of that catch. After the Navy lost it, they've kept their noses out of this system. We've thought about repairing it, but a Dreadnought is a bit beyond our skills and resources to operate.

1115503.text: Enjoying that drink? No? Well, that would be the fault of the boys over in Nome. They told us they hijacked an entire shipment of alcohol, so we told them to send it over. What they failed to mention was that it was all Liberty Ale. I'm going to smack their cargo master next time I'm over there.

1115504.text: In years past we relied on the Zoners for most of our food, water and good times breathing needs. But with the surpluses provided by Refugio we're more than self sufficient. Though we still need to retrieve some specialty supplies, such as pharmaceuticals, from the Mining guild on Freeport 4.

1115505.text: Richard York, Captain of the Prospector and leader of the Sons of Liberty's no small legend amongst the Xenos. I'll bet them navy boys get a turn of their guts when that blip on their scopes turns out to be that gunboat of his! We used to mark the kills on the side of her hull, but we ran outa space ages ago!

1115506.text: Leo Mathews is one of our native sons, born a Xeno of a family that these bases of ours was built around! The Mathews have been at the heart of the movement since the first layoffs back in 600 AS Rumor has it that the first Xeno to gun down an LPI officer was a Mathews, but who's to say?

1115507.text: Hey, you been to mid-level kitchens? They may look like a dump, but Joe serves good food! Say I sent you and he'll give you a bottle of the good stuff.

1115508.text: We're really proud of the city we've built here at Refugio. Most of our families live here, well away from the front lines.

1115509.text: I don't know where everyone gets the idea that we want to take over the Cardamine trade here in Liberty. True, we fight the Junkers because of their role in it, but not because we want it. We want to stop it. It's one of the biggest corrupting factors in Liberty, and it's rotting the core of Liberty's soul, and destroying it's workers.

1115510.text: Have you ever seen a Bounty Hunter in '45? I thought not. Wonder why? Scan one of our very own system guard next time ya see one, and you'll see why. I'm telling you -that- is power.

1115511.text: Heh, me and some 'o the lads had some fun with a Junker the night before last. She got lost and wandered into Kepler, so we herded her to '45 and listened to her squeal all night long! Haw haw! If ya look real carful, ya might find her ship. Somewhere in the asteroid field surrounding us.

1115512.text: If yer in a fix and you're gonna get caught, get caught by the LPI. Bounty Hunters will like as not put a bullet in your head, but the LPI needs to keep Huntsville producing. Remember, for every live Xeno that goes into Huntsvillve, three come out.

1115513.text: Despite the clamoring that we should seek ties with those other 'unlawful' faction within Liberty, the pirating Rogues and slave trading Junkers, the only groups with whom we have any accord are the Zoners, IMG and The Order. The Zoners are, well, the Zoners. But the IMG are almost like brothers in their struggle and The Order represents a righteousness and sense of justice that Liberty desperately needs to see return. That's why we remain neutral with both groups.

1115514.text: You think we'll ever complete our goals? I don't think we will in the near future, but we will suceed! Foregin companies can only take so many losses!

1115515.text: I sure like Barrow, but it it's mighty small and the lads over there speak kinda funny. A 'lil like this 'ere boy! Heheh, they crack me up.

1115516.text: Say again, which base did you say you come from? Was it Ouray in Colorado? Or Nome in Kepler? Heh, of course not, damn my drink addled mind, Barrow in Hudson right? No? I give up...

1115517.text: Whoa, I'm telling you, don't mess with the Zoners. One of mah buddies jumped a Zoner Dromedray and they weren't best pleased. Some sort of Zoner heavy fighter gave him a visit and showed him the error of his ways.

1115518.text: Hell we had a few Bounty Hunters crash through the Kepler hole a few days back, musta gotten mighty lost. We took em out just before they could transmit Refugio's location. Remember, a dead 'Hunter is a good 'Hunter.

1115519.text: Heh, it sure can get warm down by the hangers. If you want a warm room bed down over there, if you like a bit 'o nip to the nights, the upper levels away from the generators'd be a good choice.

1115520.text: Our opperations in New York were based mainly around Detroit base where we would lift side arms, but now we've redirected some of our forces to grab mining convoys heading to Pittsburgh. We've caught the LPI a little unprepared on that side. They don't know what we want them for.

1115521.text: We won this place from the DSE a fair while ago. In that time maintanence has got a little bit scetchy. If you see any signs like, well, radiation, variable gravity, electricity, poisonous gases, vaccum or explosives just stay away. Please?

1115522.text: Things can get loney out here away from any other Xenos. We run on a skeleton crew and the only fresh contact we get is the occasional freighter from Refugio.

1115523.text: Gotta love the scenery here. Ice and water as far as the eye can see. At least the drinks are cheap. I just wish it wasn't that Liberty Ale garbage that the Alamo boys sent over.

1115524.text: The Kushan Freighter might be an ugly box, but if you put the right guns on it, it's the perfect tool for interdiciting trade and carrying off plenty of captured goods.

1115525.text: The Blazer is the traditional ship of the training wing. With decent armor, huge size, no CD and abhorrently underpowered guns you'll be guaranteed a lifestyle of learning how to be sneaky, avoiding fights you can't win and group think mentality.

1115526.text: The Hawk's got some moves, looks darn sleek, can mount a CD all in a package that's still incapable of actually doing any lasting damage to anything that can actually defend itself for a darn. It can, however, put the hurt on some lower level vessels and is ideal for those Xenos looking to punch the ticket of smarmy junkers and other ne'er-do-wells on a budget.

1115545.text: A large field of ice asteroids similar to those found in the Omicron Delta system. Largely unexplored, the Deshret Cloud holds many wonders of the Omicron Mu system. Initial reports show medium to low levels of Iridium.

1115547.text: Very little has been discovered about this anomalous cloud. Patrol wings occasionally report comm signals emanating from the cloud's depths, as if hearing distant speech in an unknown language, but these signals have not been successfully recorded. So far, nothing exceptional has been definitively recorded regarding the cloud. However, energy readings suggest past massive scale weapons usage, or an ion explosion. After securely establishing operations on Planet Akabat, Order High Command plans to form a research expedition to study the cloud further.

1115549.text:

The minefield around Omicron Minor minefield had been placed by the Order to control traffic and protect the system from unwanted intrusions. The Order keeps the Minefield under constant surveillance and unauthorized ships attempting to enter or leave would be hard-pressed indeed to survive.

1115552.text: A damaged depot once serving as a makeshift installation to support Toledo survivors. Built upon the core of an listening outpost constructed by The Order to explore Omicron Mu beforehand, a drydock was delegated to repair and maintain the Thebes dreadnought. Since completion of that task, the station was shut down and salvaged for equipment aboard. Most of its hull has been rendered beyond use due to extensive Nomad attacks over the years, including docking amenities.

1115562.text: Planet Braillia is the main settlement of those who wish to join the Reapers' cause. All non-military personnel such as families of combatants and public officials reside here, making this a lightly defended area in the Cayman system. All structures and colonies are constructed underground due to the Aftermath of operation "Safe Haven". The project's main purpose was to spread cardamine throughout the Planets Atmosphere by using a mixture of Thermonuclear devices and liquid Cardamine. Although once a beautiful and scenic world it is now uninhabitable and filled with gamma radiation until the planet can be properly terraformed to suit the climate.

1115564.text: The Cayman Field is a cluster of asteroids trapped within the Flare nebula. The heat of the contracting nebula is causing the asteroids to melt and deform. While it is likely that some of the asteroids contain valuable minerals, the extreme heat inside the Flare prevents all mining.

1115569.text:
CLASS: Ranseur
CREW: CLASSIFIED
ARMAMENT: CLASSIFIED

The Battleship Fuen Lebrada is commanded by Adalberto Alarico, a former Maltese Captain. The Fuen Lebrada has seen many battles in the time since it was built eight years prior to the settlement of Cayman. The former captain Lorenzo Montoya was killed when the bridge was struck during one of the many battles in Omicron Eta over two years ago. The key role the Reapers played during the Eta battles resulted in them being rewarded this ship as a symbol of power. The ship played a key role in the Reaper exodus from the Omicrons, and their subsequent settling in Cayman.

1115570.text: Greetings my friend. If you have some time to stay on this base, why don't you speak to some of my subordinates? You could learn much about us and maybe yourself if you do.

1115571.text: We Reapers came here a long time ago in search of a new home. How were we expected to find the Solan colonists here? I cannot really complain, as it makes me happy knowing we were not the only ones left. Enough of my babble though, I'm sure you have things to do my friend, my apologies for holding you up.

1115572.text: Greetings my friend, I am Lohingren Hikari Rala'state, leader of the Reapers. I bet you are wondering why such a highly prestigious individual would leave himself so wide in the open, when half of this area wants his head on a plate. Well, even the higher ups have to unwind every now and then.

1115573.text: We Reapers, or "Angels" as we were named then, were quite the quiet bunch before we joined the Outcasts, with quite a few more of us than there are now. Unfortunately for us, survival is a priority and we joined the Outcasts to ensure the survival of our 'organization'. Our relationship quickly soured as the Outcasts, regrettably, do not share our goal of an end to war. So here we are now my friend, fighting to stabilise this screwed sector of space. All in the name of peace.

1115574.text: Ah, it's you again. You seem to be rather interested in hearing about us. Come then, I shall tell you about our enemies, these Coalition dogs. A remnant of theirs managed to destroy our one and only settlement once, it was a blood bath unfortunately. Most of the "Angels" were laid to rest that day. Only three, sorry, four of us remain now, but alas, the moral of the story my friend is this: The Coalition are a failed part of humanity who no longer have a right to exist in the world to come. Of course, I am sure you don't want to hear all this, my friend, I shall let you go now.

1115575.text: Ha! Look at you right there staring at me like a fool! What, ain't you seen a handsome old man such as I before? I bet you didn't know I was sixty, eh?! Aanyway since your here, you're gonna listen to what I have to say. Got it? Good.

1115576.text: So, since you're standing there gawking at me like a buffoon, I shall tell you about the Reapers' Knights, Skull Squadron. They are the Archon's personal guard and do-gooders. Although you would not think it, I am the General of such a prestigious squadron, where only the finest and most loyal become one of Lohingren's Guard. If you see them escorting the Archon my friend, you had best hurry away. They do not take kindly to strangers getting to close to him.

1115577.text: Are you still here, eh? I ain't getting any younger or any prettier here you know my son! Oh well since you're here, you're gonna listen and listen good, got it? Good. The Archon works in mysterious ways, you might not know it but a sensitive chap he is. All he wants to do is see our glorious little species in this odorous little pump in the galaxy thrive and flourish. When the time comes and the Reapers rise my friend, you would be wise to listen to him, you may learn something. Now be gone, you're making me look bad in front of the senoritas.

1115578.text:
Oh for all that is beautiful and holy, it's you again! Do you enjoy tormenting a beautiful old man such as I? Fine, fine have it your way, I will tell you the glorious tale of the "Angels". Once upon a time there was a great warrior, his name was Gabriel. Gabriel fought without ever thinking twice for his kind, the "Great Alliance". Then came a horrible, nasty enemy known as "The Coalition". After many years of fighting a war for the Alliance, it became stale, pointless, full of bickering and strife, all for nothing. Gabriel began to doubt his King and began to wonder what his true purpose was. So to seek out this answer, he left, taking the group of one hundred men and women with him.

After many years, Gabriel and his men flourished. Weeks, months, years, centuries past and the legacy that was passed on by him and his men were still thriving amongst the vast lands and wilderness, until one day. The evil Coalition arrived and slaughtered the people who upheld Gabriel's legacy. Now the few survivors of that legacy fight the evil Coalition and try to bring peace to this region. Ha! This a nice story no? But anyway you bore me now, be gone, and if you stop by on Braillia, tell that pompous buffoon Juan that I'm going to shove a torpedo up his engine next time I see him!

1115579.text: Ah Sir, it is a pleasure to meet you. I am Allesia Rommer, from the Maltese News Service. Or at least I was until I followed this bunch here to this base. Why did I do that you ask? Well... the chance to find out everything about this little group is a reporter's dream! If you wish to know anything about them please do ask, I wouldn't mind giving out some info.

1115580.text: So it's you again, okay then I can give you some info about this lot. Don't worry: they give out about everything they know, not much secrecy about them at all when it comes to this stuff. Anyway, I'll stop rambling. It's commonly believed the Reapers betrayed the Outcasts and are trying to forcefully take over the Omicrons and Omegas. This simply could not be more wrong. They truly do wish to join this part of Sirius together for some "Greater Battle", still to come. Although I don't know much about this "Greater Battle" they speak of.

1115581.text: Even I don't know why the Reapers attacked the Red Hessian Army that day, something about securing a convoy of some kind. I really don't know what the deal with that was. Watching these people in action has shown me not to assume anything about anyone.

1115582.text: Hello again. It seems you like to hear about this lot, or maybe you're just curious. Oh well, no matter I suppose. You see the main goal right now of the Reapers is to eradicate The Coalition and to stabilise this part of Sirius. But that's no small task considering this is the most dangerous sector within Sirius, what with the blood feud between the Corsairs and Outcasts, with the Hessian's moving in and the Bounty Hunters and Order squabbling for power in the outer rim, they have quite the task ahead of them I would say. Still though, I'd like to see it with my own eyes.

1115583.text: Hey you, you one of the new recruits? If you are, you better get to the training area right now or I am gonna eat your damn soul for breakfast, understand?!

1115584.text: You still standing there?! Wait, you better be an outsider if you're not wearing a uniform! Well move along swiftly, bub, I got myself a ton of fresh nuggets in the hanger bay with my name written on 'em. What shall I teach them today...? Oh yes, how to dodge a bullet!

1115585.text: Still here? I got to sift through all these damn applications in fifteen minutes or I'm gonna have old Gontfried running into me in a blazing fury again. If you go speak to him you might get a faint hint of what I am talking about. Now get out of here, commanding these little runts ain't an easy job when I'm stuck here talking to you!

1115586.text: Hey, Senor, would you like to hear about my little darlings the "Devil Wings"? Well they certainly aren't my darlings anymore, I tried to kill the Archon and he stripped my own organization away from me and left me as a lower subordinate you see. Why didn't he kill me you ask? Who knows? That man works in ways I shall never understand. Sadly enough, now that he's dragged me along on this crusade now, I can never go back, the Maltese army will probably shoot me on sight now.

1115587.text: The Devil Wings used to be my little pride and joy, with our original goal being the destruction of Cryer Pharmaceuticals by any means necessary. That damned drug they are trying to develop would make Cardamine obsolete and the Outcasts would be ruined. I guess those goals are out the window now. After Lohingren went on this crazy crusade for 'love and peace', going after Cryer would be detrimental to our health, it seems.

1115588.text: Yeah, yeah, take a good look why don't you. That's right, I'm the guy who tried to kill the 'Archon'. Why you ask? Well I got a little bit feisty one day, I wanted to take what he had because I trust the man like I trust that lunatic Amadeus. Moral of the story is, not a lot. But what am I saying is, I failed and the Archon got me good. Now I'm stuck helping them whether I like it or not, I just have to get used to it.

1115589.text: Hey ladies, you want some of this eh? Hold it a second, hey senoritas, come back! Hmph look at that, you're cramping my style man! Now what is it you want eh? You know who you are speaking to? I am the Waran master man you hear that?! The damn Waran master six take downs in that baby, six! I would like to see you get that tally in one of those. Now leave me alone, I got to go wash your ugliness off me, or imma punch you instead. Call me uncle. CALL ME UNCLE!

1115590.text: Kara Research Station is the primary research and development installation of the Reaper forces. It is charged with the development of our weapons technology, it is also used as the Reapers' primary weapons manufacturing site making this installation a key asset for the Reapers' future.

1115591.text: Planet Braillia is the Reapers' main settlement. The planet's surface was once full of resources and was a stunning place to observe. After a certain operation the Reapers carried out on its surface, all structures have been moved underground to escape the lasting effects of the experiment. Currently, the planet only holds a couple of hundred personnel and a equal number of automatons that help with keep the colony's systems up and running. Braillia is in no way a military stronghold, in fact now it is primarily just a trade outpost the Reapers use.

1115592.text: Safe Haven base is similar to Planet Braillia as it is also a main settlement for Reaper forces, however, mostly military personnel reside on this base and its defences are considerably more impressive than those on Braillia's surface. It is protected with thick armor and numerous anti-fighter and bomber guns. Any capital ship that comes within range of the base will also have a Reaper bomber wing along with our capital ship fleet bearing down on them within sixty seconds. This makes Safe Haven the last and strongest line of defence before reaching Planet Braillia.

1115593.text: So, while you are here would you like to know about the Reapers' flagship? Well tough luck, not much is known about the ship outside of the core command. She's called the 'RFS Silent Edge', I can tell you that for sure. She hardly gets used in the open and appears only to execute targets and fades back into the darkness. I have personally never seen it falter in battle and it is commanded by Lohingren's brother, Raemmus. Compared to her, the Puppetmaster is a mere child's plaything.

1115594.text: The only other Reaper battleship in service at the moment is the 'RBS Fuen Labrada'. She is a ship formerly commanded by Lorenzo Montoya, a Maltese, during the battle for Omicron Eta two years ago against the Corsairs. The ship's bridge was stricken during one of the concluding attacks and Lorenzo died. After the battle was over, the Reapers were rewarded the Fuen Lebrada for their key role in the Eta battles. She is now flown by Commander Adalberto Alarico. After the Omicron Eta battle, the Reapers were also dubbed the 'Sword of the Maltese Army', our former "occupation" you could say. Now then, I am a busy man, I have a mission to be taking care of soon and must be off.

1115595.text: Besides the three current battleships under Reaper control right now, there was another during the days of the Reapers' arrival to Sirius. It was dubbed the 'Archon'. Named after our great leader, she stood as the symbol of trust and loyalty between the Outcast and Reaper forces. The ship flew many battles and was never forced to retreat from one. After a while the Outcast government became lax and overzealous with their resources and began to mass produce M1-class destroyers, giving them to anyone with the proper rank. The Archon was later destroyed in a controlled environment as propaganda to cut the resources being wasted on the masses. Of course the Council of Dons did not appreciate this act of 'heroism' and found it to be a major waste of resources. They managed to ground the Reapers for numerous days on charges of espionage and betrayal. The charges where then over ruled by Adora Encarnita, a Don at that current time within the Council.

1115597.text: Dammit, seems now that I have to actually talk to someone. Fine, fine, what would you like to know about then, eh? The Fallen Angels, my brother, or - God forbid - me? Ha-ha!

1115598.text: As you may or may not know, I am the "silent" leader of the Fallen Angels. They call me the "Silent" around these parts, although to be honest, I can be quite the rowdy character at times. Most times though, I like to keep things brief: why waste my time babbling on for hours when I can just give you the short and sweet version, know what I mean? Anyway I'll need to speak with you later. I'm away for my bath before it gets cold.

1115599.text: Well since you're here, let me give you the short rundown on my squadron, the "Fallen Angels". There's quite a bit of history behind that name. The "Fallen Angels" was a title given to my people, a long, long time ago. With our new role within Sirius we took on the "Reaper" name you no doubt know of. However, I did not want to just ignore the history of my people, I feel that would be highly disrespectful to our former leader and my father's legacy to disregard a title which we hold in such high regard. Anyway, if you wish to know more about the Fallen Angels, ask and you shall receive my friend. I think I hear the space-van, and I need to get some more space-juice!

1115600.text: Since you have taken it upon yourself to occupy the space right in front of me - which did originally belong to that beautiful lady standing at the bar - I suppose you want something? Well, since my fun has been ruined for now, let me tell you of the Fallen Angels' current goals. You could call my little winged beauties the Reapers' core. With a highly diverse skill base, the Fallen Angels are by far the most all-round squadron within the Reapers of Sirius. This makes us a very important aspect of this campaign and our input will determine whether or not the Reapers get through this little crusade. From tactical espionage and assassination to all out war, we are trained for any situation. Now then, clear on out of here space or I'll have you escorted to the airlock without the benefit of an escape pod.

1115603.text: In fights, any fight, big or not, my best advice would sound as 'Fight as one!'

1115604.text: Regardless of my position, the plans of the Archon are obscure. You can never predict his next step, but each of his decisions are certainly good for all of us.

1115605.text:
One of the most lethal and secretive squadrons within the Reapers of Sirius are codenamed "Garuda Wing". Pilots who have distinguished themselves through superior effort and achievement while participating in skirmishes and displaying acute proficiency in various areas of combat may receive the honour of being invited to the squadron.

The secret behind Garuda Wing is not the intense and extremely effective tactical training, but the fact that the members are personally hand-picked by Lohingren himself. Each member possesses a plethora of talents which are utilised for various types of operations conducted by the squadron. As a symbol of squadron membership and as a method used in order to impose confusion during battle, all pilots of Garuda Wing carry a specific codename, inherited from mythical creatures of earthen lore.

There is very little information regarding who exactly leads Garuda Wing except that his codename is, "Yggdrasil" which roughly translates as, "Tree of Life".

1115606.text:
The initial purpose of creating Garuda Wing was to compile a group of elite pilots who would conduct special operations, with the intent of damaging Colonial interest within the Tau region of Sirius. Intercepting various convoys and assassinating high-profile members of the Crayter Republic were two areas of conflict which Garuda Wing focused on. The secret behind their success was the combination of expert dog-fighters and weaponry load out adapted to neutralize Colonial-type vessels.

When the Outcast-Corsair battlefield moved to the Omicron Eta system, Garuda Wing was launched for their second large-scale operation. Due to the heavy quantity of resources concentrated on fending off incoming Corsair assaults, the Outcast forces had trouble staying on the offensive. Therefore, Garuda Wing conducted special stealth operations to assist the Outcasts, mainly behind enemy lines, largely within the Omicron Gamma system.

It was clear by now that Garuda Wing would be used in future special operations when required.

1115608.text: Not seen you around here before, stranger. Well to be honest, I actually don't have enough time to stay here and chat, as I am leading the Research division on this base. Being such a young system in development, I have much to do. Actually, I'm only here to see if I could find a Mr. Schiff Toha to find out about my next assignment, maybe we can talk in more detail some other time.

1115609.text:
Would you be interested in hearing about the research I have been given the task of carring out? The Archon has asked me to be the lead scientist in the development of the Reapers' new ships and weaponry: the "Z-Series fighter" which, along with the rest of the line's predecessors, are very fine ships indeed. Overall, they are the perfect ships, but with them being in such small number, the Reapers need their ships to be attuned to every situation. We have managed to get rid of some unnecessary "user friendly" devices in the Z-Series and added on more thruster output along with a whole new aerodynamics system to enhance its planetary combat capabilities.

Due to its new design and work given into the development of this upgraded Z-Series the Reapers re-dubbed this ship the "R1-Series, P-Lich Very Heavy Fighter".

1115610.text:
Along with the "R1-Series" very heavy fighter, two other craft were created to provide it with some backup. With similar design aspects to the very heavy fighter, the heavy fighter was to be designed as an interceptor class ship, boasting enough firepower to rival some of the lighter very heavy fighter class ships used by rival factions.

Ships of the heavy fighter series are dubbed the, "R1-Series, P-Wight Heavy Fighter".

1115611.text: The lightest ship in the Reaper arsenal was created as a heavily armed light fighter. Taking ideas from the Outcast 'Dagger' and mixing them along with the new propulsion systems of the Reapers, we managed to create what we now call the, "R1-Series, P-Skeleton Light Fighter". This fighter has excellent interception ability along with a forward firing turret similar to its predecessor, making this ship a troublesome foe in battle even to the heaviest of ships if flown correctly.

1115613.text: I am afraid that I cannot talk right now, I have some business which I must attend to. Comprende?

1115614.text: What would you like from the great Doctor Russ Mexan, eh, eh? Would you like to hear about the human genome? How about those interesting little, "Angel Genes"? Well I can't really tell you much because that would be giving out secrets now wouldn't it? What I shall tell you is that it is not all that far from the Cardamine gene, ha! Except only that it is superior in one way. But I shall not tell you this information because frankly I do not like you enough. Good day!

1115616.text:
The Kara Minefield protected the station within from unwanted visitors. While it was not designed to prevent a serious siege by determined attackers, the defensive screen would force smaller ships to approach through bottlenecks, providing time for fighter squadrons to be scrambled.

Unfortunately, the effectiveness of minefield proved to be the undoing of the very station it was designed to protect. When Corsair raiders attempted to pillage the Laboratory, they performed a controlled chain reaction that would allow their ships to pass through a section of the minefield. The resulting detonation spread much further than anticipated and though the field was successfully thinned, the concussive blasts effectively tore Kara Stellar Laboratory apart. Destroying most, if not all, the scientific data and research the Reapers had collected.

1115618.text: Born a Maltese always a Maltese man, or so they say. I wasn't born there, but I have got their 'problem' if you catch my meaning.

1115619.text: Not all of us are of Outcast descent, although the vast majority are. There are few left with true Reaper blood flowing through their veins.

1115620.text: The exodus from Alpha was an experience to say the least. We were vastly outnumbered, and had to avoid most of the enemy force. They would have ripped us in two. The Outcasts were not too pleased when we broke up that fight in Omicron Theta between the Corsairs and themselves. That war simply has to stop, but we made a mistake, much as I hate to admit it, by leaving a large part of our forces in Omicron 81.

1115621.text: There are a few regrets we've all got, but I suppose we've just got to set things straight.

1115622.text: Lohingren is a good man, and a good friend. I don't always understand his actions or agree with them, but he's done more for me than he knows.

1115623.text:
The Archon was my saviour. Ha, I was in a convoy when it all happened you see. We were bound for Freeport 9 in the Omicron Theta system. My old man and lady used to run a small trading business shipping consumable supplies to the Zoners. That day was no different to any other, we got past what we thought was the most dangerous part of the route through Sigma 13 and carried onto the Sigma 17 jumphole. That's where it all happened. A bunch of Corsairs stopped the ship and started to demand money. We were hardly the richest of folks back then, my old man pleaded to them asking them to follow us to Freeport 9 so we could drop off our supplies and get their payment. Unfortunately for us, the Corsairs did not believe us and opened fire on our ship. My old lady threw me in an escape pod and launched it before I could say a word. Here I am now my friend.

I bet you are wondering why I am fighting to save the Corsairs and not simply joining the Outcasts to destroy them. I don't hate the Corsairs for what they did that day: they were just doing all they have known for many years. I am here to prevent such a thing from happening again. The destruction of an entire civilisation is not, in my opinion, the way to go about it.

1115624.text: Come, sit and have a beer with me, we can look at all the fine ladies and we can talk about old times! I lead the Devil Wings you know, along with Mr Lucio Octavia that is. But we can talk about the Devil Wings another time. For now, we drink!

1115625.text:
Ah if it is not a little girly man coming to drink with the big boys. Well who am I to turn down a rookie wanting a swig, eh? Come, sit, I shall tell you about my fine squadron of men, known as the "Devil Wings". Our original purpose was to destroy Cryer Pharmaceuticals at any cost, but the old leader tried to assassinate the Archon and take his position of power. Obviously, the Archon being as skilled as he is prevented such a weak attempt at his life. Instead of killing him, he put him under my command, where the poor fool has been left to rot for so long.

Enough of him, back to the story, the current Devil Wings squadron is nothing like the previous, Cryer hunting lunatics we had before. We are now one of the ace squadrons of the Reapers, made up of the prime soldiers from the voluntary military. We are given rigorous training in order to keep the front lines clear of hostiles under any circumstance.There was one tale that springs to mind that occurred quite recently, but I reckon I have taken up enough of your time as is, ciao.

1115626.text:
Ah why hello there, sit and have a drink, I shall tell you of a most recent and epic battle my friend. The Archon ordered a conflict on every front, a massive squadron of fighters and bombers were to simultaneously strike three different positions. The Fallen Angels squadron were to fly into Colonial Territory, where they were to prevent any mishaps with the Omicron Gamma team. Skull Squadron was to escort a convoy to pick up some nuclear devices from the Mollys in the Newcastle system, while the Devil Wings held off the Corsairs until the Fallen Angels' arrival to help clean up.

The battle was bloody, and it was a true test to our training. The Devil Wings fought hard with no losses and one hour into the battle, the Fallen Angels arrived after successfully dealing with all Colonial ships in the vicinity. While the battle raged, Skull Squadron had completed their mission and the diversionary tactics in Gamma were a resounding success. Due to the amount of ships in Omicron Gamma however, retreat was made quite impossible. Skull Squadron caught up two hours into the battle and we managed to force our way out of the system. A glorious battle my friend and a truly splendid opening scene for the magnificent Devil Wings squadron wouldn't you say?!

1115627.text: Now that I look at it, that's a nice jacket. You, uh, looking to part with it anytime soon? Alright, I'm only joking stranger, but hey, since I just put you a little on edge, let me share a rumour about strange things that have been going around lately. Apparently, the Archon has been working with the "Spirits" in order to get the terraforming process on this planet well under way, whatever that means. It's true I tell you, just the other night I looked out of my quarter's window and saw one of their ships fly over the colony. Who am I kidding though? I bet you didn't believe a word I've said!

1115628.text: I am Francisco Palencia, former second in command of the Epigoni Squadron and a proud founding member and stand-in second in command of the Devil Wings squadron. Not bad for a drunken buffoon you might think, eh? I am quite an easygoing man in terms of work ethic, but I suppose the Archon has plans for me in some way, as they haven't gotten rid of me yet!

1115629.text: I doubt that someone cares about that I'm even alive... *Sigh*

1115630.text: This is the only place where I can find some peace. All of these robots and mechanisms are so lonely, so perfect. It's like an Eden for my own being. Walking into the bar makes me feel... strange.

1115631.text: Do you even have time to listen to the tiresome story about my life? A pathetic and very vague one it is too. It isn't really worth even a small part of your time...

1115632.text: Gran Canaria Resident\nGran Canaria Bartender\nGo Savona

1115633.text: Gran Canaria Population\nGran Canaria Commodity Trader\nRoland Notor

1115634.text: The Tau systems are rich in resources but not very inhabitable. There are virtually no usable planets here. It doesn't surprise me the Bretonians tried to -make- one habitable, but from the look of it they have failed in the attempt.

1115635.text: We keep an eye on the independent miners here at Holman. So far they've been cooperative, in selling us what they mine here, but there's no telling if that will last. Many of them seem Bretonian by birth. Should they side against us though, this station of theirs wouldn't last 5 minutes.

1115636.text: I do not think His Grace will bother with the nearby planet. It's barren and probes revealed no amounts of resources that would warrant committing troops to an invasion. No, once we capture New London and fully conquer Bretonia these stranded Bretonians will likely submit. And then we'll see if this planet "Harris" can be made useful in any way.

1115637.text: This sytem is one big icefield, but it's the gateway to Bretonia. It took us a while to amass a sizeable force here to drive the Kusari and Bretonians out. That Sirian gate can only handle so much traffic before it must recharge. Inferoir engineering I tell you...

1115638.text: The Gallic invasion has left us completely surrounded, but the minefields have thus far deterred their forces from making a direct assault. After Grimsby left I was sure we'd be invaded, but those Gauls simply moved on, onto Leeds. Perhaps they realised we're unable to mount any assault from this world.

1115639.text: There are still a lot of Armed Forces ground troops stationed here on Harris. Planetary warfare is a messy business, and I do not think the Gauls have the stomache for it. That's probably why they left this planet be. We'll be allright if we don't become too much of a thorn in their side I think.

1115640.text: I wanted to get out of here when the Kusari first invaded, but didn't have the credits to arrange for passage. Now that I finally do, there's nowhere left to go. We're cut off and surrounded, with only a minefield keeping those damned Gauls at bay. Damn it all!

1115641.text: Silver is a necessary and very expensive part of the terraforming process. It is used in our cloud-seeding operations. We have serious shortages of it right now, and the terraforming process is starting to suffer from it. Cloudseeding is a time-critical process, it should not be interrupted. We're already trying to see if we can recycle some of the Silver Iodide once it is washed out onto the surface, or if we can use dry ice as a temporary replacement instead. Problem with that is that you need to use seeder aircraft rather then groundbased generators.

1115642.text: Alien Organisms are brought here as a catalyst to the terraforming process. They speed up the operation at least three fold. They are difficult to come by these days, but we still receive the occasional shipment directly from the Omicron edge world, where they are found. We've begun concentrating our life-seeding efforts in smaller areas to compensate for the lack of available materials.

1115643.text: Terraforming Gases help to create an environment that is capable of sustaining life on otherwise barren planets. While undesirable on most terrestrial planets, greenhouse gases are vital in kickstarting a new ecology. The Gases we pump into Harris used to be shipped from Stokes, but what little we receive at the moment comes all the way from Rheinland.
