1115652.text: These amulets some of these Zoners have, curious little trinkets, aren't they? No clue where they come from. But sometimes, out there, when a Zoner freighter foolishly goes without escort... well, safe to say, some of those Pineal Amulets end up for sale on Crete.

1115653.text: It isn't easy flying a Corsair freighter these days. The Hessians are still furious about losing Casablanca, and in their usual disorganized fashion they still attempt to move in on it from time to time. Nothing our people can't handle now that the station defenses are back under our control, but still, it's not healty to fly into a raid with just a freighter.

1115654.text: Our people don't have a home like this anymore. All Mollys live in bases, except for a few like me who make a living down here. We used to have a planet to live on... until these trice damned Corsairs bombed it and rendered it uninhabitable. I hope these Zoners realise who they're getting in bed with.

1115655.text: We try to keep an eye on the Corsair activity in this system. If they intend to strike at Dublin we'll try to get ahead of them and send word to the boys. Then they'll have a little surprise ready by the time those Corsairs get there.

1115656.text: We sometimes purchase gold here and smuggle it back towards Rheinland. We don't get it from the Zoners though. We arrange to have the Mollys ship us some, so the funds spent go to their cause. They, like us, fight an oppressive house government, after having been exploited for centuries.

1115657.text: This is really the furthest we go in the Omega borderworlds. We have no business in Bretonia. I'm here to purchase a load of food for Viernheim. That trip has gotten more dangerous now that the Corsairs have taken Casablanca from us.

1115658.text: Oh, did you make your way here coming from Omega-47? Congratulations. Not many people make it through there unharmed. Many ships, and even more lives have been lost there. If you want to return to house-controlled space, try to reach the jumphole to Dublin. Bretonia keeps a close eye on the goings-on around there. Be careful of the Mollys though.

1115659.text: This station was built as a storage and supply station for the mining of the Gold we found on Planet Fuerteventura, but it's importance has diminished over the past years. There just isn't as much Gold as we thought there would be. Right now, this base is mostly a way station for traffic between Dublin and Omega 47.

1115660.text: Gran Canaria has become a major port of trade in the Omega systems. Mollys, Hessians, Corsairs, Zoners... even some of the house shippers make their way there to do business. Lanzarote gets very little traffic in comparison, aside from the shipments to keep the base operational. Usually it's the folk who don't want to be seen on Gran Canaria that come here.

1115661.text: Sure, there's the occasional Bounty Hunter, Hessian, Molly and Corsair that comes aboard Lanzarote. But not in the numbers they visit Gran Canaria in. I guess folks prefer the luxuaries the planet has to offer, rather then the cramped quarters here. Too bad they'll miss out on the best cocktails in the sector, courtesy of our tavernkeep!

1115662.text: I prefer roughing it on this station. Sure, you can get pampered or wasted down on the planet, but after the twelfth or so bar, you always end up in a brawl with some 'Sairs or Mollys. Which is a good way to get yourself killed. I almost went that way a few times, that's why I prefer the peace and quiet out here.

1115663.text: I'm on the trail of a specific Corsair who lead a strike on the Bowex transport Chesterton a few days ago. The refueling facilities down on Gran Canaria are always overcrowded, and there's usually a half hour waiting time before the docking ring can lift your ship. I don't have that kind of time when I get a lead - I need to be able to leave rightaway. That's why I prefer Lanzarote.

1115664.text: Sometimes some Zoner hires me on an escort job or two. Sure, I know they'll turn tail as soon as things get hot, but I guess that's what I get paid for, being a distraction. The Zoners run a lot of low-value cargo such as water, food and oxygen to keep the nearby Freeports afloat. Most pirates consider them unattractive targets. Besides, most of them use the Freeports as repair stations, or places to sell their loot.

1115665.text: I'm headed to Omega 15. My last mission took me up in the Taus, to hunt down an Outcast pilot that had pissed off some boffins in Liberty. Some big bucks right there. I'm just not sure if I was sober when thinking to come this way. Going over the lower Omegas is near suicide. I might just mosey back up to Dublin and head to Dresden by the lanes. I ain't risking my neck if there's no credits to show for it.

1115666.text: Ah, yes. Those colonists of ours on Gran Canaria. Shameful. It isn't the Corsair way to become vagrants on a Zoner planet. There are other ways to sustain ourselves. Bah, I wonder why we don't simply capture that planet and be done with it.

1115667.text: Yea, we're pretty alone out here. There's the Mollys to the west, the Hessians to the east, and Bounty Hunters everywhere in between. Still, we're here. What does that tell you about the Corsairs?

1115668.text: I hit a Bowex transport filled with gold a few days ago. It was a bit of a trek to haul the cargo back to Crete but it was well worth it. One more haul like that and I can retire for the rest of the year. Probably a good thing too, Bowex probably put a bounty of about my weight in gold on my head.

1115669.text: Striking deals with the Hessians? Hells no. We took Casablanca without needing words. The Omegas are ours. Anyone who dares say otherwise will get a few neutrons up their tailpipes. THAT is how Corsairs do diplomacy.

1115671.text: All that remains of a fighter from the Olympia's air wing.

1115673.text:
The CFV Olympia commanded a Crayter Republic battlegroup during the Gallic War. The Olympia fought in the Battle for Trafalgar in 825 AS, participating in the rearguard action that would culminate in the scuttling of Southampton Shipyard. Bretonia's subsequent demand to the IMG for Aland Shipyard's nationalisation placed the Republic in the untenable position of balancing relations between two hostile allies. Despite the Olympia's best efforts to mediate a lend-lease agreement for the duration of the war, no compromise could be found. Hostilities erupted during this process due to the Battleship Norfolk's deployment to Omega-3, with the battlegroup pressured by both Bretonia and the IMG to support their competing claims.

The Olympia's captain ultimately decided to support Bretonia's seizure of the station, believing that the Republic's long term survival hinged on Bretonia remaining a viable fighting force. Over the following weeks, the Olympia would fight alongside the Armed Forces fleet as an auxiliary, preventing Red Hessian and IMG bombers from pushing through the Wilkes Ice Field into the Bretonian flank. The Olympia would go on to play a pivotal role during Aland's capture, successfully covering the Bretonian boarding force as it closed with the Shipyard. This duty subjected the ship to withering counter-fire, crippling its engines and reactor. The immobilised ship was later scuttled due to the extensive damage redering repair infeasible.

The ship is currently hurling close to the star of Omega-3 and is expected to be consumed completely within a few years.

Recent events such as the destruction of the Stirling and the Bretonian withdrawal from Gran Canaria have left this base in a difficult situation, and it is unclear if the base will be used for its intendeed purpose, or at all.

Traffic to and from Rippon Tor is very tightly regulated, and the station was constructed to have as low a sensor profile as possible to further hide it within the Tenerife Cloud. The design of the base suggestions something was meant to be attached to it.

1115694.text: We patch up a lot of commercial transports at this base. A lot of ships get damaged in Corsair and Hessian raids, so there's always work for us here. Right now we have more than 10 transports and 15 escort craft in repair, and I hear there's 3 more on the way. It's going to be a busy month.

1115695.text: We build new civilian ships for whoever fronts the credits. Zoners, Bretonians, Rheinlanders. Business has been very good of late now that Gateway has secured permits for building the Bretonian main transport line. They've selected our yard as their main construction site, which means we'll be quite busy in the coming months.

1115696.text: On occasion a larger military ship comes into drydock here. We don't encourage it but we won't turn a repair job down, regardless of the ship. The Bretonian gunboat HMS Bainsley was recently repaired after hitting "asteroids" during a routine patrol, although the damage looked suspiciously like Molly neutron weapon impacts. Sometimes it pays not to ask questions.

1115697.text: IMG builds and maintains most of it's Bretonian and Omega mining and transport fleet at this base. Many smaller and larger mining vessels often receive repairs and refits here. Aland is a large facility that can handle many jobs simultaneously, and as such keeps a lot of folks employed.

1115698.text: This base always has a shortage of available supplies. We try to keep spares, but anyone coming here with Hull Panels, Engine Components, Superconductors, Quantum Multiplexers or Super Alloy will make a tidy profit.

1115699.text: This shipyard has repaired some of the escort ships that guard the nearby freeports from time to time. We occasionally commission a freighter or two to help maintain the supply lines between Freeport 1 and Freeport 5. Our ships sometimes get caught in the crossfire between Hessians and Corsairs sometimes. Any ships surviving that are sure to need repairs.

1115700.text: We supply this base with some basic commodities such as Food, Water and Oxygen. The biodome at Freeport one generates a surplus of food, and whatever the Corsairs don't buy up, we ship here.

1115701.text: Supplying this base with Engine Components, Hull Panels and Super Alloy from Bretonia brings in a tidy sum, however, it's a risky run. The Trade Lanes in Omega 3 are often targeted by Corsairs, who need those materials just as much as this shipyard does. Even the Hessians like to run off with shipbuilding supplies.

1115702.text: I'm waiting until my transport is patched up. We were on our way here with a load of Basic Alloy, but a group of Corsairs ambushed us on the last lane. Although two of my cargopods were lost, I managed to save the transport. Staying alive is the main thing out here.

1115704.text: A very large comet, possibly a rogue planetoid, caught in the gravitational well of the Omega 3 star. Initial scans have revealed immense quantities of Cobalt locked under it's icy crust. Due to it's proximity to the star, the comet cannot be mined directly, but the star is slowly eroding the comet. The comet's tail contains small quantities, easily retrievable Cobalt.

1115705.text: I've heard the governor eventually wants this planet to be self-sufficient. I'm not sure how that's going to work when all I've seen is mud, sand and small, sick looking plants. Planet Cambridge is a short stint through the Jump Gate. Usually it wouldn't be a problem to ship Food Rations and Fertilizers down, but the Corsairs have been making things exceptionally difficult for us.

1115706.text: Bretonia Mining and Manufacturing\nEngineer Ivor Silvester

1115707.text: Bretonia Mining and Manufacturing\nRep. Dex Newton

1115709.text: This base has two main exports: Scrap Metal and Robotics. Scrap Metal is left over from damaged ship components. It's not very valuable, but taking it back to a smelting facility can still bring in some cash. Robotics are more valuable, and therefor more risky to carry.

1115710.text: Bretonia is rapidly developing Nottingham. I'm not sure what that will mean for us. Probably not a whole lot, unless Rheinland decides to violently oppose it. If that happens we'll be right at the frontline.

1115711.text: We get our supplies both from Rheinland and Bretonia. Gateway brings in most of them. They used to not have many options when returning from Rheinland after delivering Beryllium to Dortmund, but bringing us Engine Components has changed that rather drastically.

1115712.text: If you're looking for a relatively safe bulk cargo run, bring Scrap Metal to Dortmund and come back with a load of Basic Alloy. Those are both low-value cargoes and aren't very interesting to the many pirates in the Omegas.

1115713.text: Ah, yes, the new Bretonian Transport jobs. I'm sure Bowex and BMM are foaming at the bit that we're building their iconic Shires here as well now. Nothing like a bit of competition to break their extortionate prices. We managed to sign on a few ex-BMM shipwrights who were fed up with the excessive hours at Southampton. I'm sure their experience with these designs will come in handy. Who knows, we might even be able to improve on them with our own knowhow.

1115714.text: As far as neighbours go, these miners aren't half bad. Most of them are as fed up with the megacorporations as we were. Unlike us though, they don't try to stay neutral with the Hispanics. Both the Corsairs and the Outcasts are enemies of theirs. It's amazing that they manage to survive without a house backing them.

1115715.text: Sirius Robotics is a relatively young enterprise. The market on Robotics was previously cornered by Kusari, which was quite a problem for Bretonia when they were at war with that nation. Robotics are so widely used - automated cargo handling, automated mining rigs... you name it. Without access to replacement parts, Bretonian industry had a lot of costly breakdowns until we offered an alternative.

1115716.text: Kusari, naturally, isn't happy with us. We basically broke their monopoly on Robotics. It's one of the reasons why we are here in Omega-3, co-located with an IMG base. It's as far from Kusari as you can possibly get, and the nearest house authority, Bretonia, wasn't too receptive to Kusari complaints at the time.

1115717.text: Our robotics get shipped to both Bretonia and Rheinland. We're still expanding, our market share isn't very big yet, but especially Bretonia has been quite happy with us. Our main problem with ramping up production is the lack of an adequate supply of Optronics - for obvious reasons, Kishiro does not ship to us directly. Republican and Gateway are suitable intermediaries.

1115718.text: It's quite handy to have this shipyard around. The Omegas are a rough place for a Hunter, and you can expect to get roughed up quite often. Most bases can do patchwork, but every now and then your ship just needs a total overhaul, which means heading for a yard.

1115719.text: The miners here don't post bounties on Hessians. They say it's because the Hessians don't attack them, but I think there might be more to it. A lot of these miners are ex-Daumann or ex-Kruger, and there's no love lost with their old employers. Wouldn't surprise me if some of em were in league with the Hessians.

1115720.text: Officially, the borderworlds are still neutral territory. Unofficially, Rheinland has claimed Omega-7, and Bretonia has taken most of Omega-3. That makes this station kind of the unofficial border between the houses.

1115740.mapped:
Battleship Kassel was constructed in 820 AS, and initially served as a rear guard vessel stationed in the Omega-47 system. The ship was then deployed to Omega-7 in 825 AS, where it raided the passing traffic, the local mining operations and Rheinland patrols that lost their way in the Walker Nebula.

Following the Bretonian push to nationalize Aland Shipyard, the Red Hessians decided to take the opportunity to deliver a decisive blow against the invaders. This was both an attempt to aid their IMG suppliers as well as an assertion of dominance over the Omegas. The Kassel moved to Omega-3 and surprised the Bretonian garrison at Planet Sprague. Using its forward gun and its bomber squadrons, the Kassel managed to destroy the Battleship Gwent. What the Hessians had not anticipated however, was that the Bretonian Norfolk Fleet was in Omega-3. The Norfolk's bomber wing launched a counterattack which heavily damaged the Kassel, causing it to retreat. Unfortunately, due to the damage sustained, its engines failed only a short time after arriving in Omega-5.

With assistance from Coalition allies, the Kassel was tugged to Aralsk Research Station in Omega-52 where it underwent repairs. Once the Rheinland Civil War occurred the Kassel was finally repaired and primed to take advantage of the situation. The Kassel and her sister ships were sent into the vulnerable Cologne system, tasked with capturing Tholey Station from the Bounty Hunters and securing the Saarbrucken orbit, a task completed with minimal casualties. Once Rheinland reunited however, it quickly became apparent that holding the world would be untenable and the Kassel was forced to fight a retreating battle while providing cover for evacuees leaving the planet. Having succeeded in its objective, the Kassel now sits at Wolfsburg Shipyard undergoing repairs from its fight with the Altenburg before going back into action.

This was both an attempt to aid their IMG suppliers as well as an assertion of dominance over the Omegas. The Kassel moved to Omega-3 and surprised the Bretonian garrison at Planet Sprague. Using its forward gun and its bomber squadrons, the Kassel managed to destroy the Battleship Gwent. What the Hessians had not anticipated however, was that the Bretonian Norfolk Fleet was in Omega-3. The Norfolk's bomber wing launched a counterattack which heavily damaged the Kassel, causing it to retreat. Unfortunately, due to the damage sustained, its engines failed only a short time after arriving in Omega-5.

With assistance from Coalition allies, the Kassel was tugged to Aralsk Research Station in Omega-52 where it underwent repairs. Once the Rheinland Civil War occurred the Kassel was finally repaired and primed to take advantage of the situation. The Kassel and her sister ships were sent into the vulnerable Cologne system, tasked with capturing Tholey Station from the Bounty Hunters and securing the Saarbrucken orbit, a task completed with minimal casualties. Once Rheinland reunited however, it quickly became apparent that holding the world would be untenable and the Kassel was forced to fight a retreating battle while providing cover for evacuees leaving the planet. Having succeeded in its objective, the Kassel now sits at Wolfsburg Shipyard undergoing repairs from its fight with the Altenburg before going back into action.

1115752.text: Welcome to Wolfsburg. You want to find a Hessian engineer, this is the place you look in. They do the construction of most of the big ships in the Red Hessian fleet just here, in the superstructure beneath us. You can't see it from here obviously, a viewport would be too dangerous. This place might not be built for comfort, but it sure is cool to be part of.

1115753.text: [832 AS] Bautzen Station and Strausberg destroyed!

1115754.text: DRESDEN -- 832 AS -- A successful blitz attack has been launched against the Bautzen Station by Cruiser Heppenheim and its escort wing! Bautzen Station went down in flames, along with most of its crew - deservingly so for their continued defiance against us. While Heppenheim was lost with all hands to the Battleship Strausberg's immediate counter-attack, it managed to disrupt the enemy fleet long enough for our bomber wings to retaliate. The Strausberg was damaged beyond the possibility of repair, with its cowardly crew scuttling rather than fighting to the death. The enraged Rheinwehr has foolishly sent what remained of their forces to try and destroy Leipzig, but only managing to disable the station before the Kassel and its escorts arrived. Those invaders were promptly dispatched, with operations on Leipzig Station expected to resume in short order.

1115756.text: PETRA -- 832 AS -- Grinding stalemates against the Hessians in Omega-5 and Omega-47 have gone on for decades, with tens of thousands having met their end in these systems. High Elder Montoya once pioneered the Road to Rheinland strategy to break this impasse. He envisioned an assault through the Sigmas into Rheinland, crippling the Hessian back lines in Dresden. While the High Elder has since passed, today we have the power to once again put his bold plan into action. Our scouts aboard the Battlecruiser Penitence report that the Rheinland Military and Hessians have severely bloodied one another in clashes across Dresden. Both are weakened and preoccupied; all we must do is administer the fatal blow. The Elders have directed our forces to assemble at Petra and prepare to break through Frankfurt into Dresden. Be wary of the Bundschuh, who have harassed our raiders and resupply freighters in the area. They will likely try to stop us, and are to be shot on sight.

1115758.text: DRESDEN -- 832 AS -- The Red Hessians have attempted to expand their control over the Dresden system. This time, their target was the Bautzen Station, used to extract precious Blue Diamonds, often referred to as "Hessian Tears". Their merciless ambush was so quick, that the Battleship Strasberg stationed in the system was unable to respond in time, and the only survivors was the quarter of the crew that made it to the escape pods before the station depressurized. Strasberg has, however, managed to catch the Hessians before they've managed to slip away, taking out their 'flagship' in quick order. Admiral Schwarz has ordered the forces under his command to press the advantage, and led his forces towards Leipzig, a former Daumann installation that was taken over by the Hessians over a decade ago. The Admiral's quick decision-making allowed our brave forces to heavily cripple the Hessian presence in the system, possibly sufficiently to drive them out of the system entirely.\n\nThe victory did not come without a price, however: The main reactor of Strausberg suffered heavy damage during the battle and the ship had to be abandoned after having it's functional components stripped out. Admiral Schwarz in an interview earlier today stressed that the situation in the system is definitely an improvement after the recent events, and that the Hessian defeat in the system is imminent. In other news, various projects for Bautzen's replacement are already being discussed.

Fleet of Rheinland headed towards Kusari was equipped by one Nomad Power Cell that was handed over to them by the Nomads somewhere in the Sigma space in 800 AS By miracle, the Cell has survived when scattered forces of a group that would later be known as The infected passed through Rheinland and headed towards the distant Omega worlds.

Power Cell was necessary to collect silicate matter from nearby planetoids and asteroid fields to complete building the massive Gate. Right now, the Cell has transformed into a small but rapidly growing black hole that consumes all objects dragged into its gravity well. 1115795.text:
The Battlecruiser Trier was built shortly after the Hudson War’s armistice with Liberty, implementing the lessons Rheinland learned from that bitter conflict. The cutting-edge warship vanished during its maiden voyage in Hamburg, after reporting that it was investigating an urgent distress signal. An extensive search was conducted, yet no trace of the vessel or its crew could be found. In reality, the Trier had been lured into the Kielfeld by The Wild, and was quickly overrun by external attackers and infiltrators within the crew.

The Trier was a significant prize for the Nomads, who -- cultivating lurid tales of ghost ships -- used it to brutally target civilians across Rheinland. More significantly, the Trier was ideally positioned to infect poorly-protected Independent World pirates, and intercept Artifacts bound to Liberty. In recent times, the Trier has abandoned its Kielfeld lair and redeployed through Thuringia's Suhl into Omicron Theta. The Wild have begun an overt campaign of terror there, seeming to conspicuously and intentionally draw attention to themselves in the process.

1115797.text: A rotating torus in orbit of Omega-2 with a such a high concentration of diamond dust that it glitters in very high frequency light, this body is expected to eventually accrete into a handful of rocky bodies near the star. In its current state, as it slowly cools and concentrates, the heat and density of high velocity dust make construction near Omega-2 impossible. As it cools and slows over the next fifty million years, the diamond dust is a concentration of riches that Daumann, the Hessians, BMM, and the IMG cannot ignore, and there have been bloody conflicts over mining rights.

1115799.text: Little more than scattered, molten remains ejected from a protoplanetary collision, Rheinland coporate vessels have repeatedly been sighted in and around this area, apparently thinking along the same lines as Bretonia Mining and Manufacturing. If there are valuable resources to be found, it is only a matter of time until conflict arises.

With a solid crust and a superheated core, Salme is in a period of great geologic upheaval. It's mostly nickel-iron core is estimated to be cool by 130 degrees Celsius every billion years but has yet to develop any solidity.

As the core cools, it will shrink, and the planet's crust will continue to twist and rupture under the strain for the next two billion years, when the crust will finally rest on a fully solid, crystalized core. Until then, this world, with its rapid rotation and quick cooling will be geologically active, with nearly constant volcanism and lava flows for millions of years.

1115822.text: This mobile dry-dock is used by the Independent Miners Guild to retrofit, and maintain their Tau warships, exploration vessels, and other large combat and civilian craft. Named Endeavour by the workers who utilize it, this platform, while not yet fully in use, is continually being upgraded to ease the maintenance of Guild ships, and keep the platform ready for the occasional large project that requires more secrecy then the guild can provide at other, more public locations.

1115824.text: Proudly protecting Jakarta Orbital Station from any would be attackers, the Barrington is a relatively old capital vessel. Brought into service as a prototype in 816 AS, it has seen significant action in the volatile Tau systems against the Outcasts and their allies. It has since been brought to Tau-39 to provide added security to the expanding Jakarta station.

1115826.text: Independent Miners Guild\nJakarta Commodity Trader\nHans Helver

1115827.text: Independent Miners Guild\nJakarta Equipment Dealer\nElias Thorpe

1115828.text: Independent Miners Guild\nJakarta Ship Dealer\nRichard Dawson

1115833.text: Jakarta is the de-facto headquarters of the Independent Miners Guild. We use this base in many ways: Exploration mission preparation, stellar cartography, ship construction and prototyping. You name it, it happens here. That's why this base is so tightly guarded.

1115834.text: We launch survey missions from here towards unexplored Tau stars, by conventional travel. It can take several months up to a full year to travel to another star. Cryostasis is essential in those journeys, as you could never take on supplies for a full crew. House corporations, spoiled with their lanes and gates, have all but lost the knowhow and experience for extrasolar travel. But for the Guild, it's key to survival.

1115835.text: Have you seen the latest ships? The Himalayan line? Sure, they don't look as good as the Colonial designs but they're a whole lot more practical for the work we do. It makes me wonder what those R&D boys will come up with next.

1115836.text: I'm on a break, chump. Worked a straight 10 hour shift loading the exploration cruiser Pennitry for a survey mission. Not sure where it's going, but she'll be leaving soon. Best cargo handlers get picked for the mission - there's no better pay in the IMG then on the survey teams. Of course, you have to put up with being away from any form of civilization for at least 2 years, and the chance of not coming back at all, but beyond that it's the best job there is!

1115837.text: We mine the nearby gas giant for water and oxygen, and a little bit of deuterium. It's enough to supply this base and Timor, so for those commodities, we're pretty self sufficient. We bring in food from Freeport 10, and most other commodities from Kusari. Transports usually leave this system with a load of copper from Timor.

1115838.text: Outcasts are a major headache for us here in the upper Taus, more so than the Gallic forces. Gallia is focused on Bretonia, and where their own corporations don't go, their Navy keeps out of as well. This is both good and bad: Some of the Taus are left to us, and us alone. But we truly are alone out here now, and that's risky.

1115844.text: I suspect Samura are using civilians against us. Some of their more important military camps are embedded deep into civilian areas. Its the only reason they still exist.

1115845.text: Sometimes our supply lines can't keep up with our movements. I've gone many days on the bare minimum. Although we're getting better at being prepared for this now.

1115846.text: I know many of us believe that Samura isn't worth any respect. However there is a officer in their security forces who proved to me that maybe some do. I hope such a man doesn't die on this planet.

1115847.text: With the Matsumoto being re-deployed elsewhere, our fighter pilots can focus on the Samura security forces, though some Naval ships still patrol the system.

1115848.text: Commander Wei Hong saved my ass during our last operation. Had a Samura guard pop out right behind me. Thankfully he was watching my six and put two rounds into his chest and dropped him. I really should have checked that corner better, he didn't say anything but I could tell he wasn't pleased.

1115849.text: Fighting against the Samura Security detail is too easy. We're starting to let our guard down more than we should, and a few of us have paid the price for it. The Commander is making sure to straighten us up.

1115850.text: Getting supplies here from Kyoto base is tricky. Not only do we have to get past Samura and the Naval Forces. But the Hogosha and Farmers Alliance like to loiter around too.

1115851.text: The Kokura being in system helps us greatly getting the supplies we need, while also keeping Samura convoys on their toes. Sometimes we let the convoys pass only to launch a raid on them when they think its safe to land.

1115852.text: I lost my good friend Izanagi recently. What he thought was a civilian turned out to be a Samura guard and it got him shot in the back. He didn't deserve to go like that.

1115853.text: The Navy has started to send marines down here. Things are about to get a lot harder.

1115854.text: I'm originally from Rheinland. Used to work for Kruger right up until 789, when they cut the pay for the Bautzen crews for the third time. It became impossible to support my family just by working for the big man. "For the good of Rheinland" means nothing if your son is starving. I asked around, and ended up on Freistadt. Joined the Guild there, and managed to sign up with a mining crew.

1115855.text: I used to work in the fields in Omega-7 as part of a transport crew. Miner transports need a small crew to operate them. The ship got hit badly during a Corsair ambush. I got out safe, but the ship was lost. I couldn't find another transport to sign up on in the Omegas, so I had to hunt around further. Eventually, I wound up here.

1115856.text: Deep space exploration is dangerous business. Every 4 ships we send out, 1 isn't heared from again. FTL Commbuoy paths keep track of where ships are lost so we can mark areas or even systems as unsafe. Those "breadcrumb" paths are ancient technology, dating back from the establishment of the colonies. I don't think anyone other then the Guild and the Zoners are still using those.

1115857.text: I work in the astrogation facility. Our job is to chart the galaxy, which isn't as easy as it sounds. Given that Sirius is a gigantic, three dimensional jigsaw of massive nebulas, small darkmatter spots, the occasional singularity and a rather densely packed field of stars, gravitic anomalies cause "lensing" effects that make triangulating positions almost pointless.

1115858.text: One of the things we do is to analyse each star's emission spectrum. That tells us a good bit about the expected composition of the star and the planetary system around it. It is not precise, but it gives us some guidance on the potential of systems beyond the explored ranges. Systems with good potential are then explored further by probes or a manned mission.

1115859.text: It can be difficult to determine the contents of some regions. Nebulas can obscure anything within or behind them, so it helps to survey every nebula from every known system visually and spectrally. Once you feed all that information into a single starplot, you can pick up systems noone else has noticed. That is how we picked up Tau-113.

1115860.text: One of the Samura employees is feeding us information. They've been extremely useful so far in enabling us to raid fully stacked warehouses of supplies.

1115861.text: I'm currently the squad's marksman. I've killed at least thirty Samura armed guards and potentially crippled more. But they always find fools to give a gun to and throw into the grinder.

1115862.text: The new Jump Gate is a real boon for our operations here. It's a pity a Trade Lane could not be built in this asteroid field, but all the same, it has made our travel to the Core Worlds much shorter and safer.

1115863.text: We mine Beryllium east of this base. Just follow the trail of Bretonian wreckage and you'll find the richest field. The Outcasts often attack miners, so be in your guard if you go there.

1115864.text: Our soldiers captured this facility from Bretonia. It'll take some time to figure out how to repair and operate all this machinery - meanwhile we'll simply ship the raw ore back to Gallia and process it there.

1115865.text: While they are technically competitors, we're not really looking to drive the IMG out quite yet. They know the system, and being further north, are typically the first to get hit when Outcast raiders show up. So they're both a shield and workforce for Gallia, without even realising it.

1115866.text: It's a good thing we found these rich pockets of resources this early in the Sirian campaign. It'll help alleviate the shortages back home. The King's demand to expand our military to the level of readiness it's at now has all but exhausted the known mineral resource sites in Gallia, both on-planet and in space.

1115867.text: It will take a few years before this station has smelters of it's own. Meanwhile we're forced to ship raw Beryllium ore back home for processing. It isn't very efficient, but it's all we can do at the moment.

1115868.text: Our troops captured what's left of this lane that was under construction. It appears to be quite new, perhaps there are some Ageira improvements that we do not yet know about, hidden inside the wrecks. I'm not holding my breath though, they appear to be scuttled quite thoroughly.

1115869.text: Apart from the unfinished lane, the real prize here in the Jump Gate. It's a brand new one, and fully functional too, although some parts seem unfinished. It'll help in getting troops and supplies through to Tau-31, but it'll also allow us to analyze the latest ideas Ageira uses in their design, so we can reverse engineer those.

1115870.text: We run this captured base as a supply depot and mining station. There are deposits of Beryllium nearby, which our company is mining and returning to Gallia. The resource deposits here are far richer then those in Gallia itself.

1115871.text: There are two other Sirian groups in the system: The Outcasts and the IMG. The IMG are miners, much like us, but the Crown has chosen not to remove them... yet. I hear they are cooperative, trading with IDF. The Outcasts on the other hand are savages, who attack anyone other then themselves.

1115872.text: I made the run to Carcassonne two days ago. It's a dangerous journey. As soon as you leave through the gate you're in a no-mans-land. The Tau-31 system simply doesn't lend itself to being secured properly. The dense asteroid field provides many hiding places for enemy fightercraft. Luckily, my run was uneventful, but I'm not looking forward to my next run tomorrow.

1115873.text: We'll eventually have to rebuild this base into a proper Gallic station. Having to jury-rig the moorings is a major problem. And then there's the guidance systems. Either the Bretonians sabotaged the docking sensors or their mooring procedures consist of ramming the station at full engine power to get a positive seal on the airlocks.

1115876.text: The Guillestre has been outfitted to function as a combat carrier. Since this system was unsuitable for capital ship use, and the Bretonian front being one fought out in the open now that we're past the Tau systems, we've been assigned to a flank defense role. Not as glorious, but important all the same. The resources we've captured here fuel the shipbuilding industries back home.

1115877.text: The Guillestre has been outfitted to function as a combat carrier. Since this system was unsuitable for capital ship use, and the Bretonian front being one fought out in the open now that we're past the Tau systems, we've been assigned to a flank defense role. Not as glorious, but important all the same. The resources we've captured here fuel the shipbuilding industries back home.

1115878.text: We'll likely be here a while. La Riche could have kept the border at the far side of the Orkney hole, but His Grace wishes to claim this system and it's resources. It's a messy claim. The full force of the Fleet can't be used here, just smaller fighters, so the battleground here favors those criminals. I wonder how those Independent Miners managed to survive out here this long.

1115879.text: This system is a single, vast asteroid field, which limits the size of ships that can be used here. The Guillestre is essentially a fortified carrier, and not a true battleship, in this area. We run regular patrols through the system, but when we come upon Outcasts, the fights aren't easy.

1115880.text: These Outcasts know how to handle a fighter, but so do we. We're not familiar with the terrain, so they have a small advantage here, for now. Once we gain experience here we'll be able to take the fight to them. When they are suppressed in this system, the Guillestre will hopefully be tasked to a more important part of Sirius.

1115881.text: Bah, the indignity. Here I joined the Navy to bring glory to His Grace, and now end up in this godforsaken cloud of rocks, with nothing more than scrapes against pirates to look forward to. If the Royal Police were half as competent as us, it'd have been their job.

1115882.text: Solar Engineering prefers not to leave the Gallic Core. But when the Crown calls upon us for specific tasks outside of the Core, we'll do what we can as any Gallic organisation should.

1115883.text: The Guillestre itself guards the entrance to Gallia now. The Jump Gate leads straight into Languedoc. Not the safest of systems, but it at least takes the run over Brittany out. Our shippers can travel by means of the Trade Lanes, with the exception of this system.

1115886.text: At least those Outcasts are putting up a fight. They certainly put up more of a fight then the Gallic Brigands did back in Languedoc. I might actually be able to skip our combat simulations without worrying about going soft.

1115887.text: Those miners up north? Not worth my time. They've been here long enough to know what to expect from the Outcasts, and the Crown has seen fit not to remove them... yet. I wouldn't be surprised if that moment will still come, once the Outcasts are subdued.

1115888.text: There is not a whole lot going on in this system, compared to the heavy activity of the core worlds. I suppose the fact that this entire system is one big rockpile will have something to do with that. The system does have some valuable resources, so there's a bunch of miners here.

1115889.text: Our main task here as fighter pilots is to keep the Outcasts off of the traffic moving between the Languedoc and Tau-31 Jump Gates. These include the supplies for the front in Leeds, which keep the momentum of our troops going.

1115890.text: I hear things are going well at the front. The first Bretonian core system has been taken, in less then 2 years after our premature exposure to Sirius. I hear analysts say we'll be in control of all of Bretonia within the next 5 years.

1115891.text: The Colonials did a real number on this station. Even if we knew how it was put together in the first place, we'd have a hard time repairing it. I suspect His Grace will simply order this floating piece of garbage scuttled, as it has no real value.

1115892.text: I wonder what made the Colonials build this station in the first place. Putting up a station inside an asteroid field is asking for disaster. Even before our Navy boarded it, it was clear that this base has had several significant asteroid strikes, most of which had never been repaired.

1115893.text: How long are we expected to hold this heap of decompressing metal? Oblique can handle the patrols, and Minato is more suited as a supply base. Why has Oblique not put this station out of it's misery?

1115894.text: The Outcasts are not as much a problem here as in Tau-23. We suspect this system is too remote, even for them. A pity, because it means we're just sitting here, twiddling our thumbs while those fighting on the Bretonian front get all the glory.

1115895.text: The only thing of value in this system is that planet out east, Borneo. It is habitable, but rather unpleasant, unlike many of the Core worlds. Unless the GMS finds resources on it, I doubt we'll have much of a need for this system.

1115896.text: We know of that shipyard those miners have hidden behind that nebula northeast. Big as it is, it's not exactly easy to hide. Did they think we would not notice? But we have no need for it. It's too small for our warships, and too remote to be supplied. I wonder how those miners keep it running.

1115897.text: The Oblique would be better served defending a more important system, like Tau-31 now Carcassonne has moved up. Unfortunately, none of the facilities we captured in this system is suitable as a Navy base, and the Crown does not want to deploy a small outpost here. Unless we withdraw from this system entirely, Oblique will need to stay.

1115898.text: It doesn't help to be this far from Gallia. Supplies to Tau-44 have to come from Languedoc, then pass by that miner outpost, Java, in Tau-23, then arrive here by jumphole. So much can go wrong -- the jumphole can be unfit for travel, the Outcasts or even Colonial raiders can hit the ships while they transit. Some convoys even lose their way in that asteroid field. I hear one of them ended up in Kyushu instead.

1115899.text: We still see some Colonial raiders here on occasion. Perhaps they still have a hideout in the system, but we've not been able to find it thus far. It does not matter, whatever remains of that little republic is no more than a nuisance to us.

1115904.text: Our Vaches were not made for travel through asteroid fields, but I must say they are holding up nicely. A testament to Gallic engineering that even the most incompetent pilot can only manage to become a pinball, rather then a fireball. I just wish they'd install better cuchioning on the seats. It is so easy to get spacesick among those asteroids.

1115905.text: One good thing about all this space is that there's plenty of room for a few small workshops. While ships on a carrier can be repaired with spare parts, fabricating the new spare parts on-site from standard templates is somewhat more difficult, and requires more space then can be alotted on a frontline vessel. We manufacture some spare parts for fightercraft and even gunboats right here, then ship them off to where they are needed. We also refurbish damaged parts, so we don't need to import as much.

1115906.text: This station used to be equipped with farming domes, according to the stations schematics. The Crayterians appear to have deconstructed them and taken them along. It's a shame, if they too had been left behind we could have halved the supply shipments to the Tau forces, as we'd have all the Food, pure Water, and Oxygen we'd need.

1115949.mapped:
Erected deep within the Koryu Cloud in the utmost secrecy, Yurasu is an unusual departure for Samura. In the face of multiple GMG affronts, resulting in open corporate warfare around the periphery of Kusari and the lack of significant Naval Forces presence in the Sigmas, the corporation decided to take matters into its own hands.

Samura's upper echelon paid a considerable sum of credits to the Hogosha and Farmer's Alliance to stage a massive diversionary raid not far from Niigata in order for a number of construction vessels to steal away into the Koryu Cloud, where a supply depot and hangar was hastily constructed over the course of weeks. This depot grew as Samura snuck more and more resources into the system until it grew to present-day Yurasu.

To the best of Samura's knowledge, the Guild is unaware of the station's existence, but the staffers take few risks. Resident Samura employees along with pilots from the Hogosha, Alliance, and occasionally even the Corsairs congregate here in a desperate effort to inflict as much damage as possible to nearby GMG assets. The aim is to create enough pressure here to end or at least relieve pressure from the siege of Kurile.

1115951.text: Eventually the isotopes we use for H-fuel are going to run out, but to mine out the entire Crow Nebula would take thousands of years at least. We know that these isotopes aren't here naturally - not in this concentration. Projections show that this nebula should have coalesced into stars, but instead the nebula is dispersing. The implications are unnerving. Only a very large star - a blue hypergiant - could have dispersed this much interstellar gas, and given the isotope density, the star did not meet a natural end. If you were a scientist and tried to understand this it would boggle your mind. The force needed to rip a star apart without it being destroyed by the star before it can achieve it's purpose is almost inconceivable, almost. Think about it, the gases that were left over from that explosion have powered nearly all of Sirius for over eight centuries, and we haven't tapped more than a fraction of the Crow.

1115952.text: Thanks to Kishiro Technologies our ships have been upgraded with many technological innovations. Our Gas Miners are the most efficient in use in Sirius, and we continue to refine our fighter avionics and sensor suites to be able to build on the advantages our combat tactics offer us. This is no small accomplishment.

1115953.text: We have shared some of our technologies with the Blood Dragons, who are resisting the Outcasts and other threats emerging from the Omicron region. The most important technologies we have shared with them are our sensor suites, which allows their own fightercraft to be more effective when fighting inside nebulas. This does not help those among the Dragons who would seek to attack Kusari targets directly, but it gives them a significant advantage in systems like Chugoku and Tohoku, where they use the cover of the nebulas.

1115954.text: H-fuel is the bread and butter of Gas Miners Guild. We are always trying to perfect the quality of our product, and develop new, more efficient Gas Mining technologies. We are at the forefront of all developments in this field, mostly because we fund the bulk of the research into it. We intend to keep it that way.

1115955.text: It really is only a matter of time before we will be ordered to begin work on warships of our own, but I wager they will be a lot smaller than these Rheinlandish monstrocities we captured. The analysis of the Yanagi wreckage has given us a solid understanding of the technologies behind Rheinland capital ship engineering, and we also know a good deal about Kusari warship construction - a parting gift we took from our partnership with Samura in the past. Combining that knowledge with our own is a potent mix of technologies. Question is if they are compatible - Rheinish design favors oversizing everything from armor thickness to weapon sizes. Kusari construction doctrines emphasise form over function. Ours emphasise on pure function, but hasn't gone beyond fightercraft. Choosing a course will be difficult for the engineers.

1115956.text: The basic components of H-Fuel are Hydrogen, Deuterium and Helium-3. The amount of Hydrogen to the Helium-3 and Deuterium content determines how enriched the mixture is. Different engines require a different mixture - generally, the bigger the engine or reactor, the purer the mixture can be. Since all the isotopes are stable, H-Fuel will not decay under normal circumstances, and can be stored indefinitely - unlike the fuel Gallia is rumored to use. It will react chemically with oxygen, since a large portion of the fuel consists of hydrogen isotopes. The main gas we mine for in the Crow is Helium-3. It forms as a byproduct of stellar fusion, and isn't normally found in a nebula. Why the Crow is so rich in this isotope has been subject of much scientific debate, but the Gas Miners Guild has built their fortunes on this anomaly. We use more Deuterium then we can extract from the Crow, so we actually import that isotope from elsewhere in Sirius.

The Farmers Alliance has a long history of procuring ships from their Corsair allies, the most notable being the Battleship Kumamoto. Unfortunately for the Farmers Alliance, the Kumamoto would prove to be nothing more than a White Elephant for the group, unable to provide the ship enough support or procure enough supplies for large scale operations, in addition to being too large for use within Kusari house space, the ship did little to further the Farmers cause.

The exchange of the Praefect Cruiser however came with a condition, the return of the Kumamoto to Corsair service, as the Corsair elders seek to recoup losses to their fleet as a result of ships lost supporting the ill-fated Gallic invasion of Bretonia, and conflict with the Coalition and Hessians in Omega-47.

Surveyed in late 655 AS, Hiura is a small rocky moon covered in a deep layer of ice. Despite its relatively small size, deep scans have revealed the moon to be primarily composed of silicate rock with a dense iron core. The resulting mass has enabled Hiura to retain a thin atmosphere composed mainly of oxygen, although it is still not breathable by humans. Several probes have examined the moon in greater detail over the years, but a lack of any appreciable resources has precluded any mining development.

In addition to a thin atmosphere Hiura also sports several rings, composed mainly of dust particles and ice crystals. At certain periods during its orbit of the stars, the light from both stars catch the rings at such an angle that the rings shimmer in every color of the light spectrum. If it weren't for the highly secretive nature of the system and presence of the Golden Chrysanthemums, Hiura would likely be a popular tourist destination. Even so, many within the Blood Dragons and the Golden Chrysanthemums visit the nearby Morioka base to catch a glimpse of the spectacular view that the planetoid offers.

1116054.text:
DIAMETER: 13,512 km
MASS: 6.20 x 10e24 kg
TERRAIN: Terrestrial
TEMPERATURE: -22°C to 32°C
ESCAPE VELOCITY: 12.60 km/sec

Originally charted in 655 AS by the Golden Chrysanthemum exploration vessel Hikki Maru, the planet Kitahara was noted for its extreme similarities to Malta, even down to a virtually identical climate and atmospheric composition. Fully habitable with a comfortable surface pressure and an atmosphere that is well within the tolerable limits for human respiration, the planet was eventually settled by large numbers of the Sisterhood and their families in 678 AS, with farms and homesteads becoming commonplace across the planet after only a few years.

Substantial deposits of iron, aluminium and niobium were discovered in the Okimura mountain range on the northern continent by several Blood Dragon planetologists, although it was not until 723 AS that mines were opened to take advantage of the availability of these resources. Initially the work was done by robotic mining machinery and human overseers, but as more prisoners were captured during fights against the Kusari Naval Forces, Farmers Alliance and the Hogosha, they started to be put to work within the mines. Captured female prisoners were either inducted into the Golden Chrysanthemums if suitable or sold off to the Outcasts and Blood Dragons in exchange for Cardamine and supplies.

By 766 AS, the planetary population was estimated to have reached at least twelve thousand. The majority of the inhabitants were still members of the Sisterhood, but a significant number were also Blood Dragons by now, who had relocated from Kyoto Base to a more pleasant planetary environment after having grown weary of living in space. The Blue Lotus Syndicate even constructed a number of offices and warehouses within the capital city of Yomi, to serve as a base to which to ship Cardamine to the Golden Chrysanthemums, all the way from Malta.

In 805 AS, after a convention held in Yomi by many eminent Golden Chrysanthemum and Outcast scientists, it was decided to attempt to seed Kitahara with Cardamine. The planetary conditions were largely ideal and very similar in many ways to Malta itself, so it was widely believed that Cardamine could indeed be grown on Kitahara. Experimental plantations were set up the following year, but unfortunately most of the seeded Cardamine initially died out due to inexperience by Sisterhood farmers in cultivating the grasses. By 809 AS, the Cardamine did manage to take hold in a few areas, but the yields were of horrendously poor quality compared to the Cardamine from Malta, but there was a severe side-effect to the meddling in the planet's ecosystem. The influence of the Maltese orange grass on Kitahara's ecology had begun killing off almost all other native and important crops and with the planetary population in excess of thirty thousand, starvation was looking to be a serious prospect. Many Blood Dragons also became appalled at the Cardamine experiments occurring on the planet and began moving off-world once more, most returning to Kyoto Base, while others moved to the Ryukyu and Mito bases.

To counter the potential starvation issues, the Golden Chrysanthemums have since embarked on the ambitious Chanai Biodome Project, covertly aided by Synth Foods, Inc, while at the same time continuing the Cardamine experiments on Kitahara with the Blue Lotus Syndicate. The Cardamine experiments have drawn considerable interest and outrage on Malta, with many Outcast Dons arguing amongst themselves on the viability and threat of such an undertaking. Some argue that it provides the Outcast people with a fallback safety net should Malta ever be nuked by the Corsairs, while others feel that it undermines their ability to effectively control the entire Cardamine market within the Sirius sector. Nevertheless the Blue Lotus Syndicate, an influential Outcast organisation by its own merits, maintains its support of the venture and has a sizeable presence on the planet.

1116056.text:

Planet Kushiro was surveyed in early 656 AS by the Golden Chrysanthemum scouts that were sent into Tau-65 to chart the system and list its suitability for secret installations. Deep scans revealed that the planetary composition is roughly 74% Hydrogen, 22% Helium and 4% of various other elements. Despite the large quantities of Hydrogen and Helium, no mining operations of any kind have as yet taken place to extract these valuable resources from Kushiro's atmosphere.

1116058.text: The X-ray Pulsar is officially classified as X-384 by scientists and interstellar navigation organisations, but most Golden Chrysanthemums simply refer to it by the name Ekitei. Ekitei releases periodic bursts of X-ray radiation, which can last from a fraction of a second up to several minutes between bursts. The pulses also tend to be directional, and any unshielded life forms would instantly die if exposed to an X-ray burst.

1116060.text: The Hachiman ice field has long been a source of water for the Golden Chrysanthemums and a number of small mining machines are scattered throughout the ice fields collecting water to bring back to Morioka base, where it is purified into a drinkable form.

1116062.text: An asteroid field with no appreciable resources, although it has a small measure of scientific interest as it is believed that the field may be the remnants of a large asteroid or small planetoid that got too close to one of the stars and broke up.

1116064.text:
The Nishiara asteroid field is believed to have once been a planet that collided with the X-ray Pulsar at the heart of the field. The asteroids contain reasonable quantities of uranium, niobium and iron, but due to the extremely high levels of radiation pouring from the X-ray Pulsar it is far too difficult and dangerous for anyone to extract the materials. The heavily shielded Kawada Research Complex lies within the field, and fortunately the area lying in the "shadow" of the base remains largely radiation free, thanks to the shielding provided by the station.

Due to the strength of the bursts, it is highly recommended for all vessels to avoid the Nishiara Asteroid Field at all costs, and numerous wrecks lie within the field as a testament to those who did not heed the warning buoys.

1116066.text: The Takkinai Cloud is beautiful mass of multiple inert gases, but despite the visual aesthetics of the cloud it remains a dangerous area to enter. Sensor efficiency is reduced to almost nothing and there are rumours of a dangerous minefield near the centre of the nebula, although what it defends is anyone's guess.

1116068.text: This debris field is all that remains of the Goyomai Outpost, destroyed by the Farmers Alliance in a large attack on the Tau-65 system in early 817 AS

1116070.text: The wreck of a Golden Chrysanthemum fighter destroyed in combat against the Farmers Alliance. The pilot of the fighter was either killed or taken prisoner by the Farmers Alliance, though there may still be equipment worth salvaging.

1116072.text: The wreck of a Farmers Alliance fighter destroyed in combat against the Golden Chrysanthemums. The pilot was captured and sent to Morioka Base for interrogation, though there may still be equipment left onboard.
