1116085.text: Takada Shipyard constructs a small amount of ships, but its main job is to provide maintenance for our existing craft and service the larger vessels of the Blood Dragons, Bretonians and the Outcasts. To fulfil this task, high temperature alloys, engine components and ship hull panels are the three components that we are always in need of here.

1116086.text: The Blood Dragons are over three hundred years older than our organisation. The Kusari Naval Forces never took the Golden Chrysanthemums seriously until 710 AS Then a diversionary attack that we carried out on Narita Outpost allowed the Blood Dragons to board Yokohama Shipyard in secrecy and steal the templates which were used on the construction of Takada Shipyard three years later.

1116087.text: Takada Shipyard sells a fairly large amount of Cardamine on board. You may say it's an odd place to find Cardamine, but it's all because of our experimental plantations down on planet Kitahara. We bring in the harvest here after it has been processed planetside. Some supplies are sold, others are shipped to Kawada Research Complex for research purposes. Only a very little amount of Kitahara's orange is used. Its quality is too poor for the rituals we perform at Chanai.

1116088.text: Stay away from that Outcast girl, Kaela Chavez; she's nothing but pure trouble. Honestly, I don't know why the Outcasts send along troublemakers like her on the Cardamine runs. She almost got into a fight the other day with one of the Blood Dragon supervisors, Toshio Yamada. I heard she doesn't like anyone from Kusari, and Toshio apparently spent a long time undercover in the Kusari Navy. Who really knows what it was about, though?

1116089.text: Planet Kitahara is in many ways common to Malta, which has grown countless tons of Cardamine every year for centuries, but adopting the orange culture here seems far more difficult than expected. There were some experimental plantations, but efforts proved to be almost futile as the grass produced only a small harvest of the drug. Cardamine grown here seems to be of lesser quality and also contains some previously uncalculated side effects. Kawada Research Complex has inched closer to eliminating these side effects, but for now the situation remains uncertain. I don't know if the research will ever be completed though, as the Outcasts are starting to protest against growing Cardamine off Malta. I guess they really don't want to lose their monopoly on the market.

1116090.text: I do not think much of the Outcasts around here. They bring the Cardamine in and we buy it and ship it around Kusari, that's all that there is to it. They are great fighters, for sure, but if it was up to me I would try to harness Cardamine on Kitahara. That would reduce the influence of the Outcasts in the region and provide a cheaper source of the drug.

1116091.text: Takada Shipyard is yet another sign of independence for our Sisterhood. With many of us showing an interest in what were typically male dominated arenas, such as engineering and computer technicians, it's only a matter of time before we get an independent source of ship repair and construction. At the present our allies are required for some of the things we simply cannot do ourselves. A few willing sisters are at Chanai, learning various things about engineering that will greatly help us in the future.

1116092.text: We have a lot of pride in our Sisterhood, and it manifests itself the most at Chanai Biodomes and here at Takada. While we may not be as visibly large and powerful as the Outcasts, the Golden Chrysanthemums certainly get a lot of money from our exclusive control of the Cardamine market in Kusari and this allows us to fund such expensive undertakings.

1116093.text: While we sometimes do manufacture the Corvo Cruiser here it is very rare. Our shipyard can handle capital class vessels however, and we often get those of our allies come in for repairs, which we are only too happy to do. Once we even had a Liberty Rogue destroyer dock here, which was quite a sight to behold. The vessel's name was the "Drax", I think. Her captain, Hugo Dravis, was taking her up for maintenance at Corsica, although whether his ship ever reached the Outcasts we do not know.

1116094.text: I spend most of my time out on patrol, and I'll be going out again shortly, just as soon as I've finished my drink. My squadron has to head over to the Battleship Matsuda in the Okinawa system, guarding a pirate transport full of supplies. It's a tough run, what with the infected in Tohoku, Farmers Alliance in Tottori and the Hogosha in Okinawa itself.

1116095.text: We do not design our own ships here; that is done at Kawada. Instead we assemble craft according to specific construction templates and give them occasional test runs before full service starts. Takada Shipyard serves as a ship maintenance facility for all our allies as well, although we don't get many out this far usually.

1116096.text: Even though Takada Shipyard is nearly a hundred years old, servicing ships is still a rather new business for us. It's not something which is easy to get the hang of, especially when women are denied careers in engineering at New Tokyo University. That is why Takada supports a certain amount of Outcasts and Blood Dragons. They help us with engineering issues that we simply have little to no expertise in.

1116097.text: We are lucky that the Outcasts stationed on Takada are of a calm, intelligent disposition. It can get much worse on Morioka base. Yesterday an Outcast had a little too much to drink and started picking on people in the bar. Three of our sisters tried to calm him down to no avail until a Blood Dragon, who walked in on the scuffle, came to our aid.

1116098.text: Lena Perabo often spends her time in this bar. She is an Outcast transport pilot that brings us regular Cardamine shipments. I have had a few talks with her before and she seems a decent type. She is always asking me about our culture and social life, and seems genuinely interested. She brought a new friend with her on her Cardamine run a couple days ago, by the name Kaela Chavez. This girl is pure trouble. I walked over to her and Lena to say hello when they first arrived. Kaela clammed up and left the docking bay with a scowl on her face, after I called her sister.

1116099.text: I wish I was stationed on the Battleship Matsuda. Working here at Takada is an honourable position and of great importance, to be sure, but nothing much ever happens here. It's the same stuff, just a different day.

1116100.text: Takada Shipyard has a well planned production cycle. All hijacked materials in Kusari fit for ship building are sent here. Then we process them into various alloys. Finally, processed metal is used to build ships; Pirate Transports and Eagles mainly. These consist of raiding parties, which will bring even more materials in.

1116101.text: Niobium is brought here from the mines on Planet Kitahara mostly. Prisoners work there continuously to provide Takada Shipyard with some raw materials that are readily available from the planet. Only male workers are used in the mines, however. Females either willingly join the Chrysanthemums and take the Rites of Matsuda, or are sold to the Outcasts as slaves. We detest slavery, but we cannot afford to risk female infiltrators in our ranks, nor for them to learn of our base locations by letting them go.

1116102.text: There's a jump hole that leads to the Blood Dragon Guard system, in the Ishijima asteroid field. It would be a good idea to ask permission though, as they sometimes don't like us travelling through there.

1116103.text: Most of the Golden Chrysanthemums pilots are women, although some are Blood Dragon Cardamine addicts. In recent years some Bretonian men and women have started to show an interest in our ways. I've recently met a man by the name of Charles Worthington on Morioka Base. He told me that certain military laws limit him in fighting the enemies of the Bretonian Queen to full extent that he'd like, and he wished to join our cause. We will probably keep him under surveillance for a while, but eventually he will have to participate in the Rites of Matsuda on Chanai before he is considered to be a true member of our organisation.

1116104.text: I met an old man on Roppongi station, who insisted on accompanying me back to the Tau-65 system. He did not seem suspicious and I offered him some Cardamine that I had brought to Roppongi with me. He not only refused, but he broke out in lectures about the evils of drug abuse. He even dropped my tube on ground and stepped on it. Now I understand why my sisters all believe that the old male hierarchy needs to be replaced.

1116105.text: I remember the very first time that I got to use Cardamine, as it happened before the initiation ritual. My friend took me to Cali Base in Tau-23, and we tried some there. All prospective recruits have to undergo Cardamine usage as a part of their training program, however, as it is needed to detect and remove all infiltration attempts. To this day, we have never been infiltrated because of our security measures, something that the Kusari navy or police can hardly claim.

1116106.text: I wasn't as skilled as many other sisters during my first years with our group and it was a very hard time for me. The Golden Chrysanthemums try to regulate the usage of Cardamine to lessen the chances of serious DNA mutations, but everyone inevitably gets changed in the end. While Cardamine enhances your fighting abilities, it can often be harmful in the long run. But I desperately craved for recognition within our sisterhood, and secretly acquired more of the drug from the Outcasts. Needless to say, the trick worked up until the point where my body could ingest the drug with no added benefits to my fighting skills. Now I know why it is strictly regulated, despite the need for continual doses.

1116107.text: If you're looking for a Cardamine expert, you came to the right place. I will not tell you many formulas on how to produce it or get into semantics, but I can surely give you a few tips on practical usage of the drug. There is no shame in admitting to being an addict. We are all addicts here. I was one of the top fighter aces in the Golden Chrysanthemums, but as we all know, luck only lasts so long. I know I helped out my sisters a lot when I was able to fly, but unfortunately my injuries forced me into retirement. I am just jealous about those who are still capable of fighting for our cause. I can't even pilot a transport now, which is why I work on Takada Shipyard.

1116108.text: I'm one of the Blood Dragons who supervises the workers here on Takada Shipyard. There is some honour in this work as we support our allies in our mutual struggle, but I'm still young and I could fight for the Hideyoshi. However, somebody must forge weapons so that other warriors can carry them into the heart of combat if the situation arises.

1116109.text: The Blood Dragons have a strict code of honour. A man who loses his honour must then also lose his head. We do not need drugs to define a true samurai from an imposter.

1116110.text: I do not agree with the use of Cardamine amongst the Golden Chrysanthemums, although I sympathise with their plight because I too have been oppressed. The Blood Dragon men are not as bad as those who run Kusari, but we still have less equality, as evidenced by the fact that I oversee dock workers in this shipyard, rather than fighting for the Hideyoshi clan.

1116111.text: There are Outcasts here from time to time, most notably Lena Perabo over there. She is always flying transports here and is a very excitable and personable girl, although the Outcasts always make me uneasy. It's those damn mask breathers they always have to wear. Sometimes I wonder if they're really human.

1116112.text: Joint projects like this should keep us all on good terms, proving that we're all able to work together. The Outcasts have mixed feelings however over the Cardamine production on Kitahara. We have no say in this, although our opinion on Cardamine is clear. However I am not so sure we will sit easy knowing there is a planet so nearby that is producing Cardamine.

1116113.text: Takada was built according to construction blueprints that the Blood Dragons stole from Yokohama Shipyard. Our enemy's designs will be used in the struggle against them now. There's a certain irony in that, don't you think?

1116114.text: Do not be mistaken. There was an alliance treaty signed between the Blood Dragons and the Golden Chrysanthemums, but the Kusari media often likes to portray us badly. Sometimes the Chrysanthemums can give us a bad image through their Cardamine usage, but there are strong ties that connect our two groups and we would never cause dishonour by abandoning or ignoring our allies.

1116115.text: I am a supervisor here at Takada. Monitoring the various industrial processes is my particular line of work, though. The conditions here are rather satisfying and the time is well spent, but there is one more reason why I'm here. It's Kitahara. I've been born and spent all my life on Kyoto base and I have never stepped on solid ground, until I came here. Kitahara looks breath taking from the orbit, and more so from the surface.

1116116.text: I do not believe in matriarchic rule, or patriarchal rule, for that matter. This is bunch of idealistic nonsense. No great revolution will bring happiness to people. Revolutions always come around again, hence their name. There will always be an elite minority with their foot firmly on the neck of a downtrodden majority, and also people who profit from the crushing, such as me. I'm an escort � the muscle.

1116117.text: I don't think much of the Golden Chrysanthemums myself. If you're looking for friendly company talk to Lena Perabo over there. She is a transport pilot for the Outcasts, and she's always running transports here, delivering building materials and supplies. Lena kept babbling about the sisterhood and their culture all the way here and it gives me a headache to think about it. To me the Golden Chrysanthemums are nothing but a bunch of extremists. The fact that I'm a woman doesn't make me your friend.

1116118.text: Honestly, sometimes I think Lena Perabo wants to join the Golden Chrysanthemums, the way she goes on about it. You'll always find her in this bar chatting to the Golden C. Girls while we're docked here. Go talk to her if you want to chat about the Sisterhood, because I'm not interested.

1116119.text: I really don't like the idea that Cardamine is being produced on Kitahara, and some see it as their attempt to steal the market for it. With the failures of the harvest and protests getting more frequent, the sisterhood are rethinking if they should try to grow it. If Cardamine is grown successfully I would expect the Dons back home to either shut it down or take it over completely, and I'll be glad of that, for one.

1116120.text: There are not many Outcast males here on Takada. The Golden Chrysanthemums prefer it that way and we don't have a problem with it. Their culture is definitely interesting, but they don't let us in too much. I hear there is some kind of ritual performed during the ceremony of initiation. I think it's called the Rites of Matsuda, but as I've said before, not much is revealed to people outside of their Sisterhood, not even to the Blood Dragons.

1116121.text: I pilot a transport here on a regular basis from Malta and Ruiz Base. The Golden Chrysanthemums are so much easier to deal with than the Blood Dragons, who view us with great suspicion. We often have trouble running our Cardamine shipments past their sentries, which is of course the reason why I'm often here. These ladies always need additional supplies of Cardamine.

1116122.text: I have just finished my Cardamine run to Chanai, and I docked here to get my transport checked out before I make the run back to Malta, so I thought I'd drop into the bar here for a chat. So feel free to pull up a seat and join me. I'd love to hear any tales of Kusari that you might have!

1116123.text: I want to hear Kusari gossip! I love Malta, don't get me wrong, but it is so boring there! All we do is grow Cardamine. That's often all the men talk about too; either that or the latest news from the core systems, and most of the news is out of date by the time it reaches Malta.

1116124.text: The Golden Chrysanthemums distribute Cardamine throughout Kusari space, but they seem to limit its' usage within their own community, especially among men and children who do not fight or participate in their cultural rituals. I've often thought of requesting permission to join, because I think their struggle is a worthwhile one, but I wonder how others in the Outcast community would react. Come to think of it, I expect that Kaela Chavez wouldn't be surprised or care much.

1116125.text: Don't be too hard on Kaela. She doesn't like anyone from Kusari very much, especially after her parents were killed by a Kusari Navy raid on Cali base, back in 796 AS She obviously doesn't share my optimism and enthusiasm for your cause.

1116126.text: For over a hundred and seventy five years, the Golden Chrysanthemums have been fighting for their equal rights. The organisation is only three years older than I am. I was here when they were constructing our first station in this system, Morioka Base, and I sincerely hope that I live long enough to see our struggle come to a positive conclusion.

1116127.text: I was born in 645 A.S, onboard Shinagawa station in the New Tokyo system. My mother was an ardent follower of Yuyu Matsuda's work and she was devastated when the news of Yuyu's death in 648 AS was broadcast on the colony news networks. She took me and left my father, moving to join the fledgling Golden Chrysanthemum movement onboard our secret base, Ainu Depot, in the Hokkaido system. I grew up there, being homeschooled by many different women from all walks of life, eventually taking the Rites of Matsuda myself and becoming a fully fledged member.

1116128.text: The Rites of Matsuda? Oh, that's our initiation ceremony into the Golden Chrysanthemums. The new potential member has to not eat any food for twenty four hours before we read sections of the book "Golden Chrysanthemum in Bloom" with them. They are then given a ceremonial dose of Cardamine, which is usually the very first one they have ever had, and is just enough to get them addicted, though sometimes people need further doses. Finally, the person is placed in a sensory deprivation chamber for a further twelve hours to acclimate themselves to the Cardamine. After that, you are inducted into the Golden Chrysanthemums organisation, and sworn to uphold the secrecy of our bases and the sanctity of our goals.

1116129.text: I put my long life down to healthy eating, plenty of exercise and Cardamine. The Outcasts have long told us that Cardamine has many adverse effects on the human genetic structure. Our own researchers, and those at Sendai Research Complex in the Okinawa system, believe that Cardamine was originally engineered by the Daam-K'Vosh for the Nomads. All I know is that it has increased my already fine intelligence and given me a much greater lifespan than I might otherwise have had.

1116130.text: We captured the Battleship Matsuda during the attack on Tekagi's fortress in 801 AS, although it was crippled outside Sendai Research Complex in the Okinawa system. We spent years hijacking various transports and supply convoys to get the parts we needed to bring it back up to complete operational status. These days, with the help of Synth Foods and Interspace Commerce, parts are slightly easier to come by, although we still have to smuggle them out here from Roppongi.

1116131.text: I remember the attack on Chanai like it was only yesterday. The Farmers Alliance somehow learned of our dealings with Synth Foods, and launched an attack to destroy our biodomes. They broke through our defensive perimeter and fired several torpedoes into the central biodome. My great granddaughter was killed in the attack. She was only fourteen. It just fills me with sorrow; that we must fight this terrible war just so we may enjoy the same rights and privileges as men do in our own nation.

1116132.text: Because we were only just starting to get organised, shortly after Yuyu's death in 648 AS, Morioka base took several years and a phenomenal portion of our resources to build, but it paid off in the end. Thankfully we have never needed the fallback position that Morioka initially represented, and it has allowed us to further develop the Tau-65 system as a whole. I do remember one particular incident though, in 703 AS, when several habitation modules on Morioka were destroyed in an accident involving a damaged fighter craft. A lot of people died, and it took months to fully repair the damage.

1116133.text: My mother once said that I am related to our honoured founder, Yuyu Matsuda. Apparently, one of my ancestors was Yuyu's sister, Chiemi Matsuda. I like to think that Yuyu would be proud to know that her family follows in her footsteps.

1116134.text: It is amazing to think that Hisako Takahashi was alive when Yuyu Matsuda was, even if she was only three years old when Yuyu performed ritual suicide. I often enjoy talking to her about history and the things she has seen, and the people that have come and gone in both our organisation and throughout Kusari. It gives you an insight into life that history books and archive footage simply cannot. I suggest talking with her sometime; she knows many things that might be of interest to you.

1116135.text: Chanai is called "The village" within our community, because that is where our families live. Golden Chrysanthemums are mostly women, but our families reside here in safety. When Golden Chrysanthemums take off after visiting their relatives, they usually leave their husbands and children behind. Sometimes the men fight also, but most of them occupy other positions such as engineers and station security.

1116136.text: Blood dragons addicted to Cardamine are forced to leave Kyoto. The only other ally they have is us. Sometimes they come looking for sanctuary onboard Chanai, but the majority maintain their flying skills intact and apply for a new vessel the moment they land on Takada Shipyard. Such valuable pilots are far too skilled to waste their abilities by having them work as mechanics on Takada like most other men. They are normally recruited to our ranks and become one of the very few men to fly in our organisation.

1116137.text: Chrysanthemums come and leave Chanai, but most can never afford to stay here for too long, due to our never ending efforts against the Kusari Navy. Only older, veteran women live and retire here. The veterans watch after the local population and run the medical facilities, while most elders spend their retirement teaching the children in our schools.

1116138.text: I've been on sensor duty for the last twelve hours and just signed off, but I'm back on duty again in six hours because my replacement is sick. Apparently she hasn't been taking her daily Cardamine supplements and is going through severe withdrawal symptoms, so she's down in medical. Please leave me be, I want to have a drink in peace before I try to grab what little sleep I can.

1116139.text: I was on sensor duty the other day and we picked up some strange readings. According to the computers we had two Farmers Alliance fighters inbound, and we dispatched a fighter wing to take care of them. Just before they engaged, they realised that it was a heavily damaged Golden Chrysanthemum fighter. The IFF was malfunctioning and the damage had destroyed her communications array. She was lucky to have not been destroyed by our automated defences.

1116140.text: The Farmers are manipulated by Samura, but they aren't our primary concern. Samura is the one to look out for, as they have their sticky fingers in ever pie throughout Kusari. The Golden Chrysanthemums used to be content with the Farmers Alliance's activities before the Chanai biodome project started, but after we made a deal with Synth Foods our relationship has become increasingly hostile towards each other. The Battle of Chanai resulted in a virtual declaration of war between the two factions and the fighting has been vicious ever since.

1116141.text: I've returned to Chanai after two months spent in space with only the occasional resupply landings on Roppongi. I was delighted to see my children and partner again, but today an elder has contacted me with instructions to lead an assault wing into space again soon. It never ends.

1116142.text: Chanai is home for most of the Golden Chrysanthemum medical facilities, and many injured pilots end up here for treatment. We also use Cardamine contained in storage depots for medicinal purposes. Our sisterhood is quite advanced in this area of expertise, and our medical facilities are such that even the Blood Dragons sometimes come here to use them.

1116143.text: Many come to Chanai to relax and enjoy a peaceful life which is largely present on the station. Schools, medical facilities and even recreational centres are present here. Some of our people will occasionally move to Morioka Base, but Planet Hiura is the only thing to see around there now. The whole base has turned into a highly specialised commercial outpost. Most of the visiting Blood Dragons go to Morioka or Takada though. Chanai is just another space station for them and they are always thrilled to see more planets. You would be too if you'd spent whole your life on Kyoto.

1116144.text: As you know, a large portion of the population on Chanai consists of our male partners and elders. The Golden Chrysanthemums sometimes have the opportunity to visit their families, but we cannot stop the fight for equal rights for too long. It is a shame really, because I miss my friends and family a lot while I am away.

1116145.text: I joined the Golden Chrysanthemums in ignominy after coming second place in the Miss New Tokyo pageant in 806 AS The all-male judges were so furious after they found traces of Cardamine in my quarters, that I was lucky I wasn't disqualified or arrested. I bet that Hiro Mamiya put the drug in there; it would be just like her. She didn't deserve to win!

1116146.text: Hiro Mamiya's career went down in flames in 807 AS, not longer after my own. She was a superstar who had it all, but threw it all away on her drug crazed binges. Now look at us both, Cardamine addicts on a forgotten outpost in the middle of nowhere, remembered only with dishonour in our home nation. And yet, it is all her fault!

1116147.text: I used to be a supermodel and singer back on New Tokyo, but I ended up becoming addicted to Cardamine. The media eventually found out and my career came crashing down in ruins, not long after I won the Miss New Tokyo pageant in 806 AS I know it is my fault for that, but I cannot help but feel a little bitter. In any case, after the Golden Chrysanthemums approached me I took up their offer and joined, donating a large portion of my money to their cause.

1116148.text: I've always wanted to be a singer, ever since I was a little girl on Kyushu. My father was a good man who paid for my private tuition with a music teacher, because the colleges on Kyushu don't allow women to take courses there. It is just another damning indictment of the male-driven society that the Kusari government perpetuates.

1116149.text: Don't listen to Eri Kitayama bitching about me, she's just sour at not being crowned Miss New Tokyo in 806 AS She still came in at second place though, so she has no cause for complaints. I swear I didn't plant any Cardamine in her quarters, although she will tell you differently, no doubt.

1116150.text: We used to buy Cardamine from the Outcasts only to satisfy our own needs and perform ceremonial rituals, but once the Golden Chrysanthemums started to distribute it amongst the Kusari population, we soon realised the previously untapped commercial potential within our nation and started dealing ourselves. The Outcasts are suspicious about our intentions of expanding the Cardamine trade, but we still buy most of our Cardamine from them, rather than producing it ourselves on Kitahara, which leaves them with the monopoly.

1116151.text: Biodomes bought from Synth Foods have greatly increased our food production and our ability to sustain larger population, but it came at a heavy cost. The Farmers Alliance launched a full scale attack on Chanai in 812 A.S and over two thousand people were killed during the battle. Our hatred became mutual and full scale war broke out between us. Was it worth it? Decide for yourself.

1116152.text: Most of our sisters enjoy Synth Paste with a passion. It is relatively cheap and symbolises the free market economy and equal rights in Liberty, things that we greatly desire to see in our own nation.

1116153.text: The Blood Dragons are not the only ones to come to Chanai for a rest. In fact, Chanai is a popular recreational centre amongst all of the Tau systems. I think I even saw a Synth Foods employee walk into the bar earlier.

1116154.text: We, the Blood Dragons, take our duties seriously. Every man, woman and a child regardless of age knows how to handle a blaster and has at least basic piloting skills. Remaining sharp at all times is difficult and occasional rest is crucial. That is why I'm here. I will be back to the forbidden city with my senses ready and mind sharp.

1116155.text: I used to live on Planet Kitahara before the Cardamine experiments were started there, and after that I moved to Chanai. I can't stand that drug. While the Golden Chrysanthemums embrace it, the Blood Dragons have refused to touch it. How can the Golden Chrysanthemums not see that Cardamine is ruining our society?

1116156.text: In many ways Chanai is a much more relaxed station than Takada Shipyard or Morioka base, regardless of the luxury of vacationing planetside on Kitahara. The nebula clouds of Chugoku often become quite claustrophobic and Chanai offers all a broken spirit needs. There are many recreational centres along with various resorts and tranquil gardens within the biodomes.

1116157.text: I've been assigned to the Golden Chrysanthemums in an advisory capacity to oversee the biodomes they have here. It has taken a great deal of resources for these women to construct the biodomes, but their efforts have finally paid off. Now nobody in their organisation will go hungry, at least.

1116158.text: I was present during the attack on this facility by the Farmers Alliance in 812 AS The destruction of the central biodome killed over a thousand people, including my friend Richard Stackpole, a Synth Foods engineer who was working on the biodomes.

1116159.text: Have you heard of South Park? It's not far from Crichton Springs on Planet Denver. I was born there in 765 A.S, to a chef who worked in one of the restaurants there. After graduating from Denver High, I applied to join Synth Foods Inc. and I've been working for them ever since. It's not a bad job if you can avoid running afoul of the angry farmers in Rheinland and Kusari.

1116162.text: We made a considerable amount of profit from the biodomes project, while also expanding Synth Foods, Inc. influence further into Kusari, but it was all to everyone's good, since now none of the Golden C. will starve. I know that the credits that we received are most likely stolen from the Kusari government or made from the sales of Cardamine, but to me the Golden Chrysanthemums are all legitimate business partners. It is the fault of the Kusari government that they exist, and we sympathise with their cause.

1116163.text: ...I'm gonna make love to you woman, gonna lay you down by the fire...Oh sorry, I didn't see you there. I was just practicing my singing for the concert tonight.

1116164.text: Kawada Research Complex has a great need for Superconductors and MOX as well as a great deal of scientific equipment. All these materials will speed up our research on weapons technology.

1116165.text: The Suncannon D was a breakthrough in our weapons technology. It was designed right here on Kawada and assembled on Takada Shipyard in 815 AS It's one of the few weapons to match the advanced weaponry that the Kusari Naval Forces use these days.

1116166.text: The Golden Chrysanthemums have been through a lot since the beginning. The most recent event was the Nomad War. The Blood Dragons had a fair amount of knowledge about the Nomads as they worked together with the Order back in the day, but the Golden Chrysanthemums never knew that such a threat existed until the battle for Tekagi's fortress in the Tohoku system in 801 AS Regardless, we aided the Blood Dragons in their siege of Tekagi's fortress. We gained control of the Battleship Matsuda during that battle, which you will find stationed in the Okinawa system these days.

1116167.text: The Ekitei X-Ray Pulsar is the jewel of this system. It periodically releases massive bursts of energy in the form of x-ray radiation into space. It does not take advanced technology to shield oneself from the radioactive pulses, but the rays may still become deadly if we could concentrate them into a straight line, rather than spreading outwards in a directionless manner.

1116168.text: Ekitei is the reason why this research complex was built in the first place. Well, that and the development of new weapons and space craft. If we could tame the power of the X-ray pulses and combine this technology into a new weapons line, we could punch through our enemies' shielding like it wasn't even there. I know such research is already underway, but the theories behind the technology are nothing but conjecture so far.

1116169.text: The purpose of this research station is far more complex than exploring the anomalies such as Ekitei. One such practical use of this station is an attempt at creating new blasters and rifles. Some ships are designed here also, but all of the final safety checks and structural testing are done on Takada Shipyard.

1116170.text: There are so many fields and planets capable of holding resources in the Tau-65 system. Too bad they are so hard to reach due to the radiation and deep space conditions. Did you know that the temperature on Hiura can go down to 140 degrees below zero, and that is during the day time? At least Planet Kitahara is fully capable of supporting life. I am told it is almost identical to Malta, but I have never been there before.

1116171.text: The Nishiara Asteroid Field is heavily saturated with radiation, but Kawada's shielding protects very well. If we could understand better how Ekitei works, it would allow us to harness the power of the pulsar to provide this station with cheap energy.

1116172.text: I'm an assistant to Minako Okada, the research team leader of the Blood Dragons on Kawada. She used to run the research in the facility, but now all the interns have passed their training and acquired enough experience to carry out research on their own. Perhaps soon I will be appointed to the staff myself.

1116173.text: The Takkinai Cloud has unusual readings. Scans reveal frequencies common to the Ice Fields around Planet Harris in the Tau-31 system. Unfortunately, the radiation from the nearby pulsar prevents further scans into Takkinai Cloud.

1116174.text: The Ishijima Asteroid Field was created when a small planetoid collided with the Ekitei pulsar. We're not sure what really happened, but it sure is fuelling the imaginations of our more excitable researchers. However, besides its scientific interest Ishijima Asteroid Field has no value whatsoever.

1116175.text: Have you heard of Hisako Takahashi? She is over a hundred and seventy years old. Surely an amazing age to live up to, isn't it? We believe it to be a result of DNA mutations caused by Cardamine. Regular doses must have changed her genetic structure somehow and extended her lifespan. Don't get too enthusiastic just yet, though. The mutations seem to be erratic and probably do cause unknown side effects. It is possible that Hisako has been incredibly lucky, but unfortunately more research needs to be done before we can conclusively prove anything.

1116176.text: Ekitei represents a great scientific opportunity for us. Perhaps we would have never even been appointed here if not for the privilege of studying pulsar radiation. Training a self-sufficient research station wasn't our primary concern, although don't think I didn't enjoy it. Many of these Golden Chrysanthemum women are very enthusiastic and highly intelligent.

1116177.text: Many of the Golden Chrysanthemums see it as some kind of reward for working with me, and I suppose I symbolise something to them as they cannot easily become engineers themselves since most of them have never received any formal training in Kusari colleges and universities. Most of them that I work with here have shown a natural talent for engineering and can pick up multiple concepts quite quickly. I can see it's only a matter of time before we start seeing plenty of Golden Chrysanthemums engineers working out of our stations.

1116178.text: I am proud of the Golden Chrysanthemum scientists on Kawada. They were completely green when we first arrived. Although they were well disciplined and well taught, they had little expertise on how the practical side of things work. The girls have made an astonishing progress so far, and that's what you can do with a small group of progressive students when you give them a solid grounding in scientific processes.

1116179.text: Our work is mostly done here, but we have been granted a unique opportunity to study the Ekitei X-ray pulsar in the system, therefore very few of our scientists actually left. Ekitei presents a lot of untapped potential. The power behind its untamed fury may be the key to solving power crises throughout Kusari, and give us a bargaining chip with which to force political concessions from the government.

1116180.text: Greetings, what drink may I get you? Certainly, take a seat and it will be delivered directly.

1116183.text: Some people treat us with contempt for the creation of Synth Paste, but we're helping to put an end to starvation throughout the colonies with our product and there are many people alive today who wouldn't be if it weren't for our food. Just ask the Golden Chrysanthemums if you don't believe me.

1116184.text: It was Interspace Commerce who put us in contact with members of the Golden Chrysanthemums, so that we could negotiate a deal for the biodomes. We help them and in return they are better able to attack the Farmers Alliance, which further helps our business interests in Kusari. This way, we all win.

1116185.text: I joined the Golden Chrysanthemums in ignominy after coming second place in the Miss New Tokyo pageant in 806 AS The all-male judges were so furious after they found traces of Cardamine in my quarters, that I was lucky I wasn't disqualified or arrested. I bet that Hiro Mamiya put the drug in there; it would be just like her. She didn't deserve to win!

1116186.text: The Blood Dragon researchers on Sendai are now are only a little more experienced than the scientists onboard the Kawada Research Complex. That's why we used to need their help, but now Golden Chrysanthemums are able to run the place on their own. Together, with our Blood Dragon friends, we make a fine team in solving mysteries of the galaxy.

1116283.text:
Early geological surveys show remarkable heterogeneity in the debris, with a small but significant fraction exhibiting an uncommon, squamous spongey deposition of sulfur deposits that have, up until now, only been seen in Texas - while no other surveyed samples show anything remotely similar.

A significant part of the debris consists of wreckage of derelict Libertarian technology of approximately 300 years old. Preliminary research indicates a possibility of a link to the infamous Dallas incident. Further research attempts are stalled by ships regularly going missing in the field due to unknown reasons.

1116285.text: A large cloud covering the western edge of the Omicron Nu system. Initial attempts to navigate and explore the nebula quickly revealed just how dangerous the Omicrons can truly be. The Mariana Trench Nebula contains large explosive gas pockets, significantly slowing down any surveys.

1116288.text:
Initial surveys of the interior shows a relatively intact superstructure and pockets of thin pressurization in some of the more well preserved sections near the service and waste reclamation sectors. Many of the crew and command quarters exhibit signs of indiscriminate and intense struggle. Cursory analysis of the intensive carbon scoring found throughout the habitation decks seem to exclusively correspond to blast profiles of Detroit Muntions Lot E291-F standard issue service firearms, the manufacturer and model of a firearm widely distributed to the servicemen of the Liberty Navy between 492 and 534 AS. While dried blood and small amounts of vacuum preserved human tissue have been found, the initial survey and reclamation teams have yet to find any substantial collections of human remains that can be tied to a specific service roster, but it is possible that this is the Battleship Tennessee, lost during the Texas Incident.

Engineering and Instrumentation sections are entirely depressurized, and show signs of multiple attempts at salvage over the course of many decades. Several generations of derelict breaching pods remain anchored to the hull, while empty breach points show scorching characteristics of emergency thruster burns that are quite unusual in normal detachment and return operations.

1116290.text:
DIAMETER: 68,900 km
MASS: 1.56 x 10e27 kg
SURFACE TEMPERATURE: -56°C to 0°C
ESCAPE VELOCITY: 49.89 km/sec

A lonely, cyan gas giant inhabiting the far periphery. Preliminary orbital scans conducted by Ageiran pioneers proved futile, due to the dense gasses found in the stratosphere. Its ring has faint traces of Azurite Gasses.

Pairing this initial data, researchers speculate that a surface probe would unearth more than meets the eye.

1116297.text: Senor, I swear to you on my honor I had no idea what was going on at this base. Our patrol orders always emphasized that we should tractor in any Outcast escape pods, whether the pilot was alive or dead, and bring them back to base. How were we to know that the organs being sent to Crete were from Slaves instead?

1116298.text: Si, of course I had suspicions, I am no fool, but the doctors here had us all convinced that organs from Outcasts were not saturated with cardamine after all, in spite of all that we were taught in our training. Who am I to argue with doctors? I am just a pilot. When a superior officer gives you instructions, you don't debate them, you just shut your mouth and obey.

1116299.text: I'm glad those traitorous scoundrels were executed for bringing Slaves here and slaughtering them for profit. Everyone knows that the Outcasts use Slaves to work in their cardamine fields. The Corsair nation is far too noble and virtuous to allow such things. If we find any other traitors involved in slavery, we should execute them also. Personally, I suspect the nearby Zoners of being involved somehow. Who else has easy access to this region of space and connections back in the Houses? Those Freeports are dens of iniquity and infamy, I tell you!

1116300.text: So, it appears that the Corsairs are not so honorable after all! They have spread their loathsome propaganda for years about the "crime of Outcast slavery." Now they are revealed as hypocrites and liars who massacre the innocent out of greed. No one with any sense could believe that organs from Outcasts could be implanted into non-Outcasts. The Corsairs are not even smart enough to invent credible lies to cover up their criminality.

1116301.text: When the Corsairs started retrieving even the escape pods of our dead from battles, we knew they were up to some new treachery. Now we know they were using our fallen heroes to cover up the truth of their awful deeds: killing Slaves to harvest their organs for sale to their rich "Elders" on Crete. What an abomination! Outcasts have no need for such wickedness to sustain us in our old age, as long as the cardamine fields continue to give us life.

1116302.text: Of course there are no Slaves working our cardamine fields. That's just Corsair propaganda. Those workers are liberated from the bondage of crushing poverty in Liberty, or are poor convicted Rogues and Junkers whom we save from corrupt LPI wardens. These people literally beg us for the chance to come to Malta and labor like men for their bread, instead of wasting away their lives in Liberty's corrupt dungeons.

1116326.text:
1. COMMUNITY RULES

1.1 This is a Freelancer-based role-play community. Character names and behavior must be realistic in the Discovery Freelancer universe (no player nationality tags, memes, pop-culture references, or direct imports from other universes like Star Wars). Realistic role-play also means that characters can't use information they didn't receive in the game universe.

1.2 Don't insult, harass, or threaten players outside of role-play. Don't use racist, graphic, pornographic, obscene, or law-violating materials in or out of role-play. Don't repeatedly target specific players or groups with the intention of ruining their game experience. Don't mislead players about rules or pose as an admin or "admin friend" to gain an advantage.

1.3 Everything must be in understandable English. Some non-English words can enhance role-play, but the meanings should be kept understandable to English-only speakers.

1116328.text:
2. SERVER GAMEPLAY

2.1 Out-Of-Character (OOC) chat should be avoided in local and system chat. Using // in front of OOC messages is recommended.

2.2 A character/ship must use one single ID and follow the permissions and restrictions of ID, ship, and equipment infocards.

2.3 Players using Recruit ID and players below level 30 may not be attacked unless they: attack first, fire cruise-disruptors, refuse to stop stalking, carry a codename weapon, or take active part in role-play.

2.4 All attacks must be a result of roleplay. Players must say more than one line and give reasonable time for the opponent to react before initiating an attack. Non-Nomads may always attack Nomads, but role-play is still required. See rule 5.1 before attacking a Player Owned Base.

2.5 If you die in any way during PvP, you must leave the system the fight took place in and not re-enter it on any characters for two hours. You may not carry cargo, engage in player interactions, or be attacked while leaving. You also can't attack the player(s) you died to on any of your characters for two hours.

2.6 The same as 2.5 applies if you dock within 15K of your enemy while in PvP, with the exceptions that you may re-enter the system to trade, keep your cargo, and players may attack you while you're leaving the system.

2.7 Demands should be reasonable and only one monetary or cargo demand can be issued during each piracy interaction.

2.8 Don't disconnect in space to escape interaction. If you get disconnected, log back on immediately and apologize to the players you were interacting with. If you can't apologize ingame, do so in the forum thread titled "DISCONNECTED". Don't rejoin a fight without permission from your adversary after getting disconnected.

2.9 Connecticut is a system where players aren't required to role-play and may only attack with the adversary's consent. Bastille is a system that imprisons rule breakers until they agree to obey server rules.

1116330.text:
3. HIRED GUNS AND BOUNTIES

3.1 All contracts and bounties must be justified within roleplay and conform to IDs. A character may be hired ingame or on the forum by non-generic IDed (non Freelancer, Pirate, or miner) players, for a minimum of 1 million credits per target. Targets must be informed of the contract/bounty originator before the attack. The reputations of employer and employee must be neutral or friendly to each other, and they must both be hostile to the target.

3.2 Bounties and contracts made while the employer is offline or PvP-dead must be posted in the "Bounty Offices" sub-forum. Employers must specify their name and affiliation, and also specify and verify the affiliation of those who may claim the bounty. A limited payout number, expiry date, or exclusivity to pre-registered bounty board members may be specified beforehand. Players may not hire exclusively their own characters.

3.3 Forum-Bounties on factions instead of named individuals (blanket bounties) may only be issued (or sponsored within roleplay) by official factions and governments. These may also be compensated through flat rate payments of at least 30 million credits per month to individuals or factions. Non-generic IDed unofficial factions may sponsor internal blanket bounties for members of their player or NPC faction only.

3.4 Attacking someone for non-existing contracts or non-claimable bounties, as well as not visibly claiming payment within 7 days of an alleged forum-bounty kill, will result in sanction. Payments must be made within two weeks of a legitimate claim.

1116332.text:
4. FACTIONS

4.1 Players may create a faction for any publicly available ID they want, if the faction uses a single ID, IFF, and tag. Every faction must have one leader and at least one second-in-command who speak for it. It's recommended but optional for unofficial factions to post descriptions in the Unofficial Factions and Groups sub-forum, explaining their background, diplomacy, goals, and to ask for community feedback. It's also recommended to create roleplay message logs on the forum.

4.2 Official status is awarded following the "Achieving Official Faction Status" post on the forum. Official Factions (OFs) must have a public feedback thread they answer to on the forum. They have the following Official Faction Rights (OFRs). All instances of OFR use must be documented by forum roleplay.

-OFR 1: OF leaders ranked first or second in command have in-roleplay authority over characters of the same NPC affiliation, regarding diplomacy and strategic/tactical direction. They may not require anyone to follow non-canon or unreasonable roleplay. Disobeying legitimate orders may result in roleplay consequences such as ingame arrest, court-martial, and in extreme cases ingame force.

-OFR 2: OFs who planned an event with at least 24 hours notice on the forum can restrict the participation of others in that event. It shouldn't severely limit another faction's activities in their own ZoI or provide unfair protection from logical roleplay consequences.

-OFR 3: OFs may request that the reputation of a player's ship be set hostile towards their NPC faction, by posting in the appropriate Violation Reports sub-forum. They must provide evidence of forum roleplay and interaction between the OF and the character. Ships subjected to OFR3 may treat ships of the issuing faction (except transports) as hostile targets.

-OFR 4: OFs may bounty or attack a player who uses their affiliation's technology without the faction ID nor official permission, regardless of their diplomacy with the user's faction. Permissions may only be given by an OF affiliated with the manufacturer of the technology, and must be documented in roleplay on the forum.

1116334.text:
5. PLAYER OWNED BASES

5.1 Dealing more damage to a Player Owned Base (POB) than needed to prevent a ship from docking must be preceded by forum roleplay and a post in the Attack Declaration Thread at least 8 hours (core 1 bases) or 24 hours (core 2 and higher) prior to the attack. Attack declarations are valid for 2 weeks.

5.2 No roleplay is required prior to building a Core 1 base, but it must make sense in roleplay. Name, location and IFF of bases are permanent and can't be changed after construction. Bases within 15k distance of mining fields may not advance beyond Core 2. Core upgrades have requirements listed in the "Player Owned Base Upgrades" forum thread.

5.3 POBs are destructible when unprotected, so it's recommended you inform yourself about House laws and fees and local diplomacy in order to build in a well protected location. POBs in systems bordering House space may not be engaged by House forces for lack of payment of fees, but can still fall prey to other factions.

1116336.text:
6. CHEATING

The following cheats and exploits are forbidden:
6.1 Modifying your Discovery Freelancer installation, using third-party tools, or abusing glitches/bugs in order to gain advantages over other players.
6.2 Running the game with framerates above 155fps. Computers running uncapped framerate must use a third party program to limit the FPS to below 155.
6.3 Using cruise disruptors or missiles in order to track a ship that has successfully cloaked.
6.4 Intentionally ramming a capital ship in order to ''flip'' it or ''catapult'' your ship away from it.
6.5 Suicide trading and intentionally self/team-killing during Combat-Event-Plugin battles in order to prevent the opponent from scoring points.
6.6 Connecting to the server with more than one character at a time (Multiboxing). Players sharing a network connection may not engage in trading/mining at the same time.

1116338.text:
7. SANCTIONS

7.1 Administrators will impose sanctions on players who violate rules or harm server gameplay. Admins are obliged to:
-Safeguard the community, server, and forums.
-Be fair and treat all players equally.
-Not mix server roleplaying with server administration in any way.
-Not ignore reported rule violations.

7.2 Depending on severity and amount of rule violations, sanctions can range from a warning, credit fine, loss of equipment, probation periods with removal of certain privileges, and bans of varying duration. Sanctions will appear in forum threads detailing the offenses and punishments.

7.3 If someone shows disregard for the rules even after being informed of rules and violations, players can file a rule violation report in the appropriate sub-forum. Playing Discovery Freelancer as a community is less anonymous than other games, and therefore things are often taken more personal. Don't attempt to use violation reports for personal revenge. If you're angry, take time to gather and present the evidence properly and make sure you're not mistaken when you're calm.

1116394.text: Normally, captains of Zoner capital ships try to avoid our patrols. However, some of them seem to have lost their mind. We shot down one of their "Fearless" cruisers this week. It's not an honor, but when duty calls, you pay the price, heh?

1116395.text: Yeah, just having a quick drop here since we're mobilizing to Los Dragos. It's a cushy job, since the local Zoners dropped their guns the moment the 5th Cavalry dropped from the sky. We have no problems apart from some drunkards still thinking they live without law since then.

1116396.text: Welcome to Planet Exeter, the gateway to the deep Omegas. If you're headin' that way, you'd be wise to pack up with supplies, the jump holes tend to be more unstable further into the Walker Nebula.

1116397.text: Did you hear about that riot over in Las Palmas? Someone riled up the Zoners and they took out their frustations on the local constabulary. Smashed the building up pretty bad, and even roughed up a few of the constables on duty

1116398.text: This planet is a nightmare for counter-terrorist operations. Seems like half the population left in towns is probably either a Molly or a sympathizer, the Zoners are all packing heat, and I haven't even mentioned the Corsairs hiding in the hills.

1116399.text: I've just gotten back from a 14-hour shift doing forensic work on a caravan that was hit by the Corsairs. They chased off most of the civilians and shot anyone that tried to fight back, before stealing anything not tied down. Absolutely barbaric, really.

1116400.text: There's a broadcast going around of that terrorist group, you know the one from the Nomad War, that declared war on Bretonia for invading Gran Canaria. Can't say I'm too worried though, we run a pretty tight ship here.

1116401.text: Can't say I'm too fond of what we're doing here- most of these people are just civilians that wanted a bit of space to themselves. But the Kingdom needs its space now, and I've got family back home that could use a safe place like this

1116402.text: CO says we'll have to start doing patrols out into the forests. New Scotland Yard wants us to clear out all the pirates hiding in them, but here's the thing: I'm from Leeds, I'd never even seen a forest till I was stationed on Cambridge, and even then there was so much red tape involved to go in them that I never could. So how am I supposed to chase a bunch of pirates in one?

1116403.text: You know, as far as Invasions go this one was fairly easy, and bloodless. I guess we just came out of nowhere so quickly, the Zoners didn't have time to react. Not that they're happy about it of course, I hear there are some die hard types in the country side, wanting to wage a resistance campaign. Bloody fool idea if you ask me, we have more troops than the entire population!

1116404.text: You know, as far as Invasions go this one was fairly easy, and bloodless. I guess we just came out of nowhere so quickly, the Zoners didn't have time to react. Not that they're happy about it of course, I hear there are some die hard types in the country side, wanting to wage a resistance campaign. Bloody fool idea if you ask me, we have more troops than the entire population!

1116405.text: The initial invasion may have gone seamlessly, but now that everyone has settled in the Corsairs are kicking up a fuss in the hills. Not sure what makes them think they can win but they've already caused some problems for us by blowing up bridges and a few dams. It's not helping the situation, every time they made a display of themselves, it gives the rest of them the idea that resisting is a good thing. If we don't correct this soon, more people will get hurt.

1116406.text: My job is basically peacekeeping and liaison work with the locals. The Armed Forces are on security detail, so they don't have time to deal with angry shopkeepers or disgruntled traders. Personally, I think it's just them wanting to avoid the locals, make the Police deal with the fallout. All those troops and they can't spare a few to do my job? Rubbish.

1116407.text: We've been sent to oversee the establishment of a police garrison here on Sydney, it's a far easier place to police than the slums of Leeds that's for sure, but we're having a hard time getting recruits. The local militia proved to be unwilling to help us so we disbanded them, from what I hear, most of them have taken up with the corsairs in the hinterlands, so we've had to call in more officers and up the recruitment campaign. I guess we'll see how well it works

1116408.text: Been hauling for Bowex for a couple of years now and got a lot of experience under my belt when it comes to the Omegas. I've been extorted by Corsairs, Hessians and who knows what else. In comparison to that, bringing all kinds of equipment for the Armed Forces to this frozen rock isn't all that bad. Only the Mollys really cause some trouble from time to time, but with the Stirling just next door, we've never had to worry about travelling without escort. s

1116409.text: People are giving me strange looks on the streets. I'm just doing logistics for the Armed Forces here, but I swear some of the inhabitants here can bore holes into your soul with their stares. Worse still, even when I'm out of the uniform, it seems like people aren't really sure who to trust anymore. There are so many citizens of Bretonia who came here recently, the natives encounter every stranger with a lot of distrust. I'm not sure how healthy this is going to be in the long run.

1116410.text: [826 AS] University Of Cambridge Chancellor Is Missing

1116411.text: CAMBRIDGE -- 826 AS -- The Chancellor of the University of Cambridge was reported missing last month by the Vice Chancellor. Professor William Mortimer was reported to have been on Planet Gran Canaria at the time of the nuclear explosion that occurred last month following the failed negotiations that took place prior to annexation. Police say they are following several leads, although the current situation within the house and the Omega-49 system may delay the investigation "We believe that the disappearance of the Chancellor is likely to be politically motivated" A police spokesperson said earlier, adding "Because of the situation in the Omega-49 system, the Bretonian Police Authority is working closely with Armed Forces personnel on the ground to examine whatever evidence may arise". Professor Mortimer was known to have been a supporter of the Zoner position in the Annexation and was not on official business at the time of his disappearance. Police are appealing to the public for any leads.

1116413.text: GRAN CANARIA -- 826 AS -- Following the recent detonation of a nuclear device on Planet Gran Canaria and the failure of Bretonian diplomats to secure an agreement from the local Zoner population, the Bretonian Government has authorized the annexation of the planet. This comes after years of tension as the system was well known to have supplied and aided Corsair and Molly raiders. Now with the Gallic Invasion reaching New London, the patience of the Bretonian Crown has reached its end. Unwilling to allow the removal of the planet's Corsair population, the Zoners chose to resist the advances of the Bretonian diplomatic corps and as a result the Annexation began in force last Monday with all major settlements falling to the Bretonian Armed Forces within a few days. While sporadic resistance continues, the Armed Forces, along with elements of the Bretonian Police Authority report success in pacifying most of the population.\n\nWhile the Order have publicly condemned the annexation and promised to defend Zoner interests within the system along with the Corsair Empire, other local groups have remained uncharacteristically quiet with only the Hessians launching a propaganda campaign in order to boost their numbers.

1116415.text: NEW LONDON -- 826 AS -- The looming siege of New London is not as inpenetrable as Gallia likes to claim. In December last year, our brave allies from the Republic of Liberty made a daring sally into the Gallic Trinity at Southampton. Losses were suffered, but ultimately the Gallic battleship Beuvray was destroyed, together with most of her fleet.\n\nRecently it was reported that the Beuvray had been replaced by the Athos, a Corsair battleship. This confirms the existence of the Gallo-Corsair alliance. Contrary to what Gallic admirals might think, this is a gain for us, because they now rely on an ally who we know is unreliable. It is suspected that the Athos managed to reach New London using a largely unknown and unstable network of jump holes, thus avoiding our defenses in Cambridge and Omega-3. In order to do this, they had to avoid our defenses instead of penetrating them because it is widely known that no Corsair warship or crew is fit to face our own in direct combat.

1116416.text: Since the annexation of Gran Canaria, there have been a lot of people coming here. Can't really say I ever had much contact with any other Zoners that are not with us in the Omicrons. Sirius is quite big, after all. These new arrivals seem kind of bitter. I mean, their home was just stolen from them. Guess I can't blame them for feeling this way. I just wish they wouldn't act like the people around them are at fault for it.

1116417.text: I've been doing supply runs for the Zoners on Freeport 9 and Freeport 5 for a long time now, and believe me, if anyone has the right to get a bed here on Corfu, it's me. Since all those settlers arrived here to make it to Pygar, Corfu's living quarters are hopelessly crowded. Life support really is giving all it can. Instead of investing all of their efforts into that ball of dust down there, maybe they should extend Corfu instead.

1116418.text: A lot of people want to go down to Pygar. Problem is, there's only so many shuttles that can bring them there. I get it, traffic needs to be orderly, but come on, I've been sitting here for weeks waiting for my transit. My wife is already on the surface with the children, so what is holding them up for so long?

1116419.text: You know, seeing the planet from up here really makes me reconsider. Is living in the ruins of that supposed alien city really worth giving up the comfortable life we had on Gran Canaria? Seeing how unorganized the entire transit down there is currently, I am not so sure if I want to go.

1116420.text: [825 AS] Kusari Declares War! Speech by Yukihara Reijiro, Prime Minister

1116421.text:
NEW TOKYO -- 825 AS -- No more than a month ago I addressed this Noble House with our intention to bring a new future to this new region of space, this new member of our family of stars. Shizuoka. Before that, we of Kusari expressed concern and sadness upon witnessing the discord that had befallen our neighbors of Rheinland, and the corporate heads of the Gas Miners Guild, that threatened the stability of the region and could eventually put in danger our House and our people's way of life.

With effort, we established a security corridor linking to Rheinland, and pledged to both conflicting sides that we would do the utmost to prevent the bloodshed in the Sigma-59 system, ensuring free traffic and relief from the strains of war that would engulf the rest of the sector, unless the House of Rheinland made efforts to sit at the negotiations table with the Guild to settle for peace. We hoped for intelligent heads to prevail, to see the demerits of a prolonged war, of a vague quest for vengeance and grievances that were well below the amount of wrath that the Rheinland spirit demonstrated. We expected that they would know who they were looking for, fighting for, defending from.

We were ignorant. No, Kusari demonstrated a naiveite that has become too common in its complacency. By believing in our apparent strength and the pride we hold for ourselves, we made ourselves victims to Rheinland Military, who blinded by bloodshed, had forgotten who was their enemy. From seeking justice to just meeting any other human being they found on the battlefield with their destructive force, they struck. And they struck those who held no blame.

On the past day, KNF local forces had confirmed our suspicions that the Rheinland Military had indiscriminately attacked and annihilated joint Kishiro and GMG civilian installations part of the Shizuoka Colonial Commission project to colonize the Planet Saigon, as it is commonly known. Neither Kishiro or GMG units were of military flair, and all transponders were clearly identified as a civilian operation, just a dozen clicks away from KNF sanctioned security corridor. It is with sadness that we have confirmed the death of Commissioner Akemi Yamashita, senior Kishiro executive and well known promoter of Kusari economy and society development for many years.

Rheinland Military, without quarter, attacked these installations, destroyed these peaceful efforts for progress. They ignored the pleas for mercy, and then expected the Kusari Naval Forces to stand idle before this onslaught. They were not idle.

Upon confirming the destruction of Kishiro Survey Vessel Unzen, Kusari Naval Forces took the initiative of retaliation against RM breach of the peace of the Shizuoka system, and notified the government of these horrible crimes. The Diet of Kusari has just now through its processes condemned the actions of the House of Rheinland, validated the Naval Forces actions of retaliation, and pressed further.

By decision of the Diet of the Reformed Kusari Empire, and by the name of our august Emperor, the House of Kusari has entered a state of war with Rheinland. Such state and any special provisions related with it will remain, until Rheinland ceases all military activities in the Sigma cluster, agrees to withdraw from the Shizuoka system, and accepts the necessity of sitting down to negotiate peace with the Gas Miners Guild and the people of Kusari.

Furthermore, due to the crisis situation in the Shizuoka system, the mandate of the Shizuoka Colonial Comission is suspended for a yet undetermined period, and the control of the affairs of the system placed under the military command of the Shogun Ikeada Yamato, as commanded by the Emperor.

We hope that our people remain strong and vigilant against the threats to our House, and that together we prevail against the challenges ahead of us. Kusari will prevail.

1116423.text:
PROVENCE -- 826 AS -- Following last week's engagement in the Provence system over Planet Marseille, what little Royalist and Council forces survived the battle withdrew indefinitely from the system, leaving Provence in the hands the local planetary government under Marquise Renée Hennequin d'Avignon of Marseille. Marquise d'Avignon, whose brother, the Duke of Provence, was killed in the attack, called for solidarity and continued loyalty to the Roi. These calls went unanswered, as Marseille's infamous sunken cities surfaced today for the first time in over two centuries. Hundreds of thousands of people emerged from the mysterious cities, which have gone uncensused since their construction in the 550's.

On the shores of Castellane, a resort island in Marseille's southern hemisphere devastated by wreckage from the Oblique, emergency relief teams from the sunken cities rushed in to help. As the relief crews worked to provide aid to the shell shocked citizens, a spokesperson for the ocean dwellers - who claim citizenship to a state calling itself the Syndicated Minarchy of Provence - made a statement espousing not only anti-royalist sentiment, but growing doubts in the Council's leadership as well. Among concerns cited were the Council's reputation as a military junta with no vision of a post-royalist Gallia, disregard for the safety and wellbeing of Gallia's citizen's, and rumors of an overwhelming influx of Council immigrants from Toulouse to be settled on Marseille.

The planet remains in a state of emergency as debris continues to rain from low orbit on islands like Castellane. The Minarchy, a libertarian state run by syndicated trade unions, has called for a vote of no confidence against the Marquise. No official statement has been released by the local royalist government, but eye witnesses claim to have seen numerous shuttles departing from the private spaceport of d'Avignon's residence. For now it seems that the crown has ceded their holdings in Provence to its new rulers, and it remains to be seen how the Council will be greeted should they return to the system themselves.

Dane Capshaw, North Tau News Service

1116430.text:
NEW BERLIN -- 826 AS -- Sector-renowned ALG Waste Disposal purportedly "declared war" on Bretonia and her assets two weeks ago, in response to their controversial decision to commandeer the Independent Miners' Guild's Aland Shipyard, in orbit of the Omega-3 star.

The Guild and ALG have long shared a mutual partnership for security in the face of pirate and terrorist organizations, but this incident has forced their defense pact's enactment against a Colony authority for the first time in their histories - An action without precedent, and with potentially far-reaching consequences for both Bretonia and Rheinland.

These skirmishes between a House authority and a corporation may mark the first time such a conflict has occurred without the backing of the latter's own house since the Eighty Years War. Defending Aland Shipyard are IMG security forces complimented by the ALG battlecruiser Erdbeben and her vaunted Beta Squadron. Augmenting this corporate phalanx are several cruisers and bomber wings of the dangerous terrorist organization known as the Red Hessians, adding to the bizarre diplomatic fiasco.

ALG's bold declaration and subsequent actions in the Omegas have worried investors as well as Bundesrepublik-and-private banking agencies alike. Brokers are reported to be selling company stock at record speed; with some economists pointing to this desperation as having the hallmarks of a possible market crash or recession.

The waste disposal giant's financial assests have been frozen, and most of its planetary facilities in Rheinland have been seized. The Rheinland government has made it clear that no ALG ship will be welcome on official stations and bases until further notice, and have instructed other Rheinland corporations to deny them access as well. What's more, the corporation has been publicly denounced by the Federal Republic, with some political pundits even going so far as to label ALG a "terrorist organization". It is unknown whether Bretonia has pressured Rheinland into denouncing ALG's behaviour, or if they are acting of their own initiative. What is certain however, is that ALG's future in Rheinland seems bleak, and the company will need to shift its activity outside of the Federal Republic for the foreseeable future.

Rheinland Correspondent Albric Hagen, Colony News Service
