1118083.text: [817 AS] Kusari Victorious at Leeds Gate

1118084.text: NEW TOKYO -- 817 AS -- In February 817, the Kusari Naval Forces launched a long-prepared assault against the Leeds Jump Gate. Four specially modified Bumblebees were sent through the gate, carrying two powerful EMP bombs each. The bombs disabled all Bretonian ships in a radius of 3K around the gate. The brave transport crews knew of the dangers involved, their sacrifice will be remembered well.\n\nThe Naval Forces attack following the EMP explosion had not only managed to break through to Leeds itself, but also destroy what was later confirmed to be a large part of the Leeds fleet, leaving the system largely defenceless. This prompted celebrations in certain neighbourhoods in New Tokyo, as the public anticipates the war will end in the few coming months with a decisive Kusari victory, and quite likely the seizure of Planet Leeds itself. The Emperor's spokesman has said a speech emphasising the situation will be transmitted by the Emperor himself early tomorrow. All Kusari citizens are encouraged to tune in.

1118085.text: [817 AS] Stokes Now Under Kusari Control

1118086.text: NEW TOKYO -- 817 AS -- Glorious Kusari forces have today announced the seizure of Stokes station amidst the offensive on Planet Leeds itself. After Bretonia's defeat at the Tau-31 gate, the Armed Forces still reeling from the blow have retreated to Planet Leeds itself where they are attempting to muster a defense. Naval Forces have easily dispatched the paltry defenders left around Stokes. The crew itself however was defiant in the face of the Emperor's benevolence, and rebuffed the request to surrender with a threat of overloading the station's reactors and destroying it in the process. Such terrorist tactics however cannot be let slide. Kusari marines have used a paralysing gas attack to neutralise the defenders and seize the station with only minor damage. Praise the Emperor!

1118087.text: [817 AS] Tau-31 Gate Lost In EMP Strike

1118088.text: NEW LONDON -- 817 AS -- As of late last year Kusari have all but pushed the Armed Forces out of Tau-31, and despite this Armed Forces admirals stood adamant that no Kusari attack can breach the Leeds gate without serious losses, thanks to the overlapping fields of fire of several battleships watching over it. This situation changed abruptly after a Kusari attack utilised suicide bombers armed with EMP devices of great scale and power. In a completely unexpected move, the entirety of the garrison defending the gate was powered down and forced to watch hopelessly as the Kusari navy jumped through to Leeds one ship at a time.\n\nBretonian officials were quoted confirming this as a "great setback" and that forces from the capital system itself will be expected to reinforce Planet Leeds. Despite such an unbelievable defeat, the morale amongst the population remains high with recent polls suggesting that only an overwhelming proportion of Bretonians is supportive of the war effort and strictly opposes the idea that Bretonia should offer any concessions to Kusari. Armed Forces personnel remain in high spirits also with spokesmen confirming that a counteroffensive effort will be launched soon.

1118090.text: LEEDS -- 817 AS -- Earlier this year Kusari's lightning strike on the Tau-31 gate successfully disabled much of the defense forces within Leeds in a single engagement. Later on an atrocious chemical strike on Stokes killed a large number of civilian and military personnel onboard, as Kusari seemingly dispersed with any sort of humane laws of engagement. LD-14 was only saved by the thick asteroid fields it is surrounded by, and yet civilian traffic to and from it is attacked and destroyed by the Kusari Navy on a daily basis. And now, the Kusari Navy has set its eyes on a new target: Planet Leeds itself. Long known as the industrial capital of Bretonia, Leeds is home to many of the facilities required for the continued production of Bretonian ships. The Armed Forces, keen on defending the planet for as long as it's possible, have mobilised the New London and Newcastle garrisons to Leeds orbit where a second line of defence will be established. With the government officially declaring a war economy, with all citizens being ordered to help the war effort, Kusari is expected to be held at the planet orbit until a new fleet can be commissioned to begin retaking Leeds.

1118091.text: [817 AS] Powell Responds To Rheinland Aggression

1118092.text:
MANHATTAN -- 817 AS -- In a long expected move President James Powell today issued a press release statement on the situation in the Hudson system:

"It is regrettable that it has come to this, but after the recent string of attacks on our patrols by what has been proven to be Rheinland Military forces, we just cannot afford not to respond. As of this morning any Rheinland ship breaching the Hudson/Bering blockade will be disarmed on sight. We will also begin plans to disarm any standing Rheinland forces still within the Hudson system."

Rheinland forces have been recently reported to not only attack Liberty Navy patrols within the Hudson system, but civilian vessels belonging to Planetform have also came under fire from ships that have been confirmed to hail from Rheinland. Furthermore, a Liberty Navy spokesman confirmed suspicions last week, saying that Rheinland is indeed massing forces along several border systems, including the relatively little known system designated as New Hampshire. The Navy spokesman assured us that the Navy is well aware of the "potential backdoor" this presents and will move to secure those pathways to prevent any terrorist attacks some Rheinland forces may attempt to carry out against Liberty holdings in Texas.

1118094.text:
HAMBURG -- 817 AS -- Recent tensions between Rheinland and Liberty have recently escalated further after the Liberty Navy was spotted advancing toward planet Atka in the Hudson system by a Rheinland patrol. According to the report presented by the patrolling servicemen, the Navy was protecting a number of corporate vessels identified as belonging to Planetform, Inc. while they set up an installation in the orbit of Atka.

The Liberty Navy buildup around Atka and Planetform operations within Hudson despite the Liberty-Rheinland embargo has led officials to believe this as Liberty's attempt to push Liberty's border further toward Rheinland, and has caused a wave of unsettling discussions within the Reichstag. Further reports claim of another Liberty fleet group in place at planer Houston in the Texas system. Analysts and officials are beginning to assume the worst: could Rheinland be a target for conquest in the eyes of President Powell?

A Military spokesman has assured us that the Rheinland Military is already preparing to counter the situation. The Hamburg defence fleet is expected to be mobilised and moved into Bering and Hudson soon in an effort to further secure the Rheinland border.

1118095.text: [817 AS] War! Liberty Launches First Strike

1118096.text: NEW BERLIN -- 817 AS -- Today, 5th of October 817 AS, House Liberty has officially declared war on House Rheinland. The declaration was transmitted amidst news of an escalating battle already under way within Hudson. Although little information is available at this time, Military officials have already stated that the Liberty Navy fired the first shots and launched a full scale attack afterwards, forcing the Rheinland Military to respond with deadly force. Liberty's President James Powell has made an official speech condemning Rheinland shortly after the incident and claimed an intention to ensure Rheinland forces would not be able to "threaten Liberty ever again". Considering Liberty was the one who attacked first, it can only be assumed Liberty plans to pacify the increasingly critical Rheinland government with a pre-emptive strike. An official statement from the Rheinland Military and the government is expected later today.

1118097.text: [817 AS] The Wild Delay Corsair Conquest

1118098.text: MINDELO -- 817 AS -- Corsairs' long-term plans of conquest into the Tau systems have once again been delayed due to reasons beyond any control. The Wild, savage Rheinlanders basing themselves from somewhere in the Omega sector, are frequently raiding Cadiz and many other Corsair operations in attempt to cripple defenders and capture ships for their own use. Their superior technology, as well as the great coordination and efficiency in which they carry out their raids makes them far more dangerous than any of the Corsairs' present enemies.\n\nAn idea to present a temporary cease fire to the Red Hessians so that the threat can be dealt with has been rejected by a number of prominent Corsair elders however, citing the possibility of a Hessian ruse if Corsair forces were to become occupied with these new attackers. Information presented by scouts deployed along Red Hessian defense lines paints a starkly different picture: one of the Hessians having a Wilde problem of their own. It can only be expected that both sides will inadvertently cool down the scale of the conflict in Omega-5 to concentrate on defense, at least temporarily.

1118099.text: [817 AS] Bretonia Attempts to Encircle Kusari Navy

1118100.text:
CALI -- 817 AS -- The war between Kusari and Bretonia continues with increased intensity. Kusari has achieved its goal and finally captured the Jump Gate between Leeds and Tau-31. After forcing Battleship Derby to retreat and defeating the fleets of Bretonia that defended the passage towards Planet Leeds, the Kusari Naval Forces put Planet Leeds itself under siege. Military targets planetside have not been attacked yet, but most of the planet's defenses were eliminated in the first weeks of the siege. On the surface, the Bretonia Armed Forces is gathering whatever equipment and human resources it has to counter a ground assault that is expected to start near the end of the year, or sometime in 818 AS

Bretonia has attempted to break the siege and attacked Kusari forces near Leeds. However, the attack was a failure rather than success: after suffering heavy casualties, Bretonia was able to control only part of the space around the planet, with Kusari gathering forces on the other side, not far from the Trade Lane exit.

Meanwhile, the situation in the Dundee system proved to be much better for Bretonia than we could expect. With the help of Mollys, Bretonia has defeated Kusari Naval Forces detachments in the area and come close to the jump hole in Tau-31. Instead of bringing the Dundee fleets back to Leeds to defend the planet, the Bretonia Armed Forces chose to attack a barely defended Tau-31 and finally encircle the Kusari Navy that concentrated its capital ships near Leeds. If Kusari fails to bring reinforcements from Tau-29, supply lines that connect Leeds with Kusari will be threatened by Bretonian ships, which will almost inevitably result in a devastating defeat of Kusari near Leeds. Our analysts, however, speculate that Bretonia is exhausted by the war more than Kusari and may not have enough military resources to drive Kusari back to the Tau sector during this year.

1118101.text: [817 AS] Wilde Open A New Offensive

1118102.text:
VOGTLAND -- 817 AS -- With the Rheinland Military preparing itself for a possible war with Liberty, the Red Hessians have gained more freedom than ever to operate in the core systems of Rheinland. Although this presents an ideal opportunity for a large scale strike, the movement is facing different, more difficult issues in the Omega systems.

New assaults on the Corsairs have been delayed by a renewed and - one could say frenzied - attack by the Wilde, the alien infested forces loyal to Niemann. Although reports confirm the Corsairs are facing similar pressure, Red Hessian commanders remain concerned as time works against them should hostilities between Rheinland and Liberty commence soon. Active attacks on both Ronneburg and Freital have been confirmed, and several wings of fighters lost so far to the almost suicidal attacks by the alien weaponry enhanced Military traitors.

Although these attacks are brutal in nature, a prominent Red Hessian commander was quoted saying that "peace with the Corsairs is still not an option". Orders remain for fighter squadrons in Omega-5 to maintain perimeter around Ronneburg until the Wilde assaults give in.

1118103.text: [817 AS] New House Joins The Colonies

1118104.text:
JAVA -- 817 AS -- The remote system of Orkney which is part of Bretonian space, although it is not considered part of Bretonian territory, has become a site of events that will change the history of the Sirius sector forever.

On day 320 817 AS, 1704 Manhattan time, a massive explosion was sighted by local Independent Miners Guild patrol in an old mine field. First it was thought that the explosion was an accident. Later, however, several consequent explosions followed. The explosions cleared a wide pass within the mine field that lead to a previously unknown jump hole. From the jump hole, a large fleet of unknown ships came through the passage between the mines and ventured into the clear area of Orkney. IMG first considered them to be unknown aliens and brought warships from Dounby Station in case their intentions were hostile. However, very soon IMG ships were contacted by the newcomers who identified themselves to be representatives of the lost French House, bearing the Latin name of Gallia.

Gallia has been aware of existence of Sirius Houses for centuries but, however, chose a path of intentional isolation. The fleet of ships that breached the mine field belonged to a group named the Council, a political and military opposition of the Gallic central government. It took many years of fighting for the Council to suppress the powerful defenses of the Gallic Navy and reach the mine field. Now, isolation is a thing of the past, and Languedoc system to which the jump hole from Orkney leads can be freely visited by any ships from any Sirius Houses. Systems beyond Languedoc are still under control of the Gallic Navy, and the Council warns everyone willing to explore the distant Gallic systems that forces loyal to the Gallic government have most likely received an order to attack any unknown ships on sight.

Shortly after breaching the mine perimeter, the Council began to construct a space station not far from the mine field using hull components brought from Languedoc. The station was named Reunion, not only after an island in the Indian ocean that belonged to France until the year 2088 A.D., but also as a reminder of what happened on 320 817, day that will be remembered in history as the Day of Reunion.

1118105.text: [817 AS] New House On The Outskirts of Bretonia Space

1118106.text:
NEW LONDON -- 817 AS -- Bretonian information agencies are receiving contradictory news upon unidentified ships that appeared in the Orkney system at the edge of Bretonia space. Orkney is currently beyond the reach of Bretonian lawful forces, since the path through Tau-31 and Tau-23 is blocked by the advancing Kusari, and the path through Edinburgh is blocked by a significant Gaian presence in the system. Trustworthy sources within the Independent Miners Guild, however, indicate that the information has been confirmed and that the ships belong to the House of Gallia, the existence of which has never been known to anyone in the Sirius Sector.

If the information is confirmed, the discovery of Gallia is expected to become one of the most important dates in the whole history of Sirius. It remains unclear why the information about a previously unknown French sleeper ship remained secret from the other nations of the Alliance, and why this House was never discovered before. Our records indicate that France, Italy and Australia lost their sleeper ships and the launching facility to a surprise attack by the Coalition shortly before the other 5 sleeper ships launched from Jupiter. The Australian ship was fully loaded with colonists who were all killed in the attack, and the ship belonging to Italy had started to unload the cryogen cameras several days before the attack due to a technical problem aboard, many of them urgently transferred to Hispania that ended up severely overloaded. Information about French colonists, however, is rather vague and contradictory.

Bretonia will seek the aid of historians from other Houses to clarify what could happen at that time. We are expecting more information from the Independent Miners Guild and other sources soon.

1118107.text: [817 AS] New Power in Tau Sector

1118108.text:
NEW TOKYO -- 817 AS -- Kusari news agencies are receiving a massive amount of information and footage about the newly discovered House of Gallia. A group that calls itself the Council has informed IMG ships located in Orkney that the mine fields that separated Gallia from the rest of Sirius have been breached, and that now the Council will allow any ships from Sirius to venture into previously unknown space.

No trustworthy information is present right now about the origins of the Gallic house, since our records indicate that the French sleeper ship was destroyed along with Italian and Australian sleeper ships prior to the day when Liberty, Bretonia, Kusari, Rheinland and Hispania launched from Jupiter. Records of the destruction show no possibility of rebuilding or repairing the ship, especially considering the fact that later the Coalition took the whole launch facility under its control.

The situation deeply concerns the Shogun and his councillors, for the newcomers appear to have powerful warships that may threaten our plans of Bretonia conquest. Military is expected to increase security on all supply lines of our forces that run through the Tau sector.

1118110.text: MANHATTAN -- 817 AS -- Liberty agencies have received information confirmed by their partners in Bretonia about the new House that has been recently discovered. Descendants of this House that reached Sirius through a path in the mine field claim that it is Gallia, a French house populated with descendants of Terran France. This information will need additional proof, for it is known that France was one of the nations of the Alliance that lost its sleeper ship shortly before it was launched.\n\nPresident Powell held a brief press conference in which he said that "Liberty, and hopefully all constructive powers of Sirius, welcome our new neighbors". "However", he added, "we will need to investigate the origins of the new House more thoroughly, for more than eight hundred years have passed since our sleeper ships launched from Sol, and no information indicated that France could rebuild and launch its own sleeper ship almost simultaneously with ours". "Even if the French could re-build Gallia, a question remains: why were the other nations of the Alliance left behind? Liberty could not interfere, since it could compromise the security of our main launching site on Jupiter, but if the French knew about any other means of escaping Sol, they could warn the others and offer them help".

1118112.text:
NEW BERLIN -- 817 AS -- Reports from Bretonia indicate that Independent Miners Guild ships in the Orkney system have stumbled upon unidentified ships that belong to the previously unknown House of Gallia. The two available jump holes into Gallia have been hidden from the rest of the Sirius by huge mine fields, and, according to the information we are receiving, the fields could have been set up intentionally to prevent us from finding the entrance into Gallia.

Now, as the field in Orkney is breached by a dissident group named The Council, all ships in Sirius are offered passage into Gallia. However, the new House is not expected to be a safe area to travel. Gallic Royal forces are likely to attack all unknown ships venturing into their territory. Rheinland does not recommend any of its citizens, regardless of their location, to go to Gallia before we establish diplomatic relations with its central House government.

Astronomers indicate that information about the core worlds of Gallia is rather contradictory. The Council has informed us that Gallia arrived at New Paris in 84 AS If the French sleeper ship was travelling at the speed similar to known sleeper ships, the Gallia would have reached New Paris in about 35-40 AS The New Paris star is located about 245 light years away from the Manhattan star, and the whole star cluster that forms the central part of Gallia is considered to be the most remote part of the Sirius sector ever populated by humans, even more remote than Nomad systems charted in 800-801 AS As such, it is disputed whether Gallia should be considered part of the space known as the "Sirius Sector". Such distances are beyond the reach of currently available navigation computers, and on the nav maps the Gallic systems will be placed close to Tau space between Bretonia and Orkney, while in reality they are separated by dozens of light years of unexplored space.

1118113.text: [817 AS] Gallia: A New Power Emerges?

1118114.text: CADIZ -- 817 AS -- A rather unexpected announcement graced our footsteps in the recent days: it appears an entire House, previously unknown to the colonies, has emerged from hiding to the prying eyes of Sirius. Not only that, but this House appears the be the largest of all the colonies, and the ones who opened the first passages seem hell bent on warning everyone else about an impending invasion. This "Gallia" (as they call themselves) seems to be preparing an assault on Bretonia, hoping to seize it for themselves in the name of revenge and conquest. It is also already on hostile terms with the Outcasts, which means Corsair goals for the Tau sector might become reality after all.\n\nUnfortunately, we did not manage to obtain more information than this. However, one thing is clear: a strike must be launched on Dublin and Cambridge at once if we are to reap the rewards of the Bretonian navy being obliterated in the north - whether by Kusari or these new invaders.

1118116.text: GENOA -- 817 AS -- For years Omicron Tau was considered to be a safe system, a long way away from even the edge world conflicts of Sirius. All that changed recently with the discovery of what appears to be a manmade explosion in the distant reaches of the system. reconnaissance footage has shown only a large explosion seemingly from nowhere followed by a number of moving contacts appearing on long range sensors. Ships were dispatched to ensure that these intruders are identified and destroyed so that they will not reveal us to the colonies. The stories they brought back with them however were nearly beyond belief: the explosion was actually generated by the destruction of a hidden mine field guarding a concealed jump hole - one that leads straight into the space of a previously unknown house, Gallia. Of course, unknown is just a synonim for "a market waiting to be conquered". Plans must be put into motion regarding the spread of cardamine into these new lands immediately.

1118117.text: [ARCHIVE] Second Gallic Civil War - Part I

1118118.text:
710-716 AGS (794-800 AS) -- Some historians name the year 798 as the beginning of the Second Gallic Civil War, for that was the year when the Council acted openly against the Gallic Army for the first time. Yet it is commonly considered that the war started in 794 AS on Planet Marne located in the Champagne system, when a massive rebellion broke out in three out of five of Marne's prime industrial centers. The rebellion was apparently well-prepared and organized. Gallic media reported that many rebel commanders were former military officers or even professional criminals hired to fulfill this task. Those reports were denounced by the Council, but it is apparent that there were a number of experienced soldiers and military commanders among the rebels. Initial tactics involved taking control over the main Marne cities and industrial facilities with minimal destruction and civilian casualties.

At fist, the rebellion was an overall success: police forces in the cities were defeated, as well as army detachments recently deployed within the cities to preserve order. However, most Gallic ground troops resided on well-defended bases in desolate areas of the planet. Their resistance was much heavier than the rebels first expected. Despite numerical superiority, rebels were heavily outgunned and could not establish control over the planet's terrain. At first, the government hesitated to use heavy weaponry against the cities. Rebels used this time to reinforce their defenses and capture space ports which were used to deliver weaponry and reinforcements. Light military vehicles and artillery were mainly supplied by the Council, while Gallic Brigands supplied firearms and ammunition. During this time many volunteers from the Council, various pirate groups, and even citizens from other planets joined the rebellion. The space around the planet was controlled by the Gallic Navy at that time, but the Navy apparently underestimated the amount of help the rebels were receiving from off-planet. Patrols assigned by the Navy were not enough to isolate the planet.

Attempts of the army to capture any of the rebel-controlled cities and settlements failed, much like the rebels themselves failed to take control over military objects. In the middle of 798 AS, a large army of over 110,000 troops was assembled in the Core Worlds and prepared for transport to Marne. Only about 45,000 made it through, for the Council finally interfered and attacked incoming Navy forces near Reims station and planet Sezanne. These were the first of many space fights that occurred during the war. The Navy was caught completely unprepared, and had to retreat. The Council failed to destroy any of the transports carrying the troops, but prevented them from proceeding to Marne.

The ambush near Reims happened before the Council forces landed on the planet, although some sources state otherwise. The Gallic Army, reinforced by fresh manpower, launched a massive attack against the rebels, striking on every front. After that, the rebels were probably aware that the Council would arrive in a matter of days, and threw all their forces to defend space ports where Council transports could land. The Council, however, could not break through the planetary blockade soon enough: they had to capture Reims Station in order prevent the Gallic Navy from striking from behind. Once Reims was captured and reinforced with heavy anti-capital-ship weaponry, the Council fleet proceeded to planet Marne. Attacking forces of the Gallic Royals were scattered by the newly arrived Council units, but resistance did not end until 801 AS when it was perfectly clear that the Gallic Navy would not be able to break through Council defenses, at least for the next several years.

1118119.text: [ARCHIVE] Second Gallic Civil War - Part II

1118120.text:
717-724 AGS (801-808 AS) -- After the fight on Marne was over, the war was mostly fought in space and on space stations, with the notable exception of a large-scale ground operation on Planet Quillan. Marne and Quillan are responsible for over 90 percent of all war casualties, which are estimated at 105,000 from both sides of the conflict (numbers are for year 816 AS and don't take into account later events). After overtaking Marne, the primary goals of the Council were securing the whole Champagne system and eliminating any Gallic lawful presence there, and preparing the attack against Lorraine and Languedoc. By the year 803 AS, the entire Champagne system was under control of the Council. The next obvious target was Lorraine. The Lorraine Jump Gate was located only one Trade Lane away from Marne, and in 803 AS the Council assembled a large fleet to attack the system.

It was unknown to the Council that the Royal Navy was preparing for this attack, aware of the final goals of the Council to gain access to the mine fields. The Navy used an alternative route from the Core Systems to reinforce Lorraine's defenses. Council High Command realized its mistakes only after the Navy had launched an offensive against the fleet in Champagne in the beginning of 804 AS, scattering the forces preparing to attack Lorraine just days before the attack was scheduled to start. Casualties from both sides were very high, with over 12 battleships and hundreds of smaller vessels completely destroyed. Nevertheless, daring Gallic Navy admirals ordered an advance on Marne, thinking that they had destroyed all Council capital ships in the system. Near Marne, they were engaged by a large defensive fleet quickly assembled of what was remaining of Council forces, heavily reinforced by Maquis and reportedly even Brigands. With the Trade Lane behind them consistently disrupted by smaller support crafts, the Navy was completely surrounded. Fierce battle continued for several hours before the Council gained the upper hand. Only a handful of the Royal Navy ships escaped. The rest were destroyed or captured.

The forces of the Gallic Royal Navy in Burgundy could not aid their Lorraine colleagues, for they were attempting to fight back the Council raiding parties that appeared in every part of the system with even more regularity than pirates. By that time, Council High Command had already moved from Macon Base in Burgundy to Marne. Macon has become a primary place for Council military preparations, overcrowded with new recruits coming from Marne, as well as weapons, equipment and ships produced in Champagne and in other systems. Due to fights taking place in Burgundy and Lorraine, Navy numbers in Languedoc and Languedoc became much smaller than before the war had started. Additionally, both Languedoc and Languedoc did not contain any defensive installations that the Navy could use to delay the offensive, with the exception of Montpellier Guard Station defending the Languedoc Mine Field.

By the end of 806 AS, Council was fully aware of this weakness and had prepared a multiple-step operation that involved attacking Languedoc, capturing or destroying any Navy ships that would oppose them, and quickly proceeding to Languedoc to complete their initial goal of creating a path through one of the mine fields. A surprise attack against Languedoc would disrupt Gallic communications and allow large fleets of the Council to pass from Burgundy to Languedoc. At the same time, a plan of a covert operation in the Lorraine Mine Field was being prepared.

1118121.text: [ARCHIVE] Second Gallic Civil War - Part III

1118122.text:
725-728 AGS (809-812 AS) -- The plan of the Languedoc offensive developed by the Council did not work as well as initially expected. In 809 AS, Council sent a large fleet into Languedoc to secure the area of Bourgon-Jailleu Station. Bourgon-Jailleu proved to be a tough target, equipped by multiple defensive systems and providing cover for numerous Police patrols that deteriorated the progress of Council fleets. In the end, Council decided that the station had to be destroyed. A diversion was prepared to distract Police ships to the Burgundy Jump Gate. During the diversion, the Council launched its bombers and very heavy fighters against Bourgon-Jailleu that now had only a few ships to defend it. After the defensive systems of the station were eliminated, a Council heavy transport on autopilot was directed into the station hull, destroying the station and killing over 120 Police and Navy officers. The number reportedly includes a few civilians as well.

In the same year, one of the most controversial events of the whole Second War followed. Gap Station, which occupied a crucial location on the route from Burgundy into Languedoc, was attacked by the Council. Because destroying the massive and heavily guarded station that had many civilian inhabitants was not an option for the attackers, their goal was to drop marines within the station and capture it with minimal casualties. Once again, the plans of the Council became known to the Navy command, and Gallic Army detachments were brought to defend the station. Eventually, a large Council fleet arrived to the Gap area, neutralized station defenses and launched dropships. Fighting within the station lasted for more than 4 days and ended only when all Council landing troops were defeated. The victory cost both sides greatly, with over 400 killed and many more wounded. While the Gallic soldiers were stationed near the airlocks to prevent a new assault, a large Royal Navy fleet finally arrived to breach the blockade. Before retreating, desperate Council ships launched a final missile attack against all Gap's airlocks, which could have potentially resulted in the station de-pressurizing. Gap Station's engineers had to seal the inner airlocks before the Gallic soldiers could escape; trapped outside, they were blown into space and perished. Very few of the military and police personnel survived the attack, and civilian casualties were low only by a miracle.

With no chance to capture Briancon or Gap stations located in the central part of Languedoc, the Council chose the tactic of sporadic raids to distract Navy and Police patrols from outer regions of the system that were used to relocate Council fleets into Languedoc. By the end of 812 AS, Council had built multiple storage banks and small repair facilities near the Jump Gate path between Languedoc and Languedoc. Most of those facilities were equipped with simple but deadly self-destruct mechanisms that activated when Navy or Police ships were approaching. The next year, an offensive against Languedoc was set to begin.

Meanwhile, the situation in Burgundy and Lorraine was under dense control of the Navy. Security of the two systems was declared the highest priority for the GRN, and most available forces in the Gallic Border Worlds were ordered to defend them. Attempts to breach defenses in Lorraine failed repeatedly, and Council presence in the system remained minimal. Maquis secured a small base in one of the Lorraine asteroid fields, but they could do nothing with the Navy fleets and mostly concentrated on smuggling and piracy against small corporate shipments.

1118123.text: [ARCHIVE] Second Gallic Civil War - Part IV

1118124.text:
729-731 AGS (813-815 AS) -- The Languedoc offensive caught the Gallic Royal Navy completely unprepared. Apparently, their previous means of gathering intelligence on the Council failed them. A massive armada of Council capital ships came into Languedoc directly through the Jump Gate, which was not guarded by any Navy ships at that time. At the same time, hundreds of Council fighters began advancing from the Lozere asteroid field in Languedoc. Local Navy detachments delayed capital ships advancing to Remoulins, which gave the station's inhabitants time to evacuate. It was rumored that the Council allowed this intentionally to avoid civilian casualties, for most of Remoulins' inhabitants were miners employed by Gallic Metal Service.

The decisive battle for Languedoc took place in the middle of 813 AS near Remoulins. The station was empty at that time, and during the fight one of its outer storage tanks filled with explosive fuel was damaged by battleship fire. The tank detonated shortly afterwards, destroying the whole station. It remains unknown which ship damaged the tank, since Council and GRN used similar types of weaponry in this battle. It is also unknown if it was done intentionally or not. However, it is certain that the explosion helped the Council to achieve a victory, for Royal Navy cruisers that used the station as cover from Council battleship fire were crippled in the explosion and became easy prey for Council bombers.

Nimes Station was the next target, and in 814 AS the Council attempted to use the same tactic that failed with Gap Station. This time, however, previous mistakes were taken into account. The Council made use of inside support from civilians loyal to its cause. While Council fleets were stationed next to Remoulins' wreck and Nimes was preparing for an assault from space, a group of Council special operatives breached the station through a maintenance airlock that was left unguarded. Before local Police and Army guards could organize any resistance, the Council took over control of the station's life support, computer mainframes, internal and external defensive systems. Later, a Council fleet arrived, and station defenders had no other choice but to surrender. With minimal casualties from both sides (4 men killed), this operation is known as the most bloodless in the whole Second Gallic Civil War.

The Council offensive on Planet Quillan was the second planetary operation of the war. Capturing the planet was vital for the final success in breaching the mine field defenses. Breaching planetary defenses was a relatively easy task. However, after Council ground forces landed on the planet in the end of 815 AS, they discovered that a Gallic army of 90,000 was stationed on the planet and prepared to defend its settlements and factories. Outnumbered, the Council forces had to fortify their positions and prepare for a lengthy fight for the planet's surface.

This moment was crucial for the whole war. The Royal Navy was planning to launch a counter-assault against Council in Languedoc. If the Navy's assault was successful, the Council would lose ground in Languedoc and fail to breach the mine field. TheCouncil suffered heavy casualties, and launching a new offensive was not an option until losses were recovered. During that time, the Navy could concentrate all forces near Champagne and take back the system, undoing all progress that the rebels had made since the start of the war.

1118125.text: [ARCHIVE] Second Gallic Civil War - Part V

1118126.text:
732-733 AGS (816-817 AS) -- In 816 AS, the Council had no option other than to request support from the Maquis, who, in turn, rallied their allies in the Core Worlds to attack Royal Navy from behind. While it was impossible to stop the whole fleet that was moving to Languedoc, Maquis succeeded in using terrorist tactics to bomb several battleships of the GRN offensive fleet. An array of brutal and merciless attacks from Maquis and Brigands against civilian convoys followed shortly afterwards, forcing the Navy to relocate resources from the Languedoc offensive to local security tasks.

Now, with the Navy's progress slowing down, the Council gained more freedom to act in Languedoc. Moving the last reinforcements from Burgundy, the Council established lines of defense near the Languedoc Jump Gate, wreck of Remoulins, Nimes Station, and Quillan itself. More Council troops landed on Quillan, increasing the numbers of Council corps on the planet to 95,000. The Council soldiers were mostly unemployed Marne workers, badly armed and trained. They would be no match for Gallic Army in open combat. However, the Council used a waiting tactic and successfully rallied local miners to aid its cause. Army detachments were stationed in the miner settlements, causing numerous conflicts between miners and soldiers. In several settlements, the unrest turned into rebellions aided by the Council. Overtaking settlements one by one, the Council slowly advanced, and in the beginning of 817 AS the remaining Gallic Army soldiers were scattered and forced to surrender.

In the end of 816 AS, the Council finally gathered a large fleet to attack Montpellier. Being the largest fleet ever brought to battle in this war, and possibly the largest fleet ever assembled in the whole Sirius sector since its colonization, it was opposed by a matching number of Gallic Royal Navy capital ships, fighters, support crafts, and stationary defenses. For several weeks, fighting next to Montpellier continued; at the same time, the Navy advanced from Languedoc and breached the Council's defenses near the Jump Gate.

It was too late to retreat at this point, and despite very heavy casualties, the Council advanced to the mine field, destroying numerous weapon platforms, smaller supplementary mine fields, and hundreds of enemy ships. A large part of Montpellier station itself was destroyed in a suicide attack by a Council battleship packed with thermonuclear explosives, with most station defenders killed in the explosion or shortly afterwards. Path to the mines was now clear, and Council moved forward to destroy the mines and create a large corridor that would allow all ships, even the largest ones, to pass through without being at risk of mine explosions. After the path was ready, the Council started to build a new space station on the other side, baring a symbolic name of Reunion.

At the same time, using the aid of local Maquis and several Junker turncoats, the Council started to set up a covert path within the Lorraine mine field. With the Royal Navy relocating all available forces to advance into Languedoc, the part of Lorraine that was far from the Champagne Jump Gate was left loosely defended. Finally, by the end of 817 AS the path to the Outcast system of Omicron Tau was revealed. Unlike the route in Languedoc mines, Lorraine's path was narrow and dangerous, having no navigation buoys nor other ways that could help to make this route safer. It is still likely that it will be discovered by Gallic Royal Navy patrols in a matter of months, and will possibly be remined.

1118127.text: [733 AGS] WARNING: Unidentified Ships in Gallic Space

1118128.text:
NEVERS -- 733 AGS -- The Gallic Royal Police service hereby issues a warning for all civilian and corporate ships located in Gallic Border Worlds. A large number of unidentified ships has entered Gallia space from Languedoc and Lorraine. Those ships belong to the long-lost Colonies of Sirius, nations that were involved in a treachery that forced us to build our own Sleeper Ship in secret from the other major powers of the Alliance.

Those ships are not an organized force and belong to various factions and organizations. They mostly use jump holes to navigate between systems, and avoid Trade Lanes and Gallic lawful space stations. We are already receiving reports of several attacks against our civilian shipments staged by the intruders. It is likely that they will seek refuge on pirate stations in case they are in danger or run out of supplies. Also, we should not forget that it was the Council who let those ships pass through the mine fields, and it is likely that some of those ships might join the Council and openly attack Police or Navy ships. All ships that are currently located in Gallic Border Worlds are advised extreme caution. The Navy and Police are increasing patrols on all major Trade Lanes. For your own safety, avoid venturing far from commonly used trade routes and populated areas. If attacked, hail any Navy and Police patrols in your area, and escape towards the nearest space station.

We have already started to gather information on the newcomers. The King and his Foreign Office on New Paris is preparing necessary measures to establish diplomatic relations with the selected powers in Sirius Sector, however, this will become possible only after the Gallic Royal Navy liberates Languedoc system from the Council, and opens a way for our own diplomatic couriers to pass through the mine fields. In the meantime, we are sealing all Jump Gates leading from Gallic Border Worlds into the Core Systems. In total, 4 gates will be closed, 2 in Burgundy, 1 in Languedoc and 1 in Lorraine. This is done to prevent the intruders from reaching densely populated areas of Gallia. Without sufficient knowledge and navigation maps, pilots of the newly arrived ships will not be able to find alternative ways into the Core Worlds.

The measures that we undertake now are temporary, and very soon we will ensure complete safety for all law-abiding citizens of the Gallic Border Worlds. Please stay tuned and await for further announcements

-- Burgundy Royal Navy Headquarters, Planet Nevers, August 17, 733 AGS

1118130.text: NEW TOKYO -- 817 AS -- The glorious Emperor's forces are expected to begin a siege of the Planet Leeds within the next few weeks, as the transfer of required forces from Tau-31 was finished and the space around Stokes successfully fortified against Bretonian attacks. Kusari commanders have pressed for an attack to commence quickly citing the planet's importance for the Bretonian war machine. If Leeds could be seized, they claimed, the war would end immediately with a complete Kusari victory, and quite likely - the occupation of Bretonia. A large ground assault force is currently being massed on Kyushu for this purpose, and is expected to leave for Bretonia within the following few weeks, after which Kusari Naval Forces will be expected to secure Leeds orbit so that a ground invasion may commence.\n\nWhen asked about the supposed setbacks in the Dundee system, a Naval Forces spokesman mentioned Molly terrorists working together with the Bretonians to retake the system, but refused to comment further.

1118131.text: [733 AGS] Second Gallic Civil War Continues

1118132.text:
MARNE -- 733 AGS -- While the gate into Sirius from the Languedoc system has been opened, and a secret passage in Lorraine is now complete, the Second Gallic Civil War still continues. Despite facing the inevitable, the Gallic Navy will continue to consider us enemies of the state. We could not expect anything else from the corrupt monarchy that was bringing our whole nation towards an inevitable doom of interstellar war and bloodshed that was prevented by our recent actions. Future generations will be grateful to our soldiers who fought bravely and died on the battlefields of this lengthy and devastating conflict.

Still we, leaders of the Council, have to think about our present. We achieved the victory at a very high price, and a vengeful Gallic Navy will not wait long to retaliate. We will be able to defend Languedoc for no longer than a year from now. Without serious help from other Sirius factions we will not be able to hold longer. Exhausted and isolated, our fleets will have no choice other than to seek refuge in desolate areas of Sirius not claimed by any of the larger Houses. After that, the Gallic Navy will gain full control over Languedoc and passage into Sirius. While the Navy has not yet achieved the strength necessary to fulfill the insane plan of Sirius conquest, Gallia still has the strongest military of all the Houses, by far exceeding Liberty and Kusari space military forces, let alone Rheinland and Bretonia. The technological superiority of Gallia is also not as significant as Navy analysts predicted, however, there are certain unique weapon technologies that Gallia will be able to use against Sirius forces. With diverse tactics and advanced weaponry, Gallia will have an advantage over any opponents, at least in the first several years of the conflict that may or may not take place.

Those facts are already known to the Navy command, because it is no secret that there are many government spies and Junker spies among our ranks. We have to act openly in Languedoc, and Junkers, along with other groups, have full access to whatever information on Sirius we gain now. It is also rumored that Junkers, which are present in Sirius as well, are actually part of the same group that was spying for the interests of Gallia and selling information on Sirius houses, their technology and military disposition to the Crown, the Navy, and the corporations.

1118134.text:
SOLARIUS -- 817 AS -- Although much of the Omega sector is obscured by the encompassing Walker Nebula, there are some parts that can be visible to long range telescopes. Normally, these parts are only of interest to those working in the field of astronomy, but one of the star sectors visible to Solarius station has recently been receiving a lot more attention.

The star system, identified by astronomers as Omega-58, has been noted for intense energy emissions that have at first been attributed to the system's stellar configuration, but was later found to be intermittent. Attempts to launch long range probes to the location to identify the source have met with unusual failure, with the probes failing almost instantaneously after crossing the interplanetary medium boundary.

Initial projections have defined the object in question as artificial, although that explanation was quickly denied after initial object power calculations placed the output far beyond anything capable by any man-made energy source. Plans for an expedition to the Omega-58 system were delayed due to the ongoing conflict with Rheinland, but have been shelved indefinitely following the unexpected cessation of all energy emissions of any kind from Omega-58. The star has gone dark without the typical supernova shockwave one would expect from a dying star. This has led scientists to speculate the star is either being obscured, or has met an unnatural end.

1118135.text:
Adapted Nomad Blaster
This appears to be an attempt to configure Nomad weapon technology to be compatible with ships from the colonies. Order and Core scientists originally developed the experimental mountings that were capable of utilising the energy conversion units, however the poorly understood technology has since leaked onto the black markets and proliferated across Sirius.

1118141.mapped:
Kruger's experiences in Munich showed that dispersed automated platforms are vulnerable, so Daumann chose a different strategy when they initiated a mining operation there. Daumann constructed a small station in orbit of Rosenheim, near a field rich in Aluminium, one of the most widely used metals in spaceship construction. While a fairly common metal, Daumann gambled that the ease of access to the deposits in the Chiemsee would help them in dominating the Aluminium market.

Raubling had been in continuous operation since its construction, despite the disaster that struck Munich. That finally changed early in the Rheinland Civil War, when a Federalist task force seized the station as part of efforts to secure the Munich system. With no mining expertise among Federalist forces, Raubling's refineries sit silent for the first time since their construction. Federalist forces are assessing possible uses of Raubling's equipment moving forward.

1118144.text:
A huge aluminum-rich asteroid field named after a large lake on New Berlin, Chiemsee has been mined by Daumann Heavy Constructions. The Munich disaster fractured the field into two smaller pieces. In 827 AS, Daumann left the field entirely, their base of operations Raubling no longer in their hands due to the polical changes in Rheinland.

Aluminum remains a cruical element in the manufacture of spacecraft and guided munitions - a vital resource for the Republic.
