Rosenheim is an unremarkable barren world with thin atmosphere and ancient planetary crust devoid of any easily accessible resource deposits. Raubling Station was constructed in the planet's near orbit.

1118148.text:
Before 816 AS, Glasgow Outpost was the headquarters for Bowex (Border World Exports), a very large, very old shipping conglomerate. Bowex, which received its royal charter from Prince Harry XXI himself in 310 AS, claims a long and storied history in which the company was involved in most of the major events of Bretonian history. Prior to the war with Kusari, Bowex was the leading Bretonian shipping concern and handles most of the shipping in and around Leeds.

When Kusari's onslaught against Bretonia reached the Leeds system, Bowex officials moved to New London and other stations located in safer areas of Bretonia. The outpost still formally belonged to the company, but in fact was operated by Bretonia Armed Forces. Glasgow was reinforced with hull plates and modern station weaponry, yet, the Armed Forces did not have time and resources to renew the dated and inefficient internal security systems. The Kusari Navy used this weakness in the battle for the Jump Gate, dispatching several small groups of commandos that were able to neutralize many of the station's defenders by a surprise attack, and gaining partial control of weapon systems. Yet, the remaining defenders of Glasgow did not surrender, and fighting on the station continued long after the surrounding space was cleared of Bretonia Armed Forces presence.

After the war between Kusari and Bretonia was forced to a conclusion by the invasion of Gallia into the Tau systems, Bowex reclaimed the station, but its perilous position so close to the Tau-31 Jump Gate made the station a hazardous duty post for Bowex's employees.

1118149.text:
Stokes Mining Station was run by Bretonia Mining and Manufacturing (BMM) until 817 AS It was the largest orbital facility in all of Bretonia and has operated continuously for centuries. Aside from BMM, representatives from Kusari shipping companies were also present, negotiating for the basic materials required to fuel their own industries.

In 817 AS, when Kusari fleets reached Stokes, the Bretonia Armed Forces chose to defend the station at all costs. The decision was rumored to be inspired by the BMM lobby within the New London government elite. From a strategic point of view, this was a grave mistake, since Stokes is a large and spread out installation hardly suitable for defensive purposes. Bretonian fleets around Stokes were swiftly scattered and had to retreat, and the station itself was captured by the Kusari Naval Forces with minimal casualties.

Samura and Kishiro, despite their fierce competition, joined forces to operate the facility after it was seized from BMM. The mining operations were restored in a matter of weeks by Kusari workers brought from Kyushu and it was rumored that certain IMG members and former BMM employees collaborated with Kusari companies.

Following the withdrawal of hostile Kusari forces from Leeds in early 818 AS, BMM reclaimed the station and immediately began refitting it for Ship Hull Panel construction. Within weeks the station was in full production and supplying the Bretonian and Liberty militaries with vital capital ship components to repair and rearm their fleets for action against Gallia.

1118150.text: [733 AGS] Path into Sirius Opened by the Council

1118151.text:
DIJON -- 733 AGS -- Shortly after the path into Sirius was opened by advancing forces of the Council, a large number of unidentified ships were detected in the Languedoc and Languedoc systems. Disturbing reports come from Lorraine where powerful and agressive ships of unknown configuration were reported engaged in several fights with the Royal Navy not far from the Luneville Guard Station. During last week, several sightings of the as of yet unidentified ships were reported in the Burgundy system as well.

The mine paths created by the Council are narrow and dangerous, and very few ships of heavier class can pass through them. Newcomers from Sirius do not appear to be organized as one power and belong to a number of various groups and factions. Gallic officials are now collecting information on the factions that dispatched those ships, their possible goals, and level of technology. Before this information becomes publically available for ship pilots, we advise civilian and Royal Police pilots to avoid any contacts with the newcomers, reporting all unidentified contacts to the local Navy patrols as soon as possible.

It already became known that some pirate bases offer docking and repair services to ships from Sirius. The newcomers also appear to have access to our Trade Lane and Jump Gate initiation procedures. To secure the Core Worlds and prepare for establishing official contacts with the other Sirius nations, Gates leading to them are now blocked for any and all ships. Gallic Royal Police and Gallic Royal Navy apologize for the inconvenience to passengers and shipping companies, but maintain that this precaution is necessary for reasons of national security.

1118153.text:
Nomad Trial ID

The Nomads are sentient biological machines left over from a highly advanced alien race known as the "Daam K'vosh". The Daam K'vosh had intended to let the Nomads develop and colonize Sirius, but the human arrival disrupted this. The humans have taken many secrets which were left behind for the Nomads: Trade lanes, Jump gates, Cruise engines, Cardamine longevity. The Nomads can subvert humans by infesting their bodies.

Pilot carrying this unlawful ID is a young Nomad, who :

- Can attack only in self-defense or assisting Nomads and Wild in combat.
- Cannot ally with anyone except Nomads and Wild.
- Cannot demand credits or cargo.
- Cannot dock anywhere except on Nomad and Wild bases.

Allowed ships: Nomad Light Fighter (Nomad Morph) only.

1118155.text: Toggles camera leveling in 3rd person view. Use with caution.

1118158.text: [817 AS] The Real Reason Behind The Hudson War

1118159.text:
NEW BERLIN -- 817 AS -- It has been a few months now since Liberty aligned forces shot at Rheinland ships in the independent worlds between the two houses, in an attempt to punish Rheinland for what they claim is "a lack of financial and political responsibility of House Rheinland to House Liberty". The conflict has since escalated into an all-out border war slowly being pushed toward the Hamburg system. But is simple revenge and looting the only reason Liberty is attacking Rheinland? It would appear not.

It is not news that Liberty is fortifying the rather backwater New Hampshire system, with fleet movements large enough to be detected easily. At first thought to be a deterrent force, analysts soon began to suspect otherwise as new information was made available by sources within the Marinenachrichtendienst. About a week ago the Rheinland Military has scored a searing success against the Liberty Navy, ambushing and disabling an entire patrol, including a gunboat class vessel. Upon boarding the craft, its neural net codes were used to access the Liberty Navy internal network from which partial plans for a larger scheme were recovered - including the idea that Liberty pushed for the war in Hudson to detract attention from a different target, deeper within Rheinland.

Although the true target of Liberty remains unknown, the Rheinland Military is now well aware of the possibility of an encirclement in Hamburg and has begun gathering forces within the Bremen system to respond to any attempts at a Libertonian strike. One thing is clear however: if Liberty is willing to go to war over whatever they are seeking, Rheinland must do all it can to deny them their prize.

1118160.text: [817 AS] Liberty Companies Maintain a Stake in Rheinland

1118161.text:
NEW BERLIN -- 817 AS -- Unilateral Libertonian aggression against Rheinland continues to dominate the Sirius-wide news, facing the Berlin Reichstag not only with military choices, but also important and difficult questions concerning the nation's economy. Both major and minor Liberty companies with holdings in Rheinland space have been continuing their withdrawal back to New York, leaving their assets mostly frozen and protected by Interspace Commerce. This does not include Synth Foods Inc. however, which is determined to keep its stranglehold on Stuttgart strong and unquestionable. Several parties in the Reichstag have described this as a move of economic warfare on the part of Liberty, and have asked for a vote towards the immediate nationalisation of Planet Stuttgart - a motion which was surprisingly denied by Chancellor Reinhardt himself, quoting financial claims by Interspace and Synth Foods as the reason behind his decision. While there is speculation that this move may have been prompted by different motives, many economists in both Rheinland and Kusari disagree.

"Rheinland in its present state is very fragile. If we were to make moves against Synth Foods now, the IC would certainly demand compensation per the contract we agreed to with Liberty over a century ago, and that move would devastate the currency by increasing our already considerable national debt. We would find ourselves needing to borrow money from Kusari just to keep the government afloat, and at that point Liberty could simply withdraw its Navy and wait for Rheinland to dissolve on its own." - says Jonas Koehler, chief advisor to the Minister of Finance.

When asked why exactly did Liberty not follow this move in the first place instead of aggressively pursuing a shooting war, Herr Koehler mentioned the exact reason being unknown at the time, but also said that "Liberty officials are likely hoping to force us to capitulate without collapsing our economy, and having to invest even more money into restarting it afterwards". This would mean that Liberty is in fact hoping for a quick and decisive victory.

1118162.text: [817 AS] Rheinland Patriots Prepare for War

1118163.text:
BRUCHSAL -- 817 AS -- With the first invaders at the gates of Rheinland, the prospect of the unification of our homeland against a common enemy stands strong. Many idealist Bundschuh party members have left Frankfurt to help defend the border from the imperialist tendencies of Liberty. The Liberty Navy has since reported increased attacks against their convoys and patrols, something they dare not attribute to a political organisation such as the Bundschuh out of fear of other Rheinland revolutionaries joining in the fight.

A few weeks ago a successful buildup has managed to reactivate the old Bundschuh base in Bremen without intervention on the part of the Rheinland Military residing there. It is unlikely that they are unaware of the situation, as reports of skirmishes between the Libertonians and the Bundschuh along the Hamburg and Bremen border arrive in Rheinland at a steady basis, meanwhile the formerly dense Bundschuh attacks against most military targets have severely lessened during the last weeks.

The question that the people of Rheinland now ask themselves is: Is this the day on which we put all our differences aside in order to battle a common enemy?

1118164.text: [817 AS] Red Hessian Expansion Still Under Way

1118165.text: VOGTLAND -- 817 AS -- Despite the increased Wilde attacks and the prospect of war in Rheinland, the Red Hessians still pour significant resources into their expansion in the Omega edge worlds, especially the Omega-47 flank. In a recent unexpected development the Hessians have begun reactivating their old diamond smuggling routes to Hudson and the rest of Liberty via the Unioners and Liberty Rogues. These diamonds however are unlike any other ever encountered. Their reddish tint and plentiful applications serve as both a political statement and a lucrative source of income for the Red Hessian movement. Some believe that this is connected to their recent build-up in the edge systems, however no such rumours have been confirmed so far.\n\nWhile the corporate backed Rheinland government lobbies Kusari to outlaw this new commodity in order to assure continued income for Daumann, opportunists flock to Hessian bases with the market in Liberty standing wide open, as the house stands in their refusal to declare it as contraband. Whether future political developments will change this attitude is unknown, but the Red Hessians plan to use the resulting profit to further their goals for as long as they can.

1118167.text: Now the path into Sirius is open anyway, we can openly state that our military power is more than twice as large as any other Sirius House possesses. If there was a war, no one could possibly stop us from winning.

1118168.text: The offensive from Languedoc into Languedoc was scheduled to begin, but we were too late. Breaching the mine field is a loss that we'll never be able to recover from.

1118169.text: Can you deny the might of the Royal Navy? We swept all opposition in Languedoc aside. Taking the Tau region from the Sirians was like taking candy from a baby. Why they continue to fight despite our clear superiority is beyond me.

1118170.text: The failure of Languedoc's defenses was the most devastating defeat for the Navy in over 300 years. Many of our admirals will lose their posts after the military investigations have been completed. Some already have, and they certainly deserve it.

1118171.text: If Languedoc was defended as well as Lorraine, we would never have been in the position we are now. Our isolation minefield has been breached, and we'll be forced to establish relations with the other Houses. But what troubles me even more is that the Council does not prevent any unlawfuls from Sirius from entering Gallic space. As if we didn't have enough of our own pirates to deal with.

1118172.text: We know the Council have a base in the Nievre Asteroid Field, the field is to dense for our capital ships to enter and they've a sizable defense force that has thwarted all our attempts to destroy it using fighters and bombers. We keep three wings of pilots on alert in case they launch an attack in the system.

1118173.text: I've been reassigned to Battleship Ambazac in the Languedoc system. I don't ship out until next week. I got seated on a transport full of Marines. Just my luck.

1118174.text: The Council have turned the whole Champagne system into a pirate haven. Pirate groups openly build bases there, and the Council uses their help in defending the system. Once any of our ships enter Champagne, we've got the Maquis, Brigands and the Council acting in unison against us.

1118175.text: Languedoc faced some of the most bloody battles of the Second Gallic Civil War, of which the Battle for Gap is the most well-known. We thought that liberating Languedoc was a glorious victory, but only now we realized how blind we were. They gave up Languedoc only to gather their forces in Languedoc.

1118176.text: I have to admit that the attack against the Languedoc defenses was brilliantly executed by the Council. They did sacrifice thousands of their pilots and soldiers to achieve their goal, but they didn't have much choice, and in the end they were victorious. Who cares about casualties?

1118177.text: You see my leg? That is why I am a bartender. Lost it at the beginning of the war. Instead of taking a medical discharge and licking my wound back home, I sucked it up and do what I can here. At least here I still have a chance to fight. I may be the only soldier on this ship that hopes we get boarded! That's the only way I'll see any action.

1118178.text: If you're looking for some work and have the credits, you could purchase a freighter from my brother-in-law on Nevers. There is no shortage of work for a freelancer trader.

1118179.text: I am glad I am stationed here on Avallon and not on Beuvray. The further away from those unsavory Junkers I am the better. Can't trust them, they'd sell their mother for a quick credit.

1118180.text: The IDF supplies Battleship Beuvray and Battleship Rocroi with Light Arms. They are always in need of more arms. If you stumble on any, they will pay well for them.

1118181.text: Setting up the mine fields was an extremely lengthy process. It took over a hundred and fifty years to complete, and Sirius could have discovered us at any time during this period.

1118182.text: A friend of mine works on a defensive Navy installation in Lorraine. I think it's called Luneville. He is a communications officer there, and says that they frequently get strange transmissions from the direction of the mine field. Also, he says that the Junkers are occasionally seen wandering in remote areas of the station! Can you believe that?

1118183.text: The traditional path to Lorraine through Champagne was blocked by the Council. To aid our fleets in Lorraine, we had to use the Jump Gate into Artois, and even the Jump Hole from Burgundy. I've heard that Sirius pilots are discouraged to use jump holes because of the dangers involved. But space travel is dangerous anyway, and securing Lorraine was of the utmost importance for us.

1118184.text: The Rocroi is the first line of defense against attacks from the Council coming from Champagne. Entering Champagne via that Jump Gate is suicide. Same for them. When the resources on Marne dry up, we'll be able to retake the system.

1118185.text: Shhh, quiet. I've got just what you're looking for. Authentic Nox, fresh from Marseille. Wait....you see that guy, I think he is watching us.

1118186.text: One of the reasons why we were not able to stop the Council from capturing the Border World systems was our command's unwillingness to reveal the true strength of the Gallic Royal Navy. When our armadas from Ile-de-France reach Languedoc, no power in the world will be able to save the Council forces there from elimination in a matter of weeks.

1118187.text: The Council stands no chance against our capital ships in open space. Their forces in Burgundy though are fighting a guerilla war of sporadic raids; ships come from asteroid fields, attack our patrols, and retreat into the fields before reinforcements arrive. Our capital ships cannot venture inside those fields, which makes Council bases there impervious to harm.

1118188.text: The Rocroi took part in almost every major battle in Burgundy and Champagne. I hope we lead the charge into Champagne when the time comes. Many Council fighters flee when they see the Rocroi's colors on the sides of our fighters.

1118189.text: Since the outbreak of the Second Gallic Civil War, we've fortified the station. Heavy armor plating, reinforced bulk heads, and upgraded weaponry all helped us repel the Council when they came for the station. They still sometimes attack our patrols, but they haven't mounted another attack on the station.

1118190.text: The Corse, like the Junkers, try to play on both sides of the law. Catching the high ranking members red handed is all but impossible. They do serve a purpose though, as they've no objections to killing a Brigand or two at our request. You'd be wise not to cross them, you never know who is working for them.

1118191.text: Our positions in the Core Worlds are much more well-established than here. The defence of the Border Worlds heavily depends on the Navy, and we don't have much to contribute, given the military power and resources of our enemies.

1118192.text: Our Navy has the strength, but not much in the way of wisdom. Their humiliating defeat in Languedoc is something that proves my words better than anything else possibly could.

1118193.text: Royal Navy officers have a nasty habit of blaming us for the rising crime rates here. Do they think that we assist criminals in any way? I'm insulted that they would ever consider such a thing.

1118194.text: The Royal Navy always shows up at the worst time. Need their support to push some Brigands back? Nowhere to be found. Beating up on a trader trying to make some credits on the side? They show up and tell you to leave.

1118195.text: Last year, a police officer from this station was sentenced to death for murdering someone on planet Nevers. We later heard rumours that the person he had killed was an important Unione Corse member, and that the officer had had long-term business ties with him. I wonder what the Corse member would get for killing an officer. Probably six years in a prison cell that resembles a luxury resort apartment. This job stinks.

1118196.text: The Navy sometimes says that we are cowards. Fear is the mind killer, they say. You know what? Those Council freaks sacrificed thousands of their men to remove a couple dozen of mines that was all that stood between them and their ultimate goal. I openly admit that we are not ready send our officers to stop those psychos. It is suicide.

1118197.text: The Maquis are our primary target in this system. The King is really upset with their recent actions and wants them to be dealt with swiftly and efficiently. Too bad that it requires some unnecessary risk on our part.

1118198.text: I'll admit it, the Maquis scare the hell out of me. They don't fight like the Council, Corse, or the Brigands. They don't care if they die as long as they kill you too. We lost a transport awhile back because a lone Maquis came out of nowhere and rammed the bridge of the transport with his Gecko light fighter. What could we have done?

1118199.text: The Brigands are now so numerous that they have become a danger even for the strongest convoys. Two officers that I was friends with were killed in an attack near Alesia last week. I am afraid for my own life. They said it'd be an easy life in the police, but boy am I a fool. There are many days when I wish I had never joined.

1118200.text: Navy officers talk of honor and pride, yet many in their ranks have openly defected to the Council and now that the Sirian colonies know of Gallia they seem to be unsure of their role.

1118201.text: We had a problem with a large Brigand gang raiding some convoys between here and Dijon. By the time additional patrols could get to the scene to assist, they were gone and most of the orginal patrol dead. One of the dead officers happened to be the lover of a rich noble woman.

1118202.text: The Junkers are not exactly pirates, although they are heavily involved in the Gallic black market. Neither the government officials nor the pirates trust them completely, but their intermediate position grants them many benefits that they could never gain if they were allied with any one particular side.

1118203.text: Many Council families had settled on Quillan after the Gallic Army corps on the planet were defeated. They thought that the planet would now be safe from the Royal Navy. Now few of us believe that we'll hold Quillan for long after the main naval forces enter the system. We only have a few months to evacuate the colonists to a new location. Dozens of thousands of colonists, and we don't even know where to go.

1118204.text: In the Saiun Cloud there's a jump hole leading to Kyushu. Smugglers often use it to move contraband through. Those who know of this station tend to make a stop here and sell their wares while restocking for the journey ahead.

1118205.text: My heavy fighter wing initially had 8 ships in it. We were fighting alongside each other for six years, in Burgundy, Languedoc, and then here. Before 816 AS - this new Sirius chronology is hard to adopt, but I'm trying - our wing only lost one ship near Gap. And then that battle for Montpellier... I was the only one who survived. What will I tell to their wives and kids if I survive the next Naval assault?

1118206.text: They say that the King was in a panic when he heard that the Languedoc defenses had been breached by our military. I doubt that it's true. The King could order his fleets to reinforce the Languedoc defenses long ago, but he did not do that. Most of my comrades disregard my suspicions, but I can't help thinking that we had all fallen into a carefully prepared trap.

1118207.text: We are fully aware of the dangers that Sirius could pose to our nation. But the greater danger comes from within. Our government is seeking military supremacy over the whole of Sirius, and many of us think that it's something more than simple revenge.

1118208.text: All the newcomers are so curious about Gallia's borders and what lies within. We can give you some basic information, but the rest you will have to discover for yourself. It may well be dangerous, but it will also be rewarding.

1118209.text: You start any fights in this bar and you will be eating the street in less than 5 minutes, you hear me?

1118210.text: You probably think that breaching a mine field is an easy task. One mine explodes, and other nearby mines explode in a chain reaction. Reality is much more complicated: Gallic mines are resistant to nearby explosions and even weapon fire, and each one has to be defused manually.

1118211.text: Minefields consist of millions of mines. All of them were produced by Solar Engineering and EFL in their facilities all over Gallia, and then carried to Languedoc and Lorraine to be set in position by trained Navy personnel.

1118212.text: Now that the Ryugu Comet is gone, the nearby mining operations have also come to an end until it passes through here again. For raiders like me that is a setback. Fortunately for me, Samura has uncovered a more lasting source of platinum elsewhere in the system, a legacy of the same comet of sorts. Sadly the location of this enterprise if far beyond the safety of the nebula, so more risk involved. So time to slap on some more armor, heavier guns, and start blasting those Samuroaches.

1118213.text: We're transporting Refugees to Sirius where they are working to rebuild our forces for the next assault on the Royal Navy.

1118214.text: We're able to keep in contact with the Council that is in Sirius via the Gallic and Sirian Neural Nets. You'd think that since they developed independent of each other they wouldn't be able to integrate, but you'd be wrong. They are both based on old Alliance architecture and thus we found a way to integrate them.

1118215.text: We're forced to deal with the likes of the Corse and Brigands, otherwise we wouldn't be able to wage this war. They are nothing but a means to an end. I'd much rather deal with the Corse and Brigands than with the Junkers. At least I know where their loyalties lie.

1118216.text: I must admit that Marne has become a terrible place. We would never admit this in public, but we don't have nearly enough ground troops to enforce law and order there. Criminals swagger about like they own the whole planet, and there is precious little we can do.

1118217.text: The Brigands are very excited about some new business venture that they've started. It has something to do with imported labor from Sirius. I can't imagine what their scam is.

1118218.text: We never had much information about what was happening outside Gallia to begin with. We could only buy the occasional pieces of data delivered by Junker agents, for a very high price. Our knowledge of the other Houses is very patchy and incomplete at best, while our government knows considerably more, as they can afford the high prices the Junkers demand for their information.

1118219.text: One of the most unpleasant revelations that we have had is that the Junkers are present all across Sirius and that no one really knows of their true origins, not even most of the Junkers themselves. It is highly likely that the Junkers were agents of the Royal Dynasty. If so, the government has an immense amount of information on what is happening in Sirius right now, information they could perhaps use against us.

1118220.text: Some of the High Command suspected that the Junkers were related to the Gallic secret services and had a hidden agenda. Most others thought that the Junkers' only goal was attaining wealth by any means necessary. Somehow nobody seemed to realise that neither goal contradicts the other one.

1118221.text: We are negotiating with the Independent Miners right now. We have to trade our technology for the extended star maps that the IMG are using, maps much more detailed than ones found in the Sirius Neural Net. The goal is to use those maps to find a new home for us, or at least a hideout to escape the advancing forces of the Royal Navy.

1118222.text: It is no longer a secret: we trade technologies with the Independent Miners Guild. They are a peaceful faction independent of other Houses, and they share many of our concepts and ideas. In addition to that, the IMG has powerful enemies to defend oneself against. I think that we were lucky that they were the first faction we met when we reached the Orkney system.

1118223.text: Unlike the other corporations, we try to stay out of politics. We aren't military pilots or police officers, if we see the Council, Brigands, or Maquis coming our way we run. We don't stick around and help the Police or Navy. That is their job, not ours.

1118224.text: We've started mining operations in the Tau region, hauling the ores back for refining. If you come across any kind of metal, we'll buy it off you at Alesia.

1118225.text: The Brigands attack our convoys just like everyone else. In most cases they are easy to scare away, but sometimes you can encounter a truly enormous gang. If our escort fighters are losing the fight and try to retreat, the Brigands sometimes go on the rampage, chasing down and killing everyone. They have occasionally been known to forget about the convoy itself in their bloodlust, which often allows it to escape.

1118226.text: Of all the pirate groups of Gallia, the Unione Corse are the ones I hate the most. They are extremely cruel, totally unpredictable, and strike only if their success is assured. Attacks are rare, but the Corse target the most valuable cargoes that we have, and rarely leave any survivors behind.

1118227.text: I've been employed with the GMS since I was twenty two. Two years ago, my wife and only child were killed by a suicide bomber in a cafe. They said that the Maquis were responsible for it. I asked for a transfer into the Border Worlds, and now I'm waiting for an opportunity to find out the location of one of their bases, fill my transport with explosives, and run directly into their primary airlock.

1118228.text: I work on a GMS transport hauling supplies to and from the Tau region for our miners out there. On one trip we got stopped by a bunch of Council ships, but I can't remember what happened. None of the crew does. We all woke up tied up in the cargo hold. The captain wasn't with us but we found him beaten on the bridge.

1118229.text: The EFL are not present here as much as in the Core Systems. In terms of the oil trade, only Planet Nevers poses some interest to us. As far as station building is concerned, the war has put an end to our construction plans in this area.

1118230.text: Oil is present on most of the Core Worlds in Gallia. With abundant oil supplies, we produce high-quality fuel for our engines. It might be old-fashioned and bad for the environment, but it's also cheap. Think about it: finally, almost everyone can afford a good car and never worry about the cost of fuel.

1118231.text: EFL Oil & Machinery is one of the biggest corporations in Gallia, but we are not exactly competitors for GMS as many would think. The government controls both companies and defines which areas of the market we can operate within.

1118232.text: The Council are a pirate group, much like the Maquis or Brigands. I have always found it strange that most of the citizens of Gallia don't understand that they are nothing more than mere criminals.

1118233.text: Pirates and criminals are our enemies, and this war never ends. The Brigands are the most troublesome, due to their large numbers, but their pilots are hardly ever capable of playing as a team. If one ship is damaged or destroyed, occasionally the others will simply flee in random directions.

1118234.text: The Junkers sometimes help us against other pirate groups, for example, warning us about an ambush. I was once flying on a transport and saw our captain handing over a case to a Junker representative. Then we changed course. I don't even want to think what could have happened if the Junker wasn't there to warn us.

1118235.text: Kinkaku-ji is divided into four sectors. Currently we're in Sector One. The Shrine is located in Sector Two, but you need special permission to enter if you're not part of the Sisterhood. Sector Three is only accessible to the Sisterhood and their closest allies. Then it's Sector Four, but, yeah... you really don't want to be caught snooping around in Sector Four.

1118236.text: The Council will never win this war, they are too idealistic. They can't stomach doing what needs to be done to overthrow the Crown. Anyone who helps the Crown is the enemy and deserves to be shot dead.

1118237.text: There are several wrecked Royal Navy fighters near the Champagne Jump Hole, I wonder if there is any salvagable equipment on them? I'm sure there are those who would pay well for Royal Navy equipment.

1118238.text: The Council deny the truth, they have no chance at winning this war. They let their ideals get in the way of what needs to be done. Killing the pawns isn't how you win a chess match, you kill the King to win. That is what needs to be done, kill the King. Checkmate.

1118239.text: I like working in Sector Three. You can really lavish in the Cardamine that's being pumped around through the ventilation systems. There are special masks, designed to filter out the Cardamine particles, for the odd visitor that's allowed to enter Sector Three. But, they're locked in a safe, only the priestesses know the passcode.

1118240.text: This is Kinkaku-ji, a sacred place dedicated to our goddess - Amaterasu - and the founder of our movement - Yuyu Matsuda. I have been a priestess on this station ever since it became operational. We have many visitors now, but few are allowed to enter its inner sanctum. When you do have permission to visit our shrine, make sure to listen to the instructions of the presiding priestesses.

1118241.text: Those who enter the Shrine need to undergo purification rituals before they can approach the altar. These rituals find their origin in ancient Shinto and are designed to cleanse oneself of evil spirits and impurity. Every ritual has meaning, which might not be apparent to outsiders at a first glance. But those who walked the path may discover some traits and emotions, as the mirror of their bodies and minds appear below them.

1118242.text: What has happened to Marne's economy after the Council established its control over the planet? Theoretically, all the factories should have stopped because they don't have any market to supply their manufactured goods to. In fact, more than 70% of those factories are still working. How is it possible?

1118243.text: I hear rumours that the Junkers proved to be traitors who sold information on Sirius to our government. I'm not surprised at all. The Junkers are scum who should have been exterminated a long time ago.

1118244.text: Since the Gallic Royal Navy pushed the Council out of Gallia, we have lost the chance to secretly work for both sides unnoticed. Now we are forced to look for other potential business partners. So far it seems that trade in Artifacts with the Corsairs and Hogosha could be very valuable.

1118245.text: It is truly an honor to be in the presence of the goddess. The ceremony hall is a place of peace and tranquility, where people are expected to keep their voice down when speaking. It is here that we keep a monumental statue of Amaterasu, the goddess of the sun. It is a place of ceremony and self reflection, where we keep our most treasured writings, and educate people in the ways of Matsuda.

1118246.text: You might have seen the large Akegata transports moored at the Shrine. They're transports we've intercepted and taken here for ourselves. Some get too damaged to be salvaged, but a lot of them are repurposed to serve as our Cardamine transports. The crew you say? Let's not go into too much detail, shall we?

1118247.text: We steal from the rich and give to ourselves. That's my motto, and others have said its rather amoral, but so what? I mean, how can you steal anything from the poor?

1118248.text: Our bases are rather unreliable. The airlocks are known to be faulty, and people get sucked into space every month or so. What can I say? We just don't have enough qualified engineers or replacement parts availablefor repairs. So my advice to you is: be smart, and stay away from the airlocks.

1118249.text: We admire the Maquis for their dedication and we even support them where we can, but we will never act like them. Personally, I find their terrorist tactics more efficient than the Council's but that's just me.

1118250.text: The Outcasts are always in need of manual labor, so we send them all of the Royals we capture. The expression on a naval pilots face when he finds out we sold him into slavery is very satisfying.

1118251.text: The Junkers are shady characters with whom we sometimes trade and also occasionally kill for sport. Still, they have no choice but to trade with us. No one else has the capability to smuggle goods into the dangerous areas of Gallia like we do.

1118252.text: Junkers are fast running out of allies. We have remained fiercely loyal to the crown, and as such the enemies of the crown all dislike us. Now that the existence of Sirius and its technology is no longer a secret, we are not as useful to even the crown as we once were. Our future is very uncertain.

1118253.text: ALG Waste Disposal\nDortmund Ship Dealer\nAlbert Vogt

1118254.text: Welcome to Nimes, stranger. I'm taping a street magic special. You wanna see some magic?

1118255.text: See the bartender over there, stranger? Order me some orange soda please.

1118257.text: The Navy is in charge of protecting transport convoys that carry valuable and otherwise important goods through the Gallic Border Worlds. Less important shipments are escorted by the Police. During the Second Gallic Civil War, situation with piracy here became so bad that every other convoy gets attacked, and without a strong escort cargo delivery is plain impossible.

1118258.text: Gallia officials prefer to travel on Royal Navy ships rather than civilian transports or liners. It's less comfortable, but these days it's definitely a safer way to go.

1118259.text: Neural Nets of Gallia and Sirius are based on similar principles and, therefore, are easy to integrate. They are both based off the Alliance computer architecture that developed differently in Gallia and Sirius during the last eight hundred years, but still retains similar origin, and, moreover, is backward compatible.

1118260.text: The Junkers created the first nigh complete backup for the Sirius Neural Net in about 770 AS The data occupied over 140 exabytes of disk space. To transfer it using the compact ships that were used for getting through the mine fields, Gallic engineers had to produce new modifications of small, energy efficient and extremely fast hard drives.

1118261.text: The Sirius Neural Net that the Junkers transferred to Gallia contains publically available information on all Houses, including interactive data archives, billions of web sites, and massive amounts of technical stuff. It is what was called an internet archive in ancient times, only much faster and containing confidential information that very few users have access to.

1118262.text: Neural Net backups were transferred to Gallia from Sirius three times, in 770 AS, in 792 AS and, most lately, in 810 AS The latest copy is the one that the Council bought from the Junkers for about 5 billion credits just recently. The price is very high, and a month before, when the mine field was not breached yet, they demanded ten times more! It was well worth it though. Imagine, almost 200 exabytes of data... Not easy to find needles in a haystack, of course, but the Junkers had catalogued all of the valuable stuff before it was transferred to Gallia.

1118263.text: Hey, you want a drink? You are one of those guys who came here from Sirius, right? Doesn't matter much for me. I'm a pilot, you know. And I'm going to quit my bartender job soon and head into the unwary populated worlds of Sirius. They say that law enforcement there is not nearly as tight as in Gallia.

1118264.text: See, people think that most Brigands are males. In fact, almost a quarter of our pilots are women. Yes, fighter pilots, don't look at me like I'm a simple bartender! Epernay is where many of us prefer to live, or at least stay for long periods of time. Our commander here is a woman too, by the way.

1118266.text: [817 AS] New Diamonds Conquer The Market

1118267.text: A lot of our movement was opposed to the expansions here and at Skye in Newcastle. "Takes away our focus", they say. Personally, I think it just expands our possibilities.

1118268.text: Us here at Holmirth are really getting tired of the Lane Hackers. I was -THIS- close to catching a Planetform ship, when all of a sudden a group of hackers show up!

1118269.text: The Shetland is a major concern for everyone here. It's bad for Gaia or some such things. Personally, I agree - the Hawaii is much nicer! I'd appreciate if you kept that under your hat though.

1118272.text: It's a quick and quiet trip from here to either Dresden or Stuttgart. Hamburg might not be drastically far away, but getting to Frankfurt or Munich takes much longer.

1118273.text: It's nice to be back in the heart of Rheinland. We may have been enjoying some great successes in Omega space, but it's right here that we first began. It means a lot to some of us. The rest prefers shooting Corsairs though.

1118274.text: The LWB doesn't have the greatest pilots, but I hear they managed to free some members from Vierlande. Quite impressive, if it's true. You never know from the boasting around here.

1118275.text: Many of our smugglers stop here on their diamond runs to Liberty. The LWB manages to grow quite a bit of nice food. It's certainly a welcome change from the usual liberated paste! Too bad the government doesn't understand the value of real food.

1118276.text: It's good to see the LWB are developing as pilots. If their numbers keep increasing as they were, we might be able to transfer enough pilots from Rheinland to crush the Corsairs invading our space once and for all.

1118277.text: Liberty's slave trade is an abomination. The only thing worse than that is how Daumann purchases those same slaves for their brutal mines in the Von Rohe belt. Many of our people fighting in Omega-11 are former slaves, either liberated from the miners or from the shipments. They know full well what they are fighting against.

1118278.text: It's a great thing they are working to repatriate slaves here. It really helps our movement increase its numbers, especially considering the war with the Corsairs.

1118279.text: Though many join up with us with mostly retribution in their minds, a lot of them eventually end up embracing the revolutionary cause. Then they either advance through the ranks, or join up with the Bundschuh to fight on the home front. Our leaders aren't bothered much by this. After all, we're all in this together.

1118280.text: This station was originally ran by the Hessians. They passed control on to us, what with all their fighting in the Omega systems. It has proven to be an effective depot for us to launch attacks against Synth Foods convoys heading to Frankfurt and Hamburg. We couldn't hit those much before.

1118281.text: One of the first things the LWB did when they took control of Kaiserslautern was plant several gardens. We may have become pilots these days, but we still know our roots.

1118282.text: I'm glad the Hessians are our allies. I even hear they're working on some kind of heavy battlecruiser. If we had one of those, we could remove Synth Foods in no time!

1118283.text: Some members are saying our cause is already lost because of the changes to Stuttgart's atmosphere. I don't know about that. I read the Bretonians have had a lot of advances with terraforming.

1118284.text: Not only do the Hessians provide us with training and assistance, they also donate plenty of equipment to our cause. Their Asgard line of ships does remarkably well out there. Anything's great if it is helping though.

1118285.text: We are quite sympathetic with the idea of freeing the enslaved population of Sirius. Being forced off our land and being told what to do by Synth Foods and all, many can really sympathise. The more people we free, the better.

1118286.text: I like those red diamonds the Hessians are ferrying through here these days. They're pretty.

1118287.text: The LWB may be lacking in numbers, but we do have one advantage over the other groups: our experience with hydroponics lets us grow plants here without the need for real soil. This helps us with our food, and even helps life support by providing some oxygen recirculation. It cuts down on maintenance costs, and is actually quite efficient in the long run.

1118288.text: Compared to Planet Stuttgart oxygen levels are far lower here. On Darmstadt, we often times increase them to at least try and mimic Stuttgart's atmosphere, but it rarely hits the mark.

1118289.text: With aid from the Red Hessians and the Bundschuh, the LWB has been trying to make up for their lesser skill by increasing the power output of our weaponry. The "Destroyers" we use make up for the occasional misses.

1118290.text: Kaiserslautern is a nice stop for us. With most of our members closer to Bruchsal, it's hard to get word of our cause to New Berlin. Rest and refueling here has really made a difference.

1118291.text: The conversation here is much different than back on Bruchsal. There we speak of philosophy and political theory. Here, conversations are a lot more down to earth. It's nice for a while, but I prefer intellectional stimulation.

1118292.text: Our movement often uses this station as a place to recruit. Those declared unlawful by the government tend to be friendly to our cause. We try and get those who are above piracy to help us whenever we can.

1118293.text: I run supplies from here out to Eltmann sometime. If you stay in the asteroid fields, it's not the riskiest run and Eltmann needs those goods badly. It's a long ride between those jumpholes though.

1118294.text: I'll probably be leaving this station for Omega-11 soon. Freital and Ronneburg are both always in need of good doctors, what with both the radiation and the Corsair onslaught there. Ronneburg might not be bathed in the outbursts of a dying sun, but the amount of injured the sickbays there get more than makes up for that fact.

1118295.text: NIVERTON -- 817 AS -- Red Hessian diamonds always fetch a good price in Liberty, but a new type of diamond now being shipped in by Unioner, Hessian and Junker transports alike has been making a proverbial killing in the black markets. Hessian and Unioner transports are claimed to be buying up Slaves by the hundreds, citing a "campaign of providing freedom". We see it for what it is: a cheap way of increasing their own numbers. The profits however are high, and it's cheaper to simply not ask too many questions.

1118296.text: [817 AS] Liberty Patrol Meets Vigilante Justice

1118297.text: HAMBURG -- 817 AS -- A Liberty Navy recon patrol in Hamburg was attacked yesterday by what the onlookers claim was "local police forces flying in league with designated criminals against Liberty". A high ranking Hamburg Police officer denied allegations of the Federal Police encouraging consorting with criminals when questioned about the situation. He later added that such incidents, while unsanctioned, will likely continue occuring on account of the popular rage of the nation against Libertonian invaders. He has assured us that the officers involved will be disciplined for "taking the law into their own hands".

1118299.text: PACIFICA -- 817 AS -- Ever since their eviction from Freeport 2, the Unioners as a faction survived through cargo obtained from the various Liberty and Rheinland transports heading to and from Texas through both Hudson and Bering. With the start of the Hudson War this trickle of ships quickly dried up, and the Unioners are now almost fully dependent on the blood diamond trade for revenue and the Junkers for supplies. As if that wasn't enough, the growing militarisation of the Hudson and Bering systems make regular operations difficult. However, a determined Unioner raider wing can easily ambush and take down a naval patrol, and scavenge whatever weapons and cargo the patrol may have been carrying.

Constructed at the southern end of the Orkney system, Fort Albi was a small waystation for Gallic shipments and patrols being sent to the Bretonian front through the Hebrides and Taus. Additional modules were installed throughout the Gallic War to fortify the station against threats pouring from the Tau region.

With the end of the Gallic War, Fort Albi became a reinforced border station, providing much needed vigil from the lawless Taus. Although, recently the Gallic Union had repurposed the station to instead serve as a Bounty Hunters Guild headquarters in Gallia, deeming their potential to be more fruitful at her borders, rather than the heartlands.

The Charlemagne battleships were designed around 760 AS, specifically for defensive and support purposes. Battleships of this class were configured to hold and maintain large numbers of fighters and cover them with powerful point defense turrets. By the time of the Gallic invasion of Bretonia, the dated Charlemagnes were used as the rearguard for advancing forces and for protecting vulnerable supply lines. After the destruction of the Oubli fleet in 822 AS, the Gallic Royal Navy dispatched the Betheny to garrison Leeds and provide support for the Carcassonne fleet's blockade of the Independent Worlds.

In 824 AS the Betheny received orders to advance into Magellan as the rearguard of the Carcassonne's continued assault into California. Its primary task was to maintain the "Starvation Strategy" blockade that prevented Libertonian supplies reaching Bretonia. An Allied invasion of Cortez in late 825 AS forced a rapid redeployment to prevent the re-opening of this route during the critical Siege of New London. After months of probing feints and skirmishes, the Betheny cunningly divided its forces to draw away the Bretonian Battleship Harlow, before committing itself to an attack on Liberty' Battleship Yukon.

The Betheny possessed a decisive edge in tonnage and armament, and quickly overran the elderly Yukon. Despite this, the veteran Liberty ship tenaciously clung on, inflicting damage and fighting a delaying action until the Harlow could arrive. While the Yukon was destroyed during the engagement, the combined Bretonian and Liberty fleets ultimately dispatched the Betheny and its escorts in turn. The wreckage of the battle eventually formed the Aruba Debris Field -- work to scrap the Betheny's broken hulk began in 828 AS.

With Battleship Betheny advancing into Magellan in 824 AS to reinforce Carcassonne's flank, Battleship Castres shifted its position and primary task of guarding supply lines in Aquitaine to providing orbital defense in the vicinity of Planet Leeds as well as reinforcing Royal Navy assets in the system.

With the successes in Leeds, Magellan and Manchester, the Castres and it's battlegroup advanced into capital system of Bretonia. There, it formed a tenuous beach head allowing Royalist forces to launch raids and operations to disrupt the Bretonian defences in preparation of the invasion.

Castres' extended fighter bay is now used to its full capacity, providing fighter support for the Battleships Dax and Nogent-le-Rotrou as they advance on Planet New London.

1118342.text:
An abandoned Crayter supply depot, part of a past exploration effort.

Omicron Lost is considered to be the place, where the Crayter refugee flotilla first set foot in Sirius, so to speak. A scientific expedition codenamed "Cradle", composed of the 88th Task Force under admiral Constantine Breetai along with several survey ships reached the system after a long and difficult journey from the Taus. Despite the best efforts, the operation failed to produce any results that could prove valuable. After several months of surveys, research and skirmishes with aliens, the whole operation was called a "minor success" and the 88th Task Force was recalled. The operation received a great deal of criticism. Some Crayter policy-makers called it a "waste of resources beyond understanding", while the Order, Bounty Hunters and some Corsairs considered the presence of a carrier group in Omicron Delta's vicinity a threat to the local balance of power.

Closed down and stripped of any valuable equipment, the FPS 07 serves as a reminder of the first organized effort to explore the system.

1118345.text:
ALLIES:
-

ENEMIES:
Liberty Navy, Liberty Police, Liberty Security Force, Liberty Rogues, Outcasts, Lane Hackers, Junkers, Gallic Royal Navy

The Liberty Insurgency is a well trained and well armed organization serving as the military arm of the Commonwealth of House Liberty, a sovereign state of Libertarian-Socialist nature which lays claim to the systems of Vespucci, Humboldt, and Kansas. The Commonwealth settled on the borders of the Republic following the rebellion of Drake Thastus and his battlegroup from the Liberty Navy in 800 AS with the intent of reclaiming their House from an overreaching expansionist government, it's corrupt incorporated police force, and its criminally invasive intelligence agency.

These early Insurgents soon recognized, however, that their goals of overthrowing Liberty's government would not be accomplished overnight. With this realization they went on to form the Commonwealth, a separatist government embodying the ideology of their movement. While still hoping to eventually wrest control of Liberty's core systems from the Republic, today the Insurgency acts more as a peacekeeping force, policing Commonwealth and Republic space against pirates and smugglers. Although they continue to conduct frequent operations against the Republic's military, police, and intelligence assets as they remain at war.

While this contrast to the early actions of the Insurgency rooted in outright rebellion and terrorism has drawn the attention of Libertonian citizens and foreign nations alike, a large degree of stigma still exists towards the Insurgency, and it may be some time before they and the Commonwealth are recognized as a legitimate entity in Sirius.

1118362.mapped:
The fifth sleeper ship, the Hispania, launched at the same time as its sister ships and broke through the Coalition blockade in the Sol system. Unfortunately, sabotage by Coalition agents that had secreted themselves onboard crippled the engines just as the vessel arrived in the Sirius sector. The passengers awakened from their cryogenic sleep to discover the ship was drifting towards an unknown star system. When the Hispania drifted within range of a red dwarf system, conflict aboard the ship escalated, and about half of the surviving colonists decided to take escape pods, chancing their survival on the promise of a habitable world. The remaining half coaxed the damaged vessel onwards to its eventual destination in the Omicron Alpha system, arriving some time in the year 41 AS Upon their arrival, the crew discovered a planet capable of supporting human life in orbit of the primary star. The Hispania's passengers named the planet Malta -- a harsh place of acidic oceans, gray skies, and vast plains covered in a species of tall, thin, orange grass. Taking whatever equipment they could salvage from the crippled Hispania, they left the hulk in orbit of Malta and began to make a home for themselves on Malta.

Eventually the Outcasts -- as they came to think of themselves -- began a limited exploration of their home system. As pilots wandered farther and farther afield in search of resources, many became seriously ill. Upon returning to Malta fall, the crews recovered quickly. After making a number of genetic scans of critically ill pilots, the doctors made a startling and disturbing discovery. Their genetic code had been altered considerably. The Outcast human DNA was found to contain strands identical to that of the orange grasses that covered the planet -- from which the drug Cardamine was derived. Trace amounts were present in everything on the planet, in their food, their water, even the very air. Once pilots made lengthier journeys away from Malta, their bodies went into shock, followed by death.

The Outcasts were now truly separated from the rest of humanity -- changed so that they could never expand beyond the planet on which they had landed. They needed the Cardamine now, like air, food or water. But with the origin of the sickness solved, they could at least compensate by carrying supplies of Cardamine with them and resume their exploration of their surrounding systems. Over time, their knowledge of Cardamine improved, and the Outcasts learned that distributing it in a highly concentrated dose causes extreme euphoria. When they finally encountered the rest of the Houses in the seventh century, a new strategy emerged. The Outcasts would deliver the poison that would rot the other Houses from the inside out and grow rich from the profits of their trade.

The planet's crust is largely devoid of usable metallic elements, with a few notable exceptions, namely at the heart of her largest continent, and highly unusual deposits of metallic Copper on the ocean floor. Most of its land mass is covered in prairies with natural, low-grade Cardamine grass; large plantations with heavily bred and modified strains have been built on the most fertile sites. Malta's architecture is a largely low-hung and flat, one-story affair in the rural areas; cities are an expression of extremes, built almost entirely in the rare hilly regions of the planet. There is little at ground-level, except starports; most structures are built both deep into the ground and into massive towers that reach towards the sky, constructed yet again as to mimic the textures of the ground. Malta's oceans are strongly acidic and home to algae that tolerate it's high acidity. They appear to hold a slightly green tint from the surface.

These days the Outcasts conduct a lucrative drug-smuggling operation using the network of Jump Holes to escape detection and transport their product into the heart of the House systems through various proxies. They remain relatively few in number; a crash in the birth rate seems to have been another side effect of their genetic modification, although the modifications have lengthened the Outcasts lifespan and physical resilience considerably. There have been no known cases of cancer on Malta since the Outcasts made planetfall.

A new development has been Cryer's continued efforts to create a synthetic version of Cardamine that would be approved as a legal medication within Liberty. This poses a direct threat to the Outcasts' source of income. The Atka Research Station, with nearby access to Edge Nebula clouds, is the most immediate threat to the Outcasts. The location of the base within Corsair territory has brought the Outcasts into conflict with their ancient brethren. The Atka Research Station has come under repeated attacks by Outcast raiding parties in recent years, and the Outcasts always destroy any Cryer transports encountered throughout Sirius without mercy.

The Imperial Kusari Navy are the remnants of Kusari Naval Forces and civilian personnel left behind after the war between Kusari and Gallia was over.

1118384.text: Casablanca is a loss, but not one we haven't anticipated. Corsairs are getting more and more desperate in getting forces through to Dublin, something must be going on there. We will focus on Cadiz first then shut down their supply lines in Omega-47 and eventually starve them to death.

1118385.text: Did you know there's an automated mining colony on the planet below? Yea, they send us what they mine by launching rockets filled with all kinds of ores all the way into the atmosphere. There's enough of it that some of it is set aside for sale so we can keep funding the movement. If you know any enterpreneurs with transports, send them over to this base, or Freital - our other resource stockpile.

1118386.text: After the loss of Casablanca the leadership made a conscious effort to fortify this base. I don't think we can afford losing this base. The Corsairs don't seem too concerned though, we don't get many stragglers around here and our raiders are still laying the pressure on them by Rabat. They seem to be more concerned with getting through to Dublin than fighting us though.

1118387.text: Rumour has it the Mollys weren't very happy with us losing Casablanca. The Corsairs now have an open route all the way to Gran Canaria. I can see what they mean, but the base frees up some of our forces for a build up here at Viernheim. Something tells me the next push we do on Casablanca will simply destroy that base though.

1118388.text: This system is one of the few places in the Omega region where Corsair capital ships can operate at full capacity. They can't break us in Omega-5 because we have the advantage and experience in guerilla warfare, but here it's a completely different matter. This might change soon though. More of our own big ships are being deployed here, and our bomber squadrons are a big thorn in the Corsairs' side. We'll keep hitting their supply line and eventually we'll drain their resistance to the point where we can attack Casablanca again.

1118389.text: Welcome to Viernheim, our main base of operations in Omega-47. The space around Tangier is pretty safe and secure, but watch yourself elsewhere - the Corsairs are pretty protective of their supply lines, though hitting them can score you some big time money. The recruitment office is down the hall on the left!

1118390.text:
"Sickle Mk II" Edge Worlds Particle Cannon
This is a particle-based weapon which, although delivering significant damage at a decent fire rate, requires enormous amounts of energy. This weapon is most effective against graviton shields, and weakest against molecular shields. This is the best Edge Worlds Particle Cannon available.

1118392.text: ARRANMORE -- 817 AS -- Kusari wastes no time in smashing the broken Bretonian Armed Forces before them. They pushed through Tau-31, ignored Harris and went straight for Leeds. Molly leaders are well aware of the danger this poses, but it appears like Bretonia is set to fail even despite Molly help at Harris. Seizing Dublin holdings is thus the only thing left to do before the inevitable Kusari victory. Of course it would be far preferred by everyone if the Kusari did not win. Newcastle Molly clans are expected to continue helping the Armed Forces behind enemy lines, and chances that such behaviour will be discouraged in any way by any clan leaders are quite slim.

1118394.text: BRUCHSAL -- 817 AS -- Our extensive information networks have today provided us with news that can only be described as unprecedented. A new House has been revealed by a group calling themselves "The Council", supposedly a revolutionary group fighting against a corrupt government and corporations - just like ourselves. While brothers in arms are equally welcome regardless if they operate on the other side of Sirius, the rest of their message was far bleaker: the House government they fight against is about to send an assault of grand scale into Sirius with intent to conquer. Kusari seems to be right in its path, and Bretonia soon after. Only time will tell however if such an action will even take place.

1118395.text: [817 AS] Down With The Outcast Alliance!

1118396.text: VOGTLAND -- 817 AS -- The Outcasts finally reveal their treachery. We have suspected them of infiltration attempts in our movement, hoping to gain a foothold in Rheinland through which they can peddle their drugs to our society. Groups within the Red Hessians have been working silently against this, but required proof to be sure of the Outcasts' intentions. This proof was delivered after a transport carrying cargo of advanced weaponry was attacked and destroyed by the Outcast Reapers of Sirius wing. The Revolutionary Council immediately declared all standing agreements between the Outcasts and Hessians as null and void. All Outcasts found within Rheinland or its border systems are to be removed from those systems. All Cardamine transports within Rheinland are now a target of opportunity. The Red Hessians will not be enslaved to drug lords, let this be a message that proves it!

1118398.text: MALTA -- 817 AS -- After the success that our alliance with groups across the colonies brought in eradicating Corsair influence outside of the edge worlds, it seemed rather unlikely that any group would be unsatisfied with the result. And yet the Red Hessians, always blocking the flow of Cardamine into Rheinland, continued to look at us with stark suspicion and seeming disgust. Recently this disgust turned into outright hatred as the Red Hessian leadership unjustly blamed the Outcasts for an attack on one of their transports deep within the Omega systems. No Outcast pilots have or ever will operate in that area, but the Hessians will hear nothing of it. We have anticipated such a scenario a long time ago however and arrangements have been made to ensure that the Outcasts do not lose any business elsewhere as a result of this.

1118399.text: [817 AS] Rheinland's Military Withholds Critical Research

1118400.text: MANHATTAN -- 817 AS -- It has been a few months now since Rheinland has unfoundedly accused Liberty and President Powell himself of leading unsanctioned research on aliens (defined as an act forbidden by intercolonial law), an accusation that led to a large increase of tensions between the two Houses and quite likely accelerated the actual war itself.\n\nBut now it seems that the pot is actually calling the kettle black as information has been revealed by the LSF that Rheinland is stockpiling their own alien biological materials in a facility hidden deep in the Bremen system. Our heroic Navy is already preparing to put an end to this stockpile to ensure that no side in Sirius has access to any kind of weapons of mass destruction that may be gained from knowledge of such forbidden tech.

1118450.text:
Ile du Palais is one of the three main space entrance points for Planet New Paris. The space port derives its name from the Island of Palace (Ile du Palais), named after an island on the river Seine in the heart of ancient Paris where Notre-Dame was located. The island was also known as Ile de la Cite.

Ile du Palais is currently a name for the large island where the main summer residence of the Kings and Queens of Gallia is located. The island is 2102 square kilometers large, making it some 6,000 time larger than its historical prototype. The residence was built in the year 94 AGS by one of the first monarchs of the Valois-Clermont dynasty. When the Valois-Anjou dynasty came to power in 418 AGS, the residence was not used for over 150 years. After the return of the Clermont branch to power in 514 AGS, the residence was rehabilitated. The last significant renovation was undertaken during the reign of King Richard V.

The space port of the same name is actually located on a nearby, smaller island, near a large city named Luxembourg. The city contains a number of government institutions, including the Royal Administration and Chancellor's Office. Governmental and parliamentary bodies of power are located in other cities across New Paris' major continents. The planet has no distinct capital city.

Nowadays, Ile du Palais is one of the main destination points for civilians and civilian cargo going to and from New Paris. The space port is located near a large seaport and several airports that connect Luxembourg with the rest of the planet.

Gallic records of the first steps of Ile-de-France space exploration are known to be incomplete. Existing records indicate that the area where Montmartre is now located was the site of the very first station construction in Gallic space, dated between 80 and 90 AGS. The first station known as Montmartre Space Colony was built in 197 AGS and was fully rebuilt several times, the last rebuild taking place about 200 years ago.

Montmartre in its modern state is a huge station that houses almost one and a half thousand people, making it one of the largest and most well-equipped space colonies in Gallic space. The station docking facilities are administered by the Gallic Navy, but most of the station is under civilian administration. The structure and competency of Montmartre's administration mostly replicate local governments found on populated planets of the House. The station has its own light industry that employs much of its population, producing a wide array of consumer goods, many of which are exported to New Paris and elsewhere.

1118458.mapped:
The Triomphant-class Montreuil was an old battleship in service of the Royal Navy, responsible for defending Ile-de-France from Council strikes from the less secure Burgundy system during the latter half of the Second Gallic Civil War. Its extremely deprecated spaceframe was woefully outclassed even by the weakest of the Council's warships, and the ship was almost immediately crippled by the Council's fleet during the opening minutes of the Battle of New Paris.

Although the Montreuil's hull remained relatively intact, the ship's reactor was heavily damaged and put into emergency shutdown to prevent a catastrophic failure. With its weak hull and outdated systems, the damaged Montreuil was deemed too old to repair, and the vessel was converted into a museum ship in commemoration of the Second Gallic Civil War. The historic ship is a popular tourist destination, and even Sirian visitors are a common sight throughout its corridors.

1118461.mapped: The Fontainebleau Space Colony was built in the year 259 AGS as the very first space residence for Gallic monarchs. Unlike Versailles which was built some 350 years later, Fountainebleau was (and still is) a medium-sized facility that resembles a common space residence rather than a gorgeous palace. Even before Versailles was built, it was not popular with the Gallic monarchs who preferred the vast spaces and plentiful services of their planetside residences. After Versailles was completed, the station was refitted to become an open civilian residence, catering mainly to wealthy Parisians who prefer to live in space. Since the end of the Second Gallic Civil War, public interest has turned against the symbols of former Royalist power. As a consequence, the population is steadily dwindling.

1118464.text: Vincennes is a huge gas nebula, the largest of two nebulae found in the Ile-de-France system. Neither the nebula nor the asteroid field that lies within it contain any valuable ores, and the area was never of much interest for local corporations. Gallic authorities have warned civilians to stay away, as the area is frequented by pirates, smugglers and terrorists.

1118466.text: Vincennes Asteroid Field is located within the nebula of the same name. Is it an relatively small field compared to the size of the nebula. Vincennes field is best known as a place where Brunoy asteroid base is found, currently occupied by the Maquis.

1118468.text: Verrieres is a mined-out asteroid field located not far from the Jump Gate leading to Maine. This field was a site of active mining for about three hundred years. The field was fully depleted of any valuable minerals circa 600 AGS, and mining facilities were relocated to other systems. Verrieres is currently an unremarkable place visited only by Police patrols, sight seeing freelancers and junkers who search for mining loot.

1118470.text:
DIAMETER: 9,430 km.
MASS: 4.48 x 10e24 kg.
TERRAIN: Desert
TEMPERATURE: -146°C to 20°C
ESCAPE VELOCITY: 9.87 km/sec

Chateau-Tierry is a desert world in Ile-de-France. In the earliest days of Ile-de-France's colonization it was considered as a potential site for a human settlement. Discovery of jump holes around the system rendered those plans obsolete and Chateau-Tierry was nothing more of a landmark until the conversion of Compiegne Station into a Military Academy. The Gallic Navy began to construct a small ground base on Chateau-Tierry's surface, aiming to make use of the harsh environment for the training of specialised ground troop units.

1118472.text:
DIAMETER: 1,143 km.
MASS: 6.92 x 10e22 kg.
TERRAIN: Desert
TEMPERATURE: -144°C to 80°C
ESCAPE VELOCITY: 2.71 km/sec

Brunoy is the largest moon of Planet Creteil. It is a barren world devoid of atmosphere, located within the Senart Debris Field.

1118474.text:
DIAMETER: 9,475 km.
MASS: 7.87 x 10e24 kg.
TERRAIN: Barren
TEMPERATURE: -200°C to -40°C
ESCAPE VELOCITY: 6.44 km/sec

Clermont is a medium-sized icy world located on the outskirts of Ile-de-France. The planet is devoid of any volcanic activity and has a crust comprised of water and methane ice. The planet is presumed to contain a dense rocky core. Thin atmosphere and lack of internal heat sources make the planet one of the coldest large solar bodies of Ile-de-France. By contrast, Montataire, the only moon of Clermont, is known for substantial volcanic activity and is actually warmer than its parent planet.

1118476.text:
DIAMETER: 2,541 km.
MASS: 6.14 x 10e23 kg.
TERRAIN: Barren
TEMPERATURE: -120°C to -10°C
ESCAPE VELOCITY: 3.26 km/sec

Montataire is the sole large moon of Planet Clermont. It is known for relatively high internal volcanic activity that once attracted a great deal of attention from Gallic astronomers. Some mining companies attempted to mine hydrocarbons from the planet, but deposits were hard to reach, and no further mining attempts were made.

1118478.text:
DIAMETER: 8,506 km
MASS: 3.23 x 10e24 kg
TERRAIN: N/A
TEMPERATURE: N/A
ESCAPE VELOCITY: 5.14 km/sec

Dourdan is located in the center of Chevreuse Asteroid Field. The planet was once extensively researched as a site for possible future terraforming. Ironically, surveys of the surrounding asteroid field conducted at the same time indicated presence of a jump hole leading to another system that was later named Provence. Discovery of a new means for interstellar travel rendered all ideas of terraforming Ile-de-France planets useless, since habitable planets were found in several systems that were one jump away from Ile-de-France.

1118480.text:
CLASS: Belfry
GRAVITY: Complete
DOCKING: Yes
AMENITIES: Yes
CREW: 540
1118480.mapped:
Located Deep in the Somme asteroid field, Fort Etaples was built in 552 AGS as a base of operations for the Gallic Police and Navy in Picardy. The station was responsible for the security of the nearby Calais Research Facility, and routinely scans all traffic to and from the base.

Etaples became notorious for its aging systems, most of whom were never upgraded since the station's construction. Breakdowns were frequent, to the point that, according to rumour, many pilots of the garrison slept in their ships, mistrustful of the station's life support system. A much-needed overhaul was scheduled to occur in 715 AGS, but the Marne Rebellion diverted the resources needed it for it away.

Nowadays, Etaples maintains its original role. New administration and the end of the war have lead many to believe that the station would finally undergo a complete refit, and some minor replacements have already been carried out. Due to more urgent rebuilding priorities in Picardy, it will be some time before the massive upgrade works start, and it will be longer still for Etaples to lose its unreliable, hazardous reputation to the superstitious soldiery.

CLASS: Q.T.
GRAVITY: Complete
DOCKING: Yes
AMENITIES: Yes
CREW: 1130
1118486.mapped:
The core of Saint-Quentin was the first station established in Picardy. Originally, the station was little more than a production center and supply depot for the construction of the jump gates and trade lanes within the system. When the lanes were completed, the station lay abandoned for over a century, until it was purchased by EFL and converted into a civilian base. Saint-Quentin was opened for colonists in 354 AGS after a lengthy fifteen year reconstruction effort. At that time, it was by far the largest space colony in Gallic space - and possibly in all human space - capable of housing over 14000 inhabitants. Dense spaces and lack of many amenities did not drive off the colonists, the majority of whom came from Amiens and New Paris, and in less than ten years all quarters within Saint-Quentin were purchased or rented.

The population of the colony consisted mainly of space workers and their families. The number of settlers has fluctuated from 8000 to over 12000, reaching its maximum around 500 AGS when massive space construction commenced in Picardy. The population then declined steadily until the start of the Second Gallic Civil War. Royalist refugees have used Saint-Quentin as a waystation as they fled Council space, swelling the station's population by 4000 in the last 15 years. Nowadays, this trend is increasing, though for more concerning reasons, as the climate of Amiens continues to deteriorate. As such, Saint-Quentin is quickly growing thanks to various hastily assembled extensions. These measures are expected to at least slightly ease demographic pressure in Picardy.
