1118489.mapped:
CLASS: Ribeauville
GRAVITY: None
DOCKING: No
AMENITIES: None
CREW: 0
INMATES: 0
La Fere was built in 364 AGS, only ten years after the nearby Saint-Quentin colony was constructed. Ironically, the convicts who were employed to assist the prison's construction were housed in Saint-Quentin until La Fere was completed. While prisoners did not form the majority of the construction workforce, several acts of sabotage were attempted with only one such plot being enacted. An explosive device detonated behind a bulkhead which caused an entire module to be jettisoned from the station, eventually burning up within the atmosphere of planet Laon. The only casualty; the convict who was foolish enough to detonate the bomb while aboard the doomed module. Though the act was only moderately successful, it did serve to highlight the dangers of a criminal workforce and the use prisoners was immediately ceased.

La Fere eventually became known as possibly the worst space prison currently maintained in Gallia. The facility was not particularly large yet held more than 40,000 prisoners at its peak, many being convicted for collaborating with the Council and Maquis. In 724 AGS after a barrage of reports and constant complaints, the Crown was forced to investigate conditions within La Fere culminating in the demotion of the warden and plans to enlarge the facility. Yet the outbreak of war in 733 AGS diverted much of the allocated resources, leaving the prison in it's heavily overcrowded state.

In 740 AGS Council forces launched a daring raid against the facility, successfully freeing the numerous supporters and criminals incarcerated within. The battle and subsequent riot by the newly liberated prisoners has left La Fere as a lifeless charred monument, dedicated to Royalist cruelty. While the Council's ranks and morale may have been bolstered by the storming of La Fere, the group's actions have also granted the freedom of thousands of hardened criminals who are new free to descend upon the unsuspecting citizens of Gallia once more.

1118492.text: A small ice nebula caught in the gravitational pull of planet Montdidier. The Jump Gate to Burgundy is located within the cloud.

1118494.text:
DIAMETER: 4,905 km
MASS: 3.76 x 10e24 kg
TERRAIN: N/A
TEMPERATURE: N/A
ESCAPE VELOCITY: 3.68 km/sec

A small planet which is yet classified as a "gas giant", Montdidier is located within the Nouvion Nebula. The nearby Burgundy jump gate is one of the few, if not the only, jump gates built in the stationary orbit of a planet. The name of the planetoid is derived from a community in the Somme department of ancient France, a place where settlements existed since pre-Roman times. The name is derived from Desiderius (Didier in French), the last king of Lombard who was imprisoned by Charlemagne in 774 A.D.

1118496.text:
DIAMETER: 5,276 km
MASS: 4.83 x 10e24 kg
TERRAIN: Barren
TEMPERATURE: -26°C to 98°C
ESCAPE VELOCITY: 5.26 km/sec

Laon is a medium-sized world whose surface is fully covered with desert. Crystal life forms were found on the planet's surface; some of the initial explorers reported that the crystals have shapeshifting capabilities and can mimic surrounding objects, but later those claims were denounced as fake. The crystals are actually sulfur-based objects which resemble Earth mineral crystals only in appearance. They are cellular colony organisms with primitive analogs of organoids and molecules with properties that resemble DNA in function, transferring procreative information.

1118498.text:
DIAMETER: 12,910 km
MASS: 6.07 x 10e24 kg
TERRAIN: Terrestrial
TEMPERATURE: -55°C to 85°C
ESCAPE VELOCITY: 11.47 km/sec

Lyon is a planet in many ways similar to Orleans. Its discovery in 119 AGS raised questions about the possibility of early sentient interference, in order to introduce similar carbon life forms and similar climatic conditions on those planets. Despite the fact that Lyon, New Paris and Orleans are located only several light years away from each other, and all proved habitable for humans without any terraforming, no remnant of alien presence was found on the planet.

Lyon is different compared to the aforementioned planets, here life has taken longer to evolve within the same time frame. The planet is dominated by a class of species very similar to Earth mammals. Most of Lyon's animals are relatively small, with the largest being not much larger than a human. Imported cows are currently the heaviest terrestrial animals present on the planet. Lyon is one of the most lucrative places for hunting in Gallia. Animals are abundant, not threatened by pollution or overpopulation, and hunting is allowed almost everywhere, with licenses forming a notable amount of income for local communities.

Colonization of Lyon started in 286 AGS. Unlike the ad-hoc colonization of previous planets, it was a well-prepared enterprise that transferred over a million people to the planet after construction crews had prepared basic housing and infrastructure to receive them. The population has grown steadily since that date, up to 1.1 billion people at the last count, which makes it makes it the third most populated planet in Gallic space. The population growth has been slowing down during the last 80 years due to somewhat high unemployment rates around the planet, and nowadays it is projected that the population will start declining in the next 10 or 20 years if the trend continues. Lyon does not possess any heavy industries. Most of the planet's economy revolves around agriculture, light industry and petrochemical industries.

1118500.text:
DIAMETER: 12,910 km
MASS: 6.07 x 10e24 kg
TERRAIN: Arctic
TEMPERATURE: -60°C to 12°C
ESCAPE VELOCITY: 11.47 km/sec
1118500.mapped:
The planet Metz is just inside the habitable zone of Lorraine's binary stars, and only receives enough light to warm the equatorial regions above freezing. Here, the warmest summers rarely exceed 20 degrees celsius, and only where the warm waters hold sway over the weather. Inland, thousands of kilometers of glaciers and snow raise the albedo of the continents such that the continental bodies of Metz, even the most equatorial of them, are thoroughly glaciated. Icy fall winds from the higher altitude interior falls onto the lowlands, disrupting the local climates. To increase the habitability of the planet, EFL has been contracted by the Gallic Office des Eaux et des Forêts to construct a massive mirror array that will warm the equatorial region.

Most of the economic activity on Metz originally supported the Royal Hunt, as organized by the Office Royal des Eaux et Forets, in a centuries long plan to introduce large coniferous arboretums overtop the reasonably bare microbiota of the planet. With the dissolution of the Royal Government, the Great Hunts are no longer held, though Metz remains a popular hunting destination for sportsmen across Gallia. There are many hunting lodges situated across the equatorial lowlands, taking advantage of the amazing views of fjords, circques and hanging valleys carved into the coastlines for tourist income.

Since the fall of the Royal Government, the planet has been subject to serious terraforming. Carbon fuels are burned to increase the greenhouse gasses of the planet, water is melted from glaciers and used to rinse acids out of the soil, and GEOF has contracted EFL to build the Metz Mirror Array,The MMA will provide Metz with approximately 30% more sunlight for 20% more of Metz's 28 hour day once completed.

While the climate is not ideal, during the Marne Rebellion, much of the greenhousery that had been dedicated to expanding boreal forests across the lowlands was turned over to agriculture to support the system. The acidity of the available soils made this a very risky time for the Lorraine System, as any shortage or bad season could have led to system wide famine. The greenhouses and nurseries of GOEF have expanded since that crisis, but their primary product is still flora necessary for the terraforming effort, not agriculture.

The terraforming work on the planet was showing quite good early results, even just a few years into the project, until the Kusari blockaded the planet and later razed all space-based infrastructure in the system. Climate shocks that were caused by the sharp limit of imported carbon fuels caused huge fluctuations in the planet's atmospheric currents, and when the MMA project was destroyed, not only did that reduce the amount of light hitting the planet, some of the material has entered the atmosphere, increasing the amount of solar energy the planet sheds into space. GOEF has promised that it will arrest the problems and restart the terraforming, but their near term efforts are constrained by the lack of space based infrastructure in the system.

CLASS: Eugene Arquette
GRAVITY: Complete
DOCKING: No
AMENITIES: Yes
CREW: 20
1118506.mapped:
The Roanne facility was initially a prominent mining station built by Gallic Metal Service in 392 AGS. At that time it was the largest and most technologically advanced mining base in Gallic space. Over the space of a century however, the Longwy asteroid field was slowly mined out. In 594 AGS, mineable areas of the surrounding field were almost completely depleted, and GMS made the decision to convert Roanne into a large production center with habitats for numerous factories and workers. The construction was personally overseen by one of the most famed GMS directors, Eugene Arquette, who spent most of his life on the station. After Arquette's death, the class designation of the station was officially changed to his name. Over time, Roanne became the primary off-world headquarters of the Gallic Metal Service. It is a tradition that the chief executive of the company spends at least one third of each year onboard the station, personally overseeing the production process.

In the surprise invasion by Kusari, the base found itself in the firing line, its large vertical design proving vulnerable to explosives used in the fighting around the facility between the KNF and retreating Confederacy forces. In light of the damage the base received and the occupation of Lorraine by Kusari, the base, like many others in the system, was abandoned except for a small crew, and docking was removed.

Luxury Liner Belleville is one of the oldest but well-known cruise vessels operated by Bouvet Space Entertainment, formerly a subsidiary of Solar Engineering. After the dissolving of Solar Engineering by a Royal Decree, Bouvet was purchased by IDF Shipping.

The Belleville is currently in the Ile-de-France system, holding a stable orbit close to Planet Meudon after the tumultuous events in Lorraine.

1118511.text:
CLASS: Normandie (Refit)
CREW: CLASSIFIED
ARMAMENT: CLASSIFIED
1118511.mapped:
The Normandie battleship design was first deployed around 656 AGS (740 AS) for offensive assault purposes. These ships were produced in large numbers by royal Gallic shipyards until the early 730s (810s), when the battles of the Second Gallic Civil War revealed several critical flaws in the ships’ construction. Existing vessels were retrofitted to correct various defects, but no new Normandies were built - instead the modernized Richelieu class was developed. Normandie battleships formed the bulk of Gallia’s original Sirius invasion forces.

The Venissieux spent the majority of its service at Kusari's doorstep, ensuring that none would challenge Royal Gallia's dominance over the Taus as the Second Gallic Civil War drew onwards.

This was, however, the ship's very downfall, as it was hit by a streak of bad luck following the dissolution of the Kingdom and the arrival of the Confederacy as the successor state.

For its service in the border regions, the Venissieux was rewarded with the flagship title for one of the Confederacy's states, acting as the mainstay of the eastern fleet. While it marked a new age for the crew, it quickly became evident that the vessel would not fare well in this endeavor once it suffered equipment issues en route to the border.

Initially dismissed, the warship continued making its way to Kusari's frontier, however the unexpected invasion culminated in a full rout of the Venissieux and its subsequent near-guaranteed destruction. It was saved through the efforts of Gallic repair teams, and, despite the vessel making little progress in the field of battle, it eventually recaptured the regions conquered by Kusari.

Once the war had ended, and with control established over the reunified forces, the Gallic Union chose to scrap the Venissieux in 745 AGS.

1118516.text:
CLASS: Massenet
GRAVITY: Complete
DOCKING: Yes
AMENITIES: Yes
CREW: 1200
1118516.mapped:
Vandoeuvres was built in 429 AGS by Tannier Industries as one of the more remote space colonies in Gallic space. Circa 610 AGS, when Tannier was restructured, the site was purchased by Ile-de-France Shipping under Crown permission. Before the IDF transfer, the facility was not prospering. It reached less than half its maxium housing capacity, and the station was notorious for a high unemployment rate and poor accommodations.

IDF dismissed most of the crew and moved the inhabitants to temporary housing on Metz. The station's structure was renewed and expanded with new habitats. In 619 AGS, Vandoeuvres was re-opened for settlers, becoming one of the more convenient and affordable space settlements in Gallic space. Vandoeuvres lies away from major trade routes and areas of pirate activity, making the colony very safe and calm to live in. The facility does not have any notable industrial capacity, but it is almost fully self-sufficient, with hydroponic farms and food production available to serve the colonists' needs. The station also produces a wide array of Luxury Consumer Goods, most of which are exported to other stations and planets by IDF and their partners, allowing the station's residents to enjoy a comfortable middle class income. Currently, most of the station's crew is employed by IDF, although it is technically administrated by the Gendarmerie.

Due to the station's food production capabilities, Vandoeuvres has been pressed into the unusual role of ad hoc breadbasket to Metz and Nevers, where agriculture is difficult. This is expected to be a temporary measure, as the Grand Duchy enacts plans for expanded agricultural projects, including more greenhouses on Metz and floating farms on Nevers..

Pelussin Base was construced circa 500 AGS by the Brigands as an outpost for strike groups flying raids against the nearby Trade Lanes. Over recent decades, Pelussin was expanded with whatever Brigands could steal from corporate ships in order to better accomodate its ever-growing slave population. In recent times, Pelussin reached the status as primary hub for slave trade in Gallia, capable of harboring almost two-and-a-half times as many slaves as the bases permanent population.

Most slaves are typically uneducated citizens of Gallia's lower strata, often willingly signing off their lives without reading the fine print, or unfortunate civilians who have to payback their debts the harsh way. The Brigands account a large demand for attractive women or strong men in their twenties to thirties, though the they also specialized on taking custom orders. Next to the extensive slave market, Pelussin offers various recreational opportunities of which some are not found anywhere else in Gallia but there.

1118527.text: Gourdon is the smallest moon of Privas and not quite massive enough to be spherical by gravitational compression but maintains an ever so slight elongation around its rotational equator. It is thought to have originated in the outer solar system, as its slowly degrading orbit suggests it was captured about half a billion years ago and will be completely submerged in the atmosphere of the planet in a hundred million more.

Once, one of the newest BMM installations that mined several Hydrocarbon deposits in the Manchester system, Birmingham Station was selected as a target of opportunity by the GRI during the blitz on New London, not only for its mining operations but also for its MOX fuel production center.

Using the cover of the Sheffield North Ice Field, the Embrun battlegroup lay in wait as the defense wings present at the base were called to New London to support the defense effort. In a swift attack, the Embrun and its support wings decimated the station with several bombing runs, disappearing into the Sheffield North Ice Field as the Harlow battlegroup arrived on site to defend the base, only to find it a smoldering wreck.

One of the largest mining facilities IMG has produced to date, Cardiff Mining Facility collects Beryllium from the nearby Cardiff Asteroid Field. Despite being a highly lucrative operation, corporate takeover attempts have been few and far between. The majority of the Beryllium mined at Cardiff is shipped to either Liberty or Rheinland. Some Beryllium was originally transported to LD-14 and Stokes for use in the fusion reactors and production facilities there, although with the invasion of the Leeds system by the Kusari Navy and then the Gallic Navy, the IMG ceased shipping to the station.

Normally a busy though uneventful place, war reached Cardiff in 826 AS. With the IMG's refusal to lend Aland Shipyard to the Armed Forces after the destruction of Southampton and mutual declarations of hostility between the IMG and the Kingdom of Bretonia, the latter ordered all of the IMG's assets in Bretonia space seized. IMG decided to focus most of their efforts on defending Aland and abandoned Cardiff due to its unsustainable defensive location in Bretonia core space. The BPA team that was sent to board it found the station completely empty and only one man was injured in action, who suffered a sprained wrist.

The station was subsequently transferred to the administration of Bretonia Mining and Manufacturing, who had resumed beryllium mining operations in the Cardiff Asteroid Field.

The icy world of Mayenne was colonized in 452 AGS. The conditions on the planet were long considered to be too harsh for any mining operation, yet the presence of rare minerals that were difficult to acquire elsewhere in Gallia eventually led the Gallic Metal Service (GMS) to establish a small mining post. The facility grew steadily until the First Gallic War. When the planet ended up on the frontline, the GMS ceased operation and pulled most of the miners out. The Normandy seperatists launched several attacks against the facilities from orbit, destroying many structures in large scale, indiscriminate bombing. This was followed up by a two ground invasions, both of which failed miserably. The seperatists and their equipment were completely unprepared for the extreme conditions on the planet, and many soldiers either froze to death were submerged by snow during the planet's many blizzards.

After the war, the mining facilities were rebuilt and the planet's industry started to grow once again. The current population is nearing 130.000, but due to Mayenne's proximity to the Normandy border, 50.000 of these are part of the Gallic Marine detachment which is permanently stationed on the planet.

Barra Anchorage was a small Gallic Royal Navy outpost originally known as New Tours, erected to serve as a stable base of operations and a waystation for patrols in Tau-31. The station was captured by the Crayter Republic during Operation Ice Lance in mid 826 AS and renamed to Barra Anchorage, although the station is not yet capable of servicing larger vessels and the Crayterian Military's plans for a gunboat scale drydock facility are unlikely to be actualized in the near future.

Due to its position adjacent to Holman, this facility also monitored the activities of the Independent Miners Guild, a role which it has continued to serve under its new administration. It has spacious hangar facilites to maintain a number of fighter wings, and an advanced sensor array to monitor incoming and outgoing traffic within Tau-31.

The base was held by the Crayter Republic following the Gallia war, however with the invasion of Gallia by Kusari, the base was evacuated by Crayter following demands to vacate the system by Kusari.

A hollow structure made of an unknown material. Nomad Hives similar to this can be found in dangerously remote or far-flung locations around the sector, each sharing the same disk-like shape and containing a variety of smaller chambers. Unlike other hives, the mysterious font of energy that usually resides in its core seems absent or otherwise greatly diminished.

This hive in particular is believed to be the first of its kind discovered within the fringes of Sirius, scans have indicated that its construction predates Humanity's arrival in the sector by several thousands of years. However, as no active hive has ever been recorded there is speculation to the true function of these structures. Xenoarcheologists continue to debate if Nomad Hives serve any purpose other than to provide shelter and respite for the alien creatures.

Recently reactivated, anyone unfortunate enough to stumble upon this hive's forgotten hiding place is likely never be heard from again.

Saint-Calais is a dwarf planet located within the Sarthe Ice Field. In the past it was the core part of a much larger planet that was destroyed, possibly due to a planetoid impact. The huge Sarthe field mostly consists of icy debris that was once part of the planet's crust. Saint-Calais itself has no distinguishable atmosphere, and its surface is fully covered with asteroid impact craters.

Le Lude is a relatively small planet of the gas giant class. In addition to its small size, its core appears to be quite small. As a result, the world is rather light, with its average density much lower than the density of liquid water. The atmosphere of Le Lude contains significant amounts of methane. Methane absorption bands contribute to the planet's distinct green color which is otherwise explained by the presence of certain rare gases in its lower cloud layers. Chateau-Gontier Freeport orbits the planet.

1118585.mapped:
Chateauroux was once considered a candidate for terraforming, to create a biosphere suitable for human life. This would not be an easy undertaking as the planet had no liquid surface water. The severe lack of water in the atmosphere also causes extremely high differences in temperature, which in turn spawned massive dust and lightning storms. Early attempts to colonize the world failed as the electrical storms routinely fried any equipment brought down to the surface. While terraforming remains an option, the amount of water that would need to be brought in to the planet is staggering, and there are no suitable sources available in Berry.

The little water the planet does have is locked in the polar icecaps. When scientists came to study them, they found an unusually high concentration of Deuterium within the deeper ice layers. Recognizing its potential as a fuel source, EFL acquired mining rights for both the poles at the stipulation that in times of war the Royal Navy would acquire its fuel at cost price. As a result, EFL's operations on Chateauroux are currently operating at a loss.

The planet also has a few smaller mining operations unrelated to the frigid Deuterium mines. Since the atmosphere is unbreathable, environment suits are needed outside of shielded areas (such as the main spaceport). The planet currently has about 96.000 inhabitants, most of whom are employed in the various mining industries.

First charted in 539 AS, after the discovery of the Munich system in the same year by a Kruger survey vessel, the planet Nuremberg was largely ignored for nearly twenty years, despite a pleasantly temperate climate, with large tracts of plains and savannah that were suitable for farming and settlement. Kruger was instead more interested in the Schwarzwald and Alps clouds, which contained significant amounts of cobalt and silicon, and constructed several small automated mining platforms within the nebulas.

In 557 AS a jump gate was constructed, connecting the Munich system with Frankfurt, and civilian traffic was able to move freely into the system for the first time. Upon further inspection of Nuremberg, it was agreed to begin colonisation immediately, and hundreds of thousands of people from across Rheinland flocked to the new planet in the hopes of securing some of the available land for themselves. Deep Space Engineering soon moved in to begin construction on a series of trade lanes, and the Battleship Erlangen was stationed in orbit of Nuremberg to maintain order.

Nuremberg's oceans were soon revealed to be largely unsuitable for fishing, as most of the dangerous oceanic predators, such as the Pirasharq, quickly destroyed any imported fish stocks. On the land it was a similar story, and it was discovered that the initial planetary scans had missed the dangerous Gimeni worms that inhabited the soil across much of the planet. Virtually all of the imported crops also failed to germinate, despite seemingly ideal conditions. After several years, science teams from Planetform were able to determine that a chemical in the soil was responsible. It was soon found that the skin of the Gimeni worm secretes a chemical that kills any plant life not native to Nuremberg.

In despair, many of the planet's population started abandoning Nuremberg and returning to other parts of Rheinland, leaving the planet largely deserted, until in 738 AS when Daumann and Republican Shipping jointly purchased the planet from the bankrupt Rheinland government in order to build manufactories for the construction of military vehicles. As such, many of Nuremberg's current population and available land was devoted to the manufacture of the heavily armored vehicles, and the heavy industry had slowly been polluting the planet.

Despite population numbers still climbing as of 816 AS and the increasing demand for imported food to Nuremberg to support them, the Rheinland government has refused to grant construction approval for any farming concerns, despite continual lobbying by the legitimate political arms of the LWB and Bundschuh, especially after it was discovered that the native grasses could be safely ingested by a number of animals - including pigs and cows - thus making it safe for livestock farming. This had angered the LWB and the Bundschuh, and to some extent even the Unioners, and raids on the planet's surroundings became fairly commonplace over the last few decades.

In advent of a massive dark matter storm that descended upon the system seemingly from nowhere, Nuremberg's population began to undergo a second and likely final exodus. Planetside meteorologists discovered that the dark matter was quickly eroding the entire planet's atmosphere, as what few crops upon the planet remained universally failed. Cancerous diseases increased exponentially upon the surface population and entire cities were thrown into chaos.

Opposition movements both legitimate and otherwise within Rheinland criticized the government, Daumann, and Republican for their tepidly slow response in providing refuge or aid to the masses of desperate Rheinlanders still fleeing the system by the millions. While still nominally capable of its former wartime output, thousands of craft from civilian-fighters to trains routinely breach the atmosphere every day, despite the best efforts of law enforcement to maintain some semblance of order.

The dying planet has in the span of a single year grown to become the most dangerous and lawless place in Rheinland, dropping to the bottom in nearly every civil demographic.

1118593.text: Charost Depot was the result of a collaboration between the Maquis and Council, carved into one of the more massive ice rocks in Tau-31 during the Gallic War. It fulfills the most basic needs of the Maquis by providing a fairly remote staging point from which to launch guerilla strikes on Gallic Navy assets and Gallic shipping in the Tau systems. Since the nearby Hebrides have been infested by Gallic Royalist forces following the war, the Maquis of Charost have been working with the Gaians to coordinate acts of terrorism against the Royalist remnants and the new Gallic Navy that expand outside of Gallia.

Fourchambault was built in 591 AGS, initially as a small ship building facility. The shipyard was expanded several times during the Second Gallic Civil War, winding up to become one of the largest shipyards in the entirety of Gallia. It was quintessential in providing the Gallic Royal Navy with the considerable numerical and qualitative advantage it needed to breach into Sirius, although at a significant cost to its workers as the place was perpetually overcrowded and operating well past its initial intended capacity.

Fourchambault Shipyard was the primary target of the Kusari forces as the shipyard was the main Gallic Navy infrastructure in the Gallic Border Worlds. The shipyard was destroyed in the second battle of Languedoc when the Kusari reinforcements arrived. A large part of the workers however managed to evacuate from the shipyard facility before the Kusari fleets arrived at Fourchambault.

Hastily constructed shortly after the initiation of the planet Erie's occupation in 830 AS, the Pinnacle Outpost stands as a symbol of defiance following the decimation of the local Zoner flagship, Pinnacle. It currently serves as the refuge for Zoner resistance against the Liberty Republic within the Pennsylvania system. True to its impromptu origins, Pinnacle provides its inhabitants with minimal luxury and scarcely any semblance of privacy. In fact, this asteroid-battered space outpost, known as Driftwood, has gained notoriety for its severe overcrowding.

Although the inception of this space installation was modest, the Zoner Resistance, led by the composed and self-appointed Zachary Graham, successfully established contact with various factions and individuals who played pivotal roles in averting a more dire situation for the entire Zoner Resistance.

Despite these relatively positive developments, the security situation in Pennsylvania remains dire. Particularly, the Bethlehem Exodus of 831 AS has left the local Zoners grappling with material and moral repercussions. The ongoing suppression of the Resistance on Planet Erie is another substantial setback, causing them to lose ground in major fortified cities to the advancing Liberty Republic.

In light of these significant challenges and the seemingly unwavering dominance of the Liberty Republic in the Pennsylvania system by early 833 AS, the leaders of various resistance cells continue to grapple with adjusting to the realities of guerrilla warfare against the self-proclaimed mightiest House in Sirius, marked by profound struggles and losses.

1118607.text: Cher is a large asteroid field consisting mainly of ice asteroids. The field is notable for high pirate activity: a jump hole into Orleanais is located inside, as well as a depot belonging to the Maquis. The whole field is slowly orbiting around Planet Briare, and in several hundred million years the field will fully condense around Briare, forming a new moon.

1118609.text: A large field of rock asteroids that contain small amounts of Beryllium. GMS has tried to establish mining operations several times, but Brigand attacks proved to be too intense in the field to make a mining operation economically viable.

1118611.text: A sparse cloud of space dust and small asteroids orbiting Planet Mereau.

Briare is an icy world with a crust containing water ice and silica compounds. It is the gravitational center of the Cher Ice Asteroid Field which is slowly condensing around the planet.

TERRAIN: Barren
TEMPERATURE: -36°C to 680°C
ESCAPE VELOCITY: 4.47 km/sec

Mereau is a small terrestrial planet that has a complex orbit lying between the two suns of the Berry system. Detailed surveys of its surface are complicated by its high orbital speed and extremely hot temperatures.

1118617.text: Arnon is an asteroid field located far away from the orbital plane of the Berry system. It was not explored thoroughly until about 660 AGS, when large deposits of Platinum were found within many of the field's asteroids. GMS succeeded in acquiring the concession to mine the precious substance. Since then, Vierzon Mining Facility was built inside the field. A Trade Lane leading from Planet Berry is operating to deliver Platinum shipments.

1118619.text:

MASS: 1.47 x 10e24 kg
TERRAIN: Barren
TEMPERATURE: -195°C to -50°C
ESCAPE VELOCITY: 3.90 km/sec

Trouy is the only moon of Planet Bourges. In ancient France, the name belonged to a small community dating from the XI century and located not far from the city of Bourges. The moon, on the contrary, is relatively large and impacts the geology of Bourges in a major way. It is one of the causes of high seismic activity on Bourges. Trouy itself has multiple asteroid impact craters typical for stellar bodies of its kind.

1118621.text:
DIAMETER: 4,562 km
MASS: 3.22 x 10e24 kg
TERRAIN: Ice
TEMPERATURE: -210°C to -30°C
ESCAPE VELOCITY: 4.49 km/sec

Le Blanc is located in the central part of the Creuse Nebula. The whole nebula is condensing around the planet, and it is presumed that Creuse was once its actual atmosphere that was dispersed due to an impact of another large stellar body over one billion years ago.

1118625.mapped:
Dunedin Station is a medium-sized listening post on the fringes of the Empire. Nestled away in the Inverness system, the station is charged with the collection and analysis of data and information that is gathered or intercepted by agents of the BIS. The station relies more on its remote location as its primary defence, rather than overwhelming firepower, although several jamming towers add to its security alongside a number of other classified defences.

Dunedin also serves a role as an embassy to certain groups looking to work with the Bretonian Intelligence services, although admission to the station is highly restricted and movement onboard even more so.

MASS: 2.25 x 10e25 kg
TERRAIN: Barren
TEMPERATURE: 16°C to 220°C
ESCAPE VELOCITY: 7.90 km/sec

Ramsen is a medium-sized volcanic moon orbiting around Planet Avers, slightly larger than its sibling, Cresta. Its orbit crosses the ring system of the gas giant at a great angle, resulting from frequent collisions with the ring fragments. These collisions leave permanent scars on the moon's surface, though the rings themselves are largely unaffected due to the huge difference in orbital velocities. Ripples created on the rings during impact seem to rapidly restore the relatively small hole Ramsen carves upon each pass. The intense surface activities resulting from this unique feature have significantly helped astronomers to inspect the moon's composition, but so far nothing of interest has been found.

1118632.text:
DIAMETER: 4,201 km
MASS: 7.17 x 10e23 kg
TERRAIN: Desert
TEMPERATURE: -130°C to 190°C
ESCAPE VELOCITY: 2.12 km/sec

A relatively low-weight planet for its size, Montferrand was deliberately named after a medieval Earth city that was located near Clermont and was unified with its neighbor (and rival) into Clermont-Ferrand in 1630. A site near the planet was found suitable to build a large station, to be named Clermont. As planned, Clermont was built on Montferrand's border, and grew to be one of the largest installations in Gallic space with over 9,000 residents.

1118634.text:
DIAMETER: 1,816 km
MASS: 1.26 x 10e23 kg
TERRAIN: Desert
TEMPERATURE: -110°C to 220°C
ESCAPE VELOCITY: 1.46 km/sec

Billom is a small desert moon that orbits Planet Montferrand. Much like its home planet, Billom is a desert world devoid of any notable atmosphere and subject to extreme temperatures. Changes in temperature depend on this moon's own rotation, and its orbit around Montferrand.

1118636.text:
DIAMETER: 6,711 km
MASS: 5.24 x 10e24 kg
TERRAIN: Ice
TEMPERATURE: -270°C to -190°C
ESCAPE VELOCITY: 6.71 km/sec

La Rouget is an extremely remote cratered world in the far orbit of the Auvergne sun. It was never visited by manned expeditions, and automated surveys showed its terrain is mostly comprised of rock and ice. The temperature on the surface of Le Rouget is extremely low, making it one of the coldest large planets in all Gallia.

1118638.text:
DIAMETER: 152,384 km
MASS: 2.35 x 10e27 kg
TERRAIN: N/A
TEMPERATURE: N/A
ESCAPE VELOCITY: 64,16 km/sec

As the sole gas giant of the Zurich system, Avers is accompanied by two moons, the icy Cresta and the volcanic Ramsen, as well as an astouningly extensive sytem of rings. The range and dispersion of the size of the fragments making up the rings suggest the two moons used to have other siblings in the distant past, although astronomers don't exclude the possibility of the formation of new ones in the future either.

Frejus Base was built around 600 AGS (684 AS), shortly after the first illegal settlements on Planet Marseille. Initially established to smuggle goods to Provence's unsanctioned colonists, the Brigand hideout is notable for being the first location to experiment with synthesizing Nox's narcotic properties. Despite lofty ambitions, these attempts proved less successful than the Unione Corse's own experiments, with the Brigands eventually settling into the role of distributor for Corse product.

Brigand activity in Provence frequently targeted tourist traffic for ransoms, and the GMS mining operations of the Vaccares Belt. Despite this, most piracy was tempered by threats or bribes by Corsican enforcers, ensuring there was little need for a heavy Royal garrison that could upset the Corse's plans in Provence. In 740 AGS (824 AS), disaster struck when a Brigand raiding party intercepted and boarded a pleasure yacht that was bound for Monte Carlo Freeport.

The Brigands did not realize they had disturbed Corsican patriarch Carisio Lucchesi while entertaining an influential patron -- Felicien Leroux, nephew of Duke Auguste-Henri Hennequin. Both were killed during the chaos of the hijacking. The Corsican response was immediate and furious, with their agents boarding Frejus and massacring all aboard. When officers of the Arles fleet arrived to investigate an anonymous tip, they found a deserted slaughterhouse. The Gallic Royal Navy bombarded the station to prevent its re-occupation, then departed.

GRAVITY: Complete

AMENITIES: Yes
CREW: 310
1118641.mapped:
Luxury Liner Antibes is operated by Bouvet Space Entertainment, a subsidiary of IDF Shipping. Built in 724 AGS, the Antibes is one of the latest examples of the Snapdragon class, a vessel designed by Bouvet to be the pinnacle of luxury in a defendable and opulent package. With former military officials espousing the strength of the vessel's armor and comparing it hyperbolically to the Royal Navy's Obstinate-class, those who booked passage aboard the Antibes had no qualms with paying an increased rate to see the beauty of Gallia in priceless comfort and safety.

Despite her defensive armament and almost fortress-like qualities, both the Maquis and the Brigands have made their attempts at raiding the Antibes over the years, although the ineffectiveness of the latter especially has led some to believe that the Brigand attacks in particular are actually paid programs, put on by Bouvet executives looking to give a good show for their guests.

In 737 AGS, Bouvet's parent company Solar Engineering was dissolved by royal decree, and the majority of its assets were sold off to EFL Oil and Machinery. One of the few exceptions, however, was Bouvet, acquired by IDF Shipping in the latter half of the year. The acquisition meant that all of Bouvet's luxury liners - including the Antibes - were now IDF property. In truth, the acquisition meant little for the liners or their regular visitors, the latter of which noticed no real change in quality of service.

As with everything in Provence, the peaceful mirage of luxury was shattered overnight with the arrival of the Oblique and her attendant Council battlegroup. Council forces had been probing Provence for some time, and the earliest skirmishes served as a warning Bouvet did not take lightly - moving the Antibes into orbit around Avignon, far from the center of the system. The Royalist VIPs on the observation deck saw little beyond the flashing of lights in Marseille's orbit, and were actually quite enthused at the impromptu display. The crew of the Antibes decided it best to keep the Royalist losses a secret, and ensured that the first notice they received of the system's loss came from the Crown itself, long after they'd departed the liner.

Now, with the appearance of the Syndicated Minarchy, the Luxury Liner stands as one of the only attractions of pre-war Provence that remains untouched by agents of the Unione Corse or the Minarchy. Eager to cut its losses in the wake of the Monarchy's fall, Ile-de-France Shipping, which was almost entirely funded by the Crown, sought to sell Antibes to the highest bidder in order to generate much-needed cash reserves and withdraw its assets from a system considered by IDF's board to be too volatile. Sirius' leader in tourism, Orbital Spa and Cruise, has expressed its interest in the legendarily profitable liner.

1118644.mapped: Chateau d'If is the last station built in Gallic space before the Second Gallic Civil War. It was completed in 708 AGS, the construction being a joint effort of the Royal Navy and Royal Police. The prison is meant to be a high-security facility for dangerous criminals, notably Maquis and Council members, as well as other space-based unlawfuls unfortunate enough to be caught alive. Conditions onboard Chateau d'If are rather cold compared to other Gallic prisons. The facility is new, but it was designed to provide minimal space and conveniences for inmates. For all practical purpose a sentence to Chateau d'If means it will be served in solitary confinement. The prison's guards can track every step of each inmate via sophisticated surveillance equipment. The station has a restricted area to which most of the guards don't have access, where the Gallic Navy keeps it's most dangerous enemies.

1118647.text: Originally part of the greater Mer Méditerranée, the Esterel Nebula was created in 201 AGS when an extremely powerful coronal mass ejection tore the nebula from its parent cloud, leaving it to drift aimlessly throughout the Provence system.

1118649.text: The Maures Nebula is classified as a "giant molecular cloud" by the Société Astronomique Gauloise, consisting primarily of condensed helium gas and trace impurities that give a distinctive blue color. Thick and dense, the nebula offers excellent protection from scanners, and rumors abound of a Brigand base deep in the cloud.

Known colloquially as "Le bijou aigue-marine" or "The Aquamarine Jewel", Planet Avignon has stood proudly as a titan among the celestial bodies of Provence. Its massive gravitational well affects nearly every other planet in the system, even causing small ripples in the still waters of Planet Marseille. Avignon has an atmosphere primarily composed of methane and chlorine with traces of several exotic gases, giving the planet its distinctive sea green hue. Avignon's satellites are numerous yet largely indistinguishable from large asteroids, with Cavallion being the sole distinguishable body in the gas giant's sphere of influence.

1118661.text:

Aix is a gas giant located in the central region of the Provence system. Its blue color comes from the methane compounds present in its atmosphere, which is mostly composed of hydrogen and helium.

1118663.text: Nanterre is a large storage depot built in the close orbit of Planet New Paris. It is capable of holding nearly any type of cargo prepared for transfer to and from the planet. Docking is currently restricted.

1118672.text: EFL Oil and Machinery\nBeauvais Production Facility Bartender\nRule Breton

1118673.text: EFL Oil and Machinery\nBeauvais Production Facility Commodity Trader\nSoren Noel

1118674.text: EFL Oil and Machinery\nBeauvais Production Facility Equipment Dealer\nToussaint Royer

1118675.text: EFL Oil and Machinery\nBeauvais Production Facility Ship Dealer\nBeltane Berube

1118691.text: Gallic Navy\nBattleship Montreuil Commodity Trader\nGaspar Loiselle

1118692.text: Gallic Navy\nBattleship Montreuil Equipment Dealer\nFabrice Lachance

1118693.text: Gallic Navy\nBattleship Montreuil Ship Dealer\nCampbell Plourde

1118722.text: I often take a little Tobacco with me for sale when I ship Oil to the Auvergne system. The price I can get at Cannes Resort, Planet Marseilles, and Antibes in Provence earns me a nice little bonus.

1118723.text: Some of the Oil we send out to the Auvergne system is made into Polymers, and returned to us here in Il-de-France. Truly, EFL lubricates the wheels of industry.

1118724.text: Being the largest corporation in Gallia does come with more responsibility. If one of the Trade Lanes ever goes down, who does the government call? Us of course. We're always out there fixing it within a couple of hours. It's best not to keep the Crown waiting...for obvious reason.

1118725.text: Can't you see I'm busy! I have a flood of orders coming in for our Oil - straight to Riom Shipyard in Auvergne. The Royal Navy is insatiable in its appetite for Oil and other war commodities. Alright enough small talk, its back to work for me!

1118726.text: EFL Oil is shipped right across Gallia. Right now I have an order on the docks, ready to be shipped out to Briancon Station in the Languedoc system. A pilot like yourself could come in handy when we are running behind schedule, think you might be interested?

1118727.text: Business is booming for us. The Gallic war machine hungers for ever larger quantities of our Oil. Plus our construction efforts in the Gallic Border Worlds have been taking off as well. It's sad to say we profit from the war, but someone has to fulfill the demand.

1118728.text: The EFL has some big new contracts coming in from the Crown this next month. Something about refurbishing Sirian space stations up to Gallic standards. I don't know exactly what is going on way out there in Sirius, but if there is good money to be made, we will gladly take the work.

1118729.text: We basically dominate the Oil market, so EFL demands top dollar for the work we do. Since we have such a competitive advantage, it's extremely lucrative for our company. The EFL Oil engineers are paid some of the highest starting salaries in Gallia.

1118730.text: To tell you the truth, I'm really looking forward to my retirement in a couple of years. We work hard here at EFL but it can get quite stressful at times, especially nearing a deadline for a contract with the government. We aren't so lucky as those GMS guys and their multiple Wine breaks each day. Those lazy bums.

1118731.text: Our workers here on Beauvais process basic Hydrocarbons into Petrochemicals. We ship them out to places like Clermont and Montlucon in the Auvergne system. They are either consumed on site, or processed into Polymers.

1118732.text: In addition to supplies from New Paris, EFL brings in Oil from Planet Mayenne in the Maine system. That place has had a violent past, but now EFL looks to a bright future thanks to the Royal Family - I am proud to be a part of it!

1118733.text: Obviously, we do a lot of work for the government. This makes us a major target of the Maquis. We hear of our employees getting ambushed by them all the time out in the Gallic Border Worlds. I sure am glad I'm stationed here and not out in the more dangerous areas.

1118734.text: I am making a fortune here, shipping Petrochemicals out to Lorraine. Metz and Chateau Salins have the best price hands down, now is the time to get in before someone else does!

1118735.text: EFL buys Robotics from a manufacturer based out of an IMG station in Omega 3. Many people hate robots as they put people's jobs at risk - but I would rather work with a robot than the Junkers that loiter here!

1118736.text: A fellow I used to work with got killed last month while traveling to a work site out in the Gallic Border Worlds. He was an older gentleman, and one of the nicest guys you could meet. Of course, that doesn't matter to the Maquis. They just want to bring down the government, even if it means killing innocent civilians. It makes me sick to think about it.

1118737.text: Sizable profits can be made by shipping in simple Hydrocarbons from South Shields Refinery. It's unfortunate that we have to begin relying on foreign sources, but our domestic production cannot keep up with the demand.

1118738.text: Our quarterly profits depend on the steady, strong price of Oil. We'll do anything it takes to make sure it stays that way. And I mean anything.

1118739.text: People think we in the EFL are all uptight boring businessmen and engineers. But I'm actually a musician in my spare time! Want to hear one of the songs I wrote? No? Oh, well, alright then.

1118740.text: I see a lot of Nanotubes come through this station. The people at Solar Engineering tell me they do quality assurance on them before they get shipped out. I have my doubts, but there is no doubting the demand for their goods. Forget what the Solar people might tell you - Riom Shipyard in the Auvergne system offers the best price, as it's backed by the Royal Navy.

1118741.text: The Oil industry directly and indirectly supports millions of jobs across Gallia. If you care about fixing the economy, then you're in favor of continuing to develop this potent resource. Oil really is the lifeblood of Gallia.

1118742.text: Unfortunately, government employees are crawling all over the EFL. Half the time I don't know if I'm talking to another EFL employee or an agent of the Crown. I even hear that some of the King's auditors go undercover and pose as EFL employees to make sure we aren't cooking our books. It makes me uneasy.

1118743.text: It's my job to source Engine Components here on this station. Being an EFL employee, I can confidently say our Laval Shipyard produces the best space craft you will find in Gallia, but demand is outrunning supply, so we are having to import some components from Kusari. I am happy to cut you in if you want to make some shipments.

1118744.text: Hard work and loyalty have rewarded me with the easy job of purchasing Cracking Catalysts from this station. I send them to Beauvais Production here in this system. When I want to go home to Le Mans I simply hitch a ride on one of our transports. Life under the King's rule has never been better.

1118745.text: You see a lot of Cryocubes being shipped out to Languedoc. My manifest has me down to move a shipment to Briancon Station after lunch. Its boring, but honest work - just the way I like it!

1118746.text: I heard that a recent shipment of Consumer Goods from this base was stolen by pirates, on the way through Berry. They were destined for our people on Montlucon, as well as Clermont. Stealing clothing and shoes, what a disgrace!

1118747.text: I just got in with a load of Polymers from Montlucon. You can get a good price for them just about anywhere in Il-de-France. Hardly surprising, EFL are the leaders in this kind of technology.

1118748.text: We do good work and support the Crown as much as we can. In turn, the Crown hands us a significant chunk of no-bid government contracts. So far it's been working out great for all parties involved. The GMS could learn a thing or two from us.

1118749.text: I am a logistics manager for EFL. In addition to refueling ships at this station, we also ship Promethene out to Laval Shipyard, and other bases in Maine. The work never stops, if it did I guess all of Gallia would stop with it.

1118750.text: EFL ships in a lot of Promethene from Briancon Station, out in Languedoc. There is always work available for shipping agents coming this way, be they EFL employees or contractors.

1118751.text: What did I do to deserve this? It's now my job to bring Manifolds from the Junkers on Bourg-en-Bresse. The Dockmaster makes me decontaminate my ship whenever I show up. If I can't get off this delivery run I might as well join the Navy!

1118752.text: I see quite a few of the staff here returning as Vacationers from Luxury Liner Belleville. It might be worth taking a holiday out there myself someday. Even better if I can pay for it by bringing back some fellow travelers in my transport.

1118753.text: The wealthy do enjoy their luxuries here on Fontainebleau. I just picked up a nice collection of Blue Diamonds that came in from Planet Metz. They aren't for me, they are for a 'friend'. You won't tell anyone about this will you? One needs to be discrete about these things.

1118754.text: I'm in awe of the bravery and determination of the young men and women of the Gallic Royal Navy. Going off to fight for their House so far from home in hostile territory against a largely unknown enemy really takes some guts. This is why you'll never see me in one of those Royal Fighters. Ha!

1118755.text: At one point GMS controlled more than twenty-five mining installations in Gallia. Many of them are still operational, others have been scrapped due to the fields around them being mined dry. Hopefully, our expansion into Sirius will open up many new opportunities for us.

1118756.text: I've worked many jobs in my life. No company has ever taken care of me or my family as well as the Gallic Metal Service does. When my son was diagnosed with cancer guess what the higher ups in GMS did? They moved my entire family to New Paris and put me in an office position. The best cancer hospital in Gallia is two blocks from my home now. You think IDF would have done that?

1118757.text: There were some stirrings within Gallia when GMS acquired Arcadia Materiaux Distribution, one of its major competitors. With the acquisition, GMS gained almost complete control over space mining in Gallia. Only a handful of independent mining firms remain, and they're too small for GMS to notice.

1118758.text: I manage the warehouses that store the refined minerals that GMS sells. Saint-Flour Mining keeps warehouse number three stocked with Holmium, which is used to create Magnets, Lasers, and various alloys.

1118759.text: We store Tantalum in our warehouses. Vierzon Mining facility refines the Tantalum before it is sent here for storage.

1118760.text: Palladium is in such high demand that keeping our stores of it topped off is difficult. Sancerre operates nonstop to meet the demands. The recent loss from Warehouse 2 was a setback.

1118761.text: I'm the captain of the Pomerol, a Vache-class transport. We're preparing to head to Toulon Mining Facility with some Oil for their mining craft and machinery. As important as metals are, without that black gold to lubricate the ships and machinery, we'd be unable to mine.

1118762.text: If you've got the space to spare and are going to be near Saint-Flour Mining Facility, that guy over there will pay you well for any Holmium you bring back.

1118763.text: My brother made his fortune hauling basic supplies out to Vierzon Mining Facility and shipping Tantalum back here. He is living the good life now as a regional manager in the Picardy system.

1118764.text: The Gold obtained by the GMS in Sirius is shipped out from Battleship Castres for use here in Gallia. We store some of it here before moving it on to wherever the Crown directs it.

1118765.text: We've begun warehousing H Fuel from Kusari here at Sarcelles. We have enough traffic from Sirius now that we have to make their type of fuel available so they can resupply for the return trip.

1118766.text: Sorry, I don't have time to chat. I've got to schedule a shipment of Cracking Catalysts for Planet Le Mans. They always wait until the last minute to place their orders.

1118767.text: While the government does have a large stake in our company, they let us operate more independently than the other major companies. We have no government official on our board of directors either.

1118768.text: I used to work for IDF. I made less money and my benefits were horrible. I was surprised when I came to work for the GMS, not only is my salary higher, the benefits package is amazing!

1118769.text: I'm not sure why, but I hear other employees talking about how the Council tends to ignore GMS miners and transports when encountered. As I said, I'm not sure why they do it.

1118770.text: You! You have a transport, right? Good, I need some High Temperature Alloy. I'll pay you well for a shipment of it. There is some planet in Rheinland that produces it, Nuremburg, I think it's called. Hurry now!

1118771.text: What, you don't know where to get High Temperature Alloy from? Do I have to do everything for you? Alesia Station. Go get me some alloy!

1118772.text: I've heard stories from the miners returning from the Tau region. They talk about a guild of miners who work for no one but themselves! The equipment they use to mine, though, they say is horrible. Our miners are able to work twice as fast with our superior technology.

1118773.text: I overheard someone say they need some Luxury Consumer Goods. I'll tell you what, you go get the goods from Vandoeuvres and I'll broker a deal. Sound good?

1118774.text: The Gallic Metal Service has the best perks of any of the large space-based corporations. We get 40 paid vacation days a year, relatively safe and comfortable working conditions, good job security, and free Wine and Cigar breaks throughout the day. I expect to work here for the rest of my career.

1118775.text: Working in the Taus, we've seen the kind of mining technology that the Sirians use. Needless to say, our fleet of mining ships is top of the line. We're in and out of the mining fields before the Sirians can even get their rusty old pulverizer units to start. Sometimes I wonder how the Sirians even manage to dress themselves in the morning.

1118776.text: We mine Titanium here. Our trade agreements with Rheinland have opened up vast new market opportunities for us. We are now shipping to The Ring regularly.

1118777.text: I overheard that some operation on Shinagawa Station in New Tokyo pays good money for our Titanium. I'm not sure what they use them for there. A peculiar demand if you ask me.

1118778.text: You again? If you don't mind I am trying to enjoy this bottle of Wine. It'll be the last chance I get to once the new Mining Machinery gets here from Etampes Shipping. Then it'll be nonstop work getting it all installed and running.

1118779.text: You look like you're well traveled. Do you have any idea what they use our Titanium for on Wuppertal Refinery? I'm not complaining since they keep us working. I'm just curious.

1118780.text: We send a shipment per week, laden with Titanium, to Misaki Station. Whatever it is they do with them, they have to be making good money doing it.

1118781.text: We use both Mining Machinery and Robotics to aid us in our mining operations. Having automated machines do some of the work means we are kept out of harms way. However, there are times that we have to do it manually, machines do break down you know. Ours come from Etampes Shipping and Aland Shipyard.

1118782.text: Our Titanium is made into Ultralloy on Roanne Production Facility in Lorraine. Ultralloy is used in all sorts of ship building, and since they are partially made of Titanium, I know my job is safe!

1118783.text: If you want some work, we're short a transport. Which means we're also unable to fill an order. A customer on Riom Shipyard wants a shipment of Titanium. It pays well, how about it?

1118784.text: The GMS dominates the mining industry in Gallia. What's the secret to our success? Innovation, flexibility, hard-work, strategic business decisions, and of course Wine. Lots and lots of Wine.

1118785.text: I have just come back from the front lines, with tribute to the Crown in the form of Bretonian Gold. Battleship Castres forms a strongpoint for the collection of such booty. I hear there used to be a luxury liner orbiting the planet called 'Gaia', now there stands the might of the Royal Navy. This wealth I bring with me forms but a small part of the wages owed to Gallia by those Bretonian fools!

1118786.text: There is still a fair amount of Industrial Materials left over from Bretonian activity in the Tau-31 system. I myself have just got back from a rotation on Battleship Carcassonne. We intercepted several Bretonian transports trying to escape the war zone. They didn't stand a chance against us! The King demands that all Bretonian goods be brought back to Gallia as tribute to the Crown. Expect to be handsomely rewarded if you are willing to do your part against the betrayers of our people.

1118787.text: Contrary to some opinions, Gallia is not at war with all of Sirius. The King was very specific in singling out Bretonia for its past injustices against us. Some of the other Houses were fighting Bretonia themselves not very long ago, and are only too happy to trade with us. I have recently returned from the longest journey I have ever been on. Through contacts in Rheinland and Kusari I arranged for Military Vehicles to be shipped to the GRN. As a procurement officer, I tell you it is an epic journey to go all the way out to Planet Nuremburg and back!

1118788.text: We in the Royal Navy almost never make mistakes or break our own laws in the line of duty. But even when we do, the Crown has our back. We are immune from general prosecution due to the special circumstances of Gallia being in a time of war. Besides, legal consequences are to keep the rabble in line, not to hinder us benevolent elites.

1118789.text: A few months ago, we started a domestic program aimed to add more eyes and ears to our security mission. It's called the 'See something, say something' campaign. We instruct the Gallic civilians to report any suspicious or seditious behaviors by their neighbors to the authorities in order to help keep the House safe. Once we receive a tip, we take it from there and punish those responsible. We've been receiving less and less tips lately, so that must mean it's working.

1118790.text: The Royal Navy has had to partner with contractors in the private sector to assist us with our more advanced but controversial surveillance systems. They are all too happy to help when they realize the large amounts of money and patriotic pride they will receive in return. And we can always promise them that the surveillance is 100% legal, because it's being carried out by the good guys: us.

1118791.text: I don't know if the Royal Police are lazy or just stupid. We end up capturing tons of contraband from Brigands in the Core Worlds. There's no way that they could avoid all of the Police. Sometimes I wonder about those officers.

1118792.text: We have a very simple governing structure in Gallia: The King is the embodiment of the law, and everyone who opposes the King opposes the law.

1118793.text: The King is our chief commander in war and all of our military successes are thanks to Him. It is an honor to serve under His command and I would never dream of defying His orders.

1118794.text: I have had the great pleasure of field-testing the latest in Side Arms technology, brought straight from The Ring in New Berlin. Armed transports bring the weapons to us and we submit our feedback in order to keep the engineers informed of our needs. If you are thinking of picking up work as an escort, be sure to stick to the Trade Lanes. The Navy cannot afford to lose sensitive war materials to common thieves or terrorists. I for one wouldn't like to face questions about the loss of government property!

1118795.text: If you've got loyalty, integrity, and courage, I would recommend you look into joining the Royal Navy. We are always accepting new recruits to help win the war. Hopefully you come to us with some skill as a fighter pilot as well.

1118796.text: My last patrol was a disaster. A pack of Maquis jumped us near a downed Trade Lane. They were able to take out three of our fighters and capture their pilots before retreating back into the Vincennes Asteroid Field. I shudder to think of what they are doing to those poor officers now.

1118797.text: The Royal Navy is looking for good pilots such as yourself. Apart from combat vessels, we are in great need of transport pilots to keep the Navy moving forward. Right now I have a contract to ship in Deuterium from Planet Chateauroix in the Berry system. You will have an easy run - Trade Lanes all the way and a full military escort. We have the resources and the manpower to keep up the momentum in this war, but we need your help too! Everyone has to do their part for the Crown.

1118798.text: Ile-De-France is the most impressive beacon of human civilization in the entire galaxy. The pinnacle of human achievement. When flying my patrol around the Hexagon, I can't help but be filled with a deep sense of pride and patriotism. Long live Gallia!

1118799.text: The Gallic citizens have been promised elections and democratic reforms by the King once the war against Sirius is over. Even if the fighting does eventually cease, don't expect those reforms to come anytime soon. Squabbling representatives can't be trusted to do what's right for all of Gallia.

1118800.text: Our Royal Marines are in top fighting form. They are all gung-ho, and ready to kick those Sirians out into the depths of space, where they belong! We are looking for transports to ship them out to our staging points across the front. Brittany, Aquitaine, Tau-31 and Lorraine. There are entire legions of troops waiting to move out. If you are willing to sign up, you can expect a good bonus for the safe and efficient delivery of our fighting men. Gallia needs you!

1118801.text: We in the Royal Navy have all sworn an oath to the House of Gallia. We would gladly die defending her glory.

1118802.text: When someone in high office commits a crime, it is typically too disruptive to prosecute such an important person like a commoner. So they usually get off with a warning. I think the Gallic people recognize the law should be flexible in times of war.

1118803.text: The Junkers are good to keep around. Whenever we need to send some scouts into Sirius on an undercover reconnaissance mission, we usually send them first. They certainly pass for Sirians better than we ever could.

1118804.text: Whenever we take over a Council-held planet, there's typically a long struggle to win the hearts and minds of the populace. In order to accomplish this, the first thing we do is pressure the local media to give us favorable coverage. Our failures or mistakes are omitted from broadcasts that instead focus on our benevolent rebuilding and development efforts. Some call this propaganda, but I call it good strategy.

1118805.text: Royal Navy pilots are some of the most highly regarded people in Gallia. Walking into a bar with a Navy uniform is good for free drinks all night. People routinely come up to me to thank me for my service. It's a healthy cultural characteristic to have a citizenry that so reveres its military men and women.

1118806.text: When we go to recapture the Council-held stations, we try our best to avoid civilian casualties. But at times their deaths are unavoidable. If it gets too bad, we sometimes just launch back into space and blow the entire base. That's the easiest way to cover up our mistakes. Uh, wait, I shouldn't have said that. Ha ha, don't believe everything you hear from a liquored up Navy man. Right? You won't repeat that will you?

1118807.text: These are indeed evil times. Out on the front lines, it's either kill or be killed. Almost nobody gets captured anymore. That's because they know that death is a day at the beach compared with being a prisoner of war in Gallia.

1118808.text: Gallic citizens should relax when it comes to all the new surveillance measures the Crown has developed in order to keep our House safe. If you've done nothing wrong, then you have nothing to hide, right?

1118809.text: If Sirians want to enter Gallia, they need to play by our rules. We can't take a chance by letting them just come and go as they please and wander around our space. We don't want any sensitive information falling into the wrong hands.

1118810.text: Citizens are not entitled to an expectation of privacy in public areas, and that includes out in space. Therefore, expect tracking, cargo scans, and questioning by the Royal Navy and Royal Police at any point along your travels through our Gallic systems. We're always watching.

1118811.text: The other day we stumbled upon a Unione Corse pilot that was carrying some Nox. He should have just dropped it and we would have left him alone. Instead he chose the hostile route, taking out two of our fighters before we finally subdued him. Now he's headed to prison which means I will be watching my back. His friends will surely be coming for revenge.

1118812.text: The Royal Navy has a great interest in Solar Engineering's Lasers. Our research teams here on Melun are developing new applications in the fields of hyperspace navigation, strategic artificial intelligence and fire control systems. We like to keep abreast of the latest developments. Each time Solar makes a new prototype we have samples shipped to us from their labs on Gien Space Colony.

1118813.text: Many people don't know that all of the weapons platforms strewn about Gallia actually double as an advanced surveillance network. The Royal Police and the Royal Navy are able to monitor all traffic and cargo passing through the areas near the weapons platforms. So don't be surprised when an officer stops you and he knows more about your trip than you do.

1118814.text: IDF Shipping does a good job of shipping out essential supplies to our front lines. The route is dangerous and IDF handles it bravely. But don't worry, they are compensated accordingly.

1118815.text: EFL has been crucial to our successes in the war. They've converted almost all of their civilian shipyards into ones for building warships. We could never build all of the ships we need by ourselves. It's good to have a reliable partner like EFL to lean on in times of need.

1118816.text: Most of the major media companies don't need to be checked for overly-critical or seditious stories. They comply with the Crown's preferences willingly in order to secure access to high-ranking government officials for their reports. It's an equitable cycle: if you do your job to the King's liking, he'll make your job easier and more profitable. Everybody wins.

1118817.text: There's a particular department of the government called the "Media Accuracy Ministry". It's their job to sift through the various publications and find any books, articles, or broadcasts that are unduly critical of the King or arguing for policies outside of the mainstream. Once they find some, we are sent over to the responsible publishers to 'clean things up'.

1118818.text: After learning the mistakes of what happened on Planet Marne, the King is determined never to let that happen again. If riots or mass protests were ever to pop up on Planet New Paris, we'll use any means necessary to crush them before they got out of hand or gained popular support. Mass popular unrest is the only thing that the King truly fears.

1118819.text: We show no remorse for criminals before, during, or after their trials. We can always tell which ones are guilty, just by looking at them. Trials in Gallia have mostly just a ceremonial role in the justice system.

1118820.text: Those who can afford to pay us when they are caught can nearly get away with murder. Oh, who am I kidding? They can get away with murder too!

1118821.text: Leniency and pardons for the elite. Crushingly harsh punishments for the lower classes. That, my friend, is the definition of 'justice' in the Royal Police handbook.

1118822.text: You hear rumors around the bars and such that many people in Gallia think we in the Royal Police are corrupt. Well, I'm not worried. A bad reputation is nothing a little cash can't fix.

1118823.text: Yes, we've had a few moustache competitions here at this bar. It's all a big team-building exercise. Nothing brings the Police together like growing out and maintaining our fabulous lip rugs.

1118824.text: On slow days, sometimes we get bored and make our own fun. We'll pull someone over, plant some Nox under their ship, and then let them go to get caught by our buddies down the lane. We all get a roaring good laugh out of the episode, but the victim of the prank usually lacks a sense of humor. I guess heading off to jail for five years isn't as funny for them as it is for us.

1118825.text: Fresh pastries are the Royal Police's only Achilles' heel. You could have a cargo-hold filled to the brim with Nox and Cardamine, but if we're in the middle of an afternoon pastry snack, you're likely to skate by. Just don't count on being so lucky next time.

1118826.text: The pilots in the Royal Navy always talk down to us like we're a second rate defense force. Sure, we may not be equipped for dangerous warfare, but at least we get to go home to our families every night. I bet it gets awful lonely for those Navy boys out on the front lines. I'm happy to be where I am. Those Navy flyboys' wives and girlfriends are happy I'm here too.

1118827.text: If you're carrying Gallic Artifacts when I stop you out in space, you'll be paying me some cash. If you're carrying Cardamine when I stop you out in space, I'll be paying YOU some cash!

1118828.text: The law does not apply to the good people who run this fine house. It is meant as a tool to keep the dirty rabble under control. This is the way it's always been in Gallia, and the way it always will be.

1118829.text: No amount of hinting can get a Maquis pilot to hand over some credits for letting him go. Believe me I've tried. So by now, my policy is just to blow him up rather than try to take him in to prison. It's much easier for everyone that way.

1118830.text: So, are you here to buy or sell? Relax. I've already swept the room for bugs - including yourself. You're clean, so let's talk business. I have customers literally dying to get their hands on Cardamine. I've never seen anything like it. They say it fends off the aging process by decades. I don't know about that, all I know is that people will pay anything to get their hands on it after a while. I will be paying a top price for a good, quality supply. But make no mistake, cross me and you will end up on Gallia's Most Wanted list in no time!

1118831.text: Peaceful dissent is still dissent in Gallia, and it is punished just as harshly. The King will not risk a popular uprising or civil war in his House, least of all in Ile-De-France. Anyone who plans on defying the King better know that he has a whole lot of pain coming their way.

1118832.text: Do you have any idea how difficult it is to keep my moustache properly shaped and maintained in zero-gravity? Well, do you? I didn't think so. Let's just say, the first scientist that invents zero-G moustache wax is going to be an extremely wealthy man.

1118833.text: We do get in a fair amount of practice shooting with our Light Arms, but sometimes training gets kind of boring. Shooting at paper targets just isn't as fun as it used to be. That's why we've started using live moving targets during our target practices. That way, Light Arm training is no longer so dull and repetitive, and we finally have a good use for those Council prisoners in our jail!

1118834.text: The new class of recruits just started working with us on the beat. You know what that means? It's hazing time! We plan on faking a tip for a narcotics bust in an old abandoned station somewhere. We'll send the recruits in and then seal the entryways off, trapping them inside! Then we'll pretend like we can't hear their radio distress calls and leave them there for a few days. Ha Ha Ha Ha Ha! Such good lessons we teach to the kids!

1118835.text: Being a Royal Police officer is the best of both worlds. You have the authority to stop any civilian for any reason and force them to bend to your will under the full weight of the Gallic government. And conversely, you have free license to do whatever the hell you want regardless of established law because there's no one to stop you! I'll say I really made the right career choice.

1118836.text: New surveillance technology has made our jobs even easier than before. All of the Trade Lanes and stations are filled with live-feed video cameras that catch the criminals in the act. Evidence gathering and suspect identification is already done for us. From there, all we need to do is follow the suspect on the screens and bust them. What a wonderful futuristic world we live in today.

1118837.text: The benefits of being an officer in the Royal Police don't end when you retire, no sir! The extremely generous pensions and leniency from former colleagues whenever you get into trouble are just a few of the perks that former Police officers receive. It turns out I really hit the jackpot when I first received my badge.

1118838.text: Money makes the world go 'round. In Gallia, having a lot of money will get you anything you could possibly want. And I do mean anything.

1118839.text: Sometimes on slow nights, we get drunk on Wine and go racing around the Hexagon. It's a good time and it makes the night go much faster. Fighting crime can wait until morning.

1118840.text: I studied at a University on New Paris to be a Quantum Engineer, but the only job I could get out of college was this one with the Royal Police. I feel like my skills are going to waste. But I guess that's what happens when the government controls so much of the economy. The only jobs available are government jobs.

1118841.text: Our main job is supposed to be to protect and serve the good people of Gallia. But we only see the Gallic citizens as one thing: sources of more revenue!

1118842.text: You're going to want to stay out of the Vincennes Nebula. There's a strong Maquis presence and they likely have some sort of base established in the area. They wouldn't think twice about taking out an intruder like you.

1118843.text: The Royal Police have been releasing several autonomous flying "Snitchbots" out into Gallic space to patrol the more dangerous areas off of the Trade Lanes. They roam around, gathering evidence, ID'ing suspects, and alerting police without having to put our men and women in harm's way. Judging by the violent reactions to the Snitchbots from the Maquis, that's definitely a good thing.

1118844.text: We've been shifting a lot of our resources to breaking up the Brigand Slave trade. There's nothing worse than being held against your will and forced to work for your whole life. Those nasty Brigands deserve the harsh punishment that is coming to them. The strange thing about it is that so far we haven't been able to rescue any Slaves that have been held for any substantil length of time. They all seem to be new captives on their way to their first 'workplace'.

1118845.text: After a few weeks on the job, a new Royal Police officer can basically throw out everything he learned at the academy. It just does not apply to the real world of police work. I don't recall even once learning about the proper way to solicit a bribe or covering up evidence of police brutality while in training. Such critical lessons should not have been left out of the curriculum. How else are our new recruits going to be prepared to be a Royal Police officer?
