1118846.text: Crushing political protests? Ah yes, that's one of our specialties. The King won't risk the chance of another Marne, so we strike hard and fast before any problems flare up. In Gallia, you have the right to assemble and protest, as long as your views are in the mainstream.

1118847.text: I hear you're interested in joining up with the Royal Police. That's good, we can always use more qualified officers. Don't worry, we won't be too hard on you - at least not after the first week.

1118848.text: Whenever we catch those Brigand monsters shipping Slaves, we release most of the captives to freedom. Why did I say 'most'? Well, someone has to clean the bathrooms on this station, and it sure as hell isn't going to be me!

1118849.text: Anyone we catch out on our patrols usually gets roughed up pretty good before they are even processed at the nearest Police station. Why? Well, I guess I hadn't really thought of that yet.

1118850.text: Gallic citizens need to be protected from their own worst instincts. That's the impetus for the entire war on drugs in Gallia. People can't be trusted to make their own decisions with dangerous narcotics like Nox, Synthetic Marijuana, and Cardamine because they often make them wrong. And that's where we come in.

1118851.text: EFL has long been loyal to the Crown and this has not gone unnoticed. We assign extra security to EFL convoys whenever they traverse through the Border Worlds. The King rewards fealty with His generosity whenever possible.

1118852.text: Most people like working here in Ile-De-France, but not me. I don't like having all of those government officials and my supervisors watching my every move. I would much prefer an assignment out in the Border Worlds. I've heard anything goes out there, and the Royal Police are basically free to do whatever they want. With my new Cardamine hobby, that could come in handy.

1118853.text: There's something odd about the amount of Slaves coming in to Gallia. They arrive by the boat-loads, brought in by Brigands and other less than savory folks. I just can't see the Brigands needing that much work to be done on their tiny bases. But no worries, our detectives will get to the bottom of this!

1118854.text: Pssst. You wouldn't happen to know where I can get a hold of some Cardamine do you? I am just trying to, um, make a bust. Yes, that's it. We have to keep that stuff off the streets, you know. It will be much safer in my possession.

1118855.text: The last sucker I pulled over got himself a ticket for flying too fast in a Trade Lane. He said he can't control the speed and that he is at the mercy of the Trade Lane's magnetic propulsion system. Waa Waa Waa. While all that may have been true, I still couldn't give up the chance for some easy money, so I doubled his fine for arguing and threatened to arrest him if he kept talking. That shut him up real quick and got me a nice bonus for the day.

1118856.text: You like the wall rug behind me do you? So do I, and so does everyone who passes through here! High quality Furs like that just hit the market this year. Nobody seems to know where they come from, but I have heard some rumors that Junkers supply the shoppes. I also heard that Brigands are involved, but Brigands are involved in anything that makes credits. You know what I think? I think somebody has discovered some new habitable planet somewhere and doesn't want the Crown to find out about it.

1118857.text: There's always a lot of traffic around Ile-De-France since it's Gallia's capital system. It makes it easy for a Royal Policeman like me to just park at a junction along the Hexagon and nail people for violations. There are so many obscure laws to pick from that filling my quota for the day is a piece of cake.

1118858.text: One of the most effective ways to stop drug crime is to tap the communication lines of the criminals and listen in on where a big narcotics deal is going down. Then we show up at just the right time and crash the party. Sometimes we get the wrong person and listen in on some innocent civilians chatting. But the people of Gallia know not to expect any privacy when conversing remotely, so it's not a big deal. They understand we have a job to do and that job is keeping them safe.

1118859.text: The criminal scum in Gallia fund their organizations mainly with smuggling and trading on the black market. We make a lot of busts each year, but there's no way we can keep up. The demand in Gallia for these illegal commodities is just insatiable. Sometimes I wonder what would happen if suddenly everything was legalized. Then how would these gangs of thugs be able to operate?

1118860.text: My shift today is just babysitting duty. I will be escorting Passengers heading out to Vendome Residence. You can find work easily enough doing simple deliveries around here. I honestly don't know why they put me on this assignment. There might be somebody important among the Passengers, but more likely I will be escorting somebody's contraband. It's only a hunch, not enough to demand a search warrant. Besides, if it's my commanding officer organizing this - he might be in on the whole thing!

1118861.text: Cargo piracy is a big problem in Gallia and the Royal Police can't keep up. The big corporations have had to resort to hiring heavily-armed escorts to fight off potential Trade Lane robbers. Unfortunately that's part of the cost of doing business out in space.

1118862.text: There has been quite a bit of traffic coming in to Ile-De-France from Sirius. We know they are all too stupid to know what a reasonable fee is, so we try to squeeze as much out of them as we can. Those fools will pay millions to us for any obscure law we make up. Ha! Those gullible Sirians.

1118863.text: In addition to my desk-duties, I am charged with importing the little luxuries we get to enjoy out here on Fontainebleau. We have a holo-entertainment allowance, and I am expected to ship in only the best from Mortagne Production and Luxury Liner Hawaii. We are Gallia's Finest, charged with protecting the Royalty and elites who live out here. It is only fitting that we receive such rewards for our efforts.

1118864.text: Nox and Cardamine make for one dangerous narcotic cocktail. Trying to take down pilots who are high on that mixture is an impossible ordeal because their erratic flying makes them impossible to hit. The best method is just to sit and wait until the drugs overtake their body functions and they start to seizure. That's when it's time for us to go in and make our seizure!

1118865.text: I like working the late shift when on patrols in this system. There's less congestion and obnoxious idiots flying around. I can instead focus on my job, dealing Nox with the Corse. Oh wait, did I just say that out loud? Uh, forget I said that. That was just a joke, you know?

1118866.text: Over the years, the Royal Police have been enhancing our equipment and weaponry to a point where we are now basically a paramilitary force. Numerous justifications have been used in order to accomplish this. First it was piracy, then rebellion by the Council, then the drug war, and now to fight the Sirian spies. Instead of the civilians seeing us as their neighbors and friends, we are now feared by many. I like this dynamic a lot. People have to do as I say, or else!

1118867.text: Hey you! Don't let me catch you with any Nox in your cargo hold in this system. Or else you'll be shipped off to Fleury-Merogis faster than you can say: "But I thought I'm supposed to get a trial"!

1118868.text: The men in this Police force are all pigs, even by Gallic male standards. They are a bunch of misogynistic children that frequently make inappropriate comments to me, especially when they are drunk on Wine. I wish I could go to a supervisor and report this behavior, but he just gives me the old 'Boys will be boys' saying. Ugh, how did I get stuck in this miserable job?

1118869.text: People who defy the King will always suffer his wrath. I've seen it over and over. Those young idealistic kids start protesting against the Crown's rule one day, and the next day they are shipped off to prison for the next ten years of their life. I always ask them: "Was it worth it?"

1118870.text: Ile-De-France is the safest system in all of Gallia due to the high ratio of Royal Policemen to civilians. The King has prioritized security in this system since it is our capital, so we take this task very seriously. We do not want to disappoint the King, lest we end up in jail cells next to the very prisoners we locked away.

1118871.text: During one traffic stop last week, some young Brigand punk called me a 'pig'. Can you believe that? Well, don't worry, I took him back to the station and me and the boys roughed him up pretty good. By the end, it was him who was squealing like a pig!

1118872.text: By God I am ever so grateful to be getting out of here! Unless you have made your boss angry, police officers get rotated regularly between hell-holes like Fleury-Merogis and much better stations like Ile-du-Palais. Yes indeed, the corrupt or favored get their pick of assignments, and the pariahs end up here for life, like the prisoners they are supposed to watch over. I am just glad the rest of us get a chance to breathe fresh air once in a while!

1118873.text: We lost one of our best young officers the other day over near the Vincennes Nebula. Those vicious Maquis blasted his ship, and then even shot his escape pod! Such barbarism is astonishing to me. From now on, I will show no mercy with the Maquis, as I am sure that I will receive none from them.

1118874.text: Using intelligence and good old fashioned detective work, we've been able to disrupt numerous Council plots against Royal Navy bases in the Core Worlds. The Council are cunning, but we have the full powers of the Gallic government behind us, against which the Council are no match. Hundreds of Councilmen are rotting in jail now thanks to us.

1118875.text: You the pilot who brought in the Light Arms from Calais? If not, I guess you are here for the live-fire tests then? Nice to see some of the scum here 'volunteering' to be the targets. There is nothing quite like justice at the end of a barrel - it's more than these traitors deserve!

1118876.text: Those Junkers can be easily manipulated into giving up their cash. If we ever stop them and try to levy some strange new tax, they usually counter with a bribe of an equivalent amount. That gets us off their backs, but we still got their money. Those Junkers aren't the sharpest knives in the shed.

1118877.text: According to the Royal Police manual, we aren't supposed to smoke Cigars while on duty. Lucky for me, that's what my fifteen daily breaks from work are for!

1118878.text: It's a grim job, but somebody has to do it. The worst kinds of criminals are brought here from across Gallia. Police stations and military battleships are our main control points for the movement of Prisoners to this station. Once you have the right security clearance, there will always be work for you moving these human cattle to their pens.

1118879.text: I refuse to rest until every single drug-running, cargo-stealing, Nox-snorting criminal in Gallia is locked up behind bars! That or until I get tired. Whichever comes first.

1118880.text: Lately we've been forgoing civilian trials in favor of military commissions. The military version of justice is much quicker and less messy. It gets those criminals behind bars faster, which is where they belong. Lawyers and juries, who needs them? The Royal Police and Navy are perfectly fit to decide on a person's guilt.

1118881.text: We ship Tobacco to Metz Station in Lorraine. After a hard day enforcing the law, Gallia's finest deserve a good smoke!

1118882.text: IDF often brings in Gadolinium from Planet Quillan. Despite the influence of the Council on Quillan, we manage to do good business there.

1118883.text: Watch your six if you are looking to bring in Pearls from Planet Bourges! Good profits are to be had, but we have had several shipments come under attack when they enter Orleanais. Some of our crews never made it to Gien Space Colony...

1118884.text: IDF transports Oil to Planet Chateauroux in Berry. It's a safe run for the most part, though we do sometimes run into Brigands sniffing around for fuel to steal.

1118885.text: If taking Oil to Chateauroux is too risky, the alternative point of sale is Fourchambault Shipyard - a naval installation located nearby.

1118886.text: Want to make some quick credits? Bring us some Fertilizer from Planet Holstein. With so many people enlisted in the military, we have to make our agriculture as productive as possible.

1118887.text: You can make excellent profits shipping Nanotubes to Laval Shipyard in Maine - provided you can make it through the Picardy system in one piece!

1118888.text: Gallic Metal Service supplies us with Tantalum from Vierzon Mining Facility. The precious metal is in demand here, expect a fair price for it should you bring it to us.

1118889.text: Our main objective is to make money. And the best way to do that in Gallia, is to have some friends in the government. Securing consistent government contracts is what propelled us to the top of the Gallic shipping industry.

1118890.text: Many of our executives were once high level bureaucrats for the Crown. And many of our employees get appointed by the King to government posts. Naturally, this exchange keeps us close with the Crown and allows us to "fix" new regulatory policy that might hurt our bottom line.

1118891.text: I'm part of the special division of IDF Shipping that is assigned exclusively to serve the Royal Family. They call us up with all sorts of exotic requests and it's our job to fill them as quickly and as courteously as possible. This division is extremely profitable, both financially and politically.

1118892.text: I don't like running routes outside of Gallia. The space is dirtier, the Sirians talk funny, and the green lights on their Trade Lanes are extremely confusing. Not to mention the high proportion of unsavory folk out there. If it were up to me, I would run intra-Gallic shipments only. There's no place like home.

1118893.text: We seem to be shipping a lot of Petrochemicals to Planet Marseille these days. I don't know what they make from them and I don't ask too many questions.

1118894.text: We ship our unique Gallic Plastics to the New Tokyo system. Kusari has its own wonders, as well as dangers. Many Kusari don't like outsiders, I guess that makes them a lot like us?

1118895.text: If you are willing to take the risk, then push through the front lines and deliver this shipment of Cryocubes. They are going to an old Bretonian Battleship in the Dublin system, one that is run by a guild of independent miners.

1118896.text: Our people on Clermont Space Colony need a good supply of Petrochemicals. There isn't really anything planet-side out in the Auvergne system, so it is up to companies like IDF to keep those space stations operational.

1118897.text: We are moving a lot of Cracking Catalysts out to EFL stations across Gallia. EFL pays us a good price. They're used in EFL refining processes somehow. I think you've got to have a chemical engineering degree to understand the answers if you ask any EFL technicians about them.

1118898.text: I just got back from selling a load of Cryocubes in the Kusari capital New Tokyo. An amazing place - I can't wait to get back there! There are great opportunities for us traders in Kusari. The government is somewhat ambivalent towards us, but nothing greases the wheels like profitable commerce.

1118899.text: Consumer Goods that are made here are shipped further than New Paris. In fact one of the best prices you will get is out at Metz Station in the Lorraine system. Everyone needs life's essentials, especially when you are living off-world.

1118900.text: We bring in Pearls from Planet Bourges. The locals here on this station do like to spend on luxuries when they can - who are we to refuse them!

1118901.text: We're always looking to expand our shipping markets to grow the business. Now that we're allowed to ship to some of the Sirian systems, the number of orders has grown significantly. In fact, I'm heading out on another run to Kusari later today!

1118902.text: Passengers depart from here frequently, bound for Clermont Space Colony in Auvergne, and Metz Station in Lorraine.

1118903.text: The residents here in Versailles surely appreciate fine art. Holosculptures bought from the artists that reside on Luxury Liner Hawaii are in great demand among the elite of Ile-de-France.

1118904.text: We bring in Luxury Consumer Goods from Vandoeuvres Space Colony, just a short run from the Lorraine system. It's a quick, safe way to make money. You can't go wrong when you give the wealthy and powerful what they want!

1118905.text: You can make some very easy money taking Spaceship Crew back home to New Paris. Crews will pay good money in their desire to get planet-side, I know I would too.

1118906.text: If you are thinking of bringing in Engine Components from Kusari, be careful. It looks like a nice easy run, but we have had ships come under attack once they leave the safety of Gallia's patrols.

1118907.text: The impressive Trade Lane technology you see around here was an unprecedented team effort between the EFL, the Crown, and IDF Shipping. The EFL designed and built the Lane components, then we shipped them to the construction site and assembled them, and the Crown funded the projects. The investment has paid off many times over with the resulting economic growth of the last century. The Trade Lanes will always be seen as a genuine achievement of the Gallic people worthy of pride.

1118908.text: I'm taking a shipment of Oil out to Lixheim. The pay isn't that great for this run, but the important thing is that it gets me off the lanes and out to Lorraine. Once I get to Battleship Beuvray, its all open space from there. You see, it's the return journey where you make your profit. Lixheim has the good stuff passing through. Oh that sweet Cardi! You smell Cardamine, I smell money!

1118909.text: I got me a hold full of Cardamine from Lixheim to sell. I have literally dozens of short runs I can make that keep me in space as little as possible. With the short runs, I also get to know the people and the turf really well. Seriously, if you sit here and have yourself a meal, I can have this shipment delivered and be back before you finish!

1118910.text: I am heading out tonight to New Paris. I got me a big deal going down right at midnight, when the Customs officers change shift. I know a guy that can get me in with some of that magic NOX I got with me. Normally I would go to Saint-Germain, but my sources tell me they are having a crackdown on smugglers there tonight. Fortunately it means they took staff away from Saint-Denis. Fine by me, Saint-Denis is full of industrial workers looking to unwind. Easy money my friend!

1118911.text: When the price is right, I fly out to Planet Marne to pick up Black Market Munitions. We Junkers do our best to avoid problems with our less, ah, friendly neighbors, but a smile can only deter so much. Ammunition has to deter the rest.

1118912.text: I bring in Cardamine from Torino Base. Those Outcasts creep me out! Sure they are friendly enough when it's down to business, but they look at me funny. I reckon it's the same look I have when I watch mice on a spinning wheel. I don't touch Cardi myself, but sometimes if a packet splits I can't get the smell of it out of the airducts in my ship for days. I have to stay in drydock until all traces are gone so the police sniffers won't ping me for it. They tell me that a little spilt Cardi won't hurt, but I don't know - I just don't know.

1118913.text: Oh this is going to be a sweet run! I have a shipment of Petrochemicals to take out to Monte Carlo. Yeah I know the money isn't great, but Monte Carlo is the biggest party house - in a system full of parties. I'm going to do some business, then let my hair down big time. When I am ready to come back I will have some choice cargo to bring with me. It's a working holiday when you head out to the Provence system, as long as you know the right people you won't have any trouble.

1118914.text: We bring in Manifolds from Bourg-en-Bresse, in the Burgundy system. We Junkers don't mess around - gather the scrap, melt it down and ship it out. The smelters we sell it to can sort out the rest. The demand for metal from the Navy, as well as the other heavy industrial companies, means we don't get held up too much by the police when we are coming back through Ile-de-France. Manifolds are our bread and butter, and makes us legit in the eyes of the law.

1118915.text: I have been feeling so sick these past few days. A friend and I indulged a little too much at a party, and we took some Cardamine. Ever since then I have been feeling off, and I haven't heard from my friend at all! I think I will take a shipping run out to Lixheim with a load of Petrochemicals. I can probably get some more Cardi while I am there, I think that should take the edge off.

1118916.text: Gallic Metal Service does a roaring trade in Holmium, straight out of Saint-Flour Mining Facility in the Auvergne system. The wars are great for business, there is so much demand for metal for construction and repairs that the big companies can't handle all the shipments. Then it falls to sub-contractors like us Junkers to fill in the gaps. Speaking of gaps, we have a habit of making some gaps in the delivery schedules of our own, where goods can fall into the hands of our other customers. All very discrete of course...

1118917.text: All those years of smuggling sensitive Sirian technology into Gallia and the Sirians never even found out. How could they be so stupid? I guess they really do deserve to get steamrolled by the Royal Navy. Poor bastards.

1118918.text: Heading into Sirius nowadays is like traveling back in time. They are so far behind Gallia. I think it's even wearing off on our Sirius-based Junker brothers. They are becoming simpletons just like their Sirian hosts.

1118919.text: The advancing Royal Navy is an unstoppable force so we are a little worried about our Sirius-based Junker friends. But they should be wise enough to get out of the way when the time comes.

1118920.text: Just brought in another shipment from Sirius the other day. Even now that the Sirians know of Gallia, they still haven't caught wind of our tech-smuggling operations out of Sirius. We'll be doing this as long as we can get away with it.

1118921.text: Despite our humble appearance, we Junkers have done quite well for ourselves. We have bases all over Sirius and credits stashed away in all the major houses except Kusari. But keeping a low profile is part of our standard operating procedure. Speaking of which, forget I told you this.

1118922.text: I feel a little bad for our Junker brothers in Sirius. They're busy salvaging metal in the scrap fields and risking their skin on dangerous smuggling routes, while we back in Gallia are taking junkets to Cannes Station, smoking cigars, and drinking wine with the ladies. But the feeling of guilt is nothing a little wine can't fix, right?

1118923.text: The Maquis are some scary folks. We just lost a small convoy to them last week. Junkers, EFL, Civilians,...it doesn't matter to them. If you have any involvement with the Crown, you're a target.

1118924.text: If you ask me, we Junkers aren't getting the respect we deserve around here. Where would EFL be today without the Sirian tech we sold them? Still back in the stone-age, that's where.

1118925.text: Sure you can make some quick credits doing little milk runs around Galla, but the real money is in shipping goods in from Sirius. Though, it's a long trip and a lot can go wrong. High risk, high reward. You know how it goes.

1118926.text: Be careful going down unlighted passageways on Brunoy. Most of the dangerous areas are sealed off, but you never can tell if opening a long abandoned compartment will depressurize the whole deck or not. We've never managed to scrape together enough funds to fully renovate the entire base, so instead there are emergency depressurization seals scattered across all the levels. If the atmospheric pressure sensors set them off, you don't want to be on the wrong side of them...or under them, for that matter. I saw a guy get sliced clean in half by one.

1118927.text: The Maquis bigshots like to talk like Brunoy is fully under our control, but there are plenty of mercenaries around here that have no loyalty to anything apart from their finances. If you've got a bounty on your head, I don't suggest going anywhere alone here. Every so often somebody in the movement goes AWOL, but I think they mostly just find themselves shot out an airlock to pad some greedy merc's pocket. I mean, where are they going to go AWOL to, exactly? But if you're not a wanted man, you shouldn't have anything to worry about.

1118928.text: This base is mostly fairly quiet. The system is almost entirely locked down by the Royal forces, so we can't afford to conduct many standard patrols or raids. This base survives because the Royals can't find it, and we can't risk leading them back here. That doesn't stop the smuggling we do, though. Sometimes I worry about some greedy smuggler deciding to reveal our location to the authorities in exchange for a pay day, but we keep good track of all the outsiders who do business here. They know they wouldn't survive long if they ran their mouth off.

1118929.text: While it is not produced here, we are heavily involved in smuggling Counterfeit Software throughout Gallia. It's one of the few sources of our income that do not force us to rely on selling pirated goods. We have contacts ready to arrange shipments to the population centers of Lorraine, and the resorts in Provence, but our most reliable route is to the Junkers of Monte Carlo Freeport in Provence.

1118930.text: Most of us aren't very happy about dealing with the Junkers, and normally I wouldn't trust them at all, but they are running as much risk as we are by buying Counterfeit Software from us...so as long as they'll pay for it, we'll take their credits and put them to good use against the Royals. If they double-cross us, they won't live long enough to have any regrets.

1118931.text: We have been receiving discreet inquiries about possibly supplying the Corse and Brigands with Counterfeit Software, but so far the only dependable information to go on is the losses when they raid our smugglers. It's not infrequent that clashes between our own pilots and those thugs end up with fatalities, but they seem to be content to just take our cargo instead when they ambush our freighters. Maybe they figure that they'd rather leave us with intact freighters that they can raid later, rather than score kills in the short term.

1118932.text: If you're interested in earning some credits, we schedule regular shipments of Nanotubes going to Vichy Base in Auvergne. I'm not sure what they do with them, but The Council does tend to be tight lipped about sharing information with The Maquis. You'd think they would be more appreciative, given the sacrifices we've made, but more often than not they just want us to do their bidding then shut up and disappear. Bunch of pompous ingrates, if you ask me.

1118933.text: We have some contacts on Compiegne Space Colony that arrange for allotments of Nanotubes to 'accidentally' disappear from random cargo manifests. The managers haven't been able to pick up on the creative accounting so far, although there has been some chatter about production irregularities. Somebody higher up in Solar apparently is up in arms about the raw materials waste, since they aren't delivering as much finished product as they should be in order to consume so many resources.

1118934.text: We have some fairly clever people in the Maquis. We're not all the bloodthirsty terrorists that the Royal media portrays us as. A couple of technicians have set up shop on Brunoy, and they claim that soon they'll be able to reproduce Solar's Nanotube technology. If that's true, we could break their monopoly, and earn a substantial income. I'll believe it when I see it, though. Every crackpot in Gallia wants to sell their new, great strategy to The Maquis as a way to bring down the Crown.

1118935.text: Have you been down to the canteen and tried out the latest fad yet? Somehow the Corse managed to open up a smuggling route to Sirius, and they've been bringing in something called Synthetic Marijuana. You smoke it like Tobacco, but it doesn't feel like Tobacco, let me tell you!

1118936.text: The Corse seem to be the main suppliers for the Synthetic Marijuana that is being smuggled in from Sirius. Personally, I'm not thrilled about having anything to do with the Corse. The Brigands are a bunch of filthy criminals, but at least you know they value their own skins too much to have anything to do with the authorities. The Corse, though, seem to have way too many dealings going on among regular Gallic society. Most people say they can be trusted so long as they're earning profits from dealing with us, but what happens if that changes?

1118937.text: I'm scheduled to head over to Joinville Base with Nanocapacitors. Everybody on Brunoy is clamoring for another load of Synthetic Marijuana. It does do quite a number on you, that's for sure. Everybody is talking about how it makes you just forget all about your cares, but I don't want to forget. I joined The Maquis because I wanted to change Gallia for the better, not just dream away the rest of my life on some forsaken rock in the middle of space. Some of these men need a good kick in the pants.

1118938.text: If you're interested, I can secure passage for you to the new Council haven on Planet Toulouse with the rest of the Refugees headed that way. Some think we're better off just starting a new life out there, away from the Crown's authoritarian control. I think that would be a betrayal of our principles. We aren't separatists, we're reformers and patriots. We have to rebuild our strength, then when the time is right we strike again and finish off this corrupt dynasty once and for all.

1118939.text: If you can manage it, we desperately need the Black Market Munitions that our brothers in arms are producing on Planet Marne. The next time The Council and Maquis strike out against the Royal forces, we need to have plenty of reserves stockpiled for a fight to the finish. This corrupt regime's days are numbered. Hasten the day of victory!

1118940.text: At the rate we're going, I wonder if we'll manage to just depopulate all of Gallia. I never knew we had so many supporters, but every transport to Roussillon is filled to capacity. If the Crown figures out what we're up to out there, we could be in for some serious trouble.

1118941.text: We sell a lot of Tobacco to the resorts in Provence since the wealthy playboys and tourists like their cigars rolled fresh. Marseille, Frejus, Cannes, even the Antibes - its all good as long as you make it there alive.

1118942.text: We were lucky to avoid getting involved in the Second Gallic Civil War. I've heard it was pretty rough out there in the Gallic Border Worlds. The large companies that were sealed out of the home systems took heavy losses.

1118943.text: Our Research and Development department has produced some of the most advanced technologies in Gallia. It's embedded within our corporate culture to always keep pushing existing technologies forward in creative ways. Though we are smaller than the EFL, our brain-power cannot be matched.

1118944.text: If you don't mind doing some work for EFL, haul Cracking Catalysts from Sarcelles Shipping to Saint-Quentin Space Colony. It's just over in Picardy, the next system across. Don't listen to the rumors - on the remote chance you do get held up by Brigands, help is always close at hand in the seat of Royal power.

1118945.text: Solar is primarily involved in space-based operations. As I always say: let the EFL toil around in the dirt, we're happy being out here amongst the stars.

1118946.text: It's tricky working with the EFL and IDF Shipping. You try to be candid and upfront when dealing with clients, but in this case you need to always watch what you say. The representatives in those two companies have one ear for their organization and one for the Crown.

1118947.text: A lot of the work we do around here requires a thorough background check for security clearance. We can't take the chance of someone stealing away our competitive advantage. Here at Solar, we're at the forefront of the technology world in Gallia. So an unauthorized leak or some stolen information would devastate the company.

1118948.text: As you can tell by this corporation's name, we started out by being focused on Solar Energy. Drawing power from the sun, rather than Oil, gave us our niche to push our company through the difficult early stages. Had we been just another Oil and construction company, we probably would have been taken over by EFL long ago.

1118949.text: Back in the old days, the way to succeed in growing a business was to innovate a marketable product, make the customers happy, and then focus on expanding your market share. But nowadays, it seems like the quickest way to quarterly profits is just to lobby the Crown for more no-bid government contracts and tax loop-holes. I think you can guess which corporation I'm talking about.

1118950.text: Nanotubes have a large variety of high tech applications, including vastly shrinking the size of the components used in manufacturing Holotainment Bands. We make regular deliveries of Nanotubes to Mortagne Production in Maine.

1118951.text: We ship in a lot of Cobalt from Briesen Mining Facility over in Omega 3. Just don't ask what a space colony does with it. It all goes to Solar's secure section - that is all you need to know.

1118952.text: Our solar power research is a threat to the political and corporate elites who have large stakes in the Oil industry. If they found out how close we are to powering stations cheaply without Oil, they'd do everything they could to shut us down. That's the reason for all the secrecy around here.

1118953.text: My colleague is risking his neck taking Nanotubes to Fourchambault Shipyard, while I get the easy run taking them to Mortagne Production Facility in the Maine system. Looks like someone really made the boss angry!

1118954.text: Solar pays top price for Gadolinium to be shipped in from Planet Quillan in the Languedoc system. We use it to...well I don't know really, I'm no engineer!

1118955.text: The research we do on this station is kept secure with tightly controlled access. Therefore I am not at liberty to discuss any of it with you.

1118956.text: If you are prepared to take the risk of traveling off the Trade Lanes, the Consumer Goods made here can be sold for a good price in the Provence System. I've been to Cannes and the Antibes, both were well worth the trip.

1118957.text: Next time you are passing through Lorraine, consider carrying Passengers to Provence. The people there will pay a good fare for a speedy and safe journey. You will find them departing from Metz, or Chateau Salins.

1118958.text: Several years ago, we did a study to determine an approximate date as to when the Oil in Gallia will run dry. What we found shocked even our own experts. Naturally, we kept the findings internal. Once our Board of Directors read the report, we doubled our R&D in solar power research and other renewable energies.

1118959.text: We get a lot of sight-seers from Gap Station, but they don't stay more than a day. Why not fly some of them down there and collect an easy fare?

1118960.text: Can you believe that anyone would want to leave Gallia's resorts? Well, they do. You can make some good money by bringing passengers from Planet Nevers, out in the Burgundy system.

1118961.text: Versailles is just one of the Royal residences that you can tour. People often travel to Vendome Residence in Orleanais next, after seeing all the splendor of Versailles.

1118962.text: There is a constant stream of metal shipments coming in from Rheinland. With the war under way, I don't see an end to this demand any time soon.

1118963.text: The war against the Sirians is supposedly about revenge for the events in Sol. But 800+ years is a long time to hold such a grudge, so that must only be a pretext. I have a strange feeling that EFL and the Crown have done their own classified studies on Gallia's rapidly diminishing Oil reserves, and that this new war of territorial conquest has something to do with the outcome of those studies.

1118964.text: I ship out this week to a work site in the Gallic Border Worlds. I'm going to miss all the comforts of home: the Wine, the Cigars, the real gravity. I pray that I can make it back here safely to enjoy those simple pleasures once again.

1118965.text: I make regular runs taking Scientists out to locations throughout Ile-de-France. Some say they are just taking a holiday, others say they are studying the environs. What do I say? Hey I just fly the transport.

1118966.text: I guess if you made it this far, you probably already know. If you have the right security clearance, or know the right people in charge, you can make a fortune bringing in the Gallic Artifacts that are rumored to be out there in space. So much money, so much secrecy, did I mention the part about the money?

1118967.text: The research on this station has benefited greatly in recent times. With trade open to the newly discovered nation of Kusari, there is a great demand for Optronics brought in from a water planet called Honshu. Maybe one day I will see it for myself.

1118968.text: I'm here for a diplomatic mission on behalf of the Kusari government, having arrived with a large group of VIPs that disembarked from Golden Dragon Casino. There are many in Kusari who do not trust Gallia, since they attacked our forces in Tau-31, but I am hopeful that we can forge a long term alliance.

1118969.text: I am certainly impressed with the military forces that Gallia has deployed for their war in Sirius. If only we had known how futile resisting them would be, Kusari might have avoided the humiliation of being forced into a peace accord with Gallia.

1118970.text: At first, the Gallic military seems primitive by comparison to our own, since Gallia's economy and technology relies on fossil fuels almost exclusively. But their weaponry is truly devastating, and their commanders and pilots are the equals of any in Sirius. After what I've seen here, I'm very relieved that Kusari is not part of their plans for vengeance.

1118971.text: Patriotism keeps us from complaining about it back in Rheinland, but the war with Liberty greatly hurt our profitability. We were forced to walk a very fine line in trading with Bretonia or Kusari since they were at war with each other. Of course, neither Bretonia nor Liberty can be happy about Rheinland trading with Gallia, but we have few options.

1118972.text: Unfortunately, Kusari's armistice with Bretonia and peace treaty with Gallia put a temporary halt to their purchases of military hardware from Rheinland. That has started back up again, but in the meantime the Gallic military expressed an interest in purchasing the surplus, and now we are shipping large allotments of Military Vehicles to Gallia.

1118973.text: Trade between Gallia and Rheinland is fairly difficult. Obviously we have some difficulty in taking the fastest routes because those go through Bretonia, although some creative explanation sometimes works. Gallia's economic output is oriented towards the war, not trade exports, so finding products for the return trip is the tricky part. There does seem to be a lot of interest in Kusari technology in Gallia. I'm not entirely sure why, though. It's hard to figure how the Gallic fleets could use incompatible components, and the middle of a war is no time for retrofits.

1118974.text: Things were looking very bleak for Samura after the emperor was deposed and Kishiro became dominant in the government. Fortunately, we managed to interest the Gallic Navy in our Kyushu Rice while Kishiro was distracted with consolidating their control of the government. The Gallic Royal Navy is incorporating our Rice into their fleet rations because it is easily stored and has a long shelf life. I'm not sure why longevity is so important on a battleship. It's not like they're deployed for years without resupplying, but I learned a long time ago not to question military decisions.

1118975.text: Rambouillet Shipyard is a major transit hub for the Royal Navy. There are always Spaceship Crews newly on leave here who are anxious to take passage to Planet New Paris. They can't afford to pay top rates, but it's better than nothing. It's nice to have a cargo that loads and unloads itself for a change, and quickly, too.

1118976.text: I heard there are Plastics for sale at Sarcelles Shipping Platform. They are mostly shipped to destinations around Gallia, but if the price is right I think I can make a profit hauling them back to Kusari. The dealers at Osaka Storage Facility are always looking for new opportunities to branch out into new markets.

1118977.text: Gallia is advanced in many ways, but their environmental regulations are archaic to say the least. Actually, it's more accurate to say that they're nonexistent. All the Gallic shipyards simply discard their waste into space! Most of them are far outside the orbit of nearby planets, so you could argue that it doesn't matter all that much, but just look at the debris fields here in Gallia. They're a major eyesore.

1118978.text: I'm here in an attempt to secure contracts for ALG with the Royal Navy. So far, I've had a hard time convincing them that paying for waste disposal is a net gain. But ALG has proven that recycling is both better for the space environment, and profitable, so I haven't given up yet.

1118979.text: There seems to be some sort of strange relationship between the Junkers in Gallia and the Royal Navy. Every time I bring up scrap recycling, the Naval Officer I'm talking to tries to change the subject. I seem to make some headway talking about Toxic Waste, but there may be no way to convince the GRN that ALG can handle scrap better than the Junkers. You'd think the massive debris fields would be evidence enough that the Junkers can't handle the volume, but Gallians don't seem to think like we do.

1118989.text: You're relatively safe around the bar area, stranger, but keep your distance from some of the deeper areas of the station. They're filled with filth and blood, so to speak.

1118990.text: It's not just the Brigands on this station. The population here on Salbris is a lot more diverse than that. You got representatives of every space crime faction, and from many planetary crime factions, too.

1118991.text: Look, the area down to the right from here, towards the center of the asteroid, is controlled by some thugs from Picardy. And up to the right there are some folks from Orleanais, and know what? Even we brigands rarely visit that place.

1118992.text: They say that a Brigand's life is tough. Well that might be the case, but look at the drug trade business. It's not just illegal and profitable, it's downright fun!

1118993.text: Yep, those junkies...You see, sometimes you feel some pity for those poor marks who line up to spend their last credit on a quick fix. Pity's bad for business though.

1118994.text: We manage to raid Chateaudin's Silver convoys every so often. Frejus Base in Provence is where we haul most of it. From there we can offload it to the Junkers on Monte Carlo. I think they mint it into coins and souvenirs to sell to rich tourists at the resorts. What Frejus won't take, we take to Valence Base in Languedoc.

1118995.text: Oh, sir, what was that thing called? Libertine Ale? Bartender, fetch me some more!

1118996.text: Ale! Or I shall blow a hole in this bar's window! Hey, stranger, do you know they serve ale twice faster with each dozen of light years away from Ile-de-France? Wait, where was that blaster...

1118997.text: Look, I'm a drunkard, but I know a hell of a lot about business. You know, grab some silver from here, get it elsewhere, or vice versa, I don't remember. How much do I earn? Look, that's not some cheap liquor I got over here. Try some! Bartender! Ale!

1118998.text: Hey, strangeling, don't look at me like that. Men stare at me all the time. And who cares, I'm not interested.

1118999.text: You mean, why am I not interested? Because I'm all business. You'll find prostitutes of all sorts you need a just another corridor away. What I am looking for is sensuality.

1119000.text: And, know what? The sensuality is not something any guy can offer. Not just here. Anywhere. All rude and plain and stuff. Girls, on the other hand, are completely different story. Now that you know, care to hear a few stories?.

1119001.text: Welcome to Corse central! Don't let yourself be fooled by all the overcrowding, this is the entertainment capital of Gallia. You can get anything you want here, just find an open seat and plug yourself into a Hypnotainment Band. I have a wide variety of holo-scenarios available for purchase.

1119002.text: I've heard that Solar is ready to pay huge bounties for accurate intel about this base's whereabouts. They'll stop at nothing to shut down our Hypno Band operations. Fat chance of that happening. We've got friends in high places, if you know what I mean. Low places too, for that matter. Speaking of which, you want a drink or what?

1119003.text: You know what? There's only one thing better than having a product that everyone wants and will pay top credit for, and that's having a high demand, high grossing product that someone else paid the research and development costs for. I don't blame Solar for being so mad at us for hijacking their Holo Bands. They must have been crazy if they thought they could just keep this technology for themselves, though.

1119004.text: Oh yeah, I got some sweet Hypnotainment Bands ready for sale out on the Provence resorts. If you can slip past the patrols and get yourself in there, prepared to make some serious credits! Just don't be too quick to sample our 'product'. I need pilots free from distraction, not sitting in the pilot's seat laughing to themselves when the Police show up for a scan.

1119005.text: Nothing like some hard currency coming in from outside Gallia. We have some contacts that are ready for our freshly hacked Hypnotainment Bands. Some place called Kusari has plenty of bored technicians who are pretty interested in our handiwork. Shina...Shinagawa Station it's called. Funny sounding language, funny looking people. Nothing funny about the money though, it's all serious when it comes time to negotiate the price!

1119006.text: After the Council brought down the minefields between Gallia and Sirius, every Brigand and Corse between Auvergne and Lorraine has been scheming to make their fortune with the new black market opportunities. The more things change, the more things stay the same, you know? Gallia has some interesting diversions to offer Sirius, and Sirius has some that Gallians will pay top credit for. I'm working on establishing contacts in Liberty for distributing Hypno Bands. If you can help, I can cut you in on things at an early stage. The sky's the limit!

1119007.text: We are doing big business in the Sirius sector now. Hypnotainment Bands will be the next big thing to hit their black markets. Those Kusari people have a station called Golden Dragon Casino in the Shikoku system, a good place for a few shady deals to go down. I plan on visiting it myself someday. Shouldn't be too difficult now that Gallia has a treaty with them. I wonder if I need to get a visa or some other paperwork? Shouldn't be too hard to get one forged.

1119008.text: If you want to tap into the new Sirius markets, you have to be prepared to travel. I made a few contacts, did a few months travelling and scored big! Now I can run Hypnotainment Bands right out to some planet called Stuttgart. Nice place, those Sirius planets are so sparse, they are like country hamlets compared to our Core Worlds.

1119009.text: The fastest routes from Gallia to Rheinland aren't easy. In fact, they're downright insane. You've got a choice between GRN battleships in the Taus, or on Bretonia's flank in Edinburgh. Either way, get too close to a Navy patrol and you're in hot water. Maybe...Last trip, I ran into a high ranking officer leading a patrol and I thought I was looking at a long stay at La Fere for sure, but instead they just 'confiscated' my cargo and let me go. I wish I had gotten that officer's name. I have a feeling that he wouldn't be unhappy to run into me again sometime.

1119010.text: I managed to establish my Hypnotainment network right in the heart of enemy territory. Our hacked Bands now take pride of place in the black market run out of Planets New London and Leeds in Bretonia. I had the fun of watching a Bretonian prisoner we found being 'holointerrogated'. We used one of the Royal Navy's propaganda simulations of Bretonia being defeated, and plugged the bastard right into it with no filters! After three weeks of that he was a gibbering shell of a man. Priceless! He divulged some interesting intel in between his jabbering.

1119011.text: Bretonian factions are all eager for 'distribution rights' for Hypno Bands. They're apparently unhappy about having been left out of all the contraband trade in Sirius, and they want something of their own to sell to Bretonia's entertainment-hungry masses. Hypno Bands are just the thing for taking one's mind off of an impending invasion and civilizational collapse.

1119012.text: Bretonia's underworld is a tricky place. The Junkers, well, they have contacts throughout Sirius, although I'm not sure they can be trusted. The Mollys have the deepest infrastructure, but the Gaians seem to have almost endless contacts among the social and intellectual elites. Now, I like mass marketing as much as anyone, but selling less at a higher margin can put just as much profit into my account, and at potentially less risk. There's a raging debate about which faction is the better commercial ally for Hypno Band distribution. I expect the debate will rage on even after we set up a network with one of them.

1119013.text: EFL transferred administration of its Rapid Transit Division to Solar Engineering. Personally I think that was a mistake. Sure, EFL still owns the rights to the technology, but Solar has a knack for innovation. What will happen if Solar comes up with entirely new applications, or technology based on our work? We could probably get our connections in the Royal Elites to intervene, but my fear is that they will become too distracted by the war effort and not care about the losses EFL would have to face.

1119014.text: Here on Planet Orleans we have a need for significant quantities of LPG for various light-fuel applications. Most of it is imported from our distribution facility on Saint-Quentin, in the Picardy system. With the economies of scale that EFL has, it is cheaper to ship basic commodities like fuel across systems. In emergencies, we can crack heavy Oil compounds, or even break down Plastics and other Polymers. We have experimented with some forms of bio-fuel as well. With Gallia's population as large as it is, biological sources of Hydrocarbons will never take over from our fossil fuel reserves. We would have to convert all our arable land over to fuel-crop production, and famine would grip our nation.

1119015.text: Gallia's planets bring in heavy Oil primarily from Maine, where Planets Mayenne and Le Mans have it in plentiful supply. Certainly, our Oil will eventually run out. Our engines already recycle the catalyst we use in our fuel. We use a fusion process with our Oil, not simple combustion, and the consumption rates are nowhere near what the doomsayers predict. 'Peak oil' won't be a problem for us, not with improvements in engine efficiency that will surely come in the future. Even then, Sirius will no doubt have Hydrocarbon reserves of their own we can tap into. Whether it be from trade or acquisition by force, Gallia will be using Black Gold for the foreseeable future.

1119016.text: There are great expectations put upon us by the new war starting in Sirius. The Crown expects EFL to be the major logistics provider backing this new enterprise. The elites expect their standard of living to be maintained. Everyone else expects...well we don't particularly care about them now do we?

1119017.text: I wonder if the Crown will introduce conscripts into the Marine Corps as a way of dealing with idle citizens. I can think of a better use for them, as workers in our facilities. We all have to do our part for the war effort - whether it be working longer hours for less money, not being wasteful of resources, rationing, military service or informing the authorities of seditious behavior. Some cheap labor would certainly offset some of EFL's substantial losses as a result of the King's venture into foreign space.

1119018.text: The CNO cycle used in our fusion reactors stands for 'Carbon-Nitrogen-Oxygen'. This is because the fusion process forces carbon atoms to fuse with hydrogen, forming the slightly heavier elements nitrogen, then oxygen. Eventually this process is supposed to end up back with carbon, a complete circle of fusion reactions where the only input is simple hydrogen - and the only output is energy. EFL hasn't quite been able to complete the cycle though. We can only go as far as converting the carbon into nitrogen. Sure there isn't much use for nitrogen as an element - but at least it is a clean, inert gas as a waste product.

1119019.text: Promethene is the primary fuel used to power our great nation. We ship in ready-made tanks of it from Briancon Station. Just swap and go. No mess, no fire hazards from spills or ruptures, no recycling or messing around with catalytic binders. We mark many of our Promethene shipments as normal Oil, to make it more difficult for potential thieves to target our shipments. Of course it doesn't stop people from scanning us in space, that is what the Royal Navy is for!

1119020.text: Our fusion engines are perfect for utilizing Oil, as we have everything we need bound together in one compound. LPG, Oil, and really all hydrocarbons have hydrogen and carbon as their primary ingredients. The only difference is the length of the molecules. LPG generally consists of short-length chains of carbon atoms, up to four long when you get up to butane. Oil is a good deal longer, with chains of perhaps eighteen or more carbon atoms strung together. In the old days of ancient Sol the mid-length hydrocarbons, particularly octane, were prized as fuel for ground vehicles. Nowadays they are considered too volatile for use as fuel, and see their way into our Petrochemical plants for conversion into more useful forms.

1119021.text: The discovery of Prometheum was like a gift from God to the people of Gallia. When chemically bound to hydrocarbons, it acts as a catalyst and greatly lowers the temperature needed to start off the CNO Cycle. It's small wonder that Prometheum is so heavily regulated by the government. I swear there are more rules and regulations surrounding this element then there are for illegal drugs!

1119022.text: The rewards for assisting the Crown have been tremendous for EFL. Short of joining the Navy, working through the ranks of our company is one of the few ways a commoner can hope to join the elite classes. It is the dream of many of us in EFL. Once there, you can be assured of the benefits that come with power and privilege - for your entire family for generations.

1119023.text: It's funny, how Gallia's Oil is both the cause and cure for many of our problems. We have one department within EFL that specializes in making some of the most toxic Petrochemicals humanity has ever seen. I could swear they are making some kind of chemical warfare agent some days! In another department, they are utilizing special Plastics that are able to contain the hazardous materials.

1119024.text: I think that if EFL is looking to sell off more assets that are not related to our core business of Oil, we should buy into the Petrochemical and Plastics assets of our competitors. After all, Gate and Lane Parts don't add value to our business, as transports use less of our product as a result. On the other hand, Petrochemicals and Plastics are simply refined and manufactured from what EFL pumps out of the ground. It makes sense that we should invest in our own 'value-added' lines of business.

1119025.text: Here on Chartres we take simple Hydrocarbons or Polymers, and use our advanced chemical plants to produce the most sophisticated Plastics humanity has ever known. I have some shipments headed out to Metz and Chateau Salins, out in the Lorraine system. It's going to be a tough flight for whomever is assigned the job. The risks of Council attack are great, as is the prospect of travel off-lane. The Royal Navy has to spend a lot of resources on escort and forward patrol for these transports. Without them, Lorraine would effectively be cut off from the rest of Gallia.

1119026.text: Rheinland has several transports of Plastics headed its way now. The human race has depended on Plastics for centuries. Forget the Age of Steel, that has long passed. We can now produce Plastics with the strength of steel, with a weight that's lighter than Aluminium. Temperature resistance is not a strong point of course, but one can't have everything! Still, the sheer diversity of compounds we can make will see the 'Age of Plastique' last for many, many generations to come.

1119027.text: EFL needs to ensure we get our share of the plunder coming out of Bretonian conquest. We have already sold enough of our assets to the competition. Now is the time for EFL to be paid its fair share for doing our part in the war. I think the Crown could start by giving us the system they like to call 'Edinburgh'. I would love to go prospecting on Planet Gaia for Oil, and then partake in a hunting safari when I have time off.

1119028.text: One of our more specialized clients is Solar Engineering. We sell very specific types of Plastics to Mortagne Production Facility. It is Solar's Holotainment Band Factory, responsible for Gallia's latest trend in the arts and media. As a trader, I look forward to making the trip out to Maine. The Dockmaster always makes sure I get a free upload with the latest holo-recordings. Nice to know he is looking after me.

1119029.text: Complex, special-purpose Plastics are shipped out to the Royal Navy's special research base at Calais. We have seen some of our products integrated into the innovations they research there. From time to time though, we get special orders. Sometimes we can guess what these Plastics might be used for. Other times, your guess is as good as mine.

1119030.text: I don't think Gallia was wise to set ourselves on a path for all-out war with Sirius. We could have played it cooler, and ingratiated ourselves more with the Sirians. The Kusari Empire was having a perfectly good war with Bretonia, and beating them back too. I think if we let them go on a couple more years, we could have saved the Royal Navy, and our own company, a good deal of lost men and resources.

1119031.text: I can't wait to get my hands on some mining machinery used by Sirian miners. To be sure, we have had a lot of reports and blueprints coming back to us over the years. That being said, it simply doesn't compare to having live demonstrations carried out, or working with the machine itself. There is always something new you will find out about a machine when you give it a try it yourself.

1119032.text: This whole notion of 'revenge' only played into the hands of those Council traitors. It gave them oxygen they should have been starved of long ago. Unless Gallia can secure resources inside Sirius as it pushes through, the entire war effort will grind to a halt as the war machine will not be able to keep on going. Then EFL will be the ones left to foot the bill, and take the blame as corporate sponsors of this war.

1119033.text: The Sirius invasion could not have come at a better time for EFL. We needed new horizons to explore, and a new focus for the population of Gallia. Our advertising department is working overtime to convince the people that EFL is working to secure Gallia's future. Every transport laden with war loot should be shown off as a trophy of war. EFL should also look to Sirian Houses like Kusari as exciting new trade partners. Win the hearts of the people, and fatten their wallets, and you will have their support for life.

1119034.text: Fortunately for Gallia, EFL had stockpiled Prometheum here on this station for years before The Council seized Planet Marne. Until the GRN retakes the Planet, Gallia's Promethene fuel supply depends on our ability to carefully ration this supply.

1119035.text: Stressed? You bet I am stressed! I have been pouring over the balance sheets for our division. We have lost many transports to terrorist attack in the last year. Normally this wouldn't be an issue, but with the war underway in Sirius I can't replace them anymore. Sooner or later I am going to fall behind on quotas. There goes my end-of-year bonus!

1119036.text: The pressure of meeting deadlines was too much for one of my colleagues. One day he simply decided to change course heading out to Provence, and disappeared into the dust cloud. The Police escort we had didn't want to pursue him. Because our fuel delivery was for a Royal connection, that guy is now a wanted criminal. He needs mental health care, not a prison sentence.

1119037.text: Cobalt Mining Machinery is shipped off to Saint-Flour from here. Given the decreasing yields of Cobalt being reported from Gallic Metal Service, I often wondered where we would source that metal from in the future. After looking at the new star charts for the Sirius region, now I know. Once the Royal Navy smashes its way into Bretonia, we shall have access to the Cobalt fields of Omega-7. With such a raw display of Gallic power, Bretonia's neighbour Rheinland will be only too willing to trade with us - out of fear if nothing else!

1119038.text: Some people in the company are getting nervous about the strain the war is putting on us. They need to remain focused, and flexible in their approach. It may well be that some departments will have to take more risks, and bring in some foreign resources from trade, or as spoils of war. Some of our under-performing areas, well, frankly they might have to go. Good thing I am not in one of those areas.

1119039.text: Romorantin is a classic example of EFL's problems. This place should have been sold off or scrapped years ago. Instead we have a large station with little going on in here. The upkeep of this place must be huge, even with parts of the station sealed off. And don't get me started on the cost of patrol ships to keep us all safe. There is enough material in this station to build a new fleet for Gallia - why not take advantage of that during this time of war?

1119040.text: We ship Prometheum to Briancon Station in Languedoc, but we are very careful to take precautions so that criminals don't ambush the deliveries. All cargo manifests leaving this station are encrypted, and the transports have several special surprises awaiting any inquisitive idiots who decide to take a peak.

1119041.text: I heard a rumor that my department would be sold off if we didn't reach our production quota for this year. We are doing the best we can, but upper management keeps adding 'special orders', you know the ones we have to fill to keep their connections among the elite classes happy. Management gets the honor for our success, and we take the blame for any failures. It's just not right.

1119042.text: If this station ends up being shut down, I have no idea where my family and I will go. Some say it won't happen in our lifetime, others say it could happen next quarter. I think it depends on whatever promises that management has been making to impress the government officials.

1119043.text: I am out here on Vendome as part of an EFL engineering conference. I saw the people who were in our rooms last, they were a Tourist group heading back to Djion Station in the Burgundy system. I am sure they were visiting for their first time. I am fortunate enough to come here every year with EFL. We get a chance to discuss the latest engineering developments, network with other project managers, even meet members of the Royal Elite. Impress the right people here and your future in the company is assured.

1119044.text: By God, do those Tourists from Clermont Space Colony ever stop complaining about the heat? Vendome would have to be one of the most spacious and well conditioned stations ever to grace humanity. Yet those ingrates still mutter about how humid it is and how their fat wives have to endure such 'tropical' conditions. I can't wait for them to go home. Then I can finally enjoy my own vacation in peace!

1119045.text: Dealing with the elite classes can be a royal pain, pardon the pun. I have seen contracts won or lost over the pettiest things here in EFL. Last year I saw a workgroup lose its five-year contract to another one, just because some fat Viscount had indigestion after stuffing his face at our EFL-sponsored luncheon. Well, if it happens to me I am taking my skills straight to Solar Engineering.

1119046.text: I joined GMS as a low-level mining apprentice just after graduating high school. Since then I've risen through the ranks and achieved great success here. Even if I had the option of going to another company, I would turn it down because I am completely satisfied at GMS.

1119047.text: Even though there is bauxite here on the planet, it's actually cheaper to ship in Aluminium from Guise Mining Facility. Personally, I think GMS prefers space mining because it makes it easier to control the work force. It's hard to walk off the job when you're deep in an asteroid field strapped into a multi-million credit mining ship. I suppose you could just stop mining, but then, GMS can just deny you docking clearance when you're running low on oxygen, too.

1119048.text: The GMS miners on Planet Quillan are working hard mining Gadolinium to make up for lost time while the planet was controlled by the Council. The Crown has ordered stockpiles of raw materials be created on all planets in case something like that happens again. Of course, the government also assures us that something like that can't ever happen again. Better safe than sorry, I suppose. In any case, I've got a brand new warehouse ready to receive shipments, if you're interested in a run out to Languedoc.

1119049.text: If your ship is outfitted for Passengers, there are usually a large number of GMS employees sight-seeing here on Vendome Residence who could use a transport back to the Provence system. Blois isn't the ritzy destination that it used to be, now that Marseille has regular passenger routes, but it's still a prime stop for GMS employees who benefit from the company's special rates here at the resorts.

1119050.text: More and more I see Sirian traders flying about Gallic space. There has to be a good reason for all the traffic. I'd imagine our Gallic exports must fetch an impressive price in the Sirian systems.

1119051.text: GMS is extremely fast and efficient when it comes to mining. The only problem is that we mine out asteroid fields rather quickly. This means we're constantly surveying new asteroid fields for valuable metals. First we expanded from the Core Worlds to the Border Worlds, and then to the Sirian border systems. Nothing can quench our thirst for fresh minerals.

1119052.text: Spaceship Crew who have just rotated off duty are eager for a ride over to Planet Orleans, if you're available. They don't pay a lot for a short trip, but there aren't that many options here. We're a shipyard, not a shipping platform, after all.

1119053.text: The IMG have been surprisingly accommodating to our arrival in Sirius. With them there has been little competition over mineral fields or docking privileges. It was quite a relief to find another mining company that we could work with instead of resorting to hostilities.

1119054.text: Luckily for us, the Crown has stayed out of our business for the most part. We are able to operate independently and in our own business interest, not always having to obey the dictates of the King as EFL does. When the war against the Sirians started, EFL was practically conscripted into military service.

1119055.text: Planet Marseille apparently isn't capable of supplying itself with anything other than ocean right now, so everything else has to be shipped in at considerable expense. Not that I'm complaining, mind you. Gallia is a bad place to be out of a job right now, unless you actually want to get conscripted. I'm scheduled to run a shipment of Plastics from here to Marseille tomorrow.

1119056.text: We've been researching a new extraction method for mining metals out of very large asteroids. The initial test runs have gone pretty well. If we are able to bring this process to production, it is estimated that our yield rates would increase by over 200%! But I'm sorry, I can't discuss any details with you now.

1119057.text: We do have a size-able fleet of transports for the purpose of shipping mined ores to processing or exchange facilities. But sometimes our ore haulers cannot keep up with our miners. In those cases, we like to hire IDF Shipping to pick up the rest of our ores. That way, both companies can focus on their core-competencies for maximum profits.

1119058.text: When venturing into Sirius for trade missions in the past, we had our share of missteps. Some cargo that is perfectly legal and appreciated in Gallia is not so warmly received in Sirius. Specifically, representatives from some Sirian bases balked when gift crates of Tobacco arrived on their stations. I can't imagine why. My son's been smoking Cigars since he was five and he doesn't seem to have any health problems.

1119059.text: The favorite part of the typical work day in the mineral fields is the mid-day Wine break. It helps to take a breather and relax before the second half of the day's operation. This break also provides various team-building benefits.

1119060.text: The worst part of my job is when a couple of pirates pop up while we are out mining in the fields. Corse or Brigands can usually be bought off for a relatively small fee, but the Maquis aren't interested in our money. They are bloodthirsty monsters who just want us dead for being aligned with the Crown.

1119061.text: Our brothers in the Council face a hopeless task. They expect to lead a revolution to overthrow the King? With all of his Royal Navy and Police forces at his command? I cannot see this ending anywhere else but at the guillotine for the Council's leaders.

1119062.text: We grew tired of all the piracy from the Brigands and Maquis and the lack of protection from the Royal Police, so GMS created its own security force. We have a small wing of ships designated exclusively to protect GMS shipping and mining operations. Most of those pilots are ex-Royal Navy people who sign up for the extra pay. To us, it's still worth the extra cost.

1119063.text: Many of our ores and metals that we mine are critical for making components and panels for the Royal Navy fleet. The Royal Navy realizes how important GMS is to the war effort, even if only indirectly, so they have been very good about protecting us whenever they can spare the ships.

1119064.text: Instead of hostility, the IMG have chosen cooperation with the Crown. Therefore, we are pleased to work alongside IMG miners in the mineral fields.

1119065.text: I just got back from my vacation in Provence. For the most part, I enjoyed my trip. But the government has a much smaller footprint out there so it can be scary at times knowing that help, if needed, is so far away.

1119066.text: The King's plans for House security and law enforcement are none of our business as long as he continues to stay out of our affairs.

1119067.text: To see how far the Gallic people have come since the landing of the sleeper ship in a few short centuries is quite remarkable: so many systems and planets colonized, so many space stations and capital ships constructed. Truly, we must be the chosen people.

1119068.text: The Royal Police like to pick on traders and miners because they see it as easy cash. They hate having to actually work for their money, so they stop us and write ridiculous tickets. Unfortunately, our complaints to the Crown go unanswered.

1119069.text: I heard the King has been diagnosed with some terminal illness that will take his life in a few short years. So he is focusing all of his energy, as well as the might of all Gallia, on forging his legacy. That may be the cause of all this territorial aggression recently.

1119070.text: I just finished the academy last week and arrived here a few days ago. I really thought we would finally get some real action while patrolling here, shooting down enemies of the Crown. Well, right now the only dangerous thing we have seen is the canteen food.

1119071.text: The Royal Police is tasked with capturing criminals to bring them to their well earned justice, we don't have to deal with such niceties. If we see someone breaking the law we are well within our rights to take care of it our way. They will only be spared if they surrender.

1119072.text: The major corporations, like EFL and IDF Shipping, are our partners in the war effort. While we do the actual fighting, logistics and supplies are handled by the contractors. This frees up more of our men for our main task: killing the bad guys.

1119073.text: A key element of security is intelligence: having the information about coming threats before they happen in order to disrupt them. This is why we were granted the authority to monitor the telecommunications of suspected terrorists and militants. Don't worry, we only use it on the bad guys. Those citizens who don't plan on committing any crimes have nothing to worry about.

1119074.text: The King has authorized us to arrest and imprison any citizens who threaten His rule. This phrasing of the dictate gives us wide leeway for executing the policy. So if enough protesters gather somewhere and start embarrassing the Crown, you can bet they'll be on the next shuttle to La Fere Prison Station.

1119075.text: If we need information out of one of the Council prisoners that we've captured, we send them off to secret sites for 'enhanced interrogations'. It is there that we can break them and get any information we want, even if it's not necessarily true.

1119076.text: It seems that for almost my whole life, the Gallic Royal Navy has been at war. One conflict just blends into the next, the enemies change but the bloodshed carries on. I wonder when it will finally be over.

1119077.text: Our patrols in this system have been reduced as of late. More and more men are getting sent out to the front lines. This leaves fewer pilots to guard the Trade Lanes around here. It's only a matter of time before the Maquis discover this vulnerability.

1119078.text: Trials?! We have no time for trials. We are at war! If militants are caught fighting for or supporting the Council, then their guilt is obvious and their punishment shall be swift. No patriotic Gallic citizen could oppose this policy.

1119079.text: I can only pray that I will survive long enough to see the end of this wretched war.

1119080.text: The Brigands we capture out in Orleanais are typically as dumb as rocks. So the intelligence value from capturing them alive is about zero. Half of the time, I'll just blast their pods in space to save myself the trouble of bringing them in.

1119081.text: This shipyard you are standing in is crucial to the war effort. It's been pumping out Navy vessels for centuries. We keep a close eye on security around this base.

1119082.text: Fear is one of the many tools at our disposal. A citizenry with a healthy fear of their government is more likely to comply with the law. It makes our jobs much easier.

1119083.text: Planet-side policing is much different than police work in space. Here on Planet Orleans, criminals have no remote asteroid base that they can run to. If they commit a crime here, we'll catch them. We always do.

1119084.text: You seem to be trustworthy, so I think I can tell you a little secret. We are paid to take care of people that disrupt or endanger the shipping in this sector, but we are not exactly paid well. Some Brigands pay good cash if we look the other way. So if nobody else is watching we make sure that we get the payment we deserve.

1119085.text: Agriculture has always been very important on this planet, since it was the second planet colonized in Gallia. In addition to basic foodstuffs, Luxury Food is grown here and shipped to all of the resorts. Most of the delicacies enjoyed by the Royal Court are all grown here.

1119086.text: There's always been a struggle between liberty and security in Gallia. Some value their personal freedoms and privacy more. Others prefer to relinquish some of their rights in favor of a safer world for them and their children. But that whole debate ended after the Marne rebellion and with the Sirius contact. And liberty lost.

1119087.text: I've done assignments out in the Border Worlds all the way to the edge of Gallic-held space. Let me tell you, the further you get from Ile-De-France, the scarier it is. The Crown's reach only goes so far, and in absence of the stability from a strong Royal Navy or Royal Police presence, other factions step in to fill the void. The problem is those factions usually aren't very pleasant.

1119088.text: It's hard to compete with Planet Le Mans when it comes to Basic Alloy production, but when shipyards on this side of Gallia need a last minute shipment, they usually get it from here. Despite our higher prices, we have shipped Basic Alloy to Riom Shipyard regularly. The Montlucan and Clermont Space Colonies serve as staging areas for construction in the Provence system, so they receive some deliveries also.

1119089.text: Now that Solar Engineering managed to get Hypnotainment Bands outlawed, the Royal Police will have to add it to our list of contraband. Not that we'll complain, we're always happy for another reason to fine someone. Personally, though, I think the whole controversy is just a publicity stunt to get Solar some free press coverage. After all, there's no law against reselling a used Holo Band, so what difference does it make if it's been hacked first?

1119090.text: Don't think you can sneak anything past us. We are always watching.

1119091.text: As a precaution, we monitor all transmissions that are sent in and out of Gallia. We can't take a chance with domestic agents that may be working with outsiders against the Crown. So if you ever have to make a call out of Sirius, feel free to say "Bonjour" to the officer who is listening in.

1119092.text: The Royal Police are doing our best to hunt down all of the Brigands in Orleanais and bring them to justice. But we are having trouble locating their base in this system.
