If you happen to come across it in your travels, be sure to notify the nearest Royal Police officer immediately. Information like that would be very useful to the Crown.

1119093.text: Police efforts in Gallia are applied based on income. The poor typically commit the most crimes, so we have to crack down hard on them. Rich folk already live comfortable lives so they are less likely to be criminals. Why expend the resources against the good people when there are so many lower class folks breaking the law?

1119094.text: One of these days I hope I can get transferred to working in Ile-De-France. That's the best post to be assigned to in all of Gallia. Patrolling the Hexagon while flying Gallia's colors has always been a dream of mine. One day my friend...one day.

1119095.text: What's the best part of my job? Hmmm, I guess it would have to be my smoke breaks. Gallic Cigars are the best around and always help me relax on stressful days. You should really try one.

1119096.text: If you ever get hailed by a Royal Policeman, here's some free advice: stop and be polite. Some people start to mouth off or even try to run. Big mistakes. If you do something that stupid, you'll be headed straight to jail, if you're lucky.

1119097.text: We've been working on infiltrating the Gallic black market. The most effective thing we can do to cut down on the number of gangs and criminals is to disrupt their cash flow. Contraband is where their money comes from, so that's what we're after.

1119098.text: I've noticed that when the Kusari come in to Gallia for business, they are unfailingly polite and deferential. But once I took a little vacation to Planet New Tokyo, and wow, those people hate foreigners! I think I would be more welcome on Planet Marne than in Kusari! I guess those people are only nice when they want something.

1119099.text: Those rat-bastard Council traitors are being snuffed out of Gallia as we speak. Their only remaining sizable holdings are in the fortress system of Champagne. I heard a bunch of them fled to Sirius too, to aid the Bretonians. No matter, we'll catch up to them and then they'll get what they deserve.

1119100.text: I've come across some of the IMG folks from Sirius. They are surprisingly polite and knowledgeable in their craft. I believe GMS has a good relationship with them also. If there were more groups in Sirius like the IMG, life would be much better.

1119101.text: Maquis don't know the meaning of the word 'bribe'. So we teach them the meaning of the word 'death'.

1119102.text: If you're looking to do anything illegal in Gallia, you just need to have money. We run the Royal Police like a business, and if it's in our financial interest to look the other way for your transgressions, then that's just a good business decision.

1119103.text: After the rebellion on Marne, the King is being extremely cautious with citizen protests and public dissent. What we were once able to ignore as benign whining is now crushed immediately. The King will not risk the chance of losing another planet to the Council.

1119104.text: The Sirians are fools for dealing with the Council, whom have neither honor nor integrity. Fine, let the Sirians feel the pain of a Council knife in the back. It's only a matter of time before those treasonous terrorists turn on their new hosts.

1119105.text: Stopping a Brigand freighter usually ends up in us seizing contraband. I wonder if those Brigand pilots ever carry anything legal. If they do, we certainly haven't come across one.

1119106.text: Not every police patrol goes perfectly. Last month we stopped a Maquis punk in a gunboat. We thought we had enough men on the scene to deal with the threat, but apparently not. One of my buddies got his ship blown apart and his pod didn't stay in one piece. In the Royal Police, you just never know when it'll be your turn to bite the dust.

1119107.text: In my opinion, ladies belong in the home, not in the Royal Police. I can never depend on a woman to have my back when all hell breaks loose. She would probably still be at the station doing her hair or something. Women, who needs them?

1119108.text: Yes, the Royal Police are funded by the government. But what you may not know is that we get most of our revenue from fines and tickets. So next time you get pulled over and fined for whatever reason, you can feel happy that your fee will help pay for things like this shiny uniform.

1119109.text: Have you ever tried one of those Holotainment Bands? Man, those things are wild! It's an entire entertainment system all strapped right onto your head. Sometimes I call in sick to work so I can hang out at home and use my Holo Band. Who needs friends when any exhilarating fantasy can be realized with the help of your magical electric toy?

1119110.text: Anytime we catch a Brigand smuggling Nox, we make sure to take that contraband back to the station for "testing and analysis". We don't want that stuff falling into the wrong hands, now do we?

1119111.text: I cooked two Councilmen earlier today on my patrol. That's in addition to the Brigand I bagged yesterday. Yes, I know, I'm amazing. I love the trill of combat and the euphoria of victory. I can't wait to get back out there and blast some more scumbags! My business is killing, not writing tickets and making arrests like the other officers out there.

1119112.text: IDF Shipping's big break was during the First Gallic War when we were supplying the Royal Navy. By assisting and bringing a swift end to the war, we likely saved many Gallic lives. In the process, we managed to establish ourselves as the premier shipping company in all of Gallia.

1119113.text: I regularly transport Shape-memory Alloy here from Alesia Station in Burgundy. GMS can't keep up with the demand for metals with so much ship construction going on. Industrial needs are shunted aside when the Navy places an order, too. IDF often finds that a cask of top quality Wine or a crate of Cigars delivered to the right dockmaster's office can move our customers up the priority list, though.

1119114.text: While GMS likes to advertize its alloys to the public, industry relies on their pure metals even more. Fortunately, they're less likely to be rationed by those zealous Royal bureaucrats, too. Saint-Flour Mining Facility is a main source for Holmium in Gallia, and IDF ships it here to the planet pretty frequently.

1119115.text: Solar Engineering requisitions some of the Yttrium we mine here for the Laser laboratories on Saint Exupery Space Port in Lorraine. It seems strange to me that a metal is so useful in making Lasers, but...well I flunked all my science classes in school so I went into business instead.

1119116.text: We in IDF Shipping are always proud to ship military materials for the Royal Navy. We feel it is our patriotic duty to support the war effort in any way we can. The fact that we are able to profit from this service is just icing on the cake.

1119117.text: If the Unione Corse ever need something from you, it's best to quickly comply and move on with your life. Otherwise you'll be moving on without your life.

1119118.text: EFL is so busy supplying the Navy that they can barely spare any transports for the export market with Kusari, not that IDF Shipping minds that. Apparently, EFL's Plastics are superior to what they have in Kusari, because we are shipping large quantities to Planets Kyushu and New Tokyo.

1119119.text: Kusari has some strange trade practices, although we Gallians understand their reluctance about foreigners. Some of our products can be shipped directly to Kusari consumers, but there's always a percentage that gets randomly diverted to Narita Outpost. I suppose they conduct inspections of some sort, or maybe they are just building up a stockpile, who knows.

1119120.text: The Brigand presence in this system is annoying but not too disruptive. With the Royal Navy and Police here and being so close to Ile-De-France, Orleanais is safer than many of the other Gallic systems. The Navy generally does a good job of responding to pirate emergencies here.

1119121.text: I'm tired of the Council lecturing all of us on the evils and corruption of the Crown. My question is: what is their alternative? They say they favor democracy, but all democracies in history have ended up collapsing once they reach a deep economic crisis. They should be happy given all that the King has done for Gallia.

1119122.text: I have a badly-needed vacation coming up in a few weeks. The piracy and danger that I have to deal with on a daily basis is getting out of hand. I signed up to be a transport pilot, not a helpless hostage.

1119123.text: I hate shipping goods out to the Border Worlds. It's far too dangerous. Besides Burgundy, the Royal Navy does not have the numbers to keep piracy under control out there. Usually we're left to fend for ourselves and against most enemies, our escorts are simply inadequate.

1119124.text: This space station serves as our primary distribution point for Mining Machinery. We mainly ship to GMS space stations for their space mining operations, but we do also supply equipment to planetary oil drilling sites. We ship out specialized Mining Machinery to the Gallic Metal Service out at Vierzon Mining Facility. They need dedicated mining equipment to extract Tantalum from the asteroid field out there. Such a rare metal needs precision machinery and forging lasers, so none goes to waste. Inaccurate forging lasers won't form the nuggets of ore GMS wants - instead the rocks will be shot away at speed by the jet that forms when a laser starts to vaporize the rock. A complete waste of time!

1119125.text: We support the Royal Navy in any way we can. Whether it be shipping military goods to the front lines, hauling prisoners to their jails, or even some extra firepower to tip the battle in the Navy's favor. We're always quick to help the good guys whenever we can.

1119126.text: The savages in the Council have been intercepting our convoys and raiding our cargo. This cannot stand. The sooner that the Royal Navy eradicates the Council, the better. I actually suspect the Council is secretly in league with the Brigands and Corse. They're all the same if you ask me.

1119127.text: Solar Engineering is still so small because they resist the influence of the Crown. They should know by now that the government helps businesses that it deems vital to Gallia and once you have the King on your side, suddenly, bankruptcy is no longer possible.

1119128.text: Over the course of His reign, the King has greatly expanded the greatness and prominence of Gallia. We should all thank Him for His benevolent rule.

1119129.text: One more Border Worlds run and I can head back to Ile-De-France to see my wife and children. The shipping can get very stressful but having a loving family to come home to makes me forget all about work.

1119130.text: Only the luckiest Tourists are fortunate enough to see Vendome Residence. The Royal elites can come here whenever they want, but the regular folks have to get lucky in the lottery for tickets. There do seem to be an awful lot of them that live on Gap Station, though. Funny, I think that's where the government headquartered the lottery, too.

1119131.text: The Council try to preach their benevolent revolutionary platform about freedom and democracy to the citizenry as if they are a group of enlightened philosophers. But they never mention the piracy and cowardly tactics that they are employing now against their own people. Luckily those thugs and terrorists will never claim the throne of Gallia.

1119132.text: We are partnering with the Royal Navy to eliminate the scourge of those terrorists in the Maquis. With the eyes of all of our pilots and the deadliness of the Royal Navy fleet, we will soon vanquish this terrible foe.

1119133.text: Solar Engineering focuses most of its attention on research and production, so IDF handles a lot of their distribution. Their transport fleet is growing, though. I hope the IDF's executives are keeping an eye on that. For the time being, we are shipping to all the shipping platforms in Kusari: Tokai, Osaka, Narita, and Roppongi.

1119134.text: Samura Industries on Planet Kyushu has placed some large orders for Solar's Bio-Stability Monitors. I heard something about wanting to improve the safety of their agricultural employees. I'm not too keen on sharing our high technology with Sirians, but if that's what management decides, well, the Crown has people regulating all this trade, don't they? Who am I to question.

1119135.text: Most Brigands aren't very smart, so I've developed some tricks over the years to survive my encounters with them. One good trick is to ask him a riddle and that you'll double the payment if he can figure it out. While he's thinking, you call the Royal Navy or Police. By the time the Brigand has solved the riddle, he's usually sitting in a jail cell.

1119136.text: I do a lot of Sirius-Gallia routes. Sirian high-technology stuff to Gallia, and useless consumables back into Sirius. Making the Sirians fat, dumb, and happy wasn't the original plan, but it sure seems to be working out in the Crown's favor.

1119137.text: Look, I support the King like any good Gallic citizen. But this huge invasion of his seems a little too ambitious. If the Sirians get smart and unite against their common enemy, this won't end well for our beloved Gallia.

1119138.text: Corruption is rampant within the Gallic Royal Police. If no one else is around, they'll tax you for anything they can think of. One time one of the Gallic policemen stopped me and I was forced to pay a Police Moustache Maintenance fee. The funny thing was, this guy didn't even have a moustache!

1119139.text: You can tell the folks in the Gallic Royal Police are all crooks. Whenever a normal transport stops at a base, there are five of them that show up to levy some strange type of new municipal tax. But when I get swarmed by Maquis and call for help, suddenly they are nowhere to be found. It's sad that our tax credits go to propping up such a failed institution.

1119140.text: The Sirians did have some nice ship and weapon technology that exceeded what was found in Gallia. But we took away that competitive advantage by sharing it with the Crown and the Gallic engineers did the rest. Now the Sirians get to die by their own designs. How ironic.

1119141.text: I lost a buddy of mine the other day that got jumped while hauling in some Trade Lane parts from Sirius. I suspect it was a couple of Maquis that did it. How else do you explain the un-plundered cargo still floating near his bullet-riddled corpse? Those vicious dogs.

1119142.text: If you want to get a good deal on commodities - always go straight to the source. I am here to buy some Bio-Stability Monitors to take over to Chateau-Gontier. From there, we can make a good profit re-selling this gear to our other customers who want to keep their activities off the grid. They are very appreciative for the services we provide them. The prices we charge are in line with the fact we operate outside the normal business channels. No refunds!

1119143.text: As Junkers, we usually try to stay out of politics and keep everyone happy. But that doesn't seem to work with the Maquis. If they sense a whiff of the Crown on you, you're dead meat.

1119144.text: The Wine in Gallia is good, very good. It's funny how the Sirians have no taste for it. I've been to a couple planets in Sirius where farmers are trying to make their own Wine. Needless to say, it's all terrible. Leave the Wine to the experts, you foolish Sirians!

1119145.text: I do a good trade in Energy Field Equipment for Solar Engineering, importing it here from the Picardy system. My family lives on Solar's Abbeville Production Facility. What's it like? Sure I could complain about the wages, but with the economy the way it is there's no point complaining too much. I mean our quarters are much nicer than what my distant relations living on Amiens can afford, not to mention the wife and kids can get around the station and feel safe. Quality of life is just as important as how much money you make right?

1119146.text: What's going on out there in Sirius? I've never been to that area of space and all I hear in the news is how great the Royal Navy is doing in steam-rolling the Sirians. But I never know how much of that to believe. What are we missing back here in the home systems?

1119147.text: Since we're one of the biggest names in the technology sector, we're able to recruit the most talented engineers and scientists from Planet New Paris. Instead of becoming a corporate robot working for the EFL, new employees are able to design and produce robots that work for the EFL. It sounds kind of funny now that I think about it.

1119148.text: People, people everywhere! Not only is Planet Blois a popular destination in its own right, but Tourists also take in the sights over on Planet Nevers. There must be some pretty sweet holiday packages going. Me? I prefer Nevers myself if I were to take a vacation, but Blois is a cheaper place to live, with housing being a little cheaper.

1119149.text: I could sit here and watch the people go by all day. Tourists coming in and going out, with their sun tans and expensive novelty gifts. My friend just scored a job on one of the Liners heading out to Languedoc. "Gap Station Express" - that's his ship alright. I think for many of those space-bound people, coming here is the first real sunshine they have ever seen!

1119150.text: Tourists can get around pretty safely in Gallia. That is why there is so much space traffic carrying civilians. In all my years working in space I have only witnessed one incident. It was a few years ago when I was a junior cadet on a Liner headed to Djion Station, over in the Burgundy system. We were attacked by pirates before we got to the Beuvray. We lost two escort fighters and the Liner took a hit, killing twenty people. The bastards never got to board us though. I moved on since then, taking a more senior position within Solar Engineering, but I will never forget that day as long as I live.

1119151.text: I came here as part of a Solar Engineering Liner crew. But I think I will have to bring my family here on a vacation someday. I see the tourist Liners headed back to my home on Metz Station depart daily. This place is simply magic! It's the only chance a lot of us regular citizens have to see the majesty and splendor of the Royal Family. I mean sure you don't get a lot of actual Royals visiting, but the museum, the relics, just the architecture is so much better than any holo-simulation.

1119152.text: Tourists taking holidays often buy themselves a package deal. They take in a number of destinations over a few weeks. Some like to make Vendome their last stop before heading out-system to other resort planets like Planet Nevers in the Burgundy system. I hear this place leaves a lasting impression on people. It does for me. It reminds me of everything that was good about Gallia - and everything that is bad about it now. The pure opulence of this place, and what it took to build it - what was it all for in the end?

1119153.text: I just got back from a construction site out in the Border Worlds. The work was pretty interesting until the Maquis showed up. Twenty-two employees at that site lost their lives in just the few weeks that I was out there. I'm lucky to have escaped with my life. The only point the Maquis have proved is that when they are finally brought to justice, they deserve no mercy.

1119154.text: Solar Engineering operates many of the stations in Gallia. We have an unparalleled reputation for safety and data security on our stations. If you ever happen to build a station around here, you should check out our services.

1119155.text: Some folks in this company like the excitement and novelty of traveling out to the remote sites in the Border Worlds for work. Me, I prefer staying close to home in the core systems. My family and I live on Planet Paris, so being so far away from Ile-De-France does not appeal to me. I'll let the young and brave employees work out in the unforgiving Border Worlds.

1119156.text: Since we're a smaller company than EFL and IDF shipping, we're better able to adapt to fluctuating market conditions in Gallia. For example, when the Oil price plummeted back a few years ago, Solar shifted our priorities to station management services. It wasn't perfect, but the company survived without massive layoffs. The same cannot be said for EFL.

1119157.text: Bio-Stability Monitors enable commanders to keep track of the health and location of their troops, and make it much easier for wardens to track the movements of prisoners too. There are rumors that senior diplomats and maybe even members of the Royal family are using them as well.

1119158.text: Gien's Bio-Stability Monitor production lines simply do not stop. They are becoming an essential piece of equipment for pilots these days. I am in charge of organizing the daily shipments to GRN battleships across Gallia and the front lines.

1119159.text: Solar may not be joined at the hip to the Crown like some of the other large corporations in Gallia, but we still have very good insider sources. I can't elaborate on those sources for obvious reasons, but they keep us one step ahead of the competition. Outsiders view them as smart business moves, but actually, we had some help.

1119160.text: I heard a rumor that some of our Bio-Stability Monitors wind up at a secret government facility out in Picardy. It wouldn't surprise me at all if it were true. I mean if you want to do high-level research, you would need to have access to the best in cutting edge technology - and that's us. I couldn't begin to imagine what the government would do with them. New artificial intelligence units? Holo-band military simulators or interrogation units? It creeps me out a little just thinking about it.

1119161.text: It's so hot in this bar! I came out from Planet Le Mans to bring back a shipment of Bio-Stability Monitors from here. At least I can control the temperature in my personal quarters and my cubicle on the ship. The common areas of Gien? Death by heat exhaustion I tell you. The ship doctor tells me it takes a lot longer for the body to adapt from cold, to hot climates. My crewmates tell me I am simply soft. I hope they all freeze to death when we get back to Le Mans!

1119162.text: Solar doesn't specialize in war machines like some of the other Gallic companies. We're satisfied producing consumer electronics and construction components. There is much more pride in producing products that better people's lives instead of products that are designed to destroy things.

1119163.text: Looks like I drew the short straw! I have been 'volunteered' to take a shipment of Bio-Stability Monitors to Metz Station in Lorraine. They say it will be an unbelievable experience when I get there, I just have to make it there in one piece. Once you get off the Trade Lanes in Burgundy things can get pretty sketchy. Even with the military running escort, you can be pretty sure of being attacked when you get into the nebula.

1119164.text: The Bio-Stability Monitors we make here are shipped all over Gallia, and now to Sirius too. This is some prized technology that Solar has here. It's these sort of innovations that will see Solar rise to become the corporate giant it deserves to be. We've begun shipping to Bonn, Altona, Mainz, and the capital of Rheinland.

1119165.text: I think some of the robots we make in Solar Engineering are really pushing the boundaries of what we can handle. These things have more brainpower than twenty humans and some of them have arms or wheels. The CEO keeps pushing us to speed up the processors and increase the memory. But I wonder, what is the end-game here? I certainly wouldn't want to make one angry.

1119167.text: Gallic Navy\nFort Etaples Commodity Trader\nTalbot Levasseur

1119168.text: Gallic Navy\nFort Etaples Equipment Dealer\nBenjamin Dupuy

1119169.text: Gallic Navy\nFort Etaples Ship Dealer\nMaslin Gousse

1119179.text: EFL Oil and Machinery\nSaint-Quentin Bartender\nSaber Duranseau

1119180.text: EFL Oil and Machinery\nSaint-Quentin Commodity Trader\nMandel Joly

1119181.text: EFL Oil and Machinery\nSaint-Quentin Equipment Dealer\nRoland Covillon

1119182.text: EFL Oil and Machinery\nSaint-Quentin Ship Dealer\nDexter Simon

1119188.text: Gallic Navy\nLa Fere Prison Bartender\nHugh Nadeau

1119189.text: Gallic Navy\nLa Fere Prison Commodity Trader\nMarlon Ailleboust

1119190.text: Gallic Navy\nLa Fere Prison Equipment Dealer\nLegget Henrichon

1119194.text: We get along famously with the Maquis. We have very similar views when it comes to slaying Royalist dogs.

1119195.text: We and the Unione Corse have a cold war over Gallia's black market, only we are winning. Just don't repeat that to one of them unless you're out of firing range.

1119196.text: This base has a cottage industry manufacturing Light Arms, and from here we ship them out to various allied bases. We also ambush Royal shipments from Calais, and resell them on the black market.

1119197.text: The decision to support the Council with our own ships was the right one. Now we have a lot of freedom to do almost anything we want in Council controlled areas.

1119198.text: I was a police officer until I realized I could have a better life for myself out of the Crown's reach. The life of a Free Brigand is the only life of a man of spirit!

1119199.text: This base is in a strategically advantageous location for striking transports filled with prisoners headed to the nearby La Fere Prison. Many of those vessels have members of the Brigands trapped aboard who we wish to free.

1119200.text: I feel safest when flying with a Maquis ship. They are hardened warriors and enjoy killing for their cause.

1119201.text: The Gallic Royal Police officers are very good when it comes to doing nothing. When they actually do something, they can be easily bribed to cease doing it.

1119202.text: Ever since the Second Gallic Civil War, we managed to keep contact with some Sirian groups like the Outcasts. Our relations have improved, and since then they have supplied us with a new product for the Gallic black market: Cardamine.

1119203.text: There's significant activity on the part of both Maquis and Gallic Brigands in this system. This is due to the close proximity of the prison and the Liquefied Petroleum Gas shipments that cross the region.

1119204.text: If you need to pass under the radar in this area I am someone who can help you out. As a long-time Brigand, I am familiar with all the jump holes in this system.

1119205.text: We have a diverse range of activities in this system. We are constantly on the look out for weapons and Munitions shipments leaving Calais and Amiens, and we usually receive decent rewards for freeing prisoners bound for La Fere. The production stations run by GMS, EFL, and Solar in Picardy make for lucrative raids, also.

1119206.text: Council supporters who have given up hope of their lives on Planet Amiens ever improving are eager to escape to the new Council settlement on Planet Toulouse in Roussillon. We have transports leaving here all the time, and they are booked to capacity weeks in advance.

1119207.text: Many Council sympathizers on Amiens have extensive experience in mining. Some decide to try their luck in Liberty, where the Boron mines on a planet called Pittsburgh are apparently in critical need of trained miners. We arrange for their passage to Liberty, and in return they pledge some of their pay to help fund the Council. It's a win for everyone.

1119208.text: The Council has many supporters on Planet Amiens. So many people left the planet to settle in the Gallic border systems that the real estate market collapsed. That left most of the remainder of the population in too much debt to allow them to leave to seek better opportunities elsewhere in Gallia. The Crown's debt laws are far too oppressive. Those that leave for Roussillon have to walk away with basically nothing.

1119209.text: EFL brings in daily shipments of Oil from our planet-side operation in the Maine system. The official word on Gallic fuel reserves is that supplies are virtually unlimited. Those of us in the know will tell you nothing is further from the truth. Even if all of Gallia's planets were made entirely of pure Oil, they would be just a few drops in the bucket compared to the fuel sources used by the Sirius foreigners. I think that is the real reason the government is making war - our survival depends on it!

1119210.text: Why do I have to be stuck out here on Amiens? This place has so little going for it compared to the planets of Maine. Ever since the Trade Lanes went out towards Burgundy, Amiens has been in a steady decline. I don't think it will ever recover. Maybe this place will become Gallia's retirement village, full of elderly citizens living out their days. I know that is how I feel staying here.

1119211.text: I was looking forward to seeing one of Gallia's top entertainers, live, on a whirlwind tour on her way out to Provence. You think Planet Amiens would have been on the list? Not a chance. This place gets ignored by almost everyone, except for terrorist groups like the Council who come to stir up trouble.

1119212.text: Boy am I glad to be here. I was one of the last EFL employees to make it out of Champagne with my skin intact. It's bad times for loyalists out that way since the Council's propaganda has infested the workers there. I expect it will be only a matter of time until the Royal Navy strikes back at them. When they do, I expect a lot of people are going to die. Their death will be well deserved I should think!

1119213.text: I saw what happened out on Marne, and I see the same thing starting to happen on Planet Amiens. Unemployment and hard times are a breeding ground for rebellion. When I visit Amiens I see the same slogans etched on buildings, the same hacked messages sprawled across the local neural net. It's all rebellious talk put out by the Council, and I fear for our future out here in Picardy if the government does not act soon.

1119214.text: I make sure I don't wear the company logo when I visit Amiens. EFL employees are a soft target for Council agents. Kidnappings are not unheard of. I do wonder though, if some of our employees are simply using the disquiet on Amiens as an excuse to leave Picardy for systems with more opportunity. I think if people are that keen for new horizons, they should join the Royal Navy and go see what Sirius has to offer.

1119215.text: Saint-Quentin is the primary distribution point for Liquiefied Petroleum Gas. I have some major shipments headed out to Lorraine, including Metz and Chateau-Salins. When combined with a secret element used as a fusion catalyst, LPG makes an ideal light fuel for small spacecraft and bases. The positrons released can be contained by simple magnetic fields, so no heavy shielding is required. Better yet, electricity is generated directly from the fusion reaction - simple, effective and cheap.

1119216.text: We are the primary distributor of LPG fuel stock out to the Auvergne system. Bases like Montlucon and Clermont won't last long without a regular supply. Sure, life support can run off just about anything, even solar power. But with fusion reactors offline, base shielding and heavy industry will shut down. Bases would then be at the mercy of the next pirate who comes along. Make no mistake, without EFL Gallia stops - end of discussion!

1119217.text: Not too many jobs out here for EFL these days. The only people we see getting shipped out to work here are people ready for retirement. If you are young and looking to make a name for yourself, you are better off getting a transfer to the Maine system. I wouldn't be surprised if some of EFL's Picardy concerns get sold off in the near future.

1119218.text: We sell major quantities of LPG out to the Languedoc system. I have orders for up to 5000 tonnes per ship heading to Briancon Station, shipping out daily. Don't listen to the rumors about Gallia running out of Oil or LPG. EFL will come through, and we will finally develop a fusion system that completes the CNO cycle as it occurs in stars. Then the carbon we now burn in our reactors will be recycled, and we will only need to add plain old hydrogen - which you can source from anywhere. Gallia will be the undisputed power across all humanity if we reach this goal.

1119219.text: It's sometimes cheaper to import complex aromatic Hydrocarbons from South Shields Refinery over in Newcastle. Cosmic rays and other radiation do a great job in converting simple hydrocarbons into more complex forms over millions of years. Sure we can do it ourselves in petrochemical plants. Perhaps one day when the hydrocarbon fields run out we will have to invest in more local plant and machinery to take over the job. For now though, it's as simple as ordering in shipments over our Neural Net.

1119220.text: I was hoping the war in Sirius would kick-start the economy out here in Picardy. We haven't seen much improvement though. This is a bad omen, as now the Council has yet another argument to make against the Crown. Amiens gets ignored while the King makes His war. The sooner the Royal Navy crushes the rebellion the better off we will all be.

1119221.text: We've been struggling to keep up with the ever-increasing tax burden coming from the Crown. It seems every other day there's a new fee or new tax on consumers and businesses which they justify as 'supporting the Navy'. I guess this war against the Sirians is becoming more expensive than they originally thought.

1119222.text: We're always looking to recruit new pilots for cargo running, especially for shipping goods in from Sirius. Those are typically the most dangerous routes we Junkers do, but by far the most rewarding. And in the end, what's more important? Getting rich or your personal safety? I think the answer is obvious.

1119223.text: Junkers occupy a very different place in Sirian society compared to in Gallia. In Sirius, Junkers maintain a healthy neutrality, hidden away in the scrap fields usually unbothered by most groups. But in Gallia, the less than lawful types regard us as in cahoots with the Crown, and therefore a legitimate target to attack. I think we have a bit of an image problem in Gallia that needs to be carefully tweaked. It's hurting business.

1119224.text: If you want to make a few credits and don't mind the risk, the munitions made here are needed on planet Quillan in the Languedoc system. The GRN is using the planet as a staging area for fleet actions outside Gallia.

1119225.text: If you do make the trek out to Quillan, some of our refineries are in dire need of Gadolinium. I hear they have an abundance on Quillan despite the disruption due to the invasion and the strikes that Maquis operatives are constantly instigating.

1119226.text: My living is made hauling Holmium here from Saint-Flour Mining Facility in Auvergne. We have to watch out for the Maquis in Auvergne though. They've destroyed a few of our transports on their suicide runs.

1119227.text: I hope you like Wine and baguettes because that is all I've got in stock right now. Our supply transport was attacked by a group of Brigands and they made off with most of the food stuffs.

1119228.text: You don't have to be a miner to work for the Gallic Metal Service, they have plenty of non-mining positions. I'm the perfect example. I couldn't tell you the difference between Aluminium and Cobalt! I just keep the miners happy and in return I get a good pay check, benefits, and treated as if I was family. I LOVE my job!

1119229.text: Most of our mining is done is space. Our planet-side division is far smaller than our space division. Why bother with all the environmental regulations on a planet when you can mine the same resource from a rock in space and nobody cares about the mess?

1119230.text: The dock workers are loading my transport down with Molybdenum, once they finish I'm off to Alesia Station in the Burgundy system. The GMS workers there tell me they use the Molybdenum to manufacture Shape-memory Alloy.

1119231.text: My brother just left to board his transport for pre-flight checks. He is hauling a load of Molybdenum to Riom Shipyard. It's kind of hard to figure why a shipyard was built way out of the way in Auvergne, but I heard from a Navy pilot that the GRN found a jump hole network to a whole new batch of systems down there. Apparently they're inhabited by some non-humanoid alien race that is really war-like. That's all we need, another war! Don't tell anyone I told you that. It's hush hush.

1119232.text: You see that transport there? It's laden with Mining Machinery. You'd be surprised how quickly that equipment breaks down. The miners are trying out some new equipment from Etampes Shipping. If their products hold up, I hear we'll source all of our machinery from there.

1119233.text: We send out Molybdenum shipments to Maintenton Shipyard. Wonder why? It's because it is essential to transportation, construction, and aerospace applications.

1119234.text: You have a transport right? Have you been to the Maine system? I need a shipment of Molybdenum hauled to Mortagne Production facility.

1119235.text: The Molybdenum we export to Roanne Production Facility is used by GMS workers in the construction of the Ultralloy they ship throughout Gallia.

1119236.text: I just got my orders in: a shipment of Molybdenum to Bourg-en-Bresse. I shouldn't be surprised. I knew headquarters would be knocking after the Royal Police found some NOX on my transport. Guess I'll be in one of those rehab centers on New Paris for awhile.

1119237.text: What? Don't judge me. Do you know how boring it can get on a transport? I've hauled Molybdenum to Fourchambault and Maintenon, those aren't short runs. I had to find a way to pass the time.

1119238.text: If I was working for ELF or IDF, I'd already be fired. The GMS actually takes care of its employees. I'm sure I'll lose some pay and end up in a rehab center somewhere, but at least I'll still have my job.

1119239.text: My job is simple, our mining facilities need LPG. I ensure they have it. In fact, the guy you passed on his way out is heading to Toulon Mining Facility with some now.

1119240.text: Hold on a second, let me check this message. Right on schedule, Saint-Flour Mining Facility needs some LPG. They'll have to wait. The GMS has no transports on station currently, unless you'd be willing to make the trip?

1119241.text: Now that Planet Quillan is back under Royalist control, we've been able to restart some of our planet-side mining operations there. They go through LPG like I go through Wine.

1119242.text: The GRN sources nearly all of its Munitions here on Planet Amiens. I have standing orders to make daily shipments out to our battleships on the front lines. The war will be a boon to the local economy here on Amiens. Without the demand for war materiel, I would fear for the livelihood of many of Amiens' citizens. Everybody should rally behind the Royal Family in these times. It is both our patriotic duty, and a pragmatic benefit for citizens to help in any way they can.

1119243.text: It is the war that is keeping unrest here on Amiens to a minimum. With the Royal Navy's demand for Munitions out in the field, workers are kept gainfully employed. We give them hope and a sense of purpose and this in turn puts rebellious thoughts out of their minds. Our men in the Taus are grateful for the Munitions we send out from Amiens, I get a Cigar every time I make a shipment as thanks from the battleship crews.

1119244.text: One of our patrols the other day turned up a small human trafikking ring operated by some Brigands. Those heartless bastards will now become the Slaves as they are now impressed into hard labor gangs for the remainder of their lives. My only regret is for the poor people on the shipments we have missed up to this point.

1119245.text: The military is becoming more and more prominent in Gallic society. What once was just a separate branch of government out defending the House from invaders and usurpers has now become the most revered institution in everyday life. Sporting events, parades, schools, public spaces, and popular entertainment all prominently feature our fighting men and women. This new focus on civic duty and service to the House is a welcome development.

1119246.text: The capacity to assassinate seditious Gallic citizens, like the traitors in the Council, away from the battlefield without a trial is an authority entrusted only to a King. Surely His good graces shall prevent Him from abusing this awesome power.

1119247.text: Every time the Crown announces another successful targeted killing of a terrorist in the Council, the Gallic citizens cheer and their support for the King solidifies. It's funny how hunting down and killing someone is one of the few things that still produces feelings of Gallic unity and collective celebration in our society.

1119248.text: When we are finished interrogating the traitors we capture, we ship the Prisoners off - broken - to nearby La Fere Prison Station. I almost feel sorry for them, heh who am I kidding! Once they have spent a few years on La Fere, they will yearn for our gentle touch here in the interrogation rooms. I hope they like bunking down with the other scum they ship in from Amiens. Why the King doesn't indulge us with public executions of these traitors, I just don't know. Truly the King is merciful to all His subjects.

1119249.text: We've killed scores of high-level Council leaders. But as we kill these terrorists, there are always more that pop up elsewhere. We can never let up or lower our guard, because the overall threat level remains unchanged.

1119250.text: The Council must see the folly in their goals to overthrow the King and defeat the Royal Navy. What, do they really think they can unite all of Sirius under one banner to fight the Crown!? It's such a ridiculous notion that it's not even worthy of consideration! It will simply never happen. Never!

1119251.text: We like to keep our Deuterium reserves as full as possible. You can ship it in from Planet Chateauroux for a very good price. Of course, a fuel component like Deuterium makes you a target for terrorist attacks, so be sure to keep the Royal Navy or Police frequencies open. Once they know you are shipping to a GRN base they will do their utmost to see you deliver on-time, and with your hull intact! With a good supply of Deuterium to fortify our Promethene reserves, this base can operate even under the most extreme defensive conditions. Not that we expect any terrorists to make such an aggressive move, but orders are orders, and we must be ready for anything.

1119252.text: If those lazy Royal Police actually did their job and kept the petty criminals off the lanes in this system, then we would have a lot more time to focus on our missions on the battlefield. But due to their incompetence, we are stuck doing the Police's job for them by taking down local pirates and smugglers. What are the Gallic citizens even paying them for?

1119253.text: Our King is wise, just, and a benevolent leader. I shall follow His command to any fate that awaits me for the glory of Gallia.

1119254.text: The King has ordered three new Council terrorists to be killed. I'm part of the task force that is being sent out to locate them. Don't worry, the King has assured the people of Gallia of their guilt. And the Gallic citizenry will cheer elatedly when the operation is executed successfully.

1119255.text: If you ever notice a Royal Policeman doing his job honorably, courteously and professionally please let me know. I will then owe my friend 10,000 credits from our bet.

1119256.text: We're making steady progress against the Council, but it is not time to let up. We still need the public's help in finishing off this menace. That's why scans, random searches, and questioning will continue to increase across Gallia. We thank you for your cooperation.

1119257.text: Those savages in the Maquis will stop at nothing to destroy the Kingdom of Gallia. They are heartless monsters who attack civilians, diplomats, and even peace negotiators if they have any connection to the Gallic government. How can one expect to deal with these people other than with overwhelming force?

1119258.text: The Brigand pilots we typically face are good for training the new recruits. There is little danger and we trainers can usually just relax and laugh as the new Royal Navy pilot easily takes down the Brigand. It's also good for getting their confidence up for when a real challenge comes by, like an angry Corse pilot.

1119259.text: The King has ordered the executions of a list of dozens of Council and Maquis terrorists. He has assured the Royal Navy that we need not trouble ourselves with warrants, capture attempts, nor trials since it is clear that they are guilty. This is a big relief for us, because we can focus on doing our job: eliminating the enemy.

1119260.text: Our engineers here at Calais are responsible for testing and calibrating imported Side Arms. I have a requisition order from the Royal Navy to approve them in quantity for our battleships. Local patrols need to be well stocked when the time comes to board suspicious vessels. Military and other approved transports heading towards Lorraine will stop to prepare themselves should they face hostile boarding parties. One can never be too vigilant when heading off-lane.

1119261.text: Here at Calais, our Side Arms engineering department also services the needs of the Royal Police. GRP border and prison stations need ready access to weapons. Rapid-response teams to counter pirate raids, riot control in prisons, and general peacekeeping duties. All of this is just a day's work for Gallia's finest. Our precision engineering and high level of quality assurance means that, in the event of a fight, our officers will be the last ones left standing!

1119262.text: No organization has brought more death and destruction to more corners of Gallia than the Royal Navy. And no organization is more highly revered in Gallic society than the Royal Navy.

1119263.text: Apart from planet-side police forces, the biggest demand for the Side Arms we test is from GRN battleships. Travel off-lanes is hazardous at the best of times, more so if you have a ship packed with luxury goods or wealthy citizens. Our military and police escorts need plenty of weapons to ward off any attempts to board liners and transports headed to the resorts in Provence. Our elite citizens expect a guarantee of safety at all times. It is our duty to see they are kept safe from harm, and that all efforts by the criminal classes shall be in vain.

1119264.text: Our engineers insist that the latest versions of Solar Engineering's Bio-Stability Monitors be shipped into Calais. They come straight from Solar's Gien Space Colony, in the Orleanais. As early adopters of technology, our research teams gain an exclusive insight into the potential benefits, and flaws, of the innovations coming out from Solar's labs.

1119265.text: While some may consider it a 'victimless crime', shutting down the smuggling and possession of unapproved drugs, like Synthetic Marijuana and Nox, is a top priority for us. It has led to an increase in typical middle class folks getting locked away in prisons, but they should have known better. The King's efforts to stomp out these vices in Gallia are virtuous indeed and the Gallic people support his 'tough on crime' stance.

1119266.text: EFL ships significant quantities of Side Arms out to EFL's Riom Shipyard, in the Auvergne system. They need to keep local security personnel well-equipped to deal with terrorist threats. EFL is often in the firing line of traitorous types, thanks to their close ties to the Royal Family. Ships that are constructed at Riom will most likely have their armories fully stocked before they take their first flight. It prevents terrorist groups like the Maquis from stealing their ships the second they leave the dry-dock!

1119267.text: Our close ties to EFL means we get fresh samples of their Plastics technology delivered straight to our door. It is an honor to work with their scientists, and I am sure the feeling is mutual. From ship components, to composite materials, to integrated applications in Light Arms, EFL delivers the best quality product. EFL extracts the Oil, which makes the Petrochemicals, and in turn the Plastics. Some researchers believe that we should start using Sirius H-Fuel instead of Oil, in order to preserve our carbon. What nonsense! Soon enough we will perfect our engines to recycle the carbon, we will get by perfectly well without having to rely on those foreigners for fuel.

1119268.text: There have been numerous reports over the years of attacks on convoys that drift too close to the Avre Asteroid Field. There has to be a Maquis base somewhere in there. Once we find it, expect that field to go back to how it once was: nothing but rocks.

1119269.text: Let me give you some advice: If you ever get fined by a GRP officer, always keep in mind that you can either pay the fine to the government...Or you can pay the Officer to just 'forget it'. Most officers will settle for 25% of the actual fine.

1119270.text: Even if you pay a cop 500,000 Gallic credits, I doubt he would go too far from the Crown core systems. The outer systems are too dangerous, we rather just leave it to our Royal Navy Counterparts.

1119271.text: A large number of Council military pilots are former Royal Forces ones. A lot of them got captured and decided to switch side once the Council brainwashed them, just like happened in the Redemption-class ship La Fierte. It got captured after a minimal fight after a large part of the crew decided to defect before the Council Marines even boarded it.

1119272.text: A lot of things are forbidden around Gallia, so you should be wary from being caught with contraband by any policemen. Unless, of course, you're talented enough to convince a Gallic officer that it's not contraband.

1119273.text: In the battle for Languedoc, the Royal Navy discovered that the Council must have transported a large portion of the local civilian population somewhere else before we even managed to break their defences. Their only escape could be the Sirius sector. I still wonder where they have gone.

1119274.text: Generally the Unione Corse are regarded as a neutral party in Gallia, however some of its members decided to pick a side and are now working for us in assassinating Gallic Brigands that stand in our way.

1119275.text: I think the King should have sent the forces to eradicate the Council in their Champagne safe haven first, rather than storming Sirius. The Council are not just some loose criminal organisation, they are numerous and they support the Gallic underworld, get rid of them and you will have a far more united Gallia.

1119276.text: If a Unione Corse pilot comes by and he is carrying contraband that in my opinion is not that dangerous, I would rather ignore him than stop him. I wouldn't like to find out it was an important person or such, and end up in unknown grave.

1119277.text: We often call the Navy for support when we engage in a fight with the Maquis. Unlike other Gallic unlawfuls, Maquis are mostly trained military personal, that also have a bloodthirst that knows no end.

1119278.text: You can find a large number of former Royal Police officers in the Gallic Brigands' ranks. They were mostly corrupted officers that got shut down by the higher ranks and the King's men, and decided that if they can't take anymore bribes they will simply join the other side.

1119279.text: Unlike other criminal groups the Maquis are not driven by greed. Maquis wouldn't hesitate to shoot down a civilian transport just because it was doing something that they don't like.

1119280.text: I hate to do ground patrols, luckily I don't need to do them anymore. They are lower paid, far more boring and worse than all that you have to deal with young punks that think they deserve everything because they have a rich dad.

1119281.text: Tell you what, you look like nice folk so if you will buy me a bottle of that wine over there I will give you a permit to park in Royal Police docks inside Gallic stations. You have no idea how much time it saves you.

1119282.text: I tend to ignore when a Gallic shipper commits a small offense rather than giving them a fine, but a trader from Sirius? Hell no. If they come to Gallia and wish to be treated nicely, they should earn it.

1119283.text: I can't stand Sirius residents. I shoot them when I find the smallest reason to, and I am following them to see if they breach even the most minor law. I am not going to let my nation get back-stabbed twice.

1119284.text: What's going on outside of Gallia? I've three kids, a dead end desk job, an ulcur, a mortgage and a sky full of people who think they're the law, shooting at everything. I don't give a damn about what's going on outside of Gallia.

1119285.text: What's going on outside of Gallia? Look around, you see me sitting here? You see anyone else sitting here? That's because I drink alone, yeah with nobody else. So know you know when I drink alone I prefer to be by myself. Remember it.

1119286.text: My brothers think I am a coward because I chose to join the Royal Police rather than the Navy. I simply decided that I wish to fight against the criminals inside Gallia rather than unknown people from Sirius.

1119287.text: The Kusari emperor chose unwisely when he refused to move his forces from our way. We crushed them and then he was back to attack our forces in the Leeds system? Now I truly believe that idiocy has no limits.

1119288.text: Sirian mercenaries - there's an variable we never expected. We've never had need for such things within Gallic space, yet now they prowl our lanes looking for their next source of revenue. I've looked into their eyes and seen the promise of future wars of pay or play.

1119289.text: I heard in Liberty that their police is not even run by the government. I imagine to myself a bunch of lazy officers, doing nothing to assist their nation while eating a snack and watching the local holotransmissions.

1119290.text: You may notice ships carrying H Fuel to this station. Now that the Crown is allowing Sirian vessels to trade in our territory, we have stock supplies of their fuel. Personally I think they should just offload onto our own transports at the border, but I suppose they'd want to do the same to us in their space too. The difference is that we have the Gallic Royal Navy behind us, they don't.

1119291.text: Hydrocarbons are in high demand at EFL production stations throughout Gallia. GMS's own supply operations can't keep up with the orders anymore, so IDF Shipping takes up the slack by importing Hydrocarbons from the IMG in Sirius.

1119292.text: We receive regular shipments of Niobium from Falkland Base in Tau-37. The manufacturing centers in Maine and Picardy rely on us to provide them with just-in-time inventory, so they don't have to store large quantities themselves.

1119293.text: From all the dangers out there the Maquis are the worst. They enjoy the killing and will kill you just for their amusement.

1119294.text: The Council don't realize what damage they have done to the civilian population and the Gallic economy. They call themselves "saviors of Gallia" but so far I have only seen death and destruction at their hands.

1119295.text: I come from a big family. With this civil war, we've been separated across the house. Who knows, my third cousins might even be flying with the Council.

1119296.text: I'm a transport captain in Ile-De-France shipping. Of course you've heard of us. We are one of the largest corporations in Gallia!

1119297.text: Sometimes I am ordered to import Sake from New Tokyo. Personally, I think the stuff is vile, but those Kusari transport crews won't touch our local beverages. Their loss. Funny that we have to import their own liquor for them to drink here...but so far I haven't heard anyone complaining about getting to sell it to them, and at a significant mark up price too!

1119298.text: Every time I am being sent to take a delivery to the Border Worlds I say goodbye to my family, as I realize that it may be the last time I see them since those areas are extremely dangerous.

1119299.text: The only "favor" that the Council did to Gallia is protecting the Gallic Brigands, leading to a massive growth in their numbers.

1119300.text: The LPG exported from this system is what keeps its economy going. Lately many miners have migrated from the system, creating a need for experienced miners in the mining sites.

1119301.text: The Royal Navy is transporting personal side arms, military grade of course, to other places where the Royal Navy is based. I often prefer to fly near those convoys since they are usually escorted by military personnel.

1119302.text: We ship Drill Bits to supply local mining throughout Gallia. It's not a glamorous occupation, but without the right equipment, the miners can't work, and the shipyards don't get the metal to build all those ships that those hot shot pilots get to fly. Maybe those pilots should be us transport pilots a drink once in a while!

1119303.text: Straying off the Trade Lanes and the patrol areas is extremely dangerous in this system. There is quite a lot of activity in here by both the Maquis and the Gallic Brigands.

1119304.text: Sometimes I think the board members have lost their minds. Sending us transport pilots to areas filled with piracy and to war zones without heavy escorts is practically asking us to commit suicide.

1119305.text: Some Ile-De-France Shipping employees have been fired if members of their families have joined the Council.

1119306.text: These Council fools think they can last long against the King's forces. What they don't understand is that they only cause unnecessary loss of lives.

1119307.text: My husband has joined up with the Council and has taken our kids with him. I pray that when the King defeats the Council that His Majesty will have mercy on them since I've always been loyal to the Crown.

1119308.text: There are Military-grade light weaponry shipments from this area to various battleships. Occasionally we raid the convoys to make sure we are always carrying the best equipment available.

1119309.text: The Maquis are doing the dirty job for the Council. In return, the Council ignores their crimes and any other unlawful activity some of its members are doing.

1119310.text: We often coordinate attacks on convoys with the Gallic Brigands who are also based in this system.

1119311.text: Some of our Refugee transports head to Grenoble Depot to join up with a convoy heading out to Roussillon. Others decide to risk the trip alone, figuring that a single ship is less likely to be detected by the Royal forces. History shows there is safety in numbers, though, so I'm not sure how good of a plan that is.

1119312.text: We are often ambushing convoys that head in and out of La Fere Prison Station. Many of those convoys are carrying Maquis and Council captives that were brought to the Core Worlds.

1119313.text: The Gallic Brigands and the Maquis are supplying allied bases with Energy Field Equipment that are produced by Solar Engineering in this system by raiding the many convoys of different corporations that ship them.

1119314.text: We've had a lot of success raiding EFL shipments of Liquefied Petroleum Gas. You have to be very careful handling the containers, but the EFL pilots are just as concerned about that as we are. If you can take down their shields, they get very nervous about weapons fire that might rupture one of those containers in their cargo bay. I saw a transport vaporized once, when a lucky shot zipped right into a breach in the hull and hit a LPG container. There wasn't even enough debris left of that ship to register on scanners.

1119315.text: Council and Maquis agents are often encouraging people to move from bases controlled by the oppressive Gallic Crown to their bases and join the revolution.

1119316.text: If your wish is to ship various goods off the lawfuls' radar you should contact either the Maquis or the Brigands, both of whom are experts in avoiding the patrols in this system.

1119317.text: The vast majority of the Refugees book passage to Roussillon, and some want to try their luck in Liberty's Boron mines, but there are a few who are so tired of conflict and hopelessness that they want to escape Gallia and its wars altogether. Apparently there is a faction of isolationists or separatists - I'm not really sure - in Sirius called Zoners who settled a planet called Gran Canaria. We've heard they are open to taking in new settlers, so some people are willing to try their luck there.

1119318.text: Many believed that with the split of the Maquis and the Council there will be inner conflict, but the opposite happened. Each side found more freedom in minding its own business.

1119319.text: The Royal Navy may give the Gallic population the feeling it has taken over the Gallic Border Worlds, when in fact it is not true. The Council and its allies possess many bases in that area.

1119320.text: I just landed planet-side with a shipment of Solar's Bio-Stability Monitors, brought in from Gien Space Colony out in Orleanais. They are most likely going to find their way into general industrial applications on a planet like this one. It seems that every company wants to impose greater monitoring on its employees. Smaller, civilian locations like Amiens can't always afford our latest models. They go straight to the military and police. Besides, Amiens has a history of showing sympathy to the Council - and I am sure the authorities wouldn't want Solar's latest hardware falling into their hands. So the good people of Amiens will have to make do with slightly older versions.

1119321.text: I hear rumors about Solar wanting to buy up industrial facilities here on Amiens. I can see how cheaply they could do it too. I get the feeling that management is waiting to see if Amiens ends up like Marne. No point investing heavily in this planet, only to see it fall to the Council. I think that Solar will have to wait it out for the time being. There are plenty of good investment opportunities elsewhere in Gallia.

1119322.text: About the only Freelancers making a profit out here on Amiens are the passenger transports heading out of here. People who can find work elsewhere are leaving in droves. They can add themselves to the tens of millions of others who have left for greener pastures. I think the only people who are left here are those who can't leave, or people who want to create a new Amiens - one that doesn't include any Royal influence.

1119323.text: I am here sourcing LPG to be shipped off to Solar's Gien Space Colony. We can recycle our own Prometheum from spent fuel. We just need to top it off with the LPG. Prometheum only gets lost if a ship is unable to be salvaged - or disappears completely. Due to the scarcity and strategic value of raw Prometheum, the Government only allows small amounts to be released - and those are mainly reserved for processing by EFL. The rest of us have to ensure we recycle what we have, or order in fresh Promethene fuel from EFL.

1119324.text: This station is one of the most crowded I have ever seen. There are more than a few Refugees from Champagne on this station, and they could well have been the lucky few. I heard that EFL employees were not spared from reprisal attacks by the rebels. I just hope that Solar never paints itself as a target for terrorism.

1119325.text: All the recent arrivals to this station have a story to tell. Some escaped from Planet Marne with little but the clothes on their back. Others talked of the deaths of family and loved ones - the ones that didn't make it. There is a lot of anger at the Council out here. Down on Amiens it is a different story though, with more and more anger being directed at the government.

1119326.text: Abbeville is one of the best places you can live in this part of Gallia. I can't believe I wasted so much time trying to eke out a living on Amiens. Once I get a job for my wife here, we will be in a good position to start our own family.

1119327.text: Abbeville does big business in the Picardy system. Solar made a wise move in buying up this old piece of space-junk, next to Amiens. That planet is a recruiter's paradise. It has a nearly endless supply of skilled, unemployed workers. Solar gets to pick the best people, and the lowest rates of pay. All they had to do was polish up this old station so that living conditions here are better than anywhere you will find in Picardy. Then by comparison, Abbeville is clearly the better choice.

1119328.text: There is a lot of talk down on Amiens of the Council stirring up discontent. Really though, it doesn't take much to make people angry when they have no job and no prospects. I am pretty sure that if there was more incentive to build new industry on Amiens, then people would be happier and less likely to cause trouble. I mean just look at us here on Abbeville. Crime and other incidents are the lowest you will get in this system, and all the surveys point to a good degree of satisfaction among the residents. Trust Solar to show the others how it's done!

1119329.text: Looks like I get all the fun jobs. I have to make a trade run out to the New Berlin system, delivering our Energy Field Equipment to Oder Shipyard and Planet New Berlin. I get to choose a suicidal run across the Taus - or risk the infrequently patrolled Trade Lanes in Tau-53. I hope the military escort is as big as they say it will be, or I don't expect to be returning!

1119330.text: The Energy Field Equipment manufactured here go right across Gallia. I have shipments leaving today to Fourchambault Shipyard in the Berry system. I expect they will be going straight into the civilian spacecraft they make there. It's an easy run, good for training our less experienced pilots. Should you fly for us, you can expect to get a start making runs just like it.

1119331.text: I have no doubt that if Solar Engineering had the capital to invest, they could do for Amiens what they have done for Abbeville. This place used to be a mining station, now it is concerned with manufacturing. Amiens is a perfectly good place to live, it just needs new life breathed into its industry.

1119332.text: We send regular shipments of Energy Field Equipment into Lorraine. One of our convoys was attacked heading out to Saint-Exupery last week. There are some long and lonely Trade Lanes once you get into the Berry system. The Royal Police responded to our distress calls, but it was too late to save two of our ships. Two trade vessels lost, along with their crews. Space travel isn't as glamorous or safe as the resort brochures for Provence make it out to be!

1119333.text: I have a pretty long journey ahead of me, shipping Energy Field Equipment out to Riom Shipyard in the Auvergne system. I don't have the luxury of relaxing on this voyage. Sure it's not as insane as running supplies to Lorraine, but there is still danger to be had. If those terrorists like the Maquis get wind of our supply run, we will come under attack for sure! Riom itself is a potential target - I never feel safe when I am docked there. We won't be until we have made our deliveries and started our return trip home.

1119334.text: If the government doesn't do something about the situation on Amiens, they are facing a repeat of the Marne rebellion. That would be a disaster for Solar. I mean out here on Abbeville we have it pretty good. I don't want the Council showing up to destroy everything we have worked for. If anything, the government should be looking to us to see how things can be turned around.

1119335.text: While some of my colleagues risk their lives out there, I get the easy runs to Orleanais. Maintenon Shipyard has an ongoing contract for the supply of our Energy Field Equipment. I can trace my good fortune back to helping an old lady get around a spaceport one day - it turned out she had Royal connections. I guess she put in a good word for me, because by the next week I was off the Lorraine runs, and onto the 'milk run' through Ile-de-France. Like most companies in Gallia, if you know the right people you can make life easy for yourself.

1119336.text: The orders just keep coming in from Alster and Aland Shipyards. As a Energy Field Equipment dispatch clerk I am working over twelve hours a day to keep pace with demand. They say that war makes fools of us all - I say it makes Solar Engineering and its employees rather well off! Some of my friends have joined the Royal Navy and Marine detachments. I prefer to do my part by working here.

1119337.text: I sure hope the Royal Navy makes speedy progress in its war in Sirius. I don't think we can afford to take our attention off the problems at home. We are lucky here on Abbeville. Down on Amiens they have it a lot tougher. Most of my friends there are worried about their jobs. I managed to get a couple of them employment here on the station, but Solar can't take everyone who applies. Most are going to miss out, that is just the way it is I'm afraid.

1119360.text: Gallic Metal Service\nRoanne Commodity Trader\nJavier Frappier

1119361.text: Gallic Metal Service\nRoanne Equipment Dealer\nBruce Achin

1119362.text: Gallic Metal Service\nRoanne Ship Dealer\nFletcher Therrien

1119373.text: Liberty Navy\nLiberty Assembly Commodity Trader\nHenry Ribs

1119374.text: Liberty Navy\nLiberty Assembly Equipment Dealer\nManny Suns

1119392.text: Rheinland Military\nRheinland Assembly Commodity Trader\nEnsel Styne

1119393.text: Rheinland Military\nRheinland Assembly Equipment Dealer\nBob Saltz

1119399.text: Sirius offers all sorts of opportunities. For instance, take the new supply of 'labor' that we're importing. These poor souls were condemned to useless lives of inconsequence in Sirius, but here in Gallia they have the chance to serve a larger purpose: making Brigands rich! I've got a share invested in a consignment coming in soon. I'll get to inspect them myself before they continue on to Ecommoy Base to take up their 'assignments'.

1119400.text: Our raiding parties steal Wine shipments, but not just any Wine shipments: the best Wine in Gallia! It's a Brigand's life for me!

1119401.text: The Wine that is brought here by the raiding parties is typically on its way out to Luxury Liner Belleville. The EFL spares no expense treating its executives to the best vintages, and we have no pangs of conscience while enjoying it.

1119402.text: Cardamine is our new best-seller among the Gallic people. I haven't tried it myself, but the news in Sirius is that it creates steady customers, and more importantly, steady profits.

1119403.text: Not everyone is up for using Cardamine, so we are also importing a different, less-addictive drug: Synthetic Marijuana. The Corse seem to have buttoned up all the Sirian supply contacts, though, so right now we have to bring it in from Joinville Base. If those sneaky Corse tricksters think they can just keep the supply lines to themselves, they'll soon find out different.

1119404.text: Alloys: you can't ever seem to have enough of them. Instead of buying them from other bases we simply steal them from the nearby convoys - easy, quick and cheap! The resale is a little tricky, especially at GRN shipyards, but logistics managers at companies like IDF and EFL don't mind buying them cheaper than Solar is selling them, especially not when they can charge off the full price in their records and pocket the difference themselves.

1119405.text: We always need entertainment and other up-to-date software, but since we can't risk sending it via transmission, we transport it on chips. We acquire most of our Counterfeit Software from Evron Base - Council made, always reliable. I'm not partial to their politics, especially not when it gets in the way of business, but contacts with them can come in handy when you need to deal in something the Crown frowns on.

1119406.text: The L'ane is a true masterpiece! That fine ship will get what you need to where you need it. Or alternatively, will get you what you need from a hapless convoy in large quantities.

1119407.text: The Brigand's ship designs are built to be efficient. Take for example the Jaguar: it will tear apart any transport in seconds. Hit and Run.

1119408.text: There are all sorts of shipping convoys in this area, from Diamonds to Oil. If you happen to "acquire" any of those, feel free to bring them in here or any other Brigand base. We can use anything you might have!

1119409.text: There are weekly prisoner convoys from the Venissieux battleship to Fleury-Merogis Prison, many of which have captured Brigands onboard. It's our duty to free them.

1119410.text: The life of a Brigand is the best life any Gallic citizen could wish to have. Of course, if you are unwilling to face death on a daily basis, it might not be the career for you.

1119411.text: Money is never a problem for us. If we need to buy something big in a pinch, the bosses always seem to come up with what we need and more.

1119412.text: We have operated a sizable piece of the Gallic black market for centuries. We never get shut down because the Royal Police can never pin anything on us. It's probably in the best interest of their health and safety that they don't.

1119413.text: If you ever consider attacking the Corse, the first thing you should do is call your wife to say 'Goodbye'.

1119414.text: We're able to conduct a fairly decent trade in Blue Diamonds from this base, even though we don't mine them ourselves. Our Corse pilots are very charming and persuasive, apparently. Every time a convoy from Planet Metz comes across one of our patrols they start jettisoning cargo like their lives depend on it. We sell large quantities to the Junkers on Monte Carlo Freeport. They don't pay market prices for it, but they have to resell it at less than market prices themselves. It seems that nobody believes the Junkers' merchandise is not preowned.

1119415.text: Thionville Base supplies us with some very interesting items on occasion. I'm not sure where they come from, but if you can get your hands on them you can make astronomical profits selling them to very rich collectors.

1119416.text: We respect the Maquis for their dedication and bravery in battle. Everyone else is just one of our pawns.

1119417.text: Sometimes we need to 'borrow' certain supplies from passing IDF Shipping convoys. Most of their escorts know better than to try and stop us. The ones that don't tend to end up as corpses floating in space.

1119418.text: We have fairly regular shipments of Blue Diamonds headed to Monaco Base in the Provence system. I've never been able to figure out why that is. It's not like we're designing jewelry or manufacturing anything there. Monaco supplies us with Nox for distribution around Gallia, but what would Blue Diamonds have to do with that? Your guess is as good as mine. Don't question what the Corse head honchos decree, that's for certain.

1119419.text: I can cut you in on a Nox supply run from Monaco Base if you're interested. The GRN is getting bolder with its attempts to interdict our supply lines. They haven't found Monaco yet, but they do know it is coming from the Provence system, though, so the trips through the jump holes is sometimes dicey.

1119420.text: We're able to keep on good terms with the Law despite some of our shady dealings. We seem to have a knack for finding the kinds of government officials that understand our business and are willing to engage in some mutual back-scratching.

1119421.text: We ship Blue Diamonds to Joinville Base pretty regularly. The Council, Maquis, and Brigands in Champagne are always willing to pay top prices for it due to the GRN blockade of the system. They try to smuggle it in themselves, but nothing beats the top shelf product that we liberate from convoys. Corse have an eye for value that is envied throughout Gallia.

1119422.text: We have tenuous relations with the Maquis, but they're good enough to facilitate mutually beneficial business dealings. Key supplies comes from Maquis contacts. The Maquis somehow manage to acquire fuels from EFL without blowing everybody up. I suspect they've got some transport pilots on their payroll, but they are very tight lipped about their logistics. I don't blame them. It's not like they can bribe their way out of prison like we Corse can. Maquis are done for if they're captured, and they know it. The dirty little secret is that so few of them ever make it to trial not because they are so rarely caught, but because they hardly ever survive their 'interrogation'.

1119423.text: You smell that? It's Oil, the smell of Gallic Power being shipped out to Riom Shipyard. As far back as ancient Sol, civilization has depended on the Black Gold for prosperity. For a while there we were left with only simple and inefficient Deuterium for fusion power. Now we are much more advanced, using the sort of Carbon-based fusion power found in the hearts of stars. Who would have thought that such an ancient fuel source would find new life among us?

1119424.text: Every day, EFL sends out thousands of tonnes of Oil to shipyards across Gallia. There is one headed out to Fourchambault right now if you want to watch it taking off. The Prometheum catalyst they add to the Oil is expensive, so the vast majority of it gets recycled. It makes it a lot easier for us Oil workers to keep supplies moving out, as we don't have to handle the technical stuff ourselves.

1119425.text: We bring in Promethene fuel from Briancon Station, for local power generation. Raw Prometheum requires special licensing to store and handle. We can get around it by shipping in the Promethene fuel, then just recycling the Prometheum catalyst as required. With our access to Oil supplies, one batch of Promethene could last us for all eternity. Though in practice, some of the catalyst always manages to get lost. When Oil is turned into Promethene, the energy required to ignite the carbon fusion cycle is much less, enough for smaller engines to handle it. One day our scientists will perfect the system, and we can then recycle the carbon we now burn up. Then all talk of Gallia running out of Oil will be a thing of the past.

1119426.text: We send out the crude Oil, it comes back to us as Polymers from Montlucon Space Colony. Everything from membranes to pipe-work: most of it is plastic-based these days. The goods just keep pouring in to this port and the demand never stops. I wouldn't want it to. Gallia has a lot at stake here in making its mark on our new neighbors in Sirius. We have to take the initiative and show them we are strong. If we didn't press the attack, they would surely have declared war on us first - just like they do to each other.

1119427.text: With the constant terrorist attacks, and our logistics stretched by the demands of war, something is going to have to give. I could have nominated a dozen EFL departments that are good candidates for being sold off. Some people in the company don't want to give our competitors an edge in the market.
