But I say that EFL can offload its riskier assets - let our competitors bear that burden while we focus on more lucrative business.

1119428.text: I don't think that the government will force EFL to ration Gallia's Oil supplies, even if the war turns badly. There are known hydrocarbon reserves in border systems like Tau-29. Our company should look at dealing with Kusari for access and trade for such a vital resource. I am sure Kusari will be willing to help us finish what they started, and obliterate Bretonia once and for all!

1119429.text: So, you're new around here? Looking for a party? I have one going on in this bottle. You see that? It's NOX, straight from Planet Marseilles. I get my hands on the good stuff now and then, and the customers are seeing weird fishes all night. You don't have any phobias do you? That would be bad if you wanted to try some of this stuff. I mean, if you are scared of mice, you could well be seeing scary mice that aren't real. Worse, if you did see a real one, it might look like a six-meter sabre-toothed mouse that could rip your arms off! Maybe that's why I hear about some users freaking out.

1119430.text: Given our close ties to the Crown, the current war being waged in Sirius is perhaps one of our biggest challenges in terms of company public relations. Every victory will be an asset, every defeat a liability. My biggest fear is that we will become stretched too thin, and the Government will start rationing fuel supplies in the Core Worlds. This will be a disaster for EFL in terms of our public image. What good is it for EFL to boast of exceeding production quotas if there are fuel shortages at home?

1119431.text: Our company has extensive links to the Royal Family, and the elite classes of Gallia. This has given us great scope to influence government policy and garner the best of the Royal contracts. It has also linked our corporate image directly to the fortunes of the Crown. As monarchs over the centuries have risen and fallen in the public eye, so too has EFL.

1119432.text: I am out here as an EFL technician. Once the job is done, we will be heading back to Planet Metz. I wouldn't say Metz is my ideal choice for shore leave, but it's got solid ground and fresh air. That is, once you get away from the Oil refineries. Work out there on the Liner isn't too bad. As long as you keep your boots clean you can get around most places on the ship. Some of the other workers get too much into on-board entertainment, and spend their pay before they even have a chance to get home!

1119433.text: I see a lot of economy class Vacationers heading out to the resorts in Provence. I guess they have too much fun out there, and can't afford to fly first class anymore. I haven't had anyone tell me it wasn't worth the trip out to Provence. Rumor has it that if you aren't flying out that way with a decent escort, you stand a good chance of coming under attack by pirates. Perhaps the people that I never heard say bad things about Provence never made it back here to speak ill of it.

1119434.text: I frequently see people heading out to Lorraine as Passengers. I am not surprised they needed a vacation. I mean they are staring at the Council on one side, and God knows what is on the far side of that minefield on the other side. I hear the people on the other side of the mines are partially non-human. It is seriously scary out there, and the people of Lorraine must be very brave to live under the sorts of threats they do.

1119435.text: We top off our fuel reserves here with LPG brought in from Saint-Quentin Space Colony. The Promethene fuel we make up from the LPG is light, perfect for smaller ships and light engine applications. Simple Deuterium fusion produces nasty neutrons that smash into everything around them and make the ship itself become radioactive. Our carbon-based fuels don't have that problem, so magnetic fields are all we need for containing the reaction.

1119436.text: We have a load of Polymers coming in from Montlucon today. It is an essential part of EFL's business plan to add value to our Oil product. We are more than just simple miners of the Black Gold. The more we can diversify into manufacturing of Polymers, the greater market share we can achieve across a larger range of economic sectors. War is a boon for demand certainly, but we cannot afford to take our eyes off the domestic markets. Already there are potential threats like Solar Engineering sniffing at our heels. I would hate for EFL to come out a winner in the war, only to lose at home!

1119437.text: Ready-made Promethene fuel is brought in from Briancon Station in the Languedoc system. Briancon itself is safe from terrorist attack. But out there in space, Promethene convoys are juicy targets for every would-be pirate and criminal in Gallia. Promethene is the sort of fuel you can tractor in and inject directly into your engine. No pre-processing required first. I expect that Gallia's enemies are desperate for Promethene all the time. They will need their stolen fuel to keep running from the police and navy!

1119438.text: No risk, no return - that is what I tell the boys running Nox in from Monte Carlo. If the cops don't get you, the competition will. Some of us reckon it's better to simply pay off the GRP and have them move it for us. Me, I am too cheap for that. There are always plenty of rubes who have lost money in the Monte Carlo casinos, I use them to move the Nox for me as payment of their debts. I even have insurance too, by way of a nice little pellet of Nox the rubes swallow for me. I tell them it's a tracking device, but really it's tuned in to the scanner frequencies used to detect Nox in space. If they get scanned, it releases enough of the drug to turn my mules into gibbering wrecks. Crazy men don't make for reliable witnesses!

1119439.text: When we come back from a run to Sirius, we're often viewed with suspicion by other Gallian's. For some reason they think that our loyalty to the Crown may have deteriorated from the frequent trips out there. I know, it's a ridiculous assertion. We Huissiers are a very different breed. We have had centuries to infiltrate. We know our jobs better than anybody.

1119440.text: The Wine here in Gallia is good, don't get me wrong. But I'm the kind of fella that needs a bit more variety in my life. It's why I joined up with the Junkers in the first place. And after weeks of coming to this bar and drinking nothing but Wine, I'm kind of starting to miss that Liberty Ale.

1119441.text: Monte Carlo out in Provence is our clearing house for the Tellurium that gets mined out there. We have all kinds of customers here on Metz that have a demand for the metal. Not everyone can afford to wait for the backlog of orders to clear from the GMS books. And not everyone wants to have their orders logged and audited by any kind of government officials.

1119442.text: Unsurprisingly, the war has been good for our scrap metal salvaging division. The ships we produce these days have pieces of Council, GRN, EFL, and Brigand ships all stitched together. It's not always pretty, but it keeps material costs way down, which means we can keep our prices low for the value-conscious customers.

1119443.text: Hmmm, there aren't too many ladies around here. Maybe one of these days I ought to make a run out to Sirius and buy a few. There are more than a few parts of Sirius only too willing to indulge in that kind of trade.

1119444.text: Solar is shipping Gate/Lane Parts out to Nimes Station, near the border in Languedoc. Maybe the government is finally going to build a proper gate into Sirius? In their rush to get the fighting started they are going to be hard pressed keeping their supply lines running smoothly. They are going to have to build lanes as they go - into the minefield and out the other side into Sirius itself. If they can link up with the lanes in Tau-31 or Leeds, it will be all over for Sirius.

1119445.text: The Junkers have been around longer than most people realize, much longer. We were one of the first groups to operate in outer space after the initial landing on Planet New Paris. What's the secret to our success? Loyalty, ingenuity, shrewd business sense, connections, oh and Wine. Lots and lots of Wine.

1119446.text: We support the King in his quest to conquer parts of Sirius. Many of the systems across Sirius could benefit from being under new management. For example, the conditions in Leeds prove that the Bretonians are incapable of effectively running that system. I have confidence that once under the complete control of the Crown, Leeds will be a shining beacon in Sirius attracting others to the Gallic way of life.

1119447.text: I've just come from Planet Quillan. The Navy says it's once again safe for civilians, but I'm not convinced. Not a day goes by that there isn't an explosion in one of the mines or refineries. Still, given the situation the kingdom is in, we can't afford to let those mines sit idle. Gadolinium is needed for alloy fabrication, and the factories on this planet are no exception.

1119448.text: If you're looking for an interesting trade opportunity, you can always try to ship refined Neodymium from Senonches to here. I recommend you get several ace escorts if you do however. Raw Neodymium is very valuable and rumor has it, highly sought after on the black market. The Brigands take advantage of that.

1119449.text: One of the most dangerous runs that ends here is the Tellurium route, from Toulon in the Auvergne system. For every 2 transports sent out, one doesn't make it, if the statistics are accurate. Auvergne is at the edge of the kingdom, and with the invasion of Sirius, securing it isn't high on the King's wish list apparantly.

1119450.text: This planet is the heart of all diamond mining in Gallia. From the mines on the west continent, to the cutting facilities around the spaceport, to the diamond synthesizer plants a few hundred kilometers south - a large percentage of the planet's industrial capacity is geared to diamonds. Synthetic diamonds are also suitable for jewelry, but what sort of lady is content with a fake? So, they mostly get used in mining drills. The Chateau Salins and Metz stations in Lorraine take a portion of both types.

1119451.text: The highest quality of diamonds are used in our jewelry. There is no finer quality, than those produced by the greatest Gallic artisans. Of course, those artisans have their standards, and many of them have relocated to the luxury resorts and liners in the Provence system. They expect the raw materials for their trade to be delivered to them there. The good thing about it? The payout.

1119452.text: Some of the diamonds produced here get shipped out as far as Auvergne, although it's only a small portion. Some of the space colonies in that system have a demand for these. Very few people choose to make that run, because of the risks involved. Those that do often return with Tellurium from Toulon, for the industrial port on this planet.

1119453.text: I used to be a miner, out there cracking rocks with the best of them. Then some damn Brigand gang attacked one of our operations out of nowhere. After three months in the hospital the doctor told me I wouldn't be able to operate a mining ship. Luckily, the execs here take care of us.

1119454.text: I was sent to Nevers and trained as a bartender, then brought here. I've worked as the bartender here ever since. One of the execs told me I was transferred here to remind them of the dangers faced by our miners everyday. So they fully understand that their decisions can have severe consequences.

1119455.text: You're here looking for some work? Look around, most of the people in this bar can point you in the right direction. Here, take this drink and give it to that man right there. It's his favorite. Be polite and chat him up and I'm sure you'll find some work.

1119456.text: Roanne is a huge base for us, both in size and importance. Aside from serving as an administrative center and training facility, there's mining still going on. We also produce a lot of goods and half-fabricates here. Ultralloy is always in demand at shipyards throughout Gallia, such as Riom and Laval. You can make a tidy sum on those runs, but watch out - the Brigands need it for their own shipbuilding too.

1119457.text: This station still bears the classname of it's founder. The GMS honors and rewards those who are loyal to the company. Loyalty is important to us. Motivating people to go beyond what is asked of them by rewarding them has been GMS policy for the past five centuries and it has worked in our favor. We are now virtually the sole raw materials producer within Gallia, and no one is unhappy about that.

1119458.text: Ultralloy are difficult to produce. Not only is the process dangerous and tedious, the raw materials are difficult to acquire. Molybdenum is mined locally as much as possible, but not always available in sufficient quantities. Tellurium has to be imported from the Toulon facility in the Provence. That's a dangerous, but neccesary run.

1119459.text: Ah, yes. Ultralloy. You know, shipyards are not the only facilities who have a need of those. For certain weapons and ammunitions these are needed as well. Some of the Solar factories have a need for Ultralloy, so we send the occasional shipment to Abbeville Production in Picardy also.

1119460.text: Ultralloy production is complex and difficult. When you start from scratch, you're basically combining a number of metals together under the right pressure and temperature, so the molecular lattice of the alloy has the precise structure you want it to have. The selection of the metals is also important. Most Ultralloys start with a basic light weight alloy, which is primarily Aluminium. Aluminium gets shipped here from the Raubling mining station, we do not have a shortage of that. Some alloys are shipped here as half-fabricates, for instance from Bourg-en-Bresse.

1119461.text: I enjoy staying on this station. The good thing about it being the company headquarters is that the company cares about public perception here, more than anywhere else. Accomodations are quite good as a result, and the tavern as you can see is quite well-stocked. Not too sure about the crippled bartender though...

1119462.text: I'm just a junior member of the company still. Currently, I am doing some of the supply runs within the Core Worlds, getting to know the tricks of the trade. One of the runs I make is out to Gien Space Colony, carrying Ultralloy. That takes me through Languedoc, which is usually pretty safe to travel through.

1119463.text: The Junkers often try and restore old ships to working condition I'm told. They salvage wrecks left over from the Gallic wars and try to restore them to spaceworthiness. You'd not catch me on one of those, that's for sure. Many of the wrecks must have bad fuel lines, because the Junkers ask for Manifold shipments quite often. A friend of mine used to ship those in from Lodeve, in the Languedoc system. I imagine they still need them here, but that system's too dangerous for my tastes.

1119464.text: Some of the more advanced components we make here require very rare materials. One such resource is Gadolinium, which we import from Planet Quillan. It's a route I'm scheduled to take tomorrow, once my escort arrives. Something tells me we'll be needing them.

1119465.text: I'm here on vacation with my family. Fully paid by the GMS, I might add. My boys are enjoying the pool and me and the wife have been enjoying some quality alone time, if you know what I mean.

1119466.text: We're enjoying a two week vacation, longer than your typical vacation because I took advantage of the Belleville being in the system. Since we live on Roanne Production Facility the travel time was minimal. Time to kick back and relax.

1119467.text: I caught some guy trying to sell my teenage son some Nox, turns out he is a member of a local Brigand gang. Probably just a low level dealer, but at least that is one less of them that will be unable to peddle that crap to our children.

1119468.text: Many of the manufacturing facilities on this colony require raw materials to be imported. There is, after all, little more than a vacuum outside of the colony. Much of our Luxury Consumer Goods industry requires Gold as an embellishment. We ship it here from BS Castres in the Edinburgh System.

1119469.text: Aside from the industry, this colony has a thriving artisan population. Jewelers and craftsmen of all kinds - and they do enjoy working with only the finest materials. Take for instance the Pearls we bring here from the Planet Bourges aquafarms - the finest quality available.

1119470.text: The amenities here are better than those on Roanne so my wife chose to raise our kids here. We have to pay the rent for our apartment, but the company picked up the tab for the school. Many GMS families choose to live here, so the company now provides us with shuttle transportation to and from Roanne on a daily basis.

1119471.text: The Royal Navy has engaged the Council in multiple theaters of combat over the years. We go to great lengths to hunt them down, even into the Border Worlds and Sirius. It is our policy to fight them out there so we don't have to fight them here.

1119472.text: Our bomber attack drones target many of the Council's most well defended bases and planets. If children or civilians are accidentally killed by our drones, so be it. Collateral damage is part of the cost of war.

1119473.text: Part of our strategy to eliminate the Council is to pound the rebellious cities and colonies into submission. The people need to be taught that anything other than complete loyalty to the Crown will be punished severely. We do not expect any significant blowback from the Gallic citizenry from these tactics.

1119474.text: We gather up the most troublesome Prisoners here onboard the Venissieux, and ship them off to Fleury-Merogis Prison Station. I for one am glad to be rid of such filth! We do our utmost to keep the Prisoners from finding out where they are headed, as it cuts down on incidents of rioting and suicide. It's only a short run to Fleury-Merogis, so we don't get into too much trouble on the way there.

1119475.text: We are very pleased to offer our soldiers the latest in Side Arms technology - brought in from The Ring in Rheinland. The Royal Navy deserves only the best that the galaxy has to offer. We have to deal with the worst of the worst, traitors and other fiends that require our 'special attention'. The Navy also has its hands full with counter-terrorism missions. Such missions often require us to get up close and personal with the enemy. When the heat of battle is on, I am ever grateful for the most lethal weapons available.

1119476.text: Securing Jump Gates and Trade Lanes are a priority for the Royal Navy. Commerce must continue to flow, despite all of the conflicts going on. Any disruptions would end up hurting the war efforts.

1119477.text: Ahh, shore leave! As one of the many crew on rotation here I am off to Planet Metz for three days. I intend to make the best I can of them. We have our choice of spaceports, but I prefer Croix-Rousse. Who wants to land among the cargo haulers and oil workers? I want to be where the civilians are, especially the pretty ones!

1119478.text: I am charged with coordinating the many Marine companies that come in from the Montreuil. From Ile-de-France, to Lorraine, then onto who knows where. It's a Marine's life to be always moving from ship to ship, mission to mission. It will be very interesting to hear first-hand accounts of war from the invasion forces. I expect the first Marine companies will start being rotated back to local battleships like this one soon.

1119479.text: The Junkers have done a valuable service over the years by bringing in Sirian technology. The insights we've gained from the imported cargo has helped accelerate technological advancement in Gallia. This is why the Royal Navy gives them the benefit of the doubt around here and mostly keeps out of their affairs.

1119480.text: We have had several shipments of Deuterium come under terrorist attack recently after leaving Planet Chateauroux. Lorraine is considered relatively safe - Berry and Orleanais, not so much. There are a lot of long lanes to travel, with less coverage by the battleships of the Royal Navy in those two systems. There could well be enemy bases out there as staging points for raiders, but we have yet to find them. Slippery as they are, they will not evade the dragnet, and the noose, forever!

1119481.text: Gallic ships rely on a good supply of Promethene fuel to get around. We have our supplies shipped in from Briancon Station in the Languedoc system. The Royal Navy ensures that EFL transports are well defended on their supply runs. Demand is going through the roof with the war getting underway. As a Supply Officer, I sometimes struggle to compete with the front-line forces in getting what we need here on the Venissieux. I haven't had to ground any patrols yet, but that may be just a matter of time.

1119482.text: I've been stationed on this battleship for a very long time, almost two and a half years now, without any leave. I miss my family back on New Paris. I fear my children will no longer recognize their mother when I return.

1119483.text: If you're an outdoorsman, Planet Metz is a great place to go hunting. There's thousands of species of animals that populate this planet, many of which offer good sport. If you have some free time while you're planet-side, I recommend checking out all that Metz has to offer.

1119484.text: The high unemployment here is making people restless. There is widespread dissatisfaction with the government and I fear it will only get worse. The Royal Police will try to control the people as best we can, but eventually things need to improve for people's everyday lives or we're headed for a wave of chaos.

1119485.text: Trials? Ha! Terrorists like the Council or Maquis don't deserve trials. They renounced their citizenship the moment they spoke ill of the King. Now they're thrown in jail immediately after being caught, if they're lucky.

1119486.text: Despite all the rights for free speech and assembly put forth in this House's founding documents, the Crown has ways to keep the citizenry under control. It's our job to make sure the angry rabble doesn't amass a serious threat to the established order. We know that if the people are intimidated out of exercising their rights that are enshrined on paper, then those rights effectively cease to exist.

1119487.text: Whenever we crack down hard on a group of protesters that mock the King, the main focus is NOT the rioters of the moment. They could be dealt with in many different ways. The point is to create a healthy sense of fear in the rest of the populace, showing them that if they want to try to dissent publicly and disrupt the status quo, then there will be a whole lot of pain coming their way.

1119488.text: We like to dress up in full paramilitary battle gear whenever we go out to crush some riots. We look really cool and it helps ratchet up the fear in those people as we club them mercilessly. It's a whole lot of fun.

1119489.text: In times of war, the Crown has less patience for political dissent. If you have a grievance with the King, it's best you just keep it you yourself. Believe me, you don't want us to come knocking on your door late at night.

1119490.text: Cargo interdiction is the most effective type of operations we can do to bring down crime here in the Gallic Core Worlds. All of the criminal groups get their cash from smuggling. If we starve them of funds, soon enough they will not be able to function. That will mean a safer Gallia for everyone.

1119491.text: We at the local Lorraine Royal Police precinct want to get a new fleet of ships for our patrols. That means all fees and tickets will get hiked up by 50 percent. As for bringing those fees down after we buy the new ships: no guarantees.

1119492.text: The big corporations like GMS and EFL have so much money that they don't even notice the losses they take when we charge their transports with fees. On their balance sheet, the payments to the Royal Police don't even add up to a tiny percentage of a rounding error. I'll be doubling my ticketing of those guys. It's the easiest money out there.

1119493.text: There is no law in Gallia that says I have to be courteous or pleasant to foreign traders. They're lucky we even let them inside our borders. I'll usually charge them with an import duty and an export duty and anything else I can think of. If that makes them feel unwelcome, well, that's not my problem.

1119494.text: We suspect the Brigands are operating a base somewhere out in the Toul Nebula. We'll be increasing patrols around that area and see if we can make some more arrests. You need to be careful though when flying around in those nebulae. Danger could lurk behind any whiff of cloud.

1119495.text: I have always been proud to wear the badge and serve this house. Everything I do in uniform is with pride for the Kingdom of Gallia. Once the uniform comes off, umm, don't ask.

1119496.text: The Council are a cancer in Gallic society. This disease is seeping out of Champagne and into the other systems. In my medical opinion, the only solution to this scourge is amputation.

1119497.text: The Royal Police have been monitoring the Unione Corse and their shady dealings. We've nailed a couple of low level thugs, but the Corse bosses are always very cautious. We're persistent though. Once they slip up, we'll pounce.

1119498.text: This system gets a lot of trade traffic going in and out of Ile-De-France, and do you know what that means? Cargo duties! Charging tolls to hapless transport captains passing through Lorraine is what put my kids through college!

1119499.text: Yes, we are aware of the threats against the Luxury Liner Belleville. That's why the Royal Police has upped patrols around the liner. If those Maquis want to come and blow up all those civilians, they'll have to get through us first.

1119500.text: I have some family on Marne. They are probably terrified living under Council control. If the Council ever finds out that their relative is a Royal Policeman, my family will probably be locked up. I just hope they are OK. Curse those treacherous Councilmen!

1119501.text: I overheard some of the Solar Engineering employees saying something about the Crown paying high prices for Jump Gate and Trade Lane Parts that are shipped to Fort Albi. You better get in on that deal while you can.

1119502.text: Looking to do something that isn't exactly legal? Well, just throw some cash our way and the Royal Police will make sure no one knows about it. We'll call it our little 'Gentleman's Agreement'. Don't worry, you can trust us.

1119503.text: Solar Engineering is run like a well-oiled machine. They make the Royal Police look like incompetent, inefficient, slothful, and stubborn blunderbusses. Well, to be fair, I guess we just come across like that anyway.

1119504.text: We bring in quite a bit of Basic Alloy from Bourg-en-Bresse. It goes into general construction right across Metz, from civilian housing to industrial girders. On planets there is generally enough space to use a lot of cheap local materials like traditional steel and old-fashioned concrete. Basic Alloy reinforcement in the right places can more than double the length of girder spans, and greatly increase the fire rating of materials. Don't get me started on the various applications for construction plastics, I could talk all day if you let me.

1119505.text: Local industry depends on High-Temperature Alloy being brought in from Planet Nuremburg out in Rheinland. Fusion reactors and industrial processes can involve extreme heat, enough to vapourise most materials. Temperatures can rise to millions of degrees for short fractions of a second, just like the interior of a star. This is exactly what you need to trigger fusion reactions, or break down toxic chemicals.

1119506.text: Some might understand the poor people that support the revolution. But the rich ones? I will never understand them. The crown basicly gave them everything one can dream of, and they run away to support it's sworn enemies? You know what they say - don't bite the hand that feeds you.

1119507.text: Unione Corse. Never fly around with those. Some might come and assassinate you while the rest will point a gun at your head trying to claim your money. I still don't understand how they stay partly legal, they should all be declared enemies of the state.

1119508.text: Watch yourself if you are bringing in Holmium from out at Saint-Flour. I never feel safe until I reach Gien Space Colony. There have been reports of recent pirate attacks along the lanes between Chateauroux and Gien. The Police haven't turned up anything yet - I think the only thing they are 'turning' is a blind eye to what is happening out there.

1119509.text: I always wondered who is less expected - Gallic Brigands or Unione Corse. Just some time ago, I was stopped by a Brigands raiding party and they let me off. While I was getting on my way, a GMS convoy came through. Needless to say the Brigands butchered them. One could say it's all about the cargo - but I was carrying Oil while the GMS convoy was carrying Ultralloy!

1119510.text: I thought I had seen everything, then I agreed to take a risk running luxury Cigars out from Planet Holstein in Rheinland. People pay top money for Tobacco to be shipped out there, hand-rolled, then shipped back out again. It is a testament to the skills of my security escorts that I made it out alive. Equally, it is a testament to the decadence of our society that I had to go there at all!

1119511.text: I am charged with a shipment of the latest in Holosculpture technology, manufactured at Luxury Liner Hawaii out in the Sigma 19 system. With the focus now on Bretonia, I can move goods with a lot more confidence. Besides, with all the traffic moving too and from Leeds, what pirate would bother with me? There is much more valuable cargo to be had near the front.

1119512.text: It's funny, out here on a luxury liner, there is still a strong demand for Holotainment Bands brought in from Mortagne. I mean people have paid good money to travel and go somewhere exotic - why would they want to pay more money to pretend to be somewhere else? Ahh, to live such a life of luxury and indulgence. Perhaps they are watching travel shows promoting the latest tourist havens over in Provence. I am pretty sure the guests here on the Belleville are envious of them.

1119513.text: I don't trust the GMS. Too many of their space miners seem to have accidents. Just take a look at the way they treat any small nobody who is working for them. A janitor shouldn't be treated with such little respect - he is probably just another school dropout being taken advantage of.

1119514.text: I have very little trust in the Gallic Royal police. One day I was pirated by a Unione Corse pilot, and got forced to drop all of the cargo I carried. And guess what I see two days later? The Unione Corse pilot is selling that very same stolen cargo on a Royal Police base! That is simply outrageous!

1119515.text: I don't trust pilots of other companies, especially their escorts. For them we are competetion for hauling contracts and they might just ignore other corporation ships that are in trouble! Of course if I see such a thing I report it to the Royal court - we are all on the same side!

1119516.text: Montigny has some of the best deals you will find on high tech Magnets in all of Gallia. I have orders heading out to Laval Shipyard right now. EFL sends orders over the Neural net, as well as their own trade reps to inspect batches as they come through. I think this is a pretty fast and safe run, if you want to some work we have plenty of it. Why not get involved and do your part to keep our great nation on it's feet?

1119517.text: It was a bit worrying heading out of Alesia Station with this load of Magnets in my hold. With the Council still holding on to the Champagne system, raids on important cargo like mine are inevitable. The Royal Navy is constantly on patrol along the lanes, and in the nearby cloud. They can't stop all the raids though. Sooner or later I will come across the raiders, then I can only pray to escape with my life.

1119518.text: Ile-De-France is the largest shipping corporation in Gallia. Started from a small ambitious company - we turned into a massive corporation that have more hauling contracts than any other corporation and shipping company in Gallia!

1119519.text: You have to be careful taking Magnets out to Riom Shipyard. I have heard of the odd terrorist attack in the Berry system. It's not like they actually want the Magnets to use themselves, or to sell. They hit the transports until they dump the cargo, then simply destroy it right there on the spot. The demons are simply trying to hurt us with their actions.

1119520.text: I bring in Aluminium from Raubling Station out in the Munich system. Not much demand for my cargo among the rabble of pirates that lurk in Kusari. I have had a couple try to extort money from me, but I can usually bluff them until the Police show up. As long as I am not carrying anything too valuable, or that has strategic value, I can get by unnoticed for the most part.

1119521.text: The obvious Pro-Royal stance that Ile-De-France founders took, and their willingness to supply the Royal Navy even in dangerous places gained them a lot of hauling contracts. Following that we had massive growth.

1119522.text: I shall be requesting a Police escort for my cargo, as this is a shipment of Ultralloy headed out to Maintenon Shipyard in the Orleanais system. If the Royal Navy wants this material to build their warships, they will have to make an effort to protect it. Otherwise I will be a certain target for every pirate and would-be terrorist out there. They will want to stop my delivery, and steal the cargo for their own devices. For the sake of the Crown, this must not be allowed to happen!

1119523.text: Sometimes I regret ever volunteering for hauling contracts to the front. When a Maquis aims his gun at your oil tanks you get a new perspective about life. However, they are great money and come with a large bonus.

1119524.text: I could nearly swear a few days ago I saw a GMS transport entering Champagne with a full load of Oil and construction materials. I am not sure whether or not to report it. If my eyes misled me I can expect serious blowback, not to mention that I will ruin a decent man's life.

1119525.text: EFL and IDF compete for Oil shipping contracts. Usually EFL get the better ones inside Gallia since they can offer lower prices, after all they mine it. But they aren't couragous as the IDF are, we take the more profiting and dangerous contracts in the far reaches.

1119526.text: The Council, while being blind, did make a lot of smart strategic choices. Planet Marne is one of the best examples - it's rich with different valuable minerals and with Oil. But they are truly are blind if they can't see the Gallic Royal forces' strength. The GRN will do the fighting while we will bring all the needed war materials - in the name of the king!

1119527.text: The Council say they fight for a free Gallia, I say lies. How can they even think of freeing anything if they support the piracy and murder of decent civilians that is done by the Maquis. The Maquis, whom are former Council members!

1119528.text: We are not barbarians here in Gallia. On certain occaisions I am able to transport Luxury Consumer Goods across Kusari-controlled space, out to Luxury Liner Hawaii in the Sigma 19 system. As the goods can be classed as humanitarian aid, I am a low-priority target for aggressors. I like to try and team up with fuel or ammunition transports, so they can take the heat while I sneak past. Yes I know how that sounds, but we do what we must.

1119529.text: I am off to Provence with a load of Luxury Consumer Goods. I get to take what is arguably the easy road into Provence, down in Auvergne. The jump hole there is guarded by a battleship of the Royal Navy. It is still risky heading off the Trade Lanes. Help takes that much longer to arrive, and there is no lane network for the authorities to monitor. At least I know there is a powerful and friendly support ship at the end, not just a jump hole to nowhere.

1119530.text: All of my brothers joined the Royal Navy, but I chose to work for Ile-De-France Shipping. At first, my family thought I was a coward who was afraid to fight for his nation and his king. But once they saw the dangers that lay out there for a supply transport pilot they started to give me the credit I was due.

1119531.text: Flying Luxury Consumer Goods out to Planet Nevers is not a bad run really. Strong demand means good prices, with a relatively low risk of pirates. I think I have it pretty good with what I am doing. Sure I could probably make more money flying more exotic goods around Gallia, or even try my hand at looting my way into Sirius. But I have a family at home now, one that I want to see when I am on leave. I don't want my family to see me in a coffin until I am very, very old!

1119532.text: You can't get a better job than this. I run Luxury Consumer Goods out to the Royal residences like Versailles and Vendome. I never get refused docking clearance, and am almost treated like royalty myself! Of course it helps being moderately attractive like I am. Maybe i will get lucky and be proposed to, by one of the nice rich men out there someday.

1119533.text: I like being an Ile-De-France pilot. I get good money and see lots of places and meet lot of people. I call it the Gallic Dream in it's best form. Adventures, new friends and very good money, what more a girl could wish to have?

1119534.text: Solar Engineering got its start with mostly government work. But as time went on, we grew more and more independent on the Crown. Nowadays our types of clients and services are so diversified that we can handle any market shocks that come our way.

1119535.text: Those stupid Brigands cost me several hundred thousand credits in repairs and nearly destroyed my ship. But all that is preferred to giving them the satisfaction of paying their ransom. They'll never get a single credit from me.

1119536.text: I wonder if EFL realizes that if the Oil in Gallia ever ran out, two-thirds of their employees would be planet-side, unemployed and begging for food. Oil is the lifeblood of that company and unfortunately for them, it is finite.

1119537.text: We began offering space station construction services following the First Gallic War. Ever since, this has been one of our most lucrative divisions. The more hostility and destruction that is brought on by war and piracy, the more money we make building new stations. It's a bit cynical, but it's good for the bottom line.

1119538.text: Kusari has turned out to be a valuable trade partner for Gallia. Though, I'm surprised that some parts of Sirius can get along with Gallia and achieve mutual benefits.

1119539.text: Solar Engineering learned long ago that if you want to retain top talent, you need to pay for it. That's why Solar has the highest compensation levels of any of the large Gallic corporations. In business, money buys success.

1119540.text: I work as an engineer for Solar Engineering. Most of my research and development work is kept under tight secrecy. It is frustrating at times to come home to my family and not be allowed to tell them what I've been doing all day. Luckily, my paychecks more than make up for it.

1119541.text: I'm about to make a shipping run out to the Border Worlds. I made sure to install the best armor upgrade and shield I could afford. I have a feeling I'll be needing them.

1119542.text: Station operation is a sweet gig. Mostly it's just simple management tasks: keeping everyone happy, making sure you have enough supplies onboard, and ensuring adequate defenses. The money you make from the tenants and visitors yields huge profits once you have an efficient model of operations established.

1119543.text: Within Gallia we are the main supplier of high-tech machinery. While EFL builds the huge frames of the various gates and lanes, we are the company responsible for actually bringing those hulks to life. We produce Gate/Lane Parts at Mortagne Production, then ship them to Metz Station for storage until they are needed for repairs or new construction.

1119544.text: High Temperature Alloys are one of the base components our manufacturing plants here need. They are primarily used in Engine Component manufacturing. Rather than producing this half-fabricate ourselves, we import the neccesary amount, usually from the factories on Planet Nuremburg in Rheinland.

1119545.text: I've been encouraging my son to study Sirian language and history in school. I believe there will be a lot of lucrative opportunities for Gallic citizens with a Sirian education background in his generation as time goes on.

1119546.text: I hear the Navy captured a Bretonian station out in the Tau worlds. They called in Solar Engineering teams after they found a partially constructed Jump Gate and Trade Lane. They want that Gate completed, I hear, so we'll have to send over some shipments of Gate/Lane Parts to the captured station, which was nicknamed Indochine. I just hope they'll be compatible with that Sirian frame.

1119547.text: One of the base components all of our high-tech industries require are Bioneural Processors. Unlike conventional electronic or optronic switching circuits, Bioneural circuits can offer "best guess" solutions to problems that are near impossible to calculate. This makes them invaluable for Gate/Lane Parts production, as the variables involved in initiating a stable jump field are almost impossible to calculate exactly. A drawback is that, like all organic matter, they do deteriorate much more quickly then conventional processors.

1119548.text: The Royal Police and Royal Navy do a fine job of securing Lorraine, at least compared to some of the more distant systems like Provence, Auvergne, and the Border Worlds. I'm glad that I'm stationed here.

1119549.text: It's only a matter of time before the King asks us to build a Jump Gate leading to the Provence system. Gallia has too much invested there to have some half-stable Jump Hole be the only way in and out. Given the location I think they'll aim for Languedoc as the recipient system, rather then Auvergne, but that's not my call. Meanwhile, to expedite matters, we've begun stockpiling Gate/Lane Parts on Planet Marseille. That way, when the request comes, with it's usual unrealistic timeline, we can deliver.

1119550.text: One of the components most heavily used in Gate/Lane Parts manufacturing are Nanocapacitors. I can't go into too much detail, but the short-term energy storage properties of Nanocapacitors are ideal for creating and sustaining the jump field when a Jump Gate is asked to activate. Maintenance requirements for especially the Trade Lanes have gone down by 30% since we switched to Nanocapacitors for energy balancing. Planet Hamburg specializes in the production of these.

1119551.text: Solar Engineering recruits top graduates from the most prestigious universities on New Paris. In a down economy, the hand of the employer is strengthened and you can be even more selective than usual. This bodes very well for Solar when we need to fill important positions with talented new hires. Unfortunately, it's not so good for those kids in the bottom 98% of their class who are desperate to get a decent job.

1119570.text: Gallic Navy\nDe Grasse Bartender\nAlexander du Lac

1119571.text: Gallic Navy\nDe Grasse Commodity Trader\nHarcourt Boisvert

1119572.text: Gallic Navy\nDe Grasse Equipment Dealer\nNicolas Rocheleau

1119573.text: Gallic Navy\nDe Grasse Ship Dealer\nJullian La Leroy

1119587.text: Let me tell you a little secret. The Goverment is too busy with the Council to bother with us. That means there's barely any law enforcement menacing our activities, so now would be the best time to expand our black market activities.

1119588.text: Brigand bases are usually heavily defended. Be careful when flying near one of our bases. We won't take any chances, if you seem suspicious we'll attack. Questions will be asked in case you survive. You won't, though.

1119589.text: We Brigands have only a single station in our possession: Epernay. Our other bases consist only of Asteroid bases, as they're easier to defend.

1119590.text: Battleship Carcassonne is right on the front lines of the conflict, and when they have mass casualties the supply of organ donations can't keep up. We Brigands aren't keen on helping out the Navy, but the truth is that a lot of the troops were conscripted, so the rank and file aren't all that different than us. Anyway, the Navy medical staff on the front line will pay for the Human Organs we ship them, so that's enough for me.

1119591.text: If you don't have time to wait for your number to come up for an organ transplant, you can buy yourself a spot on an operating table in Provence. The advertizements all talk about how Provence is such an exotic destination for a holiday, but what they don't tell you is that part of the draw is that you can get medical procedures done out there away from prying eyes. If you can afford it, that is. I bet the Provence resorts are receiving more Human Organs than Wine casks nowadays.

1119592.text: The Brigands are known as the largest outlaw group in Gallia, consisting of numerous members and having a tight control over the black market. The Corse like to brag about their connections, but Brigands know that we don't need to brag about our cash flow.

1119593.text: You might think it strange that Brigands decided to get involved in the medical industry, but the fact is that the dying will pay just about anything to stay alive. The rich, sick folks on Planet New Tokyo seem to be able to afford an awful lot, if the amount of Human Organs we are shipping to them means anything.

1119594.text: We bring Gallic Artifacts here from Thionville Base. This is quite profitable for both those who bring it in, and for those who buy it from the transports. We pay them a decent profit margin, and we earn an even nicer profit margin when we sell them on the local black markets.

1119595.text: Most of our bases did not belong to us originally. Some were taken by force, some were abandoned when we found them, but a mere fraction of our bases were constructed by us.

1119596.text: Government regulated organ transplantation probably allows more people to die than those who receive a transplant, so we're actually saving the lives of the common folk here. What more could a Free Brigand want than to make a lot of credits while helping the common man and shafting the government? Nothing, that's what. Those Sirians think the same way. We're shipping our excess supply of Human Organs to Atka Research Station. The major downside to this product is that it doesn't have a long shelf life, so we have to sell them when we have them.

1119597.text: If you want quick, good money, bring in some of that labor that we've sourced from Sirius. We have a great need for labor here, just don't ask me what they do. Nobody in the transport side of the business seems to know.

1119598.text: The Brigands might be numerous, but are far from being united. Each base acts on it's own, while maintaining friendly relationships with other Brigand bases. Centralized, top down authority is a big conflict with our outlook on life. This way, every Brigand can do his own thing, so long as he doesn't hurt another Brigand's turf.

1119599.text: While it is not openly discussed, many of us Council pilots quietly support the Maquis. They've done us enough favors in the past.

1119600.text: The Council and the Maquis are really just two sides of the same coin. While we all want freedom from the Crown, we have vastly different methods that we use.

1119601.text: Many thought that the split of the Maquis and the Council would damage their relations. On the contrary - each side can now mind its own business with more freedom.

1119602.text: My younger brother is a Maquis pilot. I don't agree with him that killing civilians to achieve the goal of freedom is wise. But when it comes to getting rid of a few of the King's dogs, I'm in.

1119603.text: The King's loyalists think their King will keep the throne. Not on our watch. With each day's passing we gain new members and supporters. Soon we will grow large enough to overthrow him!

1119604.text: Gallia used to have a true democracy, but the King intervened in the democratic process and it resulted in an unacceptable situation where the King has absolute control.

1119605.text: While the Council is determined to protect civilians, we tend to suddenly become "too occupied" with the war when we see civilians hauling goods to the Royal Navy. It's a shame they aren't able to get assistance from us.

1119606.text: We opened the Gallic border for Sirians. Most of us get really angry when we see those ungrateful traders supplying the Crown. This is why if one of them gets blasted, we don't even try to give any excuses about why we abstain from aiding them... Unless of course, the perpetrator is a Royalist!

1119607.text: While I disagree with the way of life the Brigands have chosen for themselves, I understand why they prefer it. Living under the Crown's authority isn't much of a good life at all.

1119608.text: The reason why we tolerate the Brigands more than Unione Corse and giving more freedom in our space is because they helped us in the Second Gallic Civil War, notably the liberation of Planet Marne.

1119609.text: This base is a good staging ground to liberate Prisoners that are being transported from this system to Fleury-Merogis Prison.

1119610.text: Many people from the nearby planets seek to escape the Royalists grasp. We are making Refugee convoys every week for them as a result. Planets Pittsburgh, Gran Canaria and Toulouse are among the most frequent locations we send them to.

1119611.text: We sell a fair amount of Oil to Briancon Station out in the Languedoc system. Briancon is one of our major refineries, and the machinery there needs regular maintenance. Some replacement parts can be machined on-site. The base itself is very well defended, but terrorist attacks could result in lanes being cut, and relief could be some days away if the Royal Navy is tied up elsewhere. We need to be self-sufficient in these times, to ride out any storms that come our way.

1119612.text: I am heading out to Riom Shipyard with a load of Oil soon. The Royal Navy will be out in the field for a long time, with supply lines stretched to the limit. It is vital that our warships are as well stocked with supplies, even for basics like lubricants.

1119613.text: Oil at the planet-side extraction operations is getting harder to come by these days. We need to keep drilling further and further down to meet our production quotas. This increased difficulty with the extraction ends up raising the cost of Oil throughout Gallia, much to the displeasure of the populace. I think we need to explore for more sources of Oil beyond the borders of Gallia.

1119614.text: Narita Outpost has just sent in another order for Cryocubes. If you want something frozen in a hurry, we have the technology to do it. Likewise, Cryocubes are the best technology we have for space station cooling units. You can't just open a window out there you know!

1119615.text: Yokohama Shipyard has regular orders for Cryocubes. These are one of GMS's best selling manufactured products. A sealed unit that is very easy to use and very effective. In space there is no such thing as heat convection, so heat can build up inside space stations very quickly. We can recover some of it and use it for heating hot water, and some we can safely radiate into space. All the rest has to be neutralised by using something very cold - that is where the Cryocube comes in.

1119616.text: We have urgent need of Cryocubes out on Metz Station, in Lorraine. The station population has ballooned since Planet Marne fell to the Council. More people means more energy consumption, and that means more heat generated. Even the hot air from their breath and bodies would be suffocating without enough coolant supply. Waste heat has always been a problem with living in space. It is well known that you can die faster from losing coolant supply than losing anything else - even air and water. That's because air and water can be filtered and recycled, heat cannot.

1119617.text: There's a back-log of hundreds of crates of goods stacked up in the station's loading bay waiting to be shipped out. If you're looking to earn a little extra cash and you have a decent sized cargo hold, head over there and see what needs to be hauled out. We could sure use the help.

1119618.text: We're doing everything we can to support the Royal Navy and the war effort. We've added shifts at the shipyards and focused more resources on military hardware production. Everyone's pushing themselves really hard. Gallia will not fail.

1119619.text: One would think that the EFL's close ties with the Crown would mean that the Royal Police would behave around us. But no. We're still subject to the same random ridiculous fees just like everyone else out there.

1119620.text: Nothing like a little time off. I am heading home to Planet Le Mans on the next Spaceship Crew transport. I think Laval offers one of the better jobs available in EFL. No dirty Oil drilling, no dangerous transportation. My work team is six days on, eight days off, and home is just a few hours away.

1119621.text: The cold emptiness of space starts to get to you after a while. Some people develop depression or other psychological problems during long assignments out here. I've always been a planet-side guy on New Paris until now and being out here is really getting irritating. I need to get off this stinkin' metal contraption as soon as possible.

1119622.text: Our Oil drilling technology has improved dramatically in recent years. We are able to reach pockets of Oil deep underground that were inaccessible just a few years ago. Still, it's hard to keep up with the growing demand.

1119623.text: I envy the Spaceship Crews heading home to Planet Mayenne. They get to live most of their days planetside, with their families. My family is out in Picardy, I can't convince them to move out here where it's safer. I only hope they will see the light before too much trouble brews back home. Even if the police do crack down on the Council troublemakers, or even if they drive them out completely, there is always a chance my family could be caught in the crossfire. I don't know what I would do if anything happened to them.

1119624.text: We're a huge company, so don't be surprised to find out that nearly every currently operating station in Gallia was at least partially built by EFL. Except the crappy ones...those were built by Solar Engineering.

1119625.text: You can make a nice living working for EFL, especially in space. Many people are afraid to work out here, but it's really not so bad. The sight of that big paycheck every month is all I need to keep me going.

1119626.text: We ship in Promethene fuel from our refinery on Briancon Station, out in the Languedoc system. This is where many civilian ships, and most of the Royal Navy's transport fleets, are launched. Ever since the Second Gallic Civil War our drydocks have been at full capacity. I don't expect to see a decline in ship commissioning orders during my working life here for EFL, and maybe not even for the next generation of employees.

1119627.text: When you've been working at this shipyard as long as I have, you begin to realize how two-faced other corporate folks can be. Sure we're all smiles and high-fives at the bar. But once the contract bidding starts and there's money on the table, that's when the knives really come out.

1119628.text: I don't like the idea of having all these other contractors around here. I just don't trust them. You can tell they are always trying to pry some corporate gossip or insider information out of you, especially at this bar.

1119629.text: We keep our reserve power plants supplied with Deuterium, brought in from Planet Chateauroux. We also fortify our Promethene fuel with Deuterium for the larger ships we build here. We saturate the Oil with Deuterium, squeezing out the normal hydrogen. As a result, we get more energy yield from the fuel, at the expense of neutron radiation that needs to be protected against. For larger ships the bigger engines you need for that are not a problem to install.

1119630.text: Government contracts keep our business running. Without them, I think we'd quickly go out of business. That's why it's important to always stay on the good side of the Royal Navy folks around here. We just need to keep our heads down, do our jobs, and the money will keep coming in.

1119631.text: It's surprising how many contracts we've been winning from the Royal Navy that are out in Sirius. But if that's where the money is, that's where we will go. We never say 'No' to the Royal Navy.

1119632.text: Although there are more exotic goods in demand in the Provence system, we Junkers still have to deliver the basic supplies. Monte Carlo still manages to move several tonnes of Oil a day to customers who can't just order it from GMS over the Neural net. Their need for discretion means that simple Oil transactions can be quite profitable, as well as dangerous.

1119633.text: I'm worried for our Junker brothers in Sirius. Now that the origin of the Junkers has been revealed, I would expect the Sirian governments to try to round them up and throw them in jail. This is not how we planned it.

1119634.text: The Royal Police can be easily manipulated with a little cash. If they ever stop you and try to levy some strange new tax on you, try to covertly offer a bribe of an equivalent amount. That should get them off of your back. Those Police aren't the smartest knives in the drawer.

1119635.text: The Corse are a curious group of folks. We don't really know which side they're on. They aren't as blood-thirsty as the Maquis or Brigands and they certainly aren't very pleasant to the corporate folks. But don't be fooled, they are a powerful little group, and they seem to have connections to the Crown. It's best not to make them angry.

1119636.text: We in the Junkers revere the discipline and honor of the brave folks in the Royal Navy. Obviously most of us aren't cut from the same mold as those people. The Navy defends our freedoms from the barbaric hordes in Sirius, something I would never have the guts to do.

1119637.text: I'm getting sick and tired of the Royal Police taking away all of my profits! Every time I run into one of them, I always have to pay up. At this rate, it's more profitable to sit on the station and twiddle my thumbs than to go out and try to make money. This is getting ridiculous! Argghhh!!

1119638.text: When the local EFL pilots can't keep up with demand, that is where we come in. We can ship Oil out to places like Briancon Station just as easily as anyone else. Anything that gets me closer to Provence, where the real money is made, is a good thing.

1119639.text: While our Sirian brothers have dealt mainly in Scrap Metal, we go one better and melt it all down into Manifolds. These mixed ingots are a lot easier to transport over long distances, such as Lodeve Freeport. It will be interesting to see how the composition of the Manifold changes, as we come across more Sirian ships to salvage. I am hoping we can get a better price for any exotic metals we find.

1119640.text: I wonder if the Council realizes how hopeless their cause is. Their forces are dwindling, always retreating, against the might of the largest and most powerful armada in the history of human-kind. They are doomed. The Junkers learned long ago, it's better to be at the right hand of the Devil than in his path.

1119641.text: We Junkers are very keen to supplement commercial fuel supplies for Gallia. I expect we will be getting a lot of the surplus Oil demand offloaded to us. As demand rises and falls for various commodities, the Junkers have moved in to fill the needs of the average citizen. As much as the big corporations might not like us, we are an essential part of the Gallic economy.

1119642.text: You know how to make a fine Provence Cigar even better? I slip in a little Synth Weed I get shipped in from Lixhiem. No hangovers from Wine, I can't think of a better way to relax - nor can my many customers!

1119643.text: Yes, the Police can usually be bought off. But the folks in the Royal Navy, they're incorruptible! If you ever get yourself in trouble with the Royal Navy, honesty is your best bet. Offering some cash for them to look the other way will land you in Fleury-Merogis real fast. I would rather volunteer for the Marines than end up there!

1119644.text: I have several shipments of Oil headed out to Fourchambault Shipyard today. It's all right here on the manifest. Yes I know it's an EFL invoice, but look at the timestamp. When EFL has shipments like this that fall weeks behind schedule, they are simply dumped on us marked 'urgent'. Urgent, in my dictionary, means lucrative.

1119645.text: Our hottest moving item is coming in from a remote base called Torino, I don't know where that is, nor do I care to. All I know is that this orange powder they call Cardamine has my customers begging - literally begging - for more. If the Police knew, or cared, about how dangerous this stuff was - I might have to pay a bigger bribe!

1119646.text: Many in the Junker leadership get to live planet-side on New Paris. It's an extraordinarily beautiful place if you've never been there. I've been to Sirius a few times and there's no place that compares to our capital. I hope to retire to there one day.

1119647.text: I transport Oil from this planet to Planet Marseille. It's quite a trek for such a simple cargo, but all industry needs raw materials. Having a lower value cargo makes you less attractive to the Brigands, but that doesn't stop them from trying to seize some for themselves.

1119648.text: I ship in Beryllium from the Java facility. It's not an easy run to do. Beryllium has become scarce, with the military demanding a substantial amount to repair and replace damaged engine components and reactor casings. Scarce materials are expensive materials. And criminals know this all too well.

1119649.text: I've just returned from the Border Worlds, where the Navy took Languedoc from the Council and pushed into Sirius. I hear they even took a station just on the other side of the jump hole from them. You'd think that would make it safer, but nothing really changes for us. The Council never really bothered our ships.

1119650.text: Enjoying your time on Mayenne? I didn't think so, no one here really wants to be here. It is a cold and unforgiving place, perched near the door to Normandy. What? You've not heard about Normandy? The First Gallic War, ring a bell? The Royal Navy wasn't fighting the Council back then. No, the Council is the second group to oppose the Crown and they aren't doing any better than the Normandy Seperatists did.

1119651.text: The army units here are specially trained to fight in the extreme cold here on Mayenne. They protected us from the Normandy Seperatists back in the 500s AGS when they dropped troops planet side. They couldn't do to much about the orbital bombardments though.

1119652.text: We've been mining here since around the mind 400s AGS, the First Gallic War saw a decrease in our activity here, but when that conflict ended operations here picked up considerably. EFL has taken more of an interest in Mayenne as of late. I'd bet it is because they've found some oil here.

1119653.text: I work in one of the Cryocube production facilities here on Mayenne. A fine piece of Gallic engineering these are. I hear IDF is trying to find markets for these outside of Gallia now, in Rheinland. Given the recent surge in orders, I think the demand for them is quite high. Many of the cubes leaving Gallia are headed to the industrial complex in New Berlin made up of Oder Shipyard and The Ring.

1119654.text: This world wasn't always a frozen wasteland. Many thousands of years ago, there must have been a lush jungle instead of this icy desert, otherwise there wouldn't be any Oil down here. The icy conditions don't make mining a very pleasant job, but they do make the drilling itself easier. We use the Oil to run our local Cryocube production plants, and export the rest to various places in Gallia.

1119655.text: Now that the Navy has secured their path into Sirius, they've begun allowing select Sirians to trade with Gallia. It has helped boost our economy, but is it enough? How long can we sustain the Navy at its current size?

1119656.text: I ship in Gadolinium from Quillan, now that our soldiers are once again in control of that world. It's one of the raw materials needed in our Cryocube production plants. Gadolinium is still scarce - the Quillan mining facilities are not running at peak capacity yet. They say the Council left boobytraps behind, although that sounds more like the Maquis, if you ask me.

1119657.text: This world is dangerous for the reckless. The temperature outside would kill you in minutes without proper protection. And I don't mean just a winter coat. For going outside of the compounds, special environmental suits are needed. Naturally, each of our workers working outside of the base facilities is issued a pair, and give an instruction course on how to use them. If you're issued one, I suggest you listen carefully to the briefing. Your life could depend on it.

1119658.text: My entire family works for the GMS, we've been miners for generations. Originally my family worked for Arcadia Materiaux Distribution, when AMD was acquired by the GMS they kept them on and we've worked for the GMS every since.

1119659.text: I've brought in a load of Cobalt from Briesen Mining in Omega 3 It was a hectic trip. We got attacked by pirates three times, but each time the local law enforcement arrived and drove them off. The military budget may be recklessly high, but all these soldiers make our lives as traders a lot easier.

1119660.text: Sirius is both a curse and a blessing to us. On the one hand, we were perfectly fine with servicing our own glorious nation. But on the other hand, our fine products now have a new potential market, and items we produce have no equal outside of Gallia. Right now we have a hard time getting our goods out, but we have a little help. Those Independent Miners for instance, have agreed to allow us to use a place called "Freeport 4" to resell Cryocubes. No idea where it is though. Beyond the Bretonian line I think.

1119661.text: I'm just here relaxing before I head home. I live on the outskirts of town, just before you get into the ruins. Yea, you heard me ruins. They are the ruins of the older mining encamptment that was here, destroyed by the Normandy Seperatists during the First Gallic War.

1119662.text: Bonjour! A new face around here is a rarity, this facility is the oldest Gallic structure in the system. It's long past its prime to, the Service barely turns a profit here.

1119663.text: I've heard rumors that the Council tend to ignore our convoys in the Border Worlds. I've not ventured out there since I was a young lad. If the rumors are true, we're lucky. In the First Gallic War, the Normandy Seperatists didn't ignore the Metal Service. They bombarded our facilities on planet Mayenne and even tried a ground assualt!

1119664.text: We've shifted from astroid miners to modified transports using cargo beaming technology to gather Copper from the De Perseigne Asteroid Field. Even though our operations are less dangerous than those in other regions of Gallia, we're still well paid. Those smug IDF transport crews can't say that!

1119665.text: This is an old base, and an old operation that has fallen out of favor. Neodymium simply isn't as available in the asteroid fields as it once was, and we are having to hunt longer for new veins to harvest. Still, there are a few miners left, and we make enough to convince GMS to keep this operation in business.

1119666.text: We ship the Neodymium we mine here to facilities like Saint-Exupery and Montigny. Once purified, our Neodymium generally ends up in Magnets, or Lasers. Given the current state of our nation, there is a high demand for both, and that has helped this facility immensely.

1119667.text: Those smug IDF transport crews annoy the piss out of me, but I've found the perfect way to stick it to them. When they are bragging about how they get all the fancy government contracts and such, I calmly point out I get paid twice what they do for the same job and have better benefits. That always shuts them up.

1119668.text: I've just come back from bringing a load of Neodymium to Roanne Production. The factory there can always use the raw materials. I brought a load of Oxygen and Water back here from Planet Le Mans - not very valuable, but someone has to keep the station supplied with the basics.

1119669.text: One of the runs I make is the Neodymium run from here to Riom Shipyard. They use the Neodymium in their ship building, of course, producing some hull panels and electric wiring locally. The demand isn't very large though, the shipyard only needs a load every week or so.

1119670.text: I've visited every GMS station in operation and even some of the ones that have been scrapped. Around twenty-five or so if I remember correctly. Let's see there is Roanne, Senonches, Soissons, Chateaudin, Guise, Sancerre, Vierzon, Saint-Flour & Toulon to name some of the ones I've visited. No matter which one you go to, you'll always find good people. We're all family here in the GMS and we'll go out of our way to help one another.

1119671.text: I've made the odd run around the block. One location that can use our Neodymium is Fourchambault Shipyard. Ship building uses many raw materials, and Neodymium is no exception. Although most of it is mined on planets these days, we can stay competative by delivering to the locations that don't have rich Neodymium sources nearby.

1119672.text: I like it here. Criminal activity is very low, and you're about as far from the war as you can be. Yes, it's just me, my transport, and all the Neodymium I can scoop up and deliver here. People say it gets dull after a while. I'll take dull over getting your ship shot out from under you any day!

1119673.text: Sit, sit! Have a brew with me. You looking for work? Sure you are, why else would you be here. I'm not sure what's on the job board, but we're always hiring miners. Good pay, greate benefits, and a spiffy retirement fund. Think you can do better with the IDF or EFL? Good luck!

1119674.text: The EFL build a lot of civilian ships on this station, some of which we use ourselves. Smaller transports, trains, civilian fighters. Our larger mining vessels also return to shipyards as these for refits, repair and upgrades. It is convenient to have one close by in this system, especially if you were hit along the way.

1119675.text: Laval has been in operation for over 200 years. It celebrated its second centennial not long ago. It's been expanded several times now. I still question the wisdom of EFL having built such a huge facility inside an asteroid field. You've noticed all the repair ships roaming around outside, yes?

1119676.text: I'm going to head back to Alesia to pick up a load of Shape-memory Alloy soon. Alesia is our most successful raw materials processing operation, and we are using it as a springboard for expanding out of Gallia...behind our glorious Navy of course. It won't be long before his Grace permits us to set up a permanent outpost outside of the Gallic Core.

1119677.text: Death awaits all who challenge the will of the Throne. Our King has no patience for challenges to His rule and we crack down hard on anyone who threatens the stability of Gallia, foreign or domestic.

1119678.text: Given some of the enhanced daily punishments that prisoners receive for treason, most Gallic citizens have to think twice, three times, or even four times before they even utter a word of discontent about our Royal Highness. That makes my job easier, so I'm all for it.

1119679.text: Those traitors in the Council pay dearly for their crimes. The King considers them the worst of the worst, and the Gallic people support the very harsh punishments that they receive daily in prison.

1119680.text: Life is good out here. To think where we are now used to be the front lines of the Second Gallic Civil War. Now we are very much the rearguard of the Royal Navy. The most action I see these days is escorting Prisoner transfers to Fleury-Merogis over in Ile-de-France. Oh how they cry and scream when they find out where they are headed! Officially, we are supposed to keep quiet about their destination, to keep the transfers calm and orderly, but sometimes we get bored and let slip where we are going. It's the perfect excuse to break out the stun-guns!

1119681.text: We keep a reserve supply of Deuterium on board to fortify the Promethene in our heavy reactors. It gives us more power output when we need it, but it releases some quite nasty neutron radiation as a consequence. I learned about it at school, growing up on Planet Chateauroux. Being from a family of Deuterium miners teaches you a thing or two about it, non? I am the only one in my family to have joined the Royal Navy. It was an easy choice to make as I was fortunate enough to marry into a mid-ranked Naval family. I gained enough favor to be assigned to a quieter part of Gallia. It's not as cushy as being stationed in Ile-de-France, but I am not being shipped off to the front lines either!

1119682.text: Many of the tools and technologies that we developed for the battlefield have been converted for use domestically. Surveillance and attack drones are used to disrupt and quash anti-Crown protests and military tribunals have taken the place of civilian courts when dealing with crimes against the state. Naturally, we see these as positive developments to enhance the security of the people of Gallia.

1119683.text: I am shipping out for shore leave in the next few hours. Here on the Nogent-le-Rotroi it's quieter than it's been for generations. With the war getting under way I look forward to heading out to the Maine planets along with the other Spaceship Crew. I mean it's not as though we hunger for leave due to the combat hardship we experience. It's more just a way of staving off boredom for a few days. There is an ancient Sol saying "War is long periods of boredom, broken by short periods of terror" - truly wise words!

1119684.text: Lock and load! I always get excited every time we bring in a new shipment of Light Arms from Calais. My men and I are reduced to school children visiting the local candy store. As long as weapons discipline is maintained, I let the men enjoy themselves with their new toys. I feel it is also important that the men give their frank opinions on any new weapons being trialed. Our lives may depend on it one day.

1119685.text: The central duty of the King is to protect the national security of the Gallic citizenry. He is vested with vast powers to do so. We in the Royal Navy are His favorite tools to accomplish this.

1119686.text: Marines that are not ready to go to the front are shipped out here from Battleship Montreuil. A few months additional training and they will be ready to face battle in Sirius. Apart from general combat drill and marksmanship, we practice a lot of ship-boarding and zero-G combat. Until we are landing on Sirian planets, it's what the Marines will have to contend with for the most part.

1119687.text: Ahh, Promethene fuel fresh from Briancon Station ready to go straight into the engines of our ships. With a full load of Promethene, all we need is to top up our Oil reserves from Planet Mayenne, and we can keep ourselves running at full power as long as have to. I do hope our war planners have located Hydrocarbon supplies inside Sirius. I feel we shouldn't be relying on the home reserves of Oil for the entire duration of the war. Why not use the enemy's resources against them?

1119688.text: The Maquis carry no honor in life nor in death. They attack women, children, and civilians without remorse. We shall not rest until they are all brought to justice.

1119689.text: I just helped escort a fleet of transports into Maine. Surprisingly, this time there were no disruptions. I'm used to at least bumping into a gang of Brigands along the trip. But, you don't hear me complaining.

1119690.text: Last night I shot down seven Council fighters all in one night. Afterwards I celebrated with a refreshing victory Cigar. I can't wait to head out again for today's mission.

1119691.text: The Council should know better than to defy the will of the Crown. They are supposedly the intellectual ones, but it is clear now that they have neither the brains nor the numbers to topple the government.

1119692.text: This is the final stop for Prisoners heading to Fleury-Merogis Prison Station. They get one last chance to see the stars here, because they will never see the heavens again when they reach the end of the line. I think it would be more entertaining for public executions to be held for these creatures. It might put thoughts of rebellion out of the minds of many. Perhaps over time, the war with Sirius will harden people's hearts against the traitors of Gallia. Then we might see real justice awarded to them!

1119693.text: With little to do on this station, we have more time to try out the Light Arms that pass our way from Calais. After all, we have an obligation to ensure that equipment released into Maine is of the highest quality right? Controlling the border here also obliges us to check military convoys for contraband that criminal elements within the Royal Navy might be trying to pass. The GRN themselves are very clean, the Marines not so much. It will take time for the fresh Marine recruits to learn proper discipline, and cause us less trouble.

1119694.text: I've been chewing up those Brigand dogs since I was 19. They're wily pilots, but a little patience usually ends up being enough to pop one of them. The lucky ones die in the inferno. The others head to one of Gallia's many infamous prisons for years of 'enhanced punishments'.

1119695.text: The crew of the Nogent-le-Rotroi like to gloat about the Light Arms they get shipped out to them from Calais. What they don't know is that those shipments have to pass by us first. That means we get the first pick, not them! You won't find a single piece of weaponry on this station that malfunctions. And the gold-plated sidearm that was destined for the Captain of the Nogent? Now at the side of the Station Commander. Hey it's a tough job out here guarding the border to Ile-de-France. The Royal Family deserves nothing but the finest men and equipment guarding the seat of Gallic power.

1119696.text: Sure, this base doesn't really serve much use these days. The Normandy wars are long over, and all the action is headed towards Sirius.
