There is still one thing we try to keep on top of though - Artifacts. We still get smugglers trying to ship out Gallia's alien heritage through the quieter systems like Maine. When we find them we impound them immediately and send the ship's crew off for interrogation. If you ever come across unusual relics, alert the authorities straight away. And for God's sake don't touch them! They could be dangerous.

1119697.text: You mess with the King, and you'll feel the sting! Of my Musketoon that is, piercing through your hull. Many fools in the Council have learned this the hard way.

1119698.text: We like to ticket Gallic corporations, Brigands, Maquis, Junkers, but not the Corse. We find it's in our financial and safety interests to just let them go on with their business.

1119699.text: The poor saps in GMS always pout when we do a routine traffic stop. They complain that we are corrupt and abusing our powers. But if they don't want to be ticketed, then they shouldn't break so many traffic ordinances.

1119700.text: The most prestigious assignment for a Royal Policeman is to patrol the hexagon in Ile-De-France. Being stationed in Maine isn't too bad I guess. At least I'm not stuck out in the Border Worlds like my cousin. He can't wait to get transferred back to the Core Worlds.

1119701.text: One of the Brigands I stopped last week had a cargo hold full of Nox. He offered to give me a few samples if I let him off with a warning. After trying it, I find myself longing for another taste. I have a feeling I will be stopping that Brigand the next time he flies through Maine.

1119702.text: 'Bribe' is such a dirty word. We prefer to call them 'Mutual Understandings' or 'Gentleman's Agreements'. The fact is, we've all got our jobs to do. And as long as it's a victimless crime, who's to say we can't be paid to look the other way just this once?

1119703.text: Whenever we catch a Brigand cargo ship with a hull full of Slaves, they always try to deny it. The pilots will say they are just transporting Refugees or regular Passengers. That story falls apart once we notice the chains and restraints. It's funny how the Brigand pilot usually ends up living in similar conditions in prison as his victims.

1119704.text: A few fellow policemen and I had a skirmish with the Council a few weeks ago in this system. Those Councilmen really know how to fight, unlike the clumsy Brigands. Luckily we were able to call in some Royal Navy backup from Battleship Nogent-le-Retroi. Had it not been for the GRN, we probably wouldn't have made it back.

1119705.text: Most of the officers in the Royal Police have well-groomed moustaches. But this upper-lip excellence does not come cheap. That's why the Police created a Moustache Maintenance Fee to be paid by civilian transports when traveling through a police checkpoint. Some people think it's just some made-up way for us to get extra money, but that's ridiculous. Moustache wax doesn't grow on trees!

1119706.text: Sometimes the only thing that keeps me entertained on boring patrols is playing with my moustache. I can bristle it, twitch it, twirl it, comb it, and fluff it. But the one thing I'll never do is shave it!

1119707.text: You're going to want to stay away from the Sarthe cloud if possible. There's a lot of Brigand activity in there so there is likely a base. We haven't been able to scout around and find it yet because we keep getting ambushed by those bastards in the cloud.

1119708.text: The salaries for Royal Policewomen like me are quite miniscule. So to supplement our income and bring home a decent wage, we need to squeeze the Gallic citizens for any and all infractions. It's the logical result of years of department budget cuts. If people don't like it, they should petition the Crown to raise taxes.

1119709.text: The most interesting cases are stopping Brigand transports. You never know what they will be carrying but you know it's something illegal. Those fools are basically addicted to shipping contraband.

1119710.text: I am organizing shipments of Cryocubes out to Gap Station in the Languedoc system. Out there, we need to ensure we are totally self-sufficient in the event of terrorist attacks. Nobody wants a repeat of the battle that was needed to take the station from the Council. The civilian population relies on these Cryocubes to keep the station's cooling systems operating efficiently. We in the Police also use them to put certain types of confiscated evidence on ice. With the amount of traffic heading off-lane into Provence, we have our work cut out for us intercepting and processing the movement of illegal goods.

1119711.text: I just graduated from the academy so I'm new to the department. When I first started going out on patrols, I was struck by how much criminal activity goes on, even so close to Ile-De-France. The Gallic citizens have no idea how many thugs lurk in the dark shadows of space.

1119712.text: In what may be slightly counterintuitive, the Police hand out more tickets and fines to civilians and businessmen than to gangs and pirates. This is because the civilians are more easily stopped and always pay without putting up a fight. But the pirates really make us work for that money and it can be dangerous. Ask yourself, which group would you rather pursue?

1119713.text: I still run into Council ships sometimes while out on patrol in this system. I thought the Royal Navy had vanquished all of them from the Core Worlds. That's the trouble with revolutionary political factions like the Council: every time you kill one of them, two more are inspired to join up with the group. We need a game-changer in this conflict.

1119714.text: The department has noticed a significant up-tick in Slave shipments in this system. We know the Brigands are involved, but other groups are assisting them. What they are doing with all those poor people is still a mystery.

1119715.text: Most of the times, the Maquis don't like to play our game. I give them plenty of opportunities to buy their way out of trouble but they insist on the hostile approach. Once my backup arrives, the Maquis tend to regret their hard-line stance.

1119716.text: Our weekly Prisoner transport is departing for Fleury-Merogis shortly. I might go down to the dock and wave them adieu as they are taken on board. Everybody needs a good send-off. It isn't the sort of send-off I would like to give these scum, but unlike them we are merciful, and follow the laws set down for us by our betters.

1119717.text: Out here among the rearguard, we gain access to a reasonable selection of Light Arms, shipped in from Calais Research Facility. Special Ops and the Elite Guard of Ile-de-France get first pick of course - but we manage to get our hands on some pretty sweet hardware! Of course if you know the right people, or are prepared to put money into the right hands, then you can even pick up an item or two to take home. I have a nice collection going myself, and I plan on shipping some of them out to the front lines in exchange for some of the war booty they are bringing home.

1119718.text: The Chief has asked us to start cracking down on ships with lights that are more than 2 different colors. It seems kind of strange to me, but we're financially incentivized to enforce the ordinance so enforce it I shall.

1119719.text: My squad is scheduled for leave very soon. The Spaceship Crews heading to Planet Le Mans are looking forward to some time off. Some of them are natives, most are visitors keen to take in the sights. I am looking forward to fresh air and open skies. Some of my colleagues like to go hunting wildlife. I myself prefer to enjoy nature alive and unspoiled. I spend night and day in this artificial environment, and I want to get away from most anything related to other men when I go planet-side.

1119720.text: Our backup power plants run off Deuterium shipped in from Planet Chateauroux. Our orders are to run the reserve power supplies at least once a month. If we didn't, then we wouldn't be able to guarantee their successful operation in the event of an emergency. In the old days they never had to do this, as the Normandy War ensured that every day was an emergency! Now that things are quiet around here, surviving the endless days depends on routine, routine and more routine.

1119721.text: Whenever we encounter any type of political protesters, we are under orders from the Crown to "lawfully discourage" their activities. We know exactly how far we can go with violence and harassment without causing a major scandal. By now very few groups choose to protest the government because they know they don't stand a chance.

1119722.text: I am being shipped out along with a number of other Spaceship Crews down to Planet Mayenne. Some are going home on leave, but most of us will rotate from base patrol to escort duty for the Oil transports leaving the planet. It's certainly no holiday destination, not even for people looking for a frozen wonderland. The polar regions of Planet Le Mans are better suited for nature-lovers wanting that sort of thing.

1119723.text: Once we get a report of Council ships in a neutral area, we go out in strike teams to hit them before they can retreat back to the Mayenne Asteroid Field. If we're lucky we'll be able to take them down and capture the pilots. If we're unlucky, a bunch of their angry friends will show up.

1119724.text: The worst part of this job is writing up all the paperwork after ticketing or arresting someone. That's why I usually like to handle the infraction in space more, uh, informally. It's much cleaner and easier for everyone and it can stay off the books.

1119725.text: Le Mans is the main production center in this system. The bulk of raw materials gets shipped here for processing. One of the less exotic commodities produced here is Oil, used in a lot of industrial and construction activities. We ship it to industrial bases like Metz, and shipyards like Fourchambault.

1119726.text: Le Mans, much like any inhabited world in the Core Systems, is one of our primary destinations. We have our intra-system routes, with the usual needs of artificial habitats - Water, Oxygen, Food. All space stations need these to some degree or another, especially the ones without biodomes. Those are quick and easy routes, which new pilots often take advantage of.

1119727.text: IDF Shipping has been around for hundreds of years, but we're still young by Gallic corporation standards. GMS was established more than 100 years before us. As for EFL, they're practically as old as Gallic civilization itself. We're trying to catch up to the others' size and strength by focusing on winning government contracts.

1119728.text: Ah, yes. Cryocubes, why else would I be here in this frozen wasteland? Feels like we're shipping part of the planet's spirit away, or so the bartender over there claims. I for one can't wait to leave again. Once my hold is loaded with Cryocubes, I'll be heading for Metz Station in Lorraine.

1119729.text: Cryocubes, cryocubes, cryocubes. Couldn't they make them in a warmer place? No, I suppose not. And if they weren't in demand in so many places, I can tell you, I wouldn't be here.

1119730.text: The only run I actually like to make out of this place, is the one to Chateau Salins. Yes, a Space Colony. Why? Because they also import the finest selection of Wines there, and a cousin of mine is the local quartermaster. Ach, who am I kidding...I wish the docking crew could finish loading those Cryocubes a little faster. This cold is unbearable.

1119731.text: Ah, yes. EFL does produce the finest Polymer products in Gallia, and they are used throughout our worlds. I've just delivered a shipment here from Montlucon Staton. Located outside of the core worlds, closer to the raw materials, they can produce the goods more cheaply - but at the same time, there's more trouble. The Maquis will frequently hit the lanes in Auvergne and the Brigands in Orleanais. Still, it's a very profitable run.

1119732.text: I can't wait to get off of this stinking shipyard and back to my shipping run. I'm grounded here thanks to a pack of Brigands circling the system looking for easy loot. We've called in help from Ile-De-France but it takes some time for them to respond. Until then I just have to sit here and wait while IDF loses money.

1119733.text: I attended one of the most prestigious universities on New Paris but when I graduated, I couldn't get a decent planet-side job. It seems the only way to having a successful career in Gallia is to be well-connected with government or military officials or launch to space to make your living. I fear Gallic society can only take so much of this before serious unrest comes to the Core systems. As you know, it has already started in the Border Worlds.

1119734.text: I am taking software from this base that cannot be safely transported otherwise to Metz Station. The Royalists call it Counterfeit Software, but I call it money and dead Royals. Nice combination don't you think?

1119735.text: My brother Jerome is a Council pilot. While he doesn't always agree with my methods of achieving liberation, he has a lot of respect for me and won't hesitate to engage Royal forces alongside me.

1119736.text: I just love hunting down Oil shipments. If we get the cargo, the Maquis get the benefit of lots of fuel, necessary for our next fight. If we miss and the cargo explodes, the flames are magnificent. It's a win-win situation for me.

1119737.text: No, I don't live on the planet myself. I'm just here while the cargo handlers cram the hold of my ship with Oil. Then I'll head back to Alesia Station. High tech industries still need the most basic of materials, after all.

1119738.text: I sometimes make the run from Battleship Castres, when reports suggest the Brigands are laying low. Bringing in a full hold of Gold from the raiders on the battleship is very profitable, but the civilians of Le Mans aren't the only ones who have an interest in Gold. I usually call for an extra escort when we make that run.

1119739.text: Solar Engineering was proud to bring high tech industry to Le Mans. This planet has a storied history and its economic revival over the last few hundred years is quite inspiring. Once people get used to the cold weather, they tend to really like it here.

1119740.text: I do not like coming here. Too cold for my tastes. The running joke is that they make the Cryocubes here with pieces of the planet - because this planet is -always- cold. They're also the only reason I'm out here.

1119741.text: We ship Cryocubes from this planet to Montlucon and Clermont, depending on which colony has a need for those shipments. They are used in all sorts of industrial ventures, from Consumer Goods to military grade weapon coolers. Our colonies prefer not to produce military goods however. It would give the Maquis and Council a reason to start targeting them.

1119742.text: Yes, it's true that the Council have taken posession of an old base in the asteroid field north of the planet. Everyone knows it, but there's just not much anyone can do about it. The military can't send their heavy ships into the asteroid field, the asteroids would chew them up before they'd reach their target. So they just patrol the perimiter and keep the Council ships bottled up there. Maine is safe enough for us civilians, they see to that.

1119743.text: The women on Planet New Paris have to be the most beautiful in the entire galaxy. There must be something in the water over there that breeds strikingly gorgeous ladies. I hope to find a wife on New Paris one day.

1119744.text: Some of the cargo that comes in to Gallia from Kusari is quite impressive. I think the Gallic people initially underestimated the technological abilities of the Sirians. They may not be as weak as we originally thought.

1119745.text: Police patrols have increased in this system due to a bunch of recent Brigand attacks. But even with the extra security, if you stray from the Trade Lanes and well-defended bases, you're on your own.

1119746.text: I'll soon be heading back to Luxury Liner Antibes, with a hold full of the finest Holotainment Bands available in all of Gallia. I'm sure we'll have Brigands on the scope at some point or another. But Brigands or not, all of Gallia deserves to relax with a Solar Holotainment Band. For a fair price of course.

1119747.text: Mortagne has, despite the war, never been busier. The Holotainment industry is booming, and now we have a whole new market to supply. The Sirian market. But we do have trouble getting the goods out there, so some of our distant deliveries focus on diversions for the Royal Navy crews. The Gallic Navy has given us permission to deliver Holotainment Bands at one of their battleships, the Carcassonne, where they are available for even deck hands. Well, that's the official story, anyway. I suspect most of these end up in the officers' quarters.

1119748.text: No matter what their political leanings, everyone I know respects the integrity and professionalism of the Royal Navy. Those honorable men and women are simply incorruptible. I think the Royal Navy is probably the most trusted institution in all of Gallia.

1119749.text: While this facility produces mainly civilian goods, that does not mean we do not support the war. No, the finest Holotainment Band programs are created here for those brave men fighting at the front. To give them a taste of home, away from home. We rarely run the shipments ourselves, but when we do, they often go to Battleship Villeneuve, over in one of the seized systems.

1119750.text: Holotainment Bands are in strong demand with our rich and famous. Virtually every Resort Planet, and luxury Liner in Gallia is always in short supply of these. We encourage independent traders to deliver these goods there - you wouldn't happen to have a transport yourself, yes?

1119751.text: When I'm not at the bar, I work security for Solar Engineering. Nobody gets past me without the proper security clearances. No exceptions. Our research is simply too valuable.

1119752.text: The Sirian house Kusari is a new market for us, and a good one at it. Their elite has barely even heard of Holotainment Bands, so getting them familiar with this Gallic pleasure, for a price, has been quite profitable. We're selling them directly to the markets at New Tokyo. Of course, getting there is another matter, but the reward is high enough that many risk it.

1119753.text: Cargo bay 15 is off limits to anyone without proper clearance. I don't have clearance myself, so I don't know what goes on in there. What I do know is this. We produce a lot of Holotainment bands, and not much else at this facility. Sometimes the sections around 15 are sealed off. Hours later, a transport leaves, usually heading for one of the Royal Residences. You do the math - I bet His Grace likes our "private" collection of holo art just as much as the next man.

1119754.text: We've been pushing ourselves really hard over the past few weeks on a major project for the government. I can't tell you what it is, though. All I can tell you is that I really need a Cigar break.

1119755.text: Oh, don't mind me. I'm just here to drop off a scheduled shipment from Compiegne. Nanotubes, which are then used throughout ships' systems. There's few ships in Gallia that don't have a bit of Solar technology in them. From the lowest shuttle to the largest battleships, the most advanced parts of the ships are always from our factories.

1119756.text: On occasion I make the run from Saint-Exupery to this shipyard. I carry Lasers then, which are used in the ship's targeting and navigational systems. Solar's latest versions are even being incorporated into engines, to monitor pressure and temperature levels.

1119757.text: Our company was founded by some economists and investors from New Paris, so we at Solar know a thing or two about getting a good return on our investment. We are selective on the station properties that we purchase because we're always seeking high profit margins. So far we've been very successful in the station operation field.

1119770.text: Kusari State Police\nAsahikawa Commodity Trader\nKawaji Nagami

1119771.text: Kusari State Police\nAsahikawa Equipment Dealer\nWakagi Tsuyuki

1119772.text: Kusari State Police\nAsahikawa Ship Dealer\nTaizen Kusama

1119807.text: Being a Brigand does not necessarily mean you are a pirate. For example I mostly deal with transporting goods. I have quite a nice, profitable route. I take Gallic Artifacts to Frejus Base.

1119808.text: The planet of Marne is important to us. Its large population gets us many new recruits, and the factories help us with much needed supplies and arms.

1119809.text: While we try to not actively fight the Royal forces because of the great danger in doing so, sometimes we have to do so. For example we had to help the Council in the Languedoc system, while we covered the flight of civilians and VIPs. Many Council and Brigands members were killed in the process.

1119810.text: Brigands almost never get involved in political conflicts, like the one between the Council and the Crown, but we did indirectly help the Council in the Second Gallic Civil War.

1119811.text: Many of the members of the Free Brigands of Gallia are experienced criminals that used to be Police officers in their past. They simply came to understood that a Brigand's life is much better!

1119812.text: When fighting Royal forces, try to avoid killing the pilot. Even though the Goverment doesn't really care about them and won't pay much, they're still worth more alive.

1119813.text: Let me tell you a secret. In this base we collect Gallic Artifacts. While we have nothing to do with these around here, we ship them to other bases such as Joinville to be sold to the locals or transported outside of Gallia to some wealthy collectors in Sirius.

1119814.text: Even though we Brigands promote the image that we rob the rich and give to the poor, it's almost never true. The large rich corporations often have heavy protection around them, unlike the poorly defended smaller companies.

1119815.text: The loss of Quillan to the Royal forces was a tough blow to our forces, even though it belonged to The Council. It was a good source of recruits and supplies, now we are more heaviliy dependent on Marne.

1119816.text: While it is not openly discussed, quietly many of us Council pilots support the Maquis. They've done us enough favours in the past. The Council has to officially distance itself from the Maquis' tactics, but that doesn't mean we'll allow the Royal forces to kill them with impunity. We're all fighting for the same thing, even if we go about it differently.

1119817.text: I came to this base as part of a supply convoy. We will be returning to Planet Toulouse with Refugees who wish to escape the fighting and start a new life outside of Gallia. It's going to be a hard life there, but we're up to the challenge and freedom is its own reward.

1119818.text: I will not stop fighting. None of us ever will, not until the King has paid for his crimes against our people and the powers in Gallia have become accountable to the people.

1119819.text: I see the local jewelers are making arrangements for another shipment of Pearls to be sent off to Luxury Liner Belleville. I wish I could go with them because I am overdue for a vacation. With the war getting underway all leave in my section has been cancelled indefinitely. How long does management expect us to keep working under these conditions? I expect to see people resigning by year's end - if they don't go crazy first.

1119820.text: We bring in Petrochemicals from Beauvais Facility over in Il-de-France. Personally, I wouldn't say that Beauvais has the best quality product out there. I blame the Junkers cutting corners. There are a wide variety of Petrochemicals that industry needs. Many of them require precise control over temperature, pressure and the concentration of ingredients. Any slip-ups and you start getting fatty acids or wax, instead of solvents. You know how many container valves have been jammed with waxy crud every month? I think the Junkers deliberately contaminate our supplies, as the cleanup of their mess puts us behind schedule - and makes them look good!

1119821.text: Ever since the Marne Rebellion, Planet Bourges has seen a boom of economic development. This had to replace the production lost from Planet Marne, I guess that's why I'm here. So far I like it, though I'm still trying to get used to all the earth tremors.

1119822.text: The supply lines for the war in Sirius are very long. I am responsible for sending supplies of Deuterium out to the Royal Navy's forward supply points. These are mainly our battleships, like the La Riche over in Brittany, or the Guillestre in Tau-23. It would be nice to find a source of Deuterium in Sirius itself, but the intel we have suggests the major sources are within reach of our enemies in Bretonia and Liberty. I don't like the idea of our Navy's backup fuel supply subject to the same risks as the Oil shipments have, but we have no choice but to push forward.

1119823.text: We supply Deuterium to all of Gallia from here. It's no substitute for Oil or Promethene, but it does have certain uses that make it a viable product line.

1119824.text: These lazy GMS folks don't even know the meaning of a hard day's work. They usually clock out and head to the bar before the sun even goes down. No wonder they're always late filling our orders.

1119825.text: Any excess Promethene fuel we have here is immediately sold off to Riom Shipyard. The Navy needs ships prepped and fueled as fast as possible. We work around the clock to recycle our fuel catalyst from ships coming in for repairs. Whilst those ships are in drydock we can get fresh tanks of Promethene ready for use somewhere else.

1119826.text: We ship in Oil here, by the kiloton. Pumped straight out of the ground in Maine, refined and loaded up by us. Gallia feeds on Oil, and her appetite is rapacious! Gallia's appetite for Oil is matched only by the hunger for war. Sirius is about to reap the whirlwind for centuries of vengeance festering in our hearts.

1119827.text: With the war going on, we're really pumping out a lot of new ships here. The demand has created many job opportunities. It's amazing how fast the population on this station is growing. Sometimes I wonder if Planet Bourges has any more people left on it.

1119828.text: Surplus Copper dug up in the Maine system finds its way onto the Chateau-Gautier Freeport. We get orders to ship the metal across Gallia to places with high demand like Planet Bourges. While the war is making it hard to get hold of some commodities, it's making it easier to cut deals with the corporations. Even a few years ago they wouldn't have let me set foot on some of their bases. With the massive demand for commodities, and the people to move them, they have little choice but to accomodate us.

1119829.text: We're starting to see some contraband in Gallia that we've never had contact with before. There's some new drug the kids call "Cardi" that seems to be all the rage these days. I've heard it's terribly addictive and destructive to the body. All signs point to Sirius as the source for this poison. If it sells like some of my collegues claim it does, I want to get my hands on some.

1119830.text: You would think that the military success of the Royal Navy would make things better for us back here in Gallia, but that's not what has been happening. It seems like prices of everything are going up. More and more resources, both financial and human, are going towards the war effort. This isn't at all like the government said it would be.

1119831.text: There is planty of Deuterium in the oceans here. Makes for an easy run to Beaumont, our base in Il-de-France. We like to keep a stockpile of it to make heavy water for the old backup reactors we have there. That way we never have to fear EFL threatening to cut off our fuel supply to the station. It always pays to have an insurance policy in our line of work.

1119832.text: I am taking a load of Deuterium out to Lodeve, in the Languedoc system. Out there it's all business with the war effort going on. We can't always be guaranteed an Oil supply, so we need to run Deuterium as a backup. You have to learn pretty quickly to be self-sufficient when you are a Junker.

1119833.text: I'm scared to go out on another shipping run. My last trip was ended by a Maquis ambush. I was barely able to thrust to the safety of this station. I dropped off my ship in the hangar and the mechanic immediately labeled it 'scrap'. I just know they are out there, still watching and waiting for me.

1119834.text: While Senonches Mining Facility produces Copper much more cheaply than we can mine it here, there is a modest mining operation on Bourges that supplies nearby markets. We even manage to schedule some shipments to Riom Shipyard in Auvergne, since the price there is so high.

1119835.text: The constant earthquakes on Bourges create difficult circumstances for industry and building construction. Because it's so light weight, Aluminium is very important as a building material, although we have use it in alloys to bolster its strength. Our local sources can't keep up with the demand, so we import Aluminium from Guise Mining Facility on a regular basis.

1119836.text: Let IDF Shipping have their sweet connections to the Crown. We prefer the independence. Sure, IDF may get access and more government contracts, but they sacrifice control over their own affairs. I can see that getting very irritating, very quickly.

1119837.text: I just returned from delivering Deuterium to Battleship Arles in the Provence system. The battleship itself rarely uses it for fuel, but they keep it stocked as a backup if a passing civilian ship needs fuel. I think some of the Navy's scout craft may use it during long patrols.

1119838.text: Planet Bourges' small Copper mining operation can't keep up with our demand here, so we have to import it from Senonches Mining Facility in Maine if we want to stay on our production schedule.

1119839.text: It's hard to believe that Gallic Metal Service is several hundred years old. We've been around even longer than IDF Shipping! As they always say, the first hundred years are always the hardest. I can't imagine this company every folding. As long as there are rocks out there, GMS will be around to harvest their valuable contents.

1119840.text: We owe much to the Royal Navy. Numerous attacks by the Maquis on our bases have been foiled by those brave men and women. If not for the GRN, I fear GMS would have no more than 25% of our current stations still intact.

1119841.text: Even after all these years, I'm still not sure what to make of those Junkers. They are mysterious folks that seem like just a bunch of simple merchants. But my guess is they have some other, more sinister plot that they're working on.

1119842.text: It's hard to imagine what would happen if the Council actually did succeed in their revolution. After hundreds of years of rule by monarchy, I can't even fathom Gallic society without the King in charge. If it were just a rebellion led by the Council, I would say it was hopeless. But with the Council's growing alliance with the Sirians, I'd say anything is possible now.

1119843.text: Roanne Production Facility in Lorraine is our top priority for Beryllium deliveries.

1119844.text: The industry in the Croix-Rousse region of Planet Metz has been consuming a lot of Beryllium during the past few years.

1119845.text: I just got back from a Beryllium mining operation in the Aubigny field. Everything was going well until a couple Brigands showed up. Their combat skills weren't very impressive so our escorts could handle them. We still were forced to cancel the operation and head back to base without our work being complete. Now I'm stuck on this station until the mining coordinator gives us the blue light to head back out there. There's nothing to do now but drink and wait.

1119846.text: All the GMS transport pilots fight to get the run to Mortagne Production Facility in the Maine system. As a bonus for on time delivery, Solar Engineering gives each of the crew a complimentary holoscenario for their Holotainment Band. There's a Beryllium shipment coming up, and I intend to be its pilot.

1119847.text: Looks like I'm out of luck. I was assigned a Beryllium delivery to Planet Le Mans in the Maine system instead of the run to Mortagne. Oh well, maybe there will be time to swing by Mortagne and upgrade my holosoftware in person.

1119848.text: The mining operations have been going well, perhaps too well. Our storage bays are stuffed full of Beryllium. If you have a decent sized cargo hold and some cash, head on down to the commodity vendor and pick yourself up a load. You can ask around this bar for ideas on where to ship it.

1119849.text: Abbeville Production Facility in the Picardy system uses Beryllium in Superconductor production, so they are scheduled for regular shipments. I wish someplace like Marseille started using Beryllium, I could use a chang of scenery.

1119850.text: I'm transporting a shipment of Beryllium to Planet Mayenne sometime soon. I don't think they use it themselves, but they stockpile it so there is some locally on hand if Mortagne Production needs larger amounts on short notice.

1119851.text: We see the Council as our Gallic brothers, not as enemies like the Crown does. We cannot bring ourselves to fire on the Councilmen, nor snitch on their whereabouts. If the Royal forces need help eliminating the Council, they will have to look to others for assistance.

1119852.text: The High Temperature Alloys we deliver here from Alesia Station are used mainly to refurbish ships' engines. We do build some new engines here as well, though.

1119853.text: The greatest need here at Fourchambault is for Superalloys from Roanne Production Facility in Lorraine. Massive amounts of Superalloys are necessary to build modern Trains and Liners. Since the beginning of the war, we have to fight a bureaucratic battle constantly with the GRN over allocation of resources. EFL is willing to pay for priority shipments.

1119854.text: If that EFL fellow over there extends his hand, don't shake it. I once saw him in the lavatory and he left without washing his hands. It's disgusting, I know, but not surprising for someone working for EFL. That was probably the cleanest his hands were all day.

1119855.text: IDF Shipping prefers not to haul the 'dirtier payloads' like ores and minerals. They like to stick to upscale freight like Holotainment Bands, Cigars, and Wine to name a few. Those fancy-boys can't handle getting their hands dirty. That's fine with us though. It's more money for GMS shippers.

1119856.text: When passing a wing of Council fighters in the Border Worlds, It seems I tend to 'accidentally' jettison some Food Rations or consumables out of my cargo hold. Somehow it seems to happen almost every time. Ain't it just the darndest thing?

1119857.text: Our multi-decade war against the rocks is not going well. We've been blasting rocks for dozens of years now, but each large rock we shoot is instantly replaced by several smaller, faster rocks in its place. It seems there's just no way to vanquish this treacherous foe.

1119858.text: As valuable as it is, Platinum is used in miniscule amounts in high explosive Munitions manufactured on Planet Amiens.

1119859.text: Alesia Station is like heaven for metals. There they are refined, combined, and enabled to reach a degree of purity and usefulness that is possible nowhere else. Even Platinum becomes more valuable in the refining fires of Alesia.

1119860.text: Any young, talented Brigand pilot is quickly recruited into the Unione Corse. Ship for ship, the fighter wings that the Corse have mustered are the most fearsome in Gallia. Our GMS escorts are useless against them. Meek submission is our only defense against the Corse.

1119861.text: Solar Engineering uses Platinum in Superconductor production at the Abbeville Facility in the Picardy system.

1119862.text: Platinum is essential to the high quality Nanocapacitors produced by Solar Engineering at Compiegne Space Colony.

1119863.text: We in GMS do our best to stay out of the war Gallic civil war between the Royalists and the Council. We see them both as fellow Gallic citizens representing mere political differences. It's such a shame that the Royal Navy devotes so many lives and resources toward shedding fellow Gallic blood when there are more sinister enemies lurking just beyond Gallic borders.

1119864.text: I overheard someone claim that a Holotainment Band was worth its weight in gold to a miner out in a deep space asteroid field for days at a time. He should have said worth its weight in Platinum, because that's what actually goes into the finished product. I'm due to transport a load to Mortagne Production in the Maine system just as soon as I finish my drink.

1119865.text: GMS stockpiles Platinum on Planets Le Mans and Mayenne in the Maine system. It's easier to protect stockpiles from criminals if they are on planets.

1119866.text: If you're jetting out of here with a cargo bay full of Platinum, watch your scanners for Maquis. They won't hesitate to blast your hull and spill your bays into space. The value of your cargo's contents means nothing to them. They are motivated only by bloodshed and explosions.

1119867.text: The Council claims they are saints, fighting for the Gallic nation and democracy, but they don't mention all their wrong-doings. I guess they never mentioned the Gap incident when capital ships' captains of the Council ordered their gunners to fire on a civilian base, killing civilian onboard did they?

1119868.text: The Council claims to help everyone by protecting the residents of Sirius. They forget that the very same people stabbed the Gallic nation in its back, leaving it to perish in Sol. I am not willing to take the risk of letting them do the same while I am fit to do my duty.

1119869.text: The Council will tell you lies that we are killing our own citizens and army personnell. Well, if that would actually happen we wouldn't have the strongest and largest army mankind has ever seen, would we?

1119870.text: Issoudun is the beating heart of Gallia's strategic war planning. If we deem that certain Prisoners might have war intelligence to offer, they are interrogated here first. Provided their intel is not too sensitive, they are allowed to live out their pathetic days on Fleury-Merogis Prison Station. If the intel is too sensitive, well, we have lives to preserve out on the front lines. The life of a potential spy is always forfeit, when weighed against the lives of our fighting men.

1119871.text: If I was the King I would order to kill each and every Unione Corse member out there. They are wolves in sheep's clothes, and they won't hesitate to attack an unsuspecting civilian transport that is carrying cargo that they need or can make a profit with.

1119872.text: We let some of Sirius' traders in our house. Not the treacherous ones, mind you, but those who belong to Houses that have demonstrated their honorable nature.

1119873.text: After evaluation here on Issoudun, we pass on shipments of Light Arms to Battleship Le Cendre. The regular pirate activity in the borderworlds demands the formation of a good many counter-terrorist squads. This means ship-boarding action, as well as raids conducted planet side. We ensure our men are given only the finest quality weapons for their kit. We cannot afford a misfire when civilan lives are at stake.

1119874.text: If we were to find any trader supplying Council bases we would kill him and show off his body to everyone so they could see. Being greedy and supplying traitors is worse than being a simple traitor.

1119875.text: I can't think of any reason to let Junkers roam our space. While they are civilians and haven proven helpful, they often get their cargo from illegal sources and thus assist the enemies of the crown.

1119876.text: Our evaluation teams perfom a secondary analysis of the Light Arms produced at Calais Research Facility. This is the last stop before a weapon is deployed in the field. Light Arms have to perform to the standards we set. After all, we are the people who gather and process the field intelligence coming in from Sirius. Only we know the sorts of conditions the weapons will face, as well as the requirements of our men. Yes it can take longer for field deployment with the extra layer of bureaucracy, but it's worth it in the long run.

1119877.text: One of the most dangerous groups out there in Sirius is a group known as "Outcasts". They have a very dangerous drug they are using to poison the Gallic civilian population with, and are attacking our fighters at the front.

1119878.text: The reason we have such a great urge to attack Bretonia and Liberty is because they abandoned the Gallic nation to die many centuries ago. They will finally pay for their betrayal!

1119879.text: While Kusari and Rheinland are not the main culprits behind the betrayal of our ancestors, I think they bear some of the blame too. After all, they have benefited from that betrayal, and they should repay us for our suffering if they have any real honor.

1119880.text: I don't understand all of the poor in Gallia who say the Crown is doing nothing to help them. The Crown is helping those who do their duty. I was born to a poor family consisting of five children. All of us joined the Royal Navy or the Royal Police, and you can no longer say our family is poor.

1119881.text: The Council is trying to poison the poor civilians of Gallia with democratic ideas and and slanders against the King. They are not any better than the former Alliance houses that stabbed Gallia in the back. In fact, they are even worse!

1119882.text: Ever heard of the group called Corsairs? They claim that the other Houses have betrayed them. Now, this story is starting to repeat itself over and over, you simply can't trust the houses of Sirius.

1119883.text: We don't have a lot of Council and Maquis prisoners in our prison stations for a simple reason: we kill most of them in battle rather than capturing them. They don't deserve to live anywhere, including a prison station.

1119884.text: I despise the Council's methods. They poison young people's minds and send them to fight us and die. I truly am sorry when I am forced to kill teenagers who have no idea of what they are really doing.

1119885.text: I am fighting in the Champagne front for the King. My fellow pilots say that my habit of smoking cigars will one day kill me, but there are far greater chances that I will die in combat than from smoking.

1119886.text: In order to ship Prometheum you need a lot security. The King said it must not be exported out of Gallia or end up in unlawful hands. If you don't have enough escorts to ensure that the Prometheum won't end up in the wrong hands, you should contact the Royal Navy contribute to their fund for war orphans in exchange for escort.

1119887.text: The King allows some of the shipping companies and individuals to bring their trade into Gallia. I personally follow them and make sure that their cargo ends up in our hands rather than the Council's or any other Gallic unlawful. I am not going to get back-stabbed twice by them.

1119888.text: I heard rumors about the presence of Alien species in Sirius. This might explain the weird phenomena that can be found across Gallia and have no chance to be the hand of nature. For example take the Privas planetary structure, there is no way this thing is naturally made!

1119889.text: At unpredictable times, you can find yourself interviewed by the Navy's internal security force to find out if you are a traitor. While it's a great annoyance, it is very much necessary. After all, nearly all of the Council pilots and fighters are Gallic Royal Navy defecters.

1119890.text: When I get to come across a Unione Corse pilot in space, and he is not one of the families that are known to be supporting the Crown I will shoot him down. One less potential criminal for the future. It's his problem that he chose the way of the Corse rather than the King's forces.

1119891.text: Have you heard of the journalist murders that happened a few years back? That is what happens to people that stick their nose into others' business. You should be smarter than them.

1119892.text: Those Maquis are dangerous, but you cannot ignore that they plan their strikes well. They attack different parts of a system at the same time, making it nearly impossible to do something about their strikes. Even if we are lucky and catch some they never give us the required information.

1119893.text: You have to be careful while flying close to the Cher Ice Asteroid Field, the Maquis attack our patrols in this area frequently. I would even suggest that you generally avoid this place if you want to stay alive.

1119894.text: Corruption is a big problem within the Royal Police, many officers gladly accept bribes in order to have a bit more cash at the end of the month. Sadly, the civilians tend to generalize things like this and ignore the honest officers' good work.

1119895.text: The most successful NOX smugglers know how to avoid our patrols. Some of our own people must sell information about the patrols to them.

1119896.text: If you want to see some Brigands in action you should visit the Indre Asteroid Field. They seem to like this place a lot, most of the traffic coming close to this place, however, does disappear.

1119897.text: What a great job, I risk my life nearly every day and even the pirates I am supposed to fight have more money than me. Maybe it's time to find better employment.

1119898.text: We are under orders to ignore the Unione Corse until we have proof of them doing something illegal. I really wonder who tries to protect them. They are hardly anything close to innocent in my opinion.

1119899.text: We usually send out three patrols a day, that allows us to cover all of the system's shipping activities. However, if our people run into real trouble we sometimes have to hope for the Royal Navy being close.

1119900.text: I had quite a stressful patrol today. At first everything looked good but after the halfway point we ran into some Brigands. Fortunately we were able to fight them off. I am sure the IDF captain was glad to see us out there.

1119901.text: I am supposed to spend two more years out in the field, then I will have a desk job waiting for me. Finally a calm place and no more unnecessary risks for an underpaid job.

1119902.text: A few Police officers from here defected to the Council shortly after the war started. I can not understand how they could betray the kingdom like this.

1119903.text: We don't stray far away from the lanes in most cases. They simply don't pay enough to make us risk our lives like this. Some of the young officers fresh from the academies, however, seem to search out the thrill of following criminals even deep into the asteroid fields. They mostly don't return from their adventures.

1119904.text: This system has rich resources. Since the beginning of the war many new jobs were created. Economic booms always attract people that want to profit from them, most with work, some others choose a criminal approach. Those people secure our jobs.

1119905.text: A prison convoy for Fleury-Merogis was destroyed by the Maquis a month ago. We suspect that one of the prisoners was one of them who knew things that could have been dangerous for their operations. We had to double the protection for those convoys due to this incident.

1119906.text: We have noticed increasing criminal activity in this system lately. Many of us regular patrolmen think there are criminal bases located here in the core systems, despite what the official line is.

1119907.text: I was stationed at New Paris before, then they sent me here. The Capital is far more exciting than this place and the food was certainly better.

1119908.text: I can't wait for the next patrol. I need to get out into space again. Chateauroux is one of the most boring places I can imagine.

1119909.text: The IDF will do all in its power to make sure that the Royal forces have everything they need. This is how it goes when a large part of the company is owned by the Royal family itself.

1119910.text: I had some sympathy for the Council's goals when they first rebelled. But now, after I can see their true face of supporters of murder and piracy, my only hope is that they are crushed by the Navy.

1119911.text: Flying in the borderworlds, most pilots see the danger as their last moments alive, but I see it as an adventure - supplying our brave soldiers while facing the hazards of pirates, terrorists, and hostile militaries!

1119912.text: Of all the luxuries that the rich and Royalty afford themselves I can only think of one I adore - Wine! The taste is wonderful, and it only improves with age!

1119913.text: I am less scared of the Gallic Brigands than of most other pirates. Sometimes they simply choose not to shoot us, I certainly think that they are getting the occasional payment to turn a blind eye.

1119914.text: When you see a Maquis patrol coming at you, you better start praying or calling Royal forces. I heard that the Maquis became so good at murder that they managed to destroy a convoy before the Royal forces that were nearby even got there. The Maquis patrol managed to evade them too!

1119915.text: You can never feel safe in Council controlled areas. If you are not directly aiding them, any pirate or Maquis in the area might attack you. And the Council's response is complete ignorance and indifference.

1119916.text: I don't understand why the Council and their supporters have problems with the Royals. The King only brought us glory - look how big, mighty and powerful Gallia is!

1119917.text: All of the poor that claim that their state is the fault of the Royals are simply lazy. Look at me, I was born to a poor family and now I am a well-off, with three children, two of which are going to the Royal Military academy, and one is working hard in EFL.

1119918.text: Here in the Maquis, we have two kinds of members. The majority of us are ex-soldiers, many of whom have lost everything they care about. The latter are hardened criminals and anarchists, who are quite happy to burn Royalists and fill their own pockets at the same time.

1119919.text: The Maquis and the Council fight their battles very differently. While the Council has to maintain an image of benevolent freedom fighters, we of the Maquis will do whatever is necessary to see the Royalists crumble, even if that means hitting civilian targets.

1119920.text: Our preferred tactical approach to combat is guerilla warfare. We pick our targets, infiltrate, eliminate, and leave. The Maquis is much smaller than the Council, so we don't have room for heroic self-sacrifice.

1119921.text: The Maquis are not as structured as the Council. We have much more freedom to operate individually. However, at each of our bases there is always a group of senior members who have earned the respect of their compatriots, and they determine how and where we fight.

1119922.text: You see this? It's a knife. I like sharp knives. The only thing I like more is plunging them into the soft flesh of Royalists. Unfortunately, due to the nature of this war, I have to make do with an Agama instead. Most of the time.

1119923.text: The Council is too soft, in my opinion. They take little action against the very corporations which feed the Royalist war machine!

1119924.text: I've killed my fair share of Royalists. Everyone here has blood on their hands, and we're not ashamed. I lost track after a hundred, and that doesn't count collateral damage.

1119925.text: Oil, such a wonderful thing to explode. The flames are just like in the liberation-day fireworks on Planet Marne.

1119926.text: Allied transports ship us vital supplies such as Black Market Munitions from the Council's base on Planet Toulouse, back in Sirian space.

1119927.text: Nothing satifies me better than a great, big, fiery explosion. Last week one of my torpedoes penetrated the drive core of an IDF transport...the catastrophic damage was a glorious sight to behold.

1119928.text: The Council and the Maquis are really just two sides of the same coin. While we all want freedom from the Crown, we have very different methods that we use.

1119929.text: We have a symbiotic relationship with the Council. In exchange for doing the dirty work that would otherwise tarnish their reputation, the Council supplies us with a lot of the equipment we need.

1119930.text: Believe it or not, Solar actually pays bonuses at Mortagne Production Facility in Pearls instead of credits. Rumor has it that some Solar major stockholder won a gambling bet with a GMS stockholder, and the result is that Solar now owns rights to a certain amount of Pearls on an annual basis for the next ten years.

1119931.text: We stockpile Superconductors from Abbeville Production Facility here on Bourges so that La Charite can make more efficient use of space. Whenever they are running low, we can just transport them up to the station. The important thing is that the Robotics production line never stops for lack of materials.

1119932.text: Our Robotics are top of the line in Gallia. Our surveys have shown that integrating a robotic work-force into the manufacturing process cuts up to 40% of the production cost. That's pure profit that our clients can enjoy. If you were a plant manager, you'd be crazy not to bring in some robots!

1119933.text: We stockpile Nanocapacitors from Compiegne Space Colony here on Planet Chateauroux so that La Charite can make more efficient use of space. Whenever they are running low, we can just transport them up to the station. The important thing is that the Robotics production line never stops for lack of materials.

1119934.text: There isn't a tremendous amount of high tech industry here on Chateauroux, but our Deuterium harvesters use Superconductors from Abbeville Production in order to operate in the field for extended periods of time. Solar's product greatly decreases energy loss due to friction, and that translates into greater efficiency.

1119935.text: We're always looking for new applications for our Robotics. A colleague recently suggested that shipping companies could use Robots to fly transport ships on some of the shorter runs between the Core Worlds. A nearby transport pilot balked at the idea. But deep down, he knows it's only a matter of time before his job is made obsolete by technology.

1119936.text: Can you believe it? Some Gallic citizens get angry at us for building all these robots. They say the robots take their jobs. Well, I say if these 'hard working people' weren't so lazy with their bathroom, lunch, and cigarette breaks, maybe they could compete better against the robots and win their jobs back.

1119937.text: IDF Shipping would be a tiny planetary transport operation right now if it weren't for their coziness with the Crown. Once they sold their souls and started getting all those government shipping contracts, their business grew ten-fold in a matter of months. I guess it shows you the power of the Crown to pick winners and losers in the Gallic economy.

1119938.text: We're all still waiting to see what Solar Engineering's role will be out in Sirius. Obviously it's a large untapped market for our many goods, but there are surely dangers lurking out there that we have not yet come across. I think it's best to wait for the Royal Navy to secure some of the areas before we go venturing out there in search of profits.

1119939.text: If all you need to motivate you is a jingle and a poster of some pretty scenery to inspire you, then you're probably an EFL employee whose job will be done by robots soon. In fact, your replacement is probably already in the shipment of Robotics headed to Briancon Station.

1119940.text: Petrochemicals production is one of the less sought after jobs in Gallia, even with the labor troubles on Amiens. Beauvais Production uses a lot of Robotics to minimize the hazards to humans by the chemical processes that take place on the station.

1119941.text: Beware of the Maquis. They know we work with the government and they would very much like to punish us for it. Always keep an eye on your scanners and be ready to run.

1119942.text: After a leak caused a disastrous vapor explosion that killed several workers, Robotics have begun to replace human labor at Saint-Quentin Space Colony's Liquefied Petroleum Gas facility. In that case, I don't think even the EFL employees complained about the loss of jobs.

1119943.text: GMS employees are very hostile to the use of advanced Robotics in mining operations if they use artifical intelligence. The miners rightly fear that the thinking machines will replace them. Toulon Mining Facility in the Provence system, however, is a fairly dangerous place to work due to all the criminal activity in the system, so the miners don't seem to mind so much if they can send the Robots out to do the mining, or can sit at a console safely on the station and direct the Robots out in the mining fields.

1119944.text: Much of this station is off-limits to visitors. I can't tell you why, but I can assure you it's for a good reason.

1119945.text: Solar Engineering obviously makes extensive use of advanced Robotics in our own manufacturing processes. Mortagne Production Facility has top of the line artificial intelligence involved at every stage of Holotainment Band production, from basic manufacturing to sorting and even holoscenario development. Naturally, the AI doesn't yet have the creativity of the human mind, but we've got our top minds working on that problem.

1119946.text: The Robotics that we ship to Guise Mining Facility in the Picardy system for the Aluminium fields are strictly the 'dumb' variety, no artificial intelligence allowed under the contract with GMS. Last year GMS tried to integrate AI into their operations, and the miners went on strike. GMS caved in, but even the most stubborn miners can't hold back the future forever.

1119947.text: We didn't build this station, but we operate it now. Space Station operation is one of our core competencies. When we go into a new base, we're able to quickly cut costs and squeeze out as much revenue from the place as possible. Our record of success in this field is unmatched.

1119956.text: Gallic Metal Service\nOmicron Rho Gate Bartender\nYvon Austin

1119957.text: EFL Oil and Machinery\nOmicron Rho Gate Commodity Trader\nZerbino Barrette

1119958.text: EFL Oil and Machinery\nOmicron Rho Gate Equipment Dealer\nHenry Guimond

1119959.text: EFL Oil and Machinery\nOmicron Rho Gate Ship Dealer\nCharles Fontaine

1119964.text: Bretonia Intelligence Service\nDunedin Commodity Trader\nHenry West

1119965.text: Bretonia Intelligence Service\nDunedin Equipment Dealer\nNeil Dixon

1119966.text: Bretonia Intelligence Service\nDunedin Ship Dealer\nDonnie Lloyd

1119970.text: Even though The Council ain't official allies of ours, they keep the Royal forces busy. So we help them from time to time and make sure not to stand in their way.

1119971.text: If you want to trade anything in the black market, you better have some Brigand friends. We control most of the Gallic black market.

1119972.text: The loss of Quillan to the Royal forces was a tough blow to our side, even though it was the Council's. It was a good source of recruits and supplies, and the Council was less concerned with smuggling than the GRN is. Now we are more heavily dependent on Marne.

1119973.text: Planet Marne is important to us. The large population gets us many new recruits, and the large factories help us with much-needed supplies and arms.

1119974.text: Let me tell you something. When you're surrounded by the enemy, be it on land or on a station, escape like a Brigand. Take as a hostage the person with the most luxurious clothing. The "high class" always wear them as status-symbol.

1119975.text: When fighting Royal forces, try to avoid killing the pilot. Even though the government doesn't really care about them and won't pay much, they're always worth more alive.

1119976.text: I feel sorry for the poor citizens that live under the Crown's control. But hey, the Brigands are both free and not picky when it comes to new recruits.

1119977.text: Gallic Artifacts - I can't believe people are paying so much for these useless pieces of junk. They don't even do anything! But hey, if someone will pay, I will deliver. It's all just business for me.

1119978.text: Many poor and homeless folks are brought here because this base functions as a way station. We transport them to Ecommoy Base in Maine for...I'm actually not sure what they do there. Whatever it is, it must be important and require a lot of fresh labor.

1119979.text: We are bringing Synthetic Marijuana to this station from Verdun Base. It's some quick credits that we can make off of those who don't wish to try out Cardamine.

1119980.text: This base is a supply spot for Counterfeit Software from Evron Base that goes on to Planet Marseille. Some of it stays here while the rest is being shipped away.

1119981.text: Oil shipments are extremely vital to the Brigands. While seeing these shipments explode is great fun, it's more important to keep the cargo intact.

1119982.text: There are always Refugees that wish to escape the crown. In this system we have 2 convoys each week transferring them to Planet Toulouse.

1119983.text: We ship Cobalt from this base to Planet Marne. Cobalt is vital to the production of High Temperature Alloy that we use in our ships.

1119984.text: New software updates to our defense systems are brought here weekly from Evron Base.

1119985.text: Can you smell it? This is the smell of freedom! I bet you won't find it anywhere under Royal control.

1119986.text: We don't trust the Unione Corse. They often work for the Royalists, and even with the Royalists when the money pays them well enough.

1119987.text: If we see a Gallic Metal Service ship in need of help we immediately supply it. The Gallic Metal Service is supporting the Council, both financially and with supplies.

1119988.text: While we don't attack civilian targets, when we do see an IDF transport in trouble, we might get "occupied", since many of the IDF shipments are supplies to the GRN.

1119989.text: Oil is vital to our ships. This is why whenever some is offered to us we take it without asking too many questions.

1119990.text: Some say that opening the minefield played into Royal hands. The devices that were used were far too unstable, but what's better than using the enemy's navy to do the risky work for you?

1119991.text: Wine, such a marvelous thing! Unfortunately, we don't get much of it here in the Council. But hey, soldiers are supposed to remain sober, no?

1119992.text: I was formerly a pirate. When the Council aided me to escape a Royals ambush, I realized where I belong.

1119993.text: When we come across a Royal patrol we always offer them to join the right side. Sometimes our words make them rethink their actions, and sometimes they actually do join us.

1119994.text: Planet Quillan, even while under Royal control, is sympathetic to the Council in its people's hearts. When we controlled it, most of the population gladly supported us, and a large number of them joined our ranks.

1119995.text: Roussillon is our second safe heaven. The defenses are heavy and the population is growing fast with all the new immigrants that go to live there.

1119996.text: When you can, come to Planet Marne's liberation day celebrations. It's amazing! Stay in Council controlled areas, though. I hear that the Brigand regions blur the line between celebration and mayhem.

1119997.text: LPG is used by many of the light vehicles and machines on this station. We import it from Saint-Quentin Space Colony in Picardy.

1119998.text: While most of the machinery in Clermont Space Colony use LPG as their source of fuel, we employ several very heavy machines and some parts of the station require such large amounts of energy that LPG wouldn't be sufficient. The station's life support and defense systems use nuclear fusion as their source of fuel, so my job is to bring Promethene from Briancon Station.

1119999.text: The King is both wise and just. I believe once the Monarchy's mission is complete and the Sirians are conquered, the King will surely relinquish his war powers and establish some form of democracy in Gallia. I just couldn't imagine such a benevolent leader doing anything else.

1120000.text: Well, you didn't hear this from me, but EFL has a way of keeping the company at the forefront of technology in the Energy industry, and it's not innovation. Consultants in our business development group seek out researchers and technology startups that are about to push breakthrough energy technologies into the market. EFL pays good money for their patents or buys their entire company. Then we cancel development and sit on the patents. The domination of petroleum products will not be supplanted as long as EFL has its way.

1120001.text: At the risk of sounding like a disgruntled employee, I feel I must get this off my chest. Back when it first started, EFL's growth was due to harnessing the latest technologies to deliver energy safely and efficiently. But these days, corporate profits come not from technology or R&D, but from government contracts via connections to the Crown and intense lobbying for weaker environmental and employee regulations. A once proud culture of innovation has been replaced by an obsession with exceeding quarterly profit expectations. Welcome to the business world.

1120002.text: Back a few decades ago, EFL had a major Oil spill a few kilometers from the largest city while drilling on Planet Marne. Over 10 million tonnes were spilled before the well could be capped. I'll bet you didn't hear THAT in the news! Using his connections to the government, our CEO was able to block journalists and news outlets from reporting this incident to the other Gallic systems. This was actually one of the grievances that helped spark the Marne Rebellion. Keep this to yourself. If it gets out that I told you, I'll likely be fired.

1120003.text: At Riom Shipyard we stockpile Light Arms for outfitting new vessels, and resupplying the local Navy forces. From here we take the gear to Battleship Le Cendre.

1120004.text: At Riom Shipyard we are manufacturing ships in large numbers. This of course requires lot of materials, one of which is very vital - Super Alloy. We bring that from Roanne Production Facility.

1120005.text: We're patriotic here and we do everything we can to support the Royal Navy. We know our existence, and revenues, depend on them. That is why failure in the war in Sirius is not an option.

1120006.text: As being part of a large, Crown-loyal company we have an obligation to produce large amounts of ships in Riom Shipyard. Promethene is used in the ship's power cores, and well, in a place where you produce ships it would be a vital element. Briancon Station supplies us with bulk quantities of Promethene regularly.

1120007.text: Among the materials that we need to use in our production lines onboard Riom, we have a vast need for High Temperature Alloy in the process of building the engines. At Alesia they have the ability to create this alloy, made from several rare minerals that GMS mines.

1120008.text: If you run into a hostile Unione Corse member out in unprotected space, it's best to cooperate. It's better to escape with your life than to blow up with your cargo.

1120009.text: Production shifts on Riom Shipyard are long and tiring. Fortunately, Montlucon Space Colony is not far and it offers facilities for rest and relaxation. Transports heading over to the Colony always find plenty of eagers hitchhikers who just ended their shift.

1120010.text: We bring Light Arms from Calais Research Facility to Riom shipyard. In the research facility they develop new weaponry and warfare gear, and we have to fight for access to the newest prototypes.

1120011.text: EFL's public relations division is nearly the size of its research and development division. And with EFL's troubling track record of employee and environmental safety, you can understand why. It takes a lot of work to convince Gallic citizens of our supposed benevolence.

1120012.text: We may be a big corporation, but that just means there are more of us that care about the citizens of Gallia. We are the most charitable corporation in terms of sponsoring good causes and giving back to the community.

1120013.text: You may not realize it, but a large company like EFL has a great relationship with local small businesses all across Gallia. Everywhere we operate, we spend billions on local small businesses like electricians, carpenters and mechanics, for contractor work that, in turn, supports our projects. The relationship is mutually beneficial and we depend on each other.

1120014.text: At EFL Oil and Machinery, we're focused on bringing affordable energy to the consumer. For hundreds of years, Oil has been the fuel to provide that energy, and it's worked out well for everyone in Gallia.

1120015.text: One of the things that occupy the residents of the Montlucon Space Colony is the production of Polymers. We try our best to give all the residents labor, and my labor is to ship these Polymers from here Planet Amiens.

1120016.text: We bring Petrochemicals into this space colony. They are used in the manufacturing of a large variety of products including rubber and Polymers. We have a large use for them in our Polymer factory, thus shipping them in from Beauvais Production Facility.

1120017.text: EFL often supports local schools by offering guest presenters and free advanced instruction tools in the classroom. We're all Gallic citizens, so helping children learn about science and the environment is something we are proud to be involved in.

1120018.text: We try to maintain a good relationship with other Space Colonies. One of the methods is by having a well-established trade with them, thus we transport Polymers that are manufactured here to Chartres Space Colony.

1120019.text: Maintaining a space colony is a complex process, one that require many machines and components. These machines and components require fuel to operate, thus we bring in LPG from the Saint-Quentin Space Colony.

1120020.text: Many critical ship parts are manufactured here for the Royal Navy and our production quotas have increased over the past year. The safety of this station is very important to the Navy so we are well protected here.

1120021.text: Since there is not an inhabited planet in Auvergne, the space colonies have to double as supply depots for every other operation in the system. IDF Shipping stockpiles Mining Machinery here, and it is distibuted as needed to Saint-Flour Mining Facility.

1120022.text: The nuclear reactor powering this station requires precise attention. Cryocubes from Planet Mayenne are essential to keeping the station from heating up too much. We stockpile a substantial inventory in case of any supply disruption, and we also serve as a supply hub for the other stations in Auvergne and Provence that use them.

1120023.text: Not everyone working for the Gallic Metal Service is a miner. For example, I am the residence coordinator for the GMS here on Clermont. I am responsible for acquiring lodging for our employees and their families here on Clermont.

1120024.text: Even though it's a long trip, the Polymers manufactured here are still cheaper than what can be manufactured on Planet Mayenne. One transport crew is less expense than an entire manufacturing facility, after all, so GMS supplies all it's needs from what is manufactured here.

1120025.text: Soissons Mining Facility in Ile-de-France provides us with a steady supply of Hydrocarbons to use in manufacturing Polymers. I know what you're thinking - it would make a lot more sense to manufacture Polymers at the site of the main Hydrocarbon supplier. What you forget is that the Crown is more heavily invested in EFL than GMS, and the Crown is also interested in settling new systems. So, when EFL opens a new facility, naturally they're going to do so in a system designated by the Crown. It may not make much business sense, but there are larger considerations involved. IDF Shipping also now benefits from added shipping routes.

1120026.text: You'll have to forgive me, monsieur, but I am rather busy at the moment. The families of two employees just arrived and I don't have rooms for them. Someone over on Roanne neglected to inform me I'd have additional personnel here!

1120027.text: Bonjour, take a seat and I'll get you some Wine! You like wine right? Doesn't matter, that is all I serve here! The job board is over there if you're looking for work, but I'd bet you could also ask around and find some.

1120028.text: Even though the GMS has primary dominance over the mining industry here in Gallia, 95% of the industry to be exact, the executives have not been corrupted with greed as others have. Instead of maximising profits by cutting corners, they spend the extra credits to ensure worker safety and the quality of our products.

1120029.text: We had a close call awhile back. Somehow a Maquis got aboard the station and tried to blow himself up right over there. Luckily, his bomb didn't go off. Unluckily for him, our airlocks work perfectly.

1120030.text: The logistics officer at Alesia Station is always breathing down our necks about their Cobalt shipments. I know they are under enormous pressure to produce High Temperature Alloys according to the shipyards' schedules, but there's only so much we can do here. If an asteroid just doesn't yield mineral, we can't just magically conjure it into existence. Mining takes patience. If that logistics officer doesn't take a hint, I'm going to hitch a ride up their and he'll take a fist in the nose!

1120031.text: The next shipment of Cobalt is headed for Abbeville Production Facility. That should last them for a while. Cobalt is a critical component of the Superconductors they manufacture there.

1120032.text: Cobalt, Cobalt, Cobalt! That is all you ever hear around here. I can't wait for my transfer to Soissons is approved. I just hope I get to take a passenger shuttle there. Hitching a ride on a cargo transport is more dangerous. Both the Corse and Brigands need the raw materials we provide to Gallia and they've no qualms with taking them.

1120033.text: Roanne Production is clamoring for more Cobalt, but they need to fight it out with Alesia Station. For some reason, GMS has had a hard time integrating overall logistics. Each facility places its own supply orders separately, and they all scream for priority over each other. Fail to supply the wrong logistics officer who has a father-in-law in an executive suite, and you can find yourself pounding rocks on Mayenne like my predecessor did.

1120034.text: Occasionaly we get an order from Compeigne Space Colony for Cobalt. That's where Solar Engineering manufactures their Nanocapacitors. They don't need vast quantities of metals like our alloy processors do, but they do rely on just in time shipments so they don't have to waste space on stockpiling inventory. Lucky for me, they're also smart businessmen, and I can expect a very nice gift with each and every requisition. Nobody at Solar ever has to ask twice for an order, if you know what I mean.

1120035.text: If there is one thing I've learned working for the Gallic Metal Service, it is that the Royal Police are just as shady as the Brigands or the Corse. If you aren't careful around them, they'll rob you quicker than a criminal would. Better hold onto your wallet when they are about, monsieur!

1120036.text: Planet Amiens has been requisitioning more and more Cobalt in the past few years. The planet's industry has been on a long downhill slide for decades, but the Munitions factories that were established there since the loss of Marne have rejuvenated the planet's infrastructure somewhat. Until the wars are over, anyway.

1120037.text: Mortagne Production Facility places orders for Cobalt far in advance of when they need them. They must have their Holotainment Band manufacturing and deliveries down to a science. I don't complain though. Knowing so far in advance of when they need a shipment lets me plan things out so that nothing interferes with all the demanding GMS stations that also want Cobalt. It's a good thing, too, because that supply officer at Mortagne is pretty stingy with his 'tokens of appreciation'. Still, free holosoftware is still free.

1120038.text: My brother was a officer in the Royal Navy before the Council broke through the mine fields and ignited the Second Gallic Civil War. He defected to the Council shortly afterwards and I haven't seen him since. I'm hoping the rumors that the Council doesn't shoot our transports holds true, I'm slated to captain my own transport hauling goods to Kusari soon!

1120039.text: While it may take a few more years, the Council threat will be put down. There is no hope for those challenging the rule of the King.

1120040.text: We try our best to protect the financial and personal security of Gallic businesses in space. A strong economy is vital for the war effort and we defend it accordingly. The citizens of Gallia can count on us!

1120041.text: The Royal Navy is under direct command of the King. We are loyal, professional, and deadly. All those who oppose the Crown shall be destroyed.

1120042.text: There is a lot of illegal activity going on in this region of space. Fortunately, we transfer Prisoners directly to Chateau d'lf Prison in the orbit of Planet Marseilles, so we don't have to house them here for very long.

1120043.text: Unlike battleships in the core systems, we don't receive our supplies from distribution centers. We have to ship Promethene directly from Briancon Station under heavy Naval escort.

1120044.text: There is a contingent of Maquis in this system with a well-hidden base somewhere in the Limagne nebula. Once we locate it, we believe we can purge the Maquis from Auvergne once and for all. Their acts of terrorism will earn them nothing but a brutal death.

1120045.text: Marines that aren't deployed to the front often get stationed here after a journey from Battleship Montreuil. The corporations that do business in Provence like to have the added security nearby in case something goes wrong on board the prison station, Luxury Liner Antibes, or Cannes.

1120046.text: Out here on the frontier of Gallic space you would think we would get top priority with the brass, but we seem to be constantly last in line for Light Arms allotments from Calais Research Facility. Apparently part of the problem is the hesitancy of the Navy to schedule shipments that don't coincide with Naval patrols - the usual military bureaucracy giving the shaft to the troops who are actually taking the risks.

1120047.text: Brigand fighter pilots are a joke. Their only hope against the GRN is cowardly tactics and having far superior numbers, and sometimes even that isn't enough. That's why most times we see Brigands, we see only their engine trails disappearing into the distance.
