1120048.text: You might think we wouldn't have much need for heavy munitions out here, but actually we use quite a bit, when the shipments actually arrive from Planet Amiens without getting blown up by the Maquis. There are plenty of nearby asteroid fields and planets in Provence that are uninhabited, so we schedule live fire drills frequently. If the Le Cendre is ever deployed to the front line, we'll be destined for a lot of meritorious citations, I'm certain. Our gunners brag that they can put their rounds right through the building doorways of their choice at this point. Funny thing is, there aren't any buildings, much less doorways, in our exercises, but gunners are always running their mouths about something.

1120049.text: Our Lynx-class fighters are the most deadly in the galaxy. Its turn-rate and strafing abilities are top-notch and it still manages to house a sizable power plant. The Lynx gives the Royal Navy the strength to vanquish all enemies in our path.

1120050.text: Gallic Metal Service does good work and is crucial for supplying the war effort with essential minerals and resources. But their lack of professionalism at times can get rather irritating. When I encounter them, sometimes I feel like I am talking to children. It must be all of that exposure to toxic asteroid dust.

1120051.text: Don't tell my superiors, but I am terrified of the Maquis. They are merciless butchers who have no limits nor moral obligations to anything or anyone.

1120052.text: Many wonder how I got to my rank, don't tell but the answer is simple: bribes. Have no illusions, everyone in the Royal Police is taking bribes and they hand them over to others.

1120053.text: The Brigands in this system tend to move a lot of Counterfeit Software. Most of it is made by the Council and includes software updates. We must stop them. The more we take down the easier the combat will be for us.

1120054.text: EFL moves large quantities of LPG which is a target for all sorts of unlawful parties around here. It's our duty to defend them for two reasons: First, we need it ourselves. Second, it also hurts the unlawful factions' ability to power their ship's engines.

1120055.text: Prisoner convoys are always subject to raids from pirates and various unlawfuls. You can't always know who is who in these organizations and when an important leader is imprisoned they are quite keen on getting him back.

1120056.text: Tell you what. You look like a nice person, for a small fee I might ignore if you move a few "restricted" items. I mean, we all want to be free to do as we wish. As long as it's kept between the two of us, we can even make it a deal on regular basis.

1120057.text: Some police officers are taking bribes for all sorts of things: Turning a blind an eye towards some smuggler, avoiding paying taxes and so on. If I will catch one doing this he will be reported directly to the Crown.

1120058.text: While the Royal Police are on duty monitoring pirate and any illegal activity that is done in space, we are also assigned to the occasional patrol in the cities. Just yesterday I caught some punk spraying "Pancakes rules" on a wall. Needless to say he learned a lesson about vandalism.

1120059.text: Nox is an extremely dangerous drug and it's our duty to stop any and all export and import of it in our space! We swore to protect the King and children of Gallia from any danger out there, and fighting for their own future is among our goals.

1120060.text: There is that new Sirian drug called "Cardamine" that I've heard about. We have yet to study it, but it seems to be very addictive among those who use it even a few times. We let small shipments of it pass on, only to get a chance to study it further in the general population.

1120061.text: The King ordered us to stop all of the Gallic Artifacts shipments. I still don't understand why though. These Artifacts are mostly just some random junk, and if Sirians are ready to pay for it why not use it to assist our economy?

1120062.text: The King is not willing to assist our economy with the export of those useless Artifacts that you can find across Gallia. Well, if he is not willing to help his own pocket with their export, I am! Just don't tell anyone that I am allowing these shipments off-radar and you could be rich, for a small fee of course!

1120063.text: We sometimes spare the little criminals if the right person pulls the right strings, but if it's about Maquis, we don't show mercy. They just don't deserve any of it.

1120064.text: I am not willing to transport any Brigand leader captive to anywhere. I am not even willing to escort any transport doing so, I just too much like myself being alive. The Brigands often attack these transports and kill the police officers nearby.

1120065.text: The Royal Navy is shipping large amounts of Light Arms for its Marines and ground forces elsewhere from this system. We often check the Trade Lanes before they move, to make sure they are safe.

1120066.text: IDF is supplying all kinds of bases and stations with a large variety of cargo. I have managed to discover that a quite profitable contract is shipping Luxury Consumer Goods from here to Planet Marseille. After all, my business is purely about the income.

1120067.text: You will find out that the paycheck of the simple Royal Police officer is not much at all. For that reason, most of them buy Tobacco and smoke it, rather than buying Cigars. Well, and what is more patriotic than supplying our great nation's police officers with their need? I bring them Tobacco from Planet New Paris, they give me a nice price for my goods. Sort of a win-win situation.

1120068.text: When flying around in this system, you need to keep your eyes peeled for Maquis. They are usually very aggressive and not in the mood to negotiate. We lose shipments to them all the time.

1120069.text: Polymers have a huge number of potential uses. For that reason the managment decided to open a Polymers factory onboard this space colony. In turn, I ship it to Peronne Shipping Platform, where the polymers are sorted to different groups by their future use. Don't ask me why production and distribution is so far apart. I suspect someone in the executive suite figured out how to increase billings by making our trade network as complex as possible.

1120070.text: There is one thing everybody love: Diamonds. It's a symbol for luxury and wealth, thus the upper class always demand more of them. For that very reason I bring Diamonds from Planet Metz, Croix-Rousse. Even the poorer citizens of the space colony want lower quality stones.

1120071.text: Out here we businessmen have to stick together. Auvergne may not be officially considered part of the Border Worlds, but it sure feels like it. We're a fair distance from Ile-De-France, and generally, the further you go from New Paris, the less control the Crown has. And when there's Brigands, Maquis and Councilmen around, that's not a good thing.

1120072.text: The Unione Corse are the only people that understand where we are coming from. The Crown is hopelessly corrupt. Peaceful protests and governmental reform have failed. It's time to do whatever is necessary to right the wrongs of the past several centuries.

1120073.text: I pity the Brigands, in their unfashionable clothing and the low-quality food they eat. We may all be living in giant rock bases but we don't have to act like it. Have some class, people!

1120074.text: We're trying to spare civilians as best we can, but we don't let the corporations off the hook. Their close partnership with the government makes them fair game when it's time to blow something up.

1120075.text: The Council are a bunch of fools. They let those corporate transports skip right past them out in space since they don't want to harm innocent people. Don't they realize that the corporations feed the Gallic war machine and the only way to bring down the regime is to starve the beast? Eventually, they will learn the wisdom of our tactics.

1120076.text: Roasting Royal Policemen is one of my favorite hobbies. Just pop their fuel tanks and they go up in flames. It's fun, you should try it sometime. Join the Maquis and you'll get plenty of chances.

1120077.text: The commercial traffic heading towards Riom Shipyard is especially vulnerable to our attacks. Several ships that make up the Royal Navy are produced there. We try to ambush the supply transports frequently. And as an added bonus, the loot we collect can be used to build and maintain our fleet.

1120078.text: The GMS are hauling quite large amounts of Cobalt from this system to other Royal bases. It's within our duty to make sure that at least some of it end up in either Maquis or Council hands. Our raiders attack the occasional transport and in turn I am shipping it to Planet Marne.

1120079.text: The Maquis at Limoux Base in Languedoc are unmatched for their fierce resolve. Only the most dedicated and daring Maquis choose to live there, since the system was a war zone. Somehow they have managed to acquire large numbers of Nuclear Devices and we are bringing some of them here. I don't know what the leadership plans to do with them. I hope it's something spectacular, but it might just be a plan to convert our ships to nuclear power.

1120080.text: The shameless vermin in the EFL deserve no mercy. Their weapon systems are responsible for the deaths of thousands of patriots of the rebellion. Their loyalty to the Crown marks their own death sentence. And we are all too happy to carry it out with our guillotines.

1120081.text: While the Maquis are generally a terrorist organization, some people tag along for the fearsome reputation to serve their greed. Others, use it as a shield for their transports and smuggling operations. I know several pilots that fly under the safety of the Maquis flag and transport Cobalt from here to Verdun Base. Personally, I don't mind them. Ideological purity is less important for transport pilots.

1120082.text: We generally don't deal in drugs, as they enslave people to them. This contradicts our agenda that stand up for freedom, however the Sirius made Synthetic Marijuana is only considered as a "light drug", and if the income from it's sale will promote our goal we will deal with it. Personally I escort transports that bring it in here from Verdun Base.

1120083.text: Sometimes I feel pity for the corporate employees that we kill. Oh wait, no I don't. I love watching them fry in fiery explosions. And I'd murder their family and mutilate their bloody corpses if I could. Then I would dismember all of the bodies and mail them to the corporate bases as a warning of what happens to people who are loyal to the Crown.

1120084.text: Our group engage a lot of fighting with the local police and navy forces. For that reason we always require large amounts of ammunition of high quality. The Council are our main source for those, and their new production facilities in Planet Toulouse are filling our demand.

1120085.text: You'll notice there aren't many other women on this station. And the ones that are, I don't think they came here by choice. I prefer not to know a lot of what goes on at Lapalisse because I know that revolutionaries tend to have to get their hands dirty in order to accomplish their goals. Killing Royalists: that's something we can all agree on.

1120086.text: One thing that has always united the Council with the Maquis is the relentless pursuit of the Crown's destruction. We proudly fight side by side against this entrenched enemy. One day the King will be executed and all his corrupt weasels in the government will be purged. From the ashes shall arise a new Gallic order of peace and justice. Victory shall be ours, I can assure you, not His.

1120087.text: Clermont Space Colony stockpiles Jump Gate and Trade Lane Parts for repairs in Auvergne and for eventual use in Provence. It's safer to only ship small quantities to Provence, but we are regularly transporting them from the colony's storage to Planet Marseille.

1120088.text: There is a Royal Police academy onboard this station, and they use Holotainment Bands in their early training of face-to-face situations. Since the bands tend to disappear, it is necessary to constantly replace them. We have a contract to transport the bands from Mortagne Production Facility.

1120089.text: We tried to resist being drawn into the ongoing war against the Sirians, but that now seems to have been naive in retrospect. War touches every aspect of life in Gallia. I hope our society can recover once it's all over.

1120090.text: The main export of Montlucon Space Colony is Polymers. This is due to the fact that the managment of the colony decided to create a large Polymer factory onboard. We are transporting these polymers to Saint-Exupery Space Port, where it awaits further distribution or use in the base's production processes.

1120091.text: As part of the school program for the children that live in the colony, there is a virtual trip around Gallia. For that, the school uses Holotainment Bands. Some of the cleverer children always seem to find ways to turn off the safety protocols and load adult software onto the Bands. Of course, we adults always have to confiscate those Bands for inspection.

1120092.text: Solar Engineering doesn't operate any stations out in this system, nor would we want to. Fly around and you will see why.

1120095.text: EFL Oil and Machinery\nAntibes Bartender\nSatordi Sabourin

1120096.text: EFL Oil and Machinery\nAntibes Commodity Trader\nFaustin Perillard

1120097.text: EFL Oil and Machinery\nAntibes Equipment Dealer\nBeaufort Pouliotte

1120104.text: Gallic Royal Police\nChateau d'If Bartender\nLucas Lariviere

1120105.text: Gallic Royal Police\nChateau d'If Commodity Trader\nRoyden Beaupre

1120106.text: Gallic Royal Police\nChateau d'If Equipment Dealer\nChappell Sciverit

1120110.text: One major opportunity that has opened up for the Brigands since the mine fields were breached is that we've found some like minded organizations in Sirius that are eager to expand their trade contacts. We've established ties with an outlaw group in Liberty that is supplying us with cheap labor. I'm not sure why we need all this labor all of a sudden, though. Maybe it has to do with our position on Planet Marne. That must be it. All the turmoil probably doesn't create a reliable labor force. It's kind of strange that we have to route all the new recruits through Ecommoy Base first.

1120111.text: The Gallic Brigands might attack smaller, less escorted Gallic companies due to the fact it's quite easy. But we can't only sustain ourselves from the small shippers, they simply don't carry enough cargo and are not sighted often. That is why ambushing large convoys is more likely - greater danger with greater profit potential.

1120112.text: We have sort of a "cold war" with the Unione Corse. We are in competition for the Gallic black market, which we dominate, while we also assist each other a lot. We help one anther to build ships and sometimes go on raids together.

1120113.text: You can't ever trust a Corse. One second he might be very nice and welcoming, and the next he might shoot you for the Crown. Why the elders let them stay around our bases is still unknown to me.

1120114.text: Gallic artifacts are in high demand in Sirius. They are a new, exciting commodity they have yet to witness and every rich bastard wants some shiny new thing for his collection. But heck, what do I care? Easy profit for me.

1120115.text: Nox is a real dangerous substance. While the feeling might be nice, the aftereffects aren't. I had a brother that was a heavy user. One day in the middle of a long flight he ran out of it, and went crazy. He ended up ejecting into space without a pod or a space suit.

1120116.text: There are lots of rumors about what's going on with all the labor we're shipping in from Liberty. Some say we're trying to build up our industrial colony on Planet Marne, others say we're recruiting an army for the Council. Personally, none of it makes any sense to me. I'd rather just deal with cargo that doesn't talk back, and doesn't need to be fed and watered, much less cleaned up after. Have you smelled a cargo hold after it's been packed with people for several days? Ecommoy Base must smell like a sewer. Course, Brigand bases don't smell like perfume to start with.

1120117.text: We bring in Deuterium from Planet Chateauroux. We have experiments with ships running on alternative energies, and Deuterium is proving to be useful for this very task since it is more easily accessible than EFL's processed fuels.

1120118.text: I refuse to try any of those drugs. Not going to even get near Nox, not to mention Cardamine. Both of those are deadly if you stop using, and the Synthetic Marijuana is made by an unknown Sirian party - like I am going to try that out.

1120119.text: I heard that in Sirius there are some sort of advanced aliens. I can only think from looking at the Privas planetary structure that it's their doing. I mean, look at it! Five Planets in a most unlikely formation? Not a creation of nature in my opinion.

1120120.text: Fortunately, the resorts here in the system attract elite visitors, so the luxury goods are top quality. That means our raids provide top quality delights for us as well. If you can't afford to live the high life, then mug somebody else who is! That's the Brigand way.

1120121.text: Several Sirian parties have shown great interest in Prometheum. The Gallic Brigands have a big black market trade in this commodity, and if them Sirius residents will pay enough I will bring this highly unstable matter to their doorstep. The Brigand leadership and the Council might not like that idea, but they don't have to know about it. Say, you don't happen to have any contacts in Sirius, do you?

1120122.text: Sirian traders flying through Gallia tend to be the easiest prey. They are always woefully unprepared for an encounter with the Unione Corse. I don't feel bad because they have no business being here.

1120123.text: Generally, we try to maintain a status of neutrality with the Junkers. But if they screw us over, we are quick to exact our vengeance, as the Junker fools on Bourbon Base in Burgundy found out.

1120124.text: You ask far too many questions for your own good. Our organization's business is none of yours! Get lost!

1120125.text: Nox is highly addicting, therefore the rule "Once a customer, always a customer" applies to it. Now we ship Nox in quite large amounts to nearly everywhere, but from this base mainly to Planet New Paris. If they want, we are here to supply!

1120126.text: Among those who are using Nox there are civilian from both Council controlled areas and Royal controlled ones. Since we are in it for the money we supply both sides. Personally I bring large shipments to Planet Marne. We don't want only one side to enjoy our fantastic drug right?

1120127.text: Being in the Corse is like being family. Once you're in, you're in for life. We would never think of betraying a fellow Unione member. And no Corse would ever think about leaving. If they did think about it, they'd just jettison themselves out an airlock to save the rest of us the trouble.

1120128.text: Nox is a dangerous substance and it's not a fact that only a few know. This is why we decided to import from Sirius a new drug named Synthetic Marijuana. It's selling quite nice with those who are not willing to risk Nox, and a much larger number of officers is willing to ignore the occasional shipment for the right price.

1120129.text: We'll take on a Royal Navy officer or two if we somehow get caught with contraband. They tend to disappear and our shipment moves on long before the Navy reinforcements can arrive.

1120130.text: The Corse like to keep our operations to ourselves. Revealing too much information to a stranger like you can only hurt our group.

1120131.text: Sirius' residents are not aware of Nox's side-effects. This makes it ideal for us to export it to there, where we will sell it to a large, demanding, population that will get addicted to it and bring us, the Corse families, large profit. We just have to set up the proper distribution contacts and supply network first.

1120132.text: We typically stay out of the Council's way. While they conduct their war against the Royalists, we try not to get involved openly against the Crown. That way, whoever ends up winning, the Unione will maintain its strong position.

1120133.text: It's funny how corporate folks seem to hate the Corse until they need a dangerous pirate killed. Then their money and gratitude has no limits until we finish the job.

1120134.text: The Luxury Liner Belleville is a popular destination for people after they've stayed here on Antibes or at Cannes. After imbibing deeply of Provence's delights here, a lot of people need time to cleanse before heading back home, and Belleville is just the place. Passengers are usually willing to pay a good price if you get them there safely. You might want to look into it.

1120135.text: The problem with being so tightly associated with the government is that we rise and fall on the fortunes of the Gallic economy as a whole. When times are good with peace and prosperity, we do very well. But when Gallia has an expensive and open-ended foreign war during economic hard times, there can be a lot of pressure on the Crown from the citizenry to cut non-defense government contracts.

1120136.text: Years ago, we were looking to expand our Oil exploration outside of the core Gallic systems, and in the Gallic Border Worlds we found the untapped resources we were looking for. Now, the demand keeps picking up and Oil reserves in the Border Worlds are drying up, so we will have to be moving on into Sirius in search of fresh sources to feed Gallia's addiction.

1120137.text: Our Cigars are the best in Gallia. That's why they fetch such a good price. But if you are looking to maximize profit, bring a shipment of the Cigars to the Luxury Liner Belleville. There you'll find a heavy concentration of wealthy folks looking to relax with a good smoke. Once you see how much you can get for them there, you won't regret it.

1120138.text: The EFL has a strong history of innovation. We developed numerous new Oil extraction methods and technologies that allowed us to dig deeper, cheaper, and safer at our many Oil wells. This corporate culture for innovation extends to other sectors of our business as well, including construction and manufacturing. The Crown has noticed our high quality and efficiency, which is why we are the preferred general contractor for the government.

1120139.text: Brigands and Corse patrol much of this system, so if you take a pleasure craft for a flight away from the primary travel routes and get into trouble, don't expect help to come any time soon.

1120140.text: I've been a transport captain for many years, so allow me to share some advice. Always carry a few crates of good Wine with you while flying through Gallia. It's your best weapon if you ever get into trouble with the Police or some pirates. This is not fool-proof, but it's hard for any true Gallic citizen to fire on a ship if it means high quality Wine will go to waste.

1120141.text: Provence might seem like a strange place for a vacation, since the system is still fairly wild. The Royal Navy provides security at both ends of the jump hole to Auvergne, though, so the criminals who hide out in the outer reaches of the system have to be pretty daring to raid any ships coming to or going from the Antibes or Cannes. Provence offers certain amenities that you just can't get in the core systems, with so many prying eyes watching you all the time.

1120142.text: Oil is the lifeblood of Gallia. Without it, she will surely wither and die. Hopefully our enemies never learn this.

1120143.text: Many of our ships are quite complex - with dozens of smaller cargo sections. The authorities think it's because we piece them together from various smaller ships, but in reality, it's to be able to carry a little extra when making a run into the core worlds. Take Nox for instance, the demand for it on New Paris is insane. Of course, if you get tagged by the Navy you've got a problem. If you get tagged by the Police, you usually just arrange for a "fine". Heh.

1120144.text: Watch out for the Maquis. They aren't interested in your money or your cargo. You're only useful to them if you appear in the news in the, you guessed it, Obituaries section.

1120145.text: I feel sorry for the other Junkers back in Sirius. Most of them have lived hard lives up to now, scraping a living off of scrap metal salvaging or running shipments for unsavory folks. In Gallia, the Junkers live a much more comfortable life. And now that our true purpose in Sirius has been revealed, I can't imagine things getting any better for the Junker folks out there.

1120146.text: From what I hear, the Gallic Metal Service really takes good care of their employees. Their extensive social service benefits are the envy of many workers in Gallia. Plus, most of those GMS folks make a ton of money. I guess when a corporation dominates the entire mining industry they can afford such luxuries.

1120147.text: The Council is generally quite suspicious of the Junkers, so we don't expect anything but hostility from them. This is mostly due to our extensive cooperation with the Crown over the years. That's fine. We'd rather be on the winning team anyway.

1120148.text: Our ships are built for heavy-duty work, not for combat. That's why we Junkers try to avoid open hostility with other groups. Our excuse is that our only focus is money. But the real reason is because we know we'd get killed. Self-preservation is a strong incentive.

1120149.text: Nox, Nox, Nox. It doesn't matter where you go, if there are Gallic folk, there is a demand for it. Our "glorious navy" has now brought that demand out in Bretonia, where it is quite hard to fill. With those systems under military control, it's almost impossible to get it out there - but if you find a way, I have a contact on the Castres that will take it off of you, for an equally "glorious" sum. If Edinburgh is too far for you, taking it halfway to Fort Albi should get you a tidy sum as well. The Marines tend to handle the distribution themselves from there.

1120150.text: Ah, yes. Monte Carlo offers all kinds of wondrous relaxation programs. Why, I brought a shipment of the newest Holoprograms from Evron not three days ago. Sure, the authorities consider it Counterfeit Software, but they'll be none the wiser. The folks buying them down here tend to use them for...personal leisure...anyway.

1120151.text: The groveling IDF Shipping folks are always desperate for government contracts. They bend over backwards to satisfy the Crown's many persnickety demands. Their reward for such accommodating behavior is financial certainty and guaranteed profits for the foreseeable future. It's a bit pathetic, but I guess it works.

1120152.text: You look pretty trustworthy, so I'll give you a hint. If you're looking for a quick discreet paycheck, get yourself an inconspicuous ship and find a quiet route towards Maine. Then talk to Franc down on D level to arrange for some "special cargo". Oh, must I spit it out for you? The demand for Nox on the core world planets is as strong as ever.

1120153.text: Monte Carlo is a center of commerce - although not in the traditional sense. We frankly don't care who comes here, as long as they bring the credit to back up a purchase. Brigands, Corse...many come with some things to sell and some things to buy. Always in short supply here is Wine - folks usually take a crate or two with them when they leave. It's a legit cargo, so we ship it in directly from New Paris.

1120154.text: A clumsy Brigand attacked one of our small shipping convoys in Languedoc the other day. Luckily we had some pretty good escorts in the group and we were able to shoot him down and tractor in his pod. Afterwards we all enjoyed some victory Cigars. Everyone except the Brigand of course, who is now enjoying the confines of a prison station.

1120155.text: While most of our "special cargo" is usually destined for the Gallic core worlds, the rich and famous on the various resorts and civilian colonies indulge in Nox as well. Take Saint-Quentin for instance. But be careful, if you arrive there in a Junker ship you're going to get searched. Better to get yourself a civilian shuttle or freighter, those come and go there all the time, and won't raise suspicion.

1120156.text: We Junkers may seem like a bunch of hard-scrabble old grizzled folks, but most of us are actually quite wealthy. Many Junkers own property on New Paris and have secret bank accounts. We just like to keep that kind of stuff off the books if you know what I mean.

1120157.text: If you run into an officer in the Royal Police, watch your wallet. They are known to be very creative when it comes to issuing tickets or charging fees. I once was charged a Crown fee, King tax, Monarchy Support adjustment, and a Royalty charge...all in one stop! The worst part was, I had just paid most of those same fees to another Police officer a couple hours earlier. You have been warned.

1120158.text: I'm here on vacation, you? Work, you say? Pity. The resorts here are some of the finest in all of Gallia. I get a two-week vacation every year. It's GMS policy! My brother works for the IDF and he hasn't had a vacation in two years. Yet, he is adamant that he works for the better company. I've decided just to let him believe in his little fantasy.

1120159.text: The Gallic Police might control the docking rings here, but they haven't been able to stop the flow of Nox. Hell, I bet they let it flow and take a cut of the profits. The GMS has a strict no-use policy regarding Nox as it causes the user to become sedentary. Bad for business, ya know?

1120160.text: I heard rumors that GMS leadership is sympathetic to the Council's cause. All lies if you ask me. The Council are just a bunch of people who've not been able to get what they wanted legally so they've resorted to criminal activity under the guise of revolution. I don't think our leaders wouldn't betray the King and I think they should crack down on these rumormongers.

1120161.text: Are you here to run some Niobium? Better know what you're doing. Niobium shipments are the most dangerous runs in Gallia! 'Course the Service pays for well for successful runs. My advice? Hire some mercenaries to protect you.

1120162.text: Those paper pushers at Roanne are always making noise regarding the operational costs of Toulon. I don't understand it. They built this place in the middle of an area that wasn't fully secured by the Navy. What did they expect? Sometimes I wonder if we have the right people upstairs.

1120163.text: I've served Brigands at this very bar! Me, serving that filth. They attack us and steal from us, yet they get hired to protect our Niobium convoys. We should be hiring people who don't break the law for a living!

1120164.text: Niobium is vital in the production of many needed cargo all over Gallia. Here, in Toulon Mining Facility, the miners bring in the Niobium they mined and I, as a transport pilot, ship it off to Alesia Station.

1120165.text: You think you've got what it takes to make Niobium runs? Ha! I bet the Maquis dust you before you clear the Camargue. Your family is lucky you work for the GMS - they'll be paid well when you die. The only advice I'll give you is to upgrade the armor on that rust bucket you call a freighter.

1120166.text: I've made twenty-two runs. Twenty-two. Three more and I'll have saved up enough credits to retire! Not sure where I'm going to retire to yet. Maybe I'll go explore Sirius!? I'll make up my mind when I finish that last run.

1120167.text: You can't believe how much work it is to do all of that mining. I find it impossible to do, and I was always more into the combat part anyway. My job is to escort regular shipments of Niobium that go from here to Abbevile Production Facility, the company and the convoy's pilots get paid real good.

1120168.text: You can ignore Joseph, he is under the illusion he is the best hauler in the Service. The fact that no one else has completed twenty-two Niobium runs only reinforces his arrogance. You didn't hear this from me, but I think the only reason he is so successful is because of who he knows. I heard a rumor his brother is a Brigand and that is how he has avoided being attacked by them.

1120169.text: Just a tip, but if you ever run into a Royal Policeman and he hassles you, a subtle bribe usually blinds him to whatever it is you are doing. Don't be too obvious about it and don't let them know you have a lot of credits. Otherwise, you'll find yourself being taxed every time they see you.

1120170.text: The Gallic Metal Service are a huge company. We take care of most of the needed mining operations in Gallia, refine the mined goods and ship them over for further processing in various facilities. Personally, I find it's very profitable to take refined Niobium from this station, Toulon Mining Facility, to Roanne Production Facility.

1120171.text: Since the Royal Navy pushed into Sirius and secured the Taus, we've seen an influx in Sirian traders within Gallia. They are all so amazed at how developed Gallia is. Are the Sirian houses not as developed? Maybe I'll get lucky and make a run into Kusari or something.

1120172.text: We've only been mining the Camargue field for the century. Before then, it was too dangerous and the GMS wouldn't take the risk. Once the Navy took over securing the Provence system the GMS started constructing Toulon. I hear those were very dangerous times for a miner out here. You here to try a Niobium run?

1120173.text: I'm on vacation, well, I took vacation to come here. I lost my husband and crew during a Maquis attack on one of our convoys. When I heard I could rent a Navy ship and shoot some of them, I took my vacation time and spent my savings to make it a reality. Now I just have to wait for the Navy to find some more targets for me.

1120174.text: I've never flown a fighter or a bomber before, so I opted to be a forward-gunner on a gunboat. I might not be flying the ship that kills them, but I'll be the one pulling the trigger that ends their lives. I might even go as far as joining the Navy soon.

1120175.text: Some GMS executive was waiting for me when I woke up in the hospital and explained what had happened. He told me I was the only survivor and said I'd be 'taken care of'. I don't want their credits, what good are they when my husband is dead?

1120176.text: I might not agree with every decision the King makes, but as a GMS executive I can't complain about my life. I make enough credits to vacation anywhere in Gallia. I picked Antibes in the hopes of finding a wealthy noble or celebrity. I spent last night with a very handsome Victomte.

1120177.text: I think he rather enjoyed himself, hopefully he asks me to the ball tonight. I've no intention of living on Toulon for the rest of my life and he is my ticket off that wretched place. If it isn't my boss yelling about operational costs, it's the Brigands or Maquis trying to shoot the station apart.

1120178.text: What? You're looking for work? Can't you see I'm on vacation? Oh look, the Victomte is calling me over. Good bye now!

1120179.text: All glory to the King! He has led Gallia with strength and wisdom for many years and I would gladly sacrifice my life defending Gallia.

1120180.text: We don't have as many assets in this system as most of the other Core Worlds. That makes patrolling space a bit more frustrating. You eliminate one threat and there's always another one popping up on the other side of the system.

1120181.text: For some reason, the Gallic government has been recommending school children learn the Sirian language. I think this is ridiculous. Pretty soon all those Sirians will be speaking Gallic anyway.

1120182.text: This posting certainly has its perks! When we get shore leave, we can catch a shuttle over to Planet Marseille or Cannes Resort. We get fantastic treatment there, too. They seem to love having spiffy Navy dress uniforms strutting around, mingling with their guests. The waitresses will even sneak you free drinks.

1120183.text: Brigands, Maquis, even the Council, we can handle pretty easily. But the Corse are a different sort. They're professional killers with incredible dog-fighting skill. Normally we don't have to bust them, but when we do, we always call in backup.

1120184.text: The Royal Police can't always be counted on out here. Some of them are as crooked as the criminals we catch. The Crown really needs to do a better job of cleaning up the Police.

1120185.text: Our tours of duty are getting longer and longer. I can barely even remember what my wife looks like. My children probably won't recognize me when I return. There's just not as many Royal Navy pilots as before, and our mission is always expanding.

1120186.text: The leaders of the Council will all be executed for their treason against the Kingdom of Gallia. The King has no mercy for those who would challenge His rule, and neither do I.

1120187.text: I am proud to be part of the most trusted institution in Gallia. Everyone has their own political persuasions, but overwhelming majorities consistently support the Royal Navy.

1120188.text: Sometimes we are tasked with defending convoys for EFL and IDF Shipping through dangerous territory. More often than not, our presence has meant the difference between life and death for the transport pilots.

1120189.text: We frequently hunt down Brigand scum in this system. The Brigands don't have the best pilots, so those missions are good to use as live training for our new recruits.

1120190.text: IDF Shipping's transport services have been a life-saver for the Royal Navy. We have contracted them to ship war materials and supplies to the battle fronts and Prisoners back to the prison stations. This frees up us Royal Navy pilots to do what we do best: destroy the enemies of Gallia.

1120191.text: Why don't you sit down and have a glass of red? Gap may be known for its coffee, but I take pride in keeping the best wines in Gallia back in the store room. Getting some of these vintages all the way into Provence isn't always the cheapest, either, but the local clientele doesn't seem to be short on credits.

1120192.text: I'm sure by now you know the reputation of the Royal Police. Our officers are good at taking care of the wrongdoing they see, but you might find it's easy to have them conveniently be looking the other way.

1120193.text: I've had this bar for quite a while now, I bought this space back in 812. Although the Royal Police accounts for a fair bit of business, a few of the corporations have set up shop too, and of course there's all kinds of civilians. As long as everyone pays their bill, though, they're all the same to me.

1120194.text: Most of the Council's heavy ships that were in Languedoc and Orkney battles were destroyed, though several managed to vanish. They have been sighted in fights, but there is no confirmed destruction or capture of them. Among them there are the battleships Pamiers and La Fierte.

1120195.text: If you feel like doing a nice, quick trade you can take Nox from here, Planet Marseille, to Fort Albi and Battleship Castres. If anyone give you a hassle because you carry Nox just say I sent you.

1120196.text: Did you see the man who just walked out? Weirdest salesman I've ever seen. I bet he was one of those Corsicans. He tried to sell me something called tuna booze oil - said it was straight from Planet Nevers. Do you have any idea what he might've been talking about?

1120197.text: Maurice makes it known that he's not happy out here, but I find it to be quite nice. It's quiet, and if you're lucky you get assigned to one of the resort platforms planetside. Even for a police officer, that's a pretty nice gig.

1120198.text: They used to have us flying civilian ships out here - there just wasn't a need for the military fighters until recently. Now we've got GRN ships everywhere. As much as I loved my old battleshovel, I'm happy to have a new Serval. It makes me feel a bit more formidable in space.

1120199.text: When I found out that I'd been promoted I was thrilled. Brigadier Major for me, I was going to get a sparkling new Lynx for system patrols. Then I found out I was being stationed all the way out here. The grand Provence System, full of locked up convicts and old rich civilians. I suppose I should've given the Capitaine a bigger cut of the taxes I collected. Er, wait, you didn't hear that last part. Understood?

1120200.text: Come here monsieur, have some fine wine. You came here to relax your time and ease your mind and body after all, no? And what better way to do so, than sitting in a comfortable chair while drinking luxurious wine?

1120201.text: People all over Gallia come here to relax their time. Because this station is state owned, you will often see around high ranked navy officers enjoying their time for free.

1120202.text: In this place you can find some of the most beautiful women in all Gallia. We pay them to serve the costumers, many of which are from the upper command of the Royal Police, and have no time for family and a wife.

1120203.text: One of the best luxuries you can get around here is top quality Holotainment Bands. Using them you can go virtually visit far away places, and see creatures you've never dreamed of. Of course since they degrade over time, and we need to bring new ones, using them is costly.

1120204.text: I am here after a patrol down in the lanes of the system. The rich tourists attract greedy criminals, so we are forced to keep up high police activity. Not that I complain, having this place for the break time is like heaven.

1120205.text: I have a wife back in Planet New Paris, but I am telling you, once you see the women that hang around here - forgetting about past obligations becomes much easier.

1120206.text: Have you tried some of these new drinks the bar is serving? They say they are drinks from Sirius but I can't see those dogs coming up with our brilliant Sidewanger Feng.

1120207.text: Try and avoid getting involved within your workplace. You wouldn't believe the trouble you can get in for sneaking off during station patrol duty. Not that I have of course.

1120208.text: Sirius? Pah, I've seen stronger children! Bunch of traitors ran off and sacrificed our ancestors, it's about time we avenge them.

1120209.text: This whole system is great, and full of luxuries. I would never be able to afford holidays here, but due to my job I can be here nearly the whole year.

1120210.text: People come to this liner to enjoy their time, some like doing it with Holotainment Bands. However some would rather do it with Hypnotainment Bands, their stronger and illegal counterpart. This base is not state-owned, thus the supervision over it is by far less than on other stations. Getting Hypnotainment Bands to willing costumers on board this liner from local Unione Corse smugglers is VERY profitable, and I would know.

1120211.text: Nox is a dangerous drug and there are huge amounts of it all over this planet. Sadly we are almost completely unable to stop it's flow off the planet. Nox smugglers have money and they can buy influence with it.

1120212.text: Heard of that new drug Cardamine? Our orders are pretty clear, if we see it we can either destroy it or take it as evidence. Our commander is leaning more towards destroying it, sometimes evidence goes missing.

1120213.text: On board this station you can find all sorts of scum. From little drug dealers to known Brigands. The only exit most of them have out of here is to the Guillotine.

1120214.text: While some Police Officers might be corrupt, take bribes and support Corse families, in here you won't find any of those. On board the prison station only the best of the best are serving, and if you will try to bribe one of us you will soon become one of the inhabitants. Those that sleep in the cells by the way.

1120215.text: Marseille is a planet these rich people love. Sadly many criminals love these rich people as well, so we have to make sure that they are safe. I won't let any filthy scum get his hands on Gallic civilians.

1120216.text: Getting out of this station if you are a prisoner is nearly impossible. It is highly guarded, by the best wings the Royal Police have. Not to mention the fact that we shoot on sight any criminal that even thinks about it, these scum don't deserve to live anyway.

1120217.text: Prisoners are brought in here from all over Gallia's battleships, where they are moved when they are first captured. They come here to serve their time for their crimes, a long time usually.

1120218.text: I was escorting some scum back to the Prison Station for questioning when a bunch of his friends came along to stop me. Good job there was another patrol nearby or I would've been the one rotting in a cell.

1120219.text: Due to the huge amount of Prisoners that are locked in the station, we need large amount of guards with the best gear we can get. We get new gear all the time, and it is brought from Calais Research Facility. The haulers, who take a huge risk on themselves, are being reward with a nice sum of money.

1120220.text: All of the officers that serve here are good at all of the necessary skills for the Royal Police elite. We make sure to switch tasks every once in a while, thus we are kept good at everything, like the best of the Police should be like.

1120221.text: I have zero tolerance for smugglers, I almost never even take them to a fair trail - they will just find their way out. I find it far more effective to deploy a field execution, which is within my authority.

1120222.text: I sometimes go to check on the police officers in the other stations around here. They are simply here so they can have luxurious breaks, and enjoy rich people's lives. That also means they might do some illegal activities, to grind more money. If I catch them, their way to the Royal Court is short, very short.

1120223.text: This system has a lot of personnel transportation in and out of it. Prisoners convoys coming into the Prison Station, and lots of Tourists that come to visit the several luxuries that this system can offer.

1120224.text: There is a waiting list for people trying to get off of this planet. If you were to help them out by taking a number of Passengers to Planet Blois or Vendome Residence, I'm sure they would pay top dollar for tickets. It would be an easy way to make some extra money.

1120225.text: This planet does not have much of a manufacturing industry. Most of the Consumer Goods we use have to come from other places. That's why if you were to fly out to Montmartre Space Colony and bring back Consumer Goods, the people of Planet Marseille would make it worth your time.

1120226.text: The income earned through standard legal shipping is always better than the smuggling runs you see out in the rougher areas. You may make a big gain once or twice with a contraband sale, but law enforcement always catches up with you, negating your earnings. Too many young former IDF Shipping employees have found this out the hard way.

1120227.text: Surely you've sampled this base's famous Cigars. Well, so have other Gallic citizens. I've found that, given the distance, people on Vendome Residence and Planet Blois pay the most for this luxury item. In fact I am headed out right now to fill another Cigar order.

1120228.text: I just brought in another shipment of Consumer Goods from Montmartre Space Colony. It's a quite a trek from Ile-De-France to this station, but the selling price here makes it worth it. Just watch out for pirates along the way.

1120229.text: Most of our shipments involve hauling rather mundane cargo like metals, electronics, or consumables. But my favorites are filling the orders for the Royal Navy. Whether it be Prisoners, Munitions, or Military Vehicles, it's always more exciting and instills a sense of patriotism.

1120230.text: The clientele demand the top of the line luxuries while staying on this liner. It's why we're continuing to bring in more shipments of Luxury Consumer Goods. So far, the most efficient route I've found has me picking them up from our Vandoeuvres Space Colony over in Lorraine. If you've got a decent sized cargo hold, you should check it out. The guests aboard the Luxury Liner Antibes can never get enough of these luxury goods.

1120231.text: The Council act like they are a bunch of enlightened freedom fighters. But in practice, they are just petty thieves. I cannot see how a great new Gallic nation can be born out of pirating traders and ambushing Royal Navy patrols.

1120232.text: My last convoy was ambushed by a pack of Brigand dogs on the way to this station. We tried to fight them off, but that didn't work out so well. As for the transport captains that successfully reached their destination, you're looking at him.

1120233.text: Solar Engineering is dealing mainly with construction, though indirectly our job is to ease the life of the Gallic citizens. thus you might find the occasional Solar transport launching out of Planet Marseille with passengers that are eager to move to their new location: Gien Space Colony.

1120234.text: The Gallic education system is heavily relying on using Holotainment Bands. There is frequent use of them in the Gallic school-system and I find it quite profitable to fill that necessity by bringing them here from Mortagne Production facility. It's much cheaper to ship in holo-recordings of teachers than to pay and house those teachers here in the flesh when the living quarters are more profitably rented to rich tourists. The service personnel who do live here still have to send their children to school, of course.

1120235.text: We all have to watch each other's backs out here in Provence. We're far away from Ile-De-France, so this space is not as secure. Pirates in the Maquis, Brigands, and Corse operate much more freely out here. So be careful.

1120236.text: Cigars, such a wonderful tool to just relax one's self. The people that live in Gien Space Colony obviously share similar thoughts with me, and thus buy them in quite large numbers. So me, the nice supplier, is getting them fine Cigars for a profit even nicer than me!

1120237.text: The police that serve onboard this station need to keep their fighting skills fresh, and by that I mean both face to face and piloting ones. We bring in Holotainment Bands so they could train in a virtual world all the time and make sure they are not getting rusty.

1120238.text: It's much easier to get research work done out here in Provence compared to some of the Core Worlds due to the lack of Crown interference here. Don't be fooled by Battleship Arles. The government has very little influence out here. Government meddling is only favored by the likes of EFL and IDF Shipping.

1120239.text: This system has the most popular destinations for Gallic tourists in all of Gallic space. Take a look out any of this ship's windows and you will see why.

1120240.text: When I first moved here, I thought Mer Méditerranée was the most beautiful thing I had ever seen. But now that I've been here a while and I have to hear tourists squawk about it all the time, I have grown sick of it. It's just a stupid cloud of gas, people. Get over it!

1120241.text: This whole system is basically focused around tourism and entertainment. The ship you're flying in now is no exception. It's hard to believe people can relax and have fun even when there is so much danger lurking outside.

1120242.text: We have large amounts of spare Cigars in out stocks, so why let them rot in the storage? I take them for a nice price and move them to Luxury Liner Belleville where there is higher demand for them.

1120243.text: The Maquis would love to blow up this ship on one of its many tours around Provence. But thanks to the heavy escort we get from the Royal Navy, they haven't succeeded yet. Thank God the Royal Navy is here to protect us from those savages.

1120244.text: While our subcontractor, Bouvet Space Entertainment, may operate the guest services on this liner, the reason it's such a well-regarded destination is because of the great job we do managing and maintaining the vessel. Remember, that's Solar's name on the side of the liner. Luxury is the name of the game in Provence, and we're up to the challenge.

1120245.text: We have lots of Cigars produced in this system, making our Cigar storage always stocked full. I take the aged ones and move them from here to Gien Space Colony where they are consumed in no-time.

1120246.text: People come to this Luxury Liner to have the best time they could think of, one of the ways is traveling to the beautiful sights that this system have to offer. Not all of the visitors are willing to actually take the trip so we supply it to them using Holotainment Bands. Since the bands degrade over time we need to keep our supplies refilled with large numbers so we bring new ones all the time from Mortagne Production facility.

1120247.text: The Cigars onboard this station are some of the best in Gallia. I think I can help you with a discount. You should make your way to the commodity dealer on this ship and tell them Orva sent you.

A large desert planet. Permanent sandstorms plague its surface, rendering planetary surveys futile.

DIAMETER: N/A

1120366.text: Welcome to the Cointreau Tavern, sir. What may I get you? Ah, we get a lot of military folk in here these days. Not surprising, seeing as Angers harbors a training facility for our Marines and a recoup facility for injured Navy personnel. The war does bring activity to us.

1120367.text: Sirius sounds like an intriguing place. I'm hearing all sorts of stories from the people fighting on the Bretonian front. Seems EFL isn't the only one who knows how to make a mess in open space. The system called "Leeds" appears to be one mighty wasteland.

1120368.text: I overheard a couple of marines talk the other day. Seems their company is being shipped out to the captured Aquitaine system, in preparation for a planetary invasion. They all seem quite eager, I must say. Gloryhounds. Well, I guess there'll be plenty of glory to go around when the fleur-de-lis flies over New London.

1120369.text: Finally, the long wait is over. We've been preparing for these times for decades, and many of us are eager to finally take the fight to the dogs that would have left us to die back in Sol. Sirius will burn for what it tried to do to our ancestors.

1120370.text: Our forces are washing into Bretonia like the tide coming in on New Cote'd Azur. Already we have seized four systems. The Royal Navy is unstoppable - and we shall not stop until every Bretonian station and planet is firmly under our control.

1120371.text: I hope to be assigned to the ground forces deployed to New London when the invasion begins. The way things are going, I bet it'll be less then a year. Second Legion, Marines forever! For the King!

1120372.text: I'm waiting my next assignment. I was wounded in the fight for Quillan, and have been on medical ever since. My recovery has gone well, and I'm ready to return to active duty. With the Navy pushing ahead as far as they are now, I'm eager to rejoin my comrades. I hear they are stationed in Tau-31 now.

1120373.text: The Council is responsible for so much dissent in our nation. It's unbelievable that they still claim to do it for the good of Gallia. The King has seen to the needs of the population. Sure, there are places with hardships, but his Majesty is fair in his rule.

1120374.text: It isn't really my place to question His Eminence, but frankly, I'm a bit worried we pushed into Sirius a bit too soon. With the array of forces we have at our disposal, we could have flattened Marne and secured the north once and for all, before focusing everything towards Sirius. Now, we need to keep a sizable force up north - and the Council forces are spending most their time fortifying their positions. It'll make the fight for Marne all the bloodier.

1120375.text: Ah, I'm just one of the local ground engineers. You flyboys tend to keep us busy - but I'd much rather be down here then up there. The damage I see on some of the craft being checked in for repairs is insane. Heck, we had a Lynx come in out of Lorraine with a missile stuck in it's wing that was about one third the size of the craft itself! Bet the pilot was glad that one was a dud.

1120376.text: We've made considerable progress in ship and weapons tech over the past decade. The writing was on the wall when the king was inaugurated - we'd be saying hello to Sirius pretty soon. It sure made my job a lot more interesting. All this new tech, these new toys - wonderful times for the grease monkeys.

1120377.text: I was one of the maintenance workers on our crowning achievement, the Valor's main cannon. Now there's a gun that'll leave a mark. Sure, repeated firing tends to wear out every power conduit from the reactors to the main firing coils, but that's a small price to pay for a weapon that can drive a round clean through a medium-sized asteroid. I still remember the first test firing. Glorious. A pity the recoil drove the prototype out the rear of the ship it was on, but damn, what a spectacular failure that was.

1120378.text: Ah, yes, welcome. I suppose you're one of the trainees from d'Autun? We get a lot of those here, running maneuvers out in the edges of Anjou. Flyboys will be flyboys, but thirsty flyboys always end up here.

1120379.text: I heard some talk among a squad set to graduate soon. They will be shipped out to the Bretonian front, to a system called "Tau-31". They didn't seem too happy about it though. Something about there not being enough action for them there. Ach, I'm sure they'll find some trouble if they look hard enough. Pilots always do.

1120380.text: I don't get that many customers up here. Most of the navy boys prefer the R and R facilities down on the planet. Although a few selfproclaimed elite fighter squadrons prefer to spend their off-hours up here, practising in the flightsims. Or practising their ability to lift a bottle. Time will tell what breeds the better pilot.

1120381.text: I can't wait to get out there. No, not here in Anjou - out there, beyond the edges of Gallic space, in the captured worlds. Vast asteroid fields, exotic bases, ships and weapons, parts of space never seen by Gallic eye. It'll be one grand adventure!

1120382.text: I hear our boys captured some kind of civilian station on their way to Aquitaine. The civilians actually tried to defy our forces! The base was named Glendale I think. They were pacified without the need for destroying the base itself.

1120383.text: Not everyone who is trained here gets sent south to the front. Many of us are deemed too inexperienced, and are assigned to fly with existing patrols to secure the Core Worlds. That should be a Police task, but frankly, they aren't up to the challenge. Rumor has it they tend to take bribes easily.

1120384.text: My squad is headed out to the northeast of the system to practise some maneuvers. We've set up some virtual targets on the flight comps and I want to see how quick my boys have them all down. We've learned a bit from our early encounters with our new enemies, and have started to train our pilots to predict and counter the enemy movements.

1120385.text: My squad doesn't like me much. Good. I'm not here to be likable. I'm here to make sure those idiots manage to actually stay alive long enough to shoot down a few Bretonians. With the war going as well as it is now, it's too damned easy to get complacant. It is the human factor that remains the weakest in any conflict.

1120386.text: I don't have time for idle chatter. If you have nothing useful to say, move along. Go bother the bartender. That's what he's there for.

1120387.text: This is an old ship, although you'd not notice it from the outside. The Saumur hasn't seen much in terms of actual combat, being an old prototype. If you're looking for scorchmarks on her hull, you'll only find them near the launch bays.

1120388.text: I've just come back from maneuvers with my squad. I'm not ashamed to admit we're far from ready for the front, but we'll get there. Our instructor's a capable man, although he's not the most pleasant to be around. By the time we leave Anjou we'll be a force to be reckoned with.

1120389.text: Many of the recruits signing up with the Navy do so in hope of finding glory our on the southern front. Me, not so much. I lost my father when a pack of Maquis fighters blew up the transport he was on - ever since that happened I've wanted to get revenge. I'll be requesting a posting in Lorraine if given the choice. It'll not be hard to find Council and Maquis forces in that system.

1120393.text: The wreck of a Crayter fighter destroyed during the operation to capture New Tours Watch Station.

1120395.text: A Royal Navy casualty of the battle for New Tours Watch Station.

1120397.text:
>>>WARNING: NAVIGATIONAL HAZARD<<<
The aftermath of the final battle for New London has left a debris field far in excess of that created by the Battle of the Yanagi Pocket that ended of the 80-Years War. Debris from the battle is still re-entering the atmosphere of the planet below and numerous collisions of varying severity between space junk and shipping traffic have already been reported.

The Crown of Bretonia has claimed ownership of all debris within the field and made it clear that any unauthorized attempts to salvage wrecks will be regarded as a criminal act.

1120399.text:
The Charlemagne class warship was designed in the 680s specifically for defensive and support purposes. Battleships of this class are capable of holding and maintaining large numbers of fighters and are equipped with powerful point defense turrets, yet lack powerful anti-capital ship armament. During military campaigns, Charlemagne battleships are used as the rearguard for advancing forces and for guarding supply lines. They are also used for system defense purposes. While stationed within a system, a Charlemagne also serves as a base of operations for the local Navy patrols.

Battleship Le Cendre's last assignment was patrol duty in the vicinity of the stable jump hole between Provence and Ile-de-France. Construction of the jump gate was scheduled to happen eleven years earlier, but the war and criminal activity postponed construction efforts, forcing the Royal Navy to deploy the battleship to that location.

Le Cendre was part of the "Southampton Trinité", comprised of the Battleships Le Cendre, Ambazac and prior to its destruction, Beuvray. Military analysts fiercely debated the intelligence of withdrawing so many forces from the Gallic Core Worlds, but their warnings fell on deaf ears as the Crown pushed for a decisive end to the war.

1120401.text:
CLASS: Triumph
CREW: CLASSIFIED
ARMAMENT: CLASSIFIED
The Bellegarde is one of several ships that mutinied against the Royal Navy following the order to initiate unrestricted orbital bombardment against Planet Leeds, and one of the few ships that managed to escape before it could be intercepted and destroyed. It surrendered to allied forces in the Manchester system and is currently being detained. The Bellegarde's command staff provided vital information on Royal Navy assets in Leeds, including access codes for the Leeds gate sealed by the Royal Navy after their defeat in New London orbit.

1120405.text:
>>>WARNING: RESTRICTED AREA<<<
The Edinburgh Debris Field is a highly radioactive zone of scrap metal and gravitational eddies. It is the remains of the Aquitaine - still known to Bretonians as Edinburgh - Jump Gate, destroyed by the Order of Queen Carina herself. The order was given to destroy the gate when it became apparent that the system would not be recaptured in short order, so as to deny the Royalist remnants any additional avenues of attack should they have chosen to unlock the gate.

The operation to destroy the gate was conducted in secret by the Bretonian Intelligence Service, though from the small scale of the debris and the intense radiation, most speculate that the destruction of the gate was carried out with high yield nuclear warheads directly affixed to the superstructure of the device. Travel into the field is extremely dangerous, and Bretonia has quarantined the area, citing it as a major safety hazard to civilian traffic.

Grenoble was a small space station built by the Council in 727 AGS in order to prepare for the invasion of Languedoc and eventual breach into Sirius. Following this operation, it was given to the Maquis, whom fortified the station for their own purposes. Unfortunately for them, it proved insufficient, as Confederacy intelligence services ended up locating and demolishing the installation in one quick stroke when the Maquis refused to lay down their arms.

1120414.text:
CLASS: Sieyes
GRAVITY: None
DOCKING: No
AMENITIES: None
CREW: 0

Built shortly after the settlement of Planet Marseille, Frejus Base is nestled in a small asteroid field within the Esterel Nebula. The Brigand hideout is notable for reputedly being one of the first locations to experiment with Nox production away from Planet Marseille, though the attempts by chemists aboard the rocky redoubt proved even less successful than the Unione Corse's own efforts at Monaco Base, with the resultant product being of poor quality and quantity.

The rise of the Minarchy made Frejus redundant to the Brigands, as their freedom of movement increased dramatically alongside an even more powerful Corsican presence in the system. Consequently, the base's population gradually declined, turning its back on the notoriously makeshift, uncomfortable Frejus without much regret. By the time the Confederation was established, Frejus had been all but abandoned, allowing the Enclave's battlecruiser Sisteron to move in its cover.

1120416.text:
DIAMETER: 15,029 km.
MASS: 6.11 x 10e24 kg.
TERRAIN: Terrestrial
TEMPERATURE: -32°C to 18°C
ESCAPE VELOCITY: 11.70 km/sec

The Dark Matter storm that has enveloped the planet has rendered all data collection impossible, and little is known about the surface. As the storm moved to consume the planet, what was left of the population on the ground boarded emergency shuttles to safety, with only the a handful of die-hard settlers refusing to leave.

1120418.text:
In the first days after the declaration of the Second Rheinland Empire, the Karlsruhe Fleet, loyal to the Republic, and the Altenburg Fleet, loyal to the Empire, fought each other in battle. The Karlsruhe's command staff was aware that, even though they stood a chance against the Altenburg, the Imperials had reinforcements on the way from New Berlin. Thus, the Karlsruhe Fleet headed forward at full speed, passing through the Altenburg Fleet, raking fire from both fleets causing significant losses to both sides. Successfully passing through the Altenburg fleet, the Karlsruhe set course to the Cologne System, where they intended to escape.

However, the Altenburg was still in pursuit, and within weapons range. Desperation forced the Karlsruhe command staff to improvise. An ancient ruse of war was exploited: fire ships, or their modern equivalent. Several Donau class cruisers, manned by volunteer skeleton crews, were loaded with gravimetric mines and sent the Altenburg's way. On impact, these would detonate, destroying both themselves and whatever they hit, and also whatever smaller ships would find themselves in vicinity. The first was detonated at range by enemy fire, but this prompted the Altenburg command staff to realize what was heading towards them and order immediate evasive maneuvers. No "fire" ship hit its mark and they were easily disabled when the Altenburg Fleet reorganized, as they had no one to man the turrets, but their action allowed the remains of the Karlsruhe Fleet to escape. The Gerlingen was the only one of these ships whose cargo failed to detonate. All crew were rescued, all but the captain. The captain went down with the ship and his body was found lifeless on the bridge. There was a message written in blood on the wall his body was resting against, all in uppercase: "Long live the Republic!".

The crew were taken prisoner, but word has it that they were released in respect for their bravery.

1120429.text: It's irony. Not a week ago I flew with Bernard, whom I thought could be trusted, escorting a prisoner convoy to Fleury-Merogis. The Maquis hit us hard, and although we made it out safely, one of the prison barges was captured by those damned terrorists. Now, a week later, Bernard will be making the same trip again, this time as an inmate. I'm not sure what to think of this.

1120430.text: I don't like all this snooping by the High Commissioner and his ilk. We keep the lanes of Gallia safe from the Brigands, Maquis, Council and all the other assorted riff-raff that tries to make a buck with their guns. And what do we get for gratitude? Scrutiny and disrespect. Bah.

1120431.text: I'm only here as long as it takes the hangar boys to get my ship refitted. I used to be posted in Ile de France, but was recently promoted. My new posting will be out in the Provence system, which will mean working away from the lanes. This requires better sensors - which I'm having installed as we speak.

1120432.text: There are criminals throughout Gallia. It can get confusing with the various groups, so let me give you a quick description of each. First and most common are the Brigands, who as their name suggest are little more than pirates. The Council are more an opposing army then criminals, but are known to hit the occasional transport or two if they carry useful goods. Generally the Navy deals with them, though. The Maquis are nothing more than terrorists, they don't even pick clean ships they destroy. Who else? Ah, the Unione Corse, they can be trouble as well, but are opportunists. Much like the Junkers. But neither of those are considered targets by default. And then there's the Outcasts, an aptly named Sirian group of drug addicts who have been creeping into Gallia through Lorraine and Languedoc. They are priority targets.

1120433.text: I'm hoping to be put in charge of overseeing the Gallic Police operations in Provence, eventually. It'll be quite a challenge, having to be out there without major Trade Lanes to back us up. The criminals have the upper hand there right now, and I want to put a stop to that. It's only a matter of time before the King decides to extend the gate and lane network out there, which will give us the chance to clean that place up in no time.

1120434.text: Have you heard about officer Bernard Lavrie? He was implicated in a Maquis attack on a prison convoy. I always wondered where he got the money for that private Moonbeam from. Guess he'll not be flying that thing any time soon.

1120435.text: I was approached by someone out on the Chateau-Gontier freeport once, while checking on a lead. He seemed to be under the impression that it was legal for an officer to deliver Nox to New Paris, as long as he payed a "transportation fee". I took him into custody for drug trafficking and attempted bribery right there. To my knowledge he is still rotting up in Fleury-Merogis.

1120436.text: All this conquering our Navy is doing is going to create extra work for us. Once a civilian overseer is installed to govern those systems, we'll no doubt be asked to send people to maintain the order of law over those Bretonians. Not a job I'm looking forward to, from what I hear they're quite uncivilized. If I get sent there, I'm going to take a stun baton with me.

1120438.text: Gallic Royal Police\nTours Commodity Trader\nDavid-Jean Fournier

1120439.text: Gallic Royal Police\nTours Weapons Dealer\nSilvestre Thibodeau

1120440.text: Gallic Royal Police\nTours Ship Dealer\nJean Dumont

1120444.text: Have a seat good sir, and have some of the finest wines available in Gallia. Yes, I kid you not. One of the benefits of being the law within Gallia, is that we have first choice when it comes to reappropriating confiscated goods. That includes the private wine stocks of many convicted criminals. Merlot, vintage 435 then?

1120445.text: This station serves mainly as a repair and resupply post for us. There is little of interest here. We get most of our supplies through the Anjou system. Being quiet as it is, many officers here consider a temporary reassignment to Tours to be the equivalent of shore leave.

1120446.text: Ah, yes. The station does have the occasional transport on the scanner. Smugglers no doubt, making a beeline for the Maine system. Something is brewing up there if the rumors hold true - but no one knows what exactly. All I do know is that the postings there have become less popular over the past three months.

1120447.text: The High Commissioner is on a rampage about all the corruption being reported in the lower ranks. He's appointed a Special Prosecuter to ferret out all instances of bribery, excessive fines, and general skullduggery, and will be sending recommendations to the Special Justice Commission for summary executions.

1120450.text:
CLASS: Redemption
CREW: CLASSIFIED
ARMAMENT: CLASSIFIED
1120450.mapped:
Despite being an older design, La Fierte, true to her name, was the pride of Champagne's defenses for over two decades. At the beginning of the Gallic Invasion and the redeployment of the Royal Navy into Sirius, the Council seized the opportunity to advance their own forces. This placed the La Fierte in the sparsely defended Picardy system, where it saw extensive action and eventually victory against the Royal Navy's Battleship Saumur in orbit of Planet Amiens.

The La Fierte joined the De Grasse and Pamiers for the Battle of New Paris, but returned to the Picardy system shortly thereafter to subdue the Royalist's last open stronghold at Fort Etaples. The La Fierte had been posted to Picardy, where her crew enjoyed a quiet post, far from the bulk of the Enclave and Outcasts which are a thorn in the side of most Confederacy systems.

The collapse of the First Rheinland Republic lead to extreme alarm within the Confederal defence ministry. As Gallia heals from its own identity-shattering war, the presence of a new civil conflict on a border once seen as secure has raised questions about the instability of the Republic's new Sirian neighbours. The fall of Rheinland to a resurgent crown has raised some eyebrows within Gallia's old guard, leading to the rapid deployment of the La Fierte from Zurich. The La Fierte is on the alert due to reports that the Karlsruhe battlegroup has sought refuge in Zurich. Whilst the Gallic goverment's pro Imperial and Pro Republic Remenant sides argue decide over the fate of the Karlsruhe, the La Fierte keeps a watchful eye. In addition to fleeing Federalists, the Red Hessians taking control of Cologne and the highly vital trade route to Rheinland is also concern to the Confederacy.

The battlegroup's crew remain mindful of their pledge, to safeguard their newly-found peace against all threats, foreign and domestic.

1120456.text: In the early days of our revolution, we were joined by hundreds of sympathisers. Workers, artisans, soldiers, they all joined our cause. The first battles of the Council against the Monarchy were fought without firing a single shot, and I dare say they were decisive victories for us.

1120457.text: One of the ways the king tries to gain support with the Gallic populace for his war against Sirius, is that their ancestors betrayed us back in Sol, and left us to behind to cover their escape. This is of course a lie, like most of the bile that comes out of the Royal mouths. The reason the sleeper ship Gallia got delayed and arrived long after the others was because of technical failures. Don't believe the rumors that say the other houses did it.

1120458.text: One thing you might see Gallic Royal forces and Council forces cooperate on is the destruction of the Cardamine trade inside Gallia. Neither faction wants to see the Gallic civilian population get poisoned by it. Both Council and Royals fight the Cardamine trade. While we do it to protect Gallia, the Royals have another motive: They don't want anyone other then themselves controlling the minds of the Gallic civilian population.

1120459.text: When we opened the way to Sirius we had no idea what awaited us on the other side. While I still think that it was a good move, we shouldn't have opened the way to Omicron Tau. Now, smugglers use it to bring in Cardamine. We generally permit the trade of "lighter" drugs, but Nox and Cardamine are just fatal. Once you start using them there is no way back, you become addicted and will die without a continuous supply of the poison.

1120460.text: It doesn't matter whether the Royals are right or not about the reasons for the delay of the Gallia's arrival. It is no excuse to embark on some kind of modern crusade against the other nations. Even if they had betrayed us, you can't blame the decendents of those people that live now, eight centuries later, for the deeds of their ancestors.

1120461.text: The revolution is far from over. We will not stop until Gallia is ruled under full democratic control, and the Gallic monarchy is burned in the ashes of its sins. The atrocities of the Royal Family will not stand. Murdering thousands of innocent citizens from both Sirius and Gallia!

1120462.text: The Gap incident wasn't our proudest moment, true, the King's propaganda machine greatly exaggerates the events that took place there. The Royalists often claim that we intended to depressurize the station with the civilians still inside. Ridiculous. Besides, look at what they did to Quillan and Reunion. And they say -we- are barbarians? Hypocrites, all.

1120463.text: It's not often mentioned, but Marne isn't completely under our control yet. While we control the planet and its orbit militarily, civil control is still far from achieved. With a large portion of our soldiers fighting in its defense, we simply don't have the manpower to establish a planetwide police force.

1120464.text: Our engineers are true miracle workers. You should have seen the state of some of the wrecks that were towed back to the shipyards. Not a hull panel left intact on some of those gunboats and cruisers. But in the space of a few weeks, and using half the materials the Royalists use, they manage to refurbish those ships and press them into service. It is those ships that make up the bulk of the Marne defense.

1120465.text: It's true that in any direct confrontation with the Enclave, we would be greatly outnumbered right now. However, the concentration of our forces around Marne dissuades the King from taking direct action. Or maybe he realises that any order to overrun Marne could result in more of his forces choosing the path to a Gallic Republic. It will be quite some time before, if ever, we'll be able to mount any kind of offensive ourselves however. Unlike our brothers in the south, we don't have the luxury of an evacuation.

1120466.text: It doesn't matter that we are outnumbered. Defeating the King purely with military might would make us no better than tyrants ourselves. We have enough to defend ourselves, and to spread our word among the people of Gallia. It is they that will be the deciding factor in our struggle.
