The king would not dare to start opressing entire planets with military might.

1120467.text: Although our forces are concentrated here and around Champagne, we have bases throughout Gallia. Most of these aren't really meant for combat operations. We run supplies back to Marne out of these bases, but most importantly we receive a constant stream of new people who want to join our cause on them. It isn't always easy to arrange transportation however.

1120468.text: Ah, come, have a seat. What will you have? There were those among us that were sceptical about the intelligence that the main push of the Royalist forces would be out into Sirius, stating they would instead come here with that humongous fleet of theirs. Well, I'm glad our intelligence was on the money for a change. It would not have been good for my establishment here if the war had spilled into this system.

1120469.text: It's actually become a little easier to fetch some good wines of late. The Royalists seem content in bottling us up in Artois and Champagne, but they don't seem to be too eager to come at us full force. That suits me fine. While unlikely merchants, the Brigands do bring us the odd luxuries. In exchange for ammunition and supplies, of course.

1120470.text: Some of the bolder members of our organization keep pushing to take the initiative now that the Royalists are slacking off their pressure on us. There have been a few among us that were outright criticizing our decision to concentrate the fleet around Marne. Most of them have since left us, and joined the Maquis instead. Those radicals have no qualms about pressing the attack whenever they see an opportunity, but they are far too reckless for my taste.

1120471.text: It isn't as easy for us to obtain supplies as the Royalists, but we manage. One of the supplies we continuously need is fuel for our ships. We make it ourselves down here on Marne, but need a steady supply of Deuterium to keep the fleet well-supplied. Planet Chateauroux is our primary supplier, although it isn't always easy to get shipments here.

1120472.text: We chose the peaceful path, before Louis IV. Most of our higher ranking members back then were politicians, using the Estates-General to slowly gain support among the planets of Gallia. Louis the Brute, as we now call him, could not accept polls showing over a quarter of Gallia was openly voicing support for us, and manipulated the polls. The civil unrest that followed was the excuse used to outlaw our organization. These events, in effect, led to the foundation of the Council as a military organization.

1120473.text: Yes, we achieved our goal of reunification with Sirius. But at what cost. Thousands are dead, and whether Royalist or Republican, they were Gallic citizens. It is true what they say. All change comes at a price. We must see to it that the sacrifice of those people is not in vain. Our struggle with the Royals can not end until Gallia is free of the monarchy.

1120474.text: Blasting through the minefields was for a long time our only goal. I'm wondering if we didn't actually walk into a Royalist trap while doing it. Clearly they had a huge fleet ready to invade Sirius. We did the dangerous task of minesweeping, and what did it get us? Sure, our southern brethren are setting up somewhere in Sirius, but we're stuck between a king and those half-humans that call themselves Outcasts.

1120475.text: My brother died in the early days of the revolt on Marne. Shot by the riot police in a demonstration at the Marcour bauxite refinery. He was not the only one to die in that revolt, but you'll have to forgive me if the thousands of others mean nothing to me next to my own kin. Twenty four years ago. Let me grieve in peace.

1120476.text: I'm considering joining the Maquis. I do not like being holed up here, building defenses and training new recruits, awaiting the inevitable onslaught. Besides, I owe the Royalists a debt of pain. What was that saying again? All for one, so kill them all?

1120477.text: Fuel for our fighters is always in high demand. Nearly all Gallic subcapital craft run on Promethene, which isn't easy to manufacture. Luckily we have a few key contacts that can send the odd shipment our way. Briancon is one of the places we manage to obtain a steady supply from.

1120478.text: Running cargo between Champagne and our sympathisers in the Core Worlds isn't the easiest job, but it has to be done. Marne can produce a lot, but there are goods that simply have to be imported. Replacement engine parts used to be hard to come by, but as of late the supplies being sent south cause the Brigands to capture the occasional shipment. If the shipment contains capital ship parts, they usually sell them to us. Who else has a need for Gallic capital ship components?

1120479.text: I'm not sure about the Maquis. Yes, they share our desire to bring down the monarchy. But the methods they use, and their excessive brutality is not going to win the hearts of the people. Half the damage they do is blamed on us by the king's propaganda machine, and it's hurting our cause a lot.

1120481.text: Gallic Navy\nLa Fierte Commodity Trader\nRomain Ruais

1120482.text: Gallic Navy\nLa Fierte Equipment Dealer\nDaniel Jobin

1120483.text: Gallic Navy\nLa Fierte Ship Dealer\nBartlett Verreau

1120502.text: If Burgundy is too hot, you can always try Languedoc. A lot of the supplies sent down to the fleet down in Sirius pass by there. The Navy doesn't really start escorting them until they leave the Gallic worlds, beyond Languedoc, so they're pretty easy to hit. Just don't stick around too long in one spot.

1120503.text: I'm just here for some new weapons and hull repair. Had a bad run in with a Navy patrol up in Berry. The bastards drove us out of the asteroid field, straight into the guns of a cruiser. All we could do was scatter and run. Two of my mates got tagged, doubt I'll be seeing either of them anytime soon. Such is life.

1120504.text: If you can get a strong pack together, there's a few places that are very nice to set up an ambush at. Take Languedoc for instance. All the ships going to and coming from Sirius need to come through there, and most of them use the lanes for convenience. Of course, the Police and Navy know this as well, so expect a fight every now and then.

1120505.text: I had a brother down in Languedoc when the Navy rolled over the Council forces there. Until a few days ago, I was sure he'd been wasted in the fighting on Planet Quillan. I got a message though that he tagged along with a whole bunch of Council ships that evacuated to somewhere in Sirius. The message didn't say where exactly, but hey, at least he's still breathing. He still owes me some credits, too.

1120506.text: I handle some of the Nox runs in the edge worlds. I don't use the stuff myself, wine gets me lightheaded enough when I feel like leaving this world for a while. I hear the boys out in Languedoc have found some Sirians that have a drug even more potent. I might have to check that out - several of the folks I sell to keep asking for stronger stuff.

1120507.text: Here's a trick on how not to get tagged by the law. If you see them coming, head for the nearest asteroid field or nebula. If they're still on you in there, just keep running until you run into a Council or Maquis patrol. That will either send them fleeing, or keep them occupied long enough for you to get out of sensor range.

1120508.text: If you intend to make a living as a smuggler - or merchandise mover as we call ourselves - you need to learn the locations of the various jumpholes. Best way to do that is to find yourself a freighter bound for the system you want to go to, and just tag along in formation. If you keep it in one piece, it'll get you to the jumphole.

1120515.text: Have a seat, friend. What will it be? Wine, you say? But of course, we have a fine selection. Take this bottle, Merlot 681 if I'm not misstaken. Sure, the label is a little scorched - sometimes, IDF is not as willing to part with such wonderful Gallic products as easily. Not to worry, it'll taste fine just the same.

1120516.text: Ah, yes, we're not as organized as we could be. Every family, every base has it's own politics, it's own perks, and disadvantages. Besancon is quite secure, and we move a lot of cargo through here, but it's far from the shipping lanes. We don't get as many raiders here as the bases in the core worlds. What we do get lots of are transports - Council, Junkers, the odd Maquis who's in need of particular goods. And of course fellow Brigands looking to get rid of said goods.

1120517.text: I bounced a drunkard out the other day. Babbling about some kind of new wonderdrug stronger than Nox. Something orange, he picked up out in Lorraine. Sirian stuff probably. Me, I'm sticking to good old Gallic Nox when I want to relax. Although I wonder what would happen if you combined the two.

1120518.text: What? Looking to buy some Hull Panels? I got a cargohold full of them. Second hand, slightly charred in some places. In other words, very hot merchandise. Oh, if you intend to put them on your own ship, don't go docking on GMS bases any time soon. Just in case.

1120519.text: Burgundy is quite a nice place to fish. You got supply convoys heading to Lorraine - they can pack quite a whallop, but taking over an ammunition transport ensures there's enough loot for an entire family. There's also Alesia, where a lot of cargo gets transferred. The station itself has strong defenses, but the lanes leading to it, not so much.

1120520.text: There is one fellow down on Deck 9 who does nothing but create Neural Net viruses all day, and he is quite skilled at it too. The last time we unleashed his handiwork, we managed to overload half a dozen power substations, causing an entire city to blackout. It was the perfect distraction for us while we used orbital torpedoes to wipe out their defense grid. Well, we would have if they hadn't malfunctioned. Still, it was a good plan.

1120521.text: The most memorable raid to date for me? Ah, that would have to be on Planet Le Mans, three years ago. A royal party crash, in every sense of the world. One of the king's daughters was visiting the capitol city, and we managed to persuade some key figures in the Police to leave a gap in the security net. The entire city was in an uproar after we set the first few charges off, and that princess was sent running all the way back to New Paris. It took weeks for them to relax their guard after that.

1120522.text: My men and I have this favorite trick we like to use against the Royalists. If we're lucky enough to capture a transport before it can launch a distress beacon, we kill the crew and dump the bodies into space. We bring the ship back to base, fill it to the brim with explosives, and send it back on its planned to course to an unsuspecting Royalist base. If we can moor, we offload the explosives and create as much havoc as possible before withdrawing. If we don't manage to dock, then we just bail out and detonate them remotely.

1120523.text: The last raid on the Versailles residence did not go very well. We had thought the Royalist patrols in the area were weaker now that a large portion of the Navy is outside of Gallia. A single Obstinate was left in reserve however - and by the time we disabled it the element of surprise was gone. No matter, we'll try again another day.

1120524.text: I had a thought not long ago. It's well known that Nox usage is on the rise in all of Gallia, including the Navy. It wouldn't be too hard to spike a shipment of Nox with something. A virus, or a biological agent maybe. Then send it into the chain that'll eventually see it smuggled into the royalists' hands. Since no sane lawhound would ever admit to Nox use, they'd be searching high and low for some kind of other commonality. It has potential, I might propose it to my commander soon.

1120525.text: I'm running supplies for our fighters. Ammunition, fuel, and such. We trade bits and pieces with Junkers and Brigands, and sometimes the Council too, depending on what we can bring back from raids on the Royals. It's not as glamorous a job as that of an infiltration team, but it needs to be done. Without weapons and a bit of fuel, our cause would be severely hampered.

1120526.text: I've gone out in tow on lower risk raids from time to time. A freighter may not pack much in terms of firepower, but it sure helps bring a few liberated goods home. Raiding fuel and munitions depots is high on the list of jobs I want to participate in. The royalists lose the supplies that we gain.

1120527.text: I'll be heading out towards Besancon soon, to pick up a load of Promethene for our fighters. The Brigands aren't exactly the cheapest merchants, but they don't ask questions and get the stuff we need. We managed to liberate a shipment of Engine Components, probably headed for the warfront. It's more than we'll need in the near future, so we sell off the surplus and buy some supplies instead.

1120535.text: This base is one of our favourite hideouts. It is fairly remote, so we are hardly ever bothered by others, except for the occasional smuggler. In this bar, the Maquis come to do two things: remember our glorious victories with great cheer, or forget our losses by drowning ourselves in alcohol.

1120536.text: How does one become a leader amongst the Maquis? That's a good question. I guess it's a combination of things. You need to come up with good plans which keep us alive and send more Royalists to the grave. Prowess in combat or piloting skills aren't a bad asset... but above other things, you must be the most ruthless of us all.

1120537.text: The Maquis are anti-Royalist fighters. We don't steal, we destroy. We are not like the Brigands, who are no better than petty thieves. Admittedly, everyone needs to survive, so we only take that which the dead no longer have need for.

1120538.text: Our transports bring in Counterfeit Software from Evron Base to here. While we may appear to be just terrorists, we are also involved in the black market, which helps fund our operations. Also, we sometimes come across unusual computer technology that we keep for ourselves, if it can be manipulated against the Royalists.

1120541.text:
CLASS: Lucciana
GRAVITY: Complete
DOCKING: Yes
AMENITIES: Yes
CREW: 75
1120541.mapped:
A new addition to the Monaco facility in Provence, the Bastia Extension has all of the latest amenities sealed away behind locked doors for the exclusive use of the Unione Corse's upper echelons and their guests. It is here that plans are decided, deals are made, and friendships are established that will shape the direction the Corse will take in the universe at large.

Traders seeking to provide high value goods are permitted docking rights, but are restricted from journeying beyond the docking bay and the adjacent bar. They are almost certainly under constant scrutiny while aboard.

1120542.text:
A new addition to the Monaco facility in Provence, the Bastia Extension has all of the latest amenities sealed away behind locked doors for the exclusive use of the Unione Corse's upper echelons and their guests. It is here that plans are decided, deals are made, and friendships are established that will shape the direction the Corse will take in the universe at large.

Traders seeking to provide high value goods are permitted docking rights, but are restricted from journeying beyond the docking bay and the adjacent bar. They are almost certainly under constant scrutiny while aboard.

1120544.text: To be honest, it gets lonely out here pretty quickly in the Corse system. I can't wait to go on another smuggling run to Ile-De-France.

1120545.text: I've been studying Sirian language in preparation for some operations across the border. The Corse bosses see big money making opportunities for our family in Sirius.

1120546.text: Some new civilian pilot begged me for a loan a while ago and promised repayment. My gut instinct was to deny his request but he pleaded so much that I finally gave in. Now it's been over two months and he hasn't repaid. When I find that little twerp, I'm going to break his damn legs!

1120547.text: They don't let just anyone join up with the Unione Corse. You need to prove yourself. For my initiation tests, I had to rob three transports in ten minutes and escort the stolen cargo back here without getting caught. I missed the mark by twenty seconds and had to do it again. The Corse don't mess around.

1120548.text: Normally we leave the Junkers alone unless they need to be taught a lesson. In the School of Corse, students get to study the cadavers of their colleagues. Historically, Junkers have been fast learners.

1120549.text: I heard the Junkers have actually been in Sirius for hundreds of years. And even then, they are still viewed as scummy salvagers. Ha! Those Junkers: what a bunch of incompetent failures.

1120550.text: We've been doing surveillance on the few entrances in and out of Gallia, looking for the most valuable cargo that comes through. Soon enough, we'll know exactly who, where, and when to attack the hapless transports. Then there will be big and easy profits for us.

1120557.text: If you've made it this far, that means you're at least in decent standing with the Unione.

1120558.text: I can't wait to expose the Sirians to Nox. If they try it once, they'll be hooked. With our presence in the Gallic black market, that should mean lots more cash for the Corse. We can only hope that the Nox trade one day rivals Cardamine in Sirius.

1120559.text: The clowns in the Gallic Metal Service are really starting to piss me off. They just lack any sense of professionalism. I usually don't like to use force, but I'll make an exception if one of those jokesters try some of their slapstick shenanigans again.

1120560.text: The Royal Police usually don't try to tax us like they do with some of the other groups. After a few fatal incidents a few decades ago, they now know better.

1120561.text: Don't bother looking around this system for any hidden treasures. I've explored all sectors of this system and found nothing of interest.

1120562.text: I heard a Council fighter made a hasty retreat into the Tille Debris Field after a botched attack on a Navy Cruiser heading to the Champagne Jump Gate. Never saw it come out of the field either, I wonder if the Council has a base in there?

1120563.text: The Maquis' leadership are over confident, they think we need them. We do rely on them when it comes to getting the Brigands and Corse to all work together against the Royals, but we don't need them. Without us, they wouldn't be able to function or survive.

1120564.text: The Royal Navy can't touch us here on Macon, because their large capital ships can't enter this astroid field and our defenses are strong enough to dissuade them from sending in smaller strike craft. Through our efforts, the Council in Languedoc was able to break through the mine fields. If we hadn't provided the needed distraction and drawn parts of the Royal Navy into Burgundy, they would have been overwhelmed and defeated.

1120565.text: I don't like the Brigands, but they have proven useful to us. Sometimes you have to compromise in one area to achieve your goals in another area. That is the case with the Brigands.

1120566.text: I'm returning to New Paris, I've made enough to live out the rest of my days in luxury. I'm sure I can make money off selling stories of my time in Sirius if I ever need too. Gallic nobles claim to hate Sirians, but the amount of credits they are willing to part with for trinkets from Sirius says otherwise. They'll never admit it though.

1120567.text: I patrol the lanes between the Rocroi and the Jump Gate to Champagne. Things are usually quiet, because the Council know we are battle hardened veterans here on the Rocroi and they typically don't challenge us. She is an older vessel, a Richelieu-class, but she is fearsome.

1120568.text: You looking to make some credits? The Crown pays those who supply us with arms well. I don't know where you can get them though, you look like the enterprising type though, I'm sure you can figure that out on your own.

1120569.text: Some say times are changing and that we might not survive the war. I laugh at their naivete. Do you think we've only been planting people in Sirius? We knew the day would come when our secret would be made public and we prepared for it.

1120570.text: Living here is no different than living on Rochester Base. If the Police start nosing around too much, we give them some petty criminals or a dead beat smuggler. Just like the LPI, they don't really care as long as it looks like they are doing their job they are happy.

1120571.text: Once you've become a Junker, you are a Junker for life. You don't get to walk away alive with our secrets. Those who sell our secrets and try to hide will be found. When we find them, they will be put to death for their betrayal.

1120572.text: You look surprised to see me in uniform, you thought I'd be a civilian didn't you? No, I am an officer in his majesty's Royal Navy.

1120573.text: Each and every Naval ship has a bar, and bars need bartenders. How do you think morale is kept so high? So, the Navy created its own corp of bartenders.

1120574.text: Naval bartenders go through the same training as any other officer, in addition to spending four months on Marseille learning to bartend. I am as capable of killing you where you stand, as I am of making you a drink. Don't give me a reason to do the former.

1120575.text: The Royal Police are soft, they don't have what it takes to be out in the border worlds. We do most of their job for them, and you'd think we'd get their pay for it, but we don't. Most of them are probably Naval Academy washouts.

1120576.text: I don't understand why the Council want to help the Sirians, they aren't worth helping. I don't even know why the King allows any of them into Gallia at all, but his word is law. If I had it my way, I'd kill them all.

1120577.text: My wife and kid live on Dijon. I don't get to see them much, but at least I know if they are in danger I'll be able to protect them. Most of the families of the Rocroi's crew live on Dijon, while some of the command's families live on Nevers. They can afford it.

1120578.text: Business here is good! While transports are being inspected their crews come here and relax. Being the only bar on the station, they have no choice but to pay my prices and if they don't, they get thrown in the brig.

1120579.text: It is usually the pilots who don't want to pay their tab, and they tend to end up in the brig. Transports can't fly without a pilot either, so ship captains always pay to bail their pilots out. Have you paid your tab, monsieur?

1120580.text: Our brig is usually full as we are the transfer point for prisoners being transfered into the Core. We also serve as a stock pile for weapons used by both the Navy and other Police units.

1120581.text: I escort civilian transports from here out to Beuvray, after that they typically hire the Navy to escort them if they are heading out into the other border worlds. No complaints from me, those systems are still crawling with all types of criminals who would love to space me.

1120582.text: No one uses that Jump Gate without proper permissions, the station has to activate the gate for all users. It is how Ile-de-France is kept safe from the unsavoury type that have made their life in the border worlds.

1120583.text: The Corse tend to harass civilians between here and the Beuvray. They come from the Morvan Asteriod Field. I bet they have a base in there somewhere, but the Navy doesn't seem to care to find it.

1120584.text: We warn civilian convoys as the enter the system that the lanes to Beuvray are dangerous. We offer to escort them to the Beuvray, for a price of course. Those who don't hire us usually don't make it to Beuvray. Can't say we didn't warn them.

1120585.text: We scan all convoys coming from and going to Ile-de-France. Part of our job here is to ensure that illegal goods aren't brought into the Core. You'd be surprised at some of the places people will hide that stuff.

1120586.text: The Navy doesn't patrol the Morvan, they claim that the Beuvray's presence is enough. The Brigands and Corse don't share that view. They hit convoys on their way to Beuvray regularly.

1120587.text: I was assigned here as punishment. I was working on New Paris, but I got on the wrong side of a noble. I know he had a hand in me being sent here. If he thinks it will keep me from his daughter he is wrong.

1120588.text: My love is planning on sneaking aboard an IDF transport on its way here. She'll transmit a signal once in Burgundy and I'll stop them. I'm sure they won't want her father to know they kidnapped her, so they'll pay for my silence. With that money, we'll get a place on Dijon and she'll hide her true identity.

1120589.text: I haven't heard from her since she was supposed to board the transport and I haven't detected her signal from any of the passing transports. I hope she is okay.

1120590.text: On my down time I like to get a stiff drink at the bar. If you want something with a bit more kick than a drink, there are some Corse that can set you up. You didn't hear that from me though.

1120591.text: With all the stuff we deal with here in the border worlds, you'd think the Crown would pay us better. Nope. My pay is horrid. Most of us do things to supplement it though.

1120592.text: You'd think people would see the Council for what they really are, power hungry psychos. They were not able to get the power they crave in Gallia so they sent those loyal to them to their deaths to clear a path to Sirius. They work hand in hand with the Maquis and Brigands. Terrorists and thieves. Yet they claim to be fighting for the people.

1120593.text: The Junkers aren't trusted much, but they play a vital role in Gallia. If not for them Solar Engineering wouldn't have been able to build the Jump Gates or Trade Lanes. No one knows what they truly are or where their loyalties really lie. I don't think they are loyal to anyone but themselves at this point.

1120594.text: You see those Jump Gates and Trade Lanes out there? We built them. We don't just extract and transport oil within Gallia. We build ships and space stations too. GMS provides the materials we need to get the job done.

1120595.text: I haven't seen the Council attack one of our convoys, but I did watch a group of them fly off when a Brigand gang attacked us. How can they be fighting for us, when they allow the Brigands to rob and kill us?

1120596.text: She came to Nevers looking for some Corse, seems there are rumors that they have a shop here. They are false of course. Anyways, we advised her not to go wandering off into town alone with all the fancy jewelry she was wearing. She didn't listen to a word we said though. Couple of days later I saw her getting on a shuttle, all that fancy jewelry was gone.

1120597.text: The Crown has deemed the security of this station a high priority, as such many Royal Policemen now reside on the station. I'd rather be stationed on Avallon, the amenities there are better than those here.

1120598.text: Piracy in the Core and Border Worlds has risen since the Second Gallic Civil War started, and once the Crown makes the push into Sirius it will only get worse. There'll be less Navy and we won't get the support we need.

1120599.text: Using imported metals, Alesia is the primary source of High Temperature Alloy in the border worlds. The Brigands harass convoys making their way to the station, so raw metals fetch a good price here.

1120600.text: We lost a convoy in this system nearly 100 years ago. The Brigands attacked and destroyed it. However, no wreckage from the Pomone was ever found. If it is still intact I bet the cargo is worth a small fortune.

1120601.text: Our motto at IDF is "Loyalty over Profit." It has served us well for hundreds of years. We supply the Navy stationed in the Border Worlds with anything they need. Light Arms are in high demand on most Navy installations.

1120602.text: That debris field to the east is the left over material used in the construction of Alesia and Avallon. It's an eye sore but the higher ups see no profit in cleaning it up.

1120603.text: Sirius represents a wealth of oppurtunity for us. The riches of the Sirians will be ours, even if we have to pry it from their dead hands.

1120604.text: I'd as soon shoot a Junker as I would work with one. For some reason the police the don't bother them, for me, that is just another reason to shoot them. I wouldn't tell them any secrets, those who do tend to disappear.

1120605.text: Our actions have earned us respect from both the Brigands and the Corse, something I'm sure the Council is jealous of. I don't trust the Brigands or the Corse, however, as they are only in it for themselves.

1120606.text: Many of our new recruits come from Marne and most of the booze I have in stock came from there too. Not all of them have what it takes to be a Brigand, those who don't will typically be sent on missions with little chance of success as a means to distract the local Navy or Police patrols, so that other missions don't have to deal with them.

1120607.text: Nox? Of course I don't have any of that! Go away now or I'll have you thrown in the brig!

1120608.text: I always hear the police complaining about the piracy in Burgundy, that the Navy doesn't do enough. Do we have to do our jobs and theirs? I think they are just lazy cowards.

1120609.text: I hear there are Freeports in Sirius too. Though they are run by Zoners? What is a Zoner? You ever met one?

1120610.text: There would be less piracy if the police weren't so damn easy to bribe. They'll claim they don't take bribes, but I've seen them do it myself! Of course, my superior officer doesn't believe me either.

1120611.text: Avallon serves as the Royal Navy's bastion in the Border Worlds. All orders from High Command pass through our comm arrays. You remember the Kings announcement to Sirius regarding the Taus? We relayed that.

1120612.text: Dijon used to have a larger population, then the war broke out and freelance jobs in the Border Worlds became harder and harder to find. Many people went back into the Core looking for work. Can't blame them, sometimes I wish I had done the same.

1120613.text: The lanes are fortified, but attacks on them persist. The Brigands are the ones mostly responsible and they usually get away before we reach the scene. They are getting more daring as the war drags on, they've begun attacking Royal Navy medical transports. The fact that the Council works with these barbarians makes me sick, they should all be executed for their crimes.

1120614.text: My squadron is responsible for protecting Naval supply transports heading to the Battleship Beuvray. Navy officers sometimes say we don't do anything here in the border worlds, but if it wasn't for us their supplies would be stolen by the Council or the Brigands. What would they do then?

1120615.text: Some Gallic citizens claim we are corrupt. That is all they are, claims. They've nothing to back those claims up. Those who say they have proof are usually criminals and when we try to arrest them they attack us and we're forced to defend ourselves.

1120616.text: You a Junker? If you are, hit the road. I don't serve Junkers here, they can't be trusted. You have a problem with that? I have this badge that says you don't.

1120617.text: I'm surprised by the number of non Gallic citizens in Gallia now. Before, it seemed like the King wanted all of Sirius dead....now he allows some of them into Gallia. I'm not sure what to make of it. Perhaps our intelligence on the King's intent was wrong. No one else will even consider that.

1120618.text: Some of the Council complain that the Brigands steal from civilians. I don't see the issue, the corporations keep the common folk under their thumb, stealing from them and killing them hurts the Crown in the long run. The Royals can't operate without fuel and supplies, can they?

1120619.text: The Junkers are Royal spies who stole technology and information from the Sirians for the Crown. If we didn't have to depend on them for some supplies, I'd just as well shoot them too. Many Council members share that sentiment, but not all.

1120620.text: We may have the influence within the government, but that does not mean we've got an automatic get out of jail free card. If some of those newly joined members are stupid enough to get caught, we at least know they are not worthy to be in the Unione Corse.

1120621.text: Sirius is a challenge for us. It is a chance to get new business deals and contacts, which means even more influence. We must be careful, though, because the Sirians have the same opportunity here. What benefits us is that the government does not look fondly on foreigners.

1120622.text: This war has allowed the Brigands to grow in size, but they are still just a bunch of unorganized thieves. They lack proper skill and technique to be as effective as we are. They know this and they know if they cross us we'll put them out an airlock. This is why they rarely cross us.

1120623.text: The Brigands might be a bunch of unorganized theives, but they know how to build combat worthy space vessels. We modify them to suit our needs of course, but you can't deny their ability.

1120624.text: I doubt many of the Sirian Junkers knew what it was they were really doing for their leaders. They had to have known something was up though, where did they think all of the stuff they gathered went? Most of them probably ignored it in favor of the credits they were making.

1120625.text: We know the Sirian Junkers eventually killed some of their own, as a sign that they did not support their actions on behalf of Gallia. After this, they will of course side with those they live among. We expected this and planned for it. We've agents in all levels of their organizations. They will continue to serve us, they just won't know it.

1120626.text: All manner of goods cross the floor of our bazaar. Everyone from the Corse to Gallic nobles come here to fulfill their desires and we aim to help them, as long as they have the credits.

1120627.text: I volunteered to be on the advance force that took the Tau region. My commander denied my transfer, likely because my father asked him to. He says that a noble like me is more valuable in the Core.

1120628.text: When the Council runs out of supplies and resources on Marne, we will make a push into Champagne. Unlike in Languedoc, the Council forces will have nowhere to flee! We'll wipe them out and all that will be left of the Council will be the cowards hiding in Sirius.

1120629.text: The Beuvray is a Normandie-class battleship, which has seen extensive modification. She might not be on the front lines destroying Sirian battleships, but she is still a fearsome ship. She's one of the reasons the Council uses guerilla tactics in this system.

1120630.text: Countless tourists pass through the resorts here on a daily basis. All of them are scanned and searched as they arrive and as they leave. This is how we make sure no illegal drugs make it planet side. Of course we know we don't stop everything and admittingly we do make mistakes too.

1120631.text: Came across a smuggler while on patrol yesterday, he didn't cause any trouble and wasn't doing anything illegal so I didn't see a reason to mention it in my report. I got this fancy new coat today, cost me 3,000 credits. It's made of some Sirian animal.

1120632.text: When I got assigned a post here on Nevers, the Royal Police set me and my family up with a house planetside. My wife wanted her parents to move out here also, but they coudln't afford it. Guess who paid? I'm not crazy though, I set them up with a place on Dijon.

1120633.text: The companies that run the resorts here on Nevers pay both the Royal Navy and the Royal Police to protect their passenger transports. If you have the right connections you can get those gigs and they pay handsomely.

1120634.text: The Council are nothing more than terrorists. They say they are fighting for the people, the working class, yet they do nothing to stop the Brigands from robbing and killing civilian workers.

1120635.text: We are the premier shippers in Gallia. Since the outbreak of war many of our transports have been tasked with supplying the Royal Navy's advancing fleets. It's dangerous, but the pay is excellent. I make more doing those runs than my husband does as a Royal Policemen.

1120636.text: Since then we haven't had any problems with that gang of Brigands. We've sighted some of their ships, but they were flying with another gang. Only time I've seen a gang of that size dissapear is when their leader is killed.

1120637.text: We've been ordered to target the Maquis in this system, over Council. I think their actions here have caused a stir in the Royal Court. I made a deal with a group of Junkers, they help me and I'll help them.

1120638.text: The Navy think we can't handle the pirates here in the Border Worlds. Why would we? They do it and we get paid to do it. It's a good setup we've got.

1120639.text: IDF and EFL blindly follow the Crown. We're smarter than that, we keep to ourselves and don't show the fervor for the Crown they do. The Council and some of the pirate groups know this and harass us less because of it.

1120640.text: I overheard Gauguin over there talking about losing his family to the Maquis. If you know the location of a Maquis base, he'll buy the information off you. Not sure what use he has for that kind of information.

1120641.text: We have a very close working relationship with EFL. They build the Trade Lanes, and we haul the materials and other supplies for them. I haven't seen a Sirian Trade Lane, but I hear they have green lights on them.

1120642.text: I watch our miners take trips to nearby Planet Nevers, pouring their hard earned credits into the casinos and bars there. They always return with tales of romantic encounters with beautiful core worlders. If their wives got wind of it, I don't think the police could protect them.

1120643.text: The monarchy was suppose to make our nation prosperous. All they did was make themselves rich and powerful. That is the reason I've no problem with stealing from them, their possessions are rightfully mine.

1120644.text: The rich are always visiting Nevers, we used to take their credits and belongings. Now we take them too and sell them to the Outcasts. I'd sell the poor just as well, but you don't find transports full of them very often.

1120645.text: Navy activity in the area picked up after the Council took Champagne from the Crown. The jump hole to Lorraine is their only means of accessing that system, my squadron is tasked with destroying every supply convoy heading to Lorraine.

1120646.text: We control most of the black market in Gallia, if we find anyone encroaching on our turf, they meet a bloody end. You'd be wise to remember that.

1120647.text: We've pushed the Council out of Languedoc, it is only a matter of time until we do the same in Champagne. I hope I get assigned to the units sent there. I'll teach those traitors a lesson.

1120648.text: There aren't as many people in Burgundy as there used to be. When the war broke out, most of them fled back to the Core systems' safety. We're here to protect those who remain from the Council.

1120649.text: My wife has her eye on a certain holoscuplture she saw on Gap Station. They want 2,000 credits for it? 2,000! Can you believe that?

1120650.text: Any news from the front lines? I hear we pushed Kusari back into their little hole and they sued for peace. I hope there is still some fun to be had when I get up there.

1120651.text: A patrol confisated some cargo from a Junker last week. Turned out he was hauling some Liberty Ale. Stuff tastes like piss if you ask me, but you're more than welcome to a glass.

1120652.text: We don't actually own Dijon, we are merely tasked with its defense and ensuring order aboard the station. As such we control who can and cannot dock to ensure the safety of the civilians aboard. This also aids in our ability to stop illegal goods from being brought onto civilian stations.

1120653.text: We don't own Dijon, we just control the docking and mooring controls and are responsible for protecting the station from enemy take over. Many of the people working on the surrounding stations live here. The station provides shuttles between Dijon and their work places.

1120654.text: I don't trust the Junkers at all, but they sometimes provide sound information. We're always wary when they give us info, they usually only do it to get out of trouble. Junkers aren't poor, they were paid well for their services and many of their leaders live lives of luxury on New Paris.

1120655.text: The Crown weeded out all the corrupt officers, those whom they didn't catch joined the Council as they feared they would be caught. That is what the Council is full of, corrupt police officers and Naval officers who were upset they got passed over when promotions were handed out.

1120656.text: Even though we are in the border worlds, we still get plenty of VIPs coming through here. They think that just because they are rich and important they are above the law. They try to sneak contraband aboard thinking we'll look the other way.

1120657.text: Until the King and the government make some changes, I'll continue to fight for the Council. I fight for a free Gallia, free from enslavement to a monarch, free from enslavement to corporate executives, and free of crime.

1120658.text: I took part in a raid on a military supply convoy, they were hauling Oil and basic supplies to Languedoc. After hitting the convoy a few times, it became clear we wouldn't be able to destroy the transports due to their escorts. So one of our wingmen said he'd take care of it. He flew off, and in the distance we saw a large explosion near the Trade Lanes! He rammed his Gecko right into the bridge of the transport!

1120659.text: I'm not sure how we are going to win this war. We didn't expect to be pushed out of Languedoc so easily. We're only able to survive here because the Royal Navy can't get their capital ships in here and their strike craft aren't much of a threat to the base. We can fend them off easily enough.

1120660.text: We do indeed work with the Brigands sometimes, but that does not mean we like them or even trust them. They would rather use brute force and some of them even try to turn a profit at our expense. Those usually find themselves floating in space.

1120661.text: Some Brigands took out the Quenza. They used police weaponry thinking no one would be able to identify them. None of the ones responsible survived the week. Not only do we have various government offcials in our pockets, we've also a number of Brigands there also. I'm sure they lost no sleep over the death of their fellows either.

1120662.text: The Maquis are what the Council should be if they ever hope of overthrowing the Crown. The Council leadership can't help it, they are fighting as they were trained to by the Royal Navy and the Royal Police. The Navy knows their next move before they do. With the Maquis, they keep the Navy guessing. That is why they are successful.

1120663.text: Took awhile to cleanse this place of the Junker stench. I think I used thirty or so liters of bleach in here. We'll never have that issue again, they wouldn't dare set foot here.

1120664.text: Bourg-en-Bresse was only built after our former base was taken over by the Corse, I'll never trust a Corse because of that. Bourg has served as our base of operations in the Border Worlds, though most of the high ranking members reside on New Paris.

1120665.text: The Council has indeed put us in a dangerous position, but they've also opened up many opportunities for those willing to take the risk. We know many of our own goods are in high demand in Sirius and the demand for Sirian goods in the Core is extremely high. A bribe here and there can ensure your transport is free to trade between our home and Sirius.

1120666.text: We've seen an increase in Brigands on our bases who are traffiking illicit Sirian goods. They don't trust us, but they don't have a choice but to deal with us. They've no other way to get their goods planet side, since doing it themselves would be suicide. Except for Marne, of course, but who has credits on Marne?

1120667.text: Lorraine is much better defended than Languedoc ever was. Despite numerous attempts by the Council to breach our defenses, they have always failed. None of our stations in Lorraine have ever been captured by the enemy, and it is unlikely any ever will be.

1120668.text: I patrol the lanes between this battleship and the Languedoc Jump Gate. I see this as a test of my abilities, and once I prove myself I'll get assigned to a unit heading to fight the Bretonians.

1120669.text: You'd think those Junkers would have learned their lesson when we raided Bourg-en-Bresse, but no, they still deal with all manner of criminals. Let me catch a member of the Council on Bourg-en-Bresse and we'll teach them a lesson for harbouring terrorists they won't soon forget.

1120670.text: What? You surprised to see an officer running this bar? How do you think we keep order on this station? We control the sale of alocholic beverages. If I think someone is too drunk, they get cut off. Makes our lives that much easier.

1120676.text: Care to buy a hero a drink? Well, technically I'm not a hero yet, but just you wait. I hear there's a Gallic battleship on the other side of this Jump Gate. I can't wait for the chance to drill one up its backside!

1120677.text: These Gallic numbskulls don't know how deep they've stepped in it, that's for sure. Why, we just beat the pants off the KNF, and nobody's going to take Leeds from us again. Let them try it. Every pilot in the fleet will gladly die for the Queen!

1120678.text: Why do you look so skeptical? You're one of those defeatists aren't you? You're worse than the invaders! At least they're willing to fight. If we just gave up and pulled back we couldn't look ourselves in the mirror. Bretonian honor is worth fighting for. I can't wait for my next patrol! Bartender, another round for the bar on me! I'm going to be a hero!

1120679.text: Half the time these fresh out of the Academy lads make me sick, the other half I just smile and remember what it was like to think you could take on the galaxy. The truth is, war is death and destruction. Glory is just for Admirals, politicians, and supply clerks. Oh, and recent Academy graduates.

1120680.text: It's true, the Gallic fleet controls the other side of the Jump Gate. I hear that we're about to make an attempt at a breakthrough five or six times a day. It's all from the paper pushers or the louts in engineering, though. The pilots, the ones who saw action in the Kusari war, they know better. We didn't beat Kusari back, they just got steamrolled from behind like they did to us years ago, and limped back to Kyushu, 'cept for those battlewagons they managed to leave behind in Leeds and Newcastle, that is.

1120681.text: It's pretty hard to believe that these Kusari battleships stuck behind our lines are supposed to be on our side now. Probably hard for them to believe it too. The brass seem to believe it, though. Maybe they know something I don't, or maybe they just believe their own hot air. For certain, I know a few dozen pilots who'd like a little friendly payback if they pop their heads up out of those debris fields they're hiding in.

1120682.text: I never thought I'd say it, but bless those Samura chaps! We thought it might take months to get Stokes operational again, but it turns out that Samura left all our old equipment in place and even upgraded some of the machinery. Not a speck of rust on anything, either. Must be all that fish oil dripping off their breakfast-lunch-dinners. I just wish they took the smell with them when they turned tail and ran back to Kusari.

1120683.text: The local BAF pilots are strutting around all confident that they can beat back these Gallic invaders, but I'm not so sure. We've got orders for ship hull panels coming in faster than we can fill them, and too many of our previous machinists are too afraid of the invasion fleet to come back to work here. I don't blame them. I was here the last time we had to abandon this station. That was no stroll through the park, let me tell you.

1120684.text: War is good for business, either if you're winning it or supplying the winner. I don't know how Bretonia is going to fare against Gallia, but Liberty is buying ship hull panels like they're planning on replacing their whole fleet. Come to think of it, I hope that doesn't mean they've lost that many ships to Rheinland. Losers don't tend to pay their bills on time. Excuse me, I need to go talk to the accounting department.

1120685.text: The cooks say they've scrubbed down the kitchen twice from top to bottom, but still everything they serve has a fishy taste. The way things have gone the past few years it will probably wear off just in time for Gallia to show up and seize the station.

1120686.text: This must be the strangest peace treaty I've ever heard of. After all the effort to retake upper Leeds and drive Kusari out, we're left with a Kusari battleship as our "guest" in the system. The Armed Forces ought to board that battleship and use it against Gallia, not let it sit there spying on us for them. Allies? I don't trust those Kusari for a minute!

1120687.text: I can't believe that after all the lives lost trying to retake Stokes from Kusari, we get one of their battleships as protective cover! Those rear area big shots have really lost their wits this time!

1120690.text: Why in blazes did you stop off here? It wasn't for the liquor, I know that. This stuff is third rate, if its not recycled, and I'm not too sure it didn't go down somebody's drain before it ended up coming out of our esteemed bartender's tap. But, it's not like I joined the Guild for the refreshments. I wanted excitement, adventure, and beautiful ladies swooning over my medals. From what I can tell, regulations prohibit refreshments, excitement, adventure, and ladies from boarding this station. I think they're minting the medals from tin now, too.

1120691.text: The Guild used to do quite well running bag and tag raids against Gaians and Mollys in this region. Things are rather up in the air now that Gallia has arrived in force. At least Kusari didn't disrupt Edinburgh like Gallia has. I rather wonder if the Gaians think they've got some breathing space now, or if they are really feeling the heat.

1120692.text: The Guild sent an emissary through the Edinburgh gate to see if the Gallic Navy was open to allowing us to continue hunting Gaians in the system. That was days ago, but there has been no sign of him. The BAF has forbidden any further use of the gate, unless it is for military purposes. We're taking bets on whether the Gallic Navy shot first and scanned later, or if our man is going to sit out the war in a Gallic brig, hoping the BAF doesn't blow the ship to smithereens.

1120693.text: Bowex is making a fortune supplying Bretonia's battleships. MOX, munitions, and light arms are in constant demand. We even transport Marines up here, although they just seem to mostly sit around polishing their boots.

1120694.text: I'm not too keen on transporting prisoners, but the BAF is footing the bill to take them to Newgate Prison, and it's better than flying empty.

1120695.text: These fleet supply runs are stable money makers, but I do worry about showing up just as an assault is getting underway. Knowing the admiralty, I doubt they're going to give us any warning to stay away if they decide to launch an assault, or if Gallia launches an assault, for that matter. The BAF would probably be happy to have us cluttering up the enemy's targeting systems.

1120696.text: There were some dark days during the war with Kusari, but this feels different...more ominous somehow. At least we knew who our enemy was in the last war. We had never even heard of these Gallic chaps until just a short time ago. Still haven't seen one. Some say they aren't even human, can you believe that? Next we'll be asked to believe in alien abductions and body snatchers!

1120697.text: Soldiers and pilots always want a good drink, but when they have just got done killing, they really, really want a good drink. When they're just sitting around for days on end biting their nails until the action starts, well, that's when I double up on my supply orders for the really strong stuff.

1120698.text: One thing you learn in this business is that peace is good for running up bar tabs, war is good for running up bar tabs, and well, the only thing you really need to know is that dead men don't pay their bar tabs. I always invoice the glory hounds more frequently than the cowards. You can count on a coward to do his best to make it back to the bar.

1120699.text: I thought our Bauxite would be welcome here, given this House needs raw materials to keep itself going, especially with these angry Gauls at their doorstep. But the locals seem extremely hostile to us. I'm keeping my Crowdkiller close, that's for sure.

1120700.text: With the extended strike of the miners here on Leeds, Daumann saw an opportunity to offer the Bretonian government an alternate supply. Sure, we're being used as strikebreakers by a competitor, but BMM is paying us quite well for it.

1120701.text: I'm surprised that this strike went on so long without the government stepping in to reestablish order. In Rheinland the Rheinwehr would have long since taught these traitors a lesson. You don't backstab your own government in a time of war.

1120704.text: When you sign on with the King's Navy, you know that a bit of trouble is part and package of the job. When you sign up with the catering corps, you expect things to be a bit quieter! I really drew the short-straw with this assignment. The air smells fouler than the Bretonian Queen's breath, and the natives are duller than the Council's rhetoric! That's saying something!

1120705.text: The spaceport is the safest place to be posted, relatively speaking. I'd rather be aboard the RNS Oubli serving drinks, mon ami. We have a small regional relay generator rigged up that covers the area with a deflector umbrella. That stops a lot of the shells from getting through, but the Bretonians have been learning and are attempting to fire shots under it at extremely low trajectories. Just a few days ago, they took out a medical corps field module with one of those.

1120706.text: The food we're provided with is absolutely diabolical! How is a Gaul supposed to live on freeze-dried foreign rubbish imported all the way from Kyushu? We need flavour! We need texture! We need aroma! There's only so much one can do with ration packs. Still, at least we get our food regularly here in the interior. The troops on the front can't get anything if their supply freighters are shot down.

1120711.text: Merde! Command told us this was a planet full of miners. It seems that the Bretonian army has given every single one of them a weapon! It is sadly ironic that we were previously ordered to pen in their Refugee convoys - if they'd got out, there'd be less people shooting us in the streets now. I wonder if intelligence actually knows how many men we'll be fighting down here...

1120712.text: I feel sorry for the Armée de Terre soldiers on the ground - they're getting butchered out there. After we took the spaceport, Command ordered them to press on into the cities. The first three waves were shredded, but we took reasonable gains. We're holding our ground until we can muster more reinforcements from the Core Systems - then the rest of this planet will be ours. If these damn Bretonians push us back, we'll level the area from orbit!

1120713.text: The Bretonians may think they still hold the planet, but we're steadily advancing and have full orbital control! I'd like to see them last out the year when we're sitting on their precious food supplies from this... what was it? Cambridge, oui? We see everything that goes in, and nothing goes in without our say-so.

1120714.text: All I can say is that I am glad I was assigned to the Navy's fighter corps and not the logistics division. Logistics are having to ferry essential supplies down from orbit on a daily basis, to keep our soldiers equipped with weapons, ammunition and food. The Bretonians have been targeting them with anti-ship ground missiles. At least in space you can strike back against your foe! Here, there's just an endless sea of ruins and hidden rebel rats with anti-ship rockets and anti-armor blasters.

1120716.text: I work here as a gunnery liaison between the armée and the RNS Oubli. I provide the targeting coordinates for their torpedo strikes. It's difficult work - due to atmospheric turbulence, the salvos are often imprecise, and guidance isn't very effective due to the nature of those torpedos. It would be a simple matter to literally obliterate entire cities from orbit, but that denies Gallia the infrastructure that is already in place. And we need those industries. We're not allowed to damage it any more than we absolutely have to.

1120717.text: In the short time I've been here, I've already burned out five targeting calibrators. The atmospheric conditions are simply terrible - nothing in Gallia can prepare you for the squalor you will have to endure on this sordid rock. I don't honestly think our equipment is up to the task of fighting in such conditions. We already have scores of men reporting mysterious ailments due to exposure. We need better air filters and hazard suits, at the very least.

1120718.text: A big part of my job in this particular warzone seems to be explaining to furious armée captains why we can't simply carpet bomb the cities flat from orbit. While it's easy enough for Command to demand that we take this planet intact, it's less clear how that is done from a local perspective, when you have Bretonian insurgents garrisoning the factories and firing missiles at our supply ships. They're more or less using their own infrastructure as a hostage.

1120719.text: Residential areas do not need to be preserved, so if we have enemy activity in one, we level the entire block. Watching the habitation tower blocks burn is an interesting sight. Each has a pressurized internal atmosphere. When a room is breached, you hear the hiss of the air escaping and can see the smog being disturbed by the eddies. You'd hope they'd been evacuated, but you really can't tell with these Bretonian worms. They probably locked entire schools of children inside in order to call us monsters on the evening news.

1120721.text: There is an entire regiment of engineers and sappers stationed here on Leeds. Whenever these Bretonians fall back from a position, they leave the area rigged with traps and bombs - it is our job to clear the area so the armée can advance. I've seen nothing of the like since last dealing with the handiwork of Marquis terrorists. The sooner these barbarians are all put to the sword, the sooner we can restore some civilised law to the region.

1120722.text: The Crown wants this planet captured intact - we need the forward manufacturing capability if we are to push onwards and deeper into Sirius, bringing retribution to the cowards who betrayed us. The Bretonians seem adamant to destroy themselves before they will work with us - they detonate their own infrastructure before we can seize it. It is despicable. They selfishly throw away the lives of their soldiers and civilians in order to spite their betters.

1120723.text: It seems all is not well behind enemy lines. Shortly before our conquest of Leeds, it appears there was some kind of... rebellion? A strike, perhaps - Bauxite miners, I believe. That certainly provided the foundations for the collaborating Wilson Government. I heard a pair of commissars gossiping about one such miner who had been feeding us information in exchange for promises of rewards and titles. As if a peasant could ever join the ranks of the nobility. Foolish Bretonian.

1120724.text: Bah, you can tell where the armée has trod by looking at the local factories. Anything we need - gone. These Bretonian bastards are destroying anything that might have value to us. Ship factories are rigged to explode as we occupy them... smelters collapse as we pass. This scorched earth - it's maddening! Even if the swine do inconceivably manage to throw us off the planet, they're condemning their own House to a slow, painful death.

1120726.text: In this sector, we currently hold a perimeter around the city - that's the spaceport, industrial slums and some hab blocks - the ones that are still standing. The armée is crawling across the continent, but it's a slow, vicious fight. We've had varying luck on the other fronts. We've not deployed all of our men, but I'm not sure Command would really want to when we could simply starve these rats out. Then again, who am I to second guess the motives of the Général d'armée?

1120727.text: I cannot understand why some of these peasants fight on. Their government and Queen has abandoned them, their Navy has scurried away to hide behind the skirts of their allies and their neighbours and countrymen have colluded to ensure their survival. The Bretonian Lord Wilson leads those wise enough to see the futility of their fight. Those who collaborate with their new masters immediately will be amply rewarded. Those who continue their pointless war? Well, no quarter will be given. They can either be vassals or dead - the choice is theirs.

1120728.text: Orbital superiority has its uses - it's rendered Bretonian armor largely useless, for starters. Upon spotting large armored columns mobilising, we simply call down the firepower of the RNS Oubli and incinerate them. Of course, they seem to be learning - last week they punched a hole through the western walls using siege hovertanks that were hiding under a portable shield relay. Our sappers took them out with ground charges in their path, but it was a close thing. We weren't expecting this kind of resistance anymore.

1120729.text: Did you know that in the first week, we landed one hundred and twenty thousand troops? In the first three battles, we took almost forty percent fatalities. Impressive numbers, non? No doubt the Bretonians came off for the worse, but they do know the land. As we initially withdrew to fortify the spaceport walls, I received reports of entire platoons being lured into toxic sumps, then butchered as they attempt to flee. It's barbaric, and beneath anything I'd expect from a civilised military force.

1120731.text: We have an artillery firebase here in the spaceport. We liaise closely with forward chasseur units to locate enemy forward bases, then obliterate them from afar. My own emplacement consists of a battery of Grande Bombards, which have an effective range of almost 350 kilometers. Getting solid information on targets that far out is the issue.

1120732.text: When you step outside, you hear the constant roar of the guns, non? That would be my men, the 342nd Royal Artillerie. When the Armée de Terre's first wave were thrown back from the city after planetfall, our unit was tasked with obliterating the residential hab-blocks surrounding the spaceport. They were a warren, giving the Bretonians an ideal firing position on our men as they disembarked. Watching those buildings crumble was a pleasure.

1120733.text: My CO, Captain Renault, was killed the day before yesterday - a sharpshooter with an energy rifle struck her in the heart. She was dead before the medical corps could medevac her off the planet - a sad day, as a true hero was laid low by the treacherous Bretonian snakes. In retaliation, my batterie of Grande Bombards levelled the area the sniper was believed to be working in. We received a reprimand for excessive use of force, but at least that sniper won't be bothering anyone anymore. He's buried under 200 tons of rubble.

1120735.text: Lord Evan Wilson is the saviour of the people of Leeds. It was he who first negotiated with the Gaul fleet marshals and he who established the Breton Protectorate as a protectorate of the Kingdom of Gallia. The Queen and Bretonia abandoned us - what do we owe them? We look to the survival of our families and our planet. Lord Wilson has provided that.

1120736.text: For those who cooperate with Gallia, there are opportunities to be had. A life to live. You can purchase work visas for their corporations once you have been security cleared. They also provide us with a ration of food. It is not much, but it stops us starving. Those who continue fighting will have to resort to eating their boots before long.

1120737.text: The people of Planet Leeds have been at the bottom of the pile for centuries. We've been an untouchable caste, shunned by the wealthy of New London and the academics of Cambridge. We're just an inconvenient necessity for them, required to build the things they want. Why should we put up with that? As the first members of the new Breton Protectorate, things will be changing here. Soon New London will know how it feels to be the oppressed class!

1120739.text: Leeds has been a part of Bretonia for hundreds of years - nothing changed that, not even the civil war. It seems wrong that we should lose our heritage now, after so long fighting to save it... But we have to think of our families. Lord Wilson made the hard choices that the others were unwilling to make. Even if I don't like living with Gallia, I would rather cooperate and earn a wage than resist and earn a noose.

1120740.text: What Lord Wilson did has got people here pretty riled up. Most of us recognise he did what he had to do to save all of our lives, but there're some who disagree. There's killing going on, even in the 'pacified zones' that the Gauls have conquered. For every man and woman who's quietly trying to resume their lives, there's another preparing bombs or feeding information to the Queen's Army. They'll destroy everything for all of us!

1120741.text: As well as the Army, there's a resistence movement forming. So far, they seem to just be passing on information on what the Gallics are doing and... who's working with them. The captain of the battleship in orbit has already said there's a death-sentence for anyone who cooperates with the resistence, and a bounty for anyone who turns one in. I don't know if I could do that, but if they keep reducing the food rations...

1120742.text: This is one of the most dangerous contracts IDF has taken. Our freighters pick up goods from transports that moor in orbit, then shuttle them down to the spaceport. It's a seven minute descent from your worst nightmares, and the Bretonians will go hell for leather with the anti-air when it comes to taking us out. We have to replace our our retroburners once every three drops because of the intensity of the evasive manoeuvres we pull.

1120744.text: Whatever the squaddies tell you, the navy isn't all gone. Not all of us scurried off to New London and Newcastle. I used to fly for the Derby, before she rammed a hole in the side of the Villeneuve to try and buy time for the rest of the fleet. After that, I ignored orders to retreat and flew my Crusader back to Leeds. There's a wing of us here, along with some Police Authority interceptors, waiting for the moment to take to the skies and make an impact. They don't know we're here. The element of surprise will be with us.

1120745.text: Even if I'm grounded at the moment, there're benefits to having a pilot on the surface. No-one knows how to kill an enemy ship better than someone who used to do it on a daily basis. I've been out to the front several times, training the missile battery crews. Usually we're targetting logistics freighters, seeing as the Mollys, Gaians, and Outcasts don't like sending their expensive fighters down into the smog. Makes sense since space superiority fighters lose their maneuverability in the atmosphere - ground based guns have an easy time taking those out. We've got a good kill rate so far, despite losing Leeds.

1120746.text: The battleship in orbit is an issue, but it's one we can deal with. We've found ways to mess with their sensors - recalibrating the shields on our armor to absorb their torpedo targeting lasers was a good first step. We're trying to crack their communications so we can redirect their guidance completely, but that could take some time. Wouldn't it be a shame if a few Frog munitions dumps got vapourised by their own ship?

1120747.text: It's challenging working as a Police Officer right now, with the war on the ground. Also the fact that we've got cities that change control from the Armed Forces to the Gauls from week to week doesn't make it easier. We try to make sure the front line is evacuated, but some folk just won't leave. I still can't believe that people are staying in their homes while there is a war going on right infront of their doorstep. Stubborn Leedsmen.

1120748.text: Whenever we manage to get some ground back we try to get all civillians out so that casualties can be kept at a minimum when the line rolls back again. Keeping control of it all is hard, criminals that take advantage of this war are not rare, catching them is nearly impossible - when we do, they are generally tried under martial law and executed. We have no tolerance for profiteering. Luckely most of the civillians didn't make a big fuss up until now, I just hope that we don't have to start rationing.

1120749.text: The Armed Forces and the Police here on Leeds aren't really two different entities anymore to be honest. I've done my fair share of shooting aswell. Every able body needs to fight or we won't win this, that much is certain. We've also already educated some basic skills to a few Civilian Auxiliary Volunteer units, mostly in laying boobytraps and the likes. Those also gather cursory intelligence in the occupied areas.

1120750.text: Oh God, I never realised how horrible atmospheric landings were until I took this job. Food Rations, Consumer Goods and Pharmaceuticals to the troops and stranded civilians, Casualties and Refugees out. The fatality rate for blockade runners is pretty high though, so usually people won't risk it unless they're really desperate. We actually hold a funeral for each freighter crew before they set out, just so we can have a bit of a last party. Probably isn't doing my liver any good.

1120751.text: Operations centers are always on the move, and can never be approached directly. Once the Frogs realised what we were up to with the supply runs, they intentionally let a few ships through unchallenged, then glassed the area where they landed. We lost a depot or two that way. Now we use sensor decoys and signature spoofs to throw their scanners off during the descent. We never fly directly to this base. The ships are either unloaded elsewhere, or transported along the underground transit systems after we touch down. Much safer, at least, until they wizen up to that.

1120752.text: I've taken a few prisoners off-planet for interrogation on New London. The last one we had was a freighter pilot, just like me. One of the missiles near the spaceport tagged his ship, blasted the engines clean off. The ship went straight through a block of flats and ended up on our side of the battlefield. Lucky sod was still alive when a platoon investigated, so we nabbed him and got his cargo of rice to boot.

1120753.text: In times of war you'd think that we'd all come closer together so that we can emerge victorious. Bowex doesn't think that way so it seems, I heard instead of taking back Revugees that didn't make it off the planet in time they load up Prisoners and bring them to New London just for the extra cash.

1120754.text: Having ammo and other explosives is always dangerous, not that coming here in the first place isn't already, but it makes it all the more suicidal. One hit from anything or a damaged heat shield while you're still burning through the atmosphere makes you go poof faster than you can say Victoria. I've managed to stay alive up to now, only been hauling munitions in and Refugees out. Must be doing something right.

1120755.text: You always have to watch out to who you talk and who you can trust, the Gauls have some good spies and many traitors on their side. We've lost some good men to backstabing and betrayal, so don't expect to be greeted the same way like anywhere else in Bretonia. Was the same for me, but when you manage to get in and out alive with important shipments a few times it gets better. Hard to assume the one providing you with food and ammo is a spy, no?

1120756.text: Welcome to the Oubli, gateway to Planet Leeds. And scourge of the Bretonian rats still scurrying through the rubble below. Oui, I exhagerrate, most of the planet surface is more or less intact, and we intend it to stay that way. Doesn't stop us from raining down the Kings fury on nests of those Bretonians when we find them.

1120757.text: Oubli ensures the safety of the docking ring and moorings nearby. Any unidentified craft approaching are treated as hostile, and will be shot down without warning, so make sure you announce your intent to dock and get clearance. The weapons on the docking ring itself may be paltry, but those of the Oubli are not.

1120758.text: In the planning of the siege of Leeds, the Villeneuve was expected to take this position. She carried a large complement of Marines, Munitions and other supplies that had been stockpiled in Edinburgh. I am not sure if the Bretonians were tipped off to this, but their suicidal attack and subsequent loss of the Villeneuve was a setback for us. Oubli had been held in reserve, and we've taken over the role of providing fire support and orbital security, but we can't make up for the lost men and equipment.

1120759.text: We have almost complete control of space in this system. Military resistance is almost eliminated in space. We still have to deal with the usual troubles - pirates, occasional raids by Bretonian forces or their allies. The foul smog clouds provide cover for any attackers, so we have to run numerous patrols to prevent raiders from hitting our supply ships unchallenged. Still, Leeds space, and all stations within, are ours.

1120760.text: The docking ring allows us to safely bring freighters into a lower altitude. It actually could bring ships all the way to the surface, but the descent trajectory is fixed, and those Bretonian rats know it well. A large portion of the planet's surface can target the docking ring vector, so we need to disconnect ships from the tether while in descent, and have them fly a random pattern to the spaceport. Even so, we still lose some of them.

1120761.text: The King and admiralty want this planet intact, more or less. That's easier said then done. The planet is heavily industrialised, with the bulk of the population centers clustered around heavy industries and this spaceport. That means fighting an entrenched enemy in an urban environment, without heavy artillery support. Urban warfare also means our boys will not be able to use their armor freely. Worse still, the toxic atmosphere means fighter support is out of the question - we tried that, but the engines overloaded after less then 30 minutes, barely enough time to reach a hot zone. What the hell did these Bretonians put in this sky?

1120762.text: I'm one of the pilots that runs patrol around the planet and ensures the Bretonians don't sneak ships through. We've gotten reports of unknown craft making de-orbit burns far away from the docking rings. Probably smugglers, but it could also be the Bretonian army receiving supply drops. Either way, we need those ships destroyed. Orders are simple: Anything that isn't ours, is a target.

1120763.text: The Mollys are a bit of an unknown. We see their ships on occasion, usually they flee into one of the Smog Clouds once we approach. Standing orders are to not provoke them, but I don't trust them. Pirate scum is pirate scum. I see no reason why the kingdom should associate with the likes of those.

1120764.text: I try to not pursue anything into the Smog Clouds unless there's a full squadron with me. One thing I learned back home, is that wherever sensors aren't working well, you'll find a ton of ambushes waiting for you. The Council, Brigands and Maquis all used those tactics against us, I don't think that Bretonian pirates would be any different.

1120765.text: I lead a small squadron of Lynx fighters. Usually we are assigned to patrol along the damaged Trade Lanes, up towards the Tau gate and back here again. Most of our supplies go by that route now. We see plenty of action. Bretonian raiders, Mollys, Outcasts... Military supplies are an attractive target for pirates. It's not uncommon to stumble upon a fight in progress, or a badly damaged freighter limping to the nearest base.

1120766.text: We will push any potential threats from the Trade Lanes with extreme prejudice. We don't ask what people are doing there. We're not police. This system is under martial law, and any anomalous situations are considered threats until proven otherwise, to be resolved as such. In short, orders are to shoot first and ask questions later. Works for me, keeps things simple.

1120767.text: The only Trade Lane I will not fully patrol is the one to LD-14. That one we'll turn around on about a kilometer prior to entering that asteroid field. Anything that's waiting in that field will not survive, and there's barely any shipments heading over there anyway. The station is manned by a skeleton crew and a bunch of droids.

1120768.text: Welcome to the Carcassonne, and the vanguard of our glorious push into Bretonia. Our crew advanced further and deeper into Bretonia then any other task fleet, and we are proud of it. When the time comes to advance further, we will likely be the tip of the spear again.

1120769.text: We are currently making minor repairs to our ship and awaiting replacements for craft lost in the battle for Leeds. We secured a victory here, but as expected, we had to incur some losses. The most significant was the loss of the Villeneuve along with some of her auxiliaries. Still, overall it was a major victory for us. A significant portion of Bretonias space fleet destroyed, and complete military domination of Leeds space. A much better outcome we could not have expected.

1120770.text: Carcassonne was supposed to secure the gate to Newcastle while Villeneuve would oversee the space forces in Leeds. Neither was entirely successful in those tasks. Villeneuve suffered a suicide attack from the Derby, and the Bretonians destroyed their own Jump Gates while our forces were disorganized following the loss of the command ship. Still, they are only prolonging the inevitable that way. It is clear to us that Bretonia has no hope of standing against us.

1120771.text: Our push through Leeds has gone about as well as can be expected. The two-pronged attack we committed to was expected by Bretonia. It was an obvious tactic, but there was little they could do about it. Carcassonne was responsible for securing all the space stations in Leeds - Glasgow, LD-14 and Stokes. Of these stations, only Glasgow put up a fight, likely a delaying tactic.
