1120772.text: The only problem we are facing now is the lack of a bridgehead to the rest of Bretonia. Carcassonne was meant to keep advancing, but without the Jump Gates we'll need new orders on how to push on. Building up forces through a Jump Hole like we did in Brittany can be done, but it is a slow process. Jump Holes cannot handle entire fleets, they will eventually destabilise and pose a danger to ships. They are also a bottleneck. Dundee is at the moment our best system to advance, I think.

1120773.text: We've only achieved roughly half of the operational objectives in this system. The intent was to capture the industrial bases and infrastructure on the planet intact, so that we would have an industrial base for future operations. One of the stations would be assigned a drydock for frontline repairs - Stokes is the logical choice for that - while the vanguard of the fleet moves on to capture the remainder of Bretonia's industrial base. But the planet isn't secure yet, the systems Jump Gates deeper into Bretonia are scuttled, and the bases were stripped before we gained control of them.

1120774.text: We've had some EFL and Solar engineers take a look at what's left of the gates to New London and Newcastle. They told us those are unsalvagable, at least with our technology. Jump Gate parts from Liberty are much more compact then ours, so ours won't fit. Without these critical components, there is no way we can get these gates operational again, even when their main structure is still in good condition.

1120775.text: These Bretonians aren't so dumb as they look. Their tactics seem bent on delaying us, and drawing us into a costly war of attrition. They are also getting help from Liberty if the reports we've received are correct. Both are cause for major concern - our supply lines won't be able to handle this kind of a military operation indefinitely, especially if the level of resistance increases.

1120776.text: We've found an alternate way into Newcastle by trailing those Outcasts and some of the miners. They both used a jumphole in Tau-31 while we were stationed near Holman. The density of the asteroid field only allows us to launch fighters and gunboats through there. Bigger ships simply won't fit through, so at most we can try to destabilise Bretonian interests in that system. We're still looking for other avenues of attack. We have the forces to go on the offensive again, just no available front. Ironic no, since we are in space?

1120777.text: Be careful talking to these scientists. Some of them are a bit off in the head. Some of them say working in the ruins can do strange things to a person, but I think some of them were already loony when they got here. Most of them come in here, order a drink, then sit alone muttering to themselves. One of them yesterday seemed to be having a heated debate with the wall about some transdimensional mumbo jumbo. I can't believe these nutters are cleared to handle supposedly dangerous artifacts. They'll blow us all up sooner than they'll discover some new secret alien weapon, if you ask me.

1120778.text: These scientific twerps are no fun, let me tell you. I decided to prank one of them, so I gave him synth ale when he ordered a Sidewinder Fang. That supposed astrophysical genius couldn't even tell the difference. Told his friends on the way out that it was the best Fang he'd ever had! First one, more like. I should have given him a real Fang. Watching him sputter and spit it out all over the bar would have made the clean up worthwhile.

1120779.text: I've been putting in requisitions for that new tea from Planet Curacao. So far, all I get from logistics is excuses about shortages and exhorbitant prices. These scientists are so dense when it comes to such things, I could probably serve them brown water and charge them for tea and they'd never know the difference.

1120780.text: Gateshead is perfectly located to support our operations in Newcastle. We don't have to keep administrative offices among all the noise of the industrial operation on Scarborough, or the hustle and bustle on Lancaster. The best part is that we can conduct business here without our competition seeing who we're meeting with, like they would on Lancaster. The BPA sweeps the station regularly for listening devices also, and any espionage on this station is treated like treason, so our meetings are more secure.

1120781.text: We have some major deals in the works with Ageira. Apparently they need a special new alloy for some top secret project they're working on in the Alberta system. I don't know the details yet, but they are very anxious to get us to guarantee delivery schedules. Don't they know there's a war on? ALG is also desperate to strengthen their iridium supply lines. The Omicrons are dangerous for shipping, but if anyone can do it, Bowex can do it better. The Corsairs love credits as much as anyone, you know. We just need to find the right pirate big shot to pay off.

1120782.text: Some rumors suggest Samura is going to start it's own terraforming division. Ha, I'd love to see them try. Planetform has been doing this for well over 3 centuries, and our first projects are bearing fruit. Most likely they're just that, though, rumors. They might just want to tweak the climates on one of their planets instead, and adjusting a climate isn't exactly terraforming. Taking a wholly dead world, and creating life on it, -that- is terraforming.

1120783.text: Many of us at Planetform have long suspected that the "expert" consultants we have contracts with from Cambridge's universities have been feeding information to the Gaians. Everyone knows that many Cambridge academics sympathize with the Gaians, but our security department claims their screening process is air tight. Still, the Gaians have an uncanny amount of information about our operations.

1120784.text: Everyone at Planetform is concerned about the Harris and Ayr projects. When we first heard news of Kusari pulling back out of the Taus, we breathed a sigh of relief, but now that Gallia is setting up a blockade, everything is up in the air. We're already way behind schedule, and now that the blockade extends to Edinburgh, the government may finally pull the plug on our funding. That would be a disaster for the company and for Bretonia. Planet Harris has the potential to feed the entire nation once terraforming is completed.

1120785.text: All of us based off the Ark Royal are really glad that Scarborough is so close by. The swill that passes for liqour on an Armed Forces battleship smells like what gets washed off a Gaian when he gets tossed in the tank for delousing prior to going into the brig. Bowex doesn't skimp on the good stuff, and I'm glad for it, even if it does cut into my paycheck. Morale has a price too I suppose, heh.

1120786.text: Belfast is a blight on Bretonia. I can't understand why the Ark Royal failed to boot those ruffians from the station when they took it in the first place. The fleet must have been caught off-guard, for even that entire station isn't a threat to a Battleship. With the loss of Leeds and the Mollys not exactly in a cooperative mood, I dare say it may be time for some... agressive negotiations concerning the return of that station to Bretonian control.

1120787.text: South Shields isn't especially worth much to Bretonia anyway. Cardiff, on the other hand, could really help the war effort. I don't have any great love for BMM, but I'd still rather see loyal Bretonians running a vital industry rather than shifty neutrals who you can't trust. The IMG wanted to be free from Bretonia anyway, so why should they exploit the nation's resources for their own gain?

1120788.text: The Outcasts seem to be keeping to themselves lately. It gives me the creeps, actually. They must be planning something big. Everybody knows they hate the IMG. My bet is that South Shields is going to be the target of a hostile takeover, and I'm not talking about somebody buying up the voting stock, know what I mean? My squadron commander just laughs off that suggestion though. He says the Outcasts have pulled out of Newcastle altogether. Right. He doesn't sign up to patrol the northern asteroid field himself, though, does he?

1120789.text: The Yamaguchi was pretty heavily damaged when we finally managed to get it away from the Gallic lines. It took weeks of work by Bretonian mechanics to get us back up and running. But it was futile. The battleships that followed behind the Gallic fighter swarms are strong enough to take on our battleships head-on, so we dare not use it on the front lines.

1120790.text: Turns out this new "Gallia" is made up of the French people who managed to escape Sol. They should advance to the rear soon enough.

1120791.text: Have you seen the massive alien ruins the Bretonians were hiding from us here in Newcastle? Don't those morons understand that stuff is dangerous?

1120792.text: Talk about a reversal of fortunes! One day we're battling to seize Planet Harris, and the next we're suddenly in a new peace treaty with it's owner, stranded in one of their systems, and fighting side by side with them against an entirely new House.

1120793.text: How could the Admirals let this happen? I'll never understand what happens to people's brains after they get promoted. I lost so many friends to those bloodthirsty Bretonians while trying to seize control of Leeds, and now we have to help defend them! If I'd have known this was going to happen, I'd have eaten a mine on my last patrol.

1120794.text: It takes all my self control to stop myself from pointing my guns at the Bretonians here. I don't care if there is a new navy out there trying to shoot us, honor demands we best our opponents, not join with them.

1120795.text: When the Gallic Navy attacked our fleet's rear in Tau-31, Kishiro Technologies used the debacle to topple Samura's supremacy of the government. I'm not sure if that is a good or a bad thing. Samura may have had some questionable practices, but they were the industrial power that fueled our nation. All I know, is they won't take this lying down. By the time we manage to return, Kusari could be in a civil war.

1120796.text: Our commanders made the right choice in working with the Bretonians. They were honorable enemies, unlike these blood-thirsty Gallians who snuck into the Taus and shot us in the back. Our combined fighting experience will give us plenty of opportunities to make the Gallian's lives hell.

1120797.text: My wife and two children were killed on Glasgow Outpost during a Kusari Navy foray into Leeds, when a stray firestalker missile slammed into the station. I swore revenge, but the Bretonian Armed Forces wouldn't take me, they have war rules and all of that and I didn't want them to be sued by the military court for whatever I'm going to do next. One of my friends got me in touch with the Golden Chrysanthemums, who eventually transported me out here on one of their undercover transports. I now fight alongside them against the Kusari Navy to avenge my family.

1120798.text: We had an advantage with our battleships against the Bretonians. The Yamaguchi and Nagasaki both have destroyed their fair share of fish. But the Gallians brought a battleship that rivals our own in firepower. We have to rely on our fighters and bombers in this war.

1120799.text: We might be working with the Bretonians, but we follow only the orders of our commanders. The Bretonians want to save their House. We want to kill as many Gallians as we can. The methods for those two goals are not always the same, as we'll just as soon offer up the Bretonians as bait.

1120800.text: If we ever get home, I'm going to give Kishiro the death they deserve. Using the death of our comrades in the Taus to take over the government was unforgiveable.

1120801.text: Fortunately, the BAF have granted us permission to supply the Yamaguchi just like the BAF's own battleships get supplied. We're having to train our own boarding teams, though. There's no way we're going to allow Bretonian Marines on board a Kusari battleship, even if they are supposedly our allies now.

1120802.text: Bretonian arms aren't as elegant as what we manufacture in Kusari, but they will get the job done, and the job is a dead Gallian!

1120803.text: Putting MOX from LD-14 in a Kusari battleship is like feeding gruel to a princess for breakfast, but we don't have much choice. We're contemplating hauling it in from Rheinland, but the cost is going to be enormous. ALG is not likely to give us credit, either. Bretonia has to extend credit to us if they want our help. Rock - hard place - rock...

1120804.text: Bowex claims this to be the center of trade in Bretonia. Are they serious? This station doesn't remotely compare to the volume being handled at Waterloo. At most it handles the bulk of trade between the various Bowex and BMM affiliates, but that's all on the internal Bretonian market. Peanuts compared to inter-house trade.

1120805.text: Bowex does not really like us Interspace folk. They just can't stand that there's something much bigger than them out there. Too bad, because Interspace isn't going anywhere any time soon. We maintain a presence here to keep an eye on the ebb and flow of the Bretonian internal market. It helps guide our own business ventures here in Bretonia.

1120806.text: I don't get why Bowex built this station so damned far from the capitol. You'd think if they want an economic center to flourish, they'd put it near the center of trade, in Bretonia. Across from Southampton would have been a much better location, as Southampton is the industrial heart of New London.

1120810.text: A field of bare rock asteroids in far orbit of Cologne's star. Unioners swarm throughout the field, and it is believed by Federal authorities to be a primary route for diamond smuggling.

1120867.text: Svinoy is a medium-sized field of ice asteroids that is used by the Gaians to mine water. A jump hole leading into Orkney is located within the field.

1120869.text: An ice field located within the Faroe system.

Fugloy is a planet relatively close to the largest of the Faroe stars. The strong solar winds have eroded away the atmosphere of this planet, thus rendering it sterile. No attempt at a planetary landing has yet been made, but Spaceport Torshavn was constructed in orbit.

1120879.text:
DIAMETER: 6,211 km
MASS: 5.87 x 10e24 kg
TERRAIN: Barren
TEMPERATURE: 12°C to 63°C
ESCAPE VELOCITY: 9.66 km/sec

A hot, dry world. Orbital scans have detected that massive sandstorms, with surface winds well in excess of 400KPH are the norm on this planet. Underground habitation may be possible, however landing and launching spacecraft through the intensely unstable atmosphere would be extremely risky. No landing attempts have yet been made.

1120881.text:
DIAMETER: 7,486 km
MASS: 2.93 x 10e24 kg
TERRAIN: Barren
TEMPERATURE: -91°C to -24°C
ESCAPE VELOCITY: 4.21 km/sec

A planet with a relatively low density, it has most likely formed by drawing in material from the Sandoy asteroid field. The presence of a thin, very cold atmosphere and continuous asteroid strikes make this planet unattractive for habitation.

1120883.text:
DIAMETER: 1,241 km
MASS: 1.21 x 10e24 kg
TERRAIN: Barren
TEMPERATURE: -51°C to 126°C
ESCAPE VELOCITY: 1.23 km/sec

A rocky, lifeless moon that orbits planet Fugloy.

1120884.text: I keep hearing whispers about Gallia wanting to colonize Gaia. If there is even a shred of truth to that, we should never have agreed to any nonagression pact. Protecting the Gaian ecology is at the heart of our organisation. If we allow Gallia to defile the planet, what purpose does our existance still serve?

1120885.text: This is the largest installation we've ever constructed. It's a technological marvel in how efficient it's operations are. I wish we could share the lessons we learn here with the rest of Sirius, to show them there's a better way to live in space. But it's too risky, if we're found here, this base will likely end up like Glendale.

1120886.text: As far as I'm concerned, the Unione Corse have blood on their hands. They helped start a chain of events that led to the loss of so many of our numbers. That can't slide!

1120887.text: Remember: While in Faroe, what you see and do here and even how you got here is strictly Gaian knowledge. Protect it with your life, because your life depends on it. We understand each other, yeah?

1120888.text: Why don't we just declare independence? We are well out in the boondocks and if what I've been hearing is true, then we have a way into unexplored space. We could be Frontiersmen. I'd be more than happy to work on the ground floor towards a Free Gaian Republic. You should attend one of our rallies sometime and see what we're about.

1120889.text: The Green Front? Bah! Who needs them? All they know how to do is talk and their voice doesn't carry much weight out this far anyway.

1120890.text: I still miss the view from my quarters of the Islay Ice Cloud sometimes, but it's much quieter here and I can raise my family in a more relative peace than I'm normally accustomed to.

1120891.text: Seems to me that The Council would be a good ally to have. They could help us strike back at the Gallic Navy without directly getting dirt on out hands and risking a reprisal that we might not recover from.

1120892.text: The more I think about it, the less I am convinced that us coming here is a good thing. Gaians should not settle down and grow complacant. Pacificm makes you irrelevant and the powers that be will simply brush you aside as if you never were. Only by keeping to our ways, by fighting, will we be able to voice ourselves.

1120893.text:
DIAMETER: 12,515 km
MASS: 5.96 x 10e24 kg
TERRAIN: Terrestrial
TEMPERATURE: -34°C to 52°C
ESCAPE VELOCITY: 11.01 km/sec
1120893.mapped:
Gaia is a tropical paradise - a rich, green world of plants and animals - the likes of which have not been found anywhere else in the Sirius Sector. Its flora and fauna is not yet fully understood, but rumors of the aphrodisiac qualities of certain animals have generated a tremendous demand among those who can afford to pay for the privilege of sampling. The University of Cambridge had for over a century operated a small research outpost on the planet and visits to Gaia were restricted to prevent poaching.

Soon after tourists began to arrive in Edinburgh in 690 AS, Cambridge scientists voiced their concern over the enormous ecological damage that even the most regulated visits could inflict on the planet. Almost from birth Cambridgers had drilled into them the stories of how New London and Leeds were blighted, so they tended to be very environmentally sensitive. A few of the younger and more militant scientists studying Planet Gaia actually went so far as to begin a campaign to sabotage tourist transports in an effort to discourage visits, but with little effect.

Once Cobalt was discovered on Gaia in 740, BMM began to lobby for the need to establish a mining base there. What had been a quiet, bloodless campaign of active resistance blossomed into full-fledged conflict. Graffiti with slogans such as "GAIA WILL NOT BLEED" were spotted soon after. The eco-terrorist movement had begun.

Eventually any plans to mine the surface of Gaia were dropped - mostly out of fear that it might cut into the burgeoning tourist industry - but the Gaians had already broadened their horizons by an influx of radical elements from Cambridge who sought a ban on terraforming technologies. Planetform was the natural target. What emerged was a militant terrorist group philosophically opposed to the exploitation of planets, and terraforming in particular. The group enjoyed considerable popular support on Cambridge, funded by the efforts of the legitimate arm of the Gaians called the Green Front.

Following the Gallic invasion, the orbit of Planet Gaia was occupied by the Gallic Royal Navy. Gaia remained unsettled until the Glassing of Leeds, when its purpose shifted to provide sanctuary to retreating Royalists, fleeing Nobles and the Bretonian serfs they managed to take with them from Leeds.

Notwithstanding, the settlement lasted temporarily, as the Kusari invasion of Gallia incited reunion among the Gallic people and the Royalists abandoned Gaia and sacrificed La Riche's battlegroup to reunite with their compatriots. The remaining population on Gaia consists of refugees from Leeds and leftover Gallic personnel.

Following an upwards ramp of activity from Mollys and Gaians attempting to take control of the population to recruit, the remaining Gallic forces united claiming a new County of Gaia. This resulted in a flurry of conflict as the Count used their power and influence to gather mercenaries, while the Mollys attempted to supply their own population onto the planet.

In a last ditch effort, the Gaians decided to use a bio-weapon modified to work with Gaia's biomes. In the form of a strain of the human-slaying bacteria from Planet Carlisle. Over the next few weeks the remaining human population plummeted until the remaining survivors were driven off the world. Gaia is once more an untampered Green Jewel, achieved through bloody means.

Gaia is a tropical paradise - a rich, green world of plants and animals - the likes of which have not been found anywhere else in the Sirius Sector. Its flora and fauna is not yet fully understood, but rumors of the aphrodisiac qualities of certain animals have generated a tremendous demand among those who can afford to pay for the privilege of sampling. The University of Cambridge had for over a century operated a small research outpost on the planet and visits to Gaia were restricted to prevent poaching.

Soon after tourists began to arrive in Edinburgh in 690 AS, Cambridge scientists voiced their concern over the enormous ecological damage that even the most regulated visits could inflict on the planet. Almost from birth Cambridgers had drilled into them the stories of how New London and Leeds were blighted, so they tended to be very environmentally sensitive. Perpignan Spaceport was built in 818 AS as a framework for a future trading outpost in the Roussillon system. Currently, since not much trade actually takes place along the surrounding war-torn region, it serves as a supply station and a defensive hub to keep the system secured from possible intruders. The spaceport is located on the edge of the Ariege Nebula, halfway between planets Toulouse and Foix.

After the fall of Le Boulou Outpost Council forces gathered at the station to form several defensive lines between the Montmorency Battlegroup and Toulouse to cover the planet's evacuation, with the venerable Battleship Pamiers assigned to be the flagship of this defensive contingent.

1120916.mapped:
Sponsored by the Gallic crown and given a priority over other projects, Solar Engineering, which was later divided between EFL and Ile-de-France Shipping, researchers attempted to disassemble and reverse engineer what remained of the ruined Sirian FTL network as soon as the first captures of such tech were made in Tau, but made little progress understanding the activation mechanisms without destabilizing the links.

With the capture of Leeds System and the Bretonians scuttling the gates to New London and Newcastle in 818 AS, EFL had numerous opportunities to tinker with existing systems. With their expertise in the physics of jump gates combined with a mandate and nearly unlimited budget direct from the Crown, EFL researchers and mathematicians spent five years calculating the exact wormhole physics to interrupt and override the existing link between Newcastle and New London, which they finally achieved in 825 AS. On the London side, now knowing which parts of the Ageira mechanisms to activate, EFL directed GRN demolitionists to carefully destroy Ageira's control mechanisms and install their own.

When the New London blitz failed and the final battle over the Bretonian capital concluded, the Royal Navy's rear echelon forces in Leeds locked down the jump gate. Within a week, a Gallic destroyer, the RNS Bellegarde, defected and supplied Bretonia with the gate codes. By the time Allied Forces arrived in the system however, Planet Leeds had been glassed, and a trap had been laid at the New London gate site.

Gallia had no time to scuttle the site, which the Bretonian military occupied in order to secure the area. This led to considerable tensions between FTL giant Ageira, the Liberty government, and Bretonia, out of fear that the Bretonians may successfully use knowledge gleaned from the site to achieve FTL travel of their own. A resolution was eventually reached when the Bretonian government ceded the gate site to Ageira, who concluded that whatever information Bretonia could have recovered from the gate site would be minimal, and limited to the redirection of existing jump tunneling. The final, extensive Ageira report stated definitively that there is no way Bretonian scientists could have successfully reproduced FTL technology from their time spent studying the New London gate.

With there being no gate to construct, normally the base would be withdrawn. However following a request from the Liberty Navy, Ageira undertook a new task using the base, the handling of the Ottawa wreck near the gate.

Originally planned to be finished by 824 AS, the Cryer Board of Directors for the longest time was uncertain as to where to construct Pentecost Outpost. Ultimately, to be worth the cost of maintenance, Pentecost would need to be constructed in a place where it would be able to fulfill a role that was not already being fulfilled by Atka Research Station in Sigma-17 but would share the same benefits of seclusion.

Recently completed, Pentecost Outpost serves as a sequestered hive of activity less for research but more for the acquisition of materials that the Houses would deem illegal or dangerous, judging by the lack of visible scientific staff. Curiously enough, both the Corsairs and the Core seem to be leaving the station alone, despite knowing about it, giving credence to the theory that Cryer either is sparing no costs in incentivizing both Crete and the Core to leave them alone or that Cryer has separate deals of natures different than money with both that allows them to operate unimpededly. Given this fact, however, Pentecost's position is a quite secure one, at least for the time being.

The surface of the planet is mostly covered by methane ice, and water ice that was discovered under the methane layer proved too difficult to extract. However, the Corsairs consider the world as a possible source of water in case more easily accessible sources are depleted.

Marratxi is a huge dark world that is considered to be the remnant of an ancient star, its core deprived of atmosphere and now slowly cooling down. The Marratxi star most probably became a nova over two billion years ago, most of its matter accumulated within the new Lambda sun. The remnants formed a dark matter cloud around Marratxi itself. One of the star's former planets, Binissalem, still orbits the dying sun.

1120952.text:
DIAMETER: 10,817 km
MASS: 3.92 x 10e24 kg
TERRAIN: Barren
TEMPERATURE: -212°C to -92°C
ESCAPE VELOCITY: 6.29 km/sec

Binissalem was once a huge gas giant orbiting the Marratxi star. Over two billion years ago, after Marratxi went nova, most of its atmosphere was lost and drifted away into interstellar space. Part of the atmospheric gases, along with gases that once comprised the nearby star's atmosphere, later accumulated around the planet's core, forming a thin secondary atmosphere that is still present around Binissalem. The planet could provide a great opportunity for astronomers to directly study a gas giant's core if Lambda was not located so far away from House worlds and if it was accessible to civilian researchers. Neither is the case, and Lambda is controlled by the Corsairs who shoot unauthorised intruders on sight.

1120960.text: Gallia moves a lot of supplies through Orkney, especially fuel. Their engines do not use H-Fuel like the rest of Sirius, so their entire fleet has to be supplied from Gallia. Orkney is a key system for them, so the Gallic Navy has this system under heavy guard. We don't get in their way, and I don't recommend you to either.

1120961.text: The La Riche has been stationed in the Orkney system to ensure no one hits our supply line in the flanks. While our capital ships would have a hard time maneuvering in the Tau asteroid fields, that problem does not exist here in Orkney.

1120962.text: The La Riche is a relatively new vessel, and I must admit, her crew isn't as experienced yet as it could be. That'll improve over time. I suspect this is the reason why we've been assigned to rear guard duty, and that we'll be sent out to Bretonia, or possibly even Liberty, in a few months.

1120963.text: The Bretonian front is proceeding smoothly. Our forces are proceeding faster then anticipated. That's why it is vital we keep our supply line secure. It's getting a bit longer then we are comfortable with as it is. Running out of fuel in the middle of a major counterattack would be catastrophic.

1120964.text: The Outcasts are still a problem in this system. We know they have a base around here somewhere, most likely in one of the asteroid fields. Our ships patrol the perimeter of those fields, so that when they rear their ugly, breather supplemented heads, they are met with a hail of fire. If we keep them bottled up, they'll eventually starve from either Food or Cardamine deprivation. According to a briefing on the substance, the latter is a very painful way to go.

1120965.text: We keep an eye on the civilian traffic coming through from Tau-23. Kusari, IMG traders and those of our own design are a common sight. On occasion the Outcasts start trouble in our perimeter, but our patrols have little trouble sending them fleeing.

1120966.text: Occasionally we "test fire" our main cannon on a nearby planetoid. While the commanders always call it a weapons proficiency test, it's no coincidence these "tests" coincide with IMG or Kusari transports passing through the jumphole. I suspect His Grace wants to give both these Sirian factions constant reminders of who's in charge here.

1120967.text: The Royal Police are supposed to be handling the civilian traffic bound for Gallia, but they're barely able to keep themselves and that wrecked station they're holed up in, in one piece. Earlier this month a few patrols of theirs had to come here because their own docking facilities failed. Amateurs... You can guess who has to pick up the slack. Oui, yours truly.

1120968.text: The Royal Police do not seem too effective at keeping the border secure. We've begun to see Gallic Brigands pop up in Orkney and Tau-23, and evidence suggests they come from Languedoc, which suggests they run through the minefield to get there. So far they are little more than a nuisance, but there's no telling how long it will stay that way.

1120969.text: Now that our forces have moved into Leeds, traffic can move completely by Jump Gate. That is much safer since jumpholes can destabilise unexpectedly, which makes supply routes through them very unreliable. The engineering corps did a fine job erecting the prefabricated gate, I just hope it is as reliable as a normal gate.

1120975.text: Ah, the Gaians. Overwhelming that insignificant group of ecological fanatics proved quite effective. We still see some of their ilk around here every now and then. They know better than to cause trouble. We had no trouble establishing ourselves in Aquitaine.

1120977.text: Welcome to Fort Albi. Enjoy your stay. This facility is largely automated. Should your craft need repairs, inform the maintenance droid. Should you require resupply, inform the quartermaster droid. Again, enjoy your stay.

1120978.text: I don't know what's worse, this place or that wreck near the Languedoc hole. Sure, this station isn't coming apart at the seams, but at least at Reunion you can speak to fellow human beings.

1120979.text: This station was erected as part of the plan to push deep into Bretonia through Aquitaine. We knew we would have to build waystations like this in order to keep the supply lines secure. This station often receives transports with Outcasts hot on their tail. They usually break off when the station launches it's fighter wings, fleeing back into the asteroid field.

1120980.text: People rotate in and out of this station quite quickly. This isn't a comfortable place to stay. Prefabricated modules are easy to piece together, but they make for terribly cramped quarters. But I suppose that's what you get on a military outpost, we're not on vacation here.

1120981.text: We chased a number of Outcasts into the asteroid field a few weeks ago, against standing orders not to go in there. The bastards had spaced an IDF freighter convoy carrying food. Vengeance is blind, they say. We didn't see their backup waiting in ambush until they opened fire. Only two fighters out of a wing of ten made it back to Albi, I was in one of them.

1120982.text: The navy does what it can to keep the path from Gallia to the Bretonian front safe, but there are still risky areas out there. The stretch from Reunion to Albi is one of those. Most pilots tend to veer away from the asteroid fields a little bit as they pass Reunion. Flying near them increases the chance of an Outcast ambush.

1120983.text: I was part of a freighter convoy bound for the Glendale Depot. My two wingmen and the aft freighter didn't make it. Outcasts overtook us just as we approached Albi, and took out our escorts in under a minute. The Navy chased them off though. People die in wartime, it's a given. I'll complete the run once my ship has been repaired, this time with a Navy escort.

1121016.text: I can't believe that our brothers and sisters abandoned us on this lone piece of Zoner junk. Some comrades came here with wounded soldiers, but I heard that many were left to die as the remnants of the Yaren defense fled. We feel betrayed by our honourless brethren since they turned their back towards us, who supply them with Iridium, months ago when they sought to focus on the Omegas and Bretonia itself. The Order seems to value their soldiers, I might even consider enlisting myself. Everything is better than this hellhole of a Freeport. I see the Nomads on the horizon, they are always around, waiting for us to abandon the safety of our home. No, the Order will be our salvation.

1121017.text: My sister in battle, Valeria, who also resides on the station, seems to have lost all of her hope. She thinks that the Corsairs have forgotten about us, but I can not believe that this is true. We still have our honour and wouldn't abandon our principles like this. We are like a brotherhood, after all.

1121018.text: I haven't seen something this astonishing in a while! We only listened to the radio and could get an image of what was going on out there. Our brethren fought well, though I realized that we are weak in the upper Omicrons if we do not know our priorities. The Core however seems to be a promising alternative for everyone of us. And how bloody they fight - hah! That's just my style. Reckless, fearless, ferocious - combined with invaluable tactics. For me, it's only about fights, and certainly can have more of those with the Core.

1121020.text: A shadow looming in the upper part of Omicron Delta, the Palau Ice Cloud conceals the access into the deeper Omicrons. Plenty of scout patrols and trade convoys have gone missing in the cloud since the Nomads started to become more ferocious in their offensive. Extreme caution is advised, and adequate escorts are mandatory.

1121021.text: A Bretonian carrier prototype, still under construction. Most systems are still offline.

After this coup failed, the remaining forces retreated into Liberty's border systems. Their main force is the Battlegroup Harmony but other remaining Navy and LSF elements work together with them. They receive support from the Lane Hackers, the Unioners and other sources from outside of Liberty.

1121054.text:
Nomad "Dione" Vagrant

A modified form of the fearsome yet outdated Sascya morph, the Dione was intended by the Vagrants to be a heavily armed combat drone until a disastrous skirmish with a wing of Human fighters shattered their preconceptions.

Startled by how quickly human technology had advanced since their twenty year exile the Vagrants hastily relegated the archaic Dione to a less combat oriented role.

By reconfiguring its extensive array of weapon cysts and softening its outer membrane the one-time heavyweight was repurposed into an effective tunnel borer, currently being used to create a new hive for the Vagrants deep beneath the crust of planet Moros.

Due to the softened shell needed to survive its subterranean maneuvering the Dione is much less robust than its original form and, as such, a lone morph will display less aggressive tendencies towards intruders for the sake of its own survival.

Gallic GCG-4 "Ardent"-class Gunboat

While most operations against fighters and bombers can be countered with other fighters, occasionally there is a need to thoroughly ensure that an opposing force is violently deconstructed. The Ardent-class gunboat is the Gallic Defense Force's new and improved platform for delivering heavy intervention where elite wings of hostile snubcraft are involved. The fixed forward gun, a holdover from the Perilous-class gunboat formerly fielded by the Gallic Royal Navy, gives the Ardent a dedicated option for forcibly dismantling smugglers' transports if needed.

Though only recently deployed in the field, the Ardent-class gunboat has started to make a name for itself. Fleets that have opted to outfit the gunboat with multiple infrared tracking missile launchers have found their kill counts to be higher than with previous incarnations of the Gallic gunboat line, and in cases where pilots are recovered from mangled fighters, said pilots have been known to use the phrases "unsportsmanlike" and "not fair" to describe their takes on the engagements that led to their capture.

With the hull-integrated cannon removed, the Gallant is used as a frontline support warship, commonly seen escorting larger warships or accompanied by more Gallants. The Obstinate-class was designed as a battlecruiser to interdict and subdue criminal elements in opposition to the Gallic government. But with some of the entities that were once considered to be part of those underworld operations now being the foundation of the democractically-elected, progressive government, the stated purpose of the Obstinate has changed somewhat. As part of the joint refresh of technology and appearance in the third-generation Gallic capital ship line, the newly-renamed Adamant-class battlecruiser was born.

Based on the materiel of the Royal Navy's Obstinate-class with the field-tested design modifications of the Council's own variant, the new Adamant is a modern assault battlecruiser at the same level of the Liberty Navy's Interdictor-class and Bretonia's own brand-new Fortitude. It integrates the last decade's changes in technology and philosophy for the design and deployment of the ever-popular mid-level classification of capital ships and in some ways is as much of a leading ship in the Confederation fleet as the mighty and iconic Remembrance-class is.

1121093.text:
CTX-405 "Zapper" Transport Turret
The Zapper Photon Ray is a recent invention derived from a study by a small OSC engineering team tasked to design a sustained photon emitter that could create a brilliant beam of light over several thousand meters continuously. Orbital Spa intended for this technology to be used in orbiting commercial billboards. However, during one of the tests a power surge overcharged the emitter, causing it to discharge well beyond its operating limits. When the resulting blast blew clean through the armor of a nearby Pelican class armored transport, the design team realised they might have stumbled onto something more useful then a floating billboard.

Unable to design it further on their own, Orbital Spa contacted several science teams to help further develop it. Two months later, the "Zapper" was installed on the first Orbital Spa transport. A few months later, all the major houses "miraculously" made similar breakthroughs, making the weapon a widely available point defense for transports and capital ships.

As a weapon, the Zapper is a highly accurate but low damage point defense turret. Gunners are encouraged to train multiple turrets on a single target, as individual shots are unlikely to do significant damage.

1121095.text:
DCP-2 "Pointe de Lumiere" Battleship Photon Pulse Turret
The Pointe de Lumiere is a point defense weapon for Gallic capital ships. It fires a burst of energy at incredable speed, with pinpoint accuracy. Individual shots do not deal high amounts of damage however, limiting this weapon to anti-strikecraft use.

1121097.text:
BPR-1X "Zapper" Photon Ray Battleship Turret
The biggest version of the Zapper Turrets, this weapon can only be powered by a fullsize Battleship core. While still a point defense weapon, this version deals enough damage to repel gunboats that stray into range, if used in sufficient numbers. A sideeffect of the high velocity of the energy emission at high range is a strange "reverse doppler" effect, often causing a gunnery crew to shoot behind the target. Gunners are required to lead their targets slightly, even when visually some shots would appear to miss.

1121099.text:
Liberty "Boltstorm Mk II" Tachyon Cannon
The Boltstorm Mk II was developed by Ageira Technologies, and is now sold primarily to Libertonian corporate and private security interests. This is a tachyon-based weapon that has the longest range of all energy-based weapons, but trades damage output for energy efficiency. It is most effective against molecular shields, and weakest against positron shields.

1121101.text:
Rheinland "Werfer-P2" Plasma Cannon
The Werfer-P2 was developed by Daumann, and is now sold primarily to Rheinlandic corporate and private security interests. This plasma-based weapon has a slow refire, but exchanges damage output for energy efficiency. It is most effective against graviton shields, and weakest against molecular shields.

1121103.text:
Kusari KW1 "Cleanser" Photon Blaster
The KW1 Cleanser was developed by Kishiro Technologies, and is now sold primarily to Kusari corporate and private security interests. This photon-based weapon which has a high refire rate, but exchanges damage output for energy efficiency. It is most effective against positron shields, and weakest against graviton shields.

1121105.text:
Bretonia "Star Hammer" PP4 Particle Blaster
The Star Hammer PP4 was developed by BMM, and is now sold primarily to Bretonian corporate and private security interests. This particle-based weapon provides a decent rate of fire, but trades off damage output for energy efficiency. This weapon is most effective against graviton shields, and weakest against molecular shields.

BLH-5 "Denier" Transport EMP Defense Turret
The Denier is a new development in transport weapons technology. It fires a slow-moving, energy-sensitive EMP charge, designed to detonate in proximity of enemy ships or projectiles. 1121182.text:
"Scorcher" Plasma Bomb
The Scorcher Bomb is a high-yield, plasma-based explosive that is contained within a sphere with a small motor unit attached. Whilst the technology itself is not advanced, its simplicity and reliability has ensured it is a mainstay within fleet arsenals. The warhead contained has been specifically designed to inflict maximum damage upon hull and armor, by producing large shockwaves and then projecting its plasma-based charge into the plating itself. The relatively slow speed of the bomb makes it unsuitable against smaller vessels such as gunboats or smaller cruisers, but is a premier choice against larger vessels that are unable to avoid it. Due to the nature of the warhead, it is not as effective against shield generators as it is against armor plating.

*Fired by Scorcher Bomb Launcher

1121184.text:
CT-402K "Acheron" Heavy Transport Turret
The Acheron is the latest entry to the CT-400 transport turret line. Designing it on the basis of the CT-402 "Charon", it's engineers pushed the DCE converter and energy-storage modules to their physical limits. By connecting a newly developed DCE-OC module, mounted inside reinforced storage containers, to a transports central powercore unit it is possible to inject additional energy into the drive core energy circuit, which is then distributed to the CT-402K. While the increase in energy flow enables the weapon to fire more powerful energy bolts, it also puts immense stress on the ship's energy circuit and heat transfer system. Thusly, this weapon should be used only over a short period of time, as it may otherwise permanently damage EC, DCE, and HTS components.

1121186.text:
CT-504 "Lyre" Transport Point Defense Turret
The Lyre is an unusual transport weapon, firing superheated ferrous nanoshards via a magnetic slingshot instead of being a true energy weapon. This makes it very powerful and efficient, but the weapon's long breech is less flexible and thus much harder to aim than conventional weaponry. With its high rate of fire and fast projectiles, it is intended as a point defense weapon against smaller craft.

1121328.text:
Nomad Desolator Missile Turret
A Nomad capital missile. The Desolator as a project was developed in an unusual way, in that the missile itself was designed before the launching mechanism. The concept was of a missile with a tremendous payload, but still small enough to be carried on a cruiser in sufficient numbers. The problem was the launching mechanism; a standard non-fixed launcher would have been far too unwieldy to mount and load. It was decided to fix this by creating a rotary-loading integral silo, which means it must be fired at a fixed angle away from the ship. This limits it to very long range engagement of very slow targets, but this is balanced out by the missile's terrifying speed and unmatched destructive capability

*Requires Nomad Desolator Missile.

Battlecruiser EM9M "Shockwave" Pulse Torpedo
The EM9M is a torpedo launch system created to surpass the ever-popular pulse cannons. Dubbed the Shockwave, this double-barreled launch platform fires two dumbfire torpedoes which contain electromagnetic pulse devices at their core. The torpedoes are armed with proximity fuses designed to pick up on the unique signatures an active shield generator radiates, and automatically detonate the volatile core once near - or in contact with - a shield bubble. The Shockwave torpedo is built for the sole purpose of making heavy capital ship shields obsolete, dealing tremendous damage.

This model has seen very little field-testing, but initial results done by various organizations were positive, and battlecruisers positioned for long-range fire support will find these weapons highly effective. Due to the need of the heavy and sizeable torpedoes needing to be physically reloaded into the tubes after a barrage has been fired, the weapon is only able to be used once before needing to enter reload cycle.

1121421.text:
A gas cloud in the Zurich system that was once a single gas ring along with other clouds. A more detailed analysis of the cloud suggests that it is of stellar origin and corresponds in composition to the upper layers of the Zurich star. Current scientific knowledge cannot satisfactorily explain this phenomenon, as the Zurich star is not currently at the end of its life, but only in the first third of its estimated lifetime.

The Avers cloud is named after the gas giant Avers and for good reason. The Oerlikon Observatory has detected an unusual electromagnetic coupling between the gas giant and this gas cloud and apparently it is these hypercharged plasma storms in the gas giant's upper atmosphere that charge and ionize the Avers cloud every time these two bodies come into close proximity.

Avers cloud's storms are strong enough to jam sensors not only inside the cloud but also in its vicinity, making it seem like a near perfect hiding place for criminals. Other than for temporary shelter or scientific research, however, the Avers Cloud is worthless in the long run precisely because of these potentially deadly and high-energy storms which can destroy everything human and alien in the long run.

1121423.text:
INHS Saint Helene, formerly known as LL Bounty Star, originally began its career as a civilian liner and ferry. It was launched in 752 AS from Baltimore Shipyard and serviced routes between all major planets in Liberty. Later in 828, the Bounty Star was boarded and captured by Insurgency forces and pressed into service as hospital ship, rechristened INHS Saint Helene, to provide support for stranded Insurgency units.

When the Liberty Navy began its assault on the Insurgency's holdings in 829 AS, the Saint Helene served as an evacuation ship and was used to ferry key personnel from soon-to-be-overrun Insurgency bases. The vessel was evacuating personnel from Fort Leniex to the Magellan system when it was intercepted by the Liberty Navy and destroyed. INT Arlington attempted to rescue the survivors once the situation had calmed down, but was intercepted by another patrol and destroyed not so far away, sealing the fate of all crewmen and passengers from the Saint Helene.

1121425.text:
INS Hughton was an Archer-class siege cruiser employed by the Insurgency for the desperate defence of planet Veracruz. INS Hughton always operated in pairs with its sister ship, INS Hancock, and they were tasked with ambushing the Ohio as it was on its course from the Kansas anomaly to Veracruz.

As both ships were maneuvering through Sonora Ice Field to get into a perfect ambush position, they were discovered by a recon flight from the battlecruiser Guam, which promptly scrambled available squadrons from the Ohio to destroy both ambushers.

INS Hughton led the charge against the Guam in hopes of disabling it quickly and then retreating, but they were quickly overwhelmed by Ohio's fighter and bomber wings and forced to retreat deeper into the field. Hughton's engines were eventually disabled by a lucky hit from a torpedo and the unlucky cruiser was bombarded until its reactor and fuel tanks exploded, killing everyone onboard and wrecking the ship.

1121427.text:
INS Hancock, was an Archer-class siege cruiser employed by the Insurgency for the desperate defence of planet Veracruz. INS Hancock always operated in pairs with its sister ship, INS Hughton, and they were tasked with ambushing the Ohio as it was on its course from the Kansas anomaly to Veracruz.

As both ships were maneuvering through Sonora Ice Field to get into a perfect ambush position, they were discovered by the recon flight from the battlecruiser Guam, which promptly scrambled available squadrons from the Ohio to destroy both ambushers.

INS Hancock was staying a bit behind the INS Hughton as they attempted to destroy the Guam, but they were quickly overwhelmed by Ohio's fighter and bomber wings and forced to retreat deeper into the field. Damaged but still operational, INS Hancock managed to disengage from the Navy and ventured deeper into the Sonora Ice Field. Its last black box recording suggested that it was trying to make a run for the Magellan system, but it was later found crippled beyond repair and with all of its escape pods missing, the fate of its crew unknown.

1121429.text:
INT Arlington was a Bison-class transport commissioned by the Insurgency in the late 826 to serve as a troop transport and fleet supply vessel. INT Arlington was under a command of legendary and daring Captain Jerry Fathoms, who used his vessel to rescue dozens of downed insurgent pilots and to recover escape pods from crippled Insurgency vessels despite the risks of interception by the Liberty Navy.

His luck ran out when he was rescuing survivors from a crippled hospital liner, INHS Saint Helene, and they were discovered by a Liberty Navy gunboat pack. Despite Captain Fathoms' best efforts to seek the safety of the Guerrero Asteroid Cloud, he failed to reach the cloud before his engines were disabled. Captain Fathoms and his crew fought a valiant last stand before the ship's reactor was struck and detonated, killing everyone onboard and breaking the ship's spine.

1121431.text:
The LNS Guam was an Interdictor-class battlecruiser, commissioned solely for the purpose of serving as the lead escort vessel for its flagship, the Ohio. The Guam had a relatively inexperienced crew and suffered several security accidents during its previous deployment in Colorado. Prior to its assignment to the Insurgency campaign, however, the vessel received Captain Margarette Dovers, a famous Liberty-Rheinland war veteran. It was thanks to her command that the vessel finally reached full combat readiness shortly before its deployment to the Kansas system, where it provided a necessary escort duty for the much heavier Ohio.

As the Insurgency forces were dwindling and retreating from Vespucci, Captain Dovers underestimated the desperate defenders aboard the Marshall Reconstruction Site and was taken by surprise with an unexpected missile salvo from the station. Fusion missile warheads, covertly supplied by Rheinland, have managed to breach the battlecruiser's armour and set off its starboard fuel cells, depressurizing a good third of the ship in one strike. Captain Dovers gave the order to withdraw and get the damage under control, but despite their best efforts, one of the follow up missile salvos managed to strike the ship's torpedo racks. The resulting chain of explosions tore the battlecruiser in half and killed most of its crew, including once famous Captain Dovers.

1121433.text:
CLASS: Horus
CREW: CLASSIFIED
ARMAMENT: CLASSIFIED

1121434.text:
The battleship Horus is the result of the long-running HORUS project developed by a small group of scientists in the Order, and was originally a competing project to the super battleship Thebes. The HORUS project itself has been interrupted several times and cancelled completely a few times due to lack of viability.

The HORUS project was revived when, towards the end of 827 AS, the HADES weapon system, a weapon system specifically designed to permanently destroy Nomads by targeting the basic rules of their anatomy and physiology, was finally demonstrated in the laboratory. Unfortunately, the installation of this system required a complete redesign of the standard Osiris hull, including a new propulsion and power distribution system, leaving the battleship Horus as the only Order ship carrying the system for the time being.

Parametrically, the Horus battleship is the opposite of the super battleship Thebes - it is faster and more agile than the previous Osiris-class, and rather than focusing on blunt offense and defense expressed in the strength of its armor and volume of its firepower, its strengths lie in its smarter firepower, sensors and countermeasures.
While it offers no noticeable improvement over the Osiris in normal conventional combat, the Order's engineers have equipped it with more accurate targeting systems with advanced prediction capabilities, and new sensors allow it to monitor and assess the situation around it and react in time to any cloaked threats before they can actually become a threat. Her new propulsion system allows her to operate the cloaking device for very long periods of time, and even without the cloaking device, her long range sensor picture is interchangeable with a larger cargo ship.

As remarkable as her conventional abilities may seem, it is not the main strength of her design, and that is the presence of the HADES, MINDBREAKER and jump-inhibiting ANCHOR systems that make her the most dangerous ship in Sirius designed to take out the Nomads themselves and their slaves, the Wild.

1121449.text:
E56-15 "Yari" Blood Dragon Freighter

Upon first inspection, you would be forgiven for assuming that this vessel is merely another freight ship. But beneath the humble exterior and round silhouette is a venerable troop transport, also possessing an exemplary ground support systems suite. The Yari is capable of confounding sensor scopes and delivering small fireteams of Blood Dragon Commandos to their destination in short order. A novel feature of this ship is the fact that its tractor beam array has been extensively modified, now capable of extracting personnel both expediently and safely. This affords it a vital role in the war for Kusari's legacy.

1121451.text: These bastards have the audacity to treat us like some drooling clientele, they hold this place for now, but underestimate what the potential costs of this will be. If Eska would waive our fees, we might be sufficiently motivated to protect his claim. I'm sure overly ambitious lieutenants and Outcast reprisal will move him in the direction of sense soon enough.

1121452.text: Try not to tell anyone, but Sue Williams is looking to retire here. You know, the LA surf champion from 800? Yeah, her. I figure she likes the idea of finally being able to live out by the water, and not having to worry about Ageira or Interspace's lackeys getting in the way of a good wave. Can't say I blame her, if anything I'm a little jealous, it's a picturesque way to settle down.

1121454.text:
During the uprising of 831 AS, the Mollys succeeded in drawing away the Battleship Essex from its position guarding the New London jump gate, enabling them to attach a large explosive charge to the gate's superstructure. When the charge was detonated, the gate's outer housing was shattered, destabilizing the core mechanism.

While the Battleship Essex was able to activate the damaged gate and escape back to New London, some elements of its support fleet were mid-transit and consequently lost when the deteriorating core detonated. It is theorized that hyperspace feedback from the destruction of an activated gate may have knocked many of the system's jump holes out of phase alignment.

Ageira Technologies has advised that it will not be possible to comment on the prospects of reconstruction until the system has been fully secured and their proprietary technology recovered.

1121457.text:
Near the wreck of the Hood lies an asteroid field, already plundered of any Gold it may have once held. The field is the site of an extremely hazardous race course that the jaded inhabitants of the Hood once liked to run when hopped up on the sunshine that passed for alcohol aboard the ship. Racing largely halted following the Hood's destruction, save by the Corsairs who now control the area.

NOTE: The Mollys claim control over Dublin; they will attack any outsiders who enter areas under their control.

1121459.text: Intended to serve as a representation of its namesake, the Goodwill is a strategic move by the Liberty food giant to corner Kusari as a market. Boasting state of the art facilities, and a bounty of products intended for distribution as part of the relief effort, the liner has become as much a sign of the times as it is a target. Samura had initially hoped to lobby against its entry into Kusari altogether, but incentives offered by the competition proved too tempting to refuse. Rumours abound that a deal has been brokered with the Blood Dragons to ensure that the Farmers Alliance is kept in check. The Liners continued pressurized state lends some credence to this theory, as State Police patrols are often paid off by Samura to ensure vulnerability.

1121462.text:
Originally constructed in 521 AS, to oversee the transition of trade lanes and jump gates to Rheinland ownership after Interspace Commerce was all but forced to sign agreements to nationalise them, Bonn Station has since become the headquarters of Interspace within Rheinland, and is the station where all cargo being shipped out of Rheinland is insured for the journey.

Thoroughly angry with having to wipe countless billions of credits of debt away almost overnight, after Kusari and Rheinland both nationalised their trade lanes and jump gates, Interspace Commerce has never been satisfied with the two hundred years of tolls it got in exchange, and it is for this chief reason that a good deal of animosity towards Rheinland and Kusari exists even today. As a result, Interspace Commerce often allows ships from the Bundschuh, Red Hessians and even the Unioners to dock and purchase supplies, and even going so far as to donate money to their causes or share information of cargo shipments with them.

This has angered the Rheinland government considerably, although as yet it has been completely impossible to prove. However, the Rheinland Military has recently stationed the Battleship Strausberg outside the station to keep an eye on Interspace's activities.

1121463.text:
Initially charted in the original exploration of the Frankfurt system in 82 AS, the planet Holstein was ignored for centuries by the government as its primary concern was the industrial development of Rheinland. Eventually, with the help of prominent politicians on New Berlin, Kruger Minerals succeeded in obtaining the financial loans from Interspace Commerce in order to terraform Holstein, which started in 519 AS

With the outbreak of the Eighty Years war between Rheinland and the GMG in 589 AS, the terraforming operations were abandoned as Kruger hastily pulled out of the system. The Frankfurt system became a staging point for military supplies moving to the frontlines in Sigma 13 for many years, with little corporate activity, until the war came to an abrupt end in 668 AS

After the war, Kruger suffered a stock crash and was forced to make considerable reparations to the Gas Miners Guild, and its operations in Frankfurt never really recovered, with the mining corporation focusing more attention on the Omega 3 and Omega 7 systems. Republican Shipping seized upon the opportunity to acquire the Mainz Storage Facility in orbit of Stulingen, a moon of Holstein, with Daumann constructing Mannheim and a number of deuterium gas miners in the atmosphere of the gas giant Heidelberg.

With the end of the Nomad War, Kruger Minerals offered to transfer ownership of the planet Holstein to Daumann in exchange for the gas miners on Heidelberg. Daumann readily agreed, and upon gaining the rights to the planet, eagerly restarted the terraforming process. Since the planet is already habitable, although with somewhat unpleasantly cold conditions, a number of settlements have already sprung up on the surface under Daumann's watchful eyes, with the current population settling at slightly over 60 million. It is expected that the terraforming operation will be completed within the next couple of years, so patrols have been stepped up to ensure the final stages are completed without interruption.

1121464.text:
Despite the inherent dangers of the Ruhrfeld, including lethal radiation fields and explosive gas pockets, a large population of Junkers moved into the asteroid field and began building Kreuzberg Depot, which finished construction in 618 AS

Most of the Kreuzberg Junkers spend their time sifting through the wreckage of ships destroyed in gas pockets or in fights with the local law enforcement who occasionally venture into the field. They also do a steady trade in artifacts and all manner of other goods that both the Corsair smugglers and Red Hessian pirates who dock at the station are only too happy to dispose of.

Many LWB and Unioners also frequent the base to resupply while on their way to raid planet New Berlin, or repairing on their way back to their bases. It is also rumoured to be one of the waypoints for the illegal blood diamond smuggling rings that the Red Hessians are known to be involved in, though the diamonds are not actually acquired from here.

The Rheinland authorities dislike the Junkers, but have so far made no attempt to remove them, as they provide a valuable service in clearing up dangerous wreckage and debris that not even ALG is willing to deal with, and so for now their presence remains tolerated, albeit barely.

1121465.text: Originally built in 326 AS to handle all the goods flowing into Rheinland from Liberty and back, Altona Station has been an important base for Rheinländische Großspedition for centuries. Prior to the Eighty Years War, Liberty transports were required to transfer their cargo at Altona - usually Engine Components and Superconductors, and return with cargo bought at Altona - usually Copper, Silver or Cobalt. After the Eighty Years War this practise ended. Part of the Rheinland bailout deal was that Liberty shipping companies would have access to goods throughout Rheinland, bypassing Rheinländische Großspedition. Altona became obsolete overnight. With the return of the Rheinland Empire, the terms of this deal in doubt, potentially seeing a revival of the fortunes of Altona.

1121466.text:
The Battleship Westfalen has had a long and turbulent history, ever since the original battleship was commissioned in 676 AS It was the only battleship to survive the Eighty Years War against the GMG, with the broken remains of her sister ships still scattered across the Sigma 13 nebula even today.

Falling apart, with a serious shortage of manpower and spare parts, the Westfalen was eventually relocated to the Hamburg system in order to clamp down on the ever-increasing Bundschuh and Unioner attacks.

After nearly a hundred and thirty years of increasingly unreliable service, the battleship was finally scrapped, its parts sent to ALG for recycling. However, due to the exemplary record of the ship, and its history of service, it was agreed to christen the first of the new Bismarck class battleships as the new Westfalen, and the vessel is once again stationed in Hamburg, serving as a highly visible symbol of the Chancellor's growing military power.

1121467.text:
CLASS: Westfalen
CREW: N/A
ARMAMENT: N/A

The Battleship Strausberg was completed in 815 AS and deployed to bolster security in New Berlin. During its initial years of service, the Strausberg acquired a reputation for ruthlessness, with a disproportionately high kill to capture ratio against Bundschuh and Red Hessian targets. During the Fall of Dresden in 820 AS, the Strausberg was ordered to prevent “contagion” disorder in Berlin by conducting aggressive anti-Hessian operations in the Saarfield. It departed New Berlin in 825 AS with the outbreak of the Saigon War, where it assisted with the invasion of Sigma-21 and occupation of Planet Saigon. Similar to the Battleship Kolleda, Strausberg initially refused to honor the Sigma Treaty ending the war, only withdrawing to Rheinland when threatened with desertion charges.

In the days before the Civil War, the Strausberg returned to Oder Shipyard for ‘unscheduled’ maintenance. From there it unsuccessfully attempted to arrest the Federal government, who were instead evacuated by the loyalist Carrier Saar. The Strausberg fired several times on Planet New Berlin during the war, and frequently fought the Saar’s strike wings as they sortied from Frankfurt. Following the Holstein Accords in 828 AS, the Strausberg participated successfully in the Recapture of Cologne, alongside the Battleship Altenburg. Believing the Hessians to be significantly weaker than previously thought, the Strausberg later led Rheinland’s Dresden Campaign in 832 AS.

The expedition was ambushed by the Hessian Battleship Kassel in the Innenstadtfeld. Despite suffering heavy damage to its reactor plating, the Strausberg’s heavier armament and fleet allowed it to overpower its opponent. The fleet was forced to abandon the attack on Leipzig, initiating a slow retreat towards New Berlin. Near the Bautzen Wreck, the Strausberg again came under heavy assault by Hessian bomber squadrons. These wings successfully landed several torpedoes on the damaged reactor, leading to a critical meltdown. Orders were given to strip and scuttle the ship to prevent it falling into enemy hands. Some in the Military have bitterly complained that the Hessian defense was significantly aided by the operation’s start date being announced by the Emperor at a social event, while gloating about the Hessians’ impending destruction.

1121468.text:
Commissioned in 805 AS, the Karlsruhe was assigned to protect Rheinland interests in the Stuttgart system, stationed near the Planet Stuttgart Docking Ring, an area frequently raided by LWB fighters. This has led to some rumors that Synth Foods did more than merely appeal to the Rheinland government for better protection of its assets. The Karlsruhe did its job well in orbit, but did little to stop the extremists on the surface.

Following the Imperial coup in 827 A.S., the Karlsruhe was faced with a choice to either join the Imperialists or remain loyal. The latter option was taken, in contrast to the vast majority of the Rheinland Military. This would lead many to think that a career long service in defense of Synth Foods interests in Stuttgart, had resulted in the officer corps being in the pay of the corporation. A more common theory is that many of the men and women of the fleet were Stuttgart natives, whose families had not suffered economic turmoil under the Federal government as other planets had. The victims of the Synth Foods monopoly were not a common recruit of the Military that served to protect it, so anti-corporate, anti-federal sentiment was at a minimum.

There was a brief period of uneasy calm before the scale of their predicament, and the gravity of their choice became clear. The Imperials were quick to respond, and the Altenburg pursued from Omega-7. The Karlsruhe opted to flee to Cologne, however the Altenburg arrived just as the Karlsruhe left orbit, and a brief yet bloody engagement ensued. Losses were many, but the Karlsruhe succesfully disingaged. and entered Cologne.

This would not be the final destination however, as the system was beset by reports of Hessian fleets building in the Weisskugelfeld. Fearing the worst, the Karlsruhe took the only path available to it, and entered Zurich directly through the new jump gate, and into the unknown.

1121469.text:
CLASS: Bismarck
CREW: CLASSIFIED
ARMAMENT: CLASSIFIED

1121470.text:
The Sunderland Research Aerostat was constructed at Scarborough Shipyard in 736 AS, and towed to the gas giant Darlington later the following year. The Aerostat is the Bretonia Intelligence Service’s most ambitious and expensive project, acting as the headquarters for the research and exploration of the Dom’Kavash structure known as Site Jarrow. Sunderland relies on a combination of locally harvested buoyancy gasses, onboard thrusters, and secured anchor struts to maintain its altitude in spite of the planet’s tumultuous atmosphere and intense gravity well.

The decision to deploy Sunderland followed a breakthrough in the study of the Amiatinus Cache, a recovered Artifact that had progressed the then-rudimentary understanding of Dom’Kavash glyphs. This hinted at an acoustic, almost musical, component to their language. Experiments in this area revealed the presence of a concealed airlock on Site Jarrow, allowing for the creation of the Sunderland Umbilical to gain access to further sections of the interior. While scientists now have access to several isolated compartments within Jarrow, understanding of its purpose and technologies remains stubbornly limited.

Despite this, even small insights have occasionally advanced Bretonian science by decades. Notable examples include the 798 AS discovery of an Artifact fragment depicting part of a novel chemical process for the production of Super Alloys. By 806 AS, Sunderland provided an experimental procedure to Scarborough Shipyard for implementation; this revolutionized the previously inefficient and expensive method used aboard Stokes Smelter, allowing the faltering industry to catch and then surpass Liberty's progress in the field.

Bretonia’s recent wars and dire situation have placed Sunderland under incredible pressure to produce useful military technologies. This created a culture of high-stakes risk-taking, causing the injury or death of numerous explorers and scientists. In 831 AS, Sunderland also received significant damage during “The Blink”, in which Jarrow’s anti-gravity pylons momentarily failed, causing it to drop over a kilometer. As of 834 AS, there are signs that Jarrow may be preparing to fully awaken. Most other avenues of research have been halted, in favor of investigating the implications of an activation scenario -- and developing contingencies for Jarrow’s destruction should this pose a threat to Bretonia.

1121471.text: Wreck of a Bretonian Fighter, most probably destroyed in Yorkshire station explosion.

1121472.text:
The Lancaster Trade Centre was the first station to be constructed in Newcastle after its discovery. From Lancaster, DSE built out the trade lanes to Carlisle and beyond, while Border World Exports and Bretonia Mining and Manufacturing used it as a depot to establish their own facilities.

In recent times, the importance of Lancaster has been greatly diminished. Border World Exports administers the station, using it mainly as a storage depot for Scarborough and the Carlisle settling efforts.

1121473.text:
CLASS: Hawking
GRAVITY: Complete
DOCKING: Yes
AMENITIES: Yes
CREW: CLASSIFIED

1121474.text:
First charted in 539 AS, after the discovery of the Munich system in the same year by a Kruger survey vessel, the planet Nuremberg was largely ignored for nearly twenty years, despite a pleasantly temperate climate, with large tracts of plains and savannah that were suitable for farming and settlement. Kruger was instead more interested in the Schwarzwald and Alps clouds, which contained significant amounts of cobalt and silicon, and constructed several small automated mining platforms within the nebulas.

In 557 AS a jump gate was constructed, connecting the Munich system with Frankfurt, and civilian traffic was able to move freely into the system for the first time. Upon further inspection of Nuremberg, it was agreed to begin colonisation immediately, and hundreds of thousands of people from across Rheinland flocked to the new planet in the hopes of securing some of the available land for themselves. Deep Space Engineering soon moved in to begin construction on a series of trade lanes, and the Battleship Erlangen was stationed in orbit of Nuremberg to maintain order.

Nuremberg's oceans were soon revealed to be largely unsuitable for fishing, as most of the dangerous oceanic predators, such as the Pirasharq, quickly destroyed any imported fish stocks. On the land it was a similar story, and it was discovered that the initial planetary scans had missed the dangerous Gimeni worms that inhabited the soil across much of the planet. Virtually all of the imported crops also failed to germinate, despite seemingly ideal conditions. After several years, science teams from Planetform were able to determine that a chemical in the soil was responsible. It was soon found that the skin of the Gimeni worm secretes a chemical that kills any plant life not native to Nuremberg.

In despair, many of the planet's population started abandoning Nuremberg and returning to other parts of Rheinland, leaving the planet largely deserted, until in 738 AS when Daumann and Republican Shipping jointly purchased the planet from the bankrupt Rheinland government in order to build manufactories for the construction of military vehicles. As such, many of Nuremberg's current population and available land was devoted to the manufacture of the heavily armored vehicles, and the heavy industry had slowly been polluting the planet.

Despite population numbers still climbing as of 816 AS and the increasing demand for imported food to Nuremberg to support them, the Rheinland government has refused to grant construction approval for any farming concerns, despite continual lobbying by the legitimate political arms of the LWB and Bundschuh, especially after it was discovered that the native grasses could be safely ingested by a number of animals - including pigs and cows - thus making it safe for livestock farming. This had angered the LWB and the Bundschuh, and to some extent even the Unioners, and raids on the planet's surroundings became fairly commonplace over the last few decades.

In advent of a massive dark matter storm that descended upon the system seemingly from nowhere, Nuremberg's population began to undergo a second and likely final exodus. Planetside meteorologists discovered that the dark matter was quickly eroding the entire planet's atmosphere, as what few crops upon the planet remained universally failed. Cancerous diseases increased exponentially upon the surface population and entire cities were thrown into chaos.

Opposition movements both legitimate and otherwise within Rheinland criticized the government, Daumann, and Republican for their tepidly slow response in providing refuge or aid to the masses of desperate Rheinlanders still fleeing the system by the millions. While still nominally capable of its former wartime output, thousands of craft from civilian-fighters to trains routinely breach the atmosphere every day, despite the best efforts of law enforcement to maintain some semblance of order.

The dying planet has in the span of a single year grown to become the most dangerous and lawless place in Rheinland, dropping to the bottom in nearly every civil demographic.

1121475.text:
DIAMETER: 3,316 km
MASS: 4.92 x 10e23 kg
TERRAIN: Barren
TEMPERATURE: N/A
ESCAPE VELOCITY: 1.34 km/sec

A rocky, airless moon of the planet Nuremberg, pock marked with craters. Despite extensive surveys, no significant amounts of any valuable resource have been discovered and it is unlikely that anything will be done with this planetoid beyond the occasional weapons tests done by Daumann and the Rheinland Military on its surface.

1121476.text:
Ingolstadt Station was constructed in 730 AS, a considerable amount of time after the initial colonisation of the planet Nuremberg, in order to handle the ever increasing raw material imports and finished product exports from the many facturies on the planets surface. Most of the space onboard the station is made up of enormous storage bays, and automated loaders.

After the Nomad War ended in 801 AS, Republican Shipping decided to move its center of operations to the Munich system, and although there were large corporate offices planetside, Ingolstadt Station was expanded considerably to serve as the corporate headquarters for Republican Shipping. In 815 AS the station was the target of a Unioner attack, which left over seventy people aboard the station dead.

With the dark matter storm drawing ever closer to Planet Nuremberg, Republican struggled to save their investment, dismantling Ingolstadt Station before it, too, was devoured by the storm front. Ingolstadt's ample berth points, designed for incoming shipping, unintentionally became the residence of Insurgencys of refugee vessels squatting in the docks in the long, human trail off the surface of Nuremburg. Stripped down to the armoured hangarbays, core habitats and service modules, the armored shell of Ingolstadt served as an accidental storm shelter for hundreds of fleeing Rheinlanders, saving many from the horrors of radiation poisoning.

The fall of the Rheinland goverment in 827 AS and the rebranding of Republican into Rheinländische Großspedition, halted dismantling the remains of Ingolstadt.
